BOSTON – A Roslindale man was sentenced yesterday in federal court in Boston for conspiring to distribute fentanyl following a series of controlled drug purchases in Brookline and Boston.

Shaquylle Burden, 32, was sentenced by U.S. District Court Judge Leo T. Sorokin to five years in prison to be followed by four years of supervised release. In July 2026 , Burden pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute fentanyl. In December 2025 , Burden and his co-conspirator Kerry Charlotin were arrested and charged.

In June 2025, an investigation began into drug trafficking activities conducted by Charlotin and Burden. The investigation revealed that the defendants were actively selling fentanyl in the greater Boston area. On two separate dates in October and December 2025, Charlotin and Burden sold or arranged the sale of fentanyl to undercover law enforcement during controlled purchases. One firearm was found in Burden’s Roslindale residence at the time of his arrest.

In July 2026 , Charlotin pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute fentanyl. He is scheduled to be sentenced on Nov. 2, 2026.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation in Boston; and Boston Police Commissioner Michael Cox made the announcement. Valuable assistance was provided by the FBI’s Columbia Field Office in South Carolina. Assistant U.S. Attorney John T. Dawley of the Organized Crime & Gang Unit is prosecuting the case.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.
title: Roslindale Man Sentenced to Five Years in Prison for Drug Conspiracy

Graduation Information
Graduation will occur at “The Airborne Walk” at 0900 for classes that graduate from 01 APR to 30 SEP and 1100 from 01 OCT to 31 MAR. For inclement weather or other unforeseen reasons, the graduation area, day or concept may change. Soldiers will be released for the day once the company is done with their administrative tasks and a safety brief is given to those who are not shipping.

Crow Earns Perfect “A” Grade for Fighting to Protect Democracy
AURORA — Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO), co-chair of the End Corruption Caucus, earned a perfect “A” grade from pro-democracy group Defend the Vote. The legislative score reflects Crow’s work protecting every American’s right to vote, upholding the integrity of our elections, and combating corruption.
“Donald Trump and Congressional Republicans have attacked our democracy by sowing doubt in our elections and making it harder to vote. At every step of the way, I’ve fought back,” said Congressman Crow. “Every American has a right to elect their leaders and vote at the ballot box. I’ll continue fighting in Congress to protect our democracy, get dark money out of our politics, and take on special interests.”
Crow has also received a perfect 10/10 score from Democracy Defenders Action on their Stop Corruption Now Congressional Scorecard and an A+ from good governance group End Citizens United for his work to root out corruption in politics, the only member of Colorado’s House delegation to receive the grade.
Crow is fighting to protect elections in Colorado. He recently hosted an election security roundtable alongside local officials to coordinate and discuss efforts to keep Colorado’s election system strong.
Throughout his time in Congress, Crow has stood up to special interests and has not taken a dime of corporate PAC money. He is an original cosponsor of the TRUST in Congress Act to ban members of Congress and their families from owning or trading stocks and has led the call to ban members of Congress and their staff from insider trading on prediction markets. Crow is leading the fight to root out corruption in our elections, including through his End Dark Money Act and SHINE Act to crack down on dark money’s influence on U.S. elections.
Crow is also leading the charge against this Administration's corruption. He’s demanding answers about potential corruption and favoritism with federal contracts benefiting the Trump family; uncovering conflicts of interest at the Pentagon stemming from Pete Hegseth’s special adviser Tim Parlatore; and is leading a slate of historic pro-democracy reforms aimed at preventing presidential abuses of power, rooting out corruption, strengthening checks and balances, and protecting American elections against foreign influence.

title: Crow Earns Perfect “A” Grade for Fighting to Protect Democracy

Davids, Local Business Owners Discuss Responsible AI, Industry Growth
Leading tech executives recently advocated for slowdowns to AI
OVERLAND PARK, KC — Today, Representative Sharice Davids joined the KC Tech Council and more than a dozen business owners for a roundtable on emerging technology, artificial intelligence (AI), infrastructure, and business innovation. The conversation centered on finding a balance between economic growth and safety regulations — a perspective Davids plans to bring to Washington.
“Today was a real learning opportunity for me,” said Davids. “Artificial intelligence holds incredible promise for our small businesses, but we cannot ignore the real dangers. AI companies need to be held accountable especially when their products put kids at risk, and local communities shouldn’t be left footing the bill for the massive energy infrastructure these corporations require. I’m taking what I heard from our local business leaders today back to Washington to make sure Congress strikes the right balance between supporting economic growth and keeping our families safe.”
According to a recent survey, about 3 out of 4 small businesses use AI tools today, and almost all of them say it’s helping their business run better and faster. Even as local businesses use these technologies to grow, most Americans say the government needs to step in with basic safety rules. Recent national polls show that over 80 percent of voters want clear standards to keep AI safe for kids and families. Davids made clear that Washington must listen to both sides — helping local businesses succeed while putting sensible guardrails in place to protect the public.
During the discussion, attendees covered a wide range of policy areas impacting the regional economy, including:
- Federal AI Policy and Data Privacy: Developing a clear, unified national framework for responsible AI deployment and strong federal data privacy standards.
- Energy, Grid Capacity, and Infrastructure: Addressing high-power energy demands through permitting reform and targeted infrastructure investment.
- Manufacturing and Supply Chain Resilience: Strengthening domestic manufacturing, electric vehicle (EV) battery investment, and supply chain security across the Midwest.
- Healthcare IT and Interoperability: Improving healthcare data systems to enhance patient outcomes and streamline health IT operations.
- Workforce Development and Veteran Training: Expanding tech training pathways, including funding for veteran tech workforce programs.
- Small Business and Entrepreneurship: Increasing access to capital and federal resource programs for local startups and small business owners.
Participants Included:
- Beale Infrastructure
- Black & Veatch
- Centriq Training
- Comcast
- Delta Dental of Kansas
- Garmin
- Hallmark Cards
- Kiewit Engineering
- NvisionKC
- Panasonic
- Stinson LLP
- Veracity Consulting
- WellSky
Davids will use the feedback gathered from today’s session to inform her legislative work as D.C. considers federal AI guardrails, energy infrastructure, and economic development legislation.
title: Davids, Local Business Owners Discuss Responsible AI, Industry Growth

KOLDING, Denmark — Thirteen U.S. Army Veterinary Corps officers recently completed Europe Dairy Pasteurizer Audit Training in Kolding, Denmark by participating in specialized technical instruction and on-site field evaluations across eight Danish dairy manufacturing facilities.
The intensive course, held Sept. 13-26, was led by Chief Warrant Officer 4 Clayton Davenport, command food safety officer for Public Health Command Europe. The training brought together military auditors stationed across multiple commands and operational theaters, including Public Health Command Europe, Public Health Command Pacific, Multinational Force and Observers Egypt, Area Support Group Kuwait, and the 445th Medical Detachment Veterinary Service Support.
"The primary training objective was to provide progressive and sequential auditor development training in pasteurizer operations that enhances understanding of the public health controls of various pasteurizers," Davenport said.
The program directly supports military readiness by safeguarding the Department of War food supply, ensuring safe, wholesome dairy products reach service members, warfighters and military families overseas.
In the United States, commercial milk processing adheres strictly to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s Pasteurized Milk Ordinance (PMO), widely recognized as the domestic standard for the design, operation and testing of pasteurization equipment.
"The milk sanitation program of the United States Public Health Service is one of its oldest and most respected activities," Davenport said.
However, public health experts note that commercial pasteurization systems across Europe, Africa and the Middle East often do not conform to standard PMO criteria. To bridge that regulatory difference, the specialized course has been developed, taught and refined since 2004 to equip overseas Veterinary Corps officers with the technical expertise needed to assess foreign pasteurization machinery.
Armed with that training, officers can determine whether pasteurizers operating outside the United States provide an equivalent or superior level of food safety compared to American standards.
Public health officials consider the Public Health Command Europe program the only training of its kind in the world. It offers military inspectors an exclusive opportunity to examine more than 65 distinct pasteurizer configurations that supply dairy products to the largest concentration of U.S. forces stationed outside the United States.
Field evaluations were conducted at eight Danish commercial plants currently certified as approved sources for U.S. military procurement, giving inspectors practical experience evaluating equipment controls and safety margins under active operating conditions.
“Maintaining specialized auditing capabilities remains essential to force health protection, particularly amid budgetary pressures,” added Davenport.
title: Army Veterinary Officers Complete Specialized Dairy Pasteurizer Audit Training in Denmark

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Rob Menendez (NJ-08) introduced the Socket Full of Sunshine Act, legislation that expands access to plug-in solar panels and helps families lower their utility bills The legislation would support rebates for eligible households, protect renters’ access, and require states to consider removing unnecessary regulatory hurdles. In New Jersey, monthly utility bills rose nearly 17 percent in 2025, twice the national average.
“Families are getting squeezed by electric bills that keep going up,” said Congressman Rob Menendez. “Plug-in solar is a simple, affordable way to cut those bills, but outdated rules and unnecessary fees are standing in the way. The Socket Full of Sunshine Act clears those barriers so more families, including renters, can start saving.”
A typical plug-in solar system consists of 1-4 panels, with current costs ranging from $285-$3,500 depending on size and inclusion of a battery. They can cut electricity bills by hundreds of dollars a year without complicated installation costs. The use of plug-in solar systems can also help households and businesses meet their energy needs through sustainable and renewable energy and lessen America’s dependence on fossil fuels and other sources of pollution.
While plug-in solar systems are intended to be “plug-and-play,” some utilities and state laws require that they be subjected to utility connection agreements that apply to larger rooftop solar installations. These agreements and other unnecessary installation costs or requirements can double the price of these systems and prevent renters, apartment dwellers, or other households from accessing this practical option to reduce electricity costs.
The Socket Full of Sunshine Act would:
This legislation has been endorsed by the Sierra Club, the New Jersey chapter of the League of Conservation Voters, The Consumer Federation of America, Evergreen Action, the Solar Energy Manufacturers for America Coalition, and Bright Saver.
“Plug-in solar can help households reduce energy bills, lower demand on the grid, and decrease dangerous emissions,” said Sierra Club Deputy Legislative Director for Clean Energy and Electrification Xavier Boatright. “This bill would help renters and low- and moderate-income households access the benefits of clean energy. We are grateful for Representative Menendez’s leadership in introducing this bill to bring American-made plug-in solar panels to more people.”
“Plug-in solar can help put clean energy within reach of more American families, giving renters and homeowners another way to manage their electricity costs. By expanding access to these technologies and providing rebates for low and moderate-income households, we can provide common sense ways to access cheaper clean energy,” said Allison McLeod, Interim Executive Director, New Jersey LCV. “The Socket Full of Sunshine Act recognizes that the benefits of the clean energy transition should be accessible to everyone. We applaud Representative Rob Menendez Jr. for advancing an approach that connects energy affordability, consumer choice, and American-made clean energy.”
“Balcony solar is a safe and accessible way to reduce individual home energy costs. This Act will bring solar power to far more American homes,” said Consumer Federation of America Director of Climate and Energy Policy Karim Marshall. “CFA enthusiastically supports the 'Socket Full of Sunshine Act' and applauds Representative Menendez for his visionary leadership in introducing this bill. It reflects a thoughtful and meaningful package of solutions that will enable consumers to save real money on their skyrocketing electric bills and ensure that deployment is done in the safest way possible.”
“Americans are being squeezed by record-high energy bills and they need relief now. The Socket Full of Sunshine Act would put solar energy and the savings it offers within reach for renters and low to moderate income households who have been shut out for too long,” said Evergreen Action Federal Affairs Director Dani Hupper. “By making it easier to access plug-in solar panels, this legislation will let families generate their own clean power and save hundreds of dollars a year on their bills. Solar is already saving families money. This bill makes sure renters and working families aren't left out.”
“As America works to rebuild its domestic solar manufacturing industry, we need to make sure growing demand for solar energy also supports the workers and companies making these products here at home,” said Solar Energy Manufacturers for America Coalition Executive Director Mike Carr. “The Socket Full of Sunshine Act recognizes that expanding access to affordable solar energy and supporting American manufacturing should go hand in hand. By prioritizing American-made products and tying federal rebates to domestic manufacturing and content requirements, this legislation can help create new demand for U.S.-made solar products and strengthen our domestic supply chains. Plug-in solar offers another way for Americans to lower their electricity bills while supporting American jobs and building a brighter future for domestic manufacturing.”
“Representative Menendez has just taken a giant leap toward energy affordability for all Americans,” said Bright Saver Co-CEO and Co-Founder Cora Stryker. “10 states now have laws on the books to open the door to affordable solar that plugs into a standard outlet. Representative Menendez has just opened the door to energy equity in all 50 states, for renters and homeowners alike.”
Congressman Rob Menendez has been a leading voice for lowering energy costs for New Jersey families, earlier this year introducing the PRICE Act, the Data Center Transparency Act, and the Load Forecasting Enhancement Act which passed the House in September. Congressman Menendez has represented New Jersey’s Eighth District since 2023. He serves on the Energy and Commerce Committee and its Subcommittees on Environment, Energy, and Communications and Technology. To learn more about his work, click here.
Read the full bill text here.
title: Menendez Introduces Bill to Expand Access to Plug-In Solar and Lower Electric Bills

text:
The American Psychological Association defines resilience in part as: the process and outcome of successfully adapting to difficult or challenging life experiences, especially through mental, emotional, and behavioral flexibility and adjustment.
Leonard Adams embodies this definition, overcoming a difficult childhood to become a resilient Soldier, father, counselor and published author.
Adams is an operations research systems analyst at the Security Assistance Command, within its G2/6 directorate. Most colleagues know him as the soloist who sings the national anthem at ceremonies a cappella. Or they know him as a soft-spoken friend with sage advice.
Not many of his teammates know the hardships he and his nine siblings endured in their south side of Chicago environment. If they see the scar on his head, they may think it came from an injury during his Army service, and not an attack by his father.
Adams’ parents divorced when he was very young. Most of the children ended up with their father after being told their mother had abandoned them. He learned later that was not true.
After their father remarried, most of the physical abuse began. Beatings, being tied up, and even one younger sibling being placed inside a hot oven, were just some of the horrors he endured or witnessed.
When he was 16, he described his childhood to his school psychologist who told Adams that if he became a mass murderer, no one could blame him. His descriptions were not sensational; they were real life.
His mother came to see her children after learning where they lived years after the divorce. She told the children if they ever wanted to see her to, “Hop in a taxi and I’ll pay for it.” Slowly the siblings moved out of their father’s house to go live with their mother. Adams was 14 when he moved to her house.
It was crowded at his mother’s, but full of love and safety. His mother had taken in five of her nieces and nephews, plus other children of friends. At one time there were 17 people living there. Sometimes they were eating off $5 a day. But they were not being mistreated or abused.
Adams enlisted in the Army in Chicago, and landed at Fort Sill, Oklahoma. He admits he entered the Army as an angry young man, carrying his trauma from his years of abuse and belittling. “Particularly in my early 20s and as a teenager, I was full of hate, full of fear. I hated life and was miserable all the time.”
His older brother had enlisted in the Army and served as a nurse. Since a nurse was close to being a doctor, which he aspired to be, Adams decided that was a good route to take.
While at Fort Sill, he took college courses at night. Eventually he entered the Green to Gold program, where the Army allowed him to attend school full time, and he was a cadet in the Reserve Officer Training Corps. He was pinned with his second lieutenant bar once he finished with a degree from Cameron University, in Lawton, Oklahoma.
Adams’ entry tests showed he was color blind, which prevented him from entering the nursing field. He wanted to stay in the medical arena, so he chose counseling. That decision was the beginning of Adams’ future endeavors. “I did not know the benefits counseling would have on my life.”
After leaving his Army service Adams worked as a counselor in the Tennessee Department of Corrections. Specifically, Adams worked in a mental health prison where he had to determine the level of incarceration for prisoners. Included in his duties was developing training for the guards and prison staff on behavioral therapy.
It was during a counseling session with an inmate that a light bulb went off for Adams. “I had a person in a session ask what I knew about pain? He said I was always smiling, and that I must have grown up in a ‘Leave it to Beaver’ household.’” Adams then started to share his childhood trauma and began to see how his background could help others, including himself.
People have asked him how he has avoided becoming jaded or bitter. He shares that he was not always the man he is now. “Once I became a counselor and learned the techniques of behavioral therapy, I started applying them to myself because I did not want to spend the rest of my life unforgiving, bitter and miserable. I knew I had control of the rest of my life.”
He eventually moved to Huntsville, worked as a defense contractor and then became an Army civilian. In 2021 he joined USASAC.
For years Adams has been writing and journaling about his childhood, and ways to overcome adversity. In 2018 he finished his first book, “Things I Wish My Father Had Told Me” and set out to have it published. After numerous rejection letters, he self-published. One rejection from a publisher said that he would have to make significant edits, so Adams decided he would not work with a traditional publishing house. The book was updated and re-released in August 2026. The new edition includes more questions he wished he could have asked his father.
His second published work, “Prepare to Love: 100 Questions and Answers,” was published in 2024 and includes honest, raw questions that real people have asked him over the years. Questions include ones about self-worth, relationship advice, and growing as a person.
Adams says he is not finished writing. He will retire in October and plans on writing a 12-part series called “Breaking the Beliefs That Break You.” Each book will cover an irrational belief, such as the need for perfection, or talking negatively about yourself. This upcoming series will be an extension of the training he developed for the Tennessee Department of Corrections but will be more in-depth.
What makes a person more resilient than others from the same environment is still an evolving field of study. Adams shared that the other five siblings who were as exposed to the abuse as he was have had different outcomes. One sibling became an alcoholic but is better because of rehab, while the sister who was placed in the oven ended up in psychiatric institutions.
He gives a lot of credit to the Army for helping him become who he is today. The Army gave him the tools to turn his experiences around and heal from his trauma. “It made me the man I have become. I remain a grateful person in a grateful nation.”
title: Security enterprise author credits Army for his healing, growth

CONGRESSMAN JOE MORELLE ANNOUNCES $500,000 IN FEDERAL FUNDING TO SUPPORT SURVIVORS OF GUN VIOLENCE IN ROCHESTER
Funding secured through the Fiscal Year 2026 appropriations process will help Rise Up Rochester provide emergency housing assistance, victim advocacy, and critical support services
(Rochester, N.Y.)—Today, Congressman Joe Morelle announced $500,000 in federal funding for Rise Up Rochester's Safe Housing Gun Violence Response Program, which provides critical assistance to individuals and families impacted by gun violence. The funding, secured through the Fiscal Year 2026 Community Project Funding process, will help survivors access emergency housing relocation, victim advocacy, and other essential services as they work to rebuild their lives.
“Gun violence leaves lasting scars on individuals, families, and entire neighborhoods, and we have a responsibility to ensure survivors are not left to navigate the aftermath alone,” said Congressman Joe Morelle. “I'm proud to have secured this investment to strengthen the important work of Rise Up Rochester and help ensure more people in our community have the stability, security, and support they deserve.”
“Communities most impacted by gun violence deserve more than sympathy, they deserve resources,” said Chiamaka Ikpeze, Executive Director of Rise Up Rochester. “This funding allows us to provide immediate safety, housing support, and advocacy for survivors and families facing some of the hardest moments of their lives. We are deeply grateful for Congressman Joe Morelle and his commitment to our community.”
Rise Up Rochester, in partnership with Coordinated Care Services, Inc. (CCSI), will utilize the funding to address the immediate safety, housing, and recovery needs of gun violence survivors throughout Rochester. The Safe Housing Gun Violence Response Program will provide real-time relocation assistance and temporary housing support to help individuals and families move to safer living environments following incidents of gun violence.
The program will also provide victim advocacy, court accompaniment for survivors participating in legal proceedings, transportation assistance, and support services to help individuals navigate the challenges that often follow violent incidents. By combining immediate crisis intervention with longer-term stabilization efforts, the initiative aims to help survivors regain a sense of security while strengthening the safety and well-being of families and neighborhoods across Rochester.
###
title: CONGRESSMAN JOE MORELLE ANNOUNCES $500,000 IN FEDERAL FUNDING TO SUPPORT SURVIVORS OF GUN VIOLENCE IN ROCHESTER

PHOTO RELEASE: “Josh on the Job” — Gottheimer Visits Wendy’s in Bogota
Above: Gottheimer with staff at Wendy’s.
BOGOTA, NJ — Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) visited Wendy’s in Bogota to meet with local owners and employees, working alongside their team and hearing first-hand from Jersey customers as part of his “Josh on the Job” series highlighting locally owned businesses and franchises across northern New Jersey.
During his visit, Gottheimer joined staff behind the counter, speaking with employees and customers from across the community about the challenges and opportunities facing small businesses today.
“Franchises like our local Wendy’s are run by neighbors who invested in this community, and they’re powered every day by the hard-working crew behind the counter,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “Spending a day working alongside the team gives me a first-hand look at what our franchise owners and their employees are really up against. I’ll keep fighting to lower costs, cut through the red tape, and make sure our workers and local businesses have what they need to thrive.”
Gottheimer regularly visits small businesses and franchises across New Jersey’s Fifth District as part of his Josh on the Job series to hear directly from workers, owners, and customers about the issues impacting their jobs and their communities.

RM Raskin, Rep. Ansari Demand Answers on Trump Administration’s Efforts to Help Tate Brothers Evade Rape and Sex Trafficking Charges as They Face Extradition to U.K.
Lawmakers Press Blanche and Rubio to Disclose Intervention and Answer Whether Administration Will Honor Extradition Requests
Washington, D.C. (October 20, 2026)—Today, Rep. Jamie Raskin, Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Committee, and Rep. Yassamin Ansari are demanding answers from Attorney General Todd Blanche and Secretary of State Marco Rubio about the Trump Administration’s reported efforts to help Andrew and Tristan Tate evade criminal charges and whether it will comply with the United Kingdom’s request to extradite the brothers to face rape and sex trafficking charges. The longtime Trump supporters remain in federal custody and face a stunning 59 criminal charges in the United Kingdom. The Administration has yet to substantively answer Ranking Member Raskin’s earlier inquiry into its efforts to help the Tates leave Romania, while new reporting has revealed further intervention on their behalf.
“Despite the looming prosecutions, the Tate brothers have continued to accumulate new criminal accusations and charges since returning to the U.S. [...] However, given the Trump Administration’s reported willingness to intervene both internationally and domestically on the Tate brothers’ behalf as they face serious criminal charges involving violent crimes and given the failure of any official to provide substantive responses to Ranking Member Raskin’s previous correspondence, we remain skeptical that the Administration will sit on the sidelines rather than jump into the game to help the Tates,” wrote the lawmakers.
The brothers have continued to face new allegations of sexual violence and trafficking since returning to the United States. Less than two weeks after their arrival, Andrew allegedly assaulted his girlfriend, Bri Stern, in Los Angeles; reported text messages show him repeatedly telling her he wanted to hit and beat her and that she deserved it. Former right-wing influencer Lauren Southern also accused Andrew of choking and assaulting her in a Bucharest hotel room in 2018. The brothers were arrested in Miami in July 2026 after British authorities issued 38 additional charges, including nine additional rape counts between them, bringing the total to 59. Romanian prosecutors subsequently announced a second indictment, charging Andrew with trafficking minors, money laundering, sex with a minor and witness tampering, and Tristan with complicity in those alleged crimes.
Ranking Member Raskin first sought answers in April 2025 about Administration pressure on Romania to lift the brothers’ court-imposed travel restrictions. No Trump Administration official provided a substantive response. Instead, Special Presidential Envoy Richard Grenell called Judiciary Committee Minority staff to complain about the inquiry, which highlighted reports that he raised the Tates’ case with Romanian officials at the Munich Security Conference.
Rep. Ansari also called on House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer on July 23 to investigate the Tate brothers’ ties to the Trump Administration. Chairman Comer has not responded.
Subsequent reporting exposed further efforts by a Trump Administration official to help the brothers. ProPublica reported that White House official Paul Ingrassia, a former lawyer for the brothers, urged senior Department of Homeland Security officials to return electronic devices seized from them when they entered the United States in February 2025. Ingrassia denied intervening. Andrew Tate also reportedly cultivated a relationship with President Trump’s son Barron, with the two allegedly agreeing that the Romanian criminal case was an attempt to silence the brothers.
Ranking Member Raskin and Rep. Ansari are requesting disclosure of any consultations, communications or directives from Justice Department leadership concerning the extradition proceedings, including contacts with the prosecutors handling the case. They also seek an accounting of U.S. efforts to lift the Romanian travel restrictions, whether the Tates’ support for Trump influenced those efforts, and records of government engagement with Romanian officials, British officials and the brothers’ attorneys since January 20, 2025.
Click here to read the letter.
title: RM Raskin, Rep. Ansari Demand Answers on Trump Administration’s Efforts to Help Tate Brothers Evade Rape and Sex Trafficking Charges as They Face Extradition to U.K.

FBI Chicago Special Agent in Charge (SAC) Ryan Whalen announced today that Joseph “Troubles” Matos has been added to the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list, increasing the reward amount to $1 million. Matos is wanted in connection with the shooting death of National Guard member Chrys Carvajal.
“Today’s addition of Matos to the FBI’s notorious Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list ensures that his face and description will be found on every FBI-affiliated website and social media platform, and this case will now be on every phone around the world until he is apprehended,” said SAC Whalen. “The FBI is committed to utilizing every tool in our arsenal to ensure that violent criminals are identified, apprehended, and removed from the community. This announcement would not have been possible without the support of our investigative partners at the Chicago Police Department, the prosecuting team under U.S. Attorney Andrew Butros, and the unwavering support from Chrys Carvajal’s incredible family.”
On July 3, 2021, during what should have been a festive Independence Day weekend celebrating Carvajal’s graduation from the National Guardsman Basic Training, it is alleged that Joseph Matos, and a fellow gang member, shot and killed Carvajal while he was walking to his car. After the shooting, the Chicago Police Department began their investigation and a hunt for the perpetrators.
Matos is believed to be a member of the Milwaukee Kings street gang, a criminal organization whose members and associates have engaged in narcotics trafficking and committed acts of violence, including murder and assault, to acquire and preserve the gang’s perceived territory on the North Side of Chicago, Illinois.
A joint investigation by the Chicago Police Department and the FBI resulted in an arrest warrant being issued for Matos in the United States District Court, Northern District of Illinois, Eastern Division, Chicago, Illinois, after he was charged with murder in aid of racketeering and murder through the use of a firearm on May 14, 2024. Several days later, FBI Chicago SWAT operators with the partnership of local law enforcement, conducted SWAT operations to locate Matos and his associate, Gary Roberson. Roberson was taken into custody without incident. Matos was not located and has remained a fugitive.
Matos is a 44-year-old Hispanic male. He stands at 6’2”, weighs approximately 220 pounds, has brown hair, and brown eyes. Matos has the following tattoos: "M-Town Kings" on the right side of his neck; "1300" on the left side of his neck; "Move in Silence" on his right hand; “Trust no one” on his left hand; "MOST WANTED" on his belly; and "Heavensent, Hellbound" on his arms. Matos is believed to be armed and dangerous. He is presumed to still be in the United States, and has ties to Dallas, Texas and California, but is believed to be hiding in the greater Chicago area. Anyone that may be aiding him is committing a serious federal offense and offender(s) will be held accountable.
Matos is the 544th fugitive to be added to the FBI’s Most Wanted Fugitives list. Since inception, the FBI has apprehended or located 504 fugitives, a success rate of over 92%. Since Director Kash Patel’s confirmation to the FBI, eight of FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives have been successfully captured and six of the FBI’s Most Wanted Fraudsters have been captured since it launched in June 2026.
If you have any information, please contact the FBI's Toll-Free tipline at 1-800-CALLFBI (1-800-225-5324); your local FBI office; the nearest American Embassy or Consulate; online at tips.fbi.gov. All information can be submitted anonymously.
title: Joseph “Toubles” Matos, Wanted for Murder, Added to the FBI’s List of Ten Most Wanted Fugitives

FORT HOOD, Texas — III Armored Corps and multinational partners concluded a five-day planning exercise Oct. 2, culminating in a brief to prepare for the corps’ upcoming Warfighter training exercise. Military planners from the three nations worked through the military decision-making process (MDMP) while testing emerging artificial intelligence technologies to support staff analysis and inform commanders during large-scale combat operations.
“We had the opportunity today to work with our allies from the United Kingdom and Poland to learn about their capabilities and how they see III Armored Corps being able to fight as part of a multinational task force, with their unique capabilities and strengths,” said Lt. Col. John Albert, III Armored Corps chief of future operations.
MDMP is a framework for developing risk-mitigated strategies and contingencies for the operational missions Soldiers face; it reduces uncertainty and issues that could cause mission failure.
“The military decision-making process is a staff process that leverages the ability of warfighting function experts to make an optimal military plan,” Albert said.
The process brings together expertise across a headquarters to analyze the operational environment, develop courses of action and determine how to execute them.
“Today’s MDMP process focused on developing the tactical plan that will be fought in a simulation to help stress the staff and the commanders across the corps and division levels,” Albert said.
Allied representatives participated directly in the planning process throughout the week, helping the staff better understand what multinational partners can do before testing those capabilities in the upcoming Warfighter Training Operation.
“It was very good to hear the different perspectives and be able to get it from the horse’s mouth, understand the strengths and capabilities of our allies and be able to incorporate that directly into the plan,” Albert said.
During the MDMP process, planners stress-tested the developing courses through course-of-action analysis; however, this time III Armored Corps planners used the opportunity to use GenAI to simulate conditions and test the course-of-action analysis.
“Using GenAI, especially for III Armored Corps personnel in the Army GenAI, it was extremely helpful as we were war-gaming,” said Maj. Joshua Moore, a III Armored Corps G-35 planner.
Moore helped develop an AI-enabled tool used during the MDMP process that incorporates Army-approved generative AI capabilities, including Gemini and ChatGPT functions available through Army GenAI.
“Wargaming is one of these nebulous processes within MDMP, specifically within the course-of-action analysis steps,” Moore said. “Building the AI tool just enabled us to rapidly come to conclusions that would be helpful for the staff as they conduct their analysis and make sure that the courses of action are actually viable to present to the commander.”
The experimentation is part of a larger effort to prepare III Armored Corps for the Warfighter exercise, an Army-led exercise series designed to evaluate corps- and division-level headquarters and their ability to conduct large-scale and joint operations.
“The Warfighter is the Army’s premier method of evaluating how essentially corps and divisions fight,” Moore said. “The Warfighters are designed to test staff to make sure that they’re able to deploy and face any sort of contingency operation when our nation calls upon them.”
III Armored Corps used this training to better train with allies by including them in the planning process and experimenting with emerging technologies; the corps is building its ability to adapt before being called upon to operate in a complex environment, ultimately strengthening its readiness.
“It’s been a great privilege and opportunity to train with III Armored Corps and prepare for the Warfighter, and then to also experiment with these new tools that are at our disposal,” Moore said.
title: III Armored Corps incorporates allies, AI into Warfighter planning

Forest Service, Natural Resources Conservation Service and State of Alabama renew commitment to shared stewardship of Alabama’s forests
The U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Forest Service and Natural Resources Conservation Service today, renewed their shared stewardship agreement with the State of Alabama, reinforcing a statewide partnership to improve forest health, reduce wildfire risk, support rural economies, and expand outdoor recreation access.
The renewed agreement builds on the original 2021 memorandum of understanding and leverages new federal authorities to accelerate forest management, habitat restoration, and recreation improvements across public and private lands.
“Over the past five years, our partnership with Alabama has delivered eleven timber sales, producing over 18,000 MBF and generating more than $1.5 million in stumpage. This agreement strengthens that shared commitment to the long-term health and resilience of Alabama’s forests through collaboration across six Wildlife Management Areas encompassing over 253,000 acres,” said Forest Service Chief Tom Schultz. “Through Good Neighbor Authority, we are expanding active forest management and advancing landscape‑scale restoration projects that will increase sustainable forest management and recreation opportunities ensuring that these lands continue to provide wood products, wildlife habitat, and expanded safe, accessible outdoor opportunities.”
“Alabama is blessed with an abundance of natural resources, and we have to do all we can to protect them,” said Alabama Governor Kay Ivey. “I am proud to continue this important partnership to effectively manage and support timber across our state.”
This renewed agreement reflects a shared commitment to protecting communities, conserving natural resources, supporting private landowners, and advancing America’s timber independence. Through joint planning, expanded authorities, and strong partnerships, the partners will accelerate restoration, strengthen forest resilience, and sustain the economic and ecological benefits of Alabama’s forests.
"Forestland covers nearly three-quarters of Alabama and is one of our state's most important natural resources. The Alabama Forestry Commission is charged with protecting those forests, helping landowners manage them responsibly, and educating Alabamians about their value,” said Rick Oates, state forester, Alabama Forestry Commission. “This agreement will help us accomplish much more as we continue to work together, building strong partnerships that benefit Alabama's forests and the people who depend on them."
“The shared stewardship agreement strengthens the partnership between USDA and Alabama and improves forests for timber, habitat and recreation across public and private lands,” said Colton L. Buckley, Chief of the Natural Resources Conservation Service. “NRCS is focused on putting farmers, ranchers, and forest landowners first. By working with our partners, we can offer conservation assistance to Alabama’s forest landowners that ensure the working forests of Alabama stay healthy and productive.”
“Shared stewardship provides a framework that strengthens our long-standing partnerships with the Alabama Forestry Commission, the Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, and other state, local, Tribal, and private-sector partners,” said Linwood Butler, forest supervisor for the National Forests in Alabama. “This agreement affirms our collective responsibility to promote resilient forests, reduce wildfire risk, enhance habitat for fish and wildlife, and support sustainable recreation and economic opportunities across the state.”
Specific goals of the agreement are to increase timber sustainability and support for forest product markets; expand prescribed fire and wildfire risk reduction projects; restore longleaf pine ecosystems; enhance trails, roads, boat ramps, and public recreation access; coordinate response to forest health threats; strengthen wildlife and aquatic habitat conservation; and achieve landscape‑scale restoration projects over the next five years.
Alabama is home to four national forests: Bankhead, Conecuh, Talladega and Tuskegee, spanning more than 673,000 acres across 17 counties.
title: Forest Service, Natural Resources Conservation Service and State of Alabama renew commitment to shared stewardship of Alabama’s forests

SEMBACH, Germany — The U.S. Army Medical Command recently established its first medical officer liaison position with the German military’s medical service in Bonn, Germany. Col. Kenneth Spicer, a U.S. Army Medical Service Corps officer, assumed the role in August 2025.
Spicer, a native of Mexico, New York, and a 1998 graduate of the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry previously commanded Public Health Command Europe and served as command inspector general for Regional Health Command Europe. He also served as chief of staff for the 68th Theater Medical Command before moving to Bonn.
A career Army Medical Service Corps and Public Health Officer, Spicer brings extensive experience in European theater health operations to the post.
"It was an honor to be selected for this newly created liaison position," Spicer said. "The Bundeswehr really welcomed me as one of its staff officers. I have been consistently impressed by the professionalism, competence, camaraderie, and esprit de corps of my Bundeswehr teammates. I am deeply grateful to my German teammates for the opportunity to serve alongside them and work toward a shared purpose: strengthening collective defense and helping protect the democratic values and freedoms our nations share."
While the Bundeswehr has maintained a military medical liaison with U.S. forces for more than a decade, the new post establishes reciprocal representation.
"In late 2024, amid heightened security concerns in Europe and the need to prepare for potential large-scale operations, senior military medical leaders decided to establish a reciprocal U.S. military medical liaison officer position with the Bundeswehr,” Spicer said.
Senior military medical officials note that Germany plays a central role in allied transit and medical logistics across the continent.
"As a major allied nation in central Europe, Germany is an important transportation and medical-support hub for the movement of forces from west to east and, if required, for the movement of casualties from east to west," Spicer said. "The liaison position provides a dedicated point of contact to build enduring partnerships, maintain professional connections, and better align U.S. and German medical capabilities for collective defense."
The liaison officer's primary objective is to enhance U.S.-German medical cooperation by boosting interoperability, joint readiness, and communication across both organizations.
"My role is to help connect leaders, planners, clinicians, and subject-matter experts across the U.S. military medical enterprise and the Bundeswehr," Spicer said. "The work includes supporting recurring bilateral working groups; identifying opportunities for professional exchange and joint training; improving coordination for patient movement, host-nation medical support, and contingency planning; and helping develop more enduring relationships between U.S. and German medical organizations."
Spicer noted that he also works to ensure senior leaders share a clear picture of mutual priorities and operational challenges.
Although German fluency is not mandatory for the position, it has proved advantageous. Spicer learned the language independently during his first assignment in Würzburg, Germany, in 1998.
"In order to learn German, I took classes in the evening after work," Spicer said. "Learning the language has opened doors throughout my career, strengthened professional relationships, and helped me better understand the people and culture of the country where I have spent 25 years serving in the military."
title: Army Medical Service Corps Officer Serves as Liaison to German Military Medical Forces

FORT LEE, Va. — Gold Star families shared stories and memories of their fallen loved ones during Fort Lee’s Gold Star Family / Survivor luncheon Oct. 3 at the U.S. Army Ordnance Training Support Facility here.
Laughter, tears and heartfelt conversations filled a conference room as Gold Star families gathered for Fort Lee’s Gold Star Family / Survivor luncheon, standing around tables to share stories and memories of their fallen loved ones while honoring their lives and legacies.
For these families, the gathering was more than an opportunity to remember. It was a chance to connect with others who understood their grief and to ensure the memories of their loved ones continued to live on.
Among those attending were Kendrick and Jihan Key, whose son, 1st Lt. Kendrick Key Jr., was killed May 2, 2026, during Exercise African Lion in Morocco while attempting to save a fellow Soldier.
For the Keys, the loss remains fresh, but participating in events honoring fallen service members has become an important part of their healing journey.
“We’re here, number one, to be with other families who have lost loved ones, and to just begin the healing process,” Kendrick Key Sr. said.
Since their son’s death, the family has participated in several remembrance events, including a butterfly release and the Run for the Fallen. Each gathering provides another opportunity to honor their son, whom they affectionately called Kenny, while connecting with others who have experienced similar losses.
“These events help to keep Kenny’s memory and the memory of all these fallen Soldiers, as well as their families, alive,” Key Sr. said. “It’s easy to forget that people are making real sacrifices.”
For Key Sr., remembering his son means more than reflecting on his military accomplishments. Although he proudly recalls Kenny’s college graduation, commissioning and service as an air defense artillery officer stationed in Ansbach, Germany, it is his son’s compassion and dedication to others that stand out most.
“The most important thing is the way Kenny cared for his Soldiers,” Key Sr. said. “He cared for them in every way — their personal lives, their professional lives, and their families.”
That commitment to others is a legacy the Keys hope to carry forward as they navigate their own grief and offer support to other surviving families.
The gathering also served as a reminder of the Army’s enduring commitment to those who have lost loved ones in military service.
Maj. Gen. Sean Davis, commanding general of the U.S. Army Combined Arms Support Command, emphasized the importance of maintaining meaningful relationships with Gold Star families and providing opportunities for remembrance, fellowship and continued support.
“Our responsibility is to provide them a safe place to celebrate the lives of their loved ones, but also seek camaraderie and fellowship,” Davis said.
Through Survivor Outreach Services, the Army provides long-term support and resources to surviving family members while helping them remain connected to the military community.
Davis also emphasized that Gold Star families play an important role in reminding today’s Soldiers and leaders of the sacrifices made by those who came before them.
The observance reflected a tradition dating back to World War I, when families displayed service flags bearing blue stars to represent loved ones serving in the military. When a service member died, the blue star was replaced with a gold star, symbolizing the family’s sacrifice.
Today, Gold Star families continue to carry that legacy, ensuring their loved ones are remembered not only for their service, but also for the lives they lived and the people they touched.
For families experiencing a recent loss, attending an event surrounded by others who share that experience can be difficult. However, the Keys hope their participation will encourage others to seek the comfort and understanding that comes from being part of the Gold Star community.
It is uncomfortable at first, but it’s also comforting to know that there are people here that understand and support, the Keys shared. “Hopefully, we can be that support and place of understanding for someone else.”
As the gathering continued, families exchanged stories, shared memories and found comfort in one another’s company.
For the Keys and the other Gold Star families in attendance, the day was not simply about remembering those who had died. It was about celebrating how they lived, honoring the sacrifices they made and ensuring their legacies continue through the people who loved them.
And for Kendrick and Jihan Key, it was another opportunity to make certain their son Kenny would never be forgotten.
title: Gold Star families gather to honor fallen loved ones

- For Immediate Release:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration yesterday approved the first generic of Climara Pro (estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system, 0.045 mg per day/0.015 mg), a transdermal hormone therapy patch for women with an intact uterus applied once a week. The approval aligns with FDA’s Public Health Pillar: Increasing Access to Affordable Medicines & Medical Products.
“Menopause is a universal experience for women, and it can greatly affect a person’s quality of life. This approval makes effective treatment more accessible,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “Approvals like this reflect FDA’s ongoing commitment to expanding American patient access to safe, affordable, high-quality medications.”
The generic estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system is therapeutically equivalent to Climara Pro, which is indicated for use in women with an intact uterus for:
- Treatment of moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms due to menopause
- Prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis
Climara Pro and the generic estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system contain both estrogen and progestogen in a single patch; this differs from estrogen-only patches commonly used in menopause treatment. Climara Pro and the generic estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system are specifically approved for women with an intact uterus, as the progestogen component is included to reduce the risk of endometrial hyperplasia that can occur with estrogen use alone.
“Once-weekly dosing can make a real difference in how patients manage their care,” said Michael Davis, M.D., Ph.D., Director of FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research. “A patch offers a convenient alternative to daily oral medications, which may help patients stay on track with their treatment.”
Climara Pro and the generic estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system are contraindicated in patients with undiagnosed abnormal genital bleeding; breast cancer or a history of breast cancer; estrogen-dependent neoplasia; active deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE) or a history of these conditions; active arterial thromboembolic disease or a history of these conditions; known anaphylactic reaction or angioedema or hypersensitivity to estradiol and levonorgestrel; hepatic impairment or disease; and protein C, protein S, or antithrombin deficiency, or other thrombophilic disorders.
The most common adverse reactions (greater than or equal to 5%) are: application site reaction, vaginal bleeding, breast pain, upper respiratory infection, back pain, depression, pain, headache and flu syndrome.
In the U.S., nine out of 10 prescriptions filled are for generic drugs. Increasing the availability of generic drugs helps to create competition in the marketplace, which then helps to make treatment more affordable and increases access to healthcare for more patients. Learn more about the FDA Drug Competition Action Plan.
Climara Pro is a registered trademark of Bayer. The FDA approved Zydus Pharmaceuticals (USA) Inc.’s Estradiol and Levonorgestrel Transdermal System. Please contact the manufacturer for information about the medicine’s availability.
Related Information
- Generic Drugs
- Approved Drug Products with Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations (commonly known as the “Orange Book”)
The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation’s food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, radiation-emitting electronic products, and for regulating tobacco products.

title: October 20, 2026 - FDA Approves Once-Weekly Generic Hormone Therapy Patch for Women

SEC, FSA Hold Autumn Financial Regulatory Dialogue
Washington D.C., Oct. 20, 2026 —
The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Financial Services Agency of Japan (FSA) convened the Autumn SEC-FSA Financial Regulatory Dialogue in Tokyo on Oct. 19, 2026.
The SEC–FSA Dialogue builds upon longstanding efforts between the two authorities to increase cooperation and strengthen collaboration on key cross-border issues and developments.
SEC Commissioner Mark T. Uyeda led the Dialogue for the SEC and Mr. MIYOSHI Toshiyuki, Vice Minister for International Affairs at the FSA, led the Dialogue for the FSA.
"The relationship between our agencies is one of the SEC’s most successful and longstanding relationships,” said SEC Commissioner Mark T. Uyeda. “This Dialogue continues to build on that relationship and helps advance coordination and cooperation on shared financial sector priorities to protecting investors."
“This dialogue provided a valuable opportunity to deepen mutual understanding between two authorities at a time when the environment surrounding capital markets is undergoing significant change.” said Mr. MIYOSHI Toshiyuki, Vice Minister for International Affairs, FSA. “The FSA will continue to promote close cooperation with the SEC toward the development of sound and trusted capital markets and the protection of investors."
At the Autumn Dialogue, participants discussed recent market developments, as well as the strategic priorities of both authorities. They also exchanged views on various regulatory and supervisory matters, including developments in private and public markets, asset management, and innovation priorities.
The next SEC-FSA Dialogue is scheduled to be convened in Washington, D.C., in the spring of 2027.
###

title: SEC, FSA Hold Autumn Financial Regulatory Dialogue

Queda menos de una semana para solicitar asistencia a FEMA
INDIANAPOLIS – Los residentes en los condados Carroll, Cass, Dearborn, Decatur, Delaware, Fayette, Franklin, Hamilton, Hancock, Henry, Lake, LaPorte, Madison, Marion, Morgan, Pike, Porter, Pulaski, Putnam, Randolph, Rush, Tipton, Union y Wayne que fueron afectados por las tormentas, tornados e inundaciones que ocurrieron del 11 al 24 de agosto tienen menos de una semana para solicitar asistencia a la Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias (FEMA, por sus siglas en inglés). La fecha límite para solicitar es el domingo 25 de octubre de 2026.
La asistencia financiera está disponible para sobrevivientes elegibles que necesiten ayuda para cubrir los gastos no asegurados como reparaciones a la vivienda, pérdida de propiedad personal, daños a un vehículo y gastos médicos incluso artículos de accesibilidad, mudanza y almacenamiento y rembolsos por alojamiento provisional.
Cómo solicitar asistencia a FEMA:
Solicite en línea en DisasterAssistance.gov/es o llame a la línea de ayuda de FEMA al 800-621-3362. Si usa un servicio de retransmisión por video, proporcione a FEMA su número para ese servicio.
A continuación, algunos videos sobre la asistencia:
Lo que puede esperar antes de solicitar asistencia de FEMA | Lenguaje de Señas Americano (ASL, por sus siglas en inglés)
¿Qué ocurre después de solicitar asistencia de FEMA? | ASL
Para solicitar un préstamo por desastre a bajo interés de la Oficina de Recuperación por Desastre de la Agencia Federal de Pequeños Negocios (SBA, por sus siglas en inglés), visite el Portal de préstamos MySBA o sba.gov/disaster (enlaces en inglés) o llame al Centro de servicio al cliente al 800-659-2955. Las personas sordas, con dificultades auditivas o que tengan una discapacidad del habla pueden marcar el 711 para obtener acceso a los servicios de retransmisión de comunicaciones. Para más información o para recibir asistencia en persona, visite Appointment.sba.gov (enlace en inglés) para encontrar la ubicación más cercana a usted. La fecha límite para solicitar un préstamo por daños físicos por desastre también es el domingo 25 de octubre de 2026 y la fecha límite para solicitar un préstamo por pérdida económica por desastre es el 25 de mayo de 2027.
Después que usted solicite, la ayuda de FEMA sigue disponible
Manténgase en contacto. Informe a FEMA sobre cualquier cambio en sus circunstancias o información de contacto, incluso el estado de su reclamo al seguro. Comuníquele a FEMA cualquier duda que tenga sobre su recuperación incluso cualquier necesidad no cubierta por el seguro.
Usted puede crear una cuenta en DisasterAssistance.gov/es donde puede presentar su documentación y verificar las actualizaciones de la herramienta de seguimiento. Para recibir asistencia en persona, visite un centro de asistencia. Para encontrar el centro más cerca de usted, visite on.in.gov/August2026Disaster.
Para más información sobre la operación de recuperación tras el desastre en Indiana, visite www.fema.gov/es/disaster/4933.
Los sobrevivientes de desastres que creen que han sido discriminados por motivo de raza, color, nacionalidad, sexo, religión, edad, discapacidad, dominio del inglés o estado económico tienen derecho a presentar una queja contactando a FEMA en FEMA-CR-Intake@fema.dhs.gov o llamando al 1-800-621-3362.
###
La misión de FEMA es ayudar a las personas antes, durante y después de los desastres.
El inglés es el idioma oficial de los Estados Unidos de América. La versión original en inglés de este documento es la fuente oficial para esta información
title: Queda menos de una semana para solicitar asistencia a FEMA

FORT EUSTIS, VA — U.S. Army Mission and Installation Contracting Command Fort Eustis recently executed a task order supporting the installation of an interim BeaverFit fitness facility at Tinker Air Force Base, Oklahoma, demonstrating how responsive interservice collaboration can deliver timely quality-of-life improvements for service members.
The effort supported an urgent Navy requirement to improve conditions, morale, and access to physical fitness resources for sailors assigned to Tinker AFB. Navy leaders identified the BeaverFit gym as an immediate, tangible measure to support Sailor wellbeing at the installation.
Army, Navy, and Air Force leaders coordinated to define the requirement, align acquisition actions, and move the effort from an identified need to contract award. MICC-Fort Eustis contracting personnel Contracting Officer Kiana Hamilton, Contract Specialist, Reese Wolf, Division Chief David Clark, and Director Lindsey Nicolai executed the award in partnership with Navy stakeholders and Air Force installation representatives, with the support of the Holistic Health and Fitness (H2F) Directorate within Transformation and Training Command (T2COM) Maneuver Center of Excellence.
The action was enabled through the Tactical Readiness Infrastructure Systems and Support Small Business Innovation Research Phase III Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity contract vehicle. MICC-Fort Eustis awarded the TRISS IDIQ contract to BeaverFit North America LLC on August 4, 2026. The seven-year IDIQ vehicle has a contract ceiling of $350 million.
FDO Eustis Director Dr. Latosha McCoy summarized the contract vehicle by stating, “The TRISS vehicle demonstrates how innovative acquisition strategies can rapidly bridge the gap between emerging capability and operational need. By leveraging proven SBIR Phase III authorities and strong partnerships across the Department of Defense, we are reducing procurement lead times, increasing access to mission-enhancing solutions, and delivering greater value to the warfighter and taxpayer alike.”
The contract strategy was validated and championed by MICC Commanding General Brig. Gen. Freddy L. Adams, MICC Deputy to the Commanding General Clay Cole, as well as Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Army for Procurement Kim Buehler. H2F leaders, including Engineer and SBIR Phase III Technical Point of Contact Francesca Singhas, presented the strategy before the Vice Chief of Staff of the Army (VCSA)/Acting Chief of Staff of the Army Gen. Christopher LaNeve and senior leaders from the Office of the Director of the Army Staff, underscoring the importance of establishing a responsive enterprise solution for readiness and quality-of-life infrastructure requirements.
According to Army H2F Proponent this innovative acquisition avenue supports not only the Army's Holistic Health and Fitness System but also our sister services and the DoW's Warfighter Performance Optimization framework.
Designed for broad Department of War use, the contract vehicle will support requirements from any military service, subject to applicable acquisition, funding and approval requirements. Its flexible structure enables organizations to address tactical readiness, fitness and human-performance infrastructure needs using appropriate available funding. Currently this vehicle has supported task orders enabling mission execution for Army, Air Force, Navy, Space Force, and Coast Guard (Department of Homeland Security).
The Tinker AFB requirement also demonstrates the intent of Adams’ 2026–2027 MICC Campaign Plan. By pairing an innovative enterprise contract strategy with disciplined execution at the contracting center level, the joint team translated an urgent service-member quality-of-life need into a practical solution. The effort reflects MICC’s focus on agile, trusted acquisition outcomes and anticipating customer requirements across the joint force.
This successful joint team achievement highlights what can be accomplished with the combined efforts of an Army contracting team, Navy stakeholders, and Air Force partners working with urgency and focus to deliver a practical solution for Sailors at Tinker.
Senior Navy leadership commended cross-service collaboration as a critical mission enabler, proving essential to the operation's success. In communications following the award, Navy officials credited the responsiveness of Army contracting personnel and the support of Air Force partners to help deliver the requirement on a compressed timeline.
“The success of this effort comes down to partnership, trust, and a shared commitment to our service members. This team demonstrated exactly what can be accomplished when we work together across the joint force,” said McCoy in response to the shared success in support of the Warfighter.
The Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao expressed appreciation for the joint team and emphasized that the collaboration demonstrated the power of coordinated action across military departments. Navy leaders noted that the effort supported improved conditions and morale for sailors stationed at Tinker AFB while providing a model for future interservice initiatives. In response to Cao’s praise for the Army contracting team’s efforts, Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle indicated his desire to engage in more joint efforts in the future while indicating a personal desire to thank the Army contracting team separately.
The TRISS vehicle is also positioned to support additional pending requirements, including Human Performance Academy and readiness equipment, Soldier Physical Readiness Center design and equipment, facility conversions and covered training-zone construction at Army installations in the US and overseas.
Army and Navy senior leaders have requested the names of the contracting officer and contract specialist for formal recognition, highlighting the importance of the team’s work in enabling this interservice outcome.
The MICC-Fort Eustis office primarily supports T2COM, FASCOM, CAC (primarily AVCOE, FCOE, MCOE, and CPE ST3), and MEDCOE.In FY 26, MICC-Fort Eustis executed contracts with potential ceiling value of almost $3.1B including 6 significant Phase III SBIR IDIQs covering a broad range of labor categories and services/supply provision opportunities.
About the MICC
Headquartered at Joint Base San Antonio-Fort Sam Houston, Texas, the Mission and Installation Contracting Command consists of about 1,500 military and civilian members who are responsible for contracting goods and services in support of Soldiers as well as readying trained contracting units for the operating force and contingency environment when called upon. A subordinate command of the Army Contracting Command and the Army Materiel Command, MICC contracts are vital in feeding more than 200,000 Soldiers every day, providing many daily base operations support services at installations, facilitate training in the preparation of more than 100,000 conventional force members annually, training more than 500,000 students each year, and maintaining more than 14.4 million acres of land and 170,000 structures. See also the fiscal year 2027 MICC Fact Sheet.
title: MICC - Fort Eustis delivers joint quality-of-life solution, advances 2026–2027 campaign plan

Krishnamoorthi Leads 105 Lawmakers Urging FBI Hate Crime Probe After Attempted Mass Shooting at His Family’s Hindu Temple in Aurora
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) today led 105 members of Congress, including the entire Illinois House Democratic delegation, every Indian American member of Congress, and Senators Dick Durbin, Tammy Duckworth, Andy Kim, and Chris Van Hollen, in urging FBI Director Kash Patel to investigate the attempted mass shooting at the Sri Venkateswara Swami (Balaji) Hindu temple in Aurora, Illinois, as a potential federal hate crime. Krishnamoorthi and his family were worshipping at the temple when the attempted attack occurred on October 11. The lawmakers also demanded answers about the FBI’s efforts to identify and address credible online threats targeting Indian Americans, Hindu Americans, and other South Asian communities.
According to prosecutors, 19-year-old Alexandros Paporakis, a self-identified neo-Nazi, tried to shoot a man outside the temple, but his rifle jammed. He fled and later communicated plans to return before a coworker alerted police, who arrested him that day. Prosecutors allege that he authored an eight-page white supremacist manifesto describing violence against people of Indian descent at a Hindu house of worship. Investigators recovered a rifle, hundreds of rounds of ammunition, body armor, and white supremacist imagery.
In the letter, the lawmakers write:
“The alleged combination of targeted racial hatred, a religious setting, and preparations for mass violence demands a comprehensive federal response. We appreciate the FBI’s reported assistance to local investigators and urge the Bureau to ensure that potential hate-crime violations receive explicit attention.”
The letter comes amid a surge in online hostility toward South Asians. A September 2026 report identified more than 542,000 anti-South Asian hateful posts on X between January 2025 and June 2026, with the monthly volume rising approximately 240 percent from January 2024 to June 2026. A Carnegie Endowment survey also found that 48 percent of Indian American respondents encountered racist posts targeting their community very or somewhat often since the start of 2025, while one in four reported being called a slur.
The lawmakers also criticize Trump Administration messaging that they warn risks legitimizing racial and religious stereotypes. They cite a Department of Homeland Security post depicting a Sikh man with the message, “Get off our roads, you don’t know how to drive Mr. Singh,” and a Department of Education post declaring “Make College Football Great Again” after a Texas Republican complained about South Asians attending a University of Texas football game.
The lawmakers continue:
“We believe such messaging risks lending governmental legitimacy to racial and religious stereotyping. Federal agencies should make clear that debates over immigration or public safety never justify collective suspicion of Indian, Sikh, Hindu, or other South Asian communities.”
The lawmakers are seeking information on whether the FBI is examining potential racial, ethnic, and religious bias in the Aurora case, whether online platforms or other individuals facilitated the alleged plot, and what steps the Bureau is taking to protect houses of worship and address credible threats without infringing on First Amendment protections.
The lawmakers requested a written response to the following questions, to the extent consistent with an ongoing investigation, by October 29, 2026:
- Is the FBI investigating the alleged Aurora-area plot as a potential federal hate crime? If so, is that investigation examining both racial or ethnic bias and religious bias, and is the Bureau coordinating with the Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division and the appropriate U.S. Attorney’s Office?
- Are investigators examining whether the defendant used online platforms to communicate threats, select potential targets, obtain assistance, or coordinate with others? Are they assessing whether any individuals encouraged or materially assisted the alleged plot?
- What steps is the FBI taking, consistent with the First Amendment and applicable investigative authorities, to identify and assess credible online threats targeting Indian Americans, Hindu Americans, Sikhs, and other South Asian communities? How does the Bureau distinguish protected expression, including offensive speech, from threats and conduct warranting investigation?
- What mechanisms exist for sharing actionable threat information with state and local law enforcement and potentially targeted houses of worship? What outreach and protective resources are being offered to affected communities following this alleged plot?
- Does the FBI have adequate personnel, language expertise, and analytical capacity to assess threats involving anti-Indian, anti-Hindu, and broader anti-South Asian bias? What additional resources, if any, does the Bureau believe it needs?
The lawmakers conclude:
“No one should fear being targeted because of their ancestry, appearance, or faith, and no congregation should have to wonder whether gathering for worship will make its members targets of mass violence. We urge the FBI to investigate the evidence fully, pursue all applicable offenses, and provide affected communities with a clear account of the steps being taken to protect them.”

Walkinshaw Moves to Block Trump-Putin Diesel Deal That Would Bankroll Russia’s War
Walkinshaw joins bipartisan legislation to deny Putin energy revenue and support Ukraine
  
  
    
      Washington, D.C. ,
      October 20, 2026
    
    
    
    
  
  
  
  
  
  
    
      WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11), a member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform Subcommittee on Military and Foreign Affairs, announced he is cosponsoring the Prohibit Corrupt Russia Oil Deals Act, bipartisan legislation introduced by Congressman Gregory W. Meeks (NY-05), Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, to block President Trump’s deal to purchase and import Russian diesel.
“Americans struggling with rising costs should not be asked to bankroll Vladimir Putin’s war machine,” said Congressman Walkinshaw. “Putin is a war criminal who has devastated Ukrainian families and sent Russians to die in his war of aggression. Ukraine is a trusted partner of the United States, and its people deserve our support. Trump’s Russian diesel deal rewards Putin for prolonging this war. I’m joining this bipartisan legislation to block that deal, deny Putin revenue to fund his attacks, and help Ukraine secure a just and lasting peace.”
The legislation would:
    - Prohibit the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation from investing in Russian energy.
- Revoke Treasury Department licenses allowing the Russian energy transactions targeted by the bill and prohibit future licenses.
- Require the Trump administration to impose sanctions on Russian energy.
A copy of the Prohibit Corrupt Russia Oil Deals Act is available here.

MONROE – On October 9, 2026, United States Chief District Judge Terry A. Doughty sentenced Johnny Bradshaw, 34, of Bastrop, to 144 months in federal prison for Conspiracy to Possess a Controlled Substance with Intent to Distribute, followed by five years of supervised release. He previously pled guilty to the charge on June 22, 2026.

The same day, Judge Doughty sentenced Travis Peterson , 36, of Garland, Texas, to 57 months in federal prison for Conspiracy to Possess a Controlled Substance with Intent to Distribute, followed by five years of supervised release. He previously pled guilty to the charge on June 23, 2026.

BRADSHAW According to court records, between May and July 2025, Bradshaw worked with co-conspirators in a methamphetamine distribution network operating in and around Bastrop. Investigators intercepted communications in which Bradshaw and a co-conspirator discussed multiple drug transactions, including a large shipment being transported from Texas. Surveillance showed Bradshaw arriving at a local residence after which he and a co-conspirator discussed money owed for the shipment. On July 22, 2025, investigators conducted a controlled purchase of approximately 110 grams of methamphetamine from Bradshaw, after which he was arrested.

PETERSON According to court records, Peterson served as a primary transporter for the Texas-based source supplying methamphetamine to the distribution network. Investigators intercepted calls in which Peterson coordinated shipments with co-conspirators, including a July 2025 delivery during which he arrived at a residence carrying luggage believed to contain narcotics. In late August and early September 2025, Peterson arranged the transport of approximately 28 kilograms of methamphetamine. A second shipment followed in October, when Peterson provided another load of methamphetamine from his Texas residence. During a subsequent traffic stop involving his co-conspirators transporting that same shipment, investigators seized approximately 23 kilograms of methamphetamine concealed in an orange suitcase.

U.S. Attorney Zachary A. Keller for the Western District of Louisiana made the announcement.

These cases were investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Louisiana State Police, and Morehouse Parish Sheriff’s Office. They were prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney J. Aaron Crawford with assistance from Legal Assistant Amanda Morgan.

You may find a copy of this press release (and any updates) on the website of the United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Louisiana at www.justice.gov/usao-wdla.
