Justice Department Announces Results from Operation Not Forgotten 2026
The Department of Justice and FBI announced today results of the personnel surge in support of Operation Not Forgotten 2026, which focuses on unresolved cases in Indian country with a priority on cases involving violence against women and children, including those who are missing or murdered.
In its fourth year, Operation Not Forgotten surged personnel and investigative resources across the country from April 1 through September 30, resulting in 118 arrests, 41 individuals charged federally, 25 child victims identified or located, and 72 weapons recovered. FBI agents conducted 990 interviews and 232 search operations. Arrests increased by 123% and subjects charged by 52% over 2025.
“The Department of Justice will always work to deliver justice for the victims of violent crime in Indian country,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “Thanks to the hard work of the FBI, our U.S. Attorneys, and other federal and tribal partners, Operation Not Forgotten and Operation Steadfast Promise are helping make communities safer and providing comfort for victims and families.”
“This year’s Operation Not Forgotten continued this FBI’s largest commitment to Indian Country in the history of the Bureau,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “The results were outstanding – from April 1 through September 30, this FBI worked more than 500 cases, a 59% increase from last year’s operation; 118 arrests, a 123% increase; and 41 subjects charged federally, a 52% increase. This is in addition to 25 child victims identified or located and 72 weapons recovered. These involved life-saving operations, with cases including child sexual abuse, physical assault and abuse, domestic violence, CSAM cases, and more.
“Operation Not Forgotten sends a loud and clear message that our long-forgotten partners in Indian Country are forgotten no more,” said Director Patel. “When I assumed the position of FBI Director a year and a half ago, this FBI promised we would be there for our tribal partners. We have and will continue to be – through our 400 agents dedicated to Indian country, 30 Safe Trails Task Forces, and increased awareness with our Voices Not Forgotten program, where the FBI quadrupled the rewards to at least $25,000 for information associated with homicides, kidnappings and missing persons in Indian country. Thank you to our federal, state, and local partners who continue to work with us to ensure these unsolved crimes and cases receive the surge in resources they deserve.”
“Operation Not Forgotten demonstrates the Trump Administration’s commitment to protecting tribal communities, strengthening public safety, and ensuring that victims and their families have access to justice,” said Billy Kirkland, Assistant Secretary for Indian Affairs, U.S. Department of the Interior. “Through close collaboration across the federal government and in partnership with tribal, state, and local law enforcement, we are bringing additional resources and investigative support to Indian Country to address violent crime, advance unresolved cases, and help families find answers. The Department of the Interior, through the Bureau of Indian Affairs, remains committed to working alongside our partners to deliver meaningful results and build safer communities for generations to come."
Examples of cases charged during this period include:
In the District of Wyoming, the surge resulted in the federal indictment of 18 individuals for an array of violent crimes, and child abuse offenses on the Wind River Indian Reservation, including U.S. v. Jose Benito Ocon: This prosecution arises from an August 2025 incident near Riverton, where the defendant allegedly executed a male passenger with a gunshot to the head inside a moving vehicle before turning the firearm on two female witnesses. Leveraging the surge’s enhanced investigative assets, a grand jury returned an indictment charging the defendant with five felony counts, including first-degree murder, discharging a firearm during a crime of violence, and two distinct counts of assault with a dangerous weapon. He faces a mandatory sentence of life imprisonment if convicted. In U.S. v. Darlynn Sheree Seminole, federal prosecutors filed charges following a June 2026 domestic violence intervention by the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) Wind River Police Department, involving allegations of severe physical trauma inflicted on a 10-year-old.
In the District of Nevada, in July a federal grand jury returned a superseding indictment charging Delshay Astor with the alleged murder of Anna Scott, a member of the Pyramid Lake Paiute Tribe, on the Reno-Sparks Indian Colony in February 2022, and also charged Joel Christy for assisting Astor to avoid apprehension.
In the District of Minnesota, Operation Not Forgotten has resulted in four cases charged during the surge period with violent and sexual offenses in Indian Country, including sexual abuse of minors, domestic assault causing substantial bodily injury, assault by strangulation, and assault with intent to commit kidnapping. One recent case includes U.S. v. Courtney John Barrett Sr. indicted on September 22, 2026, on two counts of sexual abuse of a minor.
In the District of Montana, Michael Plentybuffalo was charged in the death of Shann Nomee, who went missing during an extreme cold snap in January 2024 and whose frozen body was found in a field north of Lodge Grass, Montana after a community led search and a tip to the Bureau of Indian Affairs that pointed to Plentybuffalo. His case is pending trial.
Also in Montana, Lance Crookedarm was charged with the May 2026 violent assault and non-fatal strangulation of a female victim.
In the District of Arizona, at least four cases were charged including two violent assaults, an arson, and the aggravated sexual abuse of a minor under 12, all of which occurred on the Navajo Nation, as well as an additional assault that was committed on the Fort Apache Indian Reservation.
FBI’s Operation Steadfast Promise
Operation Steadfast Promise, first announced in 2026, is a continuing comprehensive surge of resources to address a wide range of violent criminal threats impacting Indian country. Operation Steadfast Promise builds on the successes of Operation Not Forgotten with the addition of multiple new initiatives to improve public safety in Tribal communities. The FBI, in coordination with U.S. Attorneys’ Offices, the Bureau of Indian Affairs Missing and Murdered Unit, Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and Tribal and other federal law enforcement partners, is working across multiple territories to bring investigative aid to cases and resolution for victims and their families. Since Operation Steadfast Promise began in April, the FBI opened over 1,200 new investigations in Indian country, obtained criminal charges on 678 subjects, made over 700 arrests, recovered 2,260 weapons, and made 140 drug seizures.
This year, Operation Not Forgotten continued to address the over 4,000 open investigations in Indian country including death investigations, child abuse cases, domestic violence, and adult sexual abuse investigations, underscoring the persistent and urgent need for sustained resource investment in these communities.
During Operation Not Forgotten, the FBI surged personnel, including investigative, intelligence, and other support personnel, on rotating temporary duty assignments across Indian country in twelve FBI field offices, in Albuquerque, Billings, Detroit, Denver, Jackson, Las Vegas, Minneapolis, Oklahoma City, Omaha, Portland, Phoenix and Salt Lake City. Working in close coordination with Tribal law enforcement agencies, the BIA Missing and Murdered Unit, and U.S. Attorneys' Offices, together law enforcement worked to advance open investigations and pursue accountability for victims and their families.
Additionally, the FBI has brought focus to a new FBI’s Voices Not Forgotten webpage that includes a searchable and interactive map that brings attention to FBI investigations in Indian country where the FBI, in coordination with state, local and Tribal law enforcement are seeking the public’s assistance. In August 2026, the FBI announced the establishment of a new protocol which created a minimum reward of up to $25,000 for all publicly advertised cases involving homicides, kidnappings and missing persons in Indian country where the FBI has assumed jurisdiction.
The FBI remains committed to standing alongside Tribal communities, federal partners, and local law enforcement to address the violent crime threats that continue to impact Indian country. To learn more, visit www.fbi.gov/investigate/violent-crime/indian-country-crime.
The FBI encourages anyone with information related to unresolved violent crimes in Indian country to contact their local FBI field office or submit a tip at www.tips.fbi.gov.
title: Justice Department Announces Results from Operation Not Forgotten 2026

Social Security Administration Takes Initial Action Following Pressure from Horsford and Cortez Masto, Fails to Provide Feasible Solution for Foster Care Youth
NORTH LAS VEGAS – Following a joint letter from Congressman Steven Horsford (NV-04) and Senator Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), the Social Security Administration (SSA) took initial steps to address a backlog of Social Security number applications for children in Clark County’s foster care system. The agency has processed 19 applications since the lawmakers reached out, leaving nearly 1,300 foster youth still waiting for the documents they need to access critical services.
SSA has proposed accepting records printed from Nevada’s statewide vaccination system, provided each record is accompanied by an individual certification letter from the Nevada Department of Human Services (DHS). However, Nevada DHS lacks the staffing capacity to produce a separate letter for every child, creating another administrative barrier.
“While I’m glad SSA heard our concerns and took action, I’m focused on a permanent solution that will provide these young people with the federal services they are entitled to,” said Rep. Horsford. “Nearly 1,300 children in Clark County’s foster care system are still waiting for the documents they need to access healthcare, secure employment, and move forward with their lives. These children should not be caught in bureaucratic red tape, and I will continue holding SSA accountable until every pending application is processed.”
“While some progress has been made in beginning to process Social Security number applications, Nevada’s foster youth are relying on the Social Security Administration to find a meaningful, long-term solution to this issue. We will continue to push the Administration to work with Clark County to support foster children across the Valley,” said Senator Cortez Masto.
“Following the leadership of Senator Cortez Masto and Congressman Horsford on this important issue, the County has met with representatives from the Social Security Administration and a solution was proposed through a grant exemption that would require the State of Nevada to write individual certification letters for each child,” said Kevin Schiller, Clark County Manager. “Unfortunately, while well-intentioned, this is not a workable solution, and these barriers continue to impact the quality of life of the vulnerable children we serve. The County sincerely hopes that an effective solution can be reached quickly.”
In December 2025, SSA notified CCFS that Social Security number applications for children in foster care must include records physically certified by the custodian of record. However, Clark County has operated under an electronic records system for civil and family cases since 2010. This documentation discrepancy has prevented children in foster care from obtaining Social Security cards, creating barriers to Medicaid and CHIP enrollment, family reunification, permanent placements, driver’s licenses, and employment opportunities.
In their joint letter, Rep. Horsford and Sen. Cortez Masto called on SSA to immediately process all pending applications, resolve the documentation discrepancy with CCFS by the end of 2026, provide a written response within 10 business days, and deliver regular updates on the backlog.
To date, the parties have not agreed on a workable solution. The lawmakers have noted administrative barriers at SSA and will continue working to establish a permanent solution that ensures no child in Clark County’s foster care system is denied access to essential services because of outdated documentation requirements.
Read the full October 6 letter HERE. The original press release can be found HERE.
title: Social Security Administration Takes Initial Action Following Pressure from Horsford and Cortez Masto, Fails to Provide Feasible Solution for Foster Care Youth

Kristen Tapscott, ground and aviation management and program analyst at the Security Assistance Command, was chosen as the command’s Employee of the Quarter for the third quarter of fiscal year 2026.
Tapscott plans, directs, implements, and manages a program valued at $18.9 billion, which supports the Office of the Program Manager-Saudi Arabian National Guard, a subcommand of USASAC.
“Her duties include thorough case financial and trust fund analysis in support of Saudi Ministry of National Guard accrual accounting efforts, as directed by Saudi Ministry of Finance,” Paviola Duri, director of the OPM-SANG Huntsville Field Office, said.
As a foreign military sales case and trust fund analyst she plays an integral role in researching and reconciling Saudi Ministry of National Guard deposits, finances, billing, invoices and disbursements. Her efforts have been essential for MNG to meet accrual accounting reporting as directed by Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Finance. Her efforts “further solidifying our partner’s trust through fully transparent and detailed FMS program and case financial discussions and reporting,” Duri said.
Tapscott led the efforts in analyzing all MNG FMS cases ensuring that total program authority did not exceed Royal Decrees’ thresholds. Her work helped MNG find and repurpose over $887 million in unutilized case authority.
“Kristen has a strong desire to see our FMS program succeed and the Ministry of the National Guard succeed, evident by her tireless overtime work with the Ministry … answering questions on personnel, program budgeting, and future requirements,” Tiwana Coutee, another OPM-SANG program analyst at USASAC, said.
She has taken on some of the most complicated tasks in support of MNG’s unique and overwhelming financial reporting. “She continuously designs new and clear methods and processes to capture, display and disseminate information not only to her teammates but also during the internal financial reviews MNG has requested to be held annually,” Duri said.
Tapscott is a team player always going above and beyond to assist the team and her leadership even when outside of her core duties and responsibilities. Coutee said, “She provides mentorship in requirements development, case management, and budgeting to incoming military and civilian personnel on the program to ensure their success.”
Tapscott knows and understands the demands of the position and organization and has stepped up to the challenge during times when resources have been low. Due to vacancies, in 2025 she took on responsibilities across multiple positions. She successfully led the financial reporting team as requested by Saudi Arabia and continued to manage five FMS cases valued at a total of $2.3 billion.
“What I’ve always admired most about Kristen is her collaborative spirit,” Samuel Feleke, deputy chief of OPM-SANG’s land power division, said. “She doesn’t just focus on her own tasks; she actively lifts up those around her, serves as an incredible mentor, and brings an energy that makes the entire workplace better.”
title: Security Assistance Command honors program analyst

The Coast Guard awarded $300M in infrastructure contracts at Naval Station Newport and Naval Air Station Pensacola
WASHINGTON – The U.S. Coast Guard announced Oct. 20 two contracts working with the U.S. Navy totaling more than $300 million towards infrastructure improvements supporting major cutter operations.
The Navy awarded the first contract, totaling $271 million, Sept. 22 to Skanska USA Civil Northeast Inc. of Waltham, Massachusetts, for new major cutter homeport facilities at Naval Station Newport in Newport, Rhode Island, and awarded the second contract, totaling $31.5 million, Sept. 28 to Orion Government Services LLC of Houston, Texas, for hurricane damage repairs for the Coast Guard major cutter piers at Naval Air Station Pensacola in Pensacola, Florida.
Both contracts used Coast Guard funding that leverages the Navy’s site expertise and existing design contracts to lower project cost as well as technical and schedule risk.
The Naval Station Newport contract is funded by fiscal year 2022 major acquisitions infrastructure funding and the historic investment in the Coast Guard through the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Of the nearly $25 billion provided through this act – the largest capital investment in Coast Guard history – the Service has been delivering on that investment by ordering approximately $20 billion in assets, capabilities, and infrastructure to date.
“These investments will provide vital infrastructure to support the modernizing Coast Guard fleet,” said Admiral Kevin Lunday, Commandant of the Coast Guard. “These major investments in shore infrastructure for our cutters will ensure the Coast Guard’s ability to secure America’s borders and maritime approaches far at sea.”
The Newport project includes a new pier to provide berthing for four major Coast Guard cutters, a new bulkhead, stormwater management modifications and full utility installations. This collaboration with the Navy advances critical Coast Guard missions, providing access to strategic operating areas in the Western Hemisphere and the Arctic.
The work in Pensacola, funded by the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, provides for repairs to Wharf Bravo, including structural and utility improvements to the north berth, and underwater structural repairs for both the north and south berths.
For media inquiries, contact mediarelations@uscg.mil.
###
About the U.S. Coast Guard
With more than 95,000 miles of shoreline, 25,000 miles of navigable rivers and 4.5 million square miles of U.S. exclusive economic zone, the U.S. Coast Guard defends the Nation, protects the marine transportation system, regulates and safeguards ports and waterways, leads the Nation in maritime drug interdiction and secures the maritime border. As a member of the joint force, a law enforcement organization, a regulatory agency and a member of the U.S. intelligence community, the Coast Guard employs a unique mix of authorities to ensure the safety and integrity of the maritime domain to protect the economic and national security of the nation. More than 76,000 members of the Coast Guard operate a multi-mission, interoperable fleet of more than 220 cutters, 185 fixed and rotary-wing aircraft, 1,300 boats and its own dedicated cyber command to protect critical maritime infrastructure.
More information about the U.S. Coast Guard can be found at www.uscg.mil Follow @USCG on X and Instagram, like us on Facebook, subscribe on YouTube and follow LinkedIn—connect with us.
Make a difference on land, at sea or in the air with the Coast Guard. Visit GoCoastGuard.com to find out how to be part of our team.

Fort Myers, Florida – Frederick Taylor (38, North Fort Myers) has been sentenced by U.S. District Judge Kyle Dudek to 27 years in federal prison for distributing methamphetamine. Taylor pleaded guilty on March 9, 2026. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement.

According to court documents and evidence presented at his sentencing hearing, Taylor was a drug dealer in the Palmona Park neighborhood of North Fort Myers. He used a network of lower-level dealers and residences to distribute controlled substances, including methamphetamine. On multiple occasions, Taylor took an order from a confidential informant, then directed one of his subordinate dealers to fulfill the transaction, ultimately selling nearly a pound of methamphetamine. The execution of a search warrant revealed that Taylor had multiple firearms and approximately $12,000 in cash in his residence.

This case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation. It was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Benjamin S. Winter.
title: North Fort Myers Drug Dealer Sentenced to 27 Years in Federal Prison

PICATINNY ARSENAL, N.J. - One of the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) Armaments Center’s proudest accomplishments stood front and center before the warfighter in July, as Soldiers attending Project Convergence-Capstone 6 (PC-C6) tested out the Picatinny Common Lethality Integration Kit (CLIK).
Picatinny CLIK is Armaments Center’s design standard that enables plug-and-play integration of modular lethal payloads on unmanned systems (UxS), including small drones. Developed to reduce the complexity of integrating lethal payloads with unmanned platforms, Picatinny CLIK establishes a unified architecture for attachment, power, communication and safety-critical commands. By standardizing physical and electronic interface requirements across platforms and payloads, the system enables Soldiers to move, mix, and match different lethal payloads across multiple drones.
The PC‑C6 is the Army’s premier large‑scale experimentation event, bringing together the Army, joint forces, and international partners to integrate Soldiers, emerging technologies, and advanced equipment in fast‑paced, contested environments. Picatinny CLIK directly supports the Department of War’s goals of rapid adaptation and drone dominance, and Armaments Center is working hand in hand with industry partners to adopt the interface. Several industry partners received the chance to interface with Picatinny CLIK during its demonstration at Fort Irwin near Barstow, Calif.
Members of the 4th Infantry Division received a hands-on demonstration with several components, such as the Munition Air-dropped Lethality Enhancement Tool (MALET) clip-on conversion tool, the AUDIBLE Weapon Release System and the Gunslinger fire control software. Armaments Center technology integrated well with industry drones and performed accurate mortar drops on target while on the move. According to mechanical engineer Peter Resotka, the Soldiers were most impressed by the Picatinny CLIK ecosystem’s simplicity and by its reliability, and they gave valuable feedback for further improvements to the standard.
Armaments Center Director Chris Grassano, Weapons and Software Engineering Center Executive Director (A) Bhavanjot Singh, and Munitions Engineering and Technology Center Executive Director Anthony Sebasto attended the demonstrations and expressed strong confidence in the Picatinny CLIK’s abilities to unite industry and government. This event, said Resotka, will serve as a launching point for Picatinny CLIK to continue building and collaborating with industry partners.
title: Soldiers put Picatinny’s Common Lethality Integration Kit to the test at PC‑C6

BURLINGTON, VT – U.S. Representative Becca Balint (VT-AL), U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), and U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.) today announced the delivery of $60.3 million in new federal funding, administered by the Department of Transportation (DOT) to the Vermont Agency of Transportation (VTrans) to rehabilitate and complete approximately 60 miles of railway on Vermont’s Western Corridor rail line. 
“Repairing and upgrading our transportation infrastructure is a win-win for Vermont’s rural communities. This federal funding will help improve safety and reliability on the Vermont Railway, and support the development of rural towns up and down the Western Corridor,” said the Vermont Delegation. “With this $60 million investment from the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, the Western Corridor will be complete, and western Vermont will finally be connected to the New York Penn Station line.” 
“This grant will support Vermont businesses who rely on rail to get their products to market regionally and nationally,” said Vermont Transportation Secretary Joe Flynn. “For bulk commodities, shipping by rail is often the most cost-effective, and upgrades to the Vermont Railway in western Vermont will enable our businesses to efficiently tap into the nation's major Class I railroads.” 
This new funding will help replace rail, realign track, and upgrade ties, ballast, turnouts, and 22 at-grade crossings to enhance safety, improve system and service performance, and increase reliability of rail service in Vermont. The funding is made possible through DOT’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program. 
###
title: Vermont Delegation Announces More Than $60 Million in New Federal Funding to Complete Vermont’s Western Corridor Rail Line

RELEASE: Rep. Friedman Introduces Bill to Close Tax-Avoidance Loophole Used by the Ultra-Rich
Pay Your TAB Act taxes borrowing against a fortune the same as selling it, while protecting hardworking Americans & small business owners
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, October 20, 2026, U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) introduced the Pay Your Taxes Avoided by Borrowing (TAB) Act, legislation to close the “buy, borrow, die” loophole that lets the wealthiest Americans turn stock and other assets into spendable cash without ever paying tax on their gains.
The ultra-wealthy avoid paying taxes on their fortunes with a strategy known as “buy, borrow, die.” Under current law, gains on stock, real estate, and other assets are taxed only when the asset is sold. So instead of selling, the ultra-wealthy buy assets that grow in value, borrow against them, and live on the loan proceeds, which are not counted as income. When they die, those assets pass to their heirs with a stepped-up basis that erases the untaxed gain, so the gain is never taxed.
The Pay Your TAB Act taxes large asset-backed loans at 23.8%, the top long-term capital gains rate plus the Net Investment Income Tax, so borrowing against a fortune is taxed the same way as selling it.
“The Pay Your TAB Act closes a loophole the ultra-wealthy use to avoid paying taxes on fortunes 99% of Americans can’t imagine. They don’t sell the stock, they borrow against it, and a loan isn’t counted as income,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30). “My bill taxes those loans at 23.8%, the exact rate they’d owe by selling, while protecting mortgages, business loans, car loans, and student loans that hardworking families actually carry. It’s simple, it’s fair, it’s constitutionally sound, and it can be enforced the day it’s signed.”
WHAT THE PAY YOUR TAB ACT DOES:
- Imposes a 23.8% excise tax, paid by the borrower, on covered loans issued after December 31, 2026.
- Applies only to the portion of a borrower’s total covered loans above $1 million, with related parties counted together so the threshold can’t be split.
- Prevents double taxation by giving the borrower an offsetting long-term capital loss, equal to the taxed loan amount, when they later sell the asset that secured the loan.
- Requires lenders to report covered loans above the threshold to the IRS and to borrowers, and directs Treasury to issue anti-avoidance rules.
WHAT IS EXEMPT:
- Mortgages on a primary residence up to $3 million.
- Qualified student loans.
- Business loans, other than loans used to fund distributions.
- Qualified margin loans used for trading securities.
Because the Pay Your TAB Act is an excise tax on the issuance of a loan, it rests on the same constitutional authority Congress has used to levy excise taxes since the nation’s founding. It applies only when a loan is issued, so it doesn’t require taxing unrealized gains on assets that have never been sold. The bill is also simple to enforce because the tax is based on the amount of the loan rather than on calculating the changing value of an asset.
###
title: RELEASE: Rep. Friedman Introduces Bill to Close Tax-Avoidance Loophole Used by the Ultra-Rich

Today, U.S. Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02) released the following statement: 
“In the past few months, my office has received dozens of messages from constituents worried about how they are going to afford prescription medications if the Trump administration's new CBP rule goes into effect on October 22. I urged the Administration to delay the rule and stop health care from getting even more expensive, and last week, the Trump administration caved to pressure and announced a delay of the rule. I will continue to advocate for a final rule that stops dangerous and illegal drugs from entering our country without stopping affordable prescription medications.” 
On October 16, the Trump administration announced that it would delay implementation of new Customs and Border Patrol (CBP) procedures from October 22, 2026 to January 20, 2027. The new CBP procedures would increase regulations for international mail shipments, which could disrupt 2.3 million Americans’ longstanding ability to obtain lower-cost prescription medicines from Canada and other countries for personal use.
Earlier this month, Rep. Larsen joined a letter signed by 71 Members of Congress to Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) Robert F. Kennedy, Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) Markwayne Mullin, Acting Commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Kyle Diamantas and Commissioner of CBP Rodney Scott, urging the agencies to ensure Americans can continue obtaining non-controlled prescription medicines from outside the country.
“For years, our constituents who have struggled with high prescription drug prices have obtained their medicines from pharmacies outside the United States, especially from Canada,” the Members wrote. “We are concerned that the new process could be implemented in a manner that prevents personal-use prescription medicines from being shipped to the United States or results in their routine refusal, including medicines Americans have long obtained from licensed pharmacies abroad.”
The full text of the letter is available here.
Larsen Fights for Affordable Health Care 
Increasing access to affordable health care in Northwest Washington is a top priority for Rep. Larsen. He is fighting to extend the Affordable Care Act (ACA) enhanced premium tax credits, and has hosted roundtables with Northwest Washington community members to discuss policies to expand access to affordable health care, including his legislation that would reverse burdensome paperwork requirements in Medicaid.
###
title: Larsen, Colleagues Succeed in Delaying New CBP Rule Harming Access to Lower-Cost Medications

URBANA, Ill. – A federal jury returned a guilty verdict against Juan Carlos Oliva Lopez, 47, of Houston, Texas, on October 14, 2026, for possessing five kilograms or more of cocaine with intent to distribute it. Sentencing for Oliva Lopez has been scheduled for February 19, 2027, at the U.S. Courthouse in Urbana, Illinois.

Over two days of testimony, the government presented evidence to establish that, on February 19, 2024, Oliva Lopez was stopped by Illinois State Police troopers on Interstate 57 near Clifton, Illinois, as he transported 20 kilograms of cocaine from Houston, Texas. Evidence showed the cocaine was located in a suitcase underneath a bed in the semitruck driven by Oliva Lopez. Additional evidence presented at trial showed Oliva Lopez had been stopped in North Carolina nine days prior with more than $330,000 in cash, which had been hidden in a concealed compartment in a semitruck he was driving.

Oliva Lopez remains in the custody of the United States Marshal Service. At sentencing, Oliva Lopez faces statutory penalties of not less than ten years imprisonment; a fine up to $10,000,000; and at least five years of supervised release.

The case investigation was conducted by the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Illinois State Police, the Vermilion County Metropolitan Enforcement Group, and the Rowan County (North Carolina) Sheriff’s Department. Assistant United States Attorneys William J. Lynch and Rachel E. Ritzer represented the government at trial.

text:
Interview

Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Consulate General Mumbai

Mumbai, India

October 20, 2026

QUESTION: Secretary Rubio, thank you so much for giving Network18 this exclusive interview, and welcome to India.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Thank you.

QUESTION: You’ve been a well-wisher of India. You’re a tall global leader. This is your second visit in a matter of a few months. Last time you were in Delhi, you went to Agra, spent some quality time here. This time you’ve skipped Delhi, you’ve come to Mumbai, and you’re going to Jamnagar. What is the significance of this visit? What are you trying to achieve here?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, this is a big country. It’s an important country. And I think, like any big country, I say to people, if you want to learn and see what’s happening in the United States, you can’t just go to Washington. You should probably try to go somewhere in the South, maybe somewhere on the West Coast, and you probably need to get to New York and Chicago. And so for us, I mean, I don’t pretend that in my time as the Secretary of State I’ll get to see all of India or learn about every region. But I think it’s important to see a country of this size and magnitude and to learn as much about it as you can.

Mumbai in particular is the financial heart and soul of the country. It’s where so many of the companies that are investing in and with the United States – and who we want to do more trade with – are located. It’s the financial lifeblood of the country. So it’s logical to come here and, obviously, look forward to coming back and seeing the country again. I told our media earlier today we don’t – they were asking why we were here, because it’s amazing, the media wants us to go to other parts of the world sometimes, not here. I said we actually don’t come enough if you think about the importance of this relationship. So not only do I – I’m glad I’m here, but I’m glad there’s a congressional delegation in town at the same time. And I know we’ve sent people here from – the Attorney General’s been here, the Commerce Secretary’s been here, and I expect to be back.

QUESTION: Since we are in Mumbai, the commercial capital, let’s get down to business. The trade deal between India and the U.S., today you said it is very, very close. How close is close? When —

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, I —

QUESTION: Is there a deadline?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, no, I’ve felt that way before. And with these deals, it’s always important that it be totally agreed to every detail of it, before it’s announced, because you can’t afford for a relationship of this magnitude to be threatened by announcing a deal and then it turning out the deal wasn’t finalized. But it’s incredibly close. I think we’re down to some technical details that have to be worked out. Technical details matter because there has to be agreement. Both sides have to agree that the language means the same thing. So it’s down to that level. I’m not personally negotiating it because it’s done through our Trade Representative. But I know – and have been very involved in watching it happen – that it is something we anticipate seeing in a matter of weeks, not months.

QUESTION: And do you think that India can expect to some better rates than others?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, obviously the purpose of making a deal is to have better rates than what you have now. But the more important thing is about ensuring that our trade relationship is in a sustainable way. Look, the foreign policy of the United States, the trade policy of the United States is driven by a recognition that every country has national interests. We fully expect, not just India but every country we interact with, is going to defend and fight for what’s good for them.

QUESTION: Yes.

SECRETARY RUBIO: And we’re going to fight for what’s good for us. The difference is when you are friends, when you are allies, when you have so much in common, that’s what allows you to bridge those differences and come up with something that’s mutually beneficial. For a trade deal with India, or any country for that matter, to be sustainable in the long term, it has to be an agreement that is good for both sides. There are things that you’re not going to like in it, but the preponderance of it is good for you. And that’s what we aim to achieve here, and I can’t wait till we do it because we have so many things we can work together on.

QUESTION: Mr. Secretary, America imposes sanctions and tariffs on countries like India for buying Russian oil. But America itself is buying diesel now from Russia to cool pump prices, probably ahead of the midterms. How do you see this change and the shift in strategy? And how do you explain this broader picture?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah – well, what’s interesting about it is – and I’m not saying the war in Ukraine is not important; it is, and it’s something now that’s going on its fifth year. It’s very problematic in that regard. But even the people that pressure us, I could do this interview in another part of the world and they’re asking us why we’re not imposing more sanctions. And people don’t realize that sanctions come at a consequence, because sanctions aren’t just on Russia. They are on anyone who does business with Russia. So there’s a balancing act there – there always is – between on the one hand trying to pressure the countries involved in this war to enter into an agreement, and on the other hand recognizing that when you do that pressure, sometimes it spills over and has a negative impact on other countries.

It’s one of the reasons why, despite criticism from Democrats and others, the President chose to use a national security waiver on the latest bill that Congress passed, which called for an increase in tariffs – and sanctions, but tariffs – on specific countries that are still doing work with Russia. And the President chose to use a national security waiver to not immediately implement those, because he recognizes that these things have to be looked at in their totality. It can’t just be about the – you have to balance your interest, what’s happening in Ukraine and Russia, with the impact that it’s having on a global scale.

So hopefully, between that and a trade agreement with India, these issues will be resolved. But I understand the tension exists, and I understand sort of a balancing act that we have to work through.

QUESTION: One more issue that concerns us, Mr. Secretary, is that a few days back there was a block to attack a Hindu temple in the state of Illinois. The Indian Government has also drawn the attention towards racist hostility and anti-India sentiment, anti-India hate. How do you see this towards a community that is known for academic excellence, low crime rate, and it’s actually a part of the great American story?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, unfortunately – and I will just say this is not unique to the United States – in every society in the world, because it’s endemic to the human condition, there is ignorance and there’s hatred. And it happens, and you see it – these attacks in different parts of the world for different reasons. Some are motivated by terrorism; others are motivated by hatred. And the United States is not immune to that.

I do not believe, nor have I ever perceived, that anti-Indian sentiment in the United States is widespread or deep. But I must also tell you, like any large and complex society, there are individuals within our country, sadly, who are stupid, who are dumb, or who are ignorant, or who are hateful. And what I am very proud of is the way these communities react when it happens. And I don’t just mean the Indian and American community, I mean the community that surrounds them and how they rally around and reject it.

I remember, a few years ago, we had a horrifying incident with a Sikh community in Wisconsin and how the community rallied to support them. So these things happen. We have a rise in antisemitism in the United States. We’ve seen that as well; it’s very disturbing.

QUESTION: Yes.

SECRETARY RUBIO: So these are things that we address and we reject. I think the important point is that the majority of the country speaks with moral clarity about how wrong these things are and that those of us in positions of authority never do anything that is sort of encouraging it or excusing it or in any way looking the other way.

QUESTION: That’s reassuring. One more question is this U.S. stance towards Pakistan. You, as senator in 2025, you had said that you would introduce a bill to cut U.S. security aid to Pakistan if it sponsored terror against India. Has that changed? Has that policy changed at all?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, we’re against terrorism anywhere in the world. We’re against anybody who sponsors terrorism. In my new role – I’m no longer a senator; I’m the Secretary of State – I have to manage the foreign policy of the United States. And that does require us to have relationships with countries, including those that we may have some disagreements with.

In the case of Pakistan, it’s a country that we have to have a relationship with. It’s a country that possesses nuclear weapons. It’s a country that, from a geographic standpoint, we need to be able to interact with them, in much the same way as the Government of India has to have and has a relationship and meets with leaders from Iran.

QUESTION: Yes.

SECRETARY RUBIO: So these are difficult things to balance, but they have to be as part of our foreign policy. And I think in a way it could be a positive thing, because if we have a relationship and we can speak to them it could perhaps help us – help – it perhaps puts us in a position to help discourage the kinds of things that India is worried about.

QUESTION: Okay. Mr. Secretary, earlier this month you said that Iran had lost complete control of the Strait of Hormuz, but ships are being struck every now and then, and the war is spreading to Yemen and Saudi Arabia. How do you see the situation evolving? President Trump has been saying that the war will be over after the midterms. Do you see military escalation, or do you see there is a deal in the offering?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, it’s tough to make a deal with the Iranian regime. Unfortunately, they don’t know how to make a deal, and they’re controlled by radical Shia clerics. And I don’t mean Shia clerics; I mean radical Shia clerics who are driven by theology – very difficult to make a deal with them. The straits are – if you look at on any given night in the straits, the amount of traffic and oil and energy flowing through there is on – it’s 80 to 100 percent equal to what it was before the conflict.

Unfortunately, Iran is doing something – and that’s really what people should be talking about. What they really should be talking about is that we have a nation-state that is openly – openly – saying: We are targeting commercial vessels; we are trying to kill sailors who have nothing to do with the war; we are trying to sink commercial ships. You haven’t seen that since the Second World War.

QUESTION: Yes.

SECRETARY RUBIO: They are doing Nazi U-boat tactics. And that’s what the world should be rallying around and condemning. Every single night, the United States defends shipping. The overwhelming majority of these drones and missiles that they are launching at ships are being destroyed. Every now and then, unfortunately, one will get through and strike the ship. Luckily, for the most part, most of these ships are able to continue in transit. But every now and then, you do see an engine room hit. And every now and then you see loss of life, including many Indian sailors who have lost their lives in these strikes because there’s such a large number of Indian sailors out there.

So it’s something that we’re worried about, but I think it’s incumbent on Iran to stop doing it. In the meantime, we’re going to continue putting extraordinary economic pressure on them, because we know that every dollar that they get access to, every resource they get access to – they don’t use it to better the lives of their people or better their country. They use it to sponsor terrorism. They use it to make missiles and drones to try to sink commercial vessels.

QUESTION: Mr. Secretary, there hasn’t been a Quad leaders’ summit since September 2024, and it is Indian’s turn to host it now. Do you think this happening anytime soon? Will President Trump travel to India for the Quad’s next Quad summit?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, our hope is that a Quad summit will occur before the end of this year. It’s been agreement now that we’re going to do it; we’re going to do it in Manilla, at the ASEAN conference, where the four – we don’t have the specific date yet, but that’s going to happen, and we’re very enthusiastic about it. There’s been – in fact, the first meeting I ever did as Secretary of State was a Quad meeting with the foreign ministers. That is literally the first meeting I ever did. As soon as I was sworn in, I went upstairs and we did it. I think since then we’ve had seven or eight engagements. We’re about to have another one in Atlanta at the G20. And the leaders-level meeting, we look forward to being a part of that at ASEAN here in just a few weeks.

QUESTION: Mr. Secretary, one last question. You’ve been in India this time. You’ve met Foreign Minister Jaishankar. Could you give us a sense of the conversation between the two sides? And what takes you to Jamnagar tomorrow, to Reliance?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, on – with Jai, I think we have a great relationship, and I’ve gotten to know him. As I said, it was the first meeting I did as Secretary of State – he was part of it at the time; he was part of that first meeting. So we’ve met – I don’t know how many – we’ve must have met at least a dozen times, because he also came to the United States four times. We saw him – anytime we’re in the same city, at a gathering or a conference or what have you, we always make a point to meet. And so I think we’ve created a very positive and solid work relationship that’s allowed us to navigate some delicate and sensitive things over the last year and a half.

As far as moving forward on the relationship, I think we have extraordinary opportunities. I think we are aligned on so many different things. The Quad is one that’s really taking on a lot of energy, and – because the Quad is not just a process by which we meet and agree to do certain things. You are now starting to see action; you are now starting to see things happen. And that’s what we’re excited about for the leaders’ meeting, is that at that meeting they will be able to actually announce concrete actions, not just simply a nice social gathering, but something that has concrete deliverables.

QUESTION: And the agenda in Jamnagar tomorrow?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Oh, the agenda, I’m – so well, look, Reliance is a very important company and has extraordinary capacity to refine energy. Petroleum is useless if you don’t refine it into a useable product. We think there’s an opportunity for them to continue to help India diversify its supply chain, its supply of energy. For example, Venezuela is increasing its production of energy, and India has had a long history of being able to refine some of that.

But it’s also one of the few companies that’s actually invested in refining capacity in the United States. They’ve invested in increasing the refining capacity within the United States. So being so close, it made sense to go see their operations, spend some time talking to them about the way we can work together more closely, especially when it comes to energy from the Western Hemisphere that can be refined here. I think that’s helpful to India, but it’s also helpful to us.

QUESTION: Thank you so much for giving us the time.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Thank you.

QUESTION: Thank you for spending time with Network18. Through our network, you will be watched in every nook and corner of the country, through CNN-News18, CNBC, Firstpost, and at least 50 news – regional news channels in the country. Thank you so much.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Wow, good. That’s like 50 interviews in one.

QUESTION: That’s right. Thank you so much. Appreciate it.

Tags
title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio with Rahul Joshi of News18

SEC and AMF Announce Supervisory MOU To Enhance Cooperation for Investment Advisers and Investment Service Providers
Washington D.C., Oct. 20, 2026 —
The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the French Autorité des Marchés Financiers (AMF) announced that they have entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) designed to facilitate consultation and information-sharing in the supervision of certain investment advisers and investment companies regulated by the SEC and investment service providers supervised by the AMF.
The MOU establishes a comprehensive framework for consultation, cooperation, and the exchange of information between the SEC and the AMF in connection with investment service providers, investment advisers, and investment companies that operate in the U.S. and in France and are overseen by either the SEC or the AMF.
In particular, the MOU facilitates the SEC’s registration and supervision of AMF supervised asset management companies wishing to conduct business in the United States as investment advisers. The SEC will process new and pending registration applications by AMF supervised asset management companies in the light of this arrangement.
“This MOU exemplifies the necessary spirit of cooperation in securities regulation to expand opportunity and ensure our global markets thrive in ways that are flexible, innovative, and protective of investors worldwide,” said SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins. “I thank our French colleagues for their cross-border collaboration and cooperation.”
“We welcome this MOU which marks a further step in strengthening cooperation between our two authorities and reflects our shared commitment to contribute to the development of our capital markets while safeguarding the integrity and resilience of the financial system and ensuring effective investor protection,” said AMF Chair Marie-Anne Barbat-Layani.”
###
Last Reviewed or Updated: Oct. 20, 2026

ST. LOUIS – A Lincoln County, Missouri man who took sexual photos of three young boys was sentenced Tuesday to 25 years in prison.

Jeremy J.W. Crouch, 43, used a hidden camera to record three boys about a decade ago and took photos of one while he was sleeping in just his underwear. The victims were between the ages of 8 and 11 at the time. He possessed a total of at least 4,093 images of child sexual abuse material (CSAM).

The investigation began on March 27, 2025, when the St. Charles County Cyber Crime Task Force was assigned a tip about CSAM that had been detected in Crouch’s Verizon account. Investigators sought a warrant for Crouch’s account and arrested him when they received data showing CSAM in the account. A court-approved search of his home uncovered handwritten notes detailing his encounters with the victims, as well as electronic devices and DVDs that contained CSAM.

During Tuesday’s hearing, the relative of one victim described Crouch as a “master manipulator” who “had so many people fooled.”

Crouch pleaded guilty in July in U.S. District Court in St. Louis to one count of receipt of child pornography and one count of production of child pornography.

The FBI, the St. Charles County Cyber Crime Task Force and the Lincoln County Sheriff’s Office investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Jillian Anderson prosecuted the case.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Department of Justice Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc .
title: Missouri Man Who Produced Child Sexual Abuse Material Sentenced to 25 Years in Prison

Rep. Craig Announces Savage’s Designation as a World War II Heritage City
EAGAN, MN – Today, U.S. Representative Angie Craig announced that the National Park Service (NPS) has officially designated Savage, Minnesota a World War II (WWII) Heritage City, recognizing the city for its outstanding contributions during WWII and the community’s commitment to preserving its rich history.
Rep. Craig penned a letter of support to NPS last April, urging the agency to recognize Savage for its wartime contributions.
“The City of Savage and its residents played a critical role during World War II, and today, they are finally getting the recognition they deserve,” said Rep. Craig. “Whether it was offering translation services, building ships or distributing supplies to aid the war effort, folks in Savage went above and beyond to show their patriotism and commitment to America’s national security. I am proud that the National Park Service is designating Savage a World War II Heritage City and cementing its place in our nation’s history.”
From 1942-1944, Camp Savage was home to the secret Military Intelligence Service Language School (MISLS) where 6,000 Nisei American soldiers were trained in military intelligence and linguistics, significantly aiding U.S. forces throughout every campaign and major battle in the Asia Pacific.
According to Major General Charles Willoughby, the Nisei linguist soldiers helped shorten the Pacific war by two years, saving roughly one million American lives. After the victory in the Pacific, MISLS-trained linguists helped translate more than 20 million pages of documents and played a crucial role in postwar war crimes trials.
The City of Savage was also home to the Savage Shipyard, converted by Cargill to employ over 3,500 workers. The shipyard built 18 ships for the Navy and four tugboats for the Army, receiving an Army-Navy “E” award for excellence in the production of war equipment.
The City of Savage is unique in Minnesota for its preservation of heritage and legacy. Savage has established a memorial to Camp Savage and the MISLS at the Scott County Library. In addition, the Scott County Historical Society has been critical in cataloguing and preserving Savage’s wartime contributions.
###
title: Rep. Craig Announces Savage’s Designation as a World War II Heritage City

Digital Self-Service Option Makes It Easier for Americans to Financially Prepare for Floods
WASHINGTON – It is now easier than ever to prepare for the devastating financial consequences of flooding.
Today FEMA launched a new tool to purchase a National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) policy completely online through Floodsmart.gov. This online purchase option is available nationwide for anyone living in one of the almost 22,700 participating NFIP communities.
This development aligns with President Trump’s America First Resilience Strategy which outlines a risk-informed approach to resilience that empowers the American people to protect themselves and their property. Individuals are the first line of resilience and represent the nation’s greatest strategic advantage. By making it easier to purchase flood insurance, FEMA is empowering them to ensure their own resilience and reduce dependence on federal assistance.
“I’ve seen firsthand how floodwaters devastate American communities,” said FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton. “We are making it easier for people to reduce their financial risk and protect what they’ve spent their lives building. With this new digital tool, you can get a quote and buy a flood insurance policy in a matter of minutes. This innovation demonstrates how FEMA is working to cut bureaucracy and deliver results to the American people.”
Through this new self-service digital purchase option, FEMA is reducing barriers and making flood insurance more accessible to people nationwide. You can get a quote on Floodsmart.gov after providing basic information about your building. Once you receive your quote, you will have the option to purchase a policy online or through an insurance agent. If you choose to purchase online, you can do so on Floodsmart.gov in just a few minutes. If you choose to purchase through a local or national carrier, you can share your quote details with your insurance agent, or Floodsmart.gov will offer the contact information of three licensed state insurance agents.
The new self-service tool is consistent with the insurance industry’s shift toward digital engagement and aims to make it easier for more Americans to access flood coverage.
Floods are the most common and costliest natural disaster in the United States. Flood insurance provides financial protection against the unexpected to help Americans be better prepared, self-sufficient and confident in their ability to safeguard their future. FEMA’s National Flood Insurance Program provides about $1.2 trillion in coverage for approximately 4.4 million policyholders nationwide.
To learn more about flood insurance, get a quote and purchase a policy, visit Floodsmart.gov/policy-quote.
title: FEMA Launches New Option to Buy National Flood Insurance Program Policy Online

Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04) and Congressman Mike Haridopolos (FL-08) introduced the bipartisan and bicameral National American History and Founders Month Act to empower Americans to be active citizens through a deeper understanding of our nation’s early history, its founders and founding ideals, and the civic duties within the American experience.
“Our nation was established 250 years ago on the revolutionary idea that the power of government derives from the people in order to secure the inalienable rights of life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness,” said Congresswoman McClellan. “To ensure that all citizens can participate in our government by, of and for the people, each generation must fully understand the rich and complex history of its founding. The National American History and Founders Month Act provides an opportunity to reflect on that history and recommit to ensuring the great American experiment endures.”
“This year, we celebrated 250 years of freedom, independence, and the enduring principles that have shaped our nation,” said Congressman Haridopolos. “We are truly lucky to live in the greatest country in the world, and we must never take that blessing for granted. As a former history teacher, I know that by teaching future generations about our nation’s founding and the sacrifices that made our freedoms possible, we can ensure America’s remarkable story continues to inspire for generations to come.”
“This nation has lasted 250 years not because its documents are self-executing, but because in every generation enough Americans understood what they had inherited,” said Dr. Jennifer London, President and Founder of NAHFMO. “I am deeply grateful to Representatives Haridopolos and McClellan for introducing this bill together, which would give National American History and Founders Month a permanent place in federal law and invite schools, families and communities to learn about the people, ideals and events that built this nation. With a companion bill already introduced in the Senate by Senators Wicker, Kaine and McCormick, and the country marking the anniversary of its founding, this is the right moment.”
title: McClellan and Haridopolos Introduce Legislation to Establish National American History and Founders Month

Civil Rights Division and Equal Employment Opportunity Commission Secure $5,000,000 Joint Settlement with Instacart for Discriminating Against U.S. Workers
The United States Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division, in partnership with the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, announced they have secured a $5,000,000 settlement with Maplebear Inc., doing business as Instacart, a San Francisco, California-based online delivery service. The settlement addresses allegations that Instacart discriminated against U.S. and American workers based on citizenship status and national origin in violation, respectively, of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) and Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (Title VII). Specifically, the agencies uncovered evidence that Instacart’s hiring and recruitment practices undertaken as part of the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) process intentionally discriminated against U.S. and American workers by preferring workers with temporary employment visas. A summary of the settlement terms may be found here.
“This significant resolution marks the fifteenth settlement agreement the Civil Rights Division has reached under my leadership to protect U.S. workers,” said Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. “Our record demonstrates that the Justice Department is holding companies who prefer workers with temporary employment visas accountable. We will not stop fighting for U.S. workers until there is a fair playing field.”
“Today’s settlement makes clear that when employers erect unlawful barriers that harm American workers, the EEOC will act decisively,” said Chair Andrea Lucas of the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. “The EEOC is committed to holding companies accountable when they deny equal work opportunities to U.S. workers by preferring temporary visa holders for jobs. Discrimination against workers based on their American national origin has no place in our economy.”
The Justice Department’s investigation found that Instacart created additional burdens on U.S. workers to apply for job opportunities by requiring that applications be physically mailed for positions advertised as part of PERM recruitment. EEOC’s investigation uncovered similar evidence. This practice departed from Instacart’s standard recruitment process, which allowed electronic applications. As a result, many of the U.S. workers who applied were not timely considered.
Under the terms of the settlement, Instacart will establish a settlement fund of up to $4,000,000 to compensate Instacart applicants as well as deterred applicants affected by the discriminatory practices from December 2023 to February 2026. A claims administrator will contact potential aggrieved individuals and will determine eligibility for back pay and compensatory damages. Until the claims administrator establishes a contact email for potential victims, the DOJ and EEOC encourage applicants, as well as deterred applicants, to email Instacart@eeoc.gov if they believe they may be aggrieved so that agencies can share this information with the claims administrator.
In addition, Instacart will pay $1,000,000 in civil penalties to the United States. Instacart is also required to give U.S. workers fair opportunities to apply for jobs as part of the PERM recruitment process by posting the positions on its public career website and accepting electronic applications. The agreement also requires Instacart to train personnel on its anti-discrimination obligations, revise its employment policies, and be subject to monitoring and reporting requirements, to prevent future discrimination.
The PERM program allows employers to sponsor temporary visa holders for permanent resident status after performing good-faith recruitment for U.S. workers. However, during this recruitment process, companies cannot illegally discriminate on the basis of citizenship status or national origin by creating additional burdens for U.S. and American workers; publishing job advertisements that disfavor, limit, specify, or otherwise discriminate against U.S. and American workers; or use processes that limit, segregate, or classify applicants in any way that tends to deprive U.S. and American applicants of employment opportunities.
This settlement is the fifteenth reached since the Justice Department re-launched its Protecting U.S. Workers Initiative in 2025 to enforce the INA’s prohibition on citizenship status discrimination against employers that illegally favor workers with employment visas over U.S. workers. Since the original launch of the Protecting U.S. Workers Initiative during President Trump’s first administration, the Department has secured over $34 million in back pay for U.S. workers and obtained over $16 million in civil penalties from employers who discriminated against U.S. workers. Under these settlements, the Justice Department obtains civil penalties for each violation and will continue to seek the maximum penalty permitted by law. The settlements also involve awards of back pay, when warranted, and require employers to conduct comprehensive training for relevant staff and recruiters and cease restricting consideration for job opportunities based on workers’ citizenship status without a lawful reason. For information about additional settlements under the Protecting U.S. Workers Initiative, visit IER’s website.
As part of its work related to Project Firewall, the EEOC is protecting American workers by enforcing Title VII’s prohibition on national origin discrimination against employers that illegally favor foreign workers over workers of American national origin. In addition to five lawsuits currently pending in federal court, this is the fourth public settlement reached by EEOC involving anti-American national origin discrimination since 2025.
For more information about EEOC’s work combatting anti-American national origin discrimination, visit EEOC’s website.
For informal assistance, the public can call IER’s free hotline at 1-800-255-7688 for workers or at 1-800-255-8155 for employers (1-800-237-2515, TTY for hearing impaired) between 9am and 5pm Eastern Time, Monday through Friday; sign up for a live webinar or watch an on-demand presentation; email IER@usdoj.gov; or visit www.justice.gov/ier.
title: Civil Rights Division and Equal Employment Opportunity Commission Secure $5,000,000 Joint Settlement with Instacart for Discriminating Against U.S. Workers

LAWMAKERS CALL FOR UKRAINIAN TEMPORARAY PROTECTED STATUS (TPS) EXTENSION
WASHINGTON, D.C. — This week, Rep. Val Hoyle (D-OR) and Rep. Bryan Fitzpatrick (R-PA) led over 50 of their colleagues in sending a letter to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin demanding the agency ensure that Ukrainian nationals legally in the United States, particularly those with Temporary Protected Status (TPS), are able to safely access and attend their immigration court hearings, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) interviews and other required legal appointments.
This push comes as DHS recently announced that over 100,000 of Ukrainians whose TPS benefits were slated to expire on October 19th, will retain their TPS protections and work permits until the Department makes a final decision. While this announcement provides much needed relief for TPS holders, the lack of a formal redesignation and extension could potentially exclude individuals who fled the same war and cause confusion and stress for people already facing uncertainty about their future, impacting their ability to keep work. Without any safe and durable path for Ukrainians to return home, these protections must be kept in place.
The lawmakers wrote: “A redesignation would extend eligibility to Ukrainians who arrived in the United States after the current designation's cutoff date, but who fled the same war under the same circumstances and would give affected individuals clarity regardingtheir status. Those who came to our shores fleeing violence and instability deserve the opportunity to rebuild their lives and go through our country’s legal processes.”
The lawmakers concluded their letter with the following demands:
- Provide full due process for any Ukrainian TPS holders attending immigration court hearings, USCIS interviews and other required legal appointments
- Provide information about Ukrainian nationals in ICE custody, the circumstances of their arrest and the status of their pending immigration cases to allow for appropriate oversight
The full text of the letter is available here.

BISMARCK – United States Attorney Nicholas W. Chase announced that Linford Atakora, age 29, from the Republic of Ghana, was sentenced by United States District Court Judge Daniel L. Hovland to approximately 9 months’ imprisonment for time already served in federal custody, on a felony charge of Misuse of a Social Security Number. Additionally, Judge Hovland issued an order removing Atakora from the United States to the Republic of Ghana.

According to court documents, in March 2024, Atakora fraudulently used the name, date of birth, and social security number of his relative – a United States citizen – to obtain employment at a home health agency. Atakora presented his relative’s driver’s license and social security card when he applied for employment at Love & Care, Inc., located in Bismarck, North Dakota. Atakora then fraudulently completed an IRS form W-4 Employee’s Withholding Certificate and an employee information form. Atakora did not have a valid social security number and did not have authorization to work in the United States. Due to Atakora’s misrepresentations, Love & Care, Inc. falsely received Health and Human Service ineligible units and claims totaling $51,435.63.

“This case serves as an important reminder to North Dakota workers and employers that working under another person’s identity or social security number to circumvent immigration work requirements is a federal crime,” said U.S. Attorney Nicholas W. Chase. “Our office will continue to work with our state and federal law enforcement partners to investigate and prosecute these types of offenses.”

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

This case was investigated by the Social Security Administration—Office of Inspector General and prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Jonathan J. O’Konek.

######
title: Ghanaian Man Sentenced for Fraudulently Working under the Name and Social Security Number of a United States Citizen

Stakeholders Are Encouraged to Review Notice of Proposed Rulemaking and Submit Comments
Alexandria, VA (October 20, 2026) ― The National Credit Union Administration today announced the thirteenth round of proposed regulatory changes associated with NCUA’s Deregulation Project. The project is an ongoing review of NCUA’s regulations to ensure regulations are focused on credit unions’ safety, soundness, and resilience.
With today’s announcement, NCUA is requesting comments on three proposals that would eliminate obsolete regulations, unduly burdensome, and duplicative requirements in the Code of Federal Regulations.
The proposals include:
NPRM Summary
The NCUA Board (Board) proposes to remove the requirement that federally insured, state-chartered credit unions (FISCUs) maintain a special reserve for certain nonconforming investments. The proposal would also remove related references to the reserve requirement in NCUA’s capital, investment, and regulations on requirements for insurance. The Board states that the changes would reduce regulatory burden, simplify requirements, and provide greater flexibility for FISCUs while maintaining safety and soundness and protecting the National Credit Union Share Insurance Fund.
NPRM Summary
The Board proposes to remove 12 CFR 741.7, which addresses the process for maintaining federal share insurance following the conversion of a federal credit union (FCU) to a state charter. The Board states that the provision is outdated and duplicates requirements already addressed in NCUA's Chartering and Field of Membership Manual (Manual). Because amendments to the Manual have superseded 12 CFR 741.7, the proposal would remove the provision to improve regulatory clarity and eliminate unnecessary duplication.
NPRM Summary
The Board proposes to revise its share insurance regulation to simplify how federally insured credit unions (FICUs) notify members about NCUA share insurance coverage. Currently, FICUs must make certain share insurance materials available in hard copy. Under the proposal, FICUs would continue to provide notice to members but would have greater flexibility in how they do so. The proposal is intended to simplify compliance, reduce costs, and help ensure members receive current share insurance information.
Find a detailed summary for each proposal at https://ncua.gov/news/deregulation-project/.
To submit comments, type or paste the docket numbers into the search on the Federal Rulemaking Portal.
title: NCUA Announces Thirteenth Round of Deregulation Proposals

WASHINGTON — The U.S. Small Business Administration announced today the opening of a Business Recovery Center in Coconino County to assist small businesses and private nonprofit organizations affected by flash flooding at Grand Canyon National Park occurring Aug. 29 – Sept. 3.
Beginning Tuesday, Oct. 20, customer service representatives will be at the Business Recovery Center in Tusayan to answer questions and assist people with the disaster loan application process. Walk-ins are welcome, and in-person appointments can be scheduled at appointment.sba.gov.
The hours of operation are listed below:

Tusayan Town Hall
Town of Tusayan
845 Mustang Dr.
Tusayan, AZ  86023
Opens Tuesday, Oct. 20, at 10 a.m.
Monday – Friday, 8 a.m. – 5 p.m.
Closes permanently Friday, Oct. 30, at 5 p.m.
“SBA loans help eligible small businesses and private nonprofits cover operating expenses after a disaster, which is crucial for their recovery,” said Chris Stallings, Associate Administrator of the Office of Disaster Recovery at SBA. “These loans not only help business owners get back on their feet but also play a key role in sustaining local economies in the aftermath of a disaster.”
The SBA’s Economic Injury Disaster Loan program is available to small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, and private nonprofit organizations — including faith‑based organizations — with financial losses directly related to the disaster. The SBA is unable to provide disaster loans to agricultural producers, farmers, or ranchers, except for small aquaculture enterprises.
Economic Injury Disaster Loan’s are available for working capital needs caused by the disaster and are available even if the small business or private nonprofit did not suffer any physical damage. The loans may be used to pay fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills which could not be paid due to the disaster.
The loan amount can be up to $2 million with interest rates as low as 4% for businesses and 3.625% for private nonprofits with terms up to 30 years. Interest does not accrue, and payments are not due until 12 months from the date of the first loan disbursement. The SBA determines eligibility and sets loan amounts and terms based on each applicant’s financial condition.
To apply online, visit sba.gov/disaster. Applicants may also call SBA’s National Support Network Center at (866) SBA-HELP or email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov for more information on SBA disaster assistance. For people who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability, please dial 7-1-1 to access telecommunications relay services.
The deadline to return economic injury applications is July 13, 2027.
###
About the U.S. Small Business Administration
The U.S. Small Business Administration helps power the American dream of business ownership. As the only go-to resource and voice for small businesses backed by the strength of the federal government, the SBA empowers entrepreneurs and small business owners with the resources and support they need to start, grow, expand their businesses, or recover from a declared disaster. It delivers services through an extensive network of SBA field offices and partnerships with public and private organizations. To learn more, visit www.sba.gov.
title: SBA Opens Business Recovery Center in Tusayan

CAMP ZAMA, Japan – Soldiers here hosted a community outreach event Oct. 3 to strengthen ties and build cross-cultural connections with local Japanese youth through a day of interactive games, a shared meal, and shared fellowship.
Soldiers and family members from the Better Opportunities for Single Soldiers program and the 78th Signal Battalion facilitated the event, which started at the installation’s BOSS Warrior Zone. The group did indoor activities such as video games, air hockey and cornhole. After a barbecue lunch, everyone headed outdoors for active games, including tag and tug-of-war.
Initial worries about language barriers vanished as the children and Soldiers turned to translation apps on their phones.
“At first, I felt intimidated by the Soldiers and worried that we wouldn’t be able to communicate,” an 18-year-old participant said. “But once we started using the apps, communication became effortless. I realized we shared common interests and formed a bond with them almost instantly. Even though we come from different backgrounds, we’re all human beings.”
“It was a great collaboration between BOSS and the 78th Signal Battalion,” BOSS President Sgt. Dillon Bruyer said. “We want to engage with our local community here and show a positive impact.”
Bruyer noted that events like this offer Soldiers a meaningful way to give back while reflecting on their own support systems. Having been raised by his grandparents, Bruyer emphasized how working with young people reinforces the collaboration of family and community connections.
Judging by the smiles, the joint initiative succeeded in building stronger bonds between Camp Zama and the local community.
title: Bridging Cultures: Japanese youth, U.S. Soldiers find common ground
