CHARLOTTE, N.C. – The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of North Carolina joins the Justice Department, the Office on Violence Against Women (OVW), and communities across the district in observing Domestic Violence Awareness Month (DVAM).

Each year, DVAM is an opportunity to recommit to addressing domestic violence using every available resource and to strengthen our partnerships with law enforcement, victim service organizations, and community partners to ensure justice and safety for victims and survivors.

“There is no excuse for domestic violence. It creates a terrifying situation that is extraordinarily difficult for victims, and fighting and preventing it is our shared responsibility,” said U.S. Attorney Russ Ferguson. “My office is committed to pursuing justice for victims and survivors, holding offenders accountable, and working with our law enforcement and community partners to prevent domestic violence and connect those it impacts with resources they need to ensure safety and recovery.”

U.S. Attorney Russ Ferguson, along with other members of the U.S. Attorney’s Office, regularly engage in domestic violence prevention and intervention activities throughout the year such as touring shelters, visiting service providers, identifying federal grants, and attending events to stand in solidarity with victims and survivors. Domestic Violence Awareness Month is a time to amplify and emphasize those regular activities.

On October 22 at 10:30 a.m., U.S. Attorney Russ Ferguson will host a Facebook Live discussion centered on domestic violence. U.S. Attorney Ferguson will be joined by a federal prosecutor, a survivor of domestic violence, and a representative from Safe Alliance, an organization that provides services and support to survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault, to discuss the impact of domestic violence, the role of the U.S. Attorney’s Office role in enforcing federal laws to protect victims, including federal firearm prohibitions that apply to certain domestic violence offenders, and resources available to victims and survivors. Please join us for this important conversation at Facebook.com/usaoWDNC .

For more information on domestic violence, visit the Justice Department’s Office on Violence Against Women .

If you need help, contact the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233 or the Strong Hearts Native Helpline at 1-844-762-8483.
title: U.S. Attorney’s Office Observes Domestic Violence Awareness Month; To Host Facebook Live Discussion Centered on Domestic Violence

Thompson, Doggett Partner on Bill Expanding Medicare Benefits to Cover Dental, Vision and Hearing
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representative Lloyd Doggett (D-TX), Ranking Member of the House Ways & Means Health Subcommittee, announced that his colleague Rep. Mike Thompson (D-CA) will lead the effort to pass Rep. Doggett’s Medicare Dental, Vision, and Hearing Benefit Act in the next congress. As Rep. Doggett prepares to retire, he has tapped Thompson to carry forward this crucial legislation expanding Medicare coverage to include dental, vision and hearing benefits.
“Maintaining one’s dental, hearing, and vision health is critical to ensuring good nutrition, preventing cognitive decline, stopping falls, and more. I’ve always believed that expanding older Americans’ access to these kinds of healthcare just makes sense,” said Thompson. “I’m honored to work with my colleague Rep. Lloyd Doggett lead the effort to expand Medicare benefits in the next Congress.”
“We seek to assure more comprehensive health coverage for the more than 66 million seniors and disabled individuals who rely on Medicare,” said Doggett. “Though so important to overall health, Medicare coverage continues to be very limited for dental, vision, and hearing services. This expanded care could help prevent cognitive impairment and dementia, worsened chronic disease, and imbalance leading to falls with deadly consequences. This is an essential step to fulfilling the original promise of Medicare—to assure dignity and health for all. I’m pleased to work with Rep. Thompson, who has supported this bill for many years, to ensure this important legislation is carried forward.”
BACKGROUND
Expanding Medicare to cover dental, hearing, and vision services is overwhelmingly popular: A Data for Progress poll conducted in 2024 found that 92 percent of Americans supported expanding Medicare to provide dental, vision and hearing benefits.
Over 24 million Medicare beneficiaries have no dental coverage at all and have to pay out-of-pocket or forego needed care. Further, more than one in three Medicare beneficiaries have difficulty seeing and more than two in five Medicare beneficiaries have difficulty hearing.
After Republicans in Congress cut $1 trillion from our health care system in order to pay for tax breaks for the top one percent, Doggett and Thompson are fighting to reverse these cuts and to make it easier for seniors and people with disabilities to go to the dentist, audiologist and optometrist.
The Medicare Dental, Vision, and Hearing Benefit Act updates the Medicare benefits package to ensure that all beneficiaries have access to crucial items and services that are important to their overall health. Senator Bernie Sander (I-VT) leads the companion bill in the U.S. Senate. The bill makes the following changes to federal law:
- Repeals the outdated statutory exclusion that currently prohibits Medicare from covering most dental, vision, and hearing care.
- Expands Medicare benefits to include items and services such as dentures, preventative and emergency dental care; refractive eye exams and eyeglasses; and hearing aids and exams.
- Provides for appropriate payment to health providers through Medicare Part B.
The Medicare Dental, Vision, and Hearing Benefit Act is endorsed by: Center for Medicare Advocacy, Community Catalyst, Public Citizen, Social Security Works, Center for Health and Democracy, MoveOn.org, Families USA, CareQuest Center for Oral Health, Justice in Aging, People’s Action, Medicare Rights Center and Advocates for Community Health.
Read the bill text for the Medicare Dental, Vision, and Hearing Benefit Act here.
title: Thompson, Doggett Partner on Bill Expanding Medicare Benefits to Cover Dental, Vision and Hearing

FAA Proposes $351,000 Fine Against Creamer Pilot Services for Alleged Unauthorized Passenger-Carrying Operations
WASHINGTON — The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) proposes a $351,000 civil penalty against Creamer Pilot Services of Fayetteville, Arkansas, for allegedly conducting unauthorized passenger-carrying operations.
The FAA alleges Creamer operated 31 passenger-carrying flights using three aircraft that were not on its Operations Specifications. These violations occurred on various dates between October 2021 and July 2022.
In addition, the FAA alleges Creamer conducted 6 passenger-carrying flights on two aircraft that were on its Operations Specifications but travelled outside the 48 contiguous United States when unauthorized to do so. These violations occurred on various dates between April 2022 and November 2022.
The FAA alleges all 37 violations were conducted by Creamer knowingly, carelessly, and recklessly.
title: FAA Proposes $351,000 Fine Against Creamer Pilot Services for Alleged Unauthorized Passenger-Carrying Operations

Connecticut House Delegation Statement on President Trump Waiving Russia Sanctions
Hartford, CT — Today, Reps. John B. Larson (CT-01), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Rosa DeLauro (CT-03), Jim Himes (CT-04), and Jahana Hayes (CT-05) responded to recent news that President Trump waived sanctions on Russia:
“Last month, we warned that the Senate’s sanctions bill left enforcement to the discretion of a President who has repeatedly demonstrated he is unwilling to stand up to Russia. He has proved us right. Less than a month after signing these sanctions into law, President Trump waived them before they could take effect.
“It did not have to be this way. The Ukraine Support Act, which passed the House in June, paired the authorization of military aid for Ukraine with sanctions that could actually be enforced. It set a higher bar for any waiver, required advance notice to Congress, and gave Congress the power to review sanctions relief for Putin. That is exactly the accountability we needed to ensure this President could not waive sanctions on a whim.
“The Senate should take up the Ukraine Support Act now, and every Republican who voted for these sanctions should join us in demanding the President enforce them. The Ukrainian people are being abandoned by President Trump – we cannot allow this to happen.”
title: Connecticut House Delegation Statement on President Trump Waiving Russia Sanctions

BOSTON – Two Brockton men were sentenced today in federal court in Boston for the Sept. 24, 2024 robbery of Energy Credit Union in West Roxbury. The defendants stole $197,146 from the Credit Union where one brother was employed as a teller.

Jenel Flounoury, 30, and Justin Flounoury, 34, were each sentenced by U.S. District Court Judge Allison D. Burroughs to four months in prison, to be followed by three years of supervised release. Both were also ordered to pay joint restitution in the amount of $197,146. The defendants were arrested by state authorities on the night following the robbery and were indicted by a federal grand jury in January 2025 . In July 2026 , they each pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit larceny from a credit union.

Jenel and Justin Flounoury conspired to stage a robbery of Energy Credit Union, where Jenel was employed as a teller. On the day of the robbery, Justin arranged to leave work early from his job in South Boston and be driven to the credit union. Cellphone location records documented Justin’s travel to the credit union and his presence during the robbery.

Upon arriving at the credit union, Justin concealed his identity by wearing a hat, dark clothing, sunglasses and a mask. Once inside, Justin approached the teller window where Jenel was working and handed his brother a note that read, “Hand it Over.” Rather than providing Justin with the limited amount of cash in his teller drawer, Jenel entered the credit union’s vault and collected nearly $200,000 in cash. Jenel then retrieved a bag from inside the vault, filled it with cash and handed it to Justin. Justin fled the credit union and returned to the residence he shared with Jenel, as corroborated by cellphone location records.

The brothers were later observed burning dark-colored clothing consistent with the clothing worn during the robbery in a grill at their residence. During a search of the residence, more than $160,000 in cash was recovered, including ten $100 bills with serial numbers matching those recorded by Energy Credit Union employees prior to the robbery.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation; Massachusetts State Police Colonel Geoffrey Noble; and Boston Police Commissioner Michael Cox made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the Suffolk County District Attorney’s Office. Assistant United States Attorneys Mark Grady and John Potapchuk of the Major Crimes Unit prosecuted the case.
title: Two Brockton Men Sentenced for Staged Credit Union Robbery

PRIORITIZING SOLUTIONS FOR WOMEN’S HEALTH: Today, President Donald J. Trump signed an Executive Order, led by First Lady Melania Trump, to strengthen research, prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care for women and girls throughout every stage of life.
- The Order establishes the White House Women’s Health Task Force to ensure the Federal Government pursues a comprehensive approach to women’s health that recognizes evolving health needs from infancy, childhood, and adolescence through pregnancy, midlife, menopause, and aging, and supports necessary policy and regulatory reforms to ensure timely and stage-specific prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care for women.
- The Order directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services and the Director of the National Institutes of Health to establish a Women’s Health Division within the National Institutes of Health to strengthen the Federal Government’s ability to coordinate research, address gaps in scientific understanding, and accelerate the translation of discoveries into better health outcomes.
- The Order rescinds the initiatives of the prior Administration in order to broaden beyond research and prioritize translating research into improved clinical care that benefits women and girls.
ENSURING AMERICAN WOMEN RECEIVE THE BEST SCIENTIFICALLY-SUPPORTED MEDICAL ADVICE IN THE WORLD: President Trump is prioritizing the health and longevity of America’s women and girls and putting research into action. American women deserve answers, and this Administration is committed to improving women’s health outcomes.
- While previous administrations have invested in women’s health research, the Trump Administration is enhancing, streamlining, and elevating Federal efforts regarding both research and its translation into health solutions.
- Despite considerable advances in biomedical science, many diseases and conditions that disproportionately or uniquely affect women have not received the level of research, clinical attention, and treatment that other diseases and conditions have received.
- More research is needed in critical aspects of women’s health, including cardiovascular and heart disease, cancer, stroke, Alzheimer’s Disease, autoimmune and inflammatory conditions, osteoporosis, mental health, chronic pain, endometriosis, fibroids, polyendocrine metabolic ovary syndrome (PMOS), infertility, maternal health, menopause, neurological disorders, aging, and more.
- Improving health outcomes for women requires coordinated Federal leadership, bolstered scientific investment, and accelerated translation of research into clinical and community practice.
DELIVERING ON PROMISES FOR AMERICAN WOMEN: President Trump and his Administration are advancing women’s health to improve health outcomes in all phases of life and ensuring they can access more affordable healthcare by lowering costs and taking on special interest that raise Americans’ healthcare costs.
- In less than two years, President Trump has begun reshaping how America eats, moves, farms, and thinks about health to address the root causes of America’s escalating health crisis. Earlier this year, the Administration launched the new Dietary Guidelines for Americans with sections for pregnant and lactating women, marking the most significant reset of federal nutrition policy in decades.
- In his historic Working Families Tax Cuts Act, President Trump expanded access to health savings accounts for up to ten million people on Obamacare, took the most significant actions to reduce healthcare fraud and abuse in history, and deployed a record $50 billion investment to improve rural healthcare.
  - 46 states have made investments in maternal health, including specific investments in telehealth and remote patient monitoring for maternal care, obstetric workforce development, and postpartum care.
- In November 2025, the Food and Drug Administration initiated the removal of broad and misleading “black box” warnings on Hormone Replacement Therapy products for menopause.
- The Trump Administration has reached 26 deals with pharmaceutical manufacturers, covering nearly 90% of the branded drug market, to get Americans the same low prices for prescription drugs that people in other countries pay. The Council of Economic Advisers estimates President Trump’s MFN deals will save Americans $600 billion prescription drugs over the next decade.
  - In February 2026, President Trump launched TrumpRx.gov, where patients can access large discounts in line with the MFN price on many of the most popular and highest-priced medicines in the country. Since its launch, patients have saved over $700 million on medicines through TrumpRx.gov.
  - TrumpRx.gov is delivering massive savings on some of the most commonly used fertility medications in the country to help families grow. Many patients struggling with infertility pay for their medicines out-of-pocket, but now they can save more than $2,000 per cycle of fertility drugs, on average.
- In May 2026, President Trump launched Moms.gov to support new and expecting mothers, bringing together information intended to help families navigate pregnancy and early parenthood.
title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump and First Lady Melania Trump Advance Women’s Health to Improve Outcomes in All Phases of Life

DAVENPORT, Iowa – A Davenport man was sentenced on October 19, 2026, to 63 months in federal prison for possessing a firearm as a felon, following three prior state convictions for possessing a firearm as a felon.

According to public court documents and evidence presented at sentencing, Juwan Albert Shorter, 38, possessed a loaded handgun in his pocket, recovered during a traffic stop. Shorter has three prior convictions for illegal possession of firearms: 2023 and 2016, in the Iowa District Court for Scott County, and 2021, in the Oklahoma District Court for Texas County.

After completing his term of imprisonment, Shorter will be required to serve a three-year term of supervised release. There is no parole in the federal system.

United States Attorney David C. Waterman of the Southern District of Iowa made the announcement. The Davenport Police Department investigated the case.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles:

rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders;

strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and

accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies.

These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. For more information about Project Safe Neighborhoods, please visit Justice.gov/PSN.
title: Davenport Man Sentenced to 63 Months in Federal Prison for Firearm Charge

text:
Gather Operations on the Pryor Mountain Horse Range Aim to Prevent Horse Suffering and Restore Healthy Range Conditions
Organization:
Media Contact:
BILLINGS, Mont. — Wild horses in the Pryor Mountain Wild Horse Range are facing growing pressure from limited forage and water, and a bait‑trap gather is set to begin on or about Oct. 19. Herd numbers have exceeded what the land can support, increasing the risk of hunger, dehydration, and injury.
The most recent population estimate in the Pryor Mountains Range is about 185 wild horses. The area can only support approximately 107 to 120 animals based on available forage and water. Current overpopulation is contributing to deteriorating upland health, riparian/wetland health, and habitat for native plants and animals, primarily because the herd size has been above what the land can support for most of the past 50 years.
The Bureau of Land Management plans to gather approximately 100 horses and remove up to 37 for placement into private care. Removed animals will receive health evaluations, vaccinations, and care at BLM facilities before they are made available for adoption or sale.
The gather will be conducted using a temporary corral containing bait and water to safely attract the animals. Once horses voluntarily enter the corral, staff secure the gate to complete the gather. Animal safety is a top priority. All BLM and contractor staff are trained in humane handling techniques specifically designed for wild horses and burros. Learn more about the BLM’s Comprehensive Animal Welfare Program.
Mares that are gathered and not being removed will be treated with fertility control before being released back to the range to help slow future herd growth.
The BLM also monitors the genetic health of the Pryor Mountain herd to ensure it stays within healthy ranges. Recent analyses show the herd’s level of genetic variety is above the minimum level BLM uses to flag potential concerns, and also above what is seen in many other wild horse herds. Independent scientists with the U.S. Geological Survey have modeled future scenarios and found that, under the current management plan, the herd is very likely to maintain acceptable genetic diversity over time. During gather operations, the BLM collects hair or DNA samples to continue tracking these trends and ensure the herd remains healthy into the future.
Because wild horses may avoid the trap site if there is too much activity, only essential personnel will be allowed near the corral. A temporary public‑access closure is in place.
Planning documents, including the environmental assessment, decision record, and finding of no significant impact, are available at the BLM National NEPA Register. Daily gather updates will be posted to 2026 Pryor Mountains Wild Horse Gather.
The Wild Free‑Roaming Horses and Burros Act of 1971 charges the BLM with managing wild horses and burros on public lands. Federal law prohibits the commercial slaughter of these animals, and the BLM does not sell or send wild horses or burros to slaughter. The agency enforces adoption and sale requirements, strengthened the bill of sale language, and works closely with law enforcement whenever credible information suggests a violation may have occurred.
This commitment to humane care is central to the BLM’s mission and guides every action we take to ensure wild horses and burros remain responsibly managed for generations to come. Learn more about the Wild Horse and Burro Program and how qualified adopters can bring home an American living legend.
The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.

Trump’s Department of Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Announces Over $1.6 Billion in Emergency Rescue Funds to Repair State Roads and Bridges Damaged by Natural Disasters Across U.S.
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy today announced over $1.6 billion in emergency relief funding to help states accelerate critical repairs to roads, bridges, and other transportation infrastructure damaged by recent natural disasters and catastrophic events. The funding will go toward repair needs in 34 states, the District of Columbia, U.S. Virgin Islands, Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Northern Mariana Islands.
States receiving aid to rebuild include:
- $873 million to North Carolina following Hurricane Helene which resulted in historic damage in Western North Carolina, causing over 9,000 damage sites and more than 1,400 road closures.
- $81 million to Hawaii for the series of Kona Low storms in March 2026 which resulted in severe flooding throughout Hawaii.
- $52 million to Texas for heavy rainfall and severe rainfall throughout the state along with multiple bridge washouts including the FM 1431 bridge that connects Lago Vista and Marble Falls.
“USDOT is working diligently to deliver dollars needed to rebuild critical transportation and infrastructure links across American communities impacted by catastrophic natural disasters. Safe roads and bridges means rescue services arrive faster, medical professionals can reach those in need, and families can get the resources they need to recover,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy.
“The Federal Highway Administration’s work with states along with local, tribal, and federal agencies in the aftermath of disaster is essential to restoring broken transportation links,” said FHWA Administrator Sean McMaster. “We provide the necessary funding to restore mobility and help people regain a sense of normalcy in their daily lives following disruption."
FHWA’s Emergency Relief Program provides funding to help states perform repairs caused by major natural disasters and extreme weather events such as flooding, landslides, and wildfires. A listing of recent Emergency Relief Program allocations with funding information can be found at the following location: Emergency Relief Program Recent Allocations.

title: Trump’s Department of Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Announces Over $1.6 Billion in Emergency Rescue Funds to Repair State Roads and Bridges Damaged by Natural Disasters Across U.S.

HOUSTON – “It’s election season, and early voting is now underway in Texas. I want to take a moment to speak directly to the public about election integrity—and about what my office is doing to ensure American citizens’ right to vote is secure.

As President Trump has said: free, fair, and honest elections—unmarred by fraud, errors, or illegality—are fundamental to a healthy constitutional Republic.

No matter how your preferred candidate fares on Election Day, every eligible voter should have his or her vote properly counted, and for that count to determine the rightful winner.

To that end, my office—which spans from Houston, down the Gulf Coast, to the Rio Grande Valley—is taking three steps.

First, I have appointed both civil and criminal District Election Officers. In conjunction with DOJ’s Civil Rights Division, these attorneys will assist and advise teams of election monitors at key polling locations to oversee compliance with federal law. They are not armed agents; they’re lawyers, and the Justice Department has been doing this for decades.

Second, I have established standard operating procedures with the Texas Secretary of State and the Texas Attorney General so that we can take up and investigate credible referrals alleging violations of federal law.

And third, I have coordinated with DHS, FBI, and the Civil Rights Division to surge legal resources where we need them most.

Now, under the U.S. Constitution, state and local officials have primary responsibility for administering elections. If you have a complaint about the administration of an election, you should take it to them first.

My role is different.

As the senior federal law-enforcement officer and lawyer for the Southern District, I stand as a backstop—not to administer elections, but to ensure that federal law is upheld.

What does that mean?

It means that only eligible voters can vote—no barred felons, no aliens, and no foreigners. American elections are for Americans only.

It means no foreign influence on our election infrastructure, in campaign finance, or at the ballot box. Foreign actors and their NGO allies are not allowed to meddle in our elections.

It means no crooked local election administrators. They have a duty to prevent illegal voting, and I’m here to make sure they do their job.

And it means no fraud. Accurate voter rolls, honest paperwork, secure ballots, and lawful procedures are essential to a fraud-free election.

Attorney General Blanche and I believe that no country can be great without fair elections. Our elections should be worthy of the highest confidence of the American people. And as U.S. Attorney for the 10 million people of the Southern District, I’m committed to making that happen.

So let me be clear: If you violate federal election law, I will hunt you down and prosecute you.

Election Day is Tuesday, November 3rd. We’ll see you out at the polls.”
title: U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz statement on election season and federal election law

Unmanned Aerial Refueler Remotely Controlled By At-Sea Aircraft Carrier Control Station
PORTFOLIO ACQUISITION EXECUTIVE AVIATION, Patuxent River, Md. (Oct. 19, 2026) – In a historic U.S. naval aviation event, an aircraft carrier connected to, and controlled, an unmanned aerial refueler MQ-25A Stingray more than 2,100 miles away.
During a Preliminary Sea Trial aboard Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS Ronald Reagan (CVN 76), the ship's Unmanned Air Warfare Center (UAWC) used its MD-5C Ground Control Station to connect Beyond Line-of-Sight with an MQ-25A test aircraft using a Proliferated Lowe Earth Orbit (pLEO) satellite network. The Stingray was located at Boeing's facility in Mascoutah, Illinois, while the ship was underway in the Pacific Ocean.
“The MQ-25A Stingray’s carrier-based refueling capabilities enable F/A-18 Super Hornets to fly farther and longer,” said the Acting Secretary of the Navy, the Honorable Hung Cao. “The integration of this unmanned aerial refueler demonstrates the transformational change our manned and unmanned asset integration provides the Fleet.”
This test was one in a series of build-up exercises designed to validate procedures, networks and interfaces. Previously, the Unmanned Carrier Aviation Program Office’s (PMA-268) Unmanned Carrier Aviation Mission Control System team conducted pier side and at-sea tests with the MQ-25 Integrated Test Team, which includes U.S. Navy, Boeing, and Lockheed Martin.
"We have redefined naval power projection," said Capt. Daniel Fucito, PMA-268’s program manager. "This first-ever underway connection between a carrier-based UAWC and an MQ-25A aircraft proves that the Carrier Air Wing of tomorrow is a reality today."
The MD-5C GCS integrates the Navy's Command, Control, Communications, Computers and Intelligence (C4I) network with Lockheed Martin's MDCX hardware and software and other government-produced equipment to provide command and control of the MQ-25A. The system will also provide command and control for the Navy's future unmanned carrier aircraft and the Air Wing of the Future.
As the world’s first fully integrated, carrier-based unmanned aerial vehicle, the MQ-25A serves as the pathfinder for the future of unmanned carrier aviation. The Stingray will provide the Carrier Air Wing with essential organic refueling, allowing more F/A-18E/F aircraft to focus on strike missions and expand the operational reach of the air wing.
title: Unmanned Aerial Refueler Remotely Controlled By At-Sea Aircraft Carrier Control Station

Remarks

Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Bakhtiyor Saidov, Uzbekistan Foreign Minister

Congress Center

Samarkand, Uzbekistan

October 19, 2026

FOREIGN MINISTER SAIDOV: Honorable Secretary of State, dear fellow ministers, ladies and gentlemen, it’s my great pleasure to welcome you to the very heart of Central Asia, to the ancient and hospitable city of Samarkand, for this historic C5+ ministerial meeting between Central Asia and the United States. With your permission, I hereby declare our meeting open. Before we begin our discussions, I would like to invite you to watch a short video highlighting the state of our partnership and the journey we have taken together. Please.

(A video was played.)

(Applause.)

FOREIGN MINISTER SAIDOV: Thank you. Dear colleagues, first of all, Mr. Secretary, it’s a distinct pleasure and honor to welcome you to Uzbekistan on your first – in the entire region – on your first visit as U.S. Secretary of State. We sincerely appreciate your personal commitment and the dedicated efforts of your team to strengthen the strategic partnership between our countries. We also highlighted the special attention that President Donald Trump has devoted to Central Asia and the growing opportunities for cooperation with our region.

In this regard, we are particularly pleased with the friendly and trust-based dialogue established between the presidents of Uzbekistan and Central Asian countries and United States, which has opened a new chapter in our relations. It is symbolic that we have gathered once again in Samarkand, where the very first C5+1 Ministerial meeting took place in 2015. Since then, our partnership has come a long way. Its agenda has expanded and its mechanisms of cooperation have grown stronger.

Yet, even more profound changes have taken place within Central Asia itself. Central Asia has grown stronger, more united, and increasingly capable of shaping its own future and contributing to international affairs. We firmly believe that a strong, stable, and prosperous Central Asia serves the interest of all our countries and our international partners. We deeply value the United States’ consistent support for the sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of our countries.

Today we have an opportunity to give the C5+ partnership a new strategic dimension. The next stage of our cooperation should focus not only on expanding bilateral ties, but also on unlocking Central Asia’s potential as an integrated region of new opportunities. This means strengthening economic connectivity, attracting advanced technologies and investment, and expanding of our access to global markets. Our partnership with the United States should complement regional cooperation and deliver lasting benefits to all our countries.

I would like to express our sincere appreciation to Turkmenistan for its productive co-chairmanship of the C5+1 Secretariat in 2025-2026. This period was marked by important developments, including high-level engagement, an investor business forum, and new initiatives in culture and emerging technologies. As Uzbekistan assumes the co-chairmanship, we intend to build on these achievements, ensure consistency, and focus on translating our agreements into practical results. As one of our key priorities, we propose advancing a strategic partnership in critical minerals from geological exploration and mineral processing to the establishment of local industrial clusters.

Honorable ministers, Central Asia has abundant resources, growing markets, human capital, and a strategically important geographic position. The United States brings advanced technologies, investment capital, and world-class entrepreneurial expertise. Our shared task is to bring these strengths together and build an enduring partnership that delivers tangible benefits to our peoples.

For centuries, Samarkand has connected peoples, markets, knowledge, and ideas. Today we have an opportunity to give this historic role a new purpose, bringing Central Asia and the United States closer together. I hope today’s meeting will mark an important step toward that future.

Distinguished colleagues, it’s now my great pleasure to invite the U.S. Secretary of State, the Honorable Marco Rubio, to deliver his opening remarks. Please.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, thank you. And thank you for hosting all of us here this week on this historic and momentous occasion. Central Asia is, in our view – I think the view of the world – it’s the heartland of both Asia and Europe. Historically, Central Asia has been the crossroads for trade between the West and the East. And today, as part of our broader renaissance in global engagement, it stands once again to play that vital role in transnational commerce.

But Central Asia also serves as a new location for investment, and it serves as a new location for export, a central terminal out of which materials that are vital for the future of all nations are being delivered. We in the United States, we seek to secure our critical industries and the supply chains that support them so that we may be a sovereign, independent country and economy, and not ever have to rely on risky foreign partners or even adversaries.

And this forum, the C5+1, represents not only America’s interest in – but America’s commitment to – fostering closer, peaceful relations with Central Asian countries. Together, we can secure for our countries the resources, the investment opportunities, and the trade partnerships we need to remain – each of us – sovereign states, and to grow together our collective prosperity.

Last year at the C5+1 in Washington, which I was honored to be a part of, was a true milestone for all of our countries. That meeting alone – that meeting alone last year at the White House – yielded $25 billion in new deals, strengthening our transportation, energy, and finance sectors, among other crucial national pillars. Together, President Trump and your respective leaders committed to fostering a regulatory and a labor landscape conducive to increasing commerce and increasing investment.

And this week we’re working to further those commitments. We’re going to enhance the infrastructure of the trans-Caspian trade route and give our partners more ways to reach American and Central Asian markets. We’re going to work to secure our energy future by driving integrated, high-value supply chains in our critical minerals dialogue. We’re going to prepare thousands of young professionals to use and support leading American technology in Central Asia’s growing tech sectors. And through the 5+1 Forum – B5+1 Forum – we will facilitate public-private dialogue that greatly increases two-way trade and investment between our countries.

This group has an opportunity to partner and radically grow our countries in ways unseen in recent history. The countries gathered here this week are all unique, sovereign, independent states with distinct cultures and distinct interests, all in charge of their own destinies. We in the United States want to see them thrive as independent states, and we want to partner with them as they do so.

We are grateful for your openness. We are extremely proud of the success this group has brought our nation so far, and we’re looking forward to the outcome – the outcomes of this week’s meetings, and all the peaceful prosperity and growth that will come from our nations working together going forward. Thank you.

FOREIGN MINISTER SAIDOV: Thank you, Mr. Secretary, for your warm remarks and strong commitment to developing a long-term partnership with Central Asia. At this point, I would like to kindly ask the members of the press to leave the room so that I may proceed our discussions.

text:
Remarks

Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Bakhtiyor Saidov, Uzbekistan Foreign Minister

Congress Center

Samarkand, Uzbekistan

October 19, 2026

FOREIGN MINISTER SAIDOV: Honorable Secretary, dear colleagues, first of all let me warmly welcome all of you into Uzbekistan. It’s a great honor for us to receive you here in Samarkand, and we attach special importance to your visit, which comes at a very significant moment in the relations between Uzbekistan and United States. Thanks to the strong political will and close personal relationship of President Mirziyoyev and President Trump, our strategic partnership has reached a new level and our political dialogue has become more active. Economic and investment cooperation is expanding, and we are also strengthening our partnership in security and regional affairs.

So we are committed to building a strong, long-term, and mutually beneficial partnership with the United States. We highly value your personal attention to Uzbekistan and Central Asia, and your contribution to advancing our relations. And I am confident that today’s meeting will help us build on this positive momentum and I invite new opportunities. Once again, Honorable Secretary, welcome to Uzbekistan, and now it is my pleasure to give the floor to you, sir.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, thank you for hosting us this week, for hosting all of us here this week for these important meetings. We view the – the United States views the relationship between Uzbekistan and Central Asia as paramount to our national security and to our economic prosperity. Under President Trump and under the respective leaders of the five countries, we’ve fostered a very strong relationship over the last 11 years that has yielded great accomplishments for our nations and tangible results for our people.

So since last November – when we had the C5+1 presidential summit – just since last November we’ve secured over $25 billion in commercial arrangements and deals between the United States and Central Asian countries, and we plan to pursue more than $100 billion more in planned trade and investment. Over the past 10 years we’ve seen the U.S. private sector become increasingly focused on opportunities presented by the rapidly growing economies of your country and of the region – build on market liberalization reform.

For example, we’re proud Uzbekistan has agreed to participate in our country’s aerospace industry and purchase 22 Boeing Dreamliners – 22 Boeing Dreamliners. At the same time, Uzbekistan is also investing in the United States. Last year AKFA Aluminum invested 80 million in an aluminum processing facility in Kentucky. It became the first Uzbek manufacturer to operate in the United States.

We signed a bilateral critical minerals MOU together, and we’re making progress in securing key supplies of uranium and other natural resources. And we’ve also created a joint Business and Investment Council to enable greater U.S. exports and business opportunities in Uzbekistan, bringing major U.S. companies like Apple and Google and PepsiCo to the region.

And these are just a few of the highlights in a long list of successful deals and commercial arrangements, and we want to build on this outstanding relationship and do more. And that, frankly, is why we’re here today. And it took weeks to plan and put this together, but at the C5+1 Ministerial we’re looking forward to putting into action the commitments we’ve made over the last year.

So we want to continue to work on aligning our regulations, on building transportation infrastructure, on using trusted advanced technology, and on growing the region’s workforce so that all American companies who want to do business here have professional partners. We want to see this region continue to thrive into the 21st century as a hub of commercial diplomacy, because it is in our interest – because it is our interest from both an economic standpoint and from a security standpoint as well.

Each country here at this ministerial is a unique, sovereign nation with its own interests. We at the Trump Administration and the President understands that and he respects that. We want – what we want to accomplish at this meeting this week will put our countries further down the path of long-term prosperity and security. We’re excited to work with you. We’re excited to work with all of our Central Asian partners to address the challenges and the opportunities of this era as we work together. So thank you.

FOREIGN MINISTER SAIDOV: Thank you very much.

12-Year Fugitive Wanted in Child Murder Cold Case Detained in Mexico
For immediate release
Mindy Miller, Deputy U.S. Marshal
PHOENIX, Ariz. - After more than 12 years as a fugitive in Mexico, Anna Marlene Somoza, 60, wanted on a charge of first-degree murder in connection with the murder of her child, was detained on October 18, 2026, in Xochitepec, Mexico by Fiscalia General de la Republica (FGR) Interpol and Secretaria de Seguridad y Proteccion Ciudadana (SSPC) agents.
On November 30, 1998, human bone fragments were discovered by a hunter in a deserted sector of Mobile, Arizona. The remains went unidentified for nearly two decades, leaving investigators with an unsolved mystery. In August 2014, forensic DNA analysis successfully matched the fragments to four-year-old Crystal Reyes, daughter of Anna Somoza and Darren Stockwell, who is a United States Citizen.
Evidence gathered by multiple law enforcement agencies over several years was reviewed by the Maricopa County Attorney’s Office leading to a grand jury indictment on December 12, 2014, charging Somoza and her boyfriend Avelino Tamala, with first-degree murder for the death of Crystal Reyes. An arrest warrant was subsequently issued, and the Phoenix Police Department requested the assistance of the U.S. Marshals Service (USMS) in locating and apprehending the couple. Later that same day, members of the USMS led Arizona WANTED Violent Offender Task Force arrested Tamala. Task Force members quickly identified leads that suggested Somoza was in Mexico, and the USMS Mexico International Liaison (MIL) team initiated collaborative investigative efforts with the USMS MFFO (Mexico Foreign Field Office).
It would take investigators another twelve years to locate and apprehend Somoza, which was affected by her close connections with cartels.
“This disturbing case can finally move forward with justice for Crystal”, stated U.S. Marshal Van Bayless for the District of Arizona, “Phoenix Police Department and Maricopa County Attorney’s Office showed their unrelenting desire to get Somoza into court and prison for her atrocities to an innocent beautiful little girl. This case became our priority with our partners, both north and south of the border who we are grateful for, and now she will be coming back and held accountable.”
“No one can hide from American justice forever”, stated U.S. Attorney Timothy Courchaine for the District of Arizona, “The United States Attorney’s office stands in partnership with both our federal and critically our state partners to ensure defendants have their day in court. We look forward to now working alongside our Mexican partners to bring this fugitive back to Arizona.”
“The Phoenix Police Department’s commitment to pursuing justice for victims is central to its mission”, stated Phoenix Police Department, “We are grateful to the U.S. Marshals Service and our law enforcement and prosecutorial partners for their assistance in apprehending this wanted suspect. With the suspect in custody, the case of Crystal Reyes can move forward. We thank everyone whose efforts made this apprehension possible.”
Long before her indictment for the murder of her daughter, Somoza had an extensive criminal history connected to a major transnational drug trafficking network active along the southern Arizona border throughout the 1980s and 1990s. Following her 1993 arrest for the sale and transportation of marijuana, she agreed to act as a confidential informant for an Arizona law enforcement agency. Over the course of her cooperation, she entered an improper romantic relationship with Avelino Tamala, a narcotics detective.
On November 25, 1993, Somoza gave birth to Crystal. Investigative reports reveal, Crystal was born in Nogales, Mexico and the birth went undocumented. Shortly after Crystal’s birth, Somoza took Crystal to live with her and Tamala in Ahwatukee, Arizona. The investigation later revealed Tamala was not the father of Crystal.
Behind closed doors, the young child was subjected to severe physical abuse, ultimately being confined to a small dog kennel. Throughout Crystal’s brutally-short-lived life, Somoza and Tamala repeatedly tortured, starved, and abused Crystal as an infant and young girl. Reports indicate that Somoza and Tamala would leave Crystal bound by her hands and feet, gagged in a small dog crate for weeks at a time. The abuse escalated fatally on January 30, 1997, when the child was bound, suffocated with a taped towel, and left to die inside a sealed cardboard box.
In 1999, Anna Somoza and Avelino Tamala were arrested on drug and weapon offenses. Following their arrest, DNA was collected and later forensic analysis of the bone fragments found in the Arizona desert could not eliminate Somoza as the maternal source. However, investigators lacked a DNA profile from Crystal’s biological father. As a result, the case went cold while Somoza served an eight-year federal prison sentence. Somoza was released from prison in 2008 and deported to Mexico.
In August 2014, Crystal’s biological father, Darren Stockwell, who at the time of Crystal’s conception was a law enforcement officer, was located and interviewed by cold case detectives.
A sample of Stockwell’s DNA was collected and analyzed, positively identifying the remains as Crystal’s. This breakthrough along with other evidence gathered throughout the investigation, provided sufficient grounds for prosecutors to charge Somoza and Tamala for the first-degree murder of Crystal in December 2014.
On November 8, 2016, Tamala was found guilty of Crystal’s murder. He was sentenced to life in prison.
Throughout the twelve-year fugitive investigation, Maricopa County Attorney's Office, Phoenix Police Department, U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration, District of Arizona U.S. Attorney’s Office, and USMS task force members from the District of Arizona, and Mexico Foreign Field Offices conducted extensive investigative efforts to locate Anna Somoza. Investigators discovered that Somoza had taken deliberate and extensive measures to evade detection by law enforcement while remaining at large.
On October 19, 2022, through the collaborative efforts of the U.S. Marshals Service, Maricopa County Attorney’s Office, and the Phoenix Police Department, obtained a Provisional Arrest Warrant authorizing the extradition of Somoza back to the United States to face her charge.
In 2026 the fugitive investigation of Somoza was designated a Major Case; dedicating additional manpower and resources to the investigation. Beginning in early September USMS task force members developed information that SOMOZA was actively evading detection in Cernavaca, Mexico.
On October 18, 2026, at approximately 1427 local time, Anna Somoza was detained in Xochitepec, Mexico by Fiscalia General de la Republica (FGR) Interpol and Secretaria de Seguridad y Proteccion Ciudadana (SSPC). Law enforcement partners will continue coordinating efforts to secure Somoza’s return to the United States to face pending charges in Arizona.
The Arizona WANTED Violent Offender Task Force is a U.S. Marshals Service led multi-jurisdictional fugitive apprehension unit responsible for more than 2324 arrests in the last year. The task force is comprised of 25 agencies bringing together the resources of federal, state and local law enforcement agencies to locate and arrest the community’s most violent offenders and sexual predators.
title: 12-Year Fugitive Wanted in Child Murder Cold Case Detained in Mexico | U.S. Marshals Service

Since the late 1950s, Pfc. James D. Price Elementary School has educated thousands of military students in grades kindergarten through fifth garde.
Located on the Howard Cantonment Area of U.S. Army Yuma Proving Ground (YPG), the school recently gained a new piece of educational equipment: a Schmidt-Cassegrain telescope with a computerized mount.
The telescope, complete with a solar filter and accessories to support astrophotography, is a gift from Scientists Taking Astronomy to Rural Schools (STARS), a program of the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Arizona’s Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory is managed by the institution, which made the state a logical pilot location for the program.
“It is taking advantage of the beautiful night skies in rural areas and using astronomy as an entry point to feeling good about science and STEM overall,” said Jason Gurtman, Community Engagement Specialist for the Smithsonian STARS Program. “We’ve seen a lot of enthusiasm from the teachers here in Yuma County and we’re really excited to be launching the program here.”
Personnel from the organization visited Price School on October 15 to help familiarize the faculty and students with the telescope kit and facilitate an astronomy activity. Divided into multiple groups, as one group of students took turns observing the sun through the solar filter, others learned about the order of planets in the solar system and crafted their own sun dial out of a paper plate and construction paper. Principal Alexandria Johnson was on hand, as was Yuma Elementary School District # 1 Governing Board Vice President David Ibarra.
“I’m so excited and happy for this opportunity,” said Brenda Findley, who teaches a combined third through fifth grade class at the school. “When the telescope came to the classroom and we were able to put it together, they couldn’t wait until today to use it.”
That evening, Findley accompanied the Smithsonian personnel to facilitate a night observation for the public at the Foothills Branch of the Yuma County Library.
“It’s really cool,” said student Elias Barrera. “I helped set up some of the telescope with my friends.”
title: STARS Align at Price Elementary: Smithsonian Gifts Computerized Telescope to Yuma Proving Ground School

PORTLAND, Maine: A Dayton man was sentenced today in U.S. District Court in Portland for being a felon in possession of a firearm.

Chief U.S. District Judge Lance E. Walker sentenced Scott Boody , 61, to 41 months in prison to be followed by three years of supervised release. Boody pleaded guilty on January 15, 2026.

According to court records, on September 10, 2025, Portland police officers found Boody slumped over the steering wheel of a vehicle stopped at a traffic light. Officers roused Boody and had him step from the vehicle and sit on the side of the road. Officers began searching the vehicle, during which Boody remained cooperative and communicative with officers. As an officer reached the vehicle’s trunk compartment, Boody briefly began to run away from the scene before officers detained him. Officers discovered a Colt .357 Magnum revolver in a bag inside the trunk. Boody is prohibited from possessing firearms as a result of a prior felony conviction.

The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives investigated the case with the assistance of the Portland Police Department.

US Department of Labor announces field assistance bulletin withdrawing 3 opinion letters on tipped employees
WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor’s Wage and Hour Division today announced the issuance of a new field assistance bulletin addressing the treatment of related duties performed by tipped employees under the Fair Labor Standards Act. Field Assistance Bulletin No. 2026-1 brings the division’s guidance on tipped employees with dual jobs into alignment with current regulations.
The bulletin withdraws the division’s 1979, 1980, and 1985 opinion letters concerning the application of dual jobs regulations to tipped employees. The withdrawal of the three opinion letters is necessary because they no longer reflect the division’s policy or interpretation of the FLSA. The bulletin also clarifies that the current dual jobs regulation focuses on whether an employee performs duties related to the employee’s tipped occupation, rather than imposing a specific percentage-based limit on the time an employee may spend performing related, non-tipped duties within that occupation.
The publication of the new bulletin follows a 2024 federal court decision that vacated the department’s 2021 dual jobs final rule. After that decision, the department removed the regulatory text adopted under the 2021 rule and reinstated the original dual jobs regulations.
The new field assistance bulletin clarifies that no current Wage and Hour Division guidance relies on the former percentage-based limit on the time a tipped employee may spend performing related, non-tipped duties, commonly known as the 80/20 rule. The division removed its 80/20 rule guidance from its Field Operations Handbook in January 2025, and the handbook is now consistent with the reinstated 1967 dual jobs regulations.
As noted in the most recent regulatory agenda, the department is developing a notice of proposed rulemaking to amend various regulations for tipped employees under the FLSA. The department welcomes public comments on the proposed rule once it is published.
Learn more about the Wage and Hour Division, including the agency’s enforcement of tip regulations under the FLSA.
title: US Department of Labor announces field assistance bulletin withdrawing 3 opinion letters on tipped employees

PITTSBURGH, Pa. - A resident of Sharon, Pennsylvania, pleaded guilty in federal court to drug trafficking and firearm charges, United States Attorney Troy Rivetti announced today.

Daequon Hasan, 27, pleaded guilty before United States District Judge William S. Stickman IV.

In connection with the guilty plea, the Court was advised that, on April 10, 2025, Hasan possessed with intent to distribute quantities of cocaine base, methamphetamine, and marijuana, and also possessed a firearm in furtherance of his drug trafficking crime.

Judge Stickman scheduled sentencing for February 25, 2027. The law provides for a total sentence of not less than five years and up to life in prison, a fine of up to $2,250,000, or both. Under the United States Sentencing Guidelines, the actual sentence imposed will be based upon the seriousness of the offenses and the prior criminal history of the defendant.

Assistant United States Attorney Craig W. Haller is prosecuting this case on behalf of the United States.

The Mercer County Drug Task Force, Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General, Federal Bureau of Investigation, and Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives conducted the investigation that led to the prosecution of Hasan.
title: Sharon Resident Pleads Guilty to Drug Trafficking and Firearm Crimes

WASHINGTON – Markus Octavious Ham, 45, a previously convicted felon residing in Maryland, was sentenced today in U.S. District Court to 30 months in federal prison in connection with his illegal possession of a loaded semiautomatic “ghost gun,” announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

Ham pleaded guilty on May 21, 2026, before Judge Amir H. Ali to one count of unlawful possession of a firearm and ammunition by a felon, while on release status for another felony conviction of 2022 Maryland Accessory After the Fact Murder Second Degree conviction. In addition to the 30-month prison term, Judge Ali ordered Ham to serve three years of supervised release. Federal prosecutors had requested a prison sentence of 63 months.

According to court documents, on Dec. 11, 2025, about 1:38 a.m., officers from the Metropolitan Police Department were on patrol when they spotted a white Ford Explorer with Virginia plates stopped on the curb facing northbound in the southbound lane.

An officer approached the vehicle from the passenger’s side. and saw Ham behind the wheel in a deep state of sleep. Officers then approached the driver’s side and noticed a handgun between Ham’s legs. Officers called for additional units to assist.

When more officers arrived, they approached the vehicle and saw that Ham was still asleep. An officer reached into the vehicle and retrieved the pistol from between Ham’s legs. Once the gun was secured, officers opened the door and put Ham in handcuffs.

The firearm was identified as a semi-automatic Polymer 80 pistol loaded with one round of live ammunition in the chamber and 14 rounds of live ammunition inside the magazine that had a capacity for 15 rounds. Officers searched the Ford Explorer and recovered 11 additional bullets from the center console between the driver and passenger seats.

Ham’s previous offenses include a 2002 conviction for aggravated assault, a 2013 conviction for unlawful possession of a firearm, a 2019 conviction for attempted possession with intent to distribute PCP, a 2020 conviction for illegal firearm possession, and a 2022 Maryland conviction for Accessory After the Fact Murder Second Degree conviction. Because of his status as an adjudicated felon, Ham was prohibited from possessing any firearm.

This case was investigated by the Metropolitan Police Department with the valuable assistance of the Bureau of Alcohol Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives – Washington Field Office.

The matter was prosecuted under the Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful Initiative by Assistant U.S. Attorney Emory V. Cole. Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful is a law enforcement initiative in support of President Trump's Executive Order to crack down on gun violence, prioritize federal firearms violations, pursue tougher penalties, and seek detention for federal firearms violators.

HUNTINGTON, W.Va. – Ian Wyatt Justice, 25, of Huntington, was sentenced today to four years and three months in prison, to be followed by three years of supervised release, for possession with intent to distribute a quantity of fentanyl and violating supervised release.

According to court documents and statements made in court, on April 1, 2026, law enforcement officers conducted a traffic stop of a vehicle driven by Justice in Huntington. Officers arrested Justice on an active warrant during the traffic stop and seized approximately 51.13 grams of fentanyl from his person. As part of his guilty plea, Justice admitted that he possessed the seized fentanyl and intended to distribute it.

Justice further admitted that he intended to distribute approximately 15.2 grams of fentanyl and 24.2 grams of cocaine base, also known as “crack,” seized by officers during a December 4, 2025, traffic stop of a vehicle he was driving in Huntington.

At the time of these incidents, Justice was serving a term of supervised release following his conviction for possession with intent to distribute 40 grams or more of fentanyl in United States District Court for the Southern District of West Virginia on March 7, 2022. Today’s sentence includes one year and three months in prison for violating the term of supervised release.

United States Attorney Moore Capito made the announcement and commended the investigative work of the Huntington Violent Crime and Drug Task Force and the Huntington Police Department.

United States District Judge Robert C. Chambers imposed the sentence. Assistant United States Attorney Joseph F. Adams prosecuted the case.

A copy of this press release is located on the website of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of West Virginia. Related court documents and information can be found on PACER by searching for Case No. 3:26-cr-56.

title: Huntington Man Sentenced to Prison for Fentanyl Crime and Violating Supervised Release

VANCOUVER, WA – Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez (WA-03) issued the following statement on the President’s decision to sign an Executive Order yesterday waiving the sanctions on the sale of Russian oil Congress passed in the bipartisan Lindsay O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026:
“The President’s decision to issue a waiver of the recently passed Russia sanctions package is a betrayal of our ally Ukraine, the overwhelming will of Congress, and the national interests of the American people.
If Trump were serious about bringing down prices at the pump, he would end this disaster in Iran. And using American tax dollars to fund Russia through his proposed oil purchase is a shameful farce.
I am already working with a group of bipartisan members to introduce legislation that will block the President’s ill-conceived plan to purchase Russian oil. Congress must now also take steps to ensure that the sanctions we voted for and the President signed into law are fully executed and implemented.
Instead of continuing to aid and abet Putin’s fascist aggression, the President should do everything in his power to support our ally Ukraine. He should fully implement the sanctions package and reverse course on his plan to buy Russian oil.
The administration also needs to do everything in their power to immediately force the reversal of the Starlink throttle. I’m hearing directly from my constituents that their grandparents are being maimed getting water from a well in the middle of the Donbas. In the next Congress, there will be significant consequences for those responsible for facilitating Putin’s crimes.”

PORTLAND, Maine: A Sanford woman was sentenced today in U.S. District Court in Portland for theft of government money.

U.S. District Judge John A. Woodcock, Jr., sentenced Cori Godin , 47, to 18 months in prison, to be followed by three years of supervised release. Godin was also ordered to pay $37,105 in restitution. Godin pleaded guilty on November 18, 2025.

According to court records, Godin falsely claimed to be unemployed in order to receive unemployment insurance benefits, including federally funded benefits intended to address the COVID-19 pandemic. Unemployment insurance is a joint state and federal program that provides monetary benefits to eligible beneficiaries. Payments are intended to provide temporary financial assistance to lawful workers who are unemployed through no fault of their own. Beginning in about March 2020, in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, several federal programs expanded unemployment insurance eligibility and benefits. For a period of approximately 13 months in 2020 and 2021, Godin falsely claimed to be unemployed and received approximately $37,105 in benefits.

The U.S. Department of Homeland Security Office of Inspector General investigated the case.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

###
title: Sanford Woman Sentenced for Theft of Government Money
