The Department of War announced today the successful completion of its initial research security audits of 30 universities. All 30 universities have fully mitigated identified relationships with foreign entities of concern included on the most recent NDAA Section 1286 list, published in July 2026. Overall, the audits resulted in more than 80 termination-related actions across the 30 universities. These actions included the termination of relationships with entities on the NDAA Section 1286 list, as well as precautionary terminations involving entities not specifically identified on the list.
While the Department worked collaboratively with all 30 universities, several went above and beyond by quickly terminating problematic relationships with entities on the NDAA Section 1286 list and implementing significant mitigation measures to safeguard research. These institutions include:
Oklahoma State University
The Pennsylvania State University
University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
University of South Carolina
University of Southern California
University of Texas at Austin
Virginia Tech
"These academic institutions that went above and beyond deserve immense credit for setting the benchmark in domestic research security," said Joseph Jewell, Assistant Secretary of War for Science and Technology. "Rather than settling for minimum compliance, these institutions took bold, self-initiated steps to protect their labs, faculty, and intellectual property from foreign exploitation. Their proactive commitment ensures that groundbreaking research directly empowers the American warfighter and strengthens our Nation's technological edge."
The Department will continue to update the NDAA Section 1286 list, as appropriate, and assess universities that retain problematic relationships with entities on the list.
"I am proud that the Department of War went 30-for-30 in working with these top-tier research universities to terminate relationships with malign foreign entities. The Department commends the institutions that took decisive action to mitigate relationships that could expose American research to foreign exploitation," said Emil Michael, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering. "Our work will continue. Institutions that fail to meet research security standards are on notice: taxpayer dollars will not support institutions whose partnerships put the American warfighter or the Nation’s technological advantage at risk."
The Department will continue this effort alongside partners in Congress, specifically the House and Senate Armed Services Committees, the House and Senate Appropriations Committees, and the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party.

FORT BENNING, Ga. — Leaders and planners from the Maneuver Center of Excellence and Fort Benning met with representatives from the Office of the Assistant Secretary of the Army for Installations, Energy & Environment (ASA (IE&E)), Radiant Industries Inc., and key installation energy stakeholders during the initial Janus Program site visit, Oct. 16, 2026.
As a designated Janus Program host installation, Fort Benning is scheduled to receive three next‑generation nuclear microreactors. Radiant will provide, install, operate and maintain the systems, which will deliver resilient, independent power to selected mission‑critical facilities in the event of a commercial grid outage.
“To project power globally, we must ensure our critical infrastructure — especially Lawson Army Airfield and our mission command centers — remains fully operational under any circumstances. Uninterrupted, resilient energy is the lifeblood of our flight line and deployment operations,” said Maj. Gen. Colin P. Tuley, commanding general of the MCoE and Fort Benning. “This initial site visit is about setting the conditions to successfully receive and integrate this advanced power technology, protecting our operations from commercial grid vulnerabilities.”
The visit opened with an installation briefing outlining Fort Benning’s mission, vision, and current energy posture. The session grounded planning discussions on the Janus Program’s strategic goals, the Army’s broader microreactor initiative, and efforts to enhance energy resilience across military installations.
“This kickoff meeting brings together all the partners responsible for delivering micro‑nuclear power to Fort Benning,” said Dr. Ed Locke, master planner for the Directorate of Public Works and the installation’s Janus Project lead. “It’s our first opportunity to collaborate face‑to‑face with our long‑term partners.”
Radiant Industries provided an overview of its company background and capabilities, leading into technical workshops focused on integrating its Kaleidos microreactors with Fort Benning’s existing power grid.
“Radiant is proud to partner with the Fort Benning team to deliver the Department of War’s first operational nuclear microreactor,” said retired Rear Adm. Mark B. Sucato, U.S. Navy, Radiant’s director of national security business development. “Seeing how prepared and energized our Fort Benning partners are, was invigorating. We look forward to achieving Initial Operational Capability together.”
Stakeholders also reviewed administrative, regulatory, and security requirements supporting the program. Representatives from DPW; the Directorate of Plans, Training, Mobilization and Security; the Provost Marshal’s Office; and Installation Safety collaborated on emergency response integration, physical security planning, and safety protocols. The groups also discussed cultural resource considerations and environmental compliance under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA).
Local utility providers, the installation’s commercial power company, and scientific and technical defense consultants contributed to site‑selection discussions and infrastructure mapping.
The visit concluded with a physical assessment of one potential location for the microreactors. Although the site currently stands as the preferred option, final approval depends on cultural resource and environmental survey results.
“Today’s collaborative site survey marks a significant step forward for the Janus Program,” Locke said. “Our immediate priority is completing the required environmental and cultural resource surveys to secure final site approval. Every milestone brings us closer to strengthening Fort Benning’s energy resilience and ensuring our ability to project power without fail.”
With host installations like Fort Benning paired with vendors such as Radiant and planning underway, the Army is advancing toward its goal of having the first microreactors operational by 2028.
title: Fort Benning hosts Janus Program partners, surveys potential nuclear microreactor site

text:
ICYMI: Liccardo Moves to Force Vote on Protections for Afghan Refugees
SAN JOSÉ, CA— Today, The Mercury News reported on Congressman Sam Liccardo’s plans to bypass Republican House leadership and force a vote on his bipartisan Afghanistan TPS Act. The legislation would restore Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for more than 8,000 Afghans at risk of deportation after the Trump administration ended their protections last year. Liccardo plans to file the discharge petition when Congress returns on November 9.
Read the full story below:
By Grace Hase Published October 19, 2026
Silicon Valley Rep. Sam Liccardo’s bill to make Afghan immigrants once again eligible for temporary protected status has gone nowhere since it was introduced this summer, leaving more than 8,000 refugees nationally at risk for deportation. Now, the first-term congressmember plans to leverage an obscure procedural rule to advance the legislation.
Liccardo, who co-authored the “Afghanistan TPS Act of 2026” with Reps. Jason Crow, D-Colo., Don Bacon, R-Neb., and Maria Salazar, R-Fla., told the Bay Area News Group that he plans to file a discharge petition when Congress returns from recess on Nov. 9. The bill would offer Afghan refugees a shield from deportation as their immigration cases move forward, a status they held previously until the Trump administration ended the protection in 2025.
The legislative mechanism is a way for congressmembers to buck House leadership, which controls what bills proceed out of committee. If a discharge petition receives at least 218 signatures, it will force a vote on the bill.
Long considered a seldom-used tool with very little success, discharge petitions are finding new utility in the Trump era as House Speaker Mike Johnson holds a razor-thin majority that’s at risk in the upcoming midterm election.
Donna Crane, a lecturer in San Jose State University’s Department of Political Science, said that Republicans, who are facing dire reelection prospects, have used discharge petitions this year as a way to distance themselves from President Donald Trump. But for the minority party, she said, it’s also been an incredibly powerful instrument.
“This can be pretty much the only way of getting any control over the House floor schedule because the majority controls the entire schedule,” she said. “If you can hold your own group together and pick a few members off from the other side, then your bill is going to go to the floor.”
Reps. Ro Khanna, D-Santa Clara, and Thomas Massie, R-Kentucky, famously used a discharge petition last year to bypass House leadership in their quest to pry loose investigative records related to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
The discharge petition could mark a critical step in Liccardo’s efforts to reinstate TPS for Afghan nationals. The Trump administration has halted protections for immigrants from 13 countries as it looks to dismantle the program, which guards from deportation individuals who can’t safely return to their homes due to ongoing conflict or other disasters.
The Biden administration granted TPS to eligible Afghans in 2022 after the United States ended its military presence in the country the year prior.
“Regardless of political differences, we ought to be able to agree on the critical importance of keeping our promises as a country,” Liccardo said about his bill. “America promised thousands of Afghans who risked their lives as interpreters, as informants, as other support roles to our military; they risked their lives with the expectation that we would not betray them and put them in harm’s way for doing so.”
Joseph Azam, a Berkeley resident and the board chair of the Afghan-American Foundation, said that the end of TPS for Afghan nationals has “shaken people’s belief that protecting this population is a bipartisan priority.”
The decision, along with other moves by the Trump administration to ban Afghans from entering the U.S., has sent shockwaves throughout the Bay Area — especially in Fremont, which is home to one of the largest concentrations of Afghan immigrants in the country.
Azam said that it’s been “frustrating” to see Liccardo’s bill stall and applauded his plans to file a discharge petition.
“I think people who care about this population and care about the integrity of America’s word should use every tool in their toolbox,” he said. “Once it’s opened, I think that’s when the real pressure can start. Members of Congress need to step up and be counted on this issue, and they’ve gotten a pass for a while now, particularly under this new administration. I’m looking forward to people being held accountable and having to be on the record on where they stand.”
Whether Liccardo and his co-sponsors have enough signatures remains to be seen; however, the congressman said that having “five Republican co-sponsors is certainly a very strong indication.” There are 214 Democrats serving in the House of Representatives.
The success of a discharge petition filed earlier this year to force a vote on a bill that would extend TPS for Haitian immigrants could also be another positive indicator for Liccardo’s bill — four Republican congressmembers signed the discharge petition alongside Democrats, to reach the 218 threshold.
A spokesperson for Johnson did not respond to a request to comment about the discharge petition, but told reporters last year that “I am not a fan of discharge petitions. It is typically used as a tool against the majority.”
Regardless of who wins control of the House on Nov. 3, Liccardo said that Republicans up for reelection might be more emboldened to sign on.
“After Election Day,” he said, “I’d like to believe we’re going to have a lot more interest from a lot of those Republicans, particularly a lot of the veterans who served in Afghanistan, who understand what a betrayal this has been to essentially abandon our promise to protect Afghans who risked their lives alongside U.S. troops.”
title: ICYMI: Liccardo Moves to Force Vote on Protections for Afghan Refugees

WASHINGTON – On Friday, United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) Commissioner Rodney Scott toured a cargo processing facility in Arizona, seeing firsthand how CBP keeps harmful contraband from entering the United States.
At the cargo inspection facility at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport, CBP personnel inspect imported goods for illegal drugs, fraudulent labeling, and other national security threats. Among the items that were seen during the visit were baseball jerseys that were labeled as being manufactured in Mexico, but were actually manufactured in China.
“The hardworking men and women of CBP look at almost every package that comes in, so that dangerous drugs, counterfeit products, and other harmful contraband does not come into our country,” said Secretary Mullin. “The patriots at CBP understand these criminals’ patterns, how the traffickers and cartels try to get around the duties and customs, and the way they try to ship things into our country. That’s why experience matters.”
Secretary Mullin and CBP Commissioner Rodney Scott (right) tour a CBP cargo inspection facility at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport
Secretary Mullin meets with CBP personnel in Phoenix, Arizona
On Friday, Secretary Mullin also oversaw several deportation flights out of Arizona, removing illegal aliens back to Mexico. Among those deported on Friday were pedophiles, violent assailants, drug traffickers, drunk drivers, burglars, and gang members.
# # #
title: Secretary Mullin and CBP Commissioner Rodney Scott Visit CBP Cargo Processing Facility in Arizona

New Haven, CT — Today, U.S. Representatives John Larson (CT-01), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Rosa DeLauro (CT-03), Jim Himes (CT-04), and Jahana Hayes (CT-05) responded to recent news that President Trump waived sanctions on Russia:
“Last month, we warned that the Senate’s sanctions bill left enforcement to the discretion of a President who has repeatedly demonstrated he is unwilling to stand up to Russia. He has proved us right. Less than a month after signing these sanctions into law, President Trump waived them before they could take effect.
“It did not have to be this way. The Ukraine Support Act, which passed the House in June, paired the authorization of military aid for Ukraine with sanctions that could actually be enforced. It set a higher bar for any waiver, required advance notice to Congress, and gave Congress the power to review sanctions relief for Putin. That is exactly the accountability we needed to ensure this President could not waive sanctions on a whim.
“The Senate should take up the Ukraine Support Act now, and every Republican who voted for these sanctions should join us in demanding the President enforce them. The Ukrainian people are being abandoned by President Trump – we cannot allow this to happen.”
title: Connecticut House Delegation Statement on President Trump Waiving Russia Sanctions

Justice Department Announces Settlement Ending Antisemitism and Race Discrimination at UNC
This week the U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division and the U.S. Department of Education, Office for Civil Rights (ED-OCR) entered a voluntary university-wide settlement agreement with the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (UNC) to end antisemitism and race discrimination. The settlement agreement resolves investigations conducted by the Civil Rights Division and ED-OCR under Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which prohibits discrimination based on race, color, or national origin (protected characteristics).
“Title VI requires that all students — regardless of their ancestry or race — receive equal treatment under the law at federally funded colleges and universities,” said Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. “Higher ed policies and practices that tolerate antisemitism or favor certain racial groups over others, frustrate our color-blind justice system. The Civil Rights Division commends UNC for its cooperation in meeting its obligations under federal law without the need for litigation; we hope other institutions will take note and do the same.”
“Today’s agreement with the University of North Carolina Chapel Hill is an important step in upholding civil rights laws and restoring the American people’s confidence in higher education,” said Assistant Secretary Kimberly Richey of the Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights. “The Trump Administration is holding schools accountable for antisemitism at American universities and ensuring that institutions, which have no problem accessing generous taxpayer support, follow all federal laws and ensure safe learning environments. Because of today’s agreement with UNC, aspiring students will be assessed based solely on their merit — not race — and Jewish students can thrive without the threat of antisemitic discrimination.”
Under the settlement agreement — which applies to all undergraduate, graduate, professional, and other schools, components, and programs — UNC will take several steps in key areas:
- Antisemitism: UNC shall maintain policies aimed at prohibiting, preventing, and disciplining unlawful antisemitism, which includes establishing a Title VI Coordinator position, ensuring Jewish and Israeli students are covered by UNC’s Non-Discrimination Policy, promptly assess and investigate antisemitism complaints, provide mandatory antisemitism training to all students, faculty, and staff, deploy additional law enforcement resources when events or other factors warrant to protect Jewish and Israeli students, and prohibit face masks that conceal an individual’s identity. UNC will also discipline and sanction student groups for antisemitic discriminatory conduct.
- Admissions practices: UNC shall adopt and maintain a color-blind admissions system, which includes refraining from using race, analyzing racial data, altering its admissions process to change the racial composition of its student body, and disfavoring applicants who decline to identify their race. UNC shall not use race in selecting admissions personnel. And UNC may not partner with “bridge” or “pipeline” programs that consider any protected characteristic.
- Educational operations: Consistent with the U.S. Supreme Court’s 2023 decision in Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard, UNC shall adopt and maintain wholly race-blind policies regarding student benefits, scholarships, financial aid, and programming. Further, scholarship criteria will not include diversity or identification with any protected characteristic.
The settlement agreement also includes monitoring and reporting provisions. Within 30 days, UNC will select a “Merit & Civil Rights Administrator” who will be responsible for implementing the settlement agreement. And on a quarterly basis, UNC will send any antisemitism and race discrimination complaints it has received to ED-OCR and the Civil Rights Division. The settlement agreement will be in effect until Dec. 31, 2028.
Because of UNC’s cooperation, UNC will remain eligible for federal funding. In addition, ED-OCR will close 18 active investigations into UNC. And the Civil Rights Division will also close its 18-month compliance review, which was opened on April 18, 2025.
As recipients of federal financial assistance, colleges and universities are subject to federal non-discrimination laws. The Civil Rights Division will continue to investigate their compliance with Title VI.
NOTE: Read the Settlement Agreement here.
Members of the public may report possible civil rights violations at www.civilrights.justice.gov/.
title: Justice Department Announces Settlement Ending Antisemitism and Race Discrimination at UNC

The Department of War announced today that it has reached a framework agreement with BAE Systems to ramp up production of the combat-proven Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS). The multi-year agreement outlines the procurement of up to 25,000 APKWS guidance sections annually for up to seven years, pending congressional authorization and appropriations.
"The Arsenal of Freedom exists for one purpose: to guarantee our warfighters decisive advantage on the battlefield," said Michael P. Duffey, Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment. "By securing multi-year demand, this agreement keeps production lines running at capacity, provides our forces with interceptor inventory, and flips the cost calculus in the taxpayer's favor."
The agreement locks production over previous contracts, establishing the sustained demand signal BAE Systems needs to procure long-lead items and expand its skilled workforce. APKWS delivers a combat-proven, high-lethality interceptor while countering widespread aerial threats.
Beyond the baseline of 25,000 units per year, the framework establishes an actionable pathway to surge output up to 35,000 units annually for international allies. This industrial expansion will be unlocked as partner nations formalize orders via Foreign Military Sales Letters of Request.
By leveraging allied demand to capitalize new domestic production lines, the Department strengthens the nation's industrial base. Each active line directly expands sovereign U.S. surge capacity, preserving warm, high-rate manufacturing infrastructure ready to respond on short notice.
The agreement was finalized in partnership across the U.S. Army, Navy, Air Force, and Marine Corps.
title: Department of War and BAE Systems Sign Framework Agreement to Surge Counter-Drone Production to 25,000 Precision Interceptors Annually

CHICAGO – A former employee of a State of Illinois subcontractor has been indicted on federal fraud charges for allegedly fraudulently obtaining more than $4.6 million in Covid-era unemployment insurance benefits for herself and hundreds of others.

ANDREA WELLINGTON engaged in fraud related to the Pandemic Unemployment Assistance (“PUA”) program, one of the sources of relief under the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (“CARES”) Act, according to an indictment returned in U.S. District Court in Chicago. Wellington worked as a customer service representative for a company that subcontracted with the Illinois Department of Employment Security (“IDES”). The position gave her access to the IDES PUA system, the indictment states. IDES determined the amount of each payment to be issued to PUA claimants based, in part, on the amount of income that the claimant had earned prior to the filing of their claim for PUA benefits. The more wages reported, the greater the amount of the PUA payment.

The charges allege that in the fall of 2021, after Wellington had been terminated from her position with the IDES subcontractor, she and co-defendant RANDALL EASLEY accessed the IDES PUA system and fraudulently increased the wage histories of hundreds of PUA applicants, causing IDES to disburse approximately $4,680,582 in PUA payments to which the recipients were not entitled. The indictment alleges that Wellington and Easley modified the wage histories in exchange for thousands of dollars from the applicants.

Wellington, 35, of Chicago, is charged with 21 counts of wire fraud, while Easley, 38, of Chicago, is charged with 14 counts of wire fraud. Wellington and Easley were arraigned in federal court on Oct. 8, 2026, and pleaded not guilty to the charges. A status hearing was set for Oct. 23, 2026, at 10:00 a.m., before U.S. District Judge Elaine E. Bucklo.

The indictment was announced by Andrew S. Boutros, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois; Anthony P. D’Esposito, Inspector General, U.S. Department of Labor; Ryan Whalen, Special Agent-in-Charge of the Chicago Field Office of the FBI; and Nicholas Bucciarelli, Inspector-in-Charge of the Chicago Division of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service. The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorney Meredith Havekost.

Each count of wire fraud is punishable by up to 20 years in federal prison. The public is reminded that an indictment contains only charges and is not evidence of guilt. The defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.

Consistent with the Administration’s priorities to identify, investigate, and prosecute criminal fraud in the federal government entitlement and benefit programs, the United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Illinois is taking a fresh look at Covid-19 fraud.

On April 7, 2026, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division. The core mission of the Fraud Division is to zealously investigate and prosecute those who steal or fraudulently misuse taxpayer dollars. Department of Justice efforts to combat fraud support President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Former Employee of State of Illinois Subcontractor Indicted for Allegedly Fraudulently Obtaining More Than $4.6 Million in Covid-Relief Benefits

DEA Hosts the 31st National Prescription Drug Take Back Day on Saturday, October 24th
SAN FRANCISCO – The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration, in collaboration with more than 4,300 law enforcement partners, will host the 31st National Prescription Drug Take Back Day from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. on Saturday, October 24.
More than 4,400 collection sites will be set up across the country to dispose of unneeded, expired, and unused prescription medications- including over 67 drop off locations throughout the San Francisco region. This is a simple step that prevents diversion, reduces the risk of accidental poisoning, and helps protect communities.
“Since 2010, Take Back Day has helped Americans remove more than twenty million pounds of unneeded medications from their homes,” said DEA Administrator Terry Cole. “By participating in Take Back Day, you are preventing potentially addictive medications from falling into the wrong hands – a small step that can save lives. I am grateful to the thousands of law enforcement and community partners who make these events possible, and I urge everyone to take a few minutes on Saturday, October 24, to clean out your medicine cabinets.”
“Unused or expired prescription drugs sitting in our home medicine cabinets present a real threat to our families and communities across our region,” said Special Agent in Charge Bob P. Beris of the DEA San Francisco Field Division. “National Prescription Drug Take Back Day offers a free, safe, and convenient way to properly dispose of these medications before they can be misused or accidentally ingested.”
What will be collected
- Tablets, capsules, patches, and other forms of prescription medications
- Liquid medications securely sealed in their original containers
What won’t be collected
- Syringes, sharps, and illicit drugs
Why it matters
- Prescription opioids, such as oxycodone, hydrocodone, codeine, and morphine, are among the most frequently misused prescription pain medications, according to the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA).
- Removing unneeded medications from the home reduces the risk of misuse or accidental ingestion.
Visit DEATakeBack.com to find a registered Take Back location near you. If you are unable to participate in this fall’s National Prescription Drug Take Back Day, there are more than 15,300 pharmacies, hospitals, and businesses that offer safe medication disposal year-round. In addition, many police departments also provide permanent drop boxes to ensure Every Day is Take Back Day.
title: DEA Hosts the 31st National Prescription Drug Take Back Day on Saturday, October 24th

text:
State Proposals to Change Daylight Saving Time Observance
Daylight saving time (DST) is a period of the year between spring and fall when clocks in most parts of the United States are set one hour ahead of standard time (ST). The United States first adopted DST in 1918. DST begins on the second Sunday in March and ends on the first Sunday in November. The beginning and end dates are set in statute (15 U.S.C. §260a).
Congressional interest in the potential benefits and costs of DST has resulted in changes to DST observance (including changes to its start and end dates, periods of temporary year-round DST, and periods of no federal DST observance). Though the authority to change DST observance rests solely with Congress, since 2015, a majority of states have had legislation introduced to change the observance of DST—seeking to establish either DST or ST year round. State-enacted permanent DST would go into effect if and when such action is allowed by Congress.
Forty-seven states and DC have had legislation introduced proposing some variation of permanent year-round DST.
* Introduced permanent DST
* Enacted permanent DST (19 states)
* Adopted nonbinding resolution in support of permanent DST
* No DST legislation introduced
Forty-two states have had legislation introduced to establish permanent year-round ST. The Uniform Time Act of 1966 as amended (15 U.S.C. §§260-267) allows states to exempt themselves from observing DST.
* Introduced permanent ST
* No ST legislation introduced
* Observes permanent ST
Sources: State legislation information from Lexis Advance "Statutes and Legislation" database; state legislature websites/databases; National Council of State Legislature's Daylight Saving Time | State Legislation resource; CQ.com's Policy Note database.
Notes: American Samoa, most of Arizona, Guam, Hawaii, the Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands do not observe DST. CRS identified introduced legislation from January 2015 to August 2026 that would amend time observance; in this search, CRS did not identify any introduced legislation for the U.S. territories that would amend time observance.
For more information, see CRS Report R45208, Daylight Saving Time (DST).
Information as of October 19, 2026. Prepared by Corrie E. Clark, Specialist in Energy Policy; Lynn J. Cunningham, Senior Research Librarian; Cassandra E. Higgins, Geospatial Information Systems Analyst; and Amber Wilhelm, Visual Information Specialist.
title: State Proposals to Change Daylight Saving Time Observance

Peters Leads San Diego Delegation in Demanding Explanation for ICE Surge at Schools and Other Sensitive Locations
October 19, 2026 
“These are places where people turn for help, and enforcement practices that discourage access leave entire communities less safe.”
San Diego, CA. — Today, U.S. Representative Scott Peters (CA-50) led members of the San Diego Congressional delegation, Reps Juan Vargas (CA-52), Sara Jacobs (CA-51), and Mike Levin (CA-49), and U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA) and Adam Schiff (D-CA) in a letter to U.S. Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Markwayne Mullin on recent reports of increased immigration enforcement activity in San Diego and elsewhere in California. This comes a month after San Diego Unified School District (SDUSD) and San Diego City College both informed the Congressman's office of multiple U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrests outside their schools.
The Members cited more frequent reports and videos online of a growing presence of agents detaining individuals throughout San Diego. They stated that these practices are actually more harmful, as the “presence of ICE officers destabilizes the sense of safety schools offer and places an additional burden on school staff and local communities.”
The Members added that the “fear among students and families that these incidents cause can also negatively impact a student’s educational engagement, mental and physical health, academic performance, and developmental trajectories. Parents should be able to bring their children to class and return to pick them up without fearing that a routine school day could end in family separation. Teachers should be able to focus on teaching and students on learning.”
They also outlined how federal agents have been noted at other sensitive locations, such as hospitals, places of worship, and courthouses, which threatens the very safety these places are supposed to offer.
“When people are afraid to seek medical care, attend religious services, or appear in court, the consequences reach well beyond any individual arrest. These are places where people turn for help, and enforcement practices that discourage access leave entire communities less safe,” the Members added.
To address their concerns, the members demanded a response to the following questions;
- Has DHS authorized an “Operation Safe California” or similar immigration enforcement operation for California? If so, what is the scope of the operation? Who authorized it? And when was it authorized?
- Has DHS authorized enhanced immigration enforcement in San Diego, and, if so, how long is it expected to last? How many agents are involved?
- Who are the intended targets, and what criteria govern whom officers or agents stop or detain?
- Have officers or agents been directed or authorized to conduct enforcement at or near schools or other sensitive locations?
“San Diegans deserve a clear explanation of the federal activity being reported in our communities,” the Members concluded.
Background: As unregulated ICE activity has heavily increased throughout the second Trump Administration, Rep. Peters has called out DHS for allowing federal agents to terrorize communities without notice or consequences, leaving communities less safe. 
Shortly after the arrests at San Diego schools, Rep. Peters hosted a virtual training event with Rep. Juan Vargas (CA-52) to ensure community members understand how to safely interact with federal law enforcement officers, what to do if they or their loved ones are detained by agents, and what resources are available to San Diego’s immigrant community.
And last year, Rep. Peters led the Stop Excessive Force in Immigration Act,  which would establish stronger standards for immigration agents' use of force. The bill would also restrict the use of crowd munitions like tear gas and create greater transparency in enforcement by requiring the use of body cameras and strictly limiting the use of masks. Rep. Peters has pushed Republicans to pass these commonsense reforms, but they have continued to block this bill from a vote.
###
title: Peters Leads San Diego Delegation in Demanding Explanation for ICE Surge at Schools and Other Sensitive Locations

Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Announces New Mexico’s First Advanced Air Mobility Demonstration Flight Under eVTOL Integration Program
WASHINGTON — U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy announced New Mexico’s first demonstration flight under the USDOT’s Electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing (eVTOL) Integration Pilot Program (eIPP). Led by the City of Albuquerque Aviation Department, New Mexico is the sixth location to launch under the Department’s initiative, following North Carolina in late September.
Under Secretary Duffy, the USDOT has created one of the nation’s largest real-world environments for testing eVTOLs, autonomous planes, and drone technology.
The first-of-its-kind initiative has the potential to create jobs, connect communities, and strengthen American leadership in aviation. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) may use data from the pilot projects to develop new regulations that safely enable this futuristic technology at scale.
“Thanks to the vision of President Trump, these test flights are bringing the future of flight to the entire world, not just the United States.” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “Modern aviation started in America with the Wright Brothers first flight and we’re continuing to bring innovation in aviation with these new-generation aircraft.”
Last week, the City of Albuquerque Aviation Department and Reliable Robotics conducted a hybrid-electric demonstration flight at Albuquerque International Sunport to test cargo deliveries using Reliable’ s remotely piloted Cessna 208B Caravan airplane.
“These demonstrations in Albuquerque help ensure we’re getting things done safely and efficiently.” said FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford. “Every test flight provides critical data to help build a system that strengthens our nation’s infrastructure and connect communities.”
“Our city has always been a place where big ideas take flight, and we want to be a city that says yes to new technology and new opportunities,” said Mayor Tim Keller. “By putting the Sunport to work as a testing ground for the future of aviation, we’re helping bring new industries to New Mexico, strengthen our regional economy, and show what’s possible when we embrace innovation.”
“Our partnership with Reliable Robotics reflects the kind of collaboration we embrace at the Sunport—working with aviation innovators and the FAA to help shape the future of flight. It is an honor to be one of just eight designees nationwide participating in the FAA’s eIPP,” said Manny Manriquez, director of aviation for the City of Albuquerque. “With a focus on advancing autonomous aircraft operations, we take seriously our responsibility to help inform the safe integration of these emerging technologies into the National Airspace System by providing the data and insights the FAA needs to develop appropriate policies and requirements for this evolving industry”
“Reliable’s work with the FAA and the City of Albuquerque is building the roadmap for integrating autonomy into high-density airspaces, clearing a major hurdle toward commercial operations,” said Robert Rose, CEO and co-founder, Reliable Robotics. “We’re excited by this significant milestone, and to show how autonomy can both benefit national competitiveness and bring value to everyday Americans."
The City of Albuquerque Aviation Department and other eIPP participants are planning additional test flights throughout the rest of the year.
Additional Information:
In March, Secretary Duffy unveiled the eIPP program to begin testing advanced air mobility vehicles and their real-world applications. The eight selected projects span 28 states and partner with leading aircraft manufacturers, operators, and state partners, including:
- Urban air taxi services
- Regional passenger transportation (including short Takeoff and Landing aircraft)
- Cargo and logistics networks
- Emergency medical response operations
- Autonomous flight technologies
- Offshore and energy-sector transportation
The eIPP is a first-of-its-kind initiative outlined in President Trump’s Unleashing Drone Dominance Executive Order. It creates one of the nation’s largest real-world testing environments for next-generation aircraft with the potential to create jobs, connect communities, and strengthen American leadership in aviation.
In addition to offering the American people an exciting window into the future of aviation, data from the pilot projects will be used by the FAA to develop new regulations that safely enable this futuristic technology at scale.
Last year, Secretary Duffy and the FAA launched the nation’s first-ever advanced air mobility (AAM) strategy to unlock the future of flight. The Strategy and accompanying action plan outline 40 recommendations to safely and efficiently support AAM operations.
title: Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Announces New Mexico’s First Advanced Air Mobility Demonstration Flight Under eVTOL Integration Program

FORT HUACHUCA, Ariz. — For more than two decades, the Communications-Electronics Command’s U.S. Army Information Systems Engineering Command has supported Army cybersecurity engineering. During this time, USAISEC has drawn on extensive institutional experience spanning the evolution of legacy security standards from the Department of Defense Information Technology Security Certification and Accreditation Process and the DoD Information Assurance Certification and Accreditation Process to today’s Risk Management Framework.
Now, USAISEC is drawing on its comprehensive cybersecurity engineering knowledge to provide an agile RMF as a Service model. The RMFaaS model is designed to support cybersecurity compliance and mission readiness across diverse Department of War systems, directly addressing the growing technical complexity of modern security standards and the shortage of specialized cybersecurity personnel. To bridge these operational gaps, USAISEC provides dedicated subject matter experts to fill critical compliance roles, such as information system security managers and authorizing official designated representatives, for organizations lacking sufficient organic resources.
Safeguarding critical facilities and joint infrastructure
Across military installations, the RMFaaS model delivers tangible results by securing information and operational technology environments.
At the enterprise level, USAISEC provides RMFaaS governance support for the Office of the Provost Marshal General Joint Analytic Real-Time Virtual Information Sharing System. As a web-based security management and threat-tracking platform, JARVISS protects installations and force elements globally. Maintaining a continuous authority to operate for JARVISS ensures installation commanders receive real-time situational awareness. Additionally, USAISEC applies RMFaaS governance to several fire and emergency services systems for OPMG. These physical security and life-safety networks represent operational technology, which requires specialized cybersecurity engineering compared to traditional desktop networks.
The reach of RMFaaS extends into joint military construction initiatives. USAISEC currently delivers direct cybersecurity engineering support to the Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command for eight facility-related control systems at Walter Reed National Military Medical Center. This engineering effort supports a major ongoing military construction renovation at the hospital. By securing heating and cooling, utility monitoring, and building automation systems, USAISEC ensures joint medical personnel operate in a reliable, protected facility.
Cybersecurity engineering ultimately protects mission capability and warfighting readiness. Robert Little, USAISEC director of the Installation and Cyber Engineering Directorate, emphasized that operational readiness of Army commands increasingly depends on a resilient, secure infrastructure.
“Ensuring systems have a current, well-maintained authority to operate is critical for mission success,” said Robert. “The RMFaaS initiative is designed to provide that assurance, allowing commands to focus on their core missions while maintaining compliance with federal and DoW standards.”
Supporting the RMF lifecycle
The RMF lifecycle consists of seven structured steps: prepare, categorize, select, implement, assess, authorize, and monitor. Through this process, the RMF transforms cybersecurity from a static barrier into an adaptive process, allowing the DoW and its partners to field resilient systems that can withstand and recover from modern cybersecurity threats.
The RMFaaS model supports every phase of this lifecycle, from initial system categorization and security control assessment to continuous automated monitoring. This scalable, responsive service model delivers specialized cybersecurity expertise directly at the point of need, customized to each organization's distinct operational tempo. By pairing deep institutional knowledge with responsive service delivery, USAISEC’s RMFaaS model ensures the Army and broader joint force partners can neutralize emerging threats and sustain end-to-end military installation resilience.
For more information about the RMFaaS model or to inquire about other services and capabilities USAISEC provides for organizations, email USAISEC@Army.mil.
title: Risk Management Framework as a Service supports Army readiness

CAMP MURRAY, Wash. — As the Washington Army National Guard prepares for a large-scale deployment to the National Training Center and transitions to new tactical vehicles, military logisticians are sharing expertise to strengthen readiness and build a deeper understanding of how each force sustains its operations.
The Washington National Guard hosted a weeklong logistics subject matter expert exchange with representatives from the Royal Malaysian Armed Forces at Camp Murray Sept. 21-25. The exchange brought together members of the Malaysian Army, Royal Malaysian Air Force and Royal Malaysian Navy to discuss logistics operations, maintenance practices and the processes that keep military forces ready for their missions.
More than a year in the making, the exchange builds on a longstanding partnership between the Washington National Guard and Malaysia through the National Guard State Partnership Program.
“The timing is great because we are doing a massive logistics move preparing to send more than 3,000 soldiers to the National Training Center,” said Brig. Gen. Paul Sellars, commanding general of the Washington Army National Guard. “We are also going through a massive transformation from Strykers to ISVs, so the timing works out better.”
During the week, Malaysian participants visited the Combined Support Maintenance Shop and Unit Training Equipment Site to observe maintenance operations and learn about equipment support processes. The group also visited the Army Aviation Support Facility at Joint Base Lewis-McChord to explore the Washington Army National Guard’s aviation capabilities and associated logistics and maintenance operations.
The visits gave participants an opportunity to see how the Washington Army National Guard organizes and executes sustainment operations while exchanging perspectives on how each military approaches similar challenges.
“We think it is good to have these conversations, because we can tell them what we do and they can tell us about their logistical processes. But during an exchange we can talk about the why, and why we do it this way,” said Col. Rene Mendoza, Washington Army National Guard G-4 logistics officer.
That exchange of knowledge is particularly important as both forces work to understand one another’s capabilities, procedures and requirements. Logistics is essential to generating combat power, supporting deployed forces and sustaining operations over time.
“It’s a good thing for us to work together and learn from one another,” said Sellars.
The logistics exchange is the longest-running engagement between the Washington National Guard and its Malaysian partners, reflecting the importance both forces place on sustainment and the relationships that support continued cooperation.
“Ever since my days as a junior special forces guy, I knew we needed traditional logistics, specifically joint logistics, and that it is incredibly important,” said Sellars.
The exchange also supports future opportunities for cooperation. Malaysian military representatives plan to observe the Washington Army National Guard’s 81st Brigade Combat Team during its National Training Center rotation in August 2027, providing another opportunity to strengthen their understanding of U.S. Army operations and sustainment.
title: Washington Guard, Malaysian Forces strengthen logistics partnership

ROCKFORD — A Rockford man has been sentenced to 14 months in federal prison for straw purchasing ten firearms on behalf of individuals associated with a street gang.

From January 2023 to September 2024, CLESHON PHIPPS purchased ten firearms for two individuals associated with the 3-World street gang. In connection with the purchases, Phipps falsely represented himself as the buyer of the firearms, knowing that the sales would have been denied by the firearms dealers if he indicated that he was buying the guns for those individuals.

Phipps, 24, pleaded guilty earlier this year to one count of making false or fictitious written statements to a licensed firearm dealer. On Oct. 14, 2026, U.S. District Judge Iain D. Johnston sentenced Phipps to 14 months in federal prison.

The sentence was announced by Andrew S. Boutros, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois, and Christopher Amon, Special Agent-in-Charge of the Chicago Division of the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives.

“Gun violence and illegal firearm possession are a huge problem in this community and defendant’s conduct has repeatedly endangered the public,” Assistant U.S. Attorney Theodora Anderson argued in the government’s sentencing memorandum.
title: Rockford Man Sentenced to 14 Months in Federal Prison for Straw Purchasing Firearms

HOHENFELS, Germany — Soldiers from 1st Armored Division participating in Combined Resolve are evaluating combat readiness, integrating emerging capabilities and strengthening interoperability with NATO allies during a multinational training exercise at the Joint Multinational Readiness Center in Hohenfels, Germany.
The exercise, led by U.S. Army Europe and Africa, provides a training environment where units test their ability to execute missions, employ new systems, and operate alongside allied forces in a combined-arms environment.
Combined Resolve also allows units to evaluate how effectively their formations work together while adapting to the changing demands of the modern battlefield.
Specialist Harry Clinton, a cavalry scout and Unmanned Aircraft System trainer assigned to the 474th Armor Regiment, 1st Armored Division, supports the integration of unmanned aircraft systems by helping Soldiers develop the knowledge and skills needed to operate them.
“My job is to help the master trainer get Soldiers licensed to conduct their initial licensing training, make sure they understand their positions and tasks, and know how to utilize them in a combat scenario,” Clinton said.
UAS operations require coordination among Soldiers with different specialties. Clinton said drone strike platoons bring together personnel from multiple military occupational specialties to support operational requirements.
“A drone strike platoon consists of your 15 series, your drone operators, your 19 deltas,” Clinton said. “We all work together, jointly understanding each other's military occupational specialties and conducting operations based on the needs of the Army.”
The integration of unmanned systems reflects the drones’ growing role in modern warfare. Training Soldiers to use these capabilities while coordinating with allied forces is a key part of preparing units for future operations.
“So in today's modern battlefield, as we've seen, drones are now part of the biggest thing that goes on in the field,” Clinton said. “What we're trying to do is catch up and get ahead of the game of drone operations with our NATO allies.”
Through combined arms training and multinational cooperation, Combined Resolve gives participating units a chance to assess their capabilities, identify areas for improvement, and strengthen their ability to operate together.
For Soldiers like Clinton, the exercise offers a chance to develop drone-operating proficiency while contributing to a broader effort to prepare U.S. and allied forces for the demands of the modern battlefield.
title: Combined Resolve prepares Soldiers, NATO allies for modern battlefield

NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA – On October 13, 2026, MARCEL GROSS (“GROSS”) , age 56, of Slidell, was sentenced on October 13, 2026 by U.S. District Judge Darrel James Papillion, to four years’ probation and the payment of $350,272 in restitution, for conspiracy to commit wire fraud, announced U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle.

GROSS fraudulently obtained a Paycheck Protection Program loan, which was a form of assistance authorized by the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. Such loans were forgivable and designed to enable businesses to meet payroll expenses. GROSS complied with a coconspirator’s instructions to pay the coconspirator 40 percent of the loan amount in the form of numerous checks that would be negotiated over multiple weeks so as not to “flag.”

This case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Chandra Menon of the Public Integrity Unit was in charge of the prosecution.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Slidell Man Sentenced for Cares Act Fraud

DENVER - The United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Colorado announces that Joshua Lybolt, 47, Castle Rock, was sentenced to 20 months in federal prison, $5,346,802.61 in restitution, and a $50,000 fine after pleading guilty to one count of wire fraud and one count of money laundering.

According to the plea agreement and facts established at sentencing, from April 2020 until around August 2022, Joshua Lybolt applied for and received $4,950,000 in COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loans (EIDL) from the Small Business Administration (SBA) and $41,667 in Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) funds from an SBA-approved lender. Previously, Lybolt had owned and operated businesses in Indiana and had filed for bankruptcy in that state. Lybolt later moved to Colorado and applied for these fraudulent loans on behalf of the bankrupt businesses. Lybolt falsely certified in fraudulent loan applications that the business entities suffered losses as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, despite knowing that the business entities were not in operation on the dates required to receive relief funds. Lybolt then used the loan proceeds for personal expenses including the purchase of a 2022 Porsche Taycan, a 2022 Chevrolet Corvette Stingray Convertible, a 2021 Ford Bronco, a 2016 Land Rover Range Rover, memberships in a country club and a luxury vacation club, and properties in Avon, Basalt, and Snowmass Village, Colorado.

“Mr. Lybolt stole from hardworking American taxpayers so he could masquerade as something he is not: a successful businessman,” said Peter McNeilly, United States Attorney for the District of Colorado. “I am proud of the work our team did to hold this fraudster accountable and return significant funds back to the federal government.”

“The United States offered emergency financial assistance to Americans and businesses dealing with the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. But this defendant misdirected those funds for personal luxuries,” said FBI Denver Special Agent in Charge Amanda Koldjeski. “The FBI will continue to hold anyone accountable who abuses taxpayer dollars.”

United States District Judge Daniel D. Domenico presided over the sentencing.

The case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

Assistant United States Attorney Craig Fansler handled the prosecution.

The core mission of the National Fraud Enforcement Division is to zealously investigate and prosecute those who steal or fraudulently misuse taxpayer dollars. The National Fraud Enforcement Division will fulfill that mission by coordinating with agencies responsible for administering benefit programs; partnering with federal, tribal, state, territorial, and local law enforcement on fraud-fighting efforts; developing systems and processes that ensure efficient identification of fraud against taxpayer dollars; and equipping prosecutors and law enforcement with state-of-the-art tools and resources needed to bring criminal actors to justice. The attorneys in the National Fraud Enforcement Division will work every day to protect the financial integrity of our government and the tax system that supports it.

Department of Justice efforts support President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

Anyone with information about allegations of attempted fraud involving COVID-19 can report it by calling the Department of Justice’s National Center for Disaster Fraud (NCDF) Hotline at 866-720-5721 or via the NCDF Web Complaint Form at: https://www.justice.gov/disaster-fraud/ncdf-disaster-complaint-form

GOLDEN AGE OF RAIL: Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Invests Over $2.3 Billion into Rail Infrastructure and Safety Across America
The Department will support 105 projects in 45 states and improve over 2,000 miles of track
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Department of Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy today announced the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) is investing $2.3 billion into freight and passenger rail projects in 45 states and the District of Columbia. Over 2,000 miles of track across America will see improvements thanks to funding from the Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Grant Program, which received a record number of eligible applications this cycle.
Selected projects will also receive over $1.9 billion in non-Federal funding from state, local, and private partners to complete in total.
Included in the 105 projects in 45 states is:
- $33.6 million for the Arkansas & Missouri Railroad Company to improve rail infrastructure resilience including track rehabilitation and improvement between Fort Smith, Arkansas, and Monett, Missouri. The project will replace rail, install new ties, upgrade a siding to a double-ended siding configuration, add two new siding tracks, and install 14 wayside rail lubricators on high-degree curves on the Arkansas & Missouri Railroad Company.
- $43.5 million for the Wheeling & Lake Erie Railway to rehabilitate and modernize the Toledo Swing Bridge over the Maumee River in Toledo, Ohio. The project will rehabilitate eight of the 11 bridge spans and replace timber fender systems on the bridge, enabling 286,000-pound railcar capacity.
- $37 million for the Maine Department of Transportation to rehabilitate approximately 90 miles of railroad line in Northern Maine as part of the Northern Aroostook Rail Gateway Modernization and Safety project. The project will replace rail, ties, and ballast and rehabilitate the deck of a railroad bridge
- $20 million for the Aberdeen Carolina & Western Railway Company in North Carolina to rehabilitate and improve rail infrastructure in Montgomery and Stanly counties. The project will install approximately 30 miles of continuous welded rail, rehabilitate bridges, and modernize crossing signals.
- $30 million for the Texas City Terminal Railway Company to realign the Port of Texas’ vehicle entrance gate and rehabilitate and expand the yard. The project will address a safety conflict between trains and vehicles entering a petroleum facility and enable the Port to meet existing and projected demand for exporting multiple types of petrochemicals.
- $218 million for the Wisconsin DOT to support improvements to the Hiawatha West project. The project includes the extension of existing Chicago–Milwaukee Hiawatha passenger rail service to Waukesha, Jefferson, and Dane counties in Wisconsin to rehabilitate and expand the capacity of track, bridges, and crossings, and construct new intercity passenger rail stations.
“Under President Trump, USDOT is investing in rail projects that will unleash local economies and deliver real safety upgrades. From improving shortline infrastructure and port connections so critical products can get where they need to go faster to enhancing fencing along trespassing hotspots, this package will tangibly improve lives for millions of Americans,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “These improvements are all part of our efforts to rekindle a Golden Age of Rail in America.”
“The funds announced today will provide shortline railroads across the country with the resources they need to make long overdue improvements to their day to day operations,” said FRA Administrator David Fink. “These thoughtful, targeted investments will reduce congestion and improve operations instead of wasting tax dollars on politically driven boondoggles.”
FRA’s SELECTION PROCESS
CRISI applications were evaluated according to several criteria, including project readiness, technical merit, and project benefits. Eligible applications for the Crossing Safety Program were also evaluated on the basis of technical merit including Project Readiness, Project Benefits, Project Implementation and Management and similar criteria.  
The full list of selected projects can be found HERE.
Additional Information:
Last April, FRA announced a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) for the CRISI program intended to provide funding for projects that improve the safety, efficiency, and reliability of intercity passenger and freight rail. Under Secretary Duffy, the grant programs revamped criteria prioritize safety, the American family, and workforce development, job quality and wealth creation. Specifically, the Department is supporting projects that: reduce congestion, jumpstart ridership growth on passenger railroads, improve regional railroad infrastructure or develop safety programs to prevent trespassing and reduce injuries and fatalities. More information on the CRISI Program can be found here.
Under Secretary Duffy, the Department has ushered in the Golden Age of Rail by making historic investments into America’s rail infrastructure.
In August, Secretary Duffy announced a $5.3 billion investment into rail projects across the U.S. that will enhance safety, upgrade infrastructure, and purchase new trainsets for Amtrak. Roughly $2 billion of this grant package is funding Secretary Duffy saved the American people by canceling Gavin Newsom’s disastrous high-speed train to nowhere.

title: GOLDEN AGE OF RAIL: Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Invests Over $2.3 Billion into Rail Infrastructure and Safety Across America

Old Lyme, CT — Amtrak and its construction contractor recently welcomed more than 400 civil engineering and construction management college students to tour the Connecticut River Bridge Replacement Project as part of The Moles Annual Student Day.
The Connecticut River Bridge is a 119 years old and a critical part of the Northeast Corridor connecting Boston to New York and communities in between. Because of its age, the bridge is a bottleneck on the corridor with a movable bridge span that opens frequently for marine traffic but can struggle to close.
A modern replacement under construction will enhance the reliability and resiliency of passenger rail in this area, with a movable span that will reliably open and close. The new bridge will also enable a higher maximum speed, increasing the maximum operating speed from 45 mph to 70 mph.
Construction kicked off in fall 2024 and is well underway, with more than a dozen cranes across the site. During the recent event, students received a rare chance to visit the bridge up close, touring the yard where structural steel assembly is happening, visiting the west and east trestles to see drilled shaft work platforms, seeing the environmental mitigation work and more.
The new bridge will begin serving trains by 2030 and the overall project (including demolition of the existing bridge) will be completed in 2031.
title: Amtrak Hosts 400 Students on Tour of Connecticut River Bridge Replacement Project

The U.S. Department of Energy announced today that it will use up to $42 million in Defense Production Act Title III funding to advance the development of a proposed 125-mile natural gas pipeline from Pennsylvania to New York.
October 19, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) announced today that it will use up to $42 million in Defense Production Act (DPA) Title III funding to advance the development of a proposed 125-mile natural gas pipeline from Pennsylvania to New York. 
Constitution Pipeline Company, LLC's project will transport natural gas to markets across the Northeast that currently experience limited access to the low-cost reliable fuel. By leveraging DPA authorities, DOE is helping strengthen the security of the nation’s energy system and defense industrial base. The project will also dramatically lower electricity and home heating costs across the region.
“Despite America having an abundant supply of low-cost natural gas, tens of millions of Americans have limited access to this reliable energy source due to a lack of pipeline infrastructure,” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. “President Trump promised to lower energy costs and reverse the energy emergency he inherited that was caused by 17 years of energy subtraction policies. That is why he promised to build the Constitution Pipeline – a project that will transform the lives and economic opportunities for Americans across New York and New England. It will also reduce the risk of blackouts during periods of peak electricity demand and make our nation more secure.”
“For too long, families and businesses in New York and other blue states have paid the price for anti-energy policies that kneecap production, block critical infrastructure and drive up costs,” said Secretary of the Interior and Chairman of the National Energy Dominance Council Doug Burgum. “President Trump is reversing that failed approach, choosing abundance over government-imposed scarcity. This historic investment in New York will help deliver the reliable, secure energy Americans deserve while saving families across the Northeast billions of dollars.”
This investment supports President Trump’s commitment to ensuring all Americans have access to affordable, reliable, and secure energy while strengthening infrastructure critical to national defense. Thanks to the Working Families Tax Cut, $1 billion in federal funding has been appropriated for energy-related projects deemed critical to national security. Presidential Determination No. 2026-12 identifies natural gas pipelines, processing and storage as essential to national defense. 
The DPA funding will support eligible pre-construction and permitting activities necessary to advance the project and, after permits are completed, the deployment of complementary natural gas infrastructure. These activities may include environmental reviews and assessments, engineering and site-preparation work, and other costs associated with securing required regulatory approvals.
title: Energy Department Advances Constitution Pipeline Project with $42 Million in Defense Production Act Funding

As modern battlefield threats and imaging technologies grow increasingly sophisticated, the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Chemical Biological Center (DEVCOM CBC) is accelerating efforts to protect warfighters through next-generation sensor-defeat capabilities.
In August, stakeholders observed live-field demonstrations of the new Millimeter Wave Screening Obscuration Module (SOM). The Millimeter Wave SOM is a breakthrough concealment capability designed to disrupt enemy radar tracking through screening clouds containing coated fiber materials produced through a portable device. Following the successful technical validation, DEVCOM CBC officially transitioned the system to the Portfolio Management Executive for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Defense (PME CBRND), marking a crucial milestone in turning cutting-edge research into a deployable capability for the Joint Force.
For decades, battlefield obscurants were built to deceive the human eye. Legacy smoke generation systems developed during the Cold War—such as the vehicle-mounted M56 Coyote and M58 Wolf—were engineered primarily to disrupt visual observation, optical rangefinders, and early infrared sensors. While these obscuration methods mask troops and tactical movements from conventional optics, modern adversaries increasingly rely on advanced millimeter-wave radar technologies to pinpoint targets, limiting the protective impact of these smoke generation systems.
Bridging that protection gap required DEVCOM CBC scientists to rethink obscurants from the wavelength up. "Different sensors are designed to operate across distinct regions of the electromagnetic spectrum," said Dr. Jill Harland, a research scientist at DEVCOM CBC. "You have visible sensors, which operate on very narrow, microscopic wavelengths of light. As you move across the spectrum into infrared and thermal imaging, those wavelengths expand. Once you reach millimeter waves, you enter the radar spectrum—frequencies that pass straight through conventional smoke screens undetected by the naked eye."
Michael Smith, a mechanical engineer at DEVCOM CBC, explained that everything has a unique distinct signature or numerical value to the radar and those values allow the radar to detect and identify objects.
“Several targets or signatures were set up, and we had to obscure those targets,” Smith noted. “We used radar to observe the cloud formation and show the degradation of the radar signatures of each of those targets. As the cloud formed, the signature dropped and we got our obscuration that way."
When dispersed, the 30 pounds of fibers act like thousands of shields floating in the air. During the August field demonstrations, researchers put the module through rigorous open-air testing to measure how rapidly the cloud could deploy and how effectively it could suppress active radar tracking in real time. “Watching the radar screens during the live dissemination was a defining moment for the entire development team,” Smith said. "Our objective is to buy Soldiers critical time on the battlefield, improving survivability directly accomplishes our core mission."
“We have an incredible team,” Harland said. “We have everything from chemical engineers, aerospace engineers, mechanical engineers, physicists and chemists. We all came together to provide a solution and to build something from the ground up.”
Dr. Danielle Kuhn, Branch Chief for the Smoke & Target Defeat Branch at DEVCOM CBC, emphasized the value of cross-functional collaboration: “Watching these distinct teams communicate their expertise toward a singular mission has been incredible, this mission really showcased the talent we have here at the Center.”
With technical evaluations complete, the Millimeter Wave (SOM) will transition to PME CBRND for further testing before it’s in warfighters’ hands.
title: Radar Screening Obscuration Tech Moves Closer to Warfighter Hands

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswomen Yvette D. Clarke and Adelita S. Grijalva, alongside 61 Members of Congress, sent a letter urging U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) to immediately expedite pending green card applications for immigrants who have lost or are at risk of losing Medicaid, the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP), Medicare, and Affordable Care Act premium credits as a result of new eligibility restrictions under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) that went into effect on October 1st.
The lawmakers warn that thousands of lawfully-present immigrants, including refugees, asylum recipients, and survivors of domestic violence and human trafficking, could lose access to critical healthcare while waiting for USCIS to process their green card applications providing permanent residency. More than 281,000 lawfully present immigrants across nine states and Washington, D.C., were identified as facing the loss of Medicaid coverage beginning October 1. Nationwide, the Congressional Budget Office estimates that 1.4 million lawfully present immigrants will become uninsured by 2034 under Republicans’ healthcare eligibility restrictions.
The letter highlights the case of an Arizona woman with stage four metastatic breast cancer who lost her Medicaid coverage on October 1. Although she is lawfully present in the United States, delays in processing her green card application have left her without coverage for the chemotherapy she depends on to survive.
The lawmakers argue that eligible applicants should not lose access to healthcare because their immigration applications are caught in processing backlogs.
“Because Lawful Permanent Residents (LPRs), that have already waited any required time, retain federal eligibility under health law, these individuals are losing their health insurance simply because they are trapped in a bureaucratic bottleneck. This is a backlog crisis that lies within the administrative capabilities of USCIS to resolve and the agency cannot allow its own administrative delays to cause catastrophic gaps in their healthcare,” wrote the Members.
They also warn that these delays could increase healthcare costs for federal and state governments by forcing patients to forgo preventive treatment until their conditions become more severe.
In their letter, the lawmakers call on USCIS to take three immediate steps:
- Establish an emergency expedited processing pathway for Form I-485 adjustment of status applications for individuals who face the imminent loss of healthcare coverage because their applications remain pending.
- Clarify expedited processing criteria to explicitly recognize the imminent loss of federal or state healthcare coverage as grounds for expedited processing under severe financial loss or humanitarian considerations.
- Coordinate with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services and state agencies to provide guidance on delaying coverage terminations for individuals with pending adjustment of status applications.
“Needless red tape should never be the determinant between life and death,” said Congresswoman Yvette D. Clarke. “While thousands of immigrant American families remain stuck in a bureaucratic backlog that risks ripping their healthcare out from under them, USCIS has a moral obligation to ensure all those caught in its processing bottleneck do not suffer due to circumstances beyond their control. Government inefficiencies are not the fault of immigrant communities, and they deserve better than to suffer the consequences of them.”
“In Arizona, more than 20,000 lawfully present refugees and immigrants are at risk of losing their healthcare due to USCIS processing bottlenecks, including a woman with stage-four breast cancer and a nine-year-old boy with epilepsy who depends on Medicaid to attend school,” said Congresswoman Adelita Grijalva. “These cuts, thanks to Republicans’ Big Ugly Bill, are forcing Arizona families to choose between their health and their financial security. USCIS needs to act with urgency so that their bureaucratic delays do not cost people their lives.”
Read the full letter here.
###
title: REPS. CLARKE, GRIJALVA LEAD 63 MEMBERS OF CONGRESS IN URGING USCIS TO ADDRESS PROCESSING BACKLOG COSTING LAWFULLY-PRESENT IMMIGRANTS THEIR HEALTHCARE
