LAS VEGAS — The Justice Department today announced that Village Capital & Investment LLC, a servicer of home loans guaranteed by the Department of Veterans Affairs, will pay over $500,000 to resolve allegations that it failed to properly apply Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (SCRA) interest rate benefits to at least 41 servicemembers’ mortgages and retaliated against servicemembers who requested interest rate benefits.

“When lenders refuse to honor the benefits guaranteed under the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act — or worse, retaliate against those who assert their rights — they not only violate federal law, but undermine the trust that military families place in financial institutions,” said Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. “Today’s action makes clear that such conduct will not be tolerated. We will continue to enforce the law to ensure servicemembers receive the protections they have earned.”

“Protecting our nation’s heroes from unlawful lending practices is a fundamental duty, not an option,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “By failing to apply the interest rate cap correctly and misrepresenting mortgage terms, Village Capital & Investment LLC breached the trust of servicemembers. This settlement serves as a clear directive to VA home loan servicers everywhere: illegal lending practices that harm servicemembers will be met with swift accountability and strict enforcement.”

Under this settlement, Village Capital will pay at least $425,000 to affected servicemembers. The company will also be required to pay a $79,380 civil penalty, which is the maximum penalty for a first violation of the SCRA. The agreement also requires Village Capital to revise its policies and procedures to prevent future SCRA violations and provide SCRA training to its employees.

The Department alleges that Village Capital violated the SCRA by failing to reduce the interest rate on servicemembers’ pre-service debts to 6% retroactively to the date they received their military orders and by failing to reduce the monthly mortgage payments by the amount of interest forgiven. Village Capital also allegedly misled servicemember borrowers regarding the interest rates on their mortgages, telling them that their interest rate was already below 6% when the rate was in fact above 6%. The Department also alleges that Village Capital violated the SCRA by retaliating against servicemembers who requested interest rate benefits by accelerating the payment of principal on their loans and falsely reporting their mortgages as delinquent to the Department of Veterans Affairs.

The Department’s enforcement of the SCRA is conducted by the Civil Rights Division’s Housing and Civil Enforcement Section in partnership with U.S. Attorneys’ Offices throughout the country. Since 2011, the Department has obtained over $490 million in monetary relief for over 153,000 servicemembers through its enforcement of the SCRA. For more information about the Department’s SCRA enforcement efforts, please visit www.servicemembers.gov .

Servicemembers and their dependents who believe that their rights under the SCRA may have been violated should contact the nearest Armed Forces Legal Assistance Program Office. Office locations can be found at legalassistance.law.af.mil .

Note: Read the executed settlement here .

title: VA Home Loan Servicer Village Capital to Pay Over $500,000 for Violating Servicemembers’ Rights

SAN ANTONIO – Federal prosecutors in the Western District of Texas filed 476 new immigration and immigration-related criminal cases from October 2 through October 15, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons. Charges were brought against alien smugglers and illegal aliens with past convictions for violent crimes, thefts, numerous DWIs, and multiple prior removals.

Among the new cases, in Austin, Alexi Tellez-Gonzalez , was charged with illegal re-entry. He has prior convictions for theft, burglary of a building, evading arrest, possession of marijuana, DWI, and assault causing bodily injury.

Hector Castro-Lopez , an illegal alien from Mexico, was also charged with illegal re-entry for the second time. Castro-Lopez has prior convictions for failure to identify and assault family violence. He has also twice been convicted of violating a protective order and burglary of a habitation.

Gerardo Torres-Sanchez was found in the Travis County Jail and identified as an illegal alien from Mexico. Torres-Sanchez has been deported 11 times and has five convictions for illegal re-entry.

Illegal alien from Mexico Raul Reyes-Hernandez aka Aurelio Reyes-Hernandez was found in the Washington County Jail in Brenham. Reyes-Hernandez was convicted in 2023 for alien smuggling and money laundering. He’s now charged with illegal re-entry.

A Lebanese man with a Legal Permanent Resident Card was arrested in Fort Hancock and charged with alien smuggling. A criminal complaint alleges that Abdallah Mohamad Alhussni was working as a rideshare driver when he joined a Facebook group to find higher paying work, which led him to communications with an alien smuggling facilitator on WhatsApp. He allegedly conducted 10 smuggling trips, transporting approximately 20 individuals from the Fort Hancock area to various locations in El Paso for approximately $150 per trip.

An illegal alien from Honduras is charged with impersonating another and attempting to evade immigration laws by appearing under an assumed or fictitious name. Meslin Donaldo Gutierres-Cruz allegedly presented a State of Colorado birth certificate with the name and birth date of an individual with the initials of M.G. when he applied for admission into the U.S. at the Paso Del Norte Port of Entry on Wednesday. A criminal complaint alleges that a U.S. Customs and Border Protection officer scanned Gutierres-Cruz’s fingerprints, revealing he was previously removed from the U.S. on Aug. 9. Gutierres-Cruz has been deported a total of seven times and has multiple prior convictions, including driving without a license and possession of cocaine.

Amaurys Gutierrez-Nunez , an illegal alien from Cuba, was arrested near Eagle Pass and charged with illegal re-entry. Gutierrez-Nunez was previously deported for the first time in July 2025 but has an extensive criminal record that includes two convictions for grand theft, multiple petty theft convictions, resisting an officer, and driving with a suspended license.

Illegal alien from Mexico Julian Garcia-Soto was arrested near Carrizo Springs and charged with illegal re-entry. Garcia-Soto has been previously removed from the U.S. three times and has three DUI convictions, along with a conviction for possession of a controlled substance, and for obstructing a public officer.

Omar Alberto Sanchez-Briones , an illegal alien from Honduras, is charged with illegal re-entry following his arrest near Eagle Pass. Sanchez-Briones was convicted in California earlier this year of his third burglary charge and one battery count. He’s been deported twice, the last being in May 2025 through Phoenix, Arizona.

Illegal alien from Mexico Jose Miguel Aguilar aka Miguel Angel Aguilar Bustillo was arrested near Comstock after just being removed from the U.S. on Sept. 11 through Harlingen. Aguilar has been previously convicted of bringing in and harboring aliens, unlawful possession of a weapon by a felon, failure to identify, and assault causing bodily injury to a family member. He now faces a charge of illegal re-entry.

Illegal alien from Honduras Jose Luis Masias-Milla was arrested near Eagle Pass and charged with illegal reentry. He was deported for the first time on May 20 through Harlingen but has two DWI convictions and a conviction for unlawful carrying of a weapon on alcohol premises.

Luis Alberto Guajardo , an illegal alien from Mexico, was arrested near Eagle Pass and faces his second illegal re-entry charge. He’s been deported from the U.S. five times, the last being in August 2022, and has been convicted of three DWIs as well as making a terroristic threat against a public servant and possession of a controlled substance.

In San Antonio, Melvin Acosta-Martinez was encountered at the Bexar County Jail after he was arrested for theft of property greater than $30,000 and less than $150,000, according to a criminal complaint filed on Oct. 9. Acosta-Martinez is an illegal alien from Honduras whose criminal record includes a conviction for assaulting a federal officer, which resulted in a 237-day prison sentence. He has also been previously convicted of a DWI and illegal re-entry. He now faces his second illegal re-entry charge.

These cases were referred or supported by federal law enforcement partners, including ICE, U.S. Border Patrol, the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), the FBI, the U.S. Marshals Service (USMS), and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), with additional assistance from state and local law enforcement partners.

The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Texas comprises 68 counties located in the central and western areas of Texas, encompasses nearly 93,000 square miles and an estimated population of 7.6 million people. The district includes three of the five largest cities in Texas—San Antonio, Austin and El Paso—and shares 660 miles of common border with the Republic of Mexico.

Indictments and criminal complaints are merely allegations and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

These cases are part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

Today, the Federal Trade Commission sued to block Platinum Equity and its portfolio company PlayPower’s acquisition of BCI Burke, alleging the deal to combine two of the largest commercial outdoor playground equipment makers will drive up prices and decrease innovation and quality for equipment bought by schools, churches, parks and recreation departments and other organizations across the country.
PlayPower, owned by private equity firm Platinum Equity, proposes to buy Burke, one of PlayPower’s closest competitors in the manufacture of commercial outdoor playground equipment. The proposed transaction would add the Burke brand to PlayPower’s existing commercial outdoor playground portfolio, which includes Miracle Recreation Equipment Company, Little Tikes Commercial and Playworld Systems, Inc.—brands PlayPower previously acquired.
The complaint alleges that the deal will significantly increase concentration in an already concentrated market and eliminate PlayPower and Burke’s intense rivalry that benefits playground customers through lower prices, better services, higher quality and increased innovation. The complaint is joined by the attorneys general of Arizona, California, Colorado, Illinois, Nevada, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Texas, Washington and Wisconsin.
“Playgrounds are an indispensable part of daily life for millions of American kids and their families. And state and local governments spend hundreds of millions of taxpayer dollars each year on playgrounds so that their communities have places for kids to play safely,” said Daniel Guarnera, Director of the FTC’s Bureau of Competition. “Instead of investing in building better playgrounds or lowering prices, PlayPower and its parent Platinum Equity want to eliminate one of PlayPower’s fiercest competitors and continue to raise prices on American schools, parks departments, churches and municipalities.”
The loss of price competition between PlayPower and Burke is especially problematic given rapidly rising playground prices in an already highly concentrated market. Today, five companies—including PlayPower and Burke—own more than a dozen playground equipment brands and hold 85% to 90% market share in the United States, according to the complaint.
Even with Burke competing aggressively and taking share from PlayPower, PlayPower’s prices for its products have soared in recent years. And its proposed acquisition of Burke will allow it to charge even higher prices, the complaint alleges. In addition to driving up prices, the acquisition will likely lead to less innovation and poorer service and quality by eliminating Burke’s focus on providing innovative, high-quality products and robust service, according to the complaint. At the same time, the proposed acquisition could also have a negative impact on independent sales representatives who sell the companies’ equipment, leading to lower commissions or worse service terms, according to the complaint.
The combination of PlayPower and Burke will significantly increase concentration, eliminate fierce head-to-head competition and result in a highly concentrated market that is considered presumptively unlawful under antitrust case law and the FTC’s and Department of Justice’s joint merger guidelines, according to the complaint.
The Commission vote to authorize staff to seek a permanent injunction to block the proposed acquisition was 2-0.
The FTC and co-plaintiff states filed the federal court complaint and request for permanent equitable relief in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California.
The Federal Trade Commission works to promote competition and to protect and educate consumers. The FTC will never demand money, make threats, tell you to transfer money, or promise you a prize. You can learn more about how competition benefits consumers, file an antitrust complaint, or comment on a proposed merger. For the latest news and resources, follow the FTC on social media, subscribe to press releases and read our blog.
title: FTC Sues to Block PlayPower’s Acquisition of Rival Playground Manufacturer Burke

Release Number 9311-26
CFTC Secures Federal Court Orders Requiring Former Long Island Resident and His Firm to Pay Over $288 Million for Operating a Commodity Pool Ponzi Scheme
October 19, 2026
WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York entered orders granting the CFTC’s motions for summary judgment, injunctive relief, and a civil monetary penalty against Eddy Alexandre of Valley Stream, New York, and his company, EminiFX Inc., which operated in Valley Stream and Manhattan, New York.
The orders require the defendants to pay $228,576,962 in restitution to the defrauded investors, to disgorge $15,049,500 in unlawful gains of (offset by any amounts paid in restitution), and to pay a $45,148,500 penalty.
The orders stem from the CFTC’s May 12, 2022, complaint in this matter. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8527-22.]
As described in the court’s summary judgment order, the defendants held themselves out as an investment club providing investors with an affordable solution that offered easy access to cryptocurrency and Forex trading using the latest technology available.
Over the course of EminiFX’s eight months in operation, tens of thousands of investors sent contributions exceeding $262 million. According to the order, the defendants reported “astonishing” returns on investment of 5% to 9.99% per week.
In reality, EminiFX experienced net losses exceeding $49 million. At least $15 million of those losses resulted from Alexandre’s misappropriation of investor funds for his own use.
As noted by the court, “Simply put, EminiFX was a Ponzi scheme, and investors’ decisions to give their money to [d]efendants was predicated entirely on fraudulent misrepresentations.”
During the CFTC’s lawsuit, the court-appointed receiver recovered millions of dollars in investor funds and other assets held by the defendants and is distributing those funds to the defrauded investors. As of July 2026, over $98 million has been returned to more than 28,000 investors.
The CFTC cautions; however, that orders requiring repayment of funds to victims may not always result in the recovery of lost money because the wrongdoers may not have sufficient funds or assets.
Alexandre is serving a nine-year prison sentence based on a parallel action for related conduct brought by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York.
-CFTC-
title: CFTC Secures Federal Court Orders Requiring Former Long Island Resident and His Firm to Pay Over $288 Million for Operating a Commodity Pool Ponzi Scheme

FORT GEORGE G. MEADE, Md. — Col. Joshua Patton assumed command of U.S. Army Garrison Fort George G. Meade during an assumption of command ceremony here Thursday, Oct. 15, at Club Meade.
Patton takes charge of the installation following interim leadership under Deputy to the Garrison Commander Brian Foley, assuming responsibility for base operations, tenant partnerships and infrastructure across the installation.
"The Army does not train its officers to be garrison commanders—to lead cities," said Jason Condrey, director of Installation Management Command Directorate-Sustainment, who presided over the ceremony. "Instead, it is deliberate in selecting leaders who are capable, innovative, and motivated to handle these unique and complex challenges."
Distinguished guests attending the ceremony included Maryland State Delegates Mark Chang, Mike Rogers and Gary Simmons, as well as Anne Arundel County Board of Education President Gloria Dent and Vice President Dawn Pulliam. Federal delegations were represented by congressional staffers Jessica Klaitman from the office of U.S. Sen. Chris Van Hollen, Ricky Powell-Graves from the office of U.S. Sen. Angela Alsobrooks, and Taylor Donoghue, senior advisor for U.S. Rep. Sarah Elfreth. Gina Stewart, Fort Meade Community Covenant chairperson, attended representing the community at large.
As the Army's second-largest installation by population, Fort Meade supports more than 64,000 employees representing the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Coast Guard and Space Force. The garrison hosts more than 120 partner agencies and commands, including U.S. Cyber Command, the National Security Agency, the Defense Information Systems Agency, Joint Force Headquarters-Department of Defense Information Network, and War Media Activity, alongside federal entities such as the Environmental Protection Agency and the Architect of the Capitol.
Patton, a career military intelligence officer, acknowledged the shift from tactical formations to base operations.
"Up front, I came in extremely humble," Patton said. "There were nerves around it because, as a military officer, you're trained very well in your specific skill set. But as you transition into an installation, there's a lot more in terms of infrastructure management. Fortunately, I came upon a [garrison] team that has a lot of tenure, and their expertise is going to be key."
Patton emphasized that sustaining the base workforce and military families directly drives the defense and intelligence missions hosted on post.
"The priority is to make sure families and [service members] are supported for the mission," Patton said. "Part of that readiness resides with them being comfortable, understanding that their needs are met on Fort Meade, and being able to integrate into the surrounding community."
Patton underscored his focus on maintaining long-term installation initiatives, to include those put in place by his predecessor, retired Col. Yolanda Gore. These efforts encompass family support programs, childcare enhancements, higher education opportunities for spouses, construction of the $26 million Child Development Center V, Maryland's first Intergovernmental Support Agreement with the University of Maryland, and the Friends of Meade school partnership.
"If you do not continue the trajectory that other individuals start, you lose positive momentum, so it's critical to retain that direction," Patton said. "There has been great coordination not only with the community, but importantly with family support and higher education opportunities for spouses—all critical to succeeding in our operational mission."
A native of Lilburn, Georgia, Patton earned his commission through the Reserve Officers' Training Corps at the Florida Institute of Technology in 2004. His joint and operational assignments include service with the 75th Ranger Regiment, 7th Special Forces Group, Joint Special Operations Command, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence and command of Headquarters and Headquarters Battalion, 25th Infantry Division.
Patton noted that his special operations background reinforced the value of empowering specialized personnel across the civilian and military workforce.
"One thing special operations teaches you is that while I may be a colonel, but the sergeant over there actually has the expertise to do the job," Patton said. "Let those individuals who have that expertise excel. That's critical not only for the garrison, but for the broader mission of Fort Meade."
Ahead of the official ceremony Thursday morning, Condrey recognized Foley during a surprise awards presentation in the Club Meade Brass Lounge, presenting him an award honoring his service as deputy to the garrison commander.
During the assumption of command, Condrey commended Foley, a former Fort Meade garrison commander who stepped up from his civilian deputy role to guide the installation through the command transition ahead of his departure in early November after more than 13 years of service to the post.
"Brian Foley has once again stood in the gap for this garrison, providing the steady hand and seasoned leadership that Team Meade needed during this transition," Condrey said. "His enduring dedication to this community, both in uniform and as a civilian leader, represents the very best of service, and we owe him a debt of gratitude as he prepares to conclude his remarkable chapter here.”
Over Patton’s first 60 days in command, he plans to assess garrison operations, engage tenant unit commanders and coordinate with local civic leaders and school boards.
"That mission is extremely robust and far more complex than what we typically see from a brigade combat team," Patton said. "What excites me most is the opportunity to see what this unit needs to succeed and help make that happen."
title: Patton assumes command of Fort Meade garrison

Fugitive Arrested for Bronx Hit-and-Run That Seriously Injured On-Duty NYPD Officer
For immediate release
Tracy Amaladas, Supervisory Deputy U.S. Marshal
NEW YORK — The U.S. Marshals Service (USMS) Southern District of New York and the New York/New Jersey Regional Fugitive Task Force (NY/NJ RFTF) early today located and apprehended the individual responsible for Saturday’s violent hit-and-run that severely injured an on-duty New York City Police Department (NYPD) officer in the Bronx.
Eduard Paulino, 31, was arrested in the Bronx without incident.
The incident occurred late Saturday evening when officers responded to a large, rowdy gathering and a loud music complaint in the vicinity of Garrison Avenue and Whittier Street in the Hunts Point section. While managing the chaotic scene, an NYPD officer was struck by a fleeing white Honda SUV driven by Paulino, who allegedly accelerated from the scene, leaving the officer with significant leg injuries. The injured officer was rushed to Lincoln Hospital for emergency trauma care.
“There is nowhere to hide in New York for individuals who choose violence against law enforcement,” said Ricky J. Patel, U.S. Marshal for the Southern District of New York. “We promised a swift and decisive capture, and through the combined, relentless efforts of the U.S. Marshals and our partners, we delivered. If you assault those who wear the shield to protect this city, the full weight of federal and local law enforcement will find you."
The NY/NJ RFTF began operations in April 2002 and was the first regional fugitive task force to become fully operational following the Presidential Threat Protection Act of 2000. The NY/NJ RFTF was the flagship that has allowed seven other regional fugitive task forces to be created across the country. With partnership agreements with over 90 federal, state, or local agencies and 13 fully operational offices, the NY/NJ RFTF has successfully apprehended over 95,000 fugitives since inception.
title: Fugitive Arrested for Bronx Hit-and-Run That Seriously Injured On-Duty NYPD Officer | U.S. Marshals Service

RELEASE: Gottheimer Claws Back $1.2 Million in Federal Dollars for Public Safety in Passaic County
Above: Gottheimer Announces $1.2 Million in Federal Dollars for Public Safety in Passaic County.
BLOOMINGDALE, NJ — Today, October 19, 2026, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) announced that he successfully clawed back $1.2 million in new federal Homeland Security funding from Washington for Passaic County first responders, helping upgrade emergency communications, expand counterterrorism training, and strengthen public safety while delivering real tax relief for local families.
“When something goes wrong, the people who show up are the people standing right here. Today, I am proud to announce that we have clawed back $1.2 million in federal Homeland Security funding from Washington for Passaic County first responders, families, and towns. It shouldn’t be a fundraiser or a bake sale that decides whether a department can afford a working radio. I will always get the backs of our law enforcement, our firefighters, and our first responders,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), Co-Chair of the Law Enforcement Caucus and member of the Congressional Fire Services Caucus.
Video of Gottheimer’s announcement can be found here.
The federal investment Gottheimer secured will replace aging equipment and move Bloomingdale, Ringwood, Wanaque, and West Milford onto one interoperable communications standard, so police, fire, and EMS can communicate clearly and seamlessly across town lines when seconds matter most. By clawing back federal dollars to North Jersey communities and first responders, Gottheimer is helping lift high costs off local budgets, reducing the burden on Passaic County taxpayers to pay for essential public safety equipment and helping lower property taxes for local families.
The funding will be used as follows:
- Bloomingdale First Responders, $400,000 (including the $100,000 announced in September): Response drones, active-threat gear such as ballistic shields, armor, and breaching kits, and communications equipment upgrades.
- Ringwood First Responders, $300,000: A radio system upgrade, including new mobile radios in first-responder vehicles.
- Wanaque First Responders, $300,000: Upgrades to interoperable radio systems, strengthening communications between the department, dispatch, and surrounding towns.
- West Milford First Responders, $200,000: Radio communications upgrades.
Each department will also use part of its award for counterterrorism and other response training.
This investment builds on Gottheimer’s years-long work to claw more federal dollars back to North Jersey from Washington. This year alone, he has secured roughly $21 million in Homeland Security grant funding across Bergen, Passaic, and Sussex Counties for law enforcement, first responders, and the houses of worship and nonprofits that need protection.
Since 2017, he has clawed back more than $17 million in COPS grants for police departments across the Fifth District, including $2.9 million for upgraded first responder radio systems in West Milford in 2023 and $750,000 for new officers in West Milford in 2024. Since coming to Congress, Gottheimer has helped increase the return of federal funds to the Fifth District by more than 357%, delivering an average savings of about $750 for each household in the Fifth District.
Gottheimer was joined by Bloomingdale Mayor John D’Amato, Bloomingdale Police Chief Daniel Greenwood, Passaic County Prosecutor Camelia Valdes, Passaic County Sheriff Thomas Adamo, Passaic County Commissioner Nicholas Veliky, Bloomingdale Councilman David Bronkhurst, Bloomingdale Fire Chief Frank Neuberger, Ringwood Police Chief Ronald Porta, Wanaque Mayor Dan Mahler, Wanaque Councilman Ed Leonard, Wanaque Police Chief Keith Spillane, West Milford Mayor Michelle Dale, West Milford Sgt. Anthony Frassa, Ringwood Councilwoman Yvonne Echols, local first responders, and community leaders.
Below: Gottheimer Announces $1.2 Million in Federal Dollars for Public Safety in Passaic County.
Gottheimer remarks as prepared for delivery:
Good morning, everyone. It’s great to be here in Bloomingdale, in beautiful Passaic County.
First, I want to start by thanking the hardworking people standing here with us today. Jersey’s finest. Our local police departments. Our Passaic County Prosecutor’s Office. Our Passaic County Sheriff’s Office. Everyone who answers the call, who stands in harm’s way, no matter the hour.
Every single day, rain or shine, late nights, early mornings, weekends, holidays, you put on the uniform, and you answer the call without hesitation. You put yourselves in harm’s way to keep our families and communities safe. You get our backs. And I want you to know, as ever, that I’ll always get yours.
Here in northern Passaic County, you cover a lot of ground. Long stretches of road. You roll up on a call at two in the morning, not knowing what’s on the other side of that door.
You chase down a stolen car. You stand post for hours outside a house of worship because a threat came in overnight. You respond to a terrorist threat or a heart attack. You do all of that – and never miss the routine calls. The fender-bender, the alarm going off, the neighbor dispute. The job doesn’t slow down just because the risks get bigger.
When something goes wrong, the people who show up are the people standing right here. And, despite your deep ties with the community, our officers are increasingly doing it in an environment where you’re not always treated with the respect you’re due.
You aren’t just officers who protect us. You are our neighbors. You coach our kids’ teams, and you sit next to us at church and at the diner.
Just over the last year, among others, you responded to a mother and her two children lost while hiking in West Milford, a live, fully charged grenade in Bloomingdale, a deadly house fire in Ringwood, a tragic, fatal crash in Wanaque, and those are just to name a few.
We all know that being a cop today is more complex than it was twenty years ago.
Today, our officers have to think about active shooters. Mass-casualty events. Threats against our synagogues, our churches, our mosques, our temples. Terrorist threats. Cyberattacks on the systems that keep our towns running, like our water systems and electric grid. Let’s be honest, it’s a different and fast-changing world. AI, cameras, drones, and real-time intelligence tools.
That is an enormous amount to ask of any officer, any department, any town. And, increasingly, our local and county departments don’t have the resources they need to keep up – manpower, training, updated radios, equipment, and communication systems.
Gear and training for the worst-case scenarios nobody wants to think about. But, every department has to be ready for those worst-case scenarios.
Let me talk about radios for a minute, because it sounds simple, but it is a matter of life and death. Reliable radios are the backbone of any emergency response. When police, fire, and EMS can all talk on the same system, they share information and coordinate in real time. When they can’t, people get hurt.
On 9/11, many firefighters in the North Tower never got the order to evacuate because their radios couldn’t reach them. Police who saw the collapse coming were on a separate system that couldn’t warn them. We can never let that happen again.
It’s not just terrorism or crime. Communications break down in storms and in everyday emergencies, like in a car wreck, a storm, or a forest fire, when systems get overwhelmed or simply can’t link up. Aging equipment and systems that can’t talk to each other should never be what stands between a first responder and the person who needs help.
Many of the towns I represent in Passaic County told me they simply didn’t have the latest equipment to communicate, including where there are huge distances between towers and plenty of woods and roads in between. In times of crisis, we shouldn’t ever accept radios that don’t work with the radios in the town over or with dispatch.
It’s the same way I feel about training. I know how stretched our departments are for resources. There simply aren’t enough resources to pay for all the training that’s required, including everything officers need to fight the latest terrorist threat or handle everyday crime.
That’s why I proudly introduced bipartisan legislation called the Invest to Protect Act, which passed the House. It allocates resources for training, and recruitment and retention bonuses for our officers, who are facing more stress than ever.
It’s also why, since 2017, I’ve fought hard in Washington, and successfully clawed back to Jersey more than $17 million in COPS grants for police departments across the Fifth District. I was proud to secure $2.9 million for upgraded first responder radio systems for West Milford in 2023.
And in 2024, I secured $750,000 for West Milford to hire new officers as part of the COPS Hiring Program. But, that only solved part of the problem, and, as I said, these needs are changing fast, especially with our communications equipment.
It shouldn’t be a fundraiser or a bake sale that decides whether a department can afford a working radio.
So, over the last months, after hearing from the prosecutor, the sheriff, the PBA, mayors, state and local officials, and, of course, many of the police chiefs, I went back to work in Washington, with my colleagues in Congress and with the Administration.
Months of meetings. Months of calls. Months of negotiations. I took the needs of our district directly to the White House, to the Secretary of Homeland Security, and to FEMA to make sure Jersey gets the funds we deserve.
Today, I am proud to announce that we have clawed back $1.2 million in federal Homeland Security funding for Passaic County first responders, families, and towns.
Again, we are clawing back $1.2 million in federal dollars from Washington back to Passaic County. Those are dollars that are not coming from your property taxes and state income taxes – and they aren’t going to Moocher States like Alabama or West Virginia. They are coming back here, where they belong.
Let me break this out for you a little more. Of the $1.2 million, $400,000 will go to the Bloomingdale Police Department – including the $100,000 I announced on September 11th – for response drones and active-threat gear, like ballistic shields, armor, and breaching kits, and to upgrade their communications equipment. Another $300,000 will go to the Ringwood Police Department for a radio system upgrade, with new mobile radios in first-responder vehicles. $300,000 will go to the Wanaque Police Department to upgrade to interoperable radio systems. And $200,000 will go to the West Milford Police Department for radio communications upgrades.
And every one of those departments will also use part of its award for the terror and other response training that I mentioned.
When implemented, this funding will replace and upgrade aging equipment, and move these departments onto one interoperable standard, so that first responders across town lines are not locked onto systems that can’t talk to each other.
The primary use of these funds is radio upgrades, so that multiple agencies can talk to each other directly, on one channel. In Wanaque, that means stronger radio communications between the department, dispatch, and the surrounding towns. In Ringwood, it means new radios in the vehicles themselves. When the State police, the local police, fire, and EMS can all reach each other in an emergency, they can coordinate faster and save lives.
These resources will also help purchase drones and active-threat gear in Bloomingdale. These give our officers more eyes where they need them, and help them respond to incidents safely. So, our first responders are ready when the worst happens.
This year alone, across Bergen, Passaic, and Sussex Counties that I proudly represent, we have now secured roughly $25.5 million in Homeland Security grant funding for our law enforcement, our first responders, and the houses of worship and nonprofits that need protection.
Plus, I also helped claw back another $29.5 million in June for the state, which helped State Police, communications equipment, transit, for overtime for officers during the World Cup, counterterrorism, counter-drone operations, intelligence sharing, other threat training, and nonprofit security grants.
Finally, every police department in the Fifth Congressional District, including all of Passaic County – Bloomingdale, Ringwood, Wanaque, and West Milford – will receive $50,000 for counterterrorism training, because, as I said, it is not enough to have gear. This requires robust, sustained training, not just an informational binder on a shelf.
Bloomingdale, Ringwood, Wanaque, and West Milford will each receive the resources for vital training as part of their award.
By the way, the amounts I announced today are beyond and outside the traditional grants we fight to claw back every year – like LESO, $1 million for COPS, Byrne JAG, $1.48 million for AFGE, $965k for SAFER, and over $10 million in community-directed projects. Today’s numbers also don’t include the $1.7 million and $7.8 million over the last two years that I’ve already clawed back this year to protect our religious institutions in my district.
One point I want to make – these are your federal tax dollars coming home to Jersey. We send billions of dollars to Washington every year. The question is: how much of that money actually comes back to Jersey? For far too long, the answer has been not nearly enough. My job is to fight for every dollar I can, and claw it back here, where it belongs. For every dollar I get back of your federal tax dollars to Jersey, that means one less dollar hitting your local property tax or income tax lines. That’s a big deal.
That means federal dollars to help pay for a fire truck, like we did in West Milford in 2018, or equipment to keep firefighters safe, like oxygen masks or thermal imaging cameras, which I secured for Ringwood in 2020 and 2021.
Historically, states like Mississippi have gotten about $4.38 back for every dollar it sends to Washington. West Virginia gets about $4.23 back.
But in New Jersey? We get about 67 cents on the dollar. That’s the lowest in the nation.
That’s unacceptable. Why should the “Moocher States” get our money, instead of it coming back home to you?
That’s why I’m fighting every day to claw back your federal tax dollars and bring them home to Jersey. Since I’ve been in Congress, we’ve increased what we bring back home by more than 357 percent, about $750 per family.
For you, that means lower property taxes, better infrastructure, and more money in your pocket. That’s what today is. Jersey families’ own federal tax dollars, coming back home to protect Jersey.
Finally, I am so proud to stand here today. I am so grateful for everything these incredible public servants do for every single one of us, every single day.
I will always get the backs of our law enforcement, our firefighters, and our first responders. Keeping them, and our families, safe is not a partisan issue. This isn’t red or blue – this is just red, white, and blue, and about taking care of the families we all represent.
I know that if we keep working together to support our communities, here in the greatest country in the world, our best days will always be ahead of us.
Thank you. May God bless you, your families, and our first responders.
###
title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Claws Back $1.2 Million in Federal Dollars for Public Safety in Passaic County

On October 17 th , the U.S. Attorney’s Office – District of Kansas filed a Criminal Complaint against Jaden J. Read, 24, of Clearwater, KS for making Threats Against the President.

On October 15 th , a Crime Stoppers tip led authorities to a Facebook post where Jaden Read made comments in response to a KAKE News article detailing President Trump’s upcoming visit to Wichita, KS on October 19 th , 2026. Jaden J. Read’s threatening comments raised concern among the authorities. Read posted on Facebook: “ Let’s shoot Trump honestly, where’s our shooter? I’m tired of living this money life” and immediately after his first comment, Read posted a second comment on the same KAKE News Article stating: “ I just got a 308 and 305 round and I’m killing this pedo”.

Authorities found Read made two more threating comments in response to a different article by KWCH 12 News discussing President Trump’s upcoming visit. In this threat, Read commented: “Can we shoot him in Kansas please I will myself.” And a minute later Read posted “IK where your speech will be. Already mapped out roofs around. Finna get kirked since yall couldn’t help him”.

On October 17 th , authorities arrested Read in Clearwater, KS and he was taken into Federal custody, where he will remain until his detention hearing.

“Political violence and threats of political violence will not be tolerated.” Said U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser. “The first Amendment allows for robust disagreement but there are constraints. I caution people to stay within the bounds of constitutionally protected speech”.

The United States Secret Service, the Unites States Marshall Services, the Kansas Bureau of Investigation, the Kansas Highway Patrol and the Wichita Police Department investigated the case.

United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, announced today that RAMON RODRIGUEZ, a/k/a “Pollo,” was sentenced to life in prison plus twenty years’ imprisonment for the June 21, 2021, murder of Milton Grant during a robbery in Manhattan, the attempted murder of a second man, and other racketeering and firearms offenses. On February 20, 2026, RODRIGUEZ was convicted after a two-week jury trial. RODRIGUEZ was also sentenced in a separate case in which he pleaded guilty to an assault that left a fellow prison inmate seriously injured. U.S. District Judge Jed S. Rakoff presided over the trial and imposed today’s sentence.

“Today’s sentence holds Ramon Rodriguez accountable for these heinous crimes and reaffirms the commitment of this Office and our law enforcement partners to protecting the public from those who demonstrate such callous disregard for human life,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “Rodriguez decided that a watch was worth more than Milton Grant’s life, murdering him to steal it and then trying to kill Grant’s friend as he fled. Even behind bars, Rodriguez remained undeterred in his willingness to resort to violence, joining fellow gang members in a vicious assault on another inmate.”

According to the Indictment, other documents filed in federal court, and evidence presented at trial:

From at least 2018 through 2025, RODRIGUEZ was a member of the Trinitarios and an associate of the Shooting Boys, a set of the Trinitarios that operated primarily in the Bronx and Manhattan. Members and associates of the Shooting Boys engaged in murders, attempted murders, robberies, drug trafficking, fraud, and witness retaliation.

On June 13, 2021, RODRIGUEZ and members of the Shooting Boys committed a robbery outside a Bronx nightclub. During the robbery, RODRIGUEZ shot a man in the leg, causing significant injuries. Just eight days later, on June 21, 2021, RODRIGUEZ and members of the Shooting Boys committed another robbery outside another Manhattan nightclub, during which they targeted the victim, Milton Grant, for his watch. During that robbery, RODRIGUEZ shot Grant in the head, killing him, and then stole Grant’s watch from his lifeless body. As Grant’s friend ran away, RODRIGUEZ shot at him as well, attempting to kill him.

After his arrest and detention at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn, New York, RODRIGUEZ continued to participate in the Shooting Boys gang, including by repeatedly possessing weapons. On December 3, 2023, RODRIGUEZ and other members and associates of the Shooting Boys ambushed, stabbed, and slashed an inmate whom the gang suspected was cooperating with law enforcement.

RODRIGUEZ was sentenced to life in prison plus twenty years’ imprisonment for Grant’s murder, the attempted murder of Grant’s friend, and related offenses, and a separate concurrent term of 10 years’ imprisonment for the prison assault, to which he pleaded guilty. In addition to his prison term, RODRIGUEZ, 22, of the Bronx, New York, was sentenced to five years of supervised release.

Mr. McDonald praised the outstanding investigative work of the New York City Police Department and Homeland Security Investigations.

The cases are being prosecuted by the Office’s Violent Organizations and Crime Unit. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Dominic A. Gentile, James Ligtenberg, Frank Balsamello, Brandon D. Harper, and William Stone are in charge of the prosecutions, with the assistance of Paralegal Specialists William Coleman and Sandy Alcantara.
title: Trinitarios Gang Member Sentenced To Life In Prison For 2021 Murder And Other Crimes

From the misty evergreens of the Pacific Northwest to the hardwood ridges of Appalachia, America’s forests are among our Nation’s greatest natural treasures. During National Forest Products Week, we renew our commitment to conserving these incredible landscapes and responsibly harnessing their abundance to sustain households, strengthen American jobs and industry, and secure lasting prosperity for generations to come.
The woodlands of America helped build our Nation from the ground up, giving generations of citizens the resources to raise homes, establish businesses, and pursue their dreams. That proud tradition continues today in our logging, forestry, manufacturing, and construction industries, where the bounty of our land meets the skill and resolve of our people in communities across our country.
As President, I am committed to supporting these vital industries and continuing to drive economic growth. Last year, I was proud to sign two Executive Orders to increase domestic timber supply and reduce reliance on imports from foreign markets. As a result, over half a billion dollars in new domestic industry investments were announced, annual industry earnings have increased by over $5,600, and the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Forest Service has sold over three billion board feet of American timber this year, the highest volume sold in almost three decades. Under my leadership, the USDA Forest Service has also championed sustainable forests, achieving 116 percent of our annual reforestation goal, the highest level in twenty-six years.
We are cutting red tape and rolling back unnecessary environmental regulations on industries such as logging and paper manufacturing, unleashing the full productive power of American workers and natural resources. I also established the Make America Beautiful Again Commission, which brings together members of my Administration to lead active forest management and historic conservation efforts that will preserve the magnificent abundance of our wildlands for the Americans who will inherit them in the centuries ahead.
This week, we reflect on God’s gift of our beautiful and immense natural landscape, and we refocus our efforts to responsibly and boldly utilize these resources to grow our Republic, strengthen our economy, and empower American families with the tools and opportunities they need to build our Nation’s future.
title: Presidential Message on National Forest Products Week

Stanton, Ansari, and Grijalva Statement on Suspicious Letters Sent to Arizona Offices
PHOENIX – Today, U.S. Representatives Greg Stanton (AZ-04), Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), and Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07) released the following joint statement:
“This weekend, the FBI Phoenix Field Office and the Arizona Department of Homeland Security informed us that suspicious letters had been sent to our offices. Similar letters, many containing unknown substances, have been mailed to elected officials across the country.
The FBI and the U.S. Postal Inspection Service are investigating. We’re grateful to law enforcement for acting quickly and keeping our staff and communities safe.
We will not be intimidated and we’ll keep doing the work that Arizonans elected us to do.”
The letter addressed to Rep. Stanton’s Mesa office was intercepted before delivery. The letters to Reps. Ansari and Grijalva were sent to former office addresses.
title: Stanton, Ansari, and Grijalva Statement on Suspicious Letters Sent to Arizona Offices

RALEIGH, N.C.– On October 12, 2026, Cyril Domaquik Clemens, 72, a Liberian native, and convicted child rapist, self-deported by boarding a one-way flight from RDU International Airport to Europe. In late September 2026, a federal judge sentenced Clemens for naturalization fraud and revoked his naturalized U.S. citizenship. The Judge ordered him to self-deport at his own expense. About three weeks later, while under the constant supervision of the U.S. Probation Office, the U.S. Attorney’s Office in the Eastern District of North Carolina made sure that he left the United States once and for all.

“We will always fight to protect our children, God’s most perfect blessing for each parent and the community, from the evil that lurks in the shadows. To have a noncitizen committing these heinous crimes against a 4-year-old child right here in Eastern North Carolina while lying on his application to fraudulently obtain the privilege of citizenship in this United States, the greatest country now or ever, is a shocking betrayal,” said U.S. Attorney Ellis Boyle. “We applaud the court for ordering that this spider self deport after being stripped of his citizenship, and you better believe we watched him until he did just that. Promises made, promises kept: Get Out and Stay Out.”

“We will always fight to protect our children, God’s most perfect blessing for each parent and the community, from the evil that lurks in the shadows. To have a noncitizen committing these heinous crimes against a 4-year-old child right here in Eastern North Carolina while lying on his application to fraudulently obtain the privilege of citizenship in this United States, the greatest country now or ever, is a shocking betrayal,” said U.S. Attorney Ellis Boyle. “We applaud the court for ordering that this spider self deport after being stripped of his citizenship, and you better believe we watched him until he did just that. Promises made, promises kept: Get Out and Stay Out.”

Clemen’s reign of horrific, deplorable child rape began in November of 2011 when he began sexually molesting a 4-year-old child. This continued for over a decade until he was arrested and convicted in North Carolina State court. On April 3, 2023, in Durham County North Carolina Superior Court, Clemens pleaded guilty to three counts of indecent liberties with a child. The North Carolina Superior Court Judge sentenced him to prison for a range from 16 to 29 months and ordered him to register as a sex offender.

Clemens confessed to sexually molesting and raping the 4-year-old child from November 2011, through March 2022. Clemens committed these crimes before he lied in his application to become a citizen submitted to U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (CIS). But, CIS did not know about his lies at that time because the state law enforcement officers did not arrest him until after he engaged in the solemn ceremony to be naturalized.

During the investigation, law enforcement officials discovered Clemens knowingly made materially false statements under penalty of perjury on his naturalization application paperwork. During a naturalization interview process with CIS, he responded “No” to the questions “Were you EVER involved in any way with any of the following…[f]orcing or trying to force, someone to have any kind of sexual contact or relations?” and “Have you EVER committed, assisted in committing, or attempted to commit, a crime or offense for which you were NOT arrested?” Both these answers were lies. Clemens took the oath of citizenship and naturalized on February 19, 2021. If CIS had known about his crimes prior to his application and ceremony, he would have never been granted the honor of citizenship.

ICE ERO, HSI agents assigned to the Document and Benefit Fraud Task Force, along with CIS’s Fraud Detection and National Security division, investigated the case as part of Operation False Haven - an ongoing initiative designed to aggressively target child molesters and other egregious felons who fraudulently obtain immigration benefits. They also worked with U.S. Probation to ensure that this child rapist Liberian noncitizen boarded a plane at his own expense to self deport and never return to the United States.

Ellis Boyle, U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of North Carolina, made the announcement. For more information on Clemens sentencing press release, go to: Clemens Sentencing Press Release
title: Get Out and Stay Out: Denaturalized Liberian Child Rapist Self Deported to Europe on a One-way Flight Out of the United States

DeLauro Statement on Reports of Secretary Hegseth Delaying Defensive Interceptor Missile Transfers to Ukraine
WASHINGTON – Earlier today, it was reported by the Washington Post that Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth is holding up the transfer of U.S.-made Patriot interceptor missiles from European countries to Ukraine. The missiles are a crucial component of Ukraine's air defenses, protecting civilians from Russian missile strikes. The interceptors were already sold to European allies under agreements that require U.S. approval before they can be transferred to Ukraine.
House Appropriations Committee Ranking Member Rosa DeLauro (D-CT-03) issued the following statement:
“Once again, by its neglect, the Trump administration is weakening Ukraine’s ability to defend itself against Russian aggression. The administration is putting civilians at risk from Russian strikes which are only increasing in intensity. Slow-walking the approval of these transfers is putting countless civilians directly in harm’s way.
“These are defensive missiles which intercept incoming Russian ordnance before they have a chance to demolish apartment buildings, schools, hospitals, or critical infrastructure in Ukraine. Withholding these transfers does nothing to de-escalate the conflict. It only encourages the aggressor to amplify its aggression. More innocent civilians will die if the Trump administration continues to hold up this aid.
“Secretary Hegseth must facilitate the swift transfer of these defensive munitions at once. As winter approaches and these Russian missiles take out Ukraine’s electric grid that provides heat to families, the humanitarian crisis in Ukraine will only worsen. And if the Trump administration continues on its current path, countless innocent lives will be lost. This is unconscionable.”
###
title: DeLauro Statement on Reports of Secretary Hegseth Delaying Defensive Interceptor Missile Transfers to Ukraine

text:
DEA New Orleans Field Division Kicks Off National Red Ribbon Week, Championing Prevention to Advance a Fentanyl-Free America
NEW ORLEANS – The Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) New Orleans Field Division announces its observance of National Red Ribbon Week, taking place October 23–31, 2026. As the nation’s largest and longest-running drug awareness and prevention campaign, Red Ribbon Week serves as the cornerstone of the agency’s prevention efforts across Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, and Arkansas.
This year’s national campaign supports DEA’s Fentanyl-Free America initiative, serving as a nationwide call-to-action to increase public awareness and education around highly addictive synthetic drugs containing fentanyl and other emerging threats.
The 2026 national Red Ribbon theme—developed in collaboration with the National Family Partnership and created by Griswold Middle School student Ava Tackett—is “Make a Difference. Be a Hero. Stay Drug Free,” highlighting how living a drug-free lifestyle helps build a brighter future.
“This year’s Red Ribbon theme captures the spirit of this movement, reminding us that we all have the power to make a difference,” said DEA Administrator Terry Cole. “That means understanding that dangerous and deadly drugs come in many forms, including powder, pills, and vapes. Vapes can contain nicotine, marijuana concentrates, and other illegal drugs, which can be extremely addictive. The annual Red Ribbon campaign is a reminder that we all play an important role in preventing drug misuse before it ever starts and achieving a Fentanyl-Free America.”
Locally, John P. Scott, Special Agent in Charge of the DEA New Orleans Field Division, emphasized the critical role of regional education and family engagement. “Red Ribbon Week honors the legacy and ultimate sacrifice of DEA Special Agent Enrique ‘Kiki’ Camarena, who gave his life in 1985 to protect our nation from illicit drug traffickers. Across our four-state division, we are working closely with schools, parents, and community partners to spark these vital conversations and protect our youth from the devastating impacts of fentanyl and counterfeit pills.”
Ways to Participate & Educational Resources:
- Virtual National Red Ribbon Rally: Available on demand throughout October at dea.gov/redribbon and getsmartaboutdrugs.com, featuring remarks from leadership, student awards, and prevention insights.
- Wear Red & #GoRed4RedRibbon: Show your commitment to a drug-free lifestyle and honor Special Agent Camarena's legacy by wearing red during October 23–31.
- Drugs of Abuse Publication: Access the newly released 2026 edition for science-based information regarding substances that endanger communities.
- Family & Youth Resources: Utilize free tools at GetSmartAboutDrugs.gov and JustThinkTwice.gov to talk openly with young people.
- National Contests: Explore the National Family Partnership’s Red Ribbon Photo Contest (redribbon.org) and the DEA/SAMHSA Campus Video PSA Contest (campusdrugprevention.gov/psacontest).
For more information on regional events and to access the Red Ribbon Toolkit, visit dea.gov/redribbon or dea.gov/divisions/new-orleans.
title: DEA New Orleans Field Division Kicks Off National Red Ribbon Week, Championing Prevention to Advance a Fentanyl-Free America

text:
ATF, local partners secure indictment of New Jersey man on arson charges linked to retail store fire
Baltimore, Maryland – A New Jersey man is faced indictment, Oct. 16, after using fire and explosive materials in a Maryland retail store.
Anthony John Rhodes, 37, of Short Pump, is charged with malicious destruction of property by fire. The charges stem from an incident in which Rhodes set a fire in an Elkton retail store during business hours while customers shopped.
Kelly O. Hayes, U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the indictment with Special Agent in Charge Charles Doerrer, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, and Chief Caroll H. Spriggs, II, Office of the Maryland State Fire Marshal.
According to the indictment, on April 29, Rhodes maliciously damaged and destroyed the store building, along with its merchandise and inventory.
An indictment is not a finding of guilt. Individuals charged by indictment are presumed innocent until proven guilty at a later criminal proceeding.
If convicted, Rhodes faces a minimum of five years and a maximum of 20 years in federal prison.
Actual sentences for federal crimes are typically less than the maximum penalties. A federal district court judge determines sentencing after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
U.S. Attorney Hayes commended the ATF and Office of the Maryland State Fire Marshal for their work in the investigation, along with Office of the State’s Attorney for Cecil County, for its valuable assistance. Ms. Hayes also thanked Assistant U.S. Attorney Victoria Liu who is prosecuting the federal case.
# # #
ATF protects American communities from violent crime driven by the illegal use of firearms, explosives, and acts of arson. Through crime gun intelligence, forensic analysis, and relentless investigation, we identify and arrest violent offenders and gang members, dismantle trafficking networks, and sever the supply chains arming cartels, prohibited persons, and terrorist organizations. We defend the rights of law-abiding citizens by safeguarding lawful commerce and upholding the Constitution of the United States. Learn more about what ATF is doing to reduce violent crime in your community by following us on X @ATFHQ, Instagram @ATFHQ, LinkedIn @ATF, and Facebook @HQATF, or on the web at www.atf.gov.

NEWARK, N.J. – A California man today admitted fraudulently obtaining over $4.6 million from a victim company based in New Jersey, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced today.

Joseph Rodriguez, 71, of Irvine, California, pleaded guilty today before U.S. Magistrate Judge José R. Almonte to Count One of an Indictment charging him with wire fraud.

According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court:

In January 2015, Rodriguez, through his company Old American Incorporated, entered into a factoring agreement with a New Jersey company (Victim-1) to obtain loans secured or collateralized by accounts receivable. Under the factoring agreement, in which a business sells its outstanding invoices to a third party for immediate cash, Old American retained control over customer relationships and debt collection and was required to pay back Victim-1 directly within 90 days.

From February 2023 through July 2023, Rodriguez submitted to Victim-1 fraudulent invoices for millions of dollars in future accounts receivable that Rodriguez falsely represented were owed to Old American. In fact, the customers listed in the invoices Rodriguez provided to Victim-1 did not owe money to Old American for outstanding invoices and there were no accounts payable to turn over. Based on the fraudulent invoices, Victim-1 sent over $4.6 million of advance payments to Rodriguez, which he did not return.

The count to which Rodriguez pleaded guilty carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison and a maximum fine of up to $250,000, or twice the gross gain to the defendant or loss to the victim, whichever is greatest. Sentencing is scheduled for February 23, 2027.

U.S. Attorney Frazer credited special agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy in Newark, with the investigation.

The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorney Farhana C. Melo of the Economic Crimes Unit in Newark.

PHILADELPHIA – United States Attorney David Metcalf announced that four area men have been sentenced to prison by United States District Judge Joshua D. Wolson for conspiring to steal and sell thousands of U.S. Treasury checks.

The defendants were charged by superseding indictment in May of 2025. All four pleaded guilty earlier this year to conspiracy to steal government funds, theft of government funds, and mail theft.

Saahir Irby , 28, and Tauheed Tucker , 25, both of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, were sentenced today by Judge Wolson — Irby to 63 months’ incarceration, three years of supervised release, restitution of $10,841,731.83, and forfeiture of $72,510, and Tucker to 42 months’ incarceration, three years of supervised release, restitution of $2,628,984.39, and forfeiture of $28,200.

Cory Scott , 26, of Ardmore, Pa., was sentenced on October 14 to 70 months in prison, three years of supervised release, restitution of $10,841,731.83, and forfeiture of $298,973.

Alexander Telewoda , 26, of Clifton Heights, Pa., was sentenced in August to 78 months in prison, three years of supervised release, restitution of $10,841,731.83, and forfeiture of $162,144.50.

As detailed in court filings and statements, between June 2023 and September 2024, Irby and Tucker, while working as United States Postal Service (“USPS”) mail processing clerks, stole thousands of envelopes containing U.S. Treasury checks from mail sorting machines at the USPS Philadelphia Processing and Distribution Center.

Irby and Tucker removed the checks from the USPS facility and sold them to defendants Scott and Telewoda, who then advertised the stolen checks for resale on the Telegram app. Upon receiving payment from interested buyers, Scott and Telewoda mailed the stolen Treasury checks to buyers around the country who attempted to cash the stolen checks.

Over the course of the scheme, Irby and Tucker sold Scott and Telewoda thousands of stolen Treasury checks whose face value exceeded $84 million. Scott’s and Telewoda’s customers successfully negotiated approximately $11 million worth of these stolen Treasury checks at financial institutions.

This case was investigated by the U.S. Postal Service Office of Inspector General, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration, Homeland Security Investigations, FBI, and Social Security Administration Office of Inspector General, with substantial assistance from the Montgomery County Detective Bureau, Lower Merion Township Police Department, and the Bureau of the Fiscal Service. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Jessica Rice.
title: Four Defendants Sentenced to Years in Prison for Conspiring to Steal and Sell U.S. Treasury Checks Worth Millions

Everyone knows that fentanyl will kill you dead, quick, but he didn’t care one bit about his victims in the New Bern community,” said U.S. Attorney Ellis Boyle. “This case is an example of a simple lesson: Drugs Kill, Prison Awaits – Do Right.”

In early 2023, the New Bern Police Department opened an investigation into Hodges and made several drug purchases at different locations around the city. Between March and July 2023, Hodges sold 29 grams of fentanyl and 63 grams of meth.
