FORT HUACHUCA, Ariz. — The communications security community celebrated the highly anticipated return of its modernized forum, renamed COMSEC Integration for Protecting and Hardening Environments for Resilience, held May 4-7, 2026. CIPHER is a COMSEC community collaboration and training forum hosted annually by the U.S. Army Information Systems Engineering Command, a Communications-Electronics Command major subordinate command.
Formerly known as the Global Integrated Partnership for COMSEC, or GIPC, the CIPHER forum was a resounding success, welcoming the COMSEC community and expressing enthusiasm for the return of this critical gathering. CIPHER continues to serve as a cornerstone event for the COMSEC community, providing attendees with unparalleled opportunities to learn the latest information about COMSEC policies and procedures. This COMSEC community forum allows attendees to gain valuable experience, collaborate directly with subject matter experts, and engage in meaningful discussions with the leaders who make and influence Army COMSEC decisions.
On May 4, the week commenced with a highly successful icebreaker social at a veteran-owned venue in Sierra Vista, Arizona. The event established a welcoming, networking environment for collaboration and training events in the days ahead.
For the first time, USAISEC broadcast the general assemblies live on Microsoft Teams for those unable to attend in person. During the general assemblies, attendees received 15 comprehensive briefings in total provided by key stakeholder partners, such as the U.S. Army Cyber Command; Department of the Army Headquarters G-2 and G-6; U.S. Transportation Command; U.S. Army Force Management Support Agency; Program Executive Office Command, Control, Communications and Network; Defense Courier Division and Product Manager, COMSEC. This forum featured a robust schedule designed to address current COMSEC challenges, initiatives, and strategic alignments.
On May 5, the general assembly concluded with a highlight: the annual Key Management Infrastructure Operating Account Manager Award was presented to Michelle Sutera of the Maryland Army National Guard's Joint Force Headquarters, G6. This award required 100 % COMSEC materiel accountability and a satisfactory audit rating with no findings during inspections.
“The strength of Army COMSEC has always come from our KOAMs and users in the field,” said Steven Downer, director of the USAISEC COMSEC Directorate. “That’s why recognizing our KOAM of the Year matters, and it’s why we’re modernizing how we support them.”
On May 7, Downer briefed the general assembly regarding the recent implementation of the Communications Security Operations Center during the final general assembly. Downer explained the CSOC uses continuous data integration to shift COMSEC management from a reactive approach to a predictive defense model. The CSOC accomplishes this by monitoring COMSEC readiness and analyzing account health, compliance, and risk. The CSOC monitoring activities allow proactive mitigation and forecasting to ensure Army networks remain secure, resilient, and ready for complex operations.
“Modernizing the event mirrors how we’re modernizing COMSEC through the CSOC, virtual audits and data-driven readiness tools that turn complexity into capability,” Downer said.
Additionally, CIPHER offered 28 specialized group sessions led by COMSEC subject matter experts from various organizations, allowing personnel to explore specific technical and operational COMSEC topics in greater depth. As a pilot test, USAISEC broadcast the Force Management System Website group session live on Microsoft Teams to explore offering all the group sessions in a hybrid setting in the future.
To modernize feedback collection from the COMSEC community, USAISEC also implemented online feedback forms for CIPHER attendees. The data collected from these online forms will enable USAISEC to improve future events and ensure successful training, collaboration, and networking for the COMSEC community.
The successful execution of the 2026 CIPHER forum marks a pivotal moment in the modernization of the Army’s COMSEC. By integrating hybrid attendance options, adopting data-driven feedback mechanisms, and unveiling forward-leaning initiatives like the CSOC, USAISEC is actively shaping the future of COMSEC to be more accessible and impactful than ever before. As the global threat landscape continues to evolve, the insights, collaboration, and training fostered at this cornerstone event will ensure the COMSEC community remains proactive, resilient, and fully equipped to turn operational complexity into mission-ready capability.
title: The return of a modernized forum for the communications security community

SAVANNAH, Georgia: The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Georgia , in coordination with the Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division , announced its comprehensive strategy to oversee federal voting protections and investigate potential election fraud as early voting begins in Georgia for the 2026 midterm elections .

The initiative is part of a nationwide effort to ensure a secure, transparent, and accessible voting process. The U.S. Attorney’s Office, alongside federal law enforcement partners, is prepared to enforce federal election laws vigorously while protecting the right of every legal voter to cast their ballot without intimidation or interference. Voters can consult official Department of Justice and state portals to review federal election laws and eligibility requirements.

“We are committed to maintaining public trust and instilling the public’s confidence in our democratic institutions. We will work closely with our federal, state, and local partners to safeguard the states polling places and mail-in ballots to ensure the integrity of the vote,” said U.S. Attorney Margaret E. “Meg” Heap for the Southern District of Georgia. “We will enforce federal voting rights laws impartially, ensuring every eligible citizen can cast their ballot securely and without fear of intimidation.”

Key Enforcement Priorities for the 2026 Election:

Protecting Voter Rights: Ensuring that all eligible voters can participate in early voting, absentee mail-in voting, and Election Day voting free from discrimination, harassment, or unlawful coercion.

Voter Eligibility and Enforcement: Monitoring compliance with federal laws regarding voter registration and eligibility. For detailed information on ongoing reviews, eligibility laws, or federal penalties, please consult official Department of Justice guidelines and state election authority resources.

Combating Election Fraud: Investigating actionable allegations of ballot harvesting, voter impersonation, or intentional disruption of polling places and mail-in ballot processing.

Absentee Mail-In and Early Voting in Georgia

Georgia state election officials have confirmed that early in-person voting, and absentee mail-in voting will proceed as scheduled under standard state protocols. Federal oversight will remain active throughout the early voting period to monitor for compliance with the Voting Rights Act and ensure that secure ballot drop boxes and polling locations are unhindered.

Reporting Election Irregularities

The public plays a critical role in maintaining election security. Anyone who witnesses or has direct knowledge of potential election fraud, voter intimidation, or unlawful voting activity is strongly encouraged to report it immediately.

Please visit the official FBI Tips Portal or contact local law enforcement to report potential election fraud or voting irregularities. Complaints regarding voter discrimination or civil rights violations can also be directed to the Civil Rights Division via the Department of Justice Civil Rights Reporting Portal .
title: U.S. Attorney’s Office Announces Election Integrity Plan for 2026 General Election and Early Voting in Georgia

Remarks

Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Shavkat Mirziyoyev, Uzbekistan President

Congress Center

Samarkand, Uzbekistan

October 19, 2026

PRESIDENT MIRZIYOYEV: (Via interpreter) Dear Mr. Rubio, I cordially want to welcome you here in Uzbekistan. Welcome to Uzbekistan, the ancient city of Samarkand. This is your first visit to the region and Uzbekistan, and I’m convinced that it will warrant a new milestone in our relationship in further development of the C5+1 format.

Despite of your busy schedule, you’ve arrived together with your wife and a large delegation of business people. And it is a great moment for us. I would like to congratulate you on your appointment as the President’s National Security Advisor. It means a lot. It reflects the great trust in you and in – it is also a recognition of your role in active advancement of U.S. interests globally, all over the world.

I kindly ask you to convey my best wishes to President Trump. I look forward very much to meeting him in Miami. In August, we had a very significant telephone communication, by phone, and we’ve agreed on strengthening our strategic partnership. In September, during the General Assembly, UN General Assembly, he spoke highly on our contribution to the work of the Board of Peace. And we will continue working together in advancing the noble objectives and – the noble objectives of the board.

Decisive and dramatic policy of President Trump is truly admirable, and it deserves the highest praise. Thanks to his efforts, Central Asia for the first time gains strategic attention of the United States of America.

I would like to also congratulate you on the successful conduction of the ministerial meetings, C5+1. And it was here 11 years ago when the foundation has been laid for that platform to happen.

We highly value firm commitment of the United States of America in strengthening sovereignty and independence of the countries of Central Asia. Your words on the vital role of our region for the United States of America is of a special value for all of us. We truly support all the priority areas of cooperation with Central Asia that you’ve proposed.

I am also very grateful to Mr. Gor for his great support in developing our relationship. Due to your efforts and the efforts of the chief of my administration, Business and Investment Council has become efficient mechanism to promote joint projects. We do not have this kind of format with any other country of the world. By following the current meeting of the council, there were agreements achieved worth of $12 billion U.S. dollars and for us, it’s a great achievement. Today we’ve launched a dialogue for enhanced strategic partnership.

And I would also like to congratulate you with the signing of a very important document on cooperation in the area of peaceful nuclear and exploration of the Artemis peace. And thank you so very much for that.

It is right now my pleasure to pass it over to you.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, thank you. First of all, thank you, Mr. President, for hosting us, for your entire team. It was a very warm welcome. As I said, it’s my first visit not just to the region but to your country, and we come away incredibly impressed by the progress you’ve made, but also by the opportunities that we have. It’s a feature of foreign relations that oftentimes crisis and problems dominate our attention and our time, and often that comes at the expense of opportunities. President Trump has made it a cornerstone of his foreign policy that not only are we going to address and deal with the current problems of the world and the crises in the world, because those must be dealt with, but we are also, at the same time, going to ensure that we pursue incredible opportunities that we think have historic and unprecedented value.

And that’s why three months ago we began planning for this C5+1 gathering and following up on the summit in Washington D.C. The opportunity that presents itself for both the United States and the countries of Central Asia are self-evident. Throughout history, Central Asia has played an enormous role in fostering trade and relations between Eastern and Western countries. And the extraordinary opportunity is the one that’s being created by seeing this region reopen both diplomatically and economically under leadership such as yours.

Uzbekistan in particular and Central Asia as a region is having a renaissance in commercial diplomacy, and the U.S. wants to be a part of that rejuvenation. Across a variety of key sectors that include energy, critical minerals, agriculture, transportation, technology, the United States is partnering with Uzbekistan and other Central Asian countries.

Now, we enter this with a clear view that each country that’s here at this ministerial today – and in particular the United States and Uzbekistan – are unique, sovereign nations, each with its own interests; which is why we celebrate the attitude of Central Asian countries, that they are open and willing to engage with the world, but doing so in ways that suit their needs and their ambitions for themselves and for their people.

Under President Trump, the United States is doing the exact same thing. And the exciting opportunity, therefore, is when your ambitions and your desires for your future and your needs and your national interests are aligned with ours. Because what’s important for you is also important for us. That creates the sort of partnerships that create ties that bind for generations. But for these to be beyond words, they require action.

And I believe what we’ve already accomplished at this meeting this week is action that is going to put our respective countries further down the path of long-term prosperity and security. Over the last few years, over the last few days, and I hope into the future, we will prove how working together as governments and with the private sector across many initiatives we can make sure that all of our countries remain strong and remain independent.

I spoke to the President, President Trump, not two hours ago, and he wanted me to convey to you his thanks for your leadership and for your openness. And he wanted me to acknowledge to you his recognition that the relationship between our countries is strong and growing stronger largely because of you and because of your leadership, and we’re excited to work with you and with all of our Central Asian partners to address the challenges and opportunities of this new era together. Thank you.

WASHINGTON – Today, the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) announced $9.5 million in awards to two tribal organizations that will provide hands-on, in-person manufacturing training and rapid reskilling for employees of 8(a) and HUBZone-eligible small businesses in critical industries through its Manufacturing in America Empower to Grow (E2G) Program. The funding will enable these organizations to deliver free courses, practical workshops, and one‑on‑one advising to small manufacturers to strengthen their operations and workforces, improve regulatory compliance, and increase their competitiveness in government contracting.
“Tribal communities have the talent and entrepreneurial drive to help lead America’s manufacturing comeback,” said Administrator Kelly Loeffler. “These awards will help translate that potential into greater capacity on the factory floor, more opportunities for skilled workers, and stronger businesses positioned to compete for new contracts. Under President Trump’s leadership, we are investing in the people and capabilities that will rebuild American industry and bring critical supply chains home.”
The SBA’s Office of Native American Affairs (ONAA) established this grant initiative as part of its mission to ensure Native American-owned small businesses have full access to the business development and expansion tools available through the SBA’s entrepreneurial development, lending, and procurement programs.
The E2G Program manufacturing grant recipients are:
Navajo Technical University
Geographic Scope: New Mexico (Main Campus); Arizona and Utah
Total Budget: $4,538,160
Description of Training Services: Navajo Technical University (NTU) presents an innovative, highly leveraged cross-disciplinary training initiative to take education beyond the classroom. The goal is to build and nurture a Tribally-led distributed manufacturing sector and workforce – including reskilling and upskilling workers – that will create and fill jobs on the Navajo Nation and in nearby Tribal communities. NTU will draw on Sa’ah Naagháí Bik’eh Hózhóón, a foundation of Diné collective knowledge, along with its hands-on training expertise, extensive partnerships, and trusted relationships, to work with the Navajo Nation and other partners to build a tribal small business-led distributed manufacturing sector and workforce. The proposed project will scale an existing mentor-protégé program between NTU’s world-class Center for Manufacturing and Ridgeline Manufacturing and Engineering, Inc., and will build on NTU’s 27 years of successful business and entrepreneurial programming and 47 years of providing technical assistance and workforce development.
Chippewa Sustainable Solutions Inc.
Geographic Scope: North Dakota
Total Budget: $5,000,000
Description of Training Services: The Chippewa Sustainable Solutions Inc. (CSS) Advanced Additive Manufacturing and Friction Stir Welding E2G Training & Technical Assistance Initiative uses the Turtle Mountain manufacturing environment in Belcourt, North Dakota. The project focuses on small manufacturers serving advanced manufacturing, metal fabrication, pre-engineered metal buildings, aerospace and defense, construction and infrastructure, energy, precision manufacturing, robotics, industrial machinery, and related domestic supply-chain sectors. CSS will leverage the Turtle Mountain advanced manufacturing environment and planned collaboration with the University of North Dakota (UND), Turtle Mountain Community College (TMCC), and the Center for Technology Commercialization (CTC), to deliver practical training, prototype demonstrations, process improvement assistance, and measurable business outcomes for participating firms.
The SBA is committed to rebuilding American supply chains and domestic manufacturing through a series of targeted initiatives. This year, the agency waived loan fees for manufacturing NAICS codes, established the first-ever loan program dedicated to American manufacturers, created a free onshoring portal for small businesses to onshore operations, and modernized the Small Business Investment Company (SBIC) program so more private capital flows into critical, supply‑chain‑sensitive industries. The agency also announced a new 90% Made in America Loan Guarantee for small manufacturers and continues to promote existing programs such as the asset-based 7(a) Working Capital Pilot (WCP) Program.
# # #
About the Empower to Grow Program
The Empower to Grow program, formerly known as 7(j) Management and Technical Assistance program, provides eligible U.S. small businesses with free business courses, tailored training, and one-on-one consulting to support their growth, operations, hiring, regulatory compliance, and government contracting competitiveness. The Empower to Grow program uplifts businesses to be procurement ready for federal, state, and local government contracts. For more questions about the Empower to Grow program, visit: Empower to Grow Program.
About the U.S. Small Business Administration
The U.S. Small Business Administration helps power the American dream of entrepreneurship. As the leading voice for small businesses within the federal government, the SBA empowers job creators with the resources and support they need to start, grow, and expand their businesses or recover from a declared disaster. It delivers services through an extensive network of SBA field offices and partnerships with public and private organizations. To learn more, visit www.sba.gov.

Washington D.C., Oct. 19, 2026 —
The Securities and Exchange Commission announced today that it will host a roundtable on November 9, 2026, to discuss the use of machine-understandable data and Super Intelligence (SI) and related risks and costs.
“In the age of SI, high-quality information is critical. The roundtable will facilitate insightful discussions on the public’s use of machine-understandable data and SI along with associated risks and costs,” said Joshua White, Chief Economist and Director of the Division of Economic and Risk Analysis. “Feedback from market participants will give the SEC staff insight on how the market and investing public are using machine-understandable data for SI solutions and inform the SEC staff on how the Commission can better facilitate SI.”
The roundtable will be open to the public and held at the SEC’s headquarters at 100 F Street, N.E., Washington, D.C. from 9 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. EST. Please note that the number of in-person participants may be limited and visitors will be subject to security checks. The discussion will be streamed live on SEC.gov, and a recording will be available at a later date.

Pallone, Booker Push to Protect Critical Fish That Sustain New Jersey’s Marine Wildlife and Fishing Industry
Lawmakers call for major cuts to Atlantic menhaden catch to protect Jersey Shore ecosystem
WASHINGTON, DC – Congressman Frank Pallone, Jr. (NJ-06) and Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ) are calling for stronger protections for Atlantic menhaden, a small fish that plays an enormous role in New Jersey’s coastal ecosystem. Commonly known as bunker, menhaden are a vital food source for avian and marine wildlife. The lawmakers are urging the Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission (ASMFC) to significantly reduce fishing limits to ensure enough menhaden remain in the water to sustain the species that depend on them.
A 2025 scientific assessment found that the estimated average menhaden biomass was 37 percent lower than previously thought. The assessment also showed that cuts of 50 percent or more would be needed to reduce the likelihood of fishing pressure meeting or exceeding an ecological target designed to account for the food needs of striped bass. Despite those findings, the Commission reduced the coastwide catch limit by just 20 percent for 2026.
“This level of reduction is insufficient to address the ecological consequences of declining menhaden abundance. Reduced menhaden availability has been identified as the primary driver of low reproduction in ospreys throughout the Chesapeake Bay. A significant cut to the menhaden TAC is needed to prevent broad ecosystem impacts. We, therefore, urge the Commission to adopt a substantial reduction in the Atlantic menhaden TAC that reflects the best available science and supports the rebuilding of dependent species, and by extension the communities in our state and throughout the Atlantic Coast that rely on them,” the members wrote.
In a letter to ASMFC Atlantic Menhaden Management Board Chair Joe Cimino, Pallone and Booker warn that excessive menhaden harvesting, including industrial operations that process the fish into fish meal and oil, reduces the food available to predators throughout the Atlantic ecosystem. They argue that fishing limits must account not only for the health of the menhaden population itself, but also for the striped bass, bluefish and other species that depend on it.
The warning comes amid growing concerns about declining osprey reproduction along the Atlantic Coast. In New Jersey, researchers documented the state’s worst osprey breeding season in more than three decades in 2025. Research in the Chesapeake Bay has also identified reduced menhaden availability as a primary driver of poor osprey reproduction, underscoring the broader consequences of declining food supplies for coastal wildlife.
Mark Taylor states that, “As President of the Jersey Coast Anglers Association, with next year’s total allowable catch limits on the table, it’s vital that a major cut is made. We have been here before, and we saw our waters explode with life once the cutback was made back in 2013. Our member clubs all have watched menhaden disappear from New Jersey waters except for a short window in early spring and late fall. They’re gone. And when bunker disappear, everything that depends on them—striped bass, whales, tuna, dolphins, osprey, eagles—pays the price. We need fisheries managers to step in now and shut down industrial‑scale reduction fishing before it wipes out what’s left of the stock. At this point, a full stop on reduction fishing in the New Jersey–New York Bight isn’t just reasonable—it’s the only responsible move if we want our coastal ecosystem to recover.”
The Commission is expected to consider new coastwide fishing limits for 2027 through 2029 at its November meeting. Pallone and Booker are urging regulators to adopt a substantial reduction based on the best available science to protect New Jersey’s marine wildlife, recreational fishing communities and the health of the Atlantic Coast.
###
title: Pallone, Booker Push to Protect Critical Fish That Sustain New Jersey’s Marine Wildlife and Fishing Industry

Foreign Military Sales: Congressional Notification

Bureau of Political-Military Affairs

October 19, 2026

Transmittal #26-120

The U.S. Department of State has made a determination approving a possible Foreign Military Sale to the Government of the Netherlands for its purchase of Counter-Unmanned Aerial Systems Platforms and related equipment. The estimated total cost is $294 million.

The Government of the Netherlands has requested to buy sixteen (16) OT-228/U Common Infrared Countermeasure systems; and thirty-eight (38) AN/APR-39E(V)2 Radar Warning Receivers. The following non-MDE items will also be included: U.S. Government technical assistance with incidental travel; transportation; technical data and reports; ancillary items; nonrecurring engineering; site surveys; new equipment training; and other related elements of logistics and program support.

This proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by improving the security of a NATO ally which is an important force for political stability and economic progress in Europe.

The proposed sale will modernize the Netherlands’ armed forces, expand its capability to strengthen homeland defense, and deter regional threats. This enhanced capability will contribute to the Netherlands’ military goals of updating capability while further enhancing interoperability with the United States and other allies. The Netherlands will have no difficulty absorbing these articles and services into its armed forces.

The proposed sale of this equipment and support will not alter the basic military balance in the region.

The principal contractor will be Northrop Grumman, located in Rolling Meadows, Illinois. At this time, the U.S. Government is not aware of any offset agreement proposed in connection with this potential sale. Any offset agreement will be defined in negotiations between the purchaser and the contractor.

Implementation of this proposed sale will not require the assignment of any additional U.S. Government or contractor representatives to The Netherlands.

There will be no adverse impact on U.S. defense readiness as a result of this proposed sale.

For further information, please contact the Bureau of Political-Military Affairs Outreach Team at T_Outreach_PM@State.gov .

Justice Department Charges 28 Foreign Nationals in California for Election Crimes
Federal law enforcement throughout California today arrested 11 foreign nationals living in the United States who are among 28 total charged in criminal complaints with federal crimes, including that they fraudulently registered to vote in U.S. elections, electoral contests in which most of them cast illegal and fraudulently obtained ballots.
Today’s arrests are part of “Operation Protect the Vote” – a coordinated effort among all four California-based United States Attorney’s Offices to combat and root out fraud in U.S. elections and protect electoral integrity.
All 28 foreign nationals charged are lawful permanent residents (LPRs), or “green card” holders. Although LPRs have legal immigration status in the United States, they are not U.S. citizens and are not permitted to vote in U.S. elections.
The criminal charges include making false statements in a naturalization application and some of the defendants also are charged with fraudulent voter registration. Both charges are felonies that carry a maximum penalty of five years in federal prison.
The defendants arrested today are expected to make their initial appearances this afternoon in U.S. District Courts. No pleas will be taken today.
On Oct. 13, the federal government provided a list of these individuals to California to ensure that their vote-by-mail ballots were set aside until these individuals’ citizenship status could be confirmed. California declined to assist the federal government in setting aside their ballots, prompting a lawsuit by the United States that seeks a court order to prevent the unlawful dilution of American citizens’ votes and to uphold the integrity of our elections.
“Every illegal vote cancels out the vote of a lawful American citizen,” said Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter. “Each of the 28 defendants charged today appears on the list of more than 20,000 likely noncitizen registrants we provided to California election officials last week. California refused to look at that list. Today's charges show exactly what that refusal puts at risk. California must verify the citizenship of those more than 20,000 registrants before mail-in ballots are counted.”
“Today’s arrests prove what we have been saying,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli. “California is mailing ballots to noncitizens, and they are refusing to comply with federal law, which makes it a crime for noncitizens to vote. The voting rights of American citizens must be protected.”
“Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) is committed to protecting the integrity of our nation’s electoral process by investigating allegations of criminal conduct that undermine public confidence in our elections,” said HSI Acting Executive Associate Director John A. Condon. “Working with our federal, state, and local law enforcement partners, we will continue to pursue those who knowingly violate federal law, while ensuring that every investigation is conducted fairly, thoroughly, and consistent with due process.”
According to court documents, the defendants knowingly and willfully lied under oath in their voter registration applications that they were U.S. citizens to be permitted to vote in California. Their fraudulent voter registration applications were approved, and, in many cases, the defendants illegally voted in recent U.S. elections. They subsequently lied in their paperwork to become naturalized U.S. citizens that they had never claimed U.S. citizenship, nor had they registered to vote or voted in U.S. elections.
Broken down by jurisdiction, the following defendants are charged in today’s takedown:
Central District of California
All the following defendants below in this jurisdiction face felony charges,
including false statements in a naturalization application:
- Omar Alexander Muñoz, 72, a Belizean national living in Commerce, California, fraudulently registered to vote in September 2019, claiming his was a U.S. citizen, then voted in U.S. elections in 2020, twice in 2022, and in 2024. He also lied on his application to become a naturalized U.S. citizen when he falsely stated under oath to have never claimed to be a U.S. citizen.
- Amandeep Kaur, 30, an Indian national living in Rancho Palos Verdes, California, and who is seeking to become a U.S. citizen, fraudulently registered to vote in December 2022 and voted in the November 2024 U.S. election.
- Ana Domínguez, 60, a Salvadoran national living in Long Beach, California, fraudulently registered to vote in July 2006 and lied in her naturalization paperwork in March 2026.
- Axel Giovani Prera García, 46, a Guatemalan national and Pico Rivera, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote in 2002 and 2005, and lied in his naturalization paperwork in June 2025.
- Flavio Alejandro Zúñiga, 43, a Mexico national and La Puente, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote in 2003 and lied in his naturalization paperwork in February 2026.
- Butleng Taing, 43, a Cambodian national living in Long Beach, fraudulently registered to vote in July 2021, voted in the 2022 and 2024 U.S. elections, and lied on his naturalization paperwork in August 2025.
- Carlos Antonio Galeas, 54, a Honduran national and West Covina, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote in 2012 and 2016, then lied in his naturalization paperwork in September 2018.
- Ernest Gutiérrez Ruvalcaba, 57, a Mexican national living in Wilmington, California, fraudulently registered to vote in February 2024 and voted one month later.
- Jesús Narez-Madrigal, 52, a Mexican national living in Carson, California, fraudulently registered to vote in 2014, voted in the 2024 U.S. general election, and lied in his naturalization paperwork in June 2024.
- José Antonio Bañuelos-Díaz, 42, a Mexican national and West Adams, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote in 2007 and lied on his naturalization paperwork in March 2025.
- Muhammad Khan, 50, a Pakistani national and Anaheim, California, resident, submitted a provisional ballot in 2020 and lied on his naturalization paperwork five years later.
- Rouzbeh Seyamaknejad, 63, a Canadian national and Rancho Palos Verdes, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote in December 2018, lied in his naturalization application in January 2024, and voted in the November 2024 U.S. election.
- Sulema de León, 35, a Mexican national and Long Beach, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote in 2013, lied on her naturalization application in 2019, and voted in the November 2020 U.S. general election.
Eastern District of California
The following defendants are charged with voting by an alien in a federal election, a misdemeanor that carries a statutory maximum sentence of one year in federal prison:
- Maricela Nazarín González, 43, a Mexican national living in Clovis, California, registered to vote in 2020, indicating that she was a U.S. citizen, and voted in elections in 2022, twice in 2024, and 2025.
- Rony de Jesús Sicaja, 38, a Guatemalan national living in Fresno, California, fraudulently registered to vote in 2017, and voted in the June 2022 primary election and the November 2024 general election in the United States.
- Camino Giles Jiménez, 51, a Mexican national living in Kerman, California, knowingly voted in three U.S. elections despite knowing he is a noncitizen, the most recent election being the June 2026 primary.
- Juan Antonio Rivas García, 46, a Mexican national and Sacramento, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote in 2018 and 2020, both times falsely asserting under oath that he was a U.S. citizen. Rivas voted in the 2022 and 2024 U.S. elections.
- Giezell Viduya Adawag, 41, a Philippines national and Vacaville, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote the day of the November 2024 general election, falsely certified that she was a U.S. citizen, and voted in the election that day.
- Kamlesh Navnitlal Shah, 67, an Indian national living in Sacramento, California, fraudulently registered to vote on the day of the November 2024 general election and voted that day. He is charged via information.
Northern District of California
The following defendants are charged with attempted procurement of
naturalization contrary to law, false statement under oath in any matter relating to naturalization or citizenship, and voting by an alien:
- Verónica Bullene, 43, a.k.a. “Verónica Hernández Martínez,” a Mexican national living in Petaluma, California, made false statements on her naturalization application that she had never claimed to be a U.S. citizen when, in fact, she did so under penalty of perjury to register to vote in 2022 and 2023 then voted in 2024.
- David Shapiro, 41, a Georgian national living in San Jose, California, fraudulently registered to vote in 2024 and later voted in a U.S. election, and made false statements on his naturalization application that he had never claimed to be a U.S. citizen.
- Moe Thida Lwin, 57, a Myanmar national and Daly City, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote in 2024 and then proceeded to illegally vote in a U.S. citizen. She made false statements on her naturalization paperwork as well.
- Manakotau Mataele Finau, 61, a Tongan national and Hayward, California, resident, fraudulently registered to vote in the 2024 election then vote, then lied about it in naturalization paperwork.
- Maribel del Carmen Garcés Barriga, 62, an Ecuadoran national and San Francisco, California, resident, made false statements in her naturalization paperwork that she never claimed U.S. citizenship and had never voted in a U.S. election or had registered to vote. In fact, Garcés fraudulently registered to vote in 2024 and proceeded to vote in a U.S. election.
Southern District of California
The following defendants are charged with false claim to citizenship to vote, unlawful attempted procurement of naturalization, and false statement under oath in matter relating to naturalization or citizenship:
- José Probitsado Amaro, 51, a citizen of the Philippines living in National City, California, fraudulently registered to vote by falsely claiming to be a U.S. citizen. He then cast a ballot in the November 2024 general election and made false statements during his naturalization interview, denying that he had ever claimed U.S. citizenship and misrepresenting his voting history.
- Jennifer Jung, 31, a Canadian national living in San Diego, California, fraudulently registered to vote by falsely claiming to be a U.S. citizen. She then cast a ballot in the November 2024 general election and made false statements during her naturalization interview, denying that she had ever claimed U.S. citizenship and misrepresenting her voting history.
- Erick Ronaldo Soto Mendizábal, 64, a citizen of Guatemala and former Oceanside, California, resident now living in Moreno Valley, California, fraudulently registered to vote by falsely claiming to be a U.S. citizen. He then cast a ballot in the November 2024 general election and made false statements in his naturalization application, denying that he had ever claimed U.S. citizenship and misrepresenting his voting history.
- Pamele Arbués Line, 56, a citizen of the Philippines living in Escondido, California, registered to vote, cast a ballot in the November 2024 general election, and made false statements in her naturalization interview, denying that she had ever claimed U.S. citizenship and misrepresenting her voting history.
A complaint, indictment, and information merely contain accusations. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

Ranking Members Lofgren and Amo Demand Answers After GAO Report Reveals Trump-Inflicted Damage to America’s Future Weather Satellites
“The White House and OMB decided that it was more important to blind the country to climate change than to help the country more clearly see the weather and the public safety threats right in front of it.”
(Washington, DC) – Today, Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren (D-CA) and Environment Subcommittee Ranking Member Gabe Amo (D-RI) sent a letter to National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Administrator Neil Jacobs regarding NOAA’s GeoXO satellite program. GeoXO is the future fleet of the nation’s weather satellites scheduled to replace the current satellites in the 2030’s and collect life-saving data to support weather forecasting. In early 2025, the Trump administration demanded that NOAA cut the GeoXO program by 50% and exclusively focus on the Agency’s “weather data needs,” disguising blatant climate denialism as an effort to cut costs. GAO released its report on Friday, October 16, 2026, and found that the Trump administration’s actions “put vital observations at risk.”
“Two fewer satellites and three fewer scientific instruments are not line items in a budget,” Ranking Members Lofgren and Amo write in their letter. “They represent a concrete, tangible weakening of America’s ability to understand the weather, the climate, and the world around us.”
The Members continue: “We now confront the real possibility that America’s next generation of weather satellites will be no better – or even worse – than the generation in orbit today. As GAO concludes in its report, ‘it is unclear whether GeoXO will improve, or even continue, the functionality available in the current generation of satellites.’ That is an unacceptable notion, and we are determined to return this program to its proper path."
In closing, the Members focus in on the hypocrisy of the administration’s claims that these cancellations are to save costs, pointing to the war in Iran: “In exchange for a less advanced, less capable next generation of weather satellites, the only meager rationale the Trump Administration can muster is $6.6 billion in reduced lifecycle costs. At a time when the war in Iran has cost the country an estimated $38 billion and counting while President Trump proposes to spend another $1.2 trillion on checks intended to lessen the political fallout of that war, it is hard to think of a more foolish, self-defeating way to save money than by stripping capabilities from a weather satellite program of vital long-term national significance. The Trump Administration has the wrong priorities, but NOAA must get GeoXO right. We expect nothing less.”

Army leaders are working to give Soldiers and Families more time to prepare for a permanent change of station move and more support once they arrive. At the Association of the United States Army’s Warfighter and Family Forum II on Oct. 13, they described changes to household goods shipments, in-processing, medical care and housing—along with work still to be done.
The forum, “Enhancing the Permanent Change of Station and Onboarding & Integration Experience,” brought together leaders who oversee the transition. Their discussion returned to a central point: A move is not complete when the boxes are delivered. Soldiers and Families also need care, housing and a connection to their new unit and community.
Maj. Gen. Lance Curtis, Commander of the Department of War Personal Property Activity, said the organization reduced a backlog of 18,000 shipments in May 2025 to zero currently. A joint operations center and a single call center help track and resolve moving problems across the services.
Curtis said: “If you leave here today with only two things that you remember, encourage service members, Families and spouses to call 1-833-MIL-MOVE, where they will talk to an active duty service member if they’re having a challenge. We can solve almost any challenge on the spot from start to finish. Or use the website ppa.mil.”
Curtis noted service members with orders can begin booking household goods moves 48 days earlier than previously. They also now have one year, rather than nine months, to file a claim for damaged property, and their spouse or dependent who is listed on their orders can also now file an inconvenience claim. The organization, which is in the process of becoming a full agency, plans to replace its moving system with a new platform that includes mobile tools for vehicle shipments, household goods bookings and claims over the next two years.
After Curtis’ keynote address and audience questions, Sgt. Maj. Ruben Murillo Jr., Senior Enlisted Advisor to the Assistant Secretary of the Army for Manpower and Reserve Affairs, opened a separate panel discussion on the PCS and onboarding experience. Lt. Gen. Charles T. Lombardo, the Army’s Deputy Chief of Staff, G-1, said the Army wants to move beyond sponsorship that amounts to a name and phone number. Using the Integrated Personnel and Pay System – Army as a backbone, the goal is to share information earlier, reduce duplicate paperwork and give leaders more time to welcome incoming Soldiers and Families.
“The biggest thing we can do is get you to your squad leader, your platoon sergeant, your platoon leader,” Lombardo said. Getting pay and housing settled first makes it easier for a Soldier to focus on the unit, he added.
Lt. Gen. James M. Smith, Commanding General of U.S. Army Installation Management Command, said installation personnel offices are working to process orders earlier so Families can plan their moves. His team also reviews Families displaced from housing and monitors how quickly homes are made ready for incoming residents. Smith said the standard between occupants is 10 days, though some homes require more work.
Smith said his team holds housing providers to the turnaround standard. “We hold ourselves accountable,” he added. He also highlighted the Civilian Employment Assignment Tool, which helps spouses working in Army Child and Youth Services seek positions at a new installation before they move.
David H. Dentino, Deputy Assistant Secretary of the Army for Installations, Housing and Partnerships, said tenant satisfaction surveys help determine where housing needs attention. Installations use low scores to develop improvement plans, while the results also inform longer-term investments. Dentino said barracks scored lowest among the housing categories surveyed and outlined efforts to assess barracks conditions, improve heating and cooling systems and identify conditions that could lead to mold.
“Those improvements are directly driven by the results we see in the tenant satisfaction survey,” Dentino said of planned Family housing investments. He urged incoming Families to contact their installation’s Housing Services Office, which can help with off-post rentals, deposits and landlord disputes.
That same advance planning applies to medical care. Lt. Gen. Mary K. Izaguirre, the Army Surgeon General, encouraged Families to review specialty referrals, prescriptions, ongoing appointments and records from civilian providers before leaving. She pointed to Tricare’s moving checklist and said her team is working with the Defense Health Agency to improve the handoff between locations.
Izaguirre said the installation a Soldier is leaving remains responsible for behavioral health care during the move: “They are responsible for your care until you sign in at that new installation.” She encouraged those already receiving behavioral health care to discuss the move with their providers in advance and noted that telehealth may help maintain access during the transition. Izaguirre also highlighted that spouses can now access the Exceptional Family Member Program system and acknowledged that access to older children’s medical records remains a barrier the Army is working to address.
Command Sgt. Maj. Christopher C. Goodart, Division Command Sergeant Major, 101st Airborne Division, Fort Campbell, Kentucky, said reception and integration start when a Soldier is placed on assignment. A six-day reception process brings finance, transportation and other administrative support together before brigades tailor training and introductions to the Soldier’s next unit. The aim is for a squad leader to receive someone who is “ready to go and ready to fight,” Goodart said, while giving the Soldier and Family time to settle in.
The panel also looked beyond the installation gate. Smith said most Soldiers and Families live off post, making local schools, housing providers and community leaders part of the arrival experience.
In his closing remarks, Lombardo emphasized that Soldier and Family feedback will guide the Army’s broader effort to make personnel and transition services easier to access by smartphone. “The most important thing we have is our Soldiers and their Families and that feedback, because that’s going to drive the speed and direction that we go as we continue to modernize these experiences,” he said.
He described a goal of giving Families one place to look for housing, enroll their children in school and manage their transition. Helping Families navigate those changes, he said, can improve their Army experience and help retain the all-volunteer force.
Murillo urged leaders to ask incoming Soldiers what they need and carry that feedback into their work with local partners.
“Know your Soldiers, know what your Soldiers are saying,” Murillo said.
Watch the panel discussion in its entirety at DVIDS.
title: Army Leaders Discuss Changes to Improve PCS Experience at Warfighter and Family Forum

LEXINGTON, Ky. – A Paris, Ky., man, Adrian Kmari Lattimore, 31, was sentenced on Friday, October 16, 2026, to 26 months by U.S. District Judge Robert Wier for conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute a mixture or substance containing fentanyl and carfentanil. Judge Wier previously imposed sentences of 99 months and 180 months imprisonment for Lattimore’s two co-defendants.

From March 29 through April 2, 2025, a coordinated law enforcement operation led to the seizure of a significant amount of suspected carfentanil and the arrest of Lattimore, and his two co-defendants, Craig Williams and Jerome Newton, who were involved in a multi‑state narcotics trafficking conspiracy scheme.

According to Lattimore’s plea agreement, on March 29, 2025, Williams contacted a confidential informant offering to sell “car.” Williams displayed the drugs via a Facetime call, later arranging an in‑person meeting in Cincinnati, where he and Newton provided a sample of the substance.

The following day, Williams and Newton traveled to Lexington to complete the sale. Williams advised the informants that the narcotics were stored in a vehicle at a local establishment and were being held by a third associate, Lattimore. Surveillance footage captured Lattimore transferring the suspected drugs. Shortly after the transfer, law enforcement seized the narcotics and arrested Williams, Newton, and Lattimore. Laboratory testing confirmed the presence of fentanyl, carfentanil, and morphine in the narcotics.

Newton and Williams have previously been sentenced for their role in the drug trafficking conspiracy and received 180 months and 99 months, respectively. According to Lattimore’s plea agreement, he qualified for sentencing reductions based on his minimal participation in the scheme and his lack of criminal history.

Carfentanil is a synthetic opioid used as a tranquilizing agent for elephants and other large mammals. The lethal dose range for Carfentanil in humans is unknown; however, Carfentanil is approximately 10,000 times more potent than morphine and 100 times more potent than fentanyl. Fentanyl can be lethal at the 2-milligram range, depending on route of administration and other factors.

Jason Parman, United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Kentucky; Olivia Olson, Special Agent in Charge, FBI, Louisville Field Office; Commissioner Phillip “PJ” Burnett, Kentucky State Police; and Chief Lawrence Weathers, Lexington Police Department, jointly announced the sentence.

“The April 2025 operation demonstrates the effectiveness of the law enforcement partnerships that exist throughout the Commonwealth of Kentucky. Working together, the FBI and our partners will not stand by while violent criminals run illegal drug trafficking operations throughout our communities,” said Special Agent in Charge Olivia Olson of the FBI Louisville Field Office. “If you are a violent criminal running drugs and guns on the streets of Kentucky, let this serve as a warning that the FBI will find you and ensure justice is served.”

The investigation was conducted by the FBI, Kentucky State Police, and Lexington Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Mary Melton prosecuted the case on behalf of the United States.

– END –
title: Final Defendant Sentenced in Fentanyl and Fentanyl Analogue Trafficking Conspiracy

West Virginia Man Sentenced to 30 Years in Prison for Aggravated Sexual Abuse of a Child Abroad
Dustin Stover Bowles, 42, of West Virginia, was sentenced to 30 years in prison for aggravated sexual abuse of a child under the age of 12.
According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, between September 2006 and December 2006, Bowles sexually abused a minor while he babysat her at his home. The victim disclosed the abuse to several trusted adults in 2020, as well as Army criminal investigators. Bowles was later charged under the Military Extraterritorial Jurisdiction Act. At the time of his criminal conduct, Bowles had been on active duty with the Army stationed in Hanau, Germany.
At trial, witnesses testified that Bowles frequently babysat the minor victim and described Bowles as a fun “uncle.” The victim testified that when the defendant babysat her in 2006, Bowles reached his hand into her pants underneath her underwear and directly touched her genitals while she pretended to be asleep. The victim was eight years old when Bowles sexually abused her. Additionally, three other victims testified that the defendant sexually abused them while they were asleep, including one victim who was a minor at the time of the sexual abuse. On April 17, a jury convicted Bowles of aggravated sexual abuse of a minor under the age of 12 while abroad as a member of the armed forces.
Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division, U.S. Attorney Moore Capito for the Southern District of West Virginia, and Assistant Director Heith Janke of the FBI’s Criminal Division made the announcement.
The FBI and the U.S. Army’s Criminal Investigation Division investigated the case.
Trial Attorney Eduardo Palomo of the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS) and Assistant U.S. Attorney Jennifer Rada Herrald for the Southern District of West Virginia are prosecuting the case.
This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, visit www.justice.gov/psc.

SAN ANTONIO – An illegal alien from Cuba was sentenced in a federal court in San Antonio to 210 months in prison for labor trafficking, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas.

According to court documents, Yoirlan Tome-Rojas, 46, helped bring three adult females from Cuba to the U.S. by paying for their flights, drivers, hotels, and the coyotes who smuggled them across the U.S.-Mexico border. Tome-Rojas charged the women a travel debt up to $50,000 each and forced them to work in strip clubs seven days a week. Throughout the months the women were in his custody, he transported them to Indiana, Detroit, Michigan, and San Antonio for them to work in various clubs.

Tome-Rojas required the women to provide him with all of their earnings and prohibited them from leaving or ending their work until their respective travel debts were paid off. He continually added the cost of food, clothes, shelter, transportation, and more to their travel debts.

Two of the women were with Tome-Rojas for approximately three months and, according to Tome-Rojas, only paid approximately $1,000 toward their debt. Throughout their victimization, the women feared for their own safety and for the safety of their families in Cuba.

Tome-Rojas pleaded guilty on June 3 to three counts of labor trafficking. He was sentenced by U.S. District Judge Xavier Rodriguez to 210 months in federal prison on each of the three counts to run concurrently.

“As an illegal alien himself, Tome-Rojas smuggled three women out of Cuba, buried them in tens of thousands of dollars in debt, and forced them to work in strip clubs across multiple states while fearing for their own lives and the lives of their loved ones,” said U.S. Attorney Simmons. “This is modern-day slavery, and it is more common in our communities than many Americans realize. This office, along with our partners at ICE Homeland Security Investigations, will continue to hunt down and prosecute any trafficker who thinks they can exploit vulnerable people on American soil and get away with it.”

“This 17 ½ year prison sentence reflects the brutality of Tome-Rojas’ crimes and HSI’s continued commitment to dismantling human-trafficking networks,” said Special Agent in Charge, John A. Pasciucco, HSI. “Tome-Rojas preyed on vulnerable women, smuggled them into the United States, and trapped them in a cycle of fear, coercion and escalating debt while stealing the proceeds of their labor. HSI will continue to tirelessly pursue those who treat human beings as commodities and ensure survivors could reclaim their freedom.”

Immigration and Customs Enforcement Homeland Security Investigations and the San Antonio Police Department investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Alicia McNab and Karina O’Daniel prosecuted the case.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

title: Illegal Alien Who Forced Three Cuban Women to Work in Strip Clubs Sentenced to Over 17 Years in Federal Prison

Coast Guard reopens the Port of Saipan and opens the Port of Guam for daylight operations as post-Champi recovery operations continue
SANTA RITA, Guam — U.S. Coast Guard Forces Micronesia/Sector Guam crews are working to assess aids to navigation and channel conditions across the Marianas Monday following Super Typhoon Champi which passed south of Guam Sunday.
The Captain of the Port issued Port Heavy Weather Condition (PWHC) Modified WHISKEY in Saipan at 6 p.m. Sunday and fully opened Saipan at 8 a.m. Monday. Under PHWC WHISKEY status, the Port of Saipan is open to commercial traffic and cargo operations. The Captain of the Port set PHWC Modified Whiskey in Guam at 2 p.m. Monday.
The ports of Tinian and Rota remain closed while U.S. Coast Guard teams and port stakeholders conduct post-storm assessments of waterways and navigational aids.
“We are working to reopen the ports as soon as it is safe to do so,” said Capt. Jessica Worst, commander of U.S. Coast Guard Forces Micronesia/Sector Guam and Captain of the Port Guam and Northern Mariana Islands. “My teams are actively engaged in on-water and aerial assessments to thoroughly and systematically identify all storm impacts and hazards to navigation. We appreciate the coordinated efforts of our public and private partners to conduct expeditious assessments that allow the safe, reopening of maritime commerce.”
The U.S. Coast Guard asks the public and maritime community to take three actions:
- Report any maritime distress immediately via VHF Channel 16 or by calling 911. Social media is not monitored for emergencies and must not be used to report distress. Widespread VHF outages persist, which means some calls may be relayed by partner agencies or other mariners. Utilize multiple forms of communication.
- Rely on official sources for reopening and safety information: NWS Guam (weather.gov/gum) and Guam Homeland Security/Office of Civil Defense (ghs.guam.gov) and CNMI EOC State Warning Point (facebook.com/cnmieocswp).
- Observe water safety. Even as Champi moves away, the ocean remains dangerous and response ability remains limited. The marine conditions remain life threatening. Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties, piers and docks and into dangerous seas.
The U.S. Coast Guard echoes the National Weather Service's guidance:
Everyone should stay out of the water and off jetties, piers and other waterside infrastructure. Mariners should recognize that dangerous marine conditions persist and defer any non-essential operations until seas subside.
Mariners with emergencies should contact the U.S. Coast Guard Joint Rescue Sub-Center Guam on VHF-FM Channel 16 or at (671) 355-4824.

Congresswoman Schrier Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Protect Wetland Habitats, Species in Washington State
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) joined Congresswoman Val Hoyle (OR-04) and Congressman Ryan Zinke (MT-01) in introducing the Northwest Wetlands Voluntary Incentives Program (NW VIP) Act, bipartisan legislation that would restore and protect wetland habitats and species in the Pacific Northwest. Companion legislation was introduced in the Senate by Sens. Mike Crapo (R-ID) and Ron Wyden (D-OR).
“Farmers, Tribes, and local communities across our region rely on wetlands and the species they protect,” said Congresswoman Schrier. “I am proud that this bipartisan bill will take a meaningful step to make sure Washingtonians continue to benefit from these important habitats that are a critical part of our ecosystem.”
“Conservation is a team effort, and everyone needs to play their part,” said Congresswoman Hoyle. “Our bipartisan bill supports habitat restoration and active management of invasive species across Northwest wetlands that support Tribes, farmers and other local economies. This work will strengthen our climate resilience, supporting these lands for the next generation.”
“Good conservation starts by bringing everyone to the table,” said Congressman Zinke. “The Northwest Wetlands VIP Act gives farmers, ranchers, Tribes, sportsmen and local communities a way to work together on voluntary projects that restore wetlands and keep working lands working. That’s how we protect habitat and water for the next generation. I'm proud to support this legislation.”
BACKGROUND: The Northwest Wetlands Voluntary Incentives Program Act would establish a federal grant and assistance program empowering government agencies, Tribes, nonprofits and landowners, among other entities, to work together in both restoring and enhancing habitats for wetland-dependent birds living in the Columbia River Basin and along the coast of Oregon and Washington.
These projects include water infrastructure and management and enhancement of vegetative habitat, which could be implemented on public, private, Tribal and other land determined by the U.S. Secretary of the Interior.
“We’re thankful to Reps. Hoyle, Zinke, and Schrier for introducing the Northwest Wetlands VIP Act in the House of Representatives. The future of conservation is on private working lands. This important legislation will bring much-needed resources for landowners to more effectively provide multi-benefits for people, wildlife, agriculture, and wetlands in the Northwest and the Columbia River Basin,” said Jeff McCreary, Director of Operations for the Western Region for Ducks Unlimited.
"Healthy wetlands are foundational to Washington’s economy, ecosystems, and communities,” said Washington Association of Land Trusts (WALT) Executive Director Erik Kingfisher. “The Northwest Wetlands VIP Act would provide much needed investments in enhancing, maintaining and restoring these vital lands across the Columbia River Basin, Washington coastal zone, and throughout the Puget Sound. As land trusts with the skills to make these projects happen across our beautiful state, we support this bipartisan legislation that would empower landowners through a voluntary, partnership-based approach to establish an open space legacy and enable the care and restoration of these lands to sustain them for future generations."
The Northwest Wetlands Voluntary Incentives Program Act is endorsed by Ducks Unlimited, Pacific Birds Habitat Joint Venture, Theodore Roosevelt Conservation Partnership (TRCP), Trout Unlimited, Oregon Agricultural Trust, Washington State Audubon, Washington Association of Land Trusts and more.
