The U.S. Army Garrison (USAG) Hawaii has updated the Lead Service Line Inventories.
(LSLI) required by U.S. EPA’s Lead and Copper Rule Revisions for its water systems and are now available for review. The deadline for the inventories update is October 16, 2026.
Through the completion of a historical records review, conducting personnel interviews, and field surveys, USAG Hawaii has determined there are no known lead service lines in its distribution system. The inventory does include galvanized pipe material requiring replacement and unknown service lines in its distribution system.
Under the Lead and Copper Rule Revisions (LCRR), water systems are required to make their updated inventories publicly accessible (40 CFR 141.84(b)). The inventories may be made available on the water system’s website, by mail, or in-person at the water system’s office. Residents and tenants with non-lead containing (i.e. unknown) or galvanized service lines will be receiving notifications specific to their location thirty (30) days after the LSLI update is completed per regulation.
USAG Hawaii reviewed all applicable sources of information, including:
• Construction and plumbing codes, permits, and existing records or other documentation which indicates the service line materials;
• Water system records, including distribution system maps and drawings, historical records on each service connection, meter installation records, historical capital improvement or master plans, and standard operating procedures;
• Inspections and records of the distribution system that indicate service line material, including inspections conducted during normal operations (e.g., checking service line materials when reading water meters or performing maintenance activities); and
• GIS maps which include historical information of the distribution system water service lines.
In addition to reviewing the above sources of information, USAG Hawaii continues to physically inspect all service lines in its distribution system, to verify, locate, and replace galvanized requiring replacement service lines. USAG Hawaii continues to physically inspect, identify, and confirm service lines of unknown material types. This information will be used to update service line material information obtained from normal operations, such as service line maintenance, installation, or water meter readings, after October 2024 and will continue to update the baseline inventory accordingly.
USAG Hawaii has determined there are no known lead service lines in its distribution system.
EPA requires all water system notifications to include the following standard advisory language:
There is no safe level of lead in drinking water. Exposure to lead in drinking water can cause serious health effects in all age groups, especially pregnant people, infants (both formula-fed and breastfed), and young children. Some of the health effects to infants and children include decreases in IQ and attention span. Lead exposure can also result in new or worsened learning and behavior problems. The children of persons who are exposed to lead before or during pregnancy may be at increased risk of these harmful health effects. Adults have increased risks of heart disease, high blood pressure, kidney or nervous system problems. Contact your healthcare provider for more information about your risks.
If you are concerned about exposure to lead in drinking water at your residence or building, follow these tips for reducing lead exposure:
For Residences:
- Run water to flush out residential lead in fixture
- Avoid using hot water from the tap for preparing baby formula
- Boiling water does not reduce lead levels
- Consider alternative sources or treatment of water
- Consult with physician to have child’s blood tested for lead For Buildings:
- Run your tap water before drinking
- Regularly clean out faucet aerator/screen and using a filter
- Boiling water does not reduce lead levels
- Consider alternative sources or treatment of water
USAG Hawaii has prepared the LSLI for submittal to the Hawaii State Department of Health (HDOH) and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). Due to sensitive and defense critical information, the inventory with addresses, building numbers, and identifiable information will not directly be posted on the USAG Hawaii website. USAG Hawaii conducts routine water sampling per EPA Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA) to meet regulatory requirements. Water sample results can be found in the annual Consumer Confidence Reports (CCR’s)per installation that are posted on the USAG Hawaii and Island Palm Communities (IPC) websites and social media. If you would like to obtain information about sampling efforts or the water line that services your residence or building, you may contact DPW Environmental Division at 808-787-1966 and speak to the Safe Drinking Water Program or by email at: usarmy.schofield.id-pacific.mbx.army-hi-environmental@army.mil

text:
Remarks

Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Joint Base Andrews

October 17, 2026

QUESTION: Mr. Secretary?

SECRETARY RUBIO: What’s going on?

QUESTION: Nice and chilly, right?

SECRETARY RUBIO: It’s all right.

QUESTION: With everything going on in the world and with crisis all over, why are you choosing now, at this time, to go to Uzbekistan?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, it’s the time of year that worked for those leaders. It’s not just Uzbekistan, it’s the other four countries from Central Asia. This is an important relationship. I mean, one of the things that suffers is the strategic business. You’re always visiting someplace where there’s a crisis or there’s a problem or there’s a – you’re going because there’s a conference. But there’s countries you’d like to get to because we want to build our relationships with them. And so that’s what we did a couple weeks ago when we went to Greece and other places like that, and earlier, a few weeks earlier than that, we went to Latin America, and now to Central Asia. So – and the chance to see – it was the date that worked to get all five of the leaders together, all five of the foreign ministers from the five countries.

QUESTION: On Starshield, what’s going on? Because Elon Musk said it’s up to the President.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, Starshield or Starlink?

QUESTION: Well, just both.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, I know, it’s confusing. So Starlink is a commercial product, okay? And so they – it’s regulated and handled as a commercial product. Starshield is a defense product, a military product. And as I said, I mean, that is something that we have a military – the United States military uses. It’s not at this moment available to Ukraine, and that’s under conversation. It’s under discussion right now of how they would want to use it.

QUESTION: No, but did the U.S. – did the U.S. have anything to do with it not working in Ukraine? Zelenskyy said it was deliberate.

SECRETARY RUBIO: No. Well, I don’t know what Zelenskyy said. I’m not sure Zelenskyy knows what he’s talking about, but it wasn’t deliberate. We have nothing to do with that. I don’t – the United States, nobody ordered that Starlink speed to be slowed down. It sort of happened, but my understanding is it’s been restored. It’s back to where it was before. That’s Starlink, though. They were using Starlink for their drones.

QUESTION: Has Starshield been restored?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Starshield is a totally different product. Starshield is –

QUESTION: I know, but is it –

SECRETARY RUBIO: No, no, Starshield is a contract with the U.S. military. It has nothing to do with Ukraine. I know Ukraine wants access to Starshield. They do not have Starshield now. They’ve asked for access to it in order to conduct deep strikes inside of Russia. They do not have access to it at this moment. Those are two different products.

QUESTION: But you have to have a theory as to why, obviously, Ukraine has reported disruptions.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, I don’t know what their theory is, but nothing to do with the White House. I saw a report on that the other day. It’s just categorically false. No one at the White House ordered anyone to slow down internet or slow down speed so that certain drones couldn’t use it. But my understanding is it’s back up and running. That’s what I read – that’s what we heard two days ago.

QUESTION: Sir, on the sanctions waivers on Russia. Senator Ted Cruz today called it a big mistake that only serves to benefit Putin. I’m wondering what your response is to that.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, there are other countries – the problem is these sanctions were not just sanctions on Russia. They include tariffs on a number of countries – India, for example, and others. And so I think the President wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyze what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the U.S. economy. I think when the bill was passed, one of the reasons the waivers were put in there is understanding that they would need some period of time to study this, given all the different things that are going on in the world right now, including the pressure on global energy supplies that are happening not just because of Iran, not just because of the Straits of Hormuz, but increasingly because of the Houthis attacking Saudi Arabia and because of the war with Ukraine and Russia, where energy infrastructure is being hit. And so that’s having an impact on global prices as well.

So, I think you have to take all of that into account and weigh it against each other. And then you’ve got countries like India, for example, that have voluntarily diversified their energy portfolio but are still getting a substantial amount of energy from Russia because it’s hard to pivot from one day to the next, but they’re also an important ally and partner of the United States. So, the President – we need that period of time to sort of study all this and figure out what the right combination is.

QUESTION: Between this waiver and the diesel deal, I mean, there’s a criticism that you’re basically giving Putin something for nothing, we’re giving Putin these freebies. What’s your response?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, that diesel was going to be sold one way or the other. I mean, the diesel that Putin is going to sell, they would make it available to the global market one way or the other. The only difference is how much of it the United States was going to get. So – but this is not unprecedented. If you recall a few months ago, we also did a 60-day waiver on Russian oil when Hormuz was being challenged.

So yeah, these conflicts around the world are starting to crash into each other, and they’re having an impact not just on global oil and diesel prices, but on economics. And I mean, the United States, we’re paying higher prices than we all want to be paying, but you look at some of these other countries around the world, they’re near crisis mode. So, all of these things have to be managed delicately and worked with because they’re all – they’re all coming together now. It’s not just the Strait of Hormuz anymore. It’s what’s happening with Saudi Arabia and the uncertainty that that’s creating. It’s also what’s happening between Russia and Ukraine and the constraints that’s putting on global energy supplies.

QUESTION: I’d like to ask you about violence in the West Bank. My colleague, Heidi Levine, was attacked there yesterday.

SECRETARY RUBIO: I saw that. We’re all – we’re very disturbed by those images and what we’re seeing. We’ve asked the Israelis and continue to ask them to crack down on that stuff. That – the President’s been very clear. He’s said this repeatedly. He does not want to see friction or anything, a crisis, going on in the West Bank. Now, I understand that these are groups that are out there doing it, and the President has been repeatedly clear when he’s said that he doesn’t want to see that. He doesn’t want to see a new spark.

But we saw the reports about what happened yesterday. I don’t have all the details. I only go off media reports. I know we’ve inquired with the embassy, are supposed to get a cable back later today or tomorrow indicating exactly what they know about it. But from what I understand about media reports, it didn’t look good. It was an American reporter; there was a photo of a journalist who was caught behind where some of these groups came in and was beaten. There’s video of that. So look, the whole thing was just disturbing and didn’t – not a good look.

QUESTION: Mr. Secretary, the President, one of the first decisions he took was to lift sanctions against the settlers.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, I understand, but he doesn’t want to see what’s happening now.

QUESTION: No, that’s not –

SECRETARY RUBIO: Lifting sanctions, which he did earlier in the day, does not mean he’s a supporter of what he’s seeing now on television, what he’s reading about. We’d like to get all the facts and learn a little bit more about it, but that – look, that’s one instance, and it happened to involve a photojournalist. But there are other instances we’ve had complaints about. Now it’s this olive harvest season, and so traditionally that’s always been a time in which a lot of people come into those areas. So, we’ve been watching that closely. We know that’s an issue there, that’s potentially an issue in Lebanon as well. Okay?

QUESTION: Do you agree with the UK assessment, the intel assessment that Russia and Iran may be increasing hybrid attacks over the next few months?

SECRETARY RUBIO: But which assessment are you talking about?

QUESTION: The – both NATO and UK have indicated –

SECRETARY RUBIO: Oh, NATO.

QUESTION: Have indicated that in –

SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah, but those are two separate things. So in the case of – you’re asking about Russian hybrid attacks. Yeah, we’ve always been concerned that the war in Ukraine can metastasize into other parts of Europe and other parts of the world, whether it be sabotage operations or the like. We’ve always been concerned that that’s one of the risks of a stalemated conflict, is escalation, and escalation can take the form of irregular attacks or irregular events. So that’s something I raised a couple weeks ago and we’re watching that closely.

I think with Iran and UK, what the UK has said is that the Iranians were behind the plot to attack the air base. And obviously we have no reason to disagree with the assessment factually. In fact, we agree with it.

So, all right? It’s cold, guys.

QUESTION: On the case regarding my colleague, what’s –

SECRETARY RUBIO: Did you guys see my Gators today take down Texas on the road?

Go ahead.

QUESTION: The case regarding my colleague who was attacked in the West Bank, what steps will you take to ensure that there’s a proper investigation of this incident?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, we want to learn all the facts about it first. Obviously, we’ve seen the video, and we’ve seen the media reporting about it. We have a process to handle these sorts of things. And if, in fact, it turns out to be what it appears it was, then we have ways of communicating that to the Israelis about how we expect – that we would expect them to prevent that from happening in the future. And it’s – again, the President doesn’t want to see a crisis in the West Bank. We don’t need that right now. Israel doesn’t need that right now.

QUESTION: Can I ask briefly on Eritrea-Ethiopia?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah.

QUESTION: How high-risk is the chance of war between them? And do you feel like it was a mistake to lift some of those Ethiopia-related sanctions right before violence flared up?

SECRETARY RUBIO: No, I don’t think those – I don’t – no, I don’t think the sanctions lifting – these were very small sanctions, and they don’t really have anything to do with what’s happening over there. You have these separatists that were attacking inside of Ethiopia. You had an Ethiopian response to it. You see troops surging on both sides of the border as a result of that. And anytime you see troops on both sides of the border in a place like that, you’re always worried that that can turn into a broader conflict.

So, we don’t have the closest relationship with Eritrea, obviously, over the years, although we’ve had communication with them – more than usual – in the past few months. Our hope was that by lifting some of these sanctions, we can increase those links because it’s hard to serve the role of mediator and peacemaker unless you can talk to both sides.

Obviously, the Ethiopian side we talk to a lot more, and I spoke to them this week personally, a few days ago, and just reiterated how important it was – like, we understand the challenge you’re facing from these separatists, and obviously no one is supportive of terrorism and the terrorist attacks that came against them – drone attacks against their own capital – but we also think we – it’s a time to sort of be wise and measured in how you respond to that and make sure it doesn’t turn into a broader war which could ultimately pull in other countries. The last thing the world needs right now is another war.

Okay? Thank you, guys.

Washington, DC -- Representative Gregory W. Meeks, Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, issued the following statement after the Trump administration announced it would waive sanctions on Russia as set forth in the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026.
"As I predicted, President Trump will not implement the sanctions set forth in the Lindsey Graham bill. I warned on the floor that this bill would give Ukraine false hope that the administration would finally get tough on Russia. Trump has vindicated that concern repeatedly over the past month. This waiver is no surprise: he has had the power to sanction Russia for years. What he lacks is the will.
"Congress is not helpless. My Ukraine Support Act passed the House with bipartisan support. This week I introduced the bipartisan Prohibit Corrupt Russian Oil Deals Act to end this administration’s disastrous partnership with the Russian energy industry. Congress must also advance legislation fixing the Graham bill which has failed within a month of its passage. All of these measures should become law making clear where America stands: with Ukraine and against Putin.
"Donald Trump has spent years chasing the Nobel Peace Prize. After weeks of pro-Putin policy and this shameful waiver, he deserves a different honor: the Neville Chamberlain Appeasement Award."
title: Meeks Statement on Trump Waiving Russia Sanctions

text:
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, including the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 (22 U.S.C. 10802 et seq.) (Graham Act), and section 301 of title 3, United States Code, I hereby determine and order:
Section 1. Background. On September 18, 2026, I signed the Graham Act into law. The Graham Act provides for the imposition of certain sanctions with respect to foreign persons, restrictions with respect to persons, and duties with respect to goods imported into the United States from the Russian Federation and certain other countries.
Section 115 of the Graham Act authorizes the President to waive the application of any sanctions provision with respect to a foreign person, any restriction with respect to a person, and any duty under the Graham Act, subject to the submission to the Congress of a written certification that such a waiver is in the national interests of the United States and a report explaining the basis for the certification.
As described further in section 4 of this order, I am hereby waiving the application of such sanctions, restrictions, and duties provided for in the Graham Act. I have submitted to the Congress a certification that the issuance of such a waiver at this time is in the national interests of the United States.
Sec. 2. Increases in Rate of Duty. (a) The rate of duty on goods from the Russian Federation shall be increased by 500 percent ad valorem, subject to the exceptions set forth in section 114 of the Graham Act and the waivers issued in section 4 of this order.
(b) The rate of duty on goods from the largest 5 importers of crude oil and natural gas that originated in the Russian Federation shall be increased by 100 percent ad valorem if the country knowingly makes new purchases of crude oil or natural gas that originated in the Russian Federation on or after October 18, 2026, subject to the exceptions set forth in section 114 of the Graham Act and the waivers issued in section 4 of this order. The United States Trade Representative (Trade Representative), in consultation with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of Energy, and any other senior executive branch official that the Trade Representative determines appropriate, shall monitor the circumstances related to the importation and purchases by countries of crude oil and natural gas of Russian Federation origin, regularly inform the President of any such activity, and provide recommendations for further action, as provided for in section 3 of this order.
(c) The rate of duty on goods from the top 5 facilitators of Russian oil sanctions evasion shall be increased by 100 percent ad valorem, subject to the exceptions set forth in section 114 of the Graham Act and the waivers issued in section 4 of this order. The Trade Representative, in consultation with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of Energy, and any other senior executive branch official that the Trade Representative determines appropriate, shall monitor the activities of countries that facilitate Russian oil sanctions evasion, as defined in section 113(i) of the Graham Act, and report to the President on which countries are among the top 5 such facilitators.
(d) The increases in the rates of duty provided by this order shall apply in addition to any other duty, fee, tax, exaction, or charge applicable with respect to the good, including any duty imposed under title VII of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1671 et seq.), sections 122, 201, or 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 (19 U.S.C. 2132, 2251, and 2411), or section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 (19 U.S.C. 1862).
Sec. 3. Monitoring. The Trade Representative, in consultation with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of Energy, and any other senior executive branch official that the Trade Representative determines appropriate, shall monitor the circumstances related to the importation and purchases by countries of crude oil and natural gas of Russian Federation origin, as well as the facilitation of Russian sanctions evasion by countries, and regularly report to the President on those circumstances. The Trade Representative, in consultation with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of Energy, and any other senior executive branch official that the Trade Representative determines appropriate, shall promptly inform the President of any circumstance that, in his opinion, might indicate the need for further action by the President, including with respect to the waivers.
Sec. 4. Waiver. (a) Pursuant to section 115(a) of the Graham Act, I hereby waive the application of any duties provided for in sections 112 and 113 of the Graham Act or this order. I have submitted to the Congress a certification that the issuance of such a waiver is in the national interests of the United States and a report explaining the basis for the certification, consistent with section 115(b) of the Graham Act.
(b) Pursuant to section 115(a) of the Graham Act, I hereby waive the application of the sanctions provision provided for in section 102(d) of the Graham Act with respect to foreign persons and the restrictions provided for in section 102(d) of the Graham Act with respect to persons. For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this order affects any sanctions or other measures provided for under any Executive Order issued to address the national emergency that I continued on March 24, 2026, with respect to specified harmful foreign activities of the Government of the Russian Federation (91 Fed. Reg. 15515), as in effect on the day before the date of enactment of the Graham Act, including with respect to all persons sanctioned under any such Executive Order. I have submitted to the Congress a certification that the issuance of such a waiver is in the national interests of the United States and a report explaining the basis for the certification, consistent with section 115(b) of the Graham Act.
(c) Pursuant to section 115(a) of the Graham Act, I hereby waive the application of the following sanctions provisions with respect to foreign persons and restrictions with respect to persons: sections 102(a), 102(e), 103, 104, 105, 106, 107, 108, 109, 110, 111, and 117 of the Graham Act. I have submitted to the Congress a certification that the issuance of such a waiver is in the national interests of the United States and a report explaining the basis for the certification, consistent with section 115(b) of the Graham Act.
(d) The waivers described in subsections (a) through (c) of this section shall remain in effect until such time as the President or the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury and the Trade Representative, as appropriate, determine that further action is appropriate.
Sec. 5. Delegation of Authorities. (a) I hereby delegate the functions and authorities vested in the President by the Graham Act as follows:
(i) sections 102(a), 102(b), 102(c), 104(a), 108(b), 111(b), and 114(a)(2), to the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, and to the Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Secretary of State;
(ii) section 115 to the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury and the Trade Representative, as appropriate;
(iii) sections 102(e)(1), 103(a), 103(b), 103(d), 104(b), 110(a), 110(c), and 116(a) to the Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Secretary of State;
(iv) section 111(a) to the Secretary of Energy, in consultation with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Commerce, and the Secretary of the Treasury;
(v) section 112 to the Trade Representative, in consultation with the Secretary of State and the Secretary of the Treasury;
(vi) section 113(a) to the Trade Representative, in consultation with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the Secretary of Energy;
(vii) section 117(a), with respect to the termination of the application of any sanction with respect to a foreign person or any restriction with respect to a person, to the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury; and to the Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Secretary of State; and
(viii) section 117(a), with respect to the termination of any duty, to the Trade Representative, in consultation with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Energy, and the Secretary of the Treasury.
(b) The delegations in this section shall apply to any provisions of any future public laws that are the same or substantially the same as the provisions referenced in this section.
(c) The Secretary of State, the Secretary of the Treasury, the Trade Representative, and the Secretary of Energy may, consistent with applicable law, redelegate within their respective departments any of the functions or authorities delegated to them by this order. All executive departments and agencies shall take all appropriate measures within their authority to carry out the provisions of this order.
(d) Any reference in this section to the Graham Act shall be deemed to be a reference to the Graham Act as amended from time to time.
Sec. 6. Severability. If any provision of this order or the application of any provision of this order to any individual or circumstance is held to be invalid, the remainder of this order and the application of its provisions to any other individuals or circumstances shall not be affected.
Sec. 7. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect:
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; or
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.
(b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.
(c) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.
(d) The costs for publication of this order shall be borne by the Department of State.
DONALD J. TRUMP
THE WHITE HOUSE,
October 16, 2026.
title: Implementing the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026

FOLLOWING BIPARTISAN PUSH FROM CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN AND COLLEAGUES DEMANDING TRUMP ADMINISTRATION SPEED UP LIHEAP DISTRIBUTION, HHS RELEASES $356 MILLION FOR NEW YORK
Following Bipartisan Push from Congressman Pat Ryan and Colleagues Demanding Trump Administration Speed Up LIHEAP Distribution, HHS Releases $356 Million for New York
As temperatures begin to drop and fuel prices remain high due to the Iran War, Congressman Ryan demanded that the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) distribute critical home energy funds without delay
This week, $356 million in LIHEAP funding was released to New York, which is the earliest these awards have been granted
Ryan is calling on House Appropriations Committee to provide an additional $3 billion in supplemental LIHEAP funding for FY27
Ryan co-sponsors the “Heating and Cooling Relief Act,” which would expand eligibility for LIHEAP and lower home energy costs for millions more households nationwide
Heating oil prices in New York state are up almost 70% from this time last year, with prices in the Hudson Valley averaging $6.25/ gallon
WASHINGTON, DC – After Congressman Pat Ryan helped lead a bipartisan push demanding the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to distribute Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) funds to the states as soon as possible, HHS announced this week they have distributed $356,163,671 in LIEHAP funds for New York’s Home Energy Assistance Program. Heating oil prices in New York State are up more than 70% from this time last year, with prices in the Hudson Valley averaging $6.22/ gallon.
“After a summer of skyhigh gas prices and utility bills due to Trump’s war in Iran, home heating oil costs are up almost 70 percent. Now, as temperatures start to drop, Hudson Valley families are about to face more expensive heating bills on top of everything else. Thousands of families in our community rely on the LIHEAP program to keep their homes warm. We put the pressure on the administration early to ensure these funds got out the door without delay, and I’m proud they heeded our calls, distributing more than $356 million in LIHEAP funds to New York,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “The LIHEAP program is chronically underfunded, which is why I’m calling on the Appropriations Committee to increase funding for the program and pushing for legislation to ensure more Hudson Valley families can qualify for assistance.”
This week, Ryan also joined a bipartisan group of 73 members in calling on the House Appropriations Committee to provide an additional $3 billion in emergency supplemental appropriations for the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) for Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27).
In the letter, the members wrote, “As the war with Iran remains unresolved, energy prices are expected to keep rising, with heating oil up 60% since February. LIHEAP’s $4 billion in funding for the last fiscal year would fall significantly short in meeting the needs of American families this fiscal year.”
“LIHEAP is a critical lifeline for low- and moderate-income individuals, but even if your household qualifies, LIHEAP does not provide guaranteed security. Five out of six families who qualify for LIHEAP receive no financial assistance due to the program’s woefully underfunded status. When adjusting for inflation, LIHEAP funding is lower now than it was in 1981 when the program was first created. If LIHEAP was funded at the same level as it was 45 years ago, the program would have received nearly $7 billion in FY27,” they continued.
“Emergency LIHEAP assistance is urgently needed as winter weather approaches and colder temperatures have already begun. Families should not have to choose between staying warm and purchasing other essential items like food, medication, or rent. Congress must act and not leave families in the cold,” they concluded.
LIHEAP helps low-income individuals and families pay for heating and cooling and mitigates the impacts of rising energy costs and extreme weather events. Across the nation, LIHEAP helps nearly 6 million households afford their energy bills, including nearly 30,000 in NY-18, but Secretary Kennedy’s decision last year to fire all LIHEAP staff last year has put this assistance at risk. Ryan has previously blasted the Trump Administration for threatening to eliminate federal funding for LIHEAP.
Ryan is also a co-sponsor of the Heating and Cooling Relief Act, legislation to modernize LIHEAP, increase investments, and dramatically expand eligibility so that households earning up to 250 percent of the Federal Poverty Line or 80 percent of State Median Income can qualify to apply for assistance. It would lower home energy costs for millions more households nationwide.
Specifically, the Heating and Cooling Relief Act would:
- Substantially increase LIHEAP funding to ensure year-round assistance, including an additional $2 billion for emergency energy assistance and $1 billion in Just Transition Grants to help vulnerable households adapt to a changing climate;
- Broaden eligibility so that households earning up to 250 percent of the Federal Poverty Line or 80 percent of State Median Income can qualify, while ensuring lower energy burdens for lower-income households and capping household energy burdens at 3 percent of monthly income;
- Protect consumers from utility shutoffs, excessive late fees, and predatory energy practices that disproportionately impact vulnerable communities;
- Expand emergency assistance, ensuring extreme heat and cold are recognized as qualifying emergencies and that states can provide vital cooling relief;
- Increase funding for weatherization and home electrification, to help low-income households reduce energy costs, improve health and safety, and transition to clean, resilient energy systems;
- Streamline enrollment and outreach, improving coordination with other federal programs and increasing access through automatic enrollment and simplified verification; and
- Strengthen reporting requirements to better track affordability, equity, and climate resilience outcomes.

Deluzio Concludes October Town Hall Tour Across Western PA in Beaver Falls
BEAVER FALLS, PA – Today, Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17) concluded his October Town Hall Tour across Western Pennsylvania in Beaver Falls. Each town hall in Pennsylvania’s 17th District was open to the public and the press. More than 200 Western Pennsylvanians joined him across the three stops.
Congressman Deluzio’s October Town Hall Tour provided three opportunities for constituents to speak directly with their elected representative in Congress, share their opinions, and ask questions on a wide range of topics, such as: the U.S. Supreme Court in Penn Hills, AI safety in Carnegie, and veterans’ care in Beaver Falls.
“In a democracy, we can all come under one roof and discuss the issues of the day, agree on some things, disagree on others, and move forward together—that's what this Town Hall Tour was all about,” said Congressman Deluzio. “Folks are worried about rising costs, the ongoing Iran War, and raging corruption at the top of our federal government but are also hopeful for the future. I’ll bring what I heard on this Town Hall Tour back down to Washington and keep fighting to restore the American Dream—here in Western PA and across the country.”
Congressman Deluzio also provided updates on his work down in Washington this year—like all the new projects coming to Western PA that made him the #1 House Democrat to bring home community project funding (FY26), passing his Railway Safety Act out of committee, and stopping more cuts to veterans benefits.
Congressman Deluzio has attended more than twenty similar open Q&A events during the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

Neal Statement on Trump’s Surrender to Putin
SPRINGFIELD, MA— Ways and Means Committee Ranking Member Richard E. Neal (D-MA) released the following statement after President Trump announced he’d waive new sanctions on Russia under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026:
“In America, standing with our allies in Europe against Putin’s aggression is an ironclad commitment to peace and democracy and shouldn’t be optional. But when it matters most, Donald Trump has shown he’ll abandon our partners and undermine our own laws to cozy up to tyrants and benefit himself. It's irresponsible, antithetical to American values, and should shake us all. After already opening the door for us to bankroll his war machine by purchasing Russian diesel, why should anyone believe Trump won’t keep cowering to Putin and putting his interests over our own?
“We warned about what handing Trump more unchecked power meant. Every Republican outraged by this capitulation should be reminded that it’s only possible because they continue to sit idly by and allow our values and partnerships to be eroded as they refuse to hold this Administration to account. Surrendering to tyrants may fly under Republican control, but Democrats stand with our allies and will provide the accountability this moment demands.”

title: Neal Statement on Trump’s Surrender to Putin

WASHINGTON – FEMA announced today that federal disaster assistance is available to the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands to supplement territory and local response efforts due to the emergency conditions resulting from Tropical Storm Champi beginning on Oct. 16, 2026, and continuing.
The President’s action authorizes FEMA to coordinate all federal disaster relief efforts to alleviate the hardship and suffering caused by the emergency on the local population, and to provide appropriate assistance to save lives, to protect property, public health and safety and to lessen or avert the threat of a catastrophe.
The assistance is for the islands of Rota, Saipan and Tinian.
Specifically, FEMA is authorized to identify, mobilize and provide at its discretion, equipment and resources necessary to alleviate the impacts of the emergency. Emergency protective measures, limited to direct federal assistance, will be provided at 75% federal funding.
Andrew F. Grant has been named the Federal Coordinating Officer for federal response operations in the affected area. Designations may be made later if requested and warranted by the results of further damage assessments.
title: President Donald J. Trump Approves Emergency Declaration for Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands

Jacksonville, Florida – Jamal Jason James (40, Jacksonville) has been sentenced by Chief U.S. District Judge Marcia Morales Howard to 10 years in federal prison for participating in a drug trafficking conspiracy and possessing MDMA with the intent to distribute it. James pleaded guilty on December 12, 2025. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement.

According to court documents, on July 29, 2024, members of the Jacksonville Sherriff’s Office responded to Ivy Street in Jacksonville regarding a call for a male lying in the road. When officers arrived, they observed James lying outside the open door of a vehicle used by him. While arranging for aid to tend to James, officers noticed a small bag of a rock-like substance in the vehicle, which laboratory testing later revealed was 6 grams of MDMA, an amount inconsistent with personal use. James was placed in handcuffs and searched. Officers found more than $20,000 in cash on James and inside the vehicle.

After James was arrested, he was briefly incarcerated at the Duval County Jail where he made a series of phone calls to Brian Brightman and Anthony Smokes. The calls concerned finding and moving drugs belonging to James being stored in at least one trap house accessible by Brightman and Smokes. They also discussed collecting drug debts owed to James by other members of the conspiracy. In related cases, Brightman and Smokes previously pleaded guilty to federal drug offenses and are awaiting sentencing.

This case was investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Nassau County Sherriff’s Office, and the Jacksonville Sherriff’s Office. It was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Rachel Lasry.
title: Jacksonville Man Sentenced to Ten Years in Prison for Drug Offenses

TUCSON, Ariz. – A Tucson man will spend two decades in prison after fueling an international child-exploitation ring that broadcasted the real-time abuse of minors.

On Oct. 14, David Berry Garmarnik, 48, of Tucson, was sentenced by U.S. District Court Judge Rosemary Marquez to 20 years in prison. Garmarnik previously pleaded guilty to one count of Attempted Production of Child Pornography.

“Live‑streamed child sexual abuse is one of the most urgent and devastating forms of exploitation, and offenders who fuel it will be met with swift, aggressive, and unrelenting prosecution,” said U.S. Attorney Timothy Courchaine. “These crimes inflict real‑time harm on real children, and our office will pursue anyone who participates in this abuse, no matter where they hide or how they operate. We are grateful to HSI for its relentless work in dismantling international trafficking networks and for ensuring that those who prey on children are brought to justice.”

“This case demonstrates the devastating reality of child exploitation, and the lengths offenders will go to abuse children and conceal their crimes. HSI is committed to identifying these offenders, dismantling the networks that enable their abuse, and working with our domestic and international law enforcement partners to ensure they are held accountable. Protecting children and pursuing those who exploit them remains a priority for HSI, wherever these crimes lead us,” said Jason Stevens, Special Agent in Charge of HSI Phoenix.

According to the plea agreement, Garmarnik admitted that he requested and directed sexually explicit conduct of children under the age of 12 and in some cases as young as 7. Additional court records show that HSI identified David Berry Garmarnik as a participant in an international child‑exploitation network that live‑streamed the sexual abuse of minors for paying offenders around the world. Investigators linked Garmarnik to more than 100 online interactions with known or suspected traffickers between 2017 and 2022. Records obtained from Microsoft showed thousands of messages, media files, and call logs consistent with child‑exploitation activity.

In addition, financial subpoenas revealed that Garmarnik sent over 100 payments to individuals in the Philippines with no legitimate connection to him, including a known trafficker whose operation involved the abuse of children as young as two years old. After search warrants were executed, Garmarnik admitted he had paid for approximately 100 live‑streamed shows involving minors. He also acknowledged downloading child sexual abuse material and communicating with traffickers using his Skype account.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc .

Homeland Security Investigations – Tucson conducted the investigation in this case. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Nathaniel J. Walters and Jennifer H. Berman, District of Arizona, Tucson, handled the prosecution.

CASE NUMBER: 24-CR-08214-TUC-RM RELEASE NUMBER: 2026-177_Garmarnik

# # #

For more information on the U.S. Attorney’s Office, District of Arizona, visit http://www.justice.gov/usao/az/ Follow the U.S. Attorney’s Office, District of Arizona, on Twitter @USAO_AZ for the latest news.
title: Tucson Man Sentenced to 20 Years in Prison for Child Exploitation Crimes

WASHINGTON — Today, Congressman James P. McGovern, Ranking Member of the House Rules Committee and Co-Chair of the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission, along with Representatives Jesus “Chuy” Garcia (IL-04), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Eleanor Norton (DC), and Ilhan Omar (MN-5), sent a letter urging Secretary of State Marco Rubio to prioritize human rights in his discussions this weekend with Indian officials. 
“The United States-India relationship has historically been rooted in democratic values, constitutional governance, and strong people-to-people ties,” the Members wrote. “As the world’s largest democracies and state parties to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, the U.S. and India have an obligation to promote and defend the rights to freedom of assembly and expression.”
The lawmakers highlighted reports of mass detentions, excessive use of force, internet shutdowns, and restrictions on peaceful assembly by Indian authorities amid protests over examination irregularities, youth unemployment, and, most recently, the purge of more than 130 million people from voter rolls. They also raised concerns about reports that individuals associated with Indian diplomatic missions photographed and monitored protesters in Washington, D.C., Chicago, and San Francisco.
The lawmakers affirmed that freedom of expression, peaceful assembly, and the right to vote are fundamental democratic principles shared by the United States and India. They urged Secretary Rubio to address these concerns directly with Indian counterparts during his visit and take the following steps: 
    - Press the Indian government to initiate thorough, transparent, and independent investigations of alleged human rights violations connected to the law enforcement response to protests;
- Encourage the release of any individuals detained in contravention to Indian and international law for peacefully exercising the rights to freedom of expression and assembly; 
- Thoroughly investigate reports that Indian diplomatic missions engaged in the surveillance and intimidation of protesters within the United States; and
- Pursuant to Section 6 of the Arms Export Control Act, assess whether India has engaged in a consistent pattern of acts of intimidation or harassment directed against individuals in the United States and is thus ineligible for arms sales.
The full text of the letter is available here.
title: McGovern Leads Push for Rubio to Center Human Rights in Upcoming U.S.-India Talks

MIAMI – Two men have pleaded guilty to participating in a murder-for-hire conspiracy targeting a Miami woman who survived and attempt outside her home in June 2024.

Clementa Johnson, 49, of Tallahassee, pleaded guilty on Oct. 5 to conspiracy to commit murder for hire, murder for hire, stalking, and being a felon in possession of a firearm and ammunition. Diori Barnard, 49, of Miami, pleaded guilty on Oct. 6 to conspiracy to commit murder for hire, murder for hire, and stalking. Both defendants entered their guilty pleas shortly after a jury was selected to try the case.

“For years, Tatiana Pino was subjected to a calculated campaign of stalking, violence, and repeated attempts on her life,” said U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida. “Clementa Johnson and Diori Barnard joined that conspiracy, stalked their intended victim, and helped carry out a plot that culminated in an armed attempt on her life outside her home. Their guilty pleas on the day trial was set to begin bring the final two defendants in this case to account. Our message is simple: no matter how many people are recruited, how much money is offered, or how elaborate the scheme, we will pursue every participant in a murder-for-hire conspiracy and bring them to justice.”

According to court records, Johnson and Barnard participated in a murder-for-hire conspiracy orchestrated by Sergio Pino, the multimillionaire estranged husband of Tatiana Pino. Sergio Pino enlisted individuals who, in turn, recruited Johnson and Barnard to carry out the murder. After earlier attempts to kill Tatiana Pino failed, Johnson, Barnard, and others joined the conspiracy to stalk and ultimately kill her.

On June 23, 2024, the conspiracy culminated in an attempt to shoot Tatiana Pino outside her home. She survived the attack.

Johnson faces up to 45 years in federal prison, while Barnard faces up to 30 years. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

U.S. Attorney Reding Quiñones and Special Agent in Charge Brett D. Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office made the announcement.

FBI Miami is investigating the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Abbie D. Waxman and Brian Dobbins are prosecuting the case.

Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Southern District of Florida at www.flsd.uscourts.gov or at http://pacer.flsd.uscourts.gov , under case number 24-cr-20110.

title: Final Two Defendants in Murder-for-Hire Conspiracy Plead Guilty on Day of Trial

FORT RUCKER, Ala. — The Motorcycle Mentorship Program’s 9th Annual Cancer Awareness Ride traveled across Fort Rucker Oct. 16, following a weeklong delay caused by Hurricane Isaias.
Originally scheduled for Oct. 9, the ride was postponed after the hurricane swept through the region. Despite the change, Soldiers, Department of War civilians, contractors, family members, cancer survivors, and supporters participated in the event hosted by the 110th Aviation Brigade.
For Sam Baker, 110th Aviation Brigade operations officer and the event point of contact, the ride carries a personal meaning.
“My mother died of breast cancer 11 years ago,” Baker said. “I like to ride motorcycles, and I saw this ride for the post about five years ago and started riding in it.”
Baker said he later assumed responsibility for helping organize the event after the original organizer transferred to Korea. Since then, the ride has grown substantially.
“We’ve grown from eight bikes to 80 bikes last year,” Baker said. “It’s gotten more recognition and awareness.”
While the event initially focused on breast cancer awareness, it now recognizes those affected by all forms of cancer, including men, women, survivors, caregivers, and families who have lost loved ones.
“We cover all the cancers, male and female,” Baker said. “We also give certificates in memoriam, so if somebody’s lost somebody, we’re still carrying on that name and not letting that person die and fade away. They are still remembered.”
The group gathered Friday morning for motorcycle safety checks, a route brief, and remarks recognizing the installation’s support for cancer survivors, families, caregivers, and others affected by cancer.
The approximately 26-mile route took riders through Fort Rucker training corridors, housing areas, and other portions of the installation that many participants may not have previously traveled.
The route also supported the Motorcycle Mentorship Program’s safety mission by giving newer riders experience operating in formation and navigating more challenging turns and transitions.
“A lot of people don’t have a lot of formation experience,” Baker said. “There’s training involved with that.”
The motorcycle formation made stops at the School Age Center, Main Child Development Center, Lyster Army Health Clinic, Soldier Support Center, and Howze Field. At each location, riders recognized cancer survivors and family members affected by the disease.
Riders presented honorees with certificates, pink bandanas, bracelets, and single flowers in recognition of their strength, resilience, and experiences with cancer. Survivors, family members, riders, and other supporters also had the opportunity to sign a cancer-awareness flag, creating a visible symbol of remembrance, encouragement, and solidarity across the Fort Rucker community.
The Motorcycle Mentorship Program pairs experienced riders with newer riders to reinforce safe riding practices and reduce motorcycle mishaps. The annual cancer awareness ride remains one of the program’s most visible outreach events, combining motorcycle safety education, rider mentorship, and support for those affected by cancer.
To see more photos from the event, visit our Flickr page: https://flic.kr/s/aHBqjD7Kk2
title: 110th Aviation Brigade Conducts 9th Annual Cancer Awareness Motorcycle Mentorship Ride

WASHINGTON – The Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (PBGC) is proposing to collect additional information to enhance its compliance oversight of multiemployer pension plans that receive special financial assistance (SFA). The new requirements would expand the scope of information that must be filed as part of the Annual Statement of Compliance to include documentation of plan investment policies and procedures for locating missing participants.
“One of PBGC’s highest priorities is monitoring the stewardship of SFA funds to ensure that taxpayer dollars are used solely for their intended purpose,” said PBGC Director Janet Dhillon. “The proposed changes would give PBGC additional tools to verify that SFA funds are being managed responsibly and used to pay earned pension benefits to retirees and their beneficiaries.”
Stronger Oversight of Investment Decisions
Under the proposal, plans that received SFA would be required to submit documents that explain how investment decisions are made and monitored. These include investment policy statements, investment guidelines, asset allocation policies, committee charters, and other governing documents related to the management of plan assets, including SFA funds. The additional documentation would help PBGC assess whether plans are complying with SFA requirements, including rules governing how SFA funds are used, invested, and safeguarded.
Greater Focus on Missing Participants
PBGC is also proposing new information requirements related to missing participants. Plans that received SFA would be required to provide data on participants who may have lost contact with the plan, as well as documentation describing the procedures used to locate them.
The goal is to help ensure that retirees and beneficiaries receive the pension benefits they have earned.
The proposed revisions to the collection of information are published in today’s Federal Register and are open for public comment through December 15, 2026.
About the Special Financial Assistance Program
Enacted by legislation in 2021, the SFA Program provides funding to financially troubled multiemployer pension plans. Upon approval of an SFA application, PBGC makes a lump-sum payment to an eligible multiemployer plan in an amount projected to enable the plan to pay full plan benefits through 2051. The program is funded entirely by appropriations from the General Fund of the U.S. Department of the Treasury. Plans receiving SFA are subject to certain terms, conditions and reporting requirements, including an annual statement documenting compliance with the terms and conditions.
About PBGC
PBGC protects the retirement security of about 30 million American workers, retirees, and beneficiaries in both single-employer and multiemployer private sector pension plans. The agency’s two insurance programs are legally separate and operationally and financially independent. PBGC is directly responsible for the benefits of nearly 1.4 million participants and beneficiaries in failed single-employer pension plans. The Single-Employer Program is financed by insurance premiums, investment income, and assets and recoveries from failed single-employer plans. The Multiemployer Program is financed by insurance premiums and investment income. Special financial assistance for financially troubled multiemployer plans is financed by general taxpayer monies.
title: PBGC proposes additional information requirements for oversight of multiemployer pension plans receiving special financial assistance

United States Attorney Lesley A. Woods announced that Johnathan Klein, 31, of Lincoln, Nebraska, was sentenced on October 15, 2026, in federal court in Lincoln for possession with intent to distribute 50 grams or more of methamphetamine actual. United States District Judge Susan M. Bazis sentenced Klein to 130 months’ imprisonment. There is no parole in the federal system. After Klein’s release from prison, he will begin a 5-year term of supervised release.

Law enforcement learned that Klein had been dealing methamphetamine to a person between October of 2024 and March 13, 2025, in varying amounts. They stated they bought 1/8 ounce 10 times, an ounce 30 times, four ounces twice, and 5 ½ ounces once.

On March 13, 2025, a Lincoln Police Department officer committed a traffic stop on a vehicle with Klein as a passenger. During a search of the driver’s person, a small bag of methamphetamine was found, which resulted in a search of the vehicle. A larger bag, containing two baggies of methamphetamine, was found on the front floorboard where the co-defendant driver and Klein had been sitting. Syringes, scales, and baggies were also found in the vehicle.

The two baggies of suspected methamphetamine found on the floorboard were sent to the Nebraska State Patrol Crime Laboratory. Further testing showed one of the baggies containing 57.72 grams of methamphetamine with a purity of 99.3%, resulting in at least 54 grams of methamphetamine actual. The second bag contained 54.73 gram of methamphetamine. No purity analysis was conducted on that bag.

The case is pending against the co-defendant.

This case was investigated by the Lincoln/Lancaster County Narcotics Task Force.
title: Lincoln Man Sentenced for Possession with Intent to Distribute Methamphetamine

LEXINGTON, Ky. – A Lexington, Ky., man, Quentin Montez Leavell, 33, was sentenced to 144 months of imprisonment yesterday by U.S. District Judge Chad Meredith for conspiracy to distribute 40 grams or more of fentanyl, distribution of fentanyl, and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime.

According to his plea agreement, from February 2021 to July 2021, Leavell agreed with others, including codefendants, Dominque Cornell Duff and Lakwon Marquis Givens, to distribute fentanyl contained in counterfeit pills that resembled Percocet, with markings of “M, 30.” Leavell further admitted that he possessed a firearm to protect himself and to deter others from attempting to rob or steal drugs and/or money from him.

Codefendants Duff and Givens were sentenced in September 2026, to 155 months and 170 months, respectively, for their roles in the conspiracy.

Jason Parman, United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Kentucky, Dennis M. Fetting, Special Agent in Charge, Department of Homeland Security, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), and Chief Lawrence Weathers, Lexington Police Department, jointly announced the sentences.

The investigation was conducted by the Department of Homeland Security, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) and the Lexington Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Todd Bradbury prosecuted the case on behalf of the United States.

This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States.

– END –
title: Final Defendant Sentenced in a Conspiracy to Distribute Counterfeit Pills Containing Fentanyl

This is the first time in American history that there have been zero releases at the border
WASHINGTON — The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) today announced preliminary Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 data showcasing a 95% drop in southwest border apprehensions compared to the Biden Administration, alongside the lowest annual encounters in American history and the first-ever fiscal year with zero Border Patrol releases.
Driven by President Donald J. Trump’s policies and the leadership of DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, FY 2026 combined historic low crossings with strengthened border infrastructure, disrupted cartels, and protected American trade. September marked the 17th consecutive month with ZERO releases.
“President Trump promised the American people a secure border, and the data proves he delivered. Over the past year, CBP recorded its lowest numbers in American history. A stark contrast to Biden, where CBP recorded its highest illegal immigration numbers ever,” said Secretary Mullin. “The results could not be clearer: strong enforcement works. Thanks to President Trump’s leadership and the hard work of CBP and DHS law enforcement personnel, we have restored control of the border and made America safer than ever.”
“FY 2026 demonstrated what focused enforcement, strong partnerships, and the commitment of our frontline personnel can achieve,” said CBP Commissioner Rodney S. Scott. “DHS and CBP are securing the border, stopping dangerous drugs and criminals, protecting communities, and ensuring our personnel have the resources necessary for this critical mission.”
Historic Border Security Results
CBP’s enforcement posture drove U.S. Border Patrol apprehensions to their lowest level in agency history. The Border Patrol, which completed its first-ever fiscal year with no releases, recorded less than 99,000 southwest border apprehensions in FY 2026—a 95% decline compared with more than 1.8 million per year under President Biden. Total FY 2026 apprehensions (98,708) were 60% lower than the Biden Administration’s single highest month alone (249,740).
Additionally, preliminary data shows total nationwide encounters in FY 2026 were the lowest in agency history at 379,243, compared with 2.7 million per year under Biden (seven times higher). FY 2026 encounters were 88% lower than FY 2023 under Biden, which was the highest fiscal year ever.
These results reflect sustained enforcement and the deterrent effect of a secure border. Illegal aliens have received a clear message: don’t try to enter the country illegally, or you will be apprehended, detained, and deported.
A Safer Border
President Trump’s policies are also saving lives by reducing unlawful crossings, leading to a dramatic decline in border-related deaths.
Fewer unlawful crossings have contributed to a significant decline in border-related deaths. Preliminary data shows alien deaths identified by the Border Patrol fell nearly 80% in FY 2026 and since January 20, 2025, compared to the Biden Administration.
CBP personnel nevertheless remained ready to respond when lives were at risk. Across the nation, agents, officers, and air and marine personnel conducted search-and-rescue operations and delivered emergency medical aid. These efforts have included railcar rescues, a rescue effort following flooding at the Grand Canyon, and a CBP officer who responded to victims of a plane crash in Miami.
CBP’s Office of Field Operations responded to more than 3,000 medical emergencies during FY 2026, performing CPR on over 50 individuals in cardiac arrest and administering Naloxone for suspected opioid overdoses.
Stronger Infrastructure Along the Border
CBP reached a major construction milestone in FY 2026, completing 250 miles of new border barrier along the southwest border since January 20, 2025. This includes primary and secondary barriers, waterborne barriers, and supporting technology.
Funding from the Working Families Tax Cut Act enabled CBP to accelerate Smart Wall construction. From September 2025 through September 2026, CBP obligated $34.3 billion to support Smart Wall projects across all southwest border states, cementing a generational investment in physical security and operational control.
Drug Interdictions that Save Lives
As the frontline against drug smuggling, CBP is leading federal efforts to combat illicit trafficking.
CBP utilizes cutting-edge nonintrusive inspection technology and intelligence-driven strategies to seize deadly drugs, targeting not just finished products but precursor chemicals, tools, and pill presses.
As a result, preliminary data shows CBP’s drug seizures in FY 2026 totaled nearly 1 million pounds—63% higher than the 600,000-pound annual average of the last four years.
Trade and Tariff Enforcement
CBP plays a central role in enforcing trade law, supporting economic security, and interdicting counterfeit merchandise and goods made with forced labor.
In FY 2026, CBP stopped more than 4,000 shipments valued at over $325 million suspected of involving forced labor, and issued eight Withhold Release Orders along with two modifications.
CBP also seized nearly 55.5 million counterfeit goods valued at more than $12.6 billion, including 476,903 items infringing FIFA World Cup intellectual property valued at over $33 million.
By securing the border, intercepting dangerous narcotics, expanding physical barriers, and enforcing lawful trade, CBP has closed vulnerabilities across every front to ensure the long-term safety and prosperity of the American people.
title: Under President Trump and Secretary Mullin, DHS Announces Lowest Fiscal Year Border Crossings in American History

EVANSVILLE- Tonda Avery, 55, of Evansville, has been sentenced to one year and one day in federal prison, followed by one year of supervised release, after pleading guilty to five counts of Aiding and Assisting in the Preparation and Presentation of a False and Fraudulent Tax Return. Avery was also ordered to pay $1,318,455.43 in restitution. This case was brought as part of the Trump Administration’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud.

According to court documents, Avery operated Diversity Tax Service (DTS) in Evansville, Indiana. Avery prepared federal income tax returns for clients and employed other tax return preparers at DTS. Between 2020 and 2021, Avery prepared and filed approximately 123 tax returns containing false Forms 7202, causing a total tax loss of $965,203.

Form 7202 allowed eligible self-employed individuals to claim refundable tax credits for certain periods in which they were unable to work because of circumstances related to COVID-19. As part of her scheme, Avery manufactured or inflated her clients’ eligibility for these credits.

For clients who did not own legitimate businesses, Avery created fictitious businesses and prepared false Schedule C forms reporting nonexistent business income and expenses. She then used the fictitious businesses to support fraudulent Forms 7202 and claim COVID-19 sick and family leave tax credits to which the clients were not entitled.

For clients who did have legitimate businesses, Avery inflated information used to calculate the credits, including the number of days the clients purportedly were unable to work and their net earnings from self-employment. These false figures resulted in the clients claiming larger tax credits and receiving refunds greater than they were entitled to receive.

The prevalence of Forms 7202 in Avery’s returns was dramatically higher than among taxpayers generally. In 2020, approximately 33.82% of the returns Avery filed included a Form 7202, compared with approximately 0.90% of returns nationwide and 0.50% of returns in Indiana. In 2021, Forms 7202 appeared on approximately 61.14% of Avery’s returns, compared with approximately 0.90% nationwide and 0.40% in Indiana.

Avery also instructed and encouraged other tax return preparers at DTS to prepare fraudulent returns, including returns containing false Forms 7202.

Avery charged fees based on the number of forms and schedules included in a tax return. When Avery added a fraudulent Schedule C and Form 7202 to a client’s return, she increased her fee by $800.

“Ms. Avery’s scheme exploited pandemic relief programs designed to help Americans in genuine need,” said Tom Wheeler, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Indiana “By deliberately falsifying tax returns and coaching others to do the same, she undermined public trust and diverted critical resources intended to support workers during an unprecedented national crisis. Although the pandemic ended years ago, our office remains steadfast in pursuing those who defrauded these vital programs, no matter how long it takes to bring them to justice.”

“Tax preparers are paid to know the rules—not rig them,” said Robert J. Kuszynski, Acting Special Agent in Charge, IRS Criminal Investigation, Chicago Field Office. “Tonda Avery invented businesses, falsified tax forms and inflated tax credits her clients had no right to claim. That’s not cutting corners, that’s fraud. Today’s sentence sends a simple message: if you make a business out of cheating the tax system, eventually the bill comes due.”

The Internal Revenue Service – Criminal Investigation investigated this case. The sentence was imposed by U.S. District Judge Matthew P. Brookman.

U.S. Attorney Wheeler thanked Assistant U.S. Attorney Matthew Miller, who prosecuted this case.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

###
title: Evansville Tax Preparer Lands in Federal Prison for $965,000 COVID 19 Tax Credit Fraud

Amo, Auchincloss, Balint Conduct Unannounced Oversight Visit to Burlington ICE Facility
The Burlington, Massachusetts U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility serves as the New England regional headquarters and field office
Burlington, MA – TODAY, Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI-01), Congressman Jake Auchincloss (D-MA-04), and Congresswoman Becca Balint (D-VT-AL) conducted an unannounced congressional oversight visit of the Burlington Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility, where dozens of individuals have been detained. The ICE facility was designed to temporarily detain individuals for no longer than 12 hours, but under President Trump, ICE detainees have been held there for days without proper food, beds, or showers.
During the visit, the lawmakers asked about access to lawyers, the treatment of people in ICE custody, and whether the facility was complying with federal law.
“ICE and Border Patrol continue to negatively impact our communities and that’s why I conducted my congressional oversight with a visit to the Burlington facility unannounced,” said Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI-01). “During my inspection of the Burlington facility with Congressman Auchincloss and Congresswoman Balint, we witnessed individuals held for processing, questioned ICE regarding our constituents’ concerns, and pressed for more humane treatment of those in custody. I will not stop advocating for safe communities, due process, and humane immigration reform.”
“Today I conducted an unannounced inspection of the Burlington ICE facility. Persistent congressional oversight, in concert with public pressure, has driven modest improvements to detention operations over the past year since my previous inspection in June of 2025. I will continue oversight and accountability measures in pursuit of due process and human dignity,” said Congressman Auchincloss (D-MA-04).
“Vermonters deserve answers about what’s happening to people from our state who are being held in ICE custody,” said Congresswoman Becca Balint (D-VT-AL). “This facility was designed for stays of no more than 12 hours, but people have been held for days without basic necessities. We went in unannounced because we wanted to see the conditions for ourselves and get answers. ICE has a responsibility to treat people humanely and follow the law, and we’re going to hold them to it.”
Background
The visit builds on Congressman Amo’s ongoing work to hold federal immigration enforcement accountable and protect the dignity and legal rights of people in ICE custody. Amo has consistently opposed funding the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and ICE without strict constitutional guardrails and accountability.
Congressman Amo has stood with Rhode Islanders of faith praying for the end of the Trump administration’s cruel treatment of our immigrant neighbors.
In January, Amoconvened Muslim, Jewish, and Christian faith leaders to strategize about how congregations and elected leaders can work together to protect against Trump’s violent ICE and Border Patrol invasion of our cities.

On Oct. 16, 1919, Maj. Gen. (later Lt. Gen.) James G. Harbord submitted the final report from his intelligence mission to Armenia to the American Peace Commission (alternately known as the American Commission to Negotiate Peace) at the Paris Peace Conference. The report detailed a months-long investigation into political and military conditions in postwar Europe, particularly how war and genocide against the Armenians affected American efforts towards peace in Asia Minor and Eastern Europe.
At the end of the First World War, the delegate nations involved with the Paris Peace Conference were tasked with coordinating various peace negotiations across numerous affected European nations. Such negotiations required extensive information on these regions and their particular grievances. After the war, many of the reports by American military attachés stationed across Europe were passed to the Military Intelligence Division in Washington, D.C. Unfortunately, the American Peace Commission did not have the authority to examine these records for successive intelligence operations.
Needing accurate intelligence and unwilling to rely solely on the limited available attaché reports, the Americans suggested an ambitious program to establish missions to collect information in key regions of Europe. These missions were principally directed by the American Commission and primarily consisted of American government and military personnel. Ellis L. Dresel, military attaché to Berlin from 1915 to 1917, was selected as chairman of the new program, while Col. (later Maj. Gen.) Ralph Van Deman, intelligence officer with the American Peace Commission, served as one of the Army’s representatives.
The crumbling Ottoman Empire—particularly Turkey and Armenia—represented an especially fraught problem for the Peace Conference. Between 1915 and 1917, the Ottoman Turks had massacred between 600,000 and 1.5 million Armenians, more than half of the Armenian population in northwest Asia. Thousands more were deported, sold into slavery, unwillingly married to the Turks, or were forcibly converted to Islam. Under the Americans’ new program, General Harbord was appointed commander of the American Mission to Armenia to collect intelligence from this extremely troubled region. Harbord had served as General John J. Pershing’s chief of staff from 1917 to 1918 and, later in the war, commanded the 4th Marine Brigade and the 2d Infantry Division before taking over the American Expeditionary Forces’ Services of Supply. His military prestige, experience, and integrity prompted his appointment as leader of the Armenia Mission.
On Oct. 16, 1919, Harbord submitted his final report to the American Peace Commission. The report summarized the expedition through Armenia and Asia Minor and included a lengthy history of the Armenians and their relations with the Turks and Russians; interviews with government officials, as well as victims, witnesses, and perpetrators of the genocide; and recommendations for the Peace Conference to limit further conflict in the region. The report found the only way to maintain peace between nations in the region was to specifically include Armenians in mandates and relief aid ordered for the whole of Asia Minor and the collapsing empire but to avoid granting aid solely to Armenians, as this could lead to further bloodshed.
Furthermore, in “certain regions where the temptation to reprisals for past wrongs will be strong for at least a generation,” the report recommended an occupying military force be deployed to maintain order and support the establishment of native constabularies. It outlined reasons for and against the United States taking on this mandate and concluded: “If we refuse to assume [responsibility]. . .we shall be considered by many millions of people as having left unfinished the task for which we entered the war, and as having betrayed their hopes.”
Conditions in the Near East: Report of the American Military Mission to Armenia can be read in its entirety at https://www.loc.gov/item/20026422/.
Article by Erin E. Thompson, USAICoE Staff Historian. (Article updated October 2026) New issues of This Week in MI History are published each week.
