SACRAMENTO, Calif. — Las Vegas residents Ricky Lee Ware, 43, and Kimberly Ann Wallace, 30, pleaded guilty today to conspiracy to commit access device fraud, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced.

According to court documents, between July 2020 and January 2021, the defendants conspired to obtain debit cards that allowed them to access unemployment benefits. The unemployment benefits were in the names of people who did not know the defendants. The defendants then used the debit cards to withdraw more than $900,000 in unemployment benefits from ATMs.

The U.S. Department of Labor Office of Inspector General, Homeland Security Investigations, the Federal Bureau of Investigation; and the Department of Homeland Security Office of Inspector General conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Nicholas M. Fogg is prosecuting the case.

Ware and Wallace are scheduled to be sentenced by U.S. District Judge Dena Coggins on Feb. 19, 2027, and face a maximum of 7.5 years in prison. The actual sentence, however, will be determined at the discretion of the court after consideration of any applicable statutory factors and the federal Sentencing Guidelines, which take into account a number of variables.

The third defendant in the case, Carlos Lee Sanchez Jr., 46, of Sacramento, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit access device fraud in June 2026 and is scheduled to be sentenced Nov. 13, 2026.

This effort is part of a California COVID-19 Fraud Enforcement Strike Force operation, one of five interagency COVID-19 fraud strike force teams established by the U.S. Department of Justice. The California Strike Force combines law enforcement and prosecutorial resources in the Eastern and Central Districts of California and focuses on large-scale, multistate pandemic relief fraud perpetrated by criminal organizations and transnational actors. The strike forces use prosecutor-led and data analyst-driven teams to identify and bring to justice those who stole pandemic relief funds.
title: Two Plead Guilty to Unemployment Insurance Benefits Fraud Conspiracy

Media Note

Office of the Spokesman

October 16, 2026

On October 15, Deputy Secretary of State Landau hosted the U.S.-Caribbean Dialogue at the Department of State, delivering on the commitment Secretary Rubio made to Caribbean Community (CARICOM) Heads of Government at their February meeting in Saint Kitts and Nevis. High-level delegations from Antigua and Barbuda, The Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Dominica, the Dominican Republic, Grenada, Guyana, Haiti, Jamaica, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Suriname, and Trinidad and Tobago joined the United States to expand cooperation on shared economic, energy, and security priorities. At a business luncheon and an evening reception, Caribbean delegations met with American business leaders to discuss opportunities for projects in energy, critical minerals, ports, and digital infrastructure that will create jobs and growth in both the United States and the Caribbean.

Dialogue sessions addressed energy security, economic growth, critical infrastructure, trusted technology, disaster response and health cooperation, and the fight against narco-terrorists and transnational criminal organizations. Participants discussed access to U.S. energy and technology, fair and transparent procurement, trusted digital and port infrastructure, self-sufficient health workforces, and closer coordination to disrupt illicit narcotics and firearms trafficking.

Advancing U.S.-Caribbean Commercial Diplomacy

Caribbean Investment Summit: The Department of State announced that it will host a Caribbean Investment Summit in early 2027 to connect U.S. companies, financiers, and government finance agencies with Caribbean partners to help them close deals in open, competitive markets.

Promoting Trusted Digital Technology

Caribbean and Central America Undersea Cables Program: The Department of State announced $175.8 million to expand trusted, high-speed undersea cable connectivity across the Caribbean and Central America and make trusted connections more resilient to disruption.

Strengthening Health Self-Sufficiency

Americas Strategic Partnership for Independent Regional Healthcare Excellence (ASPIRE): Working with Congress, the Department of State intends to provide $61.5 million through ASPIRE to help Caribbean governments build self-sufficient health workforces by hiring health professionals ethically and transparently, with fair pay going to the workers themselves.

Advancing Regional Security Through the Caribbean Basin Security Initiative (CBSI)

Protecting Critical Infrastructure and Maritime Resources: The Department of State announced $37 million in CBSI programming to secure critical digital infrastructure and ports, and counter illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing.

Law Enforcement and Security Cooperation: The State Department announced $66 million in CBSI programming to strengthen Caribbean partners’ ability to counter transnational criminal organizations and secure the region’s borders. The total includes $55 million in International Narcotics Control and Law Enforcement assistance and $11 million in Foreign Military Financing.

CBSI Security Ministerial: The United States will work with Caribbean security ministers and the CARICOM Implementation Agency for Crime and Security (IMPACS) to convene the next CBSI Security Ministerial in spring 2027.

Tags
title: United States Hosts Caribbean Dialogue to Advance Shared Security and Prosperity

BUFFALO, N.Y.-U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Michael Herrera, 45, of the Bronx, NY, who was convicted of conspiracy to commit bank fraud and aggravated identity theft, was sentenced to serve 54 months in prison by U.S. District Judge Richard J. Arcara.

In January 2025, in Bridgeport, Connecticut, co-conspirator Vance Ashley was recruited by members of the conspiracy to pose as other persons and make unauthorized withdrawals from the other persons’ bank accounts. Ashley agreed to do this in exchange for money. Between January 28 and February 3, 2025, Ashley drove with Herrera, and two other co-conspirators, to bank branches in Wilmington, Delaware, Liberty, NY, and Lock Haven, PA, where Ashely used the identifications of other individuals to make, or attempt to make, unauthorized withdrawals from the victims’ bank accounts.

On February 5, 2025, the defendants drove to a Northwest Bank branch in Lockport, within the Western District of New York. Ashley made an unauthorized withdrawal of from the account of an individual residing in Erie, PA. Ashley also purchased a bank check using funds from the account. That same day, the defendants drove to another Northwest Bank branch in Williamsville, within the Western District of New York, and again Ashley made an unauthorized withdrawal from an account and purchased a bank check using funds from the account of a victim from North East PA. Also on February 5, 2025, Hererra illegally used the identification of another person during the commission of a felony.

The total loss amount, including actual loss and intended loss, is $91,300.00.

Ashley was previously convicted and sentenced to serve 27 months in prison.

The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Paul E. Bonanno. The sentencing is the result of an investigation by the Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigation Division, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Harry Chavis and Homeland Security Investigations, under the direction of Acting Special Agent-in-Charge Anthony Patrone.

# # # #

Coast Guard repatriates Cuban national following rescue off South Florida
Southeast Public Affairs - Southeastpublicaffairs@uscg.mil
MIAMI — Coast Guard Cutter Isaac Mayo’s crew repatriated one person to Cuba, Wednesday, following a maritime interdiction near Key Biscayne.
A good Samaritan reported to Coast Guard Sector Miami watchstanders they rescued a person after finding them on a 15-foot homemade raft without a life jacket.
A Coast Guard Station Miami Beach boat crew and U.S. Customs and Border Protection Air and Marine Operations personnel responded to the scene and took custody of the person for further processing.
“Attempting to migrate by sea aboard homemade, unseaworthy vessels is extremely dangerous. No one should risk their life to try to enter the U.S. illegally,” said Lt. Cmdr. Jon Girot, U.S. Coast Guard Liaison Officer / DHS Attaché at U.S. Embassy Havana, Cuba. “Our crews remain committed to protecting lives at sea and preventing unlawful maritime migration.”
Once aboard a Coast Guard cutter, individuals are processed to determine their identity and are provided food, water, shelter and basic medical attention before transfer or repatriation, as appropriate.
The Coast Guard, along with its Operation Vigilant Sentry partners, maintains a continual presence with air, land and sea assets in support of Operation Vigilant Sentry. The combined, multilayered approach is designed to protect safety of life at sea while preventing unlawful maritime entry to the United States and its territories.

Today, Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16) reacted to the latest report from the Joint Economic Committee (JEC) detailing how the average household in El Paso has had to spend thousands of dollars more for goods and services under the Trump administration and Republican rule. Instead of working to curb inflation, policies like the president's tarriffs and his war in Iran have pushed prices even higher.

This report is further proof that El Pasoans should take him and his party at his word when he says that he doesn't think about Americans' financial situations at all."

Housing Costs
Families have had to spend an additional $281 on housing costs such as rent and mortgage payments since President Trump took office.
Grocery Costs
Americans paid an additional $310 for groceries in President Trump’s first year than in 2024, and grocery prices are now more than 4% higher than when Trump took office. Healthcare Costs
Because of Trump and Republicans’ refusal to extend the Affordable Care Act (ACA) tax cuts that help people afford their health insurance, monthly premiums for ACA plans rose over 50% on average in 2026 compared to last year. Medicare Program; Implementation of Sections 6219, 6220, and 6224 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (CMS-4214-P)
Background
On Oct. 16, 2026, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) issued a proposed rule to implement key sections of the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2026 including section 6220 (Requiring Enhanced and Accurate Lists of (REAL) Health Providers Act) and section 6224 (Modernizing and Ensuring Pharmacy Benefit Manager Accountability). This rule also proposes a conforming change mandated by section 6219 of the CAA (Adjustments to Medicare Part D Cost-Sharing Reductions for Low-Income Individuals) that would reduce the generic drug copayment from $1 to $0 for full-benefit dual eligible individuals.
Implementing Certain Provisions of Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
On February 3, 2026, the CAA of 2026, which included several changes to the MA and Part D programs, was signed into law. In this rule, we are proposing to implement the following sections:
- Adjustments to Medicare Part D Cost-Sharing Reductions for Low-Income Individuals (Section 6219): This proposed rule implements Section 6219 of the CAA that would reduce the generic drug copayment from $1 to $0 for full-benefit dual eligible individuals at or below 100% of the Federal Poverty Level, effective for plan years starting Jan. 1, 2028.
- Requiring Enhanced and Accurate Lists of (REAL) Health Providers Act (Section 6220): CMS proposes to codify regulations to implement the REAL Health Providers Act, which establishes new provider directory verification and accuracy requirements for MA organizations beginning in contract year 2028. Specifically, CMS proposes requirements to implement this new law related to provider directory verification and maintenance standards, annual accuracy analysis and reporting, public reporting of accuracy scores, and cost-sharing protections for enrollees who rely on inaccurate provider directory information. CMS also proposes to codify the statutory requirements for contract year 2029, including that CMS must publicly display provider directory accuracy scores in a machine-readable format, and MA organizations must prominently display those scores in their provider directories. Through these proposed codifications implementing the REAL Health Providers Act, CMS seeks to promote provider directory accuracy and accountability among MA organizations to ensure that beneficiaries are provided with clear, accurate information on the network of providers available to meet their healthcare needs.
- Modernizing and Ensuring Pharmacy Benefit Manager Accountability (Section 6224): CMS has several proposals to implement section 6224 of the CAA, which established requirements related to pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) and their affiliates specific to the Medicare Part D program. These proposals include new requirements governing the remuneration that PBMs and their affiliates may receive for services in connection with the utilization of Part D drugs, data reporting by PBMs to Part D prescription drug plan (PDP) sponsors and CMS, transparency in PBM price guarantee arrangements, disclosure by PBMs to PDP sponsors of the terms of certain agreements between PBMs or their affiliates and pharmaceutical manufacturers, and other requirements added by the CAA. CMS also proposes to define key terms related to such requirements and establish compliance and enforcement mechanisms, including disgorgement of funds to CMS for violations of the remuneration requirements.
The proposed rule will be open for public comment for 60 days following publication in the Federal Register.

title: Medicare Program; Implementation of Sections 6219, 6220, and 6224 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (CMS-4214-P)

text:
Fast Facts
Ghost preparers are paid tax preparers who hide their identities on returns and avoid accountability for making errors, committing fraud, or stealing refunds. But ghost preparers are hard for IRS to identify—leaving taxpayers responsible for errors or fraud.
The IRS has started addressing this problem, but its efforts are fragmented. For example, relevant data is scattered across several databases. This makes it hard for IRS to use this information to better understand ghost preparer behavior and protect taxpayers.
IRS also doesn't have a strategy, goals, or ways to measure the success of its efforts.
Our recommendations address these issues.
A pen points to the paid preparer section of a tax return.
Highlights
What GAO Found
Ghost preparers are paid tax preparers who do not comply with requirements to identify themselves on tax returns they prepare for others. Ghost preparers may intentionally leave identifying information off to get away with filing fraudulent income tax returns, stealing taxpayers’ refunds, and stealing taxpayers’ identities. Courts have ordered individual ghost preparers to pay millions in restitution to the government, but according to Internal Revenue Service (IRS) officials, the total effect of ghost preparers is likely greater, in part, because ghost preparers are difficult to detect.
IRS maintains some data on identified ghost preparers, but the systems IRS uses to track ghost preparer cases and outcomes are not connected and have limitations that impede their usefulness. As a result, IRS does not know how many ghost preparers it has identified, investigated, and addressed. Better understanding existing data, including its limitations, would help IRS direct enforcement resources and protect taxpayers from fraudulent returns or stolen refunds.
IRS identifies and addresses ghost preparers through data analysis, referrals, taxpayer education, and enforcement actions such as investigations. However, these efforts are fragmented across six offices and IRS is missing opportunities to share information and better address risks. A comprehensive, coordinated preparer strategy, including efforts addressing ghost preparers, could help IRS better align resources with risks and identify additional needs.
Notional Example of Fragmented Activities Compared to a Comprehensive, Coordinated Strategy
While IRS has some activities to address ghost preparers, including data analysis and taxpayer education, it has not developed measurable objectives or performance goals. Defining objectives, goals, and performance measures could help IRS reliably assess whether its efforts are reducing ghost preparer activity and adjust its strategy and allocate resources more effectively.
Why GAO Did This Study
Paid tax preparers prepared more than half of all tax returns in fiscal year 2025 and have an enormous effect on IRS’s ability to administer tax laws effectively. However, ghost preparers may hide their identities to avoid accountability and leave taxpayers responsible for inaccurate or fraudulent returns they prepare.
GAO was asked to examine IRS’s efforts to address ghost preparers. This report (1) describes how ghost preparers have harmed taxpayers and IRS, (2) assesses the extent to which IRS maintains data on ghost preparers, and (3) evaluates IRS actions to identify and address ghost preparers.
GAO reviewed federal court cases, and IRS documentation and data. GAO compared IRS’s efforts to leading practices for evidence-based policymaking and consumer education planning. GAO also interviewed IRS and Department of Justice officials and stakeholder groups, such as IRS oversight and industry groups.
Recommendations
GAO is making three recommendations including that IRS identify opportunities to enhance data collecting, sharing, and analysis to inform its ghost preparer efforts, incorporate ghost preparer efforts within a comprehensive, coordinated paid preparer strategy, and define measurable objectives and goals. IRS agreed with GAO’s recommendations and described steps it plans to take or started taking, in response to each recommendation.
title: Tax Filing: IRS Should Enhance Ghost Preparer Identification and Compliance Efforts in a Comprehensive Preparer Strategy

Temporary flight restriction will prohibit unauthorized drone operations within one nautical mile of the U.S.-Mexico border, from the surface to 400 feet
WASHINGTON — The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS), along with the Department of Transportation (DOT) and Department of War (DOW), issued the following statement announcing a new, coordinated effort to strengthen airspace security along the southern U.S. border through a temporary flight restriction (TFR) for drones. The TFR – effective today – will bar any unauthorized drone activity up to 400 feet above ground level and extend one nautical mile north of the U.S.-Mexico border.
The move builds on the Trump Administration’s successful efforts to secure the southern border and defend the homeland from national security threats – including illicit cartel activity. The new measure will reduce risks to ongoing border security operations, protect federal personnel, facilities, and the Homeland, and enhance enforcement against those who violate the restrictions.
“DHS will not stop building on the historic progress made to secure the southern border,” said DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin. “This action will help counter cartel drone threats, protect our personnel, and strengthen security in the airspace above the border. President Trump promised to secure the border, and we are delivering on that promise through continued action and strong partnership with Department of Transportation and the Department of War.”
“President Trump promised to secure the Southern Border, and he did. Now we’re doubling down on that promise by protecting our skies from cartel drone threats and other illicit activities,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “I appreciate the close collaboration with our partners at DHS and DOW as we work together to defend our airspace and keep the American people safe.”
"The United States government will maintain 100% operational control of our border: land, air, and sea,” said Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. “For too long, cartels have taken advantage of gaps along our southern border. Thanks to President Donald J. Trump, those days are over. By restricting unauthorized drone activity, we are giving commanders greater awareness, greater decision space, and more options to defend the Homeland. Equipped with cutting-edge technology—including Directed Energy Weapons—our warfighters will shoot down any cartel drone that threatens America’s sovereignty.”
Additional Information:
The FAA will publish a NOTAM which will include links to the Domestic Notice and the FAA's UAS Data Delivery System.
Drone operators are responsible for reviewing all applicable NOTAMs and restrictions before operating and must comply with the requirements in effect for their planned operations.
# # #
title: DHS, Department of Transportation, and Department of War Join Forces to Protect Southern Border Airspace

Press Releases
October 16, 2026
Akron, AL — Today, U.S. Rep. Terri Sewell (AL-07) sent a letter to U.S. Postmaster General David Steiner and Senior Vice President of Facilities and Infrastructure Benjamin Kuo demanding the immediate reopening of the Akron Post Office after USPS abruptly shut down the facility on October 14, 2026, without warning to the community. Sewell spoke out against the closure on social media on Wednesday.
The closure came 16 days before the previously announced October 30 closure date and just weeks before the November midterm elections. Residents arrived to find the doors chained shut and their P.O. boxes dismantled, leaving many without clear instructions on how to access their mail at the Moundville location.
In her letter, Sewell raised serious concerns about conflicting information from USPS regarding the closure. While USPS cited failed lease negotiations, documentation provided to Sewell's office indicates that the property owner agreed in writing to maintain the existing rental rate through 2031. The property owner also denied issuing the notice to vacate that USPS cited as justification for the closure.
Sewell warned that the abrupt closure could jeopardize residents’ ability to receive and return absentee ballots in time to be counted. Completed absentee ballots must be received by Hale County by October 27, leaving voters with little time to navigate the disruption.
“By shuttering the Post Office without warning, USPS has jeopardized residents' ability to receive and return their absentee ballots in time to be counted,” Sewell wrote. “The possibility that eligible voters could be disenfranchised because of USPS's unilateral decision to close this facility, without adequate notice or a plan to protect election mail, is wholly unacceptable."
Sewell also questioned whether USPS followed federal requirements governing the suspension or discontinuance of postal services and raised concerns about the agency’s failure to provide adequate notice to residents.
In her letter, Sewell is requesting that USPS:
- Immediately reopen the Akron Post Office.
- Explain the circumstances surrounding the closure and provide documentation supporting USPS’s stated reasons.
- Develop a plan to restore mail services at the Akron location through at least October 30, the previously announced closure date.
- Detail the steps being taken to protect, process, and deliver all election mail, including ballots that were at the facility when it closed.
- Provide documentation demonstrating compliance with federal regulations governing the suspension or discontinuance of postal services.
Sewell requested a written response from USPS by Monday, October 19, 2026.
“The residents of Akron, Alabama have the right to access their mail, including but not limited to Social Security checks, medications, bills, and ballots so they can exercise their sacred right to vote in the upcoming election,” Sewell wrote.
Read the full letter here.

HONOLULU – United States Attorney Ken Sorenson announced that Heidi Cafirma, 46, of Waipahu, Hawaii, was sentenced on September 30, 2026, by United States District Judge Shanlyn A.S. Park to 24 months in prison followed by 3 years of supervised release for filing false tax returns and wire fraud. Cafirma was also ordered to forfeit $70,500 and pay up to over $1 million in restitution, which total amount will be determined by the court at a later date. Cafirma pled guilty pursuant to a plea agreement in December 2025.

In 2020, the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (CARES) Act created the Pandemic Unemployment Assistance (PUA) unemployment insurance program to provide emergency unemployment payments to certain workers whose livelihoods were impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic but who were ineligible for traditional state unemployment insurance benefits, such as business owners, self-employed workers, independent contractors, and those with a limited work history who were out of business or had significantly reduced their services as a direct result of the pandemic. To obtain either traditional unemployment insurance (UI) or PUA UI benefit payments, claimants could submit a claim online. If approved, the U.S. Treasury typically deposited payments every week into a claimant’s bank account. To continue to receive benefit payments, claimants were required to certify on a weekly basis under penalty of law that they remained unemployed or partially employed, and eligible to receive benefit payments.

According to court documents, Cafirma admitted that between June 2020 and September 2021, she submitted 22 false claims online for UI benefit payments for herself by repeatedly falsely certifying under penalty of law that she was unemployed and not receiving income, despite knowing that her certifications were false because she received over $1 million in income during that period from her and her husband’s unlicensed construction business. Cafirma fraudulently obtained at least $70,500 in unemployment insurance and PUA UI benefits to which she was not entitled.

Between 2016 and 2020, Cafirma also willfully failed to pay federal and state taxes on over $3.4 million in income from her and her husband’s construction business. She provided false documents to her tax return preparer that omitted income and then filed false tax returns with the IRS. Over at least four years, Cafirma took steps to conceal her income by directing construction customers to write checks to her personally rather than to her business, funneling income through sixteen bank accounts at multiple financial institutions, and structuring multiple cash deposits in amounts less than $10,000 to avoid banks from filing of currency transaction reports.

“Bringing to justice criminals like Cafirma – who defraud the government, divert critical and limited resources to themselves out of greed, and steal from hardworking, taxpaying citizens – remains one of my office’s top priorities,” said United States Attorney Ken Sorenson. “We will continue to leverage our resources and those of the National Fraud Enforcement Division to investigate and prosecute those who steal or fraudulently misuse taxpayer dollars.”

“Ms. Cafirma’s pattern of fraud has caught up to her with today’s sentencing. Not only did she lie to fraudulently underpay her fair share of taxes, Ms. Cafirma also stole funds meant to help others in the community that truly needed the assistance,” said Assistant Special Agent in Charge Jay Gregory, IRS Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI), Seattle Field Office. “IRS-CI is committed to protecting our communities and the financial systems we all rely on, and we will continue to investigate criminals like Ms. Cafirma.”

The IRS – Criminal Investigation investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Rebecca A. Perlmutter prosecuted the case.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Waipahu Women Sentenced to Two Years in Prison for Pandemic and Tax Fraud While Earning Millions from an Unlicensed Construction Business

David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, and Thomas Demeo, Special Agent in Charge of IRS Criminal Investigation in New England, announced that DAVANTE MALLARD, 33, of New Haven, waived his right to be indicted and pleaded guilty today before U.S. District Judge Sarah F. Russell in New Haven to an offense stemming from a pandemic relief program fraud scheme.

According to court documents and statements made in court, in March 2020, Congress passed legislation that sought to mitigate the economic harm caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. Legislation included the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act (the CARES Act), which created employee retention credits (ERCs) that were intended to repay employers for certain costs expended to retain employees during the pandemic and permitted businesses to recoup previously paid wages and certain health insurance costs, and the Families First Coronavirus Response Act, which created the sick and family leave credit (SFLC) that reimbursed small and mid-sized employers for the cost of providing paid sick and family leave wages to employees for leave related to COVID-19 during the pandemic.

Mallard owned Mallard Dynasty Realty Group (MDR Group), which provided real estate and property management services. The business earned little to no income, had no employees, had not paid wages, and had not filed W-2 forms with the Internal Revenue Service.

In early 2022, Mallard was contacted by individuals who he knew who instructed him to open an online account with a business that provided online tax preparation services. Mallard than provided the individuals with the account information and password. Between April 2022 and February 2023, the individuals accessed the account and prepared and filed with the IRS fraudulent Employer’s Quarterly Federal Tax Returns (Forms 941) for MDR Group. The Forms 941 misrepresented the number of employees and total wages paid, and were used to apply for large ERC and SFLC refunds. When contacted by the IRS to verify information about MDR Group, Mallard provided false information, including that his business had five employees.

Between August 2022 and March 2023, MDR Group received from the IRS six refund checks totaling $256,906. Mallard kicked a portion of the refund monies back to the individuals who orchestrated the scheme.

Mallard pleaded guilty to making false claims regarding IRS refunds, an offense that carries a maximum term of imprisonment of five years.

Mallard is released on a $50,000 bond pending sentencing, which is not scheduled.

This investigation is being conducted by the Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigation Division. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Christopher W. Schmeisser.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

When Christy Miller moved to Fort Bliss, Texas, with her Family, finding employment was a challenge. As a military spouse, she was looking for a job that fit her experience but also worked for her Family. Miller found an opportunity with Child and Youth Services at a child development center.
“This was my first time returning to work since becoming a mom,” Miller said. “The CDC gave me the opportunity to take that step while still having my son close by, which was incredibly important to me.”
Once at the center, Miller realized how much time and effort went into training staff to ensure children at the centers were safe, learning and developing.
“As a mom, that gives me a lot of confidence in where my son spends his day,” Miller said.
Miller, the 2025 AUSA Volunteer Family of the Year spouse, made those remarks during the Warfighter and Family Forum, “Empowering Parents and Children,” at the 2026 AUSA Annual Meeting. The session was designed to provide Army Families with information and resources for child care, details about options for care and services provided by school liaison Officers.
Speakers and panelists highlighted the Department’s priority to always provide child care directly on the installation. However, for geographically dispersed Families or for those facing extensive waitlists, the Army Fee Assistance program provides a critical bridge to approved community-based care while ensuring children can thrive and Families can maintain readiness and well-being.
The session highlighted the Army’s tiered approach to child care: maintaining on-installation care as the priority, while simplifying the process for Families to access approved community-based providers when capacity or distance requires it. Throughout the forum, panelists discussed the importance of making information accessible and processes easier to navigate.
Keynote speaker Tim Dill, Assistant Secretary of War for Manpower and Reserve Affairs, emphasized that strong Families mean a strong Army and that strong Families are anchored by parents. As the Army works to attract and retain Soldiers, Dill said Family support is the best predictor of whether a Soldier will stay in the force.
“A Soldier who does not have the support of their Family or is not confident their Family is well cared for cannot fully be in the fight,” Dill said. “I know exactly the level of discipline and concentration it takes to do the things that we call young Americans to do, and the last thing you can afford to do is be wondering how your Family is doing when you are on the front line.”
Dill said the Army cannot simply maintain the status quo but must instead put parents in the driver’s seat to determine what is best for their children.
“We must offer parents affordable, accessible and high-quality child care,” Dill said. “We are improving those offerings by refining the compensation system for child care workers. We need to make sure that we appropriately incentivize them and care for them and make it doable for them to accept employment at our CDCs.”
During the panel discussion, Stephen Simmons, Deputy Assistant Secretary of War for Military Community and Family Policy, encouraged the audience to think of Family support as an ecosystem. For example, Simmons said a child’s educational needs cannot be supported without addressing child care issues.
“It’s not as if you just fix this one thing right here, I’d be good,” Simmons said. “It’s multiple things.”
The key, according to Simmons, is empowering parents. School liaisons are embedded at every base and installation to work with Families so they can access the educational resources parents need for their children. Simmons said they also have a plan to modernize and accelerate support for homeschoolers.
“One of the first steps we did was we educated our school liaisons,” Simmons said. “We accelerated the training curriculum that our school liaisons all take so they are set up to support homeschoolers.”
Panelist Josh Gwinn, Director, Directorate of Family and Morale, Welfare and Recreation, U.S. Army Installation Management Command, said meeting child care needs requires expanded access to fee assistance. If a Family needs care at a specific installation and immediate care is not available or within a specified time, the waitlist is reviewed and Army Fee Assistance is distributed as appropriate.
“What we’ve seen is that that immediate need wait list is probably the lowest we’ve seen in the last 10 years of the Army,” Gwinn said.
Simmons said one of the benefits of addressing child care and education issues is that spouses are free to pursue employment opportunities. Finding those opportunities can be difficult, especially for spouses who move every few years. One solution is the SpouseWorks website, which Simmons said makes employment resources accessible.
“There’s multiple options for military spouses,” Simmons said. Those options include career coaching, resume building and SpouseWork scholarships. “For spouses who are more in their early career stages, we also have a SpouseWorks Fellowship … it’s a three-month paid fellowship of your choice.”
For Soldiers with a Family member with special needs, panelist Col. Anne Chiquitucto, Chief of the Exceptional Family Member Program, said she and her team recognize that frequent moves can disrupt special education services for children and cause friction for parents. Chiquitucto said the Army has created a multitiered advocacy network to help parents, which includes EFMP support at installations.
“They’re there to connect a Family member to the community and education services to ensure that the IEP requirements are being met,” Chiquitucto said. School liaisons are another level of support. “They would be a good resource if a Family member was looking to see which school in a district would be a good fit for their child.”
While additional resources and more options can better support Families, they are only useful if both Soldiers and spouses know about them. Panelist Command Sgt. Maj. Brett W. Johnson, Command Sergeant Major of the XVIII Airborne Corps, said the installation works to make information easily accessible for new Families moving to Fort Bragg, North Carolina. He said it’s also important to recognize that circumstances change as Families grow.
“The upstream effect that we are looking at on Fort Bragg (is) to connect all of those questions, resources and answers and make it very simple,” Johnson said. “Here’s a QR code for this, here are all the different resources, so when you come (here), you’re more prepared to move into your position.”
Whatever phase a Family is in, Johnson said it’s essential for leaders to understand the range of support available.
“I always think: Are we treating the symptom or the disease?” Johnson said. “Are we hopping back and forth because we’re playing Whac-A-Mole with people’s problems, or are we actually trying to find a solution?”
Miller, who is pursuing her bachelor’s degree, has moved with her Family three times in the last five years and understands the challenges many spouses face in pursuing their careers. She encourages them to take advantage of the options the military offers.
“What I’ve come to appreciate most is that CYS can support military Families in more ways than one,” Miller said. “It provides care for our children, but it can also provide employment training and opportunities for military spouses who are trying to build their careers while navigating military life. Being part of that has also given me a much greater appreciation for the work that goes into caring for and supporting military children.”
Watch the panel discussion in its entirety at DVIDS.
title: Putting Parents in the Driver’s Seat: Empowering Army Families

Trump Administration Announces New Funding to Expand Rural EMS and Bring More Care Directly to Patients Across Montana
This federal investment will give rural emergency medical teams the tools to provide in-home care, manage chronic conditions, and help Montanans avoid unnecessary emergency visits
Today, the Trump Administration announced $3.63 million in Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) funding to expand community integrated health (CIH) services across rural Montana. This investment will help rural emergency medical services (EMS) agencies deliver more care directly to patients and connect them to vital resources, keeping high-quality care close to home for Montanans.
This transformational funding will deliver awards to 17 rural EMS agencies to cover new or expanded staff positions, transportation costs, equipment, and clinical integration needs such as training and electronic health records. Participating EMS professionals will carry out patient care plans under medical director oversight, extending primary care into the home. Services include post-discharge follow-up, fall risk assessments, wound care, lab draws, point-of-care testing, and resource navigation — helping patients manage chronic conditions like asthma and diabetes while overcoming barriers such as limited transportation and mobility.
The Rural Health Transformation Program is expanding access to quality healthcare, regardless of a patient’s zip code, and equipping first responders with the lifesaving resources they need when every second counts. This funding will make critical investments to strengthen rural healthcare, expand access to lifesaving services, and bring modern technology to communities across Montana.
“President Trump understands that every American deserves high-quality healthcare, no matter where they live,” said Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “We are putting resources directly into rural communities to strengthen the health workforce, modernize infrastructure, expand access, and bring care closer to home. We are giving states the flexibility to build solutions around the people they serve, while demanding accountability for results. That is how we strengthen rural health, improve the lives of patients and families, and Make America Healthy Again.”
“President Trump gave states the resources to transform rural healthcare, and now we’re seeing those dollars move from plans into action,” said Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “Our focus now is on making sure this early progress translates into lasting results for rural patients and more resilient, sustainable health systems in the years ahead. In Montana, that means EMS professionals have the tools to manage chronic conditions and deliver care directly to patients close to home.”
Today’s investment was made possible through the Working Families Tax Cuts Act — passed by Republicans in Congress and unanimously opposed by Democrats — delivering a historic $50 billion investment to help states transform the way healthcare is delivered in America.
“Through the Rural Health Transformation Fund, President Donald J. Trump and Administrator Oz are directly addressing the health needs of rural Montana,” Gov. Greg Gianforte said. “This $3.63 million investment will support 17 EMS agencies in bringing care into Montanans’ homes, helping patients manage chronic conditions, and connecting them to critical health services. We’re grateful for the Trump administration’s ongoing commitment to our rural and frontier communities.”
“This is great news for Montana. Access to reliable, affordable medical care is essential, and this funding will help more Montanans, especially those in our rural communities, receive the care they deserve. I applaud the administration for making this possible,” said Sen. Steve Daines.
“Access to quality health care shouldn’t depend on your zip code. Our rural EMS providers are on the front lines of keeping Montanans healthy and safe, often serving communities where care is hours away. This investment will give them more tools to deliver care directly to patients, prevent emergencies before they happen, and ensure families in rural Montana aren’t left behind,” said Sen. Tim Sheehy.
“President Trump and Republicans delivered the Rural Health Transformation Program to strengthen healthcare in places like rural Montana, and this White House is following through. $3.63 million in awards going directly to help Montana EMS care for patients at home and manage chronic conditions before they become emergencies. This is the kind of practical support that helps Montanans stay healthy and independent, and keep our rural hospitals open for the long run,” said Rep. Ryan Zinke.
“For too long, rural communities in Montana have been asked to do more with less, and our EMS heroes have carried that burden with extraordinary courage and determination. Too many Montanans live in ambulance deserts, hours from the nearest hospital, and that puts the weight squarely on our first responders. I was proud to vote for H.R. 1, which created the Rural Health Transformation Program, and these $3.63 million in awards to 17 EMS agencies show what it can do by bringing care directly to patients’ doors and closing the distance between our families and the health care they deserve. I am deeply grateful to the first responders who will turn this investment into healthier, safer communities,” said Rep. Troy Downing.
Today’s announcement is one part of the larger overall funding amount awarded to Montana for fiscal year 2026.
Key initiatives the overall RHTP funding will focus on include:
- Building the rural healthcare workforce: Supporting recruitment, training, and retention strategies to strengthen the pipeline of healthcare professionals serving rural communities.
- Strengthening rural facilities and access: Supporting partnerships, operational improvements, and care-delivery changes that help rural providers maintain essential services and improve access.
- Advancing innovative care and payment models: Supporting new approaches to delivery and financing designed to improve quality, strengthen primary care, and support sustainable rural healthcare.
- Expanding community-based and preventive care: Investing in school-based care, mobile services, and other community strategies that improve prevention, address chronic disease, and expand access to care.
- Modernizing rural healthcare technology: Expanding remote care and data-driven tools to improve coordination and extend healthcare services to rural communities.
The Trump Administration is delivering on its commitment to strengthen rural America by investing in solutions that modernize technology to promote health and well-being for rural communities. Led by CMS, the RHTP is moving beyond the failed one-size-fits-all approach and giving rural communities the tools to build stronger, more innovative, and more sustainable health systems that deliver better care and better outcomes for the Americans they serve.
For more information about the RHTP, visit: https://www.medicaid.gov/resources-for-states/rural-health.

MIAMI – Ygor Fokin Saviolli, 35, a Brazilian national, was sentenced today to 12 years in prison for his role as a manager and supervisor in a money laundering organization that laundered more than $30 million in illicit proceeds, including the proceeds of drug trafficking. On Sept. 24, five co-defendants received sentences ranging from 94 months in prison to 12 months and one day in prison.

Gabriel Cezar Menezes, 29, a Brazilian national, was sentenced to 94 months; Omar Aliperti De Mello Correa, 34, a U.S. citizen, was sentenced to 30 months; Leandro De Avila Goncalves, 43, a Brazilian national, was sentenced to 24 months; and Joao Andrade De Mello, 29, and Tadeu Sebastiane Rabelo Alves Barbosa, 30, both Brazilian nationals, were each sentenced to 12 months and one day. The Brazilian national defendants were illegally residing in the U.S. at the time of their arrests.

“Drug trafficking organizations depend on sophisticated money launderers to turn dirty cash into usable profits,” said U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida. “Ygor Fokin Saviolli helped manage an international operation that moved and concealed more than $30 million in illicit proceeds, including drug money, across the United States and beyond. We will continue targeting not only the traffickers who poison our communities, but also the financial networks that make their criminal enterprises possible. His sentence of 12 years in federal prison is a consequence of helping turn the proceeds of drug trafficking into the lifeblood of international criminal organizations.”

According to court documents, Saviolli, Menezes, Correa, Goncalves, De Mello, and Barbosa were part of a sophisticated money laundering organization that operated across the U.S. and spanned several countries. Members of the conspiracy arranged for U.S.-based couriers to receive bulk cash proceeds from the sale of controlled substances and then to deposit the cash at banks across the country in order to conceal and return those profits to, among others, the sources of drug supply operating outside the U.S. Dozens of pickups across the country were coordinated through WhatsApp message chains that included facilitators and couriers. Saviolli provided upfront funds to facilitate the operations of the money laundering organization and oversaw the receipt and laundering of the bulk cash drug proceeds. Menezes also served as a facilitator, providing direction to and oversight of couriers, and personally picked up bulk cash on multiple occasions. Correa, De Mello, Barbosa, and Goncalves all served as couriers for the money laundering organization, conducting bulk cash pickups in cities including Atlanta, Charlotte, Chicago, Cleveland, Minneapolis, Rochester, and Tampa, among others. Over the course of the conspiracy, the organization concealed more than $30 million in cash.

In June 2026, the defendants’ guilty pleas to conspiracy to commit money laundering were accepted by the district court.

Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division, U.S. Attorney Reding Quiñones, and Special Agent in Charge Brett Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office made the announcement.

The FBI investigated the case, with assistance from the Drug Enforcement Administration’s Rochester Resident Office and Homeland Security Investigations’ Brasilia Attaché Office and Miami Field Office.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Monique Botero for the Southern District of Florida and Trial Attorneys James Hepburn and Jessee Alexander-Hoeppner of the Criminal Division’s Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section (MNF) prosecuted the case.

MNF’s mission is to take the profit out of crime, eliminate drug cartels, and protect the U.S. financial system. MNF pursues criminal prosecutions and criminal and civil asset recovery actions involving: financial facilitators who launder profits for criminals; financial institutions and their officers and employees whose actions threaten the U.S. financial system and financial institutions; international money launderers who support transnational organized crime; and the top command and control of international drug trafficking organizations.

MNF’s International Unit investigates and prosecutes cross-border money laundering schemes involving transnational criminal organizations, cartels, foreign official corruption and related money laundering affecting the U.S. financial system and prosecutes criminal cases and civil forfeiture matters to recover the proceeds of those crimes.

Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Southern District of Florida at www.flsd.uscourts.gov or at http://pacer.flsd.uscourts.gov , under case numbers 25-cr-20545.

SAN DIEGO – Ricky Jesus Rodriguez and his daughter, Jasmine Rodriguez, pleaded guilty in federal court today, admitting they participated in a months-long conspiracy to smuggle banned refrigerants from Mexico into the United States on behalf of American air conditioning companies.

Ricky Rodriguez admitted that he was paid tens of thousands of dollars to coordinate the smuggling of R-22, a hydrochlorofluorocarbon long banned from production and import in the United States. He admitted that he recruited others, including his daughter, to join the smuggling ring, and helped coordinate her role as well.

R-22 is strictly regulated by an international treaty known as the Montreal Protocol that has been ratified by nearly every country. Hydrochlorofluorocarbons like R-22 have an extremely deleterious effect on the ozone layer. Stratospheric ozone forms a protective shield around the earth that absorbs the sun’s harmful ultraviolet radiation that otherwise causes skin cancer, eye damage, and environmental damage. R-22, when released into the atmosphere, destroys ozone, depletes the protective ozone layer, and reduces the atmosphere’s ability to block harmful UV radiation. R-22 had been used as a refrigerant until its use was phased out after these harmful effects were recognized.

Despite the ban, at least two HVAC companies recruited and paid Rodriguez, his daughter and other smugglers to hide tanks of R-22 in their cars and drive them across the border.

Ricky Rodriguez began smuggling R-22 in the summer of 2023. He admitted he smuggled the chemicals dozens of times, bringing five to ten tanks each time, earning thousands of dollars in smuggling fees.

Ricky Rodriguez recruited more smugglers to work for him and the HVAC companies. His daughter was a driver for the HVAC companies, collecting a smuggling fee for each tank of R-22 she brought into the United States from Mexico.

Ricky Rodriguez is scheduled to be sentenced on January 11, 2027, at 10 a.m. before U.S. District Judge Benjamin J. Cheeks. Jasmine Rodriguez entered into a plea agreement that allows her to defer entry of judgment if she meets conditions of release and remains on good behavior for a period of 12 months, after which her case would be dismissed.

The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of California and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency are members of the Department of Justice’s Trade Fraud Task Force, a cross-agency law enforcement effort that also involves the National Fraud Enforcement Division, the Criminal and Civil Divisions, the Energy and Natural Resources Division, the Department of Homeland Security, and U.S. Attorney’s Offices nationwide. The Task Force was created to leverage all of the Department’s tools and authorities to prevent trade fraud that deprives the government of vital revenue, threatens critical domestic industries, undermines consumer confidence, and weakens national security. The Task Force is designed to pursue enforcement actions against parties who seek to evade tariffs and other duties, as well as smugglers who seek to import prohibited goods into the American economy. The Justice Department encourages whistleblowers to alert the government to credible allegations of fraud, including utilizing the qui tam provisions of the False Claims Act or through the Criminal Division’s Corporate Whistleblower Program at CorporateWhistleblower@usdoj.gov using the form available here .

This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Eric Chiang and Emily W. Allen from the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of California.

The Environmental Protection Agency – Criminal Investigations Division is investigating this case with assistance from Homeland Security Investigations.

DEFENDANTS

Ricky Jesus Rodriguez, Case No. 26-cr-4089-BJC Age: 47 San Diego, CA

Jasmine Rodriguez, Case No. 26-cr-4089-BJC Age: 24 San Diego, CA

SUMMARY OF CHARGES

Conspiracy to Violate the Clean Air Act – Title 18, U.S.C., Section 371

Maximum penalty: Five years in prison and $250,000 fine

INVESTIGATING AGENCY

U.S. Environmental Protection Agency

Homeland Security Investigations

NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA – DAVID MOREL (“MOREL”) , age 43, of New Orleans, was sentenced on October 14, 2026, for Possession of Materials Involving the Sexual Exploitation of Minors, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Sections 2252(a)(4)(B) and (a)(2), announced U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle.

According to court documents, beginning at an unknown time, and continuing until October 20, 2025, MOREL was found in possession of images of pre-pubescent child pornography. MOREL’s home was searched by state law enforcement officials and federal agents on October 20, 2025. MOREL was arrested during the execution of the search warrant by Louisiana Bureau of Investigation agents, after they found him in possession of electronic devices containing media depicting the sexual abuse of prepubescent children. Through a partnership between state and federal authorities, the U.S. Attorney’s Office adopted the state charges. MOREL was previously convicted in federal court by the U.S. Attorney’s Office in 2016 for Possessing Materials Involving the Sexual Exploitation of Minors and was sentenced to one-hundred twenty (120) months in prison.

MOREL was sentenced by United States District Judge Jay C. Zainey to ten (10) years imprisonment followed by a life term of supervised release.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by United States Attorney’s Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. U.S. Attorney Courcelle praised the work of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Homeland Security Investigations, and the Louisiana Bureau of Investigation. text:
AUSTIN, TEXAS – On Thursday, October 15th, Congressman Greg Casar (D-Texas), alongside Representatives Bennie G. Thompson (D-Miss.), Ranking Member of the House Committee on Homeland Security, and Pramila Jayapal (D-Wash.), Ranking Member of the Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement, and five other members of Congress held a field hearing to investigate the numerous ICE shootings across Texas, including the recent shooting of Wilber Garcés-Pérez.
Representatives Greg Casar, Bennie G. Thompson, and Pramila Jayapal were joined by Representatives Troy A. Carter, Sr. (LA-02), Lou Correa (CA-46), Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), and Al Green (TX-09).
The Members of Congress were joined by witnesses Ms. Rachel Reyes, mother of Ruben Ray Martinez, Kristin Etter, Director of Policy & Legal Services at the Texas Immigration Law Council, Carolina Rivera Nelson, Attorney at the ACLU of Texas, and Danny Woodward, Policy Attorney with Texas Civil Rights Project.
“Texas has become the epicenter of Trump’s deadly deportation machine, so we brought Members of Congress from across the country to Austin to see it firsthand,” said Congressman Greg Casar (D-Texas). “ICE shot Wilber Garcés-Pérez, a DoorDash driver and a father, in the back then denied him medical care. They even tried to deport him so he could never speak the truth. Donald Trump’s ICE isn’t going after the worst of the worst — it’s gone after people like Wilber, who have no criminal record. We will fight to hold the perpetrators in this administration accountable, and not provide another dime in funding to this rogue agency.”
“Democrats came to Austin today to demand justice and accountability for Wilber Garcés-Pérez and the others that have been shot by immigration agents in Texas. If Republicans refuse to conduct any oversight of the Trump administration, we must do so in their place,” added Congressman Bennie G. Thompson. “What we heard today was powerful and informative. Make no mistake: we will do everything possible to hold this administration accountable for what it is doing. This violence, lawlessness, and chaos in our communities must end.”
“Twenty-five days ago, ICE agents in Austin, Texas shot Wilber Garcés-Pérez in the back. Instead of taking him to the hospital, they locked him up in a detention center and did not allow him to have surgery for 11 days. This is not the most recent shooting by ICE, and is one of nearly a dozen that we know of since Trump returned to office,” said Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal. “ICE is a lawless, rogue agency that is causing generational trauma in communities across the country. House Democrats today are doing the oversight work that Republicans refuse to do — and we will continue to do everything possible to protect our communities from Trump’s mass deportation agenda.”
“The shooting and medical neglect of Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez follows the many other cases that have become synonymous with cities being swarmed with masked, armed federal agents and the nation’s dangerous descent into tyranny: Renée Nicole Good, Alex Pretti, Johan Sebastian Guerrero, and too many others. No life is meaningless, and each individual assaulted or killed by our immigration system is someone’s child, someone’s sibling, someone’s parent, and they all still belong here with us,” said Congressman Troy A. Carter, Sr. “Unless you’re Native American, we all come from somewhere else. The Trump immigration system is structured and staffed as a deportation machine that violates individuals’ constitutional rights. Democrats will fight for an immigration system that honors our history and sets forth a reasonable, compassionate path to citizenship.” 
“President Trump got elected on the promise to go after the “worst of the worst.” Instead, since January, federal immigration agents have detained over 500 U.S. citizens and killed at least three. ICE is arresting people with no criminal record to hit political quotas while cutting training and lowering hiring standards,” said Congressman Lou Correa. “There is an urgent need for major reforms to keep our communities safe from violence. DHS was created to defend Americans against foreign terrorists. Instead, we have permanent residents and American citizens being shot by ICE agents in our streets.”
“In Texas, we have witnessed at least three ICE shootings since this administration began its aggressive, unprecedented enforcement actions,” said Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher. “People across our community in Houston are still reeling from the shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo. Just last weekend, ICE agents ran over and gravely injured Miguel Parra Hernandez while pursuing someone else. ICE’s reckless and brutal actions are not only unprecedented, they’re unconstitutional. They are making us less safe, creating fear and danger for immigrants and citizens alike. This Republican-led Congress that has enabled this lawlessness has utterly failed Wilber Garcés-Pérez, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, Ruben Ray Martinez, and so many others. All Americans deserve better from our government, and that is why I joined Congressman Casar, Ranking Member Thompson, Congresswoman Jayapal, and my Democratic colleagues in Austin today to hear from some of the many people impacted, learn more, and demonstrate our commitment to bringing justice, accountability, and change.”
“Trump promised to go after the worst of the worst. But judging by what we’re seeing across Texas and the country, that sounds more like ICE’s recruitment strategy. People are being shot, injured, and killed by federal agents operating without basic law enforcement standards or accountability,” said Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia. “In Houston, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was killed on his way to work. One hundred days later, his family still has no answers. Instead they’ve been met with stonewalling and excuses. These families deserve the truth and justice, and we will not stop fighting until they get both. 
“No President is above the law, and no federal agency should be allowed to serve as judge, jury, prosecutor, and executioner while operating with impunity,” said Congressman Al Green. “Under President Trump, ICE has been emboldened to use deadly force against people in our communities while the administration evades transparency and accountability, engaging in a cover-up. These shootings are not isolated incidents. They are part of a deeply troubling pattern of conduct that threatens the constitutional rights and lives of people in this country.”
The Members of Congress’ full remarks can be found here.

SACRAMENTO, Calif. — A federal grand jury returned a single-count indictment Thursday against Stefan Schiopu, 27, of Cool, charging him with one count of sexual exploitation of a child, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced.

According to court documents, on Feb. 22, 2026, Schiopu sexually exploited a minor and created at least one video of that sexual conduct.

The Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force, the El Dorado County Sheriff’s Office, the El Dorado County District Attorney’s Office, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Douglas Harman is prosecuting the case.

Any sentence, however, would be determined at the discretion of the court after consideration of any applicable statutory factors and the Federal Sentencing Guidelines, which take into account a number of variables. The charges are only allegations; the defendant is presumed innocent until and unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.

New Orleans – Today, U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle, along with the federal, state and local participating agencies comprising the Homeland Security Task Force – Region 15 CORE – New Orleans (“HSTF”), announced the successful conclusion of a nearly four-year, extensive multi-agency narcotics investigation that dismantled multiple drug trafficking organizations operating throughout the Bayou Region. This investigation led to numerous federal indictments, state arrests, substantial prison sentences, as well as the seizure of significant quantities of illegal narcotics, firearms, and criminal assets.

The investigation was led by the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and supported by several federal, state, and local law enforcement partners. A Thibodaux Police Department Narcotics Agent, assigned to the DEA Task Force as a Task Force Officer within the Eastern District of Louisiana Financial Investigations Unit, led the investigation.

As a result of the exhaustive investigative work, intelligence gathering, surveillance operations, financial investigations, and inter-agency coordination, investigators identified and targeted individuals who were distributing dangerous narcotics throughout Thibodaux, Louisiana, Lafourche Parish, and the surrounding communities.

“Today’s Homeland Security Task Force operation announcements are, at their core, about one thing …protecting our communities from the very real threat of violence posed by drug trafficking organizations,” said U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle. “Our shared mission today has remained constant; to enforce the laws of the land and to protect the public that we are proud to serve.”

As a result of this investigation, 20 individuals were federally indicted for narcotics, firearms, conspiracy, and related offenses. Additionally, 18 other individuals were arrested and prosecuted through state court proceedings.

Collectively, the defendants prosecuted, both federally and by the state, have received sentences totaling more than 300 years of imprisonment. And, several defendants are still awaiting final sentencing or adjudication. Additional prison terms may be imposed as the remaining cases proceed through the judicial process.

Specifically, this investigation resulted in the seizure of approximately:

• 46,909.33 grams of crystal methamphetamine (more than 100 pounds)

• 178.6 grams of heroin/fentanyl

• 1,414.1 grams of cocaine (more than 3 pounds)

• 3,044.1 grams of marijuana (more than 6.5 pounds)

• More than $190,000 in seized assets

• Eleven firearms, including eight pistols and three rifles

“This investigation began on the ground with our local police officers and deputies, and as the network unraveled, we expanded it into a full Homeland Security Task Force operation,” said Special Agent in Charge John P. Scott of the Drug Enforcement Administration’s New Orleans Field Division. “There is often a misconception that federal resources are reserved only for major metropolitan areas. This case proves otherwise. The full weight and reach of the federal government extends directly into our rural communities and parish neighborhoods. Through the HSTF, we brought every federal, state, and local tool to bear – not just to make arrests, but to build rock-solid cases that resulted in real, long-term prosecutions.”

“This investigation was not simply about removing drugs from our streets,” said Chief Zeringue. “It was about identifying and dismantling the individuals and organizations responsible for supplying and distributing these dangerous narcotics throughout our region. Every arrest made, every firearm seized, every dollar taken away from illegal drug trafficking, and every major distributor removed from operation, represents a safer community for the citizens of Thibodaux and the Bayou Region. The success of this investigation is a direct reflection of the cooperation, professionalism, and commitment shared by our federal, state, and local law enforcement partners. No single agency can effectively combat large-scale narcotics trafficking alone. These cases require teamwork, shared intelligence, persistence, and the ability to work together toward one common goal: making our communities safer.”

“This investigation demonstrates what can be accomplished when law enforcement agencies at every level unite to achieve a goal,” said Lafourche Parish Sheriff Craig Webre. “By working together, we have not only removed dangerous drugs and firearms from our streets but also disrupted criminal organizations that threaten the safety and well-being of our communities. I commend the dedication and perseverance of every agency involved, and I want the people of Lafourche Parish to know that we will remain relentless in our efforts to combat drug trafficking and keep our communities safe.”

“Dangerous drugs destroy lives, tear families apart, and threaten the safety of our communities,” said Colonel Frank Besson, Louisiana State Police Superintendent. “Through strong law enforcement partnerships, Louisiana State Police remains committed to dismantling organized criminal networks across Louisiana, from our largest cities to our smallest towns. Those who profit from trafficking dangerous drugs should understand that no matter where they operate, we will continue working alongside our partners to bring them to justice.”

“I would like to thank all of our federal, state and local law enforcement partners,” said Terrebonne Parish Sheriff Timothy Soignet. “It genuinely takes a team of professionals to achieve public safety for all citizens.”

These cases were brought pursuant to the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF New Orleans comprises agents and officers from the Department of Homeland Security, Federal Bureau of Investigations, Drug Enforcement Administration and Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, Enforcement and Removal Operations, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Office of Field Operations, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, U.S. Border Patrol, U.S. Coast Guard, Coast Guard Investigative Service. State and local agencies include the Louisiana State Police, Thibodaux Police Department, Lafourche Parish Sheriff's Office, Terrebonne Parish Sheriff's Office, St. Charles Parish Sheriff's Office, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Louisiana.

An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

WASHINGTON – Omar James, 22, of Washington, D.C., was sentenced today to 30 months in prison for the shooting of a victim in a community market, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

James pleaded guilty to one count each of aggravated assault and possession of a firearm (prior conviction) on June 17, 2026, in the Superior Court of the District of Columbia. On the charge of aggravated assault, Judge Robert Salerno sentenced defendant James to 60 months of incarceration, execution of sentence suspended as to all but 30 months of incarceration. For the possession of a firearm (prior conviction) charge, Judge Salerno sentenced James to 28 months of incarceration. In addition to the 30-month prison term, Judge Robert Salerno ordered James to serve three years of supervised probation. Judge Salerno additionally denied the defense’s request for the sentence to be imposed under the Youth Rehabilitation Act.

According to the government’s evidence, on March 12, 2026, MPD officers responded to 1918 Benning Road Northeast, to reports of a shooting. When they arrived, they found one individual lying on the sidewalk across from 704 19th Street Northeast, suffering a single gunshot wound to his groin. He was accompanied by defendant James, who suffered a gunshot wound to his right elbow and a disfigurement to his index finger.

According to the government’s evidence, on March 14, 2026, James returned to Benning Market and got into an argument with the victim, one of the bystanders from the prior incident, located at 2001 Benning Road, Northeast. The victim, who was standing outside of the store, followed James into the market and repeatedly told James that he had nothing to do with the shooting that had occurred days before in the Benning Road area. Surveillance video captured the men entering the store. An unidentified suspect was then seen handing James a handgun and shortly after James shot the victim in the right foot without provocation from the victim. The suspect and defendant James fled from the scene. The victim was taken to the hospital and treated for non-life-threatening injuries.

James was arrested on March 25, 2026, and has been in custody since that date.

Joining the announcement was Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll of the Metropolitan Police Department.

This matter was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Lindsey Heimburger.

EPA Announces $109 Million WIFIA Loan to Increase Water Supply Reliability in Honolulu, Hawaii
Contact Information
EPA Press Office (press@epa.gov)
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) announced a $109 million Water Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act (WIFIA) loan to the Honolulu Board of Water Supply, which serves parts of Oahu, Hawaii. This loan will help the Board design and build a large-scale reverse osmosis seawater desalination plant that will provide 1.7 million gallons of water each day to island residents while decreasing pressure on groundwater aquifers. EPA’s WIFIA loans enable communities to make critical investments in clean, safe, and reliable water to help advance EPA’s “Powering the Great American Comeback” initiative.
“Communities across the country are facing challenges with water infrastructure—from replacing old pipes and pumps, to upgrading service to support growth, to bringing new sources of water online. EPA’s WIFIA program is a lending tool that can help communities make investments in water infrastructure that meets local needs and protects public health,” said EPA Assistant Administrator for Water Jess Kramer. “We are thrilled that Honolulu is using this $109 million WIFIA loan to create a reliable and renewable source of drinking water to benefit the community.”
The Honolulu Board of Water Supply will use WIFIA financing for its Kalaeloa Seawater Desalination Facility Project, which will help convert abundant saltwater into clean and safe drinking water, establishing an alternative drinking water source for the island. This project includes the building of byproduct disposal facilities, a recycled water pipeline, and transmission lines. These new developments will increase supply reliability and reduce reliance on groundwater aquifers. This project will strengthen water resources in central Oahu for the more arid district that the Board serves, west of Honolulu and Pearl Harbor.
“We are pleased to have partnered with the EPA on this WIFIA loan and appreciate their support,” said Ernest Lau, Manager and Chief Engineer of the Honolulu Board of Water Supply. “This financing will assist in constructing the first seawater desalination facility for our island community.”
EPA’s WIFIA program provides a powerful financial tool that can significantly accelerate investments in water infrastructure to protect human health and the environment while saving communities millions of dollars. The Honolulu Board of Water Supply is opting to make the WIFIA loan a subordinate lien, which means the loan will be second to that of the borrower’s senior lien bonds, providing more repayment flexibility. Additionally, the Honolulu Board of Water Supply will utilize the ability to defer principal payments during construction to reduce impact on ratepayers.
WIFIA funding is available to support additional water infrastructure projects: up to $11 billion is available to water systems and another $3 billion is available to State infrastructure financing authorities. EPA is currently accepting letters of interest.
Learn more about EPA’s WIFIA Program and water infrastructure investments, including how to submit a letter of interest.
Background
Established by the Water Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act of 2014, the WIFIA program is a federal loan program administered by EPA. The WIFIA program aims to accelerate investment in the nation’s water infrastructure by providing long-term, low-cost supplemental credit assistance for regionally and nationally significant projects. The WIFIA program has an active pipeline of pending applications for projects that will result in billions of dollars in water infrastructure investment and thousands of jobs.
title: EPA Announces $109 Million WIFIA Loan to Increase Water Supply Reliability in Honolulu, Hawaii
