ALBANY, Ga. – Two Georgia inmates who orchestrated a phone scheme from behind bars, extorting at least 119 citizens by demanding payment for supposed missed jury‑duty fines, have been sentenced to federal prison following an investigation conducted by the FBI.

Lance Riddle, aka “C-Port,” was sentenced to serve a total of 200 months in prison, followed by three years of supervised release, to run consecutively to any state sentence. Co-defendant Joey Amour Jackson, aka “Apes---,” was sentenced to serve a total of 120 months in prison, followed by three years of supervised release, to run consecutively to any state sentence. The Court will determine restitution for both defendants in 90 days. Senior U.S. District Judge W. Louis Sands presided over the sentencing hearings on October 14. Jackson and Riddle were found guilty of one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering on January 9, after a five-day trial that began on January 5. There is no parole in the federal system.

“Even from prison, the defendants preyed on citizens through threats and deceit, scams that too many Americans are confronted with today,” said U.S. Attorney William R. ‘Will’ Keyes. “Our office and our law enforcement partners remain firmly committed to protecting the public and ensuring that those who commit fraud face full accountability.”

“Not even prison cells prevented these criminals from harming dozens of innocent people. Hopefully, this sentence will bring some level of comfort to the victims and prevent others from falling for similar scams,” said Marlo Graham, Special Agent in Charge of FBI Atlanta. “The FBI will continue to work with our law enforcement partners in not only addressing these types of inmate-based crimes but also in preventing inmates’ access to contraband cell phones that provide the means to do so much harm to the unsuspecting public.”

According to court documents and statements referenced at trial, FBI agents in Columbus, Georgia, received information from law enforcement agencies across the U.S. about wire fraud by Georgia inmates, including local law enforcement in Colorado, Florida, Virginia, Nevada, California, and Ohio. Agents discovered that inmates at Calhoun State Prison, including Jackson and Riddle, were using contraband cellular telephones and advanced electronic techniques such as Voice Over Internet Protocol (VOIP) to contact victims from a number that mirrored the numbers of their local police departments.

The victims were told they had one or more warrants for their arrest due to missing jury duty. The defendants, posing as police officers, informed the victims that the warrants would be cleared through payment of a bond over the phone and, if not paid, the victims would immediately be arrested. The victims were also informed they were under a “gag” order and couldn’t speak about their warrants until the bond was paid, or they would be immediately arrested. The victims were almost always instructed to buy gift cards and read the numbers off the back of the cards to the defendants, although they sometimes made wire transfers. After paying the bond, victims were instructed to drive to their local police department to verify their signature on the bond.

Some victims were told that, because of supposed heightened courthouse security, they needed to go to a local Target store, enter a restroom, undress, and record themselves performing a self-conducted cavity search before verifying their signature. Some victims subsequently received lewd and sexually explicit messages, including violent threats. The scheme primarily targeted female professionals with prominent online profiles, though a small number of male victims were also identified.

The inmates impersonated both fictitious individuals and real law enforcement officers from the victims’ local jurisdictions. They worked with co-conspirators outside prison who managed the group’s financial accounts. The stolen proceeds were used to pay off personal debts such as house and vehicle loans, as well as to purchase drugs. The scheme resulted in more than $464,920 in documented losses from 119 victims nationwide, though the true number of victims is likely much higher as many cases go unreported, are not fully investigated, or are concealed by victims who are too embarrassed to come forward.

The case was investigated by the FBI Atlanta’s Columbus Resident Agency and prosecuted by Criminal Chief Leah McEwen.
title: Georgia Inmates Sentenced in Police‑Impersonation Jury‑Duty Call Scheme

LAS VEGAS – The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Nevada , in coordination with the Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division , announced its comprehensive strategy today to oversee federal voting protections and investigate potential election fraud as early voting begins in Nevada for the 2026 midterm elections .

The initiative is part of a nationwide effort to ensure a secure, transparent, and accessible voting process. The U.S. Attorney’s Office, alongside federal law enforcement partners, is prepared to enforce federal election laws vigorously while protecting the right of every legal voter to cast their ballot without intimidation or interference. Voters can consult official Department of Justice and state portals to review federal election laws and eligibility requirements.

“Maintaining public confidence in our democratic institutions is a top priority. As Nevadans head to the polls for early voting and utilize the state's mail-in ballot options, our office will work hand-in-hand with federal, state, and local partners to safeguard the integrity of the vote. We are committed to a fair election process where every legal ballot is counted accurately. Every single fraudulent, duplicate, or unlawful ballot cast completely cancels out the vote of an honest citizen. Protecting election integrity isn't about keeping people out; it’s about making sure every legal vote counts,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada.

Key Enforcement Priorities for the 2026 Election:

Protecting Voter Rights: Ensuring that all eligible voters can participate in early voting, mail-in voting, and Election Day voting free from discrimination, harassment, or unlawful coercion.

Voter Eligibility and Enforcement: Monitoring compliance with federal laws regarding voter registration and eligibility. For detailed information on ongoing reviews, eligibility laws, or federal penalties, please consult official Department of Justice guidelines and state election authority resources.

Combating Election Fraud: Investigating actionable allegations of ballot harvesting, voter impersonation, or intentional disruption of polling places and mail-in ballot processing.

Mail-In and Early Voting in Nevada

Nevada state election officials have confirmed that early in-person voting and mail-in voting will proceed as scheduled under standard state protocols. Federal oversight will remain active throughout the early voting period to monitor for compliance with the Voting Rights Act and ensure that secure ballot drop boxes and polling locations are unhindered.

Reporting Election Irregularities

The public plays a critical role in maintaining election security. Anyone who witnesses or has direct knowledge of potential election fraud, voter intimidation, or unlawful voting activity is strongly encouraged to report it immediately.

Please visit the official FBI Tips Portal or contact local law enforcement to report potential election fraud or voting irregularities. Complaints regarding voter discrimination or civil rights violations can also be directed to the Civil Rights Division via the Department of Justice Civil Rights Reporting Portal .

title: U.S. Attorney’s Office Announces Election Integrity Plan for 2026 General Election and Early Voting in Nevada

WASHINGTON – Monet Jones, 28, of Washington, D.C., pleaded guilty today for lying to the grand jury about the beating death of her 2-year-old child, Mars Jones, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

“Two-year-old Mars deserved a mother who would fight for justice, not protect the man who beat her child to death,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “Instead, she misled investigators and deleted evidence to shield him from accountability. If you obstruct justice to protect someone who kills a child, you will answer for it. No exceptions.”

“Two-year-old Mars deserved a mother who would fight for justice, not protect the man who beat her child to death,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “Instead, she misled investigators and deleted evidence to shield him from accountability. If you obstruct justice to protect someone who kills a child, you will answer for it. No exceptions.”

Jones pleaded guilty before D.C. Superior Court Judge Rainey Brandt to one count of perjury and one count of tampering with evidence. Judge Park scheduled sentencing for February 1, 2027, with her co-defendant, Dasean Matthews.

According to the government’s evidence, on October 13, 2022, 2-year-old Mars, Jones, and Matthews, (co-defendant Jones’s romantic partner) drove to a Dunkin Donuts just before noon. While in the Dunkin Donuts, video evidence shows Matthews striking the young child with a closed fist in the upper body causing Mars to fall and slam against a metal railing. Later that day, while in a parking garage, video evidence shows Matthews grabbing Mars by the neck of his clothing, swing him by the clothing, and minutes later, strike Mars in the upper body or face, causing the young child to again fall to the floor. Later the same day, while alone in a vehicle with Mars, video evidence shows defendant Matthews repeatedly strike the young child so forcefully that the vehicle shakes from the impact of the blows. Immediately thereafter, Matthews delivers an unconscious and bloody baby Mars to Jones and then flees the scene. An autopsy determined that Mars died from complications of inflicted head trauma.

Throughout the pendency of the case, Jones repeatedly lied to law enforcement and the grand jury about witnessing defendant Matthews’ assaulting her child or being in the Dunkin Donuts on October 13, 2022, in an attempt to hinder the investigation. Jones also deleted messages between her and Matthews from her phone in an attempt to protect Matthews.

Joining the announcement was Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll of the Metropolitan Police Department.

This case was investigated by the Special Victims Unit of the Homicide Section at the Metropolitan Police Department and was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Emma McArthur and Shauna Payyappilly.

Today, FEMA and its partners released a new study that provides key insights into challenges faced by emergency managers across the nation. The Emergency Management Organizational Structures, Staffing, and Capacity Study confirms that America’s emergency management system is strongest when it is locally led, state managed and federally supported. The study surveyed over 1,700 emergency management officials nationwide and found that local and state agencies are best positioned to understand and address the unique needs of their communities.
“Under the leadership of President Trump and Secretary Mullin, FEMA is focused on empowering state, local, tribal and territorial governments to lead through all phases of emergency management,” said FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton. “This study makes clear that a one-size-fits-all, federally driven approach will never be as effective as community-led efforts. FEMA will continue to partner with officials at every level of government, empowering them to build local capabilities and invest in resilience efforts.”
FEMA sponsored the study to better understand the emergency management landscape across the nation, including in cities, suburbs, rural areas and within tribal nations. The report summarizes quantitative and qualitative data from survey responses and interviews across 1,689 local jurisdictions, 37 states, 59 tribal nations and four territories.
The report finds that local emergency management agencies are critical to our nation’s resilience, but it also finds that those organizations are typically understaffed and underfunded. This finding reinforces the vision outlined in President Trump’s America First Resilience Strategy, which calls for state and local governments to develop and maintain capacity to effectively manage incidents affecting their communities.
For decades, many states have relied excessively on federal grants to maintain emergency response capabilities—to their own detriment. To strengthen their resilience against disasters and emergencies, states, tribal nations, territories and local jurisdictions should consistently invest in their own emergency management capabilities.
This study was funded by FEMA and conducted by Argonne National Laboratory. Big City Emergency Managers (BCEM), the International Association of Emergency Managers (IAEM-USA) and the National Emergency Management Association (NEMA) also collaborated on the study.
In addition to publishing the study’s findings as a report, FEMA worked with the Argonne National Laboratory to launch the National Emergency Management Data Explorer (NEMDEX) tool. This tool is available to help review and analyze the summary information gathered from the local survey component of the study. Community leaders can review the findings to make informed, strategic decisions on investment and capacity building efforts.
To view the report and access the NEMDEX tool, please visit the Argonne National Laboratory website.
title: First-of-its-Kind Study Provides Insights into Challenges Facing Emergency Management Agencies Across the Nation

DeLauro Statement on Reports of Trump Administration Weakening Ukraine’s Defenses as Russian Attacks Intensify
WASHINGTON – According to a new report, the White House issued the order to restrict Starlink service over Ukraine, interrupting missile-defense systems that protect civilians from Russian attacks. Starshield—the version of Starlink used by the military—is provided by SpaceX, a company owned by Trump ally and Republican mega-donor Elon Musk. The interruption comes as Russia increases their attacks on civilian targets. Civilian casualties in Ukraine were 85 percent higher this September compared to last, and more than 2,500 civilians have been killed in Ukraine since January, according to the United Nations.
House Appropriations Committee Ranking Member Rosa DeLauro (D-CT-03) issued the following statement:
“The White House directive to choke off a crucial component of Ukrainian missile defenses is appalling. The Trump administration is holding Ukraine’s hands behind its back even as Russian attacks intensify. Doing nothing was bad enough. Now the Trump administration is actually helping Russia in their senseless war of aggression, putting countless innocent civilians in even greater danger. America’s position on the world stage has become unrecognizable under this administration. President Trump is aiding our adversaries, abandoning our allies, and enriching himself, while American families pay higher prices for everything from healthcare and housing to gas and groceries.
“This summer, I visited Ukraine along with several other members of Congress. Everywhere we went, the need for American leadership in support of our Ukrainian allies was clear. When Democrats retake control of the House in January, we will fight to provide this support and stand up to dictators like Vladimir Putin.”
Ranking Member DeLauro’s statement on her trip to Ukraine can be found here. An op-ed she wrote on her trip and the need for continued support for Ukraine can be found here.

NEWARK, N.J. – A foreign national and convicted felon pleaded guilty to unlawful procurement of naturalization and passport fraud, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced.

Miguel Dario Bautista Jimenez, a/k/a “Carlos Chapman Hernandez,” a/k/a “Carlos Hernandez,” 42, of Hoboken, New Jersey pleaded guilty to a two-count Indictment charging him with unlawful procurement of naturalization, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Sections 1425(b) and 2, and passport fraud, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Sections 1542 and 2, on October 14, 2026 before U.S. District Judge Stanley R. Chesler in Newark federal court.

According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court:

Miguel Dario Bautista Jimenez, a citizen of the Dominican Republic, was removed from the United States in or around 2013, following a criminal conviction in New York for an aggravated felony. In or around June 2014, Bautista re-entered the United States using a false identity. Bautista applied for legal permanent residence and naturalization falsely stating that his name was “Carlos Chapman Hernandez,” a person born in Cuba, and falsely stating that he had never been convicted of a crime, had never been removed from the United States, and had never been to prison. Bautista used the false identity to fraudulently obtain U.S. citizenship documents through naturalization, including a U.S. passport.

The charges of unlawful procurement of naturalization and passport fraud each carry a maximum penalty of ten years’ imprisonment. Each offense carries a maximum fine of $250,000, or twice the gross loss or gain from the offense, whichever is greatest.

U.S. Attorney Frazer credited special agents of Homeland Security Investigations in Newark, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Michael S. McCarthy, the Social Security Administration, Office of the Inspector General, New York Field Division, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Amy Connelly, the U.S. Department of State’s Diplomatic Security Service, New York Field Office, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Nicholas Fanelli, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy in Newark, with the investigation leading to the guilty plea.

The government is represented by Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Priscilla Gabela and Assistant U.S. Attorney Katherine M. Romano of the Criminal Division in Newark.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division). The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

###

ST. LOUIS – A man on Thursday admitted conspiring to steal at least 14 properties in St. Louis and St. Louis County by filing fraudulent deeds.

James L. Townes Jr., 51, of Berkeley, pleaded guilty in U.S. District Court in St. Louis to a conspiracy charge. Townes admitted that beginning as early as Sept. 25, 2018, he began filing fraudulent deeds in St. Louis and St. Louis County on properties that belonged to others. The filings falsely claimed that Townes or his relatives had purchased the properties. Townes and his co-defendant, Charnay Bartlett, used fraudulently obtained notary seals to “authenticate” the forged signatures of the true owners of the properties.

Townes and Bartlett transferred at least 14 properties to Townes, his companies or his friends and family, his plea agreement says. Townes admitted that his scheme involved the use of the names of 10 or more individuals and that the intended losses associated with his actions exceeded $1,500,000. The real owners had to expend considerable resources to regain the titles to their properties. Others abandoned their properties because they lacked the financial resources to initiate legal action. At least three of the property owners were deceased at the time when their purported signatures were authenticated by Townes and Bartlett. In some cases, Townes gained access to the properties by forcing entry through locked doors and squatting there.

Bartlett, 30, pleaded guilty in April to the same conspiracy charge and is scheduled to be sentenced on December 2. Townes is set to be sentenced on January 21. The charge carries a penalty of up to five years in prison, a fine of up to $250,000 or both prison and a fine.

The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development Office of Inspector General, the Social Security Administration Office of Inspector General, the St. Louis County Police Department and the Hazelwood Police Department investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Gwen Carroll is prosecuting the case.
title: St. Louis County Man Admits Using Fraudulent Deed Filings to Steal At Least 14 Properties

MOBILE, AL – A New York man was sentenced to 60 months in prison for participating in a nationwide bank fraud conspiracy involving stolen and counterfeited financial instruments.

According to court documents, Curtis Jackson, 31, of Staten Island, New York, admitted that, between February 2023 and June 2024, he conspired with LaEric Marques Williams-Beverly and other conspirators based in Mobile, Alabama, to commit mail theft and bank fraud involving stolen and counterfeited checks. The checks bore the personal identifying information of numerous identity theft victims. Jackson and Williams-Beverly administered an illicit Telegram channel called “House of Pain & Drank,” where millions of dollars’ worth of stolen financial instruments were posted for sale to other fraudsters.

In January 2024, agents obtained video footage from a Mobile business (“Business-1”) showing Williams-Beverly stealing checks from the business’s mailbox. Williams-Beverly then coordinated with other coconspirators to counterfeit the checks and fraudulently deposit them into a bank account. ATM surveillance footage captured Williams-Beverly making the fraudulent deposits. Later that month, police in New York City arrested Jackson in possession of a counterfeited check for $43,686.45, drawn on Business-1’s bank account. Jackson had received the check from Williams-Beverly. Jackson’s iCloud account also contained images of stolen and counterfeited checks, including a Citibank deposit slip for a $62,673.46 check drawn on Business-1’s bank account.

In June 2024, federal agents executed a search warrant at Williams-Beverly’s home in Mobile. Agents seized numerous pieces of stolen mail, counterfeited checks, debit and credit cards belonging to other individuals, counterfeiting tools, two pistols, and Williams-Beverly’s cell phone. Williams-Beverly admitted to agents that he produced counterfeited checks and coordinated the purchase and sale of stolen checks through the fraudulent Telegram channel he operated with Jackson. Electronic evidence recovered from the conspirators’ cell phones, iCloud accounts, and social media accounts demonstrated the extensive scope of the conspiracy.

U.S. District Judge Kristi K. DuBose sentenced Jackson to serve 60 months in federal prison, emphasizing that he was a recidivist with several prior state arrests and convictions for theft, larceny, possession of forged instruments, possession of drugs, and bail jumping. In addition to the five-year prison term, Judge DuBose ordered Jackson to serve a five-year term of supervised release upon his release from prison, during which time he will be subject to drug testing and credit restrictions. The court did not impose a fine, but Judge DuBose ordered Jackson to pay $13,041.52 in victim restitution jointly and severally with Williams-Beverly and other coconspirators, and $100 in special assessments.

Williams-Beverly was previously sentenced to 120 months in federal prison for his role in the scheme.

U.S. Attorney Sean P. Costello of the Southern District of Alabama made the announcement.

The United States Postal Inspection Service, the United States Secret Service, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, the Mobile Police Department, the Jackson Police Department, and the Clarke County Sheriff’s Office investigated the case. The New York City Police Department substantially assisted the investigation.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Justin Roller prosecuted the case on behalf of the United States.
title: New York Man Sentenced to Five Years in Prison for Participating in a Nationwide Bank Fraud Conspiracy

(Washington, DC) – U.S. Representative Ed Case (Hawai‘i – District 1) was among several members of Congress recently honored as “Franchise Champions” by the International Franchise Association (IFA). 
According to the IFA, there are more than 2,800 franchise locations in Hawai‘i, with close to 30,000 employees. These largely local small businesses franchise under well-known brands like L&L Drive-Inn, McDonald’s, Subway, 7-Eleven, Ace Hardware and SERVPRO, and now generate more than $3 billion in annual revenues.
"These lawmakers have shown they will stand up for Main Street, and we are proud to honor them with the Franchise Champion Award," said Michael Layman, IFA chief advocacy officer.
"Franchise small businesses across America power jobs and serve their communities, and they depend on lawmakers for a regulatory climate that will allow the franchise business model to grow now and into the future."
Case said: “As someone who worked over three decades in Hawai‘i businesses, I fully understand what it takes to create, own, grow and work in a business, especially small businesses which are the backbone of our local economy. Extra effort and different business models are required to address various challenges including taxes, regulations and high costs. Franchising offers a great and proven model avenue for many of our own to succeed in business, generating local jobs and contributing to our economy.”
The IFA is the world’s oldest and largest organization representing franchising worldwide. IFA works through its government relations and public policy, media relations, and educational programs to protect, enhance and promote franchising and the more than 832,000 franchise establishments that support nearly 8.8 million direct jobs, $907.3 billion of economic output for the U.S. economy, and almost 3 percent of the Gross Domestic Product.
Case has also championed the broader interests of our country’s small businesses throughout his almost-twelve years in Congress. In 2023 he was honored with a Special Congressional Award by the Small Business Council of America (SBCA), a national, non-profit organization representing some 100,000 privately held and family-owned small businesses. 
The SBCA award recognized Case’s support of the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA), of funding for services managed by the SBA, and of various federal loan programs to help small businesses. The SBCA had previously given him the same award in 2006 during his earlier Congressional service when he served on the House Committee on Small Business.
 Case has also worked to advance national and Hawai‘i small businesses through his House Appropriations Committee, on which he is now serving his eighth year.
As a current example, for current Fiscal Year 2027 his Committee included his requests for key programs that directly benefit Hawaii’s small businesses including:
·         $828 million for the SBA;
·         $140 million for Small Business Development Centers (SBDCs) which supports six SBDCs in Hawai‘i;
·         $32 million for the Microloan Technical Assistance Program; and
·         $27 million for the Women’s Business Centers Program, which supports the Patsy T. Mink Center for Business and Leadership.

Real Food for Real Heroes: Secretary Kennedy Welcomes Lou Ferrigno, Dean Cain, and Kyle Reyes to The Real Food Show
WASHINGTON, D.C.—October 16, 2026—U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. today released a new episode of The Real Food Show featuring bodybuilding legend Lou Ferrigno (The Incredible Hulk), actor Dean Cain (Superman), and law enforcement advocate Kyle Reyes. Together, they highlight the importance of proper nutrition and physical fitness for America’s real superheroes: the law enforcement officers and first responders who serve and protect our communities every day.
In the episode, Secretary Kennedy and his guests prepare affordable, protein-packed steak dishes using budget-friendly cuts of beef. Using simple ingredients and practical cooking techniques, they demonstrate how families and first responders can prepare nutritious, high-quality meals at home without breaking the bank.
“Our law enforcement officers and first responders protect us every day, and we need to help them protect their own health,” said Secretary Kennedy. “President Trump and I are putting real food and physical fitness back at the center of American health. This episode gives our first responders practical ways to eat well, build strength, and stay ready for the demanding work they do every day.”
Drawing on their personal experiences with law enforcement, fitness, and nutrition, the guests share practical strategies for meal preparation, building healthy routines, and making better food choices on the job.
Ferrigno, a legendary bodybuilder and former reserve deputy sheriff, discusses how decades of bodybuilding taught him the importance of proper nutrition and planning meals ahead of time. Cain, who has also served in law enforcement, shares his appreciation for the men and women who protect their communities and the challenges they face in maintaining healthy habits.
The episode also offers practical tips for stretching grocery budgets, choosing affordable cuts of beef, and using simple cooking techniques to prepare flavorful meals. Together, the guests demonstrate that nutritious, protein-rich food can be accessible to families and first responders alike.
The Real Food Show demonstrates how every American can cook healthy, delicious meals at affordable prices. Inspired by President Trump’s Make America Healthy Again agenda, the series features budget-friendly recipes, easy cooking techniques, and practical nutrition advice to help Americans bring real food back to the table and restore the sacred ritual of preparing and eating meals together.
Every Recipe Featured on The Real Food Show:
- Uses real, whole-food ingredients, focusing on nutrient density.
- Is kid-friendly and easy for families to prepare together.
- Works in a basic home kitchen using everyday equipment.
- Costs less than $5 per serving whenever possible.
- Delivers delicious, practical meals for cooks of every skill level.
- Aligns with the updated Dietary Guidelines for Americans.

GREENSBORO, N.C. – A jury in federal district court convicted VERNON SCOTT NORTON today of multiple drug and firearm charges, announced United States Attorney Dan Bishop of the Middle District of North Carolina.

According to court documents, NORTON, age 34, was initially indicted on October 27, 2025, charged in Count One with conspiracy to distribute 500 grams or more of a mixture and substance containing a detectable amount of methamphetamine; in Count Two with possession of a firearm in furtherance of the offense charged in Count One; in Count Three with possession of a machinegun; and in Counts Four and Five with felon in possession of firearms.

Evidence at trial showed that NORTON was a previously convicted felon who possessed 31 firearms and a significant quantity of methamphetamine at his trailer in Laurel Hill, North Carolina. On December 29, 2023, law enforcement officers executed a search warrant at the property early in the morning. Officers located eight firearms inside the trailer and 23 additional firearms in a 2005 Infiniti parked in the yard. One of the firearms in the Infiniti was a machinegun—a Glock Model 19X 9mm pistol equipped with a machinegun conversion device.

Inside the trailer, officers recovered nearly 1.4 kilograms of methamphetamine hydrochloride. At the time of his arrest, NORTON had more than $6,000 in cash on his person. A readily accessible firearm—a Sturm/Ruger & Co. Inc. Model Ruger P94 9mm pistol—was found resting on the arm of a sofa next to a loaded magazine. Before executing the warrant, law enforcement had conducted multiple controlled purchases of narcotics from the property.

A jury convicted NORTON on all counts of the Indictment after a four-day trial. At sentencing, NORTON faces a term of imprisonment of 15 years to life, not less than 5 years of supervised release, fines, and restitution. Sentencing is scheduled for February 17, 2027, before Senior United States District Judge William L. Osteen, Jr. in Greensboro.

The case was investigated by the Scotland County Sheriff’s Office and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Frank J. Chut and Chase Stevens.

U.S Departments of Justice and Labor Secure Settlement with Cloudera, Enforce Two-Year PERM Debarment & Back Pay Following Discrimination Against U.S. Workers
The U.S. Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division (CRT) and the U.S. Department of Labor (DOL) today announced a coordinated enforcement resolution with Cloudera Inc., a Santa Clara, California-based data management company, following allegations that the company discriminated against qualified U.S. workers during recruitment conducted under the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) program.
“There are no exceptions: the Justice Department will hold accountable employers who discriminate against U.S. workers,” said Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. “This substantial settlement, in partnership with DOL, sends a strong signal to employers that the federal government will work together to ensure employers treat U.S. workers fairly.”
As part of the resolution, Cloudera will be barred from participating in the PERM program for two years, one of the most significant sanctions available for DOL to protect the integrity of the employment-based immigration system and safeguard opportunities for U.S. workers. The debarment follows DOL’s earlier suspension of Cloudera’s PERM processing and reflects DOL’s commitment to aggressively enforcing labor certification requirements when employers fail to provide U.S. workers a fair opportunity to compete for jobs.
The settlement also resolves a lawsuit DOJ filed in April of this year, alleging that Cloudera violated the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) by discriminating against U.S. workers when recruiting and hiring for seven positions under the PERM process. Under the terms of the settlement with the Justice Department, Cloudera will establish a back-pay fund of $1.4 million to compensate qualified U.S. workers who tried to apply for the jobs at issue but were not given fair consideration. Cloudera also will pay $600,000 in civil penalties to the United States.
In addition to the two-year debarment, Cloudera will be subject to compliance obligations designed to ensure future adherence to federal labor and anti-discrimination laws. These measures include enhanced monitoring, revised PERM compliance procedures, and reporting requirements intended to prevent future violations.
This debarment and compliance framework establish an important enforcement precedent and strengthen future efforts to protect U.S. workers. The PERM program allows employers to sponsor aliens for permanent residence only after demonstrating that qualified U.S. workers were provided a genuine opportunity to apply and that no qualified, willing, and available U.S. workers could be found. Employers who evade these requirements undermine both program integrity and the interests of U.S. workers. This resolution is one of many examples of coordinated federal enforcement designed to ensure employers comply with labor market protections established by Congress.
This settlement is also the fourteenth settlement since DOJ re-launched its Protecting U.S. Workers Initiative in 2025 to enforce the INA’s prohibition on citizenship status discrimination against companies that illegally discriminate against U.S. workers in favor of those with temporary employment visas. Under these settlements, DOJ obtains civil penalties for each violation and will continue to appropriately seek the maximum penalty permitted by law. The settlements also involve awards of back pay, when warranted, and require employers to conduct comprehensive training for relevant staff and recruiters and cease restricting consideration for job opportunities based on workers’ citizenship status without a lawful reason.
For information about additional settlements under the Protecting U.S. Workers Initiative, visit IER’s website.
For informal assistance, the public can call IER’s free hotline at 1-800-255-7688 for workers or at 1-800-255-8155 for employers (1-800-237-2515, TTY for hearing impaired) between 9am and 5pm Eastern Time, Monday through Friday; sign up for a live webinar or watch an on-demand presentation; email IER@usdoj.gov; or visit www.justice.gov/ier.

Rep. Costa Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Strengthen U.S. Defense Innovation Through Partnership with Ukraine
WASHINGTON – Today, Representatives Jim Costa (CA-21), a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee Subcommittee on Europe and the Congressional Ukraine Caucus, Don Bacon (NE-02), Wesley Bell (MO-01), and Mike Quigley (IL-05) introduced the bipartisan H.R. 10772 Frontline Innovation Act. This legislation will authorize the Department of Defense’s Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) to evaluate and invest in Ukrainian defense technologies, allowing the United States to benefit directly from innovations developed and refined on the battlefield in Ukraine.
Ukraine has emerged as a leader in developing modern defense technologies as it continues to defend itself against Russia’s invasion. Ukrainian companies are developing advanced drones unmanned systems, and electronic warfare tools that are being tested and improved under real combat conditions against a determined adversary. These innovations offer valuable opportunities to strengthen U.S. defense capabilities while supporting Ukraine’s ongoing efforts to defend its sovereignty.
However, existing U.S. defense cooperation agreements have not kept pace with these technological advancements. The last U.S.-Ukraine agreement on exchanging military research and development information dates back to 2001. Although the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) has worked with the Ukrainian government and firms since 2023, legal barriers currently limit its ability to expand these partnerships and invest directly in Ukrainian defense technologies.
“Ukraine has demonstrated extraordinary resilience in the face of Russia’s aggression, and Ukrainians are innovating and developing new defense technologies under some of the most challenging conditions imaginable,” said Congressman Costa. “This bipartisan bill will help strengthen our national security by investing in technologies that have been tested on the battlefield, while continuing to support Ukraine’s fight to defend its sovereignty.”
“Ukraine is fighting for its survival against Putin’s illegal invasion, and its forces have been forced to innovate at an extraordinary pace,” said Rep. Bacon. “They are proving new drones, unmanned systems and electronic warfare capabilities against Russia in real combat, and our military should be learning from that experience. I’m joining Rep. Costa in introducing the bipartisan Frontline Innovation Act to help bring battlefield-proven technologies into our own defense innovation system and strengthen our military while continuing to support Ukraine’s fight for freedom.”
"Standing with Ukraine is in America’s own interest, and the Frontline Innovation Act is a smart, practical way to do it. Every day, Ukrainian forces are developing and testing new technologies on the battlefield, providing valuable lessons that can help make our own servicemembers safer and prepared for the challenges of tomorrow,” said Rep. Bell. "As a member of the House Armed Services Committee, I know our military must have the best tools and technology, and after my recent trip to Ukraine, I can see how much Ukrainian battlefield innovation has to offer. I’m proud to cosponsor this bipartisan legislation to learn from our partners’ battlefield experience and help them continue defending their freedom.”
"When Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the entire world expected Kyiv to fall within days. Instead, the strength, resilience, and innovation of Ukrainians and the Ukrainian military have kept the capitol free for over four years. The United States should learn from Ukraine's battlefield innovation to strengthen and modernize our own military to ensure our forces are prepared for a new generation of threats," said Representative Mike Quigley, a Co-Chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus. "The Frontline Innovation Act would enable the U.S. military to accelerate defense innovation while continuing to support Ukraine as a critical ally."
The Frontline Innovation Act would:
- Expand defense cooperation by authorizing the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) to evaluate and invest in Ukrainian defense technologies, notwithstanding any other provision of law.
- Strengthen U.S. defense capabilities by directing DIU to ensure the United States benefits from technologies developed and refined through Ukraine’s defense against Russia’s invasion.
- Allow technology proven in combat to reach the U.S. military faster while creating new opportunities for the American defense industrial base to gain new partners and a larger market.
- Support Ukraine through increased investment and cooperation, allowing both countries to collaborate on developing the next generation of defense capabilities.
To read the full bill, click HERE.
title: Rep. Costa Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Strengthen U.S. Defense Innovation Through Partnership with Ukraine

RELEASE: Gottheimer Claws Back $3.7 Million in Federal Dollars for Public Safety in Sussex County
Above: Gottheimer Announces $3.7 Million in Federal Dollars for Public Safety in Sussex County.
NEWTON, NJ — Today, October 16, 2026, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) announced that he successfully clawed back $3.68 million in new federal Homeland Security funding for Sussex County first responders, helping upgrade emergency communications, expand counterterrorism training, and strengthen public safety while delivering real tax relief for local families.
The federal investment Gottheimer secured will replace aging equipment and move Sussex County toward a single, interoperable communications standard, so local, county, and State Police can communicate clearly and seamlessly across town lines when seconds matter most. By clawing back federal dollars to North Jersey communities and first responders, Gottheimer is helping lift high costs off local budgets, reducing the burden on Sussex County taxpayers to pay for essential public safety equipment and helping lower property taxes for local families.
Video of Gottheimer’s announcement can be found here.
“When something goes wrong, the people who show up are the people standing right here. Today, I am proud to announce that we have clawed back $3.68 million in federal Homeland Security funding from Washington for Sussex County first responders, families, and towns. I will always get the backs of our law enforcement, our firefighters, and our first responders,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), Co-Chair of the Law Enforcement Caucus and member of the Congressional Fire Services Caucus.
“We know that Josh Gottheimer is the claw back king,” said Sussex County Prosecutor Daniel M. Perez. “He works day in and day out to claw back federal taxpayer funds for first responders in Sussex County. You may not know this, but every day Josh wakes up and says ‘how can I redirect federal funds back to Sussex County? How can I claw back taxpayer dollars from Moocher States?’ Then he goes to work, reaches across the aisle, and delivers results for our families.”
The funding will be used as follows:
- Sussex County Prosecutor’s Office, $300,000: A countywide interoperable radio system linking every municipal law enforcement agency, the New Jersey State Police, and the Sheriff’s Office. It will also fund protective gear and other equipment for the Sussex County Rescue Task Force.
- Sussex County Sheriff’s Office, $200,000: 7/800 MHz radios that integrate with the New Jersey State frequency, migrating the county’s dispatched towns onto the State’s upgraded system.
- Andover Township First Responders, $200,000: A public safety video network system and training.
- Branchville First Responders, $200,000: Radio communications upgrades and training.
- Frankford First Responders, $150,000: Radio communications upgrades and training.
- Franklin Borough First Responders, $200,000: Video network enhancement and a virtual-reality law enforcement training system.
- Hamburg Borough First Responders, $150,000: Public Safety video security project and training.
- Hampton First Responders, $150,000: Radio communications upgrades and training.
- Hardyston Township First Responders, $200,000: A public safety video network system and training.
- Lafayette Township Office of Emergency Management, $200,000: Communications upgrades in the Emergency Operations Center to support interoperability and continuity of operations, plus training.
- Montague First Responders, $200,000: Radio communications upgrades and training.
- Newton First Responders, $100,000: Radio communications upgrades and training.
- Sandyston First Responders, $150,000: Radio communications upgrades and training.
- Sussex Borough First Responders, $200,000: Radio communications upgrades and training.
- Vernon Township First Responders, $200,000: Active-threat response gear and training.
- Wantage First Responders, $150,000: Radio communications upgrades and training.
The $3.7 million funding includes previously announced upgrades:
- $500,000 for security upgrades at the Andover train station;
- $200,000 for a real-time intelligence platform in Newton;
- $30,000 for a thermal search-and-overwatch drone in Vernon, so officers can run night searches and respond to incidents safely;
- $50,000 for every police department in the Fifth District, including all of Sussex County, for counterterrorism training;
This investment builds on Gottheimer’s years-long work to claw more federal dollars back to North Jersey from Washington. This year alone, he has secured roughly $21 million in Homeland Security grant funding across Bergen, Passaic, and Sussex Counties for law enforcement, first responders, and the houses of worship and nonprofits that need protection. Since coming to Congress, Gottheimer has helped increase the return of federal funds to the Fifth District by more than 357%, delivering an average savings of more than $750 for each household in the Fifth District.
Gottheimer was joined by Newton Mayor Matthew Dickson, Sussex County Prosecutor Dan Perez, Sussex County Commissioners Alan Henderson and David Silverthorne, Chief of Detectives Nicholas Elmo, Detective Andrew Moore, and Lt. Kyle Phlegar of the Sussex County Prosecutor’s Office, Andover Police Chief Eric Danielson, Newton Police Chief Daniel Finkle, Newton Police Lts. Jared Zappa and Russell Post, Wantage Township Mayor Justin VanderGroef, Vernon Township Mayor Anthony Rossi, Vernon Police Chief Daniel B. Young, Vernon Police Lt. Sean Perry, Lafayette Township Committeeman Kevin O’Leary and Kevin McGill, Branchville Councilman Jeffery Lewis, Montague Township Committeeman Fred Merusi, Sussex Councilman John Ross, Confidential Aide to the Commissioners Ken Schwemmer, Frankford Committeeman Ken Sharrock, Frankford Committeeman Ryan Phillips, Frankford Municipal Clerk Lori Niemstedt, local first responders, and community leaders.

U.S. Coast Guard urges preparedness ahead of Typhoon Champi
U.S. Coast Guard Forces Micronesia / Sector Guam
SANTA RITA, Guam — The U.S. Coast Guard, federal, territorial, and port partners are continuing to prepare Saturday for Typhoon Champi, recently upgraded from a Tropical Storm, and expected to arrive Sunday.
"We, along with our partners, are committed to the safety of Guam and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI) communities," said Capt. Jessica Worst, U.S. Coast Guard Forces Micronesia/Sector Guam commander. "We are making preparations, securing assets and safeguarding the ports. Once the storm passes, we are prepared to conduct post-storm assessments and support the ports reopening as quickly as it is safe to do so."
Ahead of the storm, the Coast Guard urges people to stay out of the water and listen to official messaging. U.S. Coast Guard Forces Micronesia/Sector Guam is actively working with on-island partners, conducting pre-storm assessments, preparing for post-storm response, and remaining focused on keeping the public safe.
Building surf, dangerous rip currents and high winds are expected. Residents are urged to secure gear. Kayaks, paddleboards, jet skis, and small boats may break loose and become hazards and could result in false distress calls. Search and rescue assets and crews are standing by. However, as the storm approaches, responders will likely be delayed in responding until the storm passes.
Prepare properly ahead of the storm. This includes acquiring a supply of water, food, medication, and fuel for 7-10 days. Review your household emergency plan and ensure dwellings are properly secured to minimize damage.
Social media is NOT a reliable means to seek immediate assistance in the event of an emergency. The Coast Guard urges the public to use 911. VHF FM Channel 16 may be intermittent. Emergency position indicating radio beacons/ personal locator beacons (EPIRBS/PLBs) are encouraged to report distress.
The Coast Guard strongly advises the public to stay informed of official weather notifications. As of 7 a.m. this morning, Typhoon Champi is approximately 340 miles east-southeast of Guam and moving northwest at 15 mph with increased maximum sustained winds at 70 mph. Champi is expected to make a slight turn towards the west and increase in speed. Intensification is likely. Guam and the CNMI could see impacts by late Saturday night, Oct. 17 (ChST) with up to Category 3-strength winds.

• Joint Region Marianas (JRM) Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/jrmguam 
-USCG-

Davids Urges Federal Action as Kansas Small Businesses Squeezed Out of Tariff Refunds While Large Corporations Cash In
New study shows without reckless tariffs, inflation would have declined
Today, Representative Sharice Davids demanded immediate action to ensure Kansas small businesses receive the tariff refunds they are owed. Following this year’s Supreme Court ruling overturning the president’s reckless tariffs, the federal government began processing billions of dollars in refunds. However, while major corporations get massive paydays, local Kansas mom-and-pop shops are facing bureaucratic hurdles that leave them behind.
"Small businesses should not need a team of lawyers or customs specialists to recover money they are owed," wrote Davids in a letter to the Small Business Administration (SBA) and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP). "The businesses with the fewest resources should not face the greatest barriers to recovering their money while large corporations are better positioned to navigate the system... I urge the administration to ensure that the refund process works for the small businesses that need this relief most."
Data from the Center for American Progress highlights the stark disparity facing Kansas main streets: the average Kansas small business importer has recovered just $49,000 in refunds compared to the $140,000 they paid out in tariffs. Meanwhile, some of the nation’s largest corporations — which possess internal legal teams and outside specialists to navigate the complex application process — have secured refunds worth hundreds of millions of dollars.
In her letter, Davids outlined how many small businesses were forced to absorb higher costs passed down by suppliers, yet remain ineligible or unable to navigate the current non-automatic refund process. She is calling on the SBA and CBP to create a realistic, streamlined, and accessible path for small businesses, including direct guidance and a simplified application process for small firms that have not yet applied.
This action builds directly on Davids’ ongoing efforts to protect Kansas workers and small businesses from unfair trade practices. Davids previously supported the RELIEF Act, legislation designed to provide automatic, hassle-free tariff refunds to small businesses and hardworking families who bore the financial burden of reckless tariff policies.
The administration’s reckless tariff policies have hit Kansas hard, driving up costs for families and threatening small businesses and farmers. Average American households will pay $2,500 more this year because of these policies. Local industries, including agriculture, manufacturing, and retail, have faced higher costs for imported goods, forcing some businesses to raise consumer prices, cut jobs, or close entirely.
Read Davids’ full letter here or below
Dear Administrator Loeffler and Commissioner Scott,
I write to share my concerns about the impact of the Trump Administration’s trade war and tariff refund process on Kansas small businesses. Local small businesses have already paid the price of higher tariffs. Now, as the federal government works to return billions of dollars in tariffs that were collected, small businesses are at risk of being left behind.
The Center for American Progress estimates the average Kansas small business importer has only received $49,000 in refunds, compared with the $140,000 paid in tariffs (as of August 2026). At the same time, some of the nation’s largest corporations have received refunds worth hundreds of millions of dollars.
Following the Supreme Court’s decision earlier this year overturning President Trump’s broad International Emergency Economic Powers Act tariffs, Customs and Border Protection (CBP) began processing refunds for eligible businesses. These refunds are not automatic. The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta found that larger firms are somewhat more likely to receive or seek refunds, relying on internal staff or outside firms to navigate the process.
Kansas small businesses often lack the staff to navigate a complicated federal refund process. Some may also be ineligible to apply, even though they ultimately paid higher prices because of tariffs. For example, a tariff may be passed from an importer to a small business through a supplier, but the refund may go to the original importer — not the small business that absorbed the higher cost.
Small businesses should not need a team of lawyers or customs specialists to recover money they are owed.
I urge the Small Business Administration to work with CBP and other federal agencies to create a realistic, efficient, and accessible path for small businesses to receive the tariff refunds they are owed. This should include a straightforward process for businesses that have not yet applied, as well as clear guidance and assistance for small businesses navigating the process.
The businesses with the fewest resources should not face the greatest barriers to recovering their money while large corporations are better positioned to navigate the system. I urge the administration to ensure that the refund process works for the small businesses that need this relief most.
Sincerely,
title: Davids Urges Federal Action as Kansas Small Businesses Squeezed Out of Tariff Refunds While Large Corporations Cash In

Panama City Drug Trafficking Organization Dismantled by Homeland Security Task Force Prosecution
Tallahassee, Fla. – Mario Swanston, 45, of Miami; Santana Wyvonne Harris, 41, of Panama City, Fla.; Shannon Jarbar Clayton, 46, of Panama City; Elizabeth Gray, 37, of Panama City; and Shontell Fedd, 49, of Panama City, each were sentenced by U.S. District Judge Mark E. Walker in federal court after previously pleading guilty to conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute cocaine and marijuana. Swanston and Harris pleaded guilty to an additional count of possession with intent to distribute cocaine. The sentences were announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida.
U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “This successful prosecution was made possible by the whole-of-government commitment under the Homeland Security Task Force to eradicate criminal organizations operating within the United States, and my office will continue to aggressively prosecute these cases and advocate for substantial punishments to be imposed against the offenders who have victimized our communities. Our citizens deserve to live on safe, drug-free streets, and my office will fight hard every day to fulfill that promise.”
According to court records, between November 21, 2023, and April 25, 2024, Mario Swanston conspired with his co-defendants, and others, to distribute controlled substances, including cocaine and marijuana. As part of the conspiracy, Swanston obtained cocaine and marijuana from California and Georgia. Swanston utilized drug couriers—namely Harris, Gray, and Fedd -to store and transport the drugs on his behalf. Swanston was responsible for over 1,700 grams of cocaine and over 550 pounds of marijuana.
U.S. District Judge Mark E. Walker sentenced Swanston to five years’ imprisonment and imposed sentences of federal supervised release on Harris (4 years), Clayton (3 years), Gray (3 years), and Fedd (2 years).
“I’m proud of our agents and Homeland Security Task Force partners for stopping this drug trafficking organization,” said DEA Special Agent in Charge Daniel Escobar, Tampa Field Division. “Cocaine is commonly trafficked in North Florida, and our agents will remain vigilant in the fight to keep this out of our communities.”
The conviction and sentences were the result of a joint investigation by the Drug Enforcement Administration, Homeland Security Investigations, U.S. Marshals Service, Bay County Sheriff’s Office, the Gulf County Sheriff’s Office, Florida Department of Law Enforcement, Florida Highway Patrol, Panama City Police Department, Panama City Beach Police Department, and Springfield Police Department. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Joseph A. Ravelo.
This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF comprises agents and officers from multiple agencies with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida.
title: Panama City Drug Trafficking Organization Dismantled by Homeland Security Task Force Prosecution

Kaptur Announces $50 Million in Federal Railroad Administration Investment in Rail Infrastructure for Northwest Ohio Rail Infrastructure
Toledo, OH — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09) announced investments of nearly $50 Million in Rail Infrastructure for Northwest Ohio. The Wheeling and Lake Erie Railway will receive a $43.5 Million award through the US Department of Transportation’s Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) and its Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) Program. The award will be used to make improvements to the Toledo Swing Bridge over the Maumee River. Congresswoman Kaptur, the Toledo-Lucas County Port Authority, and representatives from the Wheeling and Lake Erie Railway will hold a press conference Monday in Toledo to announce further details related to this major funding award. In addition, the Ohio Rail Development Commission (ORDC) will receive a $5.6 Million FRA CRISI award to be used to update track infrastructure along a section of the Indiana Northeastern Railroad in Williams County.
“Our railways are a crucial mode of transportation connecting our region, the industrial heartland of America, to markets around the world,” said Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09). “I am thrilled to see this investment in railways here in Northwest Ohio. Access to strong and safe rail infrastructure is vital for trade across the Great Lakes Region, connecting us to global markets. The Wheeling and Lake Erie Railway Company is an important part of our economy, moving tens of thousands of freight cars each year. I look forward to seeing how their improvements bolster trade and increase rail safety for years to come.”
"The Toledo-Lucas County Port Authority is glad to see that the rehabilitation of the Wheeling & Lake Erie Railway Bridge over the Maumee River will be moving forward with the assistance of the CRISI program,” said Thomas Winston, President & CEO of the Toledo-Lucas County Port Authority. “This project not only improves the efficiency of railroad operations in the port area but also improves the reliability of the functionality of the bridge, making it safer and reducing potential delays for maritime traffic moving though the area."
Wheeling and Lake Erie Railway’s award seeks to rehabilitate and modernize the Toledo Swing Bridge over the Maumee River. This includes the rehabilitation of eight of the eleven bridge spans and replacing timber fender systems on the bridge. Upon completion, the upgrades will increase the bridge’s capacity to support up to 286,000-pound railcars.
“I am thrilled that the Ohio Rail Development Commission is the recipient of this tremendous investment in rail infrastructure,” said Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09). The Indiana Northeastern Railroad Company operates over 100-miles of track throughout our region, and today’s award will allow them to improve parts of that track right here in Northwest Ohio. By making our rail systems safer, we are creating more jobs and increasing the trade that flows through our community. When our railroads are stronger, our nation is stronger.”
“We are grateful to the Federal Railroad Administration for selecting these crucial projects to receive federal funding,” said Ohio Rail Development Commission Executive Director Matthew Dietrich. “These investments directly deliver on our commitment to upgrading vital infrastructure, enhancing safety, and strengthening freight service reliability across Northwest Ohio.”
The Ohio Rail Development Commission’s award will be used to improve sections of track on the Indiana Northeastern Railroad in Williams County. Improvements will be made to extend sidings, replace rail, and resurface track along nine miles of the rail system.
Creating reliable, efficient, and affordable transportation for people and products remains a strong priority for Congresswoman Kaptur. In 2024, she secured a total of $18.57 Million in FRA awards for the Northern Ohio & Western Railway and the Napolean, Defiance, & Western Railway. These two awards were made possible through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, of which Kaptur was a staunch advocate as it moved through Congress.

title: Kaptur Announces $50 Million in Federal Railroad Administration Investment in Rail Infrastructure for Northwest Ohio Rail Infrastructure

PHOENIX, Ariz. – During the week of enforcement operations from Oct. 10 through Oct. 16, 2026, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Arizona brought immigration-related criminal charges against 279 individuals. Specifically, the United States filed 136 cases in which aliens illegally re-entered the United States, and the United States also charged 123 aliens for illegally entering the United States. In its ongoing effort to deter unlawful immigration, the United States filed 17 cases against 20 individuals responsible for smuggling illegal aliens into and within the District of Arizona.

These cases were referred or supported by federal law enforcement partners, including U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s Enforcement and Removal Operations (ICE-ERO), ICE- Homeland Security Investigations (ICE-HSI), U.S. Border Patrol, the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), the FBI, the U.S. Marshals Service (USMS), and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF).

Recent matters of interest include:

United States v. Calixtro-Rodriguez et al. Jesus Manuel Calixtro-Rodriguez and Julio Cesar Ramos-Mendez were charged by criminal complaint on Oct. 13, 2026, with Conspiracy to Transport an Illegal Alien for Profit. Ramos-Mendez was also charged in the complaint with Reentry of Removed Alien. On Oct. 10, 2026, Border Patrol cameras observed a driver in a Dodge Ram traveling south on Federal Route 15 on the Tohono O'odham Nation. The driver, later identified as Calixtro-Rodriguez, performed a u-turn and parked on the side of the road near mile marker 5, a known pick-up spot for illegal aliens. Multiple subjects were observed entering the Dodge Ram. Calixtro-Rodriguez then traveled northbound. Border Patrol Agents (BPAs) attempted to stop him to conduct an immigration inspection, but Calixtro-Rodriguez failed to yield. BPAs then deployed a tire deflation device which disabled the vehicle. All of the subjects bailed from the vehicle and ran away. BPAs were able to apprehend Calixtro-Rodriguez and three passengers, including Ramos-Mendez, who were determined to be citizens of Mexico, unlawfully present in the United States. BPAs learned that Ramos-Mendez was the group's foot guide. Records checks revealed that Ramos-Mendez had been previously removed from the United States and did not have authorization to return. [Case Number: 26-MJ-04143]

United States v. Christopher Paul Lopez. On Oct. 9, 2026, Christopher Paul Lopez was charged by criminal complaint with Transportation of an Illegal Alien. On Oct. 8, an Arizona Department of Public Safety Trooper performed a traffic stop on a Land Rover driving on the I-10. The Trooper observed Lopez lying in the rear of the vehicle during the traffic stop. Lopez began reaching for a black bag, prompting the Trooper to ask if the bag contained a firearm, which Lopez confirmed. The Trooper removed the bag and recovered a loaded Glock 19 handgun from inside. The Trooper directed Lopez to exit the vehicle to speak with them. Their conversation led the Trooper to believe Lopez and the driver were involved in human smuggling. BPAs responded to the scene and determined that the driver was a citizen of Mexico, unlawfully present in the United States. BPAs also learned that Lopez had been paid to accompany the driver from Tucson to Phoenix. [Case Number: 26-MJ-8411]

United States v. Jose Avendano-Soto. On Oct. 13, 2026, Jose Avendano-Soto was charged by criminal complaint with Transportation of an Illegal Alien. On Oct. 8, 2026, a Border Patrol Agent (BPA) observed an SUV driving directly alongside the US-Mexico border wall before stopping. Seven individuals exited the vehicle and deployed a rope ladder to climb over the wall. Five members of the group continued walking north into the United States. The two remaining individuals covered the group's footprints and returned to Mexico. BPAs found the five individuals later, hiding among vegetation wearing camouflage clothing. BPAs determined four were citizens of Guatemala and that one was a citizen of Mexico, and that all were unlawfully present in the United States. BPAs also learned that one of them, Avendano-Soto, was serving as the group’s foot guide into the United States. [Case Number: 26-MJ-1825]

A criminal complaint is a formal accusation of criminal conduct. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

text:
Secretary Rollins Builds Upon Great American Cotton Plan with Further Announcements
(Washington, D.C., October 16, 2026) – Today, U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins visited Giesenschlag Farms in Caldwell, Texas, where she announced two new actions under the Great American Cotton Plan to strengthen support for American cotton producers.
“Under the last administration, the United States lost our title as the world’s top cotton exporter. Our cotton growers have been squeezed by foreign competitors for too long, which is why we launched the Great American Cotton Plan in May,” said Secretary Brooke L. Rollins. “Today we are advancing that plan to give our producers more protection to manage their risks and improve opportunities for trade. We are not going to stop until we restore America’s cotton industry.”
The Great American Cotton Plan, launched in May 2026, is built on four key pillars:
- Promoting Domestic Cotton Consumption
- Providing Affordable Cotton by Increasing Domestic Demand and Production
- Improving Cotton Trade
- Protecting Cotton Growers from Adverse Risk
Today’s actions advance the plan as follows:
Expanded Crop Insurance Flexibility for Producers
USDA’s Risk Management Agency (RMA) will allow producers, including cotton growers, to purchase multiple endorsements on a crop insurance policy for the 2027 crop year. This action builds upon the Great American Cotton Plan by further protecting cotton growers, as well as other eligible crops, from adverse risk.
The Working Families Tax Cuts Act, signed into law by President Trump on July 4, 2025, expanded and increased the affordability of many crop insurance products, removing unnecessary restrictions and providing producers with as many options as possible to protect their crops.
RMA will release final details to Approved Insurance Providers (AIPs) and crop insurance agents by November 30, 2026.
USDA Foreign Agricultural Service to Assume Responsibility for Cotton TRQ Process
USDA's Foreign Agricultural Service (FAS) is designing a mechanism that will incentivize purchases of American cotton that will launch in 2027. This action delivers on the promises made in the Great American Cotton Plan by continuing to develop new opportunities for cotton trade.
Tariff-rate quotas establish the terms under which specified quantities of imported products may enter at designated rates. FAS will play a key role in verifying purchases of U.S. cotton by select countries, specifically Bangladesh, Indonesia, Cambodia, and Malaysia, in exchange for preferential tariff treatment on imports of apparel produced using U.S. cotton and textile inputs. This action aligns responsibility for this function with USDA’s broader agricultural trade mission.
To learn more, please view the Great American Cotton Plan (PDF, 2.7 MB).
###
title: Secretary Rollins Builds Upon Great American Cotton Plan with Further Announcements

ABERDEEN - United States Attorney Ron Parsons announced today that U.S. District Judge Charles B. Kornmann has sentenced a Little Eagle, South Dakota, man convicted of Sexual Abuse of a Child Without Consent. The sentencing took place on October 13, 2026.

Russell Lawrence Has Horns, age 53, was sentenced to 19 years and seven months in federal prison, followed by five years of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund.

Has Horns was indicted by a federal grand jury in July 2025. He pleaded guilty on May 15, 2026.

In 2016 or 2017, Has Horns began routinely having sexual intercourse with a five-year-old girl in Little Eagle, South Dakota, which lies within the Standing Rock Sioux Indian Reservation. The abuse continued until 2021.

This matter was prosecuted by the U.S. Attorney’s Office because the Major Crimes Act, a federal statute, mandates that certain violent crimes alleged to have occurred in Indian Country be prosecuted in Federal Court as opposed to State Court.

This case was investigated by the FBI. Assistant U.S. Attorney Carl Thunem prosecuted the case.

Has Horns was remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service to serve his federal sentence.
title: Little Eagle Man Sentenced to More Than 19 Years in Federal Prison for Child Sex Abuse

On October 13, 2026, the United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Louisiana charged Manuel De Jesus Arce Cruz , 42, of Mexico, by criminal complaint with Possession with Intent to Distribute Cocaine and Methamphetamine.

According to court documents, on October 8, 2026, investigators began surveillance at Arce Cruz’s Lafayette-area residence in connection with a drug trafficking investigation. Investigators saw Arce Cruz, an illegal alien, depart his residence by car with a work bag. After law enforcement stopped Arce Cruz for a traffic violation, the officers conducted a lawful search of the vehicle and recovered approximately 1.5 kilograms of cocaine and half a kilogram of methamphetamine. A search warrant executed at Arce Cruz’s residence allegedly led to the recovery of an additional half of a kilogram of cocaine along with scales, baggies, cash, and other items typically associated with drug distribution.

This case was investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration and the Louisiana State Police. It is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Lauren Sarver, with assistance from Paralegal Specialist Joanne Henry-Mills.

Baltimore, Maryland – A Baltimore man pled guilty in federal court to firearm-possession charges.

Arsenio Hall, 37, is charged with possession of a firearm and ammunition by a prohibited person. Hall is prohibited from possessing firearms and ammunition due to a prior felony conviction. Those convictions include two for second-degree assault, including a domestically related assault, along with drug-related convictions.

Kelly O. Hayes, U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the guilty plea with Special Agent in Charge Charles Doerrer, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives (ATF), and Commissioner Richard Worley, Baltimore Police Department (BPD).

According to court documents, on December 19, 2024, members of BPD’s SWAT Team arrived at Hall’s residence to assist Baltimore County Police Department detectives with executing an arrest warrant on Hall and a search-and-seizure warrant on his residence. These warrants were related to a November 2024 shooting in Baltimore County. During the search, officers recovered a semi-automatic rifle from a baby crib inside of Hall’s bedroom.

Hall faces a maximum of 15 years in prison for possession of a firearm by a prohibited person. U.S. District Court Judge Ellen L. Hollander set sentencing for Wednesday, Jan. 13, 2027, at 11 a.m.

Actual sentences for federal crimes are typically less than the maximum penalties. A federal district judge determines sentencing after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

This prosecution is part of Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) and Project Safe Home. These programs bring together all levels of law enforcement and the communities they serve to reduce violent crime and gun violence, and to make our neighborhoods safer for everyone. On May 26, 2021, the Department launched a violent crime reduction strategy strengthening PSN based on these core principles: fostering trust and legitimacy in our communities, supporting community-based organizations that help prevent violence from occurring in the first place, setting focused and strategic enforcement priorities, and measuring the results. Project Safe Home is an initiative under the Violence Against Women Act (VAWA) through the Office on Violence Against Women (OVW) to reduce domestic violence and prevent escalation to lethal violence by targeting offenders who use or possess handguns with a history of Domestic Violence.

In response, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Maryland is working closely with its federal, local, and state partners — along with Baltimore City community organizations — to reduce violent crime and enhance public safety. This partnership and coordination between the U.S. Attorney’s Office and the City of Baltimore ensures that federal resources are leveraged effectively to address intimidate-partner firearm violence.

U.S. Attorney Hayes commended the ATF and BPD for their collaborative efforts in this investigation. Ms. Hayes also thanked Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Kathleen Godwin who prosecuted this case.

For more information about the Maryland U.S. Attorney’s Office, its priorities, and resources available to help the community, visit justice.gov/usao-md .
