NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA – DANNY PATRICK KEATING, JR. , age 57, of New Orleans, was sentenced on October 15, 2026 for Conspiracy to Commit Mail and Wire Fraud, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Section 371, arising out of staged automobile accidents with tractor-trailers occurring in New Orleans, announced United States Attorney David I. Courcelle.

KEATING was indicted on November 5, 2020, and charged with knowingly engaging in a vast conspiracy involving the intentional staging of motor vehicle collisions with tractor-trailers and commercial vehicles in the metropolitan New Orleans area. Thus far, sixty-three (63) defendants have been charged in the federal probe into the staging of such collisions.

KEATING was a personal injury attorney licensed to practice law in Louisiana. At the time of his plea on June 17, 2021, KEATING admitted he knowingly paid Damian Labeaud for thirty-one (31) illegally staged tractor-trailer accidents. KEATING represented seventy-seven (77) plaintiffs involved in the thirty-one (31) accidents staged by Labeaud. KEATING settled seventeen (17) of the thirty-one (31) staged accidents. The indictment charged that KEATING and his clients received a total of approximately $1,500,000.00 in settlement monies resulting from his representation of these clients, and that KEATING kept approximately $358,000.00 of these monies as his attorney’s fees.

KEATING admitted filing lawsuits in state and federal court in Louisiana, on behalf of his clients who were involved in the staged accidents. The lawsuits he filed on behalf of the seventy-seven (77) plaintiffs fraudulently misrepresented the identity of the driver of these vehicles, fraudulently misrepresented who was at fault in the staged accidents, and fraudulently claimed injuries. KEATING used the U.S Postal Service to mail settlement demands on behalf of his clients from the Eastern District of Louisiana to various out-of-state locations. In many cases, KEATING ’s clients provided false testimony in depositions taken in conjunction with lawsuits filed by KEATING .

United States District Judge Nanette Jolivette Brown sentenced KEATING to thirty-two (32) months of imprisonment, followed by three (3) years of supervised release, as well as the payment of $657,405.34 in restitution, and a $100.00 mandatory special assessment fee.

The U.S. Attorney’s Office would like to acknowledge the assistance of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Louisiana State Police, and the Metropolitan Crime Commission with this matter. The prosecution of this case was handled by Brian M. Klebba, Deputy Chief of the Criminal Division and Chief of the Financial Crimes Unit, as well as Assistant U.S. Attorneys Matthew Payne, Edward J. Rivera, Maria Carboni, and U.S. Department of Justice Trial Attorney Ryan J. McLaren.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

* * *

United States Attorney Lesley A. Woods announced that Jessie Feaster, Jr., 50, of Lincoln, Nebraska, was sentenced on October 15, 2026, in federal court in Lincoln for conspiracy to distribute/possession with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of methamphetamine mixture and 50 grams or more of methamphetamine actual. United States District Judge Susan M. Bazis sentenced Feaster to 130 months’ imprisonment. There is no parole in the federal system. After Feaster’s release from prison, he will begin a 5-year term of supervised release.

On October 10, 2025, investigators with the Lincoln Lancaster County Narcotics Task Force were conducting surveillance on co-defendant David Leibbrandt’s Lincoln residence. They saw a U.S. Postal Service truck arrive and the driver left a package on the porch. A short time later, someone came out of the house and retrieved the package. About an hour later, Feaster, Jr. (“Feaster”) arrived at Leibbrandt’s residence and went inside. After a few minutes, Feaster returned to his vehicle and left. Investigators followed Feaster to another location in Lincoln where Feaster was contacted and he agreed to let them search his car. A sandwich bag was found on the front passenger seat which contained approximately one pound of methamphetamine. Purity testing at the Nebraska State Patrol Crime Lab showed at least 410 grams of actual (pure) methamphetamine.

Later the same day, investigators executed a search warrant at Leibbrandt’s residence. During that search, they found seven bags containing methamphetamine with a total weight of more than 2.7 kilograms. Purity testing on one of the packages showed at least 1.8 kilograms of actual methamphetamine. Leibbrandt was arrested and agreed to talk to investigators. He admitted receiving 10 pounds of methamphetamine earlier that day and said he had already sold more than three pounds from that quantity, including the pound he sold to Feaster.

Leibbrandt pleaded guilty to the same conspiracy charge and was sentenced on September 24, 2026, to 135 months’ imprisonment and a 5-year term of supervised release.

This case was investigated by the Lincoln/Lancaster County Narcotics Task Force.

SHREVEPORT – On October 7, 2026, a federal grand jury returned an indictment charging Tre'veon Jackson , 24, of Shreveport, with Carjacking Resulting in Serious Bodily Injury. Jackson faces up to 25 years in federal prison for the charge.

U.S. Attorney Zachary A. Keller for the Western District of Louisiana made the announcement.

According to court documents, Jackson escaped from custody during a medical transport on September 14, 2026, and, shortly thereafter, approached a man outside a hotel in Bossier City, violently assaulted him, and stole the victim’s vehicle. Jackson then allegedly led law enforcement officers on a high speed pursuit exceeding 110 miles per hour before crashing the vehicle and fleeing on foot. A multi-agency manhunt followed, and Jackson remained at large for several days until he was rearrested in Marshall, Texas, by the United States Marshals Service. He is now in federal custody. The FBI, U.S. Marshals Service, Bossier City Police Department, Marshall Police Department, Harrison County Sheriff’s Office, Texas State Technical College Police Department, and the Texas Rangers investigated the case. It is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Allison Foster and Samuel Crichton, with assistance from Legal Assistant Emily Favrot.

An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. This case is part of the Western District of Louisiana’s GATOR (Gun Crime Abatement and Targeted Offender Response) Task Force initiative, which focuses on investigating, prosecuting, and preventing violent crime through a unified, multi-agency strategy in the Shreveport and Bossier City area. The Task Force is built around a core group of FBI Special Agents and FBI Task Force Officers from Louisiana State Police, Caddo Parish Sheriff’s Office, and Shreveport Police Department, who work closely with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security’s Homeland Security Investigations, Sabine Parish Sheriff’s Office, Louisiana State Probation & Parole, the Shreveport City Marshal, and Caddo Parish Juvenile Services. You may find a copy of this press release (and any updates) on the website of the United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Louisiana at www.justice.gov/usao-wdla.

Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Western District of Louisiana at www.lawd.uscourts.gov or at https://www.lawd.uscourts.gov/cmecf-pacer. The case number for this matter is 5:26-cr-00399-01.

NASHVILLE – Brandon Ostein, 40, of Nashville, Tennessee, was convicted by a federal jury of multiple drug trafficking and firearms offenses following a jury trial in Nashville, announced United States Attorney for the Middle District of Tennessee Braden H. Boucek.

The jury found Ostein guilty of conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute 400 grams or more of fentanyl and five kilograms or more of cocaine; two counts involving the distribution of cocaine; possession with intent to distribute 400 grams or more of fentanyl and five kilograms or more of cocaine; possession of firearms in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime; and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon.

According to the evidence presented at trial, Ostein operated a large-scale drug trafficking business from an apartment at 1200 Broadway in downtown Nashville. The apartment, served as Ostein’s central location for storing substantial quantities of cocaine and fentanyl, cash, firearms, and equipment used to prepare and package the drugs for distribution.

The investigation began in April 2023 and involved controlled purchases of cocaine, physical surveillance, and video recordings. The investigation revealed Ostein’s distribution of cocaine and fentanyl in the Middle Tennessee area. The evidence presented at trial established that Ostein worked with another individual who sold smaller quantities of cocaine while Ostein supplied the cocaine and oversaw the operation. Ostein was also present during several of the cocaine transactions.

On August 31, 2023, law enforcement executed a search warrant at the apartment at 1200 Broadway. Inside the apartment, investigators recovered approximately 35 pounds of cocaine, four pounds of fentanyl, $350,000 in cash, and two loaded firearms. Investigators also recovered equipment associated with drug trafficking, including a kilogram press, packaging materials, and other items used in preparing drugs for distribution.

The evidence further established Ostein’s access to and control over the apartment through building access records, surveillance footage, and personal belongings recovered inside. Investigators also discovered a telescope positioned toward a nearby parking area, which was used to monitor cocaine deals.

The jury convicted Ostein on all counts charged in the indictment. In a separate phase of the trial, the jury also determined that Ostein had qualifying prior felony drug convictions, including Davidson County convictions for possession of more than 300 grams of cocaine, supporting an enhanced statutory penalty.

Ostein is set to be sentenced on January 21, 2027, and faces a mandatory minimum sentence of at least thirty years but up to life in prison.

The case was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation, the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department, and the Murfreesboro Police Department.

Assistant United States Attorneys Juliet Aldridge and Dina A. Shabayek prosecuted the case.

Rep. Sara Jacobs Pens Newsweek Op-ed on How to Win the AI Race
Rep. Sara Jacobs (CA-51) penned an op-ed for Newsweek, arguing that her colleagues have largely misdiagnosed the AI race with China. She lays out how Congress needs to address AI on the societal, model, deployer, and impact levels in order to create AI systems that people trust more and would rather use. That is America’s competitive advantage and how to ensure systems around the world are built on American models.
In part, Rep. Sara Jacobs said:
“While the U.S. is leading in frontier model capabilities and advanced computing infrastructure, China is outperforming us in model adoption. Chinese models’ share of usage on Open Router climbed from about 1 percent in 2024 to over 60 percent in May 2026. Chinese models are also cheaper and use less compute than leading American models. We may not ever build cheaper systems than China, but we can create systems that people trust more and would rather use. That is our competitive advantage and how we ensure systems around the world are built on American models.
“Still, many of my colleagues in Congress beat the drum for speed over safety in the name of competition. Speaker Mike Johnson recently said, “We’re not going to rush in and pass a piece of legislation that would do harm to the country and put China at an edge.” But what the speaker and many of my colleagues fail to understand is that we don’t have to choose between innovation or guardrails. The real question is: How do we build AI systems that people actually want to use and can safely rely on? That’s what winning looks like. Not necessarily being first—but being the most trusted, avoiding costly fixes and backlashes, and having real, lasting staying power. And it’s Congress’ job to get us there by addressing AI on four levels: societal, model, deployer, and impact.”
Background: Rep. Sara Jacobs has been a leader in AI safety throughout her tenure in Congress, sitting on the House Bipartisan Task Force on Artificial Intelligence last term and currently on the House Democratic Commission on AI and the Innovation Economy. She’s introduced several bills to address the everyday harms and catastrophic risks posed by AI, including the Sectoral AI Governance Act, the bipartisan AI Foundation Model Transparency Act, the bipartisan Economy of the Future Commission Act, the bipartisan ATOMIC Act, the AI Tax and Work Protection Act, and more. She’s also passed legislation into law to prevent AI from autonomously launching nuclear weapons and strengthening oversight and accountability of the Pentagon’s use of AI.

Trump Administration Announces $92 Million to Coordinate Rural Hospital Networks, Improve Maternal Care, and Expand Medical Services Across Ohio
This federal investment will connect rural providers and bring MRI, behavioral health, and maternal care closer to patients across Ohio
Today, the Trump Administration announced $92 million in Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) funding to help rural providers connect patients to coordinated, high-quality care and bring essential health services closer to home for Ohioans. This investment will support coordinated care networks, strengthen maternal health services, and upgrade equipment and facilities at 22 rural hospitals across Ohio.
This transformational funding will deliver $31.4 million to establish or expand coordinated rural care networks, including Clinically Integrated Networks (CINs) and Rural Health Innovation Hubs, that connect physicians, hospitals, clinics, emergency medical services, behavioral health providers, pharmacists, and higher education institutions so they can coordinate care more effectively. An additional $30.3 million will go to hospital networks and health centers to improve maternal care in rural Ohio communities, while another $30.3 million will fund one-time equipment and facility upgrades at 22 rural hospitals, including a new behavioral health unit, on-site MRI services, and expanded diagnostic capacity.
The Rural Health Transformation Program is expanding access to quality healthcare, regardless of a patient’s zip code, and equipping first responders with the lifesaving resources they need when every second counts. This funding will make critical investments to strengthen rural healthcare, expand access to lifesaving services, and bring modern technology to communities across Ohio.
“These investments will transform healthcare in rural Ohio,” said Gov. Mike DeWine. “We are grateful to Dr. Oz, CMS, and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services for standing up this important program and partnering with us to ensure that all Ohioans, regardless of where they live, have access to the care they need.”
“President Trump understands that every American deserves high-quality healthcare, no matter where they live,” said Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “We are putting resources directly into rural communities to strengthen the health workforce, modernize infrastructure, expand access, and bring care closer to home. We are giving states the flexibility to build solutions around the people they serve, while demanding accountability for results. That is how we strengthen rural health, improve the lives of patients and families, and Make America Healthy Again.”
“President Trump gave states the resources to transform rural healthcare, and now we’re seeing those dollars move from plans into action,” said Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “Our focus now is on making sure this early progress translates into lasting results for rural patients and more resilient, sustainable health systems in the years ahead. In Ohio, that means rural hospitals are joining coordinated networks and upgrading equipment to bring services like on-site MRI and behavioral healthcare closer to home.”
Today’s investment was made possible through the Working Families Tax Cuts Act — passed by Republicans in Congress and unanimously opposed by Democrats — delivering a historic $50 billion investment to help states transform the way healthcare is delivered in America.
“Despite historic obstruction by DC Democrats, President Trump made a historic pledge to rural America. These investments are converting that pledge into improved care for Ohioans. The Rural Health Transformation Fund prioritizes patients and broadens access to healthcare for the hardworking Americans who call these places home. Ohioans should remember that including every single Democrat Member of Congress voted against the creation of this transformational effort and worked to repeal it. Republicans always will stand with rural Ohio,” said Sen. Bernie Moreno.
“Ohioans living in rural communities deserve access to high-quality health care close to home. That’s why I fought for this provision in the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, which makes historic investments in rural health care. This $92 million in funding will help strengthen rural health care, expand maternal and behavioral health services and improve access to care for Ohio families, no matter their zip code,” said Sen. Jon Husted.
“For too long, rural Buckeye families have had to travel too far and wait too long to receive the critical healthcare they depend on,” said Rep. Dave Taylor. “Thanks to President Trump’s historic investment in rural Appalachia, Ohio families will have better access to high-quality, reliable care. I was proud to vote for the Working Families Tax Cut, which delivers this investment and puts accessible care within reach for those who need it most.”
“I’m pleased to receive word that the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services are announcing $92 million for rural healthcare in Ohio. Rural hospitals serve an integral role in the health and well-being of so many lives throughout Ohio’s Fifth Congressional District. This funding that will go toward enhancing behavioral health services, expanding maternal care, and several other initiatives will help Ohio families have access to the care they need closer to home. We must continue to support our rural providers who are devoted to keeping our communities healthy,” said Rep. Bob Latta.
“Ohio’s rural communities deserve access to high-quality healthcare without having to travel hours to get it. This $92 million investment will strengthen rural hospitals, expand behavioral and maternal care, and help ensure families across Ohio can get the care they need close to home. I’m proud to support President Trump and CMS as they continue delivering real results for rural Ohio,” said Rep. Michael Rulli.
“Health care works best when it stays local, with doctors and nurses who know their patients better than anyone,” said Rep. Warren Davidson. “This $92 million investment, made possible by the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, equips Ohio’s rural providers to add services, partner with one another, and expand the treatments they offer. That support gives families in small-town Ohio more options for quality care in their own communities.”
“Access to quality healthcare should not depend on where you live. This $92 million investment will strengthen rural hospitals, expand maternal and behavioral healthcare services, and help ensure Ohio families have access to the care they need in their own communities,” said Rep. Michael Turner.
“Congress took action through the Working Families Tax Cuts to strengthen rural health care by creating the Rural Health Transformation Program. This $92 million investment will help Ohio’s rural providers deliver better care and improve health outcomes for my constituents and families across the state. With this funding, we’re making sure every Ohioan has access to quality health care, no matter where they live,” said Rep. Troy Balderson.
“I believe every Ohioan deserves access to quality, affordable healthcare, and the Rural Health Transformation Program is helping bring that care closer to home for families across Ohio’s 14th Congressional District,” said Rep. Dave Joyce. “I appreciate the Trump Administration’s commitment to expanding healthcare opportunities in rural communities and directing resources where they can make a meaningful difference. This investment will expand access to maternal care, while also helping local providers improve how they deliver care and better meet the needs of the patients and families who rely on them.”
Today’s announcement is one part of the larger overall funding amount awarded to Ohio for fiscal year 2026.
Key initiatives the overall RHTP funding will focus on include:
- Building the rural healthcare workforce: Supporting recruitment, training, and retention strategies to strengthen the pipeline of healthcare professionals serving rural communities.
- Strengthening rural facilities and access: Supporting partnerships, operational improvements, and care-delivery changes that help rural providers maintain essential services and improve access.
- Advancing innovative care and payment models: Supporting new approaches to delivery and financing designed to improve quality, strengthen primary care, and support sustainable rural healthcare.
- Expanding community-based and preventive care: Investing in school-based care, mobile services, and other community strategies that improve prevention, address chronic disease, and expand access to care.
- Modernizing rural healthcare technology: Expanding remote care and data-driven tools to improve coordination and extend healthcare services to rural communities.
The Trump Administration is delivering on its commitment to strengthen rural America by investing in solutions that modernize technology to promote health and well-being for rural communities. Led by CMS, the RHTP is moving beyond the failed one-size-fits-all approach and giving rural communities the tools to build stronger, more innovative, and more sustainable health systems that deliver better care and better outcomes for the Americans they serve.
For more information about the RHTP, visit: https://www.medicaid.gov/resources-for-states/rural-health.

Tallahassee, Florida – Mario Swanston, 45, of Miami, Florida; Santana Wyvonne Harris, 41, of Panama City, Florida; Shannon Jarbar Clayton, 46, of Panama City, Florida; Elizabeth Gray, 37, of Panama City, Florida; and Shontell Fedd, 49, of Panama City, Florida were each sentenced by U.S. District Judge Mark E. Walker in federal court after previously pleading guilty to conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute cocaine and marijuana. Swanston and Harris pleaded guilty to an additional count of possession with intent to distribute cocaine. The sentences were announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida.

U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “This successful prosecution was made possible by the whole-of-government commitment under the Homeland Security Task Force to eradicate criminal organizations operating within the United States, and my office will continue to aggressively prosecute these cases and advocate for substantial punishments to be imposed against the offenders who have victimized our communities. Our citizens deserve to live on safe, drug-free streets, and my office will fight hard every day to fulfill that promise.”

According to court records, between November 21, 2023, and April 25, 2024, Mario Swanston conspired with his co-defendants, and others, to distribute controlled substances, including cocaine and marijuana. As part of the conspiracy, Swanston obtained cocaine and marijuana from California and Georgia. Swanston utilized drug couriers—namely Harris, Gray, and Fedd -to store and transport the drugs on his behalf. Swanston was responsible for over 1,700 grams of cocaine and over 550 pounds of marijuana.

U.S. District Judge Mark E. Walker sentenced Swanston to five years’ imprisonment, and imposed sentences of federal supervised release on Harris (4 years), Clayton (3 years), Gray (3 years), and Fedd (2 years).

“I’m proud of our agents and Homeland Security Task Force partners for stopping this drug trafficking organization,” said DEA Special Agent in Charge Daniel Escobar, Tampa Field Division. “Cocaine is commonly trafficked in North Florida, and our agents will remain vigilant in the fight to keep this out of our communities.”

The conviction and sentences were the result of a joint investigation by the Drug Enforcement Administration, Homeland Security Investigations, U.S. Marshals Service, Bay County Sheriff’s Office, the Gulf County Sheriff’s Office, Florida Department of Law Enforcement, Florida Highway Patrol, Panama City Police Department, Panama City Beach Police Department, and Springfield Police Department. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Joseph A. Ravelo.

This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF comprises agents and officers from multiple agencies with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida.

The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl .
title: Panama City Drug Trafficking Organization Dismantled by Homeland Security Task Force Prosecution

WASHINGTON, DC (October 16, 2026) – Orice W. Brown, Acting Comptroller General of the United States and head of the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO), today announced the appointment of six new members to the Physician-Focused Payment Model Technical Advisory Committee (PTAC).
Congress established PTAC in 2015 to improve how the federal Medicare program pays physicians for the care they provide to Medicare beneficiaries. This independent advisory committee makes recommendations to the Secretary of Health and Human Services on physician payment models and related topics. By law, the Comptroller General is responsible for naming new committee members. GAO takes a deliberate approach to appointments to health care advisory bodies, including extensive vetting of candidates, candidate interviews, and outreach to cognizant congressional committees to understand their priorities and needs. Appointments reflect the broad range of expertise and perspectives as required by law.
The newly appointed members are Jennifer R. Aloff, MD, FAAFP; Reshma Gupta, MD, MSHPM; Bruce S. Pyenson; Susan E. Sheridan, MIM, MBA, DHL; Sarah Szanton, PhD, RN, FAAN and Marta J. Van Beek, MD, MPH. Their terms will expire in 2029.
Brief biographies of the new committee members follow:
Jennifer R. Aloff, MD, FAAFP, is a board-certified family physician and owner of Midland Family Physicians, an independent medical practice. She also serves as Medical Director and Vice President of Physician Enterprise at VaxCare, a care delivery platform for streamlining business logistics related to vaccines and contraceptives. She further serves on the Board of Directors at Honest ACO of Michigan and Great Lakes Physician Organization and represents family physicians on the American Medical Association’s Resource-Based Relative Value Scale Update Committee. Previously, Dr. Aloff served as Medical Director for Great Lakes Physicians ACO. She received her medical degree from Michigan State University and completed herfamily medicine residency at MyMichigan Medical Center in Midland, MI.
Reshma Gupta, MD, MSHPM, is the Chief of Population Health and Accountable Care at UC Davis Health and co-leads population health strategy across the University of California health campuses. She holds over a decade of experience leading large-scale healthcare transformation across complex health systems including AI and digital integration and national payment reform initiatives. She also serves as a senior advisor to Costs of Care, a nonprofit that trains clinicians to deliver affordable, high-value health care. Previously, she served as a senior advisor to the CMS Innovation Center, where she helped design and scale payment models, advised on multi-payer alignment strategies, and led evaluations of targeted care management for complex patients. She received her medical degree from University of California, San Francisco and completed her residency in internal medicine at the University of Washington, Seattle. She also received a master’s degree in health policy and management from University of California, Los Angeles.
Bruce S. Pyenson, FSA, MAAA, is a retired actuary. Most recently, Mr. Pyenson served as a Principal and Actuary at Milliman, where he used data and actuarial science to address pressing issues in the healthcare industry. He was also appointed as a Commissioner of the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission, where he served from 2016 until 2022. In addition, he served as an adjunct clinical associate professor at New York University’s College of Global Public Health and a member of the Institute for Healthcare Delivery Science at the Mount Sinai Health System. He is also active in the International Early Lung Cancer Action Program. Mr. Pyenson received his bachelor’s degree in mathematics from Wayne State University in Detroit, MI.
Susan E. Sheridan, MIM, MBA, DHL, is the CEO and Founding Member of Patients for Patient Safety US, a non-profit organization with the goal of enhancing patient safety for all Americans. She is the co-chair of the National Academy of Medicine’s Patient Safety in the Era of AI initiative and is on the Board of Directors at the Leapfrog Group. Previously, Ms. Sheridan served as a Patient and Family Engagement Advisor at the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services and the Director of Patient Engagement at the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute. Ms. Sheridan received her master’s degree in International Management and Master of Business Administration degrees from the Thunderbird School of Global Management in Phoenix, AZ.
Sarah Szanton, PhD, RN, FAAN, is the Dean and the inaugural Patricia M. Davidson Endowed Professor for Health Equity and Social Justice at the Johns Hopkins University School of Nursing. She is also co-developer of the CAPABLE health delivery model and associated payment models. Dr. Szanton is on the editorial board of Health Affairs and the Journal of Advanced Nursing, among other journals. Previously, she served as Director for the Center for Equity in Aging and the Director of the PhD program at Johns Hopkins University School of Nursing. Dr. Szanton received her Doctor of Philosophy in Nursing from the Johns Hopkins University School of Nursing in Baltimore, MD.
Marta J. Van Beek, MD, MPH, is the Executive Medical Director for the University of Iowa Health Care Enterprise, overseeing ambulatory operations across the health care system. She also serves on the boards of the American Medical Association and the American College of Mohs Surgeons and has provided clinical expertise to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services on episode-based cost measures for non-pressure ulcers. Additionally, Dr. Van Beek was a Founding Chair for DataDerm™, a dermatology data registry. A board-certified dermatologist and Mohs micrographic surgeon, Dr. Van Beek received her medical degree and master’s degree in public health from the University of Iowa.
For more information, see the PTAC website or contact Marsha Clarke, PTAC designated federal officer, at PTAC@hhs.gov. Other inquiries should be directed to Sarah Kaczmarek, Managing Director of Public Affairs at media@gao.gov.
#####
The Government Accountability Office, known as the investigative arm of Congress, is an independent, nonpartisan agency that exists to support Congress in meeting its constitutional responsibilities. GAO also works to improve the performance of the federal government and ensure its accountability to the American people. The agency examines the use of public funds; evaluates federal programs and policies; and provides analyses, recommendations, and other assistance to help Congress make informed oversight, policy, and funding decisions. GAO provides Congress with timely information that is objective, fact-based, nonideological, fair, and balanced. GAO’s commitment to good government is reflected in its core values of accountability, integrity, and reliability.
title: Oct 16, 2026 GAO Makes 2026 PTAC Appointments

Rep. Subramanyam Issues Statement on U.S. Citizen and Marine Veteran Detained by ICE
Leesburg, VA – Today, U.S. Representative Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10) issued a statement after a social media post stated that ICE detained a U.S. citizen and Marine veteran in Loudoun County, Virginia.
Rep. Subramanyam issues the following statement:
“I am appalled by the recent ICE targeting of a U.S. citizen and Marine veteran here in Loudoun County. This is not how America should treat our veterans. Our servicemembers deserve our utmost respect, and they and their families should not be targeted by federal immigration agents. This administration said they were going to go after the worst of the worst, but instead ICE continues to target law abiding, non-violent members of our community, including American citizens.
My team and I are engaging with the individual who brought this to our attention. I am demanding a full investigation, and I will continue providing support to our community during this time. We need to end this madness. Enough is enough,” Congressman Suhas Subramanyam said.
Rep. Suhas Subramanyam previously introduced legislation to require ICE to publicly report on their enforcement actions, including the number of people detained who have criminal convictions.
Since the start of the second Trump administration, there have been at least 30 shootings involving federal immigration agents. A citizen from Prince William County who previously voted for Trump was detained by ICE while they were looking for someone else. Ms. Carolina Molina, another constituent of Rep. Subramanyam’s, had a firearm pulled on her by an ICE agent without justification. Another Northern Virginia resident was walking to work when federal immigration agents assaulted him, leading to a brain injury.
###
title: Rep. Subramanyam Issues Statement on U.S. Citizen and Marine Veteran Detained by ICE

Scott Honored as “Port Champion” by Virginia Maritime Association
NEWPORT NEWS, VA – Congressman Bobby Scott (VA-03) was honored Thursday with the Virginia Maritime Association’s (VMA) “Port Champion” Award in recognition of his longstanding leadership and advocacy for the Port of Virginia and the Commonwealth’s maritime industry. The award recognizes Congressman Scott’s efforts to secure critical federal investments in Virginia’s maritime infrastructure.
“I am honored to receive this recognition from the Virginia Maritime Association,” said Congressman Scott. “The Port of Virginia is a critical economic engine for Hampton Roads and the entire Commonwealth. I have been proud to work with my colleagues in the Virginia congressional delegation and our maritime partners to secure investments that strengthen our infrastructure, support good-paying jobs and ensure Virginia remains competitive in global trade. I look forward to continuing that partnership to support our maritime industry for generations to come.”
Full text of the resolution from the Virginia Maritime Association can be found below.
WHEREAS, the Virginia Maritime Association is privileged to have had the service of Congressman Robert “Bobby” Scott as the U.S. Representative for the Third District of the Commonwealth of Virginia since 1993, following service in the Virginia House of Delegates from 1978 to 1983 and the Senate of Virginia from 1983 to 1993, and as the first African American elected to Congress from Virginia in more than a century, and
WHEREAS, Congressman Scott chaired the Committee on Education and Labor in the 116th and 117th Congresses, served in the 114th, 115th, 118th Congresses and currently serves as the Ranking Member and serves as a member of the Committee on the Budget, and has strengthened the skilled trades our terminals and shipyards depend upon, and
WHEREAS, Congressman Scott has been a steadfast champion of ‘Wider, Deeper, Safer®’, working with the Virginia delegation to complete the Norfolk Harbor Widening and Deepening Project and give the Commonwealth the deepest commercial channels on the East Coast at fifty-five feet, and
WHEREAS, Congressman Scott has likewise championed the deepening of the Southern Branch of the Elizabeth River, on behalf of the marine terminals, shipyards, and waterfront industries whose berths depend on it, and
WHEREAS, Congressman Scott has consistently and generously supported this Association, joining our members year after year at the Annual Maritime Banquet and the Navigation Summit in a spirit of cooperation and partnership, and
WHEREAS, through these efforts, Congressman Scott has strengthened Virginia’s maritime transportation system and positioned the greater Port of Virginia and the Commonwealth as leaders in global trade,
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Virginia Maritime Association that sincere appreciation is expressed for the splendid service extended and readiness to assist the Maritime Industry as a “Port Champion” promoting, protecting, and encouraging Virginia’s ports.
IN TESTIMONY WHEREOF, witness by these signatures this fifteenth day of October 2026 and the seal of the Association.

The U.S. Army Aviation and Missile Command showcased future capabilities of its organic industrial base Oct. 12-14 during the Association of the U.S. Army Annual Meeting and Exposition through a joint kiosk with its two depots, Corpus Christi Army Depot and Letterkenny Army Depot.
The theme of the combined exhibit was "From Depot to Tactical Edge: How Technology Innovation and Artificial Intelligence are Delivering New Ways to Sustain an Expeditionary Global Force." The display demonstrated how the organizations use advanced manufacturing, digital scanning and data-driven systems to modernize Army organic sustainment support for an expeditionary, globally deployed force.
Exhibition technologies focused on modernizing the Army's Organic Industrial Base to extend depot-level technical capability directly to forward-deployed units. Featured capabilities included blue-light optical scanning for digital component inspection, advanced manufacturing and 3D printing for urgent and obsolete parts, nondestructive inspection techniques to detect structural defects early, and artificial intelligence-driven analytics dashboards to accelerate maintenance decision-making.
"The Organic Industrial Base is a strategic bedrock of warfighter readiness," said Ric Rincon, an AMCOM representative. "Integrating technologies like those exhibited at AUSA bridges the distance between industrial production and tactical units. We are reducing maintenance turnaround time, getting vital aviation and missile defense assets back into the fight faster."
Col. Caleb Lewis, commander of Letterkenny Army Depot, stressed that integrating technology into expeditionary operations is vital to contested logistics and sustained operational readiness.
"Modernizing our industrial base is about transforming how the military generates and sustains combat power," Lewis said. "As an example, the Dragon Fly (Cold Spray) on display at the kiosk allows for the expeditionary sustainment of critical Army and joint force systems, serving to minimize equipment downtime, reduce asset retrograde rates and preserve Army buying power."
The exhibition team included leadership and subject-matter experts from across AMCOM, CCAD and LEAD: Rincon; Josh Wigley, Lori Bonincontri and Mike Bonincontri of CCAD; and Lewis, Jessica Irving and Junie Arcega of LEAD. Together, they presented organic industrial base integrated sustainment solutions to military leaders, industry partners and allied defense representatives.
title: AMCOM, CCAD, LEAD showcase depot capabilities at AUSA

Somerset Lifesciences Inc. Agrees to Pay $4M to Resolve Allegations of Causing Medicare to Pay Claims for its Mislabeled Generic Drug
Somerset Lifesciences Inc. (Somerset) has agreed to pay $4 million to resolve common law claims for causing Medicare Part D (Medicare) to pay for its prescription-only (Rx-only) generic drug Olopatadine when it was no longer eligible for Medicare coverage. Medicare does not cover drugs that can be purchased by retail customers over-the-counter (OTC) without a prescription. In 2020, the brand name version of Olopatadine switched from Rx-only to OTC, and Somerset was required to change Olopatadine’s label from Rx-only to OTC as well. Instead, Somerset continued to label and sell Olopatadine as Rx-only and caused Medicare to wrongfully pay claims for an OTC drug.
“Today’s resolution underscores the Department’s commitment to safeguarding federal healthcare programs,” said Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate of the Justice Department’s Civil Division. “When companies cause Medicare to pay for products that are not eligible for coverage, the Department will act decisively to remedy that misconduct.”
Olopatadine (olopatadine hydrochloride ophthalmic solution USP, 0.1%) is the generic drug version of the brand name eyedrop Pataday Twice Daily Relief (olopatadine hydrochloride) ophthalmic solution, 0.1% (Pataday). Before February 2020, Pataday and Olopatadine were covered by Medicare and only available with a prescription. In February 2020, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved the sale of Pataday OTC. Generally, a generic drug’s label must mirror the label for its brand name drug. When Pataday’s label switched from Rx-only to OTC, Somerset was required to change Olopatadine’s label to OTC as well. Somerset, however, did not and continued to label and sell Olopatadine as Rx-only. By continuing to label and sell Olopatadine as Rx-only, Somerset caused Medicare to pay for Olopatadine claims by mistake. This action unjustly enriched Somerset.
This year the Administration launched the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud and the National Fraud Enforcement Division to enhance the administration’s war on fraud, waste, and abuse in federal programs. When unscrupulous actors exploit these programs for their own financial gain, they defraud the government, harm the people these programs are designed to aid and protect, and undermine American businesses that play by the rules. The Civil Division’s False Claims Act (FCA) enforcement plays a critical role in combatting such fraudulent schemes, recovering billions of dollars for the American taxpayers, and holding wrongdoers accountable. FCA matters will continue to be on the forefront of the battle against fraud, and the Civil Division’s FCA work will support and advance the mission of the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud and the National Fraud Enforcement Division.
The investigation and resolution of this matter illustrate the government’s emphasis on combating healthcare fraud. One of the most powerful tools in this effort is the FCA. Tips and complaints from all sources about potential fraud, waste, abuse, and mismanagement, can be reported to the Department of Health and Human Services at 800-HHS-TIPS (800-447-8477).
This matter is being handled by Fraud Section Trial Attorney Vince Vaccarella.
Except for the admissions contained in the settlement agreement, the claims resolved by the settlement are allegations only and there has been no determination of liability.
Press Release Number: 26-1215
title: Somerset Lifesciences Inc. Agrees to Pay $4M to Resolve Allegations of Causing Medicare to Pay Claims for its Mislabeled Generic Drug

Congresswoman Luz Rivas Joins Colleagues for Unannounced Oversight Visit at Adelanto, Raises Concerns About Inhumane Conditions
Adelanto, California — Congresswoman Luz Rivas (CA-29), representative for California’s 29th Congressional District, conducted an unannounced Congressional oversight visit of the Adelanto ICE Detention Center with her colleagues, Representatives Robert Garcia (CA-42), Judy Chu (CA-28), Norma Torres (CA-35), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), Dave Min (CA-47), and Derek Tran (CA-45). This is the first congressional oversight visit to the Adelanto ICE Detention Center since it was purchased by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) in October. The Members investigated conditions at the facility, including reports of contaminated drinking water, mold and maggots in showers, lack of access to recreation, and significant delays in visitation.
“My colleagues and I performed our congressional oversight duties to investigate the Adelanto ICE Detention Center and the serious allegations of abuse and inhumane conditions,” said Congresswoman Rivas. “We hoped to speak with detainees about their experiences and the conditions at the facility, but when we were shown the common areas, it looked as if ICE rushed the detainees back to their cells. In addition to the common areas, we were also showed the kitchen and bathrooms, where my colleagues noticed mold and food that looked inedible. ICE agents also continued to spread Trump’s anti-immigrant rhetoric that demonizes the nearly 1,800 detainees at Adelanto.”
In October, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) purchased Adelanto from the GEO Group in an attempt to evade state and local oversight. This purchase occurred after Governor Gavin Newsom signed more than 20 bills aimed at pushing back against the Trump Administration’s immigration agenda.
Congresswoman Rivas continued: “At a time when our constituents are demanding answers and accountability, ICE is being increasingly secretive about their actions at Adelanto – similar to what my colleagues and I witnessed at the Dilley Immigration Processing Center in Texas. DHS and ICE cannot buy their way out of being held accountable for the terror they are causing in our communities. My colleagues and I will continue showing up at detention centers to hold this Administration accountable and stand up for our constituents.”
Background:
Congresswoman Luz Rivas has conducted eight oversight visits at immigration detention facilities in California and Texas, including at the Edward R. Roybal Federal Building, the Adelanto Detention Facility, the California City Detention Facility, and the Dilley Immigration Processing Center. ICE blocked Congresswoman Rivas from conducting oversight of detention facilities three times: Once at the Edward R. Roybal Federal Building and twice at the Adelanto Detention Facility.
Congresswoman Rivas has also sent six letters to ICE leadership calling for accountability into the conditions at detention centers and for transparency for detainees. In addition, she joined her colleagues for field hearings into ICE abuses in Los Angeles and Minneapolis-St. Paul.
In October, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) purchased two immigrant detention facilities in Adelanto for $950 million from the GEO group. The purchase of facilities is an attempt by DHS to avoid being held accountable to California’s laws pushing back on the Trump Administration’s immigration agenda.
###
title: Congresswoman Luz Rivas Joins Colleagues for Unannounced Oversight Visit at Adelanto, Raises Concerns About Inhumane Conditions

Rep. Panetta’s Statement on Suspicious Envelope Sent to and Opened by His Santa Cruz District Office
Santa Cruz, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) issued the following statement after an envelope containing a white powdery substance was received and opened by a staffer at his Santa Cruz district office this morning:
“An envelope containing a suspicious white powder was delivered to my Santa Cruz district office and opened by staff this morning as part of her normal daily morning routine responding to constituents. Upon realizing that there was powder in the envelope, she immediately put the envelope in the garbage can, cleared fellow staff members out of the office, and called 911.
“My priority is the safety and security of my staff and, thankfully, she and the other staff have been initially cleared by medical officials.
“I’m grateful to local law enforcement and first responders for their swift response.
“Threats, fearmongering, and violence against public servants have become far too common over the past decade and undermine our democracy.
“But these attempts to intimidate us will not deter us from doing our job. Despite these difficult circumstances, we remain committed to our democracy by continuing our service to the people of California’s 19th Congressional District.”
###
title: Rep. Panetta’s Statement on Suspicious Envelope Sent to and Opened by His Santa Cruz District Office

text:
Amo Leads Colleagues in Calling on State Department and CDC to Investigate the Death of a Russian Plague Laboratory Worker
Questions remain unanswered after the death of a Russian researcher who worked at a remote anti-plague facility
Providence, RI – TODAY, Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI) led 6 colleagues in calling on Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Centers for Disease Control (CDC) Director Erica Schwartz to take swift action in response to the death of the Russian laboratory worker at the Irkutsk Research Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East from a “pneumonia of undetermined origin.”
The lawmakers write:
“We urge you to take swift and thorough action in response to the death of the laboratory worker at the Irkutsk Research Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East, including investigation and surveillance to understand the possible spread of infection. Conflicting reports regarding the cause of death, the quarantine of individuals who may have been exposed, and the institute’s work with plague and other dangerous pathogens warrant scrutiny by the United States government.”
“We are increasingly alarmed that President Donald Trump’s dangerous decision to withdraw the U.S. from the World Health Organization (WHO) has made it more difficult for the U.S. to receive information from Russia and coordinate with our international partners in responding to this incident.”
“Infectious diseases do not stop at borders, and fear and inaction from uncertainty can itself become a public-health risk. The State Department and the CDC must act now to get the facts, use every available channel to assess the threat, prepare the United States for any potential spread, and keep Congress and the American people informed.”
The full letter can be found here.
The letter was signed by Representative Gabe Amo (D-RI-01), Jasmine Crockett (D-TX-30), William Keating (D-MA-09), Stephen Lynch (D-MA-08), Seth Moulton (D-MA-06), Mike Quigley (D-IL-05), and Dina Titus (D-NV-01).
Background
As Vice-Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Congressman Amo has consistently fought to protect American global health programs, save lives abroad, and keep Americans healthy and safe.
In August, Congressman Amoled 137 Members of Congress in a letter demanding that the Trump administration release international affairs funding, including Global Health Programs funding, before its expiration and stop proposed changes to the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR).
In July, Amoled a Democratic effort on the House floor to stop Trump’s dangerous disinvestment in diplomacy and global health in the National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act of 2027.
In June, Congressman Amoled 76 colleagues in a letter demanding answers about delays in detecting and responding to the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda after the Trump administration reduced global health funding, staffing, and internal coordination.

WHEELER ARMY AIRFIELD, Hawaii – A military jury convicted an Army private for sexually assaulting another Soldier during a trial held Sept. 21-25 at the Wheeler Army Airfield Courtroom.
Pvt. Alpha M. Diallo, 27, a water treatment specialist assigned to the 524th Division Sustainment Support Battalion, 25th Division Sustainment Brigade, 25th Infantry Division, Schofield Barracks, Hawaii, was sentenced by the military judge to 17 months of confinement, reduction in rank to E-1, and a dishonorable discharge from the Army.
On April 20, 2025, at Schofield Barracks, Diallo drove to the unit’s barracks for a barbecue after being invited by the victim, a fellow Soldier. She had just completed Basic Combat Training and Advanced Individual Training and had recently arrived in Hawaii for her first assignment in the Army.
After he arrived, Diallo refused to get out of his vehicle, so the victim went over to his car to talk to him. Without warning, Diallo drove away from the party with the victim in the car. Frightened, the victim texted her friends “help.” He parked the car in a secluded parking lot and sexually assaulted her despite her telling him “no” multiple times.
The victim’s friends found Diallo’s car by using the “Find My” iPhone app because the victim had shared her location with her friends prior to the incident. Once they arrived, the assault stopped, and the victim quickly jumped out of the car and told them what happened. That evening, she reported the assault to the Department of the Army Criminal Investigation Division.
“The survivor in this case demonstrated tremendous courage in coming forward and trusting the justice process. This conviction demonstrates the Army’s commitment to holding those who commit sexual assault accountable,” said Capt. Matthew McCoy, prosecutor, Seventh Circuit, Army Office of Special Trial Counsel. “Hearing her speak about her determination not to let this traumatic experience define her Army career was truly powerful. Her courage and strength are an example of what it means to persevere.”
“The burden of safety does not rest on a Soldier’s ability to signal for help or track a location—it rests on individuals respecting boundaries and the word ‘no,’” said Special Agent in Charge Michael DeFamio, Army CID’s Asia Pacific Field Office. “The sole responsibility for this crime lies with Diallo, who was invited to the barracks barbecue by the victim only to weaponize that hospitality and trust into an act of predatory assault.”
“This court-martial was about ensuring the survivor’s voice is heard and her experience is treated with the seriousness and dignity it deserves,” said Capt. Kristen Coppock, prosecutor, Office of the Staff Judge Advocate, 25th Infantry Division. “The survivor is a service member much like the accused in this case, and to experience a sexual assault at the hands of a fellow service member can profoundly violate the trust in the system. Today’s verdict rebuilds that trust.”
Diallo is currently confined at the Navy’s Pearl Harbor Brig awaiting orders to transfer to another military corrections facility. Upon release from prison, he will be required to register as a sex offender under federal and state statutory requirements.
This case was investigated by Army CID’s Asia-Pacific Field Office and prosecuted by McCoy and Coppock.
About the Army Office of Special Trial Counsel:
The Army Office of Special Trial Counsel is composed of specially trained military lawyers, legal professionals and support staff responsible for the expert prosecution of murder, sexual assault, domestic violence, child abuse, kidnapping and other serious criminal offenses. Headquartered at Fort Belvoir, Va., OSTC has eight regional headquarters that oversee 28 field offices located worldwide, including locations in Europe and Korea. For more information visit www.army.mil/ostc.
To Report a Crime:
If you would like to report a crime, have information about a crime, or have been the subject or survivor of a crime, you can submit anonymous tips to Army CID at www.p3tips.com/armycid.
title: Schofield Barracks Soldier Convicted of Sexual Assault

NEWARK, N.J. – A North Carolina man admitted to producing child pornography in a foreign country and transporting it into the United States, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced.

Barry Grant BeVier, 63, formerly of Wilmington, North Carolina, pleaded guilty on October 14, 2026 before U.S. District Judge Claire C. Cecchi in Newark federal court to an Information charging him with one count of sexually exploiting a child outside the United States for the purpose of producing child pornography and transporting that child pornography into the United States, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Sections 2251(c) and (e).

According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court:

In November 2024, BeVier was outside of the United States and twice persuaded a child to engage in sexually explicit conduct with him by offering the child things of value including a mobile phone. BeVier filmed videos of himself engaging in the sexually explicit conduct with the child and stored the videos on his cell phone. He then took an international flight on a commercial airliner into the United States and landed at Newark Liberty International Airport while carrying his cell phone containing the videos. BeVier also agreed as part of his plea to acknowledge that in November 2024 he produced child pornography involving one additional child.

The charge of sexually exploiting a child outside the United States for the purpose of producing child pornography and transporting child pornography into the United States carries a mandatory minimum term of 15 years imprisonment and a maximum term of 30 years imprisonment, and a fine of $250,000. Sentencing is scheduled for February 17, 2027.

U.S. Attorney Frazer credited special agents of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Michael S. McCarthy and officers from Customs and Border Protection (CBP), under the direction of New York Director of Field Operation Frank Russo, with the investigation leading to the guilty plea.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS) in the Justice Department’s Criminal Division, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit: https://www.justice.gov/psc .

The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorney Trevor A. Chenoweth of the Cybercrime Unit in Newark.

Acting United States Attorney Héctor Ramírez Carbó announced the creation of the Puerto Rico Interagency Fraud Enforcement Task Force, bringing together federal law enforcement agencies, state partners, and inspectors general to strengthen efforts to identify, investigate, and prosecute fraud against government programs and American taxpayers.
The U.S. Attorney’s Office hosted the first task force meeting on Thursday, October 15, attended by federal prosecutors and representatives from participating agencies. The meeting focused on establishing an all-hands approach to investigations and prosecutions, expanding intelligence and data sharing, discussing efficient methods for identifying fraud schemes, analysis of investigative leads, and ensuring law enforcement resources are directed toward significant fraud schemes.
“Fraud targeting federal government programs steals from taxpayers and deprives intended recipients of essential resources, weakening the impact of programs meant to serve the public,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Héctor Ramírez Carbó. “Our office—working alongside our federal, state, and local partners—will apply every criminal, civil, and administrative tool at our disposal to uncover fraud, stop it, and hold offenders accountable for the harm they cause.”
The agencies joining the Puerto Rico Interagency Fraud Enforcement Task Force include:
- Federal Bureau of Investigation
- Homeland Security Investigations
- U.S. Secret Service
- Drug Enforcement Administration
- Office of Inspectors General:
  - IRS Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI)
  - U.S. Postal Inspection Service (USPIS)
  - U.S. Postal Service Office of Inspector General (USPS-OIG)
  - U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG)
  - U.S. Small Business Administration Office of Inspector General (SBA-OIG)
  - U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development Office of Inspector General (HUD-OIG)
  - U.S. Department of Education Office of Inspector General (Education-OIG)
  - U.S. Department of Labor Office of Inspector General (DOL-OIG)
  - U. S. Department of Agriculture Office of Inspector General (USDA-OIG)
  - Social Security Administration Office of Inspector General (SSA-OIG)
  - Veterans Affairs, Office of Inspector General (VA-OIG)
  - Department of the Army Criminal Investigation Division (Army CID)
- State Partners
  - Puerto Rico Department of Justice (PRDOJ)
  - PRDOJ – Medicaid Fraud Control Unit (MFCU)
  - Puerto Rico Inspector General
The Puerto Rico Interagency Fraud Enforcement Task Force employs an all‑hands approach and leverages expertise across various federal programs to advance the Department of Justice’s priorities and initiatives. Its mission is to deter fraud, waste, and abuse of federal funds, safeguard taxpayer dollars, and ensure that federal programs reach their intended recipients.
Partner agencies will invest all available resources to jointly investigate and prosecute anyone who steals from the American public.
These efforts support the U.S. Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative, and creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”), to enhance coordination among federal agencies and strengthen the government’s ability to detect and prosecute fraud.
Federal prosecutors and representatives of federal law enforcement agencies, state partners, and inspectors general in the Puerto Rico Interagency Fraud Enforcement Task Force attended the October 15, 2026, meeting at the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Puerto Rico.
title: U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Puerto Rico Announces Creation of the Interagency Fraud Enforcement Task Force

Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Dismantles Drug Trafficking Network in Southeast Louisiana
DEA New Orleans Field Division SAC John P. Scott speaks at a press conference hosted by the United States Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of Louisiana on Friday, October 16, 2026.
NEW ORLEANS – Today, U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle, along with the federal, state and local participating agencies comprising the Homeland Security Task Force – New Orleans (“HSTF”), announced the successful conclusion of a nearly four-year, extensive multi-agency narcotics investigation that dismantled multiple drug trafficking organizations operating throughout the Bayou Region. This investigation led to numerous federal indictments, state arrests, substantial prison sentences, as well as the seizure of significant quantities of illegal narcotics, firearms, and criminal assets.
The investigation was led by the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and supported by several federal, state, and local law enforcement partners. A Thibodaux Police Department Narcotics Agent, assigned to the DEA Task Force as a Task Force Officer within the Eastern District of Louisiana Financial Investigations Unit, led the investigation.
As a result of the exhaustive investigative work, intelligence gathering, surveillance operations, financial investigations, and inter-agency coordination, investigators identified and targeted individuals who were distributing dangerous narcotics throughout Thibodaux, Louisiana, Lafourche Parish, and the surrounding communities.
“Today’s Homeland Security Task Force operation announcements are, at their core, about one thing …protecting our communities from the very real threat of violence posed by drug trafficking organizations,” said U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle. “Our shared mission today has remained constant; to enforce the laws of the land and to protect the public that we are proud to serve.”
As a result of this investigation, 20 individuals were federally indicted for narcotics, firearms, conspiracy, and related offenses. Additionally, 18 other individuals were arrested and prosecuted through state court proceedings.
Collectively, the defendants prosecuted, both federally and by the state, have received sentences totaling more than 300 years of imprisonment. And, several defendants are still awaiting final sentencing or adjudication. Additional prison terms may be imposed as the remaining cases proceed through the judicial process.
Specifically, this investigation resulted in the seizure of approximately:
• 46,909.33 grams of crystal methamphetamine (more than 100 pounds)
• 178.6 grams of heroin/fentanyl
• 1,414.1 grams of cocaine (more than 3 pounds)
• 3,044.1 grams of marijuana (more than 6.5 pounds)
• More than $190,000 in seized assets
• Eleven firearms, including eight pistols and three rifles
“This investigation began on the ground with our local police officers and deputies, and as the network unraveled, we expanded it into a full Homeland Security Task Force operation,” said Special Agent in Charge John P. Scott of the Drug Enforcement Administration’s New Orleans Field Division. “There is often a misconception that federal resources are reserved only for major metropolitan areas. This case proves otherwise. The full weight and reach of the federal government extends directly into our rural communities and parish neighborhoods. Through the HSTF, we brought every federal, state, and local tool to bear – not just to make arrests, but to build rock-solid cases that resulted in real, long-term prosecutions.”
“This investigation was not simply about removing drugs from our streets,” said Chief Zeringue. “It was about identifying and dismantling the individuals and organizations responsible for supplying and distributing these dangerous narcotics throughout our region. Every arrest made, every firearm seized, every dollar taken away from illegal drug trafficking, and every major distributor removed from operation, represents a safer community for the citizens of Thibodaux and the Bayou Region. The success of this investigation is a direct reflection of the cooperation, professionalism, and commitment shared by our federal, state, and local law enforcement partners. No single agency can effectively combat large-scale narcotics trafficking alone. These cases require teamwork, shared intelligence, persistence, and the ability to work together toward one common goal: making our communities safer.”
“This investigation demonstrates what can be accomplished when law enforcement agencies at every level unite to achieve a goal,” said Lafourche Parish Sheriff Craig Webre. “By working together, we have not only removed dangerous drugs and firearms from our streets but also disrupted criminal organizations that threaten the safety and well-being of our communities. I commend the dedication and perseverance of every agency involved, and I want the people of Lafourche Parish to know that we will remain relentless in our efforts to combat drug trafficking and keep our communities safe.”
“Dangerous drugs destroy lives, tear families apart, and threaten the safety of our communities,” said Colonel Frank Besson, Louisiana State Police Superintendent. “Through strong law enforcement partnerships, Louisiana State Police remains committed to dismantling organized criminal networks across Louisiana, from our largest cities to our smallest towns. Those who profit from trafficking dangerous drugs should understand that no matter where they operate, we will continue working alongside our partners to bring them to justice.”
“I would like to thank all of our federal, state and local law enforcement partners,” said Terrebonne Parish Sheriff Timothy Soignet. “It genuinely takes a team of professionals to achieve public safety for all citizens.”
PARTICIPATING AGENCIES

• Thibodaux Police Department

FEDERAL DEFENDANTS (20)
Delvin Edmond a/k/a "Maman" – Convicted of methamphetamine and fentanyl trafficking offenses. Sentenced to 262 months in prison.
John Paul Gage Jr. a/k/a "JP" and "Pistol" – Pleaded guilty to conspiracy to distribute cocaine and methamphetamine and illegal use of a communication facility. Sentenced to 262 months in prison.

In Louisiana State Court, 18 additional defendants have been prosecuted as result of this operation in Terrebonne and Lafourche Parishes.
These matters were investigated by the United States Drug Enforcement Administration, the Thibodaux Police Department, the Louisiana State Police, the Lafourche Parish Sheriff’s Department, and the Terrebonne Parish Sheriff’s Department, with assistance from the St. Charles Parish Sheriff's Office, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, Homeland Security Investigations, the Jefferson Parish Sheriff's Office, and the Assumption Parish Sheriff's Office. The defendants were prosecuted by AUSA Stuart Theriot of the Violent Crime Unit, AUSA Briana Williams of the Narcotics Unit, and AUSA Senior Litigation Counsel, Maurice E. Landrieu. The state cases were prosecuted by the Terrebonne and Lafourche Parish District Attorney’s Offices.
These cases were brought pursuant to the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF New Orleans comprises agents and officers from the Department of Homeland Security, Federal Bureau of Investigations, Drug Enforcement Administration and Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, Enforcement and Removal Operations, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Office of Field Operations, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, U.S. Border Patrol, U.S. Coast Guard, Coast Guard Investigative Service. State and local agencies include the Louisiana State Police, Thibodaux Police Department, Lafourche Parish Sheriff's Office, Terrebonne Parish Sheriff's Office, St. Charles Parish Sheriff's Office, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Louisiana.
An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

CAMDEN, N.J. – A Philadelphia man was convicted on October 15, 2026, for his role in stealing $2 million from a Glassboro business and laundering the proceeds of his theft, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced.

Ruben Cruz, 33, of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and Davenport, Florida, was convicted of one count of conspiracy to transport stolen property across state lines, one count of interstate transportation of stolen property, one count of conspiracy to launder money, and seven counts of money laundering. Cruz was convicted following a three-day trial before U.S. District Judge Christine P. O’Hearn in Camden federal court. Sentencing is set for February 24, 2027.

According to court documents and evidence presented at trial:

Over the 2021 July 4 th holiday weekend, Cruz and co-conspirator Ricky Rivas-Ortiz burglarized a Glassboro business, stealing a safe that contained more than $2 million in money orders and cash and taking it to Philadelphia. After the burglary, Cruz and another co-conspirator negotiated money orders from the stolen safe in a manner designed to conceal that they were stolen. One method they used to launder the proceeds was altering the stolen money orders and depositing them in piecemeal fashion. For example, Cruz deposited some of the stolen money orders on the same day at different banks that were next door to each other and deposited other stolen money orders at the same bank branch over several consecutive days.

Rivas-Ortiz previously pleaded guilty to an information charging him with transporting stolen property interstate and was sentenced by U.S. District Judge Christine P. O’Hearn to 21 months’ imprisonment.

For Cruz, the count of conspiracy to transport stolen property interstate carries a maximum penalty of 5 years in prison and a fine of up to $250,000, or twice the gross loss to the victim or gain to the defendant, whichever is greatest. The count of interstate transportation of stolen property carries a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison and a fine of up to $250,000, or twice the gross loss to the victim or gain to the defendant, whichever is greatest. The count of conspiracy to launder money and each money laundering count carry a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison and a fine of up to $500,000, or twice the value of the laundered money, whichever is greatest.

U.S. Attorney Frazer credited postal inspectors of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Philadelphia Division, under the direction of Inspector in Charge Christopher A. Nielsen, and agents of the Internal Revenue Service – Criminal Investigation, Newark Field Office, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Jenifer L. Piovesan, with the investigation leading to the convictions. He also thanked the Gloucester County Prosecutor’s Office, under the direction of Prosecutor Andrew B. Johns, and the Elk Township Police Department, under the direction of Chief Lance Hitzelberger, for their valuable assistance in the case.

The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Jeffrey Bender and Joseph McFarlane of the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Camden.

26-225 ###

Defense counsel: Brian O’Malley, Haddon Township, New Jersey.
title: Philadelphia Man Convicted for his Role in a $2 Million Theft
