Livorno to demolish historic waterfront kiosks in 2027 – October 16, Il Tirreno
LIVORNO — Livorno authorities plan to demolish the remaining historic wooden kiosks along the city’s waterfront following the summer tourist season in 2027, according to public works official Federico Mirabelli. The restructuring initiative is valued at $1.4 million. While the city initially envisioned rebuilding three separate structures across the local piazze, officials currently intend to construct only a single new glass kiosk in front of Scoglio della Regina due to budget constraints. The landscape commission is reviewing the technical and economic feasibility plan before it goes to the city council for formal approval and public bidding. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Santuario di Montenero removes historic ex-voto offerings for gallery restoration – October 16, Il Tirreno
LIVORNO — Officials at the Santuario di Montenero in Livorno have temporarily removed thousands of historic ex-voto offerings from the walls to begin a much-needed gallery renovation project. Valentina Campedrer, coordinator for the diocesan cultural heritage office, announced that workers finished clearing the walls on Oct. 14. The Diocese of Livorno estimates the collection includes roughly 12,000 items detailing centuries of personal and local history. The renovation, valued at 200,000 euros, aims to conclude by the end of 2026, after which the cataloged and cleaned offerings will be carefully restored to their traditional places. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Italy plans €900 million military contract for C-130J fleet support – October 16, Il Tirreno
PISA — The Italian Ministry of Defense is reviewing a projected €900 million support program for its C-130J transport aircraft fleet, operating between military bases in Pisa and Sigonella from Aug. 1, 2027-July 31, 2032. The contract, intended to ensure fleet efficiency through 7,500 annual flight hours, would be negotiated directly with Lockheed Martin, Leonardo, and GE Avio without a public bidding process. Lawmaker Andrea Quartini has submitted a parliamentary inquiry questioning the massive expenditure and the transparency of the classified military missions, while local officials criticize the heavy investment amid broader social funding shortages. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Classic Vespa scooters arrive in Pisa for the Vespa in Vetrina showcase – October 16, PisaToday
PISA – Classic Vespa scooters from across Italy and abroad will gather in Pisa this weekend for the “Vespa in Vetrina – Concorso di Eleganza.” Organized by the Vespa Club Pisa, the event runs Saturday, Oct. 17, and Sunday, Oct. 18, marking the grand finale of the Italian Vespa Club’s historical sector season. Sixty-five entries are registered, featuring international participants like Eszter Bandzi from Budapest, alongside top national officials. Saturday features vehicle staging and a historic costume parade in Piazza Garibaldi starting at 2:30 p.m., while Sunday showcases a 1960s-style exhibition in Piazza dei Miracoli beginning at 9:30 a.m. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Calci hosts its 41st edition chestnut festival – October 16, PisaToday
CALCI (Pisa) – The annual Sagra della Castagna returns to Calci this weekend, running, Oct. 17- 18. Held near the town hall at Parco Sandro Pertini, the festival offers traditional local treats including roasted chestnuts, sweet fritters, necci with ricotta and castagnaccio. Visitors can enjoy live music, children’s entertainment, and the “Creatività” craft market on both days. Additionally, volunteers will host booths for the “Io non rischio” civil protection campaign in Piazza Garibaldi to share disaster prevention information. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Annual chestnut festival returns to San Giovanni alla Vena – October 16, PisaToday
SAN GIOVANNI ALLA VENA (Pisa) – The 18th annual Festa della Castagna will take place, Oct. 18 in Piazza della Repubblica at San Giovanni alla Vena. The event features top-quality chestnut specialties, roasted chestnuts, necci, and castagnaccio. Lunch is served starting at 12:30 p.m., with food booths opening at 3 p.m. The festival also collaborates with the Vespa Club Pontedera and offers a welcoming community tradition. Admission to the event is free. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
New bridge over the Scolmatore canal in Stagno opens to traffic – October 16, QuiLivorno
STAGNO (Livorno) – A new 158-meter bridge on the historic Aurelia state highway in Livorno opened to traffic Oct. 15. Built with a six-million-euro investment, the five-span structure features seismic upgrades and a steel-concrete composite deck. The project improves structural performance and eliminates expansion joints. Additionally, planning is underway for a pedestrian walkway connecting the bridge to a nearby underpass, while work on an adjacent bridge over the Imperiale canal is scheduled to begin later this year. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
New traffic restriction zone approved for Via Roma to curb night noise – October 16, QuiLivorno
LIVORNO – Livorno’s city council has approved a new limited traffic zone (ZTL) on a section of Via Roma between Via Cecconi and Via Giovanni Marradi. The restriction will run from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays to address noise pollution, traffic congestion and safety concerns during peak nightlife hours. While the days and times have been established, a subsequent ordinance from the mobility sector will detail authorized vehicles, exemptions and access rules. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Visual adventures of Pinocchio exhibition open Nov. 1 in Livorno – October 16, QuiLivorno
LIVORNO – Livorno’s City Museum at the Bottini dell'Olio will host the exhibition “Pinocchio. Le avventure visive di un burattino” from Nov. 1-Jan. 10, 2027. Celebrating the bicentennial of author Carlo Collodi, the display runs Tuesdays through Sundays from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. The exhibition features historical editions, original illustrations and works by students from the Carrara Academy of Fine Arts. Admission is €3, with free entry for visitors under 18, students, seniors over 65 and other qualifying groups. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Melograno Art Gallery hosts contemporary painting exhibition in Livorno – October 16, LivornoToday
LIVORNO – The Art Gallery Il Melograno presents “Olio, amore e fantasia, omaggio alla pittura,” a group exhibition running through Tuesday, Oct. 27. Located on Via Giovanni Marradi, the gallery celebrates contemporary artistic research, with an official opening reception scheduled for Saturday, Oct. 17, at 6 p.m. The exhibition explores the intersection of oil painting, passion, and creative freedom inspired by Mediterranean culture. Open daily from 10 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. and 4 to 8 p.m., with Sunday hours running from 10 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. and 5 to 8 p.m. (closed Monday mornings). Free admission. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Mercatino da Forte dei Marmi brings Versilia style market to Pisa – October 16, SagreToscana
PISA – The famous “Versilia style” open-air market comes to Pisa on Sunday, Oct. 18. Running all day from 8 a.m. to 7 p.m., stalls will line Lungarno Antonio Pacinotti and Lungarno Mediceo. The market features high-quality goods, including cashmere apparel and accessories; designer clothing for men and women; custom-made linens; Florentine lace tablecloths and home decor items. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Livorno’s Friday market holds special Sunday edition in Piazza della Repubblica – October 16, SagreToscana
LIVORNO – Livorno’s traditional Friday open-air market is holding a special one-day edition this Sunday, Oct. 18. Running 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. in Piazza della Repubblica, visitors can browse a wide selection of vendors offering clothing, shoes, food and much more. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Recent Italian News highlights 
Livorno ranks 10th in Italy for reported crimes according to Il Sole 24 Ore – October 13, Il Tirreno
LIVORNO — Livorno ranked 10th in Italy for total reported crimes in 2025, according to Il Sole 24 Ore’s annual crime index. The province recorded 15,037 total complaints, showing a slight decrease from the previous year. Despite an overall drop in total thefts and property damage, Livorno maintained high rankings in specific criminal categories. The province secured second place nationally for mopeds stolen, averaging over three scooter thefts every 48 hours, and ranked third for attempted murders. Meanwhile, digital fraud and robberies saw notable increases across the region. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Livorno manager helps luxury brands expand across the Americas – October 13, Il Tirreno
LIVORNO — Francesco Scuttari, a native of Livorno raised in the San Jacopo neighborhood, serves as the vice president of luxury fashion and beauty for the Americas region at DSV. Based in New York since 2011, Scuttari oversees business strategies and logistics networks for premier global fashion houses. He credits his pragmatic, direct roots from Livornese culture with helping him navigate international relationships. While managing operations and frequent international travel, he remains deeply connected to his hometown, balancing a high-profile corporate career with family life between the United States, Europe and South America. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Pisa airport unveils new arrivals terminal in €80 million upgrade – October 13, Il Tirreno
PISA — Toscana Aeroporti inaugurated the new arrivals terminal at Pisa’s Galileo Galilei Airport, marking the completion of the first phase of an 80-million-euro modernization project. The 7,100-square-foot building features solar panels and aims to separate passenger flows to accommodate surging traffic, which surpassed five million passengers in the first nine months of the year. Subsequent phases will renovate existing terminal spaces to expand departures and boarding areas, eventually increasing annual capacity to seven million passengers. The entire upgrade is scheduled for completion by 2028 while maintaining full operational continuity. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Bientina launches civic campaign to promote dog waste cleanup – October 13, PisaToday
BIENTINA (Pisa) – The municipal administration of Bientina has launched a new awareness campaign aimed at dog owners to encourage urban cleanliness and respect for public spaces. Titled “Chi raccoglie semina civiltà,” the initiative uses clear graphics and direct messaging in daily life areas to remind citizens that picking up pet waste makes streets, squares and parks cleaner and more livable for everyone. Environment Councilor Desirè Niccoli emphasized that the gesture is a simple, responsible act of civic duty. While the campaign focuses on education and collaboration, failure to comply with the local urban police regulations carries a €100 administrative fine. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Coltano officially renamed “Coltano Marconi” in honor of inventor – October 13, PisaToday
COLTANO (Pisa) – The Tuscan village of Coltano has officially been renamed "Coltano Marconi" to honor inventor Guglielmo Marconi, who established Italy’s first long-wave radiotelegraph station there in 1911. A dedication ceremony was held near the historic memorial marker with Pisa Mayor Michele Conti, local officials, and Marconi’s daughter, Princess Elettra Marconi. The municipality unveiled new brown tourism road signs, an informational lectern detailing the site’s history, and presented a commemorative plaque to the family. Conti emphasized that the initiative celebrates Pisa’s profound role in modern telecommunications and preserves the village’s international technological heritage for future generations. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Palazzo Blu hosts major Edward Hopper exhibition in Pisa – October 13, PisaToday
PISA – Palazzo Blu in Pisa is hosting a major international exhibition dedicated to Edward Hopper, one of the 20th century’s most prominent American artists, running until March 7, 2027. Organized in collaboration with New York’s Whitney Museum of American Art and MondoMostre, the retrospective features over 150 works, including oils, watercolors and etchings, alongside archival documents and contemporary pieces. Curated by Kim Conaty and Barbara Haskell, the five-section exhibition explores Hopper’s artistic evolution through the pivotal locations of his life: Paris, New York and the New England landscape, while highlighting the crucial collaborative role of his wife and muse, Jo Hopper. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Terre di Pisa Food & Wine Festival returns to Piazza Vittorio Emanuele II – October 13, SagreToscana
PISA – The autumn edition of the Terre di Pisa Food & Wine Festival will take place Oct. 16-18 in Piazza Vittorio Emanuele II, celebrating local culinary excellence and Pisan wines. More than 80 food and wine producers will offer tastings and sales during the three-day event, which features “White Art” as its main theme this year. Visitors can also enjoy cooking shows led by local chefs, tasting workshops, and children’s activities focused on healthy and delicious eating. Exhibition stands will be open Friday from 5 to 10 p.m., Saturday from 11 a.m. to 11 p.m., and Sunday from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Pariana to host annual chestnut festival in Villa Basilica – October 13, SagreToscana
PARIANA (Lucca) – The village of Pariana, in the municipality of Villa Basilica, will host its traditional Chestnut Festival on Sunday, Oct. 18. The day-long event celebrates local culinary traditions throughout the town’s squares starting at 10 a.m. Visitors can explore an artisan and local produce market alongside food stands offering roasted chestnuts, polenta with meat sauce, necci chestnut flour pancakes and mulled wine. The festival also features live music, roving street performances and dedicated activities for children. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Pontasserchio hosts third edition of “Mathildis” medieval festival – October 13, PisaToday
PONTASSERCHIO (Pisa) – The Parco della Pace in Pontasserchio will host the third edition of the “Mathildis” medieval festival on Sunday, Oct. 18 from 10 a.m.- 8 p.m. Organized by Antitesi Teatro Circo with support from the Ministry of Culture and San Giuliano Terme, the event celebrates Matilda of Tuscany, a powerful medieval leader and peacemaker. The day-long festival features historical reenactments; historic markets; ancient craft workshops; archery; siege engine displays; medieval fencing and medieval music and juggling performances by companies like La Compagnia del Coniglio and I Giullari del Corvo, alongside traditional food and taverns. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Pisa plans 12 kilometers of new bike paths – October 9, Il Tirreno
PISA — Pisa officials announced a plan to add 12 kilometers of bike paths across the city and coastline, expanding the existing 61-kilometer network. Mobility Councilor Massimo Dringoli said the projects will be completed between late 2027 and early 2028. The upcoming expansion includes extending the Trammino bike path toward Tirrenia, connecting San Piero a Grado to the university’s veterinary department, and linking urban areas like the National Research Council (CNR) and the Pungilupo Park to academic facilities. Funded through local procedures and ministry grants, the projects aim to enhance commuter and student mobility. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Pisa regional funding sparks clash over pine tree parasite – October 9, PisaToday
PISA — Tuscany and Pisa officials clashed over efforts to combat the invasive turtle scale parasite threatening local pine forests. Regional Environment Councilor David Barontini stated the region is actively responding, noting that the regional executive approved €506,986 for coordinated defense actions. Barontini’s comments came after Pisa Mayor Michele Conti urged regional authorities to step up funding for natural woodland areas. Conti previously announced a €207,000 municipal initiative to treat 2,600 domestic pines in urban zones. Barontini emphasized that regional funds, alongside ongoing biological research and forest thinning, demonstrate a firm, collaborative commitment to saving the endangered pine heritage. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Bientina hosts traditional polenta and porcini festival – October 9, SagreToscana
CAPANNORI (Lucca) – Bientina will host the “Festa della polenta a palle ai funghi porcini” at the local sports field, running on Sundays, Oct. 18-25, and Nov. 1. The lunchtime gastronomic event opens at noon using a self-service format in indoor and outdoor dining areas. The menu highlights traditional “polenta a palle” served with porcini mushroom sauce or Cinta Senese ragù, alongside appetizers, roasted sausage, steaks and desserts. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Vicopisano hosts 18th annual chestnut festival – October 9, SagreToscana
VICOPISANO (Pisa) – San Giovanni alla Vena, a village in the Vicopisano municipality, will host the 18th edition of the Festa della Castagna across two Sundays on Oct. 18. Festivities begin at 12:30 p.m. with a public lunch featuring grilled entrees and local dishes, with reservations available by phone. Starting at 3 p.m., afternoon food stands will highlight chestnuts in various traditional forms, including roasted chestnuts (caldarroste), chestnut flour crêpes (necci), chestnut cake (castagnaccio) and fritters. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
San Rossore clinic unveils advanced CT scanner in Pisa – October 6, Il Tirreno
PISA — The San Rossore Health Clinic in Pisa has inaugurated the state-of-the-art Naeotom AlphaPro CT scanner, marking a major advancement for local precision medicine. Featuring photon-counting technology, the new device delivers high-definition imaging with reduced radiation doses, boosting diagnostic accuracy for oncology and cardiology patients. Clinic CEO Andrea Madonna and Pisa Mayor Michele Conti attended the launch alongside medical experts. Professor Emanuele Neri highlighted that the equipment allows physicians to “see beyond the visible” through enhanced spatial resolution, reinforcing the city’s standing as a hub for advanced healthcare. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Pisa faces criticism over €900M military base upgrade plan – October 6, PisaToday
PISA — Pisa is drawing sharp political opposition following the release of Ministry of Defense documents outlining a €900 million logistics and maintenance contract for its military airport, running 2027-2032. The agreement pairs the Pisa air base with Sicily’s Sigonella facility to support the Italian Air Force’s C-130J transport fleet through a no-bid arrangement with Lockheed Martin, Leonardo and GE Avio. Local leftist opposition group Diritti in Comune condemned the investment, branding Pisa a “land aircraft carrier” and demanding the funds be redirected to social and environmental priorities instead. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Tuscany plans major highway expansion to ease traffic congestion – October 2, Il Tirreno
Tuscany regional officials unveiled a 23-million-euro project to tackle traffic congestion along the heavily traveled Fi-Pi-Li highway. The initiative kicks off with a 2.3-kilometer expansion between Scandicci and Lastra a Signa, introducing a flexible dynamic lane that shifts between an emergency shoulder and a regular travel lane during peak hours. Funded through the upcoming regional budget, construction aims to streamline the flow for approximately 50,000 daily vehicles. Future phases include renewable-powered noise barriers and subsequent infrastructure upgrades near Pisa by 2028. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Michele Abenante is Livorno’s new police chief – October 2, Il Tirreno
LIVORNO — Michele Abenante has officially taken over as Livorno’s new police chief, succeeding Giusy Stellino upon her retirement. A 57-year-old native of Calabria, Abenante transitions to Tuscany from the Terni police headquarters, mirroring the career path of one of his predecessors, Roberto Massucci. With a distinguished career in the State Police spanning nearly four decades, Abenante previously led investigative units across Calabria and Puglia, served in Rome as a ministerial advisor, and managed public safety operations in Terni. His extensive background includes numerous commendations and international investigative experience across Europe. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Ferrari’s first sailboat set for Livorno launch – October 2, Il Tirreno
LIVORNO — Ferrari will complete and launch its first sailboat, Hypersail, in Livorno, after choosing Azimut Benetti’s Porta a Mare site as the project’s strategic base. A Ferrari-branded facility will be built to house the 30-meter vessel, which is expected to arrive from Pisa by December. The launch is targeted for spring 2027, followed by six months of sea trials off Livorno. Designed by naval architect Guillaume Verdier with Ferrari design chief Flavio Manzoni, the 40-ton boat will attempt to break the Jules Verne Trophy’s round-the-world sailing record. Livorno officials view the project as a major showcase for local industry, investment and maritime expertise. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Lucca Comics & Games prepares for record 60th edition – October 2, Il Tirreno
LUCCA – Lucca Comics & Games is preparing for its largest edition yet, with more public squares, exhibition stands and investment than ever before, according to festival director Emanuele Vietina. Ticket sales are in line with 2025, when attendance reached about 280,000. The event begins Oct. 28 despite residents’ concerns about parking, installations and disruption across the city. Mayor Mario Pardini acknowledged the inconvenience but urged residents to protect an event widely credited with boosting Lucca’s economy and global profile. Celebrating six decades since its 1966 inception, the five-day festival will feature major entertainment highlights, including previews from HBO Max, Netflix and Disney+, alongside appearances by international gaming legends like Yoshinori Kitase and comic icons such as Frank Miller. The event honors its rich legacy while expanding its global footprint across multiple creative industries. New initiatives include discounted resident tickets and an exhibition at Palazzo Guinigi exploring the festival’s history and laying the groundwork for a future comics museum. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Livorno veterinary hospital unveils major renovation with 24-hour emergency care – September 29 LivornoToday
LIVORNO – The Ardenza Veterinary Hospital in Livorno has completed a major renovation of its facilities on Via Uberto Mondolfi. Unveiled during a ceremony on Sept. 23 with local officials and animal welfare representatives, the updated clinic features separate waiting rooms, examination areas and recovery spaces for cats and dogs to reduce patient stress. The upgraded facility also includes a dedicated 24-hour emergency room, the only round-the-clock veterinary emergency service in the province, alongside a private parking lot and a green space for pet families. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
New Pisa art group launches to champion diversity and youth – September 25, PisaToday
PISA — Founded by architect and painter Marco Sereni and art critic Ilario Luperini, the newly formed “Gruppo Pisano per l’Arte” welcomes all artistic trends, fosters cross-disciplinary collaboration, from visual arts and theater to music and cinema, and emphasizes contemporary culture. The group is dedicated to supporting youth creativity, promoting democratic values and strengthening social dialogue. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Exploring the natural beauty of Versilia's Malbacco waterfalls – August 25, Il Tirreno
SERAVEZZA – Nestled in the Apuan Alps near Seravezza, the Malbacco Waterfalls and the Pozzo della Madonna offer visitors a scenic natural retreat featuring emerald pools and natural rockslides. A brief 35-to-50-minute hike through wooded trails leads hikers to the picturesque ten-meter waterfall and crystal-clear stream. While the destination remains popular for summer outings and swimming, local authorities and guides urge visitors to exercise caution. The area’s rocks and boulders can become slippery and the water remains cold, requiring proper hiking footwear, careful river crossings and mindful observation of local environmental conditions. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Lucca sets Guinness record for world's longest flower carpet – August 25, Il Tirreno
LUCCA – Lucca entered the Guinness World Records on Aug. 22 for creating the world’s longest floral carpet, surpassing the previous record held by Huamantla, Mexico. Held along the city’s historic Renaissance walls during the Festival of Ephemeral Arts, the milestone event featured 13 intricate panels crafted by international artists using flowers, petals, colored sand, salt and sawdust. Mayor Mario Pardini and Tuscany governor Eugenio Giani joined thousands of spectators to witness the historic display, which spanned over four kilometers. Official certification was announced at approximately 8:30 p.m., eclipsing Mexico’s 2022 record of nearly 3,940 meters and celebrating Italy’s UNESCO bid for ephemeral floral art. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
University of Pisa ranks fourth in Italy in Shanghai ranking – August 21, Il Tirreno
PISA – The University of Pisa secured the fourth spot in Italy in the 2026 Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU), landing in the 211th position globally. The institution earned high marks for academic prestige, ranking 72nd worldwide for alumni success and 67th for faculty and graduates who have received prestigious international awards like Nobel Prizes or Field Medals. Officials noted that the university continues to perform strongly in European and national standings amid growing global competition. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Dalia Colli opens elite make-up training school in Livorno – August 21, Il Tirreno
LIVORNO – World‑renowned cinematic make‑up artist Dalia Colli is opening a professional training school in her hometown of Livorno, in a studio between the Pontino and La Venezia districts. With three David di Donatello awards and an Oscar nomination for Garrone’s Pinocchio, Colli aims to pass on 30 years of film‑set experience. The program offers structured courses from basic and HD make‑up to special effects, airbrush, and advanced cinematic masterclasses. Classes will be limited to six to eight students to ensure personalized, craft‑focused training. Colli chose Livorno to strengthen local ties to the film industry. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Tuscany allocates €4 million for Fi-Pi-Li road repairs – August 11, LivornoToday
TUSCANY – The Tuscany regional government has approved €4 million in funding for extraordinary maintenance on the Fi-Pi-Li highway, a critical transit route. The allocation, requested by the Metropolitan City of Florence, will be divided into €2 million payments in both 2026 and 2027. Officials stated the funding addresses accelerated road surface deterioration and updated costs from a new global service contract signed in January 2026. Under the current management agreement, the region provides additional resources when the Metropolitan City of Florence and the provinces of Pisa and Livorno demonstrate the necessity for priority infrastructure repairs. Work is expected to occur throughout the two-year period. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Pedestrian waterfront bans bicycles in Rosignano and Castiglioncello – August 7, LivornoToday
CASTIGLIONCELLO — The Municipality of Rosignano has reiterated a bicycle ban along the pedestrian waterfront stretching from Piazza delle Repubbliche Marinare in Rosignano Solvay to Punta Righini in Castiglioncello. Aimed at protecting pedestrians during peak summer tourism, the restriction applies to the designated walking area. Local police are launching an informational and preventative campaign to raise awareness. While supporting sustainable mobility elsewhere, officials stress that the high volume of families, elderly visitors and children makes the ban necessary to ensure safety and unhindered movement. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Pisa advances unified museum card – August 7, PisaToday
PISA – Pisa’s city council has approved a convention framework for the “Pisa Card,” a unified ticket granting access to paid cultural sites throughout the city. Scheduled for an official signing in September, the initiative unites local entities including Palazzo Blu, national museums, the university museum system, and tourism partners to enhance visitor competitiveness and extend tourist stays. Part of the municipal Tourism Development Plan, the card aims to balance visitor flows and promote integrated cultural offerings for tourists and residents alike. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Free and guided tours available at Piaggio Museum in Pontedera – May 4, TerrediPisa
PONTEDERA (Pisa) – The Piaggio Museum in Pontedera is open Tuesday through Saturday, plus the second and fourth Sundays of each month (closed on Mondays). Visitors can book 60-minute self-guided tours with a contribution of €5 per person, or guided tours for a maximum of 10 people (€5 per person). The collection showcases iconic Vespa models, Ape and Porter vehicles and 104 world-championship-winning motorcycles from Aprilia, Gilera and Moto Guzzi, which together have collected the marvelous Palmares of 104 World Titles in the various motorcycling sports, from Supermoto to MotoGP, from Trial to SBK. Pre-war railway and aeronautic pieces, along with rotating temporary exhibits, are also on display. Admire the “Vespa” from 9:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.
Rare black storks spotted at Lake Sibolla – August 4, Il Tirreno
ALTOPASCIO (Lucca) – Three rare young black storks stopped at the Lago di Sibolla nature reserve in Altopascio, Lucca, during their migration from Europe to tropical Africa. Announced by the LIPU bird conservation group the sighting marks only the second recent appearance of the species at the reserve. While black storks returned to nest in Italy in 1994 after a millennium, the population remains under 50 breeding pairs and faces threats from wind turbines, power lines and poaching. Conservationists continue working to protect these majestic birds and their habitats. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
New additions arrive at the Pistoia Zoo – August 4, Il Tirreno
PISTOIA – The Pistoia Zoo welcomed two new animals with distinct rescue and conservation backgrounds: a Eurasian lynx named Freya and a baby Turkmenian markhor named Jannik. Freya arrived at the 14-hectare Tuscan facility on July 26, after enduring a decade of illegal captivity in Lithuania and undergoing rehabilitation in Belgium. Meanwhile, Jannik was born at the zoo under the European Endangered Species Program (EEP), which focuses on preserving threatened wildlife populations. Both arrivals highlight the zoo’s ongoing commitment to animal welfare, conservation and biodiversity. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
University of Pisa students break Guinness World Record for largest paper airplane – July 2, Il Tirreno
PISA – A team of engineering students from the University of Pisa has achieved a Guinness World Record by building the world’s largest paper airplane. Developed under the ICARUS project with support from science communicator Jakidale, the aircraft features a 20.04-meter wingspan and a length of seven meters. Handcrafted using only paper and glue, the plane flew 59 meters at the WMF - We Make Future event in Bologna. The feat surpassed the previous world record held since 2013 by Germany’s Braunschweig Institute of Technology, bringing the title back to Italy. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Etruscan underground city captures tourist attention in Terricciola – June 30, Il Tirreno
TERRICCIOLA (Pisa) – Guided tours of the ancient Etruscan hypogea in Terricciola continue to draw growing crowds to the Tuscan hillside town. The weekly free tours take visitors through a network of underground chambers carved into tuff rock. These subterranean spaces originally served as Etruscan burial sites before being repurposed over centuries into cellars and shelters. Highlights include the well-preserved Belvedere Hypogeum and a historic funerary urn housed inside the San Donato church. Due to high summer temperatures, organizers have scheduled morning tours, which require reservations by calling 377–690 4739. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
New 118 emergency medical outpost to reopen in Marina di Pisa – June 23, PisaToday
MARINA DI PISA – A local emergency medical service (118) outpost will reopen in Marina di Pisa on July 1, operating 12 hours a day in Via della Repubblica Pisana. The facility, which has been closed for four years, aims to improve healthcare access and safety for residents and tourists during the peak summer season. Additionally, a beach rescue service managed by the Red Cross will launch this weekend, deploying lifeguards and defibrillators across four local pebble beach stations. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Thirty-nine Tuscan gelato shops honored in 2027 Gambero Rosso guide – June 23, Il Tirreno
TUSCANY – Gambero Rosso has awarded 39 Tuscan gelato shops in its 2027 guide, maintaining its highest “Three Cones” rating for three local establishments: Gelateria della Passera (Florence), De’ Coltelli (Pisa) and Gelateria Dondoli (San Gimignano). The region also secured a special national honor, with Lucca’s Ele Gelati & Granite winning Best Emerging Gelato Maker for its dedication to sustainability and premium local ingredients. The guide additionally awarded “Two Cones” to 23 Tuscan gelaterie, including Pisa’s Rufus and Manzi Gelateria, and “One Cone” to 13 others, highlighting the region’s diverse artisanal excellence. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Encounter with two-meter mako shark reported off Antignano coast – June 15, Il Tirreno
LIVORNO – During a fishing trip on June 13, a local fisherman encountered a two-meter mako shark about a mile off the coast of Antignano, Livorno. The shark approached the boat’s buoys before biting a fishing line in water about 56 meters deep. After a brief struggle, the fisherman photographed the animal and cut the line to release it safely back into the sea. The mako shark is an open-ocean predator known as one of the fastest sharks in the world. Experts note that while they live in the Mediterranean following prey like tuna, coastal sightings are highly unusual and do not indicate a permanent presence. Outnumbered by rare interactions mostly linked to fishing activities, the incident poses no public alarm. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Dog-friendly beaches in Tuscany offer summer relax for pets and owners – June 9, PisaToday
TUSCANY – Tuscany features numerous dog-friendly beaches, both free and equipped, allowing families to enjoy the sea with their pets. In the Pisa province, Calambrone’s Single Fin Tuscany Dog Beach offers shaded gazebos and unrestricted swimming. The Livorno province hosts several options, including Cecina’s Bau Beach with a dedicated swimming area, San Vincenzo’s Dog Beach and Piombino’s Pascià Glam Dog Beach, located in a natural park with pet showers. Further south in Grosseto, free beaches like Puntone di Scarlino and Punta Ala’s Bau Beach welcome all sizes, while Marina di Grosseto’s Fuorirotta Beach Club provides full amenities for leashed dogs. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Tuscany’s Orrido di Botri nature reserve reopens for summer season – June 5, Il Tirreno
BAGNI DI LUCCA – The Orrido di Botri Nature Reserve, a prominent canyon in the Tuscan-Emilian Apennines, officially reopened to the public on June 1. An on-site information point is active at the reserve’s entrance. The station provides visitors with updated trail conditions, safety regulations and access guidelines for the canyon. The reopening is a coordinated effort between the Municipality of Bagni di Lucca, the Carabinieri Biodiversity Unit of Lucca and CanyoNatura Toscana to promote sustainable tourism. Guided tours and safety details are available on the reserve’s official website https://www.orridodibotri.toscana.it. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Livorno “Il Mare dei Ricordi” surpasses 2,000 memories – May 26, LivornoToday
LIVORNO – “Il Mare dei Ricordi,” a unique site dedicated to shared memory and emotion, has now gathered over 2,000 personal stories, becoming a recognized destination for visitors from Italy and abroad. The Scalinata di Antignano welcomes people who come to participate in this collective journey, where the sea serves as a guardian of cherished memories. Each name represents a lasting connection, and the project continues to grow, inspiring the creation of the Kyra Inclusive Park, a space that unites inclusion, remembrance and community. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Pisa hospital debuts advanced robotic platform for super microsurgery – May 14, Il Tirreno
PISA – Tuscany President Eugenio Giani and Health Councilor Monia Monni inaugurated the Symani robotic platform for super microsurgery at Pisa's Cisanello Hospital, making it the first in Tuscany and one of only five in Italy. This acquisition expands the hospital’s robotic inventory to five systems, building on a multidisciplinary surgical robotics legacy started in 2001. The officials also toured the historic Santa Chiara site, visiting the nationally recognized Nina simulation center for high-risk maternal-infantile care training and the advanced forensic radiology department. According to Director General Katia Belvedere, the institution ranks among the nation’s top centers for complex medical cases, drawing 16 percent of its patients from across Italy. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)
Livorno honors 20th-century master Voltolino Fontani with major exhibition – May 14, Il Tirreno
LIVORNO – A comprehensive retrospective showcasing 111 works by Voltolino Fontani is open at the Fondazione Livorno in Piazza Grande, marking the 50th anniversary of the artist’s passing. Running until Dec. 13, the exhibition traces Fontani’s evolution from his early symbolic creations to his abstract experimentations, local landscapes and sacred art. The event also expands across the territory into a “widespread exhibition,” incorporating critical religious works located at the Church of San Giovanni Gualberto in Valle Benedetta. Accompanying the display is a detailed catalog by Pacini Editore, providing essential essays and unpublished writings to deepen public understanding of his complex artistic journey. (Summary by Chiara Mattirolo)

This is the first time in American history that there have been zero releases at the border
WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of Homeland Security and U.S. Customs and Border Protection today announced preliminary Fiscal Year 2026 data showcasing a 95% drop in southwest border apprehensions, compared to the Biden Administration, alongside the lowest annual encounters in American history and the first-ever fiscal year with zero Border Patrol releases.
Driven by President Donald J. Trump’s policies and the leadership of DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, FY 2026 combined historic low crossings with strengthened border infrastructure, disrupted cartels, and protected American trade. September marked the 17th consecutive month with ZERO releases.
“President Trump promised the American people a secure border, and the data proves he delivered. Over the past year, CBP recorded its lowest numbers in American history. A stark contrast to Biden, where CBP recorded its highest illegal immigration numbers ever,” said Secretary Mullin. “The results could not be clearer: strong enforcement works. Thanks to President Trump’s leadership and the hard work of CBP and DHS law enforcement personnel, we have restored control of the border and made America safer than ever.”
“FY 2026 demonstrated what focused enforcement, strong partnerships, and the commitment of our frontline personnel can achieve,” said CBP Commissioner Rodney S. Scott. “DHS and CBP are securing the border, stopping dangerous drugs and criminals, protecting communities, and ensuring our personnel have the resources necessary for this critical mission.”
Historic Border Security Results
CBP’s enforcement posture drove U.S. Border Patrol apprehensions to their lowest level in agency history. The Border Patrol, which completed its first-ever fiscal year with no releases, recorded less than 99,000 southwest border apprehensions in FY 2026—a 95% decline compared with more than 1.8 million per year under President Biden. Total FY 2026 apprehensions (98,708) were 60% lower than the Biden Administration’s single highest month alone (249,740).
Additionally, preliminary data shows total nationwide encounters in FY 2026 were the lowest in agency history at 379,243, compared with 2.7 million per year under Biden (seven times higher). FY 2026 encounters were 88% lower than FY 2023 under Biden, which was the highest fiscal year ever.
These results reflect sustained enforcement and the deterrent effect of a secure border. Illegal aliens have received a clear message: don’t try to enter the country illegally, or you will be apprehended, detained, and deported.
A Safer Border
President Trump’s policies are also saving lives by reducing unlawful crossings, leading to a dramatic decline in border-related deaths.
Fewer unlawful crossings have contributed to a significant decline in border-related deaths. Preliminary data shows alien deaths identified by the Border Patrol fell nearly 80% in FY 2026 and since January 20, 2025, compared to the Biden Administration.
CBP personnel nevertheless remained ready to respond when lives were at risk. Across the nation, agents, officers, and air and marine personnel conducted search-and-rescue operations and delivered emergency medical aid. These efforts have included railcar rescues, a rescue effort following flooding at the Grand Canyon, and a CBP officer who responded to victims of a plane crash in Miami.
CBP’s Office of Field Operations responded to more than 3,000 medical emergencies during FY 2026, performing CPR on over 50 individuals in cardiac arrest and administering Naloxone for suspected opioid overdoses.
Stronger Infrastructure Along the Border
CBP reached a major construction milestone in FY 2026, completing 250 miles of new border barrier along the southwest border since January 20, 2025. This includes primary and secondary barriers, waterborne barriers, and supporting technology.
Funding from the Working Families Tax Cut Act enabled CBP to accelerate Smart Wall construction. From September 2025 through September 2026, CBP obligated $34.3 billion to support Smart Wall projects across all southwest border states, cementing a generational investment in physical security and operational control.
Drug Interdictions that Save Lives
As the frontline against drug smuggling, CBP is leading federal efforts to combat illicit trafficking.
CBP utilizes cutting-edge nonintrusive inspection technology and intelligence-driven strategies to seize deadly drugs, targeting not just finished products but precursor chemicals, tools, and pill presses.
As a result, preliminary data shows CBP’s drug seizures in FY 2026 totaled nearly 1 million pounds—63% higher than the 600,000-pound annual average of the last four years.
Trade and Tariff Enforcement
CBP plays a central role in enforcing trade law, supporting economic security, and interdicting counterfeit merchandise and goods made with forced labor.
In FY 2026, CBP stopped more than 4,000 shipments valued at over $325 million suspected of involving forced labor and issued eight Withhold Release Orders along with two modifications.
CBP also seized nearly 55.5 million counterfeit goods valued at more than $12.6 billion, including 476,903 items infringing FIFA World Cup intellectual property valued at over $33 million.
By securing the border, intercepting dangerous narcotics, expanding physical barriers, and enforcing lawful trade, CBP has closed vulnerabilities across every front to ensure the long-term safety and prosperity of the American people.
title: Under President Trump and Secretary Mullin, DHS announces lowest fiscal year border crossings in American history

FORT LEONARD WOOD, Mo. – A Soldier who pleaded guilty to possessing, producing, and distributing child pornography was sentenced by the military judge to 28 years in prison during his court-martial Oct. 14 at the Fort Leonard Wood courtroom.
Spc. Gabriel Perez, 24, a combat engineer assigned to the 35th Engineer Battalion, 1st Engineer Brigade, was also sentenced to total forfeiture of pay and allowances, reduction in rank to E-1, and a dishonorable discharge from the Army.
In September 2024, the Department of the Army Criminal Investigation Division received Cybertips from the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children regarding three videos of child pornography that Perez distributed using his Snapchat account.
Army CID agents initiated an investigation and obtained a warrant to seize Perez’s iPhone. They discovered he had at least 18 conversations with girls under the age of 18.
He initially targeted several victims located throughout the United States on various social media platforms. After earning their trust on social media, Perez migrated their conversations to text messages. He then initiated online relationships with the girls and began engaging in sexually explicit conversations.
Perez eventually requested sexually explicit photos and videos from the victims, who ranged in age from 13 to 17 years old. He used emotional manipulation to coerce the victims into producing child pornography and sending it to him whenever he demanded. These tactics went so far as threats to expose the girls to their friends and families, or telling them to kill themselves.
Further analysis of Perez’s phone revealed that from June 2023 to December 2024, he downloaded and saved to a hidden folder a library of child sexual abuse material containing over 160 explicit videos and over 180 explicit photos.
“The Office of Special Trial Counsel, Army CID, and the Office of the Staff Judge Advocate take CSAM and crimes against children seriously. The outcome of this case is a testament to how this strong partnership ensured that justice was served,” said Capt. Derek Sanchez, prosecutor, Fourth Circuit, Army OSTC.
“Spc. Perez systematically groomed vulnerable children and betrayed their innocence for abuse and exploitation,” said Special Agent in Charge John McCabe, Army CID’s Midcentral Field Office. “While no verdict can undo the trauma he has inflicted, this sentence is a fitting end and removes a dangerous predator from our community.”
Perez will serve his prison sentence at the United States Disciplinary Barracks at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas. Upon release from prison, he will be required to register as a sex offender under federal and state statutory requirements.
This case was investigated by Army CID’s Fort Leonard Wood Resident Agency.
About the Army Office of Special Trial Counsel:
The Army Office of Special Trial Counsel is composed of specially trained military lawyers, legal professionals and support staff responsible for the expert prosecution of murder, sexual assault, domestic violence, child abuse, kidnapping and other serious criminal offenses. Headquartered at Fort Belvoir, Va., OSTC has eight regional headquarters that oversee 28 field offices located worldwide, including locations in Europe and Korea. For more information visit www.army.mil/ostc.
To Report a Crime:
If you would like to report a crime, have information about a crime, or have been the subject or survivor of a crime, you can submit anonymous tips to Army CID at www.p3tips.com/armycid.
title: Fort Leonard Wood Soldier Sentenced to 28 Years in Prison for Child Pornography Crimes

LUBBOCK, Texas – United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould today announced that a Lubbock man who led a high-purity methamphetamine trafficking operation was sentenced to more than 11 years in federal prison.

Steven Glenn Ryals, 72, also known as “Hot Tub,” was convicted of possession with intent to distribute 50 grams or more of methamphetamine. U.S. District Judge James Wesley Hendrix imposed the 135-month sentence today.

“Steven Ryals exploited his leadership of the Bandidos’ Lubbock chapter to push high purity methamphetamine into our community,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “Today’s sentence sends a clear message: we will aggressively pursue those who traffic dangerous drugs and dismantle the drug distribution networks that threaten West Texans.”

“Steven Ryals exploited his leadership of the Bandidos’ Lubbock chapter to push high purity methamphetamine into our community,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “Today’s sentence sends a clear message: we will aggressively pursue those who traffic dangerous drugs and dismantle the drug distribution networks that threaten West Texans.”

“Today’s sentence reflects the FBI’s continued commitment to protecting our communities from the dangers of high purity narcotics and the criminal networks that distribute them,” said FBI Dallas Special Agent in Charge R. Joseph Rothrock. “This case underscores the impact of strong partnerships among federal, state, and local agencies and our shared resolve to disrupt drug trafficking organizations and hold traffickers accountable.”

According to court documents, Ryals was the President of the Bandidos Motorcycle Club’s Lubbock Notorious Chapter and had served with the club for over 50 years. Federal law enforcement began investigating Ryals and other members in early 2025 for distributing methamphetamine in the Lubbock area.

On Feb. 27, FBI agents and the Lubbock Anti-Gang Center executed a search warrant at the Bandidos clubhouse, which also served as Ryals’s residence. During that search, agents discovered approximately 3.2 pounds of suspected methamphetamine inside a locked filing‑cabinet drawer, along with Bandidos paraphernalia and tools used to package and distribute narcotics.

At sentencing, prosecutors outlined the results of DEA laboratory testing confirming the substance was 1,449.6 grams of methamphetamine hydrochloride at 98% purity, an amount consistent only with high‑level distribution. Additional methamphetamine was found in Ryals’s bedroom closet and in his vehicle during a traffic stop on the same day, all of which he admitted possessing with intent to distribute.

Ryals was previously convicted of methamphetamine trafficking and in 1999 received an identical 135‑month sentence for that offense.

The FBI, the Lubbock Texas Anti‑Gang (TAG) Center and the Caprock High‑Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (HIDTA) conducted the investigation. TAG Center includes agents from DEA, ATF, Texas DPS, the Lubbock County Sheriff’s Office, and the Lubbock Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Stephen J. Rancourt prosecuted the case.

###
title: Leader of Lubbock Bandidos Motorcycle Club sentenced to federal prison for meth distribution

Concord, N.H. — Continuing her fight to hold Liberty Utilities accountable after its refusal to provide new or expanded natural gas service for customers in the Lakes Region, Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) today served discovery questions in the company’s rate case before the New Hampshire Public Utilities Commission. The questions build on Goodlander’s months of oversight and successful effort to put Liberty’s Lakes Region service denials under review, demanding answers on the company’s decisions, costs, and plans to end the moratorium.
Liberty is asking the Commission to approve a $35.8 million annual increase in distribution rates, which would add about $26 a month to a typical residential heating bill, while also continuing to refuse new or expanded service in the Lakes Region.
In June, Goodlander sent Liberty 13 questions about the moratorium. Liberty responded with a five-page letter leaving the majority of questions unanswered, including basic ones regarding who at the company made the decision, how many customers have been turned away, and what the pipeline upgrade will cost. As a formal party to the rate case, Goodlander can now require answers through the Commission’s discovery process.
The questions press Liberty to explain who decided to impose the moratorium, how many customers have been denied service and why, and why critical pipeline upgrades were delayed.
Goodlander is also demanding details on the cost and timing of temporary and permanent fixes, whether affected customers will be compensated, and the company’s profits and payments to its parent company.
“For months, families and small businesses across our Lakes Region have been left in limbo while Liberty leaves basic questions unanswered. Who decided to deny them service? Why does the timeline for a permanent fix keep slipping? Who will foot the bill?” said Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander. “Families in New Hampshire deserve answers, reliable service, and real accountability. Now that we’ve secured a seat at the table in this case, I’m using every tool available to demand those answers on the record. I won’t quit until the people I work for get the answers and solutions they deserve.”
Read the full questions HERE.
Goodlander has made lower energy costs and investor-owned utility accountability a focus of her work in Congress:
- Goodlander previously filed a petition to intervene in Liberty Utilities’ rate case, with the Public Utilities Commission granting it last month. Following Goodlander’s advocacy, the PUC also agreed to take up Liberty’s decision to deny new or expanded service to towns across the Lakes Region – identifying Liberty’s “moratorium” on new natural gas service in the Lakes Region as an issue that belongs in this PUC proceeding.
- Goodlander urged the New Hampshire Public Utilities Commission to reconsiderEversource’s approved 43.4 percent rate increase and helped introduce the Lowering Utility Bills Act to rein in excessive profits at investor-owned utilities.
- She introduced bipartisan, bicameral legislation to accelerate hydropower production and lower energy costs, launched a bipartisan Hydropower Caucus to do the same, and joined efforts to protect ratepayers from potentially costly utility transactions.
- Before taking office, Goodlander served as a Deputy Assistant Attorney General in the Justice Department’s Antitrust Division, where she took on corporate monopolies driving up costs for families and small businesses.
###
title: As Admitted Party in Liberty Utilities Rate Case, Goodlander Demands Answers on Service Refusals

The U.S. Department of Energy today announced its intent to deploy Defense Production Act (DPA) funding to accelerate the expansion of transmission capacity in Virginia and West Virginia, strengthening grid reliability and infrastructure essential to national defense.
October 16, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced its intent to deploy Defense Production Act (DPA) funding to accelerate the expansion of transmission capacity in Virginia and West Virginia, strengthening grid reliability and infrastructure essential to national defense. Virginia Energy's Grid Enhancing Technologies for Virginia & West Virginia Large Load Growth project will receive up to $50 million in DPA funding to deploy advanced transmission technologies across existing power lines to increase electricity delivery capacity, reduce congestion, and support growing energy demand across the region.
The proposed project will deploy advanced reconductoring and Dynamic Line Rating technologies along existing transmission corridors, adding an estimated 290 megawatts of transmission capacity across Appalachian Power's Virginia system, one to four years faster than conventional transmission upgrades. These improvements will make the power grid more reliable, lower electricity costs, and help ensure that communities, businesses, military operations, and government and defense-related industries across the region have dependable power, especially during times of high demand or power disruptions.
Thanks to President Trump and the passage of the Working Families Tax Cut, $1 billion in federal funding has been appropriated for energy-related projects deemed critical to national security. Presidential Determination No. 2026-10 identifies transmission lines and conductors, substations, and power-control and protection equipment as essential to national defense.
“President Trump is committed to doing everything possible to strengthen American energy security and lower costs for the American people,” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. “By deploying Defense Production Act funding to secure and expand electricity access in Virginia and West Virginia, the Trump Administration is strengthening the nation’s energy security for decades to come.”
“A stronger electric grid doesn't always mean building more power lines. Sometimes it means making better use of the ones we already have,” said Office of Electricity Assistant Secretary Katie Jereza. “This investment will help unlock more power, strengthen reliability, and ensure our grid can meet the growing demands of American families, businesses, and national defense.”
Led by Virginia Energy in coordination with Appalachian Power, Potomac Edison, and regional partners, the proposed 48-month project will demonstrate how advanced conductors and real-time transmission monitoring technologies can expand capacity using existing infrastructure. The project reflects the Trump Administration's focus on delivering critical energy infrastructure, strengthening domestic supply chains by creating infrastructure deployment of advance technologies and materials, and improving grid performance while protecting taxpayer dollars and ratepayers.
title: Energy Department Announces Virginia and West Virginia Transmission Project to Receive Defense Production Act Funding, Strengthening National Security and Grid Reliability

Pensacola, Florida – The United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit affirmed the conviction and sentence of Shannon L. Wilkerson, 46, for the 2001 murder of 19-year-old Army Private First Class Amanda Gonzales and her unborn child. In May 2024, a Pensacola jury convicted Wilkerson, a former U.S. solider, of second-degree murder. According to court documents, Wilkerson beat and strangled Gonzales to death on November 3, 2001, in her barracks room at Fliegerhorst Kaserne, then a U.S. Army base in Hanau, Germany. Evidence introduced at trial indicated that Wilkerson feared he was the father of Gonzales’ unborn child and that her pregnancy would interfere with his military career and his marriage to another soldier on the base. Wilkerson was a member of the U.S. Armed Forces at the time of the offense but was later discharged. The district court sentenced Wilkerson to 30 years’ imprisonment.

United States Attorney John P. Heekin said: “This cold case prosecution demonstrated the lengths to which my office will go to achieve justice for crime victims. I am extremely proud that we successfully defended this conviction and sentence against the defendant’s appeal. Nothing can bring back the innocent lives taken by this defendant’s heinous crime, but defending this successful prosecution against his appeal ensures he will not escape accountability.”

“This case serves as a perfect example of the Criminal Division’s pursuit of justice no matter the challenge,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “I am proud of the work of the Criminal Division prosecutors, the Northern District of Florida, and the federal agents that worked tirelessly to solve this terrible cold case murder. I also want to express my deepest condolences to the family of PFC Amanda Gonzales and hope that the affirming of Shannon Wilkerson’s conviction by the Court of Appeals brings some sense of closure to this two-decade pursuit of justice.”

Following his conviction and sentencing, Wilkerson appealed to the Eleventh Circuit. After briefing by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida defending the conviction and sentence, the Court rejected each of Wilkerson’s arguments in an unpublished opinion without oral argument. It concluded that the district court acted appropriately in keeping out purely speculative alternative-perpetrator evidence claiming that another soldier committed and pleaded to an unrelated double-homicide in 2006, refusing to entertain the defense’s discovery “fishing expedition” for validation data underlying the government’s DNA evidence, and denying Wilkerson’s motion for a new trial. It likewise found no error in the district court’s conclusion that Wilkerson committed perjury at trial when he denied murdering Gonzales and concluded that Wilkerson had not shown that his 30-year sentence was unreasonable. The Eleventh Circuit’s opinion affirming Wilkerson’s conviction and sentence is available here .

The Federal Bureau of Investigation New York and Jacksonville Field Offices investigated this case, with assistance from the Army Criminal Investigative Division. Assistant United States Attorney Jordane New handled the appeal before the Eleventh Circuit. Trial Attorney Patrick Jasperse of the Criminal Division’s Human Rights and Special Prosecutions Section and Assistant United States Attorney David L. Goldberg prosecuted the case.

The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl .
title: 11th Circuit Affirms Conviction, 30-Year Sentence in Cold Case Prosecution of 2001 Murder of Pregnant Army Private in Germany

Brad D. Schimel, First Assistant United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Wisconsin, announced that on October 14, 2026, United States District Court Chief Judge Pamela Pepper sentenced Kevin McCaa (age 40) of Milwaukee, Wisconsin, to 38 years’ imprisonment, followed by five years of supervised release.

On July 8, 2026, Kevin McCaa pled guilty to the murder of a United States Postal Employee and discharge of a firearm during a crime of violence. As detailed in the court record, veteran United States Postal Service letter carrier Aundre Cross was delivering mail in Milwaukee on the afternoon of December 9, 2022, when he was shot in the head and killed. Evidence established that Kevin McCaa and Charles Ducksworth Jr. were responsible for the homicide. McCaa and Ducksworth surveilled the letter carrier for over 30 minutes prior to the homicide and targeted him because they thought he had stolen their drug package. After the homicide, they threw the firearm in a nearby creek, changed their phone numbers, and disposed of clothing. McCaa and Ducksworth have been in federal custody since their arrest for these offenses on December 27, 2022.

At the sentencing hearing, Judge Pepper credited the “old-fashioned” investigative work that led to the arrest of McCaa and Ducksworth. Law enforcement utilized warrants for phone record data, automated license plate reader technology and surveillance footage from numerous residences and businesses in the area of the homicide to show the suspects’ activities before and after the homicide. Judge Pepper further determined that the facts of the case reflected that the crime was “premeditated, planned beforehand, with malice aforethought” and called it “incomprehensible.”

“As the Chief Judge noted, these defendants were brought to justice through excellent work by investigators and prosecutors,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Schimel. “This was a cold-blooded, senseless murder of a beloved member of his family and the community he served. McCaa will rightly spend virtually the rest of his life in federal prison.”

“Holding those accountable who commit violence against employees of the U.S. Postal Service is our agency’s number one priority. Today’s sentencing hopefully brings a small amount of justice and closure for the family and friends of Aundre Cross. The U.S. Postal Inspection Service would like to thank the Milwaukee Police Department and FBI Milwaukee for their unwavering assistance with this investigation.” stated Nicholas Bucciarelli, Inspector in Charge, Chicago Division of U.S. Postal Inspection Service.

“Kevin McCaa’s heinous crime was deserving of the significant sentence he received for murdering Aundre Cross, an innocent victim who was doing his job as an employee of the U.S. Postal Service. While the sentencing cannot bring Mr. Cross back to his family and friends, hopefully it will be a step forward in the healing process,” said FBI Milwaukee Special Agent in Charge Alan Karr. “The joint efforts of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Milwaukee Police Department, and the FBI in this case exemplifies the importance of law enforcement collaboration. The FBI remains committed to working with our federal, state, and local partners to combat violent crime and seek justice for victims.”

“The Milwaukee Police Department is grateful to all partners who worked together in seeking justice for the victims of this tremendous tragedy. This case also highlights the integral part technology plays in public safety. We thank all the agencies involved that work tirelessly to keep this community safe,” stated Chief Jeffrey Norman of the Milwaukee Police Department.

Co-defendant Ducksworth pled guilty to the same crimes as McCaa and is scheduled for sentencing before Judge Pepper on November 18, 2026.

The investigation of this case was conducted by the Milwaukee Police Department, the United States Postal Inspection Service, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation, with the assistance of the Milwaukee County Sheriff’s Office and the Wauwatosa Police Department. Assistant United States Attorneys Margaret Honrath and Abbey Marzick prosecuted this case.

WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Congressman Kweisi Mfume (D-MD), Ranking Member of the House Oversight Subcommittee on Government Operations, sent a letter to Postmaster General David Steiner and Chief Postal Inspector Gary Barksdale requesting a briefing on the suspicious mailings sent this week to congressional offices and state election offices. In the letter, Congressman Mfume commends the Postal Service employees who intercepted several of the letters before they were delivered and honors the postal workers who face the greatest risk from dangerous mail.
“I commend the Postal Service and Postal Inspection Service employees who, according to state election officials and a Senate office, intercepted several of these letters before they were delivered,” wrote Congressman Mfume. “As the investigation continues, I want to make sure Congress has a clear picture of the threat and of any support the Postal Service needs to address it.”
“This week’s mailings are also a reminder that the people most exposed to dangerous mail are the postal employees who handle it first,” Congressman Mfume continued. “Our country learned this at great cost in 2001, when two employees of the Brentwood processing facility in Washington, D.C., both Maryland residents, died after anthrax letters addressed to Senate offices passed through their facility. We owe them and their families a lasting debt.”
“I thank these inspectors, and the letter carriers, clerks, and mail handlers who keep doing this work every day, often without knowing what is inside the envelopes they carry,” Congressman Mfume concluded.
In the letter, Congressman Mfume requests a briefing on the following:
- The approximate number of suspicious mailings identified to date, including how many were addressed to congressional offices and how many were intercepted before delivery;
- How the Postal Service and the Postal Inspection Service identified and intercepted these mailings;
- How and when the Postal Inspection Service shares information about threats in the mail with the Capitol Police and the House and Senate Sergeants at Arms;
- The steps taken to protect postal employees who may have processed or delivered these letters; and
- Any changes to procedures adopted after earlier suspicious mailings, and any additional resources the Postal Inspection Service needs to address these threats.
###
title: Rep. Mfume Commends Postal Workers, Requests Briefing on Suspicious Mailings to Congressional Offices

Brazilian Man Sentenced to 12 Years in Prison for Managerial Role in Conspiracy to Launder Tens of Millions of Dollars in Illicit Cash Proceeds
Ygor Fokin Saviolli, 35, a Brazilian national, was sentenced today to 12 years in prison for his role as a manager and supervisor in a money laundering organization that laundered more than $30 million in illicit proceeds, including the proceeds of drug trafficking. On September 24, five co-defendants received sentences ranging from 94 months in prison to 12 months and one day in prison.
Gabriel Cezar Menezes, 29, a Brazilian national, was sentenced to 94 months; Omar Aliperti De Mello Correa, 34, a U.S. citizen, was sentenced to 30 months; Leandro De Avila Goncalves, 43, a Brazilian national, was sentenced to 24 months; and Joao Andrade De Mello, 29, and Tadeu Sebastiane Rabelo Alves Barbosa, 30, both Brazilian nationals, were each sentenced to 12 months and one day. The Brazilian national defendants were illegally residing in the United States at the time of their arrests.
According to court documents, Saviolli, Menezes, Correa, Goncalves, De Mello, and Barbosa were part of a sophisticated money laundering organization that operated across the United States and spanned several countries. Members of the conspiracy arranged for U.S.-based couriers to receive bulk cash proceeds from the sale of controlled substances and then to deposit the cash at banks across the country in order to conceal and return those profits to, among others, the sources of drug supply operating outside the United States. Dozens of pickups across the country were coordinated through WhatsApp message chains that included facilitators and couriers. Saviolli provided upfront funds to facilitate the operations of the money laundering organization and oversaw the receipt and laundering of the bulk cash drug proceeds. Menezes also served as a facilitator, providing direction to and oversight of couriers, and personally picked up bulk cash on multiple occasions. Correa, De Mello, Barbosa, and Goncalves all served as couriers for the money laundering organization, conducting bulk cash pickups in cities including Atlanta, Charlotte, Chicago, Cleveland, Minneapolis, Rochester, and Tampa, among others. Over the course of the conspiracy, the organization concealed more than $30 million in cash.
In June 2026, the defendants’ guilty pleas to conspiracy to commit money laundering were accepted by the district court.
Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division, U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida, and Special Agent in Charge Brett Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office made the announcement.
The FBI investigated the case, with assistance from the Drug Enforcement Administration’s Rochester Resident Office and Homeland Security Investigations’ Brasilia Attaché Office and Miami Field Office.
Trial Attorneys James Hepburn and Jessee Alexander-Hoeppner of the Criminal Division’s Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section (MNF) and Assistant U.S. Attorney Monique Botero for the Southern District of Florida prosecuted the case.
MNF’s mission is to take the profit out of crime, eliminate drug cartels, and protect the U.S. financial system. MNF pursues criminal prosecutions and criminal and civil asset recovery actions involving: financial facilitators who launder profits for criminals; financial institutions and their officers and employees whose actions threaten the U.S. financial system and financial institutions; international money launderers who support transnational organized crime; and the top command and control of international drug trafficking organizations.
MNF’s International Unit investigates and prosecutes cross-border money laundering schemes involving transnational criminal organizations, cartels, foreign official corruption and related money laundering affecting the U.S. financial system and prosecutes criminal cases and civil forfeiture matters to recover the proceeds of those crimes.

U.S. Coast Guard Releases Major Incident Investigation Report into Fatal MH-60T Mishap West off Cape Flattery
WASHINGTON — The United States Coast Guard today publicly released the Major Incident Investigation (MII) report examining the Feb. 27, 2026 aviation mishap involving an MH-60T Jayhawk helicopter (CG-6063) assigned to Coast Guard Air Station Astoria, Oregon.
The mishap occurred during a search and rescue mission at sea approximately 96 nautical miles west of Cape Flattery, Washington, and resulted in the death of Coast Guard Aviation Survival Technician Second Class Tyler Jaggers. Petty Officer Jaggers died on March 5, 2026 from injuries sustained during the rescue attempt.
"Our entire service grieves the tragic loss of our teammate,” said Adm. Kevin Lunday, Commandant of the United States Coast Guard. "The Coast Guard conducts aviation operations in an inherently dangerous environment that demands the highest levels of proficiency from our crews. We conduct disciplined operations to ensure our crews accomplish the mission and safely return. In this case, as the investigation revealed, we did not meet the high standards required, with fatal results for one of our own. We will learn from this mishap and improve the proficiency and safety of our operations.”
Investigative Findings and Cause of the Mishap
The investigation determined that the primary cause of the mishap was physical contact between the helicopter’s rescue hoist cable and the radar mast of the bulk carrier M/V MOMI ARROW which caused the hoist cable to fail.
During the hoist deployment of Petty Officer Jaggers to the ship, a pendulum swing developed in the hoist cable. During the crew’s attempts to control the swing, the helicopter drifted toward the ship’s superstructure and mast. When the crew aborted the hoist, the helicopter transitioned forward and left over the ship’s superstructure. The hoist cable then contacted the ship’s centerline radar mast, which generated shear forces far exceeding the hoist cable’s design strength, causing the cable to fail. Petty Officer Jaggers subsequently fell approximately 30 feet, impacted the vessel's port railing on the superstructure, and suffered critical injuries.
Rigorous engineering, structural, and metallurgical testing conducted at the Coast Guard Aviation Logistics Center determined that the MH-60T airframe, hydraulic systems, flight controls, hoist assembly, and hoist cable were fully mission capable and mechanically sound prior to the mishap, with no evidence of mechanical malfunction or material defects.
Next Steps
A Commandant-appointed Mishap Analysis Board (MAB) is also conducting a comprehensive safety analysis of this incident. Together, the MII report and the MAB report will inform Coast Guard corrective actions to prevent future accidents.
The complete public version of the CG-6063 Major Incident Investigation report is accessible via the Coast Guard FOIA Reading Room at https://media.defense.gov/2026/Oct/16/2004015705/-1/-1-0-MAJOR%20INCIDENT%20INVESTIGATION%20-%20CG6063.PDF.

BEAUMONT, Texas – A federal prison inmate has been convicted in an investment fraud scheme in the Eastern District of Texas, announced U.S. Attorney Jay R. Combs.

Riley Graham, 60, also known as David Drake, was found guilty by a jury of conspiring to commit wire fraud. The verdict was reached on October 15, 2026, following a five-day trial before U.S. District Judge Marcia A. Crone.

According to information presented in court, from June 2019 through October 2024, Graham, while imprisoned at the low security correctional facility at the Bureau of Prisons Federal Correctional Complex (BOP-FCC) in Beaumont, conspired with others to devise and execute a scheme to defraud others, including a Beaumont pastor, his family, and the owners of a North Carolina construction business, of over $1.4 million. Graham, who had previously been convicted of perpetrating a federal fraud scheme, began another scheme to defraud those he had access to – including a fellow inmate and his family.

The maximum statutory sentence prescribed by Congress is up to 30 years in federal prison, a potential fine, and restitution at sentencing. The maximum statutory sentence is provided here for information purposes, as the sentencing will be determined by the court based on the advisory sentencing guidelines and other statutory factors. Sentencing hearings will be scheduled after the completion of presentence investigations by the U.S. Probation Office.

This case was investigated by the FBI, Internal Revenue Service-Criminal Investigation, Homeland Security Investigations, and Bureau of Prisons and prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys John B. Ross and Chris Jackson.

###
title: Federal inmate convicted of using his time in prison to defraud local family and others
