PHILADELPHIA – United States Attorney David Metcalf announced that Mory Kante, 21, a French national illegally in the U.S., who has been residing in Wilmington, Delaware, was sentenced today to 13 years in prison and five years of supervised release by United States District Judge Gerald J. Pappert for the carjacking and attempted carjacking of two women in one night.

The defendant was arrested on a criminal complaint and warrant in January of this year and charged by indictment the same month. He pleaded guilty in June to carjacking, attempted carjacking, and using, carrying, and brandishing a firearm during and in relation to a crime of violence.

As detailed in court filings, on November 20, 2025, at approximately 9:15 p.m., a woman (“Victim 1”) parked her 2018 Honda Civic on the 1300 block of North Lawrence Street, got out of the vehicle, and walked away. She then saw the defendant run across the street and point a gun at her, saying “gimme your car keys” repeatedly. Victim 1 dropped her purse, and the defendant scooped it up and ran from the scene. Police subsequently found the purse on the street with some of the contents dumped out. Victim 1’s camera, driver’s license, two credit cards, debit card, wallet, and some cash were missing.

At approximately 11:00 p.m. that night, police responded to a report of an armed carjacking on the 700 block of West Girard Avenue, approximately seven blocks from where Victim 1 was robbed. A woman (“Victim 2”) reported that a black male wearing all black clothing and a gray hat carjacked her at gunpoint. Victim 2 provided police with location data showing that her car, a 2019 Kia Optima, was near the intersection of Marvin Street and Wyoming Avenue, about four and a half miles north of the carjacking scene.

Police located the car and activated their lights and sirens. Kante fled in the vehicle and a brief chase ensued, before the defendant abandoned the car and fled on foot. Pursuing officers saw him toss away a gun, jump on the porch of a nearby residence, and push his way into the home. A SWAT team was called and located the defendant hiding in some bushes in the backyard.

This case was investigated by the Philadelphia Police Department and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Justin Oshana.

Larsen Joins PNW Members Expressing Concerns with Potential ICE Purchase of Tacoma ICE Facility 
  
  
  
  
    
      
On Tuesday, U.S. Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02) joined colleagues from the Washington and Oregon congressional delegations in demanding answers and transparency into ongoing efforts by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to purchase existing immigration detention centers currently owned and operated by private prison companies like GEO Group and CoreCivic.  
“We are deeply concerned about the potential purchase of these facilities, as it appears to be an attempt to circumvent oversight and accountability at detention facilities,” wrote the Members. “Both GEO Group and DHS have stated that acquiring these facilities is aimed, at least in part, at circumventing attempts by states to conduct oversight at immigration detention centers located within their borders.”  
The Northwest ICE Processing Center (NWIPC) in Tacoma, Washington is the largest ICE facility in the Pacific Northwest and one of the largest in the nation. ICE has a contract with GEO group to own and operate the facility. In June 2025, Rep. Larsen toured NWIPC and heard from Lelo Juarez, a Skagit County union leader detained by ICE, about poor conditions inside the facility. Larsen and other members of Washington state’s congressional delegation have previously written to ICE to express their concerns about conditions at the facility. 
“As of March 2026, the Washington State Department of Health received over 3,500 complaints about Northwest Detention Center. Individuals have reported being sexually assaulted by an officer in their unit; unsanitary conditions, including unclean drinking water, worms, hair, and metal in food, and black mold in showers; and insufficient medical care,” continued the Members. “State oversight is an essential way to help ensure that the people detained in these facilities at U.S. taxpayer expense are being treated with dignity. Attempting to circumvent such oversight by purchasing substandard detention facilities and continuing to allow such inhumane conditions to persist is unacceptable.”  
In 2023, the Washington State Legislature passed a law guaranteeing state health inspectors access to privately-owned detention facilities. GEO Group has prevented officials from the Washington State Department of Health from inspecting the facility since 2023, which Washington state is currently challenging in court. ICE’s contract with GEO Group for NWIPC expires on October 27, 2026. If ICE buys NWIPC, it could limit the Washington State Department of Health’s ability to inspect the facility.  
The full text of the letter can be found here.  
In addition to Rep. Larsen, Representatives Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Emily Randall (WA-02), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Janelle S. Bynum (OR-05), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (WA-03), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Kim Schrier (WA-08), Adam Smith (WA-09) and Marilyn Strickland (WA-10) also signed the letter.  
Larsen Fights to Hold ICE Accountable 
In July 2026, Rep. Larsen conducted an oversight visit of ICE’s Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) facility in Ferndale to get answers for the community about the facility’s operations. Last week, Rep. Larsen conducted an oversight visit ofICE’s Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) facility in Ferndale to follow up on questions that he had about HSI’s involvement in ERO operations. 
In June 2025, Rep. Larsen conducted an oversight visit of NWIPC and met with Lelo Juarez, a Skagit County union leader and activist whom ICE detained in March 2025. 
In Congress, Rep. Larsen has refused to vote for ICE funding without placing additional guardrails on the agency and requiring that ICE follow the same rules as every other local, state and federal law enforcement agency.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Representative John Garamendi (D-CA-08) and Representative Mark DeSaulnier (D-CA-10) issued the following statement after the Government Accountability Office (GAO), the government watchdog, published Garamendi’s requested report finding that the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) decision to block a $19 million Community Change Grant to Contra Costa County violated the law.
This news comes more than one year after Reps. Garamendi and DeSaulnier confronted the EPA for violating federal appropriations law and federal court injunctions by canceling a $19.1 million Community Change Grant awarded to Contra Costa County for its North Richmond Community Resilience Initiative.
“The GAO confirmed what we knew all along: President Trump’s EPA broke the law, and now I’m demanding they pay us back,” said Congressman Garamendi. “This funding was, and still is, not a suggestion. Congress mandated years ago that these funds be delivered to frontline communities like North Richmond, which, because of President Trump’s blatant abuse of the law, has continued to suffer the health impacts of extreme pollution. Not only has Trump’s EPA acted in ways that break the law, but because of its callousness and disregard for the American people, it is endangering the health and wellbeing of some of our nation’s most vulnerable residents. The people of North Richmond deserve better. Trump took away their money, and now they need to give it back.”
“Over a year ago, I was proud to stand with Congressman Garamendi in calling on the Trump Administration to reverse course as they illegally clawed back over $19 million in federal funding for environmental protection efforts from Contra Costa County,” said Congressman DeSaulnier. “Now the GAO, an independent government watchdog agency, has confirmed the Administration violated the law in stealing this money and we demand it be reinstated immediately.”
Background
In spring 2025, the EPA terminated a $19.1 million Community Change Grant awarded to Contra Costa County for its North Richmond Community Resilience Initiative. The initiative is one of 105 applications selected for the Inflation Reduction Act’s Community Change Grants Program, the largest national investment in environmental and climate justice.
The $19.1 million in funding was allocated directly to the community for the initiative, which aimed to build a resilience center for emergencies and natural disasters and to plant 65 trees along the Verde Elementary schoolyard to shield students from pollution caused by a new distribution center.
In response to the news of the cancellation, Congressman Garamendi and Congressman DeSaulnier sent a letter to Trump-appointed EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin stating that the agency flagrantly violated the Congressional Budget and Impoundment Control Act without any explanation or due process.
In response to Garamendi and DeSaulnier’s letter, the EPA provided little to no justification for the cancellation, saying only that the agency does not support programs or organizations that promote or take part in DEI or “environmental justice” initiatives.
Congressman Garamendi then requested a report on the Trump Administration’s actions from the GAO, which published its decision on the termination of the Community Change Grants on October 7. The GAO found that the EPA violated the law and noted that Garamendi and DeSaulnier’s letter to the EPA and the agency’s response also helped inform its determination.
###
title: ‘Trump’s EPA Broke the Law’: Garamendi, DeSaulnier React to Watchdog Report, Demand Trump Return $19 Million to Contra Costa

THOMPSON, WITTMAN INTRODUCE RESOLUTION DESIGNATING 2026 NATIONAL WILDLIFE REFUGE WEEK
Washington - Representatives Mike Thompson (D-CA-04) and Robert Wittman (R-VA-01) introduced a resolution supporting the designation of the week beginning October 10, 2026 as National Wildlife Refuge Week.
The resolution celebrates the diversity of wildlife and habitats protected by the National Wildlife Refuge System and the many recreational opportunities these public lands provide, including hunting, fishing, wildlife observation, and photography. Since President Theodore Roosevelt established the first national wildlife refuge in 1903, the system has played a vital role in conserving wildlife, protecting threatened and endangered species, and preserving America’s natural heritage for future generations.
“Our national wildlife refuges play a vital role in protecting wildlife and preserving America’s natural heritage,” said Thompson. “They safeguard wetlands, forests, and coastal areas, provide essential habitat for migratory birds and endangered species, and give Americans opportunities to enjoy hunting, fishing, and wildlife observation. National Wildlife Refuge Week celebrates the importance of these public lands and the need to conserve them for future generations.”
“Virginia is home to many national wildlife refuges, " said Rep. Wittman. “In the First District, places like the Rappahannock River Valley National Wildlife Refuge protect critical habitat, support the health of the Chesapeake Bay watershed, and preserve opportunities for hunting, fishing, and outdoor recreation. I am proud to recognize National Wildlife Refuge Week alongside my colleagues as we work to support the health and conservation of these important sites and ecosystems so they can be enjoyed by future generations.”
“National Wildlife Refuge Week is an opportunity to celebrate the extraordinary places that sustain our nation’s wildlife, connect people with nature, and preserve our natural heritage for future generations. We are grateful to Congress for recognizing the importance of the National Wildlife Refuge System and the dedicated people who care for these special places. This resolution is a meaningful reminder that wildlife refuges are a shared national treasure, and that protecting them is an investment in the health of our ecosystems, our communities, and generations to come,” said Desirée Sorenson-Groves, President and CEO, National Wildlife Refuge Association.
The National Wildlife Refuge System includes 573 national wildlife refuges, 38 wetland management districts, and five marine national monuments spanning more than 850 million acres across every state and U.S. territory. The system supports hundreds of species of birds, mammals, reptiles, amphibians, and fish, and provides protection for more than 380 threatened and endangered species.
Thompson is a longtime outdoorsman and conservationist who has helped conserve nearly 5 million acres of North American wetlands and uplands through his legislative work and service on the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission.
National Wildlife Refuge Week recognizes the vital contributions of the National Wildlife Refuge System to wildlife conservation, outdoor recreation, local economies, and the preservation of America’s natural resources.
In addition to Reps. Thompson and Wittman, the resolution’s original cosponsors include Representatives Andre Carson (IN-07), Ed Case (HI-01), Debbie Dingell (MI-06), Michael Guest (MS-03), Val Hoyle (OR-04), and Kevin Mullin (CA-15).
Senator Chris Coons (D-DE) and Senator John Kennedy (R-LA) will introduce a companion resolution in the Senate.
The full text of the resolution can be found here.
###
Congressman Mike Thompson is proud to represent California’s 4th Congressional District, which includes all or part of Lake, Napa, Solano, Sonoma and Yolo Counties. He is a senior member of the House Committee on Ways and Means. Rep. Thompson is Chairman of the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force. He is also Co-Chair of the bipartisan, bicameral Congressional Wine Caucus and a member of the fiscally-responsible Blue Dog Coalition.

Trump’s Transportation Department, Air Traffic Controller Union Announce 2.8% Pay Increase Deal
Pay raise comes with new workforce reforms to track controllers’ time, align staffing with demand, & improve the controller reassignment process
WASHINGTON, D.C. - U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy announced today that the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and National Air Traffic Controllers Association (NATCA) have reached a deal to provide air traffic controllers with a 2.8% pay increase following key workforce reforms.
In the Homeland Security and Further Additional Continuing Appropriations Act of 2026, Congress directed to FAA to tie a pay increase to measurable improvements in operational efficiency.
Improvements include:
- Timecard Tracking: Most federal employees are required to “badge in” and “badge out” at their place of work. This approach will now be applied to air traffic facilities to ensure managers have the data they need to better track training and safety needs.
- Align Staffing with Demand: Local managers and union representatives will develop shift guidelines based on forecasted workload and operational requirements. This will ensure more productive controller schedules that maximize coverage during peak traffic hours.
- Improved Reassignment Process: Controller reassignments will now focus on where the staffing needs are the most severe. Past changes to the controller reassignment process resulted in significantly more controllers transferring to locations with minimal shortages.
Together, these changes will improve controller quality of life, strengthen coordination between managers and frontline employees, make better use of the FAA’s existing workforce, and improve operational efficiency to keep America’s skies safe.
“President Trump has made clear that we must modernize our skies and deliver results for the flying public,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “That means taking a hard look at how we operate, fixing outdated staffing practices, and growing our air traffic control workforce. We are making these changes to better support the men and women who keep our skies safe, get controllers where they are needed most, and improve how we utilize the airspace. I appreciate the collaboration with NATCA and the thousands of hard-working controllers they represent to reach this deal so we can build a stronger system for the future.”
“Air traffic controllers perform critical work every day to keep the National Airspace System safe,” said FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford. “By improving how we track work, schedule shifts and allocate personnel, we can make better use of our workforce and respond more effectively to operational demands. Our work with NATCA is helping us put practical changes in place that support our controllers and improve the way the system operates.”
“This increase reflects the vital role these dedicated professionals play in keeping our nation’s skies safe and efficient,” said NATCA President Nick Daniels. “Fair compensation and better working conditions are essential to sustaining a strong, experienced air traffic controller workforce.”
The pay increase takes effect Oct. 18 and is retroactive to the beginning of the year.
###
title: Trump’s Transportation Department, Air Traffic Controller Union Announce 2.8% Pay Increase Deal

ABERDEEN PROVING GROUND, Md. — Army Public Health Nursing (APHN) personnel at Kirk U.S. Army Health Clinic (KUSAHC) are taking a proactive stance on preventive medicine this October, bringing lifesaving Breast Cancer Awareness Month resources, tools, and educational campaigns directly to the Aberdeen Proving Ground (APG) workforce.
The mobile campaign, led by KUSAHC representatives Ms. Crystal Wright and Ms. Kristine Trusty, is designed to bring critical health information directly to active-duty service members (ADSMs), civilian staff, and military families where they work and live.
The motivation behind the mobile initiative is rooted in KUSAHC's broader commitment to preventive medicine, wellness, and medical readiness.
"By bringing resources directly to APG locations, Army Public Health Nursing is helping to ensure that our ADSM, civilian staff, and beneficiaries have access to vital health information and reminders of screenings right where they work," Wright and Trusty said in a joint statement.
To maximize visibility and outreach across the installation, the mobile tour is targeting high-traffic areas, including the main Kirk Clinic lobby, the APG Commissary, and various tenant command headquarters.
During outreach events, APG personnel can interact with physical, educational tools designed to take the mystery out of preventative self-care.
The team is providing:
Breast self-examination guides.
Educational pamphlets outline the critical importance of regular screenings.
Guides on what patients should expect during an outpatient mammogram.
Lifelike breast self-examination models with palpable lumps and realistic tissue textures to provide hand-on instruction.
These models allow participants to practice identifying abnormalities, reinforcing real-world self-examination techniques in a supportive, educational environment.
For active-duty female service members, early detection is directly linked to operational readiness. Early diagnosis typically translates to more effective, less invasive treatment options, which minimizes recovery times and ensures personnel remain operationally fit to support the national defense mission.
While the disease primarily affects women, the KUSAHC team is also engaging active-duty male service members, providing them with tailored information on rare male breast cancer risks and symptoms.
The mobile initiative has already generated significant emotional impacts across the installation.
"The response has been overwhelmingly positive," the team noted, recalling a recent encounter with a female soldier who was hesitant to seek a screening after losing her mother to the disease. "After our conversation, she felt empowered to make an appointment to get a mammogram and committed to providing encouragement to the women in her unit to take advantage of the screenings and resources available, highlighting the domino effect of awareness."
title: On the Move: Kirk Clinic Nurses Bring Lifesaving Breast Cancer Awareness Directly to APG Workforce

text:
Salinas, Wyden Lead 51 Lawmakers in Demanding Trump Administration Stop Fast-Tracking Deportations of Unaccompanied Children
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Andrea Salinas (OR-06) and Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) led 51 Members of Congress in a bicameral letter against the Trump Administration’s efforts to accelerate the removal of unaccompanied children while dismantling their due process protections.
The letter — addressed to the U.S. Department of Justice, the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR), U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) — warns that these agencies are colluding to fast-track children’s cases at the very moment when their access to legal support has collapsed. The letter documents a pattern of practices across agencies that rob children of the ability to make their cases fairly, such as 24-hour asylum interview notices, “mega master” hearings, restricted continuances, and the closure of every pathway to counsel. The lawmakers demanded that the Trump Administration immediately reverse course and outlined 25 questions that the agencies must answer.
The letter is endorsed by the Acacia Center for Justice. Click here or see below for the full text of the letter:
Attorney General Blanche, Acting Director Owen, Director Edlow, and Mr. Wall:
We are concerned by how the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ), the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR), U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) are coordinating to accelerate the removal of unaccompanied children while systematically dismantling the due process protections Congress established under the Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008 (TVPRA), and we call on you to reverse course immediately. As a result of your directives, immigration courts are operating as part of the Trump administration’s larger deportation agenda and prioritizing speed and cruelty over due process and fair adjudication, with an increasing focus on unaccompanied children.¹ At the end of August 2026, a one-year-old child was asked to file her own asylum application with no legal representative stepping forward.² That is not an aberration; it is the predictable result of a coordinated effort to accelerate children's cases at the precise moment when the federally funded legal services infrastructure Congress mandated has been dismantled.³
After the administration failed to renew the existing contract with legal service providers that ended on July 31, 2026, they neglected to develop a coherent transition plan to ensure unaccompanied children continued to have access to legal service providers. Instead, they sought organizations that were incapable of performing this role because they lacked the expertise, infrastructure, and consents to responsibly manage this work to the great detriment of children.⁴ According to September 18, 2026, filings in Community Legal Services in East Palo Alto v. U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (CLSEPA v. HHS), the U.S. Committee for Refugees and Immigrants (USCRI), the sole current federal legal services provider for unaccompanied children, “has provided only a handful of Know-Your-Rights presentations and has entered representation of at most a few dozen unaccompanied children since August 5.”⁵ That gap is unfolding at the same moment that EOIR is accelerating children's cases and USCIS is scheduling asylum interviews with only a 24-hour notice.
Rather than slowing proceedings to account for the extraordinary gap in legal services for unaccompanied children, courts are increasingly imposing accelerated timelines and restricted continuances due to directives from DOJ and EOIR. For example, in Philadelphia in early August 2026, 28 children's cases were continued over a four-week period to facilitate representation. Although the TVPRA mandates that the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) “shall ensure, to the greatest extent practicable…that all unaccompanied children…have counsel to represent them in legal proceedings,” only six children obtained counsel from USCRI.⁶ This is despite the organization being repeatedly involved as a friend of the court asking for continuances. Also, in the same month in Houston, four children, out of a group of twelve cases involving unaccompanied children, were informed that their next continuance, scheduled within one to two weeks, would be their final opportunity to secure representation or they would be forced to represent themselves. In another case, a judge took pleadings from a child representing themself, instructing them they had to complete and file their own asylum application and provide the court with proof within a matter of weeks.
Earlier this year, EOIR started using “mega masters” and “rocket dockets” at the direction of the administration. These consist of one hearing for sixty to over one hundred people, including children.⁷ This format creates enormous confusion for individuals trying to identify a child’s court date and ensure their attendance, as well as pressure for immigrant children to plead, accept deadlines, or move forward without counsel. One mega master occurred in early August 2026 in Seattle, where one judge heard 106 cases in one day. Over 30 children were ordered to be removed in absentia. The next day, attorneys reported a docket of 99 cases, including 30 ordered to be removed in absentia. It is clear that children cannot meaningfully participate in these mega masters, but EOIR continues to force them to make life-altering decisions, under unprecedented legal proceedings and without adequate legal representation. Federal regulation prohibits an immigration judge from accepting “an admission of removability from an unrepresented respondent who is incompetent or under the age of 18 and is not accompanied by an attorney or legal representative, a near relative, legal guardian, or friend.”⁸ Where the child has no lawyer, the immigration judge is required to “direct a hearing on the issues.”⁹ “Mega masters” that produce in absentia removal orders against tens of unrepresented children in a single sitting cannot be reconciled with this requirement.
When children are forced to navigate our immigration system alone on widely truncated timelines and without adequate assistance, subpar language access, and sometimes without a merits hearing, DOJ and EOIR cannot ensure that these children have fair, individualized adjudications.
The acceleration in immigration court is being matched at USCIS. Beginning in the summer of 2026, the Houston Asylum Office began issuing asylum interview notices to unaccompanied children in Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) custody on as little as 24 hours' notice, a departure from the prior 21-day practice. On September 11, 2026, the ORR Unaccompanied Alien Children (UAC) Bureau issued a memorandum and accompanying job aid directing ORR care providers to facilitate virtual USCIS asylum interviews for children in custody, including by providing space, technology, and, where no interpreter has been provided by USCIS or the child's representative, by having care provider staff themselves serve as interpreters in confidential asylum proceedings.¹⁰ Reports indicate that children have already been interviewed on 24 hours' notice without legal representation. This practice compromises the confidentiality of the asylum application under 8 C.F.R. § 208.6; deprives children of any meaningful opportunity to prepare for a proceeding that Congress designed to be non-adversarial precisely because of children's unique vulnerabilities¹¹; and forecloses the possibility of counsel appearing on the child's behalf. Coming at the same moment that EOIR is accelerating removal proceedings and the Office of Principal Legal Advisor (OPLA) is opposing continuances, the practice signals coordination among agencies to close every remaining pathway to relief before a child can access it.
Additionally, there are concerns that court independence and EOIR biases have eroded protections for unaccompanied children. For example, there are reports that the Trump administration and EOIR leadership have hand-picked compliant immigration judges, and have pressured current immigration judges, sometimes with incentives, to prioritize completing cases and increasing removal numbers, with some judges even citing that a child’s case must be completed by the end of the calendar year. The Trump administration has hired immigration judges who are ready to implement its directives. In fact, of May 2026, EOIR hired 153 permanent immigration judges this fiscal year, which the agency touts as “the most in any single year in the agency’s history.”¹² Additionally, approximately 100 immigration judges left or were removed during 2025, including judges who reportedly did not comply with fast-tracked juvenile dockets. From January 2025 through July 2026, in absentia removal orders as a percentage of overall removal orders against unaccompanied children approximately doubled, and the asylum grant rate for unaccompanied children in removal proceedings fell from roughly 11% to approximately 1.5%.¹³
In another report, judges said that they received directives that constrain continuances, accelerate cases, limit friend of court services, permit cases without merits hearings, and order the removal of children with certain form of relief pending, such as Special Immigrant Juvenile Status (SIJS).¹⁴ Specifically, in Chicago in July and August 2026, a new judge appointed to the juvenile docket ordered at least eight SIJS eligible children removed because it would take so long for them to get a visa that it “didn’t matter.”¹⁵ This practice appears to draw on the Board of Immigration Appeals' November 2025 precedential decision in Matter of Cahuec Tzalam, which held that an immigration judge need not administratively close a child's case to allow USCIS to process a prima facie SIJS application, notwithstanding that SIJS is a form of humanitarian relief Congress created specifically to protect abused, abandoned, and neglected children.¹⁶ In practice, the decision has become a vehicle for removing SIJS-eligible children before USCIS can adjudicate their applications.
The interagency coordination underlying these developments has now received an additional legal foundation. On September 28, 2026, HHS published a revision to the ORR System of Records Notice (SORN 09-80-0321) eliminating three protections that had governed ORR's information sharing with DHS and other agencies: the requirement that ORR obtain a written advisory that shared information will not be used for immigration enforcement, the requirement that ORR make an individualized determination that each disclosure is in the best interest of the child, and the prohibition on further use or disclosure of shared information by the Department of State recipient.¹⁷ HHS characterized the removed best-interest requirement as “administratively burdensome” and “difficult to implement.”¹⁸ And on September 29, 2026, HHS published a Federal Register notice creating a new Unaccompanied Alien Children Legal Representation Division within the HHS Office of the General Counsel, staffed by federal employees whose ultimate principal is the same administration that operates ICE OPLA and directs EOIR.¹⁹ The convergence of these developments - accelerated dockets, accelerated interviews, streamlined information sharing, and federal employees representing children in proceedings against the federal government - is not coincidence; it is the operational shape of a coordinated policy.
As of September 2026, the Trump administration has also started creating hidden courts for pro se respondents at several federal buildings, including the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), EOIR’s headquarters, and the floor at 26 Federal Plaza in New York that is leased to DHS. Specifically, there have been reports of two children being sent to the EOIR headquarters. These dockets set up folks to miss their hearings and be ordered removed in absentia. Subjecting anyone to this practice, especially children, is particularly egregious.²⁰
These practices cannot be reconciled with the statutory framework Congress established for unaccompanied children. The TVPRA guarantees children access to counsel in formal removal proceedings; vests USCIS with initial, non-adversarial jurisdiction over children's asylum claims precisely because of children's unique vulnerabilities; and directs EOIR to cooperate with HHS in providing Legal Orientation Presentations to child custodians, a requirement EOIR has now stopped fulfilling.²¹ 24-hour asylum interview notices, “mega master” hearings, restricted continuances, and the closure of every pathway to counsel reads each of these provisions out of the statute by operation.
We therefore seek your written responses to the below questions no later than October 30, 2026.
1. What directives or other guidance has EOIR issued to immigration judges regarding case completion rates, continuances, and scheduling?
2. What accommodations do immigration judges make when children appear pro se in their hearings?
3. What EOIR directives or other guidance are in place regarding the timeline for docketing children’s cases (including expedited dockets)?
4. What criteria does EOIR use to assign or remove judges from children's or juvenile dockets?
5. Since January 2026, how many juvenile dockets have been scheduled with: a. 25-50 children scheduled to appear in one hearing? b. 50-100 children scheduled to appear in one hearing? c. over 100 children scheduled to appear in one hearing?
6. Since January 2026, how many unaccompanied children have been placed on in master calendar hearings with more than: a. 25-50 children in one hearing? b. 50-100 children in one hearing? c. over 100 children in one hearing?
7. What justification does EOIR have for eliminating specialized children’s dockets in January 2025?
8. What protections exist for an unrepresented child when the only person available to identify a language, procedural, or comprehension problem is not permitted to speak in certain courtrooms (i.e., friend of court)?
9. In master calendar hearings, including those with over 50 or over 100 children scheduled for one docket, how is EOIR ensuring that interpretation is provided for each child in their best language?
10. How does EOIR reconcile the practice of accepting pleadings and issuing removal orders against unrepresented children in mega master hearings with 8 C.F.R. § 1240.10(c)? Please produce any guidance, memoranda, or training materials EOIR has issued to immigration judges regarding 8 C.F.R. § 1240.10(c) since January 20, 2025.
11. How many unaccompanied children have been scheduled for asylum interviews on fewer than 21 days' notice since June 1, 2026? Please provide monthly totals broken down by asylum office and by whether the child was represented at the time of interview. How many of those interviews have taken place?
12. What is the policy or legal basis for USCIS's issuance of asylum interview notices to unaccompanied children on 24 hours' notice? Please produce all guidance, memoranda, and communications between USCIS and ORR, EOIR, ICE, or the White House regarding accelerated asylum interview scheduling for unaccompanied children since January 20, 2025.
13. How does USCIS verify representation status at asylum interviews for unaccompanied children? What is USCIS's practice when a USCRI attorney appears at an asylum interview for a child who has existing counsel of record?
14. Please describe USCIS's coordination with ORR on the September 11, 2026 “Care Provider Supporting Virtual Asylum Interviews” job aid, including the use of care provider staff as interpreters and the waiver-of-representative provision.
15. How many asylum cases for unaccompanied children has USCIS approved since January 2025? How many of those cases were for children in ORR custody?
16. What legal orientation presentations for custodians of unaccompanied children has EOIR provided in each month of 2026, consistent with 8 U.S.C. § 1232(c)(4)? If none, when did EOIR cease providing them and on what legal basis?
17. Please provide any communications between EOIR, DOJ, ICE OPLA, USCIS, and ORR (or any component of HHS) regarding the scheduling, prioritization, or acceleration of unaccompanied children's immigration cases since January 20, 2025, including communications regarding the September 28, 2026, revision to ORR System of Records Notice 09-80-0321.
18. Please produce any policies, memoranda, or guidance ICE OPLA has issued since January 20, 2025, regarding when OPLA attorneys are directed to oppose or not to oppose continuance requests in cases involving unaccompanied children, including cases in which the child has not yet obtained counsel or has not yet had an opportunity to consult with counsel.
19. Historically, OPLA attorneys were allowed to make inquiries, request a case be expedited, or an interview be scheduled with USCIS regarding applications for pending immigration benefits on behalf of children appearing in removal proceedings. Does that access no longer exist? If it no longer exists, when was that ability taken away from OPLA attorneys?
20. How many unaccompanied children have been ordered removed in absentia each month in 2026, including August? How many of those were in ORR custody?
21. How many unaccompanied children without counsel have been ordered removed each month in 2026, including August? How many of those were in ORR custody?
22. How many unaccompanied children have accepted voluntary departure at immigration court each month in 2026, including August? How many of those were in ORR custody? How many of those children had legal representation at the time of accepting voluntary departure?
23. How many children withdrew their applications for asylum with USCIS prior to their interviews? How many of those were in ORR custody? How many of those children had legal representation at the time of withdrawing?
24. How many unaccompanied children have been ordered removed without receiving an individual hearing in their case?
25. What policies or guidance does DHS have in place regarding OPLA’s role in children’s immigration proceedings, including when to ask for and/or not oppose requests for a continuance?
Thank you for your prompt attention to these urgent matters. We look forward to your immediate response.
Sincerely,
###
title: Salinas, Wyden Lead 51 Lawmakers in Demanding Trump Administration Stop Fast-Tracking Deportations of Unaccompanied Children

VICENZA, Italy — U.S. Army Southern European Task Force, Africa (SETAF-AF) is partnering with the U.S. Army’s Global Tactical Edge Acquisition Directorate to test emerging systems in Africa and deliver them to Soldiers within 180 days.
The command’s first accelerated capability event, or ACE, is scheduled for spring 2027 in Tan-Tan, Morocco. It will focus on counter-unmanned aircraft systems and force protection, targeting capability gaps in protecting early-entry command posts and operating locations against Group 1–3 small UAS.
Africa offers an open spectrum, uncongested airspace and diverse terrain that training ranges in the United States and Europe cannot easily match. These conditions allow Soldiers to validate solutions in theater and scale them across the service.
Operating under the Army Pathway for Innovation and Technology, G-TEAD embeds personnel within Army service component commands. These teams translate urgent commander priorities into executable requirements, giving field commanders access to acquisition authorities at the tactical edge. G-TEAD teams already operate within U.S. Army Europe and Africa, U.S. Army Pacific and U.S. Army Central.
U.S. Army Col. Christopher Hill, director of G-TEAD, described the organization as the Army's answer for putting innovative solutions in the hands of the warfighter.
“ASCCs always had priorities, they’ve always had capability gaps, but the two things they’ve never had is acquisition authority and research, development, test and evaluation dollars,” Hill said.
Hill said that because G-TEAD maintains visibility across multiple commands, its personnel can align modernization efforts, maximize funding and transition proven theater solutions Army wide.
G-TEAD assigned a team to SETAF-AF in summer 2026 to link immediate operational needs with rapid acquisition resources. Together, the commands will use the ACE framework as a fast-track pathway to identify, evaluate and deliver field-ready technology.
Through a three-phase model, submission and preparation, Soldier-led demonstrations and follow-on operational evaluation, ACEs deliver rapid solutions within an accelerated acquisition timeline.
“ACEs are driven by real, urgent, theater-specific technology gaps,” said U.S. Army Maj. Katlin VanWye, a G-TEAD representative embedded with SETAF-AF. “We take commanding general's priorities and translate those immediate tactical challenges into clear, executable technical requirements that defense prize-authority partners and Portfolio Acquisition Executive partners can actually action.”
SETAF-AF will hold a Soldier-led demonstration in February and March 2027 in Tan-Tan, Morocco, followed by an operational assessment in April and May during African Lion 2027, U.S. Africa Command’s largest joint military exercise in Africa. G-TEAD will validate up to 15 solutions with PAE Fires, one of the U.S. Army’s core modernization enterprises, responsible for shaping, integrating, and delivering the Army’s most critical fires capabilities, as the transition partner.
“The ACE is structured around five capability categories,” VanWye said. “An overarching, completely integrated fly‑away kit and four subcategories focused on sUAS detection, kinetic defeat, nonkinetic defeat and passive protection. Solutions will integrate into the Army’s C-UAS command and control Integrated Battle Command System-Maneuver.”
The initiative supports broader Army modernization priorities while reinforcing partner-led security across the theater.
“Soldiers need capability,” Hill said. “We have to come in, and we have to actually perform and produce.”
Hill emphasized that every system receives evaluation with an eye toward scaling across the service, so tactical lessons learned in Africa enhance overall military readiness.
By accelerating testing and adaptation alongside G-TEAD, SETAF-AF helps provide the joint force with broader strategic options while validating innovative capabilities for the total Army.

HONOLULU – United States Attorney Ken Sorenson announced that David Yamamoto, 28, of Waipahu, Hawaii, was sentenced yesterday by United States District Judge Shanlyn A.S. Park to 264 months in federal prison for the production of child pornography, followed by 10 years of supervised release. District Judge Park remanded Yamamoto into custody immediately at the end of sentencing.

According to court records, from in or around 2023 to 2025, Yamamoto used online gaming and messaging applications to find and groom children located in the United States and in foreign countries to send him sexually explicit videos and images of themselves. Yamamoto misrepresented his age by posing as a teenager on gaming applications geared towards teens and preteens. He then offered and sent money and gifts to over ten children as payment for engaging in sexually explicit live stream video calls with him and for sending sexually explicit imagery of themselves at his direction.

Yamamoto exchanged tens of thousands of online messages with minors, ranging in age from ten to seventeen years old. In messaging minors, he directed them to expose their genitals in particular poses or insert objects into their genitals, create sexually explicit videos involving urination and masturbation, and recreate images of explicit adult pornography that he had sent to the minors.

“The devastating harm Yamamoto inflicted on his numerous victims can never be undone, but his 22-year sentence sends a potent message that those who prey upon our children will face harsh penalties in federal court,” said U.S. Attorney Ken Sorenson. “Along with our steadfast partners at FBI, we will continue to hunt down child predators like Yamamoto and bring them to justice.”

“This sentence sends a clear message to any individuals who exploit children online: the FBI will find you, and you will face justice,” said FBI Honolulu Acting Special Agent in Charge Ryan C. Noonan. “Yamamoto preyed on minors by hiding behind technology, but his actions did not go unseen. The FBI and our federal partners remain steadfast in our mission to safeguard children and to pursue those who would harm them, wherever they are and however they operate.”

The FBI investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Rebecca A. Perlmutter prosecuted the case.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC .
title: Oahu Man Sentenced to 22 Years in Prison for Producing Child Pornography

Secretary Mullin and Commissioner Scott observed ongoing construction along the southern border
WASHINGTON – On Thursday, United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin, along with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) Commissioner Rodney Scott, visited the southern border in Arizona for a tour of the border wall.
Secretary Mullin and Commissioner Scott observed ongoing construction on secondary barriers and met with construction crews as the Trump Administration marked 17 months of ZERO releases of illegal aliens at the southern border. The latest data from CBP also revealed that Fiscal Year 2026 saw the lowest amount of border crossings of any fiscal year in American history.
“Under the Biden Administration, there was no national security, because you can’t have national security if you don’t know who’s inside the country,” said Secretary Mullin. “A secure border, and knowing who’s entering your country, is where you can start actually saying we have national security. The American people deserve to be safe in their cities, in their towns, on their streets, and in their neighborhoods. Thanks to President Trump’s bold leadership, we have had ZERO illegal aliens released into our country for the past 17 straight months—that’s promises made, promises kept in action.”
Secretary Mullin tours the border wall in Arizona
Secretary Mullin meets with construction crews working on secondary barriers
Commissioner Scott (left) and Secretary Mullin talk to Border Patrol agents at the wall
Ongoing construction on secondary barriers along the border
Secretary Mullin, Commissioner Scott, and construction crews at the border wall
In Fiscal Year 2026, CBP completed construction of 250 miles of new border barrier along the southwest border since January 20, 2025. This includes primary and secondary barriers, waterborne barriers, and supporting technology.
Funding from the Working Families Tax Cut Act enabled CBP to accelerate Smart Wall construction. From September 2025 through September 2026, CBP obligated $34.3 billion to support Smart Wall projects across all southwest border states, cementing a generational investment in physical security and operational control.

El representante Tran presenta una propuesta legislativa para reducir los costos de la vivienda para las familias del sur de California.
La legislación establece una serie de créditos fiscales integrales para los inquilinos, lo que contribuye al compromiso constante del representante Tran de ampliar la accesibilidad a la vivienda.
WASHINGTON, D.C. – El representante Derek Tran (CA-45) ha presentado la Ley de Ayuda al Coste de la Vivienda para Inquilinos (COST), con el fin de ofrecer alivio a los inquilinos del sur de California que se enfrentan al aumento de los costes de la vivienda. La legislación establece créditos fiscales integrales para los inquilinos, lo que contribuye al compromiso constante del representante Tran de ampliar la asequibilidad de la vivienda.
"Los costos de la vivienda en todo el país, especialmente en el sur de California, han llegado a un punto crítico. Las familias apenas pueden pagar la renta, y mucho menos ahorrar para el futuro", afirmó el representante Tran. "Este proyecto de ley proporcionaría un alivio inmediato y tangible a los inquilinos necesitados, ayudándoles a mantener un techo sobre sus cabezas, a disponer de más margen en sus presupuestos para los gastos diarios o incluso a ahorrar para comprar una casa. Me enorgullece estar al frente de esta iniciativa en representación de todas las familias estadounidenses."
Las familias del sur de California se enfrentan a unos de los costes de vivienda más elevados del país, con un alquiler medio en el condado de Orange que supera los 3.200 dólares al mes y que se ha disparado casi un 40% desde 2017.
La propuesta legislativa introduce un nuevo crédito fiscal reembolsable básico del 8 % para las familias con unos ingresos brutos de 150 000 dólares o menos, con un límite máximo por hogar de 333 dólares al mes, lo que supone un total de 4 000 dólares al año. En el distrito 45 de California, esto beneficiaría a más de 75 000 hogares.
Mientras que otras medidas para reducir los costos de la vivienda tardarían tiempo en aplicarse, este proyecto de ley devuelve inmediatamente dinero a los inquilinos para que puedan hacer frente a los gastos de alimentación, medicamentos, cuidado de los hijos y otros gastos.
Esta iniciativa legislativa se suma al historial del representante Tran en la consecución de resultados en materia de vivienda para la región:
- El representante Tran consiguió 250 000 dólares en financiación federal para apoyar la construcción de 2700 viviendas permanentes asequibles en todo el condado de Orange.
- El representante Tran copatrocinó la Ley Saving the American Dream (Salvar el sueño americano) para crear un grupo de trabajo interinstitucional sobre la crisis de la vivienda, así como la Ley de Mejora de los Créditos para la Vivienda Asequible, destinada a financiar la construcción de más viviendas multifamiliares.
- Además, el representante Tran votó a favor de la Ley "21st Century ROAD to Housing", que entró en vigor en julio de 2026 y tiene por objeto acelerar la construcción de viviendas y reducir los trámites burocráticos.
Puedes leer el texto completo del proyecto de ley AQUÍ.
###
title: El representante Tran presenta una propuesta legislativa para reducir los costos de la vivienda para las familias del sur de California.

Grijalva, Kelly Blast Trump Administration’s Push for National School Voucher Scheme
    Friday, October 16, 2026
  
Tucson, AZ — Today, Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva and Senator Mark Kelly condemned new Treasury Department regulations advancing a national school voucher scheme created under Republicans’ Big Ugly Bill, warning that Arizona’s experience with universal school vouchers shows exactly what happens when taxpayer dollars are diverted to private schools without adequate oversight.
The Treasury Department recently released regulations implementing the federal school voucher tax credit established under H.R. 1. The program provides a tax credit of up to $1,700 for donations to eligible scholarship-granting organizations, including organizations supporting private and religious schools. The new regulations would double the credit for married couples.
In response, Senator Kelly introduced the Keep Public Funds in Public Schools Act, which would repeal the voucher scheme created under H.R. 1. Rep. Grijalva alongside Representatives Gwen Moore (WI-04), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), and Mark Pocan (WI-02) introduced the same legislation in the House.
“Arizona’s fraud-ridden school voucher program should serve as a warning to the rest of the country,” said Rep. Grijalva. “Instead, the Trump Administration is moving full steam ahead with a national voucher scheme while failing to include even basic safeguards to prevent taxpayer dollars from being wasted or abused. Congress must act to ensure taxpayer dollars strengthen the public schools that serve the overwhelming majority of America’s children, rather than subsidize privatization schemes rife with fraud.”
“Arizona is a clear example of the consequences of diverting taxpayer dollars to private school vouchers: fraud, benefits going to families who can already afford private school, and public schools losing funds they desperately need. Not to mention a giant hole blown in our budget,” said Sen. Kelly. “Now, the Trump administration wants to take that same approach nationwide. We should be investing in public schools that serve all kids, not expanding a voucher program that risks more waste and abuse.”
Arizona’s universal Empowerment Scholarship Account program now costs taxpayers more than $1 billion annually and has faced repeated allegations of waste, fraud, and abuse.
In one case, two out-of-state individuals pleaded guilty to creating dozens of fictitious “ghost students” and using forged documents to obtain more than $110,000 in taxpayer-funded voucher dollars. Other reporting has found voucher funds used for questionable purchases, including Disneyland trips, diamond rings, and lingerie.
###
title: Grijalva, Kelly Blast Trump Administration’s Push for National School Voucher Scheme
