*The garrison public affairs office translates summaries of local news articles for the convenience of non-Italian speaking community members. The information contained in these summaries is originally written by Italian news sources and does not reflect the opinion of U.S. Army Garrison Italy or any of its tenant commands. Direct any questions about the Italian news to the garrison public affairs office.*
Italian News from Vicenza – October 16, 2026
Salvini backs eastern TAV route, pledges to find fundings – October 16, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Italian Transport Minister Matteo Salvini has backed RFI’s preferred surface route for the eastern section of Vicenza’s high-speed rail line, effectively closing the door on alternative proposals, including a long tunnel. The plan includes doubling existing tracks, seven-meter noise barriers and a major overpass near Settecà. Salvini said the Vicenza-Padua section’s design should be ready by summer 2027, while approximately €4 billion must be secured. Despite opposition from Vicenza Mayor Giacomo Possamai and local representatives, Salvini insists engineers must choose the route, while his responsibility is securing funding. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
The extension of Viale Aldo Moro: 10 options and a “zero” – October 16, Corriere Veneto
Vicenza’s long-debated Viale Aldo Moro extension remains under review, with 10 options plus a no-build alternative. The technical feasibility study (Docfap) is expected by Dec. 31 and will assess three main solutions, involving Anconetta, Ospedaletto and a longer route near the Vicenza North tollbooth. Traffic surveys, environmental constraints and potential impacts on historic villas will guide the decision. The longest option would cover 5.4 kilometers and could include a public transport interchange. Bolzano Vicentino Mayor Lorenzo Cracco urges the administration to consider alternatives before endorsing a project. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Vicenza firefighters warn of critical staff and equipment shortages – October 16, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Vicenza firefighters have renewed calls for more personnel, vehicles and equipment following the Deroma fire. During a municipal commission hearing, the USB union denounced operational deficiencies, warning that simultaneous emergencies could overwhelm the system. Of 12 personnel on duty, only nine remain available after administrative assignments, while each team requires five firefighters. Staff shortages also affect provincial detachments, training and fire prevention. Equipment problems include an aging, unreliable aerial ladder, a missing truck and insufficient breathing apparatus. Unions urge municipal, provincial and regional authorities to secure concrete commitments. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Red‑Light enforcement returns to Dal Verme high‑risk junction – October 16, Il Giornale di Vicenza
The T-Red traffic camera will be reactivated at the intersection of Viale Dal Verme, Strada Sant’Antonino and Via Lamarmora after a two‑and‑a‑half‑year shutdown. The device, which catches red‑light violations, was halted in April 2024 when its rental contract expired. The city says the intersection has long been prone to accidents, prompting renewed monitoring to improve safety. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Bus station security tightened at SVT hub – October 16, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Vicenza officials have rolled out expanded security measures at the SVT bus station to prevent intrusions and protect passengers. Police patrols, private night security, upgraded lighting and time‑based gate closures are now in place as part of a coordinated plan developed by the province, SVT and the police. Surveillance cameras will be linked to the municipal control center, and full‑height gates will replace current barriers by year’s end. According to authorities, this enhanced monitoring is already reducing disturbances, especially during peak hours and weekend gatherings. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Chocolate festival in Vicenza’s historic center on Oct. 23-25 – October 16, Il Giornale di Vicenza
CioccolandoVi will sweeten Vicenza’s historic center Oct. 23–25 with 24 chocolate stands in Piazza dei Signori and Contrà Garibaldi. Now in its 21st year, the festival joins the #fuorimostra program linked to the upcoming “Italia Germania” exhibition in Basilica Palladiana. Most exhibitors are returning chocolatiers from across Italy, offering pralines, bars and drinks. New creations inspired by the exhibition debut at two stands. Activities include children’s workshops, an English puzzle game, a traveling play space, live music and an eco‑innovative “Choco Book” in Galleria San Lorenzo. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Vicenza unveils long‑hidden Valmarana garden and café – October 15, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Vicenza’s hidden Valmarana woodlands are open again after centuries behind closed gates. The restored garden at Villa Valmarana ai Nani features four themed paths, immersive sound installations, a treetop walkway and a restored pagoda with a four‑minute audiovisual experience. Visitors can also relax at the villa’s café, reopened in 2026. The site is accessible from Friday to Sunday from Via della Rotonda, or from Via Dei Nani. Tickets cost €8. More details at www.boscovalmarana.it. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Torri di Quartesolo Mayor redirects defamation payout to community mural – October 15, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Torri di Quartesolo Mayor Gianluca Ghirigatto pursued legal action after receiving insults and threats on social media following an April security blitz at a local venue. Citing the growing hostility toward public officials, he filed multiple complaints for reputational damage. One offender recently reached a financial settlement of about 2,000 euros. The mayor said the money will fund a new community mural in Marola, following a similar project in Torri, to promote respect and remind residents that online anonymity doesn’t justify harassment. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Ferrovieri neighborhood residents sound alarm over drug use – October 15, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Residents in Vicenza’s Ferrovieri neighborhood report escalating drug activity near an electrical cabin in Via Filzi, where groups of users have broken fencing and gathered to smoke substances in broad daylight. Locals say the problem began a month ago and intensified as nearby rail‑related construction displaced people from abandoned homes. Complaints also resurfaced in Viale Verona, where a street dispute among women drew police and renewed frustration over longstanding public‑order issues. Residents say repeated appeals to authorities have brought few results. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Christmas, Vicenza brings back video mapping but removes light cascade – October 15, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Vicenza will again use video mapping on the Basilica Palladiana for Christmas 2026, dropping the light cascade after last year’s unsuccessful mix of old and new displays. The projection will have a clearer Christmas theme, which residents had asked for. The show has drawn many visitors in recent years, and the city plans to connect it with the winter exhibition inside the Basilica. The Christmas market will run from Nov. 27 to Jan. 3, 2027, with wooden stalls returning to Piazza Biade and Corte dei Bissari. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
High pressure brings another warm, sunny stretch – October 15, Il Giornale di Vicenza
A strong high‑pressure system over much of Europe is keeping autumn at bay, blocking storms from entering the Mediterranean and keeping cold and rain away from northern Italy. Clear nights may still dip below 50°F. Clouds increase on Sunday, Oct. 18, as the system shifts toward the British Isles, lowering highs to around 68°F. Despite the season’s usual storminess, rain remains unlikely through next week. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Veneto autonomy: final agreement signed, parliamentary approval next – October 14, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and Veneto Governor Alberto Stefani signed the final agreement on differentiated autonomy, following government approval of the legislative bill. Regional governors from Lombardy and Piedmont also attended the meeting. The reform now requires approval by an absolute majority in both chambers of Parliament, with a vote targeted for late 2026 and early 2027. Regional League representatives welcomed the milestone, highlighting greater responsibility, efficiency and local control, particularly in healthcare. However, the approaching end of the legislature and the 2027 general elections create uncertainty over whether the reform can be completed in time. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Historic Veneto Villas open their doors across the Vicenza area – October 14, VicenzaToday
The fifth edition of the “Giornata della Ville Venete,” (Day of Villas of the Veneto) takes place October 17–18, offering extraordinary access to historic residences, Palladian villas, castles and monumental gardens across the Vicenza province. Visitors can explore Tiepolo’s frescoes, discover restoration projects, enjoy wine and food tastings, attend concerts and participate in family-friendly activities, workshops and garden experiences. Highlights include Villa La Rotonda, Villa Valmarana ai Nani, Villa Forni Cerato and Villa Pojana. Activities vary by venue, with reservations often required and some experiences subject to fees. The complete program, schedules, prices and booking information are available at https://www.giornatavillevenete.it/. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Asiago Foliage returns Oct. 17–18 with fall hikes and family fun – October 13, VicenzaToday
Asiago Foliage returns October 17–18, bringing autumn colors and seasonal activities to Asiago’s historic center. The two-day event features creative workshops, exhibitions, wooden games and activities for children and teenagers across several central squares and streets. Visitors can explore local agricultural products, wood carvings and nature-inspired art, while enjoying outdoor wellness activities, including barefoot walking, mindfulness and yoga. Guided excursions will showcase the Plateau’s autumn landscapes, with opportunities to explore mountain trails, visit mountain pastures and join mushroom-hunting outings with a mycologist. The event offers families and visitors an opportunity to experience the Plateau’s natural beauty and local traditions. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Abilmente returns to the Vicenza Fair – October 13, VicenzaToday
Abilmente, Vicenza’s popular creativity and Do It Yourself fair, takes place through Sunday, Oct. 18. The four-day event, featuring more than 400 exhibitor brands, expands the world of “making” by bringing together enthusiasts of embroidery, woodworking, textiles, and paper. A major highlight is the debut of “L’Officina del fai da te” (The DIY Workshop), a dedicated space for workshops with expert craftsmen in woodworking, decorating and 3D printing. The area will offer beginners demonstrations in crafting, decoration and small repairs. This year, the program will also introduce a dance performance taking place Saturday, Oct. 17, at 6:15 p.m. at the Teatro Palladio. The theater will host the MA.MA company’s performance “In piedi, signori, davanti a una donna” (Stand Up, Gentlemen, in Front of a Woman), addressing violence against women. Admission is €13 for adults, reduced €7 for children age 8 to 13 and free entry for children up to 8 years old. For more information visit https://www.abilmente.org/en/vicenza. (Summary by Laura Kreider)
Spritz thief strikes in Venice, targeting only cocktail ingredients – October 13, Tgcom.it
A Venice restaurant was hit by an unusual overnight break-in, with the thief stealing only ingredients used to make the city’s signature spritz. At Orient Experience in Campo Santa Margherita, the intruder forced the entrance and took the cash drawer along with about 10 bottles of Aperol, Campari and Select, leaving higher-value wines and liquors untouched. With no cameras or witnesses, the break-in caused nearly $1,000 in losses. Owners say it’s not the first time their restaurants have been targeted. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Caseificio Pennar opens new store in Vicenza – October 13, VicenzaToday
Caseificio Pennar, the historic Asiago dairy cooperative founded in 1927, opened a new retail shop Oct. 12 in Via Caimpenta, in Vicenza, near the Palladio shopping center. The store offers the cooperative’s award-winning mountain cheeses, including Asiago DOP Prodotto della Montagna, Tosela Pennar, Pennarone, Grana Padano and Gran Pennar di Montagna, along with ricotta, caciotte, butter and yogurt. Many cheeses are aged on spruce boards, a process that enhances aroma and flavor. The cooperative sources milk from about 50 farms and local alpine pastures. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Italy’s new Road Code cuts fines, tightens safety rules – October 13, Tgcom.it
On Oct. 12, Italy’s Cabinet approved a wide-ranging overhaul of the national Road Code, reducing many traffic fines while tightening penalties for dangerous behavior. The plan lowers several minimum sanctions, shortens the remote-notification deadline from 90 to 45 days and standardizes disability permits nationwide through a unified digital platform. Stricter measures target uninsured vehicles, powered bicycles, electric scooters and motorcycles, which will be allowed to use emergency lanes only at low speed during major delays. Consumer group Codacons argues the reforms will not improve safety without stronger enforcement. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Recent Italian News highlights
Crime falls in Vicenza, but cyber fraud surges – October 13, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Crime declined across Vicenza province in 2025, with reported offenses down 4.4 percent from the previous year, according to Il Sole 24 Ore’s annual crime index. Authorities recorded significant decreases in thefts, home burglaries, robberies and drug trafficking cases, helping place Vicenza 58th out of 106 Italian provinces for crime rates. However, cybercrime continued to rise sharply, with reports of fraud and online scams increasing 11 percent year over year to more than 5,300 cases. Extortion and property damage also rose, reflecting a broader shift from traditional crimes toward digital offenses. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Veneto appeals to overseas travelers amid short-term rental concerns – October 13, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Veneto showcased its growing appeal to international travelers during the 25th Buy Veneto tourism marketplace, which brought more than 150 overseas buyers to Venice, many from the United States, the United Kingdom, China and France. While tourism officials highlighted strong demand for experiences such as wine tours, cycling and cultural travel, hotel industry leaders warned that the rapid growth of short-term rentals is straining local communities. Federalberghi Veneto is calling for limits on new vacation rentals in heavily visited destinations, while regional officials continue to evaluate regulatory options. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Vicenza’s Filippi earns halal certification for four panettoni – October 13, Tgcom.it
Pasticceria Filippi, a longtime artisanal bakery near Vicenza, has become the first Italian panettone producer to obtain Halal certification for four varieties. The recognition, granted by Halal Italia, confirms that the products meet all required standards. The process included ingredient tracing, lab tests for alcohol and pork DNA, and on‑site inspections. Filippi says the move expands access to new markets while supporting inclusivity for consumers with specific dietary needs. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Vicenza traffic changes as Piazza De Gasperi closes for renovation – October 12, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Piazzale De Gasperi in Vicenza will be closed to traffic from Oct. 12 through Sunday as redevelopment works continue near the railway station. Viale Roma will operate one-way toward the station from Viale Verdi, with access to nearby homes, businesses and parking restricted to designated routes. On Corso San Felice, access between Piazzale Giusti and Piazzale De Gasperi will be limited to residents and local property users. Works include preparing the ground footprint for the Arco del Revese and final road paving. Four new bus stops are also planned, requiring temporary lane restrictions. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
San Bortolo Hospital records 1,644 births, defying regional trend – October 12, Il Giornale di Vicenza
San Bortolo Hospital in Vicenza recorded 1,644 births by the end of September 2026, an increase of 42 compared with the same period last year. The obstetrics and gynecology department, led by Dr. Marcello Scollo, continues to attract mothers from across the province, including women with high-risk pregnancies. Nearly 68 percent of mothers are Italian, while foreign mothers include women from Africa, Asia and the United States. Despite praise for medical care and staff professionalism, outdated facilities and limited space remain concerns. The hospital bucks Veneto’s declining birth trend, standing out among regional public healthcare facilities. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Beehive-inspired dessert wins creative title at Tiramisù World Cup – October 12, VicenzaToday
The 10th Tiramisù World Cup wrapped up in Treviso with international competitors showcasing both traditional and inventive versions of Italy’s iconic dessert. Marcos Muzzi, an apiarist from Brazil, claimed the top prize in the original recipe category. In the creative division, Italy’s Ciro Tommasini won with a raspberry compote, white chocolate and lemon‑honey tiramisù shaped like a beehive. Organizers said interest continues to grow, with 320 contestants from 33 countries and 130 certified tasting judges. Registration is already open for the 2027 event. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Traffic closures announced as major cycling events return to Vicenza – October 12, VicenzaToday
Vicenza is ready for the Giro del Veneto and Veneto Woman on Oct. 14, with thousands expected along the Monte Berico climb. Both races start in Verona and finish on Viale X Giugno. Officials warn of major traffic impacts: no parking along the route from 8:30 a.m. to 9 p.m., and rolling closures beginning at 10:30 a.m. on Viale Riviera Berica; Strada di Longara; Strada del Tormeno; Viale Sant’Agostino; Via Vaccari; Via Maganza; Viale Fusinato; Viale Dante and Viale Dieci Giugno. The event will showcase Vicenza’s strong cycling identity and global visibility. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
New bike path connects Vicenza and Torri – October 11, Il Giornale di Vicenza
A new cycling and pedestrian path linking Vicenza and Torri di Quartesolo officially opened in the San Pietro Intrigogna. The four-kilometer route follows the Tesina River embankment, connecting the Riviera Berica cycleway with Torri di Quartesolo. Officials said the path will promote safer, sustainable travel for commuters and recreational cyclists while strengthening regional mobility and expanding links between neighboring communities. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Artificial ski slope opens at Vicenza’s Peace Park – October 11, Il Giornale di Vicenza
An artificial ski slope will open this weekend at Vicenza’s Parco della Pace, offering children and families a chance to practice skiing without snow. The 30-meter-long outdoor track, funded and managed by local association Snow Kids Vicenza, will remain in place through Nov. 19. The recyclable surface is designed to protect the park’s grass and leave no lasting environmental impact. Free ski lessons and equipment will be available on weekends, while people can use the slope during the week. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Discover Marana’s black truffle through woods and historic villages – October 11, Il Giornale di Vicenza
The black truffle of Marana, known locally as scorzón, takes center stage in a traditional celebration in Crespadoro, in the upper Chiampo Valley. Visitors can explore a scenic walking route through forests, stream-carved valleys and historic mountain villages, including Marana and its astronomical observatory. The approximately 10-kilometer circular itinerary also features charming historic chapels, traditional stone terraces and a spectacular waterfall. The annual festival, organized by Marana Eventi, celebrates local culinary heritage with truffle displays, awards for the finest specimens, market stalls and a choral concert. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
U.S. benefactor reconnects with Italian roots – October 10, Il Giornale di Vicenza
A visit by U.S.-based entrepreneur Jim Sartori revived a long-standing bond between his family and the community of San Pietro Valdastico near Vicenza. Sartori is the grandson of Paolo Sartori, who emigrated to America in 1907 and later financed the town’s retirement home in 1949. Continuing that tradition, Jim Sartori supported the facility during the COVID-19 pandemic with medical supplies and recently donated $5,000 for residents’ well-being. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Montegalda’s Bell Museum offers a journey through centuries of sound – October 8, Il Giornale di Vicenza
The Veneto Bell Museum at Villa Fogazzaro-Colbachini in Montegalda houses one of Europe’s largest collections of bells. The museum preserves more than 200 bells from Italy and around the world. Exhibits trace the history of bell making from ancient China and Rome to modern times and is surrounded by a 95,000-square-meter historic park featuring century-old trees, manicured lawns and decorative bells. Guided tours are available by reservation every Saturday at 10 a.m. For information, call +39 0444–73 7526 or send an email to info@muvec.it. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Recent Italian News highlights
Vicenza opposes RFI’s chosen route for eastern high-speed rail plan – October 9, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Italian rail company RFI has informed the City of Vicenza that it will move forward with the final design for the eastern section of the high-speed rail (TAV) project using the surface-level track-doubling option and the Settecà flyover, citing strategic objectives and guidance from the Ministry of Infrastructure. Mayor Giacomo Possamai strongly opposes the plan, arguing it would have an unacceptable impact on the city. He is calling for a detailed assessment of the “Zero Option,” which would enhance rail capacity through technology rather than new tracks, and remains open to discuss alternatives. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Serial burglar identified but returns to stealing after police report – October 9, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Carabinieri in Altavilla Vicentina have identified and reported a 40-year-old Eastern European man suspected of a string of burglaries across the Vicenza area, but authorities say he resumed stealing days later. Investigators believe the suspect, nicknamed “Picoman,” may be linked to about 50 thefts targeting businesses and restaurants in Altavilla, Creazzo and Sovizzo. He was stopped after an attempted break-in at a laundry business, with surveillance footage and distinctive hand tattoos helping identify him. Police say he later struck a Sovizzo restaurant. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Vicenza tightens event rules after chaotic influencer gathering – October 9, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Authorities in Vicenza will impose stricter requirements on influencer-organized gatherings after a social media meetup drew hundreds of young people and descended into disorder at Campo Marzo last Saturday, Oct. 3. Officials said organizers had expected about 50 attendees, but police estimated a crowd of 400 to 500. The event, promoted by TikTok creator Hamza Messaf, ended with 10,000 euros worth of property damage and police intervention, though no injuries were reported. Future influencer events will be subject to the same authorizations, safety plans and security measures required for public entertainment events. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Vicenza unveils university hub plan centered on historic buildings – October 9, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Vicenza has launched its first comprehensive plan to redevelop nine publicly owned buildings, aiming to create a citywide university campus while revitalizing historic and underused properties. The agreement focuses on expanding student housing, academic facilities, cultural spaces and public services. Key sites include the San Biagio complex, Salvi Garden buildings, Palazzo Teatini and former government properties. City leaders say the initiative will boost education, tourism and economic development while breathing new life into long-neglected landmarks across the historic center. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
New Vicenza exhibit to honor artist Giandomenico Tiepolo – October 9, Il Giornale di Vicenza
A major exhibition at Gallerie d’Italia in Vicenza highlights the artistic legacy of Giandomenico Tiepolo, marking 300 years since his birth and exploring his emergence from the shadow of his father, celebrated painter Giambattista Tiepolo. Titled “Giandomenico Tiepolo: A New World,” the exhibition runs through Jan. 17, 2027, and features 68 works from leading international museums, including the Prado, the Louvre and the Morgan Library. Curators argue Giandomenico developed a distinctive style focused on everyday life, human experience and social observation. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Veneto opens the doors to Louis Vuitton shoe factory Oct. 17-18 – October 8, Corriere Veneto
Ever wondered how luxury shoes and high-end eyewear are made? During LVMH's Journées Particulières on Oct. 17-18, visitors can step inside two exclusive Veneto workshops normally closed to the public. In Fiesso d’Artico, artisans craft Louis Vuitton footwear through more than 200 meticulous steps. In Longarone, Thélios showcases the artistry behind luxury eyewear. The event offers a rare glimpse into generations of craftsmanship, innovation and attention to detail that transform creative visions into coveted fashion pieces. Walk-ins may be admitted as space permits. More info at www.lvmh.com/en/les-journees-particulieres-2026. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Italy’s oldest man, 109, thrives in Veneto’s Prosecco Hills – October 8, Corriere Veneto
At 109 years old, Angelo Peressini has become Italy’s oldest living man. The former artilleryman and electrician resides in San Pietro di Feletto, nestled among the UNESCO-listed Prosecco Hills of Veneto. Known locally as the “Angel of Light” for helping bring electricity to his village, Peressini credits kindness, helping others, and holding no grudges for his longevity. While Italy boasts about 23,000 centenarians, women dominate the ranks, accounting for roughly 82 percent of those aged 100 and older. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Parking upgrades by November after months of malfunctions – October 7, Il Giornale di Vicenza
After months of faulty machines, broken barriers and Telepass outages, Municipia Gestopark has begun the full overhaul of Vicenza’s parking network. The company, which manages 12 facilities and more than 1,700 spaces, is investing 1.15 million euros to replace hardware, software and access systems. The Fogazzaro lot is the first to reopen with new electric systems, Telepass gates and cash‑and‑card kiosks. Upgrades at the other parking areas will follow through November. Some smaller lots may shift to subscriber‑only access pending city approval. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Major Vicenza exhibition celebrates Italy-Germany cultural ties – October 7, Il Giornale di Vicenza
A major exhibition celebrating artistic ties between Italy and Germany was presented Oct. 6 at the Rome’s Foreign Press headquarters ahead of its Nov. 13 opening at Vicenza’s Basilica Palladiana. “Italy-Germany: Painting and Sculpture Between the 19th and 20th Centuries. From Canova to Kiefer” will feature 150 works by artists including Canova, Boccioni, Kandinsky and Kiefer. German Ambassador Thomas Bagger praised the project, while Mayor Giacomo Possamai highlighted its role in strengthening European identity. Italian President Sergio Mattarella is expected to attend the official inauguration in Vicenza. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Torri di Quartesolo, police officer scares off burglars – October 7, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Residents in Torri di Quartesolo were targeted by a group of burglars late Tuesday between 10 and 11 p.m. in several homes along Via Ancona, Via Udine and Via Bologna. The intruders, armed with a screwdriver and a powerful LED flashlight, attempted to force entry and intimidate homeowners. In one case, a police officer confronted the suspects after they tried to break into his property. He retrieved his service pistol and gave chase, prompting the burglars to flee. Carabinieri collected statements and opened an investigation. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
The Gladiator returns to the Arena: Russell Crowe in Marostica – October 7, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Oscar-winning actor Russell Crowe will bring his “Indoor Garden Party tour” to Marostica’s Piazza Castello on July 1, 2027, marking the only Italian stop on his European tour. Best known for the Gladiator, Crowe will take the stage as lead vocalist alongside a band of longtime musical collaborators. The concert opens the 13th Marostica Summer Festival Volksbank. Tickets start at €43 plus fees, while a premium €299.70 Meet & Greet package includes an exclusive encounter with Crowe; a platinum-seat ticket; dedicated entrance; welcome drink; commemorative pass; local food and wine basket. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Real estate market: room rentals triple in eight years – October 6, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Demand for room rentals in Vicenza has surged, with contracts nearly tripling from 433 in 2018 to 1,219 in 2025. Average monthly rents have risen to about €350, more than double the €150-200 typically charged eight years ago. Local experts cite rising housing costs, stagnant wages, increased worker mobility, and a growing university population as key drivers. At the same time, limited housing supply and the expansion of short-term tourist rentals are making it increasingly difficult for residents and students to find affordable accommodation. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Forever together: Venice allows pet ashes near owners' graves – October 6, Corriere Veneto
Venice has approved new cemetery regulations allowing pet owners to keep the ashes of their companion animals near their graves or burial niches. The measure recognizes the increasingly important role pets play within families and offers three options for placing pet urns in cemeteries. While current health regulations require separation between human and animal remains, local officials are seeking legal changes that could allow ashes to be kept together in the future. The policy applies to common pets such as dogs, cats, rabbits, birds and reptiles, while debate continues over whether horses should be included. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Vicenza seeks cat-shelter manager as project moves toward 2027 launch – October 5, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Vicenza has launched the next phase of its long-awaited cat shelter project, issuing a public call to identify a partner to help design, build and manage the facility near the municipal dog shelter in via Mantovani. Applications from third-sector organizations are due by Nov. 6. City officials hope construction can begin in 2027. The future cattery will provide shelter, medical care and support for feline colonies. Meanwhile, a council motion calls for stronger cat protection measures, including microchipping, sterilization programs and anti-stray initiatives. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
New Caldogno link road opens after 25-year wait – October 4, Il Giornale di Vicenza
A long-awaited link road designed to ease traffic through central Caldogno officially opened Oct. 4 after more than 25 years of planning. The €1.46 million project connects Via Monte Carega and Viale Pasubio, providing an alternative route for vehicles and heavy trucks while improving safety in the town center. The 420-meter roadway includes a pedestrian and bicycle path, new LED lighting, parking improvements and tree plantings. Local officials hailed the project as a transformative infrastructure investment expected to improve mobility and quality of life. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Rosà’s 89 kilometers of trails reveal history, nature and rural charm – October 4, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Rosà offers visitors a slow-paced way to discover its countryside through an extensive network of paths, trails and cycle routes that wind past irrigation ditches, Venetian villas, ancient boundary stones and rural landscapes. Designed by Nordic walking expert Stefano Piotto, the system spans 89 kilometers across nine main routes and three variants, suitable for walkers and cyclists of all abilities. Highlights include historic Roman-era roads, archaeological sites, natural areas and countryside landmarks, creating a unique blend of history, culture and outdoor recreation in the heart of the Veneto. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Vicenza revives San Lorenzo fountain – October 3, Il Giornale di Vicenza
The San Lorenzo fountain has returned to service after seven years, reopening as both a public landmark and a cooling refuge during summer heat. City officials inaugurated the restored fountain following 150,000 euros in maintenance work. The city hopes the fountain will help mitigate high temperatures while serving as a symbolic space for awareness campaigns marked by colored lighting. The fountain, first opened in 2004 as part of a broader redevelopment project, had faced years of breakdowns before being shut down. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Asiago Consortium wins landmark case against Citterio over misleading cheese label – October 3, Il Giornale di Vicenza
The Asiago PDO Cheese Protection Consortium has won a landmark legal battle against Italian meat producer Citterio over a product marketed in the United States as “Sopressata & Asiago Cheese.” Milan’s Court of Appeal ruled the labeling was misleading because the cheese used was not authentic Italian Asiago PDO. The decision prohibits the production, sale, import, export and advertising of the product when it suggests Italian origin or the distinctive qualities of Asiago PDO. The court also awarded damages, marking a significant victory against “Italian sounding” products in foreign markets. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Devastating fire at local plastic plant: towering flames cause million-euro damage – October 2, Il Giornale di Vicenza
A massive fire devastated the Deroma warehouse in Malo on the afternoon of Oct. 1, sending towering flames and a thick black smoke cloud visible for miles. The blaze reportedly started on the roof, where plastic flowerpots were stored, before rapidly spreading through the 20,000 square-meter facility. All employees were safely evacuated, with no injuries reported. More than a dozen fire engines, supported by a helicopter, battled the fire throughout the night. Authorities evacuated nearby families due to explosion risks from vehicles, batteries and solar panels inside the building. Environmental monitoring was activated, while damage is expected to amount to several million euros. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
New anti-smog measures take effect Oct. 1 – October 1, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Starting Oct. 1, Vicenza is enforcing stricter anti-smog measures to offset the one-year postponement of restrictions on Euro 5 diesel vehicles. Traffic limitations will now remain in place until 7:30 p.m., while heating in public and commercial buildings will be allowed only from Nov. 1 to April 12, instead of Oct. 15 to April 15. The ordinance also tightens rules on wood-, pellet- and biomass-burning stoves, with broader bans during pollution alerts. Additional measures under consideration include expanded remote work, cycling incentives and more frequent street cleaning. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Monte Berico seeks funds to restore and digitize historic porticoes – September 28, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Vicenza is seeking state-managed funding to complete restoration of the southern porticoes of Monte Berico and add a digital experience. The €1.75 million project includes conservative repairs, new waterproofing, surface cleaning and pavement restoration. A digital route with QR codes will highlight artworks depicting Jesus in the Garden of Gethsemane. The intervention targets the section built between 1746 and 1780. Vicenza previously secured €2.3 million for the northern stretch and hopes this second bid will fund the remaining work. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
San Bortolo tops national rankings for organ donation – September 28, Il Giornale di Vicenza
San Bortolo Hospital confirms its top national standing with 29 organ donors registered in 2026, thanks to strong awareness efforts by ULSS 8 and associations like Aido. The mix of DBD (Donor After Brain Death) and DCD (Donor After Circulatory Death) donors across Italy and Europe: four hearts, one lung, 17 livers, 28 kidneys, plus corneas and tissues. The most moving case is a two‑year‑old girl whose organs saved four children, a result of exceptional coordination and the hospital’s deeply rooted culture of solidarity. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Dal Molin: the deal with the US was anything but a formality – September 27, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Gian Marco Mancassola—former deputy editor‑in‑chief of Il Giornale di Vicenza and now director of TVA News—revisited the Dal Molin case during a public storytelling event held at Hangar 2 in the Peace Park Sept. 25. A witness of the period, he retraced how the proposed expansion of the U.S. military presence in Vicenza evolved from early reports in 2003 into a major civic mobilization by 2006, shaped by media, assemblies and cultural expression. The final decision, taken in Rome in 2007, allowed the project to proceed. Peace Park remains the most tangible legacy of a season now fading from public memory. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Delta to launch direct Venice-Boston service in 2027 – September 25, TVIweb
Delta Air Lines will launch a new nonstop route between Venice Marco Polo Airport and Boston Logan International Airport on May 8, 2027, expanding direct links between northeastern Italy and the United States. The service will operate four times weekly on an Airbus A330-300. Boston will become Delta’s third U.S. destination served directly from Venice, joining New York-JFK and Atlanta. According to SAVE Group, the Venice-Boston market exceeds 50,000 passengers annually and is currently the largest unserved European market for Boston. The route is expected to boost tourism, business ties, academic exchanges and family travel. (Summary by Angela Balbo)
Bassano enters the race for Italy’s 2029 capital of culture – September 25, Il Giornale di Vicenza
Bassano has officially submitted its bid for Italian Capital of Culture 2029, backed by 200 local organizations, over 40 municipalities and a strong Promoting Committee. Competition is intense, with 17 candidates nationwide. The slogan — “Culture has human intelligence” — frames a project centered on youth, heritage, landscape and innovation. Four pillars guide the dossier, aiming to leave lasting cultural infrastructure beyond 2029. Bassano’s strategy: transform its recognized heritage into a shared, future‑driven model connecting culture, young people, business, and territory. (Summary by Anna Ciccotti)
Veneto named among Lonely Planet’s top 50 travel destinations for 2027 – September 23, VicenzaToday
Lonely Planet has listed the Veneto among its 50 top global travel destinations for 2027, the only Italian region included in the guide. The award highlights Veneto’s diverse landscapes, from the Dolomites to the Po Delta, and its cities rich in art and history, including Verona, Vicenza, Padova and Treviso. The guide praises the region’s appeal for slower, less crowded travel, noting attractions such as the Prosecco Hills, the Euganean Hills and lake and coastal areas. Gastronomy also pla
title: Italian News Highlights

HONOLULU – United States Attorney Ken Sorenson announced that John Junior Fritz, 48, of Waimanalo, Hawaii, was sentenced yesterday by Senior United States District Judge J. Michael Seabright to 120 months in federal prison for possession with the intent to distribute methamphetamine, followed by 5 years of supervised release. According to court documents, in April 2025, Fritz was arrested by the Honolulu Police Department driving a stolen car that contained approximately two pounds of methamphetamine and other drug distribution paraphernalia. As part of his ongoing drug trafficking, Fritz obtained two to three pounds of methamphetamine every few days for distribution into the community and for his personal use.

While on pretrial release, Fritz absconded from Sand Island Treatment Center. He was arrested three months later and detained pending sentencing.

The Drug Enforcement Administration and the Honolulu Police Department investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Rebecca A. Perlmutter prosecuted the case.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.
title: Waimanalo Man Sentenced to Ten Years in Prison for Distributing Methamphetamine

text:
BUFFALO, N.Y.-U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Patrick Kerwin, 43, of Java Center, NY, pleaded guilty before U.S. District Judge John L. Sinatra, Jr. to possession of child pornography involving a prepubescent minor. The charge carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison and a $250,000 fine.

According to the plea agreement, on November 19, 2025, Lancaster Police officers encountered Kerwin at a local restaurant where he advised them that he had exchanged text messages with underage girls, possessed child pornography on his cell phone, and that he had been involved in previous “underage relationships.” Kerwin subsequently consented to the seizure and search of his cell phone and voluntarily agreed to be interviewed at the Lancaster Police Department, during which he admitted that he messaged underage girls using social media and encrypted applications. A forensic review of his cell phone recovered 13 images and 81 videos of child pornography. Some of the images and videos depicted the sexual abuse of an infant or toddler, as well as depictions of violence.

The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Maeve E. Huggins. The plea is the result of an investigation by the FBI, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Allen D. Davis, II and the Lancaster Police Department, under the direction of Chief William Gummo.

Sentencing is scheduled for February 15, 2027, before Judge Sinatra.
title: Java Center man pleads guilty to possession of child pornography

text:
Brad D. Schimel, First Assistant United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Wisconsin, announced a settlement with Miracle-Ear, Inc., and the Miracle-Ear Foundation to settle claims that they improperly obtained three loans through the Paycheck Protection Program (“PPP”). Miracle-Ear and its foundation agreed to pay $6,473,222 to resolve the government’s claims.

Congress enacted the PPP in March 2020 to provide emergency assistance to small businesses suffering from the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. The program was operated by the Small Business Administration (SBA) and allowed eligible small businesses and nonprofits to receive loans guaranteed by the federal government. If the borrower spent the funds on qualified expenses, the government repaid the loan on the borrower’s behalf. To qualify as a small business eligible for a PPP loan, a borrower and any affiliated companies generally could not employ more than 500 individuals. In its loan application, moreover, the borrower was required to certify that it was eligible for the PPP and that the information provided in the application was accurate.

Miracle-Ear distributes and sells hearing aids and associated products through stores owned by Miracle-Ear as well as stores owned and operated by franchisees. Miracle-Ear Foundation is a nonprofit organization that provides free hearing aids to low-income individuals. Miracle-Ear received a first-draw PPP loan in the amount of $1,962,000 in June 2020 and a second-draw PPP loan in the amount of $1,962,000 in February 2021. Miracle-Ear Foundation received a single PPP loan in the amount of $58,100 in May 2020.

Miracle-Ear is wholly owned by Amplifon (USA) Inc., which, in turn, is wholly owned by Amplifon S.p.A., an Italian public company with thousands of employees and annual sales exceeding 1.5 billion euros in 2020 and 2021. Miracle-Ear Foundation is likewise affiliated with Amplifon S.p.A. The government alleges that Miracle-Ear and its foundation falsely certified that they were eligible for the PPP loans. Specifically, the United States alleges that Miracle-Ear and its foundation were not eligible for their PPP loans because they were affiliated with Amplifon S.p.A. and that the Amplifon corporate group employed too many individuals for Miracle-Ear and its foundation to qualify for PPP loans. The United States further contends that Miracle-Ear provided false information in its loan applications to make it appear that Miracle-Ear was covered by an exemption to the SBA’s affiliation rules for “business concerns operating as a franchise.” That exemption only covered small businesses operating as a franchisee, not corporations like Miracle-Ear that issued franchises to small businesses.

“Congress created the PPP to aid American small businesses during the pandemic. Miracle-Ear and its foundation, however, were part of a large multinational corporate group with billions in annual revenue,” said First Assistant Schimel. “Miracle-Ear and its foundation, moreover, allegedly provided false information to the SBA to obtain these taxpayer funds. This settlement is part of our office’s ongoing efforts to hold corporations accountable when they submit false claims to obtain tax dollars.”

“The favorable settlement in this case is the product of enhanced efforts by federal agencies such as the Small Business Administration, as part of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, working with the U.S. Attorney’s Office and other federal law enforcement agencies to recover the product of this fraud as well as penalties. When whistleblowers uncover potentially fraudulent conduct, we work to recover SBA funds improperly obtained,” said SBA General Counsel Jennifer Prescott.

This civil settlement resolves claims brought in two cases under the qui tam or whistleblower provisions of the False Claims Act, which permit private parties to file an action on behalf of the United States and receive a portion of any recovery. The lawsuits were filed by Blockquote, Inc., and Mary Denler and are pending in the Eastern District of Wisconsin. In connection with the settlement, Blockquote, Inc., will receive $1,154,111.40.

Together with the SBA, Assistant United States Attorney Michael Carter represented the government in this matter. The settlement agreement states allegations only; Miracle-Ear, Inc. and Miracle-Ear Foundation do not admit liability for the allegations.

###

For further information contact: Public Affairs Officer Steve Caballero (414) 297-1700 Follow us on X
title: Miracle-Ear and its Foundation Agree to Pay over $6.4 Million to Resolve False Claims Allegations Concerning the Paycheck Protection Program

AC Dantzler, age 45, of Baton Rouge, Louisiana, was sentenced to 74 months in federal prison following his conviction for distribution of fentanyl and methamphetamine. U.S. District Court Judge Brian A. Jackson further sentenced Dantzler to serve four years of supervised release following his term of imprisonment.

According to admissions made during his plea, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives (ATF) received information from a confidential informant (CI) that Dantzler told the CI that he could supply the CI with fentanyl.

Subsequently, ATF was able to conduct a controlled purchase of one ounce of fentanyl from Dantzler for $1,300.

ATF once again used the CI to negotiate another controlled purchase of fentanyl from Dantzler and during this exchange, Dantzler also provided the CI with what he stated was methamphetamine for the CI to test to see if he wanted to purchase methamphetamine from Dantzler in the future.

U.S. Attorney Kurt L. Wall praised the work of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives. Assistant U.S. Attorney Paul L. Pugliese led the prosecution.
title: BATON ROUGE MAN SENTENCED TO 74 MONTHS IN FEDERAL PRISON FOR DISTRIBUTING FENTANYL AND METHAMPHETAMINE

Baltimore, Maryland – A New Jersey man is facing indictment, today, after using fire and explosive materials in a Maryland retail store.

Anthony John Rhodes, 37, of Short Pump, is charged with malicious destruction of property by fire. The charges stem from an incident in which Rhodes set a fire in an Elkton retail store during business hours while customers shopped.

Kelly O. Hayes, U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the indictment with Special Agent in Charge Charles Doerrer, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives (ATF), and Chief Caroll H. Spriggs, II, Office of the Maryland State Fire Marshal.

According to the indictment, on April 29, 2026, Rhodes maliciously damaged and destroyed the store building, along with its merchandise and inventory.

An indictment is not a finding of guilt. Individuals charged by indictment are presumed innocent until proven guilty at a later criminal proceeding.

If convicted, Rhodes faces a minimum of five years and a maximum of 20 years in federal prison. Actual sentences for federal crimes are typically less than the maximum penalties. A federal district court judge determines sentencing after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

U.S. Attorney Hayes commended the ATF and Office of the Maryland State Fire Marshal for their work in the investigation, along with Office of the State’s Attorney for Cecil County, for its valuable assistance. Ms. Hayes also thanked Assistant U.S. Attorney Victoria Liu who is prosecuting the federal case.

For more information about the Maryland U.S. Attorney’s Office, its priorities, and resources available to help the community, visit justice.gov/usao-md .

# # #
title: New Jersey Man Indicted on Arson Charges Connected to Retail Store Fire

David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, announced that VICTOR FRANCISCO BONILLA, also known as “Mostro,” 35, of Bridgeport, was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge Sarah F. Russell in New Haven to 120 months of imprisonment and five years of supervised release for trafficking cocaine.

According to court documents and statements made in court, an FBI Bridgeport Safe Streets Task Force investigation determined that a narcotics trafficking organization was distributing that distributed fentanyl, cocaine, and crack cocaine in southern Connecticut. Members of the organization regularly traveled to the Bronx, New York, to acquire kilogram quantities of fentanyl and deliver narcotics proceeds, and to Puerto Rico to acquire cocaine and ship it through the U.S. Mail to various addresses in Connecticut. During the investigation, the FBI Task Force and the U.S. Postal Inspection Service seized several packages containing a total of at least 16 kilograms of cocaine, and identified several more that likely contained narcotics.

The investigation revealed that between August and October 2024, Bonilla purchased distribution quantities of cocaine from a leader of the drug trafficking organization and sold the drug to his own customers. In 2025, Bonilla began receiving kilogram quantities of cocaine through the mail from a source in Puerto Rico and then supplied the drug to the organization and his own customers.

Bonilla has been detained since his arrest on September 10, 2025. On May 11, 2026, he pleaded guilty to conspiracy to distribute and to possess with intent to distribute five kilograms or more of cocaine.

This investigation is being conducted by the FBI Bridgeport Safe Streets Task Force and the U.S. Postal Inspection Service, with the assistance of the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Connecticut State Police, and the Bridgeport, Norwalk, Trumbull, Hartford, Fairfield, Shelton, Ansonia, Derby, Greenwich, Stamford, New Haven, Waterbury, and Louisville (Ky.) Police Departments. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Lauren C. Clark and Kenneth L. Gresham.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

ICYMI | HUD Convenes Faith, Business, and Government Leaders in Grand Rapids to Promote Opportunity Zones Collaboration
October 16, 2026
Grand Rapids, Mich. - U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development’s (HUD) Center for Faith, in conjunction with the HUD Great Lakes Regional team, hosted a conference with leaders from the faith community, business sector, and federal, state, and local government to encourage them to participate in economic and community development within Opportunity Zones (OZs). The speakers emphasized the important role faith-based organizations play in family formation and community revitalization, especially in underserved communities in OZs.
The “Opportunity Zones: Economic Development and Community Revitalization by the Power of Faith” conference featured panels on topics such as business opportunities in OZs, OZ project funding, attainable housing options, federal government resources, and the involvement of faith organizations in their communities.
“Opportunity Zones are one of the most effective tools we have to bring private investment into communities that need it most,” said HUD Great Lakes Regional Administrator Duey Stroebel. “When investors, developers, and faith leaders come together around a shared vision, we can make real gains for families and neighborhoods across Michigan. The engagement we saw today reflects what is possible when the power of faith is paired with sound economic policy.”
This landmark initiative, established in 2017 by the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, has poured more than $100 billion of private investment into OZs, making it one of the largest economic development programs in history. OZs have lifted more than one million Americans out of poverty, spurred the creation of more than half a million jobs, and led to the construction of more than 400,000 housing units in distressed communities.
Under President Trump’s transformational Working Families Tax Cuts Act, OZs have been made permanent. Enhanced incentives, such as a rolling designation cycle, expanded investment incentives for underserved rural communities, and a 10-year investment timeline will build on the program’s immense success.
“OZs are not a top-down government effort to revitalize communities, nor are they handouts. They are long-term investments created through public-private partnerships that give a hand-up to vulnerable Americans to help them achieve self-sufficiency,” said HUD Assistant Secretary of Community Planning and Development Ronnie Kurtz. “As communities prepare for new OZ designations, we must understand that OZs are not just about bringing jobs or lifting wages, they are about breathing new life into communities that have often been ignored or left behind.”
“We want to thank HUD for this incredible event, especially being able to network with faith-based organizations,” said Executive Vice President of UMH Properties Daniel Landy. “UMH really wants to build affordable housing communities in Opportunity Zones, and the important word there is ‘community.’ Faith-based organizations know how to build communities. This was a great event to help revitalize communities in OZs and build partnerships with faith-based organizations.”
“It’s great to see faith-based organizations, businesses, and non-profits come together around the same table discussing ways we can use each other’s strengths to advance the community,” said CEO of Mel Trotter Ministries Chris Palusky. “And that could be through affordable housing, jobs, or investment in communities. It was very heartening to see that there was this commitment.”
“I am very thankful to HUD for coming across the country to Michigan. I love the fact that DC is paying attention to the local and state level,” said Chairman of the Board of the Michigan Christian Chamber of Commerce Rodney Sanderson-Smith. “Every speaker had great wisdom, great insight, and had real, practical, hands-on information to share. My takeaway is that there is great opportunity here for us to come together to make a significance difference that is going to change a legacy. It was inspiring to see that some of the speakers had come from homelessness to building homes. I really hope HUD does more of these conferences so we can continue to keep the momentum going.”
This was the fifth conference in a series of national conferences hosted by HUD's Center for Faith. Learn more about Opportunity Zones, the conferences, and how the faith community can be involved HERE.
HUD Regional Administrator Duey Stroebel delivers presentation on how Opportunity Zones advance economic and community development.
HUD Assistant Secretary Ronnie Kurtz delivers the keynote address on self-sufficiency and how faith-based organizations can be involved in community revitalization.
Matt Temkin, Co-Founder of Greatwater Opportunity Capital, speaks about the great impact Opportunity Zones have on communities and housing.
The “Faith in Action in Opportunity Zones” panelists outline how houses of worship can repurpose their surplus property to address community needs.
The “Attainable Housing Options in Opportunity Zones” panelists discuss innovative housing solutions, such as manufactured and modular housing.
Faith-based organizations join HUD’s growing “Work and Dignity Coalition.”
Follow @SecretaryTurner on X, FB, and Instagram.
title: ICYMI | HUD Convenes Faith, Business, and Government Leaders in Grand Rapids to Promote Opportunity Zones Collaboration

U.S. CONGRESSMAN EVERTON BLAIR DEMANDS IMMEDIATE RELIEF FOR HIGH HOUSING COSTS; COSPONSORS THREE BILLS
Media Contact:
Allison Phipps, Allison.Phipps@mail.house.gov; Amya Enlow, Amya.Enlow@mail.house.gov
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman Everton Blair Jr. (GA-13) called out Congressional Republicans and Donald Trump for ignoring the nation’s escalating housing crisis, highlighting the direct toll that policy inaction is taking on families across Georgia’s 13th Congressional District.
In GA-13, rampant source-of-income discrimination remains an often insurmountable barrier to housing stability. Outside of Atlanta proper, current law fails to prevent landlords from turning away Section 8 voucher holders, leaving low-income families unable to secure stable housing even when they possess federal rental assistance.
"Housing costs everywhere have risen OUT OF CONTROL. And a major barrier we face here in GA-13 is widespread voucher discrimination," said Congressman Blair. "When landlords turn away Section 8 recipients simply because of how they pay rent, it leaves working families stranded. We must pass federal protections to end this practice once and for all."
This local reality is part of a broader national housing crisis fueled by an unacknowledged recession and an unsustainable cost of living. Reckless tariffs continue to drive up costs for raw building materials, hindering new construction across the country. Meanwhile, under the Republican’s One Big Ugly Bill many of the critical consumer-friendly housing tax credits that were passed under the Inflation Reduction Act have been eliminated. At the same time, international conflicts and the Administration’s haphazard use of tariffs as a staple of their thoughtless foreign policy, are driving up costs across the board. This not only increases the cost of building materials, but also daily essentials like utilities, groceries, and rent, leaving working families struggling to stretch every paycheck.
Rather than addressing these hardships, Donald Trump and his administration have shown complete contempt for working families. Instead of delivering relief, they have actively moved to gut core Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) offices and programs and refused to embrace comprehensive bipartisan solutions like the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which passed into law with no help or support from the President.
"Housing is a human right. People are struggling," Congressman Blair emphasized. "Eviction is the last sign, but it takes place after a long cycle of policy inaction and economic insecurity. We cannot allow families to be priced out of places to sleep while Congress ignores them."
To directly address these compounding pressures, Congressman Blair has co-sponsored three major federal initiatives:
- H.R. 6771 – The Housing Crisis Response Act of 2025: This legislation invests directly in constructing and rehabilitating affordable apartments, expanding housing vouchers, and improving living conditions in rural and Native communities. It provides critical funding to remediate hazardous living conditions like lead paint and toxic mold, offers down payment grants for first-generation homebuyers, and funds energy-efficient building upgrades to permanently lower monthly utility bills. [Full Text]
- H.R. 4872 – The Ending Homelessness Act: With national data showing a national shortage of 7.1 million affordable homes and over 770,000 unhoused individuals, this bill transforms the Housing Choice Voucher program into a universal federal entitlement, expands permanent supportive housing, and institutes a nationwide federal ban on housing discrimination based on source of income and veteran status. [Full Text]
- H.R. 4069 - The Down payment Toward Equity Act: This proposed legislation creates a $100 billion federal grant program offering direct financial aid at closing for first-time, first-generation homebuyers. Eligible buyers can use these grants for down payments, closing fees, or interest rate buydowns to significantly lower upfront costs and monthly mortgage payments. By targeting buyers without access to generational family wealth, the bill removes the primary barrier to purchasing a home, restoring homeownership opportunities and helping narrow the racial wealth gap. [Full Text]
Congressman Blair urges House Leadership to bring H.R. 6771, H.R. 4872 and H.R. 4069 to the House floor for an immediate vote. It is time for Congress to do its job, set aside partisan stalling, and deliver real, immediate relief to vulnerable and struggling Americans across the country.

FORT BUCHANAN, Puerto Rico — The Puerto Rico Air National Guard’s 156th Wing basketball team, the Aim High Ballers, recently defeated the Shinigami team 77-74 to capture the 2026 Fort Buchanan Summer Jam Basketball League championship at the installation’s Physical Fitness Center, concluding eight weeks of competition that brought together military personnel, federal employees and community members through sports.
Fort Buchanan’s Morale, Welfare and Recreation program organized the tournament to promote physical fitness, sportsmanship and camaraderie while strengthening relationships among military organizations and the broader installation community.
Six teams participated, representing organizations including the U.S. Coast Guard, Army Reserve, Puerto Rico National Guard and sponsored community groups. The league also featured Joint Forces, a team composed of players from different organizations.
The championship delivered a thrilling finish as Derick Osorio sank two free throws in the closing minutes to help the Aim High Ballers secure their three-point victory. Osorio led all scorers with 29 points and earned the league’s Most Valuable Player award, while teammate Luis Gabriel Tapia contributed 23 points.
For Tapia, who joined the team late in the regular season, the experience extended beyond basketball.
“This was my first tournament with the team. I joined near the end of the regular season after my friend Rafael Martínez invited me,” Tapia said in Spanish. “The guys welcomed me and made me feel comfortable with the group.”
The tournament reflected Fort Buchanan’s role as more than a military installation, providing opportunities for service members, civilian employees, families and community participants to connect through shared interests.
“Basketball is one of our most popular sports. It’s part of our community,” said Roberto Fernández, Fort Buchanan’s business operations and community recreation officer.
Although admission was free and games were open to the public, spectators primarily included families, friends and colleagues who gathered to support their teams.
During the awards ceremony, organizers presented the championship trophy to the Aim High Ballers, introduced the league’s first MVP trophy and recognized both finalist teams with medals.
The basketball league forms part of Fort Buchanan MWR’s year-round recreational sports program, which includes softball, volleyball and flag football when participation permits.
Through programs like Summer Jam, Fort Buchanan continues to provide opportunities that promote wellness, build relationships across military organizations and connect the installation with the community it serves.
For more information about sports and recreational programs at the Army’s home in the Caribbean, call 787‑707‑3767 or download the My Army Post (MAPA) app to explore activities and resources from wherever you are.
Fort Buchanan supports approximately 15,000 military personnel, including active-duty Soldiers, Army Reserve, Puerto Rico National Guard, Marine Corps Reserve and Navy Reserve members. The installation’s mission is to enable readiness and facilitate the deployment of forces anytime, anywhere.
title: Fort Buchanan Basketball League Crowns New Champion as Community Engagement Grows

HONOLULU – United States Attorney Ken Sorenson announced that Al Justin Carter, 24, of Las Vegas, Nevada, was indicted on October 15, 2026, with Coercion and Enticement of a Minor. Before being indicted, Carter was also charged by criminal complaint and arrested on October 14, 2026. Carter is scheduled to appear for a detention hearing on October 20, 2026.

According to the unsealed criminal complaint and other court records, on December 16, 2024, Carter persuaded and coerced a minor victim, who lived in Hawaii and was 13 years old at the time, to make a sexually explicit video of herself and send that video to Carter over the internet. Carter told the minor victim that if she did not send him the sexually explicit video, he would make public other sexually explicit videos Carter had in his possession that featured the minor victim.

If convicted, Carter faces up to life in prison, a $250,000 fine, plus a term of supervised release.

The charge in the indictment and criminal complaint are merely accusations, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. In the case of conviction, any sentence would be imposed by a United States District Judge based on the statutory sentencing factors and the advisory United States Sentencing Guidelines.

The FBI is investigating the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Michael Nammar is prosecuting the case.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC .
title: Las Vegas Man Charged with Blackmailing Child into Producing Child Pornography

Congressman Don Davis Calls on FCC to Preserve the E-Rate Program
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Don Davis (NC-01) sent a letter to Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chairman Brendan Carr calling on the FCC to protect the E-Rate Program for schools and libraries. The E-Rate Program helps schools in rural communities afford the reliable broadband connectivity their students need.
“For nearly 30 years, E-Rate has helped give students in rural communities, including across eastern North Carolina, the tools they need to learn and succeed. Since 1998, North Carolina’s public schools and libraries have received more than $1 billion in E-Rate discounts, helping our state to become the first to connect all K-12 classrooms to high-speed broadband,” said Congressman Don Davis.
North Carolina’s Department of Public Instruction reports that for every dollar of state funding spent on E-Rate-eligible goods and services, schools received over three dollars in value in Fiscal Year 2025, and that in 2024 the state recouped 99 percent of the fees the Commission collected from North Carolina residents and businesses.
E-Rate provided about $30 million to public school districts in North Carolina's First Congressional District from 2021 through 2025.
"If the FCC pulls back on E-Rate, we will be at risk of losing vital services many of our families and rural communities depend on," added Davis.
Congressman Davis also called on the FCC to restore E-Rate program support for school bus Wi-Fi and internet hotspot services.
The full letter is available HERE.

Statement from Office of Congressman Moulton Regarding Suspicious Letter Received in Mail
SALEM. MA — Today, Congressman Seth Moulton’s (MA-06) District Office in Salem, Massachusetts received a suspicious letter in the mail matching descriptions of previously reported suspicious mail sent to Congressional and election officials nationwide. The letter was addressed to “Seth Moulton” and had the same return address as letters received by other officials on October 15, 2026. An image of the letter is attached.
Out of an abundance of caution, using the guidance given by the House Sergeant at Arms in response to the nationwide reports and investigation, Congressman Moulton’s staff did not open the letter and instead, immediately reported the letter to Salem Police Department (SPD) and the US Capitol Police. The FBI was subsequently notified. 
SPD officers and FBI agents came to the Salem District Office to investigate the letter. During their examination of the letter, law enforcement discovered a white, powdery substance inside. Subsequent testing did not identify any substances of concern.
The Congressman deeply appreciates the quick and thorough response of the Salem Police Department, FBI, U.S. Capitol Police, and other law enforcement officials involved.

“Tôi cảm thấy nhẹ nhõm khi Orange County và GKN đạt được thỏa thuận đặt quyền lợi của người dân và các chủ doanh nghiệp nhỏ bị ảnh hưởng do lệnh di tản bắt buộc hồi Tháng Năm lên hàng đầu,” Dân Biểu Derek Trần cho biết. “Tôi hy vọng thỏa thuận này sẽ sớm được tòa phê chuẩn để có thể bắt đầu tiếp nhận hồ sơ yêu cầu bồi thường, đồng thời nhanh chóng cung cấp khoản hỗ trợ tài chính và hoàn trả các chi phí cần thiết cho những người bị ảnh hưởng. Congresswoman Schrier, Senator Murray Visit Washington State Fire Training Academy, Affirm Commitment to Invest in Wildfire Prevention and Response
***PHOTOS AND B-ROLL HERE***
North Bend, WA–Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) and Senator Patty Murray (D-WA) met with leaders and firefighters from Washington State Department of Natural Resources and Washington State Patrol at the Washington State Fire Training Academy to tour their facilities and hear about what additional federal resources and policies could better support on-the-ground efforts to prevent and respond to wildfires and structural fires.
The lawmakers were joined by: Dave Upthegrove, Commissioner of Public Lands at Washington State Department of Natural Resources (DNR); Chad Cross, State Fire Marshal; Chief John R. Batiste, Washington State Patrol (WSP); and leaders from the Washington State Fire Academy, law enforcement, and DNR.
“Communities in the Eighth District and across Washington state are reeling from the damage of this season’s devastating wildfires that threatened lives, property, and businesses,” said Congresswoman Schrier. “I was grateful to join Senator Murray and local leaders today to thank our first responders and discuss the federal resources our state needs to recover from and prevent catastrophic fires. In Congress, I’ll keep supporting our firefighters, bolstering local response efforts, and expanding fire prevention.”
“Washington state just suffered one of the worst wildfire seasons in history. That’s why I came here to listen to the people who managed these fires and understand what they need to continue this vital work. And we are hearing more and more now that wildfire season is year-round—so we need to be preparing for it that way as well,” said Senator Murray. “Now we aren’t just facing more environmental threats that worsen wildfires, we are also facing a President who has severely weakened the Forest Service and other critical agencies—from pushing out thousands of critical staff, blocking funding for crucial programs, and chaotically changing rules and procedures on a dime—Trump has left us worse off and less prepared to prevent future wildfires. But I am fighting back, tearing up his budget, and making sure we protect funding for the Forest Service and USDA so they can continue doing the hard work to prevent and fight wildfires. When we invest in fire preparedness, we save lives and communities. The Washington State Department of Natural Resources and Washington State Patrol do incredible work to keep people safe. For my part, I will not stop pushing back hard for Washington state, our public lands, and for wildfire preparedness, prevention, and safety.”
2026 was one of Washington state’s worst wildfire seasons on record, with fires causing severe damage and devastating lives. Weather conditions, exacerbated by extended drought, heat, and wind, caused over 900,000 acres, or 1,400 square miles, to burn across Washington state – taking homes and lives. Three massive fires broke out and tore through neighborhoods across Spokane, the Old Trails Fire burned in northwest Spokane, the Autumn Lane Fire burned near Nine-Mile Falls, and the Fairview Fire burned in Mead.
In the Eighth District, the Little Giant, Three Queens, Sisi, King, Goat, and West Fork fires – among others – devastated communities, property, livestock, and businesses. The damages from this wildfire season continues to overwhelm state, local, Tribal, nonprofit, and private-sector capabilities.
###
title: Congresswoman Schrier, Senator Murray Visit Washington State Fire Training Academy, Affirm Commitment to Invest in Wildfire Prevention and Response
