Reps. Castro, Ciscomani, Espaillat Renew Push to Honor Hispanic-Serving Institutions
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Reps. Joaquin Castro (TX-20), Congressional Hispanic Caucus Vice Chair of Diversity and Inclusion, Juan Ciscomani (AZ-06), and Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, re-introduced a bipartisan resolution to honor Hispanic-Serving Institutions (HSIs) and uplift their important work shaping the landscape of American higher education.
“Quality education is the foundation of opportunity in this country,” said Congressman Castro (TX-20). “This bipartisan resolution honors the contributions of hundreds of Hispanic-Serving Institutions nationwide, including the 112 such institutions here in Texas. These places of learning empower students and help young people overcome barriers to thrive. I thank the educators, faculty administrators, and staff who work tirelessly each day to ensure that HSIs can support and provide opportunities to millions of students.”
“Hispanic-Serving Institutions are opening doors to opportunity and helping more students achieve the American Dream,” said Congressman Ciscomani (AZ-06). “From Cochise College, Pima Community College, and Eastern Arizona College in my district our three state Universities - UofA, ASU, and NAU, these institutions are giving students, including many who are the first in their families to attend college, a path to a brighter future. I’m proud to support this bipartisan resolution recognizing National Hispanic-Serving Institutions Week and celebrating the vital role these schools play in strengthening Arizona’s communities and workforce.”
“Higher education is a critical pathway to economic opportunity and Hispanic Serving Institutions have opened doors for millions of Latino and Hispanic students to pursue college degrees,” said Congressman Espaillat (NY-13). “New York State is home to nearly 40 two- and four-year HSIs that serve almost 300,000 students. Unfortunately, the massive federal funding cuts and legal attacks from the Trump Administration have left many students and faculty without a clear path forward. This resolution reaffirms our commitment to protecting these communities and HSIs’ crucial work to support Latino and Hispanic students across the nation.”
“During HSIs Week, HACU joins colleges and universities across the country to recognize and raise awareness of the vital work our 645 HSIs do to expand access to education, advance opportunity, promote equity and fairness, and strengthen our communities,” said HACU President and CEO Dr. Antonio Flores.
The resolution uplifts HSIs by:
- Recognizing the achievements and goals of Hispanic-Serving Institutions across the United States;
- Expressing support for the designation of the week beginning on September 14, 2026, as “National Hispanic-Serving Institutions Week”; and
- Calling on the people of the United States and interested groups to observe the week with ceremonies, activities, and programs to demonstrate support for Hispanic-Serving Institutions in honor of Hispanic Heritage Month.
The resolution’s cosponsors include: Reps. Pete Aguilar, Nanette Barragán, Julia Brownley, Salud Carbajal, Greg Casar, Joaquin Castro, Juan Ciscomani, Gilbert Cisneros, Jim Costa, Lou Correa, Jasmine Crockett, Henry Cuellar, Mark DeSaulnier, Veronica Escobar, Adriano Espaillat, Dwight Evans, Teresa Leger Fernandez, Laura Friedman, Maxwell Frost, Chuy García, Robert Garcia, Sylvia Garcia, Jimmy Gomez, Vicente Gonzalez, Adelita Grijalva, Pablo José Hernández, Sara Jacobs, Hank Johnson, Robin Kelly, Ro Khanna, Raja Krishnamoorthi, Mike Levin, Ted Lieu, Lucy McBath, LaMonica McIver, Analilia Mejia, Rob Menendez, Kevin Mullin, Seth Moulton, Eleanor Holmes Norton, Jimmy Panetta, Scott Peters, Delia C. FORT DRUM, New York – At the Guthrie Army Health Clinic, healthcare professionals rely on complex medical technology and equipment to diagnose, monitor, treat and support healthcare delivery to the more than 33,000 Soldiers, family members, and retirees of the Fort Drum community.
Behind every laboratory centrifuge, dental sterilizer, and diagnostic device, is a small team of Medical Maintenance Soldiers and one civilian working to ensure the equipment Guthrie’s clinicians rely on is safe, functional and ready when needed.
“If you don’t hear from us, perhaps that’s a good thing,” said Sgt. 1st Class Cesar Sanchez, Guthrie’s Medical Maintenance chief and biomedical equipment repair technician. “It either means you have optimal equipment that never breaks down, or we’ve been conducting our scheduled service, our preventive maintenance.”
Having spent 19 years as a biomedical equipment specialist, Sanchez recently took the helm of Guthrie’s Medical Maintenance team, driving significant improvements in how the shop supports patient care through rigorous inspection, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair.
Sanchez said he understands the vital link between patient care and the need for dependable equipment to carry out that care.
“Our job here is to maintain all those medical devices and ensure that they are patient-ready, that they don’t cause any patient injury,” he said. “We also have a scheduled maintenance program for those devices to continue, once again, for that patient care.”
Sanchez said regular maintenance is detailed, often technical, and largely invisible to the patients and staff who depend on it.
When you conduct routine maintenance, “Just like you would on a vehicle, your vehicle will not break down,” Sanchez said. “In this case, your equipment will never go down.”
Maj. Michelle S. Bement, chief of Guthrie’s Logistics Division, who oversees the Medical Maintenance department, said Medical Maintenance is a critical part of the broader logistical operation that keeps the organization running smoothly.
“In order for our providers to be able to administer the proper level of care to our patients, they need to have the right supplies on hand with their equipment up to standard and fully operational,” Bement said. “There is a lot of behind-the-scenes synchronization that Logistics is involved in to make that happen.”
While different logistics functions can often assist one another, Medical Maintenance’s specialized qualifications make its role especially important, she added.
“Medical Maintenance is the most integral piece of logistics because in many other areas we can cover down for another,” Bement said. “That isn’t the case in Medical Maintenance because of their special qualifications.”
When equipment does fail, the team is positioned to respond quickly, determine whether it can be corrected on site, arrange for new parts if needed, and coordinate manufacturer support if necessary, limiting the time equipment remains nonfunctional.
As medical devices become increasingly interconnected, Medical Maintenance relies on coordinated support across multiple departments and specialties to distinguish equipment malfunctions from network or infrastructure issues.
“It’s working in coordination with facilities, IT, and basically all the other departments for us to be able to provide them with the support they need,” Sanchez said.
For departments such as the Guthrie laboratory, Medical Maintenance's support is essential for day-to-day operations.
“Our centrifuges, microscopes, cooling units and processing systems are required to be calibrated and serviced at least annually to confirm the reliability of the devices we use on a daily basis,” said Tina Allen, chief of the Guthrie laboratory. “Without the inspections and services, the systems could fail and cause unnecessary troubleshooting by the laboratory staff.”
Bement notes that strong communication is essential to balance scheduled maintenance with unpredictable work orders, requiring technicians to carefully prioritize repairs while keeping departments informed. It is a proactive approach that Allen said she appreciated during a recent round of annual equipment checks that occurred without disrupting lab operations.
“The workload is always high and unpredictable,” Bement said. “The Medical Maintenance team balances professionalism with updating the customers on the current situation and where their issue falls within the overall priorities.”
For Sanchez’s Soldiers, the ever-evolving environment of medical technologies requires more than familiarity with individual devices. Biomedical technicians learn troubleshooting methods, how to interpret technical manuals and schematics, and how to adapt as equipment evolves.
New equipment models and networked systems mean the education continues long after Soldiers leave initial training. And the ability to think critically and find “outside-the-box” solutions is a defining trait of the profession, according to Sanchez.
“We’ll look at a problem, and we’ll try to find a solution three or four different ways to identify the best solution, Sanchez said. “Sometimes we think of stuff that some people might not have thought of yet.”
While their day-to-day work may not always be visible, their impact is felt throughout the entire Guthrie AHC footprint. Equipment is inspected, repairs are coordinated, and patient care continues with minimal interruption thanks in large part to the routine, yet complex work of the Medical Maintenance team.
That quiet effectiveness is precisely the point, said Sanchez. While patient care continues throughout the clinics, Sanchez and his team keep the technological foundation solid so care can continue without interruption.
title: Healthcare’s Hidden Heroes: How Guthrie’s Medical Maintenance Team Keeps Patient Care on Track

SANTA ANA, California – An Orange County man who was the founder and CEO of a private equity fund was sentenced today to 33 months in federal prison for defrauding hundreds of investors out of approximately $63 million via a promissory note scam.

Marco Giovanni Santarelli, 57, of Laguna Niguel, was sentenced by United States District Judge Fred W. Slaughter, who also ordered him to pay $63,165,357 in restitution.

Santarelli pleaded guilty in October 2025 to one count of wire fraud.

According to court documents, Santarelli founded and was the CEO of Norada Capital Management (NCM), a Laguna Niguel-based private equity fund. From June 2020 to June 2024, Santarelli solicited hundreds of investors nationwide to invest in unsecured promissory notes ranging from $25,000 to $500,000. He promised via marketing a high-yield monthly interest rate – approximately 12% to 17% – over three to seven years.

Santarelli told investors they would receive monthly interest payments from income generated from five categories of businesses in which NCM would invest their money, including e-commerce, real estate, Broadway shows, and cryptocurrency.

Via webinars, Santarelli promised that the notes were backed by diversified assets under management and offered steady, predictable monthly returns. He further promised that NCM was to be a “hands-off passive investment,” perfect for retirement funds, court documents state.

Santarelli also provided balance sheets to investors listing the status of the assets, liabilities, and equity of NCM to the note holders, which listed the total asset value between $143.3 million and $224 million.

In fact, NCM did not pay the promised returns and interest payments. Instead, the fund invested in risky assets that did not provide the promised safety and security, was unprofitable, had very little return on investment, and a large amount of debt. The balance sheets sent to investors hid more than $90 million in debt and included inflated assets. In Ponzi-scheme fashion, Santarelli made interest payments to investors using other investors’ money.

In total, Santarelli caused more than 400 investors to lose approximately $63 million.

Homeland Security Investigations and the FBI investigated this matter with assistance from the United States Securities and Exchange Commission. Federal law enforcement has seized more than $5 million in proceeds connected to this scheme and continues to look for additional assets.

Chief Assistant United States Attorney Jennifer L. Waier prosecuted this case.
title: Former CEO of O.C.-Based Private Equity Fund Sentenced to Nearly 3 Years in Federal Prison for Running $63 Million Promissory Note Scam

Drug Dealer Selling Methamphetamine Near Playground Sentenced to Federal Prison
WHEELING, W.Va. – A Wheeling, West Virginia man will spend the next five years in federal prison for selling methamphetamine near a playground, announced U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey.
Matthew Luff, 42, sold more than 13 grams of methamphetamine near Heritage Port Playground in Wheeling. Luff has multiple prior convictions, including burglary, drug possession and trafficking, and obstructing justice.
Assistant U.S. Attorney Clayton Reid prosecuted the case on behalf of the government.
The Drug Enforcement Administration and the Ohio Valley Drug Task Force, a HIDTA-funded initiative, investigated.
This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime, and repel the invasion of illegal immigration.
U.S. District Judge John Preston Bailey presided.

text:
Action Disrupts Iraqi Bank Enabling Iranian Sanctions Evasion and Cuts Off Key Foreign Currency Lifelines
WASHINGTON—Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury disrupted Iran’s efforts to infiltrate the international financial system through an Iraqi bank that also supports Iran’s terrorist proxy militia groups. By dismantling these institutions—including offshore banks and shadow financiers that have moved hundreds of millions of dollars through shell companies and foreign‑exchange specialists across the Middle East and Asia—Treasury is severing critical revenue streams that sustain Iran’s military and proxy forces.
“The noose is tightening around Iran’s economy, and not even Iran’s so-called allies can save it,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “The Department of the Treasury will not relent until the Iranian regime’s coffers are empty and every remaining financial lifeline sustaining its war machine has been severed.”
In coordination with today’s action, the U.S. Department of State is concurrently designating Cuba-based Banco Internacional de Comercio S.A. (BICSA) pursuant to Section 2(a)(i)(A) of Executive Order (E.O.) 14404 for operating in or having operated in the financial services sector of the Cuban economy. BICSA has provided services to the designated Iran-based Karafarin Bank since at least 2022.
These designations, coupled with additional sanctions on Iran’s shadow banking networks, cut off some of the few remaining financial lifelines the regime can access to prop up its failing economy and fund its military. The designations also expose the regime’s deliberate use of complex offshore structures and front companies to circumvent sanctions and stabilize its economy despite mounting pressure. Taken together, today’s measures target the core financial architecture that enables Iran to evade international scrutiny and fund its destabilizing regional activities. Treasury’s action is being taken pursuant to E.O. 13902, which targets certain sectors of the Iranian economy, including Iran’s financial and petroleum sectors.
OPERATION ECONOMIC OUTCAST IS ISOLATING THE IRANIAN REGIME
Announced by Secretary Bessent on August 24, 2026, dubbed Economic D-Day, Operation Economic Outcast is severing the remaining economic lifelines that sustain the Iranian regime. Treasury has mapped the networks, facilitators, and financial channels that Iran uses to smuggle oil, evade sanctions, and fund terror. Working with partners across the U.S. government, the European Union, the United Kingdom, Gulf partners, and others, Treasury is targeting any source of the regime’s illicit revenue, as well as its sanctions evasion schemes to move funds.
Operation Economic Outcast significantly expanded sanctions risk for those who continue to choose to do business with Iran. Treasury warned that any entity facilitating money laundering or sanctions evasion on behalf of Iran risks being cut off from the U.S. financial system. It also expanded secondary sanctions exposure for those who continue doing business with the Iranian regime and will accelerate the pace of U.S. enforcement. More information on Operation Economic Outcast is available here.
Because Iran is already subject to comprehensive U.S. sanctions, it relies on multi-jurisdictional shadow banking networks to generate revenue and transfer funds abroad. Iran uses these shadow banking networks to launder funds, procure weapons, access U.S. dollar correspondent banking relationships, and bankroll its regional terrorist proxy groups. These networks rely on financial institutions such as the recently designated Golden Global Bank, and Operation Economic Outcast will continue to identify these banks and remove their access to the U.S. dollar.
IRAQI BANK PROVIDING U.S. DOLLAR ACCESS FOR IRAN
Iraq-based International Development Bank for Investment and Finance (IDB) provides financial facilitation services and U.S. dollar access for Iran. IDB has abused its access to the now-dissolved U.S. dollar wire auction and maintains ties to Iranian government entities and Iran-aligned militia groups (IAMGs) in Iraq. IDB was initially established by Iranian companies to support the Iranian economy and supply Iran with U.S. dollars. U.S.-designated Bank Melli, which was located next to IDB in Iraq, closed due to U.S. sanctions and transferred its capital to IDB. IDB uses Iranian capital to conduct business, then collects any profit made and sends it back to Iran in the form of U.S. dollars each month. The bank’s current leadership received ownership of IDB from a dual-Iranian Iraqi financier working for the U.S.-designated Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps–Qods Force (IRGC-QF). The financier continues to use his familial relationships to exert influence over the bank.
IDB is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the financial sector of the Iranian economy.
IRANIAN “OFFSHORE” BANKS
In addition to establishing correspondent banking relationships with financial institutions in allied countries, the Iranian government has authorized certain banks to operate “offshore” in free trade zones. These Iranian banks have been approved by the Central Bank of Iran and the Supreme National Security Council to conduct their operations using foreign currency to aid sanctions evasion schemes. Iran-based Jazireh International Bank Company is an Iranian offshore bank affiliated with Bank Mellat, while Chabahar International Bank Overseas Company is an offshore bank affiliated with Bank Shahr.
Jazireh International Bank Company and Chabahar International Bank Overseas Company are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the financial sector of the Iranian economy.
IRANIAN OIL “TRUSTEE”
Many of Iran’s key revenue generation streams are corruptly controlled by Iranian regime elites. These revenue streams include the shipping empire of Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani, son of Ali Shamkhani, the late advisor to Iran’s Supreme Leader, and the vast overseas property holdings of Ali Ansari, a key benefactor of Mojtaba Khamenei. One of the elites controlling Iran’s key revenue streams is Iranian national Sayyed Ruhollah Razavi (Razavi), son-in-law of Iran’s hardline Paydari Front leader and one of the top oil trustees on whom the Iranian regime relies to sell oil and repatriate the revenue.
Living in Dubai as one of Iran’s top oil intermediaries, Razavi has worked hand-in-hand with Seyed Naiemaei Badroddin Moosavi, a Hizballah financier and Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force facilitator designated on April 15, 2026. Prior to the U.S. blockade preventing Iranian oil exports, Razavi was responsible for shipping millions of barrels of oil overseas each month on behalf of the National Iranian Oil Company and its subsidiary, Naftiran Intertrade Company. Razavi has also used his network to move the revenue generated from these oil sales through Iran’s clandestine banking system of shell companies and cash and gold couriers. These networks move funds through Hong Kong to the UAE and Türkiye where they are converted to gold and cash and then smuggled on Mahan Air flights to Iran and its terrorist proxies around the world. Razavi is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petroleum sector of the Iranian economy.
In addition to his overseas work on behalf of Iran, Razavi manages Iran-based companies Tejarat Gostar Atlas Parsian Kish Company and Farzanegan Energy Pars Company, the latter of which is currently developing the Farzanegan Gas Condensate Refinery in Iran’s Bushehr Province. Tejarat Gostar Atlas Parsian Kish Company and Farzanegan Energy Pars Company are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Razavi.
SHADOW BANKING OPERATIVES
Farab Sorough Qeshm Company (FSAQ), an affiliate of Iran’s Shahr Bank, relies on a cadre of foreign exchange experts to process transactions essential to the operations of Iran’s leading oil sales companies and brokers, including the National Iranian Oil Company, Triliance Petrochemical Company, and the military-controlled Sepehr Energy Jahan Nama Pars Company. FSAQ employees help to coordinate financial transactions through its rahbar network using shell companies established in Hong Kong and the UAE. Today, OFAC is designating seven FSAQ employees who have been involved in foreign exchange operations linked to FSAQ: Zhila Mohammadi, Milad Katebi, Amir Sabeti, Nazanin Borji, Fatemeh Vasighi Meraji, Azadeh Abdolalipur, and Farzad Allahyar. Hong Kong-based Elitesphere Trading Co., Limited, which has been used by FSAQ to move funds through the rahbar network of brokers and front companies in support of Iranian sanctions evasion, is also being designated for operating in the financial sector of the Iranian economy.
Zhila Mohammadi, Milad Katebi, Amir Sabeti, Nazanin Borji, Fatemeh Vasighi Meraji, Azadeh Abdolalipur, and Farzad Allahyar are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, FSAQ.
Iran-based exchange house Seyyed Abbas Hosseini Parsa and Partners Qeshm General Partnership (Hosseini Parsa Exchange), owned and operated by Iranian nationals Seyyed Abbas Hosseini Parsa and Khaled Mohiesnejad, assists the rahbar financial activities of sanctioned Iranian banks alongside Dominican/Iranian national Sadegh Bavi. Sadegh Bavi, an IRGC-Qods Force facilitator and money launderer who also assists in weapons purchases for Iran, is the owner and general manager of the Bavi General Trading Company LLC, which was previously designated by OFAC for helping coordinate tens of millions of dollars’ worth of payments for front companies operated by the Persian Gulf Petrochemical Industry Commercial Co. and Triliance Petrochemical Co. Ltd. Hosseini Parsa Exchange has a close relationship with Bavi General Trading, which has used Hosseini Parsa Exchange’s official documents and letterhead to carry out its own business operations. Sadegh Bavi also owns and operates Bavi and Partners Exchange Company, another Iran-based currency exchange house.
Iran-based exchange house Soheil and Sorush Najafzadeh and Partners Company (Najafzadeh Exchange), owned and operated by Iranian nationals Sorush Najafzadeh, Soheil Najafzadeh, and Mansureh Mirmohammadi, has processed transactions worth hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of financial transactions for Iranian financial institutions, including entities linked to Bank Mellat and its rahbar, Tejarat Sarir Afrooz Kish. Iran-based exchange house Abolhasan Jalali and Partners Exchange Company (Jalali Exchange), owned and operated by Iranian nationals Abolhassan Jalali and Ensiyeh Mullah Mohammadi, has likewise facilitated tens of millions of dollars’ worth of payments for Iran’s shadow banking networks and sanctioned rahbar entities.
Elitesphere Trading Co., Limited, Hosseini Parsa Exchange, Jalali Exchange, Najafzadeh Exchange, Bavi and Partners Exchange Company, Sorush Najafzadeh, Soheil Najafzadeh, Abolhassan Jalali, Ensiyeh Mullah Mohammadi, and Sadegh Bavi are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the financial sector of the Iranian economy. Seyyed Abbas Hosseini Parsa and Khaled Mohiesnejad are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Hosseini Parsa Exchange. Mansureh Mirmohammadi is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Najafzadeh Exchange.
SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS
As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC. In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked. Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of blocked persons.
Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons. OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions. The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person. Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, and from engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions. Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to FinCEN’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000. In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities with designated or otherwise blocked persons.
Furthermore, engaging in certain transactions involving the persons designated today may risk the imposition of secondary sanctions on participating foreign financial institutions. OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority.
The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law. The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior. For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List.

Tallahassee, Florida – Michael Ray Pennington, 60, of Panama City, Florida, was sentenced to 10 years in federal prison after being found guilty by a federal jury of attempted enticement of a minor. The sentence was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida.

U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “Thanks to the excellent investigative work of our state and federal law enforcement partners, my office was able to secure a federal conviction and substantial prison sentence for this defendant. Keeping our kids safe from sexual predators, both online and in our communities, remains a top priority for my office, and we will continue to aggressively prosecute these cases to achieve that goal.”

Court documents and trial testimony revealed that in November 2025, federal and local law enforcement conducted an undercover operation to identify and apprehend offenders who use the internet to sexually exploit children. During the operation, an undercover law enforcement officer posted a fictitious advertisement on a website commonly used for prostitution. The defendant responded to the ad and was informed by the undercover agent that he was speaking to a 15-year-old child. The defendant then expressed an interest in engaging in sexual activity with the child in exchange for money. Upon arrival at an arranged meeting location, the defendant was arrested. A search of the defendant’s phone confirmed that he was the person communicating with the undercover agent through both text messaging and phone calls.

“Those who seek to exploit children will find no refuge online or in our communities,” said Homeland Security Investigations Tampa Acting Special Agent in Charge Nicholas Ingegno. “Predators who target vulnerable children for sexual abuse will be identified, arrested, and held accountable. Homeland Security Investigations and our law enforcement partners remain relentless in protecting children and pursuing those who would harm them.”

Upon his release from federal prison, Pennington will be required to serve eight years of supervised release and register as a sex offender.

The case involved a joint investigation by the Bay County Sheriff’s Office and Homeland Security Investigations. Assistant United States Attorney Emma Schwan prosecuted the case.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC .

The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl .
title: Panama City Man Sentenced to Ten Years in Federal Prison for Attempting to Entice a Minor to Engage in Sexual Activity

Baltimore, Maryland – Authorities arrested a Maryland father and son, today, in connection with a dog-fighting conspiracy.

A federal grand jury indicted Theodore Lamont Stinson, 48, of Whiteford, and Theodore Lamont Stinson, Jr., 25, of Whiteford, for conspiracy to engage in an animal fighting venture; buying, selling, delivering, possessing, training, or transporting animals for participation in an animal fighting venture; use of postal service or other interstate instrumentality for promoting or furthering an animal fighting venture; and interstate and foreign travel or transportation in aid of racketeering enterprises.

Kelly O. Hayes, U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the 12-count indictment with Special Agent in Charge Jimmy Paul, FBI Baltimore Field Office; Special Agent in Charge Charmeka Parker, U.S. Department of Agriculture – Office of Inspector General (USDA-OIG) Northeast Region; Alison M. Healey, Harford County State's Attorney; and Sheriff Jeffrey R. Gahler, Harford County Sheriff’s Office.

According to the indictment, since at least April 2016, until current, Stinson, Stinson, Jr., and their co-conspirators bought, sold, bred, trained, and used pit-bull-type dogs for dog fighting. Stinson and Stinson, Jr. operated a kennel under the name “KLK,” which they used to advertise their inventory of dogs. Stinson and Stinson, Jr., kept dogs at their property for the purpose of selling, transporting, and breeding dogs that they and their co-conspirators owned.

Both Stinson and Stinson Jr., provided oversight for the dogs while Stinson advised his son about proper care for the dogs. Additionally, the father and son both participated in arranging transportation for the dogs in connection with sales and breeding. Stinson often arranged transportation for dog sales while Stinson, Jr., transported them to their intended destinations.

On July 17, 2025, the Harford County Sheriff’s Office and its Animal Control Unit executed search-and-seizure warrants at Stinson’s residence. During the search, investigators found 44 pit-bull-type dogs, veterinary medication and supplies, a breeding stand, a “spring pole/rope” accessory used to train and condition fighting dogs, and paperwork relating to dog sales and pedigrees.

An indictment is not a finding of guilt. Individuals charged by indictment are presumed innocent until proven guilty at a later criminal proceeding.

If convicted, Stinson and Stinson, Jr. each face up to five years in federal prison for conspiracy to engage in an animal fighting venture, along with up to five years for buying, selling, delivering, possessing, training, or transporting animals for participation in an animal fighting venture. The father and son are also facing up to five years for use of postal service or other interstate instrumentality for promoting or furthering an animal fighting venture; and interstate and foreign travel or transportation in aid of racketeering enterprises.

Actual sentences for federal crimes are typically less than the maximum penalties. A federal district court judge determines sentencing after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

U.S. Attorney Hayes commended the FBI, USDA-OIG, Harford County Sheriff’s Office and its Animal Control Unit, and Harford County State’s Attorney’s Office, for their work in the investigation, along with the U.S. Marshals Service and Maryland National Guard 32nd Civil Support Team, for their valuable assistance. Ms. Hayes also thanked Assistant U.S. Attorneys Alexander Levin and Liane Kozik who are prosecuting the federal case.

For more information about the Maryland U.S. Attorney’s Office, its priorities, and resources available to help the community, visit justice.gov/usao-md .

title: Maryland Father and Son Indicted on Dog Fighting, Breeding, and Transportation Charges After Law Enforcement Seizes 44 Dogs

BLM Announces December Sale of Oil and Gas Leases in Arizona
Organization:
Media Contact:
PHOENIX – The Bureau of Land Management today announced an oil and gas lease sale scheduled for Dec. 15, to offer 40 oil and gas parcels totaling 78,708 acres in Arizona.
The BLM completed scoping on these parcels in June and held a public comment period that closed in September on the parcels and the related environmental analysis. A 30-day public protest period to receive additional public input opens Oct. 16 and will close Nov. 15.
Leasing is the first step in the process to develop federal oil and gas resources. Before development operations can begin, an operator must submit an application for permit to drill detailing development plans. The BLM reviews applications for permits to drill, posts them for public review, conducts an environmental analysis and coordinates with state partners and stakeholders.
All parcels that are included in a federal oil and gas lease sale include appropriate stipulations to protect important natural resources. Information on current and upcoming BLM leases is available through the National Fluid Lease Sale System. BLM lease sales are held online through Efficient Markets.
The parcels BLM analyzed, as well as maps and instructions on how to submit a protest, will be available on BLM’s ePlanning website at: https://eplanning.blm.gov/Project-Home/?id=C5F10790-8349-F111-88B4-001DD8084607.
The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.

Thanks to President Trump’s leadership, a new era of energy investment and production is taking hold in Venezuela, delivering greater prosperity and energy security for the United States and Venezuela.
September 2, 2026
PRESIDENT TRUMP IS UNLEASHING HISTORIC ENERGY INVESTMENT AND PRODUCTION IN VENEZUELA
- Thanks to President Trump’s leadership, a new era of energy investment and production is taking hold in Venezuela, delivering greater prosperity and energy security for the United States and Venezuela.
- On September 2, 2026, Secretary Wright traveled to Venezuela to oversee the signing of landmark energy agreements with Chevron, Eni, and GE Vernova that will expand oil production, unlock billions in private-sector investment, and modernize Venezuela’s electric grid.
  - Today’s agreements build on President Trump’s August 28 announcement of a historic binational agreement with Venezuela, which establishes U.S. majority control of an estimated 65 billion barrels of proven oil reserves, helping ensure U.S. energy dominance for decades to come.
- These landmark agreements represent another major step in the Trump Administration’s efforts to unlock Venezuela’s vast energy resources and rebuild critical energy infrastructure.
- These historic investments will double Venezuela’s oil production in less than five years, bringing more abundant and affordable energy to the market and putting a downward pressure on global energy prices, creating greater peace, prosperity, and economic opportunity for the United States and Venezuela.
UNLOCKING VENEZUELA’S VAST OIL POTENTIAL
- Thanks to President Trump’s leadership, major energy companies are investing in Venezuela’s future once again, unlocking Venezuela’s vast oil resources and expanding production.
- Today, Chevron announced new agreements to unlock more than $7 billion in investment and significantly increase oil production in Venezuela.
  - Through its joint ventures, Chevron will invest more than $7 billion over the next five years and more than double oil production to 600,000 barrels per day compared with 2026.
  - Chevron will expand its position in the Orinoco Belt and develop the Carabobo 1 and Carabobo-2-South-A areas through its Petroindependencia joint venture.
  - With total costs of less than $20 per barrel, Chevron’s expanded operations will bring more affordable oil to the market, put downward pressure on global energy prices, and create greater prosperity and opportunity for the United States and Venezuela.
- Eni and PDVSA signed a landmark 25-year contract to develop the Junín 5 oil field, unlocking one of Venezuela’s largest oil resources for long-term development and production.
  - Under the agreement, Eni will become the exclusive operator of Junín 5, which it has participated in since 2010. Eni will assume responsibility for the technical, financial, and commercial management of the field.
  - This agreement builds on the Head of Terms signed on April 28, establishing a new operating framework designed to bring investment, technology, and expertise needed to accelerate the development of Junín 5.
  - Junín 5 contains approximately 35 billion barrels of certified oil in place, providing an enormous resource base for long-term development and production.
  - Development of Junín 5 will support the goal of producing more than 1 million barrels per day by 2031.
STRENGTHENING VENEZUELA’S ELECTRIC GRID
- Today, Secretary Wright joined Venezuelan interim President Delcy Rodriguez to witness the execution of GE Vernova’s agreement to modernize and expand Venezuela’s electric grid, bring new power online, optimize existing capacity, and improve long-term reliability for Venezuela.
- Through this agreement, GE Vernova plans to bring 1 gigawatt of new reliable power online within the first 24 months, in addition to 5 gigawatts over the following four years, significantly expanding Venezuela’s power capacity.
- The agreement will address thermal and hydroelectric power generation, transmission and distribution infrastructure, and key substations.
- This agreement also builds on a June 15 cooperation agreement between GE Vernova and CORPOELEC, Venezuela’s state electricity company, which established a framework to rehabilitate and strengthen the country’s power infrastructure.

Chairman Jovanovic Signs Letter of Support for NioCorp's Elk Creek Mine, Tours Innovative Project with Secretary Wright, Senior Nebraska Leaders
ELK CREEK, NE.—Today, Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM) Chairman John Jovanovic joined Secretary of Energy Chris Wright, Governor Jim Pillen, Senators Deb Fischer and Pete Ricketts, Representative Adrian Smith (NE-03), and senior NioCorp leadership for a tour of its Elk Creek mine site. The mine marks a crucial development in securing American supply chains and U.S. energy dominance. When successfully developed, the Elk Creek mine will contribute to domestic production of niobium, scandium, and other rare earth elements used in everyday devices like magnets and fuel cells. During the visit, Jovanovic signed a letter of support alongside Mark Smith, Executive Chairman, President, and CEO of NioCorp Developments, to recognize the significance and the Bank’s continued support of the project.
“The Elk Creek Minerals Project is exactly the type of opportunity EXIM was always designed to support. By advancing U.S. control over the critical minerals essential to aircraft, automobiles, advanced manufacturing, and our broad industrial base, this project means more good jobs in Nebraska, more opportunities for American workers and a stronger, more secure industrial future for the United States,” said EXIM Chairman John Jovanovic.
“This is not just the economics of the United States. This is our national security that rests on what’s underground right here. We can’t just talk about them and write a few papers and then hand it off to the next administration,” Secretary of Energy Chris Wright said. “We actually have to act. We have to do something to change the situation we’re in.”
"We are extremely gratified with the tremendous support we have received from Chairman Jovanovic and the entire team at EXIM as we continue to pursue a financing partnership with EXIM. EXIM’s professionalism and attention to detail are second-to-none, and we look forward to the day when we can all celebrate the EXIM Board of Directors’ authorization of our financing package,” said Mark Smith, Executive Chairman, President, and CEO of NioCorp.
“It’s incredible to think that here in the Heartland, we will play a key role in supplying minerals that the U.S. has long relied on foreign adversaries like China, to provide. We need these materials to support new technologies, our nation’s defense initiatives, medical and aerospace industries. President Trump has made this a top priority and the project in Elk Creek will fill help the gap in our nation's supply chain while providing careers to hundreds of people and supporting our state's economic diversity,” said Governor Jim Pillen.
“I've long pushed to bring critical mineral production and processing back to the United States. I could not be prouder to see Nebraska leading the way in securing America’s energy dominance. I appreciate the administration’s focus on strengthening our domestic critical mineral supply chain, and I thank Chairman Jovanovic for supporting NioCorp’s plant in Elk Creek,” said Senator Deb Fischer (R-NE).
“Nebraskans are playing a critical role in strengthening our national security. Advanced minerals needed for key sectors like defense and energy will be made in Elk Creek. The partnership between this community, NioCorp, and EXIM is a model for how we can continue to bolster domestic supply chains,” said Senator Pete Ricketts (R-NE).
"The Export-Import Bank of the United States’ letter of support marks an important step towards making the Elk Creek Critical Minerals Project a reality. I firmly believe our region is uniquely positioned to support a project of this significance and strategic importance. I look forward to seeing this project come to fruition—not only delivering a much-needed supply of critical minerals but also creating new opportunities for families and businesses in Nebraska’s Third District for years to come," said Representative Adrian Smith (NE-03).
NioCorp plans to produce niobium, scandium, titanium, and several magnetic rare earth elements at the Elk Creek Project. These materials are used across automotive, aerospace, energy, and advanced manufacturing applications. The United States is heavily import-dependent for these materials, including 100% net import reliance for several of the minerals NioCorp plans to produce.
J.P. Morgan’s Export & Agency Finance team is serving as the sole EXIM Coordinator for the transaction to support the American critical mineral sector which is key to national security and the economy.
About EXIM:
As the United States government’s official export credit agency, the Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM) supports American jobs by facilitating U.S. exports. As an independent agency, EXIM plays a critical role in supporting economic growth, securing critical supply chains, and ensuring American businesses are given a fighting chance. To achieve this mission, EXIM offers financing including export credit insurance, working capital guarantees, loan guarantees, and direct loans. Learn more at www.exim.gov.
title: Chairman Jovanovic Signs Letter of Support for NioCorp's Elk Creek Mine, Tours Innovative Project with Secretary Wright, Senior Nebraska Leaders

WHEELING, WEST VIRGINIA – A Wheeling, West Virginia man will spend the next five years in federal prison for selling methamphetamine near a playground, announced U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey.

Matthew Luff, 42, sold more than 13 grams of methamphetamine near Heritage Port Playground in Wheeling. Luff has multiple prior convictions, including burglary, drug possession and trafficking, and obstructing justice.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Clayton Reid prosecuted the case on behalf of the government.

The Drug Enforcement Administration and the Ohio Valley Drug Task Force, a HIDTA-funded initiative, investigated.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime, and repel the invasion of illegal immigration.

U.S. District Judge John Preston Bailey presided.
title: Drug Dealer Selling Methamphetamine Near Playground Sentenced to Federal Prison

Krishnamoorthi Joins Warren, Garcia, Bipartisan Lawmakers in Introducing Bill to Hold Bankers Who Financed Jeffrey Epstein’s Sex Trafficking Operation Accountable
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-Ill.) today joined U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee, and Congressman Robert Garcia (D-Cal.), Ranking Member of the House Oversight Committee, along with Congressmen Ro Khanna (D-Cal.) and Thomas Massie (R-Ken.), and Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ranking Member of the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, and Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), Ranking Member of the Senate Finance Committee, in introducing the bipartisan Epstein Wall Street Records Act. The bill seeks accountability for the financial institutions and bank executives that may have enabled disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein’s sex trafficking operation.
“Jeffrey Epstein’s sex trafficking operation left a money trail, and Wall Street has serious questions to answer. Our legislation will force federal regulators to release their records, investigate the banks and executives who may have enabled his crimes, and hold lawbreakers accountable,” said Congressman Krishnamoorthi. “Epstein’s survivors deserve the full truth, no matter how powerful or well-connected those responsible may be.”
Extensive reporting and congressional probes have revealed the degree to which Wall Street empowered Epstein’s crimes. According to The New York Times Magazine, executives at JPMorgan assisted Epstein in evading internal controls meant to intercept suspicious activity, allowing him to avoid scrutiny. An August investigation by Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden's staff found “significant evidence that JPMorgan Chase, Deutsche Bank, and Bank of America violated federal anti-money laundering laws by failing to screen and report Epstein’s suspicious financial transactions in a timely manner.”
Krishnamoorthi has previously joined Warren in pressing Goldman Sachs over its handling of Kathryn Ruemmler’s ties to Epstein, and joined Warren and Khanna in demanding answers from Barclays about former CEO Jes Staley’s relationship with Epstein. At a May hearing with Epstein survivors, Krishnamoorthi also demanded that the Treasury Department release suspicious activity reports tied to Epstein’s financial transactions.
The Epstein Wall Street Records Act would:
- Require federal financial regulators, including the Federal Reserve, Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), and Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), to disclose supervisory records related to Epstein and his associates to Congress and the American people, while protecting survivors' identifying information.
- Force the financial regulators to investigate Epstein-connected banks and executives for possible banking, securities, or illicit financing violations.
- Require industry bars or civil penalties for executives found to have committed qualifying violations, as well as referrals to the Department of Justice when regulators identify possible federal crimes.
“I have spent the last year calling on Donald Trump’s financial regulators to launch investigations into the big banks and executives who may have enabled Jeffrey Epstein’s horrific crimes,” said Ranking Member Warren. “Since they have failed to act, Congress must. The bipartisan Epstein Wall Street Records Act will ensure overdue accountability for the wealthy and well-connected on Wall Street who put profits over people.”
“Jeffrey Epstein used his immense wealth to abuse women and girls for decades. Meanwhile, banks and financial institutions enriched him and themselves by servicing his accounts and helping him move money around,” said Ranking Member Garcia. “We need to know what financial institutions and their executives knew about Epstein, whether they complied with relevant law, and what regulatory agencies learned.”
“The Epstein Wall Street Records Act is about transparency and releasing financial records that are critical to holding the Epstein Class accountable and fighting to get justice for the survivors. I’m proud to cosponsor this bipartisan bill,” said Representative Khanna.
“The Epstein Wall Street Records Act requires the Federal Reserve, the FDIC, the Comptroller of the Currency, and the SEC to release their files on Jeffrey Epstein’s money,” said Representative Massie. “The Epstein Files Transparency Act forced the Attorney General to release DOJ, FBI, and U.S. Attorney’s Offices’ files. This bill does the same for bank regulators. Justice for the survivors means following the money.”
“For far too long, financial institutions have leveraged their power, influence, and privilege to evade accountability. Their role in enabling Jeffrey Epstein’s decades of sexual exploitation and abuse demands serious scrutiny. That is why World Without Exploitation is proud to support the Epstein Wall Street Records Act of 2026,” said Becca Zipkin, Vice President of Policy and Programs, World Without Exploitation. “We must follow the money to uncover the truth and ensure that the financial institutions that enabled this abuse are held accountable. Survivors deserve transparency, accountability, and the justice they have long been denied."
The cosponsors of the Epstein Wall Street Records Act include: Senator Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), as well as Representatives Stephen Lynch (D-Mass.), Shontel Brown (D-Ohio), Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.), Maxwell Frost (D-Fla.), Jasmine Crockett (D-Tex.), Emily Randall (D-Wash.), Suhas Subramanyam (D-Va.), Yassamin Ansari (D-Ariz.), Wesley Bell (D-Mo.), Lateefah Simon (D-Cal.), Dave Min (D-Cal.), James Walkinshaw (D-Va.), Christian Menefee (D-Tex.), Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.), Kweisi Mfume (D-Md.), Greg Casar (D-Tex.), and Delegate Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-D.C.).
The text of the legislation is available here.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03) introduced the Justice for Citizens Wrongfully Detained by ICE Act to make sure American citizens wrongfully arrested or detained by immigration enforcement officers can fight back in court. Her legislation would prevent individual officers and the government from claiming qualified or sovereign immunity to avoid accountability and give individuals five years to sue. It would also require courts to award successful plaintiffs $500,000, plus $100,000 for each additional day of detention after the first day.
“ICE does not get to trample on your rights and walk away without consequence. They cannot hide behind their masks and act like they have a license to break the Constitution,” said Congresswoman Leger Fernández. “Our government has handcuffed, hauled away, and locked up more than 500 American citizens. Citizens have been deported — including Brian Garcia Morales, who spent four months trying to get home. ICE is proving that nobody is safe from their handcuffs — and that is the purpose, to terrorize our Latino and immigrant communities. My bill is about justice for those Americans and accountability for the officers and a government who violate Americans’ rights.” 
A ProPublica investigation documented 506 U.S. citizens detained by immigration agents since the start of the second Trump administration, including children and Americans detained while recording enforcement operations. The reporting underscores the urgent need for a clear path to accountability when officers violate citizens’ rights.
Leger Fernández’s legislation would allow U.S. citizens arrested or detained without a warrant or without probable cause to sue the officers involved and the United States in federal court. It would remove immunity defenses that can shield officers and the government from liability under current law.

The legislation is endorsed by the League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC) and The Center for Law and Social Policy (CLASP). Congresswoman Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12) is an original cosponsor.
“Since 1929, LULAC has fought against the treatment of Latinos as strangers in their own country. We support the Justice for Citizens Wrongfully Detained by ICE Act because the Constitution is not a privilege granted by a badge, and when the government treats an American citizen as an enemy on American soil, justice must be more than an apology. It must carry a price,” said Roman Palomares, LULAC National President and National Board Chair.

Bill would create a tax credit of up to $10,000 for childcare providers to purchase specialized equipment; Correa to host "Together on the Spectrum" community event Saturday in Santa Ana
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Representatives Lou Correa (D-CA) and Chris Smith (R-NJ) introduced the Bright Beginnings Act, bipartisan legislation that would establish a federal tax credit of up to $10,000 per year for childcare centers and providers to purchase the equipment needed to serve children with developmental disabilities.
“Every child deserves a safe, supportive place to learn and grow, and every parent deserves peace of mind while they work. The Bright Beginnings Act helps childcare providers get the tools they need to welcome children with developmental disabilities, and helps families stay in the workforce without sacrificing their child's care,” said Rep. Correa.
Approximately 1 in 5 children in the United States, or 14.5 million, have special healthcare needs, and 1 in 12 children diagnosed with a developmental disability require specialized support and accommodations. Yet 27 percent of parents of children with disabilities report difficulty finding adequate childcare. Delayed or absent services limit children's development and often force families to cut work hours or leave their jobs entirely, deepening financial strain.
“Parents of children with disabilities go above and beyond to provide for their children, while often shouldering additional economic burdens associated with costs of care. Too often these families are forced between taking care of a loved one and earning a paycheck. The Bright Beginnings tax credit would assist eligible childcare centers and enable them to meet the costs of providing safe and appropriate services for children with disabilities, and peace of mind for their parents who need to work to support them,” said Rep. Smith.
The Bright Beginnings Act encourages childcare centers to invest in specialized equipment and create environments where children can grow and engage in the ways that best suit them. Specifically, the bill:
- 
Establishes a federal tax credit of up to $10,000 per year for eligible providers
- 
Covers qualifying expenditures for equipment that accommodates children with developmental disabilities
- 
Expands access to specialized care for families who are struggling to find it
“Access to high-quality, inclusive child care can make a meaningful difference in the lives of children with autism and their families, yet too many providers lack the resources needed to create fully accessible and supportive environments where every child can thrive,” said Keith Wargo, President and CEO of Autism Speaks. “We are grateful for Representative Correa's leadership in introducing the Bright Beginnings Act and recognizing the importance of ensuring child care settings are equipped to serve children with autism and other developmental disabilities. By promoting access and innovation in child care settings, this legislation would help providers strengthen their ability to support children with autism - expanding their opportunities to learn, develop and thrive alongside their peers from the very start.”
“Every child deserves the opportunity to learn, play, and thrive in a supportive childcare environment. Tax credits that help providers invest in accommodations for Autistic children and children with developmental disabilities can reduce financial barriers and expand access to inclusive care. The Autism Society of America applauds this legislation and its commitment to helping more children participate, connect, and reach their full potential,” said Joseph Joyce, President and CEO of the Autism Society of America.
The bill is endorsed by Access Ready Inc., Autism Speaks, Autism Society of America, Easterseals, TDI for Access, and The Learning Disabilities Association for America.
Together on the Spectrum
In conjunction with the bill's introduction, Rep. Correa will host Together on the Spectrum this Saturday in Santa Ana. The event grew out of Rep. Correa's desire to create a space to bring children and families together. The free community event is open to neurodivergent youth ages 5–18 and their families, and will feature activities and information on autism and neurodiversity, Regional Center services, family support and advocacy, therapy and developmental services, and safety and emergency preparedness. Federal resources will also be available. Participating organizations include Corazones Especiales, Regional Center of Orange County, Santa Ana PD, TACA (The Autism Community in Action), United Across Borders Foundation, Easterseals, and the Orange County Children's Therapeutic Arts Center, among others.
title: CORREA, SMITH INTRODUCE BIPARTISAN BRIGHT BEGINNINGS ACT TO EXPAND CHILDCARE FOR CHILDREN WITH DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES

RELEASE: Gottheimer Discusses AI Policy at the University of Pennsylvania
Joins Penn Leaders, Faculty, and Students to Discuss AI Safety, Innovation, and the Future of Education
Above: Gottheimer Discusses AI Policy with Vice Provost for Research David Meaney at the University of Pennsylvania.
PHILADELPHIA, PA — Today, Monday, October 12, 2026, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), Co-Chair of the House Democratic Commission on AI, visited the University of Pennsylvania to discuss federal AI policy and his work leading the commission. He met with UPenn President Larry Jameson and the university’s top AI researchers for a roundtable and then joined David Meaney, Penn’s Vice Provost for Research, for a fireside chat with Penn faculty and students.
“AI is advancing quickly and will have massive benefits for our economy and society as a whole,” said Congressman Gottheimer (NJ-5). “It’s critical that we not only understand it but are prepared for its impact. That’s why it’s great to see top universities like Penn help ensure America continues to lead the way on AI development and education.”
Watch Gottheimer’s full address here.
Gottheimer, who co-chairs the Commission with Representatives Ted Lieu (CA-36) and Valerie Foushee (NC-4), discussed its work to educate Congress and develop an AI policy agenda focused on growth, national security, child safety, energy, healthcare, and more. He highlighted the importance of universities in that effort, noting that Penn launched the Ivy League’s first undergraduate AI major and is advising Governor Shapiro’s administration on responsible AI use.
Gottheimer also discussed several bipartisan AI bills he’s led this Congress, including:
- The bipartisan American AI Security Act, with Rep. Mike Lawler (NY-17), to require pre-deployment testing to address AI’s national security risks.
- The bipartisan Stop Rogue AI Act, with Rep. Mike Lawler (NY-17), to keep humans in control of AI agents.
- The bipartisan AI LABS Act, with Rep. Jay Obernolte (CA-23), to help K-12 schools set up dedicated AI labs and teach students how AI works.
- The bipartisan Liquid Cooling for AI Act, with Rep. Jay Obernolte (CA-23), to advance more energy-efficient AI infrastructure.

Baltimore, Maryland – A Baltimore man, who a Baltimore City jury recently convicted of a gang-related murder, received a federal-prison term, today, for drug-trafficking crimes. This prosecution is in connection with a Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) drug investigation.

U.S. District Judge Julie R. Rubin sentenced Jarvis Joyner, 35, to 10 years in prison, followed by three years of supervised release, after he pled guilty to possession with intent to distribute 400 grams or more of fentanyl.

Kelly O. Hayes, U.S Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the sentence with Special Agent in Charge Cindy Marx, Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) – Washington Division, and Commissioner Richard Worley, Baltimore Police Department (BPD).

According to the indictment, in fall 2022, federal and state law enforcement officers began investigating a drug trafficking organization (DTO) in Maryland. Beginning in October 2022, and continuing until at least March 2023, investigators observed DTO members conspiring to distribute and possess with intent to distribute fentanyl. Throughout the conspiracy, the DTO members obtained bulk quantities of fentanyl from various source suppliers and then distributed the drugs to wholesale customers in Maryland, Pennsylvania, and the District of Columbia.

Between February and March 2023, an undercover (UC) law-enforcement officer conducted three controlled fentanyl purchases from Joyner. On Feb. 6, the UC contacted one of Joyner’s co-conspirators and offered to purchase a quantity of fentanyl from the DTO. The co-conspirator agreed to the sale and arranged to meet. Later that day, the UC traveled to the meeting location, where the officer met Joyner. During the meeting, Joyner provided the UC with 250 fentanyl pills.

Then on Feb. 9, the UC met with the same co-conspirator and again offered to purchase a quantity of fentanyl from the DTO. The co-conspirator agreed to the sale, so Joyner contacted the UC to arrange to meet. Joyner later met the UC who then purchased 500 fentanyl pills. On Feb. 28, the UC contacted Joyner to offer to purchase a quantity of fentanyl. Joyner agreed to the sale and arranged to meet with the UC. Then on March 1, Joyner met the UC who then purchased 1,000 fentanyl pills.

The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Baltimore comprises agents and officers from the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI); Homeland Security Investigations (HSI); the United States Attorney’s Office (USAO) for the District of Maryland; the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF); the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA); the Internal Revenue Service-Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI); the United States Marshals Service (USMS); the Washington/Baltimore HIDTA (W/B HIDTA); the Maryland State Police (MSP); the Baltimore Police Department (BPD); and the Baltimore County Police Department (BCPD) with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Maryland.

U.S. Attorney Hayes commended the DEA and BPD for their work in the investigation, along with the FBI Baltimore Field Office, for its valuable assistance. Ms. Hayes also thanked Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Keelan Diana who is prosecuting this federal case.

For more information about the Maryland U.S. Attorney’s Office, its priorities, and resources available to help the community, visit justice.gov/usao-md .

title: Convicted Murderer Sentenced for Drug Trafficking Crimes in HSTF Investigation

More than 30 U.S. Attorney’s Offices joined the Fraud Division in bringing enforcement actions against alleged fraudsters

GRAND RAPIDS, MICHIGAN – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Michigan today announced an indictment of Traverse City resident Christopher Robin Roehler as part of a nationwide enforcement action led by the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division, Internal Revenue Service, and Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation targeting tax fraud and related offenses. The Western District of Michigan was a key participant in this surge effort.

Between early September and today, federal prosecutors across the country facilitated fraud enforcement actions spanning 76 criminal defendants, including 31 newly charged defendants, reaching approximately $490 million in intended loss to American taxpayers.

U.S. Attorney Timothy VerHey said, “The Western District of Michigan joins the rest of the United States in fairly enforcing our tax laws. The tax offense charged against Roehler is especially galling because it involves taking money out of an employee’s pocket with the promise that the money will be turned over to the government as part of the employee’s tax obligation. Any employer who keeps that money for himself betrays that promise. We look forward to proving these charges in court.”

U.S. Attorney Timothy VerHey said, “The Western District of Michigan joins the rest of the United States in fairly enforcing our tax laws. The tax offense charged against Roehler is especially galling because it involves taking money out of an employee’s pocket with the promise that the money will be turned over to the government as part of the employee’s tax obligation. Any employer who keeps that money for himself betrays that promise. We look forward to proving these charges in court.”

According to the indictment returned by a grand jury in the Western District of Michigan, Christopher Robin Roehler, age 65 of Traverse City, was the owner and manager of Rolling Farms Café and was responsible for collecting, accounting for, and paying over to the Internal Revenue Service employment taxes. The indictment further alleges that Roehler willfully failed to truthfully account for and pay over a total of $47,679 in taxes on 10 occasions between September 2020 and December 2022, that were due and owing to the Internal Revenue Service on behalf of the employees of the restaurant.

Failing to collect, account for, or pay over employment taxes is a felony offense. Roehler faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison, a fine of $250,000, and the costs of prosecution on each of the ten counts in the indictment.

This press release details one way in which this office has contributed to ensuring that all Americans pay their fair share. To see the successes of other offices, please see this press release .

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

An indictment, information, or complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Michigan Joins DOJ's Fraud Division, IRS, and IRS-CI in National Tax Enforcement Surge Exposing $490 Million in Tax Fraud

ROCHESTER, N.Y. - U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Stevon K. Spencer, 29, of Rochester, NY, pleaded guilty before U.S. District Judge Meredith A. Vacca to being a felon in possession of ammunition, which carries a maximum penalty of 15 years, and a fine of $250,000 or both.

On the evening of August 5, 2025, Rochester Police officers viewed Spencer in possession of a Polymer 80 semiautomatic handgun while he appeared in a feed on Facebook Live. Later that evening, officers encountered Spencer in the area of Ackerman Street. When officers approached, he attempted to flee but was apprehended and arrested after a short foot chase. As officers were taking Spencer into custody, he continued to reach into his waistband area despite repeated demands to stop. After he was secured in handcuffs, officers located the loaded pistol, which did not have a serial number, on the ground directly where Spencer’s waistband had been. He was charged in New York State Court with Criminal Possession of a Weapon in the Second Degree and released on a $10,000 bond. Spencer was previously convicted in August 2018 in Monroe County Court of Robbery in the Second Degree and is legally prohibited from possessing ammunition.

On August 27, 2025, Spencer was arrested again in the area of Clifford Avenue and Miller Street in Rochester on a federal warrant charging him with being a felon in possession of ammunition. On August 28, 2025, law enforcement searched his residence on Wright Terrace and recovered another loaded Polymer 80 semiautomatic handgun, which again did not have a serial number, as well as ammunition.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

The plea is the result of an investigation by the Rochester Police Department, under the direction of Chief David Smith and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Bryan DiGirolamo, New York Field Division.

Sentencing is scheduled for February 16, 2027, at 10:00 a.m. before Judge Vacca.
