DETROIT – Jeffrey Royer was sentenced today to 71 months in federal prison after having pleaded guilty to defrauding multiple investors by falsely representing how their funds would be used and fabricating documents about their investments’ performance, United States Attorney Jerome F. Gorgon, Jr. announced. Royer was an FBI agent from 1996 to 2001.

Gorgon was joined in the announcement by Special Agent in Charge Jennifer Runyan, Federal Bureau of Investigation.

Royer told investors their funds would be used for foreign currency – known as forex – and commodity future trading. Instead, Royer diverted some of the collected funds to personal expenses, made false assurances to investors that their funds were protected from losses and, ultimately, fabricated earnings statements showing significant gains when, in fact, investors were losing money.

“Once a respected member of law enforcement, Jeffrey Royer now stands as a repeat fraudster who abandoned every principle that badge was supposed to represent,” said Gorgon. “Fraudsters like Royer abuse the trust others place in them and the positions they held. Abuse of the public trust will not be tolerated.”

“By choosing fraud over the oath he once took, Royer betrayed both the public and the law enforcement community,” said Jennifer Runyan, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI Detroit Field Office. “The sentence imposed today sends a clear message that misconduct, particularly by those who once held positions of trust, will be met with decisive action. I also want to recognize the dedicated work of FBI Detroit personnel and all of our partners whose persistence helped bring this case to sentencing. The FBI will continue to investigate and bring to justice those who engage in schemes that endanger the public’s financial security.”

Royer was also ordered to pay restitution of $575,999.58 to his victims and serve three years on supervised release following completing of his custodial sentence.

This is Royer’s second federal felony conviction. In 2012, Royer was released from the Federal Bureau of Prisons after serving a multi-year prison sentence for racketeering conspiracy, securities fraud conspiracy, securities fraud, obstruction of justice, and witness tampering

Those charges stemmed from Royer’s corrupt use of his position as an FBI agent to steal confidential criminal law enforcement information about companies under investigation by the FBI and the Securities and Exchange Commission. Royer passed that confidential information along to a “short seller” trader in exchange for the promise of cash and future employment. Using the confidential information provided by Royer, that trader established short positions in the stocks of companies under investigation.

The case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation. It is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Andrew J. Yahkind.
title: Disgraced Former FBI Agent Sentenced in Second Federal Prosecution

text:
CAMP MURRAY, Wash. — As more opportunities for Army training kept coming, Pfc. Dakota McConnell considered calling it enough. He had already spent months learning to be an infantryman and preparing for Ranger School. He was tired, physically worn down and unsure whether he wanted to continue from one school to the next.
“I’m burnt out. I’m beat up. I think I’m going to be done,” McConnell recalled thinking.
Then another opportunity would arrive.
“As they kept offering them, I just, you know what, why not? Another challenge,” McConnell said.
Since joining the Washington Army National Guard in May 2025, McConnell, an infantryman with Bravo Company, 1st Battalion, 161st Infantry Regiment, has completed basic training, initial infantry training, the Ranger Team Leader Initiative, Ranger School, Airborne School, Air Assault School, the Rappel Master Course and the Pathfinder Course. For the Oregon native, the training opportunities have delivered the challenge and sense of purpose he hoped to find when he enlisted.
“They’re just giving me all these schools and I get to push myself to my limits and see what I’m made of,” McConnell said. “Like, it’s exactly kind of what I’ve been dreaming of.”
Before joining the Guard, McConnell worked as an electrician and attended a year of college. Neither provided the fulfillment he was seeking.
“What I was doing back home was just getting stale and repetitive,” McConnell said. “And I just needed to switch it up. And what better way than serve your country, serve your state?”
His brother, who served as an active-duty infantryman, helped influence his choice of military occupation. The work his brother described sounded like the hands-on challenge McConnell wanted.
“Everything he was talking about just sounded like right up my alley,” McConnell said.
During infantry one-station unit training at Fort Benning, Georgia, McConnell learned that a strong performance could lead to an opportunity to attend Ranger School. He made that opportunity a goal.
“I had heard talks about if you were at the top of your company in basic, like sometimes they would offer you Ranger School,” McConnell said. “So I was really shooting to get that opportunity.”
When representatives arrived to identify interested candidates, McConnell made the cut. The Ranger Team Leader Initiative, a National Guard program that identifies promising enlisted Soldiers during initial training and prepares them for Ranger School, made the opportunity available. The initiative aims to bring Ranger-qualified Soldiers and their skills back to Guard formations early in their careers.
For McConnell, it opened the door to more training than he initially expected.
“They were explaining that it wasn’t just Ranger School,” McConnell said. “Like if you wanted, they could kind of just keep feeding you schools, everything that they had at the Warrior Training Center.”
Ranger School became both his most difficult experience and his favorite.
The Army’s 62-day course develops small-unit leadership and tactical skills through Darby, Mountain and Swamp phases. Students must plan and execute operations while managing leadership responsibilities under demanding physical and mental conditions.
“I’ve never been pushed to a limit like that and just expected to perform at not just like a regular level, but an elevated expectation,” McConnell said.
The relationships he built helped make the experience meaningful. Working through the same hardships brought him close to Soldiers he had only recently met.
“It was amazing and I just absolutely made some lifelong friends in just 62 days,” McConnell said.
Other courses expanded his skills in airborne and helicopter operations.
The Basic Airborne Course progresses through ground, tower and jump training, teaching students how to exit aircraft and land safely. Students must successfully complete five parachute jumps during the final phase.
Air Assault training covers combat assault operations, sling loads used to move equipment beneath helicopters, and rappelling. Students face written and practical evaluations and must complete a 12-mile foot march in less than three hours.
The Rappel Master Course adds training in supervising rappelling operations, including equipment inspections, anchor systems, safety procedures, and aircraft rigging and control.
While Ranger School pushed McConnell hardest physically and mentally, he said the Pathfinder Course taught him the most because of the volume of information he needed to absorb.
The course prepares Soldiers for sling-load operations, helicopter landing zones, air assault planning and parachute drop-zone operations — skills that help ground forces coordinate the movement of personnel and equipment by aircraft.
“With Pathfinder, like you’re just learning and learning and learning and just building up all this knowledge,” McConnell said.
Now back at his home unit, McConnell wants to share his knowledge with fellow Soldiers and encourage them to pursue their own training opportunities.
“I would really want to encourage everybody that I meet to go to Ranger School because I think it genuinely is life changing,” McConnell said.
He also recognizes that completing schools is only part of becoming an effective infantryman. His next priority is gaining experience with his unit and learning how those specialized skills apply during collective training.
“For now, just getting some time being an infantryman on the line and gaining a little bit of knowledge, as part of a team, squad and platoon,” McConnell said.
Despite his accomplishments, he understands he is still early in his career.
“I still just want to be the best soldier I can,” McConnell said. “Obviously, I’m still a private, so I’m going to assume that role.”
Outside the National Guard, McConnell attends Oregon State University in Corvallis, where he is studying forestry with the goal of becoming a forester. He is also considering future military opportunities, including serving in a Ranger Regiment or becoming an Army aviation warrant officer and flying Black Hawk helicopters.
For now, however, he wants to put his training to work alongside fellow infantrymen.
“Going to all these schools, gives you some great knowledge in those specific areas,” McConnell said. “But when it comes to the practicality of everything, I feel like being on the line in your unit is a whole other ballgame.”
title: Washington Guard Infantryman turns training into career growth

text:
LOS ANGELES – The Justice Department, working with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), today filed a complaint against the State of California over its voter list after determining that more than 20,000 people who are likely aliens are registered to vote in California. Under California law, every registered voter is mailed a ballot. It is unlawful for aliens to vote in federal elections.

Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), in coordination with federal partners, analyzed publicly available voter-registration records to identify potential indicators that aliens may have registered to vote, cast ballots, or received election-related mail. The Department of Justice has filed a complaint against the State of California alleging that these individuals, who are likely noncitizens, registered to vote and/or voted in a federal election. HSI and its federal partners used multiple data-enrichment and verification methods to assess whether the individuals identified were likely aliens.

According to the lawsuit, the federal government sent relevant California officials a list of more than 20,000 names of people that it believes are likely noncitizens who were sent a vote-by-mail ballot from California to participate in the federal election. The federal government asked California to review the list and, in partnership with federal agencies, to determine whether citizens were listed. California failed to do so.

“State-facilitated voter fraud is unacceptable in the United States of America,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “If found responsible in a court of law, the State of California will have seriously undermined confidence in our electoral system and violated laws that protect our nation’s representative system of government. The Department of Justice will continue working to uncover cases of voter fraud, hold fraudsters accountable, and restore trust in American elections.”

“California election officials were given an opportunity to remove noncitizens from their voter rolls and to sequester ballots returned from suspected ineligible voters. They refused,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli. “We are taking California to federal court to demand that the votes of American citizens not be diluted by noncitizens.”

“It is unlawful for noncitizens to vote in federal elections,” said Secretary Markwayne Mullin of DHS. “The Department of Homeland Security and our federal partners reviewed publicly available California voter-registration files and compared relevant records with federal immigration data to identify alien registrants. This preliminary analysis has identified a significant number of individuals in California who are likely noncitizens and appear to be registered to vote; the analysis and review remain ongoing. This is completely unacceptable — as even one noncitizen vote cancels out the ballot of an American citizen and undermines our elections. DHS is committed to identifying unlawful voting, protecting the integrity of federal elections, and ensuring that only eligible American citizens elect America’s leaders.”

“The law is clear, aliens in the United States cannot vote in federal elections,” said Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter. “What our complaint alleges is that California is facilitating unlawful voting by knowingly allowing noncitizens to vote. This needs to stop.”

The United States is requesting the court prevent California from presently tabulating vote-by-mail ballots from likely noncitizens in the upcoming federal election until the voter’s citizenship status can be determined. The lawsuit seeks an order that California set aside vote-by-mail ballots from persons identified by the federal government likely to be noncitizens and to independently – or in collaboration with the federal government – verify their citizenship status beyond relying on unverified statements of citizenship necessary to registering before tabulating their vote-by-mail ballot.

The United States seeks to prevent unlawful dilution of American citizens’ votes and to protect the integrity of our nation’s elections.
title: United States Sues California After Determining More Than 20,000 Likely Noncitizens Are Registered to Vote in the Golden State

text:
SAN ANTONIO – A California man was sentenced in a federal court in San Antonio to 30 years in prison for the sexual exploitation of a minor, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas.

According to court documents, in May 2023, Markus Hudson Jr., 28, of Sacramento, California, coerced an adult woman he met on TikTok to sexually assault a six-year-old child in Uvalde. Hudson threatened the woman, saying he would send nude images of her to her family and friends. The woman complied and sexually assaulted the child during a video call with Hudson, unaware that her act was being recorded by Hudson using a second phone. Following the recorded sexual assault, the woman refused to speak to Hudson again, and he, in-turn, sent images of the assault to one of the woman’s former classmates.

In another instance, Hudson reached out to a 14-year-old on Snapchat in June 2024 and told her he had nude images of her. Hudson threatened to shoot up her house unless she did what he wanted. Hudson made the child victim stand naked for five minutes during a video call. Again, he recorded the call on a separate phone, then threatened to distribute the images if the 14-year-old did not sexually assault another minor. After repeated threats of exposure, the 14-year-old complied. The 14-year-old, two other minors, and an adult engaged in sexual activity which Hudson recorded. Hudson sent the images to the 14-year-old's classmates.

Hudson enticed and recorded the sexual activities of the 14-year-old, three minors, and two adults. He was arrested on Dec. 13, 2024. He was charged in a five-count indictment on Jan. 8, 2025, and pleaded guilty to two counts—one for production of child pornography and one for coercion and enticement of a child—on April 30, 2026.

“Social media platforms have become an incredibly dangerous playground in which child predators victimize our most vulnerable and exploit them with sickening demands, that exponentially increase the victimization,” said U.S. Attorney Simmons. “These investigations often begin because victims of the sexual abuse and exploitation speak out about the exploitation they have endured. As evidenced by this case and others, predators like this defendant should know that the seeming anonymity of the internet will not protect them from being held accountable for their actions. In cooperation with our law enforcement partners, we will investigate and aggressively prosecute all predators who are intent on ruining the lives of innocent and vulnerable victims.”

“The sentencing of Markus Hudson serves as a powerful deterrent to anyone targeting and exploiting the most vulnerable members of our community,” said FBI Special Agent in Charge Daniel Faith. “The defendant in this case pleaded guilty to despicable and heinous acts. Thanks to our law enforcement partners at Uvalde Police Department, Guadalupe County Sheriff’s Office and FBI Sacramento for their help bringing individuals like Hudson to justice and protecting the future of our nation by ensuring our children’s safety.”

The FBI, Uvalde Police Department, and Guadalupe County Sheriff’s Office investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Sade Bogart prosecuted the case.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC .

MATSUI ACTS TO PROTECT AMERICANS FROM HIGH COSTS AT THE GAS PUMP
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Doris Matsui (CA-07) introduced legislation to require the Department of Transportation (DOT) to examine whether it can strengthen fuel efficiency requirements to counter high gas prices and reinstate penalties for automakers that fail to produce fuel-efficient vehicles.
“Across the country, Americans are being squeezed by high gas prices, rising grocery bills, and everyday costs that keep stretching family budgets thinner,” said Congresswoman Matsui. “The Gas Money Saved Act meets people where they are by strengthening fuel efficiency standards that help drivers spend less on gas for years to come. This is a practical step to lower everyday costs, give families more breathing room, and build a cleaner, more efficient transportation future.”
“With gas prices skyrocketing because of President Trump’s prolonged and illegal war, we must take immediate steps to give American consumers some relief,” said Congresswoman Titus. “In May 2026, gas prices rose at a rate ten times higher than the rate of inflation. In Nevada, they now average $5.45 per gallon. Coupled with higher prices on groceries and other goods because of the Trump tariffs, families are struggling to make ends meet.”
Congresswoman Matsui, a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, and Rep. Dina Titus (NV-01), a member of the House Transportation Committee, introduced the Gas Money Saved Act to review Corporate Fuel Economy (CAFE) standards and reinstate fuel-efficiency requirements that were stripped away by Republicans’ Big Ugly Bill in 2025. Companion legislation has been introduced in the Senate by Senator Ed Markey (D-MA).
“Fuel economy standards help American drivers get around without breaking the bank while gas prices are high, but Trump and the Republicans gutted these standards as part of their crusade to put Big Oil above American families,” said Senator Markey. “Auto innovation should give consumers better choices, not cut corners at their expense. The Gas Money Saved Act would make sure American drivers have fuel-efficient vehicle options that are cheaper to fill up and hold automakers to account—a cost-saving measure that is especially critical as the Trump Administration would rather spend billions on an illegal war than keep costs low for Americans.
The Gas Money Saved Act would:
- Require DOT to reevaluate CAFE standards if gas prices rise at a rate five times faster than inflation over a six-month period, and;
- Restore and increase financial penalties on automakers if their car and truck fleet does not meet fuel efficiency standards.
title: MATSUI ACTS TO PROTECT AMERICANS FROM HIGH COSTS AT THE GAS PUMP

FORT LEE, Va. — After 30 years of dedicated service to the U.S. Army, Command Sgt. Maj. Thomas Skelton retired during a ceremony Oct. 8, recognizing his distinguished career of leadership, mentorship, and commitment to Soldiers.
Throughout his three decades of service, Skelton served in numerous leadership positions, shaping the development of countless Soldiers and noncommissioned officers. His career was marked by a steadfast commitment to Army values, mission accomplishment, and the well-being of those under his leadership.
Reflecting on his career, Skelton expressed gratitude for the opportunities and relationships that defined his service.
"Thirty years, nine months, and two days. But who’s counting," Skelton began. "When I joined the Army, I can promise you I wasn’t thinking about this day. I wasn’t thinking about becoming a first sergeant, a command sergeant major serving around the world. Back then, I was probably just trying not to get yelled at.”
Family, friends, coworkers, and fellow Soldiers gathered to celebrate Skelton's accomplishments and recognize the impact he made throughout the Army.
Col. Dan Horn, U.S. Army Logistics School commandant, praised Skelton's leadership and lasting influence on the force as he relinquished his senior enlisted responsibility.
"Command Sgt. Maj. Skelton has an extraordinary gift for closing the gap between concept and execution, between the staff officer’s pen and the Soldier’s wrench," Horn said. "Because of his ability to foster true shared understanding, our institutional force didn't just teach doctrine - we prepared warfighters to think critically and trust their teams."
Horn also highlighted Skelton's commitment to mentorship and readiness.
"As you take off the uniform and begin this well-deserved next chapter alongside Maci," Horn said. "Know that your footprint is stamped across thousands of officers and noncommissioned officers who will carry your standards into battles yet unfought."
As he begins the next chapter of his life, Skelton said he looks forward to spending more time with family while remaining connected to the military community.
"Ive spent my career believing in one simple principle: take care of people, and they will accomplish things you never thought possible," Skelton said. "The uniform comes off. The rank goes away. But the responsibility doesn’t. I’ll continue to mentor. I’ll continue to serve. And I’ll continue to take care of people wherever this next chapter takes me."
Command Sgt. Maj. Thomas Skelton retires with the gratitude of a thankful Army and a legacy of service that will continue to inspire future generations of Soldiers.
title: LGS CSM Retires After 30 Years of Army Service

text:
LANDSTUHL, Germany — Three Public Health Command Europe employees recently participated in “The Stinky Cheese Man”, a Kaiserslautern Military Community community-theater production. Ann Larson, a chemist in the Organic Chemistry Division; Christopher Veis, an environmental health engineer and Lt. Col. Carpaccio Owens, director for Environmental Health Sciences, contributed to the show as performers and music staff.
Larson, Veis and Owens recently joined the cast and production team for “The Stinky Cheese Man”, a community-theater production that brought together volunteers from across the Kaiserslautern Military Community.
For Veis, the path to the stage began with an interest in local productions and a willingness to audition.
“Community theaters are in place not only at Ramstein, but also through KMC Onstage,” Veis said. “You can follow their social media, see what shows they are doing and if one interests you, show up for auditions.”
Veis was selected to portray the Old Man. Owens, who had previously performed with his wife in “You’re a Good Man, Charlie Brown”, auditioned because he wanted to work with the show’s director, Brianna, whom he had met during an earlier production of “Legally Blonde”.
“I liked her energy and what she brought as an actor,” Owens said. “When I saw she was directing the show, I thought it would be fun to work with her.”
Owens and his wife initially auditioned together for different roles. His wife was cast as Cow Lady, while Owens became the voice of the Giant.
For Larson, involvement began behind the scenes. She was recruited to assist with teaching music for the production, then became one of two music directors.
“I honestly did not think I had time to do this,” Larson said. “Somehow you make it work, because you want to so badly.”
The show’s fractured-fairy-tale format gave Larson an opportunity to help connect an unconventional mix of music while working with performers as they learned songs.
“I’ve done music a lot in my life, but helping with a theater production like that was new for me,” Larson said. “It was really fun, just exercising that part of yourself and working with people.”
For the three public health professionals, theater provides more than a creative outlet. It offers a space away from demanding jobs, tight timelines and the responsibilities that come with supporting the military community.
“I’ve always found theater to be a great stress reliever,” Veis said. “It is a place that is not work. You find a lot of like-minded people who usually have stressful day jobs and in the evening, we get to play, have fun, sing fun songs and do crazy characters.”
Theater also builds connections among coworkers who may otherwise interact only in a professional setting.
Veis said participating in the production helped the cast members get to know one another beyond their roles at work.
Larson said acting has reinforced the value of actively listening to others and maintaining focus on a shared goal.
“Really pay attention to the other people that you work with,” Larson said. “That is important to understand what you need to communicate and how you should respond. We are all working toward the same goal.”
Veis said theater has made him more mindful of how messages are received.
“On stage, you know immediately if you communicated well by how the audience reacts,” he said. “At work, it is important to remember that it is not just how I heard something—it is how the other person hears it.”
Owens compared live performance to the need to adapt when plans change.
“Sometimes people get nervous, sometimes things just happen, and they have to adjust,” Owens said. “The supporting cast members adjust with them so there is not a huge pause.”
That mutual support, Owens said, is one of the strongest qualities of community theater.
“People are volunteering their time, talents and resources to make it all come together,” Owens said. “They are appreciative of the people who are there and the space they are in.”
For Larson, Veis and Owens, “The Stinky Cheese Man” was more than a performance. It was an opportunity to build confidence, strengthen communication and find community.
title: Public Health professionals find connection through community theater

Illegal Alien from Mexico Sentenced for International Conspiracy to Smuggle Aliens from Canada into United States
Edgar Sanchez-Solis, 27, an illegal alien from Mexico, was sentenced today to five years in prison for his role in an international human smuggling conspiracy that illegally brought aliens from Mexico and Central and South America across the northern border with Canada into the United States.
“Mr. Sanchez-Solis profited off of a scheme that undermined the security of our northern border and placed law enforcement officers and aliens in harm’s way when fleeing law enforcement,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Thanks to Operation Take Back America and the Justice Department’s commitment to enforcing the rule of law, yet another human smuggler has been held accountable for endangering human life.”
“HSI remains relentless in our pursuit to dismantle criminal networks that profit from human smuggling along the northern border,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Anthony J. Patrone of HSI Buffalo. “These organizations exploit vulnerable individuals, endanger lives, and threaten the safety of our communities. Working closely with U.S. Border Patrol and U.S. Customs and Border Protection, HSI Rouses Point is committed to disrupting illegal entry and transnational criminal activity throughout Northern New York.”
According to court documents, Sanchez-Solis was a leader of an alien smuggling organization (ASO) that operated between December 2022 and April 2025 and smuggled hundreds of aliens from Mexico and Central and South America into the United States. Once the aliens were inside the United States, the ASO employed drivers to pick them up and drive them further into the country. The defendant personally participated in and coordinated smuggling events with other leaders of the ASO. During one smuggling event in May 2023, a van carrying aliens became involved in a vehicle chase with U.S. Border Patrol. Border Patrol had to stop their pursuit due to risk to the public, and law enforcement had to use a tire deflation device to stop the vehicle after it failed to yield. The smuggled aliens paid the ASO thousands of dollars to be smuggled into the United States, and some then worked for the ASO smuggling other aliens to pay off their own smuggling debts.
Sanchez-Solis pleaded guilty on May 7 to one count of conspiracy to commit alien smuggling and five counts of alien smuggling for commercial advantage and private financial gain. Three other illegal aliens from Mexico were charged for their roles in the conspiracy. Ignacio Diaz-Perez, 37, and Samuel Diaz-Perez, 27, each pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit alien smuggling and six counts of aliens smuggling for financial gain. Salvador Diaz-Diaz, 34, pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit alien smuggling and five counts of aliens smuggling for financial gain. They are expected to be sentenced on Nov. 23.
HSI Rouses Point and U.S. Border Patrol Burke Station investigated the case, with substantial assistance from HSI’s Human Smuggling Unit in Washington, D.C., and U.S. Customs and Border Protection’s National Targeting Center International Interdiction Task Force.
Trial Attorney Spencer M. Perry of the Criminal Division’s Human Rights and Special Prosecutions Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Carling Dunham for the Northern District of New York is prosecuting the case.
This case was supported and prosecuted by Joint Task Force Alpha (JTFA), the U.S. Department of Justice’s lead effort in combating human smuggling and trafficking committed by cartels and Transnational Criminal Organizations throughout the Americas. In partnership with the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), JTFA investigates and prosecutes the most prolific and dangerous human smuggling and trafficking networks that impact public safety and border security. Led by the Criminal Division’s Human Rights and Special Prosecutions Section and supported by other Criminal Division components, JTFA has dedicated prosecutors from U.S. Attorneys’ Offices along the Southwest border, Southern Florida, Northern New York, and Vermont. JTFA partners with U.S. Attorneys’ Offices throughout the country and supports high-priority cases in any district. All JTFA cases rely on substantial law enforcement resources from DHS components, including U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Homeland Security Investigations, and U.S. Customs and Border Protection, U.S. Border Patrol, and the Office of Field Operations. JTFA also partners with FBI and other law enforcement agencies. To date, JTFA’s work has resulted in more than 486 domestic and international arrests of leaders, organizers, and significant facilitators of alien smuggling and trafficking; more than 486 U.S. convictions; and more than 374 significant jail sentences imposed and forfeitures of substantial assets.
This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and other transnational criminal organizations, and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. Operation Take Back America streamlines efforts and resources from the Department’s Project Safe Neighborhood.
title: Illegal Alien from Mexico Sentenced for International Conspiracy to Smuggle Aliens from Canada into United States

Russian National Arrested and Extradited to New York on Charges of Evading Sanctions on Russia
Alexander Suvorov, 52, a Russian national, has been charged by a criminal complaint with three counts related to the unlawful exporting of micro-electronic components from the United States to Russia via a front company based in Hong Kong.
“Those, like the defendant, as alleged, who seek to enrich themselves by evading economic sanctions on Russia, must understand that their actions carry serious consequences and will not be tolerated,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney John A. Sarcone III for the Northern District of New York. “My office, working together with the FBI and the Department of Commerce, will continue to aggressively prosecute these types of cases and hold offenders accountable to the fullest extent of the law. This historic extradition shows that we will fly over 3,800 miles to locate and bring to justice those who threaten national security.”
“Alexander Suvorov was the alleged mastermind behind an international procurement network that illegally supplied buyers in Russia with American-made electronic components that have military applications,” said Assistant Director Roman Rozhavsky of the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division. “His extradition to face charges here in the U.S. demonstrates the FBI's commitment to keeping sensitive, export-controlled technology out of the hands of the Russian military. We will continue working with our law enforcement, intelligence, private sector, and international partners to bring to justice all who attempt to arm our adversaries at the expense of our citizens and our national security.”
“The Bureau of Industry and Security is committed to strong enforcement,” said Special Agent in Charge Jonathan Carson of the U.S. Department of Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security New York Field Office. “Working closely with out law enforcement partners, we will continue to uncover and disrupt illicit procurement and diversion networks wherever they operate.”
Suvorov was extradited from Sweden to the Northern District of New York on Oct. 15 and is expected to have his initial appearance on Oct. 16 in Albany, New York.
The complaint filed against Suvorov alleges that between about March 2022 and April 2023, Suvorov led an illicit procurement network responsible for unlawfully exporting U.S. electronic components out of the United States to Russia. One of the procurement network’s main goals was to fraudulently obtain dual-use electronic components — that is, electronic components with both civilian and military applications — from U.S. companies for shipment to Russia. As alleged in the complaint, Suvorov’s primary role in the procurement network was to maintain front companies based in Hong Kong, including GS Group Limited, which the procurement network used to order electronic components from U.S. companies in an effort to conceal that the end users of the components were in Russia, and to then transship, via Hong Kong, the components from the U.S. companies to the end users in Russia. Suvorov and his companies are also alleged to have sent multiple wires to various U.S. companies to pay for the electronic components. Some of the components unlawfully purchased and exported to Russia by Suvorov and his procurement network can be used in military communication and radar systems, as well as precision location systems.
Count 1 of the complaint alleges conspiracy to commit international promotional money laundering and carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison, three years of supervised release, and a fine of $500,000. Count 2 alleges conspiracy to commit outbound smuggling and carries a maximum penalty of five years in prison, three years of supervised release, and a fine of $250,000. Count 3 alleges conspiracy to violate the Export Control Reform Act (ECRA) and carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison, three years of supervised release, and a fine of $1,000,000. A federal district judge will determine the sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
The FBI and Department of Commerce are investigating the case. The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs secured the extradition of Suvorov with the assistance of the Swedish Authorities.
Trial Attorney Garrett Coyle of the National Security Division’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Rick Belliss for the Northern District of New York are prosecuting the case.
title: Russian National Arrested and Extradited to New York on Charges of Evading Sanctions on Russia

MIAMI – A retired Boca Raton attorney pleaded guilty to attempting to obtain sexually explicit images from someone he believed was a 16-year-old girl through an online messaging application.

Darryl Kogan, 68, of Boca Raton, pleaded guilty to attempted receipt of visual depictions involving the sexual exploitation of a minor.

According to court records, on Feb. 18, a purported 16-year-old began communicating with Kogan through an online messaging application. During their conversations, Kogan discussed engaging in sexual activity and exchanging sexually explicit images with the purported minor.

Kogan sent the purported minor a sexually explicit photograph of himself and repeatedly requested sexually explicit images in return. At one point, Kogan told the purported minor, “Need pics to start the process.” When the purported minor indicated that she was having difficulty sending images through the application, Kogan provided specific instructions for taking and transmitting a sexually explicit photograph.

Law enforcement subsequently identified multiple accounts associated with Kogan that he used to engage in sexually explicit communications concerning minors.

“This was not an accidental or ambiguous online exchange. Darryl Kogan, a retired attorney, believed he was communicating with a 16-year-old girl, sent her a sexually explicit image of himself, repeatedly asked her for sexually explicit images, and gave her specific instructions for producing them. His guilty plea is another reminder that professional status offers no shield from accountability, and that the internet does not provide anonymity or protection to those who seek to exploit children. Those who attempt to sexually exploit minors online will be identified, prosecuted, and held accountable,” said U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida.

Kogan faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in federal prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

U.S. Attorney Reding Quiñones and Special Agent in Charge Brett D. Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office made the announcement.

FBI is investigating the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Jodi Anton is prosecuting the case.

Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Southern District of Florida at www.flsd.uscourts.gov or at http://pacer.flsd.uscourts.gov , under case numbers 26-cr-60256.

BOSTON – A Brazilian national, residing in Braintree, has been arrested and charged with knowingly transferring a false identification document.

Romulo Ferreira De Oliveira, 39, is charged with two counts of knowingly transferring a false identification document. Ferreira De Oliveira appeared in federal court in Boston on Oct. 13, 2026. A detention hearing is scheduled for Oct. 16, 2026.

According to the charging documents, on two separate dates in July 2026, Ferreira De Oliveira allegedly sold fraudulent identification documents to a confidential informant (“CI”) in exchange for money. It is alleged that on July 18, 2026, Ferreira De Oliveira sold a Lawful Permanent Resident card and a fraudulent Social Security card to a CI in exchange for money. It is further alleged that on July 28, 2026, Ferreira De Oliveira sold 11 fraudulent Social Security cards and one fraudulent Brazilian Driver’s License to a CI.

The charge of knowingly transferring a false identification document provides for a sentence of up to 15 years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of $250,000. The defendant is subject to deportation upon completion of any sentence imposed. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Jeffrey Grimming, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations in New England; and Robert J. Kilroy Jr., Braintree Police Chief made the announcement today. Assistant U.S. Attorney David Tobin and Suzanne Sullivan Jacobus of the Major Crimes Unit are prosecuting the case.

The details contained in the charging documents are allegations. The defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04) and U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works (EPW), last month launched a bicameral investigation into the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) guidance exempting data center power plants from the Acid Rain Program (ARP).
By EPA’s own admission, the decision to issue new guidance came at the behest of data center companies. And according to the EPA press release issuing the new guidance, the agency took this action to “further President Trump’s agenda promoting data centers.”
“EPA’s new ARP guidance is a handout to the richest and most powerful companies in the world. And this handout comes at the expense of Americans’ health and the safety of our ecosystems and communities that were, prior to the inception of the ARP, regularly drenched in dangerous acidic rainfall,” the lawmakers wrote in their letter to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin.
The ARP regulates the emission of sulfur dioxide (SO2) and nitrogen oxides (NOx) from power plants. SO2 and NOx are both harmful to human health, damaging the respiratory system and worsening heart disease. They are also linked to adverse pregnancy and birth outcomes, kidney damage, autoimmune disorders, and cancer.
The pollutants are also the primary causes of acid rain. Prior to the ARP, acid rain poisoned rivers, lakes, and streams; damaged forests; killed and sickened aquatic animals; and corroded buildings, monuments, and statues.
“EPA explicitly bills its new guidance as a means to facilitate data center development. In so doing, EPA misapprehends its own mission, which is to ‘protect human health and the environment,’ as stated in black and white on the agency’s own website,” continued the lawmakers.
“Bizarrely, under EPA’s new guidance, massive new gas-fired power plants large enough to power cities would be exempt from NOx and SO2 caps under the ARP only as long as they do not serve the public electricity grid and instead exclusively power a privately-owned data center. This is a perverse outcome, and it is contrary to Congress’s design for the Clean Air Act, which creates specific and comprehensive regulatory requirements for significant pollution sources like these,” added the lawmakers.
The lawmakers, together with Senators Ed Markey (D-MA) and Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), requested answers from EPA by October 7th about the agency’s decision-making process while crafting this new guidance, as well as any information regarding the agency’s communications with data center companies. Senators Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Cory Booker (D-NJ), and 24 Members of the House of Representatives also signed the letter. EPA has not yet responded to the lawmakers’ letter.
The letter to EPA Administrator Zeldin is available here.
title: McClellan, Whitehouse Investigate EPA’s Decision to Exempt Data Center Power Plants from Acid Rain Protections

RALEIGH, N.C. – Today, Ellis Boyle, U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of North Carolina, announced that a federal grand jury indicted 10 noncitizens, including an illegal alien, for illegally voting in the 2024 elections under 18 U.S.C. 611 and 1015.

“Protecting American elections from criminal interference continues to be one of the top priorities of this FBI,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “Today with our Justice Department partners we are announcing arrests and indictments of ten individuals - including one illegal alien and nine non-citizens - who illegally voted in the 2024 election in North Carolina, as alleged. American elections are for American citizens.”

“There is no more important right a citizen possesses above the right to vote. All other rights flow from this Constitutional principle when we the people select our government. Every non-citizen who chooses to illegally vote subverts our constitutional republic, actively canceling out the vote of a law-abiding citizen,” said U.S, Attorney Ellis Boyle. “This is not a victimless crime, quite the opposite. Every voting citizen is a victim every time. These indictments should serve as a stark warning to anyone contemplating voting illegally in our 2026 election: we are watching, we will find you if you do it, and we will prosecute you.”

A federal grand jury in the Eastern District of North Carolina reviewed evidence gathered by the FBI and HSI as presented by federal prosecutors and determined that probable cause existed to return indictments against these ten individuals. Following the indictments, federal agents arrested the defendants.

“The integrity of federal elections is essential to the health of our democracy,” said Reid Davis, the FBI Special Agent in Charge in North Carolina. “Every FBI field office assigns dedicated election‑crimes coordinators because protecting the election process is core to our mission. When questions about voter eligibility arise, we work closely with our state and federal partners to review records, confirm the facts, and ensure election laws are honored. Any violation erodes public trust and dilutes valid votes. When any aspect of our democratic process is threatened, the FBI will act decisively to defend it.”

"The right to vote is one of American citizens' most fundamental rights, and protecting our elections' integrity is a responsibility we take seriously," said acting ICE Director David J. Venturella. "When people illegally cast ballots, they undermine the law and the trust Americans place in our democratic process. These arrests send the message that election laws are not optional, and those who violate them will be held accountable. Working alongside our federal and state partners, we will continue to investigate election fraud and hold offenders accountable."

“I want to thank the U.S. Attorney Boyle and our federal law enforcement partners for their diligent work in pursuing these cases,” said Sam Hayes, Executive Director of the North Carolina State Board of Elections. “Election security is a top priority for the State Board, which is why we established our own Election Security and Enforcement Division. We will aggressively investigate allegations of voter fraud, and other election-related crimes, and we will work closely with state and federal prosecutors to ensure those who violate our election laws are held accountable.”

The indictments allege that all ten falsely claimed to be United States citizens to register and vote in the 2024 General Election. The felony offense of falsely claiming citizenship to vote carries the possibility of up to five years in prison. These charges reflect the Department of Justice’s commitment to protecting the integrity of federal elections and ensuring that only eligible U.S. citizens participate in them.

The grand jury returned indictments against the following individuals:

Eduardd Omar Majano Sosa , 22, a native of El Salvador and an illegal alien living in Cumberland County, is charged with one count of falsely claiming citizenship to vote and one count of voting by an alien. He registered to vote in 2024 and voted in the 2024 General Election.

He pleaded not guilty, and his trial is scheduled for March 2027. Read more at: James Darius Osborne Press Release

Orlando, Florida – Rusbel Montoya Mandujano (32, Oviedo) has been sentenced by U.S. District Judge Anne-Leigh Gaylord Moe to 25 years in federal prison for attempting to coerce and entice a minor to engage in illegal sexual activity. The Court also ordered him to forfeit his cellphone, which was used during the offense. Montoya Mandujano was found guilty by a jury on March 24, 2026. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement.

According to testimony and evidence presented at trial, on June 25, 2025, Montoya Mandujano began communicating online and via text messaging with someone he believed to be a 14-year-old girl. The “girl” was actually a team of detectives working with the Seminole County Sheriff’s Office in an undercover capacity. After Montoya Mandujano learned the “girl’s” age, he initiated discussions of various sexual acts he wanted to engage in with her, and he made a plan to meet with the girl to perform the sexual acts. When Montoya Mandujano arrived at the meeting location on June 26, 2025, he was arrested by law enforcement.

This case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, and the Seminole County Sheriff’s Office. It was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Megan Testerman. The asset forfeiture was handled by Assistant United States Attorney Nicole Andrejko.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the United States Attorney’s Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc.
title: Oviedo Man Sentenced to 25 Years in Federal Prison for Attempting to Coerce and Entice a Minor to Engage in Sexual Activity

Members of Congress Hold Hearing in Austin to Investigate ICE Shootings Across Texas
Casar, Thompson, Jayapal, Democratic Members of Congress demand accountability and change with ICE
AUSTIN, TEXAS – On Thursday, October 15th, Congressman Greg Casar (D-Texas), alongside Representatives Bennie G. Thompson (D-Miss.), Ranking Member of the House Committee on Homeland Security, and Pramila Jayapal (D-Wash.), Ranking Member of the Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement, and five other members of Congress held a field hearing to investigate the numerous ICE shootings across Texas, including the recent shooting of Wilber Garcés-Pérez.
Representatives Greg Casar, Bennie G. Thompson, and Pramila Jayapal were joined by Representatives Troy A. Carter, Sr. (LA-02), Lou Correa (CA-46), Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), and Al Green (TX-09).
The Members of Congress were joined by witnesses Ms. Rachel Reyes, mother of Ruben Ray Martinez, Kristin Etter, Director of Policy & Legal Services at the Texas Immigration Law Council, Carolina Rivera Nelson, Attorney at the ACLU of Texas, and Danny Woodward, Policy Attorney with Texas Civil Rights Project.
“Texas has become the epicenter of Trump’s deadly deportation machine, so we brought Members of Congress from across the country to Austin to see it firsthand,” said Congressman Greg Casar (D-Texas). “ICE shot Wilber Garcés-Pérez, a DoorDash driver and a father, in the back then denied him medical care. They even tried to deport him so he could never speak the truth. Donald Trump's ICE isn't going after the worst of the worst — it's gone after people like Wilber, who have no criminal record. We will fight to hold the perpetrators in this administration accountable, and not provide another dime in funding to this rogue agency."
“Democrats came to Austin today to demand justice and accountability for Wilber Garcés-Pérez and the others that have been shot by immigration agents in Texas. If Republicans refuse to conduct any oversight of the Trump administration, we must do so in their place,” added Congressman Bennie G. Thompson. “What we heard today was powerful and informative. Make no mistake: we will do everything possible to hold this administration accountable for what it is doing. This violence, lawlessness, and chaos in our communities must end.”
“Twenty-five days ago, ICE agents in Austin, Texas shot Wilber Garcés-Pérez in the back. Instead of taking him to the hospital, they locked him up in a detention center and did not allow him to have surgery for 11 days. This is not the most recent shooting by ICE, and is one of nearly a dozen that we know of since Trump returned to office,” said Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal. “ICE is a lawless, rogue agency that is causing generational trauma in communities across the country. House Democrats today are doing the oversight work that Republicans refuse to do — and we will continue to do everything possible to protect our communities from Trump’s mass deportation agenda.”
"The shooting and medical neglect of Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez follows the many other cases that have become synonymous with cities being swarmed with masked, armed federal agents and the nation’s dangerous descent into tyranny: Renée Nicole Good, Alex Pretti, Johan Sebastian Guerrero, and too many others. No life is meaningless, and each individual assaulted or killed by our immigration system is someone's child, someone's sibling, someone's parent, and they all still belong here with us,” said Congressman Troy A. Carter, Sr. “Unless you’re Native American, we all come from somewhere else. The Trump immigration system is structured and staffed as a deportation machine that violates individuals' constitutional rights. Democrats will fight for an immigration system that honors our history and sets forth a reasonable, compassionate path to citizenship." 
“President Trump got elected on the promise to go after the “worst of the worst.” Instead, since January, federal immigration agents have detained over 500 U.S. citizens and killed at least three. ICE is arresting people with no criminal record to hit political quotas while cutting training and lowering hiring standards,” said Congressman Lou Correa. “There is an urgent need for major reforms to keep our communities safe from violence. DHS was created to defend Americans against foreign terrorists. Instead, we have permanent residents and American citizens being shot by ICE agents in our streets.”
"In Texas, we have witnessed at least three ICE shootings since this administration began its aggressive, unprecedented enforcement actions,” said Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher.  “People across our community in Houston are still reeling from the shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo.  Just last weekend, ICE agents ran over and gravely injured Miguel Parra Hernandez while pursuing someone else. ICE's reckless and brutal actions are not only unprecedented, they're unconstitutional.  They are making us less safe, creating fear and danger for immigrants and citizens alike.  This Republican-led Congress that has enabled this lawlessness has utterly failed Wilber Garcés-Pérez, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, Ruben Ray Martinez, and so many others.  All Americans deserve better from our government, and that is why I joined Congressman Casar, Ranking Member Thompson, Congresswoman Jayapal, and my Democratic colleagues in Austin today to hear from some of the many people impacted, learn more, and demonstrate our commitment to bringing justice, accountability, and change.” 
“Trump promised to go after the worst of the worst. But judging by what we’re seeing across Texas and the country, that sounds more like ICE’s recruitment strategy. People are being shot, injured, and killed by federal agents operating without basic law enforcement standards or accountability,” said Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia. “In Houston, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was killed on his way to work. One hundred days later, his family still has no answers. Instead they’ve been met with stonewalling and excuses. These families deserve the truth and justice, and we will not stop fighting until they get both. 
“No President is above the law, and no federal agency should be allowed to serve as judge, jury, prosecutor, and executioner while operating with impunity,” said Congressman Al Green. “Under President Trump, ICE has been emboldened to use deadly force against people in our communities while the administration evades transparency and accountability, engaging in a cover-up. These shootings are not isolated incidents. They are part of a deeply troubling pattern of conduct that threatens the constitutional rights and lives of people in this country.”
The Members of Congress’ full remarks can be found here.
###
Congressman Greg Casar represents Texas’s 35th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives, which runs down I-35 from East Austin to Hays County to the West Side of San Antonio. A labor organizer and son of Mexican immigrants, Casar serves as the Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus for the 119th Congress. He also serves on the Committee on Education and Labor and the Committee on Oversight and Accountability.
title: Members of Congress Hold Hearing in Austin to Investigate ICE Shootings Across Texas
