Chief Pentagon Spokesman Sean Parnell provided the following readout:
On October 15, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth met with his United Kingdom counterpart, Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting, at the Pentagon. Secretary Streeting highlighted the United Kingdom's recently released Defence Investment Plan, which outlines increased British defense spending. Secretary Hegseth encouraged the United Kingdom to continue increasing defense spending further and faster to advance a fairer, stronger, and more sustainable NATO 3.0. Secretary Hegseth and Secretary Streeting discussed the Review of U.S. Force Posture and Basing in Europe and the opportunity it presents to ensure U.S. posture is aligned with the alliance we need—not the alliance of the past. Secretary Hegseth urged Secretary Streeting to continue supporting President Trump's objective of a durable peace in Ukraine and global security in the Strait of Hormuz.
title: Readout of Secretary of War Pete Hegseth's Meeting With the United Kingdom's Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting

text:
Remarks

Christopher Landau, Deputy Secretary of State

Philip J. Pierre, Saint Lucia Prime Minister

Susan Walke, State Department Director for Caribbean Affairs

Juan Pablo Segura, Assistant Secretary for Western Hemisphere Affairs

Loy Henderson Conference Room

Washington, DC

October 15, 2026

MS WALKE: Good morning, everyone, and welcome. My name is Susan Walke I’m the director for Caribbean affairs here at the State Department, and I will be your emcee for today’s dialogue. We are looking forward to a day of in-depth discussions on a number of key issues of importance to all of our countries.

I am delighted to introduce you to Assistant Secretary for Western Hemisphere Affairs, Juan Pablo Segura. Assistant Secretary Segura was sworn in as assistant secretary of state on August 14th. Before joining the State Department, he was the secretary of commerce and trade for the Commonwealth of Virginia for Governor Glenn Youngkin. As secretary, he was responsible for growing Virginia’s more than $710 billion a year in GDP economy, and managed the state’s international trade portfolio. Assistant Secretary Segura, I’m pleased to welcome you up to the dais. (Applause.)

ASSISTANT SECRETARY SEGURA: Thank you, Susan, for that great introduction. It’s a true honor to be here with all of you this morning, this incredible group of distinguished leaders across the Caribbean.

I’d like to start with just a reminder that Secretary Rubio made a promise earlier this year at Saint Kitts and Nevis. He promised that the U.S. would step up in the Caribbean, and this is a manifestation of that promise. This dialogue is the U.S. making good on its promise, which is incredibly exciting for all of us at the United States.

As you review the agenda, as we have the conversation that – the conversations that will happen over the next two years, you’ll see that the agenda mirrors the objectives of the Bureau of Western Hemisphere Affairs. Our objectives are very simple. The first is we want to uplift the region through economic investment. The second is we want to end the scourge of narcoterrorist threat across the hemisphere. And the third is we want to end illegal immigration. We want countries to have sovereignty, true sovereignty, across the hemisphere.

Now, as I introduce my boss, Deputy Secretary Landau, I do want to just highlight that this conversation really touches the why of why this conversation is so important. And I was recently speaking to one of you a week ago or a week and a half ago at the OAS, and it was very encouraging to see how everyone was leaning into the dialogue with the United States, but there was also a part of conversation where folks didn’t know the tools that are available in this economic conversation, this security conversation. A lot of folks don’t know that the President has prioritized 20 percent of our foreign assistance to the hemisphere. A lot of people don’t know that the DFC, the Development Finance Corporation, the mandate has changed.

The tools, the investment opportunities have changed. The (inaudible) has changed in how we can help countries grow economically and so I feel like there’s no better person to be the keynote speaker for today than the chair of the board of the DFC, a former ambassador, someone that knows the conversations, the real conversations that are happening at posts with your countries. And so it is an honor for me to introduce our incredible deputy secretary of state for the United States of America, Deputy Secretary Landau. (Applause.)

DEPUTY SECRETARY LANDAU: Thank you, Assistant Secretary. Welcome to our friends from the Caribbean. It’s really a pleasure to have such a distinguished group of leaders here today. I think this kind of dialogue is, frankly, overdue.

And I want to just start with what to me is the central reality underlying all of this, which is the United States is a Caribbean nation. You all know that. That is true as a matter of geography. We have – Puerto Rico is in the Caribbean. It’s true of our history. I was just discussing with several of you how Alexander Hamilton is from Nevis and, frankly, a huge part of our economy was the triangular trade between Europe, the eastern shore of the United States, the Caribbean. The relationships between the United States and this part of the world have been crucial throughout our history and throughout your history. And so we’re not writing on a blank slate as we gather here.

I think you all know this far better than I do, that the ties between our countries are not only historical; they involve people. When I was in Antigua last year, I was talking to somebody and I think of his siblings, two of them were in the States, and the cousins were in the States. The personal bonds between our countries are amazing. So many successful people in the United States, in this generation and previous generations, have come from your region. I’m going all the way back to Alexander Hamilton, but people like Colin Powell, who ran this building 25 years ago. I mean, our country has benefitted enormously from the ties with your region.

And frankly, it has been a source of pain for many of us as Americans to see the United States not giving the Western Hemisphere generally the attention it deserved, and specifically the Caribbean. The Caribbean is very much part of the Western Hemisphere. So I’m sure you’ve all seen the stories about how the United States is, under President Trump and Secretary Rubio – we are making the Western Hemisphere a – we’re not – we are restoring – I think that’s the better word – the Western Hemisphere to its position of preeminence and priority in American foreign policy. For far too long, we have been looking at things that are happening halfway across the world, and we have been ignoring things that are happening right in our own neighborhood.

And so I just want to – I think it’s very important that we recognize some of the flaws of recent years in our policies and we talk together to commit to ways that we can build institutional relationships. Because all of us in this room – I mean, we all have government positions, and it’s great, it lasts for a while. But then all of us will be gone in a matter of years, right? And I think the challenge for us is to create a lasting foundation that doesn’t just depend on so-and-so being friends with so-and-so. I mean, it’s wonderful and it’s great. One of the great things about these kinds of gatherings is that we can establish personal relationships, right? It’s great if I can have you on WhatsApp or that kind of thing. But that is not the basis for a lasting institutional structure of a relationship that’s going to survive over decades.

And I think – that’s what I’m hoping that a conference like today can establish – really both those things. I mean, again, personal ties are important in diplomacy. But again, I think I’m looking to strengthen the structural ties, again, many of which are there. I mean, we’re not building this from scratch, and I think we have a lot of historical precedent. But I also want to make clear that we in the United States do not have all the answers, right? I think I entered this job with a fair dose of humility that – I grew up in Latin America myself. My father was a diplomat and – including in Venezuela, where actually when – during the years in the early 80s when he lived in – when we lived in Venezuela, I actually had the opportunity to visit many of your countries for the first time. That’s when I first got the chance to go to Haiti, to Barbados, to Grenada, way back more than 40 years ago now. And again, that only underscored for me obviously the great diversity in the Caribbean but also the importance in so many areas of the United States with these relationships in the Caribbean.

So bringing together the leaders has been a real – your leaders – all of you has been something that’s been very important both for Secretary Rubio and for me. I think he was delighted to go to CARICOM. I think it was in – was it in Saint Nevis or in Saint Kitts and Nevis? He was at a meeting or – he went recently. And so I think he very much – again, as somebody from Florida – understands better than anybody the importance of this Caribbean region to the United States, across all dynamics, again, on a human level, on a economic level, on a security level.

And so, again, I just want to underscore that I think this dialogue is overdue, and I just want to underscore that – I want to underscore the word “dialogue,” right? A dialogue doesn’t mean that you have come here to have me or anybody else in the United States just give lectures, right? I mean, I just think it’s very important that we, the United States, listen to you from the Caribbean what your vision is. I mean, you obviously are – you all are sovereign countries; you are going to decide your fate. And – but I think – honestly, I truly believe we wouldn’t be having this meeting if the Secretary and I didn’t believe that what is in your interests is also in our interests; that there are many, many areas where we should be deepening cooperation where there are great solutions.

So again, I will talk today in part about further commitments the United States is going to make, and that’s fine. I was reading through the remarks that they prepared for me here; it’s like, well, we’ll give millions of dollars for this and millions of dollars for that. Ultimately, I’m more interested – and I think you should be more interested, or I would hope that you would be more interested – in, like, where do we get the businesses that are going to be there for the long term, that are investing in real economic opportunities that are creating a lasting foundation for the relationships? Because ultimately, a particular grant can be fine to fill a particular need, but for a long-term growth strategy, a particular grant isn’t going to fix that. Now, there may be particular grants that are useful insofar as they create a framework or a foundation for private-sector-led economic development. But ultimately, I think that’s what’s going to, frankly, be the main driver here.

So again, I just was talking to the representative of Suriname before we walked in here, and they said they had a great meeting, I think yesterday, with a private American security company that offered some services that could help them really improve their own security for their country. I said to me, that is great. And I feel my job, our job here at the Department of State, is to be the connective tissue between you, the leaders from your region, and the dynamic American private sector. The American private sector is going to have more creative, cost-effective solutions for the problems you’re looking at than the U.S. Government will. I’ll just tell you that. I say that as somebody who works for the government right now.

But ultimately, the greatness of the United States is not driven by the government; it’s driven by our private sector. And so our job – or what I see our job as being is just to be an interlocutor so that our private sector is aware of the opportunities in the Caribbean, and that the Caribbean is aware of what the private sector might be interested in here. I mean, it’s a conversation that has to go both ways.

So let’s actually start talking a little bit about economics. One of the things that makes me very happy is that we’re launching an investment dialogue next year precisely to bring together all of your countries with the American private sector. And so I think – this is an issue that I also fostered out in the Pacific region. That’s another area I’ve been very focused on, some of the island states, some of which have some similarities to some of the islands – nations of the Caribbean – not that big in terms of land mass of the country or even the population. So they present kind of interesting economic models, where there can be opportunities for economic development, but it’s not necessarily the most obvious target as a mass export market for American companies, let’s say, but where there might be investment opportunities that you all are interested in.

But I think for this kind of an investment conference to work, it needs a lot of advanced thought from both sides. I think I really would urge all of your countries to think about what kind of American private sector investment you are particularly interested in in your country. If you have an infrastructure project, a port, or a digital infrastructure project, an energy infrastructure project that you’re interested in; you want to talk to people in the telecommunications area – I mean, if you all – again, it’d be most helpful if you all let us know in advance. If you want to see a specific company, you say, I would like to see Google, I would like to see Bechtel, I would like to see a shipping company, I’d like to see American Airlines – whatever it is, that will make this kind of a conference more helpful. Because we don’t want to just have a conference for the sake of bringing people together to meet; we want to actually be able to have people who are actually interested in pursuing deals. And again, we will also reach out to the private sector and say, who is interested in opportunities in the Caribbean? And again, we will try to work it both ways.

But again, I encourage you to really give some thought. I don’t really have the details about what month this is yet next year, but I know it is next year. We will keep in touch on that. Again, that just makes me very, very happy, because ultimately, again, it’s this kind of investments that will create growth and jobs in your country and build skills.

We also recognize that economic development entails health. And we understand some of the health needs in your region.

And on health, this is when I start – this is what – I’m starting to tell some of the goodies that I’m here to talk about. I’m happy to announce we have 61 – set aside $61.5 million to launch ASPIRE, the America Strategic Partnership for Independent Regional Healthcare Excellence – that’s a long one – in order to allow the region to build its own strong, self-reliant health care workforce capacity. So again, I think we can get more details on that, but that’s one of the deliverables that I wanted to announce to you all today.

Second, I wanted to talk a little bit about security, and I think the assistant secretary alluded to this. I think we have seen an uptick in recent years of drugs coming through the Caribbean from South America towards the United States. I don’t need to tell you what a danger this is for all of us. And frankly, as you’ve all seen if you read the news, the United States is not going to just sit by with business as usual where we have more than 100,000 Americans dying of overdose from some of these drugs just in perpetuity. I think we’re – we have followed a approach of using the judicial system, asking for arrests, extraditions, trying people. And I think, as you’ve seen, we now recognize that this is actually also a national security threat to our people. We’re taking actions accordingly. And we’d like to work with your countries to make sure that we’re all on the same page, at least in recognizing the common danger of this and seeing how we can try to address this scourge together.

So we already have a Caribbean Basin Security Initiative, and that’s the foundation of our security partnership with 13 of the countries. And today we are – again, my next deliverable that I’m announcing is that we’re increasing our support through CBSI, and I’m pleased to announce $37 million in new programming to protect critical digital infrastructure and strengthen port security. Obviously, strong ports are the first line of defense. If drugs are coming into your ports – or it’s not just drugs also; it’s also weapons and other illegal goods. I mean, and I think in my first week in the job, the Secretary called me down to his office and handed me an article about guns going to Haiti from the Miami River and said, “Could you please deal with this?” And that was the beginning of what has been a pretty intense involvement, as the prime minister of Haiti here, my friend, Prime Minister Fils-Aimé, knows. I’ve been very involved in Haiti, but it really stemmed out of trying to stop the flow of guns that are going from our country into Haiti and destabilizing it.

And I will say on this note, I am working closely with our U.S. attorney in the Southern District of Florida to make sure that our law enforcement capabilities are fully mobilized and that we are coordinating with them, so if there are issues where you think the American judicial system can actually be helpful to you as leaders in your countries who are trying to solve particular problems – if there are criminal networks that are exporting drugs from your country and you think your country may not have all the infrastructure or the legal infrastructure to address this problem, let’s work together on some of these security challenges, because our U.S. Attorney’s Office in Miami is very eager to work with you on that.

Another big priority is illegal fishing, and I’d like to – that’s been a priority of mine worldwide. If there are people fishing illegally in your waters, we want to work with you to address that, because obviously fish is a important resource for all of our peoples. And I’m also – on this issue, I’m announcing an additional $55.5 million to strengthen law enforcement – I told you I had a lot of millions here to talk about – 55.5 million to strengthen law enforcement and $11 million in Foreign Military Financing to build the capabilities of your security forces. So again, I think let’s talk about how we can work together with the security ministers, with CARICOM IMPACS, to convene the next Caribbean Basin Security Initiative security ministerial in spring 2027, next spring.

Third – and I see I’m running low on time, but I just want to cover a range of issues that – I’m sure that all of you can flesh out what’s on your mind – trusted infrastructure is really important, and particularly secure communications networks. Ultimately, a modern economy cannot exist without a secure network. We all have seen vulnerabilities. Every day you read about it in the news. And – but without a good digital footprint, you can’t have a solid banking system, tourism system, energy grid, or government services. And who builds those networks matters, and we would like to work with you on that. In fact, on this – in this connection, I’m announcing $175.8 million in U.S. investment in secure infrastructure through our Caribbean and Central America underseas cables program. This will provide trusted, high-speed connectivity across the region to build resilient, secure networks that serve your people and not outside interests.

So together, the numbers that I have mentioned really total hundreds of millions of dollars in new commitments, but it’s not just about a certain dollar amount. It’s about just the long term, the United States reaffirming its interest and commitment to this critical region.

So I just want to end by underscoring the values that I think that we all share: respect for national sovereignty, the rule of law, open markets. These are some of the central tenets that underlie our relationships. And these are – by focusing on these core issues, that’s how we’re going to stimulate economic growth, attract investment, and allow you and us to provide prosperity and security for our – your citizens and our citizens. So again, as somebody who is very, very committed to your region, I just say that there are few events that I have attended during my time as Deputy Secretary of State that I’m as excited to be part of as this one.

I will close by just saying my last class in college, at Harvard College, was Sociology 113 that was taught by Orlando Patterson. He was visiting at Harvard that year. And it was on the sociology of the Caribbean, just all the many fascinating aspects of culture that emerged in your region. I mean, you have such an interesting mixture, just looking at the backgrounds of your countries. And I remember my last exam in college was comparing Rastafarianism in Jamaica with Vodou in Haiti and how some of those ancestral beliefs affected the modern development of those countries.

And I just want to say that, at least in me, I want you to know that you have a true friend of the Caribbean, someone who, again, is very cognizant of the critical role that your region has always played in the development of our country, and I think it is – you’re part of our past, you’re part of our present, and part of our future, and vice versa, I think. And I just want to, on that note, say how pleased and excited I am to welcome all of you here. And I hope this is a very enriching experience for all of you, as I’m sure it will be for us. Thank you very much. (Applause.)

MS WALKE: Thank you. And may I now ask Prime Minister Pierre of Saint Lucia, our CARICOM chair, to please come to the podium to deliver your remarks? Thank you. (Applause.)

PRIME MINISTER PIERRE: Thank you very much. Good morning, everyone. Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau, Assistant Secretary Juan Pablo, fellow heads of government, heads of delegation, ladies and gentlemen, I’ve been told I have three minutes. (Laughter.)

DEPUTY SECRETARY LANDAU: I’m sorry. I went way over on mine, so —

PRIME MINISTER PIERRE: I shall remain within my three minutes. Good morning, everyone. I speak as Prime Minister of Saint Lucia and chairman of the Caribbean Community. I thank the Government of the United States for convening this dialogue and for its hospitality. This meeting responds to the call by CARICOM leaders for political-level consultations following our constructive engagement with Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Saint Kitts and Nevis in February.

We value this relationship. Our countries are connected by geography, commerce, tourism, family, and friendship. The Caribbean community is a close neighbor, a stable democratic partner, and a region open to investment. We seek a more strategic partnership sustained by regular dialogue and measured by improvements in the daily lives of our people.

For Caribbean families, energy security means affordable electricity. Economic cooperation means jobs, investment, and opportunity. Security cooperation means safer communities. Disaster preparedness means knowing that help will arrive when it is needed and will arrive promptly. These are shared interests.

Our discussions today should translate into practical commitments financing for resilient energy systems, predictable trade and stronger commercial partnerships, secure infrastructure, stronger health systems and disaster response, and coordinated action against organized crime and illicit firearms trafficking. Haiti must remain central to our attention. We appreciate the U.S.’s role and welcome the extension of the United Nations mandate for the Gang Suppression Force. CARICOM continues – continues its work through the Eminent Persons Group. Sustained international assistance and credible elections with the widest possible participation are essential to restoring confidence and supporting Haiti’s return to stability.

Our dialogue must also make room for immigration and migration matters, with profound implications for our communities and our people-to-people ties. The strength of today’s meeting will be demonstrated by what follows it. Let us connect political dialogue with sustained technical engagements, identify priorities, and establish clear arrangements for follow-up between governments and the private sector. The CARICOM Secretariat will help coordinate the community’s technical work alongside our national authorities and regional institutions. CARICOM comes to this table ready to listen, ready to engage, and ready to build a partnership that delivers mutual benefit, with respect for our sovereignty and our shared aspirations.

I look forward to these discussions and the (inaudible) development of the people of the region. I thank you. (Applause.)

Tags
title: Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau With Saint Lucia Prime Minister Philip J. Pierre at the Opening Remarks of the U.S.-Caribbean Dialogue

BOSTON – A Dominican national unlawfully residing at the Quality Inn Hotel in Revere, Mass. pleaded guilty today in federal court in Boston to possessing over 4.5 kilograms of fentanyl and an assault rifle.

Leonardo Andujar Sanchez, 30, pleaded guilty to one count of possession with intent to distribute more than 400 grams of fentanyl and one count of being an illegal alien in possession of a firearm. U.S. District Court Judge Allison D. Burroughs scheduled sentencing for Jan. 7, 2027. Andujar Sanchez was arrested and charged in January 2025 and later indicted by a federal grand jury in September 2026.

Andujar Sanchez was residing in the Quality Inn in Revere. On Dec. 27, 2024, during a search of the room Andujar Sanchez was residing in, over 4.5 kilograms of fentanyl, an AR-style assault rifle, ammunition, three rifle magazines, digital scales and an abundance of latex gloves were located. Andujar Sanchez was immediately taken into state custody.

The charge of possession with intent to distribute more than 400 grams of fentanyl provides for a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years and up to life in prison, at least five years of supervised release and a fine of up to $10 million. The charge of unlawful possession of a firearm provides for a sentence of up to 15 years in prison, up to three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. The defendant is subject to deportation proceedings upon completion of any sentence imposed. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Jarod A. Forget, Special Agent in Charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration, New England Field Division; and Thomas A. Greco, Special Agent in Charge of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives, Boston Field Division made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the Suffolk County District Attorney’s Office and the Revere Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Brian J. Sullivan and Brad A. Rocheville of the Criminal Division are prosecuting the case.
title: Illegal Alien Pleads Guilty to Possessing Assault Rifle and Kilograms of Fentanyl

Maryland Delegation Members Release Statement on Judge Ruling Halting Trump Administration Efforts to Close BARC in Beltsville, Maryland
WASHINGTON – Today, Representatives April McClain Delaney, Glenn Ivey, Steny Hoyer, Kweisi Mfume, Jamie Raskin, Sarah Elfreth, and Johnny Olszewski and U.S. Senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks (all D-Md.) released the following statement regarding last night’s ruling by a federal judge, temporarily halting the Trump Administration’s efforts to close the Beltsville Agricultural Research Center (BARC) in Beltsville, Maryland.
“As we’ve said time and again, this Administration’s attempts to shutter BARC are not only unwise – they’re illegal. BARC conducts critical research that helps farmers across our nation put food on the table for American families – including combatting serious threats to our agriculture, like cyclospora and avian flu. Last night’s ruling from a federal judge made plain: the Administration’s efforts are in clear violation of Congressional intent. We will continue fighting back against the Trump Administration’s lawless attempts to close this facility, undermining its crucial research on behalf of American farmers and families.”
The lawmakers have repeatedly stressed the importance of maintaining BARC, including, most recently pushing Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins on this matter in April. Additionally, they have raised this issue in Committee hearings with Administration officials and fought for language in Congressional Appropriations and the most recent Continuing Resolution.
title: Maryland Delegation Members Release Statement on Judge Ruling Halting Trump Administration Efforts to Close BARC in Beltsville, Maryland

DOJ, ATF, Law Enforcement Partners Conclude Operation Show Me Justice
The Department of Justice, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), U.S. Marshals Service (USMS), U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Missouri, and others today announced the conclusion of Operation Show Me Justice, an ATF-led high‑impact violent crime enforcement surge in St. Louis.
The DOJ‑sponsored operation was a whole‑of‑government initiative led by ATF and carried out in close coordination with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Missouri and in partnership with the St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department, USMS, Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), FBI, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), and other federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies.
“Operation Show Me Justice demonstrates exactly what happens when federal, state, and local partners unite behind a single mission: protecting communities from violent criminals,” said Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter. “The results speak for themselves. Dangerous criminals are off the streets, their weapons are out of circulation, and families in St. Louis are safer today than they were before.”
“Operation Show Me Justice delivered the kind of decisive action the public should expect from ATF,” said ATF Director Rob Cekada. “We removed violent offenders from the street, cut off their access to firearms, and dealt a significant blow to the criminal networks endangering this community.”
“By removing these dangerous firearms from St Louis, together, we have achieved unprecedented results, not just for the partners who participated in Operation Show Me Justice, but for all the residents, commuters, students, and visitors to the Gateway City,” said Director Gadyaces S. Serralta of the U.S. Marshals Service.
“We in St. Louis are very grateful for the women and men of ATF who left home, came to our community, and faced daily danger to assist in this enforcement effort,” said U.S. Attorney Thomas C. Albus for the Eastern District of Missouri. “Just as important, we are grateful to all local, state, and federal law enforcement and prosecutors who fight violent crime every day and who will remain. We are in this for the long haul and want so much to help continue to drive down violence for the health and safety of our city that we love.”
“Driving down violent crime takes relentless follow-through, and our partnership with ATF and our other law enforcement partners helps us turn local intelligence into cases that hold violent offenders accountable,” said St. Louis Metropolitan Police Chief Robert J. Tracy. “Operation Show Me Justice builds on that daily collaboration and our commitment to lasting progress—so every neighborhood can experience a safer St. Louis.”
The operation focused on violent criminal conduct and the illegal supply of firearms to violent offenders. During the operation, ATF and its partners arrested more than 435 violent offenders, including individuals with histories of possessing machine guns illegally, carrying stolen firearms, resisting arrest, violating felon‑in‑possession laws, engaging in straw purchasing, and committing other serious weapons-related offenses.
Agents, officers, analysts, and prosecutors combined local intelligence with ballistic leads from the National Integrated Ballistic Information Network (NIBIN) and insights from crime‑gun tracing to drive investigations forward. This coordinated approach enabled investigators to connect shootings, link firearms to multiple crime scenes, identify gun and drug trafficking patterns, and develop leads that otherwise would remain isolated across jurisdictions.
NIBIN compares ballistic evidence from crime scenes with test‑fired shell casings from recovered firearms, generating actionable leads. Crime‑gun tracing tracks a firearm’s commercial history, from the manufacturer or importer to its first retail sale. When paired with traditional investigative work, these tools help investigators identify shooters, associates, firearms traffickers, and sources of crime guns fueling violence.
Operation Show Me Justice has delivered significant enforcement results in St. Louis, with 435 criminal arrests and 166 firearms seized to date. Participating agencies have cleared 412 warrants, including the execution of 32 search warrants, and seized 81 kilograms of drugs, six machine gun conversion devices, and more than $1.25 million in currency related to suspected illegal firearms and drug transactions.
title: DOJ, ATF, Law Enforcement Partners Conclude Operation Show Me Justice

INDIANAPOLIS, IN – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Indiana today announced charges against former tax preparer Evans Kludje, 43, of Brownsburg, as part of nationwide enforcement actions led by the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division, Internal Revenue Service, and Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation targeting tax fraud and related offenses. The Southern District of Indiana was a key participant in this surge effort.

Between early September and today, federal prosecutors across the country facilitated fraud enforcement actions spanning over 76 criminal defendants, whose alleged and proven crimes resulted in over $490,000,000 in intended loss to American taxpayers.

Evans Kludje, 43, of Brownsburg, signed a petition to plead guilty to two counts of Aiding and Assisting the Making of a False Federal Income Tax Return on July 31, 2026.

Between 2017 and 2025, Evans Kludje worked as a partner and tax preparer at Millennium Tax Group (MTG), receiving about 40% of the business’s profits. In 2021, he launched his own tax preparation company, Imperium Financial Group (IFG), while preparing some returns for MTG. During the 2024 filing season, he briefly returned to MTG to assist with 2023 tax returns, working for both businesses simultaneously.

According to the indictment, Kludje prepared false income tax returns for several clients of both MTG and IFG by submitting fraudulent Schedule A forms without the clients’ knowledge. He allegedly claimed large, fictitious itemized deductions—including charitable contributions and other unsupported expenses such as “ordinary loss debt instrument,” “unrecovered pension investments,” and “claim repayments”—to inflate clients’ tax refunds.

These fraudulent deductions significantly reduced clients’ taxable income and produced refunds they were not entitled to receive. Kludje allegedly filed these returns under the clients’ names without disclosing himself as the paid preparer, as required by law.

From 2017 through 2025, Kludje was responsible for preparing and filing thousands of fraudulent tax returns, which resulted in a loss of millions of dollars.

A sentencing hearing will be scheduled at a later date. Kludje faces a maximum sentence of up to five years in federal prison for each count.

This press release details one way in which this office has contributed to ensuring that all Americans pay their fair share. To see the successes of other offices, please see this press release.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

title: U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Indiana Joins DOJ Fraud Division, IRS, and IRS-CI in National Tax Enforcement Surge Exposing $490M in Tax Fraud

BUFFALO, N.Y. – U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Michael Paonessa, 36, of Niagara Falls, NY, who was convicted of possession with intent to distribute, and distribution, of fentanyl, was sentenced to serve 198 months in prison by U.S. District Judge Richard J. Arcara.

On the evening of April 28, 2023, Paonessa and his girlfriend, identified as R.A., went to dinner at a restaurant in downtown Buffalo. The investigation determined that R.A. asked Paonessa for drugs and he promised to give her with some, which he had done on multiple occasions during their relationship, including on two occasions in March and April 2023, which resulted in non-fatal overdoses. Paonessa and R.A. stayed at the restaurant until approximately 2:00 a.m. on April 29th, before returning to R.A.’s Sheridan Drive apartment in Tonawanda, NY. In the early morning hours of April 29, R.A. suffered a fatal overdose, which was caused by consuming the fentanyl that Paonessa had given her. Paonessa was at the apartment before and after R.A. passed away and knew that she had passed away. He ultimately left the apartment at approximately noon, without alerting authorities to her death. As Paonessa drove away, he sent a text from his phone to R.A.’s phone telling her that he had just woken up and asked R.A. to call him. Paonessa sent the text to make it appear that he was not with R.A. the prior evening. On that same morning of April 29, R.A.’s family members became concerned because she had not responded to texts or phone calls. A short time after Paonessa left R.A.’s apartment at noon, R.A.’s family members arrived at her apartment and found her body.

In addition, Paonessa was caught in possession of controlled substances on multiple occasions in 2023. On March 25, 2023, law enforcement recovered approximately eight grams of cocaine, 23 grams of fentanyl, $16,795 in cash, drug paraphernalia, and a loaded magazine. On May 30 and June 7, 2023, law enforcement conducted two controlled purchases from Paonessa. In September of 2023, Paonessa was arrested and law enforcement recovered approximately 35 grams of fentanyl, approximately nine grams of cocaine, cash and a digital scale.

The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Michael J. Adler. The sentencing is the culmination of an investigation by the DEA, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Farhana Islam, New York Field Division, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Bryan DiGirolamo, the North Tonawanda Police Department, under the direction of Chief Keith Glass, and the Niagara County Drug Task Force, under the direction of Sheriff Michael Filicetti.

title: Niagara Falls man going to prison for more than 16 years for distributing fentanyl that led to a death

National Endowment for the Arts Statement on the Death of NEA Opera Honors Recipient Martina Arroyo
Washington, DC—It is with great sadness that the National Endowment for the Arts acknowledges the passing of 2010 NEA Opera Honoree Martina Arroyo, who also served on the National Council on the Arts from 1976-1982. Arroyo was a legendary soprano who captivated audiences around the world through her operatic roles, oratorio and recital performances, and recordings, while opening doors for new generations of opera singers.
Born on February 2, 1936, and raised in Harlem by her Puerto Rican father and African-American mother, Martina Arroyo studied ballet, piano, and choral singing growing up. After graduating from Hunter College with a bachelor’s degree in Romance languages, she worked as a teacher and caseworker but continued her artistic pursuits. In 1958, she won the Metropolitan Opera’s Auditions of the Air competition, the same year she made her Carnegie Hall debut. She went on to become one of the leading sopranos of her generation, performing at the Metropolitan Opera, La Scala, the Paris Opéra, Covent Garden, and Teatro Colón, while building an extensive recording career. Appointed by President Gerald Ford in 1976, Arroyo served six years on the National Endowment for the Arts’ National Council on the Arts. A dedicated educator and mentor, she established the Martina Arroyo Foundation in 2003 to help emerging singers prepare for professional careers. Her warmth, quick wit, and frequent television appearances - including more than 20 appearances on The Tonight Show - helped introduce opera to wider audiences. She was inducted as a Fellow into the American Academy of Arts and Sciences (2002) and received numerous awards, including the V.E.R.A. honor from The Voice Foundation (2006); the NEA Opera Honors (2010); and the Kennedy Center Honors (2013), among others. Arroyo is remembered as a singular talent and champion of opera who made the art form more accessible.
Her commitment to nurturing the next generation remained central throughout her life, notably to young artist development through the Martina Arroyo Foundation. As she told the Arts Endowment in a 2010 podcast, “When you’ve had the good luck to have a career, it’s your responsibility to turn around and help the next ones coming along and reach out your hands and say, ‘I’m here.’”
For more information on Martina Arroyo, including interviews and video tributes, visit arts.gov.

WASHINGTON — Today, the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) announced that its Million Dollar Pitch Competition will stream starting October 20 on Prime Video and YouTube. The high-stakes contest, hosted by Dean Cain and judged by celebrity entrepreneurs Nicki Minaj, Grant Cardone, and Joe Gebbia, was taped before a live audience in Washington, D.C., where five finalists pitched their small businesses for a chance to win a portion of a $1 million cash prize pool funded by Clover Network, Inc. (Clover). The show includes a special appearance by President Donald J. Trump and recalls the vision he shared with the nation during The Apprentice, an award-winning show that celebrated the tenacity and vision required to compete and win in business.
“The Trump SBA is thrilled to announce that the Million Dollar Pitch Competition will stream on Prime Video and YouTube reaching audiences across our country and around the world, celebrating 250 years of free enterprise, American exceptionalism, and the hardworking small businesses that make it possible,” said SBA Administrator Kelly Loeffler. “Competing nationally to reach the stage, five exceptional entrepreneurs put everything on the line to earn a share of a $1 million cash prize pool – showcasing the grit, vision, and sacrifice of Main Street leaders who believe in the American Dream. The SBA is proud to highlight the importance and contributions of our nation’s small businesses, while inspiring the next generation of entrepreneurs, risk-takers, and innovators to build their future.”
Launched as part of the SBA's Freedom 250 celebration, the Million Dollar Pitch Competition marks the culmination of a nationwide entrepreneurship contest created to honor the innovation, grit, and economic impact of America’s Main Street businesses. The five finalists put their business acumen, growth strategies, and vision to the test – while sharing the personal stories of resilience and sacrifice that brought them to the national stage. The special gives audiences across America and around the world a window into the families, workers, and communities that power our nation’s economy from jobs to innovation and growth in every state.
The following national finalists are featured in the Million Dollar Pitch Competition finale:
- Paul Melrose, Compotech, Inc. (Brewer, Maine)
- Lisa and George Winton, Winton Machine (Suwanee, Georgia)
- Dean, Ryan, and Andrew Sonquist, Plas-Tech Tooling Inc. (Garner, Iowa)
- Marshall Sasse, Red River (Gillette, Wyoming)
- Hernán Luis y Prado, VetPowered LLC (San Diego, California)
The finalists competed for five cash prizes funded by Clover:
- First Place: $400,000
- Second Place: $250,000
- Third Place: $150,000
- Fourth Place: $125,000
- Fifth Place: $75,000
To learn more about the Million Dollar Pitch Competition, including more information about how to view the streaming special on Prime Video and YouTube, visit www.sba.gov/freedom250.
# # #
About the U.S. Small Business Administration
The U.S. Small Business Administration helps power the American dream of entrepreneurship. As the leading voice for small businesses within the federal government, the SBA empowers job creators with the resources and support they need to start, grow, and expand their businesses or recover from a declared disaster. It delivers services through an extensive network of SBA field offices and partnerships with public and private organizations. To learn more, visit www.sba.gov.
title: SBA’s Million Dollar Pitch Competition to Stream on Prime Video and YouTube

United States Attorney Lesley A. Woods announced that David Pardinas, 39, of Omaha, Nebraska, was sentenced on October 9, 2026, in federal court in Lincoln, Nebraska, for one count of distribution of child pornography. United States District Judge Susan M. Bazis sentenced Pardinas to 300 months’ imprisonment. There is no parole in the federal system. After Pardinas’s release from prison, he will begin a lifetime term of supervised release. Pardinas was additionally ordered to pay $9,000 in restitution.

On December 10, 2024, an online cybertip was submitted to the FBI National Threat Operations Center regarding Pardinas being in possession of child pornography in Omaha. According to the cybertips, the reporting party had let Pardinas use her cell phone and Pardinas forgot to log out of his email account before he provided the phone back. The reporting party stated that she saw very disturbing videos and photos in his email account. Agents obtained Pardinas’s criminal history and learned that he was previously convicted in Hall County, Nebraska in 2020 for sexual assault on a child 3 rd degree and criminal attempt-possession of child pornography, both felony offenses.

FBI Omaha’s investigation discovered four additional cybertips reported to National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) which were tied to Pardinas’s email address. The most recent report was submitted by a social media platform on October 31, 2024. The cybertips indicated images were shared by Pardinas to another individual. The cybertip contained at total of 29 images and videos of child sex abuse material reportedly shared by Pardinas on the social media platform.

On December 17, 2024, Pardinas was arrested for a probation violation stemming from possession of a controlled substance. Law enforcement interviewed Pardinas and he admitted ownership of the email addresses listed within the cybertips.

Law enforcement received search warrants for his email account and the social media account tied to the cybertips. A search of those accounts revealed 74 images of child pornography and 180 videos of child pornography. A review of the social media account revealed numerous instances of Pardinas trading and sharing child pornography with other users.

“Law enforcement is to be commended for taking this predator out of the Omaha community,” said United States Attorney Lesley Woods. “Nebraska is a safer place for children with this offender behind bars for the next 25 years.”

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by United States Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.projectsafechildhood.gov.

This case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and Bellevue Police Department.
title: Omaha Man Sentenced to 25 Years for Distribution of Child Pornography

CORPUS CHRISTI ARMY DEPOT, Texas — Corpus Christi Army Depot dispatched integrated teams of artisans specializing in the Apache E-model transmission to Fort Rucker and Fort Drum following the Army’s directive to temporarily suspend flight operations for AH-64E Apache helicopters equipped with Improved Drive System transmissions.
The grounding directive spanned all active-duty and National Guard attack aviation units operating E-model Apaches equipped with this specific component. This action followed an ongoing Army technical and airworthiness assessment of the Improved Drive System transmission. Accelerated inspections were provided across participating units to rapidly restore operational readiness and meet critical movement timelines.
“When the grounding directive was issued, our depot’s integrated team immediately pivoted to support the technical and airworthiness assessment,” said work leader Wesley Bocanegra. “Our top priority has been ensuring every E-model Apache meets the highest safety standards, with focused attention on units preparing for critical movements.”
The combined effort to return Fort Rucker’s training fleet to flight status and support priority missions at Fort Drum positioned CCAD as a critical link between operational units, Original Equipment Manufacturers, and the Army’s enterprise-level logistics network.
During the initial phase of inspections at Fort Drum, which began in mid-September. CCAD served as the sole operational element on-site while Boeing and Aviation Field Maintenance Directorate technicians finalized operations at Fort Rucker. The depot's integrated team rapidly prepared seven transmissions for inspection, building strong operational momentum ahead of partner’s arrival.
“CCAD’s primary mission in the field is removals,” said depot Sgt. Maj. Jeremy Bucholtz. “We pulled the transmissions out of the aircraft and placed them into the proper configuration, so they are staged and ready for the technical teams to inspect. Once broken down, the OEM stepped in to conduct the actual safety-of-flight checks.”
The depot's integrated teams prepared numerous transmissions for inspection of the schoolhouse fleet and initial-entry aviators. Eighteen of the transmissions were staged on the ground upon arrival, while another 15 were prepared and processed.
At Fort Drum, the depot team identified significant number of transmissions requiring removal from grounded aircraft. Depot teams executed the required removals, with AFMD assisting on three, reaching 100% removal completion by mid-October.
“CCAD proved to be an indispensable combat multiplier during operations at Fort Drum,” Bucholtz said. “Within 24 hours of boots hitting the ground, the team proved every day that this mission could not succeed without depot-level expertise.”
Inspecting and clearing the Fort Rucker fleet was intended to establish an operational surplus of IDS transmissions. After retaining sufficient assets to reserve flight training requirements, the remaining cleared fleet represented the equivalent of approximately four to five combat battalions, providing the Army with a reserve or serviceable equipment to address potential fleetwide mechanical issues.
CCAD’s rapid deployment and agile field footprint demonstrated the critical importance of mobile technical capacity. By strengthening reach-back support and standardizing multisite deployment protocols, the depot proved its ability to support simultaneous operations across distributed locations without sacrificing tempo or quality.
“Our wholehearted support to the AH-64E main transmission efforts has given our artisans the opportunity to demonstrate their skill, expertise and unwavering dedication,” said Dalexis Cavaness-Flowers, director of propulsion production. “Driven by excellence, the depot's integrated teams delivered customer satisfaction that keeps the Army flying.”
Convergence and endurance set the conditions for enterprise readiness. As part of the Army’s organic industrial base, the depot remanufactures and resets equipment, generating readiness and operational capability.
“CCAD remains fully committed to enhancing warfighter lethality and ensuring our troops have the equipment they need to dominate on the battlefield, both in the homeland and abroad,” said Rod Benson, deputy and chief operations officer.
“The Army’s Organic Industrial Base is not confined to the walls of our depots,” said COL Kevin Consedine, Corpus Christi Army Depot commander. “Our ability to rapidly deploy skilled artisans and specialized maintenance capabilities to the point of need demonstrates how we bring the depot to the warfighter. This mission is a powerful example of how CCAD directly supports operational units, restores combat readiness, and ensures our Army remains ready to fight and win.”
title: Corpus Christi Army Depot deploys mobile teams to inspect AH-64E transmissions

WASHINGTON – Rayvon Applewhite, 33, previously convicted felon residing in the District, was sentenced today in U.S. District Court to 26 months in federal prison in connection with his possession of a stolen, loaded 9 mm Taurus pistol while on supervised release for three prior offenses, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

Applewhite pleaded guilty June 4 before Judge Amir H. Ali to unlawful possession of a firearm by a felon. In addition to the 26‑month prison term, Judge Ali ordered Applewhite to serve three years of supervised release. Federal prosecutors had requested a prison sentence of 70 months.

According to court documents, Metropolitan Police Officers from the 5th District Crime Suppression Team were on patrol July 14, 2025, when they spotted Applewhite in a residential neighborhood near Rhode Island Avenue NE. The area had experienced a recent surge of violent crime.

As officers observed him walking with another individual, Applewhite appeared to notice police presence and adjusted the front of his waistband, raising suspicion that he may have been concealing a weapon.

Officers approached Applewhite and attempted to speak with him. Applewhite tried to distance himself, and when officers moved to detain him, he resisted, prompting a protective pat down. Officers recovered a stolen 9 mm Taurus pistol from the front of his waistband. The firearm was fully loaded with one round in the chamber and 12 additional rounds in the magazine. It had been reported stolen out of East Point, Georgia.

Applewhite was prohibited from possessing any firearm due to multiple prior felony convictions, including conspiracy to distribute a controlled substance, unlawful possession of a loaded handgun, and second‑degree cruelty to children. At the time of this offense, he remained under supervision in three separate matters and had an extensive criminal record spanning violent crimes, drug offenses, and repeated illegal firearm possession. This case marked his fourth firearm‑related offense.

This case was investigated by the Metropolitan Police Department and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives - Washington Field Office.

It was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Michael Lee of the Federal Major Crimes Section under the President’s Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful Again initiative, which targets violent crime by prioritizing federal prosecution of armed repeat offenders and removing illegal firearms from District neighborhoods.

Officers recovered the pistol tucked in Applewhite’s pants, directly behind his belt buckle.

BÖBLINGEN, Germany — Loud shouts and metallic banging echoed from inside a darkened bunker at Stuttgart Army Airfield on Oct. 8 as senior garrison leaders crawled through smoke and confined tunnels in full firefighting gear during Fire Prevention Week.
All geared up and ready for a challenge, U.S. Army Stuttgart Garrison Commander Col. Edward J. Sanford and Command Sgt. Maj. Christopher Melendez entered the Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA) confidence maze to experience firsthand the physical and mental challenges that first responders face daily.
While firefighters typically complete the confidence course at least twice a year, this particular training was organized by USAG Stuttgart’s Directorate of Emergency Services to “create a hands-on experience of Fire Prevention Week and boost first responder morale through leadership example,” DES Director Lt. Col. Daniel Jimenez said.
To simulate a real-life training experience, trainers pump artificial smoke and raise the temperature in the bunker while trainees navigate the dark maze relying on limited flashlight beams.
“SCBA confidence maze training is a cornerstone of a firefighter’s professional qualification,” USAG Stuttgart Fire Chief Michael Ambacher said.
The training helps firefighters master life-safety survival skills and maintain operational readiness while building confidence in their ability to operate in tight spaces without panicking.
“Firefighters complete this training so that their first experience with zero-visibility and entrapment happens in a monitored training environment and not while trapped inside a collapsing, active structure fire,” Ambacher said.
Ambacher said instructors closely monitor and look for signs of stress, panic, or hesitation, such as rapid breathing, elevated speech, or freezing. They assess whether firefighters can remove and don their SCBA in zero visibility to pass through tight spaces, whether they correctly apply right- or left-hand search sweeps, and how effectively they work together as a team.
For USAG Stuttgart garrison leadership, stepping into the dark box demonstrates solidarity with the garrison’s first responders.
“Going through this course gives you an immediate appreciation for the grit and trust our firefighters must have every time the alarm sounds,” Sanford said. “It is one thing to review training reports, but experiencing the heat and sensory overload in person reinforces just how important their preparation is.”
title: USAG Stuttgart leadership tackles firefighter confidence maze

The usual quiet morning around the Strom Thurmond Building was broken by a cacophony of cars Oct. 14.
Drivers were responding to the waves of a group from the Family Advocacy Program and the Criminal Investigation Division with beeps of their car horns.
This was all part of the annual Honk and Wave event of Fort Jackson’s Domestic Violence Awareness Month.
“We started doing this probably about three years ago,” said Shenitha Shiver, victim advocate with Fort Jackson’s Army Community Service. “We’ve been trying to bring awareness to domestic violence and getting the community to understand it.”
“The honking wave is like them saying they support us out here” and are against domestic violence, Shiver added.
Shiver, who has more than 20 years’ experience as a victims advocate, was an advocate both as a civilian and a service member.
“When I first started doing this, South Carolina was ranked like in the top team for domestic violence,” she said. “We are really trying to bring awareness and educate people about healthy relationships, signs of what a healthy relationship is, and try to understand red flags so they can try to avoid domestic violence as much as possible.”
This year’s DVAM campaign is aimed at both helping victims and preventing possible domestic violence by highlighting the red flags. It aims at helping potential offenders notice the warning signs and get help before anything escalates.
“Sometimes there’s a lot of red flags; sometimes there are not,” she said. “But if we can’t get out there and educate both the offender and the victim about domestic violence … Hopefully, we can reduce or stop this from happening in our society.”
DVAM, aimed at maintaining a safe, healthy, and nurturing home environment is essential to the strength and readiness of our force throughout October, is a continuing effort.
“It’s not about one month, it’s not about one day or one week … it’s an ongoing effort,” said Col. David Gaugush, garrison commander describing the post’s domestic violence awareness program before he signed a Domestic Violence Awareness Month proclamation, Sept. 30.
title: Jackson honks, waves against domestic violence

CHARLOTTE, N.C. – Today, two drug traffickers were sentenced to prison for distributing methamphetamine and fentanyl in Gastonia, North Carolina, announced Russ Ferguson, U.S. Attorney for the Western District of North Carolina. Jesus Rubio, 33, and John Joseph Carl Hay, III, 51, both of Gastonia, were sentenced to 200 months and 120 months in prison respectively, and were ordered to a period of supervised release. Rubio was also ordered to serve an additional 14 months for violating court ordered supervision.

“Peddling drugs is bad enough; when you peddle illegal guns along with it, the danger to our community increases exponentially,” said U.S. Attorney Russ Ferguson. “That Mr. Rubio engaged in this conduct not long after being released from federal prison shows that a sentence upwards of 16 years is necessary here to ensure the safety of our community.”

“Every time dangerous drugs like methamphetamine and fentanyl reach our streets, the safety and well-being of our communities are put at risk,” said Michael J. Connolly, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the DEA Atlanta Field Division. “These sentences reflect the importance of holding drug traffickers accountable and demonstrate what can be accomplished through strong partnerships among law enforcement agencies. DEA will continue working to protect our communities and advance our commitment to a Fentanyl Free America.”

According to court documents, the DEA and the Gastonia Police Department were investigating Rubio and Hay for suspected drug trafficking in Gaston County. During the investigation, a confidential source working with law enforcement conducted multiple controlled drug buys, purchasing methamphetamine and fentanyl from the defendants. At least two times, the confidential source also purchased firearms from Rubio, including a 9mm caliber handgun and a 12-gauge sawed-off shotgun. Rubio was previously convicted of a federal firearms offense.

Both Rubio and Hay pleaded guilty to conspiracy and possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine. Rubio also pleaded guilty to possession of a firearm in furtherance of drug trafficking. They are both in federal custody and will be transferred to the custody of the Federal Bureau of Prisons.

In sentencing the defendants, U.S. District Judge Kenneth D. Bell said, that it was “apparent that Mr. Rubio did not learn from his previous conviction” and was “concerned” by the fact that he engaged in criminal conduct so quickly after being released from federal prison.

The DEA and the Gastonia Police Department investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Dana Washington and Sara Kinlaw of the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Charlotte prosecuted the case.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.
title: Gastonia Drug Traffickers Sentenced to Prison

BOSTON – A Boston man pleaded guilty yesterday in federal court in Boston to firearm charges.

Jairo Valdivieso, 24, pleaded guilty to one count of firearms trafficking and one count of engaging in the business of dealing in firearms without a license. U.S. District Court Judge Nathaniel M. Gorton scheduled sentencing for Jan. 12, 2026.

On three occasions between December 2025 and March 2026, Valdivieso sold firearms to an undercover federal agent. Specifically, on Dec. 30, 2025, Valdivieso, through two associates, sold a firearm to an undercover agent in Boston. On Feb. 6, 2026, Valdivieso, again through two associates, sold a firearm to an undercover agent in Roxbury and on March 29, 2026 Valdivieso sold another firearm to an undercover agent in Boston.

The charge of firearms trafficking provides for a sentence of up to 15 years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. The charge of engaging in the business of dealing in firearms without a license provides for a sentence of up to five years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Thomas Greco, Special Agent in Charge of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by Boston Police Department and Massachusetts State Police. Assistant U.S. Attorney Allegra K. Flamm of the Major Crimes Unit is prosecuting the case.
title: Boston Man Pleads Guilty to Trafficking Firearms

Community Development Revolving Loan Fund Grants
Alexandria, VA (October 15, 2026) ― Low-income-designated credit unions affected by natural disasters, including hurricanes, flooding, and other severe weather events, can apply for grants through the Community Development Revolving Loan Fund (CDRLF) Newly Chartered and Urgent Need program.
Eligible credit unions can receive up to $15,000 to support urgent recovery needs and help restore financial services for members. Grant funds may be used for the following activities:
- Repairing damage to the credit union caused by a natural disaster
- Replacing equipment needed to immediately restore services to members following an unexpected event, such as a storm-related power outage
- Providing financial services to members affected by the disaster, such as a special loan program to help cover members’ costs of recovering from the event
Credit unions interested in applying should review the Newly Chartered and Urgent Need Grant Guidelines for eligibility requirements, allowable uses of funds, and application instructions. While there is no deadline for the application, affected credit unions should apply as soon after the emergency event as possible to ensure timely disbursement of grant funds.
Credit unions with questions about the urgent need grants process can contact CURE by email at CUREAPPS@ncua.gov or by telephone at 703.518.6610.
title: Grant Funds Available to Low-Income Credit Unions Affected by Hurricanes

Washington, D.C. — Today, Rep. Robert Garcia, Ranking Member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, and Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), together with Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) and Ron Wyden (D-OR), with all Oversight Democratic Members and Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY), introduced the Epstein Wall Street Records Act. This bill seeks accountability for the financial institutions and bank executives that enabled disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein’s sex trafficking operation.
“Jeffrey Epstein used his immense wealth to abuse women and girls for decades. Meanwhile, banks and financial institutions enriched him and themselves by servicing his accounts and helping him move money around. We need to know what financial institutions and their executives knew about Epstein, whether they complied with relevant law, and what regulatory agencies learned,” said Ranking Member Robert Garcia.
“I have spent the last year calling on Donald Trump’s financial regulators to launch investigations into the big banks and executives who may have enabled Jeffrey Epstein’s horrific crimes,” said Senator Elizabeth Warren. “Since they have failed to act, Congress must. The bipartisan Epstein Wall Street Records Act will ensure overdue accountability for the wealthy and well-connected on Wall Street who put profits over people.”
“The Epstein Wall Street Records Act is about transparency and releasing financial records that are critical to holding the Epstein Class accountable and fighting to get justice for the survivors. I’m proud to cosponsor this bipartisan bill,” said Congressman Ro Khanna.
“The Epstein Wall Street Records Act requires the Federal Reserve, the FDIC, the Comptroller of the Currency, and the SEC to release their files on Jeffrey Epstein’s money,” said Congressman Thomas Massie. “The Epstein Files Transparency Act forced the Attorney General to release DOJ, FBI, and U.S. Attorney’s Offices’ files. This bill does the same for bank regulators. Justice for the survivors means following the money.”
“Jeffrey Epstein’s sex trafficking operation left a money trail, and Wall Street has serious questions to answer. Our legislation will force federal regulators to release their records, investigate the banks and executives who may have enabled his crimes, and hold lawbreakers accountable,” said Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi. “Epstein’s survivors deserve the full truth, no matter how powerful or well-connected those responsible may be.”
“For far too long, financial institutions have leveraged their power, influence, and privilege to evade accountability. Their role in enabling Jeffrey Epstein’s decades of sexual exploitation and abuse demands serious scrutiny. That is why World Without Exploitation is proud to support the Epstein Wall Street Records Act of 2026,” said Becca Zipkin, Vice President of Policy and Programs, World Without Exploitation. “We must follow the money to uncover the truth and ensure that the financial institutions that enabled this abuse are held accountable. Survivors deserve transparency, accountability, and the justice they have long been denied.”
The Epstein Wall Street Record Act would require federal financial regulators to disclose supervisory records related to Epstein and his associates to Members of Congress and the American people, force the financial regulators to investigate Epstein-connected banks and executives for possible banking, securities, or illicit financing violations, and mandate industry bars and civil penalties for executives who assisted Epstein’s financial operations, as well as potential referrals of criminal violations to the Department of Justice if necessary.
###
title: Ranking Member Robert Garcia and Senator Elizabeth Warren Lead Bipartisan Bill to Hold Epstein’s Bankers Accountable

text:
DUBLIN, Calif. — Military leaders, project engineers, and regional partners gathered at Parks Reserve Forces Training Area (Camp Parks) on Sept. 29, 2026, for a groundbreaking for a $36.5 million state-of-the-art barracks complex.
The project—designated as the Fiscal Year 2025 Permanent Party Advanced Skills Training (AST) Barracks Facility—represents the significant Army Reserve investment dedicated to barracks modernizing, enhancing Soldier quality of life, and strengthening the profession.
The official party for the ceremony included Maj. Gen. Windsor S. Buzza, Commanding General of the 63rd Readiness Division; Col. Jason R. McKenzie, Garrison Commander of U.S. Army Garrison Fort Hunter Liggett; and Camp Parks Commander Lt. Col. Tony S. Ibrahim and Command Sgt. Maj. David Oduro-Boafo; and Ryan Larson, Chief of the Construction Division for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Sacramento District.
Spanning approximately 48,000 square feet across two stories, the new facility will provide modern living accommodation for up to 300 Soldiers visiting Camp Parks for training, with a 172 bed capacity, expandable to 180. Designed to replace aging legacy facilities, the complex features 44 two-bedroom suites and 28 three-bedroom suites, ensuring occupants have individualized sleeping quarters and private bathrooms. The facility also incorporates shared dayrooms and lounges, high-efficiency HVAC and environmental controls, and robust digital connectivity infrastructure.
The ceremony opened with an invocation delivered by Installation Chaplain Maj. Evelio Rodriguez, followed by the national anthem and official addresses from installation leadership and engineering partners.
"Today is not merely about clearing dirt, pouring concrete, or raising steel—it is about delivering on a promise," said Lt. Col. Tony S. Ibrahim, underscoring the vital compact between the Army and its service members and linking the project to nationwide standards. "Every single day, we ask our Soldiers to undergo rigorous training and maintain continuous readiness to deploy into complex environments. In return, the Army owes them modern, dignified, and safe living conditions. Under our enterprise housing initiatives, clean, safe, and functional housing is recognized not as an afterthought, but as a direct driver of Soldier readiness, morale, and retention. This facility has been engineered from the ground up to respect Soldiers' privacy, foster unit cohesion, and provide the restorative environment they have earned."
Engineering Partnerships in Action
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Sacramento District is managing the barracks construction on behalf of the Army Reserve, following planning and design work led by the USACE Louisville District.
Highlighting the critical link between engineering execution and operational readiness, Ryan Larson, Chief of the Construction Division for the USACE Sacramento District, underscored the collaborative effort required to bring the project to fruition.
“This project is ultimately about providing Soldiers with the facilities they need to train and accomplish their missions,” Larson said. “Breaking ground is an important milestone because it represents the transition from years of planning and design to putting that work into the ground. Our team looks forward to delivering a quality facility that supports the Army’s training mission here at Camp Parks.”
A Commander's Perspective: Decades of Evolution and Readiness
In his keynote address, Maj. Gen. Windsor S. Buzza drew upon his deep personal history with Camp Parks, sharing reflections from his early career as a young officer arriving at the installation three decades ago.
"Over the last 30 years, Camp Parks has changed considerably, but the mission of the people and the Army has been constant, and that’s to build readiness," said Buzza. "So we invest money over time to meet what the requirements are as they change for building readiness. And this is just the latest example of us investing in our future for tomorrow and in our Soldiers."
Buzza pointed out how the new structure builds upon ongoing campus modernization, bringing a much-needed evolution from open-bay legacy quarters to modern individualized rooms.
"What we're going to build here is going to be much like [the neighboring building] on the outside, but a little bit different on the inside, because the rooms will be a little more individualized, which is good from a Soldier perspective," Buzza said, drawing laughs from attendees as he recalled the realities of sleeping in open-room barracks and the familiar chorus of snoring echoing across the hall.
Looking to the future, Buzza noted that the aging World War II-era wooden barracks situated nearby are slated to eventually make way for continued modernization across the footprint. He emphasized that delivering complex construction projects requires dedicated inter-agency collaboration.
"I want to reiterate how much of a team effort it is to bring something like this together," Buzza emphasized. "Project management is a thing—it doesn’t just happen on its own. So an appreciation for everybody who has pitched in and gripped hands alongside of us to get to where we are, and in anticipation of this project going smooth sailing forward so it gets completed on time—maybe ahead of schedule."
Buzza then rallied the crowd with the 63rd Readiness Division's historic motto, "Blood and Fire," as he invited the party to take up their shovels.
A Broader Modernization Campaign
The Camp Parks project represents one tangible milestone within a multi-billion-dollar campaign across the Department of War and U.S. Army to overhaul unaccompanied personnel housing. Under dedicated initiatives and aggressive budgetary priorities—including funding dedicated strictly to barracks sustainment, restoration, and modern construction—the service is driving toward strict performance targets: achieving 100 percent compliance with published habitability standards, 98 percent compliance with unaccompanied housing privacy standards, and ensuring at least 93 percent of government-owned housing achieves a Building Condition Index (BCI) score of 80 percent or greater.
By partnering with private industry to expedite timelines, projects like the Camp Parks AST barracks demonstrate how modern construction practices are bypassing traditional maintenance bottlenecks to deliver immediate quality-of-life improvements.
Following the formal addresses, members of the official party donned hard hats and gripped ceremonial chrome shovels at the dirt berm. Joined by representatives from USACE, the leadership team turned the first shovels of soil to signify the formal start of construction.
The ceremony concluded with all attendees joining in the traditional singing of "The Army Song."
Site preparations and initial grading are underway, with construction scheduled for completion in May 2028.
*Editor's Note / Attribution Footnote: Portions of this article—including project specifications, construction timelines, and commentary from Ryan Larson, Chief of the Construction Division for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Sacramento District—were adapted and folded into this report from initial reporting by Lt. Col. Kara Greene, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Sacramento District Public Affairs.
title: USACE and Army Break Ground on $36.6M Camp Parks Barracks
