WASHINGTON — By day, Spc. Troy Jones makes sure the aircraft on his Boeing program are built to the required process. On drill weekends, he keeps Soldiers' personnel records current so they're ready to deploy.
"The mission is different, but the standard is the same: be ready," said Jones, a human resources specialist with the 478th Civil Affairs Battalion (Airborne) and a program quality engineer at Boeing in the Puget Sound region.
On Monday, Lt. Gen. Robert Harter, chief of Army Reserve and commanding general of U.S. Army Reserve Command, and Jim Cutting, director of Army Systems for Boeing Government Operations, signed a proclamation designed to open doors for more Soldiers like Jones.
The signing followed the opening ceremony of the Association of the U.S. Army's Annual Meeting and Exposition, which highlighted the Army's emphasis on private-sector partnerships.
More than 87% of Army Reserve Soldiers integrate military service with civilian careers, according to the Private Public Partnership Office. Industry strengthens Citizen-Soldiers, and the Army Reserve develops talent the Joint Force depends on.
Career Ready is Combat Ready.
"Being a leader in the Army Reserve today is a full-time job for part-time pay," Harter said. "We get 39 days a year to train. That's what we're funded for."
The rest of their year depends on civilian employers, both to make ends meet and to build the skills the Army and Joint Force count on.
"When Soldiers have meaningful civilian careers, they bring those skills and stability back to the force," said Lt. Col. Xeriqua Garfinkel, director of the Private Public Partnership Office (P3O). "Career readiness strengthens military readiness."
Cutting, who served as chief of unmanned aircraft systems in the Army's Aviation Directorate before joining Boeing, has seen Soldiers' grit up close. "Somehow they always get it done," he said. "That kind of tenacity is a valuable asset in any environment."
Brett Cox, Boeing employee and Army Reserve Ambassador for Missouri and has championed the partnership for more than a decade. "These are Army Reserve Soldiers building the airframes that go into the warfighter's hands," he said. "When we leverage that experience in both their military and civilian careers, they really are Twice the Citizen."
Capt. Kailyn Heck, a 654th Regional Support Group public affairs officer and Boeing social media strategist, returned from two weeks of annual training this summer with "nothing to worry about." "Army Reserve Soldiers don't choose between two worlds. We strengthen both," she said.
With the signing, Boeing joins nearly 300 P3O partner organizations. Reserve members may be eligible for more than 1,400 open positions across its five business units, including Commercial Airplanes and Defense, Space & Security.
The proclamation connects Soldiers, their dependents and veterans with hiring pathways, internships, SkillBridge opportunities, apprenticeships and credentialing. The nonbinding agreement has no expiration date and no cost to either party.
Harter said Boeing already employs more than 400 Army Reserve Soldiers. "We're kind of codifying what's already happening," he said.
Soldiers and family members can connect with the Private Public Partnership Office at usar.army.mil/P3. For more information about the U.S. Army Reserve and opportunities to serve, visit GoArmy.com or contact an Army recruiter to learn how you can serve part time while continuing your civilian career or education.
title: Career Ready, Combat Ready: Army Reserve, Boeing sign partnership at AUSA

WILMINGTON, Del. – A New Castle man was charged by criminal complaint with illegally possessing three firearms. The charge follows an investigation into social-media posts in which he allegedly called for violence against federal officials.

Gregory Wierzbicki, 66, is charged with possession of a firearm by a prohibited person, in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(1). He made his initial appearance today, October 14, 2026, before U.S. Magistrate Judge Christopher J. Burke. He was ordered temporarily detained pending a detention hearing set for Monday, October 19, 2026.

According to court documents, Wierzbicki used Bluesky and Substack accounts from at least April 2025 through September 2026 to encourage violence against federal officials, including Justices of the Supreme Court of the United States and officers of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Wierzbicki also urged others to form an armed militia and described firearms and ammunition he possessed.

On October 14, 2026, FBI Baltimore’s Joint Terrorism Task Force executed a search warrant with support from the Supreme Court of the United States Police at Wierzbicki’s home in New Castle, Delaware. Inside the home, law enforcement found three firearms: a 12-gauge shotgun and two .22-caliber long rifles.

If convicted, Wierzbicki faces a maximum penalty of 15 years of incarceration. Actual sentences for federal crimes are typically less than the maximum penalties. A federal district court judge would determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

“The United States has alleged that Gregory Wierzbicki unlawfully possessed multiple firearms while calling for violence against public officials, including judges and law-enforcement officers,” stated U.S. Attorney Benjamin L. Wallace. “My office and our law-enforcement partners will act without hesitation to protect our nation’s public servants. We look forward to making our case against Wierzbicki in court.”

“The FBI’s Joint Terrorism Task Force acted quickly to investigate Gregory Wierzbicki’s alleged threats of violence. Today’s arrest shows that if your idea of making a point is to threaten others, you shouldn’t be surprised when the FBI shows up at your door,” said FBI Baltimore Special Agent in Charge Jimmy Paul.

The FBI Baltimore Field Office’s Joint Terrorism Task Force, Supreme Court of the United States Police – Protective Intelligence Unit and Homeland Security Investigations are investigating the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Kevin P. Pierce is prosecuting the case.

This case is part of the nationwide National Security Presidential Memorandum 7 initiative, which is a White House directed, interagency effort to integrate federal, state, and local partners in protecting First Amendment rights while targeting individuals and organizations engaged in political violence and is led by the investigative and prosecutorial Joint Task Force Vanguard.

A copy of this press release is located on the website of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Delaware. Related court documents and information are located on the website of the District Court for the District of Delaware or on PACER by searching for Case No. 26-539M.

A criminal complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: New Castle Man Charged with Illegally Possessing Firearms as a Felon

text:
MIAMI – A Miami man pleaded guilty yesterday for his role in a conspiracy to distribute over 87,000 oxycodone 30mg pills.

According to court documents and statements made in court, Jose Llerena, 49, of Miami, conspired with others, including Olushola Yusuf — a pharmacist and pharmacy owner convicted at trial earlier this year for illegally dispensing over 300,000 oxycodone 30mg pills — to illegally distribute oxycodone to individuals who had no medical need for the drug. Llerena was a “patient recruiter” who paid individuals to pose as patients and obtain illegal and unnecessary oxycodone prescriptions from South Florida clinics and doctors. Llerena then took his recruits and their illegal prescriptions to Yusuf’s pharmacies in order to get the pills. Yusuf kept a list of Llerena’s recruits at her pharmacy. Llerena paid Yusuf cash for the drug at above market value.

“More than 87,000 oxycodone pills were diverted through this conspiracy, feeding addiction and putting dangerous drugs onto our streets,” said U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones. “Jose Llerena recruited fake patients, paid them for their pills, and resold those pills for profit. Those who exploit our health care system to traffic opioids will be identified, prosecuted, and held accountable.”

Llerena Recruits List Recovered at Yusuf Pharmacy

Llerena then paid his recruits, usually via Zelle, for the oxycodone pills before reselling the pills on the street. Llerena was personally responsible for distributing 3,735 oxycodone pills.

Llerena pled guilty to conspiracy to distribute a controlled substance. A sentencing date has not been set. Llerena faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division; U.S. Attorney Reding Quiñones; Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG) Acting Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Miranda Bennett; DEA Special Agent in Charge Miles Aley, Miami Field Division; and FBI Special Agent in Charge Brett Skiles made the announcement.

HHS-OIG, DEA, and FBI investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Jacqueline DerOvanesian for the Southern District of Florida and Trial Attorney Angela Benoit of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section are prosecuting the case.

The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit .

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division. The core mission of the Fraud Division is to zealously investigate and prosecute those who steal or fraudulently misuse taxpayer dollars. Department of Justice efforts to combat fraud support President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

On October 9, 2026, the United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Louisiana charged Joseph Leyva , 19, of Castroville, Texas, by criminal complaint with Attempted Production of Child Sexual Abuse Material. If convicted, Leyva faces a mandatory minimum of 15 years and a maximum of up to 30 years in federal prison.

According to court documents, Leyva allegedly communicated with a nine-year-old child via social media and attempted to persuade the child to create sexually explicit visual material. The minor victim resides within the Western District of Louisiana, and the investigation began after the child’s parent reported suspicious activity to local authorities. Law enforcement then investigated the communications and identified Leyva as the person allegedly communicating with the minor.

U.S. Attorney Zachary A. Keller for the Western District of Louisiana made the announcement.

The Federal Bureau of Investigations and the Louisiana State Police investigated the case. This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Craig Bordelon, with assistance from Legal Assistant Tanya Broussard.

An indictment or criminal complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

This case was prosecuted as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by the U.S. Attorneys' Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. Learn more at https://www.justice.gov/psc/about-project-safe-childhood.

You may find a copy of this press release (and any updates) on the website of the United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Louisiana at www.justice.gov/usao-wdla.

Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Western District of Louisiana at www.lawd.uscourts.gov or https://www.lawd.uscourts.gov/cmecf-pacer. The case number for this matter is 6:26-mj-00247.

Trump Administration Announces $78 Million for Rural Healthcare Workforce, Chronic Disease Prevention, and Facility Upgrades Across Texas
These investments will support the rural health workforce, modernize aging equipment, and advance chronic disease prevention to keep quality care within reach for rural Texans.
Today, the Trump Administration announced $78 million in Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) funding to 216 rural healthcare providers through the Rural Texas Strong initiative to strengthen healthcare across rural Texas communities. This investment will support chronic disease prevention and improved health outcomes, rural healthcare workforce recruitment and retention, and medical equipment and facility improvements to expand access to state-of-the-art care across Texas.
This transformational funding will deliver $78 million directly to 216 rural healthcare providers, helping rural communities prevent and manage chronic diseases such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease, chronic respiratory disease, and obesity. Other initiatives are focused on keeping the best aspects of a small-town medical practice by recruiting and retaining doctors, emergency medical personnel, and other healthcare workers. These investments will help rural Texas communities upgrade aging medical equipment and facilities, bringing modern, reliable care closer to home for rural Texans.
The Rural Health Transformation Program is expanding access to quality healthcare, regardless of a patient’s zip code, and equipping first responders with the lifesaving resources they need when every second counts. This funding will make critical investments to strengthen rural healthcare, expand access to lifesaving services, and bring modern technology to communities across Texas.
“President Trump understands that every American deserves high-quality healthcare, no matter where they live,” said Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “We are putting resources directly into rural communities to strengthen the health workforce, modernize infrastructure, expand access, and bring care closer to home. We are giving states the flexibility to build solutions around the people they serve, while demanding accountability for results. That is how we strengthen rural health, improve the lives of patients and families, and Make America Healthy Again.”
“Every state knows best what its rural communities need, and thanks to President Trump’s Rural Health Transformation Program, they now have the resources to meet those needs,” said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “As states put these resources to work, we’re focused on turning these investments into meaningful, sustainable improvements for the health systems that serve rural Texans.”
Today’s investment was made possible through the Working Families Tax Cuts Act — passed by Republicans in Congress and unanimously opposed by Democrats — delivering a historic $50 billion investment to help states transform the way healthcare is delivered in America.
“This $78 million investment is a major win for rural Texas patients,” said Gov. Greg Abbott. “Providers will recruit doctors and emergency personnel, upgrade equipment and facilities, and advance prevention of chronic disease so care stays close to home. I thank President Trump, Secretary Kennedy, and Administrator Oz for their efforts to improve rural health care for Texans.”
“Investing in rural health care is just one of the key components of the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, which will improve the lives of countless Texans,” said Sen. John Cornyn. “I was proud to support this legislation, now law, to establish the Rural Health Transformation Program, and I am glad to see this additional $78 million in funding to help Texans with chronic conditions access care across the Lone Star State.”
“Rural Texans deserve quality healthcare close to home. I’m grateful to President Trump and his Administration for standing with our communities,” said Rep. Keith Self. “This $78 million investment in 216 rural healthcare providers throughout Texas will strengthen local hospitals and clinics and expand access to care. I was proud to work alongside my colleagues in the Texas delegation to secure this funding.”
“This $78 million investment helps rural Texans get better care closer to home by strengthening local providers, improving equipment, and growing the healthcare workforce. Better care means better outcomes and higher quality of life across rural Texas,” said Rep. Lance Gooden.
“The farmers, ranchers, and small businesses in rural Texas do work this country depends on every day. Those families need reliable healthcare close to home to keep themselves and their communities strong. And when getting care means hours on the road or waiting until a condition becomes an emergency, the whole community feels the impact,” said Rep. Jake Ellzey. “This funding will help rural hospitals better serve their patients and expand prevention and wellness programs that catch health problems earlier. Keeping care close to home helps families stay healthy, keeps people working, and gives our rural communities a stronger foundation for the future.”
“I’m grateful that Texas is receiving another record investment in rural healthcare. Too many rural Texans still face long drives and limited options when they need care. This $78 million investment for 216 providers through the Rural Texas Strong initiative will help them recruit and retain healthcare workers, prevent chronic disease, and upgrade critical facilities and equipment, putting care closer to home for rural Texans. Healthy communities are strong communities, and I’m grateful to CMS and our state partners for making this happen,” said Rep. August Pfluger.
“Every Texan deserves access to high-quality health care. I’m proud to have joined my Republican Texas colleagues in passing the Rural Health Transformation Program, bringing millions of dollars into our rural communities,” said Rep. Craig Goldman. “This $78 million will deliver stronger preventive care, support our rural health care workforce, and modernize medical facilities to ensure Texans receive the reliable care they need.”
“Rural Texans deserve access to quality healthcare in their communities. This $78 million investment will help strengthen rural healthcare providers, recruit and retain skilled medical professionals, and improve access to the equipment and services patients need. By supporting chronic disease prevention, workforce development, and improvements to rural healthcare facilities, we can help ensure families in TX-13 and across Texas have access to the care they deserve,” said Rep. Ronny Jackson.
“Healthcare access is a challenge for rural Texas, making this $78M investment a major win for our state. By fighting chronic illness, training future doctors, and supporting local providers, these funds ensure every Texan can access the care they need,” said Rep. Monica De La Cruz.
“Rural communities across Texas deserve access to quality, affordable healthcare without having to travel long distances to receive it. This $78 million investment through the Rural Health Transformation Program will help 216 rural healthcare providers strengthen their operations, recruit and retain qualified medical professionals, and expand access to essential services. From improving medical facilities and equipment to addressing chronic diseases, this funding will make a meaningful difference for hardworking Texas families. I applaud CMS for recognizing the unique challenges facing rural healthcare providers and making an investment that will help ensure our rural communities have the resources they need to thrive,” said Rep. Pete Sessions.
“Every Texan deserves access to quality healthcare, no matter their zip code. This $78 million investment is a major step toward strengthening rural healthcare and making sure families have the resources they need to live healthier lives. I’m proud to support President Trump’s efforts to Make America Healthy Again by focusing on prevention, managing chronic diseases, and improving access to care. For rural Texans, this funding means more resources closer to home and better opportunities to address health concerns before they become serious problems,” said Rep. John Carter.
“President Trump recognizes that strong communities depend on access to quality, affordable health care, regardless of where families call home,” said Rep. Wesley Hunt. “We secured a landmark investment in rural health care that will help ensure smaller communities are not left behind. Texas is now taking meaningful steps to turn that investment into results by supporting rural hospitals, improving access to essential medical services, and prioritizing preventive care. I was proud to stand alongside President Trump in advancing this important initiative, and I appreciate his continued leadership in delivering real solutions for hardworking families across rural Texas.”
Today’s announcement is one part of the larger overall funding amount awarded to Texas for fiscal year 2026.
Key initiatives the overall RHTP funding will focus on include:
- Building the rural healthcare workforce: Supporting recruitment, training, and retention strategies to strengthen the pipeline of healthcare professionals serving rural communities.
- Strengthening rural facilities and access: Supporting partnerships, operational improvements, and care-delivery changes that help rural providers maintain essential services and improve access.
- Advancing innovative care and payment models: Supporting new approaches to delivery and financing designed to improve quality, strengthen primary care, and support sustainable rural healthcare.
- Expanding community-based and preventive care: Investing in school-based care, mobile services, and other community strategies that improve prevention, address chronic disease, and expand access to care.
- Modernizing rural healthcare technology: Expanding remote care and data-driven tools to improve coordination and extend healthcare services to rural communities.
The Trump Administration is delivering on its commitment to strengthen rural America by investing in solutions that modernize technology to promote health and well-being for rural communities. Led by CMS, the RHTP is moving beyond the failed one-size-fits-all approach and giving rural communities the tools to build stronger, more innovative, and more sustainable health systems that deliver better care and better outcomes for the Americans they serve.
For more information about the RHTP, visit: https://www.medicaid.gov/resources-for-states/rural-health.

The United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Alabama today announced sentencings as part of a nationwide enforcement actions led by the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division, Internal Revenue Service, and Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI) targeting tax fraud and related offenses. The United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Alabama was key participant in this surge effort. Several defendants were sentenced for defrauding the United States of millions of dollars intended for businesses impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic.
Between early September and today, federal prosecutors across the country facilitated fraud enforcement actions spanning over 76 criminal defendants, whose alleged crimes resulted in over $490,000,000 in intended loss to American taxpayers.
Earlier this month, Echandza Maxie (Echandza), 43, and her husband, Glennie McGee (McGee), 42, both of Mobile, were sentenced to 20 years in federal prison for their roles in a scheme to defraud the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) by illegally obtaining more than $1.5 million in COVID-19-related tax credits intended to provide relief to legitimate businesses and individuals during the pandemic. Three additional defendants were convicted and sentenced for their roles in a related scheme to defraud the Small Business Administration (SBA) through fraudulent applications for COVID-19 relief loans. A sixth defendant was separately sentenced for his role in the tax fraud scheme. In total, the defendants were ordered to pay over $2.4 Million in restitution to the IRS and SBA for their crimes.
In response to the COVID-19 pandemic and its economic impact, Congress authorized refundable tax credits for paid sick and family leave to reimburse eligible employers and self-employed individuals for qualifying leave related to COVID-19. Congress also established the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) and Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) program to provide emergency financial assistance to legitimate businesses suffering economic losses during the pandemic.
During a cocaine-trafficking investigation involving a court-authorized wiretap of a telephone belonging to John David Clarke of Mobile, Alabama, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), working with IRS-CI, uncovered a large-scale tax fraud scheme.
Federal agents determined that Echandza, her husband, McGee, Echandza’s sister, Edeszann Maxie (Edeszann), Tiveria Populus (Populus), Jamael Nettles (Nettles), John David Clarke (Clarke), and others participated in schemes to fraudulently obtain COVID-19-related tax credits and SBA loans.
According to court documents, Echandza owned and operated a Mobile tax-preparation business known as “Self Made Taxes,” which was purportedly co-located with a clothing store, an eyelash business, and other businesses. Edeszann, who also worked as a tax preparer, worked with Echandza, McGee, and others to obtain the personal identifying information of prospective taxpayers and use that information to file fraudulent tax returns in their names.
The defendants enlisted recruiters who were paid finder’s fees to obtain names, dates of birth, and Social Security numbers belonging to prospective taxpayers. Echandza, Edeszann, and McGee generally required only that the prospective taxpayer had not yet filed a tax return and did not owe child support. They did not obtain information necessary to determine whether the taxpayer actually operated a business or otherwise qualified for the COVID-19 tax credits.
Using the personal identifying information they obtained, Echandza and Edeszann fabricated fictitious self-employed businesses, frequently claiming that the taxpayers operated landscaping or hairstyling businesses. The fraudulent tax returns routinely claimed that the taxpayers had taken the maximum amount of COVID-19-related sick and family leave and sought the maximum available credit of approximately $30,000 per return. Echandza and Edeszann also fabricated business revenues for the 2021 tax year.
Many of the fraudulent refunds were directed to bank accounts controlled by the defendants. Although the IRS identified and rejected a significant number of fraudulent returns after placing identity-theft holds on them, the scheme nevertheless generated more than $1.5 million in fraudulent tax refunds.
Some individuals whose information was used in the scheme believed they were legitimately eligible to receive COVID-19 relief and trusted the defendants to prepare accurate tax returns on their behalf. Some individuals unfamiliar with the tax-filing process paid between $10,000 and $15,000 to have their returns prepared, believing the payments were legitimate tax-preparation fees.
FBI and IRS-CI special agents identified dozens of individuals whose personal information had been used to file fraudulent tax returns. Many had no knowledge that a return had been filed in their names. Others were unaware that their returns contained false information, including claims that they operated businesses they did not own or operate.
In some instances, the defendants filed fraudulent returns as “self-prepared,” even though the returns had been prepared and submitted by Echandza or Edeszann. Investigators identified the fraud through contact and banking information on the returns that belonged to the defendants, demonstrating that the named taxpayers had no knowledge of the refunds generated using their personal information. In other cases, individuals learned that fraudulent returns had been filed in their names after receiving notice from the Social Security Administration that their disability benefits could be affected by purported business income reported to the IRS.
Fraudulent SBA Loans
The defendants, except for Nettles, also fraudulently applied for and obtained dozens of PPP and EIDL loans administered by the SBA in response to the COVID-19 pandemic.
The PPP provided eligible businesses with potentially forgivable loans guaranteed by the SBA, while the EIDL program provided low-interest loans to help eligible small businesses maintain operations during the pandemic. The programs were intended to provide financial assistance for legitimate business expenses, including payroll, rent, and utilities.
With assistance from special agents with the SBA Office of Inspector General, investigators determined that Echandza, McGee, Edeszann, Clarke, and Populus each submitted fraudulent SBA loan applications. The applications contained material misrepresentations that the defendants operated legitimate businesses before the pandemic and that those businesses generated substantial revenue.
For businesses that had some evidence of operation before 2020, investigators determined that the defendants fabricated revenue figures and the number of employees to obtain larger loan proceeds. In total, the defendants obtained more than $885,000 in SBA loans to which they were not entitled.
Each defendant pleaded guilty to charges arising from his or her participation in the fraud schemes. United States District Court Judge Terry F. Moorer imposed the sentences.
Sentences
Echandza Maxie was sentenced to 20 years in prison, followed by a mandatory two-year consecutive sentence for aggravated identity theft. She was ordered to pay $1,576,358.88 in restitution to the IRS and $257,413.93 to the SBA. Her 20-year sentence, excluding the mandatory consecutive sentence for aggravated identity theft, was ordered to run concurrently with her life sentence stemming from a multi-million-dollar cocaine and fentanyl trafficking organization related convictions. If released from prison, she will be subject to three years of supervised release. She was also ordered to pay a $300 special assessment and forfeit approximately $85,000 in fraud proceeds seized by the FBI during the investigation.
Glennie McGee was sentenced to 20 years in prison, followed by a mandatory two-year consecutive sentence for aggravated identity theft. McGee was ordered to pay $672,219 in restitution to the IRS and $340,910.16 to the SBA. His 20-year sentence, excluding the mandatory consecutive sentence for aggravated identity theft, was ordered to run concurrently with his life sentence stemming from his multi-million-dollar cocaine and fentanyl trafficking organization. If released from prison, he will be subject to three years of supervised release. He was also ordered to pay a $300 special assessment.
Edeszann Maxie was sentenced to 135 months in prison, followed by a mandatory two-year consecutive sentence for aggravated identity theft. She was ordered to pay $187,301 in restitution to the IRS and $298,667.70 to the SBA. Upon release from prison, she will be subject to three years of supervised release. She was also ordered to pay a $300 special assessment.
John David Clarke was sentenced to 20 years in prison and ordered to pay $28,764.10 in restitution to the IRS and $55,167 to the SBA. His sentence was ordered to run concurrently with his separately imposed 20-year-sentence stemming from his convictions related to a large-scale cocaine trafficking conspiracy. Upon release from prison, Clarke will be subject to three years of supervised release. He was also ordered to pay a $200 special assessment.
Tiveria Populus was sentenced to time served and ordered to pay $28,764.10 in restitution to the IRS and $46,206.29 to the SBA. Populus will be subject to five years of supervised release and was ordered to pay a $200 special assessment.
Jamael Nettles, in a separate case, was sentenced to five days in prison and ordered to pay $29,339 in restitution to the IRS. Nettles will be subject to three years of supervised release and was ordered to pay a $100 special assessment.
“The defendants exploited programs created to provide relief to businesses and individuals during an unprecedented national crisis, stealing millions of dollars through fraudulent tax returns and applications for pandemic relief,” said U.S. Attorney Sean P. Costello. “Fraud of this kind does more than steal money from the government—it undermines the integrity of our tax system and diverts resources away from the people and businesses who were entitled to receive them. I commend IRS Criminal Investigation and our other law enforcement partners for following the financial trail, uncovering this scheme, and holding fraudsters responsible.”
“The defendants carried out a coordinated scheme to defraud the government by filing fraudulent tax returns, misusing personal identities, and submitting false pandemic relief loan applications,” said Special Agent in Charge Demetrius Hardeman, IRS Criminal Investigation, Atlanta Field Office. “IRS Criminal Investigation special agents, working closely with our federal partners, traced the movement of illicit proceeds and uncovered the financial trails that revealed the full extent of the conspiracy. Their efforts ensured that those responsible were identified and held accountable.”
The case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, IRS Criminal Investigation, the Department of Homeland Security, Homeland Security Investigations, the Small Business Administration Office of Inspector General, and the Social Security Administration, with assistance from multiple state and local law enforcement agencies, including the Mobile County Sheriff’s Office and Mobile Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kasee S. Heisterhagen and Justin Kopf prosecuted the case on behalf of the United States.
In addition to its outstanding financial impact, this prosecution was also a part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership focused on investigating and prosecuting criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking organizations operating in the United States and abroad. Through interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs federal law enforcement resources toward investigating and prosecuting crimes committed by these organizations. HSTF Mobile includes agents and officers from, among others, Homeland Security Investigations, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Drug Enforcement Administration, and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, with prosecutions led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Alabama.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division). The Fraud Division investigates and prosecutes individuals and organizations that commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s efforts to combat fraud support President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to address fraud, waste, and abuse involving federal benefit programs.
This press release details one way in which this office has contributed to ensuring that all Americans pay their fair share. To see the successes of other offices, please see this press release.
If you believe you are a victim of identity theft or suspect a paid tax return preparer is engaged in fraud or misconduct, you may report it to the IRS and make a complaint about a tax return preparer online.
Individuals with information about allegations of fraud involving COVID-19 are encouraged to report it by calling the Department of Justice’s National Center for Disaster Fraud (NCDF) Hotline at 866-720-5721 or via the NCDF Web Complaint Form at: https://www.justice.gov/disaster-fraud/ncdf-disaster-complaint-form.
title: United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Alabama Joins DOJ Fraud Division, IRS, and IRS-CI in National Tax Enforcement Surge Exposing over $490 Million in Tax Fraud

Staunch opposition to Donald Trump’s proposed vanity arch grew sharpy in early October, as veterans, residents, and workers expressed hostility to the project, and the Northern Virginia county that surrounds the site filed suit against it.
On October 1st, as NPR reported: “Veterans, retirees and lawmakers spoke out — against its scale, its cost, its lack of Congressional approval, its gaudiness, its intrusion on nearby Arlington National Cemetery and more.”
On October 7th, per the Associated Press: “The union representing thousands of flight attendants said Wednesday it has safety concerns about President Donald Trump’s proposed triumphal arch that will be on final approach to Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport.”
On October 8th, the Washington Post reported: “Arlington County’s local elected body sued to block construction of President Donald Trump’s planned triumphal arch on Thursday, arguing that administration officials bypassed a key review process in their push to begin work on the structure.”
Rep. Don Beyer (D-VA), who represents a Northern Virginia district in the U.S. House that includes Arlington County, Arlington National Cemetery, and Ronald Reagan National Airport (DCA), today issued the following statement:
“The Administration’s pursuit of Donald Trump’s deeply disrespectful arch has broken the law repeatedly, and now people from many backgrounds are banding together to fight it. I applaud Arlington County’s legal challenge, which rightly confronts the Administration’s illegal attempts to bypass legally required processes to assess the project’s impacts on the local community. Trump wants to avoid these assessments because everyone knows what an honest study would say: this arch is a costly boondoggle that would increase traffic and decrease air safety for the local community. The latter point has also been echoed by workers on the planes that fly in and out of DCA, and the safety concerns would be multiplied many times over if the structure were used as a base for military drones. The bottom line is that Trump’s arch is morally repugnant, and as his pursuit of it gets more corrupt the opposition will continue to grow.”
Rep. Don Beyer is leading congressional efforts to block construction of Trump’s arch. His Northern Virginia district includes the Arlington National Cemetery, where his parents, grandparents, and sister are buried. He is the author of the Arlington National Cemetery Viewshed Protection Act, which would explicitly prohibit construction of the arch. He previously raised concerns about the projects impacts on traffic in the region, which the Trump Administration has yet to address. The arch has been a consistent source of anger and concern to Beyer’s constituents, who like much of the country, vociferously oppose the project.
The National Park Service’s “Assessment of Effect” on President Trump’s proposed 250-foot “triumphal arch” found that the arch would “adversely affect” dozens of nearby historic sites and monuments, including Arlington National Cemetery, Arlington Memorial Bridge, the Lincoln Memorial, the Washington Monument, the National Cathedral, George Washington Memorial Parkway, and many others. The proposal currently faces legal challenges, which allege that it violates the National Historic Preservation Act.
title: Opposition To Trump’s Vanity Arch Grows

Rep. McDonald Rivet Launches Portal to Amplify Voices of Michiganders Facing Skyrocketing Health Care Costs
FLINT— Today, Congresswoman Kristen McDonald Rivet (MI-08) announced a new portal where constituents can share the impact of rising health care costs on them and their families. In the coming weeks, insurance companies will be posting their 2027 rate notices, and costs are expected to rise significantly, due in part to Congress’ failure to extend the Affordable Care Act’s (ACA) enhanced premium tax credits and the One Big Beautiful Bill’s massive cuts to Medicaid.
“Working families and seniors have been paying the price all year after out-of-touch Washington policies gutted our healthcare. Now, premiums are about to go even higher in 2027,” said Congresswoman McDonald Rivet. “Higher costs will force more people to drop their coverage, make it harder to see a doctor, and stretch more families’ budgets to the breaking point. Until Congress stops the political games, we will keep bringing mid-Michigan’s stories to Washington to show how devastating these cuts are.”
Residents of Genesee, Saginaw, Bay, and Midland Counties are encouraged to share their health care story at McDonaldRivet.house.gov/ShareYourStory.
In January 2026, Congress refused to extend the ACA tax credits, which reduce out-of-pocket health care insurance premium costs for hard working Americans. The tax credits’ expiration contributed to Michigan having the sixth-biggest decline in ACA enrollment in the nation in 2026. In 2027, nearly $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts will take effect as a result of Republicans' so-called “Big Beautiful Bill.” Employer-sponsored health plans are expected to raise premiums by at least 8.2% nationally, the largest rate hike since 2003. In Michigan, rates for Individual Marketplace plans are expected to increase by an average of 14.2% in 2027.
Throughout her first term in office, Congresswoman McDonald Rivet has been working to prevent these hikes and fix our healthcare system. For example:
- In July 2025, the Congresswoman voted against Republicans’ trillion-dollar Medicaid cuts, and spoke about the local consequences alongside health care workers and a Flint family that relies on Medicaid for cancer treatments.
- Later that month, she called on Republican colleagues to join her in supporting the Health Care Affordability Act of 2025, which would make the ACA tax credits permanent.
- In September 2025, the Congresswoman led three dozen of her colleagues in demanding Congressional Leadership support efforts to extend the ACA tax credits.
- In the months leading up to the tax credits’ expiration, the Congresswoman elevated the voices of constituents from across the district. 
  - In October 2025, she stood with a mother from Midland whose insurance premiums were expected to jump by 18% to call on Congress to renew the ACA tax credits and lower costs in Saginaw.
  - In November 2025, she hosted a roundtable discussion in Flint with local health care administrators and community members who rely on the ACA tax credits.
- In November, the Congresswoman voted against the government funding package that failed to lower health care costs.
- In January 2026, the Congresswoman helped pass an extension of the ACA tax credits through the House of Representatives. The Senate refused to vote on that bill.
title: Rep. McDonald Rivet Launches Portal to Amplify Voices of Michiganders Facing Skyrocketing Health Care Costs

Davids Demands Accountability Following ICE Sweeps in Southwest Kansas, Citing Threats to Ag Economy and Grocery Prices
Today, Representative Sharice Davids called on Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin to answer for the economic fallout of recent Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) enforcement sweeps in southwest Kansas. Davids highlighted the severe disruption to Kansas’ agricultural economy, local small businesses, and food supply chains following sudden enforcement sweeps, which could raise beef and grocery prices.
"I write to raise grave concerns regarding recent... ICE operations in western Kansas... where sudden enforcement sweeps... immediately paralyzed local agricultural economies, threatened to push grocery prices even higher, and left small businesses shuttered across the region,” wrote Davids. “While I continue pushing both parties for common-sense immigration reform... we need immediate accountability. I urge you to commit to immigration enforcement that coordinates with local law enforcement, respects legal workers, and does not rely on racial profiling or significant economic disruptions for the sake of headlines or mass panic."
Recent federal enforcement operations in Dodge City, Garden City, and Liberal resulted in 104 arrests, sparking widespread panic across southwest Kansas — a crucial hub responsible for more than 20 percent of the nation’s daily cattle slaughter.
The abrupt operations severely disrupted local meatpacking plants, causing a nearly 16 percent single-day drop in fed-cattle slaughter and an overall 8.5 percent week-to-week decline, according to USDA reports. Local businesses were forced to temporarily close their doors, while union representatives and economists warned that halting plant operations will drive beef prices far beyond ground beef's already elevated $7.16-per-pound average.
Major Kansas agricultural organizations have voiced sharp criticisms of the uncoordinated federal actions:
"These ICE operations are having a massive chilling effect on the legal, documented, skilled workers that put beef on the table and keep the cattle supply chain moving. Additionally, these types of disruptions will lead to higher beef prices for consumers… These disruptions come at a time of enhanced focus and pressure on the cattle and beef supply chain. They are a costly and unnecessary impact to cattle producers already suffering from unwelcome political interference to both the markets as well as the physical supply chain. Frustratingly, the harm these actions cause to cattle producers last for days and weeks after such operations conclude.” — Kansas Livestock Association
“Kansas dairy farms depend on a reliable workforce to provide consistent, around-the-clock care for animals. Recent [ICE] enforcement activity has created significant uncertainty and concern among workers, including those who are legally authorized to work in the United States. We urge federal officials to carry out enforcement actions in a lawful, orderly, and transparent manner that respects due process and provides clear, timely communication to affected employers, workers, local law enforcement, and communities.” — Kansas Dairy Association
Read Davids’ full letter here or below
Dear Secretary Mullin,
I write to raise grave concerns regarding recent Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) operations in western Kansas, where sudden enforcement sweeps in Dodge City, Garden City, and Liberal resulted in 104 arrests, and immediately paralyzed local agricultural economies, threatened to push grocery prices even higher, and left small businesses shuttered across the region.
I believe in the importance of enforcing federal immigration laws and protecting Kansas families from crime. In this instance, however, I have heard concerns from agriculture and business stakeholders about how these activities were conducted and their impact on communities across the state. Kansans have shared with me several instances of citizens and documented persons being targeted on their way to work or going about their day, and in many cases, local law enforcement was not consulted.
Southwest Kansas is a crucial hub for American agriculture – home to more than 20 percent of the country’s daily cattle slaughter. ICE’s activities corresponded with an 8.5 percent drop in cattle slaughter week-to-week according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture as meatpacking capacity was significantly disrupted. The Kansas Livestock Association stated last month that these operations, “[had] a massive chilling effect on the legal, documented, skilled workers that put beef on the table and keep the cattle supply chain moving…. They are a costly and unnecessary impact to cattle producers already suffering from unwelcome political interference to both the markets as well as the physical supply chain.”
This comes as Americans are struggling with staggeringly high grocery prices – including the price of ground beef jumping 7.9 percent year-to-year – and the smallest cattle herd in decades.
The immigration enforcement efforts also delivered a notable hit to Kansas’ dairy industry, which accounts for more than $3 billion in economic impact and 11,000 jobs statewide. The Kansas Dairy Association shared that ICE’s activities, “created significant uncertainty and concern among workers, including those who are legally authorized to work in the United States.”
While your agency frames these multi-day September 2026 operations as targeted at individuals with criminal histories, the immediate fallout has inflicted severe collateral damage on southwest Kansas’s economy, national food supply chains, and working families already struggling at the checkout counter. In addition to notable impacts on the agriculture sector, ICE’s activities led to local business closures and school absences.
These extreme actions leave Kansans feeling less safe, strain local economies, and disrupt national supply chains. While I continue pushing both parties for common-sense immigration reform – securing our border against violent crime and drug trafficking while supporting our agricultural sector – we need immediate accountability.
I urge you to commit to immigration enforcement that coordinates with local law enforcement, respects legal workers, and does not rely on racial profiling or significant economic disruptions for the sake of headlines or mass panic.
Sincerely,
title: Davids Demands Accountability Following ICE Sweeps in Southwest Kansas, Citing Threats to Ag Economy and Grocery Prices

EPA Regional Administrators Visit Farms in Maryland and Kentucky to Highlight Soil Health, Water Quality, and Agricultural Partnership
PHILADELPHIA, PA / ATLANTA, GA (October 15, 2026) - U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Regional Administrators from the Mid-Atlantic (Region 3) and Southeast (EPA Region 4) recently toured farms in both Maryland and Kentucky to highlight the importance of regenerative agriculture practices that support healthy soils, cleaner water, and long-term farm resilience.
In support of President Trump’s recent executive order, “Advancing regenerative agriculture and strengthening American farm resilience,” these visits underscored the value of voluntary, locally informed conservation practices such as cover crops, reduced tillage, nutrient management, rotational grazing, buffer plantings, and other approaches that can improve soil structure, retain moisture, reduce erosion, and limit nutrient loss to nearby waterways.
Hosted by Regenified, a regenerative verification program, the visits provided the Regional Administrators an opportunity to meet directly with farmers and have discussions focused on practical approaches that can improve land management, reduce runoff, strengthen watershed protection, support supply chain resilience and advance the continued success of American agriculture.
“Farmers are at the heart of America’s food supply, our rural economy, and our environmental progress,” said EPA Mid-Atlantic Regional Administrator Amy Van Blarcom-Lackey. “These visits are about listening, learning, and recognizing the innovation farmers are already putting to work—from improving soil health and protecting water quality to adopting practices that keep their operations productive, resilient, and profitable for future generations.”
“Across the Southeast, we see every day how conservation-minded farming practices can strengthen both the land and the local economy,” said Southeast Regional Administrator Kevin McOmber. “EPA’s role is to support that work by partnering with states, farmers and local organizations to share information, reduce barriers, and help communities put practical solutions to work.”
About Regenified
Regenified is a practice and outcome-based land verification and product certification program that champions regenerative agriculture. Founded by a team of regenerative farming pioneers, experts, and innovators, Regenified promotes practices that enhance biodiversity, soil health, water quality, and nutrient density while aligning with nature. Regenified verifies and certifies farms, ranches, and products that restore ecosystems and regenerate soil, ensuring a legacy for future generations. Committed to cultivating a regenerative world, Regenified guides farms and brands toward practices that rejuvenate the Earth, support thriving ecosystems, and transform agriculture into a healing force for our planet.
About Harborview
Harborview Farms produces corn, wheat, and soybeans for the Mid-Atlantic region focusing on sustainable agriculture and environmental stewardship. The Hill family has been farming in Rock Hall, MD since the early 1900s. Today, Harborview Farms is owned and managed by Trey and Cheryl Hill and his father Herman Hill, and they are both committed to producing grain in a responsible and environmentally friendly manner.
title: EPA Regional Administrators Visit Farms in Maryland and Kentucky to Highlight Soil Health, Water Quality, and Agricultural Partnership

CONCORD – Kittery, Maine resident Trenton Murphy, 28, was sentenced in federal court today to 96 months of imprisonment, followed by five years of supervised release, for conspiring to distribute fentanyl and methamphetamine with a Massachusetts-based drug trafficking organization (DTO), U.S. Attorney Erin Creegan announces.

According to court documents and statements, investigators with the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) obtained Facebook messages between Murphy and the leader of the DTO arranging drug transactions where Murphy bought significant amounts of fentanyl and methamphetamine. On one occasion, Murphy also traded a firearm with the DTO for drugs. During the course of the conspiracy, Murphy bought nearly two pounds of fentanyl and three pounds of methamphetamine from the DTO, which he would then sell to his own customer base.

“This defendant was a key part of a criminal network that distributed destructive drugs such as fentanyl and meth in our communities, wreaking havoc on so many New Hampshire families, and will now be spending significant time behind bars,” said Erin Creegan, U.S. Attorney for the District of New Hampshire. “Our office continues to be vigilant in working with federal and state law enforcement partners to disrupt these criminal drug trafficking networks and impose harsh penalties on those responsible for operating them.”

“Drug traffickers who put profits ahead of human lives must be held accountable for the harm they bring to our communities,” said DEA Special Agent in Charge Jarod Forget, New England Field Division. “Fentanyl and methamphetamine continue to fuel addiction, destroy families, and threaten public safety across New Hampshire. This eight-year sentence reflects the serious consequences of trafficking these dangerous drugs and underscores our unwavering commitment to identifying, investigating, and bringing those responsible to justice.”

The DEA led the investigation with valuable assistance from the Nashua Police Department, New Hampshire State Police, Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office, and Massachusetts State Police. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Cesar Vega and Mike Shannon prosecuted the case.

This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF New Hampshire comprises agents and officers from FBI, HSI, IRS, DEA, ATF, USMS, and DSS with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of New Hampshire.
title: Maine Man Sentenced Eight Years in Prison for Conspiring to Distribute Fentanyl and Methamphetamine

Owner of Health Care Software Company Sentenced to 19 Years in Prison for $1B Medicare Fraud
A Kansas CEO and owner of an internet platform was sentenced yesterday to 19 years in prison for his role in operating a platform that generated false doctors’ orders and prescriptions to defraud Medicare and other federal health care benefit programs out of more than $1 billion.
“The Department of Justice and our agency partners dismantled one of the largest telemedicine fraud schemes ever, and yesterday’s lengthy prison sentence holds the orchestrator of that scheme accountable,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division. “The defendant’s fraud scheme lured hundreds of thousands of elderly and disabled Americans into a sophisticated international telemarketing system with one goal: stealing as much as possible from the Medicare trust fund. The Fraud Division will continue to leverage its resources to take down complex fraud operations like Blackman’s DMERx.”
“This sentence delivers a decisive warning: anyone who exploits VA programs and services for personal profit will be found and held fully accountable,” said Inspector General Cheryl L. Mason of the Department of Veterans Affairs. “The VA OIG remains committed to working alongside our law enforcement partners to uncover complex fraud schemes and protect our nation’s veterans.”
“This 19-year sentence sends an unmistakable message: those who exploit federal health care programs for personal enrichment will face serious consequences,” said Acting Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Miranda L. Bennett of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General (HH-OIG). “Schemes that corrupt medical decision-making and siphon taxpayer dollars from programs serving vulnerable Americans undermine trust in our health care system. HHS-OIG and its law enforcement partners will continue to pursue those responsible and hold them accountable.”
“This sentencing sends a clear message that those who exploit federal health care programs for personal gain will be held accountable,” said Special Agent in Charge Brett D. Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office. “This scheme undermined the integrity of our health care system and defrauded taxpayer-funded programs designed to serve those in need. The FBI remains committed to working alongside our law enforcement partners to investigate complex health care fraud schemes, protect taxpayer dollars, and hold those responsible accountable. Through these efforts, we remain focused on defending the homeland and protecting the American people from those who seek to exploit our nation’s systems for personal gain.”
“This investigation reinforces DCIS’s steadfast commitment to protecting the integrity of the TRICARE program and ensuring that taxpayer-funded military health benefits are used appropriately,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Nakia Martin Alexander of the DCIS Southeast Field Office. “Fraud schemes that divert TRICARE resources erode the support promised to our service members and their families. As the criminal investigative arm of the DoD Office of Inspector General, DCIS remains focused on identifying these schemes and holding those responsible fully accountable.”
According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Brett Blackman, 43, of Johnson County, Kansas, and his co-conspirators aggressively targeted hundreds of thousands of Medicare beneficiaries across the United States to get them to accept medically unnecessary orthotic braces and other items. They then arranged for purported telemedicine doctors to sign bogus prescription orders for these items so that their co-conspirators could bill Medicare for them. All told, Blackman and his co-conspirators billed Medicare and other federal health care benefit programs over $1 billion for this unnecessary equipment.
Blackman owned, controlled, and was the CEO of HealthSplash, which acquired Power Mobility Doctor Rx, LLC (DMERx) in Sept. 2017. DMERx was an internet-based platform that generated false and fraudulent doctors’ orders for durable medical equipment (DME) and prescriptions for other items. As part of the scheme, Blackman and his co-conspirators connected pharmacies, DME suppliers, and marketers with telemedicine companies that would accept illegal kickbacks and bribes in exchange for signed doctors’ orders created using the DMERx platform. Blackman and his co-conspirators took a cut for themselves in exchange for the referrals.
The fraudulent doctors’ orders and prescriptions generated by DMERx falsely represented that a doctor had actually examined and treated the Medicare beneficiaries when, in fact, the doctors were simply paid to sign orders and prescriptions without any meaningful interaction with the beneficiary, and in some cases, no interaction at all. Testimony and evidence presented at trial from an undercover agent who posed as a Medicare beneficiary showed the scheme in action — starting with a foreign call center that pushed the undercover agent to agree to multiple braces to a doctor signing bogus orders for the braces using Blackman’s DMERx platform. The doctor’s order for one of these undercover agent beneficiaries claimed that the doctor conducted various tests that can only be performed in person even though the doctor never even spoke with the undercover agent “patient.”
The DME suppliers and pharmacies that were paying illegal kickbacks for these orders billed Medicare and other insurers more than $1 billion. Medicare and the other insurers paid more than $450 million based on these claims. According to evidence presented at trial, Blackman and his co-conspirators concealed the scheme through sham contracts and by manipulating the doctors’ orders to avoid Medicare audits, including by removing references to telemedicine in the doctors’ orders.
As a result of Blackman’s scheme, Medicare was fraudulently billed for orthotic braces for more than 346,000 Medicare beneficiaries. On average, Medicare was billed for four braces per beneficiary, with Medicare being billed for at least 21 orthotics prescribed through Blackman’s DMERx platform to over 1,200 beneficiaries.
Exhibit from Trial Summarizing the Number of Orthotics Billed per Medicare Beneficiary as a Result of Blackman’s Fraud Scheme
After a 23-day jury trial ending in Apr. 2026, Blackman was convicted of conspiracy to commit health care fraud and wire fraud, conspiracy to pay and receive kickbacks, and conspiracy to defraud the United States and to make false statements in connection with health care matters. Blackman’s restitution and forfeiture obligations will be determined by the Court at a later date.
In Dec. 2025, Blackman’s co-defendant, Gary Cox, was sentenced to 15 years in prison.
HHS-OIG, FBI, VA-OIG, and DCIS investigated the case.
Assistant Deputy Chief Darren C. Halverson and Trial Attorney Reginald Cuyler Jr. of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section prosecuted the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit.
title: Owner of Health Care Software Company Sentenced to 19 Years in Prison for $1B Medicare Fraud

WIESBADEN, Germany — U.S. Army Europe and Africa and NATO Allies successfully concluded Avenger Triad 26 on Oct. 15, marking the end of a 10-day, distributed command post exercise that tested simulated large-scale, multi-domain combat operations across Europe.
Conducted from Oct. 6 to 15, the exercise brought together approximately 2,000 U.S. service members and 2,000 multinational personnel operating from command posts across France, Germany, the Netherlands and Poland. Avenger Triad 26 was synchronized with NATO’s premier command post exercise, Steadfast Duel 26, which linked strategic and operational decision-makers across all 32 Allied nations.
Operating primarily from the Combined Operations and Intelligence Center at Clay Kaserne in Wiesbaden, USAREUR-AF and NATO’s Allied Land Command functioned as a converged, integrated warfighting headquarters, turning NATO’s regional defense plans into synchronized operational action.
“Steadfast Duel and Avenger Triad demonstrated that our collective defense is not just an idea on paper; it is an active, trained reality,” said Lt. Gen. Jez Bennett, acting LANDCOM commander. “By deploying our LANDCOM staff to Wiesbaden to fight alongside our U.S. partners as a single, connected headquarters, we tested our people, validated our processes and refined our ability to deliver decisive action under pressure. Our strength lies in interoperability, and this exercise proved our readiness to defend every inch of Allied territory.”
Avenger Triad 26 placed headquarters staffs under continuous operational strain, simulating combat conditions against a simulated opposing force in a complex, multi-domain environment. Participating Allied corps included the U.S. Army’s V Corps, the 2nd Polish Corps, the 1st French Corps and the 1st German-Netherlands Corps, supported by specialized theater commands including the 21st Theater Sustainment Command, 10th Army Air and Missile Defense Command and Multi-Domain Command – Europe.
A central objective of the exercise was putting concepts from NATO’s Eastern Flank Deterrence Initiative into operational practice. Rather than relying solely on static lines of defense, EFDI integrates advanced sensors, unmanned aerial systems, cloud computing and shared data environments to shorten the time between threat detection and target engagement.
Command posts utilized next-generation command-and-control software, including the Maven Smart System, to establish a unified common operating picture across dispersed national headquarters. This common data backbone enabled military planners to process vast amounts of operational data, accelerate commander decision cycles and coordinate deep fires across the land, air, sea, cyber and space domains.
“What we accomplished in Wiesbaden was a real test of how we will fight if called upon,” said Brig. Gen. Thomas Lowin, LANDCOM deputy chief of staff for operations. “Operating as one team, we proved that we can connect distributed sensors to effectors through a resilient digital backbone. While artificial intelligence and modern data tools help us cut through noise and deliver information rapidly, warfare remains fundamentally human. Our staff analyzed those options and gave our commander the clarity required to act decisively.”
Lowin noted that the progress made during this year’s exercise built directly on lessons identified in previous iterations, moving NATO’s operational transformation from concept to frontline execution.
“Last year we finished at a high level, and this year we started at that level,” Lowin said. “The credibility of our deterrence rests on our capability. When an adversary sees that 32 nations can share data seamlessly, command corps-level formations across thousands of kilometers and coordinate joint fires in minutes, it sends an unmistakable signal: attacking NATO will not succeed.”
Avenger Triad 26 and Steadfast Duel 26 also underscored European Allies taking on greater operational responsibility for theater defense, ensuring that national and multinational corps can seamlessly integrate into NATO's overarching command structure during an Article 5 collective defense scenario.
The operational insights and digital workflows refined during Avenger Triad 26 will inform planning for upcoming theater maneuvers, including NATO’s large-scale field exercise Steadfast Defender 2027, where these command post concepts will be tested with live formations in the field.
title: USAREUR-AF, NATO Allies conclude Exercise Avenger Triad 26

WASHINGTON—Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) issued an Alert asking financial institutions to report potential Iranian regime abuse of religious charity networks, including diversion of religious tithes, or khums.
“Under President Trump’s leadership, Treasury will not allow the Iranian regime to continue its long history of abusing religious institutions to line the pockets of its elites and fund terrorism,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “By identifying and reporting this potential abuse, financial institutions can provide law enforcement with critical information to isolate the Iranian regime and its financial enablers.”
The Iranian regime has been known to abuse ostensibly religious organizations in Iran and neighboring countries to enrich its elites, fund the repression of the Iranian people, and support terrorism abroad. In addition, the regime co-opts khums payments from the global Shi’a community to further its destabilizing activities*.* In some cases, organizations that collect these payments do so on behalf of prominent Iranian ayatollahs with ties to the regime. These entities may use informal financial channels like hawalas and cash couriers to remit the funds to Iran or to Iran-linked actors. FinCEN’s Alert includes red flag indicators to aid financial institutions in detecting, preventing, and reporting this illicit activity.
Indicators of Potential Iranian Abuse of Religious Charities
- A charitable organization or nonprofit organization (NPO) solicits donations but does not appear to provide any charitable services, or openly supports the Iranian regime or its terrorist proxies, such as in fundraising appeals or on social media.
- A charitable organization or NPO receives large donations from an unknown source over a short period of time and then sends significant wire transfers or checks to other charitable organizations or NPOs.
- A charitable organization or NPO, or the customer’s employee, engages in behavior suggesting efforts to evade certain reporting or recordkeeping requirements.
- A customer receives transfers from a charitable organization or NPO with which the customer has no clear business relationship, and then the customer proceeds to withdraw the funds in cash or remit them onward.
FinCEN recognizes that legitimate charities should have access to financial services and can transmit funds through transparent channels. FinCEN reminds banks to apply a risk-based approach to customer due diligence requirements when developing the risk profiles of charities and other non-profit customers, as discussed in the Joint Fact Sheet on Bank Secrecy Act Due Diligence Requirements for Charities and Non-Profit Organizations.
###
title: Operation Economic Outcast Targets Iranian Regime’s Abuse of Religious Charity Networks
