FBI Little Rock Crushes Violent Crime in Operation Summer Heat 2.0
In Four Months, the FBI’s National Violent Crime Initiative Netted Thousands of Arrests
LITTLE ROCK—FBI Little Rock and its law enforcement partners made over 50 arrests as part of Summer Heat 2.0, a four-month FBI initiative to crush violent crime nationwide.
“The FBI is committed to protecting the people of Arkansas and holding accountable those who threaten the safety of our communities. Combating violent crime, disrupting drug trafficking, and removing dangerous individuals and illegal firearms from our streets remain top priorities,” said FBI Little Rock Special Agent in Charge Jason Van Goor. “We will continue working closely with our federal, state, and local law enforcement partners, leveraging our collective resources and expertise to investigate criminal activity, bring offenders to justice, and keep Arkansas communities safe.”
Between June 1 and September 20, FBI Little Rock, in coordination with its partners, made 53 arrests, secured 33 indictments, and obtained 39 convictions. In addition, 16 illegally possessed firearms were seized, as well as cocaine and fentanyl. Most importantly, the FBI and our partners located 10 child victims in Arkansas.
Summer Heat 2.0 executed federal warrants on violent criminals and fugitives, dismantled violent gangs and transnational criminal organizations, and identified and rescued child victims. Nationally, the FBI and its law enforcement partners made 8,927 arrests, recovered 5,013 illegally possessed weapons, and seized 27,512 kilograms of cocaine as well as 687 kilograms of fentanyl: an amount equal to 52 million lethal doses. Special agents and intelligence professionals investigating violent crimes against children identified or located 1,410 victim children.
The FBI first launched the Summer Heat initiative for three months in 2025 to deploy a multi-pronged offensive to crush violent crime. The FBI has compounded upon the successes of 2025, with the 2026 initiative marking a 120% increase in the number of illegal weapons recovered, a 63% increase in the amount of fentanyl seized, and a 34% increase in the number of children identified or located. The announcement of Operation Summer Heat 2.0 results follows historic drops in crime across the U.S., according to the FBI’s 2025 UCR Summary of Reported Crimes in the Nation.
title: FBI Little Rock Crushes Violent Crime in Operation Summer Heat 2.0

text:
WICHITA, KAN. – A former Kansas teacher pleaded guilty to Production of Child Pornography offenses.

According to court documents, Ryan Brungardt, 38, of Salina pleaded guilty to 3 counts of Production of Child Pornography.

Ryan Brungardt was a middle school teacher and high school coach. In those roles, he attended wrestling tournaments throughout the state of Kansas. While coaching at wrestling tournaments, Brungardt would go into locker rooms after matches and use his cell phone to film the boys in the shower.

Over the course of this conduct, Brungardt recorded 71 videos of minors at wrestling events across Kansas, including the following:

• Newton, Kansas (January 13, 2024);

• Rose Hill, Kansas (January 18, 2024);

• Hays, Kansas (January 20, 2024);

• Garden City, Kansas (January 27, 2024).

Those 71 videos captured 25 minor victims (the youngest of whom was 14 years old), as well as 4 victims who were 18 at the time of the filming. There were additional videos of minors in locker rooms where the victims could not be identified.

This all came to light after some boys bravely made a report to their schools about a coach possibly filming them. Law enforcement interviewed Brungardt at the middle school where he was teaching. Law enforcement seized his phone and questioned him about the allegations of filming minors. After the interview, Brungardt grabbed his phone back from law enforcement and snapped the phone in half. The phone caught on fire and resulted in the evacuation of the middle school.

Despite Brungardt's actions, law enforcement was able to preserve the evidence and ultimately find the videos and hold Brungardt accountable for his actions. Brungardt is scheduled to be sentenced on January 13, 2027. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

“As a society, we rely on teachers, coaches, childcare workers, and others to protect and care for our children,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser. “The Department of Justice is committed to holding those in positions of trust to account when that trust is violated. We are thankful for the bravery it took to bring the conduct in this case to light. We continue to work to identify victims, so we encourage athletes to reach out if they participated in any of these tournaments.”

The U.S. Attorney’s Office conducted the investigation in coordination with the Kansas Bureau of Investigation, the Newton Police Department, and various other local police departments.

Project Safe Childhood

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit

https://www.justice.gov/psc

###
title: Salina man pleads guilty to Production of Child Pornography Crimes

WASHINGTON — Today, Representatives Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) and Claudia Tenney (NY-24) introduced the bipartisan Internet Reach and Access Now (IRAN) Act to strengthen U.S. efforts to help the Iranian people access the open internet, communicate securely, and overcome the Iranian regime’s censorship, surveillance, and internet shutdowns.
“Freedom of expression and access to unrestricted information are fundamental human rights. The Islamic Republic regularly shuts down or restricts internet access while committing mass atrocities,” said Congresswoman Ansari. “President Trump has said 'help is on the way' for the Iranian people. Ensuring unrestricted internet access would actually help people immediately. I’m proud to introduce the IRAN Act, a bipartisan, noncontroversial, and not militarily invasive bill that would do just that.”
Iran remains one of the world’s most restrictive digital environments, with the regime routinely restricting internet access to suppress dissent, conceal human rights abuses, and isolate the Iranian people. The IRAN Act strengthens the U.S. internet freedom strategy for Iran by requiring regular reviews, implementation assessments, and congressional reporting, while evaluating emerging technologies such as VPNs, decentralized and peer to peer networks, and direct to cell satellite communications. The legislation also seeks to expand cybersecurity training and secure digital tools for journalists, human rights defenders, and other civil society actors, and directs greater coordination among federal agencies to help ensure U.S. sanctions and export controls do not unintentionally hinder access to open internet technologies.
“The Iranian regime knows that access to information is a threat to its grip on power, which is why it relies on censorship, surveillance, and internet blackouts to silence the Iranian people,” said Congresswoman Tenney. “The United States should stand with the courageous Iranians demanding basic freedoms by helping them stay connected to one another and the outside world. The bipartisan IRAN Act strengthens our internet freedom strategy, supports secure technologies that can overcome the regime’s censorship, and improves coordination across our government so these efforts deliver real results. The Iranian people deserve the ability to communicate freely, access independent information, and expose the regime’s brutality to the world.”
title: Ansari Introduces Bipartisan IRAN Act to Expand Internet Freedom for the Iranian People

FORT DRUM, N.Y. (Oct. 15, 2026) -- Families explored the wonders of universe without having to leave Fort Drum, as the Family Advocacy Program (FAP) hosted its Journey to the Star event Oct. 14 at the Child and Youth Services Sports and Fitness Center.
In addition to a gym packed with space-themed games and activities, attendees could step inside Cornell Cooperative Extension’s mobile planetarium and surround themselves in planetary marvels.
“It’s an immersive experience, kind of like IMAX, where there’s video projected 360-degrees all around you,” said Mitch McCormick, Cornell Cooperative Extension community and economic vitality issue leader. “It’s great for kids because they basically get a tour of our solar system and learn about each planet and different things in outer space, but it’s also interesting for parents, too.”
McCormick said it was a unique opportunity for family members who have never visited a planetarium before.
“This is not a typical classroom experience,” he said. “They might get this kind of education in school, but not like this. I like to think this kind of exposure might lead some of them to a hobby like stargazing or astronomy or even pique an interest in a career path.”
Outside the planetarium, children could navigate an astronaut boot camp obstacle course, meet costumed characters representing the sun and earth, and create colorful sand art stars and glow-in-the dark planets.
“I think this is a great opportunity for families to come out and have fun, do interesting things – maybe try something new,” said Nicole Wetzel, FAP educator. “I just think it gets exhausting for parents to come up with fun, enriching activities all the time. So, we kind of do that for them where they can just enjoy the fun together.”
FAP organizers said this was more than just a fun, educational intergalactic adventure. The annual event was part of the Domestic Violence Awareness Month campaign, which highlights prevention through connection.
“One of the things we like to emphasize is the concept of healthy families and healthy relationships because that is essential to helping reduce domestic violence,” Wetzel said. “So, we like to create these opportunities where Soldiers and their families can connect, unwind and strengthen those bonds.”
For those unfamiliar with the Family Advocacy Program, the event served as an open door to meet the team and learn how the organization supports the Fort Drum community. FAP is dedicated to domestic and child abuse prevention, education, prompt reporting, and intervention. They offer victim advocacy assistance, educational workshops, parenting classes and playgroups, among their services.
“This is a chance for us to talk with parents about our classes and the services we provide,” said Tom Wojcikowski, FAP educator. “So, now they know who we are, and maybe next time we’re at the PX or somewhere, they may approach us with a question or want to talk about something we can help them with. It’s just giving our program a familiar face.”
Before heading home, families received a space-themed goodie bag, as well as informational flyers and brochures about the Family Advocacy Program.
Community members can join the FAP team at the Monster Pop In and Paint event, between 3-7 p.m. Oct. 28 inside the Enrichment Center, Bldg. 10262 on 4th Armored Division Drive. This is a fun and relaxed painting activity for all ages and skill levels. To register, call 315-772-5914.
The FAP offices are located in Bldg. 10250 on 4th Armored Division Drive and can be reached by calling 315-772-5914. For more information, visit https://home.army.mil/drum/about/Garrison/directorate-human-resources/soldier-and-family-readiness-division-sfrd/SFRC/family-advocacy-program-fap.
title: Fort Drum families have some intergalactic fun with the Family Advocacy Program

text:
On October 1, 2026, the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) published for comment revised policy guidance for the Capital Investment Grants Program (CIG). In the Federal Register notice, FTA stated "the proposed revisions are intended to streamline the CIG process, improve accountability of CIG project sponsors, and improve overall readability of the policy guidance." Among other things, FTA proposes a new formal methodology for calculating the federal share of a proposed project's cost from a CIG grant. This proposed methodology includes greater CIG funding shares for projects in places with higher than average birth rates and marriage rates, in line with the Department of Transportation's (DOT's) "family friendly" policy.
CIG provides funding to support the construction of fixed-guideway transit systems (e.g., light rail), including new systems and additions to existing systems. A CIG project is categorized as a "New Starts" project, unless as a "Small Starts" project it costs less than $400 million and CIG program funding is less than $150 million. "Core Capacity" projects are investments in existing fixed-guideway systems that increase capacity of a corridor by 10% that is at or will be at capacity in 10 years (49 U.S.C. §5309(a)).
To evaluate proposed CIG projects, FTA computes ratings of statutory project justification and local financial commitment criteria on a 5-point scale (high, medium-high, medium, medium-low, low). The project justification criteria are mobility improvements, environmental benefits, congestion relief, economic development effects, land use (or capacity needs of the corridor for Core Capacity projects), and cost effectiveness. Cost effectiveness, for example, is measured by estimated capital and operating and maintenance costs per trip.
Federal law limits the maximum federal share of a project's cost from the CIG program funds to 60% for New Starts projects and 80% for Small Starts and Core Capacity projects (49 U.S.C. §5309(l)). Many projects have received a commitment from FTA for a CIG share below the maximum.
FTA's October 2026 proposal is for a "formal methodology [that] would provide a uniform and consistent approach for FTA to consider project merits, such as cost-effectiveness and transit ridership, when determining the CIG percentage share and corresponding CIG funding amount for a New Starts or Core Capacity project." Accordingly, projects with an overall medium or higher rating would start with a 40% CIG share of project costs. This share would then be adjusted on the basis of the ratings of the project justification criteria up to the maximum allowed by law (Table 1). FTA states that it "believes these adjustment factors are appropriate because they clearly put the emphasis on cost-effectiveness and ridership, which will allow FTA to provide a higher CIG percentage share to projects that are cost-effective and projected to have high transit ridership, and will ensure Federal taxpayer funds are supporting worthy investments."
Source: Federal Transit Administration, "Notice of Availability of Proposed Policy Guidance for the Capital Investment Grants Program," 91 Federal Register 62586-62595, October 1, 2026.
Note: *New Starts only; **Core Capacity only.
FTA's proposed CIG policy would also increase the CIG funding share for relatively high birth rates and marriage rates within the project corridor, defined as a one-mile buffer around the project corridor using census tract data from the Census Bureau. The increase would be an additional five percentage points each if the average birth or marriage rate in the project corridor is more than 1% above the national average, three points if the birth or marriage rate is equal to the national average or up to 1% percent higher than the national average, and one point if the average birth or marriage rate is within 1% below the national average.
According to FTA, these proposed adjustments are consistent with DOT Order 2100.7, "Ensuring Reliance Upon Sound Economic Analysis in Department of Transportation Policies, Programs, and Activities," issued on March 10, 2025, by the Secretary of Transportation. The order states DOT should "give preference to communities with marriage and birth rates higher than the national average (including in administering the Federal Transit Administration's Capital Investment Grant program)."
Some question whether this proposed addition to the funding share calculation, as FTA states in the Federal Register notice, would "ensure Federal taxpayer funds are supporting worthy investments." The birth rate and marriage rate adjustments may offset poorer scores on other metrics, possibly leading to less effective projects. For example, together high birth rate and marriage rate adjustments can be worth as much as a medium-low cost effectiveness score.
In terms of ridership, fixed-guideway transit modes are most effective in high density urban corridors. Critics of the FTA proposal point to research on the geography of birth rates and marriage rates indicating that places with relatively high rates tend to be located farther away from urban centers than places with relatively low rates. Households in high birth and high marriage rate areas tend to be higher income, more likely to own a car and drive alone to work, and less likely to walk, bike, or take public transit to work. Residents of places with high marriage and high birth rates are more likely to be White and less likely to be Black or Hispanic.
Adjusting the federal CIG funding share on the basis of marriage and birth rates may incentivize more commuter rail projects, which are designed to provide longer distance trips to outlying places with lower density uses. In a study of commuter rail agencies, the Government Accountability Office found that commuter rail can provide economic and mobility benefits for less urbanized communities but that there are "considerable infrastructure and operational costs making commuter rail more expensive to provide compared to some other transit modes."
title: Department of Transportation’s “Family Friendly” Policy and Public Transit Project Funding

A man who distributed methamphetamine, heroin, and fentanyl on multiple occasions in 2022 was convicted by a jury today after a three-day trial in federal court in Cedar Rapids.

Anthony Harris, age 61, from Cedar Rapids, Iowa, was convicted of one count of distribution of a controlled substance near a protected location and two counts of distribution of a controlled substance. The verdict was returned this afternoon following about two hours of jury deliberations.

The evidence at trial showed that, on three occasions in 2022, law enforcement officers used a confidential informant to buy controlled substances from Harris. On April 13, 2022, Harris distributed methamphetamine, heroin, and fentanyl to the confidential informant within 1,000 feet of a public secondary school in Cedar Rapids. On June 1, 2022, Harris distributed heroin to the confidential informant. Several months later, on September 6, 2022, Harris met the confidential informant at the same location as on June 1 and distributed methamphetamine, heroin, and fentanyl.

This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States.

HSTF Kansas City is headquartered in Kansas City, Missouri, covering Missouri, Kansas, Iowa and Nebraska. HSTF Kansas City is composed of agents and officers from the Department of Homeland Security Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Homeland Security Investigations, the Bureau of Alcohol Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, Drug Enforcement Agency, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Internal Revenue Service, the United States Marshals Service, the United States Postal Inspection Service, the State Investigative Agencies for Missouri, Kansas, Iowa, and Nebraska, and the Kansas City Missouri Police Department.

Sentencing before United States District Court Chief Judge C.J. Williams will be set after a presentence report is prepared. Harris remains in custody of the United States Marshal pending sentencing. Harris faces a mandatory minimum sentence of one year in prison and a possible maximum sentence of 100 years’ imprisonment, a $6,000,000 fine, and at least six years of supervised release following any imprisonment.

The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Adam J. Vander Stoep and Jennifer Schrauth and was investigated by HSTF Kansas City, with the assistance of the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Task Force consisting of the DEA, the Linn County Sheriff's Office, the Cedar Rapids Police Department, the Marion Police Department, and the Iowa Division of Narcotics Enforcement.

ALBUQUERQUE – Five people are facing federal drug trafficking charges for allegedly distributing methamphetamine and fentanyl in southern New Mexico through an operation coordinated by an American citizen incarcerated in a prison in Ciudad Juarez, Mexico.

According to court documents, beginning in mid-2025, the FBI, Las Cruces/Dona Ana County Metro Narcotics and Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) began investigating a drug trafficking organization allegedly distributing methamphetamine and fentanyl from Ciudad Juarez, Mexico, into southern New Mexico. Investigators identified Felix Anthony Salazar III , 34, an American citizen who was incarcerated in Ciudad Juarez, as a suspected member of the organization who coordinated drug transactions with individuals in southern New Mexico.

On September 5, 2025, Salazar allegedly arranged for an undercover agent to purchase approximately one kilogram of methamphetamine for $3,800 in Anthony, New Mexico. Yadira Lizett Cano , 28, of El Paso, Texas, allegedly drove a vehicle to the meeting location with a 16-year-old passenger, who delivered the methamphetamine to the undercover agent and collected the money. Laboratory testing confirmed that the packages contained approximately 973 grams of pure methamphetamine. Investigators allege that Cano knowingly used the juvenile to facilitate the transaction.

On September 17, 2025, Salazar allegedly arranged a second transaction involving approximately half a kilogram of methamphetamine for $1,800 in Sunland Park, New Mexico. Moses Andrew Gonzales , 36, and Martha Janeth Grijalva Fierro , 36, both of El Paso, Texas, allegedly arrived together, and Gonzales delivered the drugs to the undercover agent. Investigators identified communications between Salazar and Grijalva Fierro that allegedly connected her to the arrangement. Laboratory testing confirmed approximately 468 grams of pure methamphetamine.

On October 24, 2025, Salazar allegedly arranged another drug transaction involving methamphetamine and fentanyl pills in Las Cruces. Suleima Eidali Miranda , 31, directed the undercover agent to a residence, where she allegedly delivered packages of methamphetamine and fentanyl pills in exchange for $2,000. Laboratory testing confirmed approximately 984 grams of pure methamphetamine and 251 grams of fentanyl.

Salazar , Cano , Gonzales , Grijalva Fierro and Miranda are federally charged with conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine. Cano is also charged with distribution of methamphetamine and using a juvenile in a drug operation. Gonzales and Grijalva Fierro are each charged with distribution of methamphetamine. Miranda is charged with distribution of methamphetamine and fentanyl. Salazar and Miranda are additionally charged with conspiracy to distribute fentanyl.

All five defendants have been arrested and are in federal custody. Salazar , who had been incarcerated in Ciudad Juarez, surrendered to law enforcement Sunday night, October 11, 2026, after crossing the border from Mexico into the United States.

First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison and Special Agent in Charge Justin A. Garris of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albuquerque Field Office made the announcement today.

The Las Cruces Resident Agency of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albuquerque Field Office investigated this case with assistance from the Las Cruces/Dona Ana County Metro Narcotics and HSI. Assistant U.S. Attorney Devon Aragon Martinez is prosecuting the case.

The Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative was established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of U.S. law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States.

A criminal complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: Five Federally Charged Following Multiagency Investigation into Drug Trafficking Operation Run from Mexican Prison Following Homeland Security Task Force Investigation

Rep. Panetta Leads Bipartisan Letter Raising Concerns About Meta’s Use of Research Tax Credit for Data Centers
Monterey, CA – United States Representatives Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) and Greg Steube (FL-17) wrote a bipartisan letter to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent expressing concerns about reports that Meta is seeking to use the federal research tax credit for its data center buildout. The bipartisan letter, co-led by Reps. Mike Thompson (CA-04) and Suzan DelBene (WA-01), emphasized that any claims by Meta for the federal tax credit must meet the clearly defined requirements for qualified research and experimentation.
Congress established the research tax credit in 1981 amid concerns about declining private-sector research investment and U.S. technological competitiveness. By reducing the cost of qualifying research, the credit is meant to encourage businesses to pursue projects involving technical uncertainty and experimentation, rather than simply purchasing and deploying proven technology.
“We are concerned by Meta’s apparent position that expenditures associated with its massive data-center buildout qualify for the research credit,” wrote the lawmakers. “The purchase and deployment of commercially available servers, networking equipment, electrical infrastructure, cooling equipment, and other proven technologies cannot be transformed into qualified research merely because they are installed at unprecedented scale or in new configurations.”
To qualify for the credit, research must meet a four-part test, including being technological in nature, addressing technical uncertainty, seeking to develop or improve a product or process, and involving a process of experimentation. Certain activities, including research conducted after commercial production begins and duplication of an existing product or process, are excluded. The lawmakers emphasized that the scale or configuration of a data center does not, by itself, establish that its construction and equipment costs qualify.
“Allowing ordinary data-center construction and deployment costs to qualify would significantly expand the research credit beyond its intended purpose and risk converting an incentive for technological experimentation into a subsidy for capital expenditures that companies would undertake in the ordinary course of business,” continued the lawmakers.
“The research credit is an important tool for promoting American innovation. Protecting its integrity requires ensuring that it rewards genuine research and experimentation rather than subsidizing routine capital investment,” concluded the lawmakers.
In addition to Reps. Panetta, Steube, Thompson, and DelBene, the letter was also signed by Reps. Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Donald Beyer (VA-08), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Sharice Davids (KS-03), Danny Davis (IL-07), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Jared Huffman (CA-02), John James (MI-10), Greg Landsman (OH-01), Kristen McDonald Rivet (MI-08), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Chris Pappas (NH-01), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Hillary Scholten (MI-03), Terri Sewell (AL-07), Victoria Spartz (IN-05), Lori Trahan (MA-03), and Nikema Williams (GA-05).
The full text of the letter is available here and below:
Dear Secretary Bessent:
In light of concerning reports that Meta Platforms, Inc. is seeking to claim the research credit under 26 U.S.C. § 41 for substantial expenditures associated with its data center buildout, we write as Members of Congress to reaffirm that the credit is intended to incentivize qualified research and experimentation, not subsidize the routine deployment of existing technology. We believe that the credit remains a critical support for American innovation, but that an overly expansive interpretation of qualifying expenditures risks undermining its purpose by subsidizing ordinary capital investment rather than encouraging genuinely novel research.
Congress created the research credit as part of the Economic Recovery Tax Act of 1981 in response to declining private-sector research and development investment and concerns about U.S. technological competitiveness. The credit was designed to encourage companies to undertake additional research and experimentation, not to subsidize ordinary capital investment or the deployment of established technology.
Internal Revenue Code Section 41 and Treasury Regulation 1.41-4 establish specific requirements for activities to constitute qualified research. Research must satisfy the IRS four-part test, which mandates the research must aim to develop or improve a product, process or technique, be technological in nature, eliminate uncertainty about capability, design, or methodology and importantly belong to a process of experimentation. A company must pinpoint the specific components of a project that are technically uncertain and prove it used scientific experiments to overcome that uncertainty.
These limitations are particularly important in distinguishing genuine research and experimentation from ordinary commercial activity. IRS guidance makes clear that research conducted after the beginning of commercial production and the duplication of an existing product or process do not qualify. Likewise, uncertainty about how best to configure or implement existing technology does not, alone, establish that a taxpayer has undertaken the process of experimentation required by Section 41. The IRS has repeatedly found that proven and commercially available equipment and technology is not eligible for the credit.
As a result, we are concerned by Meta’s apparent position that expenditures associated with its massive data-center buildout qualify for the research credit. The purchase and deployment of commercially available servers, networking equipment, electrical infrastructure, cooling equipment, and other proven technologies cannot be transformed into qualified research merely because they are installed at unprecedented scale or in new configurations.
Allowing ordinary data-center construction and deployment costs to qualify would significantly expand the research credit beyond its intended purpose and risk converting an incentive for technological experimentation into a subsidy for capital expenditures that companies would undertake in the ordinary course of business.
The research credit is an important tool for promoting American innovation. Protecting its integrity requires ensuring that it rewards genuine research and experimentation rather than subsidizing routine capital investment.
We appreciate your attention to this matter and look forward to your response.
###
title: Rep. Panetta Leads Bipartisan Letter Raising Concerns About Meta’s Use of Research Tax Credit for Data Centers

WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs processed a record-high 3.11 million disability compensation claims in fiscal year 2026, a testament to the Trump Administration’s commitment to ensuring Veterans can more quickly and conveniently access the benefits they’ve earned.
The 3,111,399 compensation claims VA processed in FY 2026 tops the prior record of 3,001,734 claims set in FY 2025. Until the second Trump Administration, VA had never processed more than 3 million claims per year.
VA’s focus on the timely processing of compensation claims has led to a dramatic reduction in the backlog of Veterans waiting for VA benefits. That backlog has been reduced by more than 70%, after it increased 24% under the Biden Administration.
Claims processing accuracy has improved despite an increased workload and is currently at 94% — the highest rate in two years. Additionally, VBA continues to grant more than 60% of the claims submitted by Veterans, and only about 3% of VBA’s decisions are appealed to the Board of Veterans’ Appeals.
“Under the leadership of President Trump, VA is making historic progress to better serve Veterans, and these record-breaking claims processing numbers prove it,” said VA Secretary Doug Collins. “Whether we’re lowering wait times, improving healthcare, or opening new VA facilities, we will continue to put Veterans first.”
These record-breaking claims processing numbers are one of many ways the Trump Administration is making VA work better for Veterans. Since Jan. 20, 2025, VA has:
- Reduced VA’s average disability claims processing time by 46% since Jan. 20, 2025.
- Eliminated the backlog of Veteran families waiting for VA healthcare.
- VA reduced paperwork by nearly two thirds for Veterans and survivors applying for VA benefits.
- Enrolled more than 300,000 new Veterans in VA healthcare in 2026.
- Opened 43 new VA healthcare facilities since Jan. 20, 2025, expanding healthcare access for Veterans around the country.
- Offered Veterans more than 3.4 million appointments outside of normal operating hours since Jan. 20, 2025, giving Veterans more timely and convenient options for care.
title: VA in FY 2026 processes the most claims ever

In the last year, TSA officers have been forced to work 88 days without on-time payment. Now, leadership has taken away their chairs.
Atlanta, GA – Today, Representative Lucy McBath (GA-06), is leading 37 of her House colleagues in urging TSA Administrator David P. Cummins support the well-being of TSA agents and the safety of the nation by reversing his decision to remove their chairs at document check stations in airports around the country. This letter is officially endorsed by AFGE, AFGE TSA Council 100, and AFGE TSA Local 554 in Atlanta. McBath, who was a flight attendant for 30 years before she came to Congress, represents many of the employees of Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International—America’s busiest airport.
“Transportation Security Officers, or TSOs, have an incredibly important job. They are the first line of defense in keeping Americans and their families safe during air travel,” the members write. “Since October of last year, officers at TSA have been forced to work 88 days without being paid on time. They have had to fight in court to protect their collective bargaining agreement from being unilaterally canceled and are now being told that they are not allowed to sit down while they perform their duties at checker stations. It is abundantly clear that these changes are intended to try to push officers out of their jobs with TSA, not to keep the American people safe or improve service.”
“This is about more than chairs,” the members continue. “This is about the respect that every person in the United States deserves at work and on the job. American workers are tired of being treated as expendable.”
“TSA officers have continued to show up and protect the traveling public through government shutdowns, delayed pay, and attacks on their collective bargaining rights. Removing chairs from document checker stations is yet another unnecessary hardship placed on an already strained workforce, and I commend Congresswoman McBath and her congressional colleagues for standing with our officers and demanding the dignity, respect, and working conditions they deserve,” said Aaron Barker Jr., President of AFGE Local 554.
In addition to Representative Lucy McBath, the letter is signed by Representatives Nanette Barragán, Salud Carbajal, André Carson, Troy Carter, Kathy Castor, Jasmine Crockett, Danny Davis, Mark DeSaulnier, Lois Frankel, Maxwell Frost, Robert Garcia, Sylvia Garcia, Al Green, Adelita Grijalva, Pablo Hernández, Val Hoyle, Glenn Ivey, Jonathan Jackson, Hank Johnson, Sydney Kamlager-Dove, Tim Kennedy, Raja Krishnamoorthi, Betty McCollum, Christian Menefee, Seth Moulton, Eleanor Holmes Norton, Emily Randall, Mary Gay Scanlon, Greg Stanton, Mark Takano, Bennie Thompson, Gabe Vasquez, Marc Veasey, Debbie Wasserman Schultz, Bonnie Watson Coleman, Nikema Williams, and Frederica Wilson.

MANCHESTER, NH – Today, U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon visited New Hampshire as part of her Returning Education to the States Tour.
Alongside New Hampshire Commissioner of Education Caitlin Davis, Secretary McMahon began her visit at the Manchester School of Technology, where she toured the specialized woodworking, cosmetology, and aviation programs to observe how the school equips students with high-demand technical skills. Then, she visited Southside Middle School, a public school serving students in grades 5 through 8, followed by a combined tour of the campuses at St. Joseph Regional Junior High School and Trinity High School. During her time in these classrooms, Secretary McMahon observed instruction across diverse subject areas, including fine arts, English, Spanish, pre-calculus, and early college personal finance.
To conclude her visit, Secretary McMahon hosted a roundtable with parents and students to discuss how state and federal education freedom initiatives impact families. The discussion also focused on how the federal Education Freedom Tax Credit – which New Hampshire has joined – will further multiply these opportunities in the Granite State.
“At every stop on the Returning Education to the States Tour, we are seeing firsthand the impactful work happening in classrooms and communities across the country,” said U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon. “New Hampshire is demonstrating how states can build a more responsive education system by integrating rigorous academics, technical training, and flexible learning choices. By coupling local innovations with new federal tools like the Education Freedom Tax Credit, we are empowering families to bridge the gap between traditional instruction and personalized models, ensuring more students have the resources to meet their full potential.”
Background:
On her Returning Education to the States Tour, Secretary McMahon is traveling to all 50 states to hear directly from teachers, parents, students, and community leaders about what is working in their communities and to compile a toolkit of best practices to share with states across the nation. Learn more about Secretary McMahon’s Returning Education to the States Tour here.
title: U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon Visits New Hampshire on Returning Education to the States Tour

ELKINS, WEST VIRGINIA — An Elkins, West Virginia woman has admitted to fraudulently collecting hundreds of thousands of dollars in COVID-related unemployment benefits for several individuals, U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey announced today.

Leigh Ann Rinehart, 54, pleaded guilty to bank fraud. According to court documents filed, Rinehart participated in a scheme to fraudulently obtain unemployment benefits during the COVID-19 pandemic. The scheme involved unnamed individuals applying for and obtaining unemployment benefits fraudulently in the names of multiple individuals across several states, including Nevada, California, New York and others. Once benefits were approved, Electronic Benefit Payment (EBP) debit cards were sent to Rinehart’s address in Elkins. Those EBP cards were loaded with benefits totaling more than $440,000 from these various states for individuals whose identity was fraudulently used to obtain the benefits, regardless of where they lived.

Rinehart received the cards, activated them, and used them to withdraw funds, purchase money orders, buy cryptocurrency or other items which she then sent to other individuals participating in the scheme or deposited into her own account. Investigators determined that none of the named claimants resided in West Virginia, and none authorized Rinehart to possess or use their unemployment benefits.

More than twenty-four EBP cards were sent to Rinehart’s residence from June 2020 through November 2022.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Jennifer Conklin is prosecuting the case. The Department of Homeland Security Office of Inspector General, Department of Labor Office of Inspector General, U.S. Postal Inspection Service and Workforce West Virginia investigated.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

U.S. Magistrate Judge Michael John Aloi presided.
title: Elkins Woman Admits to More Than $400,000 in COVID Fraud

text:
WASHINGTON — Project Agincourt as a pathway to a four-star-led Autonomous Warfare Command has always been in the cards, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth said at the 2026 Association of the United States Army annual meeting and exposition.
Last month, Hegseth signed a memorandum detailing the creation of the short-term Project Agincourt, which is charged with laying the groundwork for creating the Autonomous Warfare Command, a new, functional combatant command that will lead the joint force in unmanned autonomous warfare.
"Project Agincourt is the end state of something we focused on since Day 1," Hegseth told Owen West, the chief executive officer of the Pentagon's Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager for Unmanned Systems, which leads the project.
"We started with drone dominance almost the minute we got here; [the] president put out an executive order," Hegseth said. "We got $1 billion of funding on drone dominance, which we put straight into the hands of operators out into the field."
The department plans to field hundreds of thousands of one-way attack systems this year, Hegseth told the audience. In coming years, he said, that'll be in the millions.
Drones have been around for a long time, but they haven't become inexpensive or proliferated across the force, Hegseth said. That's partly due to the Pentagon's bureaucracy — something that will change with Project Agincourt and, eventually, the Autonomous Warfare Command. He added that buy-in from the military services and combatant commands plays a critical role in making that happen.
"These services are not fighting us on that concept; they believe in it," Hegseth said.
The Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps and Space Force are all aiming toward autonomous warfare, and so are the combatant commands. The secretary cited U.S. Southern Command's recently established autonomous warfare unit, as well as U.S. Central Command's autonomous surface systems, which rescued two downed Apache pilots off the coast of Oman in June.
To advance the adoption of autonomous systems, Hegseth said, the War Department has made significant progress in modernizing the acquisition process and incentivizing industry partners.
However, he said widespread adoption and mastery of autonomous systems will come from the warfighters using those systems and with experts there to iterate on what's happening to make them better — both of which are expected to happen with the Autonomous Warfare Command.
"This Autowarcom is what's going to create that multidomain, that domain synthesis that you need so that, from space to what we're doing sub-sea in autonomy, is able to work together in a contested environment," Hegseth said.
Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle said just yesterday that the Army announced the creation of the Army's Futures and Autonomous Systems Command.
"This is our way to make sure that we take all of the great work that's been happening with the resources that we have today, and we centralize it," he said. "We're pushing autonomy down into our units, but when it comes to having and making sure that the left hand in the Army knows what the right hand of the Army is doing, this happens at Fascom; then Fascom feeds up into Autowarcom."
Telle said Fascom will work with the other services to create scale for purchasing power and share best practices on autonomy.
Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao said his service is now increasing its use of and investment in autonomous systems.
"In the Strait of Hormuz, we used the Corsair ... to recover two Apache helicopter pilots," Cao said. "Then, we also used the unmanned underwater vehicles to demine that area."
That kind of work, Cao said, can't be done in a contested area unless it's done using unmanned underwater vehicles. The Navy is now deploying with even more unmanned systems.
"The [Theodore] Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group just deployed on Oct. 8 with a medium-sized unmanned surface vessel," he said. "This is the first carrier strike group to ever deploy with a large-size unmanned surface vessel — and this is a force multiplier."
Cao said unmanned vessels are easier to build and will change the nature of surface warfare because they don't need the complex systems required to sustain personnel on board.
The Air Force has always been dominated by manned aircraft, and Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink said it will continue to be so. However, he said unmanned systems will play a big part of the Air Force playbook now, too.
"There's no question though that there's a shift coming," Meink said. "It's adaptability, scalability and affordability; the only way we're going to meet the threat is with autonomous systems."
Affordability is an important consideration for the Air Force, Meink said, adding that autonomy may be cheaper than manned systems.
"We've got to make sure this stuff is affordable," he said. "We've got to make sure we're buying it efficiently. And depending on how you do the comparisons, we're talking five to 10 times cheaper to field some combat power with these autonomous systems compared to not."
Meink noted that the Air Force is already integrating autonomous fighters into experimental operations units out at Creech Air Force Base, Nevada.
"[It took] from a year from when they first flew to when we are integrating them into experimental ops units — that's unheard of, and it only took two years to build the first one," he added.
With those systems, Meink said, the Air Force is focused on rapid production, scalability and lowering costs.
title: Hegseth: Autonomous Warfare Command has always been end state

Ahead of Elections, Ramirez, Immigration Advocates Introduce a People-Centered Vision for Immigration Reform
Congress last acted on immigration reform 40 years ago, when President Ronald Reagan signed the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986, which created pathways to citizenship for approximately 2.7 million immigrants.
Chicago, IL – Today, Congresswoman Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Ranking Member of a Committee on Homeland Security Subcommittee, immigration advocates, and community members unveiled the People’s Vision for Immigration Reform, a resolution outlining policy priorities to preserve and expand pathways to citizenship. As the elections approaches and the House of Representatives prepares for the 120th Congress, the resolution calls on the House of Representatives to pass real protections for immigrant communities.
The resolution calls on Congress to transform our immigration system and advance humane immigration reform with:
- Pathways to citizenship for the millions of undocumented, long-term residents of the United States who are our family members, friends and neighbors;
- Humanitarian protections that welcome with dignity those who are seeking safety and asylum in the United States, upholding our domestic and international legal obligations to provide refuge to those in need; and
- Expanded legal pathways for family and employment immigration, recognizing that family unity and strengthened protections for all workers in the United States are foundations of thriving communities for all.
“For years, administration after administration, Congress after Congress, has promised relief and has asked our communities to wait for the ‘right time,’ for the ‘politically convenient time,’” said Congresswoman Ramirez. “So today, we announced the People’s Vision for Immigration Reform – a resolution that reaffirms the commitment of Members of Congress to act in defense of our immigrant communities and preserve and expand pathways to citizenship. Now is the time to build a system that honors the contributions of our immigrant neighbors. No more excuses or peros.”
The resolution’s original cosponsors include Representatives Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Jesus “Chuy” Garcia (IL-04), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-00), Yvette D. Clarke (NY-09), Analilia Mejia (NJ-11), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Sylvia R. Garcia (TX-29), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Federica S. Wilson (FL-24), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Melanie Stansbury (NM-01), Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Emily Randall (WA-06), Judy Chu (CA-28), Adelita S. Grijalva (AZ-07), and Al Green (TX-09).
“Immigrants have bound our communities together, continue to contribute to our economy, and embody everything that Americans are made of and striving to be. All of which they do while asking nothing in return but the opportunity to reach for and obtain the American Dream,” said Congresswoman Yvette Clarke. “The 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States must not be only the opportunity to reflect on how far we have come; it must be an obligation to remember the terrible price that we pay to reach here. The People’s Vision for Immigration Reform is in large part the only future for this nation worth fighting for.”
“It’s time to send out a strong vision of where we need to be. We have spent an awful lot of time in Washington talking about immigration enforcement this year, but not nearly enough time talking about how we fix the system that has been broken for decades,” said Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia. “We need an immigration system that gives people a fair chance. We can start by making progress now. That’s why I’m leading the discharge petition of the American Dream and Promise Act; we are just one signature away from getting a forced vote. We need to get serious about real reform, not another round of empty promises.”
The bill is endorsed by a coalition of more than 60 national and and local organizations, including Immigration Law Center (NILC), Fair Immigration Reform Movement (FIRM) and FIRM Action, National Immigrant Justice Center (NIJC), League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC), Haitian Bridge Alliance, United We Dream (UWD), Refugees International, National Partnership for New Americans (NPNA), Immigrant Legal Resource Center (ILRC), Center for Law and Social Policy (CLASP), Human Rights First, Bend the Arc: Jewish Action, Justice in Motion, Indivisible, Service Employees International Union (SEIU), National Health Care for the Homeless Council, United Parent Leaders Action Network (UPLAN), Children's Rights, Unitarian Universalists for Social Justice, Community Change Action, Illinois Coalition for Immigrant and Refugee Rights (ICIRR) and ICIRR Action, CAIR Chicago, Grassroots Collaborative, Warehouse Workers for Justice, National Korean American Service and Education Consortium (NAKASEC), Indivisible Chicago Alliance, Hana Center, Here to Stay Community Land Trust, Illinois Unidos, PASO, Organized Communities Against Deportation (OCAD), Massachusetts Immigrant and Refugee Advocacy Coalition, Jewish Council on Urban Affairs (JCUA), Colorado Immigrant Rights Coalition (CIRC), Popular Democracy, Florida Immigrant Coalition (FLIC), SIREN, Iowa Migrant Movement for Justice, Maine People's Alliance, We are CASA, Workers Defense Action Fund, Make the Road States, Voces de la Frontera, Make the Road New York, Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights (CHIRLA), Council of Mexican Federations in North America (COFEM), Sunflower Community Action, East Bay Sanctuary Covenant (EBSC), Federación de Clubes Michoacanos en Illinois (FEDECMI), Nebraska Appleseed, and Pineros Y Campesinos Unidos Del Noroeste (PCUN).
“Over the last 40 years we’ve seen the consequences, not only the inability of Congress to prioritize legislation, but of the overreach of the Trump administration that has taken a sledgehammer to refugee admissions, temporary protected status, health care and food access and the basic simple notion that all people in this country deserve due process under the law,” said Lawrence Benito, ICIRR Executive Director. “We know we need permanent solutions, not chaos and fear. We’re here today to recommit to dignity and respect for all through legalization and keeping families together.”
“Let me be clear: Our economy works because of workers, and for generations, immigrant workers have poured their sweat, their strength, and their labor into building this country. Working families deserve to go to work, provide for their families, and return home safely without fear of being detained or disappeared,” Laura Garza, Executive Director at Arise Chicago. “Now is the time to demand real protections for communities. It’s time to expand pathways to citizenship and ensure all working families can live and work with dignity and safety. As communities mobilize across the country, we stand together in our power to change our country’s direction.”
“Immigrants deserve a system that provides dignity, fairness, and a real opportunity for a life in this country. Congress must do its job to defend our neighbors by creating viable pathways. Otherwise, the executive branch will be able to continue to sow chaos in our communities, return refugees to danger, and trample our Constitution,” said Keren Zwick, Executive Director at the National Immigrant Justice Center (NIJC). “NIJC stands ready to advance lasting solutions, even as we continue to fight the problems this administration created.”
“At PASO, we see the resilience of our communities, but resilience should never mean having to live in fear. Instead of being supported, our communities are increasingly being targeted because of their immigration status. But we have resisted, organized, advocated, and continue doing the work to prepare families for citizenship and help them navigate the immigration system. We have done our part, and now the federal government must do theirs. Because the truth is, no matter how much we prepare our communities, if the federal government fails to create real pathways to citizenship, our families will continue to face barriers,” Marien Casillas Pabellon, PASO Executive Director.
“While ICE and DHS terrorize our communities and attack and deport our neighbors, Congress has not acted. While most Americans support creating and ensuring legal pathways to citizenship for immigrants, Congress has done nothing. Their silence enables this administration's campaign of terror against immigrants and their families. Today, as voters, we must demand that our elected representatives take action to create pathways to citizenship and legal status and protect immigrants and their families from abuse by our government,” said Kathy Tholin with Indivisible Chicago.
“Asians are the fastest-growing racial group in the US, and 1 out of 7 undocumented immigrants is Asian. We are longstanding generations, mixed-status families, and new Americans who call this country home. We are all affected by the militarized violence, immigration backlogs, unaffordable costs, and attacks by this President and some Congress members against anyone they think doesn’t belong,” said Danae Kovac, HANA Center Executive Director. “Immigration affects all of us, and let me be clear: our country needs pathways to citizenship. HANA Center will continue to fight alongside Congresswoman Ramirez for Citizenship for All, not only for a pathway to citizenship, but also for the healthcare, education, climate justice, and more that we all need and deserve. Together, we, the people, can create an America where every person belongs and thrives.”
“It is long past time to lift up families and embrace the worth of each of our neighbors. It is time to reject the politics of fear and division that have marked too much of the discussion around immigration in recent years,” said Ed Yohnka, ACLU Illinois Director of Communications and Public Policy. “In recent months, we have seen how years of rhetoric meant to stall meaningful immigration reform can be turned to justify a military-style invasion of our communities and cause too many hard-working people to live in fear and isolation. Immigration policy does not have to be this way. Immigration policy can be based on a commitment to family unification, a commitment to fairness and due process, and a recognition of the dignity and worth that people from other countries and other cultures bring to the United States. 
“As a recently naturalized citizen, I have a message to those like me who can now exercise that power. The power of our vote. Let’s show our humanity in how we treat our neighbors, but also let’s show solidarity at the ballot box,” Fasika Alem, United African Organization (UAO) Programs Director. “Elections matter. Make a plan and vote.”
“Our church is home to Indigenous people and to immigrants, old and new. People without documents worship in our assemblies and lead our ministries. Scripture commands: ‘Love the stranger as yourself, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.’ For decades, our church has urged compassionate ways for longtime undocumented neighbors to gain legal status,” said Bishop Erik Christensen of the Metropolitan Chicago Synod of the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America. “Forty years ago, Congress opened a path to citizenship and those who received status in time became citizens, homeowners, and neighbors. Now is the time to finish that work.
"As a Haitian immigrant, experiencing the agonizing pain and fear of the Haitian community every day who have lost TPS, I particularly welcome the resolution, because it brings to light all the changes needed in our immigration system to ensure the safety of our immigrant friends and family members who are here and deserve justice and dignity,” said Tessa Petit, Florida Immigrant Coalition Executive Director and Co-Chair of FIRM. “It is time for immigrants to no longer be treated as political pawns and sub-creatures, and this resolution will engage Congress to put an end to the abuse of our communities.”
“1 of every 4 ICE arrests happen in Texas. In just over three months, ICE shot and killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston, shot Wilber Rafael Garces Perez in Austin, hospitalized Miguel Parra-Hernandez after striking him with an ICE vehicle in Houston, and has separated countless of families,” said Lizeth Chacon, Workers Defense Executive Director. “Immigrant workers and their families strengthen and build our state – Texas is their home, and for many it has been for more than 30 years. It's time for Congress to act, for there to be an end to ICE violence and a real pathway to citizenship for all immigrant workers and their families.”
“For 25 years, my mother and I were both undocumented. We were able to adjust to legal permanent residency because we qualified for a U visa, something that only undocumented immigrants who are victims of a violent crime could apply for. There are over 12 million undocumented immigrants in the United States who have no pathway to citizenship and I sure wish not a single one ever needs to apply to a U visa,” said Jose-Arnulfo Cabrera, National Campaigns and Congressional Affairs Deputy Director, Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights (CHIRLA). “But that is how broken our immigration system is and why Congresswoman Ramirez’s resolution is quite important today.”
The violence of the Department of Homeland Security under the Trump administration has only served to underscore citizenship's importance. Last week, a five year old child had to watch his father get shot by agents of our government. He is only the latest child to be failed by the unimaginable cruelty of the DHS's at-all-costs approach to mass deportations,” said Ben D’Avanzo, National Immigration Law Center. “But he was also failed by our completely broken immigration system that has allowed families to go without health care, be abused by their employers, and stripped of longtime protections. This resolution represents the right pathway, one that upholds our core values and refuses to pit immigrant communities against each other.”
“LULAC is proud to support Congresswoman Ramirez’s resolution to protect immigrant families, defend workers, and create pathways to citizenship. As America celebrates 250 years of independence, we should remember who helped build this country,” said Dr. Ray Serrano, National Director of Research & Policy, League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC). “Congress needs to act. Keep families together. Protect workers. Give people a fair chance at citizenship. Our families helped build this country. We deserve a place in its future.”

Background:
40 years ago, Congress passed the Immigration Reform and Control Act, creating a pathway to citizenship for approximately 2.7 million immigrants. Today, the American people are overwhelmingly in support of a pathway to citizenship, the popularity of which has grown because of the brutality we have witnessed over the last 2 years.
For more than a year, IL-03 has been targeted, terrorized, and attacked by DHS with zero accountability. Congresswoman Ramirez has led the call for a pathway to citizenship for all and accountability from DHS.
Ramirez co-leads Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia’s Dream and Promise Act and became the second signature on the discharge petition to force a vote on the legislation. The discharge petition currently has 217 signatures of the 218 needed for a vote.

title: Ahead of Elections, Ramirez, Immigration Advocates Introduce a People-Centered Vision for Immigration Reform

Trump’s Transportation Department Celebrates $550 Million Investment to Build New Amtrak Service in the Tar Heel State
Funds will be used to increase safety and decrease travel time between Raleigh and Richmond
RALEIGH, NC – The U.S. Transportation Department’s Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) today joined the North Carolina Department of Transportation (NCDOT) to celebrate obligating $550 million in federal funding to develop the new S-Line passenger rail route between Raleigh, North Carolina, and Richmond, Virginia. The long-awaited line will reduce travel time by up to 90 minutes, increase the number of trips, and improve reliability.
The S-Line announcement comes on the heels of Secretary Duffy’s $5.3 billion “Golden Age of Rail” nationwide grant package, which included an additional $300 million in funding to fix rail crossings as part of the NCDOT’s Piedmont Corridor Safety Program between Raleigh and Charlotte.
Roughly $2 billion of this grant package is funding Secretary Duffy saved the American people by canceling Gavin Newsom’s disastrous high-speed train to nowhere.
The federal investments into North Carolina rail include:
- $550 million for the future S-Line to make critical track repairs and upgrades on existing track with plans for additional funds to follow pending project success.
- $300 million for the existing Piedmont Corridor to close 9 at-grade rail crossings, construct 5 grade separations, and improve trespassing prevention infrastructure along the entire corridor.
“From launching the new Acela and Airo trains to overhauling New York Penn Station to today’s announcement in Raleigh, the Trump Administration is committed to investing in Amtrak to make passenger rail in America great again,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “Our additional rail safety investments are also an important reminder of the tangible difference we can make when we defund boondoggles like California’s train to nowhere and instead direct the funds to protect pedestrians, drivers, and riders in the Tar Heel State."
“This milestone is a testament to the strong partnership between the FRA, Amtrak, and NCDOT in advancing the S-Line and the earlier announced Piedmont Line corridors,” said FRA Administrator David Fink. “Through close collaboration, we are delivering vital investments that will modernize passenger rail and create a new Golden Age of Rail for the people of North Carolina.”
Additional Information:
When complete, the Raleigh-to-Richmond Passenger Rail Line is anticipated to save rail travelers 90 minutes when traveling between the two cities and will increase corridor bandwidth, allowing for more passenger and freight trips each day.
FRA’s $300 million investment in the Piedmont Corridor Safety Program is a key pillar of Secretary Duffy’s “Golden Age of Rail” package announced in August. Roughly $2 billion of this grant package is funding Secretary Duffy saved the American people by canceling Gavin Newsom’s disastrous high-speed train to nowhere.
title: Trump’s Transportation Department Celebrates $550 Million Investment to Build New Amtrak Service in the Tar Heel State

PORTLAND, Maine : — The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Maine is proud to join the U.S. Department of Justice, the Office on Violence Against Women (OVW), Tribal Nations, and communities across the country in observing Domestic Violence Awareness Month (DVAM) this October. We reaffirm our dedication to using every available resource and building strategic partnerships with local law enforcement, fellow prosecutors, and victim service organizations to ensure justice, safety, and healing for victims.

“Domestic violence is a complex and pervasive issue that affects individuals across economic, racial, gender, religious and societal lines,” said U.S. Attorney Andrew B. Benson. “Addressing the issue requires a multi-faceted approach focused on prevention, outreach, education, and, particularly with respect our office, consequences for perpetrators.”

Each year, DVAM gives us an opportunity to focus on our collective responsibility to address domestic violence and emphasize the importance of collective action. In fiscal years 2025 and 2026, OVW granted funding to multiple local organizations including the Maine Department of Public Safety, the Maine Coalition to End Domestic Violence, the Maine Department of Health and Human Services, Partners for Peace, the Maine Coalition Against Sexual Assault, Disability Rights Maine, the Next Stop Domestic Violence Project, Safe Voices, the Mi’Kmaq Nation, the Houlton Band of Maliseet Indians, the Penobscot Indian Nation, the Family Violence Project, New Hope for Women, and Pine Tree Legal Assistance.

By raising awareness about domestic violence during DVAM, we can bring everyone together to end the abuse. We encourage all who live in our jurisdiction to learn more about domestic violence and take meaningful action to support friends, family, co-workers, and neighbors who may be affected. Victims deserve safety, dignity, and justice. By understanding the signs of abuse and connecting victims to resources, we can all play a role in creating safer communities.

We are committed to prosecuting those who violate federal laws, collaborating with local law enforcement and prosecutors, and ensuring victims have access to the resources they need. Together, we can bring hope to those in need and build a future free from domestic violence. For more information on domestic violence or to access resources, please visit the Maine Coalition to End Domestic Violence website at mcedv.org.

The Department of Justice funds essential victim services through its grantmaking. Grantees of OVW and the Department’s Office for Victims of Crime (OVC) run programs that support victims in the aftermath of domestic violence. There is help available, including the National Domestic Violence Hotline, 1-800-799-SAFE (7233), and the StrongHearts Native Helpline, 1-844-7NATIVE (762-8483). In addition, OVW’s Resources for Victims and Survivors webpage lists national hotlines as well as state, territorial, and Tribal domestic violence and sexual assault coalitions that can direct victims to local resources and services, as well as opportunities to get involved.

title: U.S. ATTORNEY’S OFFICE FOR THE DISTRICT OF MAINE OBSERVES DOMESTIC VIOLENCE AWARENESS MONTH

United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, announced today that JOSHUA WANDER, the founder and former CEO of 777 Partners, a Miami-based investment firm, pled guilty to wire fraud and securities fraud in connection with a scheme to defraud the lenders and investors of 777 Partners. As part of his plea, WANDER agreed to forfeit at least $500,000,000 in proceeds from his illegal scheme. WANDER pled guilty today before U.S. District Judge J. Paul Oetken.

“This Office, together with our law enforcement partners, will continue to protect investors and lenders and to ensure that those who threaten our financial markets are held accountable,” said U.S Attorney Jamie McDonald. “As he has now admitted, Josh Wander used his company, 777 Partners, to steal hundreds of millions of dollars from private creditors and investors. Wander double-pledged assets, pledged fictitious assets, lied about the financial condition of his company, and even falsified bank statements, all to gain access to his victims’ funds. He then put those funds to uses that his lenders never permitted, including footing the bill for 777’s collection of professional soccer teams. Whether perpetrated in the private or public markets, such brazen conduct undermines the integrity of our financial system and will not be tolerated.”

As alleged in the Indictment and other public filings in this case:

WANDER, the co-founder and former CEO of 777 Partners, a private investment firm, orchestrated a multi-year scheme to defraud 777 Partners’ lenders and investors of more than $500,000,000. 777 Partners’ initial and primary business model was to underwrite and finance structured settlements. Over time, WANDER began investing capital in new sectors, including airlines and professional sports teams. 777 Partners lacked the funds to pay for these new acquisitions, and WANDER directed that restricted funds from 777 Partners’ lenders in its structured settlement business be used to cover the firm’s acquisitions and expenses. To steal these funds from lenders, WANDER pledged to his lenders hundreds of millions of dollars of structured settlement assets that 777 Partners had never purchased or had previously pledged to other lenders. To conceal the fraud, WANDER directed employees to digitally alter bank account statements to reflects millions of dollars in cash on hand that the firm did not have.

In 2021 and 2022, WANDER raised more than $200 million in outside investments in 777 Partners through the sale of preferred equity interests in 777 Partners and an affiliated entity. WANDER misrepresented the financial condition of the firm in soliciting these investments. In addition, in March 2022, WANDER solicited a $20 million loan from a lender. WANDER provided the lender with dozens of doctored bank account statements to conceal that WANDER had misappropriated the funds, spending millions of dollars of options trades.

By March 2023, WANDER’s scheme began to unravel. One of the firm’s lenders confronted WANDER about allegations of double-pledged assets, and WANDER falsely claimed there had been an error caused by 777 Partners’ antiquated computer system. A few days later, WANDER again falsely assured the lender, among other things, that the double-pledging had been inadvertent. In 2024, WANDER resigned as CEO.

* * *

WANDER, 45, of Florida, pled guilty to one count of wire fraud and securities fraud, each of which carries a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison.

The maximum potential sentence in this case is prescribed by Congress and provided here for informational purposes only, as any sentencing of the defendant will be determined by the judge. WANDER is scheduled to be sentenced by U.S. District Judge Oetken on March 1, 2027.

Mr. McDonald praised the outstanding work of the Federal Bureau of Investigation and Homeland Security Investigations. Mr. McDonald also expressed appreciation for the assistance of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

This case is being handled by the Office’s Securities and Commodities Fraud Task Force. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Thomas S. Burnett, Marguerite B. Colson, Sarah Mortazavi, and Alexandra N. Rothman are in charge of the prosecution.
title: Founder And Former Ceo Of 777 Partners Pleads Guilty To $500 Million Fraud Scheme

BILLINGS – Two Mexican citizens who illegally reentered the U.S. after having been previously removed at least once were sentenced this week, First Assistant U.S. Attorney Mark Steger Smith said.

Armando Moreno-Moya, 32, and Agustin Balderas-Jimenez, 32, who both pleaded guilty in September 2026 to illegally reentering the United States, were jailed for just over two months and now will be deported.

U.S. District Judge Kathleen S. Lane presided over Moreno-Moya's sentencing; U.S. District Judge Susan P. Watters presided over Balderas-Jimenez's.

The government alleged in court documents that Moreno-Moya and Balderas-Jimenez were pulled over by law enforcement on Aug. 4, 2026, after Montana Highway Patrol troopers flagged the vehicle for having expired registration. Upon checking identification documents of both men, law enforcement learned they were Mexican citizens and in the country without the proper documentation. Moreno-Moya previously had been removed from the U.S. in March 2020; Balderas-Jimenez had been removed in July 2022.

The U.S. Attorney’s Office prosecuted the case. The U.S. Customs and Border Protection conducted the investigation.
title: 2 Mexican men jailed for illegally reentering U.S.
