The Army's XM-30, previously known as the Optionally Manned Fighting Vehicle (OMFV), is being designed to replace the M-2 Bradley Infantry Fighting Vehicle (see Figure 1 for an XM-30 conceptual example). Optionally manned means the OMFV is to have the capability to conduct remotely controlled operations while a crew is not in the vehicle. The M-2 Bradley, in service since 1981, transports infantry on the battlefield, provides fire support to dismounted troops, and can destroy enemy fighting vehicles. Updated numerous times since its introduction, the M-2 Bradley is widely considered to have reached the technological limits of its capacity to accommodate new electronics, armor, and defensive systems.
Acknowledging the M-2's limitations, the Army is interested in adopting a fuel-efficient hybrid-electric drive to accommodate silent running and watch and to power new electronic warfare systems, counter uncrewed aerial systems defenses, and active protection and mission command systems. The Army also seeks to upgrade the M-2 Bradley's 25mm main gun to 50mm and to incorporate loitering munitions launchers to enhance lethality.
Two past efforts to replace the M-2 Bradley—the Future Combat System (FCS) Program and the Ground Combat Vehicle (GCV) Program—were cancelled for programmatic and cost-associated reasons. On June 26, 2023, on the completion of the initial digital design phase, the Army redesignated the OMFV as the XM-30 Mechanized Infantry Combat Vehicle.
According to the 2024 Department of Defense (DOD) FY2025 Program Acquisition Cost by Weapon System (DOD is "using a secondary Department of War designation," under Executive Order 14347 of September 5, 2025),
[t]he XM-30 Combat Vehicle (previously OMFV), as part of an Armored Brigade Combat Team (ABCT), will replace the Bradley Infantry Fighting Vehicle to provide the capabilities required to defeat a future near-peer competitor's force. The XM-30 is an optionally manned platform that maneuvers Soldiers to a point of positional advantage to engage in close combat and deliver decisive lethality during the execution of combined arms maneuver. It is designed to operate with and may operate without a crew and Soldiers under armor based on the commander's decision.
The XM-30 began as a Middle Tier of Acquisition (MTA) rapid prototyping program. The XM-30 is to be designed from the onset as a Modular Open Systems Architected (MOSA) platform based on an Army-defined and -owned open standard. As technology and software evolve, MOSA could facilitate rapid XM-30 modernization at a reduced cost. XM-30 open architecture could also offer more opportunities for industry competition and innovation for future XM-30 upgrades. The Army is conducting a five-phase XM-30 acquisition approach:
The Army announced the award of five firm-fixed price contracts for XM-30 Phase 2 Concept Design using full and open competitive procedures on July 23, 2021. The contracts were awarded to Point Blank Enterprises, Inc. (Miami Lakes, FL); Oshkosh Defense, LLC (Oshkosh, WI); BAE Systems Land and Armaments L.P. (Sterling Heights, MI); General Dynamics Land Systems (GDLS), Inc. (Sterling Heights, MI); and American Rheinmetall Vehicles, LLC (Sterling Heights, MI). The total award value for all five contracts was approximately $299.4 million. In this phase, competing firms were asked to develop digital designs.
On June 26, 2023, the Army announced
the award of two firm-fixed price contracts for the Optionally Manned Fighting Vehicle [XM-30] Phase III and IV Detailed Design and Prototype Build and Testing phases, using full and open competitive procedures. The contracts were awarded to General Dynamics Land Systems Inc. [GDLS] (Sterling Heights, Michigan) and American Rheinmetall Vehicles LLC (Sterling Heights, Michigan). The total award value for both contracts is approximately $1.6 billion.
Reportedly, GDLS and American Rheinmetall completed their PDR in August 2024, and development of physical prototypes was planned to begin after a CDR. According to Defense News,
[p]rototypes will take 18 to 20 months to construct after the critical design reviews wrap up. Once prototypes are delivered, the Army will move into a test and evaluation phase with both competitors before deciding on a winner in [FY]2027. The first vehicles are expected to be fielded in [FY]2029.
In June 2025, the U.S. Army reportedly approved Milestone B for the XM-30 program, advancing it to the engineering manufacturing development phase after both competitors completed CDRs. In February 2026, Army leadership reportedly opted not to sign documentation finalizing the Milestone B decision and transition to a Major Capability Acquisition (MCA) pathway to avoid locking the service into a specific design or a slow acquisition path, effectively pausing formal program transition and prompting a reevaluation of the program's approach.
According to the February 2026 report, the then Chief of Staff of the Army General Randy George and then Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll decided not to sign off on the Milestone B decision "to leave the door open to a major reworking of the XM-30 Mechanized Infantry Combat Vehicle program." Reportedly, regarding the pause, an Army spokesman stated the following:
"We are actively assessing multiple, competing designs for the XM-30 to foster a truly competitive environment.… We continue to look for partners who can deliver cutting-edge solutions now, not decades from now."
According to Army Budget documents, the Army is requesting $547 million in procurement funding for 19 prototype vehicles for evaluation. The Army notes that prime contractors have yet to be identified, but award decisions for the 19 vehicles will be based on contractor performance during testing and operational evaluations.
Reportedly, the 1st Cavalry Division at Fort Hood in Texas is to be the first unit to receive new prototypes of the XM-30 this fall. Reportedly,
[t]he Army's largest division will take on two platoons of the XM30, designed to replace the Bradley Fighting Vehicle, and one platoon of M1E3 Abrams tanks by the end of the year. From there, soldiers will be "shooting, moving and communicating" at the National Training Center [NTC] at Fort Irwin, CA, through March [2027].
The Army Test and Evaluation Command (ATEC) reportedly is to "work in conjunction with the division to monitor the assessments from 1st Cavalry soldiers, who will provide feedback to engineers for 'minor adjustments.'"
Reportedly, GDLS delivered its first prototype, the Wolf, at the end of August 2026, and American Rheinmetall delivered its first prototype, known as the Lynx, on September 1, 2026, to support Fort Hood operational testing scheduled for fall 2026.
Reportedly, "because the Milestone B didn't happen the way it had been anticipated previously," the XM-30 program will now adopt an MTA rapid prototyping pathway. According to Army officials, "MTA's help cut costs and timelines for new programs, allowing acquisition organizations develop and deliver high need capabilities to the Army faster than an MCA." Under the XM-30 MTA pathway, down selection to a single vendor is expected in late spring or June 2027.
Potential oversight issues could include the following:
With General George's retirement in April 2026 and Secretary Driscoll's reported resignation on August 31, 2026, the Army is presently without Senate-confirmed senior leadership. At some point in the future, a new Secretary of the Army and Chief of Staff of the Army are likely to be nominated for confirmation. Once confirmed, a new Secretary of the Army and Chief of Staff could have differing views on the requirements for a Bradley replacement, the current XM-30 program, and Army modernization priorities altogether. Once new Army leadership is confirmed, Congress might decide to seek clarification from the Army on its views on the future of the XM-30 program.
While the Army has stated that the XM-30 is to have an organic active protection system (APS) that can detect, track, and neutralize anti-tank threats by means of kinetic and passive countermeasures, it is not clear if the XM-30 also will have an organic C-UAS capability. Some have suggested that UAS, loitering munitions, and one-way attack drones could make armored fighting vehicles (AFVs) obsolete; others contend new technologies are needed to improve AFV survivability against UAS and other aerial systems. Congress might decide to examine the Army's approach to providing organic protection to the XM-30 against aerial threats.
title: The Army’s XM-30 Mechanized Infantry Combat Vehicle

DEA New York Task Force Division Announces Two New York Men Indicted For Fentanyl Distribution Conspiracy That Involved the On-Campus Rape and Death of One College Student and Near-Death of Another
Special Agent in Charge of the New York Task Force Division of the Drug Enforcement Administration (“DEA”), Christopher Roberts, United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, and Commissioner of the New York City Police Department (“NYPD”) Jessica S. Tisch, announced today the unsealing of a three-count superseding Indictment charging MOISES FREIRE and BRIAN PERALTA CABRERA with participating in a fentanyl distribution conspiracy that resulted in the fatal poisoning of one college student (“Victim-1”) and the near-fatal poisoning of another college student (“Victim-2”) in a college residence hall in Manhattan, New York this past March. The Indictment further alleges that after rendering both women unconscious through fentanyl exposure, FREIRE raped Victim-1, who never regained consciousness and later died. FREIRE is also charged with distributing fentanyl with the intent to commit a violent crime, specifically, rape.
“The allegations in this case are beyond disturbing and include a cruel deception and unimaginable assault. Two young college students, with their entire futures ahead of them, were allegedly deceived into taking fentanyl disguised as cocaine, leaving one dead and the other fighting for her life,” said DEA New York Task Force Division Special Agent in Charge Christopher Roberts. “Even more horrifying is the allegation that one of these young women was sexually assaulted while unconscious and defenseless. College should be a place where young people can learn, grow, and pursue their dreams, not a place where predators exploit their vulnerability. Every student deserves to feel safe, whether walking across campus, sitting in a classroom, or inside their own dorm room. The DEA New York Task Force Division, alongside the NYPD, and our prosecutorial partners, will not stand idle while individuals’ prey on young people, poison our communities, and attempt to escape accountability. Those days are over.”
“This case alleges not only the deadly distribution of fentanyl to two young women but also the sexual assault of a victim rendered defenseless by that poisoning,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “This Office remains committed to protecting college communities against the extraordinary danger posed by those who weaponize narcotics to exploit vulnerable victims. We will work tirelessly to hold accountable those who endanger young people living and learning on our campuses.”
“Moises Freire and Brian Peralta Cabrera’s actions were truly unconscionable,” said NYPD Commissioner Jessica S. Tisch. “As alleged in the indictment, the two defendants supplied the fentanyl that killed one young woman and nearly killed another. Rather than immediately seek help, Freire allegedly first raped the incapacitated victim who died and then lied to first responders. These actions are as sick and twisted as they come, and I thank our investigators, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York, and law enforcement partners for their work to hold these predators accountable.”
As alleged in the Indictment and statements made in Court:
From at least February 2026 through March 2026, FREIRE and PERALTA CABRERA conspired to distribute fentanyl. After FREIRE told PERALTA CABRERA that FREIRE wanted to distribute narcotics to the Victims that would “last the entire night,” and that if PERALTA CABRERA could provide drugs that were strong enough, the Victims would get addicted, FREIRE went on to describe that scenario as a “win win situation.” Knowing that FREIRE intended to distribute the drugs to at least the Victims, PERALTA CABRERA subsequently provided fentanyl to FREIRE.
On March 18, 2026, FREIRE brought that fentanyl to the undergraduate residence hall where the Victims were living while attending college in Manhattan. FREIRE falsely claimed that the drug did not contain fentanyl and was “pure cocaine,” even though he had previously described the substance as “fake” and “poison.”
After FREIRE encouraged the victims to ingest the substance, both women lost consciousness almost immediately. FREIRE himself did not ingest the drug that night. While the victims were incapacitated, FREIRE allegedly raped Victim‑1 in the victims’ dorm room.
Rather than immediately seeking help, FREIRE waited approximately 45 minutes, during which he sent photos of the victims to others. When he finally approached campus security, he initially falsely claimed that the victims had simply consumed too much alcohol.
Campus security responded and administered emergency aid, including Narcan. Both victims were transported to hospitals in Manhattan. Toxicology results later confirmed that both women had ingested fentanyl and no cocaine.
Victim‑2 regained consciousness after life‑saving treatment. Victim‑1 remained in critical condition and eventually died from complications of acute fentanyl intoxication.
* * *
FREIRE, 19, of the Bronx, New York and PERALTA, 18, of Queens, New York, are both charged with one count of conspiracy to distribute a controlled substance resulting in death and serious bodily injury, which carries a mandatory minimum sentence of 20 years in prison and a maximum sentence of life in prison. FREIRE is also charged with distribution of a controlled substance resulting in death and serious bodily injury, which carries a mandatory minimum sentence of 20 years in prison and a maximum sentence of life in prison, as well as distribution of a controlled substance with the intent to commit rape, which carries a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison.
Mr. McDonald praised the outstanding investigative work of the DEA, the NYPD, as well as the Special Agents, Task Force Officers, the Digital Forensic Unit, and the Complex Analytics and Social Media Enhancement Team at the New York / New Jersey High Intensity Drug Trafficking from the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York.
The case is being handled by the Office’s Narcotics Unit. Assistant United States Attorney Ariana L. Bloom is in charge of the prosecution.
The charges contained in the Indictment are merely accusations, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.
- ^ As the introductory phrase signifies, the entirety of the text of the Indictment and the description of the Indictment set forth herein constitutes only allegations and every fact described should be treated as an allegation.
title: DEA New York Task Force Division Announces Two New York Men Indicted For Fentanyl Distribution Conspiracy That Involved the On-Campus Rape and Death of One College Student and Near-Death of Another

text:
MIAMI – A Coconut Grove art dealer who sold forged Andy Warhol artwork to unsuspecting buyers using fraudulent invoices, fabricated authentication documents, and counterfeit stamps has been sentenced to 46 months in federal prison.

U.S. District Judge Roy K. Altman imposed the sentence on Leslie Roberts, 62, of Miami, after Roberts pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud.

“Leslie Roberts turned his Miami art gallery into a vehicle for fraud, selling forged Andy Warhol artwork and using fabricated documents to deceive unsuspecting buyers,” said U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida. “He exploited the trust that collectors place in art dealers and the authenticity of the works they purchase. Today’s 46-month prison sentence sends a clear message: fraud is fraud, whether it happens on Wall Street or in an art gallery. Those who profit through deception will be held accountable.”

“Art fraud undermines confidence in the legitimate art market and victimizes buyers who rely on the authenticity of the works they purchase,” said Special Agent in Charge Brett D. Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office. “This sentence demonstrates that those who use forged artwork, fraudulent documentation, and deceptive schemes to profit illegally will be held accountable. The FBI remains committed to investigating complex fraud schemes and working with our partners to protect the public and uphold the integrity of our financial and commercial systems.”

According to court records, Roberts operated Miami Fine Art Gallery in Coconut Grove, where he sold forged artwork that he falsely represented as original works by renowned artist Andy Warhol. To deceive buyers, Roberts claimed that he had acquired the artwork directly from the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts (AWF) and provided fraudulent invoices purportedly issued by the foundation.

Roberts also used forged authentication bearing the name of the Andy Warhol Art Authentication Board, Inc., and purported signatures of its authorized representatives to make the counterfeit artwork appear genuine. Roberts also used fraudulent AWF identification numbers inscribed on the backs of the artwork and counterfeit stamps to create the appearance of authenticity.

As part of the conspiracy, Roberts enlisted Carlos Rodriguez Melendez to pose as an employee of a New York-based auction company and falsely authenticate artwork to conceal that it was forged. Rodriguez Melendez has also pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud for his involvement in the scheme.

The FBI Art Crime Team and FBI West Palm Beach investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Daniel Rosenfeld and former Assistant U.S. Attorney Lindsey Lazopolous Friedman prosecuted the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Nicole Grosnoff is handling asset forfeiture.

Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Southern District of Florida at www.flsd.uscourts.gov or at http://pacer.flsd.uscourts.gov , under case number 25-cr-20142.

###
title: Miami Art Dealer Sentenced to Nearly Four Years in Federal Prison for Selling Forged Andy Warhol Artwork

The U.S. Transportation Department’s National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) today released its model year 2027 vehicle selections for the New Car Assessment Program’s 5-Star Safety Ratings.
Testing Breakdown:
- Crash Safety: 23 vehicles will undergo frontal, side, and rollover crash tests for the agency’s annual safety evaluation, with safety ratings covering 87% of all new vehicles.
- Pedestrian Protection: 18 vehicles will be evaluated under the agency’s brand-new pedestrian protection assessment.
- Driver Assistance: 10 vehicles will be tested across five advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS): automatic emergency braking, pedestrian automatic emergency braking, lane keeping assist, blind spot warning, and blind spot intervention.
Under Secretary Duffy, NHTSA is empowering automakers to invest in technology advancements that will make cars safer and more affordable for American families.
“For more than 30 years, NHTSA’s 5-Star Safety Ratings have helped families choose the vehicle that’s right for them,” said NHTSA Administrator Jonathan Morrison. “Our 5-Star Safety Rating program also rewards automakers who continuously innovate to improve safety by adding lifesaving technologies to their vehicles.”
Performance assessments and ratings will be available at NHTSA.gov/Ratings once testing and quality control of test data are complete. The Five-Star crash test ratings can also be seen on the window stickers of new vehicles.

LAREDO, Texas — U.S. Customs and Border Protection officers at the Laredo Port of Entry seized methamphetamine valued at more than $30 million.
“The steadfast dedication of our workforce remains the cornerstone of our border security strategy,” said Alberto Flores, port director. “This successful enforcement action underscores our resolve to protect our communities from dangerous contraband.”
The seizure occurred on Oct. 12 at the World Trade Bridge when a CBP officer referred a 2020 International LT625 tractor hauling a trailer manifested as salt for an enforcement inspection. Following a secondary inspection and nonintrusive inspection system examination, CBP officers discovered a total of 76 bags containing 3,395.91 pounds of alleged methamphetamine within the commodity.
The narcotics has a street value of $30,355,444.
Under the leadership of President Donald J. Trump and Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, the dedicated men and women of U.S. Customs and Border Protection, alongside our law enforcement partners, have arrested and removed thousands of criminal aliens from the country - including gang members, rapists, kidnappers, and drug traffickers - to make our communities safer.
CBP seized the narcotics. The driver, tractor and trailer were released. Homeland Security Investigations special agents are investigating the seizure.

title: CBP officers seize over $30 million in meth at Laredo Port of Entry

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Jahana Hayes (CT-05) joined Congresswoman Debbie Dingell (MI-06) to introduce the Title IX Take Responsibility Act, legislation that would hold schools accountable for mishandling reports of sexual assault and provide survivors a stronger path towards justice.
The legislation amends Title IX; a U.S. federal civil rights law passed as part of the Education Amendments of 1972 that bans sex-based discrimination in any education program or activity receiving federal money. The bill would reform how schools handle sexual assault and harassment by replacing outdated legal loopholes with clear accountability.
"One incident of sexual violence is one too many," said Congresswoman Jahana Hayes. "I am committed to protecting students, supporting survivors, and ensuring college campuses are safe learning environments for all. The Title IX Take Responsibility Act will put the responsibility on educational institutions for any mishandling of sexual assault reporting and failure to prevent further assaults. This legislation should be considered immediately, and I thank Congresswoman Dingell for partnering on this effort."
"For far too long, outdated legal loopholes have allowed educational institutions to turn a blind eye to reports of sexual assault, leaving survivors without justice or support," said Congresswoman Dingell. "Title IX was enacted to protect students, not to shield institutions from accountability when they fail to keep campuses safe. This bill closes these gaps and ensures that every student has access to a safe learning environment free from abuse."
Under current Supreme Court precedents, schools can only be held liable if high-level officials had "actual notice" and reacted with "deliberate indifference," creating an incentive for institutions to turn a blind eye. This bill eliminates that defense by holding schools legally responsible if they knew or reasonably should have known about the abuse and failed to take effective action. It also expands access to justice by allowing survivors to hold schools accountable in federal court for monetary damages and legal fees.
The legislation is endorsed by End Rape on Campus, Just Solutions, National Alliance to End Sexual Violence (NAESV), National Organization for Victim Advocacy (NOVA), Ujima, Volare, YWCA,
Survivors should never have to choose between their safety and their education. The Title IX Take Responsibility Act affirms survivors’ rights to support, to make their own choices about reporting, and to seek justice when their access to education is harmed. It also gives schools clear standards that reflect what effective, survivor-centered response looks like. NOVA strongly supports this bill,” said Claire Ponder Selib, Executive Director, National Organization for Victim Advocacy.
"Schools must take sexual misconduct more seriously. We're abandoning survivors and ignoring the enormous impact of sexual violence on their educational attainment, health, and quality of life. This is unacceptable. The National Alliance to End Sexual Violence applauds Representatives Dingell and Hayes for re-introducing the Title IX Take Responsibility Act. We must have more accountability," said Monika Johnson-Hostler, President & CEO, National Alliance to End Sexual Violence.
“YWCA USA is unwavering in our pursuit of a world where all women and girls can thrive. To meet that mission, it is essential that every student can learn in an environment free from sexual violence. Sadly, we know that violence does occur. The deeply disturbing reports from Cornell University underscore that passing the Title IX Take Responsibility Act is an essential and overdue step that would hold our educational institutions more responsible for protecting students from the start and accessing swift, meaningful pathways to justice and healing,” said Kate Kasper, VP of Public Policy and Advocacy, YWCA USA.
“I’m grateful to Reps. Dingell and Hayes for reintroducing the Title IX Take Responsibility Act. At moment when the Dept of Education is rolling back protections under Title IX and leaving survivors of sexual violence vulnerable, this bill would strengthen protections and where appropriate, hold institutions accountable,” said Lisalyn Jacobs, CEO of Just Solutions.
“Survivors should not have to sacrifice their education because an institution failed to respond meaningfully to sexual harassment or violence. The Title IX Take Responsibility Act strengthens survivors’ ability to enforce their rights and recognizes that students should be able to access meaningful support without being required to pursue an investigation. Survivors deserve options that protect their safety, well-being, and ability to continue their education,” said Volare CEO Bridgette Stumpf.
Text of the Title IX Take Responsibility Act is available here.
title: Hayes, Dingell Introduce Bill to Hold Schools Accountable for Mishandling Reports of Sexual Assault

Congresswoman Lateefah Simon Hosts Town Halls in All Seven Cities In the East Bay in 2026, Reaches Thousands Across the District
OAKLAND, CA – Congresswoman Lateefah Simon (CA-12) has completed her second town hall tour since being sworn into Congress in January 2025. In 2026, she held town halls in all seven cities that she represents in California’s 12th Congressional District, reaching thousands of constituents in Oakland, Berkeley, Albany, San Leandro, Alameda, Piedmont, and Emeryville.
This year’s town hall tour builds on Congresswoman Simon’s previous 2025 town hall tour where she held eleven town halls across the East Bay, reaching more than 15,000 constituents in person, virtually, and by telephone.
“As the Trump Administration and Republicans in Congress continue to cut vital programs and services while funding the unlawful, violent terrorization our immigrant communities, hearing stories and the impacts of the Republican agenda on the families living in our communities everyday has been invaluable. Every single day I take the voices from our district and fight for better conditions and resources in Congress,” said Congresswoman Lateefah Simon. “I am grateful to every community member from Albany to San Leandro who joined me on this year’s town hall tour to raise the issues most important to you and how I can continue to serve and fight for us. Though this year has brought challenges, the resilience and joy of the East Bay inspires me every day, and I look forward to continuing to meet with and hear from neighbors across our beautiful district.”
During her town hall tour, the Congresswoman shared updates with constituents on: (1) the Congresswoman’s legislative work in Congress during her second year, including her work as a member in the House Oversight Committee and Small Business Committee; (2) recent bills she’s introduced to support small business owners, public transportation, and workers with disabilities; (3) recent efforts to protect reproductive, disability, labor, and civil rights; (3) the over $11.1 million in federal Community Project Funding that the Congresswoman secured for projects across the East Bay; (4) updates on the Congresswoman’s work to oppose the proposed Oakland coal export terminal funded by the Trump Administration and demand answers on the status of the Alameda Point Veterans Affairs outpatient clinic and columbarium project, (5), attacks on immigrant communities and resources to help; and (6) how Californians can stay involved and continue to fight back.

Item C-2 | Docket No. PL26-3-000 | Chairman's Statement
The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) today unveiled a proposal to overhaul and accelerate its review of air quality effects for proposed natural gas projects under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA). The draft policy statement cuts unnecessary delays and duplicative analysis, while delivering greater regulatory certainty and a more streamlined path forward for project applicants.
“From my first day as Chairman, streamlining NEPA reviews has been one of my top priorities. Today’s landmark draft policy statement is a defining step in our mission to cut unnecessary delays and deliver regulatory certainty,” Chairman Laura V. Swett said. “My legacy will not be cowering timidity. It will be surgical, strategic, aggressive reform that propels the country and our next generations into energy security and prosperity.”
The draft policy statement proposes to no longer request air dispersion modeling from applicants for Natural Gas Act (NGA) projects or rely on this modeling in assessing operational air quality effects under NEPA. This proposal recognizes the extensive protections and mitigation requirements built into the Clean Air Act’s exacting regulations, which reflect the expertise and scientific judgment of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and state agencies—the expert administrative bodies Congress actually charged with safeguarding the Nation’s air quality. In light of this pervasive regulatory regime, the Commission proposes to use other information submitted by applicants, and identified by Commission staff, to analyze the air quality effects of proposed projects. The Commission will continue to thoroughly address air quality effects in its NEPA documents to disclose any adverse environmental effects, but in a more streamlined way.
Consistent with Supreme Court guidance and aligned Congressional mandates, the draft policy statement proposes to more closely align the Commission’s NEPA analysis with its statutory roles. It also proposes to end unnecessary overlap with the permitting responsibilities entrusted to air regulatory agencies under the Clean Air Act.
Interested parties may submit comments on the implementation of the draft policy statement by November 16, 2026.
(30)
title: FERC Launches NEPA Overhaul to Accelerate Natural Gas Projects

Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11) introduced the Heat Island Reduction Act, which would require federal agencies to plan cost-effective upgrades that cool their properties, improve air quality, and lower energy costs.
Parking lots and dark rooftops soak up heat and hold it, which warms nearby communities, raises cooling bills, and speeds the formation of smog. The bill targets federal properties in areas that already fail federal smog standards.
Northern Virginia is already working on the problem. This summer, more than 80 volunteers teamed up with the Faith Alliance for Climate Solutions and George Mason University’s Virginia Climate Center to map where heat hits hardest across Fairfax County, Arlington, and Alexandria. What they found points to simple fixes: more trees, more shade, and cooler surfaces. Walkinshaw’s bill would apply the same approach to federal properties nationwide.
“Extreme heat endangers workers, worsens the air our families breathe, and drives up cooling costs,” said Congressman Walkinshaw. “Volunteers here in Northern Virginia are working to pinpoint where heat hits hardest. The federal government should take the same hard look at its own properties and start with the fixes that deliver the most. Shade trees and cooler roofs protect federal workers and visitors and lower the cooling bills taxpayers pay.”
The Heat Island Reduction Act would:
    - Within six months: Require agencies to plan cooling fixes, such as trees, shade, cool roofs, and cooler pavement, for their properties in areas that fail federal smog standards.
- Six months later: Require agencies to set out each project’s cost, funding source, and timeline, and to update these plans every two years.
- Every year: Require the General Services Administration to report to Congress on progress, spending, and changes in temperature and energy use.
- At every step: Prioritize cost-effective fixes and build them into routine repairs and construction.
Congressman Paul Tonko (NY-20) and Congresswoman Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC) are original cosponsors.
Read the full bill text here. 
###
title: Walkinshaw Introduces Bill to Cool Federal Properties, Cut Smog, and Lower Energy Costs

Trump EPA Celebrates Children’s Health Month with 100 Actions to Protect the Nation’s Most Precious Resource
WASHINGTON — The Trump Administration has been racking up huge wins when it comes to protecting children’s health. In honor of Children's Health Month, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) released a list of 100 actions taken to protect children’s health and secure America’s future.
Since January 2025, the Trump EPA has taken actions that protect children’s health by reducing lead and PFAS exposure, enhancing chemical and pesticide safety, improving air quality, and growing state and local partnerships to Make America Healthy Again. The list of 100 actions to help safeguard American children illustrates this EPA’s unwavering commitment to the health and wellbeing of American families.
“Under President Trump’s leadership, EPA is focused on delivering clean air, land, and water for every American child,” said EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin, “This doesn’t just mean reducing lead exposure or more quickly cleaning up toxic sites, it also involves giving families peace of mind by equipping them with the knowledge and tools they need to keep their kids safe.”
For Children’s Health Month 2026, EPA’s educational efforts revolve around three main priorities:
- Raise Awareness: Know the environmental risks that can affect children’s health.
- Act Early: Reduce hazards in the places children live, learn, and play.
- Protect and Prevent: Support healthy environments for every child, every day.
EPA urges families, schools, and communities to learn more about children’s environmental health and use available resources to reduce exposures, support prevention, and promote healthier communities for children across the country. Children’s Health Month also includes National Lead Poisoning Prevention Week, an important opportunity to raise awareness and take action to prevent lead exposures, especially in children.
Here are 100 actions EPA has taken since January 20, 2025, to protect children’s health:
- Provided $2.9 billion in funding for states to reduce lead in drinking water through the Drinking Water State Revolving Fund (DWSRF).
- Worked with more than 100 drinking water systems to guide them through the process of lead service line removal through the Get the Lead Out technical assistance initiative.
- Released several tools to help states and water systems prepare for new requirements in the Lead and Copper Rule related to lead sampling in schools and childcare facilities. These tools include a resource guide, sampling waiver checklists, and frequently asked questions.
- Released a Lead and Children’s Health StoryMap to highlight information on national trends on lead and help ensure families stay healthy and safe.
- Released an Asthma & Children’s Health StoryMap to provide information on how environmental factors, such as air quality, affect health outcomes like asthma rates and other conditions.
- Updated the America’s Children and the Environment (ACE) data and trends tool to better present children’s environmental health data to non-technical audiences
- Updated the Children’s Unique Vulnerabilities to Environmental Hazards resource to include exposure examples across life stages and provides a more comprehensive picture of children’s health issues through life stages and windows of susceptibility.
- Updated the Children’s Environmental Health Facts resource to provide key facts and statistics and highlight trends and economic impacts of childhood health concerns.
- Released a resource for parents about how to protect children from elemental mercury, What to Do If You Find or Spill Mercury.
- Updated Sensible Steps to Healthier School Environments to address common areas of environmental health concerns in schools and provide information about existing low-cost or no-cost measures, programs, and resources that are available to help prevent, reduce, and resolve hazards.
- Highlighted children’s health on EPA’s Research Partner Support Stories, including science-based information to communities, families, caretakers, and school decision makers to protect children’s health and reduce environmental exposures to harmful contaminants.
- Presented information to the Colorado Association of Libraries about EPA Region 8’s Community Libraries Program, which offers an extensive inventory of information and resources related to protecting the health of children and indoor air, childhood lead poisoning prevention, and other environmental education assistance.
- Published four quarterly EPA Mountains & Plains Regional Healthy Schools Newsletter editions shared with EPA Region 8’s network of healthy schools contacts.
- Formed a Senior Lead Leadership Coordinating Committee to strengthen cross-agency efforts to reduce lead exposure and protect children from lead-related health risks, meeting EPA’s commitments under the Federal Lead Action Plan.
- Completed a Federal Lead Resources Guide for use by partners and the public, in particular with other federal departments and agencies.
- Published the updated Protect Your Family From Lead in Your Home pamphlet in multiple languages in collaboration with federal and state partners.
- Launched revamped lead website (epa.gov/lead) to streamline navigation and serve as a one-stop shop for EPA information on lead and quickly connect users to resources, tools and guidance.
- Hosted in-person and virtual educational sessions on the Lead Awareness Curriculum about the dangers of lead, and ways to reduce and prevent lead exposure and equip community leaders to educate their communities about lead.
- Hosted virtual National Meeting on EPA’s Lead-Based Paint Program for authorized Tribal and state programs and non-authorized state programs.
- Facilitated a webinar, Lead-Based Paint Awareness for Building Code Officials, on lead-based paint regulations.
- Published materials in collaboration with federal partners for individuals, communities and Tribal, state and local governments and organizations ("partners") to use to raise awareness during National Lead Poisoning Prevention Week.
- Published updated materials for the EPA/HUD Lead Dust Sampling Technician and Certified Renovator model courses as part of EPA’s implementation of the Reconsideration of the Dust-Lead Hazard Standards and Dust-Lead Post-Abatement Clearance Levels Rule.
- Released new guidance to reduce lead exposure in drinking water and help drinking water systems protect American children.
- Worked with states and federal partners to implement the Lead-Free Rule and reduce lead in pipes, plumbing fittings, and fixtures used for drinking water.
- Increased awareness among property management companies with lead safety requirements under the Lead Renovation Repair and Painting (RRP) Rule and the Real Estate Notification and Lead Disclosure Rule to protect military families living in privatized military housing.
- Issued the Residential Lead Directive for CERCLA Sites and RCRA Hazardous Waste Cleanup Program Facilities to accelerate lead cleanup at contaminated sites.
- Published a new webpage that provides healthy gardening practices for residents living in areas where soil may be contaminated with lead.
- Hosted public meetings in Colorado for community members to discuss lead and arsenic contamination in soils from historic smelters, including educational materials on lead exposure reduction.
- Advanced lead testing and remediation in schools and childcare settings across states and Tribal communities through Water Infrastructure Improvements for the Nation (WIIN) grant funding.
- Published a mapping blueprint for identifying locations in the United States for focusing high-impact interventions to reduce childhood lead exposure.
- Developed a resource list on lead risks in ammunition and fishing tackle to increase awareness about this exposure route and its impact on children’s health.
- Presented information about how to organize a soilSHOP health education community event that offers free soil lead screenings and education about how to reduce lead exposures to children and families at the EPA Tools & Resources August national webinar.
- Convened lead listening sessions in EPA Region 1 with state public health and environmental agencies in New England in partnership with the Association of State and Territorial Health Officials (ASTHO).
- Worked with partners in EPA Region 2 – including Families for Lead Freedom Now, the New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH), and the City of Syracuse – to develop stronger community relationships and community engagement materials on the Lead and Copper Rule.
- Held an inaugural lead workshop in San Juan, Puerto Rico – in collaboration with the Puerto Rico Department of Health, Region 2 Pediatric Environmental Health Specialty Unit (PEHSU), Puerto Rico Department of Environmental and Natural Resources, College of Engineers and Surveyors of Puerto Rico (CIAPR), and engineering partners – to teach construction workers how to prevent lead exposure at home.
- Hosted an availability session with local partners in EPA Region 2 – including the Puerto Rico Department of Health, Municipality of Vega Baja, and College of Medical Technologists – to conduct capillary lead tests for residents and children who attended the event.
- Worked with state departments of health in EPA Region 3 to determine needs regarding blood lead level testing and provided education to medical providers.
- Funded Lead Renovation Repair and Painting trainings in Region 6 locations to increase compliance awareness and prevent lead exposure to children.
- Increased compliance among states in EPA Region 9 to complete lead service line inventories.
- Issued the National Perchloroethylene Air Emission Standards for Dry Cleaning Facilities to reduce air pollution that can affect children’s health.
- Updated the Wildfire Smoke: A Guide for Public Health Officials, which included children’s health considerations.
- Hosted webinars for schools on ventilation, improved indoor air quality, and wildfire smoke to support school air quality planning and maintenance.
- Supported the PEHSU Asthma Home Visit Program in EPA Region 8, helping children with persistent asthma reduce triggers in their homes.
- Partnered with libraries and firefighters to provide Do-It-Yourself air cleaner demonstrations and asthma education to communities experiencing wildfire smoke in EPA Region 10.
- Awarded funding to Maine Department of Health and Human Services to support radon testing in Maine Schools.
- Added an additional PFAS to the Toxics Release Inventory reporting list.
- Published draft guidance to help wastewater utilities, landowners, and the public reduce risk from PFOA and PFOS in biosolids.
- EPA laboratory methods to measure microplastics in drinking water, helping decision-makers address microplastic pollution closer to its source.
- Published the final risk evaluation for 1,3-butadiene, which found unreasonable risks for some industrial settings that could lead to health risks for workers, including reduced birthweight pregnancies.
- Proposed a draft risk evaluation on octamethylcyclotetrasiloxane (D4), finding unreasonable risks for some industrial settings and a consumer use that could lead to effects related to reproductive outcomes.
- Published the final risk evaluations for six phthalates – dibutyl phthalate (1,2-benzene- dicarboxylic acid, 1,2- dibutyl ester) (DBP), butyl benzyl phthalate (1,2-benzene- dicarboxylic acid, 1- butyl 2(phenylmethyl) ester) (BBP), diisobutyl phthalate (1,2-benzene- dicarboxylic acid, 1,2- bis-(2methylpropyl) ester) (DIBP), dicyclohexyl phthalate (DCHP), and diethylhexyl phthalate (DEHP) – finding unreasonable risks for some industrial settings that could lead to health risks for workers, including hormone deficiencies and endocrine disruption.
- Proposed a draft risk evaluation on p-dichlorobenzene (pDCB), finding unreasonable risks for some workers and consumers, including air care products that could lead to exposures to children and potential health risks of neurotoxicity and developmental toxicity.
- Proposed a draft risk evaluation on 1,3,4,6,7,8-hexahydro-4,6,6,7,8,8-hexamethylcyclopenta [g]-2-benzopyran (HHCB), finding the most sensitive effects are developmental effects on offspring growth.
- Supported the Trump Administration’s continued efforts to crackdown on illegal toxic pesticides and chemical smuggling operations. EPA, joined by the U.S. Customs and Border Protection, inspected five seaports and land ports of entry across the country and identified thousands of violative products that are regulated under the Safe Drinking Water Act and EPA’s Lead Free Rule.
- Published a study – Laboratory investigation of inadvertently generated PCBs released from consumer products into lake water – investigating the occurrence and leaching behavior of inadvertently generated polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), prioritizing consumer products used by children, to better understand exposure risks.
- Published a study – Proteome profiling of emamectin-treated primary rat cortical cells following up to twelve days in vitro exposure – identifying altered protein biochemical processes that may inform mechanisms of developmental neurotoxicity related to chemical exposures.
- Published a study – Single-cell RNA sequencing of human embryonic stem cells reveals immediate and deferred transcriptomic responses to retinoic acid-mediated effects across cell subpopulations – used single-cell sequencing techniques to assess the utility of the method for understanding developmental changes related to chemical exposures for potential use in screening paradigms.
- Issued Current Progress and Research Needs to Protect Children’s Environmental Health to summarize research and policy opportunities advancing children’s environmental health.
- Led work with the President’s Task Force on Environmental Health Risks and Safety Risks to Children to improve communications and coordinate federal children’s health efforts.
- Contributed to annual reports from the Federal Interagency Forum on Child and Family Statistics.
- Created a Children’s Environmental Health Workgroup through the Association of State and Territorial Health Officials (ASTHO) to share information and best practices.
- Supported state lead program prevention programs through sharing resources and identifying areas for collaboration.
- Provided information to state officials about the Pediatric Environmental Health Specialty Units (PEHSUs) across the country.
- Supported a removal action in Massachusetts in EPA Region 1 to address lead and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) contamination in soil where families and children live.
- Worked with partners in EPA Region 5 in state and local governments and organizations to create a network of neighborhood-level air quality monitoring stations in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, focusing on neighborhoods with high asthma burdens for children and adults to improve asthma awareness.
- Held two mercury trainings in EPA Region 5 in Marion County, Ohio, focused on children’s safety, proper response procedure and tactics for local responders, and mercury health risks.
- Hosted a Children’s Health Seminar with the Arkansas Department of Health and Region 6 PEHSU to strengthen the state’s ability to identify and address environmental health risks affecting children.
- Hosted a Children’s Environmental Health Symposium in Region 6 in partnership with Children’s Health Hospital of Dallas educating pediatric providers and nurses on environmental risks that can affect children’s health.
- Worked in partnership with the Region 6 Border Program and PEHSU to train pediatric health care providers and community health workers along the U.S.-Mexico Border on children’s health topics such as Community Emergency Preparedness and Household Hazardous Chemicals.
- Trained Head Start Family Resource Specialists in Region 6 on environmental risks to children, particularly the importance of both preventing lead exposure and childhood blood lead level testing.
- Coordinated with the Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services in EPA Region 8 to provide EPA resources in a four-part webinar series on reducing environmental exposures for early childcare providers.
- Provided children’s environmental health and disaster preparedness education by helping children pack “Grab and Go” bags at a Tribal event for National Emergency Preparedness Month across EPA Region 10.
- Completed the Schools Adapting to Natural Disasters project, including an assessment for Gary Community School Corporation and a technical guidance playbook for Broward County Public Schools.
- Coordinated the internal Children’s Health Activities and Research Group at EPA (CHARGE) to improve implementation, communication, and collaboration across EPA.
- Presented EPA's Air Quality Flag Program to tribes raising awareness about air quality and its related children impacts to children's health and recruited new partners across the country.
- Worked with Tribal, federal, and state partners to characterize uranium mine sites, communicate risks, develop response plans, and address contaminated homes on Tribal lands.
- Provided technical expertise on air pollutants associated with chronic respiratory health impacts, including PM2.5, ozone, volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and wood-stove emissions, and led learning activities for the Mashpee Wampanoag Tribe’s “Preserving Our Homeland” summer camp.
- Partnered with the Shinnecock Nation of Indian's Environmental Department to develop an air quality education program with the Shinnecock Boys and Girls Club and local elementary schools and libraries to review the Air Quality Index, showcase PM 2.5 purple air sensors, and lead an Air Quality Index activity with air quality flags.
- Hosted a Children’s Environmental Health educational session at a Choctaw Nation Summit, highlighting lead-based paint, household hazardous chemicals, and air quality.
- Hosted a Healthy Homes practical training on assessing and addressing health and safety risks in homes, including risks specific to children of tribal members, in partnership with the Meskwaki Nation.
- Promoted the Air Quality Flag Program to recruit new Tribal partners in Region 6 and Region 8.
- Assisted Tribal Drinking Water Systems throughout Region 9 to complete lead service line inventories.
- Funded the replacement of water storage tanks containing lead paint in the Tohono O'odham Nation.
- Provided technical assistance to drinking water systems on Tohono O’odham and Navajo lands with lead exceedances to provide public notification and comply with Lead and Copper Rule requirements.
- Took action to address uranium contamination in the Southwest and its intergenerational neurodevelopmental health effects on the Navajo Nation and surrounding Tribal communities.
- Educated Tribal leaders on actions they could take to help protect children from environmental health risks at the Region 9 Tribal Operations Committee meeting.

DEA New Orleans Hosts 31st National Prescription Drug Take Back Day Saturday, Oct. 24
NEW ORLEANS – The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration, in collaboration with more than 4,300 law enforcement partners, will host the 31st National Prescription Drug Take Back Day from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. on Saturday, October 24.
Collection sites will be set up across Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, and Arkansas to dispose of unneeded, expired, and unused prescription medications.
More than 4,400 collection sites will be set up across the country to dispose of unneeded, expired, and unused prescription medications. This is a simple step that prevents diversion, reduces the risk of accidental poisoning, and helps protect communities.
“Since 2010, Take Back Day has helped Americans remove more than twenty million pounds of unneeded medications from their homes,” said DEA Administrator Terry Cole. “By participating in Take Back Day, you are preventing potentially addictive medications from falling into the wrong hands – a small step that can save lives. I am grateful to the thousands of law enforcement and community partners who make these events possible, and I urge everyone to take a few minutes on Saturday, October 24, to clean out your medicine cabinets.”
“Unused or expired prescription drugs sitting in our home medicine cabinets present a real threat to our families and communities across our region,” said Special Agent in Charge John P. Scott of the DEA New Orleans Field Division. “National Prescription Drug Take Back Day offers a free, safe, and convenient way to properly dispose of these medications before they can be misused or accidentally ingested.”
What will be collected
- Tablets, capsules, patches, and other forms of prescription medications
- Liquid medications securely sealed in their original containers
What won’t be collected
- Syringes, sharps, and illicit drugs
Why it matters
- Prescription opioids, such as oxycodone, hydrocodone, codeine, and morphine, are among the most frequently misused prescription pain medications, according to the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA).
- Removing unneeded medications from the home reduces the risk of misuse or accidental ingestion.
Visit DEATakeBack.com to find a registered Take Back location near you. If you are unable to participate in this fall’s National Prescription Drug Take Back Day, there are more than 15,300 pharmacies, hospitals, and businesses that offer safe medication disposal year-round. In addition, many police departments also provide permanent drop boxes to ensure Every Day is Take Back Day.
title: DEA New Orleans Hosts 31st National Prescription Drug Take Back Day Saturday, Oct. 24

David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, and P.J. O’Brien, Special Agent in Charge of the New Haven Division of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, today announced that SCOTT DYER, 35, of Naugatuck, was arrested yesterday on a federal criminal complaint charging him with threatening to kill members of the Republican Party and a high-ranking public official.

As alleged in court documents, On October 8 and 9, 2026, Dyer posted several threatening comments on YouTube, including:

“I’m prepared to kill Republicans. Eager to do it actually. I already have targets in my local community selected.”

“I have hundreds of people in an excel spreadsheet with as much info on them as I could get. I’ve been stockpiling hollow points and have some custom made drones with some… ‘neat’ features. Can’t wait for November. Gonna make a lot of people pay and I only accept Republican blood.”

“The only public execution I’d like to witness and actively participate in is (name of high-ranking public official)….I have a lot of hollow points with his name on if we ever get the chance to meet.”

“I will head to the capitol tomorrow to assassinate (name of high-ranking public official).”

“I’ve been stockpiling guns, ammo, the precursors for synthesizing explosives, food, water, fuel... I will have no problem bringing the fight to them and if they think they’ll be able so beg for mercy and surrender they got another thing coming to ‘em….”

Dyer appeared yesterday before U.S. District Judge S. Dave Vatti in Bridgeport and was released on a $100,000 bond into home confinement under electronic monitoring.

The complaint charges Dyer with making interstate threats, an offense that carries a maximum term of imprisonment of five years.

“Threats of violence, whether tied to politics or any other motive, have no place on the internet or anywhere else in our society,” said U.S. Attorney Sullivan. “We will investigate these crimes quickly and prosecute those involved to deter this behavior, neutralize any threats, and ensure the safety of the public.”

“There is no place in our democracy for politically motivated threats or acts of violence; public officials should never be targeted simply for the position they hold or for their party affiliation,” said FBI Special Agent in Charge O’Brien. “The men and women of FBI New Haven took an oath to defend our Constitution and will rigorously investigate all politically motivated threats and violence to ensure the safety of public servants, elected officials, and all those demonstrating support for a political party.”

U.S. Attorney Sullivan stressed that a complaint is only a charge and is not evidence of guilt. Charges are only allegations, and a defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.

This investigation is being conducted by the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Joint Terrorism Task Force (JTTF) with the assistance of the Naugatuck Police Department. The JTTF includes participants from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), IRS Criminal Investigation, Naval Criminal Investigative Service, U.S. Department of State, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, U.S. Marshals Service, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, Connecticut State Police, Connecticut Department of Correction, Metropolitan Transportation Authority Police Department, Norwich Police Department, Hartford Police Department, Stamford Police Department, Norwalk Police Department, Town of Groton Police Department, UConn Police Department, Yale Police Department, Stonington Police Department, New Haven Police Department, and New York Police Department. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Katherine E. Boyles.

This prosecution and law enforcement action is in support of National Security Presidential Memorandum 7 ( NSPM-7 ), Countering Domestic Terrorism and Organized Political Violence.
title: Naugatuck Man Charged with Making Online Threats

Tampa, FL – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Florida (MDFL) announced today the extradition of Adedotun Abraham Adeyemo (47, of Pretoria, South Africa) and the unsealing of a superseding indictment charging him with two counts of wire fraud and two related counts of aggravated identity theft. Each wire fraud count carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison, and each aggravated identity theft count carries a mandatory two-year prison term, consecutive to any sentence for the underlying felony. This case is part of nationwide enforcement actions led by the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division, Internal Revenue Service, Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation targeting tax fraud and related offenses. The MDFL was a key participant in this surge effort.

Between early September and today, the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section and U.S. Attorneys’ Offices across the country participated in the Department’s first-ever National Tax Enforcement Surge. The surge of nationwide resources resulted in prosecutorial actions against 76 defendants whose alleged and proven crimes intended an estimated loss of revenue to the federal government of more than $490 million.

“Stealing from taxpayers is intolerable and compromises the solvency of our public services to American citizens,” said U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe. “We will pursue and prosecute those who commit fraud against our federal institutions and programs, and bring them to justice, wherever they are.”

According to the superseding indictment, Adeyemo and other scheme participants obtained unauthorized access to United States-based businesses’ computer servers, stole from those servers the personal identifying information (“PII”) of United States residents, and then used that stolen PII to file false and fraudulent United States individual income tax returns, seeking refunds to which Adeyemo and his co-schemers were not entitled. The case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Internal Revenue Service—Criminal Investigation. The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs secured the September extradition from the United Kingdom of Adeyemo with the assistance of the UK authorities. It is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Whitney MacKay. The asset forfeiture is being handled by Assistant U.S Attorney James A. Muench.

An indictment is only an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.

This press release details one way in which this office has contributed to ensuring that all Americans pay their fair share. To see the successes of other offices, please see this press release https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/dojs-fraud-division-irs-and-irs-ci-expose-more-490m-tax-fraud-national-tax-enforcement-surge .

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

An indictment, information, or complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: Middle District of Florida Joins DOJ Fraud Division, IRS, IRS-CI, and the FBI in National Tax Enforcement Surge Exposing More than $490M in Tax Fraud

Russian National Arrested and Extradited to New York on Charges of Evading Sanctions on Russia
Alexander Suvorov, 52, a Russian national, has been charged by a criminal complaint with three counts related to the unlawful exporting of micro-electronic components from the United States to Russia via a front company based in Hong Kong.
“Those, like the defendant, as alleged, who seek to enrich themselves by evading economic sanctions on Russia, must understand that their actions carry serious consequences and will not be tolerated,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney John A. Sarcone III for the Northern District of New York. “My office, working together with the FBI and the Department of Commerce, will continue to aggressively prosecute these types of cases and hold offenders accountable to the fullest extent of the law. This historic extradition shows that we will fly over 3,800 miles to locate and bring to justice those who threaten national security.”
“Alexander Suvorov was the alleged mastermind behind an international procurement network that illegally supplied buyers in Russia with American-made electronic components that have military applications,” said Assistant Director Roman Rozhavsky of the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division. “His extradition to face charges here in the U.S. demonstrates the FBI's commitment to keeping sensitive, export-controlled technology out of the hands of the Russian military. We will continue working with our law enforcement, intelligence, private sector, and international partners to bring to justice all who attempt to arm our adversaries at the expense of our citizens and our national security.”
“The Bureau of Industry and Security is committed to strong enforcement,” said Special Agent in Charge Jonathan Carson of the U.S. Department of Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security New York Field Office. “Working closely with out law enforcement partners, we will continue to uncover and disrupt illicit procurement and diversion networks wherever they operate.”
Suvorov was extradited from Sweden to the Northern District of New York on Oct. 15 and is expected to have his initial appearance on Oct. 16 in Albany, New York.
The complaint filed against Suvorov alleges that between about March 2022 and April 2023, Suvorov led an illicit procurement network responsible for unlawfully exporting U.S. electronic components out of the United States to Russia. One of the procurement network’s main goals was to fraudulently obtain dual-use electronic components — that is, electronic components with both civilian and military applications — from U.S. companies for shipment to Russia. As alleged in the complaint, Suvorov’s primary role in the procurement network was to maintain front companies based in Hong Kong, including GS Group Limited, which the procurement network used to order electronic components from U.S. companies in an effort to conceal that the end users of the components were in Russia, and to then transship, via Hong Kong, the components from the U.S. companies to the end users in Russia. Suvorov and his companies are also alleged to have sent multiple wires to various U.S. companies to pay for the electronic components. Some of the components unlawfully purchased and exported to Russia by Suvorov and his procurement network can be used in military communication and radar systems, as well as precision location systems.
Count 1 of the complaint alleges conspiracy to commit international promotional money laundering and carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison, three years of supervised release, and a fine of $500,000. Count 2 alleges conspiracy to commit outbound smuggling and carries a maximum penalty of five years in prison, three years of supervised release, and a fine of $250,000. Count 3 alleges conspiracy to violate the Export Control Reform Act (ECRA) and carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison, three years of supervised release, and a fine of $1,000,000. A federal district judge will determine the sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
The FBI and Department of Commerce are investigating the case. The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs secured the extradition of Suvorov with the assistance of the Swedish Authorities.
Trial Attorney Garrett Coyle of the National Security Division’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Rick Belliss for the Northern District of New York are prosecuting the case.
title: Russian National Arrested and Extradited to New York on Charges of Evading Sanctions on Russia

SAN DIEGO – Hasan Korkmaz, the owner and operator of San Diego Logistics Group Inc., a Santee trucking company, pleaded guilty in federal court today to all 18 counts of an indictment charging him with bank fraud, money laundering and aggravated identity theft.

According to his plea agreement, in 2022 and 2023, Korkmaz executed a credit card “bust-out” scheme—where fraudsters establish seemingly legitimate credit card accounts in other people’s names and then “bust out” by maxing out the credit line with no intention of paying the balance.

Korkmaz admitted that he obtained names, dates of birth, social security numbers and other personally identifiable information corresponding with real individuals. Korkmaz then applied for numerous credit card accounts with that information. After opening the fraudulent credit cards accounts, Korkmaz used the credit cards to incur charges at various businesses, including Korkmaz’s San Diego Logistics Group Inc. The charges were in the thousands of dollars each, including some charges as high as $18,500 in a single transaction.

To perpetuate the scheme, Korkmaz admitted that he also made fraudulent payments, with checks drawn on accounts with insufficient funds or drawn on non-existent accounts, to the credit card accounts, thereby temporarily restoring the available credit limits. Korkmaz would then incur additional charges on the credit card accounts at or near the maximum credit limits for the accounts. In total, Korkmaz caused over $2,103,000 in losses to two banks.

Korkmaz also laundered the bank fraud proceeds, including by transferring proceeds from the fraud scheme internationally to a bank account in Türkiye controlled by Korkmaz. As set forth in public filings, immediately after pulling off the sophisticated $2 million dollar credit card fraud scheme using stolen identities—targeting two banks and almost 100 individual victims—and laundering that money to bank accounts in Türkiye, Korkmaz absconded. There, in Türkiye, Korkmaz spent the next 18 months before ultimately returning to the United States, where he was arrested in June of 2025

A sentencing hearing is scheduled for January 8, 2027, at 9 a.m. before Judge James E. Simmons, Jr.

This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kevin Mokhtari and Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Katherine Rookard.

DEFENDANT Case Number 25-cr-1405-JES

Hasan Korkmaz Age: 45 Las Vegas, NV

SUMMARY OF CHARGES

Counts 1-12 - Bank Fraud - Title 18, U.S.C., Section 1344(2)

Maximum penalty: Thirty years in prison; a maximum $1 million fine

Counts 13-14 - Money Laundering – Title 18, U.S.C., Section 1957

Maximum penalty: Twenty years in prison; a maximum $500,000 fine or twice the amount of monetary instruments involved in the offense, whichever is greatest

Counts 15-18 - Aggravated Identity Theft – Title 18, U.S.C. Section 1028A

Maximum penalty: Mandatory minimum sentence of two years in prison, to run consecutively to the specified felony

INVESTIGATING AGENCY

Federal Bureau of Investigation
title: Owner of Santee Trucking Company Pleads Guilty to $2 Million Credit Card Fraud and Identity Theft Scheme

SPRINGFIELD, Mo. – A Springfield, Mo., man was sentenced in federal court today for being a felon in possession of a firearm.

Mitchell D. Gibbs, 34, was sentenced before U.S. District Judge Megan Blair Benton to 48 months imprisonment followed by three years of supervised release as a result of his conviction. This case was part of Operation Spring Cleaning, a multi-agency law enforcement operation conducted in March that identified, apprehended, and initiated prosecution against some of the most violent offenders in the Springfield and Joplin metropolitan areas.

On Nov. 25, 2025, Joplin, Mo. Police Officers responded to a report of gun shots being fired. Upon arrival, officers conducted a traffic stop in the parking lot of a local storage facility. The driver was identified as Gibbs. As officers investigated, they located an empty shell casing near the storage unit owned by Gibbs. Officers observed a handgun partially underneath the driver’s seat of Gibbs’ vehicle. Gibbs was found in possession of two firearms, a Glock 43x, 9mm firearm, and a Smith and Wesson Model Airweight, .380 caliber firearm. Gibbs admitted he was a convicted felon and he knowingly and illegally possessed firearms in violation of federal law.

This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Patrick Carney. It was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) and the Joplin, Missouri Police Department.
title: Springfield Man Sentenced to 48 Months for Being a Felon in Possession of a Firearm

Seattle– The 64-year-old owner of a small Tacoma market will appear tomorrow in U.S. District Court in Tacoma after being returned from India, where he fled after being indicted for wire fraud in connection with his food stamp fraud scheme, announced Acting U.S. Attorney Charles Neil Floyd. Manjit Bedi, of Kent, Washington, pleaded not guilty on April 22, 2026, and within a week had fled the United States to his native India.

On September 3, 2026, Bedi was added to the FBI’s “Most Wanted Fraudster” list with his image and information on the case disseminated internationally. Law enforcement in India quickly took Bedi into custody. He was turned over to federal agents and arrived in the

Western District of Washington last night.

“I commend the work of the FBI and international partners to get Mr. Bedi back to the U.S. to face justice,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Neil Floyd. “We will ask the court to detain him pending trial as he has demonstrated he has the will and the means to flee. Those who take advantage of America’s generosity must be held accountable.”

“The arrest and return of Manjit Singh Bedi marks yet another significant moment for the historic FBI’s Most Wanted Fraudsters program,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “Bedi is one of six Most Wanted Fraudsters captured since the creation of the new list three months ago – and yet another high value target captured overseas – he is in a group responsible for more than a combined $2 billion in fraud and has been on the run for almost 4,000 days collectively prior to arrest. He is charged with defrauding the U.S. of at least $600k in SNAP funds from approximately 2024 to 2025 and now will face justice for his alleged crimes. This is the latest in a tremendously successful run of returning high value targets to the U.S. by engaging with foreign partners – with over 260 removal actions in just 20 months, up over approximately 70% from the previous period. Thank you to FBI Seattle, as well our brilliant law enforcement partners here in the U.S. and in India, for assisting in securing Bedi’s return.”

“This fraudster tried to escape justice by fleeing to his home country of India. Now the long arm of the law has brought him back to the United States to face the consequences for his crimes,” said USDA Inspector General John Walk. “Stealing SNAP benefits – food assistance benefits intended for low-income Americans – is wrong and no matter where they run, we will not stop pursuing those who perpetrate these crimes against the poorest Americans and the American taxpayer.”

“Thanks to the hard work of FBI Seattle investigators and our international law enforcement partners, as well as tips from the public about the subject's whereabouts, Mr. Bedi has been returned to the United States to face justice in a Tacoma courtroom,” said W. Mike Herrington, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI Seattle field office. “No matter how far someone may flee and no matter how long it may take, the FBI is committed to pursuing those who attempt to outrun the consequences of their criminal actions, even when they seek to evade the justice system by hiding overseas.”

The Department of Justice has created the National Fraud Enforcement Division . The core mission of the Fraud Division is to zealously investigate and prosecute those who steal or fraudulently misuse taxpayer dollars. Department of Justice efforts to combat fraud support President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

According to the indictment, Bedi owned and operated a small grocery store in Tacoma. In February 2024, the store was authorized to accept Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits – formerly known as food stamps. The indictment alleges that beginning in March 2024, Bedi agreed to provide SNAP recipients with cash in exchange for the money loaded on their electronic benefits card (EBT) at a rate of 50 cents on the dollar. For example, Bedi would charge $200 against a recipient’s EBT card, providing $100 in cash to the recipient and keeping the recipient’s other $100 as profit. The indictment alleges that between March 2024 and June 2025, when his fraud was discovered, Bedi pocketed at least $600,000 in SNAP benefits for food items that were never sold.

Both wire fraud and SNAP benefit fraud are punishable by up to twenty years in prison and a $250,000 fine.

The charges contained in the indictment are only allegations. A person is presumed innocent unless and until he or she is proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

The case was investigated by the U.S. Department of Agriculture Office of Inspector General (USDA-OIG), the FBI, and the Washington State Department of Social and Health Services (DSHS).

The FBI launched the Most Wanted Fraudsters list with 8 individuals on June 4, 2026, a new wanted list dedicated to publicly identifying individuals charged with defrauding the American people. Since then, 18 people have been added in total, and 6 have been captured. As of October 14, 2026, 12 individuals are included on the list, but no set number are featured at any given time. The list is separate from the FBI's Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list and is intended to increase visibility and generate information that may assist law enforcement in locating wanted fraud suspects. Learn more about the list: FBI Announces New Wanted List Dedicated to Fraudsters

The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Victoria Cantore. The Department of Justice’s Office of International Affairs assisted with the return of Bedi from India.
title: Owner of Tacoma grocery store, who fled when indicted for food stamp fraud, returned from India to face charges
