PHILADELPHIA – U.S. Attorney David Metcalf announced that Charles Weiner, 79, of Penn Valley, Pennsylvania, was charged by indictment with one count of conspiracy to defraud the United States, 22 counts of willful failure to withhold and pay over employment taxes, and six counts of aiding and assisting the filing of false tax returns.

The indictment is part of the Department of Justice’s first-ever National Tax Enforcement Surge, a month-long initiative involving the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section and U.S. Attorneys’ Offices across the country. The surge of nationwide resources resulted in prosecutorial actions against 76 defendants whose alleged and proven crimes intended an estimated loss of revenue to the federal government of more than $490,000,000.

As detailed in the Weiner indictment, the defendant owned two restaurants, Max’s Steaks & Eagle Bar and Clock Bar, both located on the same block of Germantown Avenue in Philadelphia. He controlled all financial matters related to the restaurants and was responsible for withholding Social Security, Medicare, and income taxes from employees’ wages and paying those funds over to the IRS, as well as filing quarterly employment tax returns with the IRS.

The indictment alleges that, from the first quarter of 2019 through the first quarter of 2023, Weiner and two others working at his direction paid wages to employees of the restaurants all or partly in cash, with Weiner then providing the restaurants’ accountant with only a part of the wages paid to employees. As a result, the restaurants’ quarterly tax returns that the accountant filed with the IRS during this period were false.

The indictment further alleges that Weiner also supplied the accountant false information regarding the amount of food and drink supplies purchased for the restaurants. As a result, Weiner also caused the annual corporate tax returns filed for the restaurants to be false.

If convicted, the defendant faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison for conspiracy, five years in prison for each count of willful failure to withhold and pay over employment taxes, and three years in prison for each count of aiding and assisting the filing of false tax returns.

On April 7, 2026, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division. The core mission of the Fraud Division is to zealously investigate and prosecute those who steal or fraudulently misuse taxpayer dollars. Department of Justice efforts to combat fraud support President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within federal benefit programs.

This case was investigated by IRS Criminal Investigation and is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Eric D. Gill and Trial Attorney Michael C. Vasiliadis of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section.

The charges and allegations contained in the indictment are merely accusations. Every defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty in court.
title: Philadelphia Restaurateur Indicted for Employment Tax Fraud

DEL RIO, Texas – An illegal alien from Honduras pleaded guilty in Del Rio today to possession of child pornography, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas.

According to court documents, on March 12, 2025, Herman Daniel Diaz-Aguilera, 26, was pulled over by a Texas Department of Public Safety (TX DPS) Trooper in Dimmit County for defective headlights. Diaz-Aguilera provided the Trooper with a Honduran identification card instead of a driver’s license. A subsequent immigration inspection by a U.S. Border Patrol agent determined Diaz-Aguilera was an illegal alien from Honduras, and he was taken to the Carrizo Springs Border Patrol station for further processing.

Diaz-Aguilera stated he was working as a scout for an alien smuggler and was going to be paid $2,000 for each person smuggled into the United States. A search of his cell phone revealed a video depicting a minor engaged in a sexual act. Further investigation led to Diaz-Aguilera admitting he was a member of a WhatsApp group chat, from which he received and saved the child sexual abuse material. A forensic analysis of the phone revealed multiple image files and seven video files depicting the sexual assault of infants and toddlers along with approximately 95 images and 301 videos depicting children engaged in sexually explicit conduct.

On Oct. 15, 2026, Diaz-Aguilera pleaded guilty to one count of possession of child pornography and faces up to 20 years in federal prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement Homeland Security Investigations, TX DPS, and U.S. Border Patrol investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Nallely Duarte is prosecuting the case.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC .

###
title: Illegal Alien Pleads Guilty in Del Rio to Possessing Child Pornography, Faces Up To 20 Years in Federal Prison

BLM Announces December 2026 Sale of Oil and Gas Leases in Utah
Organization:
Media Contact:
SALT LAKE CITY – The Bureau of Land Management today announced an oil and gas lease sale scheduled for Dec. 17, 2026, to offer 43 oil and gas parcels totaling 74,550 acres in Utah.
The BLM completed scoping on these parcels in July 2026 and held a public comment period that closed in September 2026 on the parcels and the related environmental analysis. A 30-day public protest period to receive additional public input opened today and will close Nov. 16, 2026.
Leasing is the first step in the process to develop federal oil and gas resources. Before development operations can begin, an operator must submit an application for permit to drill detailing development plans. The BLM reviews applications for permits to drill, posts them for public review, conducts an environmental analysis and coordinates with state partners and stakeholders.
All parcels that are included in a federal oil and gas lease sale include appropriate stipulations to protect important natural resources. Information on current and upcoming BLM leases is available through the National Fluid Lease Sale System. BLM lease sales are held online through Efficient Markets.
The parcels BLM analyzed, as well as maps and instructions on how to submit a protest, are available on BLM’s ePlanning website at: https://eplanning.blm.gov/Project-Home/?id=E4A3C93E-E468-F111-A824-001DD8029ED0.
The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.
title: BLM Announces December 2026 Sale of Oil and Gas Leases in Utah

PHILADELPHIA – United States Attorney David Metcalf announced that Shane Hennen, aka “Sugar Shane,” 41, of Las Vegas, Nevada, and Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, entered a plea of guilty before United States District Judge Nitza I. Quiñones Alejandro on Wednesday to bribery in sporting contests, conspiracy to commit wire fraud, and three counts of wire fraud, arising from a years-long scheme to influence or “fix” Chinese Basketball Association (“CBA”) games and National Collegiate Athletic Association (“NCAA”) men’s Division I basketball games. The defendant was charged by indictment in January of this year in the Eastern District of Pennsylvania (“EDPA”).

In addition, Hennen pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and conspiracy to commit money laundering, as charged by superseding indictment in May of this year in the Eastern District of New York (“EDNY”). Those charges arose from his participation in a scheme to defraud betting companies by wagering on National Basketball Association (“NBA”) games with the improper benefit of having non-public information that would affect the outcome of those games and the performance of certain individuals in those games, and his participation in laundering the proceeds.

As detailed in court filings, beginning in or about September 2022, Hennen and others worked together in a scheme that involved recruiting and bribing players to help fix CBA games through point-shaving during the 2022-2023 season. Hennen’s primary role in the scheme was to place bets and arrange for others to place large bets on the fixed games — betting against the teams whose players they had bribed to underperform.

After profiting on the CBA games, the schemers turned their attention to NCAA men’s basketball games. During the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 seasons, fixers agreed to recruit NCAA players who would accept bribe payments in exchange for helping to influence outcomes of NCAA basketball games. In particular, the fixers agreed to recruit into the scheme players who would help ensure that their team failed to cover the spread of the first half of a game or an entire game.

In total, the bribery and point-shaving scheme involved more than 39 players, on over 17 different NCAA Division I men’s basketball teams, who fixed and attempted to fix more than 29 NCAA games. The scheme also resulted in more than $3 million in fraudulent wagers placed on these games, and more than $1.1 million in financial losses to sportsbooks throughout the country.

In the EDNY prosecution, conspirators obtained insider information from several NBA players and coaches and distributed that information through a network of bettors, including Hennen. Hennen and others then placed and directed wagers through online sportsbooks and retail betting outlets, falsely representing that their wagers complied with the betting companies’ rules — which included not betting on non-public information or using straw bettors — while concealing that their wagers were based on confidential team information.

The defendant is scheduled to be sentenced on February 25 in Philadelphia. In the EDPA case, he faces a maximum possible sentence of 85 years’ imprisonment, three years of supervised release, a monetary fine, and restitution. In the EDNY case, Hennen faces a maximum possible sentence of 40 years’ imprisonment, three years of supervised release, a monetary fine, and restitution.

The CBA and NCAA game-fixing case was investigated by FBI Philadelphia, with valuable assistance from FBI New York and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of New York. The NBA sports betting and money laundering case was investigated by FBI New York and the New York Police Department. Assistant United States Attorneys Louis D. Lappen and Jerome M. Maiatico are prosecuting for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania.
title: High-Stakes Sports Gambler Pleads Guilty in Connection With CBA/NCAA Bribery and Game-Fixing Scheme, NBA Betting and Money Laundering Conspiracy

HOUSTON – A 32-year-old Indian national has admitted to conspiracy to commit mail fraud.

Sumit Kumar Singh admitted he participated in the scheme while serving a federal sentence for a previous mail fraud conviction involving elderly victims.

In 2025, Singh obtained a contraband cell phone while incarcerated and used it to communicate with others involved in the mail fraud and money laundering conspiracy targeting elderly victims.

As part of the scheme, fraudsters posed as PayPal representatives or federal government agents and falsely told victims they needed to send money that would later be returned to them.

One victim, a 93-year-old North Dakota woman, was instructed to mail a $45,000 check after being falsely told Attorney General Pam Bondi would help her obtain a new identification card and return her money.

From inside federal prison, Singh used the contraband phone to send messages to a phone number in India, including a photo of a bank receipt showing the victim’s check had been deposited in Edinburg.

U.S. District Judge George C. Hanks Jr. accepted the plea and set sentencing for Dec. 21. At that time, Singh faces up to five years in federal prison and a possible $250,000 maximum fine.

He has been and will remain in custody pending sentencing.

The U.S. Postal Inspection Service conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Belinda Beek is prosecuting the case with valuable assistance from AUSAs Whitney Ohlausen and Lesley Brooks in the Northern District of Texas.
title: Indian national pleads guilty in elderly fraud scheme while in prison

HOUSTON – A 46-year-old man has been convicted of possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine and unlawful possession of a firearm by a convicted felon.

A federal jury deliberated for approximately two hours before convicting Eduardo Nevares Oct. 8 following a two-day trial.

At trial, the jury heard that law enforcement attempted to stop Nevares for an expired vehicle registration.

Nevares refused to pull over and led authorities on a chase that ended when he crashed through two chain-link fences and his vehicle stalled on a baseball field at an Alief, Texas public school.

He then attempted to flee on foot before authorities apprehended him.

Law enforcement discovered a .45-caliber pistol on the driver’s seat and methamphetamine and cocaine in his pocket.

A subsequent search of the vehicle revealed more than a pound of methamphetamine with a purity level of 96%, along with baggies, a scale, and loaded pistol magazines.

The defense argued Nevares was unaware of the methamphetamine inside a black duffle bag in the back seat. However, the jury rejected that argument and found him guilty as charged.

U.S. District Judge David Hittner presided over the trial and set sentencing for Dec. 29. At that time, Nevares faces up to life in prison and a possible maximum $10 million fine.

Nevares has been and will remain in custody pending sentencing.

The Bureau for Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, and Houston Police Department conducted the investigation with the assistance of the Drug Enforcement Administration South Central Laboratory. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Charles Hagerman and Tanja Titre are prosecuting the case.
title: Houston felon convicted of trafficking methamphetamine and possessing firearm

PLANO, Texas – A Serbian national has been sentenced to federal prison as part of a Homeland Security Task Force investigation into cocaine trafficking in the Eastern District of Texas, announced U.S. Attorney Jay R. Combs.

Milan Tanovic, 59, also known as Marco, a Serbian national living in Spain, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute cocaine while aboard a vessel subject to the jurisdiction of the United States and was sentenced to 204 months in federal prison by U.S. District Judge Sean D. Jordan on October 15, 2026.

According to information presented in court, Tanovic was identified as a large-scale cocaine trafficker who worked with other drug traffickers based in Serbia and Albania to ship ton amounts of cocaine from South America to Europe, using container vessels. Tanovic was connected to multiple drug shipment seizures through analysis of multiple chats on an encrypted messaging platform.

This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Dallas comprises agents and officers from the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Dallas Field Office; U.S. Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Homeland Security Investigations - Dallas (ICE-HSI); Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Dallas Field Division; Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) Dallas Field Division; Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigations (IRS-CD; United States Postal Service, United States Postal Inspection Service (USPIS); Transportation Security Administration, Federal Air Marshal Service (FAMS); United States Secret Service (USSS); Department of State, Bureau of Diplomatic Security (DSS); TEXOMA HIDTA; DEA Country Offices in Rome (Italy), Brasilia (Brazil), Santa Domingo (Dominican Republic), Madrid (Spain), Vienna (Austria), Zagreb (Croatia), and Bogota (Colombia); EUROPOL; and U.S. Marshals Service (USMS) Eastern District of Texas with the prosecution being led by Eastern District of Texas Assistant U.S. Attorney Wes Wynne.

###
title: Serbian national sentenced to 17 years in federal prison as part of Homeland Security Task Force investigation into international cocaine trafficking conspiracy

Rep. Torres Announces Power To The Players Act, Legislation to Ensure Gamers Own Their Games
Today, Rep. Ritchie Torres (NY-15) announced he will introduce the Power To The Players Act, legislation that would direct the Federal Trade Commission to establish regulations protecting consumers’ ability to own and play the video games they purchase.
Over the past few years, video game companies have moved toward digital-only games and consoles, removing the option to buy or use physical games. These digital games are often sold as revocable licenses rather than owned outright, leaving players dependent on the company’s continued support. NBA 2K25 is a clear example. The game, which retailed for $69.99 for the standard edition and $99.99 for the All-Star Edition, will be delisted from digital storefronts on October 30 and will have its online servers shut down on December 31, only two years after its initial release. No consumer should have a game they paid for pulled out from under them on a company’s arbitrary timeline.
“When you pay for a game, you should own it,” said Rep. Torres. “Consumers must have the right to own, the right to play, and the right to transfer the games they buy. A game that can be taken away the moment a company pulls the plug is not a purchase. It is a rental disguised as a sale. Families in the Bronx and across the country save up to buy these games, and they deserve better than a license that can vanish at any time. The Power To The Players Act ensures consumers own what they buy and can keep playing long after a company moves on.”
Under the bill, buying a video game would give the consumer ownership of the game rather than a license to play it. Games with online functionality would also be required to provide an offline mode before the servers supporting them are shut down.
The legislation aims to close the gap between buying a game and owning it. By preserving consumers’ ability to own and resell their games, the bill would ensure that players can keep playing the games they paid for with friends and family for years to come.
title: Rep. Torres Announces Power To The Players Act, Legislation to Ensure Gamers Own Their Games

EPA completes cleanup of former hospital site in Colorado
EPA addressed asbestos-containing material and demolition debris in Walsenburg
DENVER – Today, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) announced the completion of a response action in Walsenburg, Colorado, to clean up and properly dispose of asbestos-containing material (ACM) and fire-damaged debris from a former hospital site and abandoned residence. The cleanup removed 1,520 cubic yards of ACM and contaminated debris, reducing the risk of asbestos fibers being released into the environment and helping prepare the site for future redevelopment.
“Cleaning up contaminated properties is essential to protecting human health and the environment, and it plays a critical role in community revitalization," said EPA Regional Administrator Cyrus Western. "By removing asbestos and debris from this site, EPA is reducing risks today and helping create a safer, stronger future for Walsenburg."
Following an October 2023 fire at the former hospital, Huerfano County Economic Development used an EPA Brownfields assessment grant to complete environmental site assessments. In July 2026, at the request of Huerfano County and Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment (CDPHE), EPA initiated an emergency response removal at the former Lamme Hospital site.
"Huerfano County is grateful to the US EPA for their assistance cleaning up the old Lamme Hospital,” said Huerfano County Board Chair Karl Sporleder. “This effort has removed hazardous materials from the property and marks an important step toward transforming this corner into a safer, more vibrant space for the community and downtown businesses.”
EPA mobilized to the site on September 17, and the response was completed on October 10. During the response EPA conducted particulate and asbestos air monitoring to ensure asbestos fibers did not migrate off site and ACM debris was transported for disposal to a permitted landfill in Pueblo.
By removing ACM and contaminated debris from the site, the cleanup reduced the potential for asbestos fibers to become airborne and protected the community from the health risks associated with asbestos exposure.
EPA and CDPHE remain available to respond to questions and will coordinate with Huerfano County if needed. For more information, please visit EPA's Old Hospital Asbestos webpage.
Learn more about EPA’s emergency response program.
title: EPA completes cleanup of former hospital site in Colorado

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) today introduced the American Integrity Act to prohibit the live-streaming of executions under the Uniformed Code of Military Justice following President Donald Trump’s decision to cancel Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth’s plans to broadcast the execution of Nidal Hasan, the perpetrator of the horrific 2009 Fort Hood shooting.
The bill would establish a federal prohibition on live-streaming military executions, ensuring that such broadcasts cannot be authorized by future administrations.
The legislation comes after widespread opposition to the proposal, including from Vindman, who publicly called on Hegseth to reverse course and abandon plans to turn Hasan’s execution into a public spectacle.
“Having overseen the post-trial legal proceedings in Nidal Hasan’s case, I know firsthand the gravity of his horrific crimes. I believed then, and I believe now, that he should face the fullest consequences of the law,” said Vindman. “But there is a fundamental difference between carrying out justice and turning an execution into a public spectacle. Live-streaming executions is what terrorists and authoritarian regimes do. I’m glad the president ultimately reversed course, but we should never have reached this point in the first place. The American justice system must uphold the rule of law and the dignity of our institutions. My legislation will ensure that no future administration can turn an execution into a televised spectacle.”
The bill is sponsored by U.S. Representatives Reps. Ro Khanna (Calif.-17), Maggie Goodlander (N.H.-02), and George Whitesides (Calif.-27).
Click here to read the full bill text.
BACKGROUND
As an Army Judge Advocate General (JAG) officer, Vindman oversaw the post-trial legal proceedings following Hasan’s attack at Fort Hood. His direct involvement in the case gave him firsthand experience with the gravity of Hasan’s crimes and the importance of ensuring justice is carried out.
###
title: Vindman Leads Effort in U.S. House to Ban Live-Streaming of Military Executions in the United States

Liberian Child Rapist Convicted of Naturalization Fraud, Denaturalized, and Judicially Ordered Removed from the U.S.
NEW BERN, N.C. — U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services assisted in an investigation that resulted in the sentencing of Cyril Domaquik Clemens, 72, a native of Liberia, for naturalization fraud. On Sept. 17, a federal judge sentenced Clemens to time served. The court also revoked Clemens’ naturalized U.S. citizenship and judicially ordered him to self-deport at his own expense. Clemens pleaded guilty to naturalization fraud on June 18. U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of North Carolina Ellis Boyle made the announcement.
Clemens knowingly made materially false statements under penalty of perjury on his naturalization application and during his naturalization interview with USCIS. He falsely responded “No” when asked whether he had ever been involved in forcing, or attempting to force, another person to engage in sexual contact or relations. He also falsely answered “No” when asked whether he had ever committed, assisted in committing, or attempted to commit a crime or offense for which he had not been arrested. Clemens became a naturalized U.S. citizen on Feb. 19, 2021.
On April 3, 2023, in North Carolina Superior Court, Durham County, Clemens pleaded guilty to three counts of indecent liberties with a child. A state judge sentenced him to a term of imprisonment ranging from 1 year and 4 months to 2 years and 5 months and ordered him to register as a sex offender. Clemens confessed to sexually molesting the child for more than a decade, from Nov. 1, 2011, through March 7, 2022. The child was a 4-year-old girl when the abuse began. Clemens committed these crimes before submitting his naturalization application and providing false statements to USCIS. However, he was not arrested until after he naturalized. At the time USCIS approved Clemens’ naturalization application, officials were unaware of his offenses.
Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s Homeland Security Investigations and Enforcement and Removal Operations personnel assigned to the Document and Benefit Fraud Task Force, along with USCIS’ Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate, investigated the case. It is part of Operation False Haven, an ongoing initiative designed to aggressively target child molesters and other egregious felons who fraudulently obtain immigration benefits.
To report suspected immigration benefit fraud or abuse to USCIS, please use the USCIS Tip Form.
For more information on USCIS and its programs, please visit uscis.gov or follow us on X, Instagram, YouTube, Facebook and LinkedIn.
title: Liberian Child Rapist Convicted of Naturalization Fraud, Denaturalized, and Judicially Ordered Removed from the U.S.

Gov Watchdog Finds National Security Gaps in Mining of Critical Minerals on America’s Public Lands
GAO could not confirm that seven of 15 sampled mining companies were incorporated in the United States, finds major gaps in what the government knows about foreign investment in mining on federal lands
Washington, D.C. – As the United States races to reduce its reliance on foreign countries for critical minerals, the federal government has been handing out exclusive rights to mine America’s public lands without checking whether the people and companies receiving those rights meet the requirements to hold them, even allowing companies with ties to our adversaries to mine our public lands according to two new Government Accountability Office (GAO) reports released today by Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.), Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-Ill.), Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández (D-N.M.), Rep. Joe Neguse (D-Colo.), and Rep. Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.).
Federal law reserves mining claims on public lands for U.S. citizens and companies incorporated in the United States. The Bureau of Land Management, which runs the mining claim system, does not collect citizenship information from claimants, does not record whether they qualify, and rarely checks in the first place. A BLM official told GAO that companies from foreign adversary nations could hold claims on federal lands through U.S. subsidiaries, and claimants do not have to disclose whether a foreign company or government owns part of them.
When GAO reviewed a sample of 15 companies holding mining claims, investigators found no evidence that seven of them were incorporated in the United States, as the law requires. When GAO asked BLM for help confirming where these companies were incorporated, the agency had no additional information to offer.
In a second report, GAO reviewed ownership information for 43 operators of critical minerals mines on federal lands and found that at least 25 were subsidiaries of foreign entities. In at least two cases, Chinese entities had a financial interest in the parent companies.
Mining claims grant the exclusive right to extract minerals such as copper and gold, royalty-free, for as long as the holder pays annual fees. Claimants do not have to disclose whether a foreign company or government owns part of them. Australia and Canada, two of the world’s top mineral producers, require foreign investors to disclose their owners and have forced some to sell stakes in critical minerals companies on national security grounds.
GAO recommends that the Bureau of Land Management collect citizenship information from mining claimants and document that they qualify.
Background
The United States depends heavily on foreign countries for critical minerals such as copper and lithium, which go into everything from electric vehicle batteries and power lines to phones and medical equipment. GAO has warned that this dependence leaves supply chains open to disruption by adversary nations. Federal lands cover nearly one-third of the country and are a significant source of these minerals.
Under the General Mining Act of 1872, individuals and companies stake claims on most federal lands without agency approval, and BLM has recorded an average of more than 60,000 new claims every year since 2021. Since 2025, President Trump has issued a series of executive orders to expand mining on federal lands and cut reliance on foreign minerals. GAO’s findings show his administration has not taken the most basic step to keep those minerals in the right hands: confirming who holds the claims and preventing our adversaries from taking our resources. A secure domestic supply of critical minerals starts with knowing who controls the mines on public lands.
###

GYPSUM, Colo. — The Colorado Army National Guard is playing a critical role in humanity’s return to the moon by partnering with NASA to train astronauts for upcoming crewed missions to the moon’s south pole region.
At the High-Altitude Army National Guard Aviation Training Site, or HAATS, military aviators use Colorado’s rugged terrain to replicate the challenging flight conditions of the lunar environment and help prepare crews to land safely on the moon’s surface.
Doug Wheelock, NASA astronaut and co-chair of the Human Landing System joint test panel, said the undulating ridges and deep craters of the moon’s south pole are remarkably similar to Colorado’s mountainous terrain. The Colorado mountains are an essential training environment because they help astronauts learn to recognize and overcome visual tricks the landscape plays, such as misjudging how far away an object is or losing sight of the true horizon.
The specialized training program, certified by NASA and the HAATS team in August 2025, focuses on high-stakes scenarios and controlling a helicopter in difficult environments.
U.S. Army Chief Warrant Officer 4 Ethan Jacobs, an instructor pilot at HAATS, said the training exposes astronauts to visual illusions, crew communication under stress and low-visibility conditions caused by kicked-up dust and snow. Operating in a high-risk flight environment helps prepare astronauts for perceived danger and the mental overload they will face while landing a spacecraft never before tested on the moon.
“You can put pilots in a simulator and have them do all this stuff, but there’s no risk to them,” Jacobs said. “Here, we are in a regime where there’s a little bit more skin in the game. It’s not a one-for-one for landing on the moon, but we can basically inoculate them against the perceived risk that they’re in.”
About 25 astronauts have completed the foundational training program through the partnership, which began in summer 2021. Future moon crews are scheduled to attend a two-week program at HAATS to practice teamwork and refine cockpit communication.
Wheelock emphasized how vital the Colorado Army National Guard’s specialized expertise and location are to NASA’s mission success.
“The skills they’re teaching out here about power management are exactly what we need,” Wheelock said. “We can't get this anywhere else. To us, it's been sort of our gemstone in our training architecture right now.”
The partnership benefits the Colorado Army National Guard as much as NASA. Working alongside space agency experts gives Colorado Army National Guard pilots new perspectives in the air, helping them sharpen their training programs and flight instruction.
“The Colorado Army National Guard is grateful for the opportunity to support NASA as humanity prepares to return to the moon,” said U.S. Army Lt. Col. Muriel Missler, state Army aviation officer. “Flying in Colorado’s challenging high-altitude terrain requires rigorous power management, seamless crew coordination and constant adaptability. We are truly honored to work alongside the NASA team and share our training environment to help prepare the Moon crews for mission success.”
NASA plans to complete its first crewed lunar landing in 2028.
title: Colorado Guard helps prepare astronauts for lunar landings

Lofgren Demands Answers to Outstanding Oversight Requests, Warns EPA that Lack of Cooperation is Unacceptable
(Washington, DC) - On Tuesday, Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren (D-CA) sent a letter to Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin demanding that he comply with outstanding congressional oversight requests from the Committee.
“Since January 2025, I have sent a number of formal oversight letters to EPA requesting agency records, documents, and communications regarding various policies and activities,” writes Ranking Member Lofgren in her letter. “However, rather than providing the requested information in a comprehensive and timely manner, EPA has failed to produce a single responsive document, communication, or record.”
In closing, she writes: “EPA’s non-responsiveness to Committee oversight during the 119th Congress has been unacceptable. The agency must respect congressional prerogatives. We remain determined to obtain the information we need to perform our duties on behalf of the American people. EPA should understand that a lack of cooperation will not frustrate the Committee’s oversight permanently. It will merely strengthen our commitment to employing all the tools at our disposal to hold the agency accountable.”
In her letter, Ranking Member Lofgren requires a response from EPA to the Committee’s outstanding oversight requests by no later than 5:00 pm Friday, November 6th, 2026.
Access the letter here and below.
Dear Administrator Zeldin,
Agencies are required to comply with congressional oversight. It is an obligation, not a choice. But under your leadership, the EPA appears to have forgotten that basic principle. Since President Trump took office in January 2025, I have made multiple requests to the agency for internal records, documents, and communications related to various topics. These oversight requests are crucial to my ability to properly carry out my oversight duties as the Ranking Member of the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, which possesses jurisdiction over environmental research and development programs at EPA. However, rather than providing the requested information in a comprehensive and timely manner, EPA has failed to produce a single responsive document, communication, or record. Instead, the agency has merely responded with letters that deflect questions rather than answering them. That was never acceptable. It becomes less tolerable with each passing month. I am writing to you to reaffirm my prior oversight requests from the 119th Congress, and to formally notify the agency that they remain outstanding. I expect EPA to promptly comply.
Since your confirmation as the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) on January 29th, 2025, roughly 20% of the agency’s workforce has quit, retired, or been fired. Irreplaceable laboratory facilities have been shut down. The independent Office of Research and Development (ORD) has been wiped out. Scientific capacity has been gutted, scientific integrity is compromised, industry capture is widespread, and climate denialism is ascendant. In short, EPA’s basic mission to use the best available science to protect human health and the environment has been damaged under your leadership.
To take just one of countless examples, I have learned that the Office of Air and Radiation (OAR), acting under direct orders from former Assistant Administrator Aaron Szabo, has refused to grant the Office of Applied Sciences and Environmental Solutions (OASES) permission to conduct or publish virtually any air pollution research without prior approval from OAR political leadership. OASES is the ostensible successor to ORD, which was a global scientific leader in air quality and air pollution research. It is my understanding that OAR has categorically denied OASES the authority to conduct and publish its own air-related research without OAR political approval, except for narrow circumstances in which technical support from OASES cannot be avoided for OAR to meet certain statutory obligations. Indeed, OASES cannot even independently initiate air-related research without approval from OAR political appointees. OAR can only assert this control because of the agency’s new “no surprises” policy for OASES, which appallingly requires that OASES research “must be supported by appropriate political leadership” before it can proceed. The policy is a clear violation of scientific integrity, and the notion that EPA’s primary science office cannot even study air pollution without getting permission from the political appointees of a different office would be laughable if it was not so dangerous.
In my role as the Ranking Member of the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (“the Committee”), I have attempted to conduct oversight of these types of actions. There are many reasons for this oversight: to document the damage done to the agency and its workforce; to understand the scientific capabilities that have been lost and the implications of those losses for human health and the American people; to identify violations of scientific integrity and administrative procedure; and to comprehend why all of this happened in order to inform legislative efforts to reverse it and prevent it from ever happening again. Since January 2025, I have sent a number of formal oversight letters to EPA requesting agency records, documents, and communications regarding various policies and activities. The agency has been non-responsive to my requests and has utterly failed to comply. I am now reaffirming these oversight requests to provide the agency with a second opportunity to demonstrate the appropriate degree of deference and respect for congressional prerogatives. I expect EPA’s full and prompt responsiveness to each of the requests detailed below, which are long overdue:
1. Agency RIF and Reorganization Plans (ARRPs)
On March 26th, 2025, I sent a letter to EPA along with several other Democratic Committee Members requesting that the agency “provide the Committee with your Agency RIF and Reorganization Plan immediately upon transmitting it to OMB and the Office of Personnel Management (OPM).” The context for this request was the revelation that EPA’s ARRP proposed to “eliminate the Office of Research and Development as an EPA National Program Office” while pushing “a majority (50-75%)” of ORD’s employees out of the agency. Of course, that is exactly what happened. But EPA never provided its Phase One and Phase Two ARRPs to the Committee, which has hindered the Committee’s ability to understand the motivations and decisions that led to the elimination of ORD. For instance, information revealed last year in a lawsuit related to agency ARRPs appeared to suggest that disagreements may have existed between EPA and the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) regarding the elimination of ORD. Without reviewing the ARRPs themselves, the Committee cannot properly assess the agency’s position towards ORD and the bureaucratic actions that contributed to its demise.
2. Laboratory Budget and Staffing Levels
On May 27th, 2025, I sent a letter to EPA along with Environment Subcommittee Ranking Member Gabe Amo requesting that the agency “share the projected post-reorganization budget and staffing levels for each of the facilities that will remain open.” The “facilities” in this case referred specifically to the ten field laboratory and research facilities managed by ORD. These research laboratories are a crown jewel of EPA science, and the agency’s intention to eliminate ORD had raised the alarming prospect that the laboratories might be shut down as well. EPA has not subsequently acted to do so, and the laboratories appear to be continuing under the management of different program offices. But while I am relieved that they continue to operate, I remain concerned that staffing shortages and reduced scientific capabilities at the former ORD laboratories could undermine their ability to appropriately study environmental hazards. EPA’s unwillingness to provide basic budgetary and personnel information for its research laboratories impedes the Committee’s ability to evaluate whether they remain capable of supporting core agency activities.
3. Endangerment Finding Repeal Documents and Communications
On August 18th, 2025, I sent a letter to EPA along with Environment Subcommittee Ranking Member Amo requesting that the agency provide “all documents and communications” exchanged between EPA and OMB, the Department of Energy (DOE), and the Trump Vance 2025 Transition Team, regarding “the repeal of the Endangerment Finding.” I also requested “all documents and communications” exchanged between EPA and DOE regarding the report developed by DOE’s Climate Working Group, and “all documents and communications” within EPA regarding “the agency’s review of the scientific basis for the proposal to repeal the Endangerment Finding.” These oversight requests relate to the repeal of the 2009 Greenhouse Gas Endangerment Finding, which the agency proposed in July 2025 and finalized in February 2026. I continue to have concerns about potential violations of administrative law in the agency’s rulemaking process to repeal the Endangerment Finding. The documents and communications that I requested are central to the Committee’s ability to conduct oversight of the agency’s actions. EPA’s refusal to provide them only strengthens my belief that these records remain highly material to my review and must be disclosed without delay.
4. Status of PFNA IRIS Assessment
Dr. Maureen Gwinn, the EPA Deputy Associate Administrator for Science, testified before the Science Committee’s Subcommittee on Environment on June 4th, 2026. The subject of her testimony was OASES and the general status of environmental research and development at the agency after the elimination of ORD. During that hearing, I questioned Dr. Gwinn about the agency’s decision earlier in 2026 to disavow chemical assessments conducted by the Integrated Risk Information System (IRIS). In particular, I asked about the status of the IRIS assessment for PFNA, which press reports indicate has been fully completed for more than a year but which the agency refuses to finalize and publish. In response, Dr. Gwinn told me that she was “not sure of the details on that” and said that she would “have to get back to you.” She also stated that she would “go back and confirm” the status of the PFNA assessment. While that hearing took place over four months ago, the agency has not provided any subsequent information regarding the PFNA assessment and whether it ever intends to finalize and publish the assessment, nor has it offered any scientific justification for refusing to do so. I continue to seek clarity on whether the IRIS assessment for PFNA, a dangerous and highly toxic PFAS chemical, will ever see the light of day under this administration.
5. Administration Delays of Environmental Research
At the same June 4th Environment Subcommittee hearing with Dr. Gwinn, one of my colleagues, Representative Suzanne Bonamici, questioned Dr. Gwinn about whether the agency under its current leadership had sought to delay or suppress any environmental research due to its perceived lack of alignment with administration priorities. Specifically, Representative Bonamici asked whether “any proposed research products, even one, [had] been delayed, modified, or declined because they did not align with the priorities set by political appointees?” In response, Dr. Gwinn acknowledged that “there have been delays” due to the agency’s review of whether certain research products complied with President Trump’s various Executive Orders. But when Representative Bonamici followed up and directly asked “what was the topic of the research,” pertaining to research that had been halted, Dr. Gwinn could only respond that she would “have to get back to you on that.” The agency has not provided any further information regarding which specific research topics were “delayed, modified, or declined” due to the political directives of agency leadership. This information is highly material to the Committee’s ability to understand the current state of scientific integrity at EPA, as well as the role played by political appointees in influencing the environmental research being conducted by the agency.
In summary, the following oversight requests remain outstanding and require compliance on the part of the agency. Please produce the requested records no later than 5:00 PM on Friday, November 6th, 2026:
1. Please provide to the Committee the EPA’s Agency RIF and Reorganization Plans (ARRPs) transmitted to OMB and OPM pursuant to OMB Director Russ Vought’s February 2025 memo.
2. Please provide to the Committee the post-reorganization budget and staffing levels for each of the agency’s field laboratory and research facilities that remain open.
3. Please provide to the Committee all documents and communications (including, but not limited to, emails, text messages, instant messages, comments, notes, analyses, legal and other memoranda, letters, telephone logs, Signal messages, meeting minutes, calendar entries, PowerPoint slides, and presentation materials) exchanged between EPA and OMB regarding the repeal of the Endangerment Finding.
4. Please provide to the Committee all documents and communications (including, but not limited to, emails, text messages, instant messages, comments, notes, analyses, legal and other memoranda, letters, telephone logs, Signal messages, meeting minutes, calendar entries, PowerPoint slides, and presentation materials) exchanged between EPA and DOE regarding the repeal of the Endangerment Finding.
5. Please provide to the Committee all documents and communications (including, but not limited to, emails, text messages, instant messages, comments, notes, analyses, legal and other memoranda, letters, telephone logs, Signal messages, meeting minutes, calendar entries, PowerPoint slides, and presentation materials) exchanged between EPA and the Trump Vance 2025 Transition Team regarding the repeal of the Endangerment Finding.
6. Please provide to the Committee all documents and communications (including, but not limited to, emails, text messages, instant messages, comments, notes, analyses, legal and other memoranda, letters, telephone logs, Signal messages, meeting minutes, calendar entries, PowerPoint slides, and presentation materials) exchanged between EPA and DOE regarding the report titled, “A Critical Review of Impacts of Greenhouse Gas Emissions on the U.S. Climate.”
7. Please provide to the Committee all documents and communications (including, but not limited to, emails, text messages, instant messages, comments, notes, analyses, legal and other memoranda, letters, telephone logs, Signal messages, meeting minutes, calendar entries, PowerPoint slides, and presentation materials) within EPA regarding the agency’s review of the scientific basis for the proposal to repeal the Endangerment Finding.
8. Please provide to the Committee a written update regarding the status of the IRIS assessment for PFNA, including whether any scientific work remains ongoing for the assessment and the date by which the agency intends to finalize and publish the assessment.
9. Please provide to the Committee a list of all research products that have been delayed, modified, or declined since January 20th, 2025, due to the agency’s review or conclusions regarding the alignment of scientific research with administration priorities, including the topics of the research products.
EPA’s non-responsiveness to Committee oversight during the 119th Congress has been unacceptable. The agency must respect congressional prerogatives. We remain determined to obtain the information we need to perform our duties on behalf of the American people. EPA should understand that a lack of cooperation will not frustrate the Committee’s oversight permanently. It will merely strengthen our commitment to employing all the tools at our disposal to hold the agency accountable.
Pursuant to Rule X of the House of Representatives, the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology “shall review and study on a continuing basis laws, programs, and Government activities relating to nonmilitary research and development.” The Committee possesses jurisdiction over environmental research and development.

MUSKOGEE, OKLAHOMA – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Oklahoma announced that Cody Dale Cole, age 33, of Park Hill, Oklahoma, entered a guilty plea to one count of Child Neglect in Indian Country, punishable by a term of up to life imprisonment, and a fine of $250,000.

The Indictment alleged that on or about April 16, 2026, Cole willfully and maliciously failed and omitted to protect a child under the age of 18 from exposure to the use and possession of illegal drugs while responsible for that child’s health, safety, and welfare.

The crime occurred in Cherokee County, within the boundaries of the Cherokee Nation Reservation, in the Eastern District of Oklahoma.

The charge arose from an investigation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

The Honorable D. Edward Snow, Magistrate Judge in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Oklahoma, accepted the plea and ordered the completion of a presentence investigation report.

A U.S. District Court Judge will determine the sentence to be imposed after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

Cole will remain in the custody of the United States Marshals Service pending sentencing.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Morgan Muzljakovich represented the United States.
title: Park Hill Resident Pleads Guilty To Child Neglect In Indian Country

Representatives Torres and Fleischmann Lead Bipartisan Bill to Build America’s Advanced Manufacturing Workforce
Legislation expands workforce training and connects workers with good paying careers in growing manufacturing industries
Washington, D.C. – Today, during National Manufacturing Month, Representatives Norma Torres (CA-35) and Chuck Fleischmann (TN-03) introduced the bipartisan Advanced Manufacturing Jobs in America Act of 2026, legislation to help workers train for and connect with advanced manufacturing careers. The legislation, which was inspired by the successful public-private partnership that created the InTech Center at Chaffey College in Fontana, would direct the Department of Labor to initiate pilot projects between local community colleges, state and tribal colleges, local boards, advanced manufacturers, and Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP) centers that are focused on education, training, and apprenticeship programs for advanced manufacturing jobs.
“Manufacturing is a cornerstone of the Inland Empire’s economy, and we need to make sure our workforce is prepared for the jobs of tomorrow,” said Congresswoman Torres. “The Advanced Manufacturing Jobs in America Act will bring manufacturers, community colleges, and workforce partners together to give workers the skills they need to secure good-paying careers while helping American manufacturers find the talent they need to grow. Investing in American manufacturing means investing in American workers, and I am proud to partner with Congressman Fleischmann on this bipartisan effort.”
“Manufacturing is the backbone of America, driving our economy, creating jobs, and building the foundation of our nation’s prosperity. East Tennessee is leading the way in America’s reindustrialization, showing how innovation and hard work can revitalize our manufacturing sector. This legislation is vital to keeping America competitive and strong. I am honored to champion this effort in Congress and remain committed to supporting American manufacturing and the dedicated people who power it,” said Congressman Fleischmann.
The Advanced Manufacturing Jobs in America Act would amend the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to establish pilot projects focused on advanced manufacturing education and training. The bill would support partnerships between advanced manufacturers and community colleges, workforce development boards, Manufacturing Extension Partnership centers, local educational agencies, and other eligible organizations. Programs could include classroom and hands on learning, on-the-job training, and registered apprenticeships and pre-apprenticeships.
The legislation would prioritize dislocated and unemployed workers. Eligible recipients must demonstrate their capacity to teach the skills needed for advanced manufacturing jobs and provide workers with a recognized postsecondary credential.
The bill is inspired by the public-private partnership at the InTech Center at Chaffey College, a regional training center that trains and upskills students and employed workers for in-demand technical careers at no cost. In 2014, the Chaffey College and the Inland Empire Regional Training Consortium (IERTC) received a $15 million grant from the Department of Labor, which resulted in the 2016 opening of the InTech Center, a partnership between Chaffey College and California Steel Industries (now Nucor-CSI). The center was California's first public-private workforce training partnership in advanced manufacturing. Located in Fontana, CA, the center now works with more than 70 employers in the region and is an example of how federal funding can jumpstart successful public-private workforce development programs in advanced manufacturing.
Earlier this month, Reps. Torres and Fleischmann led a bipartisan resolution recognizing National Manufacturing Day and the contributions of manufacturers and workers across the country. In 2022, Reps. Torres & Fleischmann also secured the inclusion of their bicameral, bipartisan National MEP Supply Chain Database Act in the CHIPS and Science Act (Public Law 117-167) to help manufacturers prepare for future supply chain challenges.
###
title: Representatives Torres and Fleischmann Lead Bipartisan Bill to Build America’s Advanced Manufacturing Workforce

Justice Department Files Complaint Against California Ticket Broker for Using Unlawful Tactics to Purchase Millions of Tickets to Popular Live Events
Today, the Department of Justice, together with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), announced the filing of a complaint against REPS & Company Inc. (REPS), a California corporation, along with three of its executives — Ryan Pancheri, Brian Archibald, and Nicholas Totagrande — for violations of the FTC Act and the Better Online Ticket Sales (BOTS) Act, which prohibits circumventing the measures Internet ticket sellers use to ensure equitable consumer access to event tickets.
“The Justice Department is committed to holding accountable individuals and businesses that drive up the cost of event tickets by illegally exceeding ticket purchase limits and reselling those unlawfully obtained tickets with exorbitant markups,” said Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate of the Justice Department’s Civil Division. “Working alongside the FTC, we will continue to enforce the BOTS Act to protect consumers from such conduct.”
The complaint, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California, alleges that since 2022, the defendants have routinely circumvented ticket issuers’ controls to purchase tickets in excess of purchase limits for thousands of events. The defendants then resold tickets to these events on the secondary market. Defendants spent more than $1.3 billion to amass over 18.5 million tickets for these events and generated at least $120.8 million in profit.
The United States is represented by Assistant Director Marcus P. Smith and Trial Attorneys Meredith L. Reiter and Austin T. Mendes of the Civil Division’s Enforcement and Affirmative Litigation Branch in coordination with the Federal Trade Commission.
The claims made in the complaint are allegations only, and there has been no determination of liability.
Press Release Number: 26-1210
title: Justice Department Files Complaint Against California Ticket Broker for Using Unlawful Tactics to Purchase Millions of Tickets to Popular Live Events

GREAT FALLS – A man and woman from Great Falls who were trafficking fentanyl together have been sentenced to prison, First Assistant U.S. Attorney Mark Steger Smith said.

Kylie Lynn Minardi, 24, who pleaded guilty in June 2026 to distributing fentanyl and conspiracy to possess with the intent to distribute fentanyl, was sentenced Wednesday to five years and two months in prison, followed by four years of supervised release.

Zachary Taylor Cortez, 28, who pleaded guilty in May 2026 to conspiracy to possess with the intent to distribute fentanyl and possession with intent to distribute fentanyl, was sentenced Sept. 23, 2026, to five years and two months in prison, followed by four years of supervised release.

Chief U.S. District Judge Brian M. Morris presided.

The government alleged in court documents that law enforcement suspected Cortez and Minardi were distributing fentanyl in Great Falls. From June to August 2024, the Great Falls Police Department launched an investigation into the pair. With a warrant to track and search Cortez’s vehicle, law enforcement pulled the two over and discovered 97 grams of fentanyl in pill form and a digital scale in the car.

The U.S. Attorney’s Office prosecuted the case. The Great Falls Police Department, the Russell Country Drug Taskforce, and the DEA conducted the investigation.
title: Great Falls pair sentenced to over 5 years in prison for trafficking fentanyl

Seattle – A 35-year-old member of the Lummi Nation, a Level III registered sex offender, was arraigned today for the sexual assault of a houseguest in a residence on tribal land, announced Acting U.S. Attorney Charles Neil Floyd. Gideon Bewley pleaded “not guilty” today in U.S. District Court in Seattle to sexual abuse. Bewley is being detained at the Federal Detention Center at SeaTac. Trial in front of U.S. District Judge Kymberly K. Evanson is scheduled for December 21, 2026.

According to court records, Bewley is a registered sex offender due to a federal felony for sexual abuse of a minor. Bewley was released from federal custody in June 2022 and was registered as living at a family residence on the Lummi Nation Indian Reservation.

On April 24, 2026, the victim spent the evening at Bewley’s girlfriend’s residence. Bewley arrived later in the evening. After consuming alcohol, the victim went to bed and later awoke to Bewley sexually assaulting her. Shortly thereafter, she confronted Bewley and his girlfriend about the sexual assault.

Bewley was originally arrested by Lummi Tribal Police and charged with rape in the second degree, failing to register as a sex offender and residing with a child in violation of his sex offender status. He came into federal custody on June 2, 2026, for violating the terms of his supervised release. He was indicted by the grand jury on October 7, 2026.

Sexual abuse is punishable by up to life in prison.

The charges contained in the indictment are only allegations. A person is presumed innocent unless and until he or she is proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

The case is being investigated by the Lummi Police Department and the FBI.

The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Celia Lee. AUSA Lee serves as a Tribal Liaison for the U.S. Attorney’s Office, Western District of Washington.
title: Lummi Nation member, who is registered sex offender, indicted for rape of incapacitated victim

text:
Sherman & Lawmakers Challenge Trump Administration’s Effort to Restart California Oil Pipeline
SHERMAN OAKS, CA — Congressman Brad Sherman (CA-32) joined Senators Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Congressman Salud Carbajal (D-CA), and a coalition of Democratic lawmakers in challenging the Trump Administration’s efforts to restart the Sable Offshore oil pipeline in California, arguing that the Administration is unlawfully invoking national defense powers to benefit the fossil fuel industry.
In an amicus brief filed with the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit, Sherman and his colleagues urged the court to reverse a lower court ruling that allowed the pipeline to continue operating despite questions surrounding the Administration’s use of the Defense Production Act (DPA).
The lawmakers argue that the Trump Administration has failed to demonstrate any legitimate national defense necessity for restarting the pipeline, which had remained idle for nearly 11 years. Instead, they contend that the Administration is misusing extraordinary federal authority to circumvent California law and financially benefit a politically connected oil company.
The brief also raises concerns about potential pay-to-play politics, noting that the project was headed by a Trump donor and questioning whether the Administration's intervention was motivated by national security considerations or political favoritism.
Sherman and his colleagues emphasized that the Defense Production Act was intended to address genuine national defense needs, not provide the federal government with unchecked authority to intervene on behalf of private companies.
The lawmakers urged the Ninth Circuit to reverse the district court's denial of a preliminary injunction, arguing that the lower court failed to adequately scrutinize the Administration's national defense justification.
The effort was led by Senators Whitehouse, Padilla, and Schiff, along with Congressman Carbajal. Sherman joined Senator Tammy Duckworth and ten other House Democrats in signing the brief.
Read the full announcement and brief here.
###
title: Sherman & Lawmakers Challenge Trump Administration’s Effort to Restart California Oil Pipeline

text:
CMS Announces Resources, Flexibilities to Assist with Public Health Emergency in Alabama and Florida
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) announced today additional resources and flexibility available in response to a Public Health Emergency (PHE) in Alabama, beginning Oct. 7, 2026, and Florida, beginning Oct. 6, 2026, respectively, due to emergency conditions resulting from Hurricane Isaias and continuing. CMS is working closely with both states and federal partners to put flexibility in place to ensure those affected by this natural disaster have access to needed care.
On Oct. 13, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. declared the PHE.
CMS will assist with resources and waivers to ensure hospitals and other facilities can continue to operate and provide access to care for those impacted by the hurricane. The following is key information on resources for those affected and actions CMS is taking.
State Waivers: CMS’ blanket waivers and other flexibilities are available to providers in Alabama and Florida who have been affected by the hurricane. Healthcare providers that need additional flexibility specific to the effects from the hurricane can submit a request to CMS here: CMS 1135 Waiver/Flexibility Request and Inquiry Form.
Disaster Toolkit and Support for State Medicaid and CHIP Agencies: To prepare for current and future disasters, CMS developed an inventory of Medicaid and Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) flexibilities and authorities available to states during a disaster to support Medicaid and CHIP operations and ensure continuity of coverage for people served through these programs during times of crisis. For more information and to access the inventory and toolkit, visit: https://www.medicaid.gov/resources-for-states/disaster-response-toolkit.
Dialysis Care: CMS is helping people obtain and maintain access to critical life-saving services by activating the Kidney Community Emergency Response (KCER) program and working with End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) Network 7 (Florida) and Network 8 (Alabama), which are responsible under a contract with CMS for assessing the status of dialysis facilities in potentially impacted areas of these states. This work includes reviewing impacts related to generators, evaluating alternative water supplies, providing education and materials for patients, and more. ESRD Network 7 and Network 8 are also helping people receive dialysis services in the affected locations to which they evacuated.
CMS, through ESRD Network 7 and Network 8, advises people to keep an emergency supply kit on hand in a waterproof bag containing important personal, medical, and insurance information; contact information for their dialysis facility; the ESRD Network hotline number; and contact information of those with whom they may stay or for out-of-state contacts. They have also been instructed to have on-hand supplies to follow a three-day emergency diet. The ESRD Network 7 (Florida) toll-free hotline is 1-800-936-2620. The ESRD Network 8 (Alabama) toll-free number is 1-877-936-9260. Additional information is available on the KCER website at: www.kcercoalition.com.
Medical Equipment and Supplies Replacements: CMS will permit people with Medicare who have lost or realized damage to their durable medical equipment, prosthetics, orthotics, and supplies because of the hurricane to receive replacements of such items and services. This will help to ensure beneficiaries can continue to access the needed medical equipment and supplies they rely on each day. People with Medicare can contact 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227) for assistance.
Access to Covered Part D Drugs: There is longstanding guidance around expectations for Part D sponsors during a Presidential declaration of a disaster/emergency or Secretarial declaration of a PHE. During any PHE declaration, where beneficiaries are displaced from their place of residence and cannot be reasonably expected to obtain covered Part D drugs at a network pharmacy, plans will be required to ensure enrollees have adequate access to drugs dispensed at out-of-network (OON) pharmacies. Plans are required to reimburse beneficiaries up to their usual plan allowance for any payments enrollees make to OON pharmacies. Similarly, if the nature of the disaster requires voluntary or mandatory evacuation, plans will similarly be required to reimburse beneficiaries for OON payments for refills of Part D medications to any beneficiary located in an “emergency area,” defined as the area in which there has been a Stafford Act or National Emergencies Act declaration and a PHE declaration. For beneficiaries who have, for instance, lost their drugs, CMS would expect all “refill too soon edits” to be removed. For more information, visit sections 50.12 and 60.1 of Chapter 5 of the Prescription Drug Benefit Manual.
Health Information Privacy/Civil Rights Accessibility Resources: During a PHE, the HHS Secretary may waive sanctions and penalties against a covered hospital that does not comply with certain provisions of the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) Privacy Rule in the emergency area and for the emergency period identified in the PHE declaration; to hospitals that have instituted a disaster protocol; and for up to 72 hours from the time the hospital implements its disaster protocol but not to exceed the time prescribed beyond the period described in section 1135(e) of the Social Security Act. The HHS Office for Civil Rights offers more information on enforcement of HIPAA during emergency responses.
Recent natural disasters have demonstrated the importance of ensuring accessibility to health and human services for everyone living in the United States, including individuals in need of interpretation and translation services. To help first responders provide on-the-ground language assistance and communicate effectively during disasters and in accordance with federal civil rights laws, the HHS Office for Civil Rights offers a plain language checklist (PDF), including recommendations, specific action steps, resources, and tips on how to identify language needs in a disaster-impacted community to effectively use interpreters. Additional information is available on the HHS OCR website.
Marketplace Special Enrollment Period (SEP) for Hurricane Victims: During a Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) declared major or emergency disaster event, individuals who reside in states served by HealthCare.gov and who miss their existing SEP or who miss enrollment during the Open Enrollment Period are eligible for an SEP to enroll in Marketplace coverage.
FEMA-emergency affected individuals will have up to 60 days from the end of the FEMA-designated incident period to select a new Marketplace plan or make changes to their
existing Marketplace plan. FEMA-emergency affected individuals must contact the Marketplace Call Center at 1-800-318-2596 or TTY at 1855-889-4325 and indicate they were eligible for an enrollment window but were unable to complete their enrollment due to a FEMA-designated emergency or disaster. For more information, please visit: https://www.cms.gov/cciio/resources/regulations-and-guidance/fema_sep.
CMS will continue to work with Alabama and Florida, and those areas impacted by the hurricane. The agency encourages beneficiaries and providers of healthcare services that have been impacted to seek help by visiting CMS’ emergency webpage.
To find additional preparedness and response resources for the health sector and emergency
management professionals, visit: https://www.aspr.gov/health-tools.
###
Get CMS news at cms.gov/newsroom, sign up for CMS news via email and follow CMS on X @CMSgov
title: CMS Announces Resources, Flexibilities to Assist with Public Health Emergency in Alabama and Florida

PHILADELPHIA – United States Attorney David Metcalf announced that Aaron Michael McComsey, 44, of Perkasie, Pennsylvania, was arrested today and charged by indictment with two counts of threatening to assault, murder, or kidnap a federal official.

I go into withdrawal in 36 hours. After that time, [the official] is no more on this earth. Fix this or he goes bye bye forever.”; and “Just tell [the official] I want 6000 dollars for this month's medication costs. He's a millionaire. Let his ass pay for it. I'm so done. That man is finished.”; and “Can't wait for the next eagle scout graduation. That's his end.”; and “I'm coming over there soon if this isn't resolved.”

text:
FORT LEONARD WOOD, Mo. — Week 3 of U.S. Army Basic Combat Training pushed more than 100 Fort Leonard Wood recruits past their fears, transforming civilian mindsets into the Soldier spirit through a battery of milestone training events.
Company A, 3rd Battalion, 10th Infantry Regiment, 3rd Chemical Brigade trainees began the week honing their buddy team tactics and drill and ceremony precision before conquering the Confidence Course, CS Gas Chamber and Warrior Tower.
According to Sgt. 1st Class Trevor Gibbs, Company A senior drill sergeant, during buddy team tactics training the platoons organized into squads to navigate themselves and critical equipment across an actively evolving bridge structure while maintaining zero ground contact.
“We give trainees a scenario and allotted amount of time to meet mission requirements, such as bringing a barrel across a bridge that is one plank short,” Gibbs said. “It forces them to communicate and work together to continuously move people across with the barrel while the planks are also being moved to complete the bridge.”
He said the task builds critical thinking skills and teaches trainees to unite their diverse capabilities to overcome obstacles and complete the mission.
At the Confidence Course Oct. 7, 2026, platoons dispersed throughout Training Area 97 to negotiate high-risk obstacles. Key stations included high-altitude, multi-stage towers; low-crawl tire pits under barbed wire; reverse-incline rung descents; rope-swing log clearances; and sliding face-first during a steep rope-bridge.
Gibbs described the Confidence Course as a series of counterintuitive physical challenges that force recruits to think outside the box and push past mental limitations they place on their own physical abilities.
“Many of the obstacles feel unnatural, like crawling face first down a wooden ladder,” Gibbs said. “Once they accomplish the obstacles, they leave the training area with a sense of pride and achievement.”
The next day, under a relentless and uncharacteristic October heat, trainees donned their M50 Joint Service General Purpose Masks and entered the chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear training area known as the CS Gas Chamber.
For Gibbs, a 74D chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear specialist, the gas chamber stood out as a highlight of the Week 3 training schedule.
“Nobody freaked out or had to go through the gas chamber a second time. They did well,” Gibbs said. “I appreciate the depth of this training event because there is a physical aspect to the gas chamber when they break the seal of their masks, but it is mostly a mental challenge.”
As Gibbs and 1st Lt. Marquis Smith, Company A’s executive officer, vaporized CS tear gas tablets over the heating elements, the chamber filled with a stinging mist and trainees executed pressure-testing drills — such as running in place and scanning left and right — to prove they could function under a pending threat.
“I tried to pay attention as much as I could,” said Pfc. Yasmine Estevez, a Company A trainee who is pushing through BCT on her path to becoming an 88M motor transport operator.
Then the real test of discipline began as recruits were ordered to break the seal on their protective masks.
“Keep 'em above your nose, trainees,” roared the chamber cadre over the coughing of the recruits.
That first breath of gas inside the chamber marked a turning point for Estevez, proving she could survive the worst and keep pushing forward.
“That is when my composure went out the window, it was just survival instincts at that point. I couldn’t breathe or see,” Estevez said. “But then I realized I could hear the instructions, so I did my best to follow them and make my way out of the chamber.”
As the trainees stumbled out into the fresh air, their drill sergeants were waiting to herd them forward, bark instructions and motivate them to open their eyes and walk off the gas.
“Open your eyes. Flap your arms. Don't touch your face,” yelled drill sergeants.
While the gas chamber is an experience few eagerly anticipate, Estevez was grateful to have confronted the training head-on, noting that she felt incredibly proud to have overcome the trial.
Estevez said the gas chamber was challenging, but less daunting than she anticipated.
She noted that her CBRN training experience was built on a foundation of trust, because being in the chamber with Gibbs and Smith demonstrated that her leadership does not just command — “they are facing the same battles they are preparing us to fight.”
Gibbs agreed.
“Leadership is from the front,” he said. “I am in the chamber with them because I am never going to require a trainee to attempt any task I would not do myself. That is part of our drill sergeant creed.”
Recruits capped off Week 3 at Training Area 136 by mastering the Swiss seat — a hand-tied rope harness — before executing a 47-foot rappel down Warrior Tower.
Company A trainee, Pfc. Cheyenne Malone, in BCT to become a 12N horizontal construction engineer, said she enjoyed rappelling and wished she could go again.
“There were multiple drill sergeants checking our Swiss seats, so I felt confident I had tied mine correctly,” Malone said. “I was pretty nervous when I got up there and looked down, but as soon as my feet were on the ledge, I felt ready. I was hyped. It was awesome.”
More Week 3 photos are available to view on Fort Leonard Wood's Flickr.
Gibbs said during Week 3, trainees also sat through a basic map reading class that served as a vital precursor to Week 4, when trainees transition away from the cantonment area to tackle land navigation and the Hammer Field Training Exercise.
title: Send Me: The making of a Soldier | Week 3
