Medical Spa Business Owner Pleads Guilty to Employment Tax Crimes
A Parker, Colorado man pleaded guilty on October 2, 2026, to willfully failing to pay over employment taxes on behalf of the medical spa business he owned and operated.
The following is according to court documents and statements made in court: Spencer Carrado owned and operated “Spectrum Med Spa,” also known as “SculptedMD,” a “medical spa” operating in various locations. Carrado exercised control over SculptedMD’s financial affairs. He also was responsible for withholding Social Security, Medicare and income taxes from his employees’ wages and paying those funds over to the IRS, as well as filing quarterly employment tax returns with the IRS. From the third quarter of 2020 through the fourth quarter of 2024, however, Carrado withheld taxes from his employees’ wages, but did not pay over those taxes to the IRS or file all required quarterly employment tax returns. In total, Carrado caused a tax loss to the United States exceeding $600,000.
Carrado pleaded guilty to one count of willful failure to account for and pay over trust fund taxes. He is scheduled to be sentenced on December 11, 2026, and faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case.
Trial Attorney Stuart A. Wexler of the Criminal Division’s Tax Section is prosecuting the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Medical Spa Business Owner Pleads Guilty to Employment Tax Crimes

The U.S. Department of Energy Alternative Fuels and Feedstocks Office released a pre-publication draft of a federal register notice announcing the Emissions Value Request process for the 45Z fuel production tax credit.
October 14, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Alternative Fuels and Feedstocks Office (AFFO) released a pre-publication draft of a federal register notice announcing the Emissions Value Request (EVR) process for the 45Z fuel production tax credit. Modified and extended under the Working Families Tax Cut, the Clean Fuel Production Tax Credit (Internal Revenue Code Section 45Z) provides a production incentive for certain feedstocks produced in the United States, Mexico, or Canada.
“Thanks to President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cut, we are creating new opportunities for American farmers and fuel producers to strengthen domestic energy production, reduce costs, and unleash American energy dominance,” said Assistant Secretary of Energy Audrey Robertson. “Through the Department of Energy’s new 45Z Emissions Value Request process, we are expanding opportunities for American fuel producers to access critical tax incentives, supporting rural economies, and bringing more American-made fuels to market. In short: putting American energy first.”
Transportation fuel producers seeking to claim the tax credit must obtain the life cycle greenhouse gas emissions rate of their transportation fuel using the applicable rate table for Section 45Z. If the fuel’s type, primary feedstock, or pathway is not included in the rate table, fuel producers must petition the Secretary of Treasury for a provisional emission rate (PER). The 45Z EVR process is the route through which fuel producers can obtain a rate value from DOE and petition U.S. Treasury for a PER.
To request an emissions value from DOE, stakeholders must follow the EVR Application Instructions to submit the following requested materials:
- Engineering information/analyses consistent with the specified section of the front-end engineering and design (FEED) study or similar indication of project maturity, as determined by DOE.
- A completed EVR form.
In addition to the required documents, an applicant also has the option to include additional information that may be beneficial in completing lifecycle analysis of the transportation fuel production pathway described in the EVR form and FEED study.
For more detailed information on how to apply for a PER or the EVR process, visit DOE’s 45Z EVR webpage or contact 45ZEmissionsRequest@doe.gov. Questions about the 45Z tax credit and eligibility for the tax credit should be directed to the Internal Revenue Service.
title: Energy Department Releases Emissions Value Request Process for 45Z Fuel Production Credit

Hoyer Statement on Unannounced Starlink Terminal Restrictions in Ukraine
WASHINGTON, DC –  Today, Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) released the following statement after SpaceX, an American aerospace manufacturer founded by Elon Musk, imposed sudden unannounced data speed restrictions on Starlink terminals utilized by Ukraine, disrupting its defensive military drone operations:
“The people of Ukraine have had to endure twelve years of Russian military aggression, occupation, full-scale invasion, the kidnapping of its children into Russia, and air attacks against their cities. Winters have been particularly brutal, with Russia targeting Ukraine’s energy and heating infrastructure. After four years of heroic fighting, Ukraine’s forces are now making steady progress on the battlefield, aided by relentless innovation and access to Starlink satellite networks crucial to command-and-control as well as to drone and missile interception. Members of Congress who traveled to Kyiv recently heard from Ukrainian officials just how critical Starlink is to civilian defense and battlefield progress.
“The turning off of Ukraine’s Starlink access today means that fewer Russian attacks against civilians targets will be intercepted. More Ukrainian families will face a harsh and difficult winter. Ukraine’s battlefield gains may slow. If Trump Administration officials were involved in this decision, as Elon Musk claims, it would represent a heinous act of betrayal to our Ukrainian allies and to a fellow democracy under assault by a despot. It would be an inversion of the American people’s will, as expressed by Congress, that we ought to be helping Ukraine win, not tipping the scales in Putin’s favor. This shameful act must be reversed, and I call on SpaceX to ensure that Ukrainian forces have their full connection restored. I also call on our Armed Forces to condemn this act as well.
“The surest way to ensure this war comes to an end is not to help Russia prolong it. It is to help Ukraine win. Because the people of Ukraine have shown the world that they will not allow their democracy, freedom, sovereignty, or territorial integrity be taken by a foreign power. They are unbowed and unafraid. America must show the same resolve in our unwavering support.”
title: Hoyer Statement on Unannounced Starlink Terminal Restrictions in Ukraine

BOSTON – A Chicago man was sentenced on Oct. 8, 2026 in federal court in Springfield, Mass. for his role in a nationwide wire fraud conspiracy that victimized businesses and individuals across the United States.

Steven Hayes, Jr. 34, was sentenced by U.S. District Court Judge Mark G. Mastroianni to three years of probation. The government recommended a sentence of 4-6 months in prison. Hayes was also ordered to pay $2,728 in both restitution and forfeiture. In May 2026, Hayes pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud. Hayes was indicted by a federal grand jury in December 2020 along with five co-defendants, including rap promoter Antonio Strong, rap artists Herbert Wright and Joseph Williams, their associate Demario Sorrells and celebrity barber Terrence Bender. In February 2026, Hayes proceeded to trial, which resulted in a hung jury.

Beginning in at least March 2017 through November 2018, Hayes, Strong, Williams, Sorrells, Wright and Bender conspired to defraud numerous businesses and individuals throughout the United States by using unauthorized and stolen payment card account information of real individuals – including the actual cardholders’ names, addresses, security codes and account expiration dates. Generally, because the payment card information was authentic, the defrauded businesses and individuals successfully processed the fraudulent transactions and provided the goods and services to Hayes and his co-conspirators. The actual cardholders discovered these transactions on their accounts and disputed the charges with their card companies who then charged back the transactions to the businesses and individuals, who consequently suffered losses in the amounts of the unauthorized transactions.

Hayes and his co-conspirators used illicit account information to obtain, among other things, a private jet charter flight, a New York City villa rental, designer puppies from a pet boutique and car insurance. In total, Hayes was responsible for $44,814 in victim losses.

On July 28, 2023, Wright pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and one count of making a false statement to a federal official, and on Jan. 11, 2024, was sentenced to three years’ probation and was ordered to pay restitution and forfeiture of $139,968 and a $5,500 fine. On Feb. 2, 2024, Sorrells pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and, on Aug. 29, 2024, was sentenced to three years’ probation and ordered to pay restitution and forfeiture of $106,481. On March 8, 2024, Williams pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and, on Aug. 13, 2024, was sentenced to three years’ probation and ordered to pay restitution and forfeiture of $155,392. On May 22, 2024, Strong pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and four counts of wire fraud and, on Oct. 29, 2024, was sentenced to three years in prison and ordered to pay restitution and forfeiture of $2,159,874. On Nov. 14, 2024, Bender pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and, on Feb. 27, 2025, was sentenced to three years’ probation and ordered to pay restitution and forfeiture of $103,811.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Andrew Murphy, Special Agent in Charge of the United States Secret Service, Boston Field Office made the announcement. Assistant U.S. Attorney Steven H. Breslow of the Springfield Branch Office and Trial Attorney Kyle Crawford of the of the Criminal Division’s White Collar and Corporate Enforcement Section prosecuted the case.
title: Chicago-Area Rap Promoter Sentenced for Role in Nationwide Fraud Conspiracy

Tallahassee Woman Sentenced to Federal Prison for Drug Distribution
Tallahassee, Fla. – Timeka Griffin, 42, of Tallahassee, was sentenced to five years in federal prison for her role in a conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute methamphetamine and cocaine, distribution of cocaine and methamphetamine, and possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine.
“Dealers of Methamphetamine in North Florida should know DEA is coming for you,” said DEA Special Agent in Charge Daniel Escobar, Tampa Field Division. “Our agents will bring criminals who distribute this poison in our communities to justice.”
The sentence was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida.
U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “This local drug trafficking ring has been dismantled thanks to the excellent investigative work of our state and federal law enforcement partners and this successful prosecution by my office. Our citizens deserve safe, drug-free streets, and my office will continue to aggressively prosecute anyone caught peddling deadly narcotics in this district to ensure we deliver on that promise.”
Court documents reflect that in July 2025, the Drug Enforcement Administration and Leon County Sheriff’s Office received information regarding the trafficking of cocaine in Leon County. Through investigation, law enforcement identified Edward Lee Cromartie and Griffin as a source of supply for cocaine and methamphetamine. Law enforcement also identified a suspected drug stash location, and upon execution of a federal search warrant at a storage unit shared by Cromartie and Griffin, seized approximately 1.6 kilograms of methamphetamine, along with multiple firearms, including a stolen handgun.
In March 2026, Cromartie was sentenced to 12 years in federal prison for his role in the drug trafficking conspiracy, distribution, and possession with intent to distribute charges.
The case involved a joint investigation by the Drug Enforcement Administration and Leon County Sheriff’s Office.
title: Tallahassee Woman Sentenced to Federal Prison for Drug Distribution

Fast Facts
U.S. adversaries are investing in artificial intelligence capabilities in ways that threaten global stability and U.S. national security. DOD issued an AI strategy in 2026—emphasizing speed in AI development. But DOD must do so responsibly to ensure quick and confident AI adoption on the battlefield.
This Q&A discusses how DOD has taken steps to implement AI responsibly, including through department-wide collaboration. But, as we previously reported, it hasn't defined responsibilities for AI collaboration or addressed workforce needs that affect AI adoption.
Our recommendations include that Congress consider directing DOD to do this and more.
Glowing computer chip in a circuit with brain icon.
Highlights
What GAO Found
Artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in a variety of scenarios, or use cases, in the Department of Defense (DOD). In guidance, DOD established AI Ethical Principles and the concept of Responsible AI to ensure the safety and trustworthiness of AI systems. DOD further defined six tenets to guide Responsible AI implementation. Most of the 10 DOD components GAO surveyed reported taking at least initial steps to establish oversight and implement Responsible AI tenets in the selected surveyed use cases.
The Office of the Chief Digital and AI Officer (CDAO), through its Responsible AI Division, established the Responsible AI Working Council as the working-level collaborative group for Responsible AI. However, CDAO officials said the council did not meet from late 2024 until August 2025. Officials from four DOD components told GAO they faced Responsible AI implementation challenges during this time that would have benefited from collaboration. Six of 10 surveyed components reported that sharing Responsible AI resources and best practices would benefit their implementation efforts. Although officials said the council resumed meetings in August 2025, it is at risk of lapsing again as it does not have a charter that defines roles and responsibilities and specifies meeting frequency. Another lapse could increase the risk of DOD facing Responsible AI implementation issues, such as inconsistent interpretation of related guidance, that it would not have the collaborative capacity to swiftly and effectively resolve.
CDAO officials identified additional actions that could help DOD implement Responsible AI. However, CDAO has experienced staffing shortages that have hindered its ability to take these actions. Specifically, officials said that as of February 2026, only three of the 10 authorized positions for the Responsible AI Division were filled. Responsible AI enables DOD to more quickly adopt AI. By addressing current workforce needs for the Responsible AI Division, CDAO could make more progress toward its goal of accelerating AI across DOD.
GAO previously made recommendations on issues related to DOD’s AI collaboration and workforce. DOD has not fully addressed those recommendations. Congressional action to ensure that DOD takes steps to fully address those prior recommendations would help position the department to meet its AI goals.
U.S. Marine Corps Service Members Conduct Training Using an Artificial Intelligence-Enabled System
Why GAO Did This Study
AI has changed the national security landscape. U.S. adversaries and competitors are investing heavily in AI and AI-enabled capabilities in ways that threaten global security. As DOD speeds AI development, it is critical for the department to do so responsibly so that warfighters can quickly and confidently adopt it.
Senate Report 118-188 accompanying a bill for the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025 includes a provision for GAO to review the implementation and oversight of DOD’s Responsible AI guidance, among other things. This report discusses DOD’s approach to the responsible use of AI, including related guidance, implementation, and oversight.
GAO collected and reviewed DOD documentation related to Responsible AI. GAO also conducted a survey of 10 DOD components to understand how they have implemented Responsible AI tenets in 10 selected use cases. GAO also interviewed cognizant DOD officials.
Recommendations
GAO is recommending that Congress consider directing DOD to implement prior GAO recommendations on its AI collaboration and workforce. GAO is also making two new recommendations that DOD develop and issue a charter for the Responsible AI Working Council and ensure it addresses workforce needs of the CDAO Responsible AI Division.
The Department provided comments via email indicating concurrence with both of GAO’s recommendations.
title: Artificial Intelligence: Actions and Opportunities to Implement Responsible Use in DOD

Trump Administration Announces New Funding to Support Early Career Physicians Who Choose to Work in Rural Delaware
This federal investment will award housing and assistance to help future physicians train and practice in rural communities, ensuring Delawareans get the care they need close to home.
Today, the Trump Administration announced over a million dollars in Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) funding to help recruit and retain physicians serving communities in rural Delaware. This investment will support medical students and physicians in residency training, reduce the financial burden of clinical training, and encourage more physicians to build their careers while expanding quality care access to rural communities across Delaware.
This transformational funding will deliver two educational awards to eligible medical students in the program’s first year and funding for an expected 61 housing and relocation awards for eligible applicants in graduate medical education programs. Recipients will commit to five years of practice in rural Delaware, with at least 50% of their practice serving qualified rural areas.
The Rural Health Transformation Program is expanding access to quality healthcare, regardless of a patient’s zip code, and equipping first responders with the lifesaving resources they need when every second counts. This funding will make critical investments to strengthen rural healthcare, expand access to lifesaving services, and bring modern technology to communities across Delaware.
“President Trump understands that every American deserves high-quality healthcare, no matter where they live,” said Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “We are putting resources directly into rural communities to strengthen the health workforce, modernize infrastructure, expand access, and bring care closer to home. We are giving states the flexibility to build solutions around the people they serve, while demanding accountability for results. That is how we strengthen rural health, improve the lives of patients and families, and Make America Healthy Again.”
“President Trump made a historic commitment to rural America, and these investments are turning that commitment into better care for patients in communities across Delaware,” said Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “This is what rural health transformation should look like: federal investment that is putting patients first, driving lasting improvements and expanding healthcare for the hardworking Americans who call these communities home.”
Today’s investment was made possible through the Working Families Tax Cuts Act — passed by Republicans in Congress and unanimously opposed by Democrats — delivering a historic $50 billion investment to help states transform the way healthcare is delivered in America.
Today’s announcement is one part of the larger overall funding amount awarded to Delaware for fiscal year 2026.
Key initiatives the overall RHTP funding will focus on include:
- Building the rural healthcare workforce: Supporting recruitment, training, and retention strategies to strengthen the pipeline of healthcare professionals serving rural communities.
- Strengthening rural facilities and access: Supporting partnerships, operational improvements, and care-delivery changes that help rural providers maintain essential services and improve access.
- Advancing innovative care and payment models: Supporting new approaches to delivery and financing designed to improve quality, strengthen primary care, and support sustainable rural healthcare.
- Expanding community-based and preventive care: Investing in school-based care, mobile services, and other community strategies that improve prevention, address chronic disease, and expand access to care.
- Modernizing rural healthcare technology: Expanding remote care and data-driven tools to improve coordination and extend healthcare services to rural communities.
The Trump Administration is delivering on its commitment to strengthen rural America by investing in solutions that modernize technology to promote health and well-being for rural communities. Led by CMS, the RHTP is moving beyond the failed one-size-fits-all approach and giving rural communities the tools to build stronger, more innovative, and more sustainable health systems that deliver better care and better outcomes for the Americans they serve.
For more information about the RHTP, visit: https://www.medicaid.gov/resources-for-states/rural-health.

CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN, NEW YORK DELEGATION DEMAND TRUMP ADMINISTRATION RELEASE $87 MILLION IN COUNTERTERRORISM FUNDING STILL OWED TO NEW YORK
Congressman Pat Ryan, New York Delegation Demand Trump Administration Release $87 Million in Counterterrorism Funding Still Owed to New York
One Year After Trump Promised Full Reversal of Funding Cuts, First Responders Statewide are Still Without Millions in Federal Investments
KINGSTON, NY – Congressman Pat Ryan joined members of the New York Congressional Delegation in demanding the Trump Administration to immediately release $87 million in FY2025 Homeland Security Grant Program (HSGP) funding that is still owed to New York. Their letter, sent to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton, highlights the danger of withholding this funding from one the largest states in the nation and a top target for international and domestic terrorism.
“Since the start of the second Trump Administration, the President has waged targeted political attacks on New York State. When he cut this counterterrorism funding, New Yorkers across the state fought back and won. Now, a year later, we’re demanding Trump deliver the rest of what’s rightly ours,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “As Trump’s war with Iran continues, Americans want and deserve to feel safe. Now is the absolute last time to be cutting security funding. The need is especially stark following the grim 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terror attacks – the tragedy that changed our state forever and inspired these vital preparedness programs in the first place. Trump’s DHS has an obligation to release these funds and protect New Yorkers.”
In September 2025, DHS issued HSGP award notifications that cut New York’s allocation by 86 percent, or $187 million, leaving the state with just $30 million compared to roughly $220 million in FY24. In October 2025, following bipartisan advocacy, President Trump committed to restoring full funding at approximately $220 million. After a court order in Noem v. Illinois that found Trump unlawfully cut emergency grant funding, the administration released $100 million, but $87 million is still owed to New York.
The missing funds affect every county in the state, including Dutchess, Orange, and Ulster, and represent $11 million in losses for New York City. The letter warns that without full restoration, the Trump Administration is severely limiting local law enforcement’s ability to plan, train tactical teams, procure equipment, and conduct operations. Created in the wake of the September 11th attacks, HSGP has protected New York State for decades. The delegation underscored that the funds are due 25 years after 9/11 and one year after the President’s promise.
The full text of the letter can be found here.

title: CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN, NEW YORK DELEGATION DEMAND TRUMP ADMINISTRATION RELEASE $87 MILLION IN COUNTERTERRORISM FUNDING STILL OWED TO NEW YORK

United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, and Assistant Attorney General of the National Fraud Enforcement Division, Colin M. McDonald, announced today that STEVEN HOLTZ, ISRAEL PELLOT, and ALTON SCOTT have pled guilty in connection with their operation of a tax preparation firm owned and controlled by HOLTZ and known as the Holtz Group. Tax preparers at the Holtz Group, including HOLTZ, PELLOT, and SCOTT, falsified information on Holtz Group clients’ federal income tax returns in order to fraudulently reduce the tax liability of the clients and improperly increase the tax refunds they claimed from the Internal Revenue Service (“IRS”). This, in turn, allowed HOLTZ to charge tax preparation fees that were, at times, tens of thousands of dollars and, in some instances, more than one hundred thousand dollars for certain clients. HOLTZ and PELLOT pled guilty on Monday, October 5, 2026, before Magistrate Judge Henry J. Ricardo. SCOTT pled guilty on Friday, October 2, 2026, before Magistrate Judge Valerie Figueredo. As part of the guilty pleas, HOLTZ agreed to pay $8,793,805 in restitution, and PELLOT and SCOTT each agreed to pay $7,129,378 in restitution. The defendants will be sentenced by United States District Judge Mary Kay Vyskocil.

“This Office will hold those who steal from the American taxpayers accountable,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “Steven Holtz led a massive tax fraud scheme through his control and operation of the Holtz Group. Holtz and other tax preparers at his firm willfully placed false information on tax returns for their clients in order to generate substantial refunds to which the clients were not entitled and enormous fees for the Holtz Group. As the owner of the Holtz Group, Holtz was the primary beneficiary of the scheme, and enjoyed a lavish lifestyle unwittingly paid for by honest American taxpayers.”

“This Office will hold those who steal from the American taxpayers accountable,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “Steven Holtz led a massive tax fraud scheme through his control and operation of the Holtz Group. Holtz and other tax preparers at his firm willfully placed false information on tax returns for their clients in order to generate substantial refunds to which the clients were not entitled and enormous fees for the Holtz Group. As the owner of the Holtz Group, Holtz was the primary beneficiary of the scheme, and enjoyed a lavish lifestyle unwittingly paid for by honest American taxpayers.”

According to the Indictment and public court filings:

From at least in or about 2014 through at least in or about 2025, STEVEN HOLTZ, ISRAEL PELLOT, and ALTON SCOTT, and other co-conspirators, executed a fraudulent scheme led by HOLTZ in which they falsified information on Holtz Group clients’ federal income tax returns. Each year, Holtz Group clients – at least some of whom have professional degrees and annual income of hundreds of thousands of dollars – met with Holtz Group personnel at one of the Holtz Group’s offices (or, at times, remotely by videoconference and/or telephone). At these meetings, and during the course of any necessary follow-up discussions, HOLTZ, PELLOT, SCOTT, or other Holtz Group personnel, prepared the clients’ tax returns.

HOLTZ, PELLOT, SCOTT, and others included materially false and fraudulent information on the Holtz Group clients’ tax returns in order to reduce the clients’ tax liabilities or increase their refunds. The false items included on income tax returns for Holtz Group clients included inflated and fictitious deductions, including but not limited to: itemized deductions, such as charitable contributions and unreimbursed employee expenses; business expense deductions; capital losses, such as deductions for bad debt; losses and expenses from rental real estate businesses and unreimbursed partnership expenses; casualty and theft losses; losses from sales of business property; and losses from sales and other dispositions of capital assets. These false items were reported on Schedules A, C, D, and E as well as other tax forms. At times, the defendants also inflated and falsified clients’ income in order to improperly qualify clients for refundable Earned Income Tax Credits and/or fraudulently elected “head of household” filing status for married clients and other clients who did not qualify for that filing status, among other things.

As the owner of the Holtz Group and its affiliated entities, HOLTZ trained PELLOT, SCOTT, and others on how to falsify tax returns to carry out the scheme. For example, HOLTZ instructed PELLOT, SCOTT, and others to urge clients to set up business entities, such as partnerships and S Corporations, through the Holtz Group, for which clients paid additional fees. HOLTZ then directed the return preparers to use these business entities to fraudulently claim additional tax deductions, such as deductions for unreimbursed partnership expenses, meals, travel, gifts, and other expenses.

The Holtz Group based the fees charged to the clients on the amount of purported “tax savings” the firm supposedly generated for clients. HOLTZ used these purported “tax savings” to justify the Holtz Group’s fees, which were as high as tens of thousands or even more than one hundred thousand dollars for certain clients. For example, after billing a fee of $175,000 for preparing a client’s 2021 return, HOLTZ emailed the client explaining that the fee charged “is 25% of the tax savings. Always has been . . . I realize the bill is very high but honestly you sou [sic] should be happy to pay me that rather than paying the government what you owed them . . . [T]he fee is determined by the tax savings, not by your earnings.” In the same exchange, HOLTZ later went on to state: “You really aren’t paying my fee. The IRS is.”

By filing fraudulent returns on behalf of numerous Holtz Group clients, HOLTZ, PELLOT, SCOTT, and others defrauded the IRS of tax revenue and generated significant revenue for the Holtz Group. This significant revenue facilitated HOLTZ’s lavish lifestyle, including use of homes in Manhattan and East Hampton.

* * *

HOLTZ, 63, of New York and East Hampton, New York, pled guilty to one count of conspiracy to defraud the United States, which carries a maximum sentence of five years in prison, and one count of aiding and assisting in the preparation of a false and fraudulent U.S. individual income tax return, which carries a maximum sentence of three years in prison, for a total maximum sentence of eight years. PELLOT, 51, of Ormond Beach, Florida, and SCOTT, 33, of Brooklyn, New York, each pled guilty to one count of aiding and assisting in the preparation of a false and fraudulent U.S. individual income tax return, which carries a maximum sentence of three years in prison. HOLTZ further agreed to pay $8,793,805 in restitution, including $7,129,389 relating to the tax conspiracy charged in the indictment and $1,664,427 owed for HOLTZ’s personal tax returns between 2020 and 2024. PELLOT and SCOTT each agreed to pay $7,129,389 in restitution.

The maximum potential sentences in this case are prescribed by Congress and are provided here for informational purposes only, as any sentencing of the defendant will be determined by the judge.

Mr. McDonald and Mr. McDonald praised the outstanding investigative work of the IRS-CI.

The case is being prosecuted by the Office’s Complex Frauds and Cybercrime Unit and the Department of Justice, National Fraud Enforcement Division, Tax Section. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Brandon D. Harper and Matthew Weinberg, Southern District of New York, and Deputy Chief Jorge Almonte and Trial Attorney Likhitha Butchireddygari of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section are in charge of the prosecution.
title: Owner And Chief Executive Officer Of Tax Preparation Firm Pleads Guilty To Federal Tax Offenses

SOUTH BEND – Shawn M. Chupp, 38 years old, of South Bend, Indiana, was sentenced by United States District Court Judge Cristal C. Brisco after pleading guilty to being a felon in possession of a firearm, announced United States Attorney Adam L. Mildred.

Chupp was sentenced to 46 months in prison followed by 2 years of supervised release.

“Shawn Chupp is a convicted felon who chose to possess a handgun in violation of federal law and threatened to use it during a domestic disturbance in March of 2026. The law prohibiting convicted felons from possessing firearms exists for a fundamental reason: to protect the public from individuals who have already demonstrated a disregard for the law. Enforcing this law is paramount to ensuring that our neighborhoods remain safe and our homes remain sanctuaries. Gun violence does not happen in a vacuum. It shatters families, traumatizes children, and destabilizes entire communities. By strictly prosecuting felon-in-possession cases, law enforcement and prosecutors remove illegally held weapons from our streets before they can be used to commit further violent acts. This prosecution is a direct result of the Safe Neighborhoods initiative, a collaborative strategy involving federal, state, and local law enforcement to target the most violent offenders and reduce gun crime. Prosecuting these cases is one of our most effective tools for preventing gun violence before it strikes. We remain fully committed to working alongside our law enforcement partners to hold illegal gun possessors accountable, take firearms out of the wrong hands, and secure the peace and safety that every resident deserves,” said United States Attorney Adam L. Mildred.

This case was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, with assistance from the South Bend Police Department. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Andrew A. Krumwied.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities .

text:
Trump Administration Delivers Second Year of Savings by Stopping Taxpayer Payments for Duplicate and Deceased Enrollees in Obamacare
After Years of Biden-era Inaction, CMS Reviews Projected to Save Taxpayers $1.5 Billion Over the Next Year
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) continue to crush fraud, waste, and abuse in America’s healthcare programs by stopping duplicative enrollment in government health programs, with the potential to save taxpayers approximately $1.5 billion over the next year.
In 2026, CMS identified 189,000 people who had subsidized Obamacare coverage through the Federal Marketplace and either had duplicate Medicare, Medicaid or Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) coverage or were deceased. CMS took swift action to remove Obamacare subsidies for these people to save taxpayer dollars.
“Taxpayers should not foot the bill for duplicate coverage or subsidies for people who have died,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “HHS is identifying improper enrollments, stopping those payments, and making sure federal dollars support the Americans these programs were created to serve."
“When it comes to program integrity, the Biden Administration was sleeping on the job,” said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “They paused looking for duplicate Medicaid and Obamacare coverage for four years, creating a backlog of hundreds of thousands of duplicate enrollments. We’ve already saved nearly $6 billion, and we will continue to work hard to restore taxpayers’ confidence that the programs they fund are spending their hard-earned dollars wisely and efficiently.”
The Trump Administration restored duplicate enrollment enforcement in 2025, ending duplicate Obamacare subsidies for approximately 551,000 enrollees already receiving coverage under Medicaid.
Historically, CMS routinely checked to ensure taxpayers were not subsidizing duplicate Obamacare policies on the Federal Marketplace for beneficiaries already on Medicaid or Medicare. It also checked if taxpayers are paying for Obamacare plans on the Federal Marketplace for deceased people.
Federal regulations require Exchanges to periodically examine data for dual enrollments in Medicaid to guard against improper enrollments in subsidized Exchange plans through a process called Medicaid/CHIP Periodic Data Matching (PDM). These essential examinations were strengthened under the first Trump Administration and increased to at least twice a year. However, these checks were paused for Medicaid/CHIP enrollees the duration of the Biden Administration, allowing hundreds of thousands of individuals to be enrolled in multiple federal health insurance programs at once.
Individuals whose records show they receive Obamacare subsidies while also being covered by Medicaid or Medicare are contacted and provided 30 days to dispute that they have duplicate coverage. If such individuals fail to do so, CMS ends subsidies for their Obamacare plan. Even after 30 days, individuals may appeal the determination of duplicate coverage or show that their Medicaid/CHIP coverage is about to lapse and regain Obamacare subsidies.
This process also contacts individuals, or their estate, when federal records say they are deceased. CMS provides 30 days to dispute this record, otherwise their Obamacare subsidy and plan is ended.

KANSAS CITY, Mo. – A Belton, Mo., man pleaded guilty to production of child pornography, transportation of child pornography, possession of child pornography, and cyberstalking of a minor.

Carter Anderson, 32, was charged by an indictment in December 2025 for Anderson’s criminal conduct occurring between October 2021 through January 2025. In his guilty plea, Anderson admitted that he engaged in a course of conduct in which he obtained sexually explicit images and videos of three minor victims by various means, including through a pattern of threats over the internet. Anderson admitted that he met one of his minor victims through the Snapchat messaging application. Anderson admitted that, after obtaining the minor victim’s sexually explicit images and videos, he threatened to publicly release them if the minor victim did not send him additional and increasingly graphic sexually explicit images and videos.

Under federal statutes, the defendant is subject to a sentence of not less than 15 years and up to 70 years in federal prison without parole. The maximum statutory sentence is prescribed by Congress and is provided here for informational purposes, as the sentencing of the defendant will be determined by the court based on the advisory sentencing guidelines and other statutory factors. A sentencing hearing will be scheduled after the completion of a presentence investigation by the United States Probation Office.

This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney David Luna. It was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Heart of America Regional Computer Forensics Laboratory.

Project Safe Childhood

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the United States Attorneys' Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.usdoj.gov/psc . For more information about Internet safety education, please visit www.usdoj.gov/psc and click on the tab "resources."
title: Belton Man Guilty of Production, Transportation, and Possession of Child Pornography and Cyberstalking of a Minor

LOS ANGELES – A Ventura County man is scheduled to be arraigned today on federal charges that he abused his access to a U.S. naval base as a civilian contractor by entering restricted areas to photograph and film sensitive military equipment, airplanes, and training exercises, then sharing these images and videos with others.

Todd Jeremy Senff, 46, of Camarillo, is charged with 14 misdemeanors: 11 counts of violation of a defense property security regulation and three counts of entering military property for an unlawful purpose.

His arraignment is scheduled for this afternoon in United States District Court in downtown Los Angeles.

According to court documents, Senff worked for a Navy construction services contractor at Naval Base Ventura County (NBVC). This naval base houses a population of approximately 19,000 personnel and is comprised of three installations, including NBVC Point Mugu. Point Mugu houses several naval logistics commands and naval weapons testings commands, including unique facilities to conduct weapons research, development, and evaluation.

NBVC also provides direct access to the Point Mugu Sea Range, which is the Navy’s largest instrumented sea range and supports air, surface, and submarine operations and exercises. It also supports weapons testing, missile defense support, and multinational training exercises.

In September 2023, NBVC awarded a three-year construction contract to Senff’s employer for various projects. Senff was involved in approximately four of these projects, and he obtained a credential that granted him access to portions of the naval base.

From June 2024 to September 2024, Senff used his access to NBVC to unlawfully take photographs and videos of sensitive military equipment and military exercises. He then sent some of the unlawfully taken photographs and videos to his associates, along with messages regarding military activities.

The United States Navy strictly regulates photography on naval installations to protect and secure U.S. Department of War property against, among other things, sabotage and subversive actions. NBVC Point Mugu maintained posted signage in conspicuous and appropriate places stating that photography was prohibited.

An information merely contains allegations. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

If convicted, Senff would face a statutory maximum sentence of one year in federal prison for each count of violation of a defense property security regulation and a statutory maximum sentence of six months in federal prison for each count of entering military property for an unlawful purpose.

The FBI and Naval Criminal Investigative Service are investigating this matter.

Assistant United States Attorney Joseph S. Guzman of the National Security Division is prosecuting this case.
title: Camarillo Man Federally Charged with Abusing His Access as Civilian Contractor to Illegally Film U.S. Naval Base Activities and Equipment

text:
The Arctic is a key strategic region for Russia with significant military and economic implications. Russia is the largest of the Arctic states in terms of territory, stretching over 24,000 kilometers of coastline. The Arctic is central to Russian strategic and military concerns and is home to Russia's Northern Fleet, which operates about two-thirds of Russia's submarine-based nuclear deterrent, according to the U.S. intelligence community's 2026 Annual Threat Assessment. The Arctic also plays an important role in Russia's energy and economic development plans. After the Cold War and prior to Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the Arctic was a region of multilateral cooperation, but tensions have since grown in the region between Russia and the other Arctic states. In a March 2025 speech at the Arctic Forum in Murmansk, Russian President Vladimir Putin stated, "the role and importance of the Arctic for Russia and for the entire world are obviously growing. Regrettably, the geopolitical competition and fighting for positions in this region are also escalating."
For over a decade, Russia has increased its military capabilities in the Arctic, including reestablishing old Soviet-era military bases, building new bases and infrastructure, announcing the creation of new units and increasing the size of existing forces, reorganizing command and control structures, and undertaking new efforts to modernize the Northern Fleet—including its submarine forces. It remains unclear whether Russia has the financial and personnel resources to carry out its military modernization efforts and plans in the Arctic, or in what time frame it could do so. Additionally, the Russian military posture in the Arctic has become increasingly precarious with the accession of Finland and Sweden into NATO (in 2023 and 2024, respectively) and heavy ground-force losses suffered in Ukraine. According to Lieutenant General James Adams, Director of the Defense Intelligence Agency, in April 2026 testimony before Congress, "As the Arctic becomes a focal point of international competition, the Kremlin is increasingly concerned by the growth of NATO forces in the region and the perceived threat they pose to Russia's economic interests. In response, Moscow is modernizing its military forces in the region to counter NATO, defend these economic interests, and ensure its dominance over the Northern Sea Route, though requirements in Ukraine constrain resources devoted to these efforts."
Depending on Russia's military modernization efforts in the Arctic, Congress may assess U.S. national security priorities in the region. Congress also may consider how increased Russian military capabilities could threaten U.S. and allied interests; evaluate allied and NATO plans and military posture; and deploy various legislative and oversight tools to support, reject, or otherwise modify the Administration's approach to the region. Potential considerations for Congress include
The Arctic region is one of Russia's top strategic priorities.1 According to the Department of Defense's (DOD's) 2024 Arctic Strategy, "The Arctic plays a significant role in Russia's security and economic calculations."2 Russia is the largest of the Arctic states in terms of territory, covering over 24,000 kilometers of Arctic Ocean coastline—some 53% of the Arctic Ocean's total coastline.3 The Arctic holds an important role in Russian strategic thinking, and the region's economic development is a central component of Russia's energy and economic growth plans.4 In March 2025, Russian President Vladimir Putin stated, "Today, the North has become central to [Russia's] development efforts. This is a sovereign and historical choice.... [T]he objectives we set for and address in the Arctic, and the projects we undertake here must match this historical scale and have a horizon spanning decades, if not centuries."5
Russia's strategic position in the Arctic has declined since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The Arctic region holds considerable economic potential, but Russia's ability to develop natural resources in the Arctic has been constrained by U.S. and European sanctions. Russia's military position also has become more vulnerable with conventional ground forces losses in Ukraine.6 In addition, the accession of Finland and Sweden to NATO (in 2023 and 2024, respectively) brought NATO military capabilities, including long-range precision strike systems, closer to—and in range to potentially threaten—Russia's Northern Fleet, with its ballistic missile submarines.7 On August 31, 2026, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov stated, "NATO and other Western countries make no secret of their true motives, openly declaring their intention to turn the Arctic into a new front for opposing the development of Russia and its like-minded partners."8 Some observers assert that these factors have contributed to a heightened Russian government perception that its Arctic economic and security interests are interconnected.9
Russia's Arctic policy focuses on ensuring Russia's sovereignty and status as an Arctic power, exploiting the region's natural resources (e.g., oil, natural gas), and developing the Northern Sea Route (NSR)—a shipping corridor running along Russia's northern Arctic coastline—as a viable transportation artery. Developing the NSR would shorten transport times between Europe and the Asia-Pacific region.10 To achieve these objectives, the Russian government has increasingly securitized the Arctic and expanded Russia's military capabilities in the region to protect and project its Arctic ambitions.
Since 2020, the Russian government has adopted several new strategy documents outlining plans to bolster Russia's Arctic military capabilities, assert its sovereignty in the region, and develop the region's resources and infrastructure.11 These documents include the following:
In addition to specific Arctic strategies, the Russian government's 2022 Maritime Doctrine of the Russian Federation identifies the "the Arctic basin adjacent to the coast of the Russian Federation, including the water area of the Northern Sea Route" as a "vital area" for Russia.12 The Russian government's 2023 Concept of the Foreign Policy of the Russian Federation also highlights the Arctic as a priority region.13
The Russian government has taken steps to improve its control and coordination of the various policy actors to guide and implement its strategies in the Arctic. In August 2024, President Putin announced the creation of the Maritime Collegium under the control of Russia's former Secretary of the Security Council Nikolai Patrushev to oversee and coordinate Russia's various policy actors.14 The Maritime Collegium has been tasked with developing and protecting Russia's status as a global maritime power, overseeing the development of the Arctic, and advancing Russia's interests in the region.15
The Arctic plays a key role in Russia's security posture and sea-based nuclear retaliatory capability (see Figure 1). Russia has invested in increasing its air defense, naval, and ground forces in the Arctic region (discussed below).16 Russia's Northern Fleet—which covers much of the Arctic and is based at Severomorsk, in the Kola Peninsula bordering Norway and Finland—traditionally has received priority in the Russian Navy.17 According to the 2026 Annual Threat Assessment of the U.S. Intelligence Community,
The bulk of Russia's Arctic forces are concentrated in the Kola Peninsula, which hosts about two-thirds of Russia's second-strike nuclear capabilities. The area is home to Russia's Northern Fleet, including seven of the country's nuclear-armed ballistic missile strategic submarines. Russia has made major investments in the fleet, including adding long-range missiles, UAVs [unmanned aerial vehicles], and underwater drones. Russia has at least three air bases on the Kola Peninsula that host fighter jets, surveillance, and transport aircraft.18
Additionally, Russia has announced a large-scale increase in conventional ground forces in the Arctic. According to DOD's 2024 Arctic Strategy,
Despite some attrition of Russia's conventional land forces due to losses in Ukraine, its strategic, air, and maritime forces remain intact. Further, Russia has demonstrated the ability to reconstitute and reorganize its conventional ground forces, which illuminates the potential for future improved readiness and combat expertise in the Arctic.19
Largely unaffected by the war in Ukraine, the Northern Fleet continues to modernize and receive new and upgraded surface vessels and submarines.20 According to the Norwegian Intelligence Service, "The modernization of the Northern Fleet is progressing slowly. More naval platforms are being armed with modern long-range precision-guided weapons. Over the course of 2026, the Northern Fleet will come to have three Severodvinsk-class multirole submarines and three frigates available, all carrying hypersonic Tsirkon missiles."21
Additionally, the Northern Fleet (as well as Russia's other fleets) was returned to the direct operational command of the Russian navy in 2023, and Russian officials and other observers have noted an increased role for the navy in Russian strategic thinking.22 In 2025, Russian President Putin approved a new naval strategy to 2050 and allocated over 8.4 trillion rubles (over $106 billion at current exchange rates) for new shipbuilding over the next decade, much of it to bolster the Northern Fleet.23 Some observers assess there is a potential disconnect between ambition and reality for further development of the Northern Fleet, especially as Russia's shipyards struggle to meet current output and maintenance requirements.24
Russia's Aerospace Forces in the Arctic are also undergoing reorganization and are essential to detect and interdict any air threats.25 Air defense units previously under the Northern Fleet's command have been transferred to the 6th Air and Air Defense Army assigned to the Leningrad Military District (see below), which coordinates air assets in the region in concert with Aerospace Forces Main Command.26 The Northern Fleet's air units have been reorganized into the 7th Composite Aviation Corps and include reconnaissance, multi-role strike fighter, transport, and rotary wing aircraft.27
Russian ground forces are an essential part of Russia's military strategy to protect its northwest border and the Northern Fleet in the Kola Peninsula.28 Amid Finland's and Sweden's accession to NATO, the Russian military is adapting its force posture and has launched a large-scale reorganization effort to bolster its military capabilities in the region, including creating new units and increasing the size of existing forces (see text box, below).29 In June 2026, Lieutenant General Pasi Välimäki, Commander of the Finnish Army, reportedly estimated that Russia could increase its ground forces based near Finland's borders from 20,000 to upwards of 80,000.30 In 2024, the Russian military reactivated the Leningrad Military District to oversee and coordinate Russia's military posture in the region.31 According to Finnish military intelligence, "the Leningrad Military District, which is located close to Finland, is planned to be significantly reinforced in the future. In the Kola region, an army corps will be expanded into an army, and a completely new army corps will be established in Karelia and several brigades will be expanded into divisions."32
To support its revised posture in the Arctic, the Russian military reportedly is supporting extensive infrastructure projects, which include renovating defunct Soviet-era military facilities and constructing new ones on Russia's borders with Finland and Norway.33
Russian military's Arctic ground forces redeployed to fight in the war in Ukraine have suffered significant casualties, posing challenges to Russia's force posture in the Arctic.34 Russia faces reconstituting units that suffered attrition in Ukraine, and it would take time for Russia's Arctic units to regain the lost experience and for personnel to be adequately trained to operate effectively in an Arctic environment.35 Some observers and allied intelligence assessments indicate that it is unclear whether the Russian military will be able to fully achieve its stated objectives in the Arctic given the demands for units and personnel in other regions.36
The Trump Administration has highlighted the importance of the Arctic for U.S. national security interests and has argued for an increased U.S. and NATO presence to counter activities by Russia and the People's Republic of China (PRC, or China) in the Arctic. According to the 2026 National Defense Strategy, "we [the United States] have seen adversaries' influence grow from Greenland in the Arctic to the Gulf of America, the Panama Canal, and locations farther south."37 The Department of Defense reportedly is working on improving coordination among the combatant commands (European, Northern, and Pacific) with areas of responsibilities that overlap in the Arctic.38 The Trump Administration also has sought to bolster some U.S. Arctic capabilities, such as the acquisition of icebreakers.39 In October 2025, the Trump Administration signed a memorandum with Finland to procure up to 11 Arctic Security Cutters (ASCs), including 4 to be produced at shipyards in Finland, to address what the Administration describes as a "critical capability gap" with potential adversaries.40
NATO has increased its operations and presence in the Arctic, including by launching a new mission in February 2026 called Arctic Sentry in response to "Russia's increasing military activity and China's growing interest in the Arctic."41 Among other actions, NATO has established a Forward Land Force in Finland's Lapland region, and the United Kingdom (UK) has pledged to double the number of UK troops deployed to Norway to 2,000.42 In May 2026, the United States, Canada, the Kingdom of Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, and Sweden released a joint statement on Arctic security that recognized the strategic importance of the Arctic and acknowledged increased Russian military activity.43
In the 119th Congress, some Members have expressed concern regarding military activity and economic development in the Arctic by Russia and other foreign adversaries (see, for example, S.Res. 763 and S. 4708, the Arctic Security and Diplomacy Act) and their implications for U.S. security—such as early warning and monitoring for potential nuclear launches or bombers circumnavigating—in the region.44 The FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (P.L. 119-60, §5143) authorizes an Ambassador-at-Large for the Arctic; among other duties, the Ambassador is to establish and carry out an "Arctic Watcher Program," including to "monitor and combat the People's Republic of China, Russian Federation, and other malign influence campaigns across the Arctic region."45 In addition, Section 5143(h) requires the Secretary of State, in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence and the Secretary of Defense, to annually submit to the "appropriate congressional committees a report on Russian and Chinese malign influence in the Arctic region." Additionally, Section 7019(e) of the National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026 (Div. F, P.L. 119-75), and H.Rept. 119-217 required the State Department to provide a report to Congress on U.S. diplomatic priorities for the Arctic.46
In the 119th Congress, some Members may have an interest in assessing and conducting oversight of U.S. policy and considering legislation regarding the following:
title: Russia’s Arctic Military Posture: Considerations for Congress

Bosnian National Sentenced for Violating International Sanctions Against North Korea
A Bosnian national was sentenced to 60 months in federal prison after pleading guilty to federal export and sanctions violations by conspiring and attempting to broker the sale of Man Portable Air Defense Systems, which are anti-aircraft missiles.
“U.S. sanctions mean little if those who knowingly evade them face no consequences,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison for the District of New Mexico. “This defendant helped carry out an international scheme to conduct business that U.S. law prohibited, and this sentence holds him accountable for his role. I am proud of the investigators and prosecutors whose hard work and dedication brought this case to sentencing in New Mexico. Their commitment to seeing this prosecution through is a testament to the caliber of the people who serve in this district.”
“Those who knowingly attempt to circumvent U.S. export controls and international sanctions to facilitate the illicit trafficking of military weapons pose a serious threat to our national security and global stability,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Ryan G. McRae of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) El Paso. “Their willingness to profit from prohibited weapons transactions demonstrates blatant disregard for the law. HSI aggressively pursues those who traffic in restricted military technology and hold them accountable for their actions.”
According to court documents, Sasa Micev, 43, a citizen of Bosnia, is an international arms dealer. Micev worked with a co-conspirator based in New Mexico and others to violate and evade restrictions imposed by the U.S. Department of the Treasury under the North Korea Sanctions Regulations by brokering the purchase of SA-18 Igla portable surface-to-air missiles from North Korea without the required license or approvals from the Department of Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control.
On multiple occasions in 2020, Micev and a co-conspirator discussed unlawfully acquiring the Igla missiles and Micev provided pricing information, participated in efforts to obtain the items through falsified documentation, and worked to procure the weapons from North Korea despite knowing that such transactions were prohibited under U.S. and international laws.
In late 2020, Micev and the co-conspirator traveled to Ankara, Turkey to meet and complete the sale of the Igla missiles. However, after a price dispute with the North Koreans, the sale fell through.
Micev pleaded guilty to violating the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and the North Korean Sanctions Regulations.
HSI’s Albuquerque and Phoenix Field Offices investigated this case.
Assistant U.S. Attorneys Tavo Hall and Holland Kastrin for the District of New Mexico are prosecuting the case with the assistance of the Trial Attorney Maria Fedor of the National Security Division’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section.
title: Bosnian National Sentenced for Violating International Sanctions Against North Korea

NEW ORLEANS – RAYMOND T. KNESEL (“KNESEL”) , age 60, of Abita Springs, Louisiana was indicted on October 9, 2026, for attempted coercion and enticement of a minor, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Section 2422(b), announced U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle.

According to the indictment, between September 24, 2026, and September 28, 2026, KNESEL persuaded and enticed an individual he believed to be a fifteen-year-old female to engage in illegal and illicit sexual activity.

If convicted, KNESEL faces a mandatory minimum of ten (10) years and up to a lifetime in prison, at least five (5) years and up to a lifetime of supervised release, up to a $250,000 fine and a $100 mandatory special assessment fee. KNESEL may also be required to register as a sex offender.

U. S. Attorney Courcelle reiterated that the indictment is merely a charge and that the guilt of the defendant must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt.

U.S. Attorney Courcelle praised the work of the Federal Bureau of Investigation in investigating this matter. Assistant United States Attorney Mary Anne Flippo of the Public Integrity Unit and Human Trafficking and Child Exploitation Task Force is in charge of the prosecution.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by United States Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.projectsafechildhood.gov .

text:
Fast Facts
The Department of Housing and Urban Development has undergone a number of changes since 2025.
For example:
HUD reduced its workforce by 29% between December 2024 and December 2025, mostly through deferred resignation programs
Over half of employees who left had worked at HUD for at least 10 years; over 40% had worked there for over 20 years
We interviewed 20 stakeholder organizations about these changes. Nearly all said that experienced points of contact had left, making it harder to navigate HUD programs. Some stakeholders had to reduce services or staffing during funding gaps; others reported delays with physical inspections of properties.
Sign that reads "U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development".
Highlights
What GAO Found
The Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) reduced its workforce by 29 percent in 2025 and modified the types of programs it funds in response to presidential directives and executive branch guidance. HUD largely achieved workforce reductions through deferred resignation programs. Over half the employees who separated had at least 10 years of service at HUD, including 41 percent with more than 20 years of service. HUD did not publish notice of any reorganization plans that led to field office closures in 2025, though in 2026 it announced plans to consolidate one field office into a nearby regional office.
Workforce Changes at the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) in 2025
Note: Percentages may not sum to 100 due to rounding.
About half of HUD’s 68 active grant programs made new awards in fiscal year 2025, but the median value of those awards was higher than in previous years. HUD also terminated about 21 percent of its active contracts in 2025, valued at about $367 million. Most terminated contracts involved professional or IT services.
Representatives of 20 stakeholder organizations GAO interviewed—including fair housing grantees and agencies, public housing agencies, and Section 8 project-based rental assistance property managers—reported confusion, delays, and operational disruptions following HUD’s changes. Nearly all said that experienced points of contact had left, making it harder to navigate HUD programs. Fair housing stakeholders reported reducing services or staffing during monthslong funding gaps. Stakeholders also reported delays with physical inspections of HUD-assisted properties.
Since January 2025, HUD has reported launching initiatives aimed at increasing efficiency and streamlining operations. For example, HUD reported developing a unified grants system to standardize grant administration and a project voucher initiative to automate aspects of rental assistance processing. HUD did not respond to GAO’s requests to discuss these initiatives or provide supporting documentation. As a result, Congress and the public have limited information on the status or effectiveness of these initiatives.
Why GAO Did This Study
HUD administers programs related to housing assistance, community development, and fair housing. To carry out these programs, HUD headquarters and field staff work with public housing agencies, private property owners, nonprofit organizations, and other stakeholders.
Executive orders and other actions issued in 2025 called for workforce and program changes at HUD. GAO was asked to examine the effects of these changes. This report describes (1) changes HUD made to its workforce, field office structure, and grant and contract spending in 2025; (2) effects of those changes on selected HUD functions reported by housing stakeholders; and (3) steps HUD has publicly reported to manage the changes.
HUD did not respond to GAO’s requests for information throughout the audit. GAO analyzed publicly available 2025 data on HUD’s workforce, terminated contracts, and grant spending. GAO selected three HUD functions for review, chosen to reflect a mix of funding levels and other criteria: (1) enforcement of the Fair Housing Act and Violence Against Women Act of 1994, (2) administration of the Section 8 Project-Based Rental Assistance Program, and (3) coordination of inspections of HUD-assisted properties.
GAO also conducted four site visits and interviewed representatives of a nongeneralizable selection of 20 local and national housing organizations, including public housing agencies and fair housing organizations. GAO also reviewed court documents and publicly available data, and agency documentation related to HUD’s workforce and efficiency planning.
For more information, contact Jill Naamane at naamanej@gao.gov.
title: Department of Housing and Urban Development: 2025 Workforce and Spending Changes

Himes Statement on U.S. Support for Ukraine
  
  
    
      Washington,
      October 14, 2026
    
    
    
    
  
  
  
  
  
  
    
      Washington, DC -- U.S. Representative Jim Himes (D-CT), Ranking Member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, today released the following statement:
“Over the past several days, Ukraine has once again endured massive strikes conducted by Russia against its population centers and energy grid, strikes that are carried out with the clear aim of terrorizing and immiserating the Ukrainian population. While I have no doubt that the Ukrainian people will continue to stand strong against Putin, I am deeply disturbed by the direction of U.S. policy and the President's recent statements. In just the past days, Donald Trump announced a likely illegal deal to buy an inconsequential amount of diesel from Russia, as well as an ‘energy ceasefire’ that he appears to have imagined. Those decisions are bad enough, but if they were to be accompanied by any pullback in the assistance the U.S. provides to our Ukrainian partners, it would be a cowardly betrayal that makes our nation and the world less safe.
“As of this afternoon, the Committee has received no notification of any change in posture with respect to intelligence support to Ukraine, but we are seeking confirmation. To the Ukrainian people, it remains the case that the vast majority of Congress and the American people stand with Ukraine in their fight to defend their country, and we will continue to do so.”
title: Himes Statement on U.S. Support for Ukraine
