Assistant U.S Attorney Eric B. Chen of the Northern District of Texas and Assistant Deputy Chief William Montague and Trial Attorney Max Willner-Giwerc of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section are prosecuting the case.

United States v. Theodore Henderson (Sentencing)

Theodore James Henderson, 51, from Coppel, Texas, was sentenced to 57 months in federal prison and ordered to pay over $300,000 in restitution to the IRS for the preparation and filing of false tax returns Sept. 29.

According to court documents, Henderson registered with the IRS as an authorized tax preparer for third party taxpayers. Beginning in 2015 Henderson intentionally included false losses for Schedule C business in multiple clients’ tax returns. Starting in 2020, Henderson selected refund anticipation advances for his clients from a financial institution. The financial institution then issued the advances and deposited the funds onto debit cards that were in Henderson’s possession. Henderson withdrew those anticipation advances from the debit cards, stealing the fraudulently obtained tax refunds from his clients for his own personal use. Henderson pleaded guilty in September 2025 to one count each of preparing false tax returns and bank fraud. He was initially charged with 22 counts of tax fraud and eight counts of bank fraud.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Elise Alendifer prosecuted the case.

United States v. John Fitzgerald (Superseding Indictment)

John Fitzgerald, 60, formerly of Grand Prairie, surrendered to federal authorities on Sept. 29, after a federal grand jury indicted him for filing false tax returns that failed to report income he misappropriated from his employer.

According to the superseding indictment, from 2018-2021, Fitzgerald allegedly underreported approximately $1.5 million in income on his federal income tax returns that he had misappropriated from his employer, resulting in about $550,000 in underreported taxes.

If convicted, Fitzgerald faces a maximum penalty of three years in prison on each of the three counts.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Elise Alendifer is prosecuting the case.

United States v. Anderson Condoll, Jr. (Plea)

Anderson Condoll, Jr., 44, from The Colony, Texas, filed plea papers admitting to one count of tax evasion Aug. 10, and formally pleaded guilty on Oct. 6.

According to plea papers, Condoll, Jr. admitted that he owed $437,245 in federal income taxes spanning 2014-2025. The defendant admitted that he would file Forms W-4 with his employers falsely claiming to be exempt from income taxes, causing his employers to not withhold income taxes from his wages.

A grand jury indicted Condoll, Jr. in April 2026 on five counts of tax evasion for years 2019-2023. Condoll, Jr. faces up to five years in federal prison.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Ignacio Perez de la Cruz is prosecuting the case.

Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

ALBUQUERQUE – A Bosnian national was sentenced to 60 months in federal prison after pleading guilty to federal export and sanctions violations by conspiring and attempting to broker the sale of Man Portable Air Defense Systems, which are anti-aircraft missiles.

According to court documents, Sasa Micev , 43, a citizen of Bosnia, is an international arms dealer. In that capacity, Micev worked with a co-conspirator based in New Mexico. Together, Micev and his co-conspirator worked with others to violate and evade restrictions imposed by the U.S. department of the Treasury under the North Korea Sanctions Regulations by brokering the purchase of SA-18 Igla portable surface-to-air missiles from North Korea without the required license or approvals from the Department of Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control.

On multiple occasions in 2020, Micev and a co-conspirator discussed unlawfully acquiring the Igla missiles and Micev provided pricing information, participated in efforts to obtain the items through falsified documentation, and worked to procure the weapons from North Korea despite knowing that such transactions were prohibited under U.S. and international laws.

In late 2020, Micev and the co-conspirator traveled to Ankara, Turkey to meet and complete the sale of the Igla missiles. However, after a price dispute with the North Koreans, the sale fell through.

“U.S. sanctions mean little if those who knowingly evade them face no consequences,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison. “This defendant helped carry out an international scheme to conduct business that U.S. law prohibited, and this sentence holds him accountable for his role. I am proud of the investigators and prosecutors whose hard work and dedication brought this case to sentencing in New Mexico. Their commitment to seeing this prosecution through is a testament to the caliber of the people who serve in this district.”

Congressman Gonzalez Delivers Over $9 Million in Federal Funds for Cameron County
Federal funds will expand public parking for commercial truckers at Los Indios Port of Entry
Washington, D.C.—Today, Congressman Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34) announced $9,182,608 in federal funds for Cameron County to reconstruct approximately 0.35 miles of Rio Grande Avenue and provide access to a new public commercial motor vehicle parking facility near the Los Indios Port of Entry. The project will include roughly 305 dedicated parking truck spaces. This investment will also support roadway improvements, driver amenities, security features, an automated weight station, and intelligent parking system technology.
“South Texas is an international hub for trade and commerce, and our infrastructure must keep pace with heightened demands,” said Congressman Gonzalez. “As working families continue to struggle with rising costs, this $9.1 million federal investment will provide commercial truckers with support to maintain efficient operations when supplying our region and the rest of the country with goods and materials. As your Congressman, I proudly passed the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law that authorized this funding, and I will continue working to ensure our ports of entry and the workers who keep it running have the resources they need to operate efficiently.”
“We’re extremely grateful to the U.S. Department of Transportation for awarding Cameron County over $9 million for the Los Indios Bridge Commercial Motor Vehicle (CMV) Parking Facility,” said Cameron County Judge Eddie Treviño, Jr. “Logistics and cross-border trade are vital to Cameron County’s economy. This investment will strengthen our connections with Mexico and improve our regional trade infrastructure by providing truck drivers with a dedicated, safe place to rest before continuing their routes. In turn, this project will help support more efficient cross-border commerce and strengthen supply chains across the nation.”
Today’s announcement was made possible by Congressman Gonzalez’s support of the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which was enacted in 2021 and provided $1.2 trillion to modernize America’s infrastructure, including roads, bridges, water and wastewater, clean energy and broadband access. Through the law’s five-year funding process, $7.25 billion was allocated to the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Nationally Significant Multimodal Freight & Highway Projects (INFRA) program to strengthen America’s supply chains and improve road safety nationwide. The Los Indios Port of Entry is one of 14 projects receiving designated funding for truck parking in Fiscal Year 2026.

text:
Protecting San Diego Through Partnerships, Resolve, and Results
This opinion piece by FBI San Diego Special Agent in Charge Mark Remily was published in the San Diego Union-Tribune on October 14, 2026.
Shortly after I arrived in San Diego in April, our community faced the tragic mass shooting at the Islamic Center of San Diego, which claimed three innocent lives. This horrific act of violence was a stark reminder of the threats we continue to face. Since then, the FBI, working closely with our law enforcement partners, has pursued the investigation with unwavering determination. The recent arrest of a juvenile co‑conspirator located in North Carolina underscores our commitment to holding every responsible individual accountable and preventing further violence.
San Diego is defined not only by its beauty but by its unity and collaboration. I am honored to serve in a region where federal, state, and local law enforcement work seamlessly together to protect the public. Having served across the country, I can say the partnership culture in San Diego is truly exceptional in how its agencies work to safeguard communities.
Over the past year, FBI San Diego has delivered meaningful results across violent crime, national security, cyber investigations, and international fraud. Nationwide, public safety has strengthened significantly. New FBI Uniform Crime Reporting data shows violent crime fell 9.3% from 2024 to 2025, the largest decline since national tracking began in 1936. Murder and robbery each dropped more than 18%, and property crime fell 12.4%. These reductions reflect strengthened partnerships and focused enforcement.
Locally, FBI San Diego and our law enforcement partners played a central role in these gains. We led significant operations targeting violent gangs, including Operation Encripted, which resulted in 33 narcotics‑related arrests and disrupted networks contributing to local violence.
Public safety also includes securing major events. FBI San Diego worked closely with military partners, local agencies, and federal entities to protect the NASCAR event on Coronado, an unprecedented undertaking requiring sophisticated coordination. We served as a base camp for the FIFA World Cup and have begun preparations for the LA28 Olympics, helping ensure major gatherings are safe and supported by the full strength of our region’s capabilities.
Another priority is combating international fraud networks. San Diego has become a national leader in dismantling overseas scam compounds—large‑scale criminal enterprises running cryptocurrency investment schemes. Earlier this year, an international operation resulted in 276 arrests and dismantled nine scam centers across Southeast Asia.
Through close partnerships with private industry and the Scam Center Strike Force, FBI San Diego helped seize malicious domains, recover tens of millions in cryptocurrency, and support a State Department reward of up to $10 million for information leading to the recovery of stolen funds. These efforts make clear that even when fraud networks operate abroad, their reach into our communities will be met with the full strength of U.S. law enforcement.
San Diego is also leading the nation in protecting older Americans. Our office is home to the only Elder Justice Task Force in the country, focused on preventing fraud before victims lose their savings. Working with law enforcement, financial institutions, and victim services organizations, the task force intervenes in real time—halting transfers, recovering funds, and returning money to victims. These efforts have prevented millions of dollars in harm and set a national standard for safeguarding seniors.
Our national security mission remains equally critical. FBI San Diego supported important terrorism investigations involving individuals alleged to have provided material support to foreign terrorist organizations. These arrests underscore the strength of Joint Terrorism Task Force partnerships and our commitment to protecting U.S. service members and citizens.
We have also played a central role in major cyber operations targeting state‑sponsored threats. Working with the Department of Justice and the FBI’s Cyber Division, our teams helped disrupt platforms used by a People’s Republic of China sponsored cyber group targeting U.S. critical infrastructure, dismantling malware designed to conceal foreign cyberattacks.
After 17 years with the FBI and over 25 years in law enforcement, I have never seen stronger momentum or partnerships. San Diego’s collaborative culture, combined with recent Bureau reforms, continues to drive results that keep our community safe.
San Diego is extraordinary, and its residents deserve the very best from their public safety partners. Every day, I am humbled and honored to lead the men and women of FBI San Diego who work to deliver exactly that.
title: Protecting San Diego Through Partnerships, Resolve, and Results

FRESNO Calif. — Keynin McGee, 27, of Oakland, pleaded guilty yesterday to sex trafficking a minor in the Eastern District of California, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced.

According to court documents, McGee met the minor victim in 2021 through Instagram. After months of speaking with her, McGee bought the victim a bus ticket for her to travel to meet him in person. When she arrived, McGee picked the victim up at the bus station, bought her clothing, and took her to a hotel. He then posted photographs of the victim online on a website commonly used to buy and sell sex. McGee then drove the victim to outdoor areas in Oakland and San Francisco known for commercial sex work and instructed her to solicit sex buyers in passing cars. Because of his conduct, the minor victim engaged in commercial sex acts with multiple buyers.

“This guilty plea illustrates the dedicated work of our law enforcement partners and prosecutors to investigate and stamp out sex trafficking and to hold traffickers accountable,” said U.S. Attorney Eric Grant. “Protecting vulnerable victims requires sustained collaboration, thorough investigations, and a commitment to prosecute to the fullest extent of the law. We will continue working together to identify and support victims and bring to justice those who exploit them.”

“Exploiting a child for financial gain is reprehensible and heinous,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Yesterday’s guilty plea of Keynin McGee to sex trafficking of a minor, who he lured to meet him in person then trafficked her for commercial sex in the Oakland and San Francisco areas, reflects our commitment to protecting children from the scourge of sex trafficking. The Criminal Division will continue to pursue and prosecute vile individuals who victimize and traffic minors.”

“Keynin McGee reduced his young victim to a commodity to be bought and sold for his own gain,” said Special Agent in Charge Brian Tosh of FBI Sacramento. “Anyone who seeks to exploit children will face relentless pursuit from the FBI and our law enforcement partners. We will hold traffickers fully accountable for the harm they inflict. Together, we can protect the vulnerable and create a safer future for every child.”

The FBI is investigating the case with assistance from the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation. Assistant U.S. Attorney David Gappa for the Eastern District of California and Deputy Chief Leah Branch of the Criminal Division’s Human Rights and Special Prosecutions Section are prosecuting the case.

McGee is scheduled to be sentenced by U.S. District Judge Jennifer L. Thurston on Jan. 19, 2027, and faces a mandatory minimum penalty of 10 years in prison and a maximum of life in prison. The actual sentence, however, will be determined at the discretion of the court after consideration of any applicable statutory factors and the federal Sentencing Guidelines, which take into account a number of variables.

Anyone who has information about human trafficking should report that information to the National Human Trafficking Hotline toll-free at 1-888-373-7888, which is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week. For more information about human trafficking, please visit www.humantraffickinghotline.org . Information on the Justice Department’s efforts to combat human trafficking can be found at www.justice.gov/humantrafficking .
title: Oakland man pleads guilty to sex trafficking a minor

FBI Operations Director to Keynote Cybersecurity Conference at Boston College Law School
FBI and BC Law Collaborate for 10th Annual Cyber Security Conference
Jose Perez, operations director of the Criminal and Cyber Branch at the Federal Bureau of Investigation, will deliver the keynote address at the 10th annual Boston Conference on Cybersecurity at 9:15 a.m. EDT on Wednesday, October 14, in Stuart Room 315 at Boston College Law School, 885 Centre Street, Newton Centre, Massachusetts.
Perez will discuss the FBI's work to address today's cyber threats, the importance of strong partnerships, and the FBI's primary role to ensure that Americans are safe, secure, and confident in our digitally connected world.
Following Perez’s remarks, two panels, each composed of cybersecurity and legal experts, will discuss the threat landscape and a simulated cyberattack, respectively.
The first panel, titled “Cybersecurity and AI Governance: Navigating the Threat Landscape and Staying Ahead of the Curve,” will be moderated by Michael Roberts, counsel at McDermott, Will, and Schulte. Panelists include Matthew Greenberg, assistant general counsel and executive director, Cybersecurity and Incident Response at Wells Fargo; Brigadier General Nathan Kearns, U.S. Cyber Command, U.S. Air Force; Mark Sutton, managing director and CISO, Bain Capital Ventures; Michael Kelly, special agent, FBI Boston-Cyber Division; and Christopher Porter, head of International Security Cooperation and Threat Intelligence at Google.
The second panel, titled “Cyber Attack Simulation: Resilient Incident Response in the Age of AI,” will be moderated by Heather Egan, partner, Cybersecurity, Incident Response and Data Privacy at Morgan Lewis. Panelists include Simon Taylor, CEO and founder, HYCU, Inc.; Katie Jenkins, executive vice president and CISO, Liberty Mutual; Scott Lashway, partner and chair, Cybersecurity and Data Privacy Group, Mintz; Jarret Wright, chief information officer, MassPort; Josh Madeley, Incident Response Practice lead, Mandiant (Google); and Doug Domin, supervisory special agent, FBI Boston-Cyber Crime Division.
Odette Lienau, the Marianne D. Short, Esq. dean and professor of Law, Boston College Law School; Ted E. Docks, special agent in charge, FBI Boston Division; and Kevin R. Powers, faculty director and lecturer-in-law, MLS in Cybersecurity, Risk, and Governance, Boston College Law School, will deliver respective opening remarks.
The half-day Boston Conference on Cybersecurity is the result of a long-term partnership between the FBI and the Master of Legal Studies (MLS) in Cybersecurity, Rick, and Governance Program at Boston College Law School.
“There’s no question, we’re reaping the rewards of unprecedented digital innovation, but our expanding digital landscape has also created more ways for malicious actors to attack us,” said FBI Boston Special Agent in Charge Ted E. Docks. “Your FBI is focused on investigating and disrupting these attacks, supporting victims, and increasing our impact through partnerships. That said, we are only as good as the information we share with each other when an incident occurs, which is why events like this are so critical to advancing our shared goal of sharing intelligence and making cybercrime harder, riskier, and far less profitable for those behind it.”
"Behind every cyberattack is a real victim. A hospital forced to divert ambulances, a small business that loses everything overnight or a family whose savings disappears with one click," said the FBI's Operational Director Jose Perez. "With cyber threats against our nation's critical infrastructure, businesses, and American families more persistent than ever, the FBI is using every tool and authority we have to disrupt these actors. Every report to the FBI helps us identify the attackers, disrupt their operations, and warn the next potential victim before they’re hit. If you or your organization experiences cybercrime, contact your local FBI field office or submit a report at www.ic3.gov."
title: FBI Operations Director to Keynote Cybersecurity Conference at Boston College Law School

BURLINGTON – The United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Vermont stated that on October 14, 2026, Marshall Gagne, 35, of Weathersfield, Vermont, was sentenced by United States District Judge Geoffrey W. Crawford to a term of 120 months’ imprisonment to be followed by a 3-year term of supervised release. On June 10, 2026, Gagne pleaded guilty to possession of firearms as a convicted felon and possession of controlled substances with intent to distribute them.

According to court records, Gagne was arrested in a hotel room in Claremont, New Hampshire on May 19, 2025, where evidence indicated that Gagne and six occupants were destroying drugs as the Claremont Police Department pried open the hotel room door with a crowbar. Gagne was carrying more than $11,000 in cash in a backpack with fentanyl residue on the shoulder strap and DNA evidence later revealed that he was armed with a handgun found in the hotel room. The next day, on May 20, 2025, Vermont State Police executed a search warrant at the home where Gagne was staying in Weathersfield, Vermont. During the search, law enforcement found in a camping van thousands more dollars in additional drug proceeds along with 13 firearms, including un-serialized privately manufactured “ghost” guns, a silencer with the serial number scratched off, and ammunition and gun parts, along with the box for the handgun Gagne was using in the hotel the night before. Gagne was previously convicted of a felony and was prohibited from possessing any firearms or ammunition. Gagne later coached a witness to lie to law enforcement by trying to claim that he had sold the camping van to a drug dealer who had subsequently been fatally shot. But DNA evidence found only Gagne’s DNA on the seized firearms, rather than the deceased drug dealer.

First Assistant United States Attorney Jonathan A. Ophardt commended the collaborative investigatory efforts of the Vermont State Police, the FBI, and the Claremont (NH) Police Department.

The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Dana E. Hill. Gagne was represented by Federal Public Defender Alejandro Fernandez.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities.
title: Weathersfield Convicted Felon Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison for Possessing Firearms in Vermont and Distributing Drugs in New Hampshire

Today, October 14, 2026, the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division), along with the Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI), announced a nationwide series of enforcement actions targeting tax fraud.

The U.S. Attorney’s Office in the Western District of Louisiana was a key participant in this surge effort. Between early September and today, the Fraud Division’s Tax Section and U.S. Attorneys’ Offices across the country joined forces in the Department’s first-ever National Tax Enforcement Surge. This surge of nationwide resources resulted in prosecutorial actions against 76 defendants whose alleged and proven crimes intended an estimated loss of revenue to the federal government of more than $490,000,000.

“Tax fraud is not a victimless crime — it harms employees, honest taxpayers, and business owners — and the integrity of our American system,” said United States Attorney Zachary A. Keller. “Our Office will aggressively pursue anyone who steals from their employees, evades lawful tax obligations, and undermines the public’s trust in the fair and unbiased application of our federal tax laws.”

According to the Western District of Louisiana’s indictment:

• Defendant: Alicia Williams Higginbotham , 51, of Lake Charles • Indicted: September 16, 2026 • Alleged conduct: Failure to account for and pay over trust fund taxes; failure to file individual income tax returns • Alleged loss amount: Over $390,000 • Charges: 14 counts of Failure to Account for and Pay Over Trust Fund Taxes; four counts of Failure to File an Individual Income Tax Return • Maximum penalties: Up to five years in prison for each count of the first charge and up to one year for each count of the second.

Higginbotham was arrested on Thursday, September 17, 2026, released on a $25,000 bond, and ordered to surrender her passport.

According to court documents, Higginbotham managed and was also a member of a home healthcare company operating in Calcasieu Parish. She is alleged to have exercised financial control over the business and to have been responsible for collecting, accounting for, and paying over federal employment taxes. The indictment alleges that Higginbotham failed to account for and pay quarterly federal employment taxes for employees for calendar quarters from 2020 through 2023. She allegedly withheld the money from her employees’ paychecks but failed to pay it to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) in an amount totaling more than $390,000. The indictment further alleges that for tax years 2020 through 2023, Higginbotham willfully failed to file required individual federal income tax returns.

The IRS – CI investigated this case. It is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney J. Daniel Siefker, Jr., with assistance from Paralegal Specialist Denise Duhon.

An indictment, information, or complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

You may find a copy of this press release (and any updates) on the website of the United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Louisiana at www.justice.gov/usao-wdla. Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Western District of Louisiana at www.lawd.uscourts.gov or at https://www.lawd.uscourts.gov/cmecf-pacer. The case number for this matter is 2:26-CR-00369-01.

To view successes of other U.S. Attorney’s offices across the country, please refer to this press release: https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/dojs-fraud-division-irs-and-irs-ci-expose-more-490m-tax-fraud-national-tax-enforcement-surge

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

Florida Man Sentenced to Prison for Tax Refund Fraud
A Florida man was sentenced on October 6, 2026, to 36 months in prison for filing a false tax return on behalf of a trust he controlled as part of a $4.2 million refund fraud scheme.
According to court documents and statements made in court, McDonald Preval, of Miami, filed numerous false tax returns for himself and trusts he claimed to control. The trust tax returns reported that the trusts had earned significant income and made tax withholding payments to the IRS, purportedly entitling the trusts to large tax refunds. In fact, the trusts did not have the claimed income, and did not make payments in the amounts claimed on the returns, and therefore were not entitled to the refunds Preval claimed. He also filed tax returns for 2023 that did not include the income from his employment. The false tax returns Preval caused to be filed on behalf of purported trusts and himself collectively sought tax refunds totaling more than $4.2 million. Preval obtained more than $580,000 from his scheme, which he used to pay off the mortgage loan on his house and other personal expenses.
Preval pleaded guilty to one count of filing a false tax return. In addition to a term of imprisonment, U.S. District Judge Cecilia M. Altonaga ordered Preval to pay $580,647 in restitution to the IRS and to serve one year of supervised release.
Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation investigated the case.
Trial Attorneys Melissa Siskind and Kavitha Bondada of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section prosecuted the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

OREGON LAWMAKERS URGE CONTINUED SUPPORT FOR OREGON’S HAZELNUT INDUSTRY
Eugene, OR – Today, Oregon’s U.S. Senator Jeff Merkley led members of Oregon’s congressional delegation in a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Secretary Brooke Rollins that calls on the Department to deliver critical federal support to Oregon’s hazelnut industry under the federal Section 32 purchase program.
“The hazelnut industry is a massive and integral part of our state’s agricultural economy; its size and longevity represent generations of farmers and handlers who have dedicated their lives to producing and distributing a product many communities depend on for their livelihoods,” wrote the lawmakers.
The lawmakers’ letter calls on USDA to include Oregon hazelnuts, which account for 99 percent of hazelnuts produced in the United States, in this year’s Section 32 purchases, supporting growers, harvesters, processors, and agricultural economies primarily in Oregon’s Willamette Valley during a period of significant market disruption and economic uncertainty in a global market.
They stressed, “In recent years, disruptions in important export markets caused by these compounding issues have been particularly difficult for certain kernel sizes and grades that are high-quality, marketable food products but have fewer commercial outlets. These imbalances and market losses create uncertainty and pressure for our farmers and producers and threaten the steady distribution needed to prevent compounding product surpluses year-to-year.”
In addition to Merkley, the letter was signed by U.S. Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) and U.S. Representatives Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Janelle Bynum (OR-05), and Val Hoyle (OR-04).

David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, announced that CHRISTIAN LOPEZ, also known as “Face,” 42, of New Haven, was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge Stefan R. Underhill in Bridgeport to 84 months of imprisonment and four years of supervised release for trafficking fentanyl.

ST. GEORGE , Utah – An illegal alien from Nicaragua was sentenced to 41 months’ imprisonment today after law enforcement recovered approximately 104,000 fentanyl pills that weighed approximately 23 pounds, during a traffic violation in August 2025.

The sentence, imposed by U.S. District Court Judge Ann Marie McIff Allen, comes after Hector Luis Castillo-Reyes, 23, residing illegally in Fresno, California, pleaded guilty on July 20, 2026, to possession of fentanyl with intent to distribute. In addition to his term of imprisonment, Castillo-Reyes was sentenced to three years of supervised release. Additionally, upon his release, Castillo-Reyes will be remanded to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) for deportation proceedings.

According to court documents and statements made at Castillo-Reyes’s change of plea and sentencing hearings, on August 14, 2025, a San Juan County Deputy Sheriff stopped Castillo-Reyes for a traffic violation. A dog sniff was conducted and the K9 alerted positive to the presence of illegal narcotics. During a search of the vehicle, law enforcement recovered approximately 104,000 blue M30 fentanyl pills inside of a toolbox set in the rear cargo area of the vehicle. Castillo-Reyes admitted to picking up the bag containing the fentanyl pills and transporting them in exchange for payment.

“This case highlights the excellent coordination of our state, federal, and tribal partners in removing this poison from our streets,” said U.S. Attorney Melissa Holyoak of the District of Utah. “We are grateful to DEA, SBI, BIA, ICE, and the San Juan County Sheriff’s Office for working together with our office to ensure that the 104,000 seized fentanyl pills never reached our communities.”

MIAMI – A West Palm Beach man has been sentenced to 235 months in federal prison for selling more than 200 videos depicting child sexual abuse.

U.S. District Judge Aileen M. Cannon imposed the sentence on Kenneth Wayne Brown III, 21, after he pleaded guilty to one count of distribution of child pornography.

“Kenneth Brown turned the sexual abuse of innocent children into a business, putting a price tag on some of the most horrific crimes imaginable. Every video represents the exploitation of a real child, and every sale perpetuates that abuse. He will now spend nearly 20 years in federal prison. Let this sentence send a clear message: if you exploit children, traffic in their abuse, or profit from their suffering, our prosecutors and law enforcement partners will find you and bring you to justice,” said U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern district of Florida.

According to court records, in November 2025, Brown used an online mobile messaging application to communicate with an individual he believed was interested in buying child sexual abuse material (CSAM). Brown provided the individual with a price sheet and sent a sample from his CSAM collection, which depicted a pre-pubescent child engaged in a forced sexual act. Brown then accepted $30 in exchange for more than 200 videos of CSAM.

U.S. Attorney Reding Quiñones and Special Agent in Charge Brett D. Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office made the announcement.

FBI Miami investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Katie Wilson prosecuted the case.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, visit www.justice.gov/psc .

Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Southern District of Florida at www.flsd.uscourts.gov or at http://pacer.flsd.uscourts.gov , under case number 25-cr-80208.

Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Delivers $200 Million Truck Parking Expansion Across the Country in Major Win For American Truckers
Funds will cover 14 expansion projects across 12 states to tackle truckers’ #1 problem when hauling critical cargo
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy today announced a $200 million investment to expand truck parking in 12 states through the Department’s Nationally Significant Multimodal Freight & Highway Projects (INFRA) program. These investments will expand public parking for hardworking truckers along America's most critical freight corridors and help reduce fatigue-related accidents, improve supply chain efficiency, and deliver significant savings.
Reminder: 40% of truckers spend over an hour a day searching for parking—costing our national economy billions in wasted time. Limited safe, public commercial vehicle parking is also a safety issue – forcing truckers to park in harm's way.
“American truckers are finally getting the attention and support they deserve thanks to President Trump,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “These patriotic men and women work hard to ensure our store shelves are stocked, our gas stations are fueled, and our packages are delivered. They shouldn’t have to spend over an hour looking for a safe place to rest at the end of the day. This nationwide investment will make America’s truckers safer, enhance our supply chains, and reduce freight costs.”
The investments are going toward 14 truck parking projects in 12 states, including:
- $11.95 million to the Georgia Ports Authority to build the Port of Savannah Commercial Motor Vehicle Parking Area adjacent to Georgia State Route 21 in Garden City, Georgia. This facility will have approximately 275 commercial vehicle spaces.
- $24.5 million to the Iowa Department of Transportation to expand and modernize commercial motor vehicle parking at six public rest areas along I-80 in Mitchellville, Wilton, Victor, Minden, and Underwood.
- $6 million to the North Carolina State Ports Authority to construct approximately 140 dedicated commercial motor vehicle parking spaces and approximately 50 container staging positions at the Port of Wilmington in New Hanover County, North Carolina.
- $5 million to the City of Fort Worth to construct approximately 100 new commercial motor vehicle parking spaces at the Pilot Travel Center in Fort Worth, Texas, along I-35.
- $9 million to Cameron County, Texas, to reconstruct approximately 0.35 miles of Rio Grande Avenue to provide access to a new public commercial motor vehicle parking facility near the Los Indios Port of Entry that will include approximately 305 dedicated truck parking spaces.
- $15 million to the Wisconsin Department of Transportation to expand commercial motor vehicle parking by approximately 106 spaces between two safety rest areas along a rural area of I-41 in Dodge County, Wisconsin.’
“Truck parking is one of the most persistent challenges faced by American truckers today, and under President Trump and Secretary Duffy, we’re tackling it head on,” said Federal Motor Carrier Administrator Derek D. Barrs. “This investment will deliver hundreds of new spots across the country, helping hardworking truck drivers get the rest they need and reducing dangerous roadside parking on some of America’s most important corridors.”
These investments were made via the INFRA program, which bolsters America’s supply chains and improves road safety for families by building highways, bridges, and port infrastructure nationwide.

Pressley, City of Boston Announce More Than $16 Million to Modernize Fairmount Apartments in Hyde Park
Pressley, City of Boston, Sec. Matias, State Rep. Consalvo Announce Initial Phase of Renovations that include Energy Retrofits, Accessibility Upgrades, Sustainable Infrastructure, and Workforce Opportunities
BOSTON – Today, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), alongside Mayor Michelle Wu, Executive Office of Housing and Livable Communities (EOHLC) Secretary Juana Matias, Representative Rob Consalvo, and Boston Housing Authority (BHA) Administrator Kenzie Bok,joined residents to announce more than $16 million in state, city, and federal funding to modernize the Fairmount public housing community in Hyde Park. This announcement represents the latest investment in the city’s public housing communities.
The funding includes $1M of Community Project Fund investment secured by Congresswoman Pressley and Senators Edward Markey and Elizabeth Warren, a $10 million High Leverage Asset Preservation Program (HILAPP) grant from EOHLC, and $5 million in City of Boston capital funding for the Fairmount Modernization Project. The Boston Public Health Commission has granted funds for open space improvements and community garden installations. Together, the funding will create a more accessible and resilient community.
“Residents in the Massachusetts 7th not only deserve a safe, stable place to call home, but also one that reflects modern-day needs in accessibility, resiliency, and sustainability—and this essential funding to modernize the Fairmount Apartments will do exactly that,” said Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley. “This investment is a reflection of community input realized and I’m grateful for every engaged resident who made their voice heard. I’m proud to deliver this funding alongside our city and state partners in Mayor Wu, Secretary Matias, Administrator Bok, Rep. Consalvo, and others to invest in existing public housing and improve livability for our communities.”
“Over the last five years, Boston has built nearly 16,000 new units of housing throughout our neighborhoods. In order to make our city a home for everyone, we must also preserve and modernize the affordable homes that already exist,” said Mayor Michelle Wu. “I’m grateful to all our partners for helping secure funding for this comprehensive, multi-phase renovation of the Fairmount Apartments, and I look forward to working with residents to deliver beautiful, upgraded homes for these families.”
“The Boston Housing Authority is so grateful to our city, state, and federal partners for investing in our public housing communities,” said Kenzie Bok, Administrator of the Boston Housing Authority. “With this funding, Fairmount will remain a welcoming place for families to call Hyde Park home for decades to come.”
The BHA is kicking off a Master Planning process for the Fairmount community, creating an area-wide vision while beginning a first phase of physical improvements. The initial phase of upgrades will focus on modernizing unit interiors, making 5% of apartments fully accessible, electrifying heating and hot water systems, and adding cooling. It will also include building envelope improvements and installing green stormwater infrastructure to support the community’s long-term sustainability and climate resilience.
“Thanks to Governor Healey’s Affordable Homes Act, HLC has been able to expand the funding needed to improve the state’s public housing system,” said Housing and Livable Communities Secretary Juana Matias. “We’re not just building new housing, but investing in the homes we already have and the people who live in them. The preservation of Fairmount Apartments is exactly what that commitment looks like.”
“I am thrilled that this enormous investment is happening at the Fairmount Housing Development, literally blocks away from my home here in Hyde Park,” said State Representative Rob Consalvo. “This partnership between the State, City, and Federal government will ensure that the residents of this development will be able to live in safe, modern and accessible units now and for years to come.”
An additional federal investment secured by the Congressional delegation is going to support flood mitigation for affordable housing developments, including BHA properties. The city and BHA have collaborated on multi-site stormwater projects serving the Fairmount, Gallivan, and Franklin Field communities, an effort bolstered by this federal backing. The project will fund a community garden and new rain gardens to mitigate stormwater pollution and prevent flooding. Through Boston’s PowerCorps program, local residents will be trained to build and maintain the rain gardens while earning green career credentials.
“As the District 5 City Councilor, Chair of the Boston City Council’s Housing Committee, and someone who grew up in public housing, I know firsthand how important it is for families to have a place they can be proud to call home,” said Councilor Enrique Pepén. “This $16 million investment in the Fairmount Apartments is exactly the kind of commitment our residents deserve, one that strengthens our communities, improves quality of life, and ensures families can continue to thrive in the neighborhoods they call home. I’m grateful to our state and federal partners for their collaboration and commitment to making this important investment possible.”
“This $16 million investment is an exciting step forward in advancing affordable, accessible, and high-quality housing for residents of Fairmount Apartments in Hyde Park,” said Councilor Ruthzee Louijeune. “By investing in our public housing communities, we are strengthening neighborhoods and ensuring that families have safe, stable homes where they can thrive. I look forward to seeing the lasting impact these improvements will have on Fairmount residents for years to come.”
Fairmount Apartments in Hyde Park was constructed in 1951 and includes over 200 units of state public housing.
As a Member of the Subcommittee on Housing and Insurance of the House Financial Services Committee (FSC), Rep. Pressley has consistently advocated for policies that affirm housing as a human right and center the dignity and humanity of all people.
In June 2026, the 21st Century Road to Housing Act passed Congress and included four bills led by Congresswoman Pressley that would address the housing crisis and increase pathways to equitable and affordable housing. The bills will address bias in home valuations, expand affordable housing, strengthen oversight of corporate landlords, and help families reach financial stability. The bill became law despite Donald Trump’s refusal to sign it.

COLUMBUS - Ohioans affected by the August storms, tornadoes and flooding can now apply for FEMA assistance until December 1, 2026. Submitting an application is an initial step in your FEMA process.
After You Apply
- You will receive a nine-digit FEMA application number. Keep this number in a safe place and refer to it whenever you contact FEMA.
- Your application will be reviewed. FEMA may contact you by phone, text, email, mail, or through your online account if more information is needed.
If you haven’t applied yet, the fastest way to do so is online at DisasterAssistance.gov or the Spanish language DisasterAssistance.gov/es. You can also call the FEMA Helpline at 800-621-3362.
A Home Inspection
Within ten days of applying for assistance, you may be contacted by an inspector to schedule an appointment at the address where damage was reported.
Here’s what to expect:
- A FEMA inspector will contact you using the phone number you provided. The contact may come from an unfamiliar or restricted number. Be sure to answer or call back so your application can move forward.
- When the FEMA inspector contacts you, write down their name, date of contact, date and time of appointment and the inspector’s phone number.
- Inspectors will show official FEMA photo identification when they arrive at your home. You should always ask to see identification.
- There is no cost for a FEMA inspection. Inspectors will never ask for money, banking information, or payment of any kind.
- During the inspection, you or your co-applicant should be present to:
  - Confirm your identity, home ownership (if applicable) and occupancy,
  - Provide a list of household occupants living in the home at the time of disaster,
  - Supply any insurance documents requested by the inspector,
  - Walk the inspector through the damaged areas or show documentation of damage, and
  - Describe your losses.
- If you are unable to meet with the inspector, you can designate someone else to meet with the inspector on your behalf. You must provide FEMA with a copy of this written designation.
- If you have already started repairs, photos and receipts can help show the damage that occurred.
After the Home Inspection
Information gathered during the inspection is only one of several criteria used by FEMA to determine eligibility for assistance. If you have questions after your inspection, please call FEMA’s Helpline at 800-621-3362.
You will receive information explaining FEMA's eligibility decision within 10 days after the inspector's visit. To receive updates and notifications faster, create an online DisasterAssistance.gov account after applying for FEMA assistance.
Learn more about FEMA’s inspection process by visiting the Home Inspections page.
title: What to Expect After you Apply for FEMA Assistance

Cities of Gilroy and Mountain View Advance Protections Restricting ICE Facility Construction
SAN JOSÉ, CA – Today, Reps. Zoe Lofgren (CA-18) and Sam Liccardo (CA-16) congratulated the City of Gilroy and City of Mountain View for taking steps to keep ICE out of their communities. On October 13, the Mountain View City Council adopted an interim urgency ordinance temporarily restricting new detention or custodial facilities. The action follows the Gilroy City Council's unanimous vote on October 5 to establish a 45-day moratorium on new detention facilities within city limits.
"I applaud the Cities of Gilroy and Mountain View for taking a stand in support of transparency, accountability, and the rule of law,” said Rep. Lofgren. "These ordinances send a clear message that no law enforcement agency should be allowed to expand its power without first demonstrating that it follows the law. ICE has too often failed to adhere to the legal standards, policies, and procedures that govern every other law enforcement agency. Unless and until ICE complies with those requirements and is held to the same standards of accountability as all law enforcement, its detention capacity and authority should not be expanded."
“After plans for an ICE detention center just outside Gilroy were halted in federal court, local leaders are taking action to make it harder for ICE to construct future facilities,” said Rep. Liccardo. “By acting now, local leaders can protect the health and safety of their residents and restrict DHS should they attempt to convert industrial or commercial property into an ICE detention center. I thank Mayor Greg Bozzo, Mayor Emily Ann Ramos and the Gilroy and Mountain View City Councils for joining communities across our region in using their local authority to push back against ICE infrastructure in our community.”
“Mountain View has long been committed to protecting our diverse community, where nearly 43% of residents are foreign-born,” said Mountain View Mayor Emily Ann Ramos. “We listened to the concerns raised by many residents when the U.S. Department of Homeland Security planned to develop a proposed immigration detention and processing facility in Santa Clara County, just outside Gilroy, which was halted by a lawsuit. Thanks to Congressman Liccardo’s encouragement for cities to consider interim land use controls, our City Council has now adopted an emergency ordinance to place a temporary moratorium on detention or custodial facilities in Mountain View.” 
“Gilroy’s future should reflect the values that define our community: care for one another, pride in our agricultural heritage, and a commitment to a safe, healthy, and thriving city,” Gilroy Mayor Greg Bozzo said. “Gilroy City Council members share our residents’ concerns about these types of facilities and their potential impacts on our future. By unanimously adopting this temporary moratorium, our Gilroy City Council has once again shown our commitment to those values and the long-term well-being of our community. I am thankful for Congressman Sam Liccardo's focus on real collaboration and his commitment to Gilroy's interests.”

title: Cities of Gilroy and Mountain View Advance Protections Restricting ICE Facility Construction

SPRINGFIELD, Mo. – A Springfield, Mo., man, who was convicted following a jury trial, of receiving several images of child pornography and using Artificial Intelligence to produce multiple obscene images of children, was sentenced today to 151 months in federal prison by U.S. District Judge Megan Blair Benton. Judge Benton further ordered that he serve 25 years of supervised release following his release from federal prison.

On June 2, 2026, Jeremy Koppenhaver, 46, was found guilty of one count of receipt of child pornography and one count of production of obscene visual representations of the sexual abuse of children, following a two-day jury trial in the United States District Court in Springfield, Mo.

The evidence at trial showed that, on June 22, 2024, the Springfield Police Department responded to a coffee shop in downtown Springfield, after another customer reported that Koppenhaver, who was also at the coffee shop using their internet, was attempting to use AI to produce child pornography. The responding officers seized Koppenhaver’s laptop. Investigators conducted a forensic examination of the laptop and found approximately 19 images of child pornography and approximately 61 obscene images of children created using AI. All images of child pornography depicted real children.

The computer data from the obscene images showed Koppenhaver was using an AI image generation website to depict female celebrities as minors who were being subjected to sexual abuse. The data also revealed Koppenhaver was refining his prompts to evade the community guidelines of the AI website and was attempting to make the images more realistic. Investigators also located images in which Koppenhaver used photo editing software to edit nude images of Koppenhaver into photographs that depicted nude girls. Data on the computer also demonstrated that Koppenhaver had multiple web searches looking for child pornography.

This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Stephanie L. Wan and Randall Eggert. It was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Springfield, Missouri Police Department.

Project Safe Childhood

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the United States Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.usdoj.gov/psc . For more information about Internet safety education, please visit www.usdoj.gov/psc and click on the tab “resources.”
title: Springfield Man Sentenced to Twelve and a Half Years in Prison for Receiving Child Pornography and Producing Obscene Images of Children

SCHNEIDER INTRODUCES LEGISLATION TO PROTECT ACCESS TO ONLINE RESOURCES FOR LGBTQ STUDENTS
LINCOLNSHIRE, IL –Today, during LGBTQ history month, Congressman Brad Schneider (IL-10) introduced legislation to ensure critical online LGBTQ resources are not blocked at schools and public libraries. Currently, public schools and libraries that receive discounted telecommunications and internet rates through the Federal Communication Commission (FCC) E-Rate program must enforce an internet safety policy that in some cases leads to the blocking of useful LGBTQ resources. The Don’t Block LGBTQ Act would clarify that schools and public libraries that block LGBTQ resources would lose access to discounted rates under the E-rate program.
“During LGBTQ History Month, we celebrate the countless LGBTQ Americans who have strengthened our communities and helped move our country forward,” said Schneider. “LGBTQ Americans, especially young people, deserve access to information, support, and resources that can make a meaningful difference in their lives. I'm proud to introduce this legislation to ensure LGBTQ individuals are not prevented from receiving support – whether asking health questions, responding to bullying, or seeking advice about coming out to family and friends.”
According to the American Psychological Association the majority of LGBTQ+ youth have turned to a mental health professional or experienced symptoms of anxiety. Access to resources on where to reach for help is critical to ensuring youth have the support they need.
View the full bill text here.
title: SCHNEIDER INTRODUCES LEGISLATION TO PROTECT ACCESS TO ONLINE RESOURCES FOR LGBTQ STUDENTS

ROCHESTER, MN – Today, U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon visited Minnesota as part of her Returning Education to the States Tour.
Secretary McMahon began her visit at Great Oaks Academy, a public charter school serving students in grades K-10. The visit included a student choir ensemble performance, a recitation of the Pledge of Allegiance in Latin, and a presentation by a fifth-grade poetry class. Afterward, she participated in a Teachers Roundtable to discuss instructional practices and faculty experiences.
Next, Secretary McMahon toured Dakota County Technical College to see how students are preparing for in-demand industries, observing programs for veterinary technology, process technology, and electrical linework. Following the tour, she joined members of the Minnesota State Legislature for a lunch and roundtable discussion focused on returning more education decision-making back to the state and local levels.
Alongside U.S. Representatives Brad Finstad and Pete Stauber, Secretary McMahon wrapped the day at Rochester Community and Technical College. The group toured the campus's hands-on training labs, checking out the dental simulation, peace officer simulation, and automotive spaces.
“Minnesota is the 44th stop on the Returning Education to the States Tour,” said U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon. “What our visits across the state make clear is that a truly responsive education system cannot be driven by federal mandates. From foundational civics and early literacy to high-tech medical and trade labs, success happens when local educators and state leaders have the autonomy to build programs that directly match the unique academic and workforce needs of their own communities.”
Background:
On her Returning Education to the States Tour, Secretary McMahon is traveling to all 50 states to hear directly from teachers, parents, students, and community leaders about what is working in their communities and to compile a toolkit of best practices to share with states across the nation. Learn more about Secretary McMahon’s Returning Education to the States Tour here.
title: U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon Visits Minnesota on Returning Education to the States Tour

WASHINGTON — The U.S. Small Business Administration announced today the opening of a Disaster Loan Outreach Center in Washoe County to assist businesses, private nonprofit organizations, and residents affected by the Bug and Hawk Fires occurring Aug. 8 – Sept. 9.
Beginning Thursday, Oct. 15, SBA customer service representatives will be on hand at the Disaster Loan Outreach Center in Reno to answer questions and assist with the disaster loan application process. Walk-ins are welcome, and in-person appointments can be scheduled in advance at appointment.sba.gov.
The hours of operation are as follows:
WASHOE COUNTY
Disaster Loan Outreach Center
North Valleys Community Center
Opens on Thursday, Oct. 15 at 9 a.m.
Monday – Friday, 9 a.m. – 4 p.m.
Closes permanently Friday, Oct. 30 at 4 p.m.
“When disasters strike, SBA’s Disaster Loan Outreach Centers perform an important role by assisting small businesses and their communities,” said Chris Stallings, Associate Administrator of the Office of Disaster Recovery at SBA. “At these centers, our specialists help business owners and residents apply for disaster loans and learn about the full range of programs available to support their recovery.”
Businesses and nonprofits are eligible to apply for business physical disaster loans and may borrow up to $2 million to repair or replace disaster-damaged or destroyed real estate, machinery and equipment, inventory, and other business assets.
Homeowners and renters are eligible to apply for home and personal property loans and may borrow up to $100,000 to replace or repair personal property, such as clothing, furniture, cars, and appliances. Homeowners may apply for up to $500,000 to replace or repair their primary residence.
Applicants may be eligible for a loan increase of up to 20% of their verified physical damage, for mitigation purposes. Eligible mitigation improvements may include insulating pipes, walls and attics, weather stripping doors and windows, and installing storm windows to help protect property and occupants from future disasters.
The SBA’s Economic Injury Disaster Loan program is available to small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, and private nonprofit organizations — including faith‑based organizations — with financial losses directly related to the disaster. The SBA is unable to provide disaster loans to agricultural producers, farmers, or ranchers, except for small aquaculture enterprises.
Economic Injury Disaster Loan’s are available for working capital needs caused by the disaster and are available even if the small business or private nonprofit did not suffer any physical damage. The loans may be used to pay fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills which could not be paid due to the disaster.
Interest rates are as low as 4% for businesses, 3.625% for nonprofits, and 3% for homeowners and renters, with terms up to 30 years. Interest does not begin to accrue, and payments are not due until 12 months from the date of the first loan disbursement. The SBA determines eligibility and sets loan amounts and terms based on each applicant’s financial condition.
To apply online, visit sba.gov/disaster. Applicants may also call SBA’s National Support Network Center at (866) SBA-HELP or email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov for more information on disaster assistance. For people who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability, please dial 7-1-1 to access telecommunications relay services.
The filing deadline to return applications for physical property damage is Nov. 10. The deadline to return economic injury applications is June 11, 2027.

About the U.S. Small Business Administration
The U.S. Small Business Administration helps power the American dream of business ownership. As the only go-to resource and voice for small businesses backed by the strength of the federal government, the SBA empowers entrepreneurs and small business owners with the resources and support they need to start, grow, expand their businesses, or recover from a declared disaster. It delivers services through an extensive network of SBA field offices and partnerships with public and private organizations. To learn more, visit www.sba.gov.

Congressman Christian Menefee Hosts First-Ever Telephone Town Hall with Hundreds of Houston Constituents
HOUSTON, TX — Yesterday, Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) hosted his first-ever telephone town hall, connecting with hundreds of constituents across Texas’s 18th Congressional District for an hour-long discussion on the issues affecting Houston families. During the event, Congressman Menefee answered questions directly from constituents on a wide range of topics, including rising costs, healthcare, the war in Iran, environmental protections, and opportunities to work across the aisle with Republicans to address challenges facing the district. He also shared updates on his ongoing work in Congress and throughout the Houston community.
"Hearing directly from the folks I represent is the most important part of my job," said Congressman Christian D. Menefee. "Families across Houston are working hard, but their paychecks aren't going as far as they used to. They're worried about paying for groceries, keeping their healthcare, and making sure their communities are safe. These are the concerns I'm hearing every day, and they're exactly what I'm fighting to address in Washington."
Affordability was a major focus of the conversation, with one constituent, Tyler, asking what Congressman Menefee was doing to address rising grocery prices as families struggle to stretch their paychecks. In response, Menefee highlighted his support for legislation to raise wages, expand tax credits, and lower everyday expenses, including the Living Wage for All Act, the Paycheck Fairness Act, and legislation to establish a permanent $300 monthly Child Tax Credit. Drawing on his own upbringing, Menefee discussed how programs such as WIC, free and reduced-price school lunches, Pell Grants, and GI Bill benefits helped his family and shaped his commitment to protecting the social safety net.
Throughout the town hall, participants also responded to three live survey questions addressing some of the most pressing issues facing the country. An overwhelming 93% of respondents said their groceries, rent, or utility bills have become more expensive, while 90% said they oppose President Trump and Republicans' war in Iran. Additionally, 53% reported that they or someone they love had been affected by Republicans' Medicaid cuts.
"These results tell us exactly what families across Houston are worried about," said Congressman Menefee. "People are tired of watching their bills go up while Washington Republicans make life harder for working families. They're worried about losing their healthcare, and they want an end to this war. I'm going to keep taking their concerns directly to Washington and fighting for the relief they deserve."
The town hall builds on Congressman Menefee's ongoing efforts to remain accessible and responsive to the residents of Texas's 18th Congressional District. Since taking office, Menefee and his team have closed more than 500 constituent service cases and helped recover over $1 million for constituents navigating federal agencies.
Congressman Menefee plans to host additional telephone town halls to continue connecting with constituents, answering questions, and providing updates on his work in Houston and Washington. Constituents can learn more about his work or request assistance with a federal agency by visiting Menefee.House.Gov or calling the main District Office at 713-655-0050.
Click HERE to listen to the full town hall.
title: Congressman Christian Menefee Hosts First-Ever Telephone Town Hall with Hundreds of Houston Constituents

NEWPORT NEWS, Va. – A federal grand jury returned a superseding indictment today charging Jordan Isaiah Pierce, 24, with the murders of two store employees during a 2022 robbery.

According to the indictment, on June 15, 2022, Pierce and a co-conspirator robbed a convenience store on Kiln Creek Parkway in Newport News, taking lottery tickets. During the robbery, Pierce, armed with a Draco pistol, allegedly shot and killed two employees. On July 11, 2022, armed with the same firearm used in the June 15 murder and robbery, Pierce and his co-conspirators allegedly robbed another Newport News convenience store and fled with cash.

Pierce is charged with two counts of using a firearm in a crime of violence resulting in death, conspiracy to interfere with commerce by robbery, interference with commerce by robbery, and using a firearm in a crime of violence.

Theophani K. Stamos, First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia; Ian Kaufmann, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI’s Richmond Field Office; and Steve R. Drew, Chief of Newport News Police, made the announcement.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Lisa R. McKeel, Brian J. Samuels, and Mack Coleman are prosecuting the case.

Related court documents and information are located on the website of the District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia or on PACER by searching for Case No. 4:26-cr-70.

An indictment is merely an accusation. The defendant is presumed innocent until proven guilty.
title: Newport News man charged with killing two people during an armed robbery

United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, announced today that LAQUAN WILLIAMS, a/k/a “China Man” was sentenced yesterday afternoon to 200 months in prison by U.S. District Judge Laura Taylor Swain for orchestrating a series of schemes to steal money from banks by sending imposters into bank branches to transfer money from victim bank accounts or to cash stolen U.S. Treasury checks. These schemes involved WILLIAMS’s possession of over 1,000 stolen or counterfeit checks, his manufacturing of over 500 counterfeit state and federal identification cards, at least $1.8 million in losses to financial institutions, and possession of two loaded firearms. On September 4, 2025, WILLIAMS pled guilty to participating in a conspiracy to commit bank fraud and aggravated identity theft. WILLIAMS was previously sentenced to 64 months’ imprisonment by U.S. District Judge John G. Koeltl in May 2018 after participating in a similar bank fraud scheme, and WILLIAMS engaged in the charged conduct while on federal supervised release.

“Laquan Williams is a bank fraudster who has stolen millions of dollars from Americans by engaging in identity theft and bank fraud,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “For nearly two decades, Williams has been stealing money from innocent bank customers with forged checks, counterfeit identification cards, and stolen personal identifying information. Today’s prison sentence protects New Yorkers and should be a reminder that we and our law enforcement partners will aggressively pursue serial fraudsters and hold them accountable.”

According to the Indictment, public court filings, and statements in public court proceedings:

Between 2021 and 2024, WILLIAMS orchestrated a series of schemes to steal money from banks by impersonating bank customers:

Scheme 1 (May 2023 – June 2023) : Between May 2023 and June 2023, WILLIAMS sent co-conspirators into various banks located in New York, New Jersey, and Connecticut to impersonate various bank customers and deposit checks that would transfer money from the victims into bank accounts controlled by members of the scheme. One of the victims was a prominent former federal government official. The defendant attempted to impersonate this victim while calling a bank and attempted to transfer money between the victim’s accounts, including by using the victim’s social security number. Total intended losses related to this scheme included approximately $827,568.33, and actual losses were approximately $43,361.28.

Scheme 2 (September 2023 – November 2023) : Between September 2023 and November 2023, WILLIAMS sent another co-conspirator into various banks in New Jersey and New York to impersonate the owners of various small businesses. The co-conspirator would request that the banks transfer funds from the victims’ business bank accounts into new business bank accounts that were opened with very similar names and controlled by WILLIAMS. Once the money was transferred, WILLIAMS would withdraw the money as cash or transfer the money through CashApp. Total intended losses related to this scheme included approximately $218,123.22, and actual losses were approximately $87,761.08.

Scheme 3 (October 2021 – May 2024): Between October 2021 and May 2024, WILLIAMS participated in a scheme to steal money from the United States by depositing stolen U.S. Treasury checks into bank accounts controlled by the scheme. Members of the scheme recruited co-conspirators to impersonate the owners of the entities that were the payees on the stolen U.S. Treasury checks and to deposit the stolen checks into bank accounts that were controlled by members of the scheme and had been opened for the specific purpose of cashing the stolen treasury checks. For example, WILLIAMS participated in the depositing of a stolen U.S. treasury check in the amount of $13.9 million into a bank account that had been recently opened by members of the scheme at a bank branch in Massachusetts. Actual losses stemming from the scheme amount to at least $1,157,029.78, and the intended loss exceeded $30 million.

WILLIAMS’s Arrest (May 23, 2024): On May 23, 2024, WILLIAMS was arrested, and law enforcement executed a search warrant for WILLIAMS’s residence and vehicle. Law enforcement recovered, among other things: (1) approximately 27 seals and holograms for placement onto identification cards; (2) a hologram identification card press; (3) approximately 1,102 blank state identification cards; (4) approximately nine stolen U.S. Treasury checks totaling approximately $506,010.83; (5) approximately 1,015 additional stolen and/or altered checks totaling approximately $3.35 million; (6) approximately 571 counterfeit identification cards; (7) approximately 524 counterfeit credit or debit cards; (8) approximately 56 stolen credit cards; (9) approximately 478 pages of blank check stock; (10) multiple printers and laminators used for printing and embossing checks and identification cards; (11) a Glock 19 9mm semi-automatic pistol; (12) a LCP Ruger .380 caliber semi-automatic pistol; and (13) approximately 19 rounds of 9mm and .380 caliber ammunition, including approximately 13 hollow-point rounds of ammunition. Actual losses stemming from fraudulent transactions linked to this physical evidence was approximately $537,596.75.

WILLIAMS was on federal supervised release while participating in these crimes, after previously being sentenced to 64 months’ imprisonment by U.S. District Judge John G. Koeltl in May 2018 for participating in similar bank fraud schemes.

* * *

In addition to the prison term, WILLIAMS, 42, of Florham Park, New Jersey, was sentenced to three years of supervised release, ordered to forfeit approximately $1.8 million, and ordered to pay restitution.

Mr. McDonald praised the outstanding investigative work of the United States Secret Service and the New York City Police Department.

This case is being handled by the Office’s Violent Organizations & Crime Unit. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Ryan Allison and Andrew K. Chan are in charge of the prosecution.

Texas Residents Charged with Promoting Illegal Tax Shelter
A federal grand jury in Dallas, Texas returned an indictment on September 22, 2026, charging four Texas residents with conspiracy to defraud the United States and other crimes for promoting an illegal tax shelter.
According to the indictment, Texas residents Duncan John MacDonald, Sarah Duren, Richard Ronald Cayce, and Thomas Weickgenant promoted and sold a fraudulent trust scheme that was used to shelter more than $1.5 billion of income, causing an estimated tax loss to the IRS of more than $200 million. The defendants allegedly sold clients the tax shelter for fees that often exceeded $100,000 by fraudulently telling clients that they could assign their income to sham trusts to defer paying taxes in perpetuity, all while continuing to enjoy the benefit and control over their assets and income. The defendants also allegedly encouraged some clients to backdate their trusts and file amended income tax returns claiming refunds for prior years’ taxes.
The indictment also alleges that Weickgenant, who allegedly filed false tax returns for tax shelter clients, obstructed IRS efforts to audit those clients. Weickgenant’s alleged obstruction included instructing clients not to speak with the IRS and encouraging at least one client not to comply with a U.S. District Court order to enforce an IRS summons.
The indictment further alleges that MacDonald and Duren, common-law spouses, evaded income taxes on the millions they received in fees from selling the tax shelter. To do so, the couple allegedly concealed MacDonald’s ownership of the tax shelter business and lied to federal investigators. They also allegedly filed false tax returns, used trusts to conceal their receipt of income, and paid personal living expenses through trusts and nominee accounts held in the names of third parties. Allegedly, Cayce, who owned the distributorship licensing the trust tax shelter, likewise received millions of dollars in fees, which he failed to report on his income tax returns.
Additionally, according to the allegations, MacDonald fraudulently solicited $2 million from investors to purportedly purchase shares in a business promoting the tax shelter by allegedly developing digital trusts. Instead, MacDonald allegedly used the $2 million to purchase luxury goods for himself, including a Rolls Royce Ghost (pictured below top with MacDonald) and the downpayment for a yacht (pictured below bottom). At the time he received funds from investors, MacDonald allegedly was under a court-ordered injunction prohibiting him from selling securities not registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case.
Assistant Deputy Chief William Montague and Trial Attorney Max Willner-Giwerc of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Eric B. Chen of the Northern District of Texas are prosecuting the case.

Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
