After investigating reports of restrictive port practices by the Government of Spain, the Federal Maritime Commission (FMC) has determined that Spain has created unfavorable shipping conditions against U.S.-flagged vessels. As a result, the FMC is proposing remedies to counteract those unfavorable conditions, including charging fees for all Spanish-flagged vessels and restricting the import of certain Spanish goods.
The FMC initiated an investigation in December 2024 to determine whether Spain is creating general or special conditions unfavorable to shipping in U.S. foreign trade by barring certain vessels from its ports, including vessels transporting cargo under the United States Maritime Administration’s (MARAD) Maritime Security Program. For more information about the initial investigation please see the Federal Register notice from December 6, 2024.
The FMC’s investigation found conclusive evidence that Spain denied U.S.-flagged vessels access to its ports, and that these actions created unfavorable shipping conditions in the foreign trade. These unfavorable conditions have grave consequences for the efficiency and reliability of the international ocean shipping supply chain, as well as the ability of the FMC to promote the growth and development of U.S. exports, encourage the development of a liner fleet of U.S. vessels capable of meeting national security needs and supporting commerce, and supporting the U.S. merchant marine.
In order to address these unfavorable conditions created by Spain, the FMC proposes two sets of remedies: (1) a per-voyage fee on all Spanish-flagged vessels of $200,000 and (2) restrictions on the import of certain Spanish goods into the United States. The trade categories possibly facing restrictions include perfumery and cosmetics, oils and fats, ceramics, articles of stone, and sugar and confectionaries.
The FMC is seeking public comment on all aspects of these proposed actions to help it decide the appropriate remedy to counter the unfavorable shipping conditions created by Spain. The FMC encourages the public to weigh in on the potential impacts of these proposed actions by filing written comments. For more information about the proposed actions and to leave a comment please visit Regulations.gov. The Commission will accept comments submitted on or before December 14, 2026.
The FMC will offer Spain an opportunity for a hearing on this matter.
Updated: October 15, 2026
title: FMC Proposes Actions to Address Unfavorable Shipping Conditions in Spain

PHILADELPHIA – United States Attorney David Metcalf announced that Jamil Ahmad, 50, of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, entered a plea of guilty today before U.S. Magistrate Judge Craig M. Straw to one count of voting by an alien.

The defendant was charged by information last month, arising from his illegally casting a vote in the 2024 general election. At the time of that election, Ahmad was a citizen of Pakistan and a lawful permanent resident of the United States. Under both federal and state law, only U.S. citizens may vote in Pennsylvania.

“We intend to prosecute anyone who corrupts our democracy by illegally voting in its elections,” U.S. Attorney Metcalf said.

The defendant is scheduled to be sentenced on January 26 and faces a maximum possible sentence of a fine, one year in prison, or both.

This case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations and the FBI.

A blood-pressure drug may activate health-promoting brown fat
Wednesday, October 14, 2026
A blood-pressure drug may activate health-promoting brown fat
Large retrospective study suggests the tissue deters more than cardiovascular disease.
In a National Institutes of Health (NIH)-funded study, scientists have demonstrated that the drug losartan, commonly prescribed for high blood pressure, boosts brown adipose tissue activity in mice, enhancing their metabolism. Researchers initially discovered the connection between brown fat and the drug class to which losartan belongs, known as angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs), through an analysis of over 100,000 patients. This indicates that repurposing a widely used drug, with a well-known safety profile, may be a clinically viable method of stimulating brown fat, which has been linked to improved cardiovascular health and, identified for the first time in this study, psychiatric health.
“The unique reverse translational approach of this study, enabled by large clinical datasets and next-generation analytical tools, provides a much-needed clinical rationale for exploring brown adipose tissue as a therapeutic target in humans across a spectrum of diseases,” said Griffin P. Rodgers, M.D., director of NIH’s National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Disease (NIDDK).
While white fat stores energy in the body, brown fat burns through it to produce heat. Coincidentally, a specific kind of PET/CT imaging often used in clinical oncology can measure this process. By assessing these kinds of images and medical records from more than 50,000 patients being treated for cancer, a research team led by Paul Cohen, M.D., Ph.D., at Rockefeller University recently drew connections between brown fat and reduced prevalence of cardiovascular and metabolic disease.
“We only looked for a few diagnostic codes before, mainly focusing on cardiovascular disease since that’s what this tissue has historically been associated with,” Cohen said. “The scope of this new analysis is far more expansive. We doubled our number of patients and considered more than 500 codes, which allowed us to unearth many new insights.”
Cohen, joined by Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center researchers Heiko Schöder, M.D., and Daniel Lafontaine, used artificial intelligence techniques to identify brown fat associations among more than 100,000 patients who received PET/CT imaging for cancer.
The authors built on top of previously known links and have now demonstrated that, in addition to having brown fat or not, a higher degree of brown fat activity is connected to more cardiometabolic benefits. They also discerned these associations across the body’s six brown fat depots, with increased activity in the armpit depot being most strongly tied to cardiometabolic health.
They uncovered some new connections as well, including a lower incidence of anxiety and depression in patients with greater brown fat presence. Another signal that stood out was the higher levels of brown fat activity among patients taking ARBs.
To examine the relationship between ARBs and brown fat more closely, the researchers tested the impact of losartan in brown fat cells, finding that the drug directly increased their metabolic activity. They also learned that the molecular interactions by which losartan induced these effects were separate from the mechanisms underpinning its more well-known blood-pressure lowering properties.
“The fact that its different effects are mediated by different molecular pathways is advantageous, since it means we could potentially isolate them in future therapies. That way you would be able to stimulate brown fat in people with normal blood pressure,” said first author Nicolás Gómez-Banoy, M.D., an instructor of clinical investigation at Rockefeller and an endocrinologist at Weill Cornell Medicine.
Healthy mice treated with losartan also exhibited many indicators of enhanced metabolism, such as increased energy expenditure, oxygen consumption, and carbon dioxide production, all while maintaining a steady body weight.
These results help form a basis for further investigation into inducing brown fat activity in humans. Depending on the outcome of such potential experiments, future studies could go in many different directions. However, no matter the result, researchers are not short on options.
“There were plenty of other medications associated with brown fat activity in our large cohort. This is just a start,” Cohen said.
NIH supported this research through NIDDK grant DP1DK139983, National Cancer Institute (NCI) grant P30CA008748, National Institute of General Medical Sciences (NIGMS) grant T32GM152349, and National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NCATS) grant UL1TR001866.
About the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK): The NIDDK, a component of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), conducts and supports research on diabetes and other endocrine and metabolic diseases; digestive diseases, nutrition and obesity; and kidney, urologic and hematologic diseases. Spanning the full spectrum of medicine and afflicting people of all ages and ethnic groups, these diseases encompass some of the most common, severe, and disabling conditions affecting Americans. For more information about the NIDDK and its programs, see www.niddk.nih.gov.
About the National Institutes of Health (NIH): NIH, the nation's medical research agency, includes 27 Institutes and Centers and is a component of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. NIH is the primary federal agency conducting and supporting basic, clinical, and translational medical research, and is investigating the causes, treatments, and cures for both common and rare diseases. For more information about NIH and its programs, visit www.nih.gov.
NIH…Turning Discovery Into Health®
Reference
Nicolás Gómez-Banoy et al. Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical phenotyping of human brown fat. Nature. October 14, 2026. DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-11162-7
title: A blood-pressure drug may activate health-promoting brown fat

Rep. Tlaib introduces bill to remove and prohibit Flock cameras, mass surveillance technologies
INKSTER, MICH. – U.S. Rep. Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) introduced the Get the Flock Out of Our Communities Act today with community leaders in front of a Flock camera in Inkster, Michigan, whose city officials just signed a long-term contract with the mass surveillance company. The bill would prohibit the use of federal funds to purchase or operate any automated mass surveillance systems, including automatic license plate readers like Flock. It would also require state and local governments to divest from such systems to remain eligible for certain federal law enforcement grants.
It is the only bill in Congress designed to completely prohibit the use of automated mass surveillance technology, including biometric surveillance systems and facial recognition technology.
“The mass surveillance crisis is not a dystopian fantasy—it is already here. Our children and neighbors cannot go to the park, drive down the street, go to work, or exercise their Constitutional rights without their privacy being breached,” said Rep. Tlaib. “Flock’s technology isn’t making us safer. Instead it has been used to stalk people, mis-identify and arrest innocent people, surveil protestors, and wrongfully record our neighbors. My bill would prevent our government on all levels from selling us out to Big Tech companies that trample our civil rights for profit.”
Over 200 cities and counties, including Westland and Lincoln Park in Michigan, have cancelled their Flock contracts due to resident outrage. According to Data for Progress, a majority of voters — 52% — view Flock unfavorably, a sentiment that continues to grow as Flock and its abuses become more widespread.
“People everywhere are starting to recognize that conflating surveillance with safety makes communities less safe,” said Tawana Petty, digital and data justice organizer from Detroit. “The persistent abuse of Flock cameras and other surveillance systems by law enforcement agencies across the United States, and the lack of transparency by the companies that market them has caused an awakening among residents and city government agencies who are ridding themselves of the technologies. The Get the Flock Out of Our Communities Act is responsive to the national call to protect all neighbors from being stalked and harmed by reckless actors and opportunistic corporations.”
“Flock cameras are overall dangerous to a free society,” said Geri Biggs, Dearborn resident and community advocate. “There have already been cases cited where individuals have been illegally stalked, including young women, by individuals in positions of power with nefarious intentions.Allowing this information to be shared with companies poses a threat to the civil rights of us all, and at the very least can be intimidating to the most vulnerable in our communities.”
“Flock cameras are a significant invasion of people’s privacy and need to be seriously controlled, or eliminated,” said Larry Biggs, Dearborn resident and community advocate. “As soon as information is gathered by Flock, it can be shared with other law enforcement agencies, including ICE and CBP, with no control. All other invasions of people’s privacy must get a search warrant or have probable cause. Flock cameras have no such requirements.”
“Flock and other vendors of AI-surveillance technology pose an existential risk to our democracy,” said Elijah Nemr, member of Metro Detroit Democratic Socialists of America. “With capabilities ranging from video and audio capture, to the processing and permanent storage of our most sensitive data, every person who values their independence and privacy must oppose this technology in all of its forms. DSA has successfully organized to end Flock in Westland, and we will continue organizing with our neighbors to get Flock out of our communities!”
“The spread of mass surveillance systems is an existential threat to political and personal freedom,” said Jibran Ludwig, Legislative Strategist at Fight for the Future. “We have seen the current administration weaponize these tools to terrorize immigrant communities and protestors, while simultaneously forcing every single person into dragnet surveillance that puts us all in danger. But the threat goes far beyond our current political moment: the history of mass surveillance is an endless litany of abuse at every level. This bill is an urgent effort to uproot the mass surveillance systems which have been built up from the local level and down from the federal.”
“Indivisible is proud to endorse the Get the Flock Out of Our Communities Act. These automated mass surveillance systems don’t just violate our fundamental rights to privacy and civil liberties – they fuel Big Tech’s broader efforts to harvest as much of our personal information as possible so they can bleed our bank accounts dry and monopolize markets,” said Andrew O’Neill, National Advocacy Director of Indivisible. “We’ve also witnessed Republicans increasingly weaponize warrantless mass surveillance as a fascist tool for political gain and to help their donors profit off massive amounts of our stolen data. This isn’t new, and it has nothing to do with safety or justice: the first surveillance laws in the U.S. passed in 1712 targeted Black, mixed-race, and Indigenous people, weaponizing public safety to enforce white supremacy. Ever since, surveillance systems and increasingly sophisticated technologies have been intentionally and disproportionately deployed in predominantly Black and low-income communities. It’s more urgent than ever that Congress protect our communities from these attacks.”
The Get the Flock Out of Our Communities Act comprehensively removes automated mass surveillance systems and similar technologies by:
- Prohibiting federal funds being used by federal, state, or local government entities to purchase, deploy, install, maintain, access, lease, or operate any automated mass surveillance system, including automated license plate readers like Flock, biometric surveillance systems, and facial recognition technology.
- Prohibiting the federal government or any employee or officer of an agency acting in an official capacity from using any automated mass surveillance systems or information derived from such systems.
- Requiring the removal of any automated mass surveillance system deployed or operated with federal funding.
- Requiring any unit of government in possession of data generated by federally-funded automated mass surveillance systems to permanently delete that data.
- Rendering data obtained in violation of the Act’s provisions inadmissible in court.
- Requiring state and local governments applying for certain federal law enforcement funding to certify that they do not operate or access automated mass surveillance networks.
The Get the Flock Out of Our Communities Act is cosponsored by 6 members of Congress: U.S. Reps. Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Summer Lee (PA-12), Ilhan Omar (MN-05), Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Nydia Velázquez (NY-07), and Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12).
The Get the Flock Out of Our Communities Act is endorsed by 50 organizations: African Human Rights Coalition, American Friends Service Committee (AFSC), Arab American Heritage Council (AAHC), Arkansas Community Organizations, Asian American Advocacy Fund, Center for Constitutional Rights, Center for Progressive Reform, Demand Progress, Democratic Socialists of America, Detroit Justice Center, Electronic Privacy Information Center (EPIC), Fight for the Future, Flint Alliance for Immigrant Rights, Freedom for Immigrants, Freedom of the Press Foundation, Grantmakers Concerned with Immigrants and Refugees (GCIR), Immigrant Defenders Law Center (ImmDef), Immigrant Guide, Immigration Justice Action Team – Indivisible Mass Coalition, Immigrant Legal Resource Center (ILRC), Indivisible, Indivisible Marin, Justice Is Global, Kino Border Initiative, Latin America Working Group (LAWG), LGBT Detroit, Louisiana Advocates for Immigrants in Detention, Metro Detroit DSA, Miami Valley Immigration Coalition, Migrant Support Collective, Minnesota 8, MPower Change Action Fund, Muslims for Just Futures, National Asian Pacific American Women’ Forum, National Immigrant Justice Center, NETWORK Lobby for Catholic Social Justice, Never Again Action, New Disabled South Rising, Nicaraguan American Legal Defense and Education Fund (NALDEF), No Detention Centers in Michigan, NorCal Resist, Oasis Legal Services, Organized Communities Against Deportations, Partnership for the Advancement of New Americans (PANA), Refugee Support Network, Southern NH Indivisible, TRUST SD Coalition, We are CASA, Western Massachusetts Immigration Legislative Advocacy Network, X-Lab

text:
United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the New York Field Office of Homeland Security Investigations (“HSI”), Pete Gizas, and Commissioner of the New York City Police Department (“NYPD”), Jessica S. Tisch, announced today the arrest and unsealing of a seven-count Indictment charging RAJAHSHUWEH RHODES, a/k/a “Skii Dot,” a/k/a “skiidot.b,” a/k/a “bdot,” in connection with the October 15, 2021 murder of Isaiah Levine who was sixteen years old when he was shot in the side of the head while standing on a sidewalk in Manhattan. RHODES will be presented this afternoon before U.S. Magistrate Judge Robyn F. Tarnofsky. The case is assigned to U.S. District Judge Lewis J. Liman.

“Those choosing to engage in gang violence, terrorize our neighborhoods, and put innocent lives at risk will be held accountable for their actions,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “The residents of the Lower East Side, just like everyone in this city, deserve safety, accountability, and peace. The passage of time does not mean a case is forgotten, and we will pursue every lawful avenue to bring justice to offenders and to victims and their family members who will always have the unwavering support of the men and women in this Office.”

“Those choosing to engage in gang violence, terrorize our neighborhoods, and put innocent lives at risk will be held accountable for their actions,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “The residents of the Lower East Side, just like everyone in this city, deserve safety, accountability, and peace. The passage of time does not mean a case is forgotten, and we will pursue every lawful avenue to bring justice to offenders and to victims and their family members who will always have the unwavering support of the men and women in this Office.”

“As alleged, the defendant’s gunfire shattered an ordinary moment on a Manhattan sidewalk, taking the life of 16-year-old Isaiah Levine, injuring a second victim, and leaving a household and community to live with the consequences,” said HSI Acting Special Agent in Charge Gizas. “Justice, even years later, cannot restore the life of a teenager taken far too soon from his loved ones and the city he called home. Today, nearly five years to the day of Isaiah's murder, we seek to provide a measure of closure to Isaiah’s family and to New Yorkers who deserve to feel safe on the streets of Manhattan and throughout our city. Together with the NYPD and the Southern District of New York, HSI New York stands resolute in our shared commitment to deliver answers for those whose lives have been forever changed by gang violence.”

“This defendant, a member of the New York Blood Brim Army, allegedly shot two people, murdering a 16-year-old, in a busy Lower East Side neighborhood,” said NYPD Commissioner Jessica S. Tisch. “Gun violence anywhere in our communities will not be tolerated, and the NYPD will continue to go after violent gangs, take guns off our streets, and hold the drivers of violence accountable. I thank our investigators and law enforcement partners for their diligent work on this case and commitment to keeping New York City safe.”

As alleged in the Indictment, and based on statements made in public court proceedings:

From at least 2019 through in or about 2026, RHODES was a member and associate of the New York Blood Brim Army, a violent gang that operates throughout New York City, among other locations, and whose members engage in murders, robberies, and the trafficking of controlled substances, including marihuana. On or about October 15, 2021, in connection with a gang-related dispute, RHODES shot sixteen-year-old Isaiah Levine in the head and killed him at the intersection of Delancey Street and Suffolk Street in the Lower East Side of Manhattan. RHODES’s gunfire also struck another individual in the leg, who survived.

* * *

RHODES, 23, of Manhattan, New York, is charged with one count of racketeering conspiracy, which carries a maximum sentence of life in prison; one count of murder in aid of racketeering, which carries a mandatory term of life in prison or death; one count of attempted murder and assault in aid of racketeering, which carries a maximum sentence of twenty years in prison; one count of conspiracy to distribute a controlled substance, which carries a maximum term of five years in prison; and three counts of using and carrying a firearm during and in relation to a crime of violence or a drug trafficking offense, each of which carries a mandatory minimum sentence of five years in prison and a maximum term of life in prison.

The statutory minimum and maximum potential sentences in this case are prescribed by Congress and provided here for informational purposes only, as any sentencing of the defendants will be determined by the judge.

Mr. McDonald praised the outstanding investigative efforts of HSI New York’s Violent Gangs Task Force, the NYPD, including the Intelligence Officers of the NYPD’s Police Service Area 4, 7th Precinct Detective Squad, and Manhattan South Homicide Squad.

The case is being prosecuted by the Office’s Violent Organizations and Crime Unit. Assistant U.S. Attorneys William Stone and Kathryn Wheelock are in charge of the prosecution.

The charges in the Indictment are merely accusations and the defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.

Minneapolis Father and Son Plead Guilty to $9 Million Fraud Conspiracy
A Minneapolis father and son pleaded guilty in October to conspiring to defraud the United States. The father also pleaded guilty to being a felon in possession of a firearm.
According to documents and statements made in court, between June 2022 and October 2024, LaMar Javis Burgess and his son, LaMar Dazjar Burgess, of the Minneapolis area, prepared and filed false federal income tax returns for themselves and others claiming refund amounts they and the other taxpayers were not entitled to receive. The defendants prepared and filed false 2021 tax returns claiming refundable sick and family leave tax credits available to certain self-employed individuals unable to work due to COVID-19. They also prepared and filed false 2022 tax returns claiming certain refundable tax credits.
During the conspiracy, LaMar Javis Burgess sought and obtained videos and instruction manuals educating himself on how to file false federal tax returns, including a guide titled “TurboTax Sauce The ‘Self-Employed’ Way.” He worked with his son and others to promote the tax fraud scheme. In exchange for filing false tax returns, he charged taxpayers a $10,000 fee from a portion of their tax refunds.
Both the father and son solicited others to provide them with their names, addresses, Social Security numbers, photo identification and bank account information to enable them to prepare and file the false tax returns. The returns included employment and tax credit information they knew to be false.
In total, the defendants prepared or filed at least 300 false and fraudulent federal tax returns claiming at least $9.2 million in refunds.
During a search warrant executed at his home in Golden Valley, Minnesota, federal investigators found that LaMar Javis Burgess was in possession of a Glock model 19, 9 mm semi-automatic handgun. The handgun contained a loaded fifteen round magazine. An empty magazine, an extended high-capacity magazine, and a high-capacity drum magazine were also found on the closet shelves, and loose ammunition rounds were in a bag inside the closet. The handgun was a reported stolen firearm. Because LaMar Javis Burgess has certain prior felony convictions, he is prohibited under federal law from possessing firearms or ammunition at any time.
LaMar Javis Burgess is scheduled to be sentenced at a later date. He faces a maximum penalty of ten years in prison for conspiracy and fifteen years in prison for felon in possession of a firearm. He also faces a period of supervised release, restitution and monetary penalties. LaMar Dazjar Burgess is scheduled to be sentenced at a later date. He faces a maximum penalty of ten years in prison for conspiracy. He also faces a period of supervised release, restitution and monetary penalties. A federal district judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and U.S. Attorney Daniel N. Rosen for the District of Minnesota made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case, with assistance from the FBI, HSI, ATF, Minneapolis Police Department, Fridley Police Department, Ramsey County Sheriff’s Office and Hennepin County Sheriff’s Office.
Trial Attorney J. Parker Gochenour of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Rebecca Kline of the District of Minnesota are prosecuting the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Minneapolis Father and Son Plead Guilty to $9 Million Fraud Conspiracy

Fugitive Mary McDonnell Added to FBI’s Most Wanted Fraudsters List for Bank Fraud and Aggravated Identity Theft In Los Angeles and Orange Counties
Up to $150,000 reward offered for information leading to McDonnell’s arrest and conviction
A Southern California woman believed to be living in Dubai and who claimed to be an heiress to the McDonnell aircraft family is one of two fugitives who have been added to the FBI’s newly formed Most Wanted Fraudsters list for allegedly defrauding banks out of millions of dollars, Patrick Grandy, the assistant director in charge of the FBI’s Los Angeles Field Office, announced today.
Mary Carole McDonnell, 75, is wanted for bank fraud and aggravated identity theft for her alleged involvement in a fraud scheme in Los Angeles and Orange counties in California. From July 2017 to May 2018, McDonnell is alleged to have knowingly, and with the intent to defraud, devised and participated in a scheme to obtain money, funds, assets, and property owned by a California bank. Through this scheme, McDonnell allegedly and fraudulently obtained a total of approximately $14.7 million from the bank to which she knew she was not entitled and has not paid back.
It is alleged that McDonnell also defrauded additional financial institutions in a similar fashion. McDonnell has falsely claimed to be an heiress to the McDonnell aircraft family, with an $80 million secret trust to which she will have access. In December 2018, a federal arrest warrant was issued for McDonnell in the United States District Court, Central District of California, Santa Ana, California, after she was charged with bank fraud and aggravated identity theft. It is believed McDonnell is currently in Dubai.
McDonnell is also known to have used multiple aliases, including Mary Carole Carroll; Mary Carol McDonnell; Mary Carroll McDonnell; Mary C. Carroll; Mary Carroll McDonald. She is 5’7” and has blue eyes. She is known to weigh approximately 145 pounds and has blonde hair, although she could have changed her appearance over the years. McDonnell has ties to Los Angeles, California; Montgomery, Alabama; and Dubai, United Arab Emirates.
"Most Wanted Fraudster Mary McDonnell is wanted for defrauding financial institutions out of millions and is known to have falsified her inheritance and background,” said Patrick Grandy, the Assistant Director in Charge of the FBI's Los Angeles Field Office. "It’s just a matter of time before McDonnell is caught as we work with our international partners to locate her. A generous reward is being offered in exchange for information leading to her apprehension and conviction, and a tip from the public might break the case.”
The Most Wanted Fraudsters list was created and launched in June 2026 to generate public interest and assistance with information leading to the location and apprehension of fraud fugitives. A reward of up to $150,000 is being offered in exchange for information that leads to the arrest and conviction of a member on the FBI’s Most Wanted Fraudsters list.
FBI San Antonio also announced a Most Wanted Fraudster this week.
The Most Wanted Fraudsters list is separate from the FBI’s traditional Ten Most Wanted Fugitives and was created to focus exclusively on fugitives wanted for major fraud. Read more about this list.
Anyone with information as to the whereabouts of Most Wanted Fraudster McDonnell should contact their local FBI office or the nearest American Embassy or Consulate. Alternatively, the FBI’s toll-free tipline can be reached at 1-800-CALL-FBI or a tip can be submitted online at tips.fbi.gov.
The case against McDonnell was investigated by the FBI. McDonnell is being prosecuted by the United States Attorney’s Office in the Central District of California.
title: Fugitive Mary McDonnell Added to FBI’s Most Wanted Fraudsters List for Bank Fraud and Aggravated Identity Theft In Los Angeles and Orange Counties

MARTINSBURG, WEST VIRGINIA – U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey has announced the convictions of three men as part of nationwide enforcement actions led by the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division, Internal Revenue Service, and Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation targeting tax fraud and related offenses. The Northern District of West Virginia was a key participant in this surge effort.

Between early September and today, the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section and U.S. Attorneys’ Offices across the country participated in the Department’s first-ever National Tax Enforcement Surge. The surge of nationwide resources resulted in prosecutorial actions against 76 defendants whose alleged and proven crimes intended an estimated loss of revenue to the federal government of more than $490,000,000.

“Every dollar stolen through tax fraud is a dollar taken from the American people,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “What we uncovered during this concentrated surge is only the tip of the iceberg. The Department of Justice is committed to expanding our investigations and exposing schemes designed to evade accountability, because there is no safe haven for fraudsters.”

“We have an obligation to the law-abiding citizens of this country to ensure that their hard-earned tax dollars are protected and distributed legally and that those that attempt to defraud the government with tax fraud are held accountable,” said U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey. “This surge shows the commitment of the Department of Justice Fraud Division, my office, and the IRS to taxpayers in West Virginia and across the country.”

“We have an obligation to the law-abiding citizens of this country to ensure that their hard-earned tax dollars are protected and distributed legally and that those that attempt to defraud the government with tax fraud are held accountable,” said U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey. “This surge shows the commitment of the Department of Justice Fraud Division, my office, and the IRS to taxpayers in West Virginia and across the country.”

In the Northern District of West Virginia, three Maryland men have admitted to a fraud scheme involving U.S. Department of Treasury checks totaling more than a million dollars. They each pleaded guilty to their roles in the scheme. They are:

Tijuan Arrington, age 49, of Accokeek, Maryland

David Walters, age 47, of Ellicott City, Maryland

Gregory Dean, age 33, of Suitland, Maryland

The defendants worked together to obtain legitimate U.S. Treasury checks issued to real individuals or businesses, creating fraudulent companies with similar names, and then securing Employer Identification Numbers (EINs) through an Internal Revenue Service portal in Martinsburg, West Virginia. The three would use the EINs to open business accounts, deposit stolen checks, and quickly withdraw the funds before any fraud was detected. Some of the fraud was detected and prevented before the defendants could successfully withdraw the money.

The fraud totaled more than $1.1 million. Arrington, Walters, and Dean are each facing up to 20 years in prison.

The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Eleanor Hurney and Greg Jones and was investigated by the Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration (TIGTA).

This case details one way in which this office has contributed to ensuring that all Americans pay their fair share. To see the successes of other offices, read the national release here .

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

Earlier today, an indictment was unsealed charging Melissa Brooks, a correctional officer employed by the U.S. Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP), with taking bribes as a public official and conspiracy to do the same. Brooks was assigned to the Metropolitan Detention Center located in Brooklyn, New York (MDC Brooklyn) and agreed to accept the illegal payments from inmates and others acting on behalf of inmates who were involved in smuggling contraband into the MDC. Brooks was arrested this morning and will be arraigned this afternoon before United States Magistrate Judge James R. Cho.

Joseph Nocella, Jr., United States Attorney for the Eastern District of New York; Ryan Geach, Special Agent in Charge, U.S. Department of Justice, Office of the Inspector General, Northeast Region (DOJ-OIG); and James C. Barnacle, Jr., Assistant Director in Charge, Federal Bureau of Investigation, New York Field Office (FBI), announced the indictment and arrest.

“As alleged, the defendant betrayed her duty as a correctional officer, endangering the safety of MDC staff and inmates, all to satisfy her own greed,” stated United States Attorney Nocella. “Our Office is committed to rooting out corruption at all levels of government and will hold the defendant accountable for her actions.”

“It is critical to the safety and security of the federal prison system that Correctional Officers perform their work with honesty and integrity,” stated Special Agent in Charge Geach. “The DOJ OIG will continue to diligently work with its law enforcement partners to investigate allegations of bribery and other wrongdoing by prison staff,” stated DOJ-OIG Special Agent in Charge Geach.

“Inmate and officer safety is at direct risk if contraband is allowed to enter prisons. Allegedly, Corrections Officer Melissa Brooks was bribed to allow contraband into MDC, putting her own financial interests above the safety and security of those she was sworn to protect. The FBI will continue to root out such corruption, so that all of New York is a safer place,” stated FBI Assistant Director in Charge Barnacle.

As alleged in the indictment, Brooks has been employed by the BOP as a correctional officer since July 2024. As a correctional officer, Brooks was responsible for maintaining security and good order within the MDC, including by ensuring that inmates did not possess contraband. Brooks’s conduct was governed by regulations prohibiting officers from accepting gifts or other things of value from inmates or their family members or associates. However, between July 2024 and December 2025, Brooks allegedly accepted cash payments from associates of MDC inmates on multiple occasions in return for smuggling contraband into the MDC. For example, on October 18, 2024, she received $5,000 via a peer-to-peer payment service from an individual who had received $5,000 just minutes earlier from the sister of an MDC inmate. And on December 15, 2025, she exchanged text messages with the same MDC inmate, who was using a contraband phone, in which the defendant recognized the potential consequences for her actions. After the inmate indicated that he thought Brooks was going to bring him contraband, she responded: “😂😂😂these mf are trying to throw my ass in jail baby.”

The charges in the indictment are allegations, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. If convicted of bribery, Brooks faces up to 15 years’ imprisonment.

The government’s case is being handled by the Office’s Public Integrity Section. Assistant United States Attorney Andrew Wang is in charge of the prosecution, with assistance from Paralegal Specialist Johnson Peow.

The Defendants :

MELISSA BROOKS Age: 37 Brooklyn, New York

E.D.N.Y. Docket No. 26-CR-280 (BMC)
title: Bureau of Prisons Correctional Officer Indicted for Bribery

WASHINGTON — In response to a Presidential disaster declaration issued Oct. 7, the U.S. Small Business Administration announced the availability of low-interest federal disaster loans to Guam businesses, private nonprofits, and residents affected by Super Typhoon Bavi occurring July 4 – 12.
The disaster declaration covers Guam, which is eligible for both physical damage loans and Economic Injury Disaster Loans from SBA.
Businesses and nonprofits are eligible to apply for physical damage loans and may borrow up to $2 million to repair or replace disaster-damaged or destroyed real estate, machinery, and equipment, inventory, and other business assets.
Homeowners and renters are eligible to apply for home and personal property loans and may borrow up to $100,000 to replace or repair personal property, such as clothing, furniture, cars, and appliances. Homeowners may apply for up to $500,000 to replace or repair their primary residence.
Applicants may also be eligible for a loan increase of up to 20% of their verified physical damage, for mitigation purposes. Eligible mitigation improvements may include strengthening structures to protect against high wind damage, upgrading to wind rated garage doors, installing a safe room or storm shelter, elevating flood prone structures, adding a sump pump, or French drains to help reduce damage from future storms and flooding.
The SBA’s Economic Injury Disaster Loan program is available to eligible small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, and private nonprofits — including faith-based organizations —impacted by financial losses directly related to this disaster. The SBA is unable to provide disaster loans to agricultural producers, farmers, or ranchers, except for aquaculture enterprises.
Economic Injury Disaster Loans are for working capital needs caused by the disaster and are available even if the business or private nonprofit did not suffer any physical damage. They may be used to pay fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills which could not be paid due to the disaster.
“A presidential disaster declaration opens the door to SBA assistance at a time when families and businesses are facing difficult decisions,” said Chris Stallings, Associate Administrator of SBA's Office of Disaster Recovery. “These loans can help eligible homeowners and renters repair or replace what was damaged while giving businesses and private nonprofits the resources to continue operating as their communities recover.”
Interest rates are as low as 4% for businesses, 3.625% for nonprofits, and 2.875% for homeowners and renters, with terms up to 30 years. Interest does not begin to accrue, and payments are not due until 12 months from the date of the first loan disbursement. The SBA determines eligibility and sets loan amounts and terms based on each applicant’s financial condition.
To apply online, visit sba.gov/disaster. Applicants may also call SBA’s National Support Network Center at (866) SBA-HELP or email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov for more information on disaster assistance. For people who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability, please dial 7-1-1 to access telecommunications relay services.
The filing deadline for returning applications for physical property damage is Dec. 7. The deadline to return economic injury applications is July 7, 2027.
###
About the U.S. Small Business Administration
The U.S. Small Business Administration helps power the American dream of business ownership. As the only go-to resource and voice for small businesses backed by the strength of the federal government, the SBA empowers entrepreneurs and small business owners with the resources and support they need to start, grow, expand their businesses, or recover from a declared disaster. It delivers services through an extensive network of SBA field offices and partnerships with public and private organizations. To learn more, visit www.sba.gov.
title: SBA Relief Available to Guam Businesses, Private Nonprofits, Residents Affected by Super Typhoon Bavi

FRESNO, Calif. —Thomas Henry Lopez, 51, of Spring, Texas, was sentenced yesterday by U.S. District Judge Kirk E. Sherriff to 30 years in prison for two counts of sexual exploitation of children, one count of distribution of child sexual abuse material (CSAM), and one count of transfer of obscene material to a minor, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced.

Lopez was also ordered to serve a life term of supervised release during which he will be required to register as a sex offender and his access to computers, cellphones, and the internet will be restricted. Lopez was also ordered to pay $24,400 in financial assessments.

“Although the defendant lived an outwardly respectable life, he secretly exploited vulnerable minors through an online platform,” U.S. Attorney Grant said. “The offenses for which he pleaded guilty represent only two of many victims of his disgusting conduct. This sentence will safeguard the public and prevent the defendant from harming other victims. Our office remains committed to protecting children and to holding fully accountable anyone who sexually exploits children.”

On July 13, 2026, Lopez pleaded guilty to the charged offenses without a plea agreement.

According to court documents, between June and July 2024, Lopez contacted minors in the Central Valley through TikTok and continued to communicate with them through text messages and the encrypted application JusTalk. Posing as a 12-year-old boy from Texas, he persuaded the victims to create and send illicit videos and images. During these communications, Lopez also sent the victims sexually explicit images of himself and others. Investigators identified Lopez through internet connections used at his home and workplace, where he was employed at a multinational corporation as their principal wells engineer. On Sept. 3, 2024, Lopez was arrested as he was leaving for a work trip to Singapore. Multiple electronic devices were seized during a search of his residence.

“Thomas Lopez befriended and ultimately exploited vulnerable children who had no idea he was not the 12-year-old he claimed to be. We are grateful to the Kingsburg Pollice department for their professionalism and commend the brave survivors and their families for trusting us to conduct a thorough investigation to hold Lopez accountable for his depraved crime,” said FBI Sacramento Special Agent in Charge Brian Tosh. “This case is an example of the collaborative work the FBI is doing to identify and investigate predators who use the anonymity of online communication to exploit our nation’s children. Justice will find you, always.”

The Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Central California Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force, principally the Kingsburg, California Police Department conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney David Gappa prosecuted the case.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the United States Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute those who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.usdoj.gov/psc.
title: Texas man sentenced for child sexual exploitation offenses against Central Valley victims

FAYETTEVILLE – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Arkansas announced the sentencings of Jason Boyd Carney and Lacey Christina Carney as part of a nationwide enforcement action led by the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division, Internal Revenue Service, and Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation targeting tax fraud and related offenses. The Western District of Arkansas was a key participant in this surge effort.

The Springdale founders of the non-profit 2nd Milk were sentenced on October 14, 2026, for defrauding donors to their charity, 2nd Milk. Jason Carney was sentenced to 192 months in prison on charges related to a conspiracy, wire fraud, and tax fraud, followed by three years of supervised release. His spouse, Lacey Carney was sentenced to 36 months on charges that she failed to report her spouse’s fraud, followed by one year of supervised release. Both received the maximum sentences allowed pursuant to their counts of conviction. When imposing sentence, Chief United States District Judge Timothy L. Brooks described Jason Carney’s conduct as “profoundly disgusting” and “egregious, repulsive, and violative.”

According to court documents, Jason Carney, age 48, previously entered a plea of guilty on the sixth day of his jury trial during the prosecution’s case in chief. He admitted guilt on four separate counts- one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, two counts of filing a false return, one for a personal return and another for 2nd Milk’s non-profit 990 tax return, and one count of structuring cash transactions to evade reporting requirements.

The Court found that Jason Carney diverted over $2 million from his non-profit, 2nd Milk, which was created to benefit starving orphans in Malawi, an African country that is one of the poorest countries in the world. Prosecutors alleged in a sentencing memorandum that for over four years, Jason Carney represented 2nd Milk as a fully transparent ministry, using emphatic language to donors. “100% of the 2nd Milk sponsorships go directly to saving the lives of the most vulnerable babies living in developing countries;” “For every dollar 82 cents goes to babies today…the rest goes for overhead…in Africa;” “We want to be accountable to our sponsors and God;” and “it’s important to know that the Carneys are not taking your money when you sponsor babies, all that money goes specifically for those babies.” Jason Carney repeatedly assured donors that he does not, and never has, taken a salary and that “[a]ll of the funds go directly to the children.”

According to prosecutors, a financial investigation and bank records revealed that Jason and Lacey Carney transferred funds from 2nd Milk for cosmetic surgery, massages, tanning, pet expenses, a cruise, personal mortgage payments, car/boat loans, and luxury vacations so often that it aroused the suspicion of donors. Using 2nd Milk funds, both Carneys traveled to exotic locations like Rome, Chili, Peru, Japan, Barcelona, Cancun, and Vietnam. Jason Carney also filed false tax returns for himself and 2nd Milk to hide his diversion of funds.

His wife, Lacey Carney, age 47, pled guilty to one count of misprision, that is, being aware of her husband’s wire fraud scheme and failing to report is as required by law.

The couple also agreed to the forfeiture of their home due to the fact that wire fraud proceeds were used to pay towards their mortgage.

“Today’s sentences highlights that those who misuse charitable platforms to enrich themselves will face significant consequences under the law,” said Kevin R. Holmes, United States Attorney for the Western District of Arkansas, in making the announcement. “By diverting funds intended to sustain vulnerable children, Jason and Lacey Carney violated the trust of donors and inflicted profound harm on the very mission they claimed to champion. This office remains steadfast in its commitment to prosecuting financial fraud and protecting the integrity of charitable giving.”

“The defendant exploited the charitable intentions of donors who believed their contributions would help save the lives of malnourished and orphaned infants around the globe,” said Special Agent in Charge Donald “Trey” Eakins, IRS Criminal Investigation’s Charlotte Field Office. “Instead, the defendant diverted nonprofit funds for his own personal expenses. Our special agents will continue to follow the money, unravel complex financial schemes, and work with our partners to ensure people who abuse charitable missions for personal gain are held fully accountable.”

“Those who exploit charitable causes for personal gain betray both the donors who trusted them and the vulnerable people they claimed to serve,” said Nicholas Collura, Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary for Diplomatic Security and Director of the Diplomatic Security Service (DSS). “DSS remains committed to working with our law enforcement partners to expose fraud and hold offenders accountable.”

The Diplomatic Security Service and Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation investigated the case. Assistant United States Attorney Benjamin Wulff and DOJ Trial Attorney, Michael L. Jones litigated the case on behalf of the United States.

The Department of Justice had previously announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

Related court documents may be found on the Public Access to Electronic Records website at www.pacer.gov , Western District of Arkansas Case Number 5:25-CR-50005.
title: Arkansas Non-Profit Founders Receive Maximum Prison Sentences for Defrauding Donors and the Government

NEW YORK - United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, announced today that LAQUAN WILLIAMS, a/k/a “China Man” was sentenced yesterday afternoon to 200 months in prison by U.S. District Judge Laura Taylor Swain for orchestrating a series of schemes to steal money from banks by sending imposters into bank branches to transfer money from victim bank accounts or to cash stolen U.S. Treasury checks. These schemes involved WILLIAMS’s possession of over 1,000 stolen or counterfeit checks, his manufacturing of over 500 counterfeit state and federal identification cards, at least $1.8 million in losses to financial institutions, and possession of two loaded firearms. On September 4, 2025, WILLIAMS pled guilty to participating in a conspiracy to commit bank fraud and aggravated identity theft. WILLIAMS was previously sentenced to 64 months’ imprisonment by U.S. District Judge John G. Koeltl in May 2018 after participating in a similar bank fraud scheme, and WILLIAMS engaged in the charged conduct while on federal supervised release.
“Laquan Williams is a bank fraudster who has stolen millions of dollars from Americans by engaging in identity theft and bank fraud,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “For nearly two decades, Williams has been stealing money from innocent bank customers with forged checks, counterfeit identification cards, and stolen personal identifying information. Today’s prison sentence protects New Yorkers and should be a reminder that we and our law enforcement partners will aggressively pursue serial fraudsters and hold them accountable.”
According to the Indictment, public court filings, and statements in public court proceedings:
Between 2021 and 2024, WILLIAMS orchestrated a series of schemes to steal money from banks by impersonating bank customers:
Scheme 1 (May 2023 – June 2023): Between May 2023 and June 2023, WILLIAMS sent co-conspirators into various banks located in New York, New Jersey, and Connecticut to impersonate various bank customers and deposit checks that would transfer money from the victims into bank accounts controlled by members of the scheme. One of the victims was a prominent former federal government official. The defendant attempted to impersonate this victim while calling a bank and attempted to transfer money between the victim’s accounts, including by using the victim’s social security number. Total intended losses related to this scheme included approximately $827,568.33, and actual losses were approximately $43,361.28.
Scheme 2 (September 2023 – November 2023): Between September 2023 and November 2023, WILLIAMS sent another co-conspirator into various banks in New Jersey and New York to impersonate the owners of various small businesses. The co-conspirator would request that the banks transfer funds from the victims’ business bank accounts into new business bank accounts that were opened with very similar names and controlled by WILLIAMS. Once the money was transferred, WILLIAMS would withdraw the money as cash or transfer the money through CashApp. Total intended losses related to this scheme included approximately $218,123.22, and actual losses were approximately $87,761.08.
Scheme 3 (October 2021 – May 2024): Between October 2021 and May 2024, WILLIAMS participated in a scheme to steal money from the United States by depositing stolen U.S. Treasury checks into bank accounts controlled by the scheme. Members of the scheme recruited co-conspirators to impersonate the owners of the entities that were the payees on the stolen U.S. Treasury checks and to deposit the stolen checks into bank accounts that were controlled by members of the scheme and had been opened for the specific purpose of cashing the stolen treasury checks. For example, WILLIAMS participated in the depositing of a stolen U.S. treasury check in the amount of $13.9 million into a bank account that had been recently opened by members of the scheme at a bank branch in Massachusetts. Actual losses stemming from the scheme amount to at least $1,157,029.78, and the intended loss exceeded $30 million.
WILLIAMS’s Arrest (May 23, 2024): On May 23, 2024, WILLIAMS was arrested, and law enforcement executed a search warrant for WILLIAMS’s residence and vehicle. Law enforcement recovered, among other things: (1) approximately 27 seals and holograms for placement onto identification cards; (2) a hologram identification card press; (3) approximately 1,102 blank state identification cards; (4) approximately nine stolen U.S. Treasury checks totaling approximately $506,010.83; (5) approximately 1,015 additional stolen and/or altered checks totaling approximately $3.35 million; (6) approximately 571 counterfeit identification cards; (7) approximately 524 counterfeit credit or debit cards; (8) approximately 56 stolen credit cards; (9) approximately 478 pages of blank check stock; (10) multiple printers and laminators used for printing and embossing checks and identification cards; (11) a Glock 19 9mm semi-automatic pistol; (12) a LCP Ruger .380 caliber semi-automatic pistol; and (13) approximately 19 rounds of 9mm and .380 caliber ammunition, including approximately 13 hollow-point rounds of ammunition. Actual losses stemming from fraudulent transactions linked to this physical evidence was approximately $537,596.75.
WILLIAMS was on federal supervised release while participating in these crimes, after previously being sentenced to 64 months’ imprisonment by U.S. District Judge John G. Koeltl in May 2018 for participating in similar bank fraud schemes.
* * *
In addition to the prison term, WILLIAMS, 42, of Florham Park, New Jersey, was sentenced to three years of supervised release, ordered to forfeit approximately $1.8 million, and ordered to pay restitution.
Mr. McDonald praised the outstanding investigative work of the United States Secret Service and the New York City Police Department.
This case is being handled by the Office’s Violent Organizations & Crime Unit. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Ryan Allison and Andrew K. Chan are in charge of the prosecution.

text:
Congressmen Thompson and Carter Visit Nation’s Largest Permanent ICE Migrant Detention Facility
(NATCHEZ, MS) – Today, Rep. Bennie G. Thompson (D-MS), Ranking Member of the Committee on Homeland Security, and Rep. Troy Carter (D-LA), Committee Member, released the below statement on their surprise oversight visit yesterday to the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention facility at Adams County Correctional Center (ACCC) in Mississippi, the nation’s largest migrant detention facility.
“One of Congress’ primary responsibilities is oversight of federal agencies, and we exercised that power – and legal right – in an unannounced visit to ACCC after a summer of crises, protests, and power outages. We wanted an unvarnished look at the institution to make sure that facility problems highlighted in correspondence our offices and in public inspection reports are being addressed, and that everyone in the facility has access to their constitutional due process rights. Regardless of a person’s station in life, they are still human and deserve safe shelter with adequate, sanitary food and water, and access to health care.
“We continue to have concerns that detainees aren’t able to obtain access to adequate mental health services, a full understanding of what crimes they are charged with, and transparency and accountability for when ACCC staff fail in upholding their constitutional rights. As the Trump administration continues to weaponize ICE against communities across the country, we will continue rigorous oversight of immigrant detention facilities so that the law is followed and immigrants have access to their full constitutional rights.”
Background:
Adams County Correctional Center (ACCC), operated by the private prison company CoreCivic, is the largest permanent immigration detention facility in the U.S. and detains an average of 1,878 men daily.
In the past six months, ACCC and the men detained there have experienced multiple crises. In May 2026, ICE’s Office of Detention Oversight inspected ACCC and downgraded the facility from a “Superior” rating to “Acceptable/Adequate,” with only 24 of 28 standards met. In July, nearly 70 detainees submitted a petition to the warden demanding an end to the practice of placing three detainees in cells meant to hold two people. During the week of August 10, 2026, a lengthy power outage at ACCC left detainees without air conditioning for two days in nearly 100-degree heat. On August 22, 2026, around 100 male detainees started a protest over poor living conditions, spoiled food, and meager rations.

HARRISBURG - The United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Pennsylvania announced that Rodney McMillian, age 44, of Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, was sentenced on October 1, 2026, to 188 months’ imprisonment by United States District Judge Keli M. Neary for distribution of fentanyl pills and firearms trafficking.

According to United States Attorney Brian D. Miller, McMillian was sentenced for his role in the drug trafficking and firearms trafficking conspiracy that was the subject of an undercover investigation conducted by the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives in conjunction with the Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General. During the course of the investigation, undercover officers purchased over three kilograms of methamphetamine, 1,600 fentanyl pills and seven firearms from the conspirators. McMillian was the source of the firearms and the fentanyl pills.

At sentencing, Judge Neary found that McMillian’s long criminal history of violence, drug trafficking, and firearms offenses warrant imprisonment of 188 months in prison. The Judged noted that previous periods of incarceration had not deterred McMillian from returning to commit crimes. McMillian had previously entered a guilty plea to fentanyl trafficking. His trafficking of firearms was considered part of the Judge’s sentencing.

Co-defendants Devonte Betts, Lamar Waters, and Tyrese Nealy entered guilty pleas to drug trafficking offenses. They are scheduled for sentencing in the coming months.

The U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and the Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General. Assistant United States Attorney lead the investigation. Michael A. Consiglio is prosecuting the case.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. text:
Lawmakers Demand Transparency After U.S. Forest Service Coordinates with ICE on Public Lands
Letter follows Labor Day incident where individuals were arrested in the middle of the night while camping at Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, 4 of 5 are still being held at Tacoma NW ICE Detention Center
PNW records devastating 2026 wildfire season – Members voice concern USFS is misusing taxpayer funds by directing resources outside of USFS scope and mission
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Last week, U.S. Congresswoman Emily Randall (D, WA-06), and Representatives Kim Schrier, M.D. (D, WA-08), Rick Larsen (D, WA-02), Suzan DelBene (D, WA-01), Jared Huffman (D, CA-02), Ranking Member of the House Natural Resources Committee, Adriano Espaillat (D, NY-13), Chairman of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, Andrea Salinas (D, OR-06), Adam Smith (D, WA-09), Val Hoyle (D, OR-04), Marilyn Strickland (D, WA-10), Suzanne Bonamici (D, OR-01), and Pramila Jayapal (D, WA-07) sent a letter to U.S. Forest Chief Tom Schultz demanding transparency regarding immigration enforcement activities on U.S. Forest Service (USFS) lands.
This letter comes after a shocking incident over Labor Day Weekend where U.S. Forest Service Law Enforcement Officers (LEO) coordinated with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents to arrest five men who were camping with their families in Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest. As of October 5, 2026, four of the five men arrested remain in detention at the Tacoma NW ICE Detention Center.
“As Members of Congress representing the Pacific Northwest and Democratic leadership of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, the House Natural Resources Committee, and the House Agriculture Committee, we are concerned that the U.S. Forest Service (USFS) is misusing taxpayer dollars by neglecting their mission and directing career staff to prioritize immigration enforcement on federal public lands. Particularly during a difficult wildfire season, we want to express our gratitude to the Forest Service for fighting wildfires in the Pacific Northwest and across the country,” wrote the members.
The U.S. Forest Service has undergone significant funding cuts and reorganizations efforts since the start of Trump’s second term. Since 2025, the USFS has lost nearly 6,000 workers through DOGE cuts and other factors, raising concerns about wildfire preparedness, forest health research, and public land management. Earlier this year, USFS announced consolidation efforts to shutter research and development facilities nationwide. USFS backtracked on their original proposal to close 57 out of 77 research labs after public outcry. In September 2026, USFS announced they will be closing 23 labs.
The 2026 wildfire season is still underway, and Washington state has recorded one of the worst wildfire seasons to date with almost 900,000 acres being burned as of early September.
The members conclude the letter by demanding answers to the following questions by October 15, 2026:
Questions for the U.S. Forest Service:
- 
Which agency first identified those arrested as targets for investigation, when were they identified, and what information about the targets was used to justify the raid?
- 
Can you confirm that the law enforcement officers that first approached the families were employees of the USFS?
- 
To what extent did USFS participate in the raid, and under what authority? Please provide any agreement or memorandum that governs cooperation between the U.S. Forest Service and DHS.
- 
Please provide any agreement or memorandum between the U.S. Forest Service and DHS that governs the collection and sharing of visitors' identification and reservation data with DHS or ICE.
- 
What other immigration raids has the U.S. Forest Service participated in since January 21, 2025?
- 
What appropriations account(s) has the USFS used to fund its participation in immigration enforcement operations since January 21, 2025, and how much funding has been obligated or expended for this purpose?
- 
Has any USFS law enforcement personnel time, budget, or resources been reallocated from other law enforcement priorities (e.g., resource protection, search and rescue, wildfire-adjacent enforcement) to support immigration enforcement operations? If so, how much of this reallocation has been disclosed to Congress since these funds were appropriated for land management and resource protection purposes rather than immigration enforcement?
- Given limited agency resources, why is it a priority of the USFS to use employees in the targeting of families on public land?
The full text of the letter is available HERE.
###
title: Lawmakers Demand Transparency After U.S. Forest Service Coordinates with ICE on Public Lands

United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, Assistant Director in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (“FBI”), James C. Barnacle, Jr., Superintendent of the New York State Police (“NYSP”), Steven G. James, and Chief of the City of Newburgh Police Department (“CNPD”), Brandon Rola, announced today the unsealing of an Indictment charging eight defendants with conspiracy to distribute crack cocaine in the vicinity of West Parmenter Street in Newburgh, New York. The defendants—Maurice Owens, a/k/a “Mo Nice,” Shaka Eggleston, a/k/a “Shak,” Troy Smith, a/k/a “Castro,” Robert Morganfield, a/k/a “MJ,” Houston Brown, a/k/a “Euro,” Walter Herring a/k/a “Noodles,” Jason LOWE, a/k/a “Boogie,” and James Tyrone Hayes, a/k/a “Country”—were presented this afternoon before U.S. Magistrate Judge Victoria Reznik. The case is assigned to U.S. District Judge Philip M. Halpern.

“Our Office and our law enforcement partners will work tirelessly to keep dangerous drugs off the streets of our communities,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “As alleged in the indictment, these defendants participated in a conspiracy to flood the streets of Newburgh with a steady flow of crack cocaine. This conspiracy allegedly transformed Newburgh’s West Parmenter Street into an open-air drug market, where they have conducted thousands of narcotics transactions in broad daylight, poisoning the neighborhood with illicit drugs for their own profit.”

“Our Office and our law enforcement partners will work tirelessly to keep dangerous drugs off the streets of our communities,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “As alleged in the indictment, these defendants participated in a conspiracy to flood the streets of Newburgh with a steady flow of crack cocaine. “The FBI Hudson Valley Safe Streets Task Force works every day alongside our state and local partners to combat violent crime, and part of that means ridding the streets of illicit narcotics,” said Assistant FBI Director James C. Barnacle, Jr. “As alleged in the indictment, these eight individuals made it their business to sell drugs in a shameless open-air market. This FBI will stop at nothing to dismantle these drug networks and make our communities safer as a result.”

“The drug trafficking alleged in this case threatens the safety and quality of life of Newburgh residents,” said NYSP Superintendent Steven James. “These arrests reflect the sustained work of our investigators and our federal and local partners to disrupt narcotics distribution and hold those responsible accountable. We remain committed to working together to protect our communities and make neighborhoods safer for the people who call them home.”

“This case demonstrates the strength of our partnership with the FBI and our shared commitment to keeping the City of Newburgh safe,” said CNPD Chief Brandon Rola. “The City of Newburgh Detective Division played an important role in this joint investigation, and our detectives and officers assisted in apprehending all of the targets as part of our ongoing work to restore safety to West Parmenter Street. I thank the FBI and everyone involved for their hard work, coordination, and dedication to our community. Our participation in the FBI Hudson Valley Safe Streets Task Force remains an important part of our efforts to protect the City of Newburgh and hold offenders accountable.”

As alleged in the Indictment, and based on statements made in public court proceedings:

From in or about 2025 through in or about October 2026, OWENS, EGGLESTON, SMITH, MORGANFIELD, BROWN, HERRING, LOWE, and HAYES conspired to distribute large volumes of crack cocaine in the vicinity of West Parmenter Street in Newburgh, New York, primarily through hand-to-hand narcotics transactions. In the course of this investigation, law enforcement conducted more than sixty controlled purchases of crack cocaine, involving each member of the conspiracy charged in this Indictment. Moreover, each of the eight defendants charged in this conspiracy were observed on surveillance video, regularly conducting apparent narcotics transactions on West Parmenter Street over the course of the last several months. A review of surveillance video collected through this investigation indicates that members of the conspiracy would often conduct dozens of narcotics transactions each day in the vicinity of West Parmenter Street.

OWENS, 48, of Rock Tavern, New York, EGGLESTON, 28, of Newburgh, New York, SMITH, 57, of Cornwall, New York, MORGANFIELD, 57, of Newburgh, New York, BROWN, 31, of New Windsor, New York, HERRING, 45, of Newburgh, New York, LOWE, 39, of Newburgh, New York, and HAYES, 56, of Newburgh, New York, are charged with narcotics conspiracy, which carries a maximum sentence of life in prison and a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years in prison.

Mr. McDonald praised the outstanding investigative efforts of the FBI Hudson Valley Safe Streets Task Force, the New York State Police, the New York Police Department, the City of Newburgh Police Department, the Town of Newburgh Police Department, the Town of New Windsor Police Department, the Orange County Sheriff’s Office, and the Port Jervis Police Department.

DEA Caribbean Division Strikes Major Blow Against Violent Drug Trafficking Organization in Southern Puerto Rico
SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — The Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Caribbean Division, working alongside its federal and local law enforcement partners, delivered a significant blow to a violent drug trafficking organization operating across Juana Díaz, Villalba, and Coamo, resulting in the federal indictment of 28 individuals.
The DEA-led investigation, conducted jointly with the Puerto Rico Police Bureau’s Ponce Strike Force, targeted a criminal network responsible for distributing fentanyl, heroin, cocaine, crack, marijuana, and controlled prescription drugs throughout southern Puerto Rico.
Operating since 2022, the organization allegedly used firearms, intimidation, and violence to control drug trafficking territories in public housing communities and surrounding neighborhoods. The investigation also uncovered the transportation of kilogram quantities of cocaine to the continental United States.
Of the 28 defendants, 20 face firearms charges, including 14 charged with possessing machine guns in furtherance of drug trafficking crimes. The indictment also seeks approximately $4.16 million in narcotics-related forfeitures.
DEA Caribbean Division Special Agent in Charge Michael Mayer emphasized the importance of unified law enforcement efforts: “Violent drug trafficking organizations have no place in our communities. Through the Homeland Security Task Force, the DEA Caribbean Division and our federal, state, and local partners are sending a clear message: we will relentlessly pursue those who profit from addiction, violence, and fear. Every investigation, every arrest, and every partnership brings us closer to safer neighborhoods and a Fentanyl Free America. Protecting the people of Puerto Rico and the remains our mission and our responsibility.”
The investigation was supported by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) and the U.S. Postal Inspection Service (USPIS), with additional operational assistance from the FBI, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), U.S. Marshals Service, and the Puerto Rico Department of Correction and Rehabilitation.
Conducted under the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative, this operation reinforces the DEA Caribbean Division’s commitment to dismantling violent criminal networks through intelligence-driven investigations and strong interagency partnerships.
28 indicted. Three municipalities. $4.16 million in forfeiture allegations. One mission: protecting Puerto Rico and its communities.
title: DEA Caribbean Division Strikes Major Blow Against Violent Drug Trafficking Organization in Southern Puerto Rico
