Proposed Rules Implement Working Families Tax Cuts Reforms to Prevent Fraud and Abuse of the Premium Tax Credit
WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of the Treasury (Treasury) and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) issued proposed regulations to implement President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts reforms to the Premium Tax Credit (PTC), a refundable tax credit that helps eligible American taxpayers afford health insurance purchased through the Health Insurance Exchanges.
“Hardworking American taxpayers should not be forced to subsidize health care for people who are ineligible under federal law,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. “Today’s proposed rules implement the common-sense reforms enacted by the Working Families Tax Cuts to close eligibility loopholes and ensure taxpayer-funded Premium Tax Credits are reserved for eligible Americans. Under President Trump, this Administration is cracking down on fraud and corruption; holding bad actors accountable; lowering health care costs for Americans; and restoring integrity to our tax code and health care system.”
“The proposed rules protect eligible taxpayers while strengthening the integrity of the Premium Tax Credit,” said IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano. “The enhanced verification measures are designed to curb improper claims, ensuring these vital tax benefits go strictly to the hardworking Americans who qualify for them.”
“The Trump Administration’s whole-of-government approach to fighting fraud, waste, and abuse is built on the idea that an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure,” said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “Ensuring health programs serve only those who are eligible is one of the most effective ways to protect these programs and the taxpayers who support them. With today’s proposed rules, the Treasury Department is taking another step forward in our collaborative effort to protect taxpayer dollars by shutting down waste and fraud before a single dollar leaves the building.”
PROTECTING TAXPAYER-FUNDED BENEFITS FOR ELIGIBLE AMERICANS
The proposed rules put the Working Families Tax Cuts’ Premium Tax Credit reforms into effect which strengthen eligibility checks, close gaps in the verification process, and help ensure taxpayer-funded subsidies go only to eligible American taxpayers.
The Trump Administration’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud exposed the need for stronger safeguards to protect the integrity of the Federal Marketplace. As part of that work, Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) announced the removal of more than 760,000 unverified “phantom” enrollees from the rolls of the Affordable Care Act (ACA), resulting in $2.2 billion in savings and sending nearly 1 million Americans $500 each who had been overcharged for their Obamacare coverage by the Biden Administration.
The Treasury and IRS proposed rules:
- Strengthen Eligibility Standards: Beginning in 2027, ensures taxpayer-funded health insurance subsidies go only to Americans who qualify under federal law.
- Protect Taxpayer Benefits for Eligible Americans: Restricts PTC eligibility to U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, and certain lawfully present noncitizens.
- Close Verification Gaps: Applies commonsense PTC eligibility checks and adds new verification criteria for any advance PTC payments.
The proposed regulations are available here.
The changes to Exchange procedures and operations necessary to implement the verification requirements are expected to be addressed in parallel proposed regulations issued by HHS under related provisions of the same statute.
###
title: Treasury and IRS Move to Protect Health Care Benefits for Eligible Americans

text:
Fast Facts
Both Customs and Border Protection and Immigration and Customs Enforcement personnel use body-worn cameras to record interactions with the public. CBP began issuing cameras in fiscal year 2021, and ICE began in fiscal year 2024.
But neither agency has updated initial plans for the body-worn camera programs to reflect changes in camera deployment. They also haven’t developed guidance for most program offices on how to use the cameras.
Our recommendations address these and other issues.
Torso of a man in a tan uniform shirt and utility belt, with a hand on a holstered gun, wearing a small black rectangular object in the center of his chest.
Highlights
What GAO Found
Body-worn cameras provide law enforcement personnel with the capability to record interactions with the public. When initiating their body-worn camera programs, the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) each developed a plan that included key components of a comprehensive program management plan. However, CBP and ICE have not updated their program plans since 2022 and 2024, respectively. They have therefore not taken into account significant changes in the program, such as increases in the number of cameras scheduled for deployment and a 2025 pause in further camera deployment.
Body-Worn Camera and Functional Buttons
CBP and ICE have stated desired results for their programs, including enhancing officer safety, transparency, accountability, and public trust. Although CBP and ICE implemented some measures to track information about camera availability and reliability, they have not implemented results-oriented performance goals and measures. Doing so would help them assess the results of their body-worn camera programs. For example, potential goals and measures might involve use of footage in use of force investigations.
CBP and ICE have established policies related to camera use and the management of footage and implemented related oversight mechanisms to help ensure compliance with policy. These include supervisory controls on camera use and monthly reviews of footage to help ensure proper categorization. However, additional controls—such as mechanisms that automatically activate the camera when a related action occurs (e.g., when emergency lights are engaged)—would provide better assurance that ICE personnel capture footage in accordance with policy.
Most CBP and ICE offices have not developed specific operational guidance that explains how personnel should use, or not use, cameras under their unique operational circumstances. The lack of guidance at this operational level increases the risk that CBP and ICE personnel will fail to use the cameras as required under policy.
Why GAO Did This Study
CBP and ICE began deploying cameras in fiscal years 2021 and 2024, respectively. As of June 2026, CBP had deployed approximately 11,500 cameras, with nearly all of these deployments to Border Patrol. As of April 2026, ICE had deployed approximately 4,800 cameras, almost evenly to Enforcement and Removal Operations and Homeland Security Investigations.
GAO was asked to review CBP and ICE’s (1) body-worn camera program planning; (2) measures to assess program impact; and (3) mechanisms that help ensure that personnel carry out related responsibilities appropriately.
GAO reviewed agency documents, including Department of Homeland Security, CBP, and ICE directives on body-worn camera use. GAO also analyzed CBP and ICE data on actual and planned deployment of cameras to component personnel. GAO interviewed DHS, CBP, and ICE headquarters officials and users of the cameras at 10 field locations that vary in geographic location and status of camera deployment.
Recommendations
GAO is making seven recommendations, including that CBP and ICE each update body-worn camera program plans, implement performance goals and measures to assess effectiveness, ICE implement controls that help ensure that cameras are activated, and that CBP and ICE implement operational guidance for body-worn cameras. DHS agreed with six recommendations, but did not agree to implement automated camera activation controls. GAO maintains that implementing additional controls would help ensure adherence to ICE policy.
title: Federal Law Enforcement: CBP and ICE Should Improve Body-Worn Camera Program Management

FBI Operation Summer Heat 2.0 Nets Thousands of Violent Crime Arrests
In four months, the violent crime initiative also seized enough fentanyl to kill 52 million people
The FBI and its law enforcement partners are announcing the results of Summer Heat 2.0, a four-month violent crime initiative that resulted in 8,927 arrests, the seizure of deadly fentanyl and cocaine, and 5,013 dangerous illegally possessed weapons taken off American streets.
“This year’s Summer Heat was our second straight nationwide offensive to crush violent crime all over the country, and the results were outstanding,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “Even after last year’s unprecedented numbers, all 56 FBI field offices stepped up and delivered even higher numbers this year—arresting almost 9,000 subjects, up 3% from Summer Heat last year; seizing 63% more fentanyl; identifying or locating 1,410 children, 34% higher than last year; and recovering over 5,000 weapons, up 120% from 2025. Major cities across America saw increases as high as 80% in arrests compared to last summer alone. When this FBI elevated ‘crushing violent crime’ to one of our top priorities, we moved 2,000 FBI personnel out of Washington and permanently into the field—making the decisive call to go on offense. This FBI isn’t waiting for violent criminals, drug traffickers, and weapons dealers to devastate our communities any longer. As a result, under the Trump administration’s leadership, we have achieved the most prolific reduction in violent crime in U.S. history.” 
Between June 1 and September 20, the FBI and its 56 field offices surged resources alongside state and local partners to execute federal warrants on violent criminals and fugitives, dismantle violent gangs and transnational criminal organizations, identify and rescue child victims, and resolve violent crime cases in Indian Country.  
The FBI’s Summer Heat 2.0 initiative achieved additional victories with 687 kilograms of fentanyl seized: an amount equal to 52 million lethal doses. Of the 8,927 arrests, more than 5,900 arrests fell under the FBI’s violent crime and gang program.
A Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) takedown across two states, Operation Turf War, kicked off the FBI’s 2026 Summer Heat initiative. FBI Pittsburgh, in coordination with West Virginia’s HSTF, netted 32 narcotics and weapons-related arrests. In a separate effort in July 2026, FBI Los Angeles executed 17 federal arrest warrants and 49 search warrants in connection with Operation Hard Ball. The operation united FBI Los Angeles with law enforcement from Canada and Europe to investigate an organized crime group accused of a litany of criminal acts. And in yet another example of the success of Operation Summer Heat, FBI San Juan and its partners led Operation Taking Back West, which resulted in the indictment of 81 members of a violent criminal gang.  
The FBI first launched the Summer Heat initiative for three months in 2025 to deploy a multi-pronged offensive to crush violent crime. The announcement of Operation Summer Heat 2.0 results follows on the heels of historic drops in crime across the U.S., according to the FBI’s 2025 UCR Summary of Reported Crimes in the Nation.
title: FBI Operation Summer Heat 2.0 Nets Thousands of Violent Crime Arrests

Today, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) announced the next step in its work to advance President Trump’s fight against the debanking of businesses and individuals on the basis of their constitutionally protected rights, including support of President Trump, MAGA, pro-life causes, and industries disfavored by the Left. The CFPB will address any consumer harm caused by the nation’s largest banks in response to the Report on debanking practices by Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC).
The OCC report, “Guaranteeing Fair Banking for All Americans,” found that the nine largest national banks under its supervision – JPMorgan Chase Bank, Bank of America, Citibank, Wells Fargo Bank, U.S. Bank, Capital One, PNC Bank, TD Bank, and BMO Bank – maintained policies or engaged in practices that denied or restricted financial access on the basis of Americans’ political or religious beliefs or a customer’s otherwise lawful business activities. The OCC report provides excerpts from bank documents, including emails, revealing this biased and discriminatory decision-making. The report shows that entire sectors were victims of debanking, most notably those related to firearms, oil and gas, and tobacco.
“It is appalling that these banks targeted American consumers for their political, social, or religious beliefs that did not align with the Biden Administration or its leftist allies. Many of those targeted were supporters of President Trump. These thuggish tactics, which were also a defining feature of the Biden-Chopra CFPB, have no place in America,” said CFPB’s Acting Director Mark Paoletta. “We thank the Department of the Treasury and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency for conducting its review to shed light on these shameful practices. The CFPB will fully investigate whether the institutions featured in OCC’s report and others have complied with federal consumer financial laws and take appropriate action.” The CFPB holds primary supervisory and enforcement authority for banks with over $10 billion in assets, including these banks, as well as certain nonbank financial institutions to assess their compliance with federal consumer financial laws.
The CFPB’s announcement is part of the agency’s latest undertaking to implement Executive Order  14331, “Guaranteeing Fair Access to Banking for All Americans,” and advance its priority to vigorously remedy debanking. The CFPB evaluates financial institutions for compliance with the Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA) and Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA), particularly the adverse action notice requirements under these laws, and Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices (UDAAP), and opens investigations when warranted. Previously, the CFPB reviewed its Examination Manual, guidance, regulations, and other materials used to regulate or examine financial institutions under its authority to ensure that they do not contain reputation risk concepts that could result in unlawful debanking. The CFPB has also been reviewing consumer complaints, as well as supervisory and enforcement data, for evidence of potential unlawful debanking, and is pursuing its own investigations, based on that data.
The CFPB recently updated its website and complaint portal with information to raise awareness about debanking, and continues to encourage consumers to submit complaints if they believe they have been debanked.
title: CFPB Announces New Initiative to Address OCC-Uncovered Debanking by Large Banks

MINNEAPOLIS – United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen announced today that a Minneapolis father and son pleaded guilty to conspiring to defraud the United States on October 9 and October 1, respectively. These pleas are part of nationwide enforcement actions led by the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division, Internal Revenue Service, and Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation targeting tax fraud and related offenses. The District of Minnesota was a key participant in this surge effort.

The father also pleaded guilty to being a felon in possession of a firearm.

Between early September and today, the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section and U.S. Attorneys’ Offices across the country participated in the Department’s first-ever National Tax Enforcement Surge. The surge of nationwide resources resulted in prosecutorial actions against 76 defendants whose alleged and proven crimes intended an estimated loss of revenue to the federal government of more than $490,000,000.

“My office is committed to investigating and prosecuting those who take money from American taxpayers for their own enrichment. No one is entitled to funds that are not theirs, and we commend the work of our law enforcement partners who made these guilty pleas possible,” said United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen.

“Most taxpayers work hard, play by the rules, and pay what they owe,” said Marta C. Grijalva, Acting Special Agent in Charge, IRS Criminal Investigation, Chicago Field Office. “This father and son decided the rules didn’t apply to them. They didn’t just file false tax returns. They taught others how to cheat, recruited people into their scheme, and treated our tax system like their own personal payday. Every dollar stolen through fraud comes at the expense of honest taxpayers, and every scheme like this one chips away at the public’s trust in a system we all depend on. IRS Criminal Investigation and our law enforcement partners will keep digging, following the money, and holding accountable those who mistake the honor system for an invitation to steal.”

According to documents and statements made in court, between June 2022 and October 2024, LaMar Javis Burgess, 44, and his son, LaMar Dazjar Burgess, 24, of the Minneapolis area, prepared and filed false federal income tax returns for themselves and others claiming refund amounts they and the other taxpayers were not entitled to receive. The defendants prepared and filed false 2021 tax returns claiming refundable sick and family leave tax credits available to certain self-employed individuals unable to work due to COVID-19. They also prepared and filed false 2022 tax returns claiming certain refundable tax credits.

During the conspiracy, LaMar Javis Burgess sought and obtained videos and instruction manuals educating himself on how to file false federal tax returns, including a guide titled “TurboTax Sauce The ‘Self-Employed’ Way.” He worked with his son and others to promote the tax fraud scheme. In exchange for filing false tax returns, he charged taxpayers a $10,000 fee from a portion of their tax refunds.

Both the father and son solicited others to provide them with their names, addresses, Social Security numbers, photo identification, and bank account information to enable them to prepare and file the false tax returns. The returns included employment and tax credit information they knew to be false.

In total, the defendants prepared or filed at least 300 false and fraudulent federal tax returns claiming at least $9.2 million in refunds.

During a search warrant executed at his home in Golden Valley, Minnesota, federal investigators found that LaMar Javis Burgess was in possession of a Glock model 19, 9 mm semi-automatic handgun. The handgun contained a loaded fifteen round magazine. An empty magazine, an extended high-capacity magazine, and a high-capacity drum magazine were also found on the closet shelves, and loose ammunition rounds were in a bag inside the closet. The handgun was a reported stolen firearm. Because LaMar Javis Burgess has certain prior felony convictions, he is prohibited under federal law from possessing firearms or ammunition at any time.

LaMar Javis Burgess is scheduled to be sentenced at a later date and faces a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison for conspiracy and 15 years in prison for being a felon in possession of a firearm. He also faces a period of supervised release, restitution, and monetary penalties.

LaMar Dazjar Burgess is also scheduled to be sentenced at a later date and faces a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison for conspiracy. He also faces a period of supervised release, restitution, and monetary penalties. A federal district judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen for the District of Minnesota made the announcement.

IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case, with assistance from the FBI, HSI, ATF, Minneapolis Police Department, Fridley Police Department, Ramsey County Sheriff’s Office, and Hennepin County Sheriff’s Office.

Trial Attorney J. Parker Gochenour of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section and Assistant United States Attorney Rebecca Kline of the District of Minnesota are prosecuting the case.

This press release details one way in which this office has contributed to ensuring that all Americans pay their fair share. To see the successes of other offices, please see this press release here .

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division. The core mission of the Fraud Division is to zealously investigate and prosecute those who steal or fraudulently misuse taxpayer dollars. Department of Justice efforts to combat fraud support President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: District of Minnesota Joins DOJ’s Fraud Division, IRS, and IRS-CI to Expose More than $490M in Tax Fraud in National Tax Enforcement Surge; Minneapolis Father and Son Plead Guilty to $9 Million Fraud Conspiracy

Tennessee Woman Pleads Guilty to Preparing False Tax Returns
A Tennessee woman pleaded guilty today to preparing false tax returns for others and willfully failing to file her own tax returns.
According to court documents and statements made in court, Lynette Hogue prepared and filed with the IRS false income tax returns for clients of the tax preparation business where she worked. These tax returns contained false and fraudulent items, which generated refunds the clients were not entitled to receive. Hogue also willfully failed to file her own tax returns, even though she earned substantial income from her tax return preparation business and was required by law to file. In total, Hogue’s conduct caused a loss to the IRS of $4.1 million.
Hogue pleaded guilty to one count of willfully aiding and assisting the filing of a false tax return and one count of willfully failing to file an individual tax return. She is scheduled to be sentenced on January 15, 2027, and faces a maximum penalty of three years in prison for aiding and assisting the filing of a false return and one year in prison for filing a false individual return. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and U.S. Attorney D. Michael Dunavant for the Western District of Tennessee made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case.
Trial Attorneys Isaiah Boyd III and Matthew C. Hicks of the Fraud Division’s Tax Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Carroll L. André III for the Western District of Tennessee are prosecuting the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Tennessee Woman Pleads Guilty to Preparing False Tax Returns

PORTLAND, Maine: The United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Maine today announced a sentencing as part of a nationwide enforcement action led by the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division, Internal Revenue Service, and Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation targeting tax fraud and related offenses. The District of Maine was a key participant in this surge effort.

U.S. District Judge John A. Woodcock, Jr. sentenced Rakiya Mohamed , 30, to five years probation. She was also ordered to pay $51,001 in restitution to the IRS.

Memphis Safe Task Force Arrests 34 Tuesday, Recovers 6 Guns
For immediate release
Office of Public Affairs
Usms.mediadesk@usdoj.gov
MEMPHIS - The Memphis Safe Task Force (MSTF) on Tuesday executed 34 arrests, including one man who had an outstanding warrant for aggravated rape, and recovered six illegal firearms.
Of note:
Christopher Harris, 38, was arrested in the 3800 block of Democrat Road on an outstanding warrant for aggravated rape. Harris was with a woman who claimed he’d kidnapped her and who told MSTF officers that Harris was in the process of raping her before they arrived. A search warrant for the vehicle was prepared and charges for kidnapping and rape are pending. Harris was transported to the Memphis Police Department (MPD) for interview by the MPD sex crimes unit.
Jalen Pierce, 25, was arrested at the intersection of Roland Street and Fleetwood Avenue and charged with aggravated assault /theft of property. MSTF recovered an unknown amount of marijuana, drug paraphernalia, and a Glock 19 handgun outfitted with a Machine Gun Conversion Device, which is illegal throughout Tennessee.
Paul Guy, 52, was arrested at the intersection of West Byfield and Horn Lake Road on an outstanding warrant for possession of cocaine. Subsequent search warrants yielded more than 70 pounds of marijuana and $40,000 in cash.
Juan Leal-Nunez, 25, was arrested at the Greyhound bus station and charged with possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine after he gave consent to MSTF to search his luggage which revealed approximately 43.5 pounds of methamphetamine. Leal-Nunez was booked at Shelby County jail.
Dontavious Simpson, 32, was arrested at an apartment complex in the 6500 block of Ballantrace Court, charged with possession of a controlled substance with intent to manufacture/deliver narcotics. Officers recovered approximately 2 pounds of marijuana, approximately $1,150 in U.S. currency, a Glock 27 handgun and various firearms components (conversion kit and high-capacity magazines). Simpson was processed at the Shelby County Sheriff's Office.
On Monday night, MSTF conducted a traffic stop at Overton Crossing and Pamela Drive of a vehicle for a moving violation that was also suspected of containing narcotics. At the stop, Tennessee Highway Patrol officers interviewed the driver and secured the driver’s license. Upon return to the suspect’s vehicle, the trooper discovered him to be unresponsive. CPR was performed by personnel on scene and medics were requested. The suspect was transported to the hospital where he was later pronounced deceased. A K9 unit made a positive alert on the vehicle, and a subsequent vehicle search led to the discovery of 3 pounds of marijuana, which was seized.
Since the launch of the Memphis Safe Task Force initiative, officers have made 13,569 arrests, including 142 for homicide, 1,460 for controlled substances, 1,335 for firearms violations, and 126 for sex offenses. Of those arrested, 433 were juveniles and 1,518 were known gang members. The task force has seized 2,283 illegal firearms. These enforcement actions reflect a sustained commitment to reducing violent crime and removing dangerous weapons from Memphis neighborhoods.
The Memphis Safe Task Force is a multi-agency initiative established via a Presidential Memorandum signed by President Donald Trump on Sept. 15, 2025. Aimed at addressing violent street crime, the task force coordinates federal, state, and local law enforcement and includes mobilized members of the Tennessee National Guard. The MSTF is focused on arresting violent criminals, clearing warrants, seizing firearms, and locating missing children. Since the operation began, the MSTF has located 196 missing children.
This operation reflects the MSTF’s commitment to coordinated enforcement efforts and its mission to identify, apprehend, and hold accountable those who pose a threat to public safety.
title: Memphis Safe Task Force Arrests 34 Tuesday, Recovers 6 Guns | U.S. Marshals Service

NAPERVILLE, Ill. — The Nuclear Regulatory Commission has begun a special inspection at the Dresden Nuclear Power Station in Morris, Illinois, after plant staff found a corroded battery connection that broke during maintenance. Constellation Energy operates the two-unit plant.
The battery is part of a backup power system that supports equipment used to safely shut down the reactor. The issue did not affect public health and safety.
The NRC determined a special inspection was warranted because the damage was not caught during routine checks, and similar battery problems have occurred at other nuclear plants.
“An independent NRC review will help us understand how this battery issue developed and whether improvements are needed,” Region III Administrator Mohammed Shuaibi said. “We’re committed to ensuring the plant’s oversight processes remain strong and that similar problems are prevented at other facilities.”
A team of two NRC inspectors will look at how the damage happened, whether the plant’s regular inspections should have found it sooner, how the plant responded, and whether other plants could face a similar issue.
Once the inspection is complete, NRC inspectors will document their findings in a publicly available inspection report, which will be distributed electronically to listserv subscribers and posted on the NRC website.
title: NRC Begins Special Inspection at Dresden Nuclear Power Plant

Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03) highlighted the awarding of $142,330,091 in federal funding to Massachusetts through the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP). The early allocation follows Trahan’s request for the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to release Massachusetts’ LIHEAP funding before the end of the month to combat surging home heating costs.
“No family in Massachusetts should have to choose between heating their home and affording groceries or medicine,” said Congresswoman Trahan. “With heating oil prices up nearly 75 percent from last year, that choice is becoming a reality for far too many households. Releasing these funds early will help families prepare for the winter ahead. But this year’s allocation falls short of last year’s at a time when the need is greater than ever. Congress must act to restore and strengthen this lifeline.”
This year’s $142.3 million allocation is nearly $4 million less than Massachusetts’ initial allocation last year, which totaled $146 million. The drop is driven by the expiration of the five-year LIHEAP increase included in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which delivered an additional $6.4 million to the Commonwealth last year alone over the baseline $139.6 million allocation.
Crude oil prices have topped $100 per barrel multiple times this year, most recently on September 15. Because heating oil is refined from crude, those spikes hit Massachusetts households hardest. State utility shutoff moratoriums protect many families through the coldest months, but they do nothing for households that must pay in full before a heating oil delivery.
The LIHEAP program has long been underfunded. On average, just 20 percent of eligible households receive assistance each year. In 2023, Trahan led an effort to increase federal LIHEAP funding. Earlier this month, Trahan, Senator Elizabeth Warren, and Congressman Stephen Lynch led 24 of their colleagues in pressing the Department of Energy to act on soaring heating oil costs and end the administration’s attacks on LIHEAP, which it has tried to eliminate.
Massachusetts residents can learn more about and apply for heating assistance HERE.

WASHINGTON — The Department of Veterans Affairs approved $2.681 billion in VA infrastructure improvement projects in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026.
These projects are being funded by VA’s $4.8 billion non-recurring maintenance budget for FY2026, the largest in the department’s history. The funds will be used by VA medical facilities for significant maintenance, replacements, and upgrades needed to maintain and improve operational capability and healthcare delivery.
“Under President Trump, we are rebuilding the department, so it puts Veterans first, and these historic investments underscore that fact,” said VA Secretary Doug Collins. “The massive improvements we’re making in VA healthcare and benefits are a big reason why more than 300,000 new Veterans have enrolled in VA care this year.”
View the complete list of fourth quarter projects here.
VA obligated all the $4.8 billion that was available in FY 2026. Maintenance projects approved in the fourth quarter of FY2026 include:
- $1.183 billion to repair and upgrade outdated infrastructure systems in medical facilities.
- $938 million for major building upgrades like elevators, electrical systems, and boiler plants.
- $560 million for maintenance and modernization of facility infrastructure to support future electronic health record system updates.
These investments are one of many ways the Trump Administration is making VA work better for Veterans. Since Jan. 20, 2025, VA has:
- Enrolled more than 300,000 new Veterans in VA healthcare in 2026.
- Opened 43 new VA healthcare facilities, expanding healthcare access for Veterans around the country.
- Completed a record high 82,083,918 direct care appointments in fiscal year 2025, up 4.1% from FY 2024.
- Completed a record high 59,989,662 community care appointments in FY 2025, up 12% from FY 2024.
- Offered Veterans more than 3.4 million appointments outside of normal operating hours, giving Veterans more timely and convenient options for care.

SAN BRUNO, CA – Rep. Kevin Mullin (CA-15), who has been demanding answers from the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) and authored the National Archives Protection Act, issued the following statement in response to California Attorney General Rob Bonta announcing a lawsuit to block the closure of the San Francisco National Archives, located in San Bruno, CA:
“The National Archives and Records at San Bruno tell the important story of what has happened here in the Bay Area and local communities have every right to want direct access to their history. The National Records and Archives Administration (NARA) failed to conduct any kind of public input process and didn’t engage with stakeholders who are impacted before making a decision to close this facility and relocate fragile, sensitive documents over 1,500 miles away.
I am glad to see California Attorney General Rob Bonta file a lawsuit to stop NARA’s closure of the facility, and emphasizing how important it is for state agencies, university researchers and tribes to have access to these records.
While I’m pleased to see the Attorney General take action today, I am also pushing for federal legislation with the National Archives Protection Act and will be doing everything in my power to prevent the closure through other means like the federal budget process.
The fact that we have developed a bipartisan, nationwide coalition of federal lawmakers interested in preserving these archives demonstrates the unique and irreplaceable value they hold. These archives aren’t just boxes of paper — they hold the stories, memories, and history of generations of Americans. Families whose ancestors immigrated through Angel Island can track their lineage, those whose loved ones served in the Navy and were stationed in the Pacific can learn about their legacy, and Native Americans whose history is documented over generations are all able to learn more by visiting this national archive.”
In June 2026, the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) announced it would be closing the San Francisco (San Bruno) and Chicago facilities, which are two of just 13 regional archives across America. The local facility in San Bruno houses culturally-significant archives from not only California but also Nevada, Hawaii, Pacific island territories, and Tribes. Its records hold deep value to the community including Angel Island immigration files, Chinese Exclusion Act and Japanese Internment records, Native American and indigenous history documents, and much more.
Read more about Rep. Mullin’s National Archives Protection Act, and NARA’s dismissive response to a letter he co-authored with Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28) along with 37 federal lawmakers, urging them to stop the closure.
###
title: Reaction to California Attorney General’s Lawsuit to Protect National Archives in San Bruno

Tallahassee, Florida – Timeka Griffin, 42, of Tallahassee, Florida, was sentenced to five years in federal prison for her role in a conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute methamphetamine and cocaine, distribution of cocaine and methamphetamine, and possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine. The sentence was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida.

U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “This local drug trafficking ring has been dismantled thanks to the excellent investigative work of our state and federal law enforcement partners and this successful prosecution by my office. Our citizens deserve safe, drug-free streets, and my office will continue to aggressively prosecute anyone caught peddling deadly narcotics in this district to ensure we deliver on that promise.”

Court documents reflect that in July 2025, the Drug Enforcement Administration and Leon County Sheriff’s Office received information regarding the trafficking of cocaine in Leon County. Through investigation, law enforcement identified Edward Lee Cromartie and Griffin as a source of supply for cocaine and methamphetamine. Law enforcement also identified a suspected drug stash location, and upon execution of a federal search warrant at a storage unit shared by Cromartie and Griffin, seized approximately 1.6 kilograms of methamphetamine, along with multiple firearms, including a stolen handgun.

In March 2026, Cromartie was sentenced to 12 years in federal prison for his role in the drug trafficking conspiracy, distribution, and possession with intent to distribute charges.

“Dealers of Methamphetamine in North Florida should know DEA is coming for you,” said Special Agent in Charge Daniel Escobar, Tampa Field Division. “Our agents will bring criminals who distribute this poison in our communities to justice.”

The case involved a joint investigation by the Drug Enforcement Administration and Leon County Sheriff’s Office. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Eric K. Mountin.

The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl .
title: Tallahassee Woman Sentenced to Federal Prison for Drug Distribution

CAGUAS, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente Pablo José Hernández anunció $13,312,817 en fondos federales para el Departamento de Salud, universidades y organizaciones de investigación en Puerto Rico. Los fondos ayudarán a prevenir enfermedades, impulsar la investigación médica, preparar profesionales de la salud y ofrecer servicios a pacientes.
“Mi prioridad es atender lo básico: que nuestra gente tenga acceso a mejores servicios de salud. Estos fondos permitirán investigar enfermedades como el dengue y el VIH, ampliar programas de prevención y preparar más profesionales de la salud en Puerto Rico”, expresó el Comisionado Residente.
Los fondos provienen del Departamento de Salud y Servicios Humanos de Estados Unidos (HHS), a través de programas federales de agencias como los Centros para el Control y la Prevención de Enfermedades (CDC) y la Administración de Recursos y Servicios de Salud (HRSA)

- $840,395 para mejorar los servicios a pacientes con Alzheimer y apoyar a sus cuidadores.
- $828,500 para fortalecer laboratorios y la vigilancia epidemiológica para detectar brotes de enfermedades.
- $472,413 para recopilar datos sobre diabetes, hipertensión y otros factores de riesgo para la salud.
Universidades y escuelas de medicina
- $1,007,923 para el Recinto de Ciencias Médicas de la UPR para formación en condiciones del neurodesarrollo, salud oral y prevención de riesgos ocupacionales.
- $905,754 para la Universidad Central del Caribe para capacitar profesionales de la salud mediante tecnología y aprendizaje colaborativo.

BOSTON – Former Massachusetts state official, Lamar Cook, has been arrested for fraudulently obtaining Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits, receiving over $500 per month, while on court ordered pretrial release in connection with a pending state indictment for alleged cocaine trafficking and firearm offenses.

Lamar Cook, 46, of Springfield, Mass., was arrested today on a criminal complaint charging him with one count of SNAP fraud and wire fraud. Cook will appear in federal court in Boston later today.

In 2023, the Governor of Massachusetts appointed Cook to serve as the Western MA Deputy Director in Springfield, Mass. Cook was terminated in October 2025 after he was detained at the Springfield State Office building and later charged by the Hampden District Attorney’s Office for alleged drug and firearm offenses. According to court documents, Cook earned a yearly salary of $130,227 and was later paid $22,374.29 in net pay for accrued vacation leave following his termination. The Commonwealth later “realized an error in paying Mr. Cook for accrued vacation leave time, the Commonwealth attempted to reverse the direct deposits, but it could not do so due to insufficient funds available in the accounts.”

According to court filings in the federal criminal case, Cook’s bank account continued to hold balances of approximately $13,000 as of January 2026 and over $8,800 in April 2026.

Cook also allegedly received a federal and state tax refund in May 2026 from his employment with the Governor’s Office for the 2025 calendar year in the amount of $2,497.88. Additionally, according to court documents, Cook’s mother won approximately $1 million in the Massachusetts Lottery in early 2026. Cook’s mother allegedly made numerous Zelle payments to him totaling approximately $12,000 between May and June 2026.

According to the charging documents, Cook applied for SNAP benefits on April 6, 2026 and falsely claimed zero income, less than $100 in his bank account, and to be living in a two person household consisting only of himself and his minor child. According to the affidavit, Cook in fact maintained at least one bank account that held more than $8,800 on the date of his SNAP application and received thousands of dollars in additional deposits, including the payments from his mother. It is further alleged that Cook failed to disclose that his fiancée and her mother lived with him at his Springfield residence and his fiancée earned income exceeding $80,000 annually from the City of Springfield Public Schools.

“The alleged conduct is simply egregious. SNAP benefits are intended to put food on the table for struggling families who cannot make ends meet, not for those who allegedly hide income to circumvent the financial requirements, much less travel to Disney World. Mr. Cook allegedly lied about his income and the makeup of his household in order to receive over $540 per month in SNAP benefits. All this occurred while Cook was on pretrial release for charged state drug and firearm offenses,” said U.S. Attorney Leah B. Foley. “What kind of system allows for someone like this defendant to receive taxpayer funded benefits? I find it disturbing that the Commonwealth of Massachusetts could not prevent this from happening, nor could it recover the ill-gained $22,000 payment for earned vacation time -- which was also paid out with taxpayer money.”

Mr. Cook allegedly lied about his income and the makeup of his household in order to receive over $540 per month in SNAP benefits. All this occurred while Cook was on pretrial release for charged state drug and firearm offenses,” said U.S. Attorney Leah B. I find it disturbing that the Commonwealth of Massachusetts could not prevent this from happening, nor could it recover the ill-gained $22,000 payment for earned vacation time -- which was also paid out with taxpayer money.”

“It is an unconscionable betrayal of the public trust for a former state official with a pending indictment for drug and gun offenses to then also steal SNAP benefits from the American taxpayer – food assistance benefits intended for low-income Americans,” said U.S. Department of Agriculture, Inspector General John Walk. “This former state employee lied about his income and family situation to cheat the program. He will now face justice.”

“Fraud against public benefit programs is ultimately a theft from taxpayers and from the beneficiaries these programs are intended to serve,” said Roberto Coviello, Special Agent in Charge of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG). “HHS-OIG remains committed to protecting the integrity of taxpayer-funded programs and ensuring that those who seek to exploit them for personal gain are held accountable.”

Cook received approximately $546 per month in SNAP benefits. Cook’s SNAP benefits were allegedly used regularly at grocery and retail stores in Massachusetts and on a July 2026 trip to Florida. Retail surveillance and transaction records show Cook’s fiancée frequently used his EBT card to make purchases for the household, despite not being listed as a member of his household on Cook’s SNAP application.

According to court documents, at the time Cook submitted his application for SNAP benefits, he was on release for a pending Hampden County Superior Court indictment charging him with trafficking more than 200 grams of cocaine, conspiracy and firearm offenses stemming from an October 2025 investigation.

The charge of SNAP fraud provides for a sentence of up to five years in prison, up to three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. The charge of wire fraud provides for a sentence of up to 20 years in prison, up to three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case.

U.S. Attorney Foley; USDA IG Walk; and HHS IG Coviello made the announcement. Valuable assistance Massachusetts State Police, Hampden County District Attorney’s Office, Homeland Security Investigations in New England and the Springfield Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Philip A. Mallard of the Organized Crime & Gang Unit is prosecuting the case.

On March 26, 2026 , United States Attorney Leah B. Foley announced the creation of the Benefit & Voter Fraud Team, a district-wide initiative established in response to the rampant fraud being uncovered across Massachusetts. Members of the public are encouraged to report suspected benefit fraud in Massachusetts by calling 1-855-SCAM-MA-1 (855-722-6621).

On April 7, 2026, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division . The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

SACRAMENTO, Calif. — A federal grand jury returned an indictment against Kyree Hall, 26, of Sacramento, charging him with theft of government property, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced. The indictment was unsealed following his arrest today.

According to court documents, Hall was an employee of the U.S. Postal Service in 2025, and worked as the sole clerk in the Rio Oso Post Office in Sutter County. Using his position, between March and May 2025, Hall issued at least 56 USPS money orders payable to himself and falsely recorded that they had been paid for by various people. The theft cost the U.S. Postal Service approximately $55,505.

The U.S. Postal Service-Office of Inspector General conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Veronica M.A. Alegría is prosecuting the case.

If convicted, Hall faces a maximum statutory penalty of 10 years in prison and a $250,000 fine. Any sentence, however, would be determined at the discretion of the court after consideration of any applicable statutory factors and the federal Sentencing Guidelines, which take into account a number of variables. The charges are only allegations; the defendant is presumed innocent until and unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.
title: Former Postal Employee in Sutter County Indicted for Embezzling Postal Money Orders

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. RepresentativesYassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Greg Stanton (AZ-04), and Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07) demand answers from GardaWorld Federal Services (GWFS) following its latest $1.2 billion contract to expand immigration detention facilities in Florence, Arizona. The lawmakers also pressed the company to answer questions it failed to address in a previous inquiry related to the Surprise warehouse facility.
The new contract, awarded September 21, raises fresh concerns about transparency and coordination with local governments. According to reporting, the Town of Florence was not notified of the planned expansion and had no additional information about the contract.
"It is deeply concerning that, despite the significant scale of these projects and their potential impact on surrounding communities, local governments continue to learn about them only after contracts have been awarded," the lawmakers wrote.
The letter also presses GWFS on questions left unanswered from the lawmakers’ March 2026 inquiry into its contract with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to convert a warehouse in Surprise into an immigration detention facility. In its April response, GWFS deferred many questions to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and failed to address basic questions about its own detention experience, staffing, facility assessments, and subcontracting plans. The lawmakers are demanding full answers.
The lawmakers also raised concerns about GWFS' previously undisclosed role in the environmental review of the Surprise warehouse. The City of Surprise revealed that a company representative had requested information for the assessment, despite neither GWFS nor federal agencies publicly disclosing its involvement.
The lawmakers are requesting written responses within 15 business days of receipt of the letter, including answers about:
- Experience and staffing: GWFS' qualifications to manage both projects, personnel overseeing operations, and plans to subcontract construction, medical care, staffing, or facility management.
- Facility safety: Structural and code-compliance assessments of the Surprise warehouse, including plans for ventilation, extreme heat mitigation, fire safety, and medical care.
- Environmental review: GWFS' role in the Surprise environmental assessment and its experience conducting comparable federal reviews.
- Florence expansion: Specific projects, facilities, and task orders planned under the $1.2 billion contract, including their scope and cost.
- Local coordination: Consultations with Surprise, Florence, Maricopa and Pinal counties, school districts, and public safety agencies.
- Taxpayer costs: Whether GWFS or DHS will cover increased demands for emergency medical services, fire protection, and law enforcement rather than shifting those costs to local taxpayers.
"The communities surrounding the Surprise and Florence facilities deserve transparency," the lawmakers concluded.
Read the full letter HERE.
title: Ansari, Stanton, Grijalva Press GardaWorld Over Unanswered Questions After Company Secures New $1.2 Billion ICE Contract

Pou Reveals New Details of Massive Data Center Diesel Spill
More than a month later, questions remain over missing oil, environmental damage, and cleanup
PATERSON, NJ – Congresswoman Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09) today revealed new details about the September 11, 2026 diesel spill at a data center in Secaucus, including a more than seven-hour delay in reporting the incident to state authorities and unanswered questions about its environmental impact.
These findings, obtained after Pou sought answers from the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection, were shared in a letter to Secaucus Mayor Michael Gonnelli as the state continues investigating the roughly 5,500-gallon spill.
On October 2, 2026, Congresswoman Pou wrote to NJDEP Commissioner Ed Potosnak seeking a full accounting of the spill, including how it occurred, a timeline of the disaster, the extent of the damage, and what safeguards would be put in place to prevent similar catastrophes.
“Although approximately 4,000 gallons of the diesel have been recovered from waterways and canals, a full accounting of the remaining fuel and cleanup is still outstanding. NJDEP reports that its daily inspections have found no evidence that diesel reached the Hackensack River. However, the agency has acknowledged reports of discoloration in vegetation along the southeast edge of the river, downstream of the tributary where the spill occurred. Although Equinix and NJDEP have stated that an unspecified amount of fuel was absorbed by cleanup materials deployed around the tributaries, I remain deeply concerned about diesel that may remain in the surrounding soil, sediment, and waterways,” Congresswoman Pou writes Secaucus Mayor Gonnelli about the data center damage around his community.
Key Findings from the NJDEP’s Preliminary Investigation
- Approximately 4,000 gallons of diesel have been recovered from the storm sewer line and drainage canals: NJDEP reports an unspecified amount was absorbed by cleanup materials. How much diesel remains in surrounding soil, sediment, and waterways is unknown.
- No evidence was found that diesel reached the Hackensack River: But NJDEP acknowledged reports of “discolored vegetation along the river’s southeastern edge, downstream from the affected tributary.” NJDEP is investigating if the discoloration was caused by the diesel spill.
- The data center falls below the threshold for certain state safeguards against major facilities. NJDEP determined that the facility is not subject to New Jersey’s major-facility discharge prevention requirements, including secondary containment systems, physical security measures, and visual inspections.
- Cleanup efforts continue, and Equinix has taken corrective measures. NJDEP has confirmed that emergency responses were undertaken following the spill. According to separately published reports, Equinix has reportedly terminated a facility site engineer and suspended automatic fuel polishing operations nationwide.
- The state probe remains ongoing with no completion date announced. The agency has committed to releasing its final report publicly and will evaluate appropriate enforcement actions.
Secaucus and surrounding communities have lived with pollution for decades. Contamination from industrial sites and landfill runoff led the Environmental Protection Agency to designate the Lower Hackensack River a Superfund site in 2022. Now as a major cleanup is underway, the September 11 Equinix spill has seen over 5,000 gallons of diesel released into the local environment.
The Secaucus spill comes amid growing national attention to the environmental impact and public costs of rapidly expanding data centers.
Timeline of the September 11, 2026 Diesel Spill
12:20PM: The spill may have begun as early as just after noon, following a failure of the overfill protection system on generator #4’s fuel tank during an internal fuel transfer.
~4:00PM: Equinix’s fuel polishing process stopped although diesel continued leaking.
6:36PM: An Equinix guard discovered the spill, approximately six hours after it may have begun.
6:46PM: Within 10 minutes of discovering the spill, Equinix isolated the fuel lines and halted the generator.
7:06PM: Spill containment kits were deployed.
7:11PM: Equinix contacted its emergency contractor.
7:43PM: Equinix notified NJDEP of the spill, more than seven hours after it may have begun. The Secaucus Fire Department arrived around the same time.
9:45PM: Equinix’s emergency contractor arrived at the facility, more than three hours after the spill was discovered.
September 12, 6:07AM: Secaucus and the local health department received electronic notification of the spill, nearly 18 hours after it may have begun.
The text of Congresswoman Pou’s letter to Secaucus Mayor Gonnelli is below.
Dear Mayor Gonnelli:
I write to share new information over the recent data center fuel spill in Secaucus that released over 5,000 gallons of diesel fuel into waterways near the Hackensack River. On October 2, I wrote to the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (“NJDEP”) demanding answers about the spill at the Equinix facility, including a timeline of events and information about its environmental impact. NJDEP responded to several of my questions. Although more information is forthcoming, I want to share what we have learned so far, including additional details Equinix recently provided to my office and to NJDEP.
On September 11, 2026, Equinix conducted an internal fuel transfer operation, during which the overfill protection system on generator #4’s fuel tank failed. Equinix has stated that the spill may have begun as early as 12:20 PM and continued until approximately 4:00 PM when fuel polishing stopped. After roughly six hours of diesel fuel leaking, an Equinix security guard discovered the spill at approximately 6:36 PM. Within 10 minutes, the facility isolated the fuel lines and halted the associated generator. Around 7:06 PM, spill kits were deployed and by 7:11 PM, Equinix contacted its emergency environmental contractor. Equinix reported the incident to the NJDEP Hotline at 7:43 PM—over seven hours after the spill began. Around that same time, the Secaucus Fire Department arrived at the facility—Equinix’s own emergency environmental contractor arrived roughly two hours later at 9:45 PM. NJDEP also directed environmental booms to be deployed to stop the diesel fuel from spreading into the drainage tributary for the Hackensack River. NJDEP also directed the use of additional equipment to vacuum and clean up the spill.
More than a month after the spill, important questions remain unanswered. Although approximately 4,000 gallons of the diesel have been recovered from waterways and canals, a full accounting of the remaining fuel and cleanup is still outstanding. NJDEP reports that its daily inspections have found no evidence that diesel reached the Hackensack River. However, the agency has acknowledged reports of discoloration in vegetation along the southeast edge of the river, downstream of the tributary where the spill occurred. Although Equinix and NJDEP have stated that an unspecified amount of fuel was absorbed by cleanup materials deployed around the tributaries, I remain deeply concerned about diesel that may remain in the surrounding soil, sediment, and waterways.
NJDEP continues to investigate the incident, including whether the vegetation discoloration was caused by the fuel spill, but has not provided a timeline for completing its probe. NJDEP has promised to provide me with additional information as it becomes available. The agency has committed to making its final report public so our community can understand the full extent of any damage. Once the report is completed, NJDEP will evaluate appropriate enforcement actions.
Importantly, within a week of the spill, NJDEP inspected the Equinix facility and determined that its fuel storage capacity falls below the threshold for New Jersey’s major facility discharge of petroleum and other hazardous substance prevention requirements. These requirements include having physical security measures, impermeable secondary containment and diversion systems, and visual inspections and monitoring.
While NJDEP has confirmed that appropriate emergency responses were undertaken following the spill and that cleanup efforts continue, and although Equinix appears to have terminated an employee serving as a facility site engineer and has halted automatic fuel polishing nationwide, more must be done to keep our communities safe. My office will continue to work with you, the Town of Secaucus, state agencies, and federal regulators to address the aftermath of this incident and prevent similar spills in the future.
Sincerely,
Nellie Pou
Member of Congress
###
title: Pou Reveals New Details of Massive Data Center Diesel Spill

BOSTON – An associate of the Lynn Chapter of the Trinitarios and drug supplier to the gang with connections to a Mexican drug cartel pleaded guilty on Oct. 7, 2026 to racketeering and drug charges, including organizing an attempted murder that the Trinitarios undertook on behalf of the cartel.

Janoy Batista, a/k/a “El Viejo,” 47, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to conduct enterprise affairs through a pattern of racketeering activity, more commonly referred to as RICO conspiracy and drug conspiracy. U.S. Senior District Court Judge Nathaniel M. Gorton scheduled sentencing for Jan. 7, 2027. Batista was arrested and charged in February 2025 with other leaders, members and associates of the Trinitarios.

The Trinitarios is a violent criminal enterprise comprised of thousands of members across the United States. The Trinitarios adhere to a Magna Carta, employ an internal hierarchy to coordinate and execute violence, and undertake extensive efforts to maintain the secrecy of the organization and its members.

During the plea hearing, Batista admitted that he was an associate of the gang and that he supplied the gang with drugs from Cartel Jalisco Nuevo Generacion (“CJNG”). CJNG would ship large quantities of cocaine and fentanyl to Batista in Lynn, Mass. utilizing car transport trucks. Batista would supply members of the Trinitarios with cocaine and fentanyl received from CJNG.

Batista further admitted that in November 2023, CJNG tasked him with killing a local drug contact who the cartel believed had stolen a large quantity of drugs. CJNG indicated that Batista would be required to kill the drug contact in order to continue receiving shipments. In November 2023, Batista organized a failed murder attempt of the drug contact utilizing a Trinitarios member’s vehicle. During the incident in Salem, Mass., two shooters opened fire on the drug contact as he sat in his driveway, striking him multiple times. Batista picked up the shooters and driver involved in the attempted murder and drove them to an apartment controlled by the Trinitarios. The drug contact survived the incident.

In February 2025 , federal racketeering charges were unsealed against 22 leaders and members of the Trinitarios. The charges were the result of a multijurisdictional investigation, which began in the aftermath of four murders as well as a series of attempted murders and shootings that took place in Lynn in 2023, allegedly committed by the Trinitarios criminal enterprise and its members. On June 9, 2026 , additional federal racketeering and drug charges were unsealed charging 26 additional leaders, members and associates of the Lawrence, Haverhill and Boston Chapters of the gang. According to court documents, the Trinitarios have allegedly participated in five additional murders in Essex County since 2017, bringing the total of federally charged murders to 11, and the total number of federally charged defendants to 56.

The charge of conspiracy to conduct enterprise affairs through a pattern of racketeering activity (also known as “racketeering conspiracy” or “RICO conspiracy”) provides for a sentence of up to life in prison, five years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Jeff Grimming, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations in New England; Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge, Federal Bureau of Investigation, Boston Division; Essex County District Attorney Paul F. Tucker; Massachusetts State Police Colonel Geoffrey D. Noble; and Lynn Police Chief Christopher P. Reddy made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the Manchester, N.H. Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Philip A. Mallard of the Organized Crime & Gang Unit is prosecuting the case.

This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Boston is comprised of agents and officers from HSI, FBI, DEA, ATF, USMS, IRS-CI, USPIS, DOL-OIG and DSS, as well as several state and local law enforcement agencies, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Massachusetts.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. Operation Take Back America streamlines efforts and resources from the Department’s Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Forces and Project Safe Neighborhood .

Reps. Carter, Moskowitz Introduce the Emergency Preparedness in Higher Education Act to Strengthen Campus Resilience
WASHINGTON, D.C. – In the aftermath of Hurricane Isaias, Congressman Troy A. Carter, Sr. (D-LA) and Congressman Jared Moskowitz (D-FL), Co-Chairs of the Disaster Preparedness and Recovery Caucus, introduced the Emergency Preparedness in Higher Education Act. This legislation authorizes $100 million in annual federal funding for the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to distribute to higher education institutions. These grants would improve institutions’ capacity, planning, and facilities to better prepare for, and respond to, disasters and other emergencies that directly impact students, administrators, and staff. The need for greater disaster preparedness was evident when Hurricanes Katrina, Ida, and Irma devastated universities in Louisiana and Florida, and when wildfires forced evacuations of California campuses.
“Our climate crisis makes extreme weather events more frequent and severe, so we need to ensure uniquely vulnerable communities, such as our colleges and universities, have the support and resources they need to prepare for and respond to disasters and emergency situations,” said Congressman Carter. “I’m partnering with Rep. Moskowitz to introduce this legislation and take necessary steps toward preparing our institutions of higher education for protecting the lives, housing, property, and futures of our young adults and the staff that support them before disaster strikes – not after a storm has already arrived.”
“As Florida’s former emergency management director, I know that the time to prepare for a disaster is before it strikes. No student should be left wondering where to go or whether their campus can keep them safe when a disaster hits,” said Congressman Moskowitz. “Families send their children to college trusting that their safety is a priority. That responsibility starts long before the first evacuation order.”
Background
American colleges and universities function as small communities, often housing tens of thousands of students, staff, and researchers in concentrated areas, making them uniquely vulnerable to a range of natural disasters and other emergencies. Campus shootings and other acts of violence, from Virginia Tech to Michigan State, have shown that institutions need well-rehearsed active-threat plans and protocols, reliable mass-notification systems, trained threat-assessment teams, and coordination with local law enforcement. Additionally, climate change is increasing the frequency and severity of hurricanes, wildfires, floods, extreme heat, and other events that can shut down campuses, displace students, and damage infrastructure.
Institutions have a duty of care for the many students who live on campus far from family, including international students, students with disabilities, and low-income students who face additional challenges. Investing in comprehensive emergency planning, resilient infrastructure, continuity-of-operations strategies, accessible communication, and other resources protects lives, preserves academic and research missions, and limits financial impacts. As these threats become more frequent and often overlap, campuses need additional support to make preparedness a core institutional responsibility.
The Emergency Preparedness in Higher Education strengthens higher education resilience by establishing a $100 million annual FEMA grant program to help eligible higher education institutions create or expand emergency management and preparedness capacity.
Eligible uses of grant funds include personnel costs to expand emergency preparedness; creating or updating comprehensive institutional emergency management plans; infrastructure and facility construction or improvements for emergency operations centers or areas of refuge; and equipment and technology to enhance interagency coordination.
Read the full bill text here.

Navy Child and Youth Programs Partners with United Through Reading to Keep Military Families Connected Through Storytime
WASHINGTON DC (Oct. 14, 2026) — Navy Child and Youth Programs (CYP) has launched an enterprise-wide partnership with United Through Reading (UTR), a nonprofit that strengthens military families’ emotional bonds, literacy, and well-being through shared reading experiences, regardless of distance.
Under the banner “Read, Record, Connect: Keeping Military Families Connected Through Storytime,” the partnership will equip Navy installations with books, literacy resources, mobile story stations, and digital tools to help families stay connected during periods of separation while supporting children’s early literacy and development.
Military life often requires families to spend extended periods apart due to deployments, Individual Augmentations (IAs), extended duty shifts, underways, temporary duty assignments (TDYs), and Permanent Change of Station (PCS) relocations. These demands can also separate families from the extended support networks they rely on. By helping children see and hear their parent reading a familiar story, the partnership reinforces meaningful family connections, supports consistent reading routines, and makes shared story time possible from thousands of miles away.
“Military life can place unique demands on families, from deployments and extended duty hours to frequent relocations that take Sailors away from home. Maintaining strong family connections is essential to Sailors’ well-being and their families’ resilience,” said Vice Adm. Brad Collins, Commander, Navy Installations Command. “Our partnership with United Through Reading reflects CNIC’s commitment to improving Quality of Service by giving military families practical ways to stay connected, even when duty keeps them apart.”
Beginning in fall 2026, the eight-month initiative will deliver literacy resources and family engagement opportunities to Navy CYP facilities and military households, including:
- 24,850 Books for Children and Youth: A diverse selection of titles for all ages, from baby board books and picture books to early and leveled readers, chapter books, middle-grade literature, and young adult novels.
- 165,000 Bookmarks: Specially designed bookmarks to encourage daily reading habits, featuring creative coloring bookmarks, Halloween-themed editions, and commemorative "Book for the Military Child" bookmarks.
- 100,000 Early Literacy Guides: From Day One: Connecting Through Storytime, practical resources tailored to families with infants and children ages 0–5.
- 65 Specialized In-Person Recording Events: 41 recording sessions staffed by UTR and 24 events using Mobile Story Stations.
- Facility Engagement Materials: Year-round outreach resources, including UTR information cards, parent bookmarks, and front-desk flyers for distribution across all CYP sites.
Flexible Ways to Share Storytime
The partnership combines in-person recording opportunities with a convenient mobile option, allowing service members to record and share stories wherever duty takes them.
Through the self-service UTR smartphone app, service members can record themselves reading a book aloud from virtually anywhere in the world. They can then upload the video and designate a co-parent or caregiver to receive it by email and through the app. Recipients also receive instructions for ordering a free copy of the featured book through UTR, allowing children to follow along with the printed pages as they watch and listen to their parent read.
In addition to the mobile app, families will have access to Local and Command Story Stations, along with on-site recording opportunities for enrolled parents and caregivers. These in-person events will focus on major fleet concentration areas, including Region Northwest, San Diego, Hampton Roads, Naval District Washington, and Florida.
Phased Rollout: 2026–2027
Resources will be distributed in phases:
- October 2026: Distribution of Halloween-themed bookmarks and early childhood literacy guides.
- December 2026: Winter shipment of children's and youth books.
- January 2027: Second distribution phase of literacy guides for ages 0–5.
- March 2027: Spring distribution of books across age categories.
- April 2027: Month of the Military Child-themed bookmarks distributed in celebration of military youth.
Through Read, Record, Connect, Navy CYP and United Through Reading are making it easier for military families to maintain meaningful connections through the simple, familiar ritual of reading together. Whether a Sailor is deployed overseas, underway, or serving far from home, a familiar voice and a favorite story can help children feel connected to their parent. The partnership reinforces CNIC’s commitment to improving Quality of Service by helping Sailors and their families stay connected, supported, and resilient wherever Navy service takes them.
Commander, Navy Installations Command is responsible for worldwide U.S. Navy Shore installation management, designing and developing integrated solutions for sustainment and development of Navy shore infrastructure as well as quality of life programs. CNIC oversees 10 Navy regions, 71 installations, and more than 63,000 employees who are focused on warfighting and manning, training and equipping the Shore to fight and win. Navy installations are warfighting platforms essential to every fleet operation.
title: Navy Child and Youth Programs Partners with United Through Reading to Keep Military Families Connected Through Storytime

KNOXVILLE, Tenn. – On October 14, 2026, Christopher Michael Anderson, 45, currently of Knoxville, TN, was sentenced to 420 months imprisonment by the Honorable Thomas A. Varlan, United States District Judge, in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Tennessee at Knoxville. Following his release from prison, Anderson will be required to register with state sex offender registries and comply with special sex offender conditions during his supervised release.

As part of the plea agreement filed with the court, Anderson agreed to plead guilty to an indictment charging him with, three counts of exploitation of a child in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 2251(a); one count of attempted exploitation of a child in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 2251(a); and one count of distribution of child pornography in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 2252A(a)(2).

From December 2018 through January 2022, Anderson, with the assistance of co-defendants Amanda Eggers and Brittany Anderson, sexually exploited nine children and possessed 138 images of additional child pornography. Anderson exchanged child pornography images with Eggers and B. Anderson of their minor children over the internet. Anderson also sexually exploited his grandchild. The ages of the victims ranged from just under two through eleven.

Eggers is currently set to be sentenced on November 18, 2026, and B. Anderson is currently sent to be sentenced on February 11, 2027, both hearings are scheduled with the Honorable Judge Varlan.

U.S. Attorney Francis M. Hamilton III of the Eastern District of Tennessee and Special Agent in Charge Terrence G. Reilly of the Nashville Field Office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) made the announcement.

The criminal indictment was the result of an investigation by the FBI and the Knox County Sheriff’s Office (KCSO).

Assistant United States Attorney Jennifer Kolman represented the United States.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood (PSC), a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006, by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the United States Attorney’s Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, PSC marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about PSC, please visit www.justice.gov/psc .

For more information about internet safety education, please visit www.justice.gov/psc/resources.html and click on the tab "resources.”
