Ranking Members Morelle, Meeks Host Queens, NY Shadow Hearing on Election Security, Fighting Trump Administration’s Attacks on Voting
With voting underway, lawmakers and voting rights leaders gathered in Queens to defend mail-in voting, combat intimidation and protect election integrity
Queens, NY – Last week, Ranking Member Joe Morelle (NY-25), Committee on House Administration, and Ranking Member Gregory Meeks (NY-05), House Foreign Affairs Committee, hosted a public shadow hearing with members of the New York delegation to confront the Trump administration’s attacks on voting and detail efforts to defend every eligible American’s right to cast a ballot and have it counted.
Experts at the shadow hearing included:
- Bethany Li, Executive Director of the Asian American Legal Defense and Education Fund
- John Cusick, Assistant Counsel at the Legal Defense Fund
- Brian Lemek, President and Executive Director of the Defend the Vote Action Fund
Experts outlined voter education and safeguards countering interference, intimidation and misinformation in the 2026 midterm election. The hearing examined federal demands for sensitive voter information and concerns about armed immigration agents at polling places. Experts detailed ongoing efforts to protect voter privacy and prevent intimidation.
“In this moment, there is nothing more urgent than protecting American democracy,” said Ranking Member Joe Morelle (NY-25). “The election is here and we are protecting every American’s right to the ballot box. Every time the Trump Administration has tried to interfere with the integrity of the midterm elections, they have lost. We need to remain clear-eyed about the threats we continue to face, and we will fight to protect our elections. Failure, quite simply, is not an option. I want to thank Ranking Member Meeks for hosting this convening and the New York delegation for continuing to be on the front lines.”
“The right to vote is the heart of our democracy,” said Ranking Member Gregory Meeks (NY-05). “As the Trump administration continues to attempt to disenfranchise minority communities and cheat their way to a Republican majority in Congress, it is important that we do not waver in our fight to preserve the right to vote. I applaud my colleagues and the experts for showing up, setting the record straight, and empowering voters to cast their ballots.”
“Election security and voting rights are under attack by President Trump and we must do all we can stop this assault on the sacred right to make our voices heard at the ballot box,” said Congresswoman Grace Meng (NY-06). “The President is pushing to add a citizenship question to the 2030 census and remove the collection of race and ethnicity data to manipulate voting maps and to dilute the political representation of diverse communities. He has consistently engaged in fearmongering about the security of mail-in voting, citing false accusations of fraud, and encouraged the use of voter suppression and intimidation tactics to make it harder for Americans to participate in the democratic process. And the Supreme Court’s conservative majority has further gutted the Voting Rights Act, weakening the political power of minority voters. Despite all these unconscionable and reckless attacks, we will never stop fighting to protect the right to vote, which is the foundation of our great democracy. I thank Congressmembers Morelle and Meeks for organizing this shadow hearing in Queens to keep a light shined on one of the most crucial issues facing New York and the nation, and thank you as well to all the witnesses who testified.”
“My grandparents, immigrants from Poland, worked hard to become U.S. citizens and earn the right to vote,” said Congressman Paul Tonko (NY-20). “Their unwavering belief in our democracy instilled in me the importance of that right for all citizens. At a time when this Trump administration is seeking to undermine our election system and disenfranchise entire communities, it is more important than ever to stand up and defend this fundamental right. I’m grateful to my colleagues for holding this important hearing and doing all in our power to ensure the American people’s voices are heard.”
“Republicans continue to push lies and intimidate voters across the country to depress voter turnout and sow distrust in our elections at all levels,” said Congressman Adriano Espaillat (NY-13). “We have a duty to ensure the safety of everyone at the ballot box not only this November, but for every election. Democracy requires our most ardent protection and hosting these hearings are part of the ongoing mission to serve all Americans who deserve fair, free, and safe elections.”
Ranking Member Morelle and the Committee on House Administration is charged with the oversight of federal elections, including considering proposals to amend federal election law and monitoring congressional elections across the U.S.
Watch a recording of the event here.

title: Ranking Members Morelle, Meeks Host Queens, NY Shadow Hearing on Election Security, Fighting Trump Administration’s Attacks on Voting

Construction Company Owner and Employees Indicted for Wide Ranging Tax and Financial Fraud Schemes
A federal grand jury in the Eastern District of New York returned an indictment on September 23, 2026, charging Arthur Nelson, of Staten Island and Sunny Isles Beach, Florida, Joseph Free, of Staten Island, Paul Vasquez, of Englishtown, New Jersey, and Ulysses Jude Devocion, of Queens County, New York with various crimes, including conspiring to defraud the IRS, tax evasion, willfully failing to withhold and pay over employment taxes, failing to file income tax returns, helping to file false corporate tax returns, interfering with the administration of the internal revenue laws, conspiracy to commit wire fraud, failure to file reports of foreign bank accounts, and obstruction of justice.
According to the indictment, Nelson owned and operated various construction subcontracting companies, including MTB AMG Inc. and PAL AMG Inc., which installed glass on commercial businesses, MTB Metal Fabricators Inc., which provided manufacturing services, and Wired NYC LLC, which provided electric installation services. Nelson’s companies were based in Brooklyn until March 2022 when they relocated to New Jersey.
Free allegedly worked as a construction foreman for the Nelson Companies from March 2017 to approximately 2022. Vasquez allegedly was the senior director of operations until approximately 2025. Devocion was an accountant and office manager, from approximately 2021 and 2023.
As alleged in the indictment, from April 2017 through May 2024, the four defendants caused Nelson’s employees to be paid weekly wages with no amounts withheld for federal employment taxes. These unreported wages totaled at least approximately $5 million. Further, they allegedly falsely classified and caused the false classification of personal expenses as business expenses and filed or caused the filing of false federal tax returns, including quarterly employment tax returns, corporate tax returns, and individual income tax returns. They also allegedly caused the Nelson Companies to issue false wage and tax statements, commonly known as W-2s, to its employees. Nelson also underreported his business gross receipts by approximately $13 million.
As alleged in the indictment, from July 2019 through March 2025, Nelson, Devocion, and Vasquez engaged in a scheme to submit false financial documents relating to Nelson and the Nelson Companies to other companies in order to obtain money or property in amounts to which they were not entitled, including, for example, loans, mortgages, lines of credit, credit cards, and surety bonding contracts.
Nelson is charged with one count of conspiracy to defraud the United States, six counts of willful failure to withhold and pay over employment taxes, one count of attempting to interfere with the due administration of the internal revenue laws, two counts of tax evasion, one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, and two counts of willful failure to file reports of foreign bank and financial accounts (“FBAR”). Free is charged with one count of conspiracy to defraud the United States, one count of attempting to interfere with the due administration of the internal revenue laws, one count of willfully aiding and assisting in the presentation of a false and fraudulent tax return, and one count of willfully failing to file an individual income tax return. Vasquez is charged with one count of conspiracy to defraud the United States, one count of attempting to interfere with the due administration of the internal revenue laws, and one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud. Devocion is charged with one count of conspiracy to defraud the United States, one count of willfully failing to file an individual income tax return, one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, and obstruction of justice in connection with his testimony before the grand jury.
If convicted, the defendants face a maximum penalty of twenty years in prison for conspiracy to commit wire fraud and for obstruction of justice; five years in prison for conspiracy to defraud the United States, for each count of willful failure to withhold and pay over employment taxes, for each count of tax evasion, and for each count of failing to file an FBAR; three years in prison for each count of aiding and assisting the filing of false tax returns and for interfering with the due administration of the revenue laws; and one year in prison for each count of willful failure to file a tax return. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case.
Trial Attorneys Richard Kelley and Michael C. Vasiliadis of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section are prosecuting the case.
An indictment is merely an allegation and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Construction Company Owner and Employees Indicted for Wide Ranging Tax and Financial Fraud Schemes

RUTLAND – The United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Vermont stated that on October 13, 2026, Arick Miller, 39, of Williamstown, Vermont, was sentenced by United States District Judge Mary Kay Lanthier to a term of 120 months’ imprisonment to be followed by a 15-year term of supervised release. Miller pleaded guilty to possession of child sexual abuse materials (also known as child pornography) on June 4, 2026, and agreed, pursuant to the terms of a written plea agreement, to be sentenced for using a minor in the production of a sexually explicit video.

According to court records, Miller was arrested in July 2023 on unrelated charges, and his phone was seized and later released to a witness. The witness saw on Miller’s phone sexually explicit images and videos of a minor who had been entrusted to Miller’s custody, and reported what was seen to the police. After Miller was released from jail in mid-August 2023, Miller made several efforts to impede the investigation by destroying explicit photographs and videos, lying to investigators, coaching witnesses to lie in court, and creating fake text messages to impugn the motives of those he thought were talking to law enforcement. Investigators nevertheless found video and photographic evidence of Miller’s abuse of this minor and Miller’s attempt to conceal it on multiple devices and computer accounts seized during the investigation.

First Assistant United States Attorney Jonathan A. Ophardt commended the collaborative investigatory efforts in this case of Homeland Security Investigations, the Vermont State Police, the Vermont Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force, and the Vermont Department of Children and Families.

The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Dana E. Hill. Miller was represented by Assistant Federal Public Defender Sam Ansell.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC.
title: Williamstown Man Sentenced to 10 Years for Possessing Sexually Explicit Materials of a Minor

USITC Makes Determinations in Five-Year (Sunset) Reviews Concerning Mattresses from Cambodia, China, Malaysia, Serbia, Thailand, Turkey, and Vietnam
The U.S. International Trade Commission (USITC) today determined that revocation of the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on imports mattresses from Cambodia, China, Malaysia, Serbia, Thailand, Turkey, and Vietnam would be likely to lead to continuation or recurrence of material injury within a reasonably foreseeable time.
As a result of the USITC’s affirmative determinations, the existing antidumping duty orders on imports of this product from Cambodia, Malaysia, Serbia, Thailand, Turkey, and Vietnam and the existing countervailing duty order on imports of this product from China will remain in place.
Chairman Brett W. Doyle and Commissioners Jason E. Kearns, Peter-Anthony Pappas, Bart Thanhauser, and David Foley Jr. voted in the affirmative. Commissioner Samuel T. Negatu did not participate in today’s vote.
Today’s action comes under the five-year (sunset) review process required by the Uruguay Round Agreements Act. See the attached page for background on these five-year (sunset) reviews.
The USITC’s public report, Mattresses from Cambodia, China, Malaysia, Serbia, Thailand, Turkey, and Vietnam (Inv. Nos. 701-TA-645 and 731-TA-1495 and 1497-1501 (Review), USITC Publication 5803, October 2026), will contain the views of the USITC and information developed during the reviews.
The report will be available on the USITC website by November 19, 2026.
BACKGROUND
The Uruguay Round Agreements Act requires the Department of Commerce to revoke an antidumping or countervailing duty order, or terminate a suspension agreement, after five years unless the Department of Commerce and the USITC determine that revoking the order or terminating the suspension agreement would be likely to lead to continuation or recurrence of dumping or subsidies (Commerce) and of material injury (USITC) within a reasonably foreseeable time.
The USITC’s institution notice in five-year reviews requests that interested parties file responses with the USITC concerning the likely effects of revoking the order under review as well as other information. Generally, within 95 days from institution, the USITC will determine whether the responses it has received reflect an adequate or inadequate level of interest in a full review. If responses to the USITC’s notice of institution are adequate, or if other circumstances warrant a full review, the USITC conducts a full review, which includes a public hearing and issuance of questionnaires.
The USITC generally does not hold a hearing or conduct further investigative activities in expedited reviews. Commissioners base their injury determination in expedited reviews on the facts available, including the USITC’s prior injury and review determinations, responses received to its notice of institution, data collected by staff in connection with the reviews, and information provided by the Department of Commerce.
The five-year (sunset) reviews concerning Mattresses from Cambodia, China, Malaysia, Serbia, Thailand, Turkey, and Vietnam were instituted on April 1, 2026.
On July 6, 2026, the USITC determined to conduct expedited five-year reviews. For all countries, Commissioners David S. Johanson, Jason E. Kearns, and Amy A. Karpel concluded that the domestic interested party group responses were adequate and the respondent interested party group responses were inadequate, and voted for expedited reviews.
Chairman Brett W. Doyle and Commissioners Peter-Anthony Pappas, Bart Thanhauser, David Foley Jr., and Samuel T. Negatu did not participate in the adequacy votes, as they were not members of the USITC at the time.
A record of the USITC’s vote to conduct expedited reviews is available on the investigations page for Mattresses from Cambodia, China, Malaysia, Serbia, Thailand, Turkey, and Vietnam; Inv. No. 701-TA-645 and 731-TA-1495 and 1497-1501 (Review).
title: USITC Makes Determinations in Five-Year (Sunset) Reviews Concerning Mattresses from Cambodia, China, Malaysia, Serbia, Thailand, Turkey, and Vietnam

text:
Vindman Joins Local Elected Officials and Advocates in Calling on Regulators to Put Main Street Ahead of Wall Street
Fairfax, Va. — Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) delivered remarks at the Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC) public hearing at the Fairfax County Government Center, urging regulators to reject the proposed NextEra-Dominion merger over concerns about its impact on Virginia families and utility ratepayers.
Vindman joined local elected officials and community advocates in raising the alarm about the proposed merger, which he warned could further drive up electricity costs for Virginians already struggling with rising utility bills.
 
Vindman Joins Advocates & Local Officials in Rallying Against the NextEra-Dominion Merger 
Prior to the hearing, Vindman joined advocates for a rally outside the Fairfax County Government Center, where attendees called for greater accountability and stronger protections for Virginia ratepayers.
“Virginians are already paying too much to keep the lights on, and the last thing hardworking families need is a merger that could send their utility bills even higher,” said Vindman. “The State Corporation Commission has a responsibility to protect the people it serves. That means looking out for Main Street, not Wall Street. I urge the Commission to reject this bad deal for Virginians.”
Vindman was the first member of Virginia’s congressional delegation to publicly oppose the proposed merger. He has continued to raise concerns about rising electricity costs, corporate accountability, and the need to ensure that Virginia families are not forced to shoulder the costs of unchecked data center growth.
Vindman’s remarks, as prepared, are below. Click here to watch a video of his testimony.
—
Good evening. Thank you for holding this public event so you can hear directly from Virginians.
I’m Congressman Eugene Vindman, and I represent about 800 thousand residents in Virginia’s Seventh District.
I’m here tonight for a simple reason: I believe the proposed merger between NextEra and Dominion is a bad deal for Virginians.
I urge the Commission to reject it.
I was the first member of Virginia’s congressional delegation to speak out against this merger.
And I did so in a letter to the Commission, which I hope you all read.
Virginians are already paying too much to keep the lights on. I hear it everywhere I go.
Families are opening their utility bills each month wondering how much more they can possibly be expected to absorb.
This merger gives them every reason to worry that those bills will go even higher.
Here’s the thing about utilities: Virginians don’t get to shop around for their electricity provider.
Where you live determines who keeps your lights on and your home warm in the winter.
That gives utility companies enormous power, and with that power comes a responsibility to the people they serve.
It is not a license to squeeze more money out of hardworking families.
NextEra’s own record should concern us. Customers of its Florida subsidiary have seen their utility bills rise by 33 percent. Now NextEra wants to take control of the utility serving millions of Virginians.
NextEra sees enormous profits to be made in Virginia, particularly with the explosion of data centers.
But I’ve been crystal clear: data centers must pay their fair share.
Virginia families should not be subsidizing corporate expansion through higher electricity bills.
This Commission’s job is to protect Main Street, not Wall Street.
My concerns do not start and end with rates, however. I am very concerned about what this merger would do to the company’s accountability structure.
Dominion is a Virginia company. Its decisions affect Virginia families, Virginia businesses, and Virginia communities every single day.
Under the proposed ownership structure, three-quarters of the new company’s board would be controlled from Florida.
And there are serious questions about NextEra’s conduct in Florida. The company agreed to a $150 million settlement over allegations involving political interference. That sounds like corruption.
That record raises concerns about the influence this company could wield over Virginia’s energy future.
When Virginians have a problem with their power bill, they deserve answers here in Virginia.
I surveyed my constituents about this deal.
More than 950 Virginians responded, and 80 percent opposed the merger.
Their concerns were remarkably consistent, worried about higher bills, less accountability, and even more power concentrated in the hands of a massive utility.
Those concerns deserve to be taken seriously.
This Commission has a responsibility to protect Virginia ratepayers.
Electricity is an essential service, not a luxury. And the privilege of serving millions of Virginians comes with an obligation to put those customers first.
I respectfully urge you to put Virginia families ahead of Wall Street profits and reject this merger.
Thank you.
###
title: Vindman Takes Fight Against NextEra-Dominion Merger Directly to Virginia SCC Hearing

Third-Largest Penalty in Treasury History; Largest in OCC History
WASHINGTON—Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced enforcement actions imposing more than $1.21 billion in penalties against Bank of America (“the Bank”), the second-largest bank in the United States, for violations of anti-money laundering and sanctions laws. These actions include the third-largest penalty in Treasury history and the largest in the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) history.
- The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) assessed a $1.2 billion penalty for the Bank’s failure to mitigate and report priority national security risks, including Chinese Money Laundering Networks and illicit finance along the southwest border.
- The OCC assessed a $750 million civil money penalty for the Bank’s deficient and ineffective BSA/AML (anti-money laundering) compliance program.
- The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced an $11.6 million settlement agreement with the Bank over apparent violations of numerous sanctions programs, including on Iran, Russia, narcotics, and global terrorism.
“Financial institutions are on the front lines of protecting our economic and national security,” said Secretary Scott Bessent. “When a bank of this size fails to meet its anti-money laundering and sanctions obligations, the consequences extend far beyond its own walls, exposing the entire U.S. financial system to significant illicit finance risks. Today’s actions send a clear message that even the biggest financial institutions are not above the law.”
Together, these actions underscore the importance of effectively complying with U.S. AML/CFT and sanctions requirements. Given the converging nature of AML/CFT and sanctions-related risks, financial institutions should ensure their AML and sanctions compliance efforts are effectively integrated and mutually reinforcing.
FAILURE TO REPORT OVER $5 BILLION IN SUSPICIOUS ACTIVITY TO FINCEN
As part of its resolution with FinCEN, Bank of America admits that it willfully violated the BSA and failed to (1) implement and maintain an AML program that met the minimum requirements of the BSA and FinCEN’s implementing regulations, (2) conduct due diligence for correspondent accounts for foreign financial institutions, and (3) file suspicious activity reports (SARs).
The central failures identified through FinCEN’s investigation involved deficiencies related to Bank of America’s suspicious transaction identification and reporting and customer due diligence (CDD) processes. As these issues arose, Bank of America prioritized its revenues and minimized the impact on its required compliance resources. The nature and extent of the Bank’s resulting reliance on law enforcement inquiries, requests by other financial institutions, and similar interventions over its own internal, automated controls to identify potentially suspicious activity meant that the Bank effectively outsourced to third parties a substantial portion of its proactive detection and reporting obligations. The Bank also allowed suspicious activity to accumulate uninvestigated for extended periods without investigation, resulting in late reporting of limited utility to law enforcement.
Bank of America maintained this approach and failed to take meaningful action even in the face of testing that highlighted significant problems. Similarly, the Bank’s CDD processes failed to account for customers’ extensive reliance on payments from unknown third parties. The Bank failed to timely and meaningfully respond to mounting red flags involving these customers—including potential ties to narcotics trafficking proceeds—even after compliance personnel escalated concerns related to possible trade-based money laundering and fraud.
As a result of these failures, Bank of America failed to timely report to FinCEN over $5 billion dollars in suspicious transactions, with over $1 billion of this activity implicating national security-related and other priority illicit finance risks, including suspicious transactions indicative of Chinese Money Laundering Networks, fraud, and potential trade-based money laundering with a substantial nexus to the southwest border.
The Consent Order published today requires Bank of America to work with a third party to complete a lookback to identify and report to FinCEN suspicious transactions that went undetected due to the failures noted above. Bank of America also must undergo an independent review of the effectiveness of its suspicious activity monitoring, CDD, and foreign correspondent account due diligence programs, as well as its data governance framework as it pertains to information used in its AML program. The independent reviews are tailored to the violations and will evaluate the effectiveness of Bank of America’s AML program in addressing priority risks, including (1) the U.S. Southwest border, cartels, and potential narcotics trafficking; (2) Iran; and (3) Russia.
DEFICIENT AND INEFFECTIVE COMPLIANCE PROGRAM
The OCC’s penalty is in response to Bank of America’s violations of the Bank Secrecy Act and its implementing regulations, including 12 CFR 21.21 and 12 CFR 21.11. The Bank is also subject to a December 2024 cease-and-desist order (2024 Order), which required the bank to address its deficient BSA/AML compliance program.
The Bank’s BSA/AML compliance program is deficient and ineffective. Its transaction monitoring system resulted in the Bank failing to properly monitor trillions of dollars in transactions. This caused large numbers of late SARs involving billions of dollars. Many of the late SARs had indicia of money laundering. The Bank knew for years that it was failing to escalate potentially suspicious activity to investigators for review to determine if a SAR should be filed but failed to correct this serious BSA violation.
In addition, the Bank’s BSA Officer and staff lacked sufficient skills and expertise to effectively manage its BSA/AML program. Key BSA personnel did not receive appropriate training regarding suspicious activity identification, investigation, and reporting, which resulted in inaccurate and late SARs. The BSA audit function failed to identify longstanding BSA concerns that examiners subsequently uncovered.
After agreeing to the 2024 Order, the Bank still failed to prioritize BSA/AML compliance. The Bank did not complete many of the significant steps needed to establish an effective BSA/AML compliance program and its program continues to have significant breakdowns. For example, more than a year after the 2024 Order, the Bank still failed to escalate potentially suspicious activities to investigators for review. Additionally, the Bank processed potential trade-based money laundering transactions due to a systemic gap in its transaction monitoring program. Bank management failed to ensure the Bank had an effective BSA/AML compliance program and continued to minimize the program’s significant deficiencies.
APPARENT SANCTIONS VIOLATIONS ACROSS MULTIPLE PROGRAMS
The Bank has agreed to settle with OFAC its potential civil liability for 475 apparent violations of multiple sanctions programs. These apparent violations occurred when Bank of America channeled correspondent banking payments through blocked banks due to technical and human error, allowed designated individuals to make payments and withdraw funds due to poor sanctions alert calibration, failed to promptly update watchlists following OFAC designations, and mishandled business accounts associated with blocked persons due to human error. As a result of these compliance failures, Bank of America processed millions of dollars in payments in apparent violation of sanctions programs targeting Russia, Belarus, Iran, Burma, Somalia, narcotics, and global terrorism.
The settlement amount of $11.6 million reflects OFAC’s determination that Bank of America’s apparent violations were non-egregious and largely not voluntarily self-disclosed. This settlement amount also reflects no reduction to the base penalty, including no mitigation for remedial measures or cooperation. As part of the settlement, Bank of America has made significant compliance commitments regarding training, testing and audit, and future communication and cooperation with OFAC.
COMPLIANCE CONSIDERATIONS
Effective AML/CFT programs protect U.S. national security by preventing financial institutions from being used to facilitate money laundering and terrorist financing. Such programs must be risk-based and commensurate with an institution’s size, risk profile, and products and services. In this matter, Bank of America failed to reasonably design its proprietary transaction monitoring system to address its risks and failed to make meaningful improvements despite testing that revealed significant deficiencies in identifying and timely reporting suspicious activity. Financial institutions cannot disregard mounting red flags or internal warnings about ineffective controls, whether under the guise of innovation or otherwise. Nor can they rely on law enforcement inquiries, referrals from other financial institutions, or other external sources as substitutes for their own effective internal monitoring and controls. Bank of America’s transaction monitoring failures resulted in material dependence on external referrals to identify potentially suspicious activity, rather than the Bank’s own controls to identify and investigate such activity.
Meaningful, risk-based customer due diligence is critical to meeting AML/CFT obligations. Financial institutions must maintain and update customer risk profiles throughout the customer relationship to reflect relevant information, including customer activity, products and services, and geographic exposure. When new information indicates heightened risks or raises AML/CFT concerns, financial institutions must take timely, meaningful action commensurate with those risks. Merely documenting concerns or engaging in prolonged internal reviews without appropriate corrective action does not satisfy an institution’s compliance obligations.
TREASURY WHISTLEBLOWER INCENTIVE PROGRAM
Through FinCEN, Treasury maintains a whistleblower incentive program for violations of the BSA and certain national security laws such as the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. Individuals located in the United States or abroad who provide information may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000 and the statutory requirements in 31 U.S.C. 5323 are otherwise met. FinCEN is currently accepting whistleblower tips. More information about the whistleblower program can be found here.
###
title: U.S. Treasury Announces Record Enforcement Actions Against Bank of America

CINCINNATI – A Cincinnati man who committed three armed robberies of Marathon gas stations in just a few weeks in February 2024 was sentenced in federal court here today to 431 months in prison.

During all three robberies, James Lockridge, 43, of Cincinnati, entered the store and fired the same 9mm gun into the ceiling.

“Lockridge endangered lives and caused panic and terror in employees and customers during three separate robberies. The evidence at trial and his own criminal history show that he is a violent offender who has no respect for the law,” said U.S. Attorney Dominick S. Gerace II. “The excellent work of the investigators and prosecutors in this case stopped Lockridge before he successfully shot or seriously injured someone else. The public is safer now that he has been sentenced to a lengthy term in federal prison.”

Following a weeklong trial in June, Lockridge was found guilty of seven federal robbery and firearms charges.

According to court documents and trial testimony, on Feb. 5, Feb. 10 and Feb. 21, 2024, Lockridge robbed a Cincinnati Marathon gas station. The first and third armed robberies occurred on Gilbert Avenue and the second robbery took place on Montgomery Road.

At each of the robberies, Lockridge was masked and brandished the same silver firearm. He fired his weapon and pointed it at store clerks. Lockridge not only pointed his gun at employees, but he also pointed his gun and used force against customers who were in his way during the second and third robberies. He also wore the same boots during each robbery and fled on foot towards a nearby apartment complex after the first and third robberies.

Lockridge was arrested 11 minutes after the third robbery. Officers discovered the firearm in his waistband.

After his arrest, officers located the boots, gloves and other clothing items used during the robberies, as well as a cash register, in and around the space where Lockridge had been residing.

As a previously convicted felon, Lockridge is prohibited from possessing firearms. His criminal history includes a previous armed robbery in 2014 in which Lockridge entered a victim’s car and pointed a gun at the victim before stealing the victim’s belongings. Lockridge was on parole for that armed robbery when he committed the three armed robberies in this case.

The defendant’s history also involves breaking and entering, burglary, theft, criminal trespass, threatening others with guns and drug possession. Police had encountered Lockridge several times in the past on assault and domestic violence calls.

Dominick S. Gerace II, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Ohio; Jorge Rosendo, Special Agent in Charge, U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives (ATF); and Cincinnati Police Interim Chief Adam Hennie announced the sentence imposed today by U.S. District Judge Douglas R. Cole. Assistant United States Attorneys Ashley N. Brucato and Danielle E. Margeaux are representing the United States in this case.

# # #
title: Cincinnati previously convicted felon sentenced to nearly 36 years in prison for 3 armed robberies

Hoyer Statement on Federal Raid on Congresswoman Omar's Home
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) released the following statement after federal agents raided the Washington, D.C. residence of Congresswoman Ilhan Omar (MN-05):
“I am deeply concerned that Rep. Ilhan Omar, an elected Member of Congress, had her home raided by federal immigration authorities after President Trump repeatedly attacked her legitimacy as an American and threatened to take action in response to her repeated opposition to his policies. It is essential that the levers of justice are never politicized. We are a nation of laws, not individuals. If law enforcement has probable cause to conduct a search or pursue charges against a sitting Member of Congress, officials ought to do so with the highest level of transparency and the utmost professionalism. Just as federal officials should always exercise sound judgment, care for individual rights, and respect for our Constitution in any encounter, no matter what directives they receive from political appointees. I will continue to monitor this situation closely and will be keeping Rep. Omar and her family in my thoughts.”
title: Hoyer Statement on Federal Raid on Congresswoman Omar's Home

The United States Space Force is launching Guardian Spark, a new annual outreach program that connects Guardians with students in grades 3 to 12 to share the mission, people and opportunities behind the nation’s newest military service.
“Bringing Guardians into classrooms across the country is a meaningful opportunity to engage with students and communities,” said Chief Master Sgt. of the Space Force John Bentivegna. “Through Guardian Spark, Guardians can share their experiences, demonstrate how space affects everyday life, and inspire young Americans to join the next generation of space leaders, innovators and problem-solvers.”
The inaugural Guardian Spark campaign will run from Nov. 9 through Dec. 20, 2026, culminating with the Space Force’s birthday. Guardians can volunteer to support through Oct. 16, 2026.
The program is designed to reach classrooms nationwide, including Department of War Education Activity school locations overseas. For 2026, the Space Force aims to engage at least 250 classrooms, reach 7,500 students and mobilize 200 volunteer Guardians. The program will also seek educator feedback and use optional student polls to assess awareness of Space Force roles.
Guardian Spark supports educators and students by creating direct connections with space professionals. Sessions will be tailored to elementary, middle and high school audiences, with Guardians sharing their experiences and answering students’ questions about space operations, technology and service.
The Guardian Spark program is coordinated by the Secretary of the Air Force Public Affairs Outreach Office. Participating Guardians will receive standardized talking points and complete required outreach training before engaging with schools. Educators and schools will coordinate classroom logistics and student participation with the program office.
title: Space Force launches Guardian Spark outreach program to inspire students nationwide

SCHNEIDER BLASTS TRUMP DECISION TO LIFT SANCTIONS ON RUSSIAN DIESEL
LINCOLNSHIRE, IL – Today, Congressman Brad Schneider (IL-10), a member of the House Ways and Means Trade Subcommittee and the House Foreign Affairs Committee, released a statement opposing President Trump’s decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel in a bid to lower diesel prices in the U.S. as prices shoot up to over $6 a gallon.  
“Nearly five years since the start of Russia’s unprovoked, illegal war against Ukraine, President Trump inexplicably continues to side with Putin and his anti-democracy agenda,” said Schneider. “Meanwhile, as American soldiers are fighting and dying in Trump’s ill-conceived war with Iran, and American families are paying the price at the pump, Russia is helping Iran target U.S. forces. President Trump is finding new ways to help Putin and worsen the state of the war in both Ukraine and the Middle East. For the more than 20 months he has been in office, Trump has had the power to impose sanctions on Russia and bring an end this war. He has chosen to do neither. Now, by lifting sanctions and allowing the United States to buy Russian diesel, the President is filling Putin’s coffers while doing little to lower diesel prices here. I will work with my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to block Trump’s purchases of Russian oil and stand with Ukraine in its fight for independence, sovereignty, and the West’s security.”

Coast Guard suspends search for missing kayaker near San Diego
U.S. Coast Guard Southwest District Public Affairs: (206) 815-6689
SAN DIEGO — The Coast Guard suspended its search for a missing kayaker near Torrey Pines Gliderport in La Jolla, California, at approximately 6:20 p.m., Tuesday.
At 6:00 a.m., watchstanders at Coast Guard Sector San Diego received notification that 27-year-old Samantha Youngs was missing, along with her kayak. 
Her family reported her missing after Youngs’ car was found at the Torrey Pines Gliderport cliffside parking lot. 
“After exhausting all reasonable search efforts, we have made the difficult decision to suspend active search operations,” said Cmdr. Celina Ladyga, acting commanding officer, Sector San Diego. “Our thoughts remain with the missing individual’s family and loved ones during this incredibly difficult time.”
Coast Guard crews from Station San Diego, Air Station Ventura and Coast Guard Cutter Haddock searched the waters near Torrey Pines Natural Reserve and La Jolla shores, for a total of 484 square miles and more than 11 combined hours. Members of the San Diego Lifeguard Service and the San Diego Police Department also assisted in the search.
—USCG—
title: Coast Guard suspends search for missing kayaker near San Diego

Cape Cod Man Pleads Guilty to Conspiring to Launder Proceeds of $6M Medicare Fraud Scheme
A Cape Cod man pleaded guilty today to a money laundering conspiracy for laundering proceeds in connection with a more than $6 million health care fraud scheme.
According to court documents and statements made in court, Leo Anzivino Jr., 35, of Falmouth, Massachusetts, conspired with others to launder health care fraud proceeds. Specifically, Anzivino agreed to be the straw or nominee owner of Advanced Medical Supply Corp. (Advanced), located in Rochester, New Hampshire, even though his co-conspirators were in fact the beneficial owners and managers of Advanced. Advanced submitted more than $6 million in claims to Medicare for durable medical equipment (DME) — such as knee braces and back braces — that Medicare beneficiaries did not need and that doctors did not prescribe. Instead, Advanced supported these claims using fake orders from physicians who did not actually write or submit those orders. Medicare paid more than $3 million as a result of these false and fraudulent claims.
Medicare beneficiaries returned boxes of DME to Advanced with notes stating that they had not ordered the products and alleging a fraud or scam, as depicted below.
Note from Medicare Beneficiary Accompanying DME Return Stating that the Beneficiary “Did Not Order” the Medical Products and that it was a “FRAUD!!” Note from Medicare Beneficiary Accompanying DME Return Stating that the Medical Products Were Sent “Without Prior Consent of My Physician or Myself” Note from Medicare Beneficiary Accompanying DME Return Stating that “This Must Be Some Type of Medicare Scam”
Anzivino helped hide his co-conspirator’s involvement with Advanced by being listed as the owner of Advanced on the Medicare enrollment paperwork. He also submitted false and fraudulent bank account opening documents to a bank in New Hampshire, falsely certifying that he was the sole owner of 25 percent or more of the equity interests of Advanced when others, including a co-conspirator, were Advanced’s true owners.
Anzivino then laundered the fraud proceeds by, at his co-conspirator’s direction, seeking to transfer more than $1 million from the Advanced bank account in New Hampshire to companies that were affiliated with the co-conspirator. When told by a bank employee that the bank had not reached a level of confidence that the other companies were legitimate, and that Anzivino should do his own research into these companies, Anzivino instead opened a bank account at another bank with branches in Massachusetts.
In addition, Anzivino learned that Advanced’s ability to bill Medicare would be revoked for various deficiencies, including an inability to verify proof of his ownership of Advanced. Anzivino then sent messages to another individual discussing that revocation, explaining that “All the ppl who gave me money are going to come back for it now my shits revoked,” stating that his co-conspirator “still wants me to wire him money,” and claiming that “I ain’t wiring shit.” Despite this, over the next five weeks, Anzivino proceeded to wire $1,494,938.09 across three separate transactions, each in excess of $10,000.
In 2024, the government seized approximately $353,768.29 in assets tied to the alleged scheme from Advanced’s bank account.
Anzivino pleaded guilty to one count of money laundering conspiracy. He is scheduled to be sentenced Jan. 21, 2027 and faces a maximum penalty of 10 years in years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division; U.S. Attorney Erin Creegan for the District of New Hampshire; Special Agent in Charge Roberto Coviello of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of the Inspector General (HHS-OIG); and Special Agent in Charge Ted E. Docks of the FBI Boston Field Office made the announcement.
HHS-OIG and FBI investigated the case with valuable assistance from IRS-Criminal Investigation and the Department of War Office of Inspector General’s Defense Criminal Investigative Services.
Trial Attorneys John Howard and Tiffany Wynn of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Health Care Fraud Section and Assistant U.S. Attorneys Matthew Hunter and Matthew Vicinanzo for the District of New Hampshire are prosecuting the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit.
title: Cape Cod Man Pleads Guilty to Conspiring to Launder Proceeds of $6M Medicare Fraud Scheme

Coast Guard repatriates 6 aliens to Cuba
MIAMI — Coast Guard Cutter Isaac Mayo’s crew repatriated 6 people to Cuba, Tuesday, following a maritime migrant interdiction and a disabled boat rescue on the Florida Straits.
Thursday, Coast Guard Sector Key West watchstanders received notification from a U.S. Customs and Boarder Protection Air and Marine Operations aircrew of a rustic vessel southwest of Cay Sal. A Coast Guard Air Station Miami HC-144 Ocean Sentry aircrew located the vessel, and Coast Guard Cutter Raymond Evans’ crew embarked three Cuban males. One person was later medically evacuated to shore for a higher level of care.
Sunday, a Coast Guard Air Station Miami aircrew located a disabled Cuban fishing vessel with four people aboard approximately 46 miles southeast of Key West. Isaac Mayo’s crew responded and rescued the four people.
“Our crews remain vigilant in protecting our maritime boarders while safeguarding lives at sea,” said Capt. Aaron Ortenzio, the commanding officer of U.S. Coast Guard Air Station Miami. “These cases demonstrate the Coast Guard’s commitment to preventing unlawful maritime entry while responding to mariners in distress.”
Once aboard a Coast Guard cutter, interdicted aliens are processed to determine their identity and are provided food, water, shelter and basic medical attention before disposition.
The Coast Guard, along with its Operation Vigilant Sentry partners, maintains a continual presence with air, land and sea assets in support of Operation Vigilant Sentry. The combined, multilayered approach is designed to protect safety of life at sea while preventing unlawful maritime entry to the United States and its territories.
-USCG-
title: Coast Guard repatriates 6 aliens to Cuba

Spokane, Washington – First Assistant United States Attorney Pete Serrano announced that on October 13, 2026, United States District Court Judge Mary K. Dimke sentenced Cameron Len Gaunt, age 43, to 144 months in federal prison and three years of supervised release for robbing the Cashmere Valley Bank on September 12, 2025.

According to court records, Guant has a long history of violent federal and state offenses. He had recently been released from Bureau of Prisons custody on July 2, 2025, following prior federal bank robbery convictions, and, at the time of the September 12 robbery, he was already in violation of the conditions of his supervised release.

On the day of the robbery, Gaunt entered the Cashmere Valley Bank branch in Wenatchee and presented a note demanding money: “$30K cash. No dye packs. No exploding bags.” The teller initially provided approximately $100 in bait bills, but after Gaunt demanded more and commented to the effect that he was “not going back to prison for such a small amount,” the teller surrendered the remaining cash in the drawer, totaling $2,462. Wenatchee Police Department officers responding to the robbery quickly reviewed surveillance footage and identified Gaunt by his distinctive face and neck tattoos. Four days later, on September 16, 2025, he was inside another local bank and a teller recognized him from the prior robbery and activated the alarm. Officers arrived and arrested Gaunt without incident.

Gaunt’s extensive criminal history spans more than two decades and includes multiple convictions for forgery, burglary, drug offenses, firearm possession, conspiracy to pass counterfeit notes, and six prior bank robberies in the Eastern and Western Districts of Washington. The September 2025 robbery was his seventh federal bank robbery. He committed the offense while on supervised release and after failing to report to a required residential reentry center, following his last bank robbery conviction.

In imposing sentence, the Court emphasized Gaunt’s repeated refusal to comply with court orders, the danger posed by his pattern of bank robberies, and the need for significant deterrence. The Court also ordered three years of supervised release to follow his term of imprisonment.

“Bank robbery is a crime that terrorizes employees, disrupts communities, and endangers the public,” stated Serrano. “Gaunt has repeatedly demonstrated that he will not abide by the law or the conditions of supervision placed upon him. Today’s sentence reflects both the seriousness of his conduct and his long history of violent recidivism. This sentence also reflects the importance of our state partnerships, where, together, we work to remove dangerous offenders from our communities.”

“Even after convictions for seven bank robberies, among a long list of other crimes spanning over two decades, Mr. Gaunt still has not learned his lesson,” said W. Mike Herrington, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI Seattle field office. “We hope this sentence sends a strong message to him, and to other career criminals: the FBI and our partners remain dedicated to combating violent crime in its many forms and to keeping our Washington communities safe.”

“We’re grateful to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for taking the lead in this case and for their strong partnership with our office,” stated Chelan County Prosecutor Robert Sealby. “Their work secured a significant federal sentence that holds the defendant accountable and protects the people of Chelan County.”

This case was investigated by the Wenatchee Police Department and the Federal Bureau of Investigation. It was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Alison L. Gregoire of the Eastern District of Washington. For additional information, please contact the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Washington.

Hagåtña, Guam – SHAWN N. ANDERSON, United States Attorney for the Districts of Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands, announced that defendant Michael Joseph Salas, age 42, from Barrigada, Guam was sentenced in the U.S. District Court of Guam to 120 months imprisonment for Distribution of 50 or More Grams of Methamphetamine Hydrochloride, in violation of 21 U.S.C. § 841(a)(1). The Court also ordered five years of supervised release and a mandatory $100 special assessment fee. In addition, defendants convicted of a federal drug offense may no longer qualify for certain federal benefits.

On February 11, 2025, Salas agreed to sell three ounces of methamphetamine to a confidential informant. Salas had the informant drive him to a location to meet up with his source of supply. After receiving $3,300 from the informant, Salas met with his source and returned with a bag of methamphetamine. Upon returning to his residence, Salas packaged three ounces of the drug for the informant and kept an unknown quantity for himself. Salas previously sold one ounce of methamphetamine to the informant for $1,200. Federal agents executed a search warrant at the residence in March 2025. It resulted in the seizure of 34.22 additional grams of methamphetamine.

Salas has criminal convictions for possession of an unregistered firearm, second degree and third degree theft by receiving stolen property, and second degree promotion of major prison contraband.

“Repeat offenders who traffic drugs are prime targets for federal law enforcement,” stated United States Attorney Anderson. “They will face mandatory minimum sentences in federal court. Those sentences will be served at a Bureau of Prisons facility on the mainland, far from Guam. We will continue to aggressively prosecute those associated with this illicit activity.”

Those sentences will be served at a Bureau of Prisons facility on the mainland, far from Guam. We will continue to aggressively prosecute those associated with this illicit activity.”

Justice Department Announces Coordinated Actions to Combat North Korean Remote IT Worker Schemes Affecting More than 70 U.S. Companies
Today the Department of Justice announced coordinated actions against the Democratic People’s Republic of North Korea (DPRK) government’s schemes to fund its regime through remote information technology (IT) work for U.S. companies. These actions include an indictment, two arrests, searches of multiple known or suspected “laptop farms” in Texas pursuant to “Operation Lonestar Roundup,” and the seizure of approximately 187 computer devices used by DPRK IT workers.
“North Korea’s rogue regime uses its pervasive IT worker schemes to raise revenue for various illicit purposes, including the development of weapons that could ultimately target the United States or its allies,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “These schemes threaten the security of the IT systems and data of the deceived U.S. employers and leave countless victims of identity theft. NSD, along with our law enforcement partners, will use every available tool to track down anyone assisting the DPRK and to protect our national security.”
“Threats posed by nation-states like North Korea are a stark reminder that our adversaries will go to great measures to exploit our nation’s economic strength to further and fuel their own nefarious agendas,” said U.S. Attorney David M. Toepfer for the Northern District of Ohio. “We are thankful to FBI Cleveland for their incredible work and persistence to put a stop to these bad actors. These charges serve as an urgent alert to all U.S. companies to remain vigilant in their hiring practices.”
“This investigation is about far more than fraud,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould for the Northern District of Texas. “It is about a hostile foreign regime infiltrating American companies through stolen identities and covert access points inside our own borders. Every laptop farm we dismantle shuts down a revenue stream that the North Korean government relies on to fund weapons programs that threaten global stability. Operation Lonestar Roundup sends a clear message: we will not allow enemies of the United States to exploit our businesses or compromise our national security.”
“North Korea continues to deploy remote IT workers using stolen identities to infiltrate American companies and generate revenue for the regime and its weapons programs,” said Assistant Director Brett Leatherman of the FBI’s Cyber Division. “Today, the FBI and DOJ announced a series of coordinated actions against this threat, securing charges against 14 individuals, conducting two arrests, seizing nearly 190 devices, and executing operations at more than 40 suspected ‘laptop farms’ across Texas. Close coordination between the private sector and federal law enforcement was central to this operation. To further combat the threat, the FBI has issued a Public Service Announcement with detailed mitigation guidance for U.S. companies.”
Sun Sheng Ming, et al. Indictment and Arrests – Northern District of Ohio
Today, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Ohio announced the arrests of U.S. nationals Michael James Bostelle of Pennsylvania and Juan Cecilio Pena Carrillo of Texas pursuant to a four-count wire fraud, money laundering, and identity theft indictment. The indictment describes a multi-year fraud scheme by Bostelle, Pena, and their co-conspirators to obtain remote IT work with U.S. companies that generated more than $3 million in revenue. The indictment also charges China-based Sun Sheng Ming, Pei Li Guang, Weng Shou Cheng, Han Guo Bin, Wang Jian Jun, Sheng Zhang Kun, Zhang Wei Ping, Zhang Li Ping, Yu Yang, Jin Long for their roles in the scheme. The identities of two additional defendants remain under seal.
According to the indictment, from 2019 to in or around July 2025, DPRK IT workers applied for and obtained remote positions by using stolen or fabricated identity documents, virtual private networks and proxy infrastructure to appear as though they were U.S. persons working from within the United States. They also relied on U.S.-based facilitators who received and hosted multiple laptop computers — issued by victim U.S. companies — at their residences in the United States (“laptop farms”), housed and configured those devices, installed remote-access software and transferred earnings to DPRK‑controlled accounts.
In total, the scheme impacted more than 70 U.S. company employers and generated approximately $3 million in revenue for IT workers. The revenue is believed to have been sent to sanctioned entities controlled by the DPRK. Victim employers included companies in the health care, communications, cyber support, retail, and manufacturing sectors across Ohio, sixteen additional states, and the District of Columbia.
The FBI Cleveland Field Office is investigating the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Duncan T. Brown for the Northern District of Ohio and Trial Attorney Neeraj Gupta of the National Security Division’s National Security Cyber Section are prosecuting the case.
Operation Lonestar Roundup Disrupts Multiple Known or Suspected Laptop Farms in Texas
Between Sept. 21 and Sept. 25, the FBI conducted searches and other law enforcement action at over 40 residences in Texas known to be, or suspected of operating as, laptop farms for DPRK IT workers. Over the course of the entire operation (Operation Lonestar Roundup), the FBI seized approximately 187 laptops and KVM (keyboard, video, mouse) devices that DPRK IT workers and their U.S.-based facilitators used to commit fraud, obtain remote employment, and generate revenue for the North Korean regime’s sanctioned weapons programs. U.S. cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike has identified this group of DPRK IT workers and their helpers as “Famous Chollima.”
Investigators discovered that the DPRK operatives allegedly used a network of fraudulent email accounts to facilitate their criminal activity. The following accounts were among those identified as being used in these schemes:
Employers are encouraged to add these accounts to the list of indicators they use to identify and disrupt DPRK IT worker employment.
Today, the FBI published a public service announcement describing the evolving DPRK IT worker threat, including tips on how to detect the threat. Increasingly, North Korean IT workers are turning to recruiting American facilitators to counter improved private sector detections and law enforcement actions. These workers are hiring facilitators to complete a wider variety of tasks, and in some cases subcontracting entire jobs to third-party foreign nationals. Additionally, CrowdStrike today published a blog post describing its efforts at monitoring customer networks for DPRK IT worker activity and its successful collaboration with the FBI to disrupt this threat.
The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Texas, the FBI’s Dallas Field Office, and the FBI’s Cyber Division coordinated Operation Lonestar Roundup. Valuable assistance was provided by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Ohio.
Today’s announcements represent the Department’s latest actions to combat North Korean IT worker schemes as part of a joint NSD and FBI Cyber and Counterintelligence Divisions effort, the DPRK RevGen: Domestic Enabler Initiative. This effort prioritizes targeting and disrupting the DPRK’s illicit revenue generation schemes and its U.S.-based enablers. The Department previously announced other actions pursuant to the initiative, including in June 2025, November 2025, April 2026, and May 2026.
As described in Public Service Announcements published in May 2024, January 2025, July 2025, and today, North Korean remote IT workers posing as legitimate remote IT workers have committed data extortion and exfiltrated the proprietary and sensitive data from U.S. companies. DPRK IT worker schemes typically involve the use of stolen identities, alias emails, social media, online cross-border payment platforms, and online job site accounts, as well as false websites, proxy computers, and witting and unwitting third parties located in the U.S. and elsewhere. North Korean IT workers leverage these third parties, which include U.S.-based individuals, to gain fraudulent employment and access to U.S. company networks to generate this revenue.
Other public advisories about the threats, red flag indicators, and potential mitigation measures for these schemes include a May 2022 advisory released by the FBI, Department of the Treasury, and Department of State; a July 2023 advisory from the Office of the Director of National Intelligence; and guidance issued in October 2023 by the United States and the Republic of Korea (South Korea). As described the May 2022 advisory, North Korean IT workers have been known individually to earn up to $300,000 annually, generating hundreds of millions of dollars collectively each year, on behalf of designated entities, such as the North Korean Ministry of Defense and others directly involved in the DPRK’s weapons programs.
The U.S. Department of State has offered potential rewards for up to $5 million in support of international efforts to disrupt the DPRK’s illicit financial activities, including for cybercrimes, money laundering, and sanctions evasion.
The details in the above-described court documents are merely allegations. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: Justice Department Announces Coordinated Actions to Combat North Korean Remote IT Worker Schemes Affecting More than 70 U.S. Companies

text:
Seattle – The pastor of a Kirkland, Washington Christian congregation called ‘Passion for Christ,’ was arraigned today in U.S. District Court in Seattle on an indictment for wire fraud and money laundering in connection with a $13 million fraud scheme, announced Acting U.S. Attorney Charles Neil Floyd. Cristian Popescu, 46, of Bothell, Washington, is a citizen of Romania, residing in the United States. Popescu pleaded not guilty and trial is set for December 21, 2026.

“As alleged in the indictment, this defendant created the mirage of a successful, valuable online marketplace and social media site in one,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Neil Floyd. “Popescu lured investors from his church with fake marketing materials, websites, and expensive offices, and then took their money for his own luxuries and day trading, betraying them financially and faithfully.”

“These charges allege that a religious leader abused the trust of his fellow believers to steal millions of dollars for his own personal benefit,” said W. Mike Herrington, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI Seattle field office. “Cristian Popescu defrauded dozens of his own church members through a series of elaborate lies, including promises of a future stock exchange listing and claims that the profits would benefit the community. The FBI and our partners will continue to follow the money to unravel these schemes and hold fraudsters accountable.”

“Financial crime is not victimless and often destroys the lives of its victims,” said Special Agent in Charge Carrie Nordyke, IRS Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI), Seattle Field Office. “Fraudsters use whatever means they can, including abusing their positions of trust, to swindle those who look to them for guidance and protection. IRS-CI refuses to stand idly by while these crimes devastate our communities, and we are proud to work with our partners to investigate and put an end to these schemes.”

According to the indictment, as early as 2015, Popescu claimed to own and operate a Bellevue company called Followone, Inc. Popescu claimed the company had an internet platform that was both an online global marketplace and social network. He claimed users of the platform could buy and sell goods and services, including cars, real estate, health care, food, and travel. In fact, the platform was a web of non-functional screens and Popescu used lies and deception to attract more than 30 investors. Popescu’s lies included: that the company earned millions in revenue; that it was about to be listed on the Nasdaq stock exchange; and that the company had grown the value of shareholder investments.

Popescu used his role as a pastor to recruit investors from his church, telling them that God had chosen them to invest in the company and that doing so would further the church’s mission. Popescu told investors their investments would remain within Followone and that they could withdraw their money at any time.

Popescu was secretive in his communications with the investors, requiring them to sign non-disclosure agreements and use encrypted messaging services. When meeting in person with investors, he required them to turn off their phones and disable ‘smart’ devices such as Amazon’s Alexa service.

Popescu maintained the image of a successful company by issuing his own press releases with false and misleading representations about the success of the company. He falsely claimed to have hired leading software engineers from major companies. He rented expensive office space in Bellevue and claimed to have twenty employees, when there were only three people working there.

Popescu told his victims they could be on the board of Followone Inc. if they reached $1 million invested. He urged victims to raid their retirement accounts, take out personal or home equity loans, and raid their children’s college savings accounts.

Popescu used shell companies to make it appear Followone had business dealings with other companies. In fact, he was just using investor money to pay fake invoices and then used those payments to shell companies he controlled for his own benefit. Popescu lulled his investors by creating a website that claimed their investment had grown substantially in value. At one-point Popescu claimed Followone Inc had a value of $1.4 billion, when he knew it had little or no value.

Ultimately, the company was evicted from the expensive offices with an unpaid rent bill of more than $350,000. When investors wanted their money back Popescu stalled, claiming repayment would interfere with the stock listing. When investors pressed Popescu for more information about Followone or expressed doubts about Popescu’s representations, Popescu invoked his position in the church, became irate, and told the investors they were demonically possessed.

Popescu transferred invested funds directly to his bank account. Then he used those funds for personal use or to fund Popescu’s personal investment account. Popescu transferred over $4.5 million of Followone funds to accounts belonging to himself, his wife, and other family members. Popescu also paid himself over $1 million in Followone wages between 2017 and 2024. He paid his wife some $300,000 though she was not a Followone employee,

Popescu is charged with ten counts of wire fraud in connection with the solicitation and payment of investments. One victim invested nearly $1 million in one wire transfer, others were nearly $600,000 and $500,00. The five money laundering counts detail how Popescu transferred invested funds from the Followone account to his personal bank account for his use.

Over the objections of prosecutors, Popescu was ordered released on electronic monitoring while awaiting trial.

Wire fraud is punishable by up to 20 years in prison and a $250,000 fine. Money laundering is punishable by up to ten years in prison and a $250,000 fine.

The charges contained in the indictment are only allegations. A person is presumed innocent unless and until he or she is proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

The case is being investigated by the FBI and Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI).

The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Seth Wilkinson.
title: Pastor of Kirkland, Washington, church indicted on ten counts of wire fraud and five counts of money laundering in $13 million fraud scheme

Illinois Woman Sentenced to Prison for Fraudulent Scheme Seeking Millions in COVID-19 Tax Credits
An Illinois woman was sentenced on September 25, 2026, to 13 months in prison for conspiring to defraud the United States by making false claims for refunds based on COVID-19 tax credits.
According to court documents and statements made in court, Lakeibia Fannin conspired with others, including Candies Goode-McCoy, from June 2022 through November 2023 to file tax returns seeking fraudulent refunds based on false Employee Retention Credits (“ERC”) and Sick and Family Leave Credits. Fannin and her businesses were not eligible to receive these refundable credits in the amounts claimed. In total, Fannin claimed more than $3.5 million in fraudulent refunds, of which more than $1.4 million were paid. Fannin used the proceeds for her personal benefit, including on vacations, a cruise, jewelry, designer clothes, and a car. In April 2026, Goode-McCoy was sentenced to 54 months in prison for her role in the scheme.
In response to the COVID-19 pandemic and its economic impact, Congress authorized the ERC for small businesses to reduce the employment tax owed to the IRS. Congress also authorized the IRS to give a credit against employment taxes to reimburse businesses for the wages paid to employees who were on sick or family leave and could not work because of COVID-19. This credit was equal to the wages the business paid the employees during the sick or family leave, subject to a maximum amount.
Fannin pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to defraud the government with respect to claims. In addition to the term of imprisonment, U.S. District Judge Andrew P. Gordon ordered Fannin to serve three years of supervised release and to pay $1,455,835.24 in restitution to the United States.
Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the District of Nevada Sigal Chattah made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation and the Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration investigated the case.
Trial Attorney John C. Gerardi of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Richard Anthony Lopez of the District of Nevada prosecuted the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Illinois Woman Sentenced to Prison for Fraudulent Scheme Seeking Millions in COVID-19 Tax Credits

WASHINGTON – U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) CEO Ben Black today spoke at a Heritage Foundation event titled “Investing in America's Future: Economic Statecraft in an Age of Global Competition.” The conversation was moderated by Heritage President Dr. Kevin Roberts.
On DFC’s mandate under the Trump administration:
“In this era of increasing global competition, President Trump has tasked DFC with a critical mandate: DFC investments must deliver for the American people and serve as a powerful tool for strengthening the economic security of both the United States and our allies and partners.”
“DFC will directly challenge our adversaries in the most strategically contested sectors by financing transactions that diplomacy and private markets alone cannot deliver... DFC will prioritize large, capital-intensive projects that are vital to U.S. strategic interests and highly transformative for our partners... And DFC will mobilize private capital through sophisticated financial structures that reduce risk for investors and create enduring American influence in critical sectors and regions.”
On the importance of bringing private capital alongside DFC investments:
“Across all priority sectors, DFC’s financial products are uniquely suited to reducing investment risk and crowding in pools of private capital that dwarf our own balance sheet. It’s what distinguishes DFC’s approach from our adversaries and the ineffective models of the past. Chinese investments often lack independent private sector participation and the price signals and risk discipline that make projects truly commercially viable.”
“State capital acting alone can never build dynamic markets the way that private capital can. Our global partners want to work with us because our model is better... The American free-market system is the engine that drives strength, growth, and goodwill around the world. It’s our greatest export and our greatest advantage.”
On advancing U.S. Super Intelligence dominance:
“America has the best technology in the world and is winning the race for Super Intelligence, but the American SI stack cannot be exported to networks compromised by our adversaries. Last month, we approved an investment with Vodafone in Eastern Europe to modernize their networks and accelerate the replacement of Chinese telecommunications equipment, ensuring that when American companies operate abroad, their intellectual property and the information they transmit remains safe and secure.”
“These telecom deals are challenging for our partners, who face immense pressure and threats of economic retaliation when attempting to diversify ownership of their networks. That is why we are committed to helping others adopt this model, especially in the Western Hemisphere, where China’s Digital Silk Road cannot be allowed to entrench its influence.”
On building energy infrastructure that advances U.S. strategic objectives:
“Under President Trump’s leadership, the U.S. is the world’s largest producer of both oil and natural gas. Across the world, we see significant opportunities to build energy infrastructure that advances U.S. strategic objectives and provides reliable, affordable energy for our allies and partners.”
“In June, DFC’s Board approved $1.5 billion for energy infrastructure across South and Southeast Asia, ensuring U.S. LNG and American equipment help power the growing energy needs of a region long dominated by our adversaries.”
These remarks have been lightly edited for clarity. You can watch the full event on Heritage’s YouTube page here.
###
The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) is the international investment arm of the United States Government and central to U.S. economic statecraft. DFC mobilizes private capital to advance U.S. foreign policy and economic development. Our investments deliver strong returns for American taxpayers, drive meaningful economic development for our allies and partners, and secure supply chains to counter and outcompete our adversaries.
title: DFC CEO Ben Black Discusses How DFC Is Investing in America’s Future
