POUGHKEEPSIE, NY – Today, Congressman Pat Ryan joined local experts and advocates to celebrate the success of his Hudson River Protection Act. After years of relentless advocacy by Congressman Ryan, bipartisan elected officials at the local, state, and federal levels, and community experts and advocates, Ryan’s bill permanently banning harmful, polluting barges from docking in the Hudson is now law.
Ryan first introduced the Hudson River Protection Act in 2023, following attempts to erode protections preventing harmful, polluting barges from using the Hudson River as a parking lot – threatening to contaminate drinking water for more than 100,000 Hudson Valley residents and destroy the environment. He has been fighting for years, alongside the Hudson Valley community – with the invaluable partnership of organizations including Riverkeeper and Scenic Hudson – to advance this legislation.
“If there’s one thing we can all agree on it’s making sure our drinking water is clean and that our Hudson River is safe and protected. For far too long, big corporations have polluted and put at risk our precious River in pursuit of profits. But not anymore. The Hudson is more than a river – it’s the lifeblood and the heartbeat of our community,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “Today we celebrated the years of effort by every single member of our Hudson Valley community. I especially want to thank my partners at Riverkeeper and Scenic Hudson for their tireless work and commitment to protecting the Hudson. Never again will big corporations be able to turn our River into a parking lot for dangerous barges, polluting the drinking water for 100,000 of our neighbors. This victory proves that when the Hudson Valley stands up with one voice to demand change, we can accomplish anything.”
“As the Coast Guard reviews comments and finalizes its rulemaking barring new anchorages along the Hudson River, we look back to celebrate the Hudson River Protection Act as a powerful testament to what we can accomplish when communities come together to defend the river they depend on,” said Riverkeeper Associate Director of Government Affairs Jeremy Cherson. “For nearly a decade, Riverkeeper and thousands of New Yorkers have fought to ensure that the Hudson is protected from the risks posed by new commercial vessel anchorages. This law honors that persistence by safeguarding critical habitat, protecting drinking water for more than 100,000 people, and making clear that the Hudson is not a place for industrial exploitation. We’re grateful to Congressman Pat Ryan, our partners, and the countless Hudson Valley residents who raised their voices and refused to let the river’s future be put at risk.”
“The Hudson 7 is an intermunicipal council representing seven Mid-Hudson municipalities that rely on the Hudson River as a drinking water source. More than 107,000 people in Dutchess and Ulster Counties depend on the river for their drinking water, with five treatment plants drawing directly from the Hudson to serve communities including Rhinebeck, Esopus, Lloyd, Hyde Park, and Poughkeepsie,” said Gary Bassett, Mayor of the Village of Rhinebeck and Chair of the Hudson 7. “The river doesn’t follow municipal boundaries. A spill doesn’t stop at a town line, and a flood doesn’t stop at a county line. Protecting this shared resource requires regional cooperation and strong federal leadership. Today, we thank Congressman Ryan for his sustained leadership in advancing the Hudson River Protection Act.”
“Residents of Ulster County have a deep and abiding appreciation for the Hudson River. County Executive Metzger recognizes and supports the more than 9,000 county residents who draw their drinking water from the Hudson River, and the thousands more who enjoy fishing, boating, picnicking, and hiking along the waterfront. On behalf of the Department of Environment, we express our appreciation to Congressman Ryan and the advocacy groups who worked tirelessly to secure passage of this legislation,” said Andy Bicking, Director of Ulster County’s Department of Environment.
“Without the Hudson River Protection Act, our river was at risk of becoming a busy highway and parking lot for marine vessels carrying crude oil or other dangerous cargo. Scenic Hudson is proud to have partnered with Congressman Ryan to finally put an end to this threat. The Hudson River Protection Act, introduced and championed by the Congressman, will permanently prevent efforts to add new upper Hudson River anchorages, protecting the ecological health of the river and the health of those who rely on it for drinking water and recreation. Scenic Hudson will continue to partner with our friends in the Hudson Valley, Albany, and Washington to vigilantly protect this critical waterway,” said Carli Fraccarolli, Scenic Hudson's Government Relations Manager.
Congressman Ryan’s “Hudson River Protection Act” bans additional barge anchorages in the Hudson, which pollute the drinking water for more than 100,000 Hudson Valley residents and damage the Hudson’s diverse ecosystem.
In 2023, when the Coast Guard issued an Marine Safety Information Bulletin (MSIB) signaling an attempt to erode protections preventing commercial vessels from anchoring in the Hudson River, Ryan immediately raised the alarm, warning of devastating environmental and health impacts for the river ecosystem and broader community.
After a more than two month delay, Michael Emerson, the Director of Marine Transportation Systems, provided a woefully insufficient response that left the door open for dangerous oil barges to line the Hudson.
In October of 2023, Ryan was joined by Riverkeeper, Scenic Hudson and the Hudson 7 in demanding the Coast Guard uphold the anchoring ban. Ryan gave a speech on the House Floor, calling on Hudson Valley families to join the fight and shared a form for those interested to register their opinion. The new MSIB, issued in November 2023 in response to overwhelming community outrage, temporarily paused the Coast Guard’s plan to allow dangerous barges to line the Hudson River but doubled down on their plan to allow unlimited anchoring in the future.
Congressman Ryan’s greatest concern has been that the Hudson River serves as the primary water supply for seven communities in his district, and serves as the backup drinking water supply for our nation’s largest city, New York City. Additionally, more oil barges on the Hudson will increase the risks of a catastrophic spill. This is especially concerning for the more than 100,000 people that draw their drinking water from the Hudson River.
Barges often carry oil, asphalt, and other hazardous materials, which pollute the river with their noisy generators and “stadium” lighting. The Hudson River and its connected waters are also home to more than 200 species of fish and provide spawning and nursery habitat for striped bass, shad, and herring that support fisheries up and down the entire Atlantic coast. The River has seen significant efforts to restore the habitats of endangered fish species which are jeopardized by barge anchors dragging along the River bottom.
President Trump signed the “Hudson River Protection Act” into law as part of the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), wherein Congressman Ryan secured numerous other wins including a pay raise for troops.

Homeland Security Task Force Arrests Alvaro Pulido Vargas to Face Charges in Multibillion-Dollar Venezuelan Money Laundering and Bribery Schemes
Note: A copy of the 2021 indictment can be found here and a copy of the 2019 indictment can be found here.
A Colombian national charged in two separate federal indictments involving the alleged laundering of more than $2 billion in connection with Venezuelan government bribery schemes will make his initial appearance on the afternoon of Tuesday, October 13, in the Southern District of Florida to face federal prosecution.
According to court documents, Alvaro Pulido Vargas, also known as “German Enrique Rubio Salas,” 62, of Colombia, was indicted in 2019 and again in 2021 for his alleged involvement in separate schemes to launder proceeds of bribery and fraud involving Venezuelan government officials of the Nicolás Maduro regime. Prior to these alleged offenses, Pulido Vargas had a prolific history of drug trafficking, including a 1997 conviction in Italy under the alias of German Enrique Rubio Salas.
“Alvaro Pulido Vargas is no longer a fugitive from justice,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Pulido is charged in two separate, significant money laundering schemes, both using the U.S. financial system to hide the profits from his bribery and greed off the backs of the Venezuelan people. The message to anyone who brings their foreign bribery or money laundering schemes inside our borders: the U.S. Justice Department will pursue these schemes and prosecute those who perpetrate them.”
“Alvaro Pulido Vargas was charged years ago with participating in massive money laundering and bribery schemes tied to the Maduro regime,” said U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida. “The allegations describe a profound betrayal of the Venezuelan people; corrupting government programs intended to provide critical food, medicine, and housing for personal enrichment. Today, because of the persistence and coordination of our federal law enforcement and international partners, Pulido Vargas is in the Southern District of Florida to face those charges. Those accused of exploiting the American financial system should understand that distance, borders, and time will not shield them from the reach of the American legal system. We will continue working with our partners at home and abroad to bring defendants before an American court to answer for the charges against them.”
“Alvaro Pulido Vargas is accused of moving vast amounts of illicit money through a corrupt network that exploited the Venezuelan people and abused the U.S. financial system,” said said Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Administrator Terrance Cole. “For years, DEA and our HSTF partners have pursued Pulido Vargas across borders. Today, that pursuit has brought him to the Southern District of Florida. Those who finance criminal networks and believe money, influence, or international borders will shield them from U.S. justice are mistaken. DEA will relentlessly pursue the people and financial networks that fuel corruption, money laundering, and transnational crime threatening the United States and our partners.”
“Today’s arrest demonstrates that HSI and our Homeland Security Task Force partners will relentlessly pursue the illicit financial networks that enable corruption, transnational criminal activity, and the exploitation of vulnerable populations,” said Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Acting Executive Associate Director John A. Condon. “Working with our domestic and international law enforcement partners, HSI will continue to follow the money, disrupt complex money-laundering schemes, and hold accountable those who allegedly use the U.S. financial system to conceal criminal proceeds.”
The 2021 Indictment
In October 2021, a federal grand jury returned an indictment charging Pulido Vargas and four co-defendants with laundering proceeds from an alleged bribery scheme involving approximately $1.6 billion in Venezuelan government contracts to provide food and medicine.
According to the Indictment, from approximately July 2015 through at least 2020, Pulido Vargas and his co-conspirators secured lucrative government contracts through the Comité Local de Abastecimiento y Producción (CLAP)—a Venezuelan government-controlled program intended to provide food and medicine to the Venezuelan people—by paying bribes to Venezuelan officials.
The defendants allegedly inflated the costs of the contracts to fund the bribes and enrich themselves. They also allegedly laundered proceeds through bank accounts in Antigua, the United Arab Emirates, the United States, and elsewhere.
As a result of the scheme, Pulido Vargas and his co-conspirators allegedly received approximately $1.6 billion from the Venezuelan government and transferred approximately $180 million through or to the United States, including bank accounts in the Southern District of Florida.
Pulido Vargas is charged with conspiracy to commit money laundering and four counts of money laundering, each carrying a maximum penalty of 20 years in federal prison.
The 2019 Indictment
In a separate case, Pulido Vargas and Alex Nain Saab Moran — a Maduro regime ally — were indicted in July 2019 for allegedly laundering approximately $350 million in connection with a bribery scheme involving Venezuela’s government-controlled currency exchange system.
According to the Indictment, from approximately November 2011 and through at least September 2015, Pulido Vargas and Saab Moran conspired with others to launder proceeds of an illegal bribery scheme through bank accounts in the United States.
Pulido Vargas and Saab Moran allegedly obtained a contract with the Venezuelan government to construct low-income housing units. They subsequently exploited Venezuela’s government-controlled exchange rate by submitting false and fraudulent import documents for goods and materials that were never imported into Venezuela and bribing Venezuelan government officials to approve those documents.
To conceal the illicit proceeds, Pulido Vargas and Saab Moran allegedly wired money related to the scheme to bank accounts in the Southern District of Florida and transferred approximately $350 million out of Venezuela through the United States and into overseas accounts they owned or controlled.
Pulido Vargas is charged with conspiracy to commit money laundering and seven counts of money laundering in connection with this scheme.
The DEA Miami Field Division, FBI Miami, and HSI Miami are investigating these cases.
Assistant U.S. Attorney Monique Botero for the Southern District of Florida and Deputy Chief Joseph Palazzo of the Criminal Division’s Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section are prosecuting the cases, together with Assistant Chief Katherine Raut of the Criminal Division’s White Collar and Corporate Enforcement Section.
This arrest and prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Miami comprises of agents and officers from the DEA Miami Field Division, FBI Miami, and HSI Miami with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Miami.
An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

Coast Guard rescues man from grounded sailboat near Coronado, Calif.
U.S. Coast Guard Southwest District Phone: 206-815-6689
Update: The video has been edited from the original version.
SAN DIEGO — A Coast Guard Air Station Ventura aircrew rescued a man trapped aboard a grounded sailboat near Coronado, California, Sunday morning.
At 4 a.m., Joint Harbor Operations Center watch standers received a transferred 911 call from the man reporting his vessel was aground and taking on water.
A Coast Guard Station San Diego boatcrew located the vessel but was unable to approach due to shallow water and hazardous conditions.
An MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter aircrew arrived on scene and lowered Petty Officer 2nd Class Mike Antoon, an aviation survival technician, to assist.
Antoon found the man trapped inside the partially submerged cabin and struggling to breathe as waves washed over the vessel. Antoon provided the man with his snorkel before tearing open part of the cabin roof to free him.
The helicopter crew transported the man to Coast Guard Sector San Diego, where he was transferred to awaiting emergency medical services personnel at approximately 7:25 a.m.
“I’m incredibly fortunate enough to be able to do this job,” said Antoon, “This morning was a culmination of everyone working smoothly as a crew, including sector getting us there in time, and a bit of good fortune."
-USCG-
title: Coast Guard rescues man from grounded sailboat near Coronado, Calif.

Today, we honor the heroic life and legacy of Brigadier General Casimir Pulaski—a son of Poland turned American warrior, a father of Independence, and a martyr of Liberty, whose courage breathed life into the Continental Army, advancing the sacred cause of freedom during the Revolutionary War.
Born in Warsaw, Poland, in 1745, Casimir Pulaski proved himself to be a battle-hardened patriot from an early age, courageously fighting to defend the freedom of his countrymen against Russian aggression. Recognizing his extraordinary military skill, fearless spirit, and profound devotion to liberty, Benjamin Franklin recruited him to cross the Atlantic Ocean and join the Continental Army’s righteous fight for Independence.
Without hesitation, Pulaski arrived on our shores in the summer of 1777 and, within weeks, displayed his bravery and tactical expertise at the Battle of Brandywine against the might of the British Empire. When American lines collapsed under a devastating British flanking attack, threatening the fate of our young Republic, Pulaski rose to the call of history and gathered a small band of horsemen to lead a defiant charge against the British, allowing George Washington and his men to escape death and retreat to safety.
In the year following, Pulaski transformed a ragtag cavalry into a unified, disciplined fighting force capable of defeating the mightiest army in the world, earning him the title “Father of the American Cavalry.” In October 1779, he gave his life for the cause of liberty while leading a cavalry charge during the Siege of Savannah—etching his name forever into the heart of America.
Pulaski’s legacy of sacrifice, courage, and strength is a testament to the unyielding fortitude of the Polish people. From overcoming the brutal despotism of Nazi Germany to defeating the devastating tyranny of communism, they have shown the world the unstoppable power of freedom and the unbreakable resolve of the human spirit, so magnificently embodied in the life and legacy of General Casimir Pulaski. As I proudly declared in Warsaw during my first term, the United States is immeasurably enriched by the contributions of Polish Americans, who have defended our freedom and made our Nation greater, stronger, and more prosperous. Bound by our shared love of liberty, the United States and Poland enjoy a steadfast bond and friendship that my Administration is continuing to strengthen.
As we pay tribute to a remarkable warrior who gave his life for our young Republic, we remember General Pulaski for his battlefield brilliance and the unwavering devotion to freedom that burned within him until his very last breath. Inspired by his bravery and patriotism, may we continue to cherish, defend, and carry forward the sacred flame of liberty that he and generations of Americans shed their blood to preserve.
title: Presidential Message on General Pulaski Memorial Day

Washington, DC -- Representative Gregory W. Meeks, Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, called on the Department of State Office of the Inspector General (OIG) to launch an immediate investigation into U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle’s reported dealings with a foreign company and a political donor. In a separate letter, Meeks requested that Guilfoyle appear before committee Members to answer questions under oath.
The investigation request follows Wall Street Journal reports that Guilfoyle gave a foreign company’s lobbyist access to official meetings, promoted the company’s commercial interests, and accepted company-sponsored private air travel. The Journal also reported that, while her nomination was pending, Guilfoyle requested $100,000 from political donor Eric Deters to cover personal debt while seeking intervention by senior Trump administration officials in his tax and legal matters.   
“The reported messages between Ambassador Guilfoyle and Mr. Deters demonstrate that the Ambassador sought to conceal the source of the payment by arranging an anonymous wire transfer and that she repeatedly admonished Mr. Deters not to put any details of their financial arrangement in writing,” said Ranking Member Meeks. “While Mr. Deters claims he ultimately did not transfer the requested $100,000, it must be determined whether Ambassador Guilfoyle solicited funds from any other source.” 
Meeks asked OIG to investigate potential violations of federal law, Department regulations, and ethics requirements, including conflicts of interest and abuse of authority.
“Together, these reports paint a disturbing picture of an ambassador using her official position and access to senior political appointees to advance the private interests of those willing to pay,” said Ranking Member Meeks. 
These letters follow Ranking Member Meeks' October 1 request for answers from Secretary of State Marco Rubio about Amb. Guilfoyle’s reported conduct. Ranking Member Meeks has called for her removal should these allegations be substantiated. 
View the letter to State OIG here and the letter to Amb. Guilfoyle here.

The Council of Economic Advisers (CEA) evaluated President Trump’s impact on the manufacturing sector— reviewing his second term to date. Reviewing a wide range of evidence, the data demonstrates that the manufacturing sector is seeing robust growth with the Trump Administration’s pro-growth policies.
Manufacturing jobs are reshoring in America after the Biden Administration shipped over 200,000 American jobs overseas in its last two years, factory construction is soaring as President Trump’s tariff policies incentivized companies to make their products here in the USA.
Made-in-America manufacturing positions the United States at the forefront of critical industries for our national security, including aerospace, aircraft equipment, natural gas and petroleum production, and metals. Now the world’s largest energy exporter, the United States continues to strengthen its leadership across the energy sector, while a new renaissance in American steel production is reinforcing domestic industrial capacity.
The manufacturing resurgence we are witnessing reinforces America’s dominance as a global leader, but also has positive impacts on the labor sector as we see more American jobs, increased wages, and company expansions that stimulate Main Street local economies and communities nationwide.
The CEA analysis outlines how the United States is pioneering the technology frontier, reshoring production, and President Trump’s pro-growth, pro-investment approach is contributing to a new American Golden Age.
title: The State of American Manufacturing

text:
Fact Sheet

Office of the Spokesman

October 10, 2026

The Trump Administration has mobilized an immediate response to the 7.7 magnitude earthquake that struck Panama on October 9. The State Department deployed Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) technical teams to conduct expert structural assessments of damage and potential immediate assistance needs at the request of the Panamanian government. Department of War teams are assisting with the response through the U.S.-Panama Bilateral Security Cooperation Memorandum of Understanding (MOU). Ambassador Kevin Cabrera and the State Department continue to liaise with President José Raúl Mulino and the Panamanian government as they assess the damage.

Disaster Assistance Response Team and Search and Rescue Experts Mobilized

The State Department mobilized a Disaster Assistance Response Team (DART) to coordinate and support the emergency response, including two USAR technical teams, with 20 people total, bringing a range of assessment, search, and rescue expertise. These USAR team members arrived in Panama within 24 hours of the earthquake. The USAR technical teams will conduct aerial and on-the-ground assessments and provide additional technical assistance in coordination with local authorities. The Department also authorized Panama’s Air and Naval Service to use two INL-supported helicopters for earthquake relief.

Humanitarian Assistance

The Department has committed to provide $5 million in assistance to support trusted on the ground implementers conducting relief efforts.

SOUTHCOM Logistical Support

Demonstrating the value of ongoing security cooperation efforts between Panama and the United States, the Department of War is supporting aerial damage assessments in the Azuero peninsula and Cocle, including joint assessments with the DART, Embassy staff, and Panamanian officials. The State Department is coordinating with SOUTHCOM to determine if additional logistical support will be required.

Supporting Americans in Panama

The Trump Administration has no higher priority than the safety and security of Americans. The Department of State is providing consular assistance to U.S. citizens in the affected area and their families. We are not aware of any American casualties at this time. Our Consular Affairs hotline is available 24/7 for affected Americans in need of support at +1-202-501-4444 from abroad and +1-888-407-4747 from the U.S. and Canada. We strongly encourage Americans in the affected areas to monitor local news, follow the emergency instructions provided by local authorities, and enroll in STEP.state.gov to receive important emergency information.

Coast Guard works to restore port operations following Hurricane Isaias
Coast Guard District Heartland - Office (504) 671-2020 / After Hours: (618) 225-9008
Editor's Note: Click here to download high-resolution photos.
MOBILE, Ala. — The Coast Guard is conducting extensive port assessments, verifying
aids to navigation and restoring critical communications infrastructure following
Hurricane Isaias as crews work to safely reopen affected waterways and resume
maritime commerce.
The ports of Gulfport and Pascagoula are back open in port condition normal. The ports
of Mobile, Panama City, and Port St. Joe are in recovery mode with some restrictions.
The ports of Destin and Pensacola remain in port condition Zulu, with vessel traffic
restricted as Coast Guard personnel assess the impacts of the storm and identify
potential hazards to navigation.
The Coast Guard has deployed multiple specialized teams throughout the affected area
to support port recovery operations, including:
- Seven aids to navigation verification teams assessing the condition and reliability
of navigational markers to ensure vessels can safely transit affected waterways.
- Five port assessment teams evaluating waterfront facilities and critical maritime
infrastructure for storm-related damage.
- Five communications teams working to restore communications capabilities in
affected areas, supported by a deployable command center truck and a Rescue
21 Remote Fixed Facility (RFF) to reestablish VHF radio coverage.
Additionally, Coast Guard aircrews are conducting aerial assessments of the affected
region using MH-60 Jayhawk helicopters and HC-144 Ocean Sentry fixed-wing aircraft.
“Our priority is to safely reopen the port and restore the flow of maritime commerce as
quickly as conditions allow,” said Capt. Mike Vega, commanding officer of Coast Guard
Sector Mobile. “Our crews are working across the affected region to assess critical
infrastructure, restore communications and identify hazards to navigation. I also want to
thank the public and our maritime partners for heeding storm warnings and taking the
necessary precautions ahead of Hurricane Isaias. Their preparation and willingness to
put safety first helped reduce risks on the water and allowed our crews to focus on
recovery efforts as soon as conditions permitted.”
The Coast Guard continues to coordinate with federal, state, local and maritime industry
partners to assess port conditions and support the safe restoration of maritime
operations.
Port Condition Zulu and waterway restrictions remain in effect for many ports in the
area. Mariners are reminded to monitor official Coast Guard communications and
applicable Captain of the Port directives for updates on port restrictions and reopening.

At 5:15 p.m., Joint Harbor Operations Center watchstanders received a medevac request from the vessel Pacific Voyager for a 74-year-old woman experiencing stroke-like symptoms.
The MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter aircrew hoisted the passenger at 9:35 p.m., then transported her to Torrance Memorial Medical Center.
“Our crews remain ready to ensure the safety of life at sea,” said Cmdr. Zachary Vojtech, Air Station Ventura’s operations officer. “It’s their timely actions and unparalleled skill that help get people the assistance they need in times of urgency.”

Comisionado Residente y congresistas presentan legislación para fortalecer el financiamiento de Medicare Advantage en Puerto Rico
WASHINGTON, DC — El Comisionado Residente Pablo José Hernández (D-PR) junto a los congresistas Raul Ruiz, M.D. (D-CA), Darren Soto (D-FL) y Gus Bilirakis (R-FL) presentaron el Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act of 2026 (H.R. 10747), legislación bipartita que busca corregir una disparidad histórica en el financiamiento de Medicare Advantage en Puerto Rico, cambiando la fórmula federal para calcular los pagos y aplicando el mismo ajuste por costos geográficos que se utiliza para las Islas Vírgenes estadounidenses.
“Estamos priorizando lo básico: que nuestros adultos mayores tengan acceso a los médicos y servicios de salud que necesitan. Este año logramos un aumento importante en los fondos de Medicare Advantage para Puerto Rico. Ahora queremos dar el próximo paso y corregir de una vez y por todas la disparidad que por años ha afectado a la Isla”, dijo el Comisionado Residente Hernández.
“Como medico de emergencias, sé que cuando la atención está fuera de alcance, los adultos mayores pagan el precio”, dijo el Congresista Raúl Ruiz, M.D. “Los puertorriqueños pagan Medicare en los mismos términos que todos los estadounidenses, y sin embargo, a sus planes Medicare Advantage se les paga cerca de un 40 por ciento menos. Esa brecha ha reducido las redes de proveedores, recortado beneficios y puesto bajo presión a médicos y hospitales. Este proyecto de ley es una solución específica y de sentido común. Agradezco a los representantes Bilirakis y Soto, y a al Comisionado Residente Hernández, por trabajar conmigo para brindar a los adultos mayores la cobertura justa que se han Ganado.”
“Estoy orgulloso de unirme al comisionado residente de Puerto Rico Hernández y a los representantes Bilirakis y Ruiz para presentar la Ley bipartidista de Equidad en Medicare Advantage para Puerto Rico, con el fin de realizar ajustes geográficos a los niveles de referencia de Medicare Advantage en la isla e igualarlos a los de las Islas Vírgenes de los Estados Unidos. Esto nos acerca a lograr la plena paridad entre la isla y el territorio continental. Los puertorriqueños son ciudadanos estadounidenses y merecen el mismo acceso a los beneficios de atención médica que todos los estadounidenses”. dijo el Congresista Darren Soto.
“Los adultos mayores merecen acceso confiable a los servicios de salud de calidad que se han ganado a través de Medicare, sin importar dónde vivan”, expresó el congresista Gus Bilirakis. “Medicare Advantage desempeña un papel importante en la atención médica de los beneficiarios en todo Puerto Rico. Debemos garantizar que el programa reciba un financiamiento justo y sostenible para que nuestros adultos mayores puedan seguir recibiendo atención de sus médicos y contando con los tratamientos y beneficios que necesitan. Me enorgullece unirme a los congresistas Ruiz, Soto y Hernández para presentar el proyecto de ley bipartidista Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act, que busca corregir las desigualdades que han persistido por años, mejorar el acceso a los servicios de salud y brindar mayor estabilidad a los pacientes y a los proveedores de atención médica.”
“Esta legislación representa un paso importante para atender un problema estructural que por años ha afectado los pagos de Medicare Advantage en Puerto Rico. Con aproximadamente el 96% de los beneficiarios de Medicare en la Isla acogidos a Medicare Advantage, la metodología utilizada para establecer las tarifas de referencia para Puerto Rico debe reflejar la realidad del mercado al que sirve. Agradecemos al congresista Ruiz, a los representantes Bilirakis y Soto, y al comisionado residente Pablo José Hernández Rivera por unirse en una solución bipartita que utilizaría a las Islas Vírgenes de Estados Unidos como referencia geográfica comparable y ayudaría a fortalecer el acceso a servicios de salud para cientos de miles de beneficiarios en Puerto Rico. MMAPA respalda firmemente esta iniciativa y espera continuar colaborando con el Congreso y los Centros de Servicios de Medicare y Medicaid (CMS) para promover un programa de Medicare Advantage más estable y sostenible para Puerto Rico”, expresó Solage De Lahongrais, presidenta de la Asociación de Productos de Medicaid y Medicare Advantage de Puerto Rico (MMAPA).
Más de 650,000 puertorriqueños dependen de Medicare Advantage para recibir sus servicios de salud, lo que convierte al programa en una pieza fundamental del sistema de salud de Puerto Rico. Sin embargo, la fórmula federal que determina cuánto dinero reciben los planes médicos se basa, en parte, en los gastos de los pacientes de Medicare tradicional, que representan una pequeña minoría en la Isla. Esto provoca que los pagos se calculen utilizando información que no refleja adecuadamente los costos de ofrecer servicios médicos en Puerto Rico, lo que ha contribuido a una disparidad en el financiamiento del programa durante años.
El Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act busca corregir de manera permanente esta disparidad. A partir de 2027, el proyecto requeriría que Medicare utilice para Puerto Rico el mismo ajuste por costos geográficos que aplica a las Islas Vírgenes estadounidenses al calcular los pagos a los planes Medicare Advantage. Este cambio busca que los fondos federales respondan mejor a los costos de ofrecer servicios de salud en la Isla.
La medida permitiría establecer una fórmula de financiamiento más justa y estable, reducir la dependencia de ajustes administrativos que se revisan año tras año y dar mayor certeza a los pacientes, médicos, hospitales y demás proveedores de salud que dependen del programa.
La legislación se presenta en un momento importante para los beneficiarios de Medicare Advantage en Puerto Rico. A pocos días de comenzar el periodo anual de inscripción abierta de Medicare, cientos de miles de adultos mayores se preparan para evaluar sus opciones de cubierta médica para el próximo año. El proyecto representa un nuevo paso en las gestiones que ha impulsado el comisionado residente Pablo José Hernández desde el Congreso para corregir las desigualdades en el financiamiento del programa.
A principios de este año, cuando los Centros de Servicios de Medicare y Medicaid (CMS, por sus siglas en inglés) propusieron un aumento nacional de apenas 0.09% en los pagos de Medicare Advantage para 2027, el Comisionado Residente encabezó una carta bipartita firmada por 17 congresistas, incluidos Raul Ruiz y Darren Soto, para reclamar un trato más justo para Puerto Rico. Tras estas gestiones y los esfuerzos del sector de salud de la Isla, CMS anunció un aumento de aproximadamente 4% para Puerto Rico, superior al promedio nacional de alrededor de 2.5%.

Hernández, Ruiz, Soto, and Bilirakis Introduce Bill to Strengthen Medicare Advantage Funding in Puerto Rico
WASHINGTON, DC — Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández (D-PR), alongside Representatives Raul Ruiz, M.D. (D-CA), Darren Soto (D-FL), and Gus Bilirakis (R-FL), introduced the Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act of 2026 (H.R. 10747), bipartisan legislation that would fix a longstanding Medicare Advantage funding disparity by changing how Washington calculates payments to Puerto Rico, using the same standard applied to the U.S. Virgin Islands.
“We are prioritizing the basics: ensuring that our seniors have access to the doctors and healthcare services they need. This year, we secured a significant increase in Medicare Advantage funding for Puerto Rico. Now, we are taking the next step to fix a longstanding funding disparity that has affected the Island for years,” said Resident Commissioner Hernández.
"As an emergency physician, I know that when care is out of reach, seniors pay the price," said Congressman Raul Ruiz, M.D. "Puerto Ricans pay into Medicare on the same terms as every American, yet their Medicare Advantage plans are paid about 40 percent less. That gap has shrunk provider networks, cut benefits, and strained doctors and hospitals. This bill is a targeted, common-sense fix. I thank Representatives Bilirakis and Soto and Resident Commissioner Hernández for working with me to give seniors the fair coverage they have earned.”
"Seniors deserve reliable access to the high-quality health care they have earned through Medicare, regardless of where they live," said Congressman Gus Bilirakis. "Medicare Advantage plays an important role in delivering care to beneficiaries across Puerto Rico, and we must ensure the program is funded fairly and sustainably so seniors can continue accessing the doctors, treatments, and benefits they rely upon. I'm proud to join Representatives Ruiz, Soto, and Hernández in introducing the bipartisan Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act to address longstanding disparities, strengthen access to care and provide greater stability for patients and providers.”
“I am proud to join Puerto Rico Resident Commissioner Hernández and Reps. Bilirakis and Ruiz in introducing the bipartisan Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act to make geographic adjustments to Medicare Advantage benchmarks in Puerto Rico to match those of the U.S. Virgin Islands. This takes us closer to achieving full parity between the Island and the mainland. Puerto Ricans are American citizens, and they deserve access to the same healthcare benefits as all Americans.” said Congressman Darren Soto.
“This legislation represents an important step toward addressing a longstanding structural challenge in Medicare Advantage payments in Puerto Rico. With approximately 96% ofMedicare beneficiaries on the Island choosing Medicare Advantage, the methodology used to establish Puerto Rico’s benchmarks must reflect the reality of the market it serves. We thank Congressman Ruiz, Representatives Bilirakis and Soto, and Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández Rivera for coming together on a bipartisan solution that would use the U.S. Virgin Islands as a comparable geographic reference and help strengthen access to care for hundreds of thousands of beneficiaries in Puerto Rico. MMAPA strongly supports this effort and looks forward to continuing to work with Congress and CMS to advance a more stable and sustainable Medicare Advantage program for Puerto Rico”, said Solage De Lahongrais, President of the Medicaid and Medicare Advantage Products Association of Puerto Rico (MMAPA).
More than 650,000 Puerto Ricans rely on Medicare Advantage for their healthcare coverage, making it a cornerstone of the island’s healthcare system. Yet a key part of the federal funding formula relies on healthcare spending among traditional Medicare patients, who represent only a small fraction of beneficiaries in Puerto Rico. As a result, payments are calculated using a limited picture of healthcare costs on the island, contributing to a longstanding funding disparity.
The Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act seeks to permanently address one of the disparities in the federal payment formula. Beginning in 2027, the legislation would require the geographic adjustment used to calculate Medicare Advantage payments in Puerto Rico to match the adjustment applied to the U.S. Virgin Islands.
This change would help establish a fairer, more stable funding structure for Puerto Rico, reduce the need for year-to-year administrative adjustments, and provide greater certainty for the patients, physicians, hospitals, and healthcare providers who depend on the program.
This legislation comes at a critical time for Puerto Rico's patients and healthcare providers. With Medicare's annual open enrollment period just days away, hundreds of thousands of seniors will soon be reviewing their coverage options for the coming year. This legislation marks the next step in the Resident Commissioner’s ongoing efforts in Congress to close this funding gap.
Earlier this year, when the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) proposed a national Medicare Advantage payment increase of just 0.09% for 2027, Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández led a bipartisan letter signed by 17 members of Congress, including Representatives Raul Ruiz and Darren Soto, urging CMS to address the payment disparity affecting Puerto Rico. Following this effort and continued advocacy from Puerto Rico’s healthcare sector, CMS announced an increase of approximately 4% for the island, exceeding the national average of roughly 2.5%.
###
title: Comisionado Residente y congresistas presentan legislación para fortalecer el financiamiento de Medicare Advantage en Puerto Rico

The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) authorized the emergency exchange to alleviate supply disruption due to inclement weather in the Gulf of America
October 10, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced the authorization of an emergency exchange of up to 4 million barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) to address supply disruptions due to inclement weather in the Gulf of America. Under the terms of the exchanges, participating companies will return the borrowed crude oil with additional premium barrels in 2027, helping replenish and strengthen the SPR at no additional cost to taxpayers. 
“With this emergency exchange, the Energy Department is acting swiftly to help maintain refinery operations, limit disruptions to fuel supplies, and ensure American families and businesses continue to have access to affordable, reliable, and secure energy” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. “In addition to helping minimize supply disruptions, these emergency exchanges will also require Exxon and BP to return more barrels to the Reserve than are currently being withdrawn, saving taxpayers millions of dollars. Rest assured, the Trump Administration is committed to strengthening America’s energy security at every opportunity.”
The Department has authorized exchanges of up to 2 million barrels each for ExxonMobil and BP America. ExxonMobil's exchange will accelerate deliveries of previously awarded SPR crude oil to address immediate supply needs. 
DOE will continue working with industry partners to support reliable fuel supplies and respond to hurricane-related disruptions. 
For more information about the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, visit energy.gov.
title: Energy Department Authorizes Strategic Petroleum Reserve Exchange to Address Supply Disruptions Due to Hurricane

Rep. Chu Leads 29 Members of Congress Demanding Answers on Barriers to Release from ICE Detention
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28) led 29 Members of Congress in a letter to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Mullin, Attorney General Blanche, and Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR) Acting Director Owen demanding answers about rising immigration bond denials, increasingly unaffordable bond amounts, and concerns about the independence of immigration judges under the Trump administration.
Immigration bond allows eligible individuals to be released from immigration detention while their cases proceed, subject to certain conditions, including appearing for future court proceedings. But since President Trump took office, bond denials have increased substantially, while individuals granted bond are increasingly being required to pay amounts that many families cannot afford.
According to data cited in the letter, immigration bond requests more than doubled from 34,845 in 2024 to 80,130 in 2025, an increase of approximately 130 percent. Meanwhile, the percentage of bond requests denied by immigration judges rose from approximately 36 percent in 2024 to 43 percent in 2025, reaching 55 percent in the first three months of 2026. The national median bond amount, which stood at $6,000 between January 2024 and November 2025, rose to $7,500 after November 10, 2025, with the average reaching $9,211.
These trends are particularly alarming at the Adelanto ICE Processing Center, which Rep. Chu has fought to close for more than a decade. Since November 2025, immigration judges have denied 57 percent of bond requests from individuals detained at Adelanto, compared to 39 percent during the preceding period. The median bond amount at Adelanto has also climbed to $10,000, well above the national median. In one particularly troubling case, a man who had lived in the United States for 25 years, maintained steady employment, supported a family, and had no criminal record was assigned a $50,000 bond, an amount an amount immigration practitioners say has traditionally been reserved for exceptional cases.
The Members also raised serious concerns about potential interference with immigration judges' ability to make independent bond determinations. Following reports that judges were being required to provide written justifications to supervisors when granting bond, EOIR released heavily redacted records in response to a Freedom of Information Act request, leaving critical questions unanswered about what instructions or guidance immigration judges may have received.
In their letter, the Members wrote:
"Taken together, these developments paint a disturbing picture. The sharp increase in bond denials and bond amounts, coupled with unresolved questions regarding potential directives and supervisory practices governing immigration judges, raises serious concerns about whether immigration judges retain sufficient independence to make individualized bond determinations based on the facts and applicable law."
“Everyone deserves a fair shot at freedom while they fight their case,” said Rep. Chu. “But under this administration, more people are being denied bond, and those who are granted it are facing amounts their families simply cannot afford. Immigration judges must be free to make decisions based on the facts and the law, not political pressure. The Trump administration owes the American people answers about whether immigration judges are being pressured to deny bond rather than make independent decisions based on the facts and the law.
“This sharp increase in bond denials shows yet again how the Trump administration is manipulating the court system to advance its anti-immigration agenda while jeopardizing the independence of judges and due process for families caught in the system,” said Kel White, Associate Director, Public Education & Training at Acacia Center for Justice. “The few people who do receive bonds are told to pay an exorbitant amount and in cash. Not only is this unheard of, especially for people with no criminal record, it is nearly impossible for a parent to do. Courts must rely on facts and the law, not an out of control anti-immigrant agenda, otherwise this is a slap in the face of meaningful due process.”
"The widespread use of bond denials and excessive bonds, regardless of the individual facts of a case, underscores why our immigration courts must be truly independent. Immigration judges should be empowered to independently interpret the law and weigh the facts of each individual case, not be reduced to rubber stamps for the administration’s detention policies. The growing practice of denying bond or imposing exorbitant bonds on people with no criminal history comes at a significant cost to not only the individuals caught in the web of injustice, but there is a cost to American taxpayers. At a time when families are struggling with affordability and rising healthcare costs, taxpayers are being asked to foot the bill for the unnecessary detention of people who have lived in our communities for decades and have no criminal record," said Benjamin Johnson, Executive Director of the American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA).
The letter was signed by Reps. Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Lou Correa (CA-46), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Robert Garcia (CA-42), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Daniel Goldman (NY-10), Jared Huffman (CA-02), Sara Jacobs (CA-51), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Jennifer McClellan (VA-04), Christian Menefee (TX-18), Jerry Nadler (NY-12), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Nancy Pelosi (CA-11), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Juan Vargas (CA-52), James Walkinshaw (VA-11), and Maxine Waters (CA-43).
The letter is endorsed by Advocates for Basic Legal Equality (ABLE), Advocates for Immigrant Rights, AFT, AfghanEvac, African Communities Together (ACT), Al Otro Lado, American Friends Service WASHINGTON— Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent announced today a key senior appointment at the U.S. Department of the Treasury. Dr. Judy Shelton will serve as a Counselor in the Office of the Secretary.
Shelton is an economist and author specializing in international financial and currency issues. She previously served as U.S. Director of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and as Chairman of the National Endowment for Democracy. She has testified numerous times before Congress as an expert witness on international financial relations and has consulted with national security officials on global economic developments.
At Treasury, Shelton will advise the Secretary on currency policy, with a particular focus on evaluating financial conditions in China.
Prior to joining Treasury, Shelton served as a Senior Fellow at the Independent Institute. She also served as a Senior Research Fellow at the Hoover Institution at Stanford University, where she authored The Coming Soviet Crash and Money Meltdown. She holds a Ph.D. in Business Administration from the University of Utah.
Shelton began her professional career as a National Fellow at the Hoover Institution, where she received a postdoctoral fellowship to study the impact of Western capital on the Soviet economy. Throughout her career, she has specialized in analyzing the internal monetary and financial conditions of nations and their impact on exchange rates.

MADISON, WIS. – Chadwick M. Elgersma, United States Attorney for the Western District of Wisconsin, announced that Creighton Mithaugen, 38, Faribault, Minnesota, was sentenced this week by U.S. District Judge William M. Conley to 97 months in federal prison for traveling from Minnesota to Wisconsin to engage in illicit sexual conduct with a minor. The prison term will be followed by a lifetime of supervised release. Mithaugen pleaded guilty to this charge on July 13, 2026.

From April 2024 through February 2026, Mithaugen chatted with what he believed to be a 14 or 15-year-old girl, when in reality he was chatting with an undercover law enforcement agent. On February 13, 2026, Mithaugen was arrested after he drove from his residence in Minnesota to a prearranged meeting spot in Rhinelander, Wisconsin, to meet the purposed minor to engage in sexual activity.

At the sentencing hearing, Judge Conley considered Mithaugen’s history, which included a conviction for sex with a fifteen-year-old girl in 2007 and credible allegations he touched a ten-year-old girl in 2022, and concluded that Mithaugen was a repeat and dangerous sex offender. Judge Conley found that a lengthy sentence was necessary to protect some of the most vulnerable members of society from Mithaugen’s predatory behavior.

The charge against Mithaugen was the result of an investigation conducted by the Oneida County Sheriff’s Office, the Rhinelander Police Department, the Wisconsin Department of Justice Division of Criminal Investigation, and the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension. Assistant U.S. Attorney Julie Pfluger prosecuted this case.

This investigation was a part of Project Safe Childhood (PSC), a nationwide initiative to combat child sexual exploitation and abuse. Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc.
title: Minnesota Man Sentenced to More Than 8 Years for Travelling to Engage in Sex With a Minor

NEW ORLEANS – NICHOLAS JOHN ENGOLIA II, (“ENGOLIA”), age 32, pleaded guilty on October 8, 2026 before U.S. District Judge Carl J. Barbier to attempted transfer of obscene material to a minor, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Section 1470, announced U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle. Sentencing is set for January 28, 2027.

According to the factual basis, beginning on or about January 28, 2026, and culminating on or about March 3, 2026, ENGOLIA , corresponded online and via text message with an individual he believed to be a fifteen-year-old female, and during that correspondence, ENGOLIA , texted explicit photos of himself, and coordinated to meet at a park in Covington, Louisiana to engage in sexual activity.

ENGOLIA faces a maximum term of imprisonment of ten (10) years, up to five (5) years of supervised release, a fine of up to $250,000 and a $100 mandatory special assessment fee. ENGOLIA may also be required to register as a sex offender.

U.S. Attorney Courcelle praised the work of the Federal Bureau of Investigation in investigating this matter. Assistant United States Attorney Mary Anne Flippo of the Public Integrity Unit and Human Trafficking and Child Exploitation Task Force is in charge of the prosecution.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Jacksonville, Florida – A federal jury has found Treashonna P. Graham (42, Lake City) guilty of all charges in a 13-count indictment, including conspiracy to commit wire fraud and multiple counts of wire fraud and money laundering. Graham faces up to 20 years in prison for the conspiracy and each wire fraud offense and up to 10 years’ imprisonment for each money laundering offense. Graham will be sentenced on January 19, 2027. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement.

According to court records, Graham and her conspirator/co-defendant, Joey Williams, created a company called “Grant Bae,” which purportedly assisted minority business owners to obtain government grants. Graham charged a fee for her services and advised clients that the company was in the process of obtaining grant money on their behalf. The evidence at trial proved that Graham never hired companies to help locate or obtain grants nor did she help to write any grant applications for her clients. More than 1,000 individuals were victimized by her fraudulent scheme. In total, Graham stole approximately $2,.9 million and used those funds to live an extravagant lifestyle. Graham used the fraudulent proceeds to purchase vehicles, jewelry, clothing, and other personal property. She also gambled away hundreds of thousands of dollars at local casinos.

Williams previously pleaded guilty for his role in this case and is pending sentencing.

This case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Florida Department of Law Enforcement. It is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney John Cannizzaro.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Jury Convicts Lake City Woman in $2.9 Million Fraud Case

LUBBOCK, Texas — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced that a New Mexico man who was caught with over 300 grams of methamphetamine and a loaded Glock pistol after leading multiple West Texas law enforcement agencies on a lengthy high-speed chase was sentenced to just over 19 years in federal prison on Oct. 8.

Erik Louis Almaguer, 32, was indicted in February and pleaded guilty in May to possession with intent to distribute 50 grams or more of methamphetamine and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime. U.S. District Judge James Wesley Hendrix imposed a 170‑month sentence for the drug offense, followed by a consecutive 60‑month sentence for the firearm offense, for a total of 230 months.

“This defendant put countless motorists and officers at risk in an effort to avoid accountability,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “This sentence reflects both the seriousness of his conduct and the strength of the partnerships that make West Texas safer. Because of the swift coordination among our federal, state and local law enforcement partners, a dangerous trafficker was stopped, and significant quantities of methamphetamine and a loaded firearm were removed from our communities.”

“This defendant put countless motorists and officers at risk in an effort to avoid accountability,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “This sentence reflects both the seriousness of his conduct and the strength of the partnerships that make West Texas safer. Because of the swift coordination among our federal, state and local law enforcement partners, a dangerous trafficker was stopped, and significant quantities of methamphetamine and a loaded firearm were removed from our communities.”

“Drug traffickers who put innocent lives at risk by fleeing from law enforcement demonstrate a reckless disregard for the safety of our communities,” said DEA Dallas Special Agent in Charge Joseph B. Tucker. “This defendant chose to endanger the public rather than face the consequences of his criminal activity. Thanks to the coordinated efforts of our federal, state, and local law enforcement partners, he will now be held accountable for his actions.”

According to court documents, on Oct. 9, 2025, narcotics agents in Lubbock were surveilling Erik Almaguer under suspicion that he was engaged in drug trafficking. A Lubbock Police Department patrol unit attempted to stop his vehicle after he committed a traffic violation, but Almaguer immediately accelerated his vehicle and led officers on a high-speed chase. Almaguer left the Lubbock city limits, traveling towards Brownfield. Multiple law enforcement agencies were called in to assist in stopping Almaguer. The defendant evaded law enforcement all the way from Lubbock to Brownfield, at times traveling over 100 miles per hour.

When Almaguer reached Brownfield, officers successfully flattened two of Almaguer’s tires using spike strips. However, he continued to evade, forcing officers to use their patrol units to disable his vehicle. Almaguer exited his vehicle and attempted to flee on foot but was quickly captured.

Officers located a torn plastic baggie containing suspected methamphetamine near where Almaguer was taken into custody. Officers searched his vehicle and located over 300 grams of suspected methamphetamine and more than 12 grams of suspected fentanyl powder. A loaded Glock 17 pistol with an extended magazine was found between the driver’s seat and center console. Officers also located a baggie of suspected fentanyl pills in Almaguer’s sock.

In plea papers, Almaguer admitted to possessing over 300 grams of methamphetamine with the intent to distribute it to others. He also admitted to possessing a loaded Glock pistol in relation to his drug trafficking.

The Drug Enforcement Administration, Lubbock Police Department, Lubbock County Sheriff’s Office, Hockley County Sheriff’s Office, Terry County Sheriff’s Office, and Brownfield Police Department conducted the investigation. Federal, state, and local law enforcement partners collaborated on this investigation under the Caprock Texas High-Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (HIDTA) initiative. Assistant U.S. Attorney Sean Long from the Lubbock Division prosecuted the case.

###
title: Methamphetamine trafficker who led law enforcement on a high-speed pursuit sentenced to 230 months in federal prison

WASHINGTON – Today, Reps. Nydia M. Velázquez (D-NY) and Adelita Grijalva (D-AZ) introduced a House resolution recognizing World Contraception Day and calling for expanded access to contraception and reproductive health care in the United States and around the world.
 
“Access to contraception is fundamental to giving people the freedom to make decisions about their own bodies, families, and futures,” said Rep. Velázquez. “Yet millions of people still face barriers to getting the care and information they need. On World Contraception Day, we are reaffirming that contraception is essential health care and that everyone deserves affordable, reliable access to it. I am proud to join Congresswoman Grijalva in continuing this fight for reproductive freedom at home and around the world.”
 
“Everyone deserves access to contraception and the freedom to make decisions about their own health and future,” said Rep. Grijalva. “Too many people still face barriers to the care they need, especially in communities that have been underserved for far too long. On World Contraception Day, we’re standing up for affordable, accessible reproductive health care for everyone.”
 
The resolution highlights persistent barriers to contraceptive access in the United States and globally. An estimated 218 million women in economically developing countries have an unmet need for modern contraception. In the United States, one-third of adult women who have attempted to obtain prescription contraception have reported barriers to access, while more than 19 million women of reproductive age who need publicly funded contraception live in areas without reasonable access to a health center offering the full range of contraceptive methods.
 
The resolution also recognizes longstanding racial, ethnic, and socioeconomic disparities in reproductive health care and the barriers faced by communities of color, Native people, immigrants, people with disabilities, LGBTQ+ individuals, and people living in areas with limited access to reproductive health providers.
 
Among other provisions, the resolution calls on Congress and the administration to expand access to free or affordable contraception, ensure access to medically accurate information and comprehensive insurance coverage, address contraceptive deserts and reproductive health disparities, and expand access and coverage for over-the-counter birth control and other forms of contraception.
 
The resolution further recognizes the broader benefits of contraceptive access, including allowing people to plan and space pregnancies and pursue their educational, career, and life goals.
 
###
title: Velázquez, Grijalva Lead Resolution Recognizing World Contraception Day

SPRINGFIELD, Ill. – A Jacksonville, Illinois, man, Daniel Brannan, 48, was sentenced last week to 12 years in prison, to be followed by a 10-year term of supervised release, for distribution, receipt, and possession of child pornography.

At the sentencing hearing on September 29, 2026, the government established that Brannan had engaged in the distribution and trading of multiple videos of child pornography between April and May 2025 on an online chatting application. These videos included prepubescent minors engaged in sex acts with adults.

Also at the hearing, U.S. District Judge Colleen R. Lawless described the number of files possessed, over five thousand images and thirty-four videos; found that Brannan had engaged in trading in child pornography; and stated that images that he possessed included toddlers and infants, as well as bondage and humiliation.

In June 2026, Brannan pleaded guilty to distribution of child pornography, receipt of child pornography, and possession of child pornography. Brannan remains in the custody of the United States Marshals Service where he has been since his arrest in December 2025. The statutory penalties for distribution and receipt of child pornography are not less than five years and up to 20 years’ imprisonment, up to a life term of supervised release, up to a $250,000 fine, and restitution. The statutory penalties for possession of child pornography are not more than 10 years’ imprisonment, five years to a life term of supervised release, and up to a $250,000 fine.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation, Springfield Field Office, and the Illinois Attorney General’s Office investigated the case with assistance from the Jacksonville, Illinois, Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Tanner K. Jacobs represented the government in the prosecution.

The case against Brannan was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative by the Department of Justice to combat the epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. FEMA urges Gulf Coast residents to finish preparing for Hurricane Isaias, which is projected to cause life-threatening storm surge and dangerous winds along the Florida Panhandle and Alabama coasts, according to the National Hurricane Center. As officials in Alabama and Florida issue evacuation orders and begin activating shelters, FEMA is actively positioning critical supplies, personnel and federal resources to quickly support needs on the ground.
At the direction of President Trump and U.S. Department of Homeland Security Secretary Mullin, FEMA is committed to working alongside state, local and tribal partners to protect and help the American people before, during and after the storm. Residents should put their emergency plans into action today and take the following steps now:
- Stay informed: Sign up for local weather alerts and listen to local officials.
- Evacuate if told to do so: Know where you will go, how you will get there and where you can stay if an evacuation becomes necessary.
- Make a communications plan: Know how you will communicate with family and friends after the storm.
As governors, local emergency managers and communities lead preparedness activities ahead of the storm, FEMA is coordinating federal resources, mobilizing staff and surging resources to boost state capabilities and accelerate potential requests for assistance. FEMA headquarters and regional offices remain fully engaged, activating the National Response Coordination Center in Washington, D.C. and FEMA Region 4’s Regional Response Coordination Center in Atlanta.
To facilitate rapid federal support, Incident Management Assistance Teams are deployed to Alabama and Florida to enhance coordination on site, expediting state requests for federal support. Additional FEMA personnel are ready to deploy to bolster state operations and multiple distribution centers across the United States are stocked and ready to provide supplies like food, water and generators.
National Urban Search and Rescue teams are positioned throughout the region ahead of potential impacts to quickly assist with life-saving rescue and evacuation operations, if needed.
For more information on preparing for hurricanes and other severe weather, visit www.ready.gov.
title: FEMA Strategically Positions Personnel and Resources to Support State and Local Officials as Hurricane Isaias Strengthens

SEC Proposes Expanding Securities Eligible for Cross Trading by Registered Funds
Washington D.C., Oct. 9, 2026 —
The Securities and Exchange Commission today proposed amendments to the Investment Company Act “cross-trading rule,” which permits transactions in securities between a registered fund and its affiliates under certain conditions. The proposed amendments would modernize and expand the cross-trading rule and would allow cross trades that are beneficial to registered funds and their shareholders (by, for example, reducing a fund’s trading costs), subject to enhanced investor protection measures.
“Today, the Commission took another step toward modernizing our regulatory frameworks to meet the realities of today’s markets by proposing amendments to Rule 17a-7 under the Investment Company Act of 1940, which permits trades in securities between registered funds and certain affiliates. When executed appropriately, cross trades allow registered funds to avoid costs associated with open market trades and to then pass those savings on to investors. The amendments we are proposing today would modernize and expand the cross-trading rule, helping to deliver additional cost savings to those investors,” said SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins in a statement.
Following the initial adoption of Rule 17a-7 in 1966, registered funds relied on the cross-trading rule to trade both equity and fixed-income securities. However, adoption of the Investment Company Act’s “fund valuation rule” in 2020 effectively restricted cross trading most fixed-income securities, although at the time the Commission recognized that potential revisions to the cross-trading rule were under consideration.
The proposed amendments would restore the ability to cross trade most fixed-income securities and modernize the rule’s conditions, including those related to pricing and oversight of cross trades. These modernizations would, among other things, recognize market developments that have led to pricing that is more verifiable and transparent. The proposal would also require aggregated reporting of trading activity and cross trades by registered funds that engage in cross trading to provide additional transparency.
The proposal will be published on SEC.gov and in the Federal Register. The comment period will remain open for 60 days after publication in the Federal Register.
###
Last Reviewed or Updated: Oct. 9, 2026
title: SEC Proposes Expanding Securities Eligible for Cross Trading by Registered Funds

Coast Guard acquires four long-range unmanned aircraft to strengthen maritime security
WASHINGTON - The U.S. Coast Guard placed a $247.8 million order with General Atomics for four MQ-9B long-range unmanned aircraft systems, ground control stations and supporting equipment Sept. 25, 2026, through a U.S. Customs and Border Protection contract.
The aircraft will give the Coast Guard greater ability to monitor offshore waters, protect borders and critical infrastructure, support search and rescue, combat drug trafficking and counter illegal and unregulated fishing. They will also improve the service’s ability to collect and share intelligence, conduct surveillance and support reconnaissance missions far at sea.
“The MQ-9B long-range unmanned aircraft systems will expand our reach and strengthen our ability to protect the nation,” said Anthony Antognoli, the assistant commandant and program executive officer for robotics and autonomous systems. “This investment will give Coast Guard crews a longer-range view of our maritime domain, helping them detect threats earlier, make better-informed decisions and act faster across our missions.”
Long-range unmanned aircraft are vital to Coast Guard missions. In fiscal year 2026, U.S. Customs and Border Protection MQ-9A aircraft operating as part of Joint Interagency Task Force South directly contributed to the seizure of approximately 60,700 pounds of illegal drugs valued at $306 million and the apprehension of around 20 smugglers.
The MQ-9B acquisition is funded by the historic investment in the Coast Guard through fiscal year 2025 budget reconciliation and fiscal year 2026 appropriations. Fiscal year 2025 budget reconciliation provided nearly $25 billion, the largest capital investment in the service’s history, through which the Coast Guard ordered approximately $16.3 billion in new assets and capabilities. This rapid return on investment demonstrates the Coast Guard’s commitment to modernizing acquisitions, integrating next-generation technology, restoring readiness and revitalizing infrastructure to deliver national mission outcomes.
For media inquiries, contact mediarelations@uscg.mil
###
About the U.S. Coast Guard
With more than 95,000 miles of shoreline, 25,000 miles of navigable rivers and 4.5 million square miles of U.S. exclusive economic zone, the U.S. Coast Guard defends the Nation, protects the marine transportation system, regulates and safeguards ports and waterways, leads the Nation in maritime drug interdiction and secures the maritime border. As a member of the joint force, a law enforcement organization, a regulatory agency and a member of the U.S. intelligence community, the Coast Guard employs a unique mix of authorities to ensure the safety and integrity of the maritime domain to protect the economic and national security of the nation. More than 76,000 members of the Coast Guard operate a multi-mission, interoperable fleet of more than 220 cutters, 185 fixed and rotary-wing aircraft, 1,300 boats and its own dedicated cyber command to protect critical maritime infrastructure.
More information about the U.S. Coast Guard can be found at www.uscg.mil Follow @USCG on X and Instagram, like us on Facebook, subscribe on YouTube and follow LinkedIn—connect with us.
Make a difference on land, at sea or in the air with the Coast Guard. Visit GoCoastGuard.com to find out how to be part of our team.

Louisville, KY – An indictment was returned by a grand jury in Louisville, Kentucky, on October 7, 2026, charging a Canadian Citizen living in Louisville, Kentucky, with illegal voting by an alien in a federal election.

The United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Kentucky made the announcement.

According to the indictment, Sandra Madeline Watson, 59, on or about November 5, 2024, in Jefferson County, Kentucky, knowing she was not a United States citizen, voted in an election held for the purpose of electing a candidate for the office of the President, Vice President, member of the Senate, or member of the House of Representatives.

Watson made her initial appearance yesterday before a U.S. Magistrate Judge of the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Kentucky. If convicted, Watson faces a maximum sentence of up to one year in prison. A federal judge will determine any sentence after considering the sentencing guidelines and other statutory factors. There is no parole in the federal system.

This case is being investigated by Homeland Security Investigations and the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Raymond McGee is prosecuting the case.

An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

###
title: Canadian Citizen Charged with Federal Election Offense

Dexter, Bonamici, Merkley Conduct Unannounced Oversight Visit to Portland ICE Facility After Reports of Denied Access to Legal Counsel
PORTLAND, OR – Today, Congresswomen Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01) and U.S. Sen. Jeff Merkley (D-OR) conducted an unannounced congressional oversight visit to the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) processing facility on Macadam Avenue in Portland following troubling reports that attorneys were repeatedly denied access to detained clients.
“No one should be denied access to legal counsel, regardless of their immigration status,” Congresswoman Dexter said. “It is a major concern when attorneys are repeatedly prevented from meeting with their clients. ICE is not above the law, and the Trump administration must be held accountable for how people are treated in federal custody. We are demanding answers, transparency and accountability.”
Rep. Dexter’s office received information from the Portland Immigrant Rights Coalition that attorneys were denied access to four clients on 12 separate occasions Tuesday. These reports, coupled with an uptick in ICE enforcement activity in the Portland area, prompted the lawmakers to conduct an oversight visit to demand answers and examine conditions at the facility.
“I just conducted a Congressional oversight visit at the ICE processing facility in Portland with Rep. Dexter and Senator Merkley,” Congresswoman Bonamici said. “ICE is not making us safer and this surge is increasing fear in the community. I encourage everyone to make a safety plan and take care of each other. I will not stop advocating for safe communities, due process, and humane immigration reform.”
“ICE and Border Patrol agents are terrorizing our friends and neighbors,” Senator Merkley said. “Time after time, they are trampling civil rights, denying due process, and utilizing secret police tactics, totally wrong in our democratic republic. I'll keep doing all I can to stop them.”
During the visit, the lawmakers asked about access to lawyers, the treatment of people in ICE custody, and whether the facility was complying with federal law. The visit builds on Rep. Dexter’s ongoing work to hold federal immigration enforcement accountable and protect the dignity and legal rights of people in ICE custody.
###
title: Dexter, Bonamici, Merkley Conduct Unannounced Oversight Visit to Portland ICE Facility After Reports of Denied Access to Legal Counsel
