FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
October 8, 2026
Contact: Jin.Choi@mail.house.gov
WASHINGTON — Congresswoman Nanette Barragán (CA-44) and Congresswoman Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03), Chair of the Democratic Women’s Caucus, introduced a resolution recognizing October 8, 2026 as Latina Equal Pay Day and calling attention to the wage gap that shortchanges Latinas and their families. In 2025, Latinas with reported earnings were paid just 53 cents for every dollar paid to white, non-Hispanic men.
“Latina Equal Pay Day is a reminder that equal work deserves equal pay,” said Rep. Barragán. “It is unacceptable that Latinas continue to face a significant wage gap compared to White, non-Hispanic men, despite decades of progress towards workplace equality. This disparity affects not only women, but American families, communities, and our economy. We must continue working to ensure every woman —regardless of her race or ethnicity— is valued fairly and paid equally for her work. Ha llegado el momento de que las latinas reciban igualdad de salarios!”
“Latinas work hard, care for our families, and keep our communities running. Yet our paychecks still do not reflect the value of our work,” said Congresswoman Leger Fernández. “When Latinas are underpaid, our families have less money for groceries, rent and child care—all things that have already been made more expensive by the Trump administration. But our contributions are not valued, and our value is not paid. Today, we recommit to closing the gender and racial wage gap. Ya basta. Latinas deserve equal pay TODAY. ”
More than six decades after the passage of the Equal Pay Act of 1963, the wage gap persists across sectors and education levels. Latinas working full time, year round were paid just 60 cents for every dollar paid to white, non-Hispanic men. The gap widens to 53 cents when including workers with part-time and part-year earnings.
The resolution recognizes how the wage gap hurts women, families, and the economy and reaffirms Congress’ support for equal pay and closing the gender wage gap. It also highlights barriers that contribute to the disparity, including a lack of affordable child care and paid family and medical leave, as well as workplace harassment.
“Latinas are paid just 53 cents for every dollar paid to white, non-Hispanic men,” said Mónica Ramírez, Founder and President of Justice for Migrant Women. “We know first hand the consequences of this gap for ourselves and our families. We also recognize the work that is being done every day to change things for the better. That is why we are marking Latina Equal Pay Day this year with three words: Power. Pay. Progress. We are reflecting on the power that Latinas hold, the pay inequities that still exist, the progress that we have made in spite of this pay gap and the work that remains to ensure that Latinas are paid fully and fairly for our work.”
“Latinas face one of the largest wage gaps in the nation, earning just 53 cents for every dollar paid to their white non-Hispanic male counterparts. That should be an urgent call to action, not a statistic we simply acknowledge,” said Jessica Ramey Stender, Policy Director & Deputy Legal Director at Equal Rights Advocates. “At a time when the federal government is rolling back basic workplace protections and attacking the rights and economic security of Latinas and other women, we cannot afford to stand by as the wage gap widens. Nearly half of Latina mothers are breadwinners, meaning the wage gap doesn’t just shortchange Latina workers; it keeps many families in poverty with consequences across generations. We know what it takes to close the wage gap: stronger protections against pay discrimination, access to well-paying jobs, and policies that support working parents. We thank Rep. Leger Fernández and the Democratic Women’s Caucus for championing the rights of women and urge all lawmakers to take decisive action to close the wage gap.”
“53 cents and 11 years after the first Latina Equal Pay Day, Latinas remain among the lowest-paid workers in the country. For more than a decade, LCLAA has stood shoulder to shoulder with trabajadoras, fighting wage theft, harassment, retaliation, and pay inequity, while championing solutions like good union jobs that deliver real, tangible economic security,” said Karla Pineda, Executive Director of the Labor Council for Latin American Advancement (LCLAA). “As meaningful contributors in our homes, communities, and workplaces across every industry, we refuse to be overlooked, undervalued, and silenced. LCLAA has, is, and will continue to commit its efforts to help ensure that all workers– including working women in our comunidad– receive nothing short of what they deserve: dignity, equity, and the real opportunity to thrive rather than merely survive.”
Cosponsors include Representatives Ansari, Bonamici, Carbajal, Castor, Chu, Cisneros, Correa, Crockett, DeLauro, Espaillat, Jesús “Chuy” García, Sylvia R. Garcia, Gomez, Mejia, Menendez, Holmes Norton, Ramirez, Randall, Ruiz, Salinas, Tlaib, Vargas, Velázquez, and Wilson.
The resolution is endorsed by numerous organizations including the A Better Balance, AFL-CIO, American Association of University Women (AAUW), California National Organization for Women (CA NOW), Clearinghouse on Women’s Issues, Equal Rights Advocates, Equal Pay Today, Family Values @ Work, Feminist Majority Foundation, FL National Organization for Women, Institute for Women’s Policy Research, Justice for Migrant Women, Labor Council for Latin American Advancement (LCLAA), Legal Momentum, Minnesota Indian Women’s Resource Center, MomsRising, Montana Chapter of the National Organization for Women for Women, National Black Worker Center, National Council of Jewish Women, National Immigration Law Center, National Network to End Domestic Violence, National Organization for Women, National Partnership for Women & Families, National Women’s Law Center Action Fund, One Fair Wage, Oxfam America, Public Justice Center, Reproductive Freedom for All, Ujima, The National Center on Violence Against Women in the Black Community, Women Employed, WorkLife Law
The resolution can be found HERE.

TEXARKANA, Texas – An Atlanta, Texas man has been sentenced to 10 years in federal prison for child exploitation violations in the Eastern District of Texas, announced U.S. Attorney Jay R. Combs.

JC Herndon, 86, pleaded guilty to possession of child pornography and was sentenced to 120 months in federal prison by U.S. District Judge Robert W. Schroeder III on October 8, 2026.

According to information presented in court, on May 6, 2025, law enforcement officers with the Cass County Sheriff’s Office and Texas Department of Public Safety Criminal Investigations Division executed a search warrant at Herndon’s residence located in Atlanta, Texas. As part of the search, officers seized a cell phone, which was found to contain numerous photos and videos depicting child pornography. Many of those images depicted prepubescent children. Herndon admitted to downloading and viewing images of child pornography on his phone. Herndon is a registered sex offender who was on probation when he was found to be in possession of the child pornography.

This case is part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc.

This case was investigated by the Cass County Sheriff’s Office and the Texas Department of Public Safety - Criminal Investigations Division and prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Lauren Richards.

WHEELING, WEST VIRGINIA — Two South Carolina men have admitted to trafficking large quantities of fentanyl, methamphetamine, and cocaine in Ohio County, U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey announced today.

Phillip Johnson, also known as “PNut,” and Mark Chisholm, also known as “Infant Premo,” pleaded guilty to conspiring to distribute the illicit drugs in the greater Wheeling area. According to court documents, Johnson and Chisholm worked together to transport and sell nearly half a pound of fentanyl, a half a pound of methamphetamine, and more than two pounds of cocaine across several locations in the Ohio Valley during a two-year period.

Johnson and Chisholm each face up to 20 years for the conspiracy conviction. Johnson also faces five to 40 years for five additional drug charges.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Clayton Reid is prosecuting the case. The Ohio Valley Drug Task Force, a HIDTA-funded initiative, and the Drug Enforcement Administration investigated.

Fentanyl has been designated by President Donald Trump as a weapon of mass destruction due to its extreme lethality which poses a grave threat to public safety, even in trace amounts. This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime, and repel the invasion of illegal immigration.

U.S. Magistrate Judge James P. Mazzone presided.
title: South Carolina Men Admit to Selling Fentanyl, Meth in Ohio Valley

Establishment of a Committee of Inquiry to Investigate Allegations of False Statements by Lisa DeNell Cook
MEMORANDUM FOR THE ATTORNEY GENERAL
THE COUNSEL TO THE PRESIDENT
THE ASSISTANT TO THE PRESIDENT FOR ECONOMIC POLICY
THE DIRECTOR OF THE OFFICE OF GOVERNMENT ETHICS
THE CHAIRMAN OF THE EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY COMMISSION
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, I hereby establish a committee of inquiry (Committee) to investigate allegations that Federal Reserve Governor Lisa D. Cook made false statements in connection with one or more mortgage instruments. The Assistant to the President for Economic Policy, the Chairman of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, and the Director of the Office of Government Ethics shall serve as members of the Committee.
As President, it is my job to ensure the laws are faithfully executed, including by firing subordinates who cannot be trusted to tell the truth and follow the law. U.S. Const. Art. II, sec. 3. To assist me in carrying out that responsibility, the Committee shall investigate the allegations against Governor Cook and report to me whether there is “cause” for Governor Cook’s removal within the meaning of 12 U.S.C. 242, as construed in Trump v. Cook, 146 S. Ct. 2234 (2026). The Committee may consult with appropriate personnel from executive departments and agencies, including the Department of Justice, to aid in its inquiry. The Committee shall, on November 5, 2026, conduct an in-person hearing to consider the evidence and allegations against Governor Cook. The hearing shall occur at the White House and shall last no longer than 4 hours.
Governor Cook may submit a written position statement to the Committee regarding the allegations, provided the statement is received at least 3 days before the hearing. Governor Cook shall appear at the hearing and be examined by the Committee, its representatives, and her legal counsel, if any. Governor Cook may present argument, written evidence, and written witness statements regarding the evidence and allegations. The Committee may also question Governor Cook about any representations she or her counsel make during the hearing, or it may authorize its representatives, including Department of Justice personnel, to conduct that questioning. The Committee may request documents or other evidentiary submissions from Governor Cook, as appropriate, and Governor Cook shall comply with any such requests.
Prior to the hearing, the Committee shall provide Governor Cook with the evidence it is considering in its inquiry. At the hearing, the Committee or its representatives may question Governor Cook or her counsel about the evidence and allegations against her. The hearing shall be closed to the public but shall be transcribed.
Governor Cook may submit a post-hearing written statement to the Committee by November 10, 2026. As soon as practicable after receipt of that statement, the Committee shall submit written findings of fact and conclusions of law to me and shall recommend whether there is cause to remove Governor Cook from her position on the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve. The Committee may establish additional procedures or make reasonable changes to the above procedures as necessary or appropriate and shall give Governor Cook adequate notice of any such changes.
The Counsel to the President shall transmit a copy of this memorandum to Governor Cook, to the members of the Committee, and to the Attorney General.
The Attorney General is authorized and directed to publish this memorandum in the Federal Register.
DONALD J. TRUMP
title: Establishment of a Committee of Inquiry to Investigate Allegations of False Statements by Lisa DeNell Cook

Fact Sheet

Office of the Spokesman

October 8, 2026

The Iranian regime continues to intentionally disrupt global energy supplies, terrorize its regional neighbors, and employ violence and illegal measures to repress its own people. To sustain its destabilizing agenda, Iran depends on a shadow network of illicit shipping facilitators across multiple jurisdictions, who deliberately falsify documentation, disguise vessel identities, and evade international sanctions to smuggle Iranian oil, petroleum products, and petrochemical products to buyers in Asia.

Today under President Trump’s Operation Economic Outcast , the Department of State is further dismantling this illicit network and cutting off the Iranian regime’s ability to fund its malign activities. The Department of State is sanctioning ten entities, six individuals, and five vessels in connection with trade in Iranian-origin petroleum, petroleum products, and petrochemical products.

All Department of State targets are being designated pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13846 , which authorizes and reimposes certain sanctions with respect to Iran.

Sanctioning Traders of Iranian-Origin Petrochemical Products

Today’s action sanctions six entities involved in trading Iranian petrochemical products, as well as three principal executive officers tied to companies involved in this activity. These entities have channeled millions of dollars to the Iranian regime, bolstering one of its most critical revenue streams and enabling its continued illicit conduct. The U.S. government is imposing sanctions on both the buyers and sellers driving this trade in Iranian petrochemical products

NOORZAD PETROKIMYA URUNLERI NAKLIYE SANAYI VE TICARET LIMITED SIRKETI ( NOORZAD PETROKIMYA ) is a Türkiye-based petrochemical trading company that imported and purchased approximately $3.8 million in Iranian-origin petrochemical products between January and July 2024. SAID AHMAD NOORZAD ( NOORZAD ) is a Turkish national and the director and Chief Executive Officer of NOORZAD PETROKIMYA.

NOORZAD PETROKIMYA URUNLERI NAKLIYE SANAYI VE TICARET LIMITED SIRKETI is being designated pursuant to section 3(a)(iii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petrochemical products from Iran.

NOORZAD is being blocked pursuant to section 5(a)(vii) of E.O. 13846 as a principal executive officer, or person performing similar functions and with similar authorities, of NOORZAD PETROKIMYA.

ARABIANPRO MATERIALS FZCO is a United Arab Emirates-based petrochemical trading company that exported $2 million in Iranian-origin petrochemical products between February 2025 and July 2025.

ARABIANPRO MATERIALS FZCO is being designated pursuant to section 3(a)(iii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petrochemical products from Iran.

SSPL SOLUTIONS PRIVATE LIMITED ( SSPL SOLUTIONS ) is an India-based petrochemical trading company that imported $2 million in Iranian-origin petrochemical products between February 2025 and July 2025. DHWANI NISARG VORA is an Indian national and a director of SSPL SOLUTIONS. NISARG SAMIR VORA is an Indian national and a director of SSPL SOLUTIONS.

SSPL SOLUTIONS PRIVATE LIMITED is being designated pursuant to section 3(a)(iii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petrochemical products from Iran.

DHWANI NISARG VORA is being blocked pursuant to section 5(a)(vii) of E.O. 13846 as a principal executive officer, or person performing similar functions and with similar authorities, of SSPL SOLUTIONS PRIVATE LIMITED.

NISARG SAMIR VORA is being blocked pursuant to section 5(a)(vii) of E.O. 13846 as a principal executive officer, or person performing similar functions and with similar authorities, of SSPL SOLUTIONS PRIVATE LIMITED.

BGZ DIS TICARET LIMITED SIRKETI ( BGZ ) is a Türkiye-based petrochemical trading company that imported approximately $20 million in Iranian-origin petrochemical products between January and September 2024, including $2 million from Iran-based PADIDEH PLASTIC POSHTIBAN COMPANY .

BGZ is being designated pursuant to section 3(a)(iii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petrochemical products from Iran.

PADIDEH PLASTIC POSHTIBAN COMPANY ( PADIDEH ) is an Iran-based petrochemical trading company that exported approximately $2 million in Iranian-origin petrochemical products between April and August 2024 to Türkiye-based BGZ .

PADIDEH is being designated pursuant to section 3(a)(iii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petrochemical products from Iran.

TUTER PLASTIK SANAYI VE TICARET LIMITED SIRKETI is a Türkiye-based petrochemical trading company that imported approximately $3.5 million in Iranian-origin petrochemical products between January 2023 and August 2024.

TUTER PLASTIK SANAYI VE TICARET LIMITED SIRKETI is being designated pursuant to section 3(a)(iii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petrochemical products from Iran.

Continued Targeting of Iran’s Dark Fleet and Service Providers

The Department of State is also sanctioning one customs broker, two vessel management companies, and one registered owner for their involvement in providing Iran a maritime pathway for selling sanctioned petroleum and petrochemical products. Today’s action also blocks three principal executive officers of the customs broker which engaged in Iranian-origin petrochemical products trading. As part of this action, the Department is also identifying five vessels these companies own or manage as blocked property. These shipping companies and customs brokers operate within Iran’s larger illicit economy, helping the Iranian regime deliver its energy products to end buyers, evade sanctions, and generate revenue. The United States will not allow actors like these who enable the continued operation of the Iranian regime.

SAMUDRA MARINE SERVICES PRIVATE LIMITED ( SAMUDRA ) is an India-based customer broker that facilitated the import of multiple shipments of Iranian-origin petrochemical products to India. KETAN MANOHAR KOCHIKAR ( KOCHIKAR ) is an Indian national and a director of SAMUDURA. BHUPENDRASINGH DHALSINGH SAHU ( SAHU ) is an Indian national and a director of SAMUDRA. HARISHYAM HARIHARAN CHUNDAKATTIL ( CHUNDAKATTIL ) is an Indian national and a director of SAMUDRA.

SAMUDRA is being designated pursuant to Section 3(a)(iii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petrochemical products from Iran.

KOCHIKAR is being blocked pursuant to section 5(a)(vii) of E.O. 13846 as a principal executive officer, or a person performing similar functions and with similar authorities, of SAMUDRA.

SAHU is being blocked pursuant to section 5(a)(vii) of E.O. 13846 as a principal executive officer, or a person performing similar functions and with similar authorities, of SAMUDRA.

CHUNDAKATTIL is being blocked pursuant to section 5(a)(vii) of E.O. 13846 as a principal executive officer, or a person performing similar functions and with similar authorities, of SAMUDRA.

ONE PLUS INTERNATIONAL CO LTD is the United Kingdom-based registered owner of YONG TAI (IMO 9231511). YONG TAI, a Gambia-flagged Oil Products tanker, loaded Iranian-origin methanol from Iran in December 2025. YONG TAI loaded Iranian-origin petrochemical products on at least twelve other occasions since 2024.

ONE PLUS INTERNATIONAL CO LTD is being designated pursuant to section 3(a)(iii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petrochemical products from Iran.

YONG TAI is being identified as property in which ONE PLUS INTERNATIONAL CO LTD has an interest.

HORIZON SHIP MANAGEMENT FZE is the UAE-based commercial manager of YASHAR (IMO: 9129380), a Comoros-flagged LPG tanker that loaded Iranian-origin liquefied petroleum gas on at least three occasions between 2025 and 2026.

HORIZON SHIP MANAGEMENT FZE is being designated pursuant to section 3(a)(ii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petroleum or petroleum products from Iran.

YASHAR is being identified as property in which HORIZON SHIP has an interest.

HESSONITE SHIP MANAGEMENT LLC ( HESSONITE ) is the UAE-based commercial manager of ARGO MARIS (IMO: 9041643), a Honduras-flagged Asphalt/Bitumen tanker that loaded sanctioned Iranian-origin petroleum products on at least eight occasions between January 2026 and August 2026. The other two tankers the company manages have also transported Iranian-origin petroleum products at least eight times during HESSONITE’s tenure as their commercial manager.

HESSONITE is being designated pursuant to section 3(a)(ii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petroleum or petroleum products from Iran.

ARGO MARIS is being identified as property in which HESSONITE has an interest.

BLACK MAYA (IMO: 9118800) is being identified as property in which HESSONITE has an interest.

ATHE NOVA (IMO: 9188116) is being identified as property in which HESSONITE has an interest.

SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS

As a result of today’s sanctions-related actions, and in accordance with E.O. 13846, all property and interests in property of the sanctioned persons described above that are in the United States or in possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to the Department of Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.

All transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons are prohibited unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC or exempt. These prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any blocked person and the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.

The power and integrity of U.S. government sanctions derive not only from the U.S. government’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law. The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.

Petitions for removal from the SDN List may be sent to: OFAC.Reconsideration@treasury.gov . Petitioners may also refer to the Department of State’s Delisting Guidance page.

ALEXANDRIA, Va. – A Herndon mental health counselor was sentenced today to 30 years in prison for engaging in a child exploitation enterprise.

According to court documents, Christopher Neal Mishik, 36, is a Licensed Professional Counselor who offered telehealth counseling to patients online, including to adolescents, young adults, and families. For years, Mishik participated in various online groups that orchestrated the online sexual exploitation of children. In the summer of 2024, Mishik participated in a social media group of adult males who coordinated to produce, distribute, and receive child sexual abuse material (CSAM). The members of the group collectively and individually engaged in various tactics to produce, distribute, and receive CSAM. Mishik and members of the group lurked on young girls' social media accounts and encouraged them to engage in sexually explicit activities on camera and to participate in their larger social media group. Mishik and other group members would sometimes pose as teenage boys or girls to encourage victims to produce CSAM. Among the victims targeted by Mishik were a child with learning disabilities as well as a 10-year-old.

On Nov. 12, 2025, law enforcement searched Mishik’s residence. Mishik’s cellphone contained videos and photos depicting CSAM, including content saved in hidden applications. Some of the CSAM possessed by Mishik included images of toddlers.

Theophani K. Stamos, First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia, and Jeffrey L. Tyler, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI Washington Field Office's Criminal Division, made the announcement after sentencing by U.S. District Judge Patricia Tolliver Giles.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Vanessa K. Strobbe and Lauren Halper prosecuted the case.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc .

Related court documents and information are located on the website of the District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia or on PACER by searching for Case No. 1:26-cr-115.
title: Mental health counselor sentenced to 30 years in prison for exploiting children online

ROCHESTER, N.Y. – U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Gary Fuller, 31, of Rochester, NY, pleaded guilty before U.S. District Judge Frank P. Geraci, Jr. to conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute, and to distribute, five kilograms or more of cocaine, 280 grams or more of crack cocaine, and 400 grams or more of fentanyl, and possession of firearms in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime. The charges carry a minimum penalty of 15 years in prison, a maximum of life, and a $10,000,000 fine.

Between 2021 and January 17, 2024, in Monroe County, Fuller conspired with Timothy Jackson, Jr., Shawnle McClary, Felicia Collins, Shamar Anderson, and others to sell cocaine, fentanyl, and crack cocaine. Fuller packaged narcotics for sale, coordinated drop offs of narcotics and pickups of proceeds from the workers at sale locations on Angle Street, and directed the payment of salaries to workers. Fuller and his co-conspirators possessed firearms at their residences and/or drug sale locations on Angle Street to protect themselves, their narcotics and the proceeds of narcotics sales. On January 17, 2024, investigators executed search warrants at numerous locations utilized by Fuller and his co-conspirators to store, process, package, and sell cocaine and fentanyl. During the searches they seized:

12 firearms

approximately$31,800 cash

210 grams of fentanyl

919 grams of cocaine

109 grams of crack cocaine

1300 capsules of crack cocaine

933 capsules of fentanyl

drug paraphernalia

numerous cell phones

a Rolex watch

money counter

2017 Chevy Tahoe

This investigation was part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of U.S. law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Buffalo comprises agents and officers from Homeland Security Investigations, the FBI, ATF, IRS Criminal Investigations, Department of Homeland Security Emergency Removal Operations, Customs and Border Protection, the DEA, the U.S. Coast Guard Investigative Service, the U.S. Marshals Service, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, the U.S. Secret Service, and the Diplomatic Security Service, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of New York.

The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Robert A. Marangola. The plea is the result of an investigation by the Rochester Police Department, under the direction of Chief David Smith, and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Bryan DiGirolamo.

Sentencing is scheduled for January 19, 2027, before Judge Geraci.

Fort Wayne – Cody Ankrum, 37, of Portland, Indiana was sentenced by Chief Judge Holly A. Brady after pleading guilty to Sexual Exploitation of Children, announced United States Attorney Adam L. Mildred.

Ankrom was sentenced to 180 months in prison to be followed by 90 months of supervised release. Restitution will be determined at a later date.

According to documents in the case, in August 2024, Ankrom persuaded, induced, enticed, or coerced a minor to engage in sexually explicit conduct for the purpose of producing a visual depiction of that conduct or for the purpose of producing a visual depiction of that conduct.

“Cody Ankrom will spend the next fifteen years in prison for his actions. These offenses have life-altering, lasting impacts on victims and their families and require severe punishment to deter others from engaging in this heinous behavior. The United States Attorney’s Office will use whatever resources at our disposal to aggressively prosecute these offenders and seek justice for their victims. Thanks to the partnership of the Homeland Security Investigations, Indiana State Police Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force (ICAC), the Jay County Prosecutor’s Office led by Wesley A. Schemenaur, and Assistant United States Attorney Lesley J. Miller Lowery, the children of the Northern District of Indiana are safer,” said U.S. Attorney Mildred.

“Those who exploit children inflict lasting harm and will be held accountable,” said Homeland Security Investigations Chicago Special Agent in Charge Matthew Scarpino. “This sentence demonstrates our shared resolve to protect children, support survivors and their families, and pursue justice alongside our federal, state and local law enforcement partners.”

This case was investigated by the Homeland Security Investigations with assistance from the Indiana State Police Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force (ICAC) and the Jay County Prosecutor’s Office led be Wesley A. Schemenaur. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Lesley J. Miller Lowery.

The ICAC Task Force encourages Hoosiers to report online exploitation, solicitation, and enticement-type crimes against children to the National center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC). The NCMEC website can be accessed through the ICAC Task Force website: https://www.in.gov/isp/icactf/

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. LAS VEGAS – Las Vegas man sentenced today by U.S. District Judge Jennifer A. Dorsey to 70 months in prison for committing three separate armed bank robberies. The government recommended a sentence of 70 months in prison.

“Violent crime has no place in our communities, and today’s sentence ensures that individuals who threaten the safety of working citizens will face severe consequences,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “Over a span of just 16 days, the defendant subjected innocent bank employees to terrifying ordeals. Our office, alongside the FBI and our local police partners in Henderson and North Las Vegas, remains unwavering in our commitment to removing violent offenders from our streets. We will continue to aggressively prosecute those who disrupt the peace and safety of the Las Vegas valley.”

“By entering these banks and threatening innocent people at gunpoint, the defendant made a reckless choice for which today’s sentence holds him fully accountable,” said Special Agent in Charge Christopher S. Delzotto for the FBI Las Vegas Field Office. “This outcome sends an unmistakable message: the FBI and local law enforcement will not tolerate violent crime. Thanks to the seamless cooperation between our agencies, a callous criminal has been taken off the streets, making our communities safer.”

According to court documents, between January 9, 2025, and January 25, 2025, Denzel Brishard Jones committed a total of three bank robberies in North Las Vegas and Henderson. At each of the robberies, he brandished an XBG BB-gun to make a display of force that reasonably caused the employees to fear bodily harm. In each robbery, Jones threatened to shoot employees and customers as he demanded money. He would then exit with the stolen money and flee the scene in a vehicle driven by co-defendant Tru’Shauna, also known as “Trashauna Outlaw.” Outlaw pleaded guilty to three counts of armed bank robbery and is scheduled to be sentenced December 10, 2026.

Jones pleaded guilty to three counts of armed bank robbery.

The FBI, the Henderson Police Department, and the North Las Vegas Police Department investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Melinda Brewer prosecuted the case.

Nicolás Maduro Moros and Cilia Adela Flores de Maduro Charged with Torture
The Justice Department announced that former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro Moros and former First Lady of Venezuela Cilia Adela Flores de Maduro have been charged in a Superseding Indictment unsealed today with conspiring to commit torture, narcoterrorism, cocaine importation conspiracy, and weapons offenses.
“Since the capture and arrest of Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores, the Department of Justice has been working to uncover the extent of their alleged crimes against the people of Venezuela and of the United States,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “These additional charges against the Maduros reflect the dedication of this Administration to delivering justice for the victims of torture, narcoterrorism, and organized crime.”
“As alleged in the indictment, the Maduro regime subjected American citizens to torture while held in custody of the Venezuelan government — including drugs, electric shock, sexual assault, and more,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “These charges follow the historic law enforcement-operation proudly supported by this FBI in January arresting Maduro and executing one of the most daring Foreign Transfers of Custody in United States history, returning him and his wife to the U.S. — an operation which required months of coordination, detailed planning, and seamless execution across multiple components of the federal government led by the Department of War. Today’s charges reflect the commitment from this FBI and this Department of Justice to accountability, the rule of law, and the protection of U.S. national security.”
“As alleged in today’s Superseding Indictment, for more than two decades, Nicolás Maduro Moros and Cilia Adela Flores De Maduro engaged in a conspiracy to commit torture, including the torture of United States citizens, in addition to the narcotics trafficking and weapons offenses already charged,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald for the Southern District of New York. “As described in the Superseding Indictment, the Maduros and other Venezuelan leaders abused their positions of trust to enrich themselves through narco-terrorism, cocaine trafficking, and other corruption, including by employing Venezuelan military, law enforcement, and other government entities under their control to flood the United States with illegal narcotics. Today’s indictment further alleges that the Maduros and other Venezuelan leaders conspired to repress dissent through grave violations of human rights by ordering and allowing violence, threats, and physical torture under color of law. As alleged, this included the torture of multiple United States citizens, who were subjected to unspeakable abuse. Today’s charges exemplify the tirelessness that we and our law enforcement partners will undertake to vindicate victims of crime, particularly American victims subjected to horrific treatment abroad.”
“Maduro’s regime is responsible for countless American victims of narcoterrorism and drug trafficking,” said DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin. “Thanks to the leadership of President Trump, our Homeland Security Task Force partners, and strong coordination among DHS, DOJ, FBI, and DEA, we’re bringing Maduro and his wife to justice. President Trump is using all tools at his disposal to make America safe again both at home and abroad.”
“These indictments demonstrate that our work did not stop with the arrest of Nicolás Maduro, who terrorized the people of Venezuela for more than two decades,” said DEA Administrator Terry Cole. “DEA will continue to follow the evidence and pursue those who use corruption, violence, and positions of power to facilitate criminal activity and protect those who profit from it. Maduro’s arrest was an important step toward accountability, but it was not the last. We remain steadfast in our commitment to work with our partners to restore law and order across the Western Hemisphere and bring to justice any corrupt leader who thinks their political position shields them from consequences.”
For over 25 years, Nicolás Maduro Moros and Cilia Adela Flores de Maduro abused their positions of public trust, enriching themselves through corruption and remaining in power through grave violations of human rights.
Through drug trafficking, the corrupt use of law enforcement and the military, the abuse of the judicial system, and the pilfering of public funds, Maduro Moros, Flores de Maduro, and other Venezuelan leaders personally benefited at the expense of the Venezuelan people. While this systemic corruption was immensely profitable for the defendants and their inner circle, it was deeply unpopular with the Venezuelan people. To undermine Venezuelan democracy and entrench themselves in power, these same leaders allegedly presided over a system of repression that relied on violence against political opposition, arbitrary detention, and the torture of detainees, including United States citizens. That torture included electric shock, asphyxiation, rape, forced nudity, prolonged isolation, starvation, punishment cells, and psychological torture, such as threats to harm and kill victims’ families.
Maduro Moros and Flores de Maduro allegedly sat atop that violent power structure. They developed and facilitated the systems which they and their co-conspirators used corruptly to amass immense wealth and power, rewarding allies with ill-gotten funds and terrorizing perceived opponents through persecution and violence. These systems relied on Maduro Moros’s and Flores de Maduro’s control over Venezuela’s military, judiciary, and law enforcement agencies, and their partnerships with organized criminal groups, including terrorist organizations and groups of state-sponsored gangs known as colectivos.
In amassing such wealth and power, Maduro Moros, Flores de Maduro, and other members of their inner circle allegedly trafficked drugs under the protection of the Venezuelan military, judiciary, and law enforcement agencies. They allegedly partnered with narcotics traffickers and narco-terrorists from designated foreign terrorist organizations, including the Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias de Colombia (FARC), the Ejército de Liberación Nacional (ELN), the Sinaloa Cartel, the Zetas, later known as the Cártel del Noreste (CDN), and Tren de Aragua (TdA), who dispatched cocaine from Venezuela to the United States via transshipment points in the Caribbean and Central America.
Maduro Moros, Flores de Maduro, and other high-ranking members of their inner circle also allegedly created and maintained a violent system of repression. Since at least 1999, thousands of Venezuelans have been harassed, threatened, arrested, prosecuted, assaulted, tortured, or killed by individuals wielding the purported authority of the Venezuelan state to ensure that Maduro Moros and Flores de Maduro remained in power. Maduro Moros and Flores de Maduro used military units, colectivos, and narco-terrorist groups involved in their drug trafficking to unlawfully detain and torture their victims. Such violence and repression increased around periods of political instability in which Maduro Moros’s and Flores de Maduro’s power was threatened. During these periods, Maduro Moros, Flores de Maduro, and other high-level Venezuelan officials jointly undertook efforts to stifle those who opposed, or were merely suspected of opposing, Maduro Moros or his regime. Those efforts included physical and psychological torture systematically used to terrify the populace and silence dissent.
In addition to Maduro Moros and Flores de Maduro, other high-level officials allegedly were integral to this system. One high-level Venezuelan official, referred to in the Superseding Indictment as CC-1, ordered the murders of certain individuals who opposed Maduro Moros or his regime, oversaw torture undertaken by officials under his command, and personally threatened the murder of a prisoner’s child as a form of psychological torture. Another senior Venezuelan officer who reported directly to Maduro Moros, referred to in the Superseding Indictment as CC-2, developed torture methods that he presented for approval to Maduro Moros, led an agency responsible for torturing scores of victims, and personally signed off on the unlawful arrest and torture of specific individuals. A third Venezuelan official, referred to in the Superseding Indictment as CC-3, personally ordered and participated in the torture of civilians and military members, including United States citizens, who were believed to pose a threat to Maduro Moros’s rule. For example, one particular United States citizen was detained in Venezuela and subjected to, among other things, deprivation of food and water, simulated drowning, repeated beatings, electric shock to his testicles, and forced injections.
The Superseding Indictment charges Maduro Moros, 63, and Flores de Maduro, 69, in Count One, with participating in a narcoterrorism conspiracy, which carries a 20-year mandatory minimum penalty and a maximum penalty of life in prison; in Count Two, with conspiring to commit torture, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; in Count Three, with conspiring to import cocaine into the United States, which carries a 10-year mandatory minimum penalty and a maximum penalty of life in prison; in Count Four, with using and carrying machine guns and destructive devices during and in relation to, and possessing machine guns and destructive devices in furtherance of, the narco-terrorism and cocaine-importation conspiracies, which carries a 30-year mandatory minimum penalty and a maximum penalty of life in prison; and in Count Five, with conspiring to use and carry machine guns and destructive devices during and in relation to, and to possess machine guns and destructive devices in furtherance of, the narco-terrorism and cocaine-importation conspiracies, which carries a maximum penalty of life in prison. The potential maximum penalties in this case are prescribed by Congress and provided here for informational purposes only, as any sentencing of the defendants will be determined by the judge.
This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by President Trump in Executive Order 14159. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of U.S. law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders.
This case is being handled by the Office’s National Security and International Narcotics Unit. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kaylan E. Lasky, Henry L. Ross, Kevin T. Sullivan, and Kyle A. Wirshba for the Southern District of New York are in charge of the prosecution, with assistance from Trial Attorney Kevin Nunnally of the Counterterrorism Section of the National Security Division.
An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: Nicolás Maduro Moros and Cilia Adela Flores de Maduro Charged with Torture

HOUSTON – A 35-year-old Houston resident will serve federal prison time for illegally transmitting proceeds from an email scam.

Edikan Adiakpan pleaded guilty May 12.

U.S. District Judge Andrew Hanen ordered Adiakpan to serve 30 months in federal prison to be immediately followed by three years of supervised release. At the hearing, the court heard evidence that from 2020 to 2022, Adiakpan used “Akama Lifestyle,” a company he controlled and advertised as a luxury car service, to transfer funds for others. He kept a percentage of transferred funds as a fee.

At the time of his arrest, Adiakpan had temporary legal status to be in the United States, but is originally from Nigeria.

The funds Adiakpan received and transmitted originated from fraudsters who carried out a business email compromise scheme targeting more than 10 victims. The fraudsters sent “spoofed” emails that appeared to come from known suppliers and creditors, tricking victims into sending payments to bank accounts the fraudsters controlled instead of the actual suppliers.

One victim, a small utility trailer company in Mississippi, provided a victim impact statement that was read at the sentencing hearing about the effect this fraud had on their company after they were deceived into wiring money they thought was to their trailer supplier, including $927,080 wired to the Houston fraudsters, who then sent portions of those proceeds to Adiakpan. Adiakpan deposited and redeemed several cashier’s checks payable to himself and his exotic car company that contained $359,000 of the victim’s money.

Another Nigerian, Ayobami Omoniyi, 27, was sentenced March 24 to 32 months in federal prison for his role in the scheme.

FBI Houston and its Bryan Resident Agency and IRS Criminal Investigation conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Belinda Beek prosecuted the case.
title: Nigerian national sentenced for role in email scam

MUSKOGEE, OKLAHOMA – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Oklahoma announced that Travon Maurice Lawrence, age 21, of Okmulgee, Oklahoma, was sentenced to 78 months in prison for one count of Assault with Intent to Commit Murder in Indian Country.

The charge arose from an investigation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Okmulgee Police Department.

On November 10, 2025, Lawrence pleaded guilty to the charge. According to investigators, on July 5, 2025, police responding to a call of a shooting at an Okmulgee residence discovered the victim in critical condition with gunshot wounds to the arm and torso. Witnesses reported that Lawrence became belligerent during a gathering, pulled a pistol, and fired shots at the victim before fleeing on foot. Officers located Lawrence at an area residence a short time later and took him into custody without incident.

The crime occurred in Okmulgee County, within the boundaries of the Muscogee (Creek) Nation Reservation, in the Eastern District of Oklahoma.

The Honorable Ronald A. White, Senior Judge in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Oklahoma, presided over the hearing. Lawrence will remain in the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service pending transportation to a designated United States Bureau of Prisons facility to serve a non-paroleable sentence of incarceration.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Lewis M. Reagan represented the United States.
title: Okmulgee Resident Sentenced For Assault With Intent To Commit Murder

SACRAMENTO, Calif. — Stephan James Evanovich, 47, of Placerville, was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge Daniel J. Calabretta to six years and five months in prison for a conspiracy to transport stolen property and for interstate transportation of stolen property, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced.

According to court documents, Evanovich led a multistate conspiracy that endangered cellular communications, including potentially disrupting 911 services. Evanovich’s co-conspirators Trevor Fountain, 38; Jonathan Matthew Curl, 37; and Andrea Carter, 36, all of Sacramento, entered communications towers to steal rectifiers (a power source necessary to maintain power at the towers) and other communications equipment.

Fountain, Carter, and Curl were responsible for stealing equipment and transferring it to Evanovich, who then paid them for the stolen equipment. Evanovich sold the stolen property to unwitting third-party vendors in California, Illinois, Colorado, and Texas. In total, the conspirators stole, sold, and shipped more than 700 rectifiers across state lines.

As part of the scheme, Evanovich instructed others to create invoices using fictitious business names to make it appear as if the rectifiers had been purchased from legitimate sources.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation conducted the investigation with assistance from Weld County Sheriff’s Office in Colorado. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Jessica Delaney and Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Nchekube Onyima prosecuted the case.

All defendants pleaded guilty. Curl was sentenced on April 23, 2026, to two years in prison and ordered to pay $282,193 in restitution. Carter was sentenced on June 5, 2025, to 29 months in prison. Fountain was sentenced on Aug. 6, 2026, to 20 months in prison and ordered to pay $225,989 in restitution.

LAS VEGAS – A Las Vegas woman made her initial appearance in federal court yesterday for allegedly travelling with packages of methamphetamine found in her suitcases at Harry Reid International Airport in Las Vegas.
“The indictment returned by the federal grand jury underscores our unwavering commitment to keeping lethal narcotics out of our communities and disrupting the supply chains that profit from addiction,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “Thanks to the vigilance of our partners at the Transportation Security Administration approximately 50 pounds of methamphetamine were intercepted before they could reach their destination. Airports are hubs for commerce and travel, not conduits for illicit drug trafficking. We will continue to work tirelessly with our local, state, and federal law enforcement partners to aggressively prosecute those who attempt to exploit our transportation networks to distribute poison into our neighborhoods."
“Drug traffickers who attempt to use commercial air travel to move dangerous narcotics through Las Vegas will be identified and held accountable,” said Jonathan Sherwin, Deputy Special Agent in Charge for Homeland Security Investigations, Las Vegas. “The substantial quantity of methamphetamine allegedly concealed in this case posed a serious threat to public safety. Homeland Security Investigations will continue working with our law enforcement partners to stop illicit drugs before they reach our communities.”
According to allegations in the indictment, on July 1, 2026, Tamya Norwood checked two suitcases at the Harry Reid International Airport. During screening, the Transportation Security Administration discovered packages containing nearly 50 pounds of methamphetamine concealed in Norwood’s suitcases.
Norwood is charged with one count of possession with intent to distribute a controlled substance. A jury trial is scheduled to begin December 14, 2026, before United States District Judge Richard F. Boulware. If convicted, the statutory maximum penalty is lifetime imprisonment, and the mandatory minimum penalty is 10 years imprisonment. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
This case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations. Assistant United States Attorney Steven Rose is prosecuting the case.
This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of U.S. law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. The Las Vegas HSTF comprises agents and officers with the FBI, HSI, DEA, ATF, IRS-CI, the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department, the United States Marshals Service, and Nevada Gaming Control Board with the prosecution being led by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Nevada.
An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

text:
Today, Congresswomen Suzan DelBene (WA-01) and Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03) reintroduced the Strengthening Welfare in Marine Settings (SWIMS) Act, legislation that would end the future capture and breeding of whales for public display.
Certain cetaceans, such as orcas, beluga whales, pilot whales, and false killer whales, are cognitively, emotionally, and socially complex animals who cannot thrive in captivity, according to multiple studies. Whales held for display often exhibit signs of suffering and distress and have significantly shorter lifespans than whales in the wild. Currently, there are approximately 70 whales held in captivity in the United States.
The SWIMS Act would:
    - Prohibit the taking, importation, or exportation of these whales for public display.
- Prohibit any breeding of these whales for future public display.
- Allow exemptions for animals being transported to a sanctuary setting or released to the wild.
“Whales and dolphins are treasures to the Pacific Northwest, and they belong in the wild,” said DelBene. “Scientific evidence shows that when these majestic animals are kept in captivity, they suffer significant distress and shorter life spans. This legislation would prevent the capture and breeding of whales for public display to ensure they remain in their natural habitats and free from abuse and exploitation.”
“Whales belong in the open ocean, not behind glass,” said Dexter. “These extraordinary animals are icons of the Pacific Northwest, forming deep family bonds and playing a vital role in healthy oceans. Captivity robs them of the space, freedom, and connection they need to thrive. Their lives should be defined by the ocean’s possibilities, not the walls of a tank.” 
“Science increasingly supports the conclusion that we cannot provide conditions in a concrete enclosure that accommodate the size, wide-ranging nature, and physiological, behavioral, and social needs of these species,” said Dr. Naomi Rose, senior scientist for marine mammal biology at the Animal Welfare Institute. “The SWIMS Act recognizes that reality and offers a path forward by prohibiting breeding, trade, and capture for public display. Let this be the last generation in captivity of these ocean predators.”
The SWIMS Act is supported by the Animal Legal Defense Fund, Animal Welfare Institute, Born Free USA, Cetacean Society International, CompassionWorks International, Humane World Action Fund, Humane World for Animals, International Marine Mammal Project of Earth Island Institute, Last Chance for Animals, Oceanic Preservation Society, People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals, Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine, Whale and Dolphin Conservation, Whale Sanctuary Project, and World Animal Protection.
The bill text can be found 
here

title: DelBene, Dexter Introduce Legislation to Stop Future Capture, Breeding of Whales for Public Display

Rep. Gabe Vasquez Statement on EPA Promoting Methane Emissions
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On October 8, 2026, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) issued the following statement after the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) announced the rollback of key regulations restricting harmful methane gas emissions:
"Energy production drives our state's economy and provides good-paying jobs, and we can continue to do it while strengthening, not weakening, protections for clean air for the workers and families who work in and near the industry,” said Vasquez. “Excess methane emissions are known to cause respiratory disease and other ailments, and many producers in the Permian Basin have implemented new technology to prevent leaks and capture more methane, and that work must continue. This harmful rollback is the wrong choice for the health of our workers, communities, and companies that have responsibly worked toward reducing excess emissions."
The 2023 methane rule established stronger nationwide standards to reduce methane pollution from oil and gas operations, including requirements for companies to regularly monitor equipment for leaks, quickly repair breaks, limit routine flaring, and reduce emissions from wells, storage tanks, compressors, and other equipment. The rule also required states to develop plans to reduce methane emissions from existing oil and gas facilities. The Administration’s rollback would weaken these protections, reducing requirements on oil and gas producers to detect and address methane pollution and potentially allowing more wasted natural gas and harmful emissions into New Mexico communities.

title: Rep. Gabe Vasquez Statement on EPA Promoting Methane Emissions

TUCSON, Ariz. – Jacob Aaron Hicks, 46, of Tucson, was arrested yesterday and charged by criminal complaint with Making an Interstate Threat to Injure. Hicks is accused of sending an email on Sep.23, 2026, threatening to commit mass bombings at the White House and around the Washington, D.C. area. Hicks made his initial appearance in federal court today.

“We must take threats of violence like this one seriously,” said United States Attorney Timothy Courchaine. “I am grateful to our local news station for referring this threat to law enforcement, and to the FBI for addressing the situation quickly, professionally, and with the level of commitment it required.”

"The FBI remains steadfast in its mission to defend the United States against criminal and national security threats and will investigate them to the fullest extent of the law," said FBI Phoenix Special Agent in Charge Rebecca Day. "We appreciate the community partner who reported the threat to law enforcement. Cooperation and partnership are essential to protecting the American people."

According to the criminal complaint, Hicks emailed a local Tucson news station on Sep. 23, claiming that there would be an imminent bomb strike against the White House and other locations in Washington, D.C. The news station notified law enforcement, who began an investigation and identified Hicks as the alleged sender of the email.

As part of its investigation, law enforcement located additional unsent email drafts from the same email account tied to Hicks. These draft emails, which were also dated Sep. 23, were addressed to other news agencies and contained similar threats to the White House and surrounding areas.

This case is part of the nationwide National Security Presidential Memorandum 7 initiative, which is a White House directed, interagency effort to integrate federal, state, and local partners in protecting First Amendment rights while targeting individuals and organizations engaged in political violence and is led by the investigative and prosecutorial Joint Task Force Vanguard.

The FBI is conducting the investigation, with assistance from the United States Secret Service. The United States Attorney’s Office, District of Arizona, Tucson, is handling the prosecution.

A criminal complaint is a formal accusation of criminal conduct. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

CASE NUMBER: 26-MJ-10107 RELEASE NUMBER: 2026-170_Hicks

WASHINGTON, DC — Today, at the Science: A New Golden Age Summit, the Trump Administration launched the most ambitious set of science initiatives in decades, representing over $6 billion in investments across the Federal Government, industry, academia, and philanthropy to usher in a New Golden Age of Science.
The Summit builds on Science: A New Golden Age, a report authored by White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios to President Trump. The report was written in response to the President’s directive to revitalize the American scientific enterprise. Today, America’s largest Federal research agencies and partners across the science ecosystem launched whole-of-nation efforts to position the United States to lead in a new era of scientific discovery. These initiatives will equip scientists with the tools to harness SI-driven scientific revolution, support the best and brightest American STEM students and early-career scientists, revive the pursuit of ambitious national scientific missions, and encourage the creation of new scientific institutions.
“Today marks the most transformative day for the American scientific enterprise since the reshaping of the Federal research ecosystem following World War II. The efforts announced today will channel billions of dollars across our science ecosystem to realize the new scientific opportunities that now exist.” said Director Kratsios. “Under President Trump’s leadership, we are ushering in a New Golden Age of Science powered by super intelligence, a return to merit, and bold national missions that will inspire Americans for generations to come.”
The Trump Administration continues to pursue a whole-of-nation approach to renew American Science for a New Golden Age of Discovery. With today’s announcements, President Trump is forging new partnerships across government, industry, academia, and philanthropy to lay the foundation for the next generation of American scientific leadership.
EQUIPPING AMERICAN SCIENTISTS WITH SUPER INTELLIGENCE: Super intelligence (SI) will be the greatest accelerant of scientific progress in human history and will transform every scientific discipline. President Trump continues to prioritize American scientists by ensuring broad access to the compute and scientific instrumentation needed for SI-enabled scientific research.
- The Trump Administration announced $2.4B in SI for science tools and compute credits for the Genesis Mission Consortium from eleven industry partners, which will support over 15 Federal agencies working towards National Science & Technology Challenges.
  - Industry partner commitments include NVIDIA ($1B), AMD ($500M), OpenAI ($200M), $150M each from Anthropic and Google, $100M each from AMP and Emerald AI, and $50M each from AWS, Armada, Crusoe, and Micron. This follows the expansion of the Genesis Mission in July to over 15 Federal agencies and a $5 billion Federal commitment to support National Science & Technology Challenges across energy, health, space, and more.
- The Trump Administration announced historic investments in scientific computing through state and regional SI infrastructure hubs, making advanced SI resources more widely available to researchers across the country. 
  - More than 14 universities across 10 states launched the Southeast Regional SI Computing Consortium to build and share leadership-class compute infrastructure for scientific research.
  - Universities, industry, and the State of Georgia announced a $1 billion investment in scientific computing and related workforce training efforts for students and faculty.
  - Five universities across North and South Carolina joined together to launch a regional compute hub, unlocking SI-enabled science for researchers across the region.
- The National Science Foundation (NSF) and the Department of Energy (DOE) announced an investment of over $100 million in SI-enabled scientific instrumentation and autonomous laboratories to increase scientific productivity and unlock new modes of research. This follows NSF’s July announcement of a $400 million investment in programmable cloud labs to accelerate and democratize access to science.
REFOCUSING ON THE BEST AND BRIGHTEST: President Trump has replaced DEI with merit across the Federal R&D enterprise, ensuring high-potential American STEM students and early-career scientists receive the resources and support they need early in their careers to pursue ambitious opportunities at the frontiers of science and technology.
- The Trump Administration is announcing new merit-based K-12 STEM opportunities focused on gifted students and meaningful hands-on technical learning. 
  - The Trump Administration revived the NSF Young Scholars Program, funded primarily by philanthropy and inexplicably abandoned in 1996, to invest in students in grades 3-12 on the basis of demonstrated mathematics ability.
  - DOE launched the Battelle-Genesis Mission High School Fellowship to provide advanced high school students with transformative hands-on research experiences at DOE National Laboratories.
- The Trump Administration is strengthening investments in American STEM PhD students, ensuring the STEM PhD remains a desirable pathway for America’s most talented students to continue their technical training.
  - The Trump Administration launched the Genesis Mission Fellowship, a $100 million initiative for students to pursue accelerated four-year PhDs with dual competency in super intelligence and another science or engineering discipline and research experiences embedded in industry and a DOE National Laboratory.
  - NSF launched a 6-year Integrated Bachelors-to-PhD program, enabling promising students to complete doctoral studies on an accelerated timeline, and speeding up their contributions to the American scientific enterprise. This builds off of NSF’s July announcement of an innovative accelerated 4-year PhD program co-funded by industry.
- The Trump Administration launched Generation Discovery, which will bring a hundred exceptional early-career scientists into the NIH’s Intramural Research Program, enabling early-career researchers to do bold, ambitious work at the most pivotal stages in their career. This continues NIH’s FY2026 support for the largest ever cohort of early-stage investigators in history.
BRINGING BACK NATIONAL MISSIONS: From the Manhattan Project to the Apollo Program, some of America’s greatest scientific achievements have come from focused national missions that united the Nation’s brightest minds behind an ambitious common goal. President Trump has brought back National Missions in super intelligence, quantum, fusion, and space exploration that will excite Americans for generations to come.
- NASA and DOE solidified a historic partnership to develop nuclear power and space nuclear fuels. NASA and DOE will collaborate to design, build, and deploy multiple space systems, including NASA’s Space Reactor-1, a nuclear-powered spacecraft to Mars expected to launch in 2028, as well as Lunar Reactor-1, the first fission reactor on the lunar surface. This MOU will support implementation of President Trump’s December 2025 Executive Order on “Ensuring American Space Superiority” and NSTM-3 launching a National Initiative for American Space Nuclear Power.
- DOE announced the Quantum Computing Priority Applications, a set of eight key problems that will guide the Quantum Genesis Q Competition, a $215 million initiative to fund teams to demonstrate the world’s first fault-tolerant, scientifically relevant quantum computers. These challenges will help achieve the goals set out in President Trump’s June 2026 Executive Order “Ushering in the Next Frontier of Quantum Innovation.”
- NSF launched two $33 million Grand Research Challenge (GRC) prize competitions in Quantum+X applications and synthetic multicellularity. These challenges will facilitate multidisciplinary collaboration, attract non-traditional entrants, and form cross-sector teams to spur rapid advances in use-inspired basic discovery.
- This week, the NIH, DOE, and Biohub launched a $1.8B virtual biology initiative to create the data and modeling foundation for virtual cells, which will develop SI models that can better predict how cells and biological systems respond to disease and develop potential interventions. This initiative will support Bio Genesis, a national mission to double the pace of biomedical innovation within the next five to ten years.
BUILDING INSTITUTIONS THAT ACCELERATE DISCOVERY: President Trump is creating new institutions of discovery to enable American Scientists to pursue major scientific and technical objectives that fall outside of disciplines and conventional funding mechanisms.
- The Trump Administration is supporting X-Labs across agencies, a new generation of independent research organizations that give multidisciplinary teams of scientists and engineers the autonomy and resources to tackle specific technical challenges.
  - The Trump Administration launched the X-Labs Consortium with over $310 million in industry and philanthropic commitments to support Federally-funded X-Labs teams with advanced scientific instrumentation and facility space. This builds on the $1.5 billion NSF X-Labs initiative announced in May, which has supported X-Labs across scientific instrumentation, quantum systems, physical SI, predictive biology, and next-generation computation.
- The Trump Administration recognizes that metascience, or applying the scientific method to evaluate how we fund and conduct science, is necessary to evaluate the impact of new experiments and maximize return on Federal investments in research.
  - NSF, DOE, NASA, and DOW launched new metascience initiatives to inform how they fund and conduct science. Agencies will run experiments and analyze data to better identify exceptional ideas, empower talented researchers, reduce unnecessary friction, and accelerate the pace of discovery.
  - The NSF and the United Kingdom Research and Innovation Metascience Unit announced metascience cooperation to measure research impact, improve research review, and test new tools for science, laying the foundation for an International Network of Metascience Units. This announcement builds on the U.S.-led Kyoto Vision for a New Golden Age of Science.
