LAS VEGAS — Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) Core 8 launched Operation Loaded Dice in July 2026. This was a strategic investigative initiative focused on disrupting and dismantling transnational criminal organizations, gangs and other criminal networks involved in illicit firearms and narcotics trafficking, as well as bulk cash smuggling, and associated violent crime in the greater Las Vegas metropolitan area.

Over the course of the approximately three-month initiative, HSTF law enforcement authorities arrested 144 suspects, seized 290 firearms, including machine guns, and seized 1,124 kilograms of narcotics and more than $1 million in cash and other assets. These enforcement actions also led to the initiation of 13 HSTF investigations in coordination with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Nevada.

Through intelligence-driven investigations, coordinated enforcement actions, surveillance, controlled purchases and sustained investigative partnerships, the HSTF disrupted multiple criminal organizations operating within the Las Vegas metropolitan area.

The investigations included networks associated with the Sinaloa Cartel and the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, or CJNG, as well as other regional drug trafficking organizations, gangs, and trafficking networks.

“This coordinated operation is a powerful testament to the relentless dedication of our multiagency task force,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “By removing 144 suspects from our streets, we have dealt a decisive blow to the criminal networks attempting to exploit our community and compromise public safety. Our message is clear: If you threaten the security of Nevadans and our guests, Homeland Security and our law enforcement partners will find you, dismantle your operations and bring you to justice.”

“Strong policing requires true partnership, respect, and community trust,” said Special Agent in Charge Christopher S. Delzotto for the FBI Las Vegas Field Office. “By unifying local, state and federal agencies, the HSTF initiative equips law enforcement to tackle crime collectively and save lives.”

“We stand proud of the results achieved by Operation Loaded Dice. This is a vast operation, which has netted more than $1 million in assets, hauled away 290 firearms, and seized 1,100 kilograms of narcotics. Just as significant, we are taking 144 criminals off our streets,” said Assistant Special Agent in Charge Brandon Lesky of the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA)'s Las Vegas District Office. “Through our whole-of-government approach, we leveraged each agency’s capabilities and relied heavily on sharp collaboration and open communication. The HSTF initiative empowers partners to continue tackling drug trafficking networks. The ultimate goal is to save lives.”

“Through ATF’s participation in Homeland Security Task Forces, or HSTF, we help to disrupt major criminal organizations and criminal activity while working alongside our local, state and federal partners,” said Assistant Special Agent in Charge Elliott Prose of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF)’s San Francisco Field Division. “By combining our resources through joint task forces and shared intelligence, we effectively and efficiently tackle the violent crime that threatens our communities head on. The investigations conducted thus far in the Las Vegas area serve as examples of the steps HSTF has taken and will continue to take when individuals choose to engage in conduct that endangers the wellbeing of our cities. ATF is proud to be a part of HSTF. We will continue to stay focused on our mission and continue to work in lock step with our partners.”

“We, the U.S. Marshals, are proud to stand with our federal, state and local law enforcement partners in the Homeland Security Task Force against the criminals who prey on our community,” said U.S. Marshal Gary Schofield for the District of Nevada. “We remain relentless in our pursuit of justice. We know we keep Nevada safe.”

“Operation Loaded Dice demonstrates the impact of a unified law enforcement response to the criminal organizations that endanger our communities,” said Special Agent in Charge Erin Burke of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Los Angeles. “By combining our collective authorities, resources, and expertise, the HSTF is identifying and disrupting the networks responsible for trafficking dangerous narcotics, illegal firearms and illicit proceeds. These results represent meaningful progress in protecting the people of southern Nevada and holding accountable those who threaten public safety.”

“Sheriff Kevin McMahill and the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department are thankful for the partnerships we share with the Homeland Security Task Force. This strategic initiative highlights the importance of collaboration in keeping our community safe. Every suspect arrested, firearm recovered or case solved makes a significant impact on the well-being of those who live in Las Vegas.”

“Criminal organizations operate beyond jurisdictional boundaries, making collaboration among law enforcement agencies essential,” said North Las Vegas Police Department Assistant Chief Adam Hyde. “The North Las Vegas Police Department remains committed to working with our federal, state, and local partners to disrupt these organizations and keep our communities safe."

“The Henderson Police Department relies on strong strategic partnerships with local, state and federal law enforcement,” said Henderson Police Chief Reggie Rader. “By sharing resources and intelligence, we're able to target the criminal organizations and keep our communities safe.”

The HSTF was established pursuant President Trump’s Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership focused on eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking networks operating in the United States and abroad. President Trump vowed to make America safe again and by empowering law enforcement agencies and establishing task forces such as HSTF, he is making our nation safer and stronger.

Through interagency collaboration, the HSTF coordinates the capabilities of U.S. law enforcement agencies to identify, investigate, and prosecute the full range of crimes committed by these organizations, which contribute to violence and instability in communities across the country. The HSTF places particular emphasis on organizations whose criminal activity poses a threat to the safety and security of the United States.

The HSTF also uses all available lawful authorities to investigate and prosecute violent criminal offenders and, where appropriate and consistent with applicable law, support their removal from the United States. HSTF Core 8 consists of special agents, officers, analysts, prosecutors, and support personnel from participating federal, state, local, and regional agencies. Federal prosecutions are coordinated with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Nevada.

Homeland Security Task Force Core 8 includes the following federal partners: ATF; DEA; the Diplomatic Security Service; the Federal Air Marshal Service; the FBI; HSI; IRS; the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Nevada; and the U.S. Marshals Service.

State, local and regional partners include the Clark County District Attorney’s Office; the Henderson Police Department; the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department; the Mesquite Police Department; the Nevada Gaming Control Board; the Nevada Highway Patrol; the North Las Vegas Police Department; the Nye County Sheriff’s Office; the Reno Police Department; the Sparks Police Department; the Washoe County Sheriff’s Office; and the White Pine County Sheriff’s Office.

Brad D. Schimel, First Assistant United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Wisconsin, announced that on October 6, 2026, United States District Judge Brett H. Ludwig sentenced Ankurkumar Patel (age 44) of Brookfield, Wisconsin, to 84 months imprisonment.

On June 15, 2026, Patel pled guilty to one count of money laundering conspiracy for laundering over $1 million stolen from elderly victims in multiple states who fell prey to a “Phantom Hacker Scam.” Phantom Hacker Scams are a type of fraud that primarily targets elderly victims. A participant in the scheme, who is often located overseas, poses as a customer service agent or government official. The purported customer service agent or pseudo government official contacts the victim and falsely claims that the victim’s identity or bank account has been hacked or compromised. The fraudster then refers the victim to a co-conspirator posing as a law enforcement agent who directs the victim to move their funds, usually in the form of cash or physical gold, to a third-party, or government account for safekeeping. The co-conspirator then coordinates the transfer of the victim’s funds to other participants in the scheme who act as couriers. In many cases, the victims lose their entire life savings to these fraud schemes.

Patel pled guilty to acting as a courier and personally retrieving and laundering over $1 million from multiple elderly victims in several states. Court documents reveal that Patel also conspired to launder the victim money by distributing it to other co-conspirators through anonymous, surreptitious transactions. The money often was then sent to co-conspirators living overseas.

At the sentencing hearing, Judge Ludwig noted that Patel targeted elderly victims, whose life savings are now gone because of Patel’s conduct, and the conduct of his co-conspirators. Judge Ludwig also ordered Patel to pay over $1.3 million in restitution to the victims.

“It was heartbreaking to hear of the financial devastation these scammers caused to Americans who worked their whole lives to save for retirement,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Schimel. “We will aggressively pursue those who steal from senior citizens.”

“Ankurkumar Patel conspired with others to fraudulently obtain and launder over $1 million from elderly victims through a fraud scheme. His scheme included posing as technical support and impersonating government officials to swindle everyday Americans out of their hard-earned money. In some instances, he would retrieve cash and gold from his victims while in other instances he would use couriers to pick up the valuables. Victims were in several states to include Wisconsin,” said FBI Milwaukee Special Agent in Charge Alan Karr. “The FBI is committed to investigating those who exploit vulnerable individuals for their own personal gain.”

If you believe you or someone you know may have fallen victim to a similar scam, please contact the FBI at 414-276-4684 or report online at IC3.gov.

This case was investigated by the FBI in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, Homeland Security Investigations in St. Louis, Missouri and the U.S. Department of Labor, Employee Benefits Security Administration. It was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Peter J. Smyczek, District Fraud Counsel for the Eastern District of Wisconsin.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Amanda Leigh Fourez, of Catlin, Illinois, was sentenced today to 31 months in prison and three years of supervised release in connection with her involvement with online groups dedicated to creating and distributing videos depicting acts of extreme violence and sexual abuse against monkeys in violation of the federal Animal Crushing statute.

United States District Judge Christy Criswell Wiegand imposed the sentence on Fourez, who pleaded guilty in April to distributing animal crush videos and conspiring with others to create and distribute the videos.

“Amanda Fourez commissioned mutilation of helpless animals on video, and then disseminated those gruesome videos to an online community of people who were seeking content that portrayed the infliction of severe pain and suffering,” said United States Attorney Troy Rivetti for the Western District of Pennsylvania. “Today’s sentencing demonstrates the ongoing commitment of the Department of Justice and our law enforcement partners to investigating and prosecuting these serious federal crimes involving cruelty to animals.”

According to Court documents and statements made during the sentencing hearing, Fourez paid thousands of dollars to commission bespoke sexual torture videos of monkeys, and later she distributed the obscene crush videos online. She was a member of several chat groups and private payment groups dedicated to the creation, distribution, and discussion of sexual and violent videos depicting monkeys being tortured, including baby and adult monkeys being burned and their genitals mutilated.

During the sentencing hearing, Judge Wiegand denied Fourez’s motion for a downward variance, and observed that the videos that Fourez created and distributed were “shocking and violent” and documented “agonizing torture” of animals. Judge Wiegand further noted that the sentence should deter others from this serious conduct.

Another member of these groups, Joseph Garrett Buckland, of Mount Pleasant, Pennsylvania, pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to create and distribute animal crush videos in April and is set to be sentenced on Jan. 13, 2027, for his role in the conspiracy ring.

“We stand ready to prosecute this depraved conduct,” said Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General Adam Gustafson of the Justice Department’s Energy and Natural Resources Division (ENRD). “We appreciate the collaboration of HSI and the U.S. Attorney’s Office in rooting out this conspiracy and prosecuting the case.”

“The conduct in this case was unimaginably cruel and highlights the depraved nature of the online networks HSI is committed to dismantling,” said Special Agent in Charge Matt Wright of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) New Orleans. “HSI will continue to utilize advanced investigative techniques and vital law enforcement partnerships to track those who facilitate these heinous crimes across international borders.”

HSI New Orleans’ Cyber and Human Exploitation Investigations investigated the case.

Assistant United States Attorneys Alyssa R. Angotti and Kelly M. Locher for the Western District of Pennsylvania and Trial Attorney Emily R. Stone of ENRD’s Environmental Crimes Section are prosecuting the case.
title: Illinois Woman Sentenced to 31 Months in Prison for Distributing and Conspiring to Create and Distribute Sexual Torture and Mutilation Videos of Baby Monkeys

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Today at the Science: A New Golden Age Summit, President Donald J. Trump presented National Medals of Science and National Medals of Technology and Innovation, our nation’s highest honors for exemplary achievement and leadership in science and technology, to six of America’s greatest living innovators.
Since 1963, the President of the United States has bestowed the National Medal of Science on those deserving of special recognition for their outstanding contributions to science in service of the United States. Since it was first awarded in 1985, the National Medal of Technology and Innovation has recognized American innovators whose vision, intellect, creativity, and determination have strengthened America’s economy and improved our quality of life.
President Trump is committed to restoring U.S. global scientific and technological leadership for a New Golden Age, from harnessing super intelligence for scientific discovery to ushering in a nuclear renaissance; from ensuring American space superiority to strengthening America’s quantum advantage.
These medalists have pioneered breakthroughs in science and engineering for the new age of super intelligence, from fundamental advances in general-purpose parallel computing and semiconductor design to engineering and business leadership in building the foundations of hyperscale infrastructure in the U.S., around the world, and even into space. Their work has advanced American global technology leadership for the 21st Century and laid the foundation for a new Golden Age of Science.
The recipients are listed below.
Recipients of the National Medal of Science
- Elon Musk – “For engineering achievements of extraordinary ambition and scale that have pushed the frontiers of space exploration, intelligent systems, communications, and beyond, renewing American technological leadership and opening a new chapter in American manufacturing.”
- Sergey Brin – “For the development of foundational algorithms for information retrieval and data processing that revolutionized how the world accesses information across science, commerce, and in the course of everyday life.”
- Jensen Huang – “For advancing the graphics processing unit into a general-purpose computing architecture through innovations in processor design and software, transforming massively parallel computation and powering breakthroughs in scientific computing and super intelligence.”
- Lisa Su – “For a lifetime of leadership in semiconductor engineering and high-performance computing through innovations in processor architecture and chiplet-based integration that powered the world’s first exascale supercomputer and opened new frontiers in computational performance.”
Recipients of the National Medal of Technology and Innovation
- Michael Dell – “For advancing a vision of widespread adoption of personal and enterprise computing; for his technical and business management skills building a worldwide technology company; and for his support for the next generation of American scientists, engineers, and technologists.”
- Satya Nadella – “For his transformative leadership of a critical American technology company, which led to its rejuvenation for a new era of cloud computing, and for his construction of the hyperscale infrastructure that enabled the training and global deployment of American super intelligence.”
“Each of these medalists has transformed their field or industry, laying the foundations for technologies we already can barely imagine living without,” said Michael Kratsios, Assistant to the President and Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy. “While we in government work to deliver the efforts a New Golden Age of Science will require, we know that scientific progress and technological innovation depend on the insight and character of individuals. Innovators like these six awardees are the architects of the future.”
About the Science: A New Golden Age Summit:
Science: A New Golden Age, released in July 2026 by White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios, is the first comprehensive rethinking of the U.S. science and technology enterprise since Vannevar Bush’s 1945 Science: The Endless Frontier.
The report observes significant changes to how scientific discovery happens today, particularly the increased role of industry in driving R&D and the close integration of applied and foundational research. It provides concrete recommendations for how government, industry, academia, and philanthropy can seize the opportunities presented by these changes to accelerate scientific discovery and empower the Nation’s best and brightest scientists. Core recommendations include strengthening support for early-career scientists, reviving the national pursuit of ambitious scientific missions, launching new funding and organizational models for transformative research, building the metascience infrastructure to continuously improve the research enterprise, and scaling SI-driven scientific discovery through the Genesis Mission.
The Science: A New Golden Age Summit convenes leading scientists and innovators to examine these changes and translate the report’s ideas into the next chapter of American scientific progress. Throughout the day, the Trump Administration will provide major announcements, in coordination with private sector partners and research institutions, to realize the vision of Science: A New Golden Age and the Kyoto Vision for a Golden Age of Science.
title: President Trump Presents National Medals of Science and National Medals of Technology and Innovation

Ex-Boyfriend Wanted for Pushing Mom and Baby From Balcony Apprehended
For immediate release
Tracy Amaladas, Supervisory Deputy U.S. Marshal
Washington, DC – Members of the U.S. Marshals Service in the Southern District of New York, alongside the New York/New Jersey Regional Fugitive Task Force, arrested Angel Carrasco today in connection with a Bronx, New York, incident that left a woman dead and an infant critically injured.
Carrasco was taken into custody safely following an intensive investigation that began yesterday when the U.S. Marshals Service took on the case. The team began searching for Carrasco after he allegedly pushed a mother and baby from a 15th- floor Bronx apartment balcony on Tuesday. According to witnesses, the mother begged the suspect to stop before plummeting to the ground.
“This horrific tragedy weighs heavily on every team member who worked this case,” said U.S. Marshal Ricky J. Patel. “We owed it to the brave mother who gave her life to save her child from a vicious individual. While nothing can undo this terrible loss, taking this suspect off the street ensures he will answer for his alleged heinous actions.”
The NY/NJ RFTF began operations in April 2002 and was the first regional fugitive task force to become fully operational following the Presidential Threat Protection Act of 2000. The NY/NJ RFTF was the flagship that has allowed seven other regional fugitive task forces to be created across the country. With partnership agreements with over 90 federal, state, or local agencies and 13 fully operational offices, the NY/NJ RFTF has successfully apprehended over 95,000 fugitives since inception.

text:
Reps. Tlaib and Green lead letter demanding release of DACA recipient in ICE custody
WASHINGTON – U.S. Reps. Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) and Al Green (TX-09), joined by 21 Members of Congress, demanded the release of Ya’akub Ira Vijandre, who was detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement a year ago as of yesterday. In a letter to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and ICE Acting Director David Venturella, the Members pressed for answers regarding Ya’akub’s unconstitutional arrest and prolonged detention after a federal judge allowed his habeas challenge to proceed.
Ya’akub, a Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals recipient, has lived in the U.S. since he was 14 years old. He spent a decade working for American Airlines as a senior safety specialist and was recognized for supporting grieving families after a helicopter crashed into a plane in Washington, D.C. Despite having no criminal record and not being charged with any crime, he was targeted and arrested at gun point for speaking out against Israel’s genocide in Gaza and for “liking” a social media post with Quranic verses–both of which are protected by the First Amendment.
“The administration’s stated basis for [Ya’akub’s] detention has been inconsistent and appears to rely substantially on his speech and social media activity,” the Members wrote. “DHS has sought to justify his detention by citing his social media commentary regarding the prosecutions of the Holy Land Foundation Five, his criticism of the treatment of Guantanamo detainees, his advocacy for Palestine, and his engagement with religious Islamic content, including ‘liking’ Instagram posts containing Quranic verses. We are deeply concerned that constitutionally protected political and religious expression is being used as a basis for his continued detention or deportation.”
The letter renews concerns and questions from a letter Rep. Green sent in June. Rep. Tlaib also spoke on the House floor urging for Ya’akub’s release in August.
“We are also concerned by reports, previously flagged in Congressman Green’s June letter, that the FBI approached Mr. Vijandre in November 2023 seeking his cooperation as a confidential informant and that he declined,” the Members continued in their letter. “His DACA status, renewed as recently as May 2024 through May 2026, was subsequently revoked. The proximity and sequence of these events—an FBI approach he declined, followed by a DACA termination and detention grounded largely in the government’s characterization of his religious and political speech—continue to raise serious questions about possible retaliation that Congress has not yet received satisfactory answers to.”

Tlaib and Green, was signed by 21 other Members of Congress: Greg Casar (TX–35), Judy Chu (CA-28), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Henry C. “Hank” Johnson, Jr. (GA-04), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Summer Lee (PA-12), Analilia Mejia (NJ-11), Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), Ilhan Omar (MN-05), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Emily Randall (WA-06), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Nydia Velázquez (NY-07), Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12).

Tallahassee, Florida – Marlo G. Davis, 47, of Tallahassee, Florida, pleaded guilty in federal court to possession with intent to distribute cocaine and cocaine base, carrying a firearm during a drug-trafficking crime, and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. The plea was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida.

U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “Thanks to the excellent investigative work by the Tallahassee Police Department, and this successful prosecution by my office, we will ensure this serial felon is kept locked away in federal prison for continuing to victimize our community with his criminality. By now it should be abundantly clear that my office is committed to aggressively prosecuting anyone who dares to violate the law in our community, and we will deliver the safe, drug-free streets that our citizens deserve by keeping dangerous felons, like this defendant, behind federal bars where they belong.”

Court documents reflect that officers with the Tallahassee Police Department were conducting surveillance when they saw the defendant and his brother get into a vehicle. The defendant’s brother did not have a valid driver’s license, so they conducted a traffic stop, during which the defendant fled from the vehicle on foot.

Officers chased the defendant and saw him remove a bag from around his chest while he was running:

Officers ultimately caught the defendant and retrieved the bag he discarded during the chase, which was found to contain a Taurus 9-millimeter pistol and drug paraphernalia.

Inside the vehicle, officers found multiple baggies of white powder concealed within an ice cream pint container; a bag containing crack cocaine; and two other sandwich baggies containing white powder. There were a total of 39 bags containing a total of 3.4 grams of alpha-PV10 (a synthetic cathinone). Another eight bags were found to contain a total of 3.9 grams of cocaine. In the larger bags, there were 2.5 grams of alpha-PV10, 13.1 grams of crack cocaine, and 1.2 grams of powder cocaine. The defendant made post- Miranda admissions that he was selling drugs and a review of material from his cellphone found multiple photographs of the same ice cream tub found in the car, including photographs of crack cocaine with the ice cream tub lid visible in the background.

The defendant is a convicted felon who faces an enhanced sentence because of prior convictions for robbery, two separate incidents of possession of cocaine with intent to sell, and trafficking in both hydrocodone and oxycodone. Based on his prior convictions, the defendant faces between 20 years’ to life imprisonment.

Sentencing is scheduled for December 10, 2026, at 2:00 pm, in the United States Courthouse in Tallahassee before United States District Judge Mark E. Walker.

The case involved an investigation by the Tallahassee Police Department and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, with assistance from the Drug Enforcement Administration. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney James A. McCain.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities .

The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl .
title: Federal Guilty Plea by Armed Tallahassee Drug Trafficker

MOBILE, AL – A Foley man was sentenced to 180 months in prison for participating in a methamphetamine-trafficking conspiracy and possessing firearms in furtherance of a drug-trafficking crime.

According to court documents, Christopher Charles Rogers, 51, sold methamphetamine to a confidential informant at his trailer in Foley on two occasions in January and February 2025. On February 11, 2025, narcotics agents surveilled Rogers as he drove from Baldwin County to Pensacola, Florida to purchase a new supply of methamphetamine. Agents coordinated with sheriff’s deputies, who conducted a traffic stop of Rogers’s truck on the Foley Beach Express. During the traffic stop, Rogers admitted that he had previously served federal prison time for being a convicted felon in possession of a firearm.

Deputies arrested Rogers on warrants relating to his drug sales to the confidential informant. Deputies also searched Rogers’s truck and found 139.18 grams of 99.4% pure methamphetamine in the center console. In a subsequent interview, Rogers confirmed that he had bought the methamphetamine from a supplier in Pensacola for $875 and intended to re-sell it for $175 per ounce. Rogers said he never bought less than four ounces at a time, and sometimes bought up to eight ounces, which he regularly sold to various customers in smaller amounts. Rogers said he had customers waiting on him when deputies arrested him. Rogers further admitted that he had several guns at his trailer, which he allowed deputies to search.

In Rogers’s trailer, agents found additional baggies of methamphetamine and several loaded pistols and rifles. Rogers admitted that he possessed the guns. The total amount of methamphetamine seized from Rogers’s truck and trailer was 161.5 grams.

In August 2026, while on conditions of release pending his sentencing in federal court, Rogers admitted to using methamphetamine twice and had his conditions of release revoked by the court.

In addition to the 180-month prison term, U.S. District Judge Terry F. Moorer ordered Rogers to serve a five-year supervised release term upon his release from prison, during which time he will be subject to drug testing and treatment. The court did not impose a fine, but Judge Moorer ordered Rogers to pay $200 in special assessments and forfeited his firearms to the United States.

U.S. Attorney Sean P. Costello of the Southern District of Alabama made the announcement.

Homeland Security Investigations, the Drug Enforcement Administration, and the Baldwin County Sheriff’s Office investigated the case. The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and the U.S. Customs and Border Protection Laboratory in Long Beach, California substantially assisted the investigation.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Justin Roller prosecuted the case on behalf of the United States.

This prosecution was part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Mobile comprises agents and officers from, among others, Homeland Security Investigations, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Drug Enforcement Administration, and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Alabama.
title: Armed Foley Methamphetamine Trafficker Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison in Homeland Security Task Force Case

MUSKOGEE, OKLAHOMA – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Oklahoma announced that Steven Ray Quigley, a/k/a Steven Woods, age 39, of Muskogee, Oklahoma, was sentenced to 15 months in prison for one count of Failure to Register as Sex Offender.

The charge arose from an investigation by the U.S. Marshals Service Violent Crimes Fugitive Task Force.

On July 8, 2025, Quigley pleaded guilty to the charge. According to investigators, Quigley was convicted by the State of Oklahoma of Lewd or Indecent Acts to Child Under 16 in Mayes County on October 11, 2012, and was required to register as a sex offender, and that from May 2022 until May 22, 2026, Quigley failed to register and update his registration despite entering, leaving, or residing in Indian Country within the Eastern District of Oklahoma.

The Honorable Ronald A. White, Senior Judge in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Oklahoma, presided over the hearing. Quigley will remain in the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service pending transportation to a designated United States Bureau of Prisons facility to serve a non-paroleable sentence of incarceration.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Morgan Muzljakovich and Nicole Paladino represented the United States.

Today, National Labor Relations Board General Counsel Crystal S. Carey has appointed Danielle Lucido as the Regional Attorney for the National Labor Relations Board, Region 32, with its office located in Oakland, California. In her position, Ms. Lucido will serve as the chief legal officer of the regional office and assist Regional Director Christy J. Kwon in the administration and enforcement of the National Labor Relations Act in part of northern California, central California, and Northern Nevada. The NLRB conducts hundreds of workplace elections and investigates thousands of unfair labor practice charges each year.

CLARKSBURG, WEST VIRGINIA — A former college basketball player and Estonian national has admitted to carrying out a fraud scheme totaling millions of dollars, U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey announced today.

Kerr Kriisa, 25, pleaded guilty to a single count of wire fraud. According to the plea agreement, he sent one of the victims an email in February 2026 holding himself out to be “Irene,” a fictious email he created to further his scheme to defraud. In the email, he demanded a payment of $9,000 to avoid litigation and publicity regarding a financial dispute “Irene” had with him.

“Financial fraud is not a game, and those who choose to deceive and exploit others will be held accountable. Mr. Kriisa’s years‑long scheme caused real harm, and today’s plea underscores that this office will pursue anyone who engages in conduct like this, regardless of any notoriety or success they may have achieved. We will continue to stand with our law‑enforcement partners to uncover fraud, defend victims, and ensure that offenders face serious federal consequences,” said U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey.

“Financial fraud is not a game, and those who choose to deceive and exploit others will be held accountable. Mr. Kriisa’s years‑long scheme caused real harm, and today’s plea underscores that this office will pursue anyone who engages in conduct like this, regardless of any notoriety or success they may have achieved. We will continue to stand with our law‑enforcement partners to uncover fraud, defend victims, and ensure that offenders face serious federal consequences,” said U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey.

According to the indictment, the February 2026 incident was one of many acts Kriisa took to defraud two individuals of millions of dollars in a scheme dating back to at least 2022 when Kriisa played basketball for the University of Arizona. For example, the indictment alleged that Kriisa repeatedly sought payments from two victims and, at times, instructed one victim to transfer money to the other under false pretenses and once fraudulently signed an agreement promising to repay one of the victims but never did.

Kriisa previously played basketball for the University of Arizona, West Virginia University, the University of Kentucky, and the University of Cincinnati.

Kriisa is scheduled to be sentenced on December 22, 2026.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Jarod Douglas is prosecuting the case, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation is conducting the investigation.

U.S. Magistrate Judge Michael John Aloi presided.

Rep. Jim Costa, Bipartisan Colleagues Introduce Resolution Recognizing National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Representatives Jim Costa (CA-21), John Larson (CT-01), Paul Tonko (NY-20), David Valadao (CA-22), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), and Gus Bilirakis (FL-12) introduced H.Res. 1611, a bipartisan resolution designating October 8, 2026, as "National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day."
"Hydrogen and fuel cell technologies are an important part of America’s energy future,” said Congressman Costa. "By investing in American innovation, we can strengthen our energy security, build a more reliable and resilient grid, create good-paying jobs, and reduce emissions. The United States has long been a leader in developing these technologies, and this bipartisan resolution recognizes the work being done across the country to ensure we continue leading the way."
"Connecticut continues to lead the nation as a hub for the research and development of clean hydrogen and fuel cell technologies," said Congressman Larson. "For years, I have worked across the aisle to enact tax incentives to boost hydrogen production and invest federal funding to grow our fuel cell economy, unleash the power of American-made clean energy, and reduce emissions. As we recognize the twelfth annual National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day, we must work together on real solutions to lower costs for consumers and grow the clean energy supply chain across the country."
"Supporting clean hydrogen unlocks a wealth of benefits — boosting our economy, protecting energy security, and reducing emissions," Congressman Tonko said. "Throughout my time in Congress, I’ve worked to advance legislation that invests in energy innovation and lowers costs, which is why I’m proud to join my colleagues to introduce this bipartisan resolution and support a stronger, healthier, more competitive nation."
"I’m proud to join my colleagues in reintroducing a bipartisan resolution designating October 8th as National Hydrogen Fuel Cell Day. Advancing these technologies is critical to strengthening our nation’s energy independence, driving continued innovation, and enhancing our energy security. An all-of-the-above energy strategy will help lower energy costs for Central Valley communities while ensuring our farms, businesses, and homes have access to the reliable energy they need to thrive," said Congressman Valadao.
"The question is not whether America will need more energy—it is whether we will lead in producing it. Hydrogen and fuel cell technologies can strengthen our energy security, reinforce the reliability and resilience of our grid, create good-paying American jobs, and help meet growing demand through cleaner, innovative solutions. National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day recognizes the incredible scientists, engineers, manufacturers, and workers driving that progress, and reaffirms our bipartisan commitment to ensuring America continues to lead the world in energy innovation," said Congressman Fitzpatrick.
"Congress has long recognized how hydrogen seamlessly fits into so many of the energy tools in America’s energy portfolio," said Frank Wolak, President and CEO of FCHEA. "Whether a feedstock for low-carbon fertilizer and export fuels such as ammonia or used directly as a fuel on its own to power data centers, heavy-duty trucks, and everything in between, hydrogen helps the U.S. meet growing power demand at home while sustaining leadership in energy markets abroad. We thank Representative Costa and the resolution’s co-sponsors for supporting Hydrogen Day and the U.S. industry at large."
BACKGROUND
National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day is observed annually on October 8 in recognition of hydrogen’s atomic mass of 1.008. The day highlights the role hydrogen and fuel cell technologies play in American energy production, transportation, grid reliability, and economic growth.
The United States produces and uses approximately 10 million metric tons of hydrogen each year. Hydrogen can be derived from a variety of domestic resources and used to store energy, while fuel cell technologies are used for transportation, stationary power, and backup power.
U.S. Representatives Jim Costa (CA-21), John Larson (CT-01), Paul Tonko (NY-20), David Valadao (CA-22), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), and Gus Bilirakis (FL-12) are co-leads of the House Resolution, with Representatives Mike Lawler (NY-17), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), and Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) joining as original co-sponsors.
Senator Richard Blumenthal (CT) led the introduction of the Senate Resolution, with Senators Bill Cassidy (LA), Chris Coons (DE), and Chris Murphy (CT) joining as original cosponsors.
title: Rep. Jim Costa, Bipartisan Colleagues Introduce Resolution Recognizing National Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Day

Ocasio-Cortez Statement on ICE Shooting in Marble Hill
NEW YORK – Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14) released the following statement tonight after federal agents shot and injured a New Yorker in Marble Hill on Thursday.
“Today in Marble Hill, ICE agents fired multiple shots at a man in his vehicle while his 5-year-old child was in the back seat.
“ICE’s already unwelcome presence in our city has been growing more escalatory and dangerous by the day. Today’s shooting is a grave development that requires a swift and immediate response to protect the safety of all New Yorkers.
“First, we must have a full and independent investigation of this incident.
“There must also be a full and immediate release of all body camera footage of the incident.
“In addition, the Target Corporation must stop offering their Bronx properties as private staging sites for ICE, in compliance with requests from New York officials. Target opening up large, active retail parking lots for paramilitary activity is unacceptable and places the entire community at risk.
“ICE is a rogue, lawless paramilitary and surveillance agency. It does not belong in New York City and it should not exist in the United States of America. Abolish ICE.”
###
title: Ocasio-Cortez Statement on ICE Shooting in Marble Hill

NSF lays the foundation for the next generation of technologies and support for American talent
The U.S. National Science Foundation today announced a series of programs and initiatives to support the ambitious vision articulated in the White House report Science: A New Golden Age and in "NSF leadership in a new golden age of science." These new programs and initiatives combined with the $1.5 billion in investments announced in August will help the agency improve how it evaluates and supports science, harness super intelligence to accelerate discovery, and invest in exceptional students and early-career researchers.
NSF is establishing an Office of Metascience to serve as a testbed for studying how scientific communities respond to novel review and funding mechanisms, applying those lessons learned to NSF programs to accelerate discovery. The office will operate with full transparency, sharing its experiments and findings with academia, industry, and philanthropy. A job announcement for the head of the Office of Metascience will be forthcoming.
In addition, both UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) and NSF intend to build on the metascience principles that the United States has outlined in the "Kyoto Vision for a Golden Age of Science," and that both agencies have articulated in, respectively, the "NSF leadership in a new golden age of science" memorandum and the UKRI Strategy 2026-31.
NSF is launching two Grand Research Challenge (GRC) prize competitions to facilitate cross-disciplinary collaboration, attract nontraditional entrants, and form cross-sector teams to spur rapid advances in scientific understanding in crucial areas of science and technology (S&T).
The first is the Quantum+X GRC that will accelerate quantum innovation for sectors like energy, biotechnology, and finance. U.S. participants will be invited to compete and showcase algorithm and application solutions that could redefine what quantum technology makes possible. Through an NSF partnership with industry, competing teams will be able to develop solutions to sector-relevant problems that will not only impact the economy but also advance solutions to fundamental questions in fields such as chemistry, mathematics, and materials science.
The second is the Synthetic Multicellularity Grand Challenge prize, a competition that will transform the ability to design biology. U.S. participants will be invited to compete in a multistage challenge to showcase new computational and experimental approaches in synthetic and engineering biology that expand capabilities to incorporate complexity and regulation into the design of multicellular systems. The results of this competition will advance our understanding of cell biology, development, and aging, and lead to new applications across sectors from medicine to biomanufacturing.
NSF is also launching the new NSF X-Labs Consortium with an initial set of founding partners representing over $300 million in commitments, supporting teams with floor space, instrument access, and direct support. This consortium is designed to provide resources to NSF X-Labs, a new generation of organizations enabling independent teams of researchers, technologists, and entrepreneurs pursuing milestone-based federal funding to solve specific scientific and technological challenges. The founding partners include research institutions, advanced computing centers, philanthropy, and industry, which will provide critical resources such as access to physical space, scientific instruments and infrastructure, and expertise, to catalyze and expedite the impact of the NSF X-Labs initiative.
In addition, in collaboration with several industry and philanthropic partners, NSF will soon release a funding opportunity tied to the NSF Programmable Cloud Laboratories Network (NSF PCLNet) announced in July 2026, with a specific focus on the development of Super Intelligence-Native Instruments (SINI). The eventual SINI awardees will enhance NSF PCLNet by incorporating instruments specifically designed for the modern era of data and super intelligence in their designs and architecture, meaning that the instruments are digital-first. This re-envisioning signals a significant advance in the automation of science and engineering solutions and the era of super intelligence-driven scientific discovery and innovation. NSF anticipates an investment of up to $75 million over the next five years.
"NSF leadership in a new golden age of science" makes clear the imperative for a merit-first approach to identify and develop the exceptionally talented Americans who will serve as the vanguard of U.S. S&T global leadership in the coming decades. To support those goals, NSF is investing in the National Math Stars and NextGen Workforce to open more scientific and technical career pathways for more talented Americans.
NSF's investment of $30 million over four years in National Math Stars, fully matched by private philanthropy, will help grow talent identification and advanced STEM enrichment programs and support the design and testing of a scalable digital platform to assist families in supporting children grades 3–12 to achieve their full potential in math.
The NextGen Workforce program will help students earning STEM doctoral degrees reach the frontier faster than ever before and make STEM Ph.D.s a desirable pathway for America's most talented students. The program will develop new accelerated ;6-year bachelor's to doctoral degree programs and innovative, interdisciplinary graduate training programs that provide direct support for enrolled students and meet critical and emerging national STEM workforce needs.
More details about all these programs and initiatives will be available in the coming days.
title: NSF lays the foundation for the next generation of technologies and support for American talent

RALEIGH N.C. – A federal judge sentenced Joseph Tyre Cumberlander, also known as “X Suave”, 31, to 25 years in federal prison for possession with intent to distribute crack cocaine. Cumberlander pleaded guilty in federal court on June 23, 2026.

“This criminal made a career as a scourge to Raleigh, peddling poison in the streets with impunity. He refuses to learn his lesson. The jury’s verdict spoke the truth, and the Court’s sentence sent a clear message: the good citizens of Eastern North Carolina will not tolerate this behavior. Go sell drugs somewhere else, stay out of the EDNC,” said U.S. Attorney Ellis Boyle.

“This criminal made a career as a scourge to Raleigh, peddling poison in the streets with impunity. He refuses to learn his lesson. The jury’s verdict spoke the truth, and the Court’s sentence sent a clear message: the good citizens of Eastern North Carolina will not tolerate this behavior. Go sell drugs somewhere else, stay out of the EDNC,” said U.S. Attorney Ellis Boyle.

On January 12, 2025, Raleigh Police Department officers saw Cumberlander—an identified Bloods gang member and drug dealer—sitting in a caron the 500 block of Bragg Street. As officers approached, he sped off. During the chase, he threw about 35.4 grams of crack cocaine out of the window before officers arrested him. A search of his car turned up $882 in cash and a digital scale used to weigh drugs. Cumberlander was arrested but bonded out shortly thereafter.

On May 22, 2025, as RPD officers monitored a camera near Mangum and Bragg Streets they watched Cumberlander make several hand‑to‑hand drug transactions and hide a small bag under a water bottle. When officers moved in, he dropped 0.83 grams of crack cocaine. Officers recovered another 1.69 grams under the water bottle and found an additional 8.72 grams hidden inside a nearby fence post. Once again, they arrested Cumberlander and seized $678 in cash.

Cumberlander has an extensive criminal history, including convictions for possessing stolen firearms, firing a gun within city limits, possessing a firearm as a convicted felon, and possessing with intent to sell cocaine and marijuana.

“The Raleigh Police Department extends its sincere gratitude to our exceptional public safety partners whose dedication and teamwork were instrumental throughout this investigation. Together, we worked to identify and remove a violent offender from our community, disrupt criminal activity, and protect the people we serve,” said Raleigh Police Chief Rico Boyce. “We are especially grateful for our strong partnership with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of North Carolina. This collaboration reflects our shared commitment to holding violent offenders accountable and making our community safer.”

This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations, and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

Ellis Boyle, U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of North Carolina made the announcement after sentencing by U.S. District Judge James C. Dever III. The ATF and the Raleigh Police Department investigated the case.

A copy of this press release is located on our website . Related court documents and information can be found on the website of the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of North Carolina or on PACER by searching for Case No. 5:25CR00246D-001.

Edenilson Alexander Castaneda-Del Valle, age 19, of El Salvador, who is present in the United States without authorization, pleaded guilty before United States District Judge John W. deGravelles to possession with the intent to distribute 500 grams or more of methamphetamine.

If convicted, Castaneda-Del Valle faces a sentence of imprisonment which may not be less than 10 years and up to life and a fine of up to $10,000,000.

According to admissions made during his plea, on February 7, 2026, a Livingston Parish Sheriff’s Criminal Patrol K-9 Deputy conducted a traffic stop on Interstate 12 on a 2017 Jaguar Model XE which was occupied by two individuals. The passenger was identified as Castaneda-Del Valle.

The deputy, having been previously informed by other law enforcement agencies that the 2017 Jaguar Model XE contained a hidden compartment or “trap,” which is commonly used to conceal illegal drugs or money, asked for consent to search the vehicle, which the driver granted. A U.S. Department of Homeland Security Task Force Officer (HSI-TFO) arrived to assist. Both officers quickly located the hidden trap under the vehicle’s center console.

In plain view in the back seat of the car were three backpacks, and one large black garbage bag. When the HSI-TFO moved the garbage bag to look for an additional entrance to the trap, he felt cabbage sized bundles through the outside of the plastic garbage bag and also detected a chemical order coming from the contents of the plastic bag. Based upon his training and experience, he immediately suspected the plastic bag contained contraband. After completing the seizure, it was determined that there were approximately 361 pounds of methamphetamine with a street value estimated at just under $4,000,000.

Additionally, officers found two digital scales, several boxes of plastic baggies, a box of plastic garbage bags that matched the plastic bags that contained the bundles in the green plastic film, a bag of rubber bands, and $7,155 in U.S. Currency. Approximately $5,000 of the currency, all $100 bills, was in three stacks, rubber-banded together. At least one of the stacks was in a backpack that also contained the driver’s license and El Salvadorian Passport for Castaneda Del Valle.

U.S. Attorney Kurt Wall praised the work of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security – Homeland Security Investigations, Livingston Parish Sheriff’s Office, and Assistant U.S. Attorney Lyman E. Thornton III.

“These agencies did an excellent job of intercepting those drugs. They quickly got the case to our office, and it was indicted within four days of the arrest,” Wall said. “Our priority is the total elimination of these drug trafficking organizations. We will move quickly and effectively to achieve those goals, and this is an example of what’s to come.”

This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF New Orleans comprises agents and officers from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Homeland Security Investigations (HSl), the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives (ATF), and the United States Marshals Service (USMS), Us. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Enforcement and Removal Operations (ICE-ERO), the Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI), the United States Postal Inspection Service (USPIS), the U.S. Coast Guard, Investigative Service (CGlS), U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Office of Field Operations (CBP OFO), U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Us. Border Patrol (CBP BP) with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney's Office for Middle District of Louisiana.

text:
Ukrainian-Russian Dual Citizen Pleads Guilty to Running International Money Laundering Organization for Cybercriminals
Oleg Korniev, 42, a dual citizen of Ukraine and Russia, pleaded guilty today to running a sophisticated international money laundering organization that laundered millions of dollars stolen from United States victims by cybercriminals around the world. In total, this international criminal organization recruited over 15,000 U.S.-based money mules to launder at least $10 million stolen by hackers from over 750 U.S. bank accounts.
“Money mules play crucial roles in cybercrime, so the Justice Department pursues mules and their recruiters wherever they operate and however long it takes,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Alongside our international partners, we will dismantle criminal networks that attack Americans. No amount of distance or time puts these criminals beyond the reach of justice.”
“Just because you are outside the borders of the United States does not mean you will get away with defrauding U.S. Citizens and businesses,” said U.S. Attorney Russ Ferguson for the Western District of North Carolina. “We will work hard to bring you to justice, as we did in this case.”
“For years, the FBI has worked tirelessly to unravel the layers of this international money laundering operation and bring Mr. Korniev to justice,” said Special Agent in Charge Reid Davis of FBI North Carolina. “This case reflects the Bureau’s enduring commitment to following the evidence — no matter how long it takes, how far it leads, or how deliberately criminals try to hide behind borders and technology. We will continue pursuing those who enable cybercriminals until every responsible individual is held to account.”
According to court documents, Korniev was one of the leaders of Your Mule Cashout (YMCO). YMCO created, maintained, and operated an elaborate and sophisticated system of money mules and internet infrastructure that allowed computer hackers, who had stolen money from the bank accounts of U.S. companies, to conceal the thefts and transfer the stolen money to countries outside the U.S. YMCO’s services operated through online infrastructure that allowed hackers to move the stolen money to countries primarily in Eastern Europe by paying YMCO a percentage of the money stolen.
YMCO provided its money laundering services through money mules who were U.S. residents deceived by YMCO into believing that they were working for legitimate companies and making genuine money transfers. YMCO falsely represented that the money mules’ job was to receive payments from businesses into their personal bank accounts, withdraw the money, and then wire the funds to the fake company’s partners overseas. The money mules instead processed the hackers’ stolen proceeds and wired them out of the country to other YMCO conspirators. The money mules never received payment for their services.
Korniev helped develop YMCO’s policies and procedures; managed, hired, and fired employees; rewarded and punished employees based on performance; and secured illegal services supporting YMCO. As part of his plea, Korniev admitted that YMCO was responsible for over $14.7 million in actual and intended losses by confirmed victims and that he intended to launder over $9.7 million from cybercriminals and did launder at least $7 million. Korniev also agreed to provide full restitution to known victims to compensate them for their actual losses as well as forfeit cash seized from him when he was arrested in the Republic of Georgia.
Korniev pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering, money laundering, conspiracy to commit computer fraud, conspiracy to commit access device theft, and aggravated identity theft. Sentencing will be set at a later date. He faces a minimum penalty of two years in prison and maximum penalty of 50 years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine Korniev’s sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other factors.
Previously, four other individuals involved with YMCO were arrested overseas, extradited to the Western District of North Carolina, and pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering. They received sentences ranging from around 37 months to 63 months in prison and the court ordered each defendant to pay over $9.1 million in restitution to numerous U.S. victims.
The FBI is investigating the case.
Senior Counsel Matthew A. Lamberti of the Criminal Division’s Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Matthew Warren for the Western District of North Carolina are prosecuting the case. The Department of Justice’s Office of International Affairs, the FBI Office of the Law Enforcement Attache in Tbilisi, and law enforcement authorities in Georgia, including the Prosecutor’s Office of Georgia, provided significant assistance.
CCIPS investigates and prosecutes cybercrime and intellectual property (IP) crime in coordination with domestic and international law enforcement agencies, often with assistance from the private sector. Since 2020, CCIPS has secured the conviction of over 180 cyber and IP criminals, and court orders for the return of over $350 million in victim funds.
title: Ukrainian-Russian Dual Citizen Pleads Guilty to Running International Money Laundering Organization for Cybercriminals

Rep. Subramanyam Issues Statement on USS Lincoln’s Return
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Representative Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10), Ranking Member of the Military and Foreign Affairs Oversight Subcommittee, issued the following statement on USS Abraham Lincoln’s return home after the end of a record long deployment.
“I am thankful for the return of the servicemembers aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln. They and their families have paid an unnecessary cost for Trump’s endless war of choice with Iran. They deserve all of our respect and support. During the USS Lincoln’s deployment, servicemembers endured a record number of days without a port call. They faced insufficient amounts of food, unfit living conditions, and inadequate mental health support. I will continue to advocate for the respect and safety of our troops. We have a duty to make sure this never happens again by holding the Pentagon accountable, ” said Ranking Member Subramanyam.
In August of this year, Oversight Ranking Member Robert Garcia and Congressman Suhas Subramanyam demanded answers from the Department of Defense (DOD) about conditions on the USS Lincoln. In the letter to DOD Secretary Hegseth, the Ranking Members asked for information on the inventory of food, medical supplies, and other critical resources for the sailors and Marines. They also asked for clarification on the timeline of when the USS Lincoln would be relieved by another aircraft carrier.
The letter can be found HERE and below. 
###
Dear Secretary Hegseth:
We write regarding the conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, specifically, the living conditions and access to mental health resources for the sailors. Recent reports have revealed disturbing sanitation conditions, food shortages, and deteriorating mental health among those deployed on the aircraft carrier, including multiple suicide attempts, with one sailor jumping overboard. Our sailors deserve better while they serve our country, and these deplorable conditions negatively impact morale and readiness. As Members of Congress, we have a duty to support our troops, and it is clear that additional oversight is needed aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln.
The USS Abraham Lincoln holds more than 5,000 sailors and Marines and departed San Diego last November. Now redirected to the Middle East to support the Iran War in Operation Epic Fury, the carrier has been deployed for over 250 days and has spent a record-setting 200 consecutive days at sea. At a town hall with Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, families of those aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln voiced their concerns directly. Among them were food shortages, water contamination, and disruptions in mail.
As the Ranking Members of the Oversight Committee and the Oversight Committee’s Subcommittee on Military and Foreign Affairs, we request a classified briefing on the USS Abraham Lincoln’s conditions and answers to the following questions by August 28, 2026:
- What is the current inventory of food aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln?
- Please detail the food supply and delivery schedule over the course of the carrier’s deployment.
- What sanitation issues have been identified aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, including broken bathroom facilities?
- What health care, including mental health care, are available to the sailors aboard?
- What behavioral health care professionals are on board and accessible to those seeking help?
- How quickly can someone on board the ship meet with a behavioral health care professional after seeking help?
- What steps can be taken to mitigate the disruptions to the mail system that sailors have experienced?
- Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao reportedly told family members that the USS Theodore Roosevelt is preparing to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln. Without jeopardizing national security, what details can be shared about the timeline for the ship’s relief?
The Committee on Oversight and Government Reform is the principal oversight committee of the House of Representatives and has broad authority to investigate “any matter” at “any time” under House Rule X. If you have any questions about this request, please contact Committee Democratic staff at (202) 225-5051. Thank you for your prompt attention to this request.
title: Rep. Subramanyam Issues Statement on USS Lincoln’s Return

The Federal Trade Commission is sending more than $15.8 million to consumers impacted by cash advance app company Cleo AI’s deceptive claims about the amounts and timing of available cash advances and the company’s hard-to-cancel subscriptions.
The FTC’s March 2025 complaint alleged that Cleo AI misled consumers with promises of fast money, advertising access to “hundreds of dollars” in cash advances when almost no one received even close to the advertised amounts. The agency also alleged that Cleo charged additional hidden fees for same-day or instant cash advances that often would not arrive until the next day and that the defendant made it difficult for users to cancel their subscriptions.
The FTC plans to send payments to 2,124,796 Cleo AI customers who paid for eligible instant cash advances. Consumers who are eligible for a payment will get an email between now and October 26, 2026. The FTC will begin sending PayPal payments on October 27, 2026. Recipients should redeem their PayPal payment within 30 days.
Consumers who have questions about their payment should contact the refund administrator, Rust Consulting Inc., at 877 788 4958, or visit the FTC website to view frequently asked questions about the refund process. The Commission never requires people to pay money or provide account information to receive a payment.
The Commission’s interactive dashboards for redress data provide a state-by-state breakdown of redress in FTC cases. In 2025, FTC actions led to more than $435 million in redress to consumers across the country.
The Federal Trade Commission works to promote competition and protect and educate consumers. The FTC will never demand money, make threats, tell you to transfer money, or promise you a prize. Learn more about consumer topics at consumer.ftc.gov, or report fraud, scams, and bad business practices at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. Follow the FTC on social media, read consumer alerts and the business blog, and sign up to get the latest FTC news and alerts.
title: FTC Returns More than $15.8 Million to Consumers Misled by Cash Advance App Company Cleo AI

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, the Justice Department and FBI announced court-authorized seizures, including seven domains, to deny access to “Microscan” and “FishHub,” two intrusion tools used by malicious cyber actors to scan and, in some cases, hack U.S. and foreign critical infrastructure systems and other networks. As alleged in court documents unsealed in the Western District of Pennsylvania, cyber actors working for Integrity Technology Group (Integrity Tech), a company based in the People’s Republic of China (PRC), operated and used the tools as part of their hacking activity known to the private sector as “Flax Typhoon.” Integrity Tech has contracts with the PRC government.

“These state-sponsored hackers continue to aggressively target and access networks and systems throughout the world in an effort to identify and steal files and otherwise exploit victims’ vulnerabilities,” said United States Attorney Troy Rivetti of the Western District of Pennsylvania. “These seizures, our second disruption of Integrity Tech’s massive operations in as many years, send another clear message to cybercriminals from the PRC and elsewhere of the Department’s dedication to defending and maintaining cybersecurity in the United States and abroad.”

“The United States will not allow China or its proxies to operate against United States interests with impunity in cyberspace,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “The National Security Division will continue to respond decisively and use every tool at our disposal to disrupt the Flax Typhoon threats, dismantle the infrastructure sustaining them, and protect the critical networks that power our daily lives and on which our Nation’s security depends.”

According to court documents, Integrity Tech created and used a network of internet-connected devices infected with a variant of Mirai malware. Among other things, this botnet employed the Microscan tool to conduct reconnaissance, via the botnet and otherwise, of victim computer networks for vulnerabilities that its clients would later exploit. Integrity Tech was able to access Microscan through one of the seized domains. Targets of Microscan vulnerability scanning included a U.S. power company based in South Carolina, a multi-national Non-Governmental Organization, Japanese and Polish airports, Taiwanese critical infrastructure companies in the natural gas and power sectors, and two Taiwanese universities.

A second Integrity Tech tool, FishHub, is alleged to have facilitated the exploitation of computer networks through spear phishing. After an initial network compromise, FishHub downloaded additional malware to the victim network. This malware, which was delivered through five of the seized domains, provided Integrity Tech’s clients with unauthorized remote access to the victim network or searched for specific files and sent them to servers controlled by Integrity Tech. Confirmed victims of FishHub activity included approximately 20 Taiwanese universities. Additionally, Integrity Tech used an unauthorized remote administration software tied to a seventh seized domain to connect several victims’ networks to an Integrity Tech server.

Today’s action marks the Department’s second public technical disruption of Integrity Tech’s hacking infrastructure. In September 2024, the Justice Department announced the court-authorized disruption of Integrity Tech’s Mirai malware botnet which consisted of more than 200,000 consumer devices in the United States and worldwide. In conjunction with the seizures announced today, the FBI, along with other U.S. and foreign-partner agencies, published a cyber security advisory . This advisory provides indicators-of-compromise associated with Integrity Tech intrusion activity and is designed to help network defenders identify and respond to Integrity Tech’s malicious activity.

“Integrity Technology Group provided China-linked threat actors with capabilities used to conduct widespread vulnerability scanning and, in some cases, intrusions targeting U.S. and foreign critical infrastructure,” said Assistant Director Brett Leatherman of the FBI’s Cyber Division. “The PRC relies on contractor and enabling companies to expand the reach and scale of its malicious cyber activity. By exposing and disrupting these enablers, we make it harder for the PRC to target American networks and infrastructure.”

“Today’s seizures underscore the FBI’s unwavering commitment in disrupting PRC state-sponsored cyber criminals who threaten our critical infrastructure and national security,” said Special Agent in Charge Mark Remily of the FBI San Diego Field Office. “FBI San Diego and our law enforcement partners around the world will continue to employ the full force of our investigative authority to protect the American people and safeguard our networks from malicious foreign cyber actors.”

The FBI San Diego and Baltimore Field Offices are investigating the case, in coordination with the FBI’s Cyber Division.

Assistant United States Attorney Brendan McKenna for the Western District of Pennsylvania and Trial Attorney Jacques Singer-Emery for the National Security Division’s National Security Cyber Section are prosecuting the case. Substantial assistance was provided by Assistant United States Attorney Thomas Sullivan for the District of Maryland and the National Police Agency of Japan.

Note: View the affidavit here .

View the seizure warrant here .
title: Justice Department and FBI Seize Vulnerability Scanning and Spear Phishing Tools Operated and Used by China-State Sponsored Hackers
