GUN VIOLENCE PREVENTION TASK FORCE CHAIR THOMPSON, JUDICIARY COMMITTEE RANKING MEMBER RASKIN AND REP. MCBATH LEAD 174 MEMBERS CALLING ON DOJ TO ENFORCE YOUTH HANDGUN LAW
Washington – Gun Violence Prevention Task Force Chair Mike Thompson, Judiciary Committee Ranking Member Jamie Raskin, and Rep. Lucy McBath lead a bipartisan letter with 174 members calling on the Department of Justice (DOJ) to enforce the 1968 law which prohibits licensed gun dealers from selling handguns to 18-20-year-olds.
“DOJ’s decision to block the enforcement of the 1968 law which prohibits 18-20-year-olds from buying handguns is unconstitutional, and will make our communities, and especially our schools less safe,” said Mike Thompson. “It is outrageous that DOJ would unilaterally overturn the law and allow an 18-year-old high school student to buy a handgun, buy a silencer, and have them shipped to their house without ever leaving their basement. That is just wrong.”
“For generations, the landmark provision prohibiting the sale of handguns to 18-to-20-year-olds has saved countless lives. Yet, now, the Trump Department of Justice has released a baseless opinion that this provision is unconstitutional and cannot be enforced. This reckless decision will allow young adults to obtain the firearms most often used in crime, jeopardizing public safety and putting those most at risk for gun violence in greater danger. Brady thanks Chair Thompson and Ranking Members Raskin and McBath for leading the effort to oppose this senseless decision and for their dedication to protecting America’s youth from gun violence,” said Mark Collins, Director of Federal Policy, Brady.
“The math here is simple: 18- to 20-year-olds commit gun homicides at triple the rate of people 21 and older, which is why more than 80% of Americans want 21 to be the minimum age to buy a gun,” said John Feinblatt, president of Everytown for Gun Safety. “Trump’s MAGA DOJ is handing the gun industry something it could never win in Congress or at the ballot box, and America will pay for it in lives lost and communities shattered.”
"The Office of Legal Counsel has no authority to erase a federal gun law and put more handguns in the hands of teenagers. This decision disregards clear evidence that minimum-age laws save lives,” said GIFFORDS Executive Director EmmaBrown. “The Trump administration must immediately reverse this dangerous action. I thank Representatives Jamie Raskin, Lucy McBath, and Mike Thompson, as well as the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force, for their leadership in defending this lifesaving law.”
The Gun Control Act of 1968 (GCA) passed the House of Representatives and the Senate with bipartisan support and was signed into law by President Johnson in response to the assassinations of President John F. Kennedy, Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., Robert F. Kennedy, and others, and to address a startling increase in gun crimes. For almost six decades, the GCA as a whole has saved countless lives by helping keep firearms out of the hands of high-risk groups, including not only Americans in the 18-to-20-year-old cohort but people who pose a danger to themselves or others. Expanding access to concealable firearms like handguns creates a significant public safety risk as the majority of gun crimes involve handguns.
The full text of the letter can be found HERE and below.
Dear Attorney General Blanche,
We urge the Department of Justice to immediately rescind its opinion illegally declaring that a 1968 law prohibiting the sale of handguns to 18-to-20-year-olds by federally licensed firearms dealers “may not be enforced.”
Since the passage of the Gun Control Act of 1968 some 58 years ago, the Department of Justice (DOJ) has faithfully enforced it according to clear congressional intent and defended its constitutionality. The Supreme Court has never questioned, much less invalidated, this statute. Its policy rationale—that 18-to-20-year-olds lack the cognitive judgment required to safely own and handle handguns has only grown more compelling with advancements in our understanding of brain development over the last six decades and the record of gun violence already associated with that age group.
The Gun Control Act of 1968 (GCA) passed the House of Representatives and the Senate with bipartisan support, and was signed into law by President Johnson in response to the assassinations of President John F. Kennedy, Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., Robert F. Kennedy, and others, and to address a startling increase in gun crimes. For almost six decades, the GCA as a whole has saved countless lives by helping keep firearms out of the hands of high-risk groups, including not only Americans in the 18-to-20-year-old cohort but people who pose a danger to themselves or others.
DOJ’s sudden epiphany that this essential law, which has been enforced by Democratic and Republican Attorneys General continuously for more than a half-century, is unconstitutional would override the judgment of the last 29 Congresses, which have staunchly stood by the law. Your personal reinterpretation would now allow 18-to-20-year-olds to purchase easily concealable handguns, a kind disproportionately used in violent crimes.
We already have a problem with young men in the 18-20 year range obtaining a firearm from family, friends or the criminal underground and using it to conduct a mass shooting. Millions of Americans remember when a 20-year-old gunman in Newtown, Connecticut killed 27 people, overwhelmingly children, in the deadliest elementary school massacre in American history. According to a study published in the American Journal of Public Health, one in eight mass shooters was between 18 and 20 years old.[1] Indeed, 18-to-20-year-olds have already been shown to be responsible for a disproportionate share of school shootings. [2] In fact, they comprise just 4 percent of the US population, but account for 17 percent of known gun homicide offenders generally. [3]
Teens and young adults are also already at higher risk for firearm suicide. Limiting access to firearms has been a proven and effective way of lowering rates of firearm suicide. One study demonstrated that when states restricted handgun sales to individuals under the age of 21, the firearm suicide rate declined 12 percent among 18-to-20-year-olds. [4]
Expanding access to concealable firearms like handguns creates a significant public safety risk as the majority of gun crimes involve handguns. FBI crime statistics from 2020 to 2024 show that 92 percent of firearms identified in murders were handguns, 6 percent were rifles, and 2 percent were shotguns. The lack of legal access to handguns by people under the age of 21 explains why crime guns traced to 18-, 19-, and 20-year-olds remain relatively low compared to the next age cohort of 21-, 22-, and 23-year-olds. The rate at which firearms recovered in crimes are traced back to young purchasers jumps 10-fold at age 21 before peaking at age 22.[5] This sharp increase tracks with the legal minimum age to purchase handguns and would therefore begin rising earlier after DOJ’s baffling new refusal to enforce the 1968 law.
Young adults engage in crime at a higher rate than the rest of the adult population and lowering the age to purchase a handgun would make an even larger percentage of youths vulnerable to coercion or cooption by traffickers. According to the ATF, “The most frequent age of a purchaser of a crime gun was 22 years old, with purchasers between 21 and 25 years old accounting for almost as many traced crime guns as all purchasers ages 45 and older.” One reason most crime guns are purchased by people in this age group is because traffickers frequently use, and often force younger individuals who don't have criminal backgrounds to straw-purchase their weapons for them.
DOJ’s reckless U-turn interpretation of the 1968 law is made exceptionally more dangerous when combined with ATF’s proposed rule that would allow Federal Firearms Licensees (FFLs) to engage in more “non-over-the-counter” gun sales than ever before. In other words, with this new opinion and if ATF’s rule is finalized as proposed, FFLs will be able to sell handguns to purchasers between the ages of 18 and 20 without them ever setting foot in a gun store and then deliver those guns directly to their door. This would eliminate critical opportunities for responsible FFLs to observe suspicious behavior that may indicate criminal intent and to exercise their discretion to decline such sales. This would be inconsistent with congressional intent and unnecessarily endanger public safety.
The sensible restriction on FFLs from selling handguns to 18-to-20-year-olds is constitutional and is helping save lives every day. Your duty is to enforce the law as Congress writes it, not to make up new laws you prefer and substitute them for the public will as expressed through Congress. We urge you to immediately rescind your unlawful and dangerous opinion.
Sincerely,
[1] Joshua D. Brown and Amie J. Goodin, “Mass Casualty Shooting Venues, Types of Firearms, and Age of Perpetrators in the United States, 1982–2018,” American Journal of Public Health 108, no. 10 (2018): 1385–138.7
[2] Paul M. Reeping et al., “State Firearm Laws, Gun Ownership, and K-12 School Shootings: Implications for School Safety,” Journal of School Violence 21, no. 2 (2022): 132–146.
[3] Eighteen to 20 year olds commit 18% of gun homicides, despite comprising just four percent of the US population. Giffords Law Center analysis of FBI Supplementary Homicide Report (SHR) data, 2016–2020.
[4] Emma E. Fridel et al., “Examining the Impact of Minimum Handgun Purchase Age and Background Check Legislation on Young Adult Suicide in the United States, 1991–2020.” American Journal of Public Health 0 (2024).

U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06), Rashida Tlaib (D-MI-12), and Haley Stevens (D-MI-11) are expressing concerns about workplace safety at the United States Postal Service (USPS) Michigan Metroplex P&DC in Pontiac, Michigan and across other Southeast Michigan USPS Facilities. Since May 2026, employees have raised safety concerns and offered solutions to management, but to date employees report that nothing has been done to rectify the situation. 
“On September 1, 2026, a non-maintenance supervisor at the facility used a maintenance bypass code, which is supposed to be known and handled by mechanics only, to start a bundle sorting machine that was placed in maintenance mode and shut down for repairs. However, a maintenance employee was inside the machine when the non-maintenance supervisor attempted to start it, which could have resulted in major injury or death. Fortunately, the machine was shut down before it could activate,”
 the lawmakers wrote. 
The lawmakers continued:
“According to employees at the facility, staff have been raising this safety concern since May 2026, indicating reoccurring negligence of this issue. Employees have brought both complaints and solutions before management, although nothing has been done to rectify the situation. It is concerning that requests for proper safety protocol have been largely neglected, especially after the death of Mr. Nicholas Acker, who was found in a similar mail handling machine at the USPS Detroit Network Distribution Center (NDC) in Allen Park, Michigan. This is unacceptable, and employees should have the confidence that they are protected on the job. USPS has the responsibility to enforce proper safety protocols and standards.” 
In a letter to Postmaster General David Steiner, the lawmakers noted that the USPS has a responsibility to ensure that employees are safe and protected on the job.
A copy of the letter can be found HERE and below:
Dear Postmaster General Steiner:
This letter is regarding workplace safety concerns at the United States Postal Service (USPS) Michigan Metroplex P&DC in Pontiac, Michigan. We are concerned by the reports of unsafe practices at this facility and across Southeast Michigan.
On September 1, 2026, a non-maintenance supervisor at the facility used a maintenance bypass code, which is supposed to be known and handled by mechanics only, to start a bundle sorting machine that was placed in maintenance mode and shut down for repairs. However, a maintenance employee was inside the machine when the non-maintenance supervisor attempted to start it, which could have resulted in major injury or death. Fortunately, the machine was shut down before it could activate.
According to employees at the facility, staff have been raising this safety concern since May 2026, indicating reoccurring negligence of this issue. Employees have brought both complaints and solutions before management, although nothing has been done to rectify the situation. It is concerning that requests for proper safety protocol have been largely neglected, especially after the death of Mr. Nicholas Acker, who was found in a similar mail handling machine at the USPS Detroit Network Distribution Center (NDC) in Allen Park, Michigan.  This is unacceptable, and employees should have the confidence that they are protected on the job. USPS has the responsibility to enforce proper safety protocols and standards.
Given the USPS’s role in ensuring worker safety, we request clarification on this matter and written responses to the following questions:
1. Was USPS aware that a non-maintenance supervisor had knowledge of and used a maintenance bypass code on multiple occasions, which could have led to serious, life-threatening consequences?
2. What steps will USPS take to ensure that only qualified employees have access to the maintenance code?
3. Have any disciplinary actions been taken, and if not, what correctional actions will USPS pursue?
4. How often are program evaluations, service talks, safety observations, and inspections conducted at this facility, as described in the Employee and Labor Relations Manual, and how will USPS adapt the safety training and protocols to address this problem at the facility?
5. What are the appropriate procedures for employees to communicate complaints or concerns with the appropriate staff when a supervisor is involved in an unsafe practice?
6. What future actions will USPS put in place to ensure a similar situation does not recur?
Ensuring worker safety remains our top priority. Thank you, and we look forward to your full and prompt response.
title: Dingell, Colleagues Express Concern Over Workplace Safety at Pontiac USPS Facility

Gabriel Allen Hargus, 49, is wanted by the U.S. Marshals Service, the West Virginia State Police, and West Virginia Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation (Parole) on federal and state warrants.

Hargus is a white man, standing 6 feet 1 inch and weighing approximately 195 pounds. He has brown hair and brown eyes.

Baltimore, Maryland – A Baltimore man received a federal sentence after pleading guilty to firearm charges.

U.S. District Court Judge Adam B. Abelson sentenced Michael Lemon, 22, to 78 months in prison, followed by three years of supervised release, for unlawful possession of a machinegun and possession of a firearm and ammunition by a prohibited person. Authorities found Lemon, a convicted felon who is prohibited from possessing firearms and ammunition, in possession of a modified Glock pistol when apprehended.

Kelly O. Hayes, U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the sentence with Special Agent in Charge Charles Doerrer, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives (ATF), and Commissioner Richard Worley, Baltimore Police Department (BPD).

According to court documents, on December 30, 2025, BPD officers responded to multiple 911 calls reporting a breaking and entering by a group of young men at a Baltimore multi-residence building. As the officers arrived at the building, they observed Lemon, who fit the description of the suspect from the 911 call, hurriedly attempting to start a motorbike.

Officers then apprehend Lemon and discovered that he possessed a Glock pistol. Additionally, there was a machinegun conversion device, sometimes referred to as a “switch,” affixed to Lemon’s pistol which enabled the gun to fire automatically.

U.S. Attorney Hayes commended the ATF and BPD for their work in the investigation. Ms. Hayes also thanked Assistant U.S. Attorney Gregory Conner who prosecuted this federal case.

For more information on the Maryland U.S. Attorney’s Office, its priorities, and resources available to help the community, please visit justice.gov/usao-md .

title: Baltimore Felon Sentenced to More Than Six Years in Federal Prison for Firearm Possession Charges

HHS’ Office for Civil Rights Settles HIPAA Privacy Rule Investigation with Dr. Linda L. Shen d/b/a Shen Smiles, P.C.
Settlement Marks OCR’s 56th HIPAA Right of Access Enforcement Action to Advance Individual Access to Medical Records
WASHINGTON — October 8th, 2026 — The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Oﬃce for Civil Rights (OCR) today announced a settlement with Linda L. Shen d/b/a Shen Smiles, P.C. (Shen Smiles), a Pennsylvania-based healthcare provider that offers dental services, for potential violations of the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) Privacy Rule. The settlement resolves an investigation of a complaint alleging a failure to provide timely access to an individual’s protected health information (PHI).
“The Privacy Rule’s administrative requirements are essential to protect not only PHI from impermissible use or disclosure, but also to ensure that covered entities are able to meet their obligations related to individual rights, such as the right of access,” said OCR Director Paula M. Stannard.
OCR initiated an investigation after receiving a complaint that Shen Smiles failed to provide an individual with timely access to her PHI despite receiving multiple requests. During OCR’s investigation, Shen Smiles asserted that it could not provide the individual with access to her PHI because a workforce member stole the records from the practice. OCR’s investigation determined that Shen Smiles failed to implement policies and procedures with respect to PHI that are designed to comply with the Privacy and Breach Notification Rules, including a failure to have right of access policies and procedures, and that Shen Smiles did not reasonably safeguard PHI from any intentional or unintentional use or disclosure that would violate the requirements of the Privacy Rule.
On July 31, 2024, OCR issued a Notice of Proposed Determination proposing to impose a civil money penalty, and Shen Smiles subsequently requested a hearing before an administrative law judge. On August 11, 2026, prior to an administrative hearing, OCR and Shen Smiles resolved this enforcement action with a resolution agreement. Under the terms of the resolution agreement, Shen Smiles agreed to pay $140,000 to OCR.
The HIPAA Privacy Rule’s “Right of Access” provisions require that individuals, or their personal representatives, have timely access to health information within 30 days, with the possibility of one 30-day extension. OCR enforces the HIPAA Privacy Rule, which establishes national standards to protect individuals’ health records; sets limits and conditions on the uses and disclosures of PHI; and gives individuals certain rights, including the right to timely access and to obtain a copy of their health records for a reasonable cost.
The Notice of Proposed Determination may be found here.
The Resolution Agreement may be found here.
OCR is committed to enforcing the HIPAA Rules that protect the privacy and security of people’s health information. Guidance about the Privacy Rule, Security Rule, and Breach Notification Rule can be found on OCR’s website.
If you believe that your or another person’s health information privacy, civil rights, or conscience rights have been violated, you can ﬁle a complaint with OCR.
Follow HHS OCR on X at @HHSOCR.
Like HHS on Facebook, follow HHS on X @HHSgov, @SecKennedy, and sign up for HHS Email Updates.

ROCKFORD — A Rockford woman has pleaded guilty to federal fraud charges for operating a scheme to illegally obtain more than $2 million in federally funded unemployment benefits under the Pandemic Unemployment Assistance program.

CARISSA JORDAN, 46, admitted in a plea agreement that she used the personal identifying information of various individuals to submit false Pandemic Unemployment Assistance applications. Jordan had obtained the personal identifying information through social media, with and without the individuals’ knowledge and consent. After receiving debit cards containing the Pandemic Unemployment Assistance funds, Jordan used the money for her own personal benefit.

Jordan pleaded guilty in federal court in Rockford on Wednesday to wire fraud charges. She faces a maximum sentence of 20 years imprisonment and a fine of up to $250,000. U.S. District Judge Iain D. Johnston set sentencing for March 31, 2027.

The guilty plea was announced by Andrew S. Boutros, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois, and Anthony P. D’Esposito, Inspector General, U.S. Department of Labor, Office of Inspector General. The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorney Robert S. Ladd.

On April 7, 2026, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Rockford Woman Pleads Guilty to Defrauding the Government of More Than $2 Million in Federal Unemployment Benefits

ALEXANDRIA, Va. – A Maryland man was sentenced yesterday to three years and one month in prison for assault of a U.S. postal worker and robbery of mail, money, or other property of the United States.

According to court documents, on Sept. 5, 2025, Dason Antonio Robinson, 28, of Bowie, and an unidentified co-conspirator traveled from Maryland to Alexandria and located a U.S. Postal Service (USPS) mail carrier who was engaged in her regular duties of delivering mail. Robinson and his co-conspirator approached the mail carrier with their hands in their waistbands to appear to be carrying firearms. The robbers forcefully grabbed at the mail carrier’s letter satchel while it was slung across her body and also grabbed at her clothing, a personal bag secured by a chain, and her necklace, causing the chain on her personal bag and necklace to break.

Robinson and his co-conspirator obtained the letter satchel, mail inside the satchel, a USPS scanner, and USPS vehicle keys, as well as the carrier’s CashApp card, driver’s license, and cellphone.

Following the robbery, Robinson and his co-conspirator fled in their vehicle. On Oct. 2, 2025, U.S. Postal Inspectors seized the vehicle in Bowie. Agents recovered stolen mail from the letter satchel and the mail carrier’s CashApp card and driver’s license.

Theophani K. Stamos, First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia, and Damon E. Wood, Inspector in Charge of the Washington Division, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, made the announcement after sentencing by U.S. District Judge Rossie D. Alston Jr.

Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Jillian Pascua and former Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Allie M. McKnight prosecuted the case.

Related court documents and information are located on the website of the District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia or on PACER by searching for Case No. 1:26-cr-37.
title: Maryland man sentenced for robbing U.S. Postal Service mail carrier

FORT WAYNE – Audra Sweet, 40 years old, of Three Rivers, Michigan, was sentenced by United States District Court Chief Judge Holly A. Brady after pleading guilty to distribution of methamphetamine, announced United States Attorney Adam L. Mildred.

Sweet was sentenced to 130 months in prison followed by 5 years of supervised release.

“Audra Sweet will spend more than the next ten years in prison for distributing large quantities of methamphetamine in the Northern District of Indiana. For months, the Defendant trafficked lethal drugs across our state line, distributing poison directly into local neighborhoods. Today’s significant sentence ensures accountability for these crimes. It sends a clear message that those who seek to profit from the destruction of our families and communities will be investigated, prosecuted, and removed from the streets. This successful prosecution was made possible by the continued commitment of local law enforcement agencies to multi-jurisdictional task forces. By combining resources and intelligence, local, state and federal law enforcement are actively dismantling drug trafficking networks that threaten our Hoosier families,” said U.S. Attorney Adam L. Mildred.

“Drug traffickers put our communities at risk every time they push methamphetamine onto our streets. Their pursuit of profit comes at the expense of families and lives,” said FBI Indianapolis Special Agent in Charge Timothy J. O’Malley. “The FBI and our partners are working together to put these criminals out of business and hold them accountable. It’s pretty simple: if you traffic poison for profit, expect law enforcement to come knocking.”

This case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation with assistance from the Indiana State Police and the LaGrange County Sheriff’s Department. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Teresa L. Ashcraft.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities .
title: Michigan Woman Sentenced to 130 Months in Prison for Distribution of Methamphetamine

CNO Visits German Navy in Wilhelmshaven, Focuses on Fleet Readiness
WILHELMSHAVEN, Germany – Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle visited German naval leaders, toured the guided-missile frigate FGS Sachsen (F 219), and observed ship maintenance facilities in Wilhelmshaven, Germany, Oct. 8, highlighting shared priorities in fleet readiness, shipbuilding and maintenance.
During the visit, Caudle received briefings from German Navy Flotilla Adm. Sven Beck, commander of Flotilla 2, and Rainer Sacher, director of the German Naval Arsenal, on the state of the German Navy, operational priorities and naval infrastructure.
“Our relationship with the German Navy is built on decades of trust, shared sacrifice and a common commitment to maritime security,” said Caudle. “Strong alliances require more than operating together at sea. We also have to learn from one another and find better ways to build, maintain and sustain the warships our Sailors need to fight and win.”
The discussions included ship maintenance, repair capacity and lessons learned in sustaining operationally ready fleets.
“Both of our navies understand that readiness doesn’t begin when a ship gets underway,” said Caudle. “It begins in our shipyards, our maintenance facilities and with the skilled people who keep our ships operational. By studying what each of us does well, we can identify smarter, faster and more effective ways to return ships to the fleet and keep them in the fight.”
Caudle, joined by Master Chief Petty Officer of the Navy John Perryman, also toured FGS Sachsen, a German Navy Sachsen-class air-defense frigate. During the tour, the Navy’s senior leaders met with the ship’s crew and thanked German Sailors who participated in the United States’ 250th Independence Day celebrations in New York City in July.
“It meant a great deal to have German Sailors standing alongside our own as America celebrated 250 years of independence,” said Caudle. “Your presence in New York was a powerful reminder that the friendships we’ve built across the Atlantic extend well beyond our military missions. We’re proud to serve alongside you, and we’re grateful for the professionalism and friendship you bring to this partnership.”
Perryman also met with Sachsen’s enlisted leadership and crew, discussing the importance of professional development, leadership and the role enlisted Sailors play in maintaining operational readiness. The engagement provided an opportunity to exchange perspectives on the challenges facing Sailors in both navies and reinforce the professional relationships that underpin successful allied operations.
“Whether you’re serving aboard an American destroyer or a German frigate, the foundation of a strong Navy is its Sailors,” said Perryman. “We may wear different uniforms, but we share the same commitment to our shipmates, our mission and getting the job done. These opportunities to connect with our German counterparts, exchange ideas and learn from one another make us better Sailors and stronger partners.”
The CNO concluded his visit with a tour of shipyard facilities supporting German naval vessel maintenance and repair. The engagement highlighted the importance of maintenance capacity, industrial expertise and efficient repair processes as both navies sustain increasingly complex warships.
“We cannot afford to have ships sitting pierside when they should be at sea,” said Caudle. “Building warships is only part of the equation. We have to sustain them throughout their service lives, and that means having the right infrastructure, workforce and processes in place. Our German partners face many of the same challenges, and there is tremendous value in comparing approaches and applying lessons learned to improve readiness across both fleets.”
The visit reinforced the U.S. Navy’s commitment to working with Germany and other NATO allies to strengthen maritime security, improve naval capabilities and deter aggression across the European theater and beyond.
The visit to Wilhelmshaven marked the final stop of Caudle’s trip through the U.S. European Command area of responsibility, which began with engagements at Naval Air Station Sigonella, Italy, followed by participation in the Trans Regional Support Squadron (TRSS) in Venice, Italy, and meetings with leadership and Sailors at U.S. Africa Command in Stuttgart, Germany. Throughout the trip, Caudle reinforced the importance of forward-deployed naval forces, operational readiness and strengthening partnerships to address shared security challenges.
title: CNO Visits German Navy in Wilhelmshaven, Focuses on Fleet Readiness

Democratic Whip Katherine Clark and Congresswoman Lateefah Simon Visit Oakland Head Start Facility and Community Health Center, Condemn Republican Cuts to Childcare, Healthcare, and Education Programs
OAKLAND, CA – This week, Congresswoman Lateefah Simon (D-CA-12) hosted, Democratic Whip Katherine Clark (D-MA-05), the highest-ranking woman in the House of Representatives, in Oakland’s Fruitvale neighborhood. They visited the Unity Council’s Head Start and Early Head Start Preschool facilities and La Clínica de La Raza, a federally qualified health center, to meet with families, frontline health care staff, and care workers who have been impacted by Republicans’ devastating federal aid cuts.
President Trump and Congressional Republicans’ “One Big, Cruel, Ugly Bill” has made deep cuts to federal funding for healthcare, childcare, education, and food assistance programs. In California’s 12th Congressional District, it is estimated that 31,000 people are experiencing rising healthcare costs and 35, 595 people will lose health coverage because of Republican cuts to Medi-Cal and decision to end enhanced Affordable Care Act tax credits. In Congress, Congresswoman Simon has consistently fought against cuts to Medicaid/Medi-CAL and SNAP and attempts to gut Head Start.
“My daughter was a Head Start child, and I know intimately that federally supported childcare and healthcare is a lifeline for many families. It allows children to learn safely and be healthy while their parents attend school or work in our local businesses,” said Congresswoman Simon. “Whip Clark and I are taking everything we heard from our visit back to D.C., where we are hell bent on fighting this Administration and reversing their harmful policies so our Head Starts, our community health centers, our care workers, our families have everything they need to continue growing and being brilliant.”
"Congresswoman Lateefah Simon is an unrivaled champion for working families," said Democratic Whip Katherine Clark. "It was a privilege to join her in Oakland to see firsthand what communities need from the federal government: investments in healthcare, childcare, and the wellbeing of regular people, not giveaways to the ultra-rich. While the Republican Party continues to bend its knee to the billionaire class, Democrats are ready to take back the People's House and get to work for the working class.”
“We are honored to welcome Congresswoman Simon and Democratic Whip Clark to Fruitvale and share firsthand the impact of The Unity Council’s work,” said CEO of The Unity Council, Chris Iglesias. “From giving our youngest learners, a strong foundation at our De Colores Head Start, to bringing La Catrina de Oakland to Fruitvale as a powerful celebration of culture and community, our work is rooted in creating opportunities and strengthening families. Their visit underscores the importance of continued investment in the people, programs, and places that allow communities like Fruitvale to thrive."
“At our De Colores Head Start Center, we see every day how a strong start can shape not only a child’s future, but an entire families’,” said Chief Early Learning Officer of The Unity Council, Luis Arenas. “Head Start creates opportunities for children to learn and grow while giving parents the support and resources they need to move their families forward. We were proud to welcome Congresswoman Simon and Democratic Whip Clark into our classrooms and share the real, lasting impact this work has on families throughout our community.”
“We are deeply grateful to Whip Katherine Clark and Congresswoman Lateefah Simon for visiting La Clínica and for their tireless advocacy on behalf of the communities we serve. Their visit shows what federal investment looks like on the ground, and highlights what is at risk when coverage and resources for community health centers are reduced,” said La Clínica CEO, Jane García. “What’s at stake is whether parents can get their children to the doctor, whether patients can access dental and behavioral health care along with primary care, whether families can afford their medications, and whether community health centers have the resources to keep the staff who provide this care. La Clínica thanks Whip Clark and Congresswoman Simon for listening to our patients and staff and for bringing their voices back to Washington. The decisions made there have very real impacts here in the Bay Area.”

text:
EDGEWOOD, MD – Amtrak has achieved a major milestone for two bridge replacement projects in Maryland: Bush River Bridge and Gunpowder River Bridge. Amtrak has selected HNTB for architectural and engineering services for both projects, which will include community engagement to inform the final design.
These bridges span a critical section of the Northeast Corridor (NEC) between Baltimore and Wilmington, each carrying over 100 Amtrak, MARC commuter, and freight trains per day. Full replacement of both bridges will help improve safety and reliability, while enabling Amtrak and MARC to add more train service in the future as needed to accommodate record growth.
Amtrak Executive Vice President, Capital Delivery Laura Mason:
“Today marks a critical step in the long journey to replace both the Bush River and Gunpowder River Bridges, key to improving the travel experience as record Amtrak ridership is projected to continue growing over the next decade. These projects are two important examples of Amtrak’s long-term vision to modernize the Northeast Corridor’s century-old tunnels, bridges, and more.”
Why it matters: The Bush and Gunpowder River Bridges serve over 100 trains from Amtrak, MARC and Norfolk Southern every day. This aging infrastructure restricts train speeds, demands constant maintenance, and bottlenecks both intercity and commuter services. Adding to the unreliability, the outdated structure of the moveable Bush River Bridge requires a 20-person crew during summer weekends to open for marine traffic, an extensive resource strain.
About the projects: Replacing the Bush and Gunpowder River Bridges will address critical state-of-good repair needs and deliver modern, reliable structures featuring several benefits, including:
- Upgrades to track alignment, signal systems, and electric traction over a 10-mile stretch of the NEC, expanding track capacity once both projects are constructed;
- Higher speeds of up to 145 miles per hour for Gunpowder River Bridge and 160 for Bush River Bridge (compared with 125 mph today); and
- A fixed-span Bush River Bridge structure that better supports marine traffic needs and no longer requires a crew.
Schedule details: Preliminary engineering is on track to conclude in 2029. HNTB has supported Amtrak on several bridge projects along the NEC in the past, including ongoing work for replacement of the Susquehanna River Bridge in Maryland and Portal North Bridge in New Jersey.
About the bridges: Completed in 1913, Gunpowder River Bridge is located between Chase and Joppatowne, Maryland. To the north is Bush River Bridge, another 113-year-old bridge located between Edgewood and Perryman, MD. Due to their age and deteriorating condition, the bridges experience reliability issues. Bush River Bridge must open for boat traffic, and its outdated infrastructure requires a team to hand crank open the structure. When the bridge has failed to close in the past, Amtrak trains between New York, Philadelphia, and Washington face massive delays. In 2019 alone, more than 72 hours of train delays for Amtrak and MARC trains were caused directly by the Bush River Bridge.
How it’s paid for: This step in the planning process is primarily funded by a grant from the Federal Railroad Administration, along with contributions from Amtrak and the Maryland Transit Administration. Both bridges are listed as key priorities on the FRA’s NEC Project Inventory. Work is currently funded through preliminary engineering and NEPA review; additional future funding would be required for final design and construction.
The big picture: Amtrak and partners are advancing several major infrastructure projects. Recent milestones across Amtrak’s portfolio of major bridge projects include:
- Portal North Bridge: Amtrak and NJ TRANSIT opened the first track on the new bridge earlier this year. The second and final track will open this fall, providing increased reliability to rail customers for generations to come.
- Dock Bridge: Amtrak will soon begin work to rehabilitate this nearly century-old bridge in New Jersey after awarding key construction and project management contracts this summer.
- Sawtooth Bridges: Amtrak and NJ TRANSIT are moving forward with initial construction for the Sawtooth Bridges Replacement Project. Attorney General of the United States, Todd Blanche, United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, Administrator of the Drug Enforcement Administration (“DEA”), Terrance C. Cole, Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security (“DHS”), Markwayne Mullin, and Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Kash Patel, announced that former Venezuelan President NICOLÁS MADURO MOROS and former First Lady of Venezuela CILIA ADELA FLORES DE MADURO have been charged in a Superseding Indictment unsealed today with conspiring to commit torture, narcoterrorism, cocaine importation conspiracy, and weapons offenses.

“As alleged in today’s Superseding Indictment, for more than two decades, Nicolás Maduro Moros and Cilia Adela Flores De Maduro engaged in a conspiracy to commit torture, including the torture of United States citizens, in addition to the narcotics trafficking and weapons offenses already charged,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “As described in the Superseding Indictment, the Maduros and other Venezuelan leaders abused their positions of trust to enrich themselves through narco-terrorism, cocaine trafficking, and other corruption, including by employing Venezuelan military, law enforcement, and other government entities under their control to flood the United States with illegal narcotics. Today’s indictment further alleges that the Maduros and other Venezuelan leaders conspired to repress dissent through grave violations of human rights by ordering and allowing violence, threats, and physical torture under color of law. As alleged, this included the torture of multiple United States citizens, who were subjected to unspeakable abuse. Today’s charges exemplify the tirelessness that we and our law enforcement partners will undertake to vindicate victims of crime, particularly American victims subjected to horrific treatment abroad.”

“Since the capture and arrest of Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores, the Department of Justice has been working to uncover the extent of their alleged crimes against the people of Venezuela and of the United States,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “These additional charges against the Maduros reflect the dedication of this Administration to delivering justice for the victims of torture, narcoterrorism, and organized crime.”

“Maduro’s regime is responsible for countless American victims of narcoterrorism and drug trafficking,” said DHS Secretary Mullin. “Thanks to the leadership of President Trump, our Homeland Security Task Force partners, and strong coordination among DHS, DOJ, FBI, and DEA, we’re bringing Maduro and his wife to justice. President Trump is using all tools at his disposal to make America safe again both at home and abroad.”

“These indictments demonstrate that our work did not stop with the arrest of Nicolás Maduro, who terrorized the people of Venezuela for more than two decades,” said DEA Administrator Terry Cole. “DEA will continue to follow the evidence and pursue those who use corruption, violence, and positions of power to facilitate criminal activity and protect those who profit from it. Maduro’s arrest was an important step toward accountability, but it was not the last. We remain steadfast in our commitment to work with our partners to restore law and order across the Western Hemisphere and bring to justice any corrupt leader who thinks their political position shields them from consequences.”

“As alleged in the indictment, the Maduro regime subjected American citizens to torture while held in custody of the Venezuelan government - including drugs, electric shock, sexual assault, and more,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “These charges follow the historic law enforcement-operation proudly supported by this FBI in January arresting Maduro and executing one of the most daring Foreign Transfers of Custody in United States history, returning him and his wife to the U.S. - an operation which required months of coordination, detailed planning, and seamless execution across multiple components of the federal government led by the Department of War. Today’s charges reflect the commitment from this FBI and this Department of Justice to accountability, the rule of law, and the protection of U.S. national security.”

According to the Superseding Indictment, statements made in public court proceedings, and court filings:

For over 25 years, NICOLÁS MADURO MOROS and CILIA ADELA FLORES DE MADURO abused their positions of public trust, enriching themselves through corruption and remaining in power through grave violations of human rights.

Through drug trafficking, the corrupt use of law enforcement and the military, the abuse of the judicial system, and the pilfering of public funds, MADURO MOROS, FLORES DE MADURO, and other Venezuelan leaders personally benefited at the expense of the Venezuelan people. While this systemic corruption was immensely profitable for the defendants and their inner circle, it was deeply unpopular with the Venezuelan people. To undermine Venezuelan democracy and entrench themselves in power, these same leaders allegedly presided over a system of repression that relied on violence against political opposition, arbitrary detention, and the torture of detainees, including United States citizens. That torture included electric shock, asphyxiation, rape, forced nudity, prolonged isolation, starvation, punishment cells, and psychological torture, such as threats to harm and kill victims’ families.

MADURO MOROS and FLORES DE MADURO allegedly sat atop that violent power structure. They developed and facilitated the systems which they and their co-conspirators used corruptly to amass immense wealth and power, rewarding allies with ill-gotten funds and terrorizing perceived opponents through persecution and violence. These systems relied on MADURO MOROS’s and FLORES DE MADURO’s control over Venezuela’s military, judiciary, and law enforcement agencies, and their partnerships with organized criminal groups, including terrorist organizations and groups of state-sponsored gangs known as colectivos .

In amassing such wealth and power, MADURO MOROS, FLORES DE MADURO, and other members of their inner circle allegedly trafficked drugs under the protection of the Venezuelan military, judiciary, and law enforcement agencies. They allegedly partnered with narcotics traffickers and narco-terrorists from designated foreign terrorist organizations, including the Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias de Colombia (“FARC”), the Ejército de Liberación Nacional (“ELN”), the Sinaloa Cartel, the Zetas, later known as the Cártel del Noreste (“CDN”), and Tren de Aragua (“TdA”), who dispatched cocaine from Venezuela to the United States via transshipment points in the Caribbean and Central America.

MADURO MOROS, FLORES DE MADURO, and other high-ranking members of their inner circle also allegedly created and maintained a violent system of repression. Since at least 1999, thousands of Venezuelans have been harassed, threatened, arrested, prosecuted, assaulted, tortured, or killed by individuals wielding the purported authority of the Venezuelan state to ensure that MADURO MOROS and FLORES DE MADURO remained in power. MADURO MOROS and FLORES DE MADURO used military units, colectivos , and narco-terrorist groups involved in their drug trafficking to unlawfully detain and torture their victims. Such violence and repression increased around periods of political instability in which MADURO MOROS’s and FLORES DE MADURO’s power was threatened. During these periods, MADURO MOROS, FLORES DE MADURO, and other high-level Venezuelan officials jointly undertook efforts to stifle those who opposed, or were merely suspected of opposing, MADURO MOROS or his regime. Those efforts included physical and psychological torture systematically used to terrify the populace and silence dissent.

In addition to MADURO MOROS and FLORES DE MADURO, other high-level officials allegedly were integral to this system. One high-level Venezuelan official, referred to in the Superseding Indictment as CC-1, ordered the murders of certain individuals who opposed MADURO MOROS or his regime, oversaw torture undertaken by officials under his command, and personally threatened the murder of a prisoner’s child as a form of psychological torture. Another senior Venezuelan officer who reported directly to MADURO MOROS, referred to in the Superseding Indictment as CC-2, developed torture methods that he presented for approval to MADURO MOROS, led an agency responsible for torturing scores of victims, and personally signed off on the unlawful arrest and torture of specific individuals. A third Venezuelan official, referred to in the Superseding Indictment as CC-3, personally ordered and participated in the torture of civilians and military members, including United States citizens, who were believed to pose a threat to MADURO MOROS’s rule. For example, one particular United States citizen was detained in Venezuela and subjected to, among other things, deprivation of food and water, simulated drowning, repeated beatings, electric shock to his testicles, and forced injections.

* * *

The Superseding Indictment charges Maduro Moros, 63, and FLORES DE MADURO, 69, in Count One, with participating in a narcoterrorism conspiracy, which carries a 20-year mandatory minimum sentence and a maximum sentence of life in prison; in Count Two, with conspiring to commit torture, which carries a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison; in Count Three, with conspiring to import cocaine into the United States, which carries a 10-year mandatory minimum sentence and a maximum sentence of life in prison; in Count Four, with using and carrying machine guns and destructive devices during and in relation to, and possessing machine guns and destructive devices in furtherance of, the narco-terrorism and cocaine-importation conspiracies, which carries a 30-year mandatory minimum sentence and a maximum sentence of life in prison; and in Count Five, with conspiring to use and carry machine guns and destructive devices during and in relation to, and to possess machine guns and destructive devices in furtherance of, the narco-terrorism and cocaine-importation conspiracies, which carries a maximum sentence of life in prison. The potential maximum sentences in this case are prescribed by Congress and provided here for informational purposes only, as any sentencing of the defendants will be determined by the judge.

Mr. McDonald thanked the Homeland Security Task Force; DEA’s Special Operations Division, New York Division, New York Drug Enforcement Task Force, Miami Division, Rocky Mountain Division, Andean Division, and Europe Division; FBI’s New York Field Office, International Human Rights Unit, Nashville-Knoxville Resident Agency, and Legal Attaché Office in Madrid, Spain; HSI’s New York Field Office and Attaché Madrid; the U.S. Department of Justice’s Joint Task Force Vulcan, Office of International Affairs, Eastern District of New York, Southern District of Florida, National Security Division’s Counterterrorism Section, National Security Cyber Section, and Office of Intelligence, and the Criminal Division’s Office of Human Rights and Special Prosecutions, Office of Judicial Attaché in Bogotá, and Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section; United States Marshals Service for the Southern District of New York; and the New York City Police Department for their assistance.

This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (“HSTF”) initiative established by Executive Order 14159. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of U.S. law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders.

This case is being handled by the Office’s National Security and International Narcotics Unit. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kaylan E. Lasky, Henry L. Ross, Kevin T. Sullivan, and Kyle A. Wirshba are in charge of the prosecution, with assistance from Trial Attorney Kevin Nunnally of the Counterterrorism Section of the National Security Division.

The charges contained in the Superseding Indictment are merely accusations, and the defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.

BANGOR, Maine: A Mexican man pleaded guilty and was sentenced today in U.S. District Court in Bangor for eluding inspection by immigration officers.

U.S. Magistrate Judge John C. Nivison sentenced Encarnacion Lara Gonzalez ,49, to time served (approximately three days).

According to court records, on October 4, 2026, Lara Gonzalez, a Mexican national, traveled into Canada through the Houlton port of entry. After stopping in a parking lot in Canada, he turned his vehicle around and drove back towards the U.S. At the Houlton port of entry, he drove through the inspection lane and entered the U.S. without stopping, despite clearly marked signs instructing motorists to stop. U.S. Customs and Border Protection officers pursued him and he pulled over shortly afterwards.

U.S. Customs and Border Protection and U.S. Border Patrol investigated the case.

Operation Take Back America : This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

NEWARK, N.J. – A Massachusetts doctor was sentenced for her role in telemedicine health care fraud and kickback schemes that resulted in more than $40 million in fraudulent claims to Medicare and TRICARE, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced.

Le Thu, 71, of Boston, Massachusetts, pleaded guilty before U.S. District Judge Susan D. Wigenton in Newark, in May 2025, to one count of an indictment, charging her with conspiracy to violate the Federal Anti-Kickback statute and, in June 2025, to a two-count information, charging her with false statements related to health care matters. Thu was sentenced on October 6, 2026, on all counts to 36 months’ imprisonment with two years’ supervised release, and ordered to pay over $27 million in restitution.

According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court:

From May 2014 through April 2017, Thu participated in a conspiracy in which she received kickbacks from a telemedicine company in exchange for approving hundreds of prescriptions for durable medical equipment and compounded medications. Thu agreed to accept kickback payments of approximately $35 from the telemedicine company in exchange for each prescription she approved, knowing that certain of the prescriptions would be used to bill TRICARE, a health care program of the U.S. Department of Defense. TRICARE paid pharmacies hundreds of thousands of dollars for compounded medications that were procured through kickbacks Thu received.

From March 2017 through November 2020, Thu participated in a second telemedicine health care fraud scheme in connection with payments for genetic tests and durable medical equipment for Medicare beneficiaries. On behalf of multiple telemedicine companies, Thu signed, and caused others who had no medical training to sign, false medical documentation and orders for genetic tests and durable medical equipment. The documentation made it appear that Thu had exercised her medical judgment in approving the orders and, in certain instances, that she would use the genetic test results to treat beneficiaries. Thu, however, had not interacted with or provided any medical care to the beneficiaries prior to signing, or having others sign, the doctors’ orders. Thu signed thousands of such orders that contained statements she knew were false and material to Medicare in exchange for payments to her totaling more than $200,000. As a result, Thu caused durable medical equipment suppliers and laboratories to submit more than $40 million in claims to Medicare based on doctors’ orders containing materially false representations, for which Medicare paid more than $27 million.

U.S. Attorney Frazer credited the U.S. Attorney’s Office, District of Massachusetts, under the direction of U.S. Attorney Leah B. Foley; special agents of the U.S. Department of Defense, Office of Inspector General, Defense Criminal Investigative Service, under the direction of Acting Special Agent in Charge Jessica Herrington, Northeastern Field Office; special agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge David R. Fitzgibbons, in Birmingham, Alabama; special agents of the U.S. Department of Labor-Employee Benefits Security Administration, under the direction of Regional Director Crystal Coleman; and special agents of the Tennessee Valley Authority, Office of the Inspector General, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Ryan Wilson, with the investigation.

The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorney Kathleen P. O’Leary of the Health Care Fraud and Opioids Enforcement Unit.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division). The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

###

Defense counsel: Elizabeth L. Mo, Esq.
title: Massachusetts Doctor Sentenced to 36 Months in Prison for Participation in Multimillion-Dollar Medicare Fraud Scheme and for Violating the Federal Anti-Kickback Statute

Attempted Murder Suspect Arrested by U.S. Marshals at Delaware Racetrack
For immediate release
Rashawn Abraham, Deputy U.S. Marshal
St. Thomas, VI – The U.S. Marshals (USMS) in Delaware on Wednesday arrested a St. Croix man wanted for a November 2025 attempted murder in the Virgin Islands.
Dumaray Iles, 34, was wanted by the Virgin Islands Police Department (VIPD) for first-degree attempted murder, first-degree assault and mayhem following a Nov. 27, 2025, shooting incident in Golden Rock, Christiansted.
On Aug. 4, the VIPD requested the assistance of the U.S. Marshals Florida/Caribbean Regional Fugitive Task Force in the District of the Virgin Islands in locating and apprehending Iles.
USMS investigators, with the assistance of Homeland Security Investigations, confirmed that Iles left the territory for Philadelphia in May 2026.
On Sept. 30, USMS investigators received information that Iles was working as a horse handler at the Delaware Park Racetrack in Wilmington, Delaware. Investigators from the District of the Virgin Islands requested assistance from their counterparts in Delaware.
The USMS Delaware First State Fugitive Task Force located and apprehended Iles at the Delaware Park Racetrack without incident. Iles is currently being held at the Howard R. Young Correctional Facility in Wilmington and is expected to be extradited to the Virgin Islands.
“Those wanted for violent crimes should understand that crossing state lines or traveling thousands of miles will not stop the U.S. Marshals Service from pursuing them,” said Kwesi R. Howard, U.S. Marshal of the District of the Virgin Islands. “Our partnerships and nationwide reach allow us to track down fugitives and bring them before the courts to answer for their alleged crimes. This arrest is another example of that commitment.”

ICYMI: Pappas-Backed AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act Passed House
The House passed the bipartisan AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act, legislation cosponsored by Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01). This legislation would ensure Americans continue to have access to AM radio in all new vehicles.
“In addition to being a source of news, music, and community connection, AM radio is a lifeline in emergencies for Americans to get important information and stay safe. This bipartisan legislation will help make sure people do not lose access to this free service in their cars,” said Congressman Pappas.
More than 50 million Americans listen to AM broadcast radio every month, and it remains one of the most reliable ways to reach the public during emergencies because it can travel long distances and reach broad geographic areas. AM radio is the backbone behind America’s National Public Warning System, which provides emergency-alert and warning information to the public during major natural disasters, extreme weather conditions, chemical incidents, health emergencies, and other domestic threats, often when cellular and Internet networks fail.
Despite the clear public safety uses of AM broadcast radio, many manufacturers stopped including it in their vehicles because they did not want to spend the minimal funds to ensure public safety during emergencies.
The AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act will require the Department of Transportation to issue a rule mandating that all automakers include AM radio as standard equipment in their vehicles, at no additional cost to consumers.
title: ICYMI: Pappas-Backed AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act Passed House

COLUMBUS, Ohio – A federal jury has convicted Davonta T. Flood, 30, of Columbus, of illegally possessing a firearm as a convicted felon. Flood is a repeat offender at both the federal and state levels.

The verdict was announced yesterday afternoon following a trial that began on Oct. 5 before U.S. District Judge Algenon L. Marbley.

According to court documents and trial testimony, in June 2026, deputies with the Franklin County Sheriff’s Office searched a residence used by Flood and recovered a firearm.

The sheriff’s office’s Special Investigations Unit had received a tip regarding narcotics activity at the residence on Wheatland Avenue. Upon executing a search warrant at the residence, officials discovered the firearm in a bedroom used by Flood between the mattress and the platform of the bed.

Flood had been released from the Bureau of Prisons for another conviction just one month prior to law enforcement searching the Hilltop residence he used. He was on federal supervised release at the time of his most recent crime.

As a previously convicted felon, Flood is prohibited from possessing firearms. His prior felony convictions include illegally possessing a firearm as a convicted felon and possessing with the intent to distribute fentanyl near a school. He also has state convictions for aggravated assault, weapon under disability, receiving stolen property and escape.

Flood was indicted by a federal grand jury in June.

Possessing a firearm as a previously convicted felon is a federal crime punishable by up to 15 years in prison. Sentencing of the defendant will be determined by the Court based on the advisory sentencing guidelines and other statutory factors.

Dominick S. Gerace II, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Ohio; Jorge Rosendo, Special Agent in Charge, U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives (ATF); Franklin County Sheriff Dallas Baldwin and Columbus Police Chief Elaine Bryant announced the verdict. Assistant United States Attorneys Jennifer M. Rausch and Elizabeth A. Geraghty are representing the United States in this case.

# # #
title: Jury finds repeat offender guilty of illegally possessing firearm

CHARLOTTE, N.C. – Anthony Eliu Acevedo, 27, of Charlotte, was sentenced yesterday to 8 ½ years in prison followed by a lifetime of supervised release, $62,000 in restitution, $10,000 in special assessments, and was ordered to register as a sex offender for transporting child sexual abuse material (CSAM), announced Russ Ferguson, U.S. Attorney for the Western District of North Carolina.

“Acevedo had over 65 hours of videos depicting the abuse of children, from sadistic and masochistic conduct to the physical and sexual torture of an infant,” said U.S. Attorney Russ Ferguson. “That material should not even exist. Those who spread it will find their way to federal prison.”

According to filed court documents, in October 2023, the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children received information related to an individual, later identified as Acevedo, uploading child sexual abuse material to an online storage account. One of the videos Acevedo uploaded to his online storage account depicted the physical and sexual torture of an infant. Law enforcement executed a search warrant in February 2024 at Acevedo’s residence and recovered two cell phones and a laptop. A forensic analysis of the devices and Acevedo’s online storage account revealed that Acevedo possessed more than 426 images and 999 videos of CSAM, including sadistic and masochistic conduct depicting children. If played without stopping, the videos depicting CSAM would run for 65.5 hours. The investigation further revealed that Acevedo used Telegram to obtain and pay for CSAM. During an interview with law enforcement, Acevedo said he intended to sell CSAM to others, though the investigation did not reveal evidence that he had sold any CSAM yet.

In sentencing Acevedo, U.S. District Judge Mattew E. Orso said that Acevedo possessed “a very large collection of some of the worst materials this Court has ever seen.”

Acevedo remains in the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service until he is transferred to the custody of the Federal Bureau of Prisons upon designation of a federal facility.

In making the announcement U.S. Attorney Russ Ferguson commended the FBI and the Charlotte Mecklenburg Police Department for their work on this case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Daniel Cervantes of the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Charlotte prosecuted the case.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse, launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc .
title: Charlotte Man Sentenced to Prison for Transporting Child Sexual Abuse Material Including Videos and Images of Infant Torture

Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries held a press conference in Brooklyn, where he emphasized that House Democrats are committed to lowering the high cost of living, making healthcare affordable and holding the crooks who are ripping off the American people accountable.

It’s an honor and a privilege to represent this area and to represent a district that Shirley Chisholm once represented here in Brooklyn in large measure. And the late, great Shirley Chisholm was a champion for making life more affordable for the people of Brooklyn, New York City and all across the country. Unfortunately, I think Shirley Chisholm would be horrified by what she’d see and what has unfolded here in the United States of America under Donald Trump and Republican control of Congress.
Donald Trump promised that costs here in the United States of America would go down on day one. But costs haven’t gone down. Costs have gone up. Life has become way too expensive as a direct result of policy decisions made by Donald Trump and the Republican-controlled Congress. The Trump Tariffs have increased costs on everyday Americans by thousands of dollars per year. House Democrats will continue to strongly oppose those tariffs and to fight to roll them back.
Donald Trump promised to love and cherish Medicaid. Donald Trump and Republicans refused to extend the Affordable Care Act tax credits. And as a result, tens of millions of people are experiencing—including right here in New York City—dramatically increased premiums, copays and deductibles, in some cases increasing by more than $1,000 a month. Donald Trump promised not to start endless wars in the Middle East but to stop them and then turned around and did the exact opposite by getting the country involved in a reckless and costly war of choice in Iran that hasn’t made our country any safer but has certainly made the American people economically weaker, particularly as it relates to gas prices. And as House Democrats, finally, we are certainly committed to combating the unprecedented corruption that the Trump cartel continues to unleash on the American people. Every day brings a new revelation, including the most recent one related to the U.S. Ambassador to Greece. What we’ve seen from the Trump cartel is that they’re more focused on enriching themselves, their family members, their friends and their donors than they are with making life more affordable for the American people. And our promise to the country in the new Congress is that, beginning on day one, we’re going to hold the crooks accountable.
