NEWARK, N.J. – A New York physical therapist was sentenced today for his role in a health care fraud scheme targeting Amtrak’s health care plan, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced.

Jaekwan Lee, 42, of Flushing, New York, pleaded guilty on May 12, 2026, before U.S. District Judge Madeline Cox Arleo in Newark federal court to conspiracy to commit health care fraud. Lee was sentenced today to 15 months’ imprisonment, two years’ supervised release, and ordered to pay $841,666 in restitution.

According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court:

From January 2022 through June 2022, Lee and his co-conspirators agreed to engage in a scheme to bill the Amtrak health care plan for fraudulent claims for services that never were provided and were medically unnecessary. Lee, a licensed physical therapist, allowed his license and business bank accounts to be used in the fraudulent billing scheme, in return for a portion of the proceeds. Other members of the conspiracy recruited Amtrak employees to participate in the scheme by paying them cash, in return for allowing the conspirators to use their personal and insurance information to submit false and fraudulent claims.

The overall scheme targeting the Amtrak health care plan involved dozens of Amtrak employees and multiple health care providers, who paid hundreds of thousands of dollars in cash kickbacks to Amtrak employees over the course of the scheme. In total, the Amtrak health care plan paid over $11 million in fraudulent claims associated with providers connected to the scheme. The Amtrak health care plan paid out $841,666 for claims associated with Lee. The investigation has resulted in the prosecution of nineteen individuals, including Lee. All have pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit health care fraud.

U.S. Attorney Frazer credited special agents of the Amtrak Office of Inspector General, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge James Harper, and the Amtrak Police Department, under the direction of Chief of Police James Cook, with the investigation.

The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorney Katherine M. Romano, Deputy Chief of the Bank Integrity, Money Laundering, and Recovery Unit in Newark.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division). The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

###

Defense counsel: Patrick J. McIlwain, Esq., Megan Rha, Esq.
title: New York Physical Therapist Sentenced to 15 Months in Prison for Role in $11 Million Scheme to Defraud the Amtrak Health Care Plan

MINNEAPOLIS – United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen announced that Eric Maurice Holliday was sentenced to 87 months in prison on one count of aiding and abetting interference with commerce by robbery.

Holliday previously pleaded guilty on June 11, 2026. He was sentenced before U.S. District Judge Patrick J. Schiltz on October 8, 2026.

According to court documents, in early April 2024, Holliday learned that a package containing approximately 10 pounds of marijuana would be delivered by a commercial package delivery service to a home in Maplewood, Minnesota. On or about April 19, 2024, the defendant traveled to the home with the intention of taking the package. Holliday traveled to the address with three associates, including Nasir Jones, who was armed with a firearm to aid their efforts in taking the package. Holliday had access to the tracking number of the package and thus knew the time the package would be delivered.

Upon arrival at the home, Holliday and his associates observed the commercial package delivery service employee bring the package to the door and also a man, James Newbill, standing at the doorway of the house. Jones and two others got out of the car, and Jones carried his gun visibly in one hand and ran up to the employee to wrestle the package from the employee’s hands and ran back into the car with Holliday. After Jones took the package, Jones and Newbill discharged their firearms towards each other, while the delivery service employee hid behind a car to avoid the gunfire. Holliday, Jones, and others then drove to a nearby home, where they split the marijuana from the package between them. The defendant intended to sell the marijuana.

During the sentencing hearing, Judge Schiltz noted that the defendant was the “instigator of the plan” and that he participated in a “reckless and dangerous crime that easily could have gotten someone killed.”

“The defendant helped execute a robbery to steal drugs and his associate brought a gun that endangered public safety while they committed the crime. Today’s sentence holds him accountable for his actions,” said United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen.

“This was not a spontaneous crime, but a coordinated effort to steal drugs using intimidation and firearms all the while putting a hapless delivery driver in a dangerous situation,” said ATF Special Agent in Charge Joseph Persails, of the St. Paul Field Division. “We are glad to see Mr. Holliday taking responsibility for his actions. ATF is committed to holding individuals accountable when firearms and criminal activity intersect. We were proud to work alongside the Maplewood Police Department on this case and will continue to work closely with the U.S. Attorney’s Office and our law‑enforcement partners to address violent criminal activity throughout Minnesota.”

This case was the result of an investigation by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), Maplewood Police Department, with assistance from the St. Paul Police Department, the Ramsey County Sheriff’s Office, and other law enforcement partners.

Assistant United States Attorneys William C. Mattessich and Nathan H. Nelson are prosecuting this case.
title: Man Sentenced to 87 Months’ Imprisonment for Role in Interfering with Commerce While Stealing Marijuana

MUSKOGEE, OKLAHOMA – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Oklahoma announced that Guadalupe Mancera-Cabello, a/k/a Guadalupe Mancera Cabello, a/k/a Guadalupe Mancer-Cabello, a/k/a Guadalupe Cabello Mancera, age 47, a Mexican national unlawfully present in Eufaula, Oklahoma, pleaded guilty to one count of Unlawful Reentry of Removed Alien, punishable by a term of imprisonment of not more than ten years, and a fine of not more than $250,000.00.

The charge arose from an investigation by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security’s Immigration and Customs Enforcement Division and the Oklahoma Highway Patrol.

The Indictment alleged that on September 3, 2026, Mancera-Cabello, an alien, was found in the United States without obtaining the express consent of the Secretary of Homeland Security to reapply for admission to the United States after having been previously removed on October 26, 2020.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

The Honorable D. Edward Snow, Magistrate Judge in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Oklahoma, accepted the plea and ordered the completion of a presentence investigation report.

A U.S. District Court Judge will determine the sentence to be imposed after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

Mancera-Cabello will remain in the custody of the United States Marshals Service pending sentencing.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Edith A. Singer represented the United States.

SIOUX FALLS - United States Attorney Ron Parsons announced today that Chief Judge Roberto A. Lange, United States District Court, has sentenced a Sioux Falls, South Dakota, man convicted of Failure to Register as a Sex Offender. The sentencing took place on October 5, 2026.

Brian Thunder Shield, age 29, was sentenced to two years and nine months in federal prison, followed by six years of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund.

Thunder Shield was indicted by a federal grand jury in January 2026. He pleaded guilty on August 3, 2026.

The conviction stemmed from Thunder Shield’s failure to register as a sex offender as required by federal law between October 17, 2025, and January 15, 2026. While unregistered, Thunder Shield allegedly committed a new sex offense. Charges related to that alleged conduct were filed by the Lincoln County States Attorney’s Office in March 2026 and remain pending. Thunder Shield had previously been convicted of a sex offense in federal court which requires him to register as a sex offender for the rest of his life.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse, launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the DOJ’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children, as well as identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc .

This case was investigated by the U.S. Marshals Service. Executive Assistant U.S. Attorney Alison J. Ramsdell prosecuted the case.

Thunder Shield was immediately remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service.
title: Sioux Falls Man Sentenced to Over 2 Years in Federal Prison for Failure to Register as a Sex Offender

The Department of War (DoW) today announced a series of initiatives to advance President Donald J. Trump's vision for a New Golden Age of American science. Building on the recommendations in the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios's report Science: A New Golden Age, these initiatives will modernize how the Department supports and evaluates scientific research, bring new talent to work on critical scientific challenges in defense of the nation, and strengthen partnerships across the science ecosystem between discovery, innovation, and national defense to ensure American warfighters are supported with cutting edge technology and capabilities.
"President Trump has made it clear that technological dominance requires us to move faster, safeguard our research, and build right here in America," said Emil Michael, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering. "We are answering that call by dismantling barriers to commercialization, modernizing our labs, and ruthlessly securing taxpayer-funded research from foreign exploitation. The Department of War will continue to turn the President's vision of a new golden age of science into unrivaled capability for our warfighters."
"Maintaining our technological edge requires balancing rapid innovation with responsible program protection," said Joseph Jewell, Ph.D., Assistant Secretary of War for Science and Technology. "As we accelerate how we move concepts from the lab to the field, we are equally committed to safeguarding federally funded research and ensuring domestic investments deliver tangible capabilities. By modernizing our testing facilities, empowering industry through initiatives like the Defense Patent Holiday, and expanding pathways for domestic scientific talent, we are safeguarding our nation's economic vitality and national security, ensuring this new golden age drives lasting domestic strength and unrivaled technological capabilities for our warfighters."
The Department's execution of the White House strategy includes major lines of effort led by the Office of the Assistant Secretary of War for Science and Technology:
1. Revitalizing America's Defense Research Enterprise
- Department of War and National Science Foundation Establish Memorandum of Understanding to Advance Science, Technology, and Innovation: The Department of War and the National Science Foundation (NSF) have established a broad memorandum of understanding (MOU) to pursue mutually beneficial collaborative activities in science, technology, and innovation. The MOU establishes a framework for the Department and NSF to explore and coordinate opportunities that strengthen the nation's research ecosystem, accelerate the transition of promising technologies, and promote collaboration among government, academic, industry, and other research partners. Initial areas of joint interest include X-Labs, the Programmable Cloud Laboratories Network, and AI Forge ($40 million), among other initiatives that advance experimentation, modernize research infrastructure, build the workforce, and push the development of emerging technologies. As part of this effort, the Department of War is dedicating $200M to Programmable Cloud Labs in Fiscal Year 2028 across the Future Years Defense Program (FYDP).
Through this partnership, the Department of War and NSF may identify opportunities for information exchange, joint workshops, research collaboration, pilot activities, and other initiatives consistent with each organization's authorities, priorities, and available resources.
- Department of War Advances Metascience-informed Framework to Strengthen the Defense Research Enterprise: Consistent with Science: A New Golden Age and the recommendations of the Defense Research Enterprise Review, the Department of War is establishing a new enterprise-wide framework to measure and improve the performance and effectiveness of its in-house laboratories, Federally Funded Research and Development Centers (FFRDCs) and University-Affiliated Research Centers (UARCs).
Implementing Recommendation 14 of the Department's recently published "Defense Research Enterprise Review," the initiative will apply metascience-informed principles to create measures of performance (MOP) and measures of effectiveness (MOE) as metrics.
The initiative reflects a metascience-informed approach to research management: using evidence and rigorous evaluation to improve how research organizations are assessed, governed, and resourced. Rather than impose a single scorecard on organizations with different missions, the Department will develop category-specific measures anchored to each institution's mission, comparative advantages, and enduring technical capabilities.
The framework will be designed to:
- Focus on outcomes: Assess whether portfolios achieve mission-relevant results commensurate with their resources and responsibilities
- Support independent verification: Use measures that can be audited and substantiated
- Measure progress over time: Track long-term performance consistent with the timelines of scientific research and engineering
- Respect institutional differences: Enable appropriate comparisons while recognizing that laboratories, warfare centers, medical research organizations, federally funded research and development centers, and university affiliated research centers have distinct missions and operating models
- Reduce distorted incentives: Avoid overreliance on narrow activity metrics that can encourage organizations to report volume instead of mission outcomes
- Inform leadership decisions: Strengthen the evidence base for portfolio management, resource allocation, and performance improvement
The Defense Research Enterprise Review found that existing enterprise measures, including activity counts and obligation and expenditure rates, remain useful for financial stewardship and oversight but do not independently capture portfolio-level outcomes. The new MOP/MOE framework is intended to complement—not replace—appropriate financial management and program oversight tools.
The Department is launching the framework with a limited pilot across representative research organizations to validate measures before engaging in a broader implementation.
- New Department of War Research Center Unites Academic Researchers with Broader Industry, Venture Capital, Non-Profit Ecosystem: The Department of War is catalyzing the university research ecosystem through the new Center for Defense Academic Research's (CeDAR) two complementary initiatives: the Problem-Based Basic Research Consortium (PBR-C) and the Translational Research Initiative for Academia and Defense (TRIAD) Partnership. Through PBR-C, the Department will unite multidisciplinary university research teams and world-class individual investigators to solve pressing scientific challenges, leveraging partnerships with non-profit research foundations, selective international collaborations, and participation from industry and venture capital observers. In parallel, TRIAD pairs transdisciplinary academic research teams with Service laboratories to develop actionable solutions for Combatant Command and Joint Interagency Task Force mission priorities.
2. Investing in America's Scientific Talent to Support the Warfighter
- Expansion of Hands-On Technical Learning: Fulfilling the White House directives to invest in individual researchers and elevate technical apprenticeships, the Department is expanding premier human capital programs. Celebrating its 20th anniversary, the Science, Mathematics, and Research for Transformation (SMART) Scholarship for Service Program welcomed its largest cohort of more than 750 scholars this year.
The DoW's SMART Program provides merit-based scholarships to bachelor's, master's, and doctoral students in STEM fields. In exchange for full tuition, stipends, and internship opportunities, scholars commit to a one-to-one service period as civilian employees with the DoW. Since its inception in 2006, the SMART program has awarded over 6,500 scholarships, with 91 percent of scholars successfully completing the program.
Beginning this fiscal year, the Department of War will explore a talent exchange initiative that would connect the Department of Energy's (DOE's) Genesis Mission Fellowship program to the DoW's SMART and National Defense Science and Engineering Graduate (NDSEG) programs. This partnership enables DoW and DOE scholars to intern with each other's laboratories and industry partners, putting opportunities in academia, government laboratories, and companies under one umbrella.
The Department's flagship SMART and NDSEG programs are producing a new generation of scientific leaders. To date, the two programs boast over 5,000 Ph.D. graduates between them; these graduates have gone on to fill critical roles within the Department, drive innovation in the private sector, and advance the frontiers of knowledge in academia.
Complementing this talent pipeline, the NDSEG program has cultivated the nation's scientific minds since 1989, awarding nearly 4,900 fellowships. The program offers full tuition and a generous stipend for up to three years to individuals pursuing doctoral degrees, with no service obligation. This provides fellows with the flexibility to pursue careers across academia, industry, and government, with 90 percent of graduates entering research and development roles, broadly strengthening the U.S. innovation ecosystem.
The SMART SEED Innovation Award supports SMART scholars as they begin their DoW employment after completing their doctorates. The technical work completed through SEED, which provides funding of up to $155,000 per year for up to three years, aligns with Department missions or critical technology areas.
The Department of War is proud to announce the Fiscal Year 2026 SMART SEED Innovation Award principal investigators:
- Jeffrey Becker, Naval Surface Warfare Center – Carderock Division, West Bethesda, MD
- Brian Burke, Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division – Patuxent River, Patuxent River, MD
- Alexander Chen, Air Force Research Laboratory – Information & Spectrum Warfare Directorate, Rome, NY
- Luke Fina, Naval Surface Warfare Center – Panama City Division, Panama City, FL
- Charris Gabaldon, Naval Information Warfare Center Atlantic, Norfolk, VA
- Nathan Gajowski, Air Force Research Laboratory – Space Warfare, Kirtland AFB, NM
- Jeffrey Koenig, Defense Centers for Public Health – Aberdeen, Aberdeen Proving Ground, MD
- Timothy Lim, Air Force Research Laboratory – Information and Spectrum Warfare Directorate, Kirtland AFB, NM
- Maile McCann, U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center – Coastal Hydraulics Laboratory, Duck, NC
- Jennifer Mejia, U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center – Environmental Laboratory, Vicksburg, MS
- Tristan Melton, Naval Surface Warfare Center – Corona Division, Corona, CA
- Alexander Perruci, Air Force Research Laboratory – Information and Spectrum Warfare Directorate, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, OH
- Nhon Phan, U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) Army Research Laboratory, Aberdeen Proving Ground, MD
- Trent Schreiber, U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center – Construction Engineering Research Laboratory, Champaign, IL
- Varsha Swamy, U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center – Geotechnical and Structures Laboratory (GSL), Vicksburg, MS
- Juliet Swinea, U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center – GSL, Vicksburg, MS
- Amani Webber-Schultz, Naval Undersea Warfare Center- Newport Division, Newport, RI
- Daniel Weitsman, U.S. Army DEVCOM Aviation Missile Center – Technology Development Directorate, Fort Eustis, VA
- Ethan Wright, Naval Surface Warfare Center- Panama City Division, Panama City, FL
Since Fiscal Year 2020, SMART SEED awards have invested $41 million in 140 projects, resulting in new patents, publications, and advanced defense technologies. Ultimately, these programs ensure the long-term sustainability of an agile, highly capable STEM workforce equipped to safeguard national security and maintain America's enduring technological edge.
3. Accelerating and Safeguarding American Defense Innovation
- Enforce Robust Research Security and Program Protection: The Department has strengthened its Science & Technology Program Protection and Maintaining Technology Advantage frameworks to support implementation of National Security Presidential Memorandum-33 (NSPM-33). The Department conducts rigorous risk-based reviews of fundamental research, screens against National Defense Authorization Act Section 1286 foreign-risk entity lists, ensures strict compliance with Section 1062 foreign institution limits, and executes mandatory foreign ownership due diligence. This ensures technological advancements made in America can be translated into operational capabilities for the United States and our allies.
- Dismantle Commercialization Barriers via the Defense Patent Holiday Initiative: The Department is responding to the White House's mandate to reform intellectual property licensing and open federal innovations to non-traditional builders through the Defense Patent Holiday Initiative. This initiative directly supports White House priorities by rapidly accelerating the transition of Department-funded technologies into the commercial sector. By granting royalty-free licensing windows to federally developed patents, the Department empowers private-sector innovators to commercialize breakthrough defense hardware without navigating months of legal friction.
- Leverage R&D to Strengthen Domestic Manufacturing: The Department of War's ManTech Program celebrated its 70th anniversary this year and serves as the Department's primary bridge from prototypes to programs of record, shaping not just what the military designs, but how it is produced affordably, securely, and at scale. The Department's Manufacturing Innovation Institutes (MIIs) include a network of nine active, defense-led institutes across the nation, including the latest addition, the FutureTEX institute in Belmont, North Carolina.
These unified lines of effort strengthen the American innovation pipeline and deliver unmatched capabilities to our warfighters.
title: Department of War Executes White House Strategy for a New Golden Age of Science

ATF operation in Washington nets 42 defendants
To combat increasing violence, ATF and law enforcement partners target violent offenders and firearm traffickers
Moses Lake, WA – Yesterday, ATF and the Moses Lake Police Department Street Crimes Unit, with assistance from other law enforcement partners, arrested six suspects and executed eight simultaneous search warrants between Moses Lake and Spokane, Washington. Floyd Young, Eutimio De Padua Contreras, Wilmer Garcia-Marquez, Juan Preciado, Juvenal Herrera-Mata, and Cristobal Rios Sostenes were arrested for various offenses, including unlawful firearm possession, distribution of methamphetamine, and distribution of cocaine. These individuals were the final six arrests stemming from ATF Operation 11th Hour, a 15-month collaborative effort to reduce violent crime in the Grant County area.
ATF Operation 11th Hour was initiated after a gang-style shooting in Moses Lake tragically claimed the life a 14-year-old and put several others in the hospital with gunshot wounds. This operation specifically targeted individuals with a high propensity of violence, gang members, those who traffic in the tools of violence, and armed drug traffickers and their organizations.
“Keeping our communities safe requires more than individual agencies working in isolation: it requires a unified commitment to confronting those who commit violent crimes and threaten the safety of our residents,” said Jonthan Blais, Special Agent in Charge of the ATF Seattle Field Division. “This operation is a clear demonstration of the strength of our partnerships and our collective resolve. By targeting violent offenders and removing unlawful firearms and dangerous drugs and from our streets, we are disrupting the criminal activity that fuels violence and puts our residents at risk. ATF will continue to leverage every available resource and partnership to hold violent offenders accountable and reduce the threat they pose to the public.”
Over the course of the operation, several local, state, and federal agencies joined forces to execute 54 federal search warrants and 37 state search warrants, netting 42 total defendants. Additionally, the following items have been seized: 25 firearms, 9 vehicles, approximately 42lbs of meth, more than 1,000 fentanyl pills, almost 2lbs of fentanyl powder, and more than 2lbs of cocaine.
“This case is an excellent example of the impact that can be made when federal and local law enforcement work together to target issues in our communities,” said City of Moses Lake Police Department Chief David Sands. “I am grateful for all the work done at every level of this operation to take illegal weapons and drugs off our streets.”
“Drug trafficking and violence go hand in hand, putting innocent lives and entire communities at risk,” said Robert A. Saccone, Special Agent in Charge, DEA Seattle Field Division. “This operation demonstrates what we can accomplish when law enforcement partners unite to take dangerous drugs, firearms, and violent offenders off our streets. Through Fentanyl Free America, DEA will continue working alongside our federal, state, and local partners to disrupt the fentanyl supply chain, reduce its availability, and save American lives.”
Of the 42 defendants identified during this operation, 24 have been federally indicted and 6 are facing state charges.
Operation 11th Hour was initiated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) and the Moses Lake Police Department Street Crimes Unit, with assistance from DEA, U.S. Border Patrol, IRS-CI, FBI, Washington State Liquor and Cannabis Board, Washington State Patrol, U.S. Marshals Service – Pacific Northwest Violent Offender Task Force (PNVOTF), and the Grant County Sheriff’s Office Interagency Narcotics Enforcement Team (INET).
Those individuals who have been federally indicted are being prosecuted by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Washington. Those facing state charges are being prosecuted by the Grant County Prosecuting Attorney’s Office.
title: ATF operation in Washington nets 42 defendants

Rollins Urges Federal Land Ranchers to Put June Grazing Directive to Work
(WASHINGTON, D.C., October 8, 2026) — Today, U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins sent a letter to all livestock ranchers holding grazing permits on U.S. Forest Service allotments, outlining the Department’s June 12, 2026 Grazing Directive and inviting producers to put it to work on their allotments.
The letter builds on the October 20, 2025 USDA Plan to Fortify the American Beef Industry and the March 31, 2026 Advancing Grazing on Forest Service and BLM Lands Memorandum of Understanding signed by Secretary Rollins and Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum. Together with the Grazing Directive issued by Secretary Rollins and Under Secretary for Natural Resources and Environment Michael Boren, the three documents describe Administration policy to streamline and expand livestock grazing on federal lands, elevate grazing as a priority, and strengthen support for America’s ranchers within the framework of existing law and regulations.
“You embody the ethos of our nation’s founding 250 years ago,” said Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins. “For the past 19 months, USDA has worked tirelessly to defend and promote our nation’s ranchers and give you the tools to help rebuild our Great American Cattle Herd. I encourage you to familiarize yourself with the Grazing Directive as we work together to accomplish shared goals on your respective allotments.”
For more information, see the full letter (PDF, 312 KB).
Background:
The U.S. Forest Service and the Bureau of Land Management administer approximately 240 million acres of rangelands across 28 states, supporting more than 23,000 permittees and lessees. Secretary Rollins noted that restoring the nation’s beef and sheep herds will, by necessity, include both Forest Service and BLM lands.
The June Grazing Directive directs the Forest Service, consistent with applicable law and regulation, to:
- Take appropriate measures to restore at least 500,000 head months across National Forest System lands within two years;
- Implement a policy of no net loss of Animal Unit Months within allotments;
- Make vacant and closed allotments available for grazing;
- Improve wildfire planning, coordination, and recovery, including the use of virtual fencing;
- Improve National Environmental Policy Act efficiencies; and
- Improve coordination and build positive relationships with ranchers.
The letter also points to the new USDA Ranchers First webpage at www.usda.gov/ranchers-first, which details actions taken under the Trump Administration to support grazing, processing, and the long-term strength of the American cattle herd.
Producers who believe they have been subjected to agricultural lawfare may submit information through the Farmer and Rancher Freedom Framework at www.usda.gov/lawfare. Grazing-specific concerns may be sent to grazing@usda.gov.

EPA Approves Removal of Burdensome Permitting Requirements Following Georgia’s Air Quality Attainment Status
ATLANTA (October 8, 2026) — Today, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) approved revisions to Georgia’s State Implementation Plan (SIP), removing unnecessary permitting requirements. Following the entire State of Georgia coming into attainment for National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) in 2022, EPA has determined that permitting requirements previously in place to help reach air quality standards are no longer required or needed under the Clean Air Act (CAA). This milestone will help promote economic growth across Georgia by removing burdensome requirements that slow energy construction and discourage reshoring of manufacturing, all while maintaining clean air within the state.
“EPA is proud to put cooperative federalism into action and work with the State of Georgia to remove these obsolete permitting requirements. By clarifying the regulatory landscape, businesses in Georgia will have certainty as they look to invest in the Peach State,” said EPA Regional Administrator Kevin McOmber. “Years of work have gone into reaching this point, and we are confident that the state continues to have the tools to maintain clean air for all Georgians.”
Today’s action will remove all nonattainment New Source Review (NNSR) requirements, certain provisions related to the use of emission reduction credits, and other mandated programs in Georgia’s SIP that were put in place when areas were still in nonattainment for the NAAQS. Under the best reading of the CAA, EPA determined that removing these permitting programs from Georgia’s SIP will not interfere with attainment or maintenance of the NAAQS or any other applicable statutorily obligations. Georgia’s SIP will continue to include permitting programs designed to protect the state’s attainment with the NAAQS.
On background:
EPA proposed to approve the removal of the NNSR program from the Georgia SIP on September 2, 2025, and held a 30-day comment period.
Georgia has not had any designated nonattainment areas since EPA’s approval of the redesignation of the Atlanta area for the 2015 ozone NAAQS on October 17, 2022.
title: EPA Approves Removal of Burdensome Permitting Requirements Following Georgia’s Air Quality Attainment Status

HUD Announces Arrests of Nearly 500 Fraudsters and Fugitives
Nationwide Crackdown Restores Safety to HUD Housing and Communities
October 8, 2026
WASHINGTON – Secretary Turner applauded the work of Operation Clean House, a multi-agency, multi-month law enforcement initiative targeting fugitives living in HUD-assisted housing, for arresting 491 criminal fugitives. HUD Office of Inspector General (OIG) Special Agents partnered with the U.S. Marshals Service and state and local law enforcement across 12 cities to carry out this mission.
“We will not allow criminal predators and fraudsters to use HUD housing as a haven or live freely on the taxpayer’s dime,” said Secretary Turner, a member of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud. “Operation Clean House removed dangerous drug traffickers, rapists, and sex offenders and delivered real accountability. President Trump promised to restore once-great American cities, and we are fulfilling that promise by making our communities safer.”
“These arrests are only one part of our strategy. Our investigators, auditors, evaluators, and analysts are attacking threats to HUD programs from every direction. Whether it is violent criminals hiding in HUD-assisted housing, fraudsters stealing taxpayer dollars, or weaknesses that leave federal housing programs vulnerable to abuse, we will use every authority and every tool available to protect these programs and the people they serve,” said Acting Inspector General Brian D. Harrison.
“Public housing is for the needy, not criminals. Thankfully, Secretary Turner will not sleep until all crooks and fraudsters are kicked out,” said Scott Brady, Executive Director of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud.
Operation Clean House carried out arrests in Memphis, Tennessee; New York City, New York; Newark, New Jersey; Chicago, Illinois; Los Angeles, California; Kansas City, Missouri; Kansas City, Kansas; New Orleans, Louisiana; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; Cleveland, Ohio; Minneapolis, Minnesota; Columbus, Ohio; and others.
Working with the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, HUD is rooting out waste and holding fraudsters accountable with real consequences.
- In June, HUD held Los Angeles’ homeless industrial complex accountable and suspended the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority (LAHSA) from receiving further taxpayer funds. LAHSA has received over $1 billion in tax dollars since 2013 despite its record of fraud.
- In September, Secretary Turner announced the arrests of LA fraudsters who stole $14 million, including taxpayer funds received through LAHSA, instead of serving the homeless.
- In July, HUD suspended funding to the Virgin Islands Housing Finance Authority, which received $1.9 billion, due to widespread financial mismanagement and improper payments.

Congresswoman Gwen Moore Leads Effort to Crack Down on Corrupt, Taxpayer-Funded Settlements
Congresswoman Gwen Moore introduced the Executive Settlement Review Act to provide stronger oversight and independent review and approval of any legal settlements that occur between the President, his political allies, or personal associates, and the federal government they oversee. This legislation comes as the Trump administration has sought to use taxpayer funds for a $1.8 billion slush fund, which could have paid violent January 6th insurrectionists.
“Trump has attempted to use sham government settlements to enrich himself and protect his family from legal scrutiny. And it likely doesn’t stop at him. I’m dismayed by recent reports that Treasury Secretary Bessent may be negotiating sweetheart deals with the IRS for himself. Congress and the Judiciary must work to prevent corruption and grift in the executive branch. My bill, the Executive Settlement Review Act, fulfills a need for a fair and comprehensive process to ensure that our tax dollars aren’t misused and that the public and Congress are aware of the details of any settlement that are at a heightened risk of abuse,” said Congresswoman Gwen Moore.
The provisions of this bill would apply to pending lawsuits brought against the United States by the currently serving President, Vice President, Cabinet members, certain senior federal officials, their families, and their businesses, with exemptions for those seeking small claims.
Key Provisions of the bill:
    - Formal filing of the proposed agreement by the Department of Justice with a federal district court, led by a panel of three judges.
- A 60-day period in which the public can and submit comments on any proposed settlements, comments that the government must address and which the court must consider. 
- Submission of written briefs to the court by both parties outlining the merits and rationale of the agreement, including the disclosure of any documents or communications that informed their decision to settle.
- Review of the settlement by the three-judge district court panel, who will assess whether the settlement agreement is lawful, factual, and settles a legitimate legal dispute, among other criteria.
title: Congresswoman Gwen Moore Leads Effort to Crack Down on Corrupt, Taxpayer-Funded Settlements

Suozzi Convenes Long Island Robotics Roundtable
      Image    
Convenes Roundtable with CEO of Standard Bots, Largest Manufacturer of Industrial Robots in America, and Other Leaders
Pushes to make region a hub for robotics and advanced manufacturing
Glen Cove, NY—Congressman Tom Suozzi (D-NY) today convened business, technology, and workforce development leaders for a roundtable discussion on how to position Long Island to become a national hub for robotics and advanced manufacturing. The roundtable was held at Standard Bots in conjunction with CEO Evan Beard, the largest manufacturer of industrial robots in the United States.
“Standard Bots is a great example of why Long Island has the talent, the universities, the skilled workforce, and the entrepreneurial spirit to be the nation’s leader in robotics and advanced manufacturing. We need to bring all those pieces together and make sure we are competing for the businesses and jobs of the future,” said Congressman Suozzi. “Robotics and advanced manufacturing are going to play an increasingly important role in our economy, not only because of their effectiveness but because the industry creates high-skilled, high-tech jobs that have good wages for the people of Long Island.”
The roundtable brought together leaders from the robotics, manufacturing, financial, and economic development sectors to discuss the rapid growth of the domestic and international robotics industry, the role of robotics in strengthening American manufacturing, the future of robotics and physical AI on Long Island, and the opportunities for Long Island to attract robotics companies, develop a skilled local workforce, and improve its existing strengths in technology, manufacturing, engineering, and research. Participants also explored federal initiatives that could promote robotics, including tariffs, grant opportunities, research and development supports, expansion of workforce development initiatives, tax credits, safety standards for newer AI-powered robots, and more.
The roundtable was held at Standard Bots in Glen Cove, the largest manufacturer of industrial robots in America. Suozzi opened the event and moderated a discussion featuring Evan Beard, Co-Founder, CEO and Chief Engineer of Standard Bots; Robert Kufner, President and CEO of Designatronics; Tommy McNulty, Head of Platform Sales at Erebor Bank; Cara Longworth, VP, Long Island Regional Director of Empire State Development; and Amy Erickson, Executive Director of Long Island Manufacturing Extension Partnership.
Beard delivered the keynote address on the state of the domestic and international robotics industry and the opportunities ahead for Long Island and the United States. 
“The next era of manufacturing will be won by the countries that build their own robots, and we believe America should lead it. That's why we design and build our robots right here in Glen Cove, with some of the most talented engineers, machinists, and builders anywhere in the world. Long Island has a proud manufacturing legacy, and we're grateful to Congressman Suozzi for bringing industry, government, and investors together to make this region a home for American robotics,” said Evan Beard, CEO & Co-founder, Standard Bots.
“Robotics is the fastest growing market in the world. It will fundamentally change how work gets done in your home and in nearly all business segments. Unfortunately, much of the global supply of robots has come from outside the U.S., but the through the good work of Rep. Suozzi and leaders across industries on Long Island that have the capability to build robots, it has been recognized that future supply can and must be made domestically with American made products. Long Island’s proximity to New York City where hundreds of robotics startups are being nurtured gives it a distinct advantage to support their growth as well as the thousands of other robotics companies across the country that are getting ready to scale. Long Island has a long history in advanced manufacturing and already has all the components to become a national hub for robotics and advanced manufacturing with the right amount of coordination,” said Robert Kufner, President and CEO, Designatronics.
“As Executive Director of the Long Island MEP (LIMEP) at Stony Brook University, I see a tremendous opportunity for our small and mid-sized manufacturers to strengthen their competitiveness through the adoption of advanced technologies, particularly robotics. LIMEP is committed to helping manufacturers understand how automation and robotics can improve productivity, efficiency, and long-term growth. Today’s event at Standard Bots, hosted by Congressman Suozzi and Evan Beard, CEO and Founder of Standard Bots, was an excellent example of how industry, government, and the manufacturing community can come together to advance this mission. Evan also served as a keynote speaker at our LIMEP–College of Engineering robotics event, helping regional manufacturers see the practical opportunities that robotics can bring to their operations. We thank Congressman Suozzi and Evan Beard for their continued leadership and support of the NY MEP Network—and especially LIMEP at Stony Brook University—as we work to strengthen Long Island’s manufacturing ecosystem and position our companies for the future,” said Amy Erickson, Executive Director, Long Island Manufacturing Extension Partnership.
title: Suozzi Convenes Long Island Robotics Roundtable

NIH announces record number of grants to support early career investigators, launches new recruitment initiative for intramural research
Thursday, October 8, 2026
NIH announces record number of grants to support early career investigators, launches new recruitment initiative for intramural research
NIH highlights actions to strengthen American biomedical science at White House Science: A New Golden Age Summit.
The National Institutes of Health (NIH) today announced significant accomplishments that underscore the agency’s progress in strengthening the U.S. biomedical research enterprise. The agency announced that 1,648 early-stage investigators are receiving NIH support through R01-equivalent extramural research grant awards in fiscal year 2026, the most ever recorded. The agency also launched Generation Discovery, a new initiative to recruit 100 early-career Principal Investigators into NIH’s Intramural Research Program.
The NIH shared these and other recent accomplishments as part of the Science: A New Golden Age Summit, an event hosted by the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) to highlight the comprehensive rethinking of the U.S. science and technology enterprise in the Science: A New Golden Age report and to showcase significant areas of progress.
“NIH is building the future of American biomedical science,” said NIH Director Jay Bhattacharya. “That means demanding the highest standards of rigor, giving exceptional scientists the freedom to pursue bold ideas, attracting new talent, and putting powerful, innovative technologies to work. These actions will help turn scientific possibility into discoveries that improve and save lives.”
The Trump Administration places a high priority on increasing opportunities for early-stage investigators to receive funding support to test new ideas. NIH has found that the average age of an extramural researcher serving for the first time as a principal investigator on a R01-equivalent grant has climbed in recent decades, from 38 years old in FY1995 to 42 in FY2025. The 1,648 R01-equivalent grants awarded to support early-stage investigators in FY2026 represented a 25% increase over the ten-year average of 1,323.
With NIH’s Intramural Research Program (IRP), Generation Discovery is a concerted effort to connect talented early-career researchers with the unparalleled resources and research opportunities found within the IRP.
Beyond these two announcements, NIH highlighted several other initiatives and accomplishments designed to reinvigorate American biomedical science.
Strengthening Scientific Rigor and Reproducibility
A cornerstone of NIH’s efforts is strengthening replication and reproducibility — the ability to test scientific findings and determine whether they hold up when examined again. Because new discoveries build on earlier research, ensuring that findings are reliable is critical to advancing science and directing time and resources toward the most promising paths.
As part of this agency-wide initiative, NIH plans to establish its first metascience office. The office will serve as a central hub for studying and improving how biomedical science is conducted and coordinating NIH efforts to make rigorous, reproducible research a more integral part of the scientific enterprise.
Those efforts include the launch of a new NIH-wide program, known as Rigor, Replicability, & Reproducibility to Promote Excellence, Accuracy, & Translation in Science, or R3PEATS, that will support research, partnerships, infrastructure and training to improve the reliability of biomedical science. They also include NIH’s Linked Discoveries, an experimental PubMed tool recently launched to help researchers see how individual findings fit within the broader body of biomedical evidence.
New Models for Tackling Complex Challenges
NIH is creating new ways to tackle complex scientific and technical challenges. In partnership with the National Science Foundation (NSF), NIH will advance X-Labs, a research model that brings together full-time, interdisciplinary teams with the resources, flexibility and operational independence to pursue ambitious technical goals that are difficult to address through traditional research approaches. NIH and NSF will seek input from the research community to identify potential X-Labs topics focused on priority biomedical research challenges.
Accelerating AI-Enabled Discovery
NIH is leading the Bio-Genesis Mission, part of the national Genesis Mission, to harness Super Intelligence (SI), data, and advanced computational approaches to accelerate biomedical discovery. Efforts include challenges focused on using SI and data to advance pediatric cancer research and repurpose generic drugs, work with the Department of Energy to build the cross-agency Genesis Mission Platform, and a new partnership with Biohub on virtual cell models for the Predicting Living Systems Challenge. NIH will also explore opportunities to develop scientists with expertise in SI and other scientific disciplines and connect trainees with Genesis Mission research opportunities at NIH and partner laboratories.
Developing Scientific Talent
NIH is expanding opportunities for scientists to pursue ambitious ideas and build independent research careers. In fiscal year 2026, NIH supported 1,648 early-stage investigators, the highest number in a single year in NIH history, as part of its commitment to helping early-career researchers establish independent scientific programs. NIH will also broaden its use of Investigator-Focused Awards (R35), which provide greater stability and flexibility to pursue promising scientific directions, and continue using prizes and challenges to spur new approaches to priority scientific and health problems.
NIH is extending that commitment to its own laboratories through Generation Discovery, a new initiative to recruit 100 outstanding investigators to the NIH Intramural Research Program over the next three years to pursue ambitious biomedical research.
Looking Ahead
Together, these efforts reflect NIH’s commitment to strengthening the foundations of American biomedical research while creating new opportunities for discovery. By advancing rigorous and reproducible science, investing in the future of the research workforce, and developing new ways to tackle complex scientific challenges, NIH is working to accelerate discoveries that improve health and strengthen U.S. leadership in biomedical research.
About the National Institutes of Health (NIH): NIH, the nation's medical research agency, includes 27 Institutes and Centers and is a component of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. NIH is the primary federal agency conducting and supporting basic, clinical, and translational medical research, and is investigating the causes, treatments, and cures for both common and rare diseases. For more information about NIH and its programs, visit www.nih.gov.
NIH…Turning Discovery Into Health®
title: NIH announces record number of grants to support early career investigators, launches new recruitment initiative for intramural research

The wing’s two flying units — the 815th Airlift Squadron and the 53rd Weather Reconnaissance Squadron, known as the Air Force Reserve Hurricane Hunters — relocated aircraft to Joint Base San Antonio, Texas. The Hurricane Hunters will continue flying weather reconnaissance missions into Isaias from Kelly Field, Texas, collecting data for the National Hurricane Center to improve storm track and intensity forecasts.
At 10 a.m. CDT, Hurricane Isaias was located about 380 miles south of the mouth of the Mississippi River, with maximum sustained winds near 85 mph. The National Hurricane Center forecasts Isaias will strengthen and make landfall along the northern Gulf Coast within the hurricane warning area late Friday or early Saturday.
“We are relocating our aircraft as a prudent measure to protect these critical assets while preserving our ability to conduct weather reconnaissance,” said Col. Jaret Fish, 403rd Wing commander. “This action enables the Hurricane Hunters to continue providing essential data to National Hurricane Center forecasters while our Airmen prepare Keesler for the storm’s impacts.”
Although El Niño conditions have contributed to a slower-than-normal Atlantic hurricane season, Fish said one storm can still have significant consequences for communities and military installations in its path.
A hurricane warning is in effect for part of the Mississippi Gulf Coast. The National Hurricane Center forecasts hurricane conditions Friday night into early Saturday, along with potentially dangerous storm surge, heavy rainfall, flooding and isolated tornadoes. Personnel and residents should monitor local weather information and follow instructions from local emergency-management officials.
Wing leadership encourages all Airmen and their families to review personal hurricane preparedness plans, complete appropriate protective actions and remain attentive to official installation messaging.
title: 403rd Wing evacuates aircraft, continues to fly Hurricane Isaias

BIRMINGHAM, Ala. – A North Carolina man appeared in federal court this week following allegations that he voted multiple times in the same election across two states, announced U.S. Attorney Phillip W. Williams Jr.

A one-count indictment returned by a federal grand jury charges Forrest Scott Woody, 68, of Hendersonville, North Carolina, with illegally voting more than once.

According to the indictment, Woody voted twice in the 2024 general election. In particular, he voted in Calhoun County, Alabama, after having already voted in the same election in Henderson County, North Carolina.

“Every election is an important opportunity for eligible voters to make their voices heard, and the integrity of the election depends on voters following the law,” said U.S. Attorney Williams. “As we approach the upcoming election, we will continue to work with our law enforcement partners to ensure that election laws are respected and that every lawful vote is counted.”

“Maintaining the sanctity of our country’s election system is one of the highest callings of federal law enforcement, and this indictment is yet another example of how seriously our office takes that mission,” said Assistant U.S. Attorney and Election Crimes Coordinator Brett A. Janich.

“Ensuring public confidence in our elections is a responsibility we take seriously,” said David R. Fitzgibbons, Special Agent in Charge, FBI Birmingham. “When individuals attempt to undermine that process, the FBI will work with our partners to safeguard the integrity of every vote.”

“I appreciate the U.S. Attorney Phil Williams and his team in the U.S. Attorney’s Office and all other federal agencies who are assisting in the investigation and prosecution of this case,” said Secretary of State Wes Allen. “I want to also thank the team in my office. Election integrity is a top priority of mine.”

FBI investigated the case, with the assistance of the Alabama Secretary of State’s Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Brett A. Janich is prosecuting the case.

An indictment contains only charges. A defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.
title: North Carolina Man Arraigned in Federal Court for Voting More Than Once in a Single Election

HAMMOND – Zachary Nelson, 27 years old, of Lowell, Indiana, was sentenced to probation by United States District Court Judge Gretchen Lund after pleading guilty to felony delay of mail, announced United States Attorney Adam L. Mildred.

“Zachary Nelson, a Rural Mail Carrier for the United States Postal Service, on multiple occasions in 2025 intentionally failed to deliver hundreds of mailers to the addresses on his assigned mail route, including mailers for private businesses and for Medicare. He sometimes threw the mailers in the garbage, abusing his position of public trust to conceal his actions. The U.S. Postal Service trusted Nelson to properly deliver the mail that was placed in his custody, and he chose to betray that trust. Government officials are held accountable to the people they serve. This case was investigated by the United States Postal Service Office of Inspector General and prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Kevin F. Wolff. The US Postal Inspector General's Office and the US Attorney's Office will always work diligently to deter, detect, and prosecute government fraud whenever it occurs,” said U.S. Attorney Adam L. Mildred.

This sentencing represents the hard work and dedication by USPS OIG Special Agents working with the U.S. Attorney’s Office to bring charges on this significant mail theft investigation,” said Special Agent in Charge Dennus Bishop, U.S. Postal Service Office of Inspector General, Central Area Field Office. The United States Postal Service Office of Inspector General along with our law enforcement partners, remain committed to safeguarding the U.S. Mail and ensuring the accountability and integrity of U.S. Postal Service employees.”
title: Lowell Man Sentenced for Felony Delay of Mail

Today, Congresswoman Suzan DelBene (WA-01) joined Washington state’s entire Congressional delegation in a letter to President Donald Trump urging him to approve Governor Bob Ferguson’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance to help communities recover and repair damage due to the devastating wildfires that swept through Central and Eastern Washington from July 23 through August 31.
For the first time, on August 1, the National Weather Service upgraded a Red Flag Warning for fire weather conditions to a Particularly Dangerous Situation, which is very rare and typically reserved for extreme fire weather conditions. Three massive fires broke out and tore through neighborhoods across Spokane: the Old Trails Fire burned in northwest Spokane, the Autumn Lane Fire burned near Nine-Mile Falls, and the Fairview Fire burned in Mead. The Spokane Complex Fires forced 67,000 people to evacuate, burned nearly 10,000 acres, with damages predicted to exceed $1 billion.
This was one of Washington state’s worst wildfire seasons on record, with fires causing severe damage and threatening lives, property, businesses, and livestock. In Okanogan County, the Kaiser Canyon, Modrite, and Sinlahekin fires burned over 350,000 acres total.
“As members of the Washington state delegation, we write in support of Washington state’s addendum to include Public Assistance to their September 28th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance due to devastating wildfire damages incurred from July 23rd through August 31st. We implore you to approve the request for public and individual assistance as quickly as possible,” the lawmakers wrote. “Washington state suffered from a historic wildfire season, with multiple wildfires ravaging parts of Central and Eastern Washington, devastating communities in Asotin, Chelan, Columbia, Douglas, Ferry, Grant, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens, Whitman, and Yakima Counties, as well as the Spokane Tribe of Indians.”
The lawmakers continued, “Local, Tribal, state, federal, and out-of-state firefighting crews deployed quickly, pooling resources to contain the fires and protect both life and property. Fire crews faced dangerous conditions, including hazardous terrain, high winds, and record-setting drought, which made the fires extremely difficult to contain. Many of these fires burned over the course of several weeks, and damaged public infrastructure like roads, bridges, public utility systems, and other essential public assets. Beyond the infrastructure that was completely lost to the wildfires, the prolonged exposure to fire, smoke, and extreme temperatures have left remaining infrastructure vulnerable to further damage and unsafe for the public.” 
“These devastating wildfires have put significant stress on Washington state’s infrastructure and emergency response resources. Throughout the crisis, local, Tribal, state, federal, and international first responders stepped up and worked tirelessly to keep our communities safe. We thank you for your timely approval of the state’s request for an Emergency Declaration which provided vital federal support for both mitigation and recovery. We reiterate our full support for the October 6th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance and thank you in advance for your prompt attention to this urgent matter,” the lawmakers concluded.
Joining DelBene in the letter to President Trump were Washington Senators Patty Murray and Maria Cantwell, and Representatives Rick Larsen (WA-02), Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (WA-03), Dan Newhouse (WA-04), Michael Baumgartner (WA-05), Emily Randall (WA-06), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Kim Schrier M.D. (WA-08), Adam Smith (WA-09), and Marilyn Strickland (WA-10).
The full letter can be found 
here
.
title: WA Delegation Supports Governor’s Request for Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance for Devastating Wildfires in Washington

CHARLESTON, W.Va. – Deon Dewayne Grundy, 29, of Cuyahoga Falls, Ohio, was sentenced on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, to two years and nine months in prison, to be followed by four years of supervised release, for possession with intent to distribute 40 grams or more of fentanyl.

According to court documents and statements made in court, on September 3, 2025, law enforcement officers executed a search warrant at a Beckley residence where Grundy was living and seized 86 grams of fentanyl and $1,659. As part of his plea agreement, Grundy admitted that he intended to distribute the seized fentanyl. Grundy further admitted that he sold approximately 5 grams of fentanyl earlier that day to a confidential informant at the Beckley residence in exchange for $300. The cash seized during the search included $40 from the controlled buy.

United States Attorney Moore Capito made the announcement and commended the investigative work of the Beckley/Raleigh County Drug and Violent Crime Unit, which consists of officers from the West Virginia State Police, the Raleigh County Sheriff’s Office, and the Beckley Police Department.

Chief United States District Judge Frank W. Volk imposed the sentence. Assistant United States Attorney Brian D. Parsons prosecuted the case.

A copy of this press release is located on the website of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of West Virginia. Related court documents and information can be found on PACER by searching for Case No. 5:26-cr-8.

Reps. Tlaib and Green lead letter demanding release of DACA recipient in ICE custody
Ya’akub Ira Vijandre has now been in ICE custody for a year for ‘liking’ a social media post
WASHINGTON – U.S. Reps. Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) and Al Green (TX-09) joined by 21 Members of Congress demanded the release of Ya’akub Ira Vijandre, who was detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement a year ago as of yesterday. In a letter to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and ICE Acting Director David Venturella, the Members pressed for answers regarding Ya’akub’s unconstitutional arrest and prolonged detention after a federal judge allowed his habeas challenge to proceed.
Ya’akub, a Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals recipient, has lived in the U.S. since he was 14 years old. He spent a decade working for American Airlines as a senior safety specialist and was recognized for supporting grieving families after a helicopter crashed into a plane in Washington, D.C. Despite having no criminal record and not being charged with any crime, he was targeted and arrested at gun point for speaking out against Israel’s genocide in Gaza and for “liking” a social media post with Quranic verses–both of which are protected by the First Amendment.
“The administration’s stated basis for [Ya’akub’s] detention has been inconsistent and appears to rely substantially on his speech and social media activity,” the Members wrote. “DHS has sought to justify his detention by citing his social media commentary regarding the prosecutions of the Holy Land Foundation Five, his criticism of the treatment of Guantanamo detainees, his advocacy for Palestine, and his engagement with religious Islamic content, including ‘liking’ Instagram posts containing Quranic verses. We are deeply concerned that constitutionally protected political and religious expression is being used as a basis for his continued detention or deportation.”
The letter renews concerns and questions from a letter Rep. Green sent in June. Rep. Tlaib also spoke on the House floor urging for Ya’akub’s release in August.
“We are also concerned by reports, previously flagged in Congressman Green’s June letter, that the FBI approached Mr. Vijandre in November 2023 seeking his cooperation as a confidential informant and that he declined,” the Members continued in their letter. “His DACA status, renewed as recently as May 2024 through May 2026, was subsequently revoked. The proximity and sequence of these events—an FBI approach he declined, followed by a DACA termination and detention grounded largely in the government’s characterization of his religious and political speech—continue to raise serious questions about possible retaliation that Congress has not yet received satisfactory answers to.”
The letter, led by Reps. Tlaib and Green, was signed by 21 other Members of Congress: Greg Casar (TX–35), Judy Chu (CA-28), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Jesús "Chuy" García (IL-04), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Henry C. “Hank” Johnson, Jr. (GA-04), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Summer Lee (PA-12), Analilia Mejia (NJ-11), Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), Ilhan Omar (MN-05), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Emily Randall (WA-06), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Nydia Velázquez (NY-07), Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12).
The letter was also endorsed by 38 organizations: American Friends Service Committee, Americans for Justice in Palestine Action, Arab American Caucus of the California Democratic Party, Arlington for Palestine, Asian Americans Advancing Justice - Atlanta, CAIR Action, Center for Constitutional Rights, Codepink, Community Alliance for Peace and Justice, Demand Progress, Havertown-Community Action Network, IMEU Policy Project, Indiana Center for Middle East Peace, Institute for Policy Studies New Internationalism Project, Maine Coalition for Palestine, Majdal: Arab Community Center of San Diego, MARUF CT, Massachusetts Peace Action, Methodist Federation for Social Action, Muslim Advocates, National Political Prisoner Coalition, NE Oakland Indivisible, NH Peace Action, Palestine Legal, Peace Action Montgomery, Peace Justice Sustainability NOW!, Philly Neighborhood Networks, Pittsburgh Palestine Solidarity Committee, Project TAHA, Restore The Fourth - Action, ReThinking Foreign Policy, River Valley for Palestine, The Justice Coalition, United Methodists for Kairos Response, US Campaign for Palestinian Rights Action, Virginia for Palestine, Whistleblower & Source Protection Program at ExposeFacts, Worcester Multifaith for Palestine.

CHARLOTTE, N.C. – Today, U.S. District Judge Matthew E. Orso sentenced William Stanley, 26, of Charlotte, to one-year of probation for impeding and disrupting the performance of official duties of government employees; failure to comply with the lawful direction of an authorized individual; and obstructing the entrance on a federal property. In addition to the year of probation, Stanley was ordered to complete 50 hours of community service in the first six months, and the community service should be in conflict resolution or emergency response. Also, Stanley must complete at least eight hours of community service per month for the first five months. Stanley was also ordered to pay a $1,000 fine immediately or $50/month within 60 days. He is also not permitted to enter any Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility without the prior consent of ICE and his probation officer, and he is prohibited from communicating with his co-defendant, Heather Morrow.

Judge Orso said at the sentencing hearing, “It is very serious to interfere with law enforcement duties on federal property.”

According to court documents, trial evidence, and witness testimony, on November 16, 2025, Stanley and Morrow, aiding and abetting one another, willfully entered federal property, specifically, the grounds of the Immigration and Customs Enforcement/Enforcement and Removal Operations (ICE/ERO) building in Charlotte. Trial evidence established that, while there, Stanley and Morrow engaged in disorderly conduct and other actions that unreasonably obstructed the usual use of the building’s entrances and parking lots. For example, according to evidence presented at trial and witness testimony, Stanley, Morrow, and three other individuals placed cones on the entrance driveway to the federal property and formed a human chain, blocking ERO Deportation Officers from entering in their official vehicles. In addition, Morrow’s vehicle was parked in the exit lane, blocking vehicles from exiting the federal property.

Trial evidence further established that Stanley and Morrow’s conduct impeded and disrupted ERO Deportation Officers in the performance of their official duties and the defendants failed to comply with the lawful direction of ERO Deportation Officers. According to trial evidence, Stanley stood in front of the government-issued vehicle of an ERO Deportation Officer, blocking the officer from entering the property. Stanley then placed his hands on the hood of the ERO Deportation Officer’s vehicle to stop the officer from entering.

“There is a difference between peaceful protest – which is permitted under the First Amendment – and interfering with law enforcemnet officers doing their jobs,” said a spokesperson for the U.S. Attorney’s Office. “Here, Mr. Stanley crossed the line, and the Court’s sentence appropriately addresses that conduct by requiring that he give back to the community through court-ordered community service and supervision.”

A sentencing date for Morrow has not been set.

The FBI investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kenneth Smith and Caryn Finley prosecuted the case.
title: Man Sentenced to One Year Probation and $1,000 Fine for Interfering with Federal Officers Performing Official Duties and Related Offenses

ROCHESTER, N.Y.-U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Stephen Odiboh, 53, of Stone Mountain, Georgia, who was convicted of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, was sentenced to serve 33 months in prison by U.S. District Judge Charles J. Siragusa. He was also ordered to pay $196,500 in restitution.

Between 2023 and March 2025, Odiboh conspired with co-conspirators to defraud four victims. The total loss and attempted loss were $356,500.

In 2023, Odiboh contacted Victim 1, a 77-year-old woman in the Western District of New York, on Facebook. Posing as “Oliver Wilson,” he falsely represented that he was a United States Citizen, a widower, and currently living in Norway. Over the course of approximately a year and a half, “Wilson” fostered a romantic, online relationship, stating that he needed gift cards to “stay online” and continue talking. As a result, Victim 1 sent “Wilson” approximately 30 $500 gift cards, totaling approximately $15,000. In addition, between January and July of 2024, “Wilson” induced Victim 1 to mail eight checks totaling over $162,000.00 to specific individuals and entities, including two checks to Stephen Odiboh. In December 2024, “Wilson” stated that he was being held by customs authorities in Norway and needed to pay a fine of $158,000. He directed Victim 1 to mail two checks totaling $158,000.00 but Victim 1’s bank detected fraud and stopped payment of the checks before they could be cashed.

In April 2024, a co-conspirator contacted Victim 2, a caterer, claiming to be “Alex Alberto,” and in need of catering services. Victim 2 requested a deposit of $800. To pay the purported deposit, “Alberto” sent Victim 2 a check for $2,800, and instructed Victim 2 to cash the check and send the extra $2,000 to the defendant via Zelle. Victim 2 realized he was being defrauded and did not deposit the check.

In 2024, a co-conspirator, claiming to be “William Rivera,” contacted Victim 3 through an online dating website. After gaining Victim 3’s trust, “Rivera” convinced Victim 3 to send $2,000 to Odiboh via CashApp, which Victim 3 did on August 14, 2024.

In March 2025, a co-conspirator, claiming to be “Alec Jonas,” contacted Victim 4 on a dating website, leading Victim 4 to believe that they were starting a romantic relationship. Once he gained her trust, “Jonas” stated that he was working in Bahrain and needed money to ship goods from Bahrain to Texas, prompting Victim 4 to wire $17,525 to a bank account he controlled.

The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Meghan K. McGuire. The sentencing is the result of an investigation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Allen D. Davis, II and the Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigation Division, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Harry Chavis.
