text:
Veterans Outdoor Rehabilitation Act would help veterans in New Hampshire and across the country connect with community and strengthen their well-being
Concord, N.H. — Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) and Congressman Jeff Hurd (CO-03) introduced the bipartisan Veterans Outdoor Rehabilitation Act, legislation to help veterans in New Hampshire and across the country access outdoor recreation programs that support their mental and physical well-being.
The Veterans Outdoor Rehabilitation Act would establish a grant program through the Department of Veterans Affairs for state veterans’ agencies to develop, administer, and expand outdoor recreation programs for veterans. States could operate programs directly or partner with local outfitters, guides, nonprofit organizations, and community-based outdoor recreation providers.
“Our obligation to those who served doesn’t end when the uniform comes off. In New Hampshire, our mountains, lakes, and trails offer veterans opportunities to build community and strengthen their physical and mental well-being,” said Congresswoman Goodlander. “I’m proud to help introduce the bipartisan Veterans Outdoor Rehabilitation Act with Congressman Hurd to make those opportunities available to more veterans. By helping cover equipment, transportation, and program costs, our bill would help more veterans get outdoors, connect with one another, and find the support they’ve earned.”
“For many veterans, the transition from military service can mean losing the sense of purpose, community, and connection that came with serving alongside others,” said Congressman Hurd. “Colorado’s public lands and outdoor spaces offer opportunities to rebuild those connections while supporting veterans’ physical and mental well-being. This bipartisan legislation gives states more tools to work with local organizations and expand outdoor recreation opportunities so that more veterans can benefit from time outdoors and with one another.”
Under the legislation, grant funding could be used to reduce financial barriers that may prevent veterans from participating in outdoor recreation programs, including the costs of equipment, program fees, and reasonable transportation expenses. Funding could also support outreach to veterans and the expansion of existing programs.
The bill would also encourage state veterans’ agencies to work with federal land management agencies, including the National Park Service, Bureau of Land Management, U.S. Forest Service, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, to expand veterans’ access to outdoor spaces, reduce administrative barriers, and identify appropriate locations for organized activities.
The legislation defines eligible outdoor recreation programs broadly as nature-based activities designed to improve veterans’ mental and physical well-being through physical engagement, peer connection, skill-building, or therapeutic benefit. Programs may also include adaptive or accessible activities for veterans with disabilities.
Each eligible state entity whose application meets the bill’s requirements would receive at least $200,000 per fiscal year, subject to available appropriations. The legislation authorizes $10 million annually for the grant program. Participating states would also report information including the number of veterans served, types of activities offered, participation frequency, and observations related to veterans’ well-being, social connectedness, and physical activity.
Read the full bill text here. Sen. Maggie Hassan (D-N.H.) leads the Senate companion to this bill.
###
title: Goodlander Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Expand Outdoor Recreation for Veterans

text:
LOS ANGELES – Law enforcement today arrested 23 defendants out of a total of 28 individuals, including residents of West Covina and Studio City, charged in federal criminal complaints with trafficking drugs, including fentanyl and methamphetamine, in and around the Skid Row neighborhood of downtown Los Angeles, an area notorious for poverty, homelessness, and drug use.

Today’s Homeland Security Task Force takedown mirrors similar takedowns earlier this year at MacArthur Park , another area of Los Angeles long known for street crime, gang activity, homelessness, and drug addiction. Prosecutors have arrested 24 individuals in those cases.

Among the defendants arrested today as part of the Skid Row action are the following individuals charged with distribution of a controlled substance:

Rodney Thomas, 55, a.k.a. “Jamaica,” of Los Angeles

Charles McIntyre, 65, of Los Angeles

Dwayne Richards, 62, of Los Angeles

Manuel Vaughns, 52, of West Covina

Larry Pitre, 70, a.k.a. “Kat Daddy,” of Studio City

Lionel Nelson, 57, a.k.a. “Popeye,” of Watts

Tyzarioun Grimsley, 28, of Los Angeles

Eric Goring, 38, of Los Angeles

Michael Taylor, 39, of Los Angeles

During the Skid Row investigation, law enforcement searched 20 residences, most of which were outside Skid Row, as well as several tents associated with drug dealing inside Skid Row, and seized firearms and drugs, including suspected methamphetamine, cocaine, cocaine base, and pills, as well as bulk currency and luxury vehicles.

“Today’s operation targeted drug traffickers who prey on some of the most vulnerable members of the community. They targeted the homeless in Skid Row, kept them addicted on drugs like PCP, and took their public assistance money for payment,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli. “We will use every lawful tool to dismantle the networks flooding Skid Row with deadly drugs. Those dealing drugs are looking at mandatory prison sentences. This operation is just the beginning. More to come.”

“It would be simple to overlook the crimes of Skid Row and act as if it doesn’t matter… confined to a small area and confined to vulnerable populations. Make no mistake about this operation, these narcotics traffickers are the single largest driver of violent crime in the Skid Row area of Los Angeles,” said Patrick Grandy, the Assistant Director of the FBI’s Los Angeles Field Office. “Our hope is that this effort will make a difference in the communities where these defendants operated, and the lives of law-abiding residents, including our most vulnerable.”

“We have thousands of unsheltered, many battling severe addiction and mental illness, many isolated from family and support. They are the most vulnerable among us. The criminals we arrested today are not low-level dealers,” said David Olesky, Special Agent in Charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration Los Angeles Field Division. “These traffickers did not hide in the shadows. They operated in plain sight. They used tents, tarps, and makeshift structures as storefronts – as drug distribution centers. They bet if they blended into the suffering around them, law enforcement would drive by, the public would look away, and they would go unnoticed. They bet on our apathy. Today, that bet failed.”

“Violence by local gang members against our vulnerable homeless neighbors will not be tolerated,” stated ATF Special Agent in Charge Kenny Cooper. “ATF will use its firearms and violent crime expertise to hold offenders accountable and protect all of our community members.”

“Drug trafficking organizations thrive on the illicit proceeds generated from poisoning our communities,” said Darren Lian, Special Agent in Charge, IRS Criminal Investigation’s Los Angeles Field Office. “By following the money, IRS CI can expose the financial infrastructure that allows these criminal networks to operate in places like Skid Row, where vulnerable individuals are exploited precisely because they are easy targets for dealers seeking a profit. Today’s takedown demonstrates our commitment to working with our federal partners to disrupt the financial networks that support fentanyl and methamphetamine distribution in Los Angeles.”

According to court documents, Skid Row is a neighborhood in Los Angeles characterized by high rates of poverty, drug addiction, and homelessness. Many of the homeless in the area are drug users, and Skid Row is a known location to purchase drugs such as fentanyl, cocaine, cocaine base, methamphetamine, and phencyclidine – commonly known as “PCP.”

Drug dealers from across the Los Angeles area travel to Skid Row to prey on the neighborhood’s homeless population and the individuals who live there. Skid Row drug dealers consist of a mixture of members of criminal street gangs and independent operators.

The tactics used by Skid Row drug dealers include dressing like members of the homeless population or social workers in order to blend in with environment and evade detection by law enforcement, using tents and makeshift structures to hide their illicit activities from public view, and stashing or storing a majority of their supply of drugs in nearby vehicles, tents, or makeshift structures, which limits their criminal liability should they encounter law enforcement.

Drug dealers also utilize single-room occupancy (SRO) units and other forms of low-income housing available in the area to store or stash their drug supply. Skid Row drug dealers often use vehicles and residences not registered in their name to elude scrutiny by law enforcement.

Skid Row has a high density of foot traffic from the homeless population that lives there. As a result of the high degree of foot traffic, street-level drug dealers often hide in plain sight and conduct hand-to-hand narcotics transactions in parks, including Gladys Park and San Julian Park. Drug users will walk up to a street-level dealer, pay them $20 or $40, and receive a small user quantity of cocaine, fentanyl, PCP or methamphetamine.

Skid Row drug dealers occupy territory and protect or control their territory through various means, including violence. The territory held by drug dealers ranges in size from single street corners to entire city blocks.

For example, Vaughns is a documented Raymond Avenue Crip gang member who regularly sells inside Gladys Park. Vaughns is associated with residences in Pasadena, California, and West Covina, California, as well as an SRO in Skid Row.

The complaints further allege that the intersection of Fifth and Crocker is controlled by a group of drug dealers all using tents and makeshift structures to sell drugs, including McIntyre, Grimsley, and R. Thomas. According to the complaint, these tents are not used as housing, but instead as a location to store and distribute drugs. Specifically, R. Thomas lived in a high rise in downtown Los Angeles near the Los Angeles Convention Center, and he would drive to his tent at Fifth and Crocker in multiple different luxury vehicles, including a white 2016 Bentley and a black 2022 Mercedes Benz that was later pictured outside of his tent at 5 th and Crocker.

Nelson, a Watts-based drug dealer was observed on August 19 selling approximately 34 grams of fentanyl for $60 out of a Mercedes-Benz automobile parked in Skid Row.

Taylor, who also allegedly sold drugs in Skid Row despite living elsewhere, would disguise himself as a transient, wearing dirty clothes to appear disheveled and employing local transients to serve as lookouts for him in return for drugs.

Additionally, the corner of Fifth and San Pedro was known to be used by members of the Pueblo Bishops Bloods gang, who would sell drugs from makeshift tents and tables. In February 2026, LAPD arrested Dent, F. Thomas, and others, after F. Thomas sold cocaine base, and recovered over 100 grams of methamphetamine, over 400 grams of PCP, and a loaded firearm from the vicinity of the tent and F. Thomas’s vehicle, along with a digital scale. Dent and F. Thomas were both arrested as part of today’s operation.

A criminal complaint merely contains allegations. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

If convicted, the defendants would each face a statutory maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison.

MUSKOGEE, OKLAHOMA – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Oklahoma announced that Drake Ryan Allen, age 22, an Oklahoma resident, was sentenced to 33 months in prison for one count of Assault Resulting in Serious Bodily Injury in Indian Country.

The charge arose from an investigation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Adair County Sheriff’s Office.

On October 7, 2025, Allen pleaded guilty to the charge. According to investigators, on January 15, 2025, Allen repeatedly struck the victim with brass knuckles, causing facial fractures, lacerations, and contusions. Allen also attempted to strangle the victim, then struck the victim with an automobile he was driving as he fled the scene of the crime.

The crime occurred in Adair County, within the boundaries of the Cherokee Nation Reservation, in the Eastern District of Oklahoma.

The Honorable Ronald A. White, Senior Judge in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Oklahoma, presided over the hearing. Allen will remain in the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service pending transportation to a designated United States Bureau of Prisons facility to serve a non-paroleable sentence of incarceration.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Edith A. Singer represented the United States.
title: Oklahoma Resident Sentenced For Felony Assault

WASHINGTON, D.C. — This week, Congresswomen Yvette D. Clarke (D-NY-09) and Julia Letlow (R-LA-05) introduced a bipartisan, bicameral resolution to establish October as World Menopause Awareness Month and October 18th as World Menopause Day. Senators Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE) and Cory Booker (D-NJ) introduced the resolution’s companion in the Senate.
These observances will contribute to the spread of global awareness and access to care during menopausal transition and post-menopause, as well as provide organizations and individuals around the world with an opportunity to advocate for resources and support for the 75 million American women in perimenopause, menopause, and post-menopause.
“Throughout our lives, women deserve the support we need to confront every trial and embrace every triumph each of our chapters has in store for us. Menopause is a natural experience that we all must face, yet the stigma that follows it continues to inflict needless ridicule and shame on women at a time when all we ask for is acceptance and understanding,” said Congresswoman Yvette D. Clarke. “World Menopause Awareness Month and World Menopause Day will be the bridges to normalizing menopause and ensuring the women confronting it have the resources, care, and confidence they need to tackle their new horizons head on, and I am proud to lead this bipartisan legislation to see both codified as national observances.”
“Through any stage of life, women need access to reliable information to make educated decisions about their health. World Menopause Awareness Month shines a light on the millions of women undergoing menopause every year, highlighting the need for women to have a better understanding of the treatments and options available to them,” said Congresswoman Julia Letlow.
“Generations of women have faced the transition to menopause, yet for too long this experience has been overlooked, under-researched, and treated as taboo,” said Lisa Senator Blunt Rochester. “It’s far past time we ensure women have the care and support they need to feel their best in all phases of life. I’m proud to introduce the World Menopause Awareness Month Resolution to elevate the challenges of menopause and encourage further investments into research that will help women meet this transition with confidence.”
“Our health care system has failed women struggling with menopausal symptoms that disrupt their livelihoods, and this unfortunate reality disproportionately affects Black and Hispanic women,” said Senator Cory Booker. “This resolution is a reminder that we must do more to support women navigating menopause and provide them with the resources they need. Menopause should not be a barrier to the quality of life every woman deserves.”
“The resolution introduced by Congresswoman Yvette Clarke represents another important step toward breaking down the barriers that have too often left women without the information, care, and relief they need throughout the menopause transition,” said Donna Klassen of Let’s Talk Menopause. “We proudly support this resolution and applaud Congresswoman Clarke’s leadership in bringing greater attention to menopause, expanding access to trusted health information and care, and ensuring women have the resources they need to navigate this stage of life with confidence and support.”
“Menopause is a universal experience for women, and yet, for too long menopause has been understudied. This has left us with significant knowledge gaps about menopause itself, including its symptoms and treatments, but also about the effects of menopause on overall health and healthy aging. Fortunately, we now have momentum to course correct. The Society for Women’s Health Research thanks Representative Clarke for her leadership on the resolution designating October as World Menopause Awareness Month and October 18 as World Menopause Day. We must collectively continue raising awareness about menopause, which can help shape research priorities and ensure women and health care providers have the evidence and information needed to make informed decisions about menopause care,” said Lindsey Miltenberger of the Society for Women’s Health Research.
Menopause is more than a personal, biological transition—it has lasting implications for women’s health and well-being, and for families, workplaces, and society. The Black Women’s Health Imperative endorses this resolution to recognize October as World Menopause Awareness Month and expand awareness, provider education, and access to the resources and care that women, particularly Black women, need for a healthy, dignified menopause, ” said Ifeoma Udoh, Ph.D. of the Black Women’s Health Imperative.
The resolution is endorsed by the American Medical Association, Astellas, Greater New York Hospital Association, Healthcare Association of New York State, In Our Own Voice: National Black Women’s Reproductive Justice Agenda, Mount Sinai Health System, National Medical Association, National Minority Quality Forum, Novo Nordisk, Inc., NYU Langone Health, One Brooklyn Health System, Reproductive Health Access Project, Ritual, The Fibroid Foundation, and The White Dress Project.
Read the full bill text HERE.

DOE’s Early Career Research Program (ECRP) Supports the Next Generation of American Scientific Leadership Across Universities, National Laboratories, and User Facilities.
October 8, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Science today announced the selection of 67 early career scientists to receive a combined $96 million through the 2026 Early Career Research Program (ECRP). Today’s announcement advances President Trump’s Executive Order Restoring Gold Standard Science by supporting exceptional researchers pursuing rigorous, mission-driven research in areas critical to America’s scientific and technological leadership, including Super Intelligence (SI), fusion energy, and quantum science.
“Groundbreaking science begins with empowering extraordinary people,” said DOE Under Secretary for Science Dr. Darío Gil. “These 67 early career researchers represent the very best of American ingenuity. DOE is proud to invest in their vision as they push the boundaries of knowledge and cement U.S. leadership in the technologies that will define our century.”
The 2026 Early Career Research Program (ECRP) selectees represent 39 universities, 11 DOE National Laboratories and Office of Science User Facilities, and 26 states. By investing in exceptional researchers at a pivotal stage in their careers, ECRP empowers the next generation of STEM leaders to pursue bold, innovative research that drives DOE’s mission and ensures America continues to lead the world in science and innovation. Since its inception in 2010, the program has made 1,238 awards, including 797 to university researchers and 441 to DOE National Laboratory researchers.
Awards to scientists at institutions of higher education are approximately $875,000 over five years, while awards to scientists at DOE National Laboratories or Office of Science User Facilities are approximately $2,750,000 over five years.
Information about the 67 selectees and their research projects is available on the Office of Science Awards page.
Profiles of previous award recipients, including information about how the program helped advance their research and careers, are available on the Early Career Program profiles page.
Selection for award negotiations is not a commitment by DOE to issue an award or provide funding. Before funding is issued, DOE and the applicants will undergo a negotiation process, and DOE may cancel negotiations and rescind the selection for any reason during that time.
title: U.S. Department of Energy Awards $96 Million to 67 Early Career Scientists

DALLAS — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced that a Dallas man has been charged with repeatedly flying a drone into restricted airspace around both Dallas Love Field and Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport.

On Sept. 16, a federal grand jury returned a four-count indictment against Pujan Prashantkumar Gajjar, 24, on offenses related to the unauthorized operation of an unmanned aircraft in protected airport airspace.

“Safe and secure air travel depends on strict compliance with federal aviation rules,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “Unauthorized drone incursions into protected airport airspace jeopardizes aircraft and endangers pilots, passengers and the entire community. This office will continue working with our law enforcement partners to ensure the safety of our airspace.”

“Safe and secure air travel depends on strict compliance with federal aviation rules,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “Unauthorized drone incursions into protected airport airspace jeopardizes aircraft and endangers pilots, passengers and the entire community. This office will continue working with our law enforcement partners to ensure the safety of our airspace.”

"Operating a drone in restricted airport space threatens the safety of pilots, passengers, and crew in the air as well as communities on the ground,” said FBI Dallas Special Agent in Charge R. Joseph Rothrock. “The FBI is committed to working with our partners to investigate these types of violations and ensure those who endanger our airspace are held accountable .”

According to the indictment, Mr. Gajjar allegedly flew a drone into the runway exclusion zone at Dallas Love Field around 11:30 p.m. on June 26, 2025, with the drone allegedly crossing an active runway. The following night, he allegedly flew the same drone into restricted airspace surrounding Dallas-Fort Worth Airport. The indictment further alleges that, in connection with the same flights, Mr. Gajjar knowingly and willfully served as an airman without the required airman’s certificate.

Federal agents arrested Gajjar Sept. 22. He made his initial appearance the same day before U.S. Magistrate Judge Renee Harris Toliver. If convicted, Gajjar faces up to eight years in federal prison.

The FBI Dallas and the Federal Air Marshal Service conducted the investigation with the assistance of the Federal Aviation Administration. Assistant U.S. Attorney Edward L. Hocter from the National Security Section is prosecuting the case.

An indictment is merely an allegation of criminal conduct and defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

text:
Fast Facts
Geothermal Energy: Bureau of Land Management Should Improve Permitting Process as Development Demand Grows on Federal Lands
Geothermal energy—natural heat under the earth's surface—can be used to generate emissions-free electricity. The Bureau of Land Management reviews and approves permit requests to use federal land for geothermal projects. Since 2019, there has been a steady increase in these requests.
We found that the Bureau could do more to improve its permitting process. For example, it doesn't have handbooks with detailed and consistent permitting procedures. It also doesn't track the status of permits. As a result, the Bureau is missing opportunities to process permits in a more timely and consistent manner.
Our recommendations address these issues.
Utah Frontier Observatory for Research in Geothermal Energy
A collection of buildings in the middle of a desert with mountains in the background.
Highlights
What GAO Found
The Department of the Interior’s Bureau of Land Management (BLM) has processed an increasing volume of land nominations, leases, and permits for geothermal development on federal lands since 2019. Geothermal projects use heat from the earth’s interior to generate electricity. Parties interested in developing geothermal projects on federal lands nominate acres for BLM to review against land use plans. Such nominations increased from about 25,800 acres in 2020 to more than a million acres in 2025. BLM then offers qualifying lands for lease at auctions known as competitive lease sales, which have also increased since 2020. Once land is leased, developers submit plans to BLM for review and apply for permits at various stages of development. Drilling permits approved annually by BLM grew from seven in 2019 to 68 in 2024.
Total Acreage Nominated for Geothermal Use and Offered for Lease, 2020–2025
Geothermal developers and BLM officials identified various challenges facing the geothermal program, including:
- Inconsistent experience navigating the permitting process. Some developers reported instances of what they believe were inconsistent BLM determinations related to permits for exploration. BLM documentation notes that inconsistencies in terminology between developers and BLM officials may contribute to confusion or misunderstandings. However, handbooks that would resolve this confusion have been in draft since at least 2022 and are not publicly available. Without finalized geothermal resources handbooks, continued inconsistencies and misunderstandings could lead to longer development timelines and additional costs for developers.
- Limited visibility of permit data. Geothermal developers have limited visibility into the status of permits once these are submitted to BLM, which creates challenges for planning timelines and resource needs. BLM does not have comprehensive information on the status of geothermal permits, making it difficult for BLM to gain insights into permitting activity—for example, to determine if there is a growing backlog of permits across BLM field offices. By establishing a unified mechanism to track permitting activity, BLM could better track progress toward producing geothermal energy on federal land and generating revenue for federal, state, and county governments.
Why GAO Did This Study
Geothermal energy is a reliable and domestically-sourced option to help address growing demand for utility-scale power generation in the United States. Geothermal power plants on federal land have a combined 2,600 megawatts of capacity and, in 2022, generated enough electricity to power more than 1 million homes. Geothermal power plants on federal land represent about 65 percent of geothermal capacity in the United States.
GAO was asked to review geothermal leasing and permitting on federal land. This report examines (1) the extent to which BLM processed land nominations, held lease sales, and approved permits for geothermal development and (2) challenges BLM faces in managing the geothermal leasing and permitting program.
GAO analyzed BLM’s data on land nominations, lease sales, and permitting, and interviewed BLM officials in states with geothermal land nominations and leases. GAO also interviewed geothermal industry officials and administered a questionnaire to 22 geothermal developers.
Recommendations
GAO is making three recommendations, including that BLM (1) finalize and publish geothermal resources handbooks and (2) establish a unified mechanism to track permitting activity. Interior did not provide comments on this report.
title: Geothermal Energy: Bureau of Land Management Should Improve Permitting Process as Development Demand Grows on Federal Lands

WASHINGTON—The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) today announced a cease-and-desist order and a $350 million civil money penalty against American Express National Bank, Sandy, Utah (bank), for deficiencies in the bank’s Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and anti-money laundering (AML) compliance program.

The OCC determined that the bank failed to establish and maintain a BSA/AML compliance program reasonably designed to assure and monitor compliance with the BSA and its implementing regulations. Deficiencies in the Bank’s BSA/AML program involved inadequate resources, including staff without sufficient expertise, systemic internal control gaps, weak independent testing, and weak BSA/AML training for employees and directors.

The OCC found that the bank failed to tailor its BSA/AML risk assessment to its business activities. The bank focused on the risks in its relatively narrow demand deposit account products and services and insufficiently on the risks in its more dominant credit and charge card products. In addition to its ineffective risk assessments, the bank’s customer due diligence processes and customer identification program procedures contributed to the bank’s monitoring and reporting failures. The bank experienced systemic breakdowns in its suspicious activity monitoring and reporting processes, resulting in a failure to timely identify, evaluate, and sufficiently report approximately $13 billion of suspected trade-based money laundering activity that took place over the past decade.

“The OCC expects banks of American Express’s size and complexity to devote sufficient resources to ensure compliance with laws and regulations designed to detect and prevent money laundering, which are critical to both economic and national security,” said Comptroller of the Currency Jonathan Gould. “American Express failed to maintain a BSA/AML compliance program properly aligned with the money laundering risks of its operations, which resulted in the bank’s failures to timely identify and report significant missed suspicious activity and to provide important information to law enforcement. Today’s actions will serve to focus American Express on properly addressing such risks as it continues to serve its customers.”

The OCC is taking these actions in coordination with a concurrent cease-and-desist order against American Express Company and American Express Travel Related Services Company, Inc., by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. The OCC-assessed penalty will be directed to the U.S. Treasury.

NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA – TYRON RAINEY (“RAINEY”) (36 years old) from Thibodaux, La. was sentenced on October 1, 2026 to serve a total of 180 months (15 years) imprisonment by United States District Judge Nannette Jolivette Brown, announced United States Attorney David I. Courcelle.

RAINEY previously pled guilty on November 6, 2025, to participating in a conspiracy to distribute 500 grams or more of methamphetamine, and possession with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of methamphetamine, in violation of Title 21, United States Code, Sections 841(a)(1), (b)(1)(A), and 846.

This investigation began in 2022, when Drug Enforcement Administration (“DEA”), Task Force Group 3 (“TFG3”), began investigating narcotics trafficking activities in Terrebonne and Lafourche Parishes. This investigation revealed that Andre Lee and Percy Howard were distributing large amounts of methamphetamine throughout both parishes.

During the investigation, acquired information about Lee and Howard’s drug trafficking operation. As a result, federal agents conducted court authorized Title III wiretaps on several cellular telephones, including those belonging to Lee and Howard. Agents were then able to record and overhear several drug related calls between Howard and RAINEY during this Title III investigation. RAINEY was identified as a local dealer with a lengthy criminal record. Agents also learned that Lee and Howard were obtaining large amounts of methamphetamine from individuals in California, Texas, and Mississippi. This investigation resulted in the conviction of seven individuals on federal drug trafficking charges.

This matter was investigated by the United States Drug Enforcement Administration, the Louisiana State Police, the Lafourche Parish Sheriff’s Department, and the Terrebonne Parish Sheriff’s Department. It was prosecuted by Senior Litigation Counsel, Assistant United States Attorney Maurice E. Landrieu.

Reps. Carter, Thompson Reintroduce the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency Securing AI Task Force Act to Address the Evolving Challenges Posed by AI
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Troy A. Carter, Sr. (D-LA), Member of the Communications and Technology Subcommittee, and Congressman Bennie G. Thompson (D-MS), Ranking Member of the House Homeland Security Committee, re-introduced the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Securing Artificial Intelligence (AI) Task Force Act.
This legislation will establish a task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency in the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) dedicated to addressing safety and national security challenges posed by AI. The task force and reporting requirements will ensure effective DHS coordination as AI threats and challenges evolve. Recently, Rep. Carter appeared on CNBC to discuss how to regulate AI while preserving innovation.
“As technology advances in sophistication and use, our commitment to safeguarding against emerging threats and ensuring the responsible advancement of AI technologies must grow stronger too,” said Congressman Carter. “I’m introducing the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Securing AI Task Force Act to take an essential step towards managing the impact of AI on our cybersecurity landscape.”
“Advancements in AI technology are expanding by the day and we need to make sure our cybersecurity defenses are moving with it,” said Ranking Member Thompson. “This bill creates a dedicated CISA task force so the agency can better understand the risks that come with AI and make sure we are prepared to protect the systems and infrastructure Americans rely on every day. I am proud to work alongside Representative Carter to reintroduce this critical legislation and help ensure our defenses are ready for what comes next.”
Background
The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act would:
- Establish a Task Force - Within one year of enactment, the Director of CISA will establish a Task Force comprised of personnel from various offices and divisions to coordinate AI-related directives and activities.
- Address AI Challenges - The Task Force will ensure coordination of efforts to improve the safe and secure design, development, adoption, and deployment of AI. It will assess relevant safety and security initiatives, advise stakeholders on potential cyber risks associated with AI deployment, and identify workforce gaps.
- Increase Accountability - The Task Force will provide biannual briefings to the Committee on Homeland Security of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs of the Senate on its activities.

MINNEAPOLIS – United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen announced that Christopher Charles Traxler, 32, of St. Paul, Minnesota, was sentenced to 120 months in prison for his role in a large-scale drug trafficking operation responsible for procuring mass quantities of methamphetamine and cocaine for further distribution. Traxler is one of three defendants in U.S. v. Cryer et al. (24-cr-206).

According to court documents, on June 3, 2024, Traxler and a co-defendant, Amir McKeever, 33, received a bulk shipment of controlled substances—seven boxes that collectively contained over 200 pounds of methamphetamine and 26 pounds of cocaine. Traxler and McKeever transported the methamphetamine and cocaine to a St. Paul apartment Traxler maintained as a stash location. The following day, McKeever transferred four of the seven boxes, which contained approximately 140 pounds of the methamphetamine, to another co-defendant, Jumoke Cryer.

On June 5, 2024, law enforcement executed search warrants at Traxler’s St. Paul apartment and at a townhome in Woodbury, Minnesota. Inside McKeever’s Woodbury townhome, law enforcement found McKeever as well as drug packaging material, an electronic money counter, an electric heat sealer, over $110,000 in cash, and eight firearms with associated ammunition. Officers also found over 85 grams of cocaine and approximately 14 grams of marijuana at the townhome.

At Traxler’s St. Paul apartment, officers found the remaining three boxes that Traxler and McKeever received two days prior. The boxes contained a substantial quantity of methamphetamine and cocaine. Officers found additional amounts of methamphetamine and two firearms, including a Glock .40 handgun and a black AR-style rifle. In total, officers seized 76 pounds of methamphetamine, 26 pounds of cocaine, and nearly $25,000 from Traxler’s apartment.

“The quantity of methamphetamine and cocaine this defendant and his associates trafficked was staggering. My office will continue to partner with law enforcement to dismantle drug operations and protect the lives of Minnesotans,” said United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen.

“This case highlights the importance of the work being done by our Non-Fatal Shooting Unit. This team thoroughly investigates all assault cases where individuals are struck by a bullet but do not die within Saint Paul. Dedicating resources to every shooting has not only shown that it dramatically decreases the number of homicides, but as highlighted in this case, can also prevent other public safety threats. We want to thank our local, state, and federal partners in this case for their work to shut down this large-scale narcotics operation,” said St. Paul Police Department Commander of the Non-Fatal Shooting Unit Nikkole Peterson.

“Preventing several hundred pounds of narcotics destined for Minnesota from reaching our communities, along with thousands of dollars in cash and firearms, no doubt saved lives,” said Drew Evans, Superintendent of the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension. “This case highlights the important work of BCA agents, our law enforcement partners and what can be accomplished when we work together to investigate cases, seize dangerous drugs and firearms, and hold offenders accountable.”

“Drugs, illegal guns and the lengths some people will go to for dirty money pose a serious threat to our communities. The massive amounts of methamphetamine and cocaine involved in this case, along with illegal firearms, show the danger HSI and our law enforcement partners face every day,” said HSI St. Paul Special Agent in Charge Travis Pickard. “I am thankful for the hard work of HSI special agents, analysts, prosecutors, and our law enforcement partners to obtain this sentencing and disrupt this drug trafficking operation. HSI will keep working to hold accountable those who bring dangerous drugs and violence into our communities.”

“The FBI brought critical investigative tools and resources to this case, supporting our partners in confronting a sophisticated criminal organization,” said FBI Minneapolis Special Agent in Charge Christopher D. Dotson. “We remain committed to working side‑by‑side with federal, state, and local agencies to hold those who traffic in violence and illegal narcotics accountable and safeguard communities across the Twin Cities.”

“The firearms recovered in this case reinforce what we see all too often: drug traffickers rely on guns to protect their operations and profits,” said ATF Special Agent in Charge Joseph Persails, of the St. Paul Field Division. “ATF is committed to disrupting criminal networks that use firearms to protect and expand their narcotics trade. This case demonstrates how strong partnerships among federal, state, and local agencies help safeguard our neighborhoods and hold violent drug traffickers accountable.”

This case is the result of an investigation conducted by the St. Paul Police Department, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension (BCA), the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF).

Assistant United States Attorneys Raphael B. Coburn and Garrett S. Fields prosecuted the case.

CLEVELAND – A federal jury has convicted a former medical doctor with naturalization fraud for providing false answers on a U.S. citizenship application and during an in-person interview.

According to court documents, Yousif Abdulraouf Alhallaq, 47, of Canton, was born in Kuwait and entered the United States on an H1B visa in 2006. In 2011, he filed an application to become a permanent resident of the United States and was approved.

In evidence presented to the jury at trial, Alhallaq began work as an internal medical doctor in Northeast Ohio in 2012. Then, in December 2014, the defendant poisoned his girlfriend’s oatmeal with an abortion drug when she became pregnant with his child, in an attempt to terminate the pregnancy without her knowledge. Several years later, the victim learned the truth about the incident and reported him to police. On March 18, 2021, Alhallaq was indicted in the Stark County Court of Common Pleas and charged with one count of attempted murder and two counts of felonious assault for trying to purposely cause the termination of the victim’s pregnancy in 2014 which caused serious, physical harm to her and her unborn child. In September 2021, Alhallaq pleaded guilty to the charges and was sentenced to four years in prison.

Before Alhallaq was indicted and sentenced for those charges in 2021, he mailed a federal application, Form N-400, in 2017 to become a naturalized U.S. citizen. In the application he answered “no” to the following questions:

14D - Were you ever involved in any way with badly hurting, or trying to hurt a person on purpose?

22 - Have you ever committed, assisted in committing, or attempted to commit a crime or offense for which you were not arrested?

Alhallaq continued with the U.S. citizenship application process in 2018 and was interviewed by an immigration officer to review the answers he submitted on his naturalization application. Under oath, the defendant verbally confirmed answers to questions 14D and 22 as “no” which matched those initially submitted by mail. On May 4, 2018, the defendant became a naturalized U.S. citizen during a ceremony in Stark County, Ohio.

Although Alhallaq knowingly committed acts of attempted murder and felonious assault by attempting to unlawfully terminate his girlfriend’s pregnancy, he nonetheless attested to federal officials that the information he provided was true and was subsequently granted U.S. citizenship.

Alhallaq faces a maximum of up to 10 years in prison for naturalization fraud and is scheduled to be sentenced Jan. 19, 2027. He also faces denaturalization as a result of his conviction.

The defendant’s sentence will be determined by the Court after a review of factors unique to this case, including the defendant’s prior criminal record, his role in the offense, and the characteristics of the violation.

The investigation preceding the indictment was conducted by U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) and the Homeland Security Investigations Cleveland office.

Assistant United States Attorneys Matthew W. Shepherd and Christopher Snyder prosecuted the case for the Northern District of Ohio.
title: Former Medical Doctor Convicted of Naturalization Fraud

Year on the Run Ends with U.S. Marshals’ Capture of Escaped Convict
For immediate release
Andrew Grillo, Deputy U.S. Marshal
Concord, NH – The U.S. Marshals Service (USMS) District of New Hampshire and the New Hampshire Joint Fugitive Task Force apprehended an escaped New Hampshire prisoner late last night in a hotel near the intersection of Perkins and Rockingham roads in Londonderry. The arrest marks the end of a yearlong search for a fugitive with gang ties and an extensive history of violence in New Hampshire, including burglary, assault, reckless conduct and firearms-related offenses.
David Hamilton, 28, escaped from the New Hampshire State Prison for Men in August 2025. At the time, Hamilton was serving the second of two consecutive sentences for second-degree assault convictions. The convictions stem from a 2022 incident in which Hamilton fled from a crime scene in a vehicle, injured three women, destroyed multiple vehicles and endangered an animal. Hamilton began serving his sentence in November 2022 and was participating in a work-release program when he escaped.
The U.S. Marshals Service worked with investigators throughout New England to track Hamilton’s whereabouts. Investigators eventually determined Hamilton had assumed a false identity using the license and personal information of a California man. That information helped investigators narrow their search and locate Hamilton in Londonderry late last night.
Task Force members developed an arrest plan designed to minimize risk to the public and law enforcement, and Hamilton was taken into custody without injury or incident.
Hamilton was previously arrested in 2016 by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives following an investigation that linked him to the burglary of a firearms store in Hooksett that year. He later violated federal pretrial release conditions in that case and was subsequently arrested in Manchester in 2018.
“Escapes from custody pose a serious public safety concern, and bringing escaped prisoners back into custody is essential to maintaining the integrity of our correctional system,” said William R. Hart, Jr., Commissioner of the New Hampshire Department of Corrections. “We appreciate the U.S. Marshals Service and the New Hampshire Joint Fugitive Task Force for their persistence and partnership in locating and apprehending Hamilton. Their work brings this case to a close and reinforces the importance of interagency cooperation in protecting our communities.”
The USMS New Hampshire Joint Fugitive Task Force was formed in the fall of 2002 and is headquartered in Concord. The task force coordinates federal, state, county, and local resources to develop leads, gather intelligence, track and apprehend targeted fugitives. The Task Force receives vital support from Strafford, Merrimack and Rockingham Counties, as well as the cities of Manchester, Nashua and Concord.

According to the indictment, on September 27, 2026, KOUTABI entered the jurisdiction of the United States aboard a vessel after boarding, entering, and secreting himself without consent of the owner, charterer, master, or person in command of the vessel, with the intent of obtaining transportation from Morocco.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

Gamble, 46, of Fort Walton Beach, Florida, pleaded guilty in federal court to charges of conspiracy to distribute and possess with intent to distribute and possession with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of cocaine and 28 grams or more of cocaine base. John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida, announced the charges and plea.

MONTGOMERY, Ala. – A New York man and two companies he operates have agreed to pay $1 million to resolve allegations that they violated the False Claims Act by supplying the U.S. Department of War (DOW) with Chinese-manufactured products and components in violation of the Buy American Act (BAA) and other federal military-procurement requirements.

Ranga Ranganathan, Nielsen Hardware Corporation (Nielsen), and J&P Khamken Industries, Inc. (JPK) entered into the settlement agreement with the United States and the qui tam relators. Ranganathan acquired the assets of Alabama-based JPK in May 2017. Nielsen and JPK manufacture and supply aircraft components, aerospace ground support equipment, missile and munition material-handling equipment, storage containers, and other machined products used in DOW procurement. The settlement agreement was unsealed by the United States District Court in Montgomery this week.

“Federal procurement requirements are designed to ensure that taxpayer dollars are spent appropriately and that American businesses have a fair opportunity to compete for federal contracts,” said U.S. Attorney Thomas Govan. “This settlement reinforces that companies doing business with the United States military must comply with those requirements and be truthful in their representations to the government.”

According to the allegations resolved by the settlement, after Ranganathan acquired JPK, the defendants began sourcing components and end products from China and supplying them to the DOW, either directly through JPK or indirectly as a subcontractor. The United States alleged that the defendants submitted, or caused to be submitted, false claims for payment supported by certifications falsely representing compliance with the BAA and federal requirements governing specialty metals.

The settlement resolves allegations that, between May 2017 and November 2019, the defendants provided the DOW with Chinese-manufactured aluminum tables, groove pulleys, storage-rack assemblies, portable bath-unit bases, Red Cross vehicle body panels, mounting brackets, and 25mm loader-replenisher tables.

The BAA, enacted in 1933, generally establishes a preference for domestically produced goods in federal procurement. The matter also involved regulations restricting the acquisition of certain articles containing specialty metals. Although the BAA and specialty-metals regulations permit procurement from certain qualifying countries, China is not among those countries.

The settlement also resolves claims brought by the relators under the False Claims Act’s qui tam provisions. The qui tam provisions allow private parties to sue on behalf of the United States for false claims and, subject to certain statutory requirements, to receive a portion of the recovery. The relators, who were founders and former employees of JPK, will receive a portion of the settlement proceeds.

The investigation was conducted by special agents with the Air Force Office of Special Investigations (OSI), the War Criminal Investigative Service (DCIS), and the U.S. Army Criminal Investigation Division (Army CID). Assistant U.S. Attorney MaryLou E. Bowdre of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Alabama handled the matter.

The claims resolved by the settlement are allegations only, and there has been no determination of liability.
title: Companies Operated by New York Man Agree to $1 Million Settlement Over Alleged False Claims and Use of Chinese‑Made Components

Customers benefit from $8 million in federal investments
NORMAN and PAULS VALLEY, Okla. – Amtrak passengers have a more welcoming experience at two Oklahoma stations following about $8 million in improvements. Amtrak Heartland Flyer trains stop in Norman and Pauls Valley twice daily on the route between Fort Worth, Texas, and Oklahoma City.
“Amtrak is committed to making our stations accessible to all customers and we are actively working on accessibility across the national network where more than 80 stations have accessibility projects under construction.” said Amtrak Vice President of Accessibility Dr. David Handera. “We want all of our stations to provide a welcoming environment for every passenger.”
Improvements enhance the passenger experience by providing a level surface for wheeled mobility devices, strollers and users of rolling luggage.
Twenty-two stations were brought into compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act in the 12 months ending Sept. 30 and another 58 stations are targeted for completion in the next year at a forecasted investment of $300 million. These improvements focus on supporting Amtrak’s goals to enhance the customer experience and bring greater integrated and comprehensive accessibility to stations across the country.
Norman (NOR) $3 million
- The station was built for the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railroad in 1909. Sitting in the heart of historic Norman, the Santa Fe depot is a well-preserved example of Mission Revival architecture, built in brick and limestone, with a cross-gable and clay tile roof. The station now features a 300-foot-long platform with reinstalled brick pavers and accessible paths of travel to and from the station building. Complete are sloped accessible walkways and safety barriers, energy efficient LED light fixtures that provide full coverage lighting at the platform, detectable warning systems, and new signage.
- The designer of record for the project is WSP USA, one of the world’s leading engineering, science and infrastructure solutions firms, bringing together top experts across disciplines and geographies. Centennial Contractors Enterprises provided general contractor services for the project. Oklahoma contractors were Olsson Engineering, Streets Mechanical, Terracon and Greenshade Trees (Oklahoma City), Jesco Electric (Yukon) and Cantera Concrete Company (Tulsa).
Pauls Valley (PVL) $5 million
- Pauls Valley opened its station in 2002 with funding assistance from the Oklahoma Department of Transportation through the Federal Transportation Equity Act for the 21st Century. Built to match the original depot in style, it incorporates a climate-controlled waiting area and restrooms. The station now features a 290-foot-long concrete boarding platform with an embedded brick paver surface. Complete are sloped accessible walkways and safety barriers, energy efficient LED light fixtures that provide full coverage lighting at the platform, detectable warning systems, and new signage.
- The designer of record for the project is HDR Inc., specializing in architecture, engineering, environmental and construction services. George Allen Construction provided general contractor services for the project. Oklahoma contractors were WW Builders and Smith Dressler Electric Services (Duncan) Greenshade Trees (Oklahoma City), Tolbert Tree Care (Pauls Valley), Mills Fene Services (Glenpool), Attaboy Striping and Parking Lot Services (Tecumseh) and Ark Welding & Fab (Ardmore)
Amtrak has invested more than $1 billion since 2011 in accessibility upgrades and improvement projects at 169 stations across the national network to ensure a safe, efficient, and comfortable travel experience for customers. The ADA Stations Program is advancing 116 station designs and 85 station construction projects as part of Amtrak’s ongoing commitment to providing accessibility by working toward 100% completion by 2029.
These Amtrak projects receive specific Congressional funding directed by the Federal Railroad Administration. The Amtrak Heartland Flyer (Trains 821 & 822) are sponsored by the Oklahoma and Texas state transportation departments.
Reactions:
“Amtrak’s improvements to both the Norman and Pauls Valley stations in Oklahoma will enhance accessibility for wheeled mobility devices, strollers, and users of rolling luggage. As the representative for both stations, I am excited to see infrastructure accessibility being enhanced throughout my district and am grateful to see Amtrak make this investment,” said Cong. Tom Cole (Okla. 4th)
“The improvements to Norman’s historic Santa Fe Depot will help ensure that this important transportation connection is accessible and welcoming to everyone who travels through our community. The Heartland Flyer is an integral part of Norman’s transportation network, and we’re grateful to see this investment in a station that has served our community for more than a century,” said Norman Mayor Stephen Tyler Holman.
“We appreciate the work Amtrak has done to improve the station here in Pauls Valley and the investment they have made in our community. These improvements help create a welcoming place for residents and visitors and support our efforts to bring more people into our downtown. We see Amtrak as an important economic driver for Pauls Valley, connecting travelers to our local businesses, attractions, and events. We value this partnership and look forward to continuing to work together to grow ridership and create more opportunities for our community,” said Pauls Villey City Manager Joe Livingston.
title: Amtrak Completes Improvements at Two Oklahoma Stations

HUNTSVILLE, Ala. – Three individuals have been charged in separate but related indictments for illegal firearms possession and threats of violence, announced U.S. Attorney Phillip W. Williams Jr.

A two-count indictment filed in U.S. District Court charges Levi Clifton Belcher, 18, of Huntsville, Alabama, with possession of an unregistered National Firearms Act Weapon and interstate transmission of threatening communications.

In separate but related indictments, Tadashi Ereckson, 38, and Anthony Elijah Slota, 28, both of Huntsville, Alabama, were charged with possession of an unregistered National Firearms Act Weapon.

“My office will take every available step to prosecute credible threats against law enforcement,” said U.S. Attorney Williams. I’m grateful for the partnership between FBI, ATF, HSI, and the Huntsville Police Department. Their diligent investigation led to these prosecutions.”

“I’m proud of the men and women of our FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force and all our partners across North Alabama," said David R. Fitzgibbons, Special Agent in Charge, FBI Birmingham. "Their partnership and dedication are vital to Protecting (capital P) the Homeland. Together, we will swiftly confront any threat to public safety in full defense of the U.S. Constitution.”

“The relationships that the ATF has fostered with our state, local, and federal law enforcement partners allows us to rapidly investigate reports of federal violations and threats of violence,” said ATF Special Agent in Charge James VanVliet. “This case is another example of those collaborative and unified efforts to protect the communities that we serve.”

“HSI is committed to working with our law enforcement partners to identify and investigate credible threats of violence against federal law enforcement personnel and the communities we serve,” said Ellen Johnson, Acting Special Agent in Charge of HSI in Georgia and Alabama. “This case demonstrates the importance of information sharing and coordinated action to address alleged threats before they can escalate. HSI will continue to work alongside our federal, state, and local partners to protect public safety and uphold the rule of law.”

According to court documents, on December 18, 2025, the FBI’s National Threat Operations Center was alerted by an individual to a social media post by Belcher that contained threats of violence against Immigration and Custom Enforcement agents.

According to court documents, on September 10, 2026, ATF agents and Intelligence Research Specialists located Belcher’s vehicle in Decatur, Alabama and began surveillance. During the surveillance, agents observed Belcher and Slota wearing body armor, carrying multiple firearms, and in possession of military-style backpacks. Belcher and Slota were observed entering Belcher’s vehicle, which then traveled toward Huntsville. Officers with the Huntsville Police Department conducted a traffic stop on the vehicle. Belcher and Slota who were armed with rifles and two 3D printed pistols. Officers searched the vehicle and located rifle and pistol magazines with various anti-government sentiments written on them, along with hundreds of rounds of ammunition. Belcher and Slota were arrested.

Officers then obtained a search warrant for the residence that Belcher and Slota were known to stay at in Huntsville, Alabama. During the execution of the search warrant, Erekson was arrested after attempting to reach for a concealed pistol on his ankle while being detained.

FBI, ATF and Homeland Security Investigations investigated the case along with the Huntsville Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney John M. Hundscheid is prosecuting the case.

An indictment contains only charges. A defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.
title: Three Individuals Indicted on Firearm Charges After One Allegedly Made Threats of Violence

WASHINGTON — The Office of the United States Trade Representative has invoked the Rapid Response Labor Mechanism (RRM) in the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) to review whether workers at GLM Components Mexico, S.A. de C.V. (GLM Components), located in Puebla, Mexico, are being denied the right to freedom of association and collective bargaining. The United States has suspended liquidation of unliquidated entries of goods from the GLM Components facility, which manufactures auto parts.
Background
The United States Trade Representative (Trade Representative) and the Secretary of Labor co-chair the Interagency Labor Committee for Monitoring and Enforcement (ILC). On September 8, 2026, the ILC received an RRM petition from the Sindicato Regeneración Nacional de Trabajadores y Empleados de la República Mexicana “Morenas,” a Mexican independent union. The petition alleges that GLM Components is violating workers’ rights to freedom of association and collective bargaining, including by interfering with union activity and unlawfully firing workers in retaliation for union activity.
The ILC reviews RRM petitions that it receives, and the accompanying information, within 30 days. After conducting this review, the ILC determined that there is sufficient, credible evidence of a denial of rights enabling the good faith invocation of enforcement mechanisms under the USMCA. As a result, the Trade Representative has submitted a request to Mexico under Annex 31-A of the USMCA that Mexico review whether workers at GLM Components are being denied the right to freedom of association and collective bargaining. The Trade Representative has also directed the Secretary of the Treasury to suspend liquidation of unliquidated entries of goods from the GLM Components facility.
Mexico has 10 days to agree to conduct a review and, if it agrees, 45 days from today to complete the review.
A copy of the request for review can be found here.
A copy of the letter to the Secretary of the Treasury can be found here.
Information about previous requests can be found here.

LAFAYETTE – On September 29, 2026, United States District Judge David C. Joseph sentenced Anthony Smith , 54, of Pensacola, Florida, to 72 months in federal prison for Conspiracy to Distribute and Possession with Intent to Distribute Controlled Substances after his July 1, 2026, guilty plea. According to court records, federal agents began investigating a Louisiana-based drug trafficking network in May of 2023. Agents identified a primary supplier and several associates who were using a storage facility in Lafayette to stash their illicit drug supply. Investigators monitored the organization and intercepted communications revealing that narcotics were being prepared for distribution to members of the network, including Smith.

On November 29, 2023, agents observed a member of the network retrieve drugs from the storage facility and transport them to two other co-conspirators. Those associates then traveled to a gas station, at which time Smith arrived in his vehicle, putting him squarely in the center of the distribution scheme. Agents then witnessed one associate place a bag containing a shoebox into Smith’s vehicle, before the group dispersed. Later, Smith was stopped by law enforcement, and a search of his vehicle revealed two kilograms of cocaine concealed inside the shoebox. Smith admitted that he had traveled from Florida for the purpose of obtaining and transporting narcotics in furtherance of the conspiracy. He also acknowledged that he had knowingly joined the drug trafficking network and fully understood its illegal purpose.

The Drug Enforcement Administration and the Harris County Sheriff’s Office (Mississippi) investigated this case. It was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Daniel Vermaelen and Casey N. Stelly, with assistance from Legal Assistant Christy Angelle.

This case was prosecuted as part of Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN), the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. Learn more at www.justice.gov/psn.

You may find a copy of this press release (and any updates) on the website of the United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Louisiana at www.justice.gov/usao-wdla.

Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Western District of Louisiana at www.lawd.uscourts.gov or at https://www.lawd.uscourts.gov/cmecf-pacer, under Case Number 23-CR-00291.

Rep. Torres Introduces the Improving Access to WIC Act to Ease Access to Nutrition Support for Moms and Children
With More Than 4 in 10 WIC-eligible families Not Enrolled, Legislation Closes Gap by Helping States Strengthen Partnerships with Healthcare Providers, Lower Barriers to Participation, and Boost Outreach Efforts
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Norma Torres (CA-35) introduced the Improving Access to WIC Act, legislation to make it easier to enroll in and stay connected to the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC). As families struggle with the ongoing affordability crisis, WIC helps feed mothers from the moment they find out they are pregnant to when their children are five years old. WIC not only helps moms access free, healthy foods, but also helps with breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health resources.
Nearly 25,000 mothers, infants, and children benefit from WIC in California’s 35th Congressional District. Nationwide, in fiscal year 2025, WIC served 6.9 million participants every month. The program is proven to save lives and improve lifetime health outcomes. Despite this, the most recent data show that more than 4 in 10 eligible individuals do not participate in WIC, and WIC utilization is lower for pregnant mothers and 1- to 4-year-olds. This legislation will tackle this participation gap.
The Improving Access to WIC Act would establish a federal grant program for states, tribes, and territories to improve access to, participation in, and retention in WIC. States that opt into the program would receive flexible funding to help strengthen partnerships between WIC agencies and healthcare providers, modernize the enrollment experience, improve community outreach, and help enroll mothers and children on SNAP and Medicaid who already qualify for WIC but do not yet participate.
“WIC provides critical nutrition assistance to moms, babies, and young children, and getting enrolled should not mean jumping through unnecessary hoops,” said Congresswoman Torres. “Moms are already juggling doctor’s appointments, work, child care, and countless responsibilities. We should be making it easier, not harder, for eligible families to access the support they need. My Improving Access to WIC Act will help states integrate WIC enrollment with healthcare providers, reduce duplicative appointments and paperwork, and make it easier for families to enroll and stay on WIC.”
“Despite the incredible public health benefits of WIC, we are still reaching only a little more than half of eligible families. Investing in targeted outreach, data sharing, and healthcare linkages will make it easier for families who qualify to connect with WIC. We thank Rep. Torres for her leadership and support for WIC.” Georgia Machell, President & CEO, National WIC Association
“WIC is an evidence-based, time-limited program with proven positive outcomes for families and communities, yet there is a significant portion of eligible families not connected to services. Supporting innovative outreach methods and healthcare linkages to improve access to the program is an important investment. We appreciate Rep. Torres’s support for WIC and young families.” Megan Esparza, Executive Director, California WIC Association
“The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants and Children (WIC) is one of the most critical tools pediatricians have to ensure infants and young children can receive proper nutrition support in their earliest years. The Improving Access to WIC Act would provide states with resources to make enrolling eligible families in WIC easier, more efficient, and more effective. The American Academy of Pediatrics thanks Representative Torres for introducing this important legislation and calls on Congress to advance it,” said Andrew D. Racine, MD, PhD, FAAP, President of the American Academy of Pediatrics.
“The American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists has a long history of supporting the WIC program and is proud to endorse the Improving Access to WIC Act,” said ACOG President Camille A. Clare, MD, MPH, CPE. “Families are facing growing financial pressure, and putting healthy food on the table can be especially difficult during pregnancy and after a baby is born. With significant changes to SNAP under H.R. 1, making WIC easier to access is more important than ever. This bill would help eligible families get the nutrition support they need instead of getting stuck in red tape. ACOG thanks Rep. Norma Torres for her leadership and commitment to strengthening the WIC program.”
"WIC is a proven intervention that supports the health of women, babies, and young children. Yet far too many eligible families are missing out on the many benefits of the program. We applaud Rep. Torres for introducing the Improving Access to WIC Act. Establishing a federal grant program to help states improve access to and participation in WIC would make it easier for eligible families to connect with this critical support. We urge Members of Congress to co-sponsor this legislation, so more families are connected to the nutrition they need to thrive." - Crystal FitzSimons, President of the Food Research & Action Center (FRAC).
The bill is supported by: National WIC Association (NWA), California WIC Association (CWA), American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), Food Research and Action Center (FRAC), Alliance to End Hunger, Coalition on Human Needs.
Bill Summary:
The Improving Access to WIC Act authorizes $50 million for Fiscal Years 2027 through 2031 for the grant program. States, tribes, and territories that choose to opt in would receive, to the maximum extent practicable, $200,000 and an additional amount based on each participating state’s national share of WIC participants.
The bill also requires the U.S. Department of Agriculture to publicly report on the program’s outcomes, including its impact on WIC participation and retention, and share best practices that states can use to improve enrollment and access.
Under the legislation, participating states could use grant funding to:
- Connect more eligible families with WIC by: 
  - Improving outreach in clinical settings and building up systems to make it easier for doctors and health care providers to directly refer patients to WIC, including through statewide referral systems, and
  - Expanding outreach in trusted community settings, including at Head Start and Early Head Start programs, preschools, schools, and other places to meet WIC-eligible families where they are.
- Improve secure data sharing between health care providers and WIC agencies to streamline WIC referrals and certification, while protecting privacy, requiring individual consent, and maintaining federal confidentiality protections.
- Reduce duplicative appointments and paperwork by making it easier for health care providers, consistent with applicable laws and with individuals’ consent, to securely provide WIC agencies with information such as height, weight, hemoglobin measurements (blood tests), and other documentation needed for WIC certification.
- Modernize the enrollment process, including by establishing or expanding online WIC applications.
- Help reach and enroll moms and children on Medicaid (Medi-Cal) or SNAP (CalFresh) who already qualify for WIC, but are not participating.
Original Cosponsors: Nanette Barragán (CA-44); Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01); Yvette Clarke (NY-09 ); Jim Costa (CA-21); Jasmine Crockett (TX-30); Chris Deluzio (PA-17); Debbie Dingell (MI-06); Sylvia Garcia (TX-29); Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04); Adelita S. title: Rep. Torres Introduces the Improving Access to WIC Act to Ease Access to Nutrition Support for Moms and Children

Justice Department and FBI Seize Vulnerability Scanning and Spear Phishing Tools Operated and Used by China-State Sponsored Hackers
Today the Justice Department and FBI announced court-authorized seizures to deny malicious cyber actors access to two hacking tools, “Microscan” and “FishHub,” used to scan and, in some cases, hack, U.S. and foreign critical infrastructure systems and other networks. As alleged in court documents unsealed in the Western District of Pennsylvania, malicious cyber actors working for Integrity Technology Group (Integrity Tech), a company based in the People’s Republic of China (PRC), operated and used the tools. Integrity Tech has contracts with the PRC government.
“The United States will not allow China or its proxies to operate against United States interests with impunity in cyberspace,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “The National Security Division will continue to respond decisively and use every tool at our disposal to disrupt the Flax Typhoon threats, dismantle the infrastructure sustaining them, and protect the critical networks that power our daily lives and on which our Nation’s security depends.”
“These state-sponsored hackers continue to aggressively target and access networks and systems throughout the world in an effort to identify and steal files and otherwise exploit victims’ vulnerabilities,” said U.S. Attorney Troy Rivetti for the Western District of Pennsylvania. “These seizures, our second disruption of Integrity Tech’s massive operations in as many years, send another clear message to cybercriminals from the PRC and elsewhere of the Department’s dedication to defending and maintaining cybersecurity in the United States and abroad.”
“Integrity Technology Group provided China-linked threat actors with capabilities used to conduct widespread vulnerability scanning and, in some cases, intrusions targeting U.S. and foreign critical infrastructure,” said Assistant Director Brett Leatherman of the FBI’s Cyber Division. “The PRC relies on contractor and enabling companies to expand the reach and scale of its malicious cyber activity. By exposing and disrupting these enablers, we make it harder for the PRC to target American networks and infrastructure.”
“Today’s seizures underscore the FBI’s unwavering commitment in disrupting PRC state-sponsored cyber criminals who threaten our critical infrastructure and national security,” said Special Agent in Charge Mark Remily of the FBI San Diego Field Office. “FBI San Diego and our law enforcement partners around the world will continue to employ the full force of our investigative authority to protect the American people and safeguard our networks from malicious foreign cyber actors.”
According to court documents, Integrity Tech created and used a botnet of internet-of-things devices infected with a variant of Mirai malware. Among other things, this botnet facilitated Integrity Tech’s computer vulnerability scanning using Microscan. Integrity Tech developed Microscan to conduct reconnaissance, via the botnet and otherwise, of victim computer networks for vulnerabilities that its clients would later exploit. Targets of Microscan vulnerability scanning include a U.S. power company based in South Carolina, a multi-national Non-Governmental Organization, Japanese and Polish airports, Taiwanese critical infrastructure companies in the natural gas and power sectors, and two Taiwanese universities. Integrity Tech accessed Microscan through one of the seized domains, c0cc[.]cc.
A second Integrity Tech tool, FishHub, is alleged to have facilitated the exploitation of computer networks through spear phishing. After an initial network compromise, FishHub downloaded additional malware to the victim network. This malware provided Integrity Tech’s clients with unauthorized remote access to the victim network or searched for specific files and sent them to servers controlled by Integrity Tech. Confirmed victims of FishHub activity included approximately 20 Taiwanese universities. Five of the seized domains helped deliver this malware: 98aicai[.]com, 98aicode[.]com, outlook3650[.]com, youtubecard[.]com, and linkedinns[.]net.
Today’s action marks the Department’s second public technical disruption of Integrity Tech’s hacking infrastructure. In September 2024, the Justice Department announced the court-authorized disruption of Integrity Tech’s Mirai malware botnet which consisted of more than 200,000 consumer devices in the United States and worldwide. In conjunction with the seizures announced today, the FBI, along with other U.S. and foreign-partner agencies, published a cyber security advisory. This advisory provides indicators-of-compromise associated with Integrity Tech intrusion activity and is designed to help network defenders identify and respond to Integrity Tech’s malicious activity.
The FBI San Diego and Baltimore Field Offices are investigating the case, in coordination with the FBI’s Cyber Division.
Assistant U.S. Attorney Brendan McKenna for the Western District of Pennsylvania and Trial Attorney Jacques Singer-Emery of the National Security Division’s National Security Cyber Section are prosecuting the case. Substantial assistance was provided by Assistant U.S. Attorney Thomas Sullivan for the District of Maryland and the National Police Agency of Japan.
Note: View the affidavit here.
View the seizure warrant here.
title: Justice Department and FBI Seize Vulnerability Scanning and Spear Phishing Tools Operated and Used by China-State Sponsored Hackers
