KANSAS CITY, KAN. – A California man pleaded guilty to targeting child victims and persuading and coercing them into creating visual depictions of themselves engaged in sexually explicit conduct using online social media and messaging apps.

According to court documents, Adrian Gutierrez, 22, of Ontario, California, pleaded guilty to one count of sexual exploitation of a minor involving a child residing in Kansas.

From approximately May 2023 through October 2024, Gutierrez communicated with dozens of minors using multiple online platforms. He used persuasion and coercion to get 21 identified victims from Kansas and 17 other states to engage in sexually explicit conduct while transmitting live video calls with him. Gutierrez often misrepresented his true identity and age by telling the victims he was also a minor of a similar age to the victim. Despite law enforcement efforts, many other victims were unable to be fully identified. Some victims reside outside of the United States.

Gutierrez is scheduled to be sentenced on January 5, 2027. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

“The lessons of ‘stranger danger’ also apply to the internet. While Mr. Gutierrez mostly targeted children between the ages of ten and twelve, his victims were as young as nine years old,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser. “We encourage parents to talk to their children about internet safety and explain to them that not everyone is who they say they are or the age they claim, particularly online.”

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is investigating the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Audrey McCormick is prosecuting the case.

Project Safe Childhood This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc .

###
title: California man sexually exploited children online across at least 18 states

CHARLOTTE, N.C. – Oleg Korniev, 42, a dual citizen of Ukraine and Russia, pleaded guilty today to running a sophisticated international money laundering organization that laundered millions of dollars stolen from United States victims by cybercriminals around the world. In total, this international criminal organization recruited over 15,000 U.S.-based money mules to launder at least $10 million stolen by hackers from over 750 U.S. bank accounts.

“Money mules play crucial roles in cybercrime, so the Justice Department pursues mules and their recruiters wherever they operate and however long it takes,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Alongside our international partners, we will dismantle criminal networks that attack Americans. No amount of distance or time puts these criminals beyond the reach of justice.”

“Just because you are outside the borders of the United States does not mean you will get away with defrauding U.S. Citizens and businesses,” said U.S. Attorney Russ Ferguson for the Western District of North Carolina. “We will work hard to bring you to justice, as we did in this case.”

“For years, the FBI has worked tirelessly to unravel the layers of this international money laundering operation and bring Mr. Korniev to justice,” said Special Agent in Charge Reid Davis of FBI North Carolina. “This case reflects the Bureau’s enduring commitment to following the evidence — no matter how long it takes, how far it leads, or how deliberately criminals try to hide behind borders and technology. We will continue pursuing those who enable cybercriminals until every responsible individual is held to account.”

According to court documents, Korniev was one of the leaders of Your Mule Cashout (YMCO). YMCO created, maintained, and operated an elaborate and sophisticated system of money mules and internet infrastructure that allowed computer hackers, who had stolen money from the bank accounts of U.S. companies, to conceal the thefts and transfer the stolen money to countries outside the U.S. YMCO’s services operated through online infrastructure that allowed hackers to move the stolen money to countries primarily in Eastern Europe by paying YMCO a percentage of the money stolen.

YMCO provided its money laundering services through money mules who were U.S. residents deceived by YMCO into believing that they were working for legitimate companies and making genuine money transfers. YMCO falsely represented that the money mules’ job was to receive payments from businesses into their personal bank accounts, withdraw the money, and then wire the funds to the fake company’s partners overseas. The money mules instead processed the hackers’ stolen proceeds and wired them out of the country to other YMCO conspirators. The money mules never received payment for their services.

Korniev helped develop YMCO’s policies and procedures; managed, hired, and fired employees; rewarded and punished employees based on performance; and secured illegal services supporting YMCO. As part of his plea, Korniev admitted that YMCO was responsible for over $14.7 million in actual and intended losses by confirmed victims and that he intended to launder over $9.7 million from cybercriminals and did launder at least $7 million. Korniev also agreed to provide full restitution to known victims to compensate them for their actual losses as well as forfeit cash seized from him when he was arrested in the Republic of Georgia.

Korniev pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering, money laundering, conspiracy to commit computer fraud, conspiracy to commit access device theft, and aggravated identity theft. Sentencing will be set at a later date. He faces a minimum penalty of two years in prison and maximum penalty of 50 years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine Korniev’s sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other factors.

Previously, four other individuals involved with YMCO were arrested overseas, extradited to the Western District of North Carolina, and pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering. They received sentences ranging from around 37 months to 63 months in prison and the court ordered each defendant to pay over $9.1 million in restitution to numerous U.S. victims.

The FBI is investigating the case.

Senior Counsel Matthew A. Lamberti of the Criminal Division’s Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Matthew Warren for the Western District of North Carolina are prosecuting the case. The Department of Justice’s Office of International Affairs, the FBI Office of the Law Enforcement Attache in Tbilisi, and law enforcement authorities in Georgia, including the Prosecutor’s Office of Georgia, provided significant assistance.

CCIPS investigates and prosecutes cybercrime and intellectual property (IP) crime in coordination with domestic and international law enforcement agencies, often with assistance from the private sector. Since 2020, CCIPS has secured the conviction of over 180 cyber and IP criminals, and court orders for the return of over $350 million in victim funds.
title: Ukrainian-Russian Dual Citizen Pleads Guilty to Running International Money Laundering Organization for Cybercriminals

MUSKOGEE, OKLAHOMA – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Oklahoma announced that Colin Reece Neher, age 22, of Ardmore, Oklahoma, entered a guilty plea to one count of Possession of Certain Material Involving the Sexual Exploitation of a Minor, punishable by up to 20 years in prison and a $250,000 fine.

The Indictment alleged that beginning in or about February 2022, and continuing until on or about May 21, 2026, Neher knowingly possessed and accessed with intent to view one or more matters which contained visual depictions of a minor engaging in sexually explicit conduct.

The charge arose from an investigation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

The Honorable Gerald L. Jackson, Magistrate Judge in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Oklahoma, accepted the plea and ordered the completion of a presentence investigation report.

A U.S. District Court Judge will determine the sentence to be imposed after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

Neher was remanded into the custody of the United States Marshals Service pending sentencing.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Morgan Muzljakovich and Nicole Paladino represented the United States.

The Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) announced today a $150 million conditional loan commitment to PsiQuantum, Corp. to enhance the company's advanced manufacturing and prototyping capabilities in the United States. Building on OSC's ongoing collaboration with the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA)'s Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, the proposed loan follows recently awarded funding agreements with DARPA and CHIPS and supports PsiQuantum's novel photonic approach to developing the world's first commercially useful fault-tolerant quantum computer (FTQC).
The potential financing executes on President Donald J. Trump's mandate to drive and sustain U.S. leadership in the strategically important field of quantum information science and technology. Quantum computing is now regarded, alongside Super Intelligence (SI) and semiconductors, as a foundational technology for future economic and military advantage.
"OSC's proposed transaction with PsiQuantum directly aligns with President Donald J. Trump's mandate to accelerate development and commercialization of quantum computing. Quantum computing will provide transformational capabilities, and the Department of War's investment into PsiQuantum serves the mission of securing U.S. leadership in quantum computing in full alignment with Department of War objectives set forth by Secretary of War Pete Hegseth," said David A. Lorch, Director of the Office of Strategic Capital and Senior Advisor to Deputy Secretary of War Steve Feinberg.
"Funding the development of fault-tolerant quantum computing is a national security imperative,"added Peter B. Zuckerman, Senior Managing Director at OSC. "We must scale this critical technology to secure our technological edge and deny adversaries a decisive strategic advantage."
"I applaud OSC for this strategic collaboration with DARPA and CHIPS, which demonstrates how the Department of War is moving at breakneck speed to meet President Trump's directive that the United States must lead in quantum. Quantum computing will shape the future of warfare and fundamentally change how the Joint Force solves its most complex operational challenges," said Emil Michael, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering.
The conditional loan commitment between OSC and PsiQuantum specifies customary additional steps the company must take to proceed toward financial close, including satisfying financial, legal, technical, due diligence, and other requirements.
title: Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital Signs $150 Million Conditional Loan Commitment With PsiQuantum

Rep. Vasquez Leads Effort with State and Local Officials to Push for Federal Coordination in Response to Recent Flooding
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On October 8, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) led a delegation of federal, state, and local leaders in a letter to federal agencies urging them to tour the damage and provide all available resources to those affected by the recent flooding across southern New Mexico.
The letter asks the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Bureau of Land Management (BLM), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), and International Boundary and Water Commission (IBWC) to visit affected communities, work with local leaders, and provide assistance to homes, communities, farms and businesses impacted by the flooding.
“It is imperative that your agencies act now to cut red tape, reduce bureaucratic barriers, increase communication and responsiveness, and act as a partner in this recovery,” wrote Vasquez. “Due to the nature of this area, the complex patchwork of federal land, critical agricultural areas, and proximity to the border, this response will require your agencies to work hand-in-hand with state, county, and local leaders on both short-term recovery and long-term mitigation efforts.”
The letter is joined by State Senator Jeff Steinborn, State Representative Nathan P. Small, Hatch Mayor Dennis Torres, and Caballo Soil and Water Conservation District Chairman Harvey Morrow.
On October 4th, Rep. Vasquez hosted a meeting in Doña Ana County with local elected officials and visited families and farms impacted by the recent flooding. He visited Hatch, the McLeod/Garfield Dam, and surrounding areas to assess the impact of the flooding and what the community needed for recovery firsthand. During this visit, Rep. Vasquez also discussed Hatch’s immediate recovery needs, available state and federal resources, and opportunities for continued coordination to support the community’s recovery and infrastructure needs.
Read the full letter HERE.

Congresswoman Schrier Joins WA Delegation in Supporting Governor’s Request for Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance for Devastating Wildfires in Washington State
WASHINGTON, D.C.– Today, Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) joined Washington state’s entire Congressional delegation in a letter to President Donald Trump urging him to approve Governor Bob Ferguson’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance to help communities recover and repair damage due to the devastating wildfires that swept through Central and Eastern Washington from July 23 through August 31.
2026 was one of Washington state’s worst wildfire seasons on record, with fires causing severe damage and devastating lives. Weather conditions, exacerbated by extended drought, heat, and wind, caused over 900,000 acres, or 1,400 square miles, to burn across Washington state – taking homes and lives. Three massive fires broke out and tore through neighborhoods across Spokane, the Old Trails Fire burned in northwest Spokane, the Autumn Lane Fire burned near Nine-Mile Falls, and the Fairview Fire burned in Mead.
In the Eighth District, the Little Giant, Three Queens, Sisi, King, Goat, and West Fork fires – among others – devastated communities, property, livestock, and businesses. The damages from this wildfire season continues to overwhelm state, local, Tribal, nonprofit, and private-sector capabilities.
“As members of the Washington state delegation, we write in support of Washington state’s addendum to include Public Assistance to their September 28th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance due to devastating wildfire damages incurred from July 23rd through August 31st. We implore you to approve the request for public and individual assistance as quickly as possible,” members of the delegation wrote. “Washington state suffered from a historic wildfire season, with multiple wildfires ravaging parts of Central and Eastern Washington, devastating communities in Asotin, Chelan, Columbia, Douglas, Ferry, Grant, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens, Whitman, and Yakima Counties, as well as the Spokane Tribe of Indians.”
Joining Congresswoman Schrier in the letter to President Trump were Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Senator Maria Cantwell (D-WA), and U.S. Representatives Suzan DelBene (D, WA-01), Rick Larsen (D, WA-02), Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (D, WA-03), Dan Newhouse (R, WA-04), Michael Baumgartner (R, WA-05), Emily Randall (D, WA-06), Pramila Jayapal (D, WA-07), Adam Smith (D, WA-09), and Marilyn Strickland (D, WA-10).
The lawmakers continued, “Local, Tribal, state, federal, and out-of-state firefighting crews deployed quickly, pooling resources to contain the fires and protect both life and property. Fire crews faced dangerous conditions, including hazardous terrain, high winds, and record-setting drought, which made the fires extremely difficult to contain. Many of these fires burned over the course of several weeks, and damaged public infrastructure like roads, bridges, public utility systems, and other essential public assets. Beyond the infrastructure that was completely lost to the wildfires, the prolonged exposure to fire, smoke, and extreme temperatures have left remaining infrastructure vulnerable to further damage and unsafe for the public.”
“These devastating wildfires have put significant stress on Washington state’s infrastructure and emergency response resources. Throughout the crisis, local, Tribal, state, federal, and international first responders stepped up and worked tirelessly to keep our communities safe. We thank you for your timely approval of the state’s request for an Emergency Declaration which provided vital federal support for both mitigation and recovery. We reiterate our full support for the October 6th request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance and thank you in advance for your prompt attention to this urgent matter,” the lawmakers concluded.
The full letter is available HERE.
title: Congresswoman Schrier Joins WA Delegation in Supporting Governor’s Request for Major Disaster Declaration for Public Assistance for Devastating Wildfires in Washington State

Winning the race for quantum leadership is essential to preserving the United States' technological edge and securing its national security. President Trump made American leadership in quantum information science a national priority through Executive Order 14413, ushering in the Next Frontier of Quantum Innovation. Today, building on the call to renew bold, ambitious national missions in the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios' report Science: A New Golden Age, the Department of War is accelerating its efforts to identify, develop, and prepare for quantum computing capabilities that will underpin future national security missions.
In support of President Trump's mandate for American leadership in quantum, the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering (R&E) today announced new initiatives and programmatic updates totaling approximately $350 million to strengthen U.S. leadership in quantum computing capabilities that support national security.
"Dominance in quantum information science is a critical priority for both President Trump and the Department of War. Maintaining American leadership in this field is essential to preserving our technological edge, and R&E is uniquely positioned to drive the innovation needed across academia and industry," said Emil Michael, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering.
R&E will direct greater attention across the Department of War's innovation ecosystem toward identifying mission-relevant applications of quantum computing, particularly as sufficiently capable quantum computers become available. R&E expects that quantum-enabled applications in disciplines such as chemistry, materials science, and physics will enable the development of next-generation weapons, platforms, and other critical capabilities that are more lethal, cost-effective, and manufacturable.
This new effort will build on existing Department of War programs and complement related national initiatives led by the Department of Energy (DOE), particularly its recently announced Quantum Genesis Priority Applications and the Quantum Genesis Q Competition, as well as initiatives led by the National Science Foundation (NSF) and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA). In coordination with DOE's Office of Science, the National Nuclear Security Administration, and the Laboratory for Physical Sciences, the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) will host a series of application workshops beginning before January 2027. The workshops will bring together end users and quantum-algorithm experts to identify high-value use cases, accelerate industrially relevant quantum advantage, create economic opportunity, and strengthen national defense.
DARPA is also advancing the technical validation needed to determine whether prospective quantum computing systems can deliver utility at scale. Through its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, DARPA announced the advancement of four prospective quantum-computing providers to Stage C of the initiative, representing approximately $200 million in new funding that builds on more than $650 million in investments from DARPA in prospective quantum-computing providers. During Stage C, participants will work with DARPA to verify and validate that their utility-scale quantum-computer concepts can be constructed as designed and operated as intended. Advancement to Stage C indicates that each participant has demonstrated a research and development plan capable of realizing a utility-scale quantum computer; characterized key program risks and mitigation measures; and developed prototype requirements to retire those risks.
A strong quantum industrial base is essential to maintaining U.S. leadership in science and technology. To help build that foundation, the Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital today announced an approximately $150 million conditional loan commitment to support PsiQuantum's advanced manufacturing and prototyping capabilities in the United States.
Together, these efforts will advance the Department's understanding of quantum computing's future national security applications and strengthen avenues for companies to deliver systems capable of executing them.
title: Department of War Announces $350 Million in Quantum Computing Initiatives

Ranking Member Raskin, Rep. Dean Demand DOJ Investigate Former Bard College President After Uncovering His Email Asking Whether Young Woman Was “for Me” or Epstein Himself, Reveal History of Sex Abuse Coverup at Bard
Records Indicate Epstein Was Trafficking the Young Woman Across State and International Lines When He Sent Her to Meet Botstein, Who Asked Epstein: “Is [She] for Me or Are You Keeping Her for Yourself?”
Evidence Contradicts DOJ Insistence That Epstein Trafficked Only to “Himself,” and Clearly Meets the Standard for Launching a Criminal Investigation; DOJ and FBI’s Inaction Left Possible Epstein Co-Conspirator in a Position of Power Over Young Students and Faculty
More Than a Dozen Whistleblowers Describe Decades of Unpunished Sexual Misconduct at Bard, Including Allegations Botstein Groped Women and Intervened in Title IX Proceedings to Protect Offenders
Raskin and Dean Call on DOJ and FBI to Investigate Botstein and Other Potential Epstein Co-Conspirators, Release Complete Files, and Protect Survivors’ Identities
Washington, D.C. (October 7, 2026)—Today, Rep. Jamie Raskin, Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Committee, and Rep. Madeleine Dean demanded a federal investigation into former Bard College President Leon Botstein after reviewing an email in which Botstein asked Jeffrey Epstein about a young woman Epstein was trafficking: “Is [Jane Doe] for me, or are you keeping her for yourself.” In a separate letter to Bard’s leadership, Ranking Member Raskin sought records concerning Epstein’s use of the college to advance his trafficking activities and allegations from more than a dozen whistleblowers about sexual misconduct at Bard, including allegations that Botstein personally engaged in misconduct and intervened in Title IX proceedings to protect offenders.
The letters—to Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel, and to Bard Board Chair Brandon Weber and Acting President Jonathan Becker—detail communications concerning a young foreign model and aspiring vocalist whom Epstein sent to Botstein in May 2014. They also question why DOJ exposed her name hundreds of times and released photographs showing her face while redacting Botstein’s email address.
“[T]his evidence, and the facts laid out in the Epstein files, surely meet and exceed the federal law enforcement standard for initiating a criminal investigation: the existence of evidence that a crime ‘may have occurred.’ These facts strongly indicate that a crime may have occurred. Yet, you have done nothing, and launched no investigation, about this incident which you and your staff must have known of for at least 18 months. In so doing, you have effectively permitted a potential co-conspirator of Jeffrey Epstein to stay in a position of power over young students, faculty and staff for an additional year at least,” wrote Ranking Member Raskin and Rep. Dean to Blanche and Patel.
Emails and messages reviewed by the Committee show that Epstein groomed the young woman throughout 2014, offering advice and assistance with her education and career in the United States. After meeting Jane Doe in Paris, Epstein directed his assistant, Lesley Groff, to arrange private flights from her home country to destinations including Canada, New York, Florida, New Mexico and his island. A message to Epstein included a photograph of Jane Doe giving a woman, possibly Ghislaine Maxwell, a nude massage.
That May, Epstein sent Jane Doe to meet Botstein, ostensibly to assess her musical abilities and provide educational guidance. In an email from his Bard account, Botstein asked whether Jane Doe was “for me”. As he did with other survivors, Epstein relied on Botstein to assuage parental concerns about the sex offender, in this case by requesting orchestra tickets for the young woman’s parents to attend a Bard concert abroad. Epstein also asked Botstein to give them special treatment.
The evidence uncovered by the Committee contradicts the July 2025 DOJ–FBI memorandum and numerous follow-up claims by FBI Director Patel and Attorney General Blanche asserting that investigators found no evidence warranting an investigation of Epstein’s uncharged associates. Ranking Member Raskin demanded answers about why DOJ exposed the young woman’s identity while redacting Botstein’s email address, who directed that disparate treatment, and whom they were seeking to protect. Committee staff identified documents that still expose her name and provided the list separately to DOJ for redaction. The letters omit citations to DOJ documents to protect her identity.

CHICAGO — The creator of the digital asset Kishu Inu has been indicted in federal court in Chicago for allegedly operating a $9 million “rug pull” fraud scheme.

ALEXANDER SISEMORE, also known as “Kishu man” and “Kimbo,” founded and created the digital asset Kishu Inu, which launched in 2021 and subsequently reached a market capitalization of more than $1.6 billion. An indictment returned Tuesday in U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois alleges that Sisemore and others made materially false statements to investors in order to maintain Kishu Inu’s liquidity and increase its price in the cryptocurrency market while surreptitiously selling a large quantity of Kishu Inu tokens that Sisemore and others secretly allocated to themselves at the time the asset was created. Many of Sisemore’s alleged misrepresentations and falsehoods were made to actual and potential investors on social media applications, including Telegram, Twitter, Facebook, and Reddit.

The alleged fraud scheme—known colloquially as a “rug pull”—generated personal profits for Sisemore of approximately $9 million, the indictment states.

The indictment charges Sisemore, 28, of Fayetteville, Ark., with three counts of wire fraud, each of which is punishable by up to 20 years in federal prison. Arraignment in federal court in Chicago has not yet been scheduled.

The indictment was announced by Andrew S. Boutros, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois, and Ryan Whalen, Special Agent-in-Charge of the Chicago Field Office of the FBI. The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Elie Zenner and Matthew Getter.

The public is reminded that an indictment is not evidence of guilt. The defendant is presumed innocent and entitled to a fair trial at which the government has the burden of proving guilt beyond a reasonable doubt. If convicted, the Court must impose a reasonable sentence under federal statutes and the advisory U.S. Sentencing Guidelines.

The FBI Chicago Field Office is seeking to identify investors in Kishu Inu. If you invested in Kishu Inu or have information relevant to this investigation, you are encouraged to complete this online form . Responses are voluntary but may be useful in the federal investigation and to identify potential victims.
title: Creator of Digital Asset Kishu Inu Indicted for Allegedly Operating $9 Million “Rug Pull” Fraud Scheme

Over $10 million invested in North Carolina station accessibility improvements
HAMLET AND ROCKY MOUNT, N.C., Oct. 7, 2026 – Amtrak joined federal, state and local officials this week to celebrate the completion of accessibility improvement projects at its stations in Hamlet and Rocky Mount, marking more than $10 million in investments to improve accessibility, safety and the customer experience for rail travelers in North Carolina.
“These investments demonstrate Amtrak’s commitment to providing safe, accessible and convenient rail travel for all customers,” said Amtrak Vice President of Accessibility, Stations & Facilities Dr. David Handera. “Stations like Hamlet and Rocky Mount are important community assets, and these enhancements will help ensure they continue serving residents and visitors for many years to come.”
At Hamlet Station, Amtrak completed approximately $3.2 million in improvements, including construction of two 200-foot accessible boarding platforms, accessible pathways and walkways, safety barriers, LED platform lighting, detectable warning systems, and new signage.
At Rocky Mount Station, Amtrak completed approximately $7.3 million in improvements, including construction of an 840-foot accessible boarding platform, accessible pathways connecting the station, public right-of-way and parking areas, LED platform lighting, detectable warning systems, and new signage.
Together, these projects improve accessibility for customers of all abilities and support better travel experiences. The improvements were made possible through strong collaboration among Amtrak, the North Carolina Department of Transportation, the Federal Railroad Administration, local officials, and community partners.
These efforts support Amtrak’s broader efforts to modernize stations and create a more seamless travel experience for customers nationwide. Amtrak continues to advance station accessibility projects across the country as part of its long-term commitment to achieving a fully accessible national passenger rail network.
REACTIONS
Jason Orthner, NCDOT Rail Division Director
“Continued investments in stations like Hamlet and Rocky Mount make it safer and easier for passengers of all abilities to access rail service and continue their journeys These improvements strengthen the passenger experience today while supporting the continued growth and future of intercity passenger rail across North Carolina.”
Hamlet Mayor, Amy Guinn
“Amtrak’s recent substantial investment in our historic train depot demonstrates their continued commitment to rural communities. Enabling passengers of all abilities to access travel enhances the experience and ensures everyone can enjoy the freedom of travel by rail. The City of Hamlet greatly appreciates the collaboration of all the departments working together to accomplish these improvements.”
Rocky Mount Mayor, Sandy Roberson
“As much as any place in North Carolina, Rocky Mount is a railroad town. We are grateful to Amtrak in partnership with the NC Department of Transportation and the Federal Railroad Administration for the improvements that will make our historic train station more accessible, more welcoming, and more convenient for everyone who uses it.”
title: Amtrak Celebrates Completion of Accessibility Improvements at Hamlet and Rocky Mount Stations

Boyle Statement on Nonpartisan Watchdog Finding Trump Administration Illegally Withheld Health Research Funding
PHILADELPHIA, PA — Congressman Brendan F. Boyle (PA-02), Ranking Member of the House Budget Committee, issued the following statement after the nonpartisan Government Accountability Office (GAO) found that the Department of Health and Human Services violated the Impoundment Control Act by withholding congressionally appropriated funding for the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ). The finding comes after Boyle raised concerns about cuts affecting research at Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) and the University of Pennsylvania and demanded answers from the Trump Administration:
“GAO has made clear that the Administration violated the law by withholding funding Congress provided for critical health research. In Philadelphia, these cuts threaten lifesaving work, along with good-paying jobs and one of the most important drivers of our regional economy. I will continue fighting to protect Philadelphia’s research institutions and ensure the funding Congress provides is actually put to work.”
BACKGROUND
In August, Boyle joined researchers from CHOP and Penn to oppose the Administration’s cuts to AHRQ-supported programs and highlight their impact on Philadelphia. Researchers warned that the funding losses threatened ongoing medical research, research jobs, and programs training the next generation of scientists.
Boyle also sent a letter to Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought and AHRQ Director Roger Klein seeking information about the canceled and withheld funding, including whether the Administration intended to fully obligate funding appropriated by Congress. To date, the Administration has not responded to Ranking Member Boyle's questions about withholding this money.
GAO concluded that HHS violated the Impoundment Control Act when it refused to spend appropriated AHRQ funds, without submitting the special message to Congress required by law.
The stakes extend beyond individual research grants. Philadelphia is one of the country’s leading life sciences hubs, with more than 88,000 life sciences workers across the Greater Philadelphia region, and recent data show employment in biotechnology research and pharmaceutical manufacturing reaching record levels. Federal research investments help support that broader ecosystem of hospitals, universities, scientists, startups, and high-skilled jobs.
As the top Democrat on the House Budget Committee, Boyle has made protecting Congress’s constitutional power of the purse a central focus of his oversight work, repeatedly challenging efforts by the Executive Branch to freeze or withhold funding approved by Congress. Congressman Boyle’s Congressional Power of the Purse Act strengthens Congress’s authorities under the Impoundment Control Act (ICA) and creates criminal penalties for violations of the ICA.
###
title: Boyle Statement on Nonpartisan Watchdog Finding Trump Administration Illegally Withheld Health Research Funding

ST. LOUIS – A man from Lincoln County, Missouri on Wednesday admitted producing and receiving child sexual abuse material.

The investigation of Michael Anthony Lynch, now 24, began with a CyberTipline Report to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children that was triggered when three files containing child sexual abuse material (CSAM) were detected on one of Lynch’s online accounts. A court-approved search of the account uncovered more CSAM, and a search of his home uncovered more CSAM and evidence that he had produced CSAM involving one underage girl.

Lynch pleaded guilty Wednesday in U.S. District Court in St. Louis to one count of production of child pornography and one count of receipt of child pornography.

He is scheduled to be sentenced on January 14. Both the U.S. Attorney’s office and Lynch’s lawyer have agreed to recommend a sentence of 18 years in prison.

The St. Charles County Cyber Crime Task Force, the Lincoln County Sheriff’s Office and the FBI investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Jillian Anderson prosecuted the case.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Department of Justice Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc .
title: Lincoln County, Missouri Man Admits Child Pornography Charges

CHARLOTTE, N.C. – U.S. District Judge Matthew E. Orso sentenced Reginald Curtis, 47, of Morganton, to 210 months in prison followed by five years of supervised release today for distributing large quantities of methamphetamine, announced Russ Ferguson, U.S. Attorney for the Western District of North Carolina.

“People like Curtis, who traffic methamphetamine by the kilogram, are supplying the drug dealers,” said U.S. Attorney Russ Ferguson. “Getting wholesale drug distributors off the street is a key step in making our communities safer, and the community won’t have to worry about Curtis for another 17 years.”

According to court records, law enforcement determined that Curtis was trafficking large quantities of methamphetamine in Burke and Catawba Counties. During an undercover controlled purchase in December 2023, Curtis sold an undercover officer nearly half a kilogram of methamphetamine. During a second controlled purchase in January 2024, the undercover officer purchased from Curtis approximately a kilogram of methamphetamine. In August 2024, officers with the Burke County Sheriff’s Office conducted a traffic stop on Curtis’s vehicle. During a subsequent search of the vehicle, the deputies located approximately 1.2 kilograms of methamphetamine inside the vehicle.

In October 2025, Curtis pleaded guilty to distribution of methamphetamine and aiding and abetting.

This investigation was led by Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and the Burke County Sheriff’s Office.

Assistant U.S. Attorney William Wiseman of the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Charlotte prosecuted the case.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.
title: Judge Sentences Morganton Methamphetamine Trafficker to Over 17 Years

FORT SMITH – A Van Buren man was sentenced to 240 months in federal prison to be followed by lifetime supervised release after being convicted for Online Enticement of a Minor in violation of federal law. The Honorable John Thomas Shepherd presided over the October 5, 2026, sentencing hearing, which was held in the U.S. District Court in Fort Smith.

According to court documents, Brian Fay Jeremiah , age 66, a twice-convicted sex offender, messaged an online covert employee with the Federal Bureau of Investigation who was posing as a fourteen-year-old female. During the online conversations, Jeremiah asked the purported fourteen-year-old to create and send him sexually explicit images and to engage in sexually explicit video chats with him. Jeremiah was previously convicted and served prison time for similar offenses in the Western District of Arkansas in 2003 and in Colorado in 2015. Jeremiah was indicted by a Grand Jury in the Western District of Arkansas in December of 2025 and entered a plea of guilty in May of 2026.

"This sentence underscores our unwavering commitment to protecting children from those who repeatedly seek to exploit them," United States Attorney Kevin R. Holmes of the Western District of Arkansas said in making the announcement. "The defendant’s conduct represents a grave and ongoing threat, and our office will not hesitate to use every tool available to remove offenders like him from our communities. We will continue working with our state, local and federal partners to ensure that those who target our children face swift and uncompromising justice," Holmes added. Assistant United States Attorney Devon Still prosecuted the case on behalf of the United States.

“Protecting the children of Arkansas is one of the FBI’s highest priorities, and we remain committed to working alongside our federal, state, and local law enforcement partners to hold those who target children accountable for their crimes,” said FBI Little Rock Special Agent in Charge Jason Van Goor. “Predators who seek to exploit our children have no place in our communities, and we will use every resource available to identify these offenders and bring them to justice.”

The Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Van Buren Police Department, and the Arkansas State Police investigated the case.

This case was prosecuted as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc .

Related court documents may be found on the Public Access to Electronic Records website at www.pacer.gov .

Czerniak was arrested this morning and will make an initial appearance in federal court in the Western District of Arkansas later today. He will appear in federal court in Boston at a later date.

“Threats of violence against elected officials are not protected speech. They are federal crimes,” said United States Attorney Leah B. Foley. “We will not tolerate behavior intended to terrorize public officials, their families or their communities. We take all threats extremely seriously. If you make them, we will find you – and we will hold you accountable.”

“Threats of violence against elected officials are not protected speech. They are federal crimes,” said United States Attorney Leah B. Foley. “We will not tolerate behavior intended to terrorize public officials, their families or their communities. We take all threats extremely seriously. If you make them, we will find you – and we will hold you accountable.”

Today, the FBI arrested David Czerniak whose rhetoric crossed the line into alleged criminal conduct,” said Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Boston Division. “We urge everyone to engage respectfully, recognize the legitimacy of differing viewpoints, and uphold the principles that allow our democratic process to function safely and effectively because the FBI and our partners will not tolerate attempts to intimidate, coerce, or endanger anyone.”

SIOUX FALLS - United States Attorney Ron Parsons announced today that Chief Judge Roberto A. Lange, U.S. District Court has sentenced a Sioux Falls, South Dakota, man convicted of Possession of a Controlled Substance with Intent to Distribute. The sentencing took place on October 5, 2026.

Bryan Bruins, 24, was sentenced to 22 years in federal prison, followed by five years of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund.

Bruins was indicted for Possession of a Controlled Substance with Intent to Distribute by a federal grand jury in April 2026. He pleaded guilty on July 20, 2026.

Sioux Falls Police Officers responded to a report of an overdose at an apartment rented by Bryan Bruins in Sioux Falls. They later searched the apartment and discovered approximately two pounds of methamphetamine and a stolen pistol. Investigators found text messages on Bruins’ phone that showed he had been distributing methamphetamine in Sioux Falls. Bruins was on parole at the time the methamphetamine was found in his apartment.

This case was investigated by U.S. Postal Investigation Service and the Sioux Falls Area Drug Task Force. Assistant U.S. Attorney Mark Hodges prosecuted the case.

Bruins was immediately remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service.

Tallahassee, Florida – J’Shawn Tikariyon Walker, 21, of Tallahassee, Florida, pleaded guilty in federal court to illegal possession of a machinegun and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. The plea was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida.

U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “I applaud the excellent investigative work by Customs and Border Protection agents to thwart this repeat offender’s attempt to acquire machinegun conversion devices from China. The fact that he was already under federal supervision for a prior weapons conviction amply demonstrates that he has no intention to lead a law-abiding life and he must be incarcerated to keep our community safe.”

Court documents reflect that Department of Homeland Security Customs and Border Protection intercepted a package from China addressed to “Jay Walk” at the defendant’s residence. When inspected, the package was found to contain three Glock machinegun conversion devices (MCDs). The defendant was on federal supervised release at the time for charges that included illegal possession of a Glock machinegun. On August 7, 2026, Homeland Security Investigations executed a search warrant at the defendant’s residence and found a Glock 19 that had been converted into a machinegun in a shoebox in the defendant’s bedroom. The defendant admitted to ordering an MCD, commonly called a “Glock switch,” from China, and further admitted ownership of the converted Glock machinegun found in his bedroom.

The defendant was prohibited from possessing firearms based on his prior federal felony convictions, which involved the theft of multiple firearms from gun stores and the illegal possession of a machinegun. The defendant had been sentenced to 18 months in prison and was on supervised release at the time of the instant offense.

The defendant faces up to 25 years’ imprisonment.

Sentencing is scheduled for December 9, 2026, at 3:00 pm, in the United States Courthouse in Tallahassee before United States District Judge Mark E. Walker.

The case involved an investigation by Homeland Security Investigations, with assistance from Department of Homeland Security Customs and Border Protection and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney James A. McCain.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities .

The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl .

FLORENCE, S.C. — Alando Gentles, 43, of Jamaica, has been sentenced to three years in federal prison for wire fraud conspiracy involving a telemarketing lottery scam targeting elderly victims. Investigators with Homeland Security Investigations and the United States Postal Inspection Service learned that individuals in Myrtle Beach, were operating a cash award/lottery telemarketing scam with domestic and international connections, targeted at elderly victims, that occurred from around June 2015 until around May 2022. The investigation revealed the scheme involved a total of at least 115 victims. The investigation identified Alando Gentles as an individual who participated in the scheme in Jamaica. As part of the scheme, Gentles and co-conspirators contacted elderly victims via phone and mail and falsely informed the victims they were the winner of a sweepstakes. Gentles and co-conspirators then told the victims they must pay taxes and fees to claim or receive their winnings. The victims then purchased prepaid cards, USPS money orders, and bank money orders; mailed cash or personal checks; made deposits into co-conspirator’s bank accounts; or sent wire transfers to co-conspirator’s bank accounts. In addition to calling victims, Gentles received wire transfers of funds obtained from the scheme in Jamaica and made ATM withdrawals in Jamaica from an account containing funds obtained from the scheme. Following his indictment, Gentles was extradited from Jamaica for federal prosecution. Chief United States District Judge Sherri A. Lydon sentenced Gentles to 36 months’ imprisonment, to be followed by a three-year term of court-ordered supervision. There is no parole in the federal system. The Court also ordered Gentles to pay $349,433.75 in restitution to the victims of his crime. This case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations and the United States Postal Inspection Service. Assistant U.S. Attorney Lauren Hummel prosecuted the case.

###
title: Jamaican National Sentenced to Federal Prison for Role in Telemarketing Lottery Scam Targeting Elderly Victims

Elfreth Leads Colleagues in Urging $11 Million in Additional Funding for Mental Health Support at Cyber Command Following Suicides
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth (D-MD-03), a member of the House Armed Services Committee, led her colleagues on the Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation (CITI) Subcommittee of the House Armed Services Committee and the Maryland Delegation in requesting an additional $11 million in funding for mental health support at U.S. Cyber Command following reports of multiple suicides earlier this year. On the letter from the CITI members, Elfreth was joined by Representatives Don Bacon (R-NE-02), Ro Khanna (D-CA-17), Rich McCormick (R-GA-07), Chrissy Houlahan (D-PA-06), Herbert Conaway (D-NJ-03), Eugene Vindman (D-VA-07), and Pat Ryan (D-NY-18). On the letter from the Maryland members, Elfreth was joined by her Maryland delegation colleagues, including Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), who co-led the letter, along with Senator Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), and Representatives Steny Hoyer (D-MD-05), Kweisi Mfume (D-MD-07), Jamie Raskin (D-MD-08), Glenn Ivey (D-MD-04), Johnny Olszewski (D-MD-02), and April McClain Delaney (D-MD-06). Both letters were directed to the heads of the House and Senate Appropriations Committees.
“We respectfully urge you to retain the $11 million program increase for U.S. Cyber Command high-performance team training… Headquartered at Fort George G. Meade, U.S. Cyber Command is central to Maryland’s national security community and relies on service members, civilian employees, and families throughout our state to conduct some of the Nation’s most demanding and persistent missions,” wrote the CITI members.
“As the Congressional Delegation of Maryland, we are troubled by recent public reporting describing several deaths by suicide among personnel in cyber operations and the Fort Meade community over a short period. These deaths have a severe impact on the family, friends, and wider community. The concentration of these tragedies within a small, highly specialized workforce demands sustained attention and an institutional response proportionate to the operational strain these personnel bear,” wrote the Maryland lawmakers. “Cyber personnel operate in a uniquely stressful environment. Many are effectively ‘deployed in place’ for two- or three-year assignments, conducting real-world operations against capable adversaries without the clear start and end points, protected recovery periods, or unit-level reconstitution cycles associated with conventional deployments. Because much of their work is classified, they may be unable to discuss the sources of their stress with family members or medical professionals who lack the clearances or access to secure facilities necessary for a complete conversation. These conditions can isolate personnel, delay appropriate care, and ultimately weaken readiness, retention, and operational effectiveness.”
“One loss of life is one too many. We must do everything we can to make sure our servicemembers and everyone at NSA and Cyber Command has the full mental health support and resources they need, so that a tragedy like this does not occur again,” wrote the CITI members.
In last year’s National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), Elfreth specifically secured a provision, H.R. 6630, the Expanding Mental Health Access for Cyber Command Personnel Act (Sec. 1506), requiring U.S. Cyber Command and the Cyber Mission Force to hire mental health professionals with security clearances at each of their operating locations. The amendment also requires quarterly briefings on the status of the initiative, validating the clearances, challenges carrying out the initiative, and efforts to improve awareness among troops regarding the cleared physicians. The $11 million in funding would ensure full funding of this provision.
Elfreth continues to work alongside U.S. Cyber Command to bring additional mental health resources to Fort Meade. Elfreth is working to rectify the reporting requirements and include civilian employees in DoD’s suicide data, especially at installations like Fort Meade where civilian and uniformed officers work side by side on the same projects.
Elfreth is also working to address delays with the transfer of mental health licenses from out of state. During conversations with mental health professionals, Elfreth heard that the transfer of licenses can take several months to almost a year before these professionals can begin practicing in Maryland and on military bases. At the state level, she is working with partners, including Senator Dawn Gile and Secretary Ed Rothstein of the Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families, to address delays and barriers to military-connected mental health professionals transferring or obtaining professional licensure in Maryland.
The full CITI letter can be accessed HERE. The full Maryland letter can be accessed HERE.

title: Elfreth Leads Colleagues in Urging $11 Million in Additional Funding for Mental Health Support at Cyber Command Following Suicides

Washington, DC – Today, Congresswoman Julia Brownley (CA-26) joined 189 Members of Congress in demanding that the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) withdraw its proposal to remove more than 90 percent of Head Start’s standards that ensure children receive a high-quality early education. Under the proposed rule, nearly one in ten children currently enrolled in Head Start could become ineligible overnight.
In the House, the letter is led by Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (D-VA-03), House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY-08), Early Childhood and Elementary and Secondary Education Subcommittee Ranking Member Bonamici (D-OR-01), and Representative Nikki Budzinski (D-IL-13). In the Senate, the letter is led by Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee Ranking Member Sanders (I-VT), Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Senator Raphael Warnock (D-GA), and Senator Ben RayLuján (D-NM).
The Members are concerned that the proposed rule would illegally modify and weaken the services required by the Head Start Act. Specifically, the rule would eliminate federal quality standards for Head Start classrooms, including safety standards, staff-to-child ratios, staff qualifications, and standards for teaching. Additionally, the rule would erode critical services Head Start provides children and families, including health services. It would also shorten Head Start operating hours, eliminate enrollment protections for children with disabilities, and undermine services for dual language learners.
“This proposed rule is a brazen attempt to dismantle Head Start without regard for the hundreds of thousands of young children and working-class families who depend on these programs and services every year. Under your proposal, Head Start children could be subject to corporal punishment; left unsupervised; have larger class sizes; have less qualified teachers; and no longer receive preventative and continuous health services, including oral health and mental health services,” wrote the Members. “We strongly urge you to withdraw the proposed rule, obey the law, and protect the legacy of Head Start.”
Since the beginning of the second Trump Administration, HHS has repeatedly attempted to undermine and disrupt Head Start programs with an aggressive deregulation agenda, illegally withholding funding, firing federal staff, and threats to eliminate the program entirely. These actions serve the Trump Administration’s goal to end the Head Start program as laid out on page 482 of Project 2025.

Representative John W. Mannion Announces $500,000 Federal Grant for Brownfield Cleanups and Infrastructure Investments in the City of Utica
UTICA, N.Y. – Representative John W. Mannion today announced that the City of Utica will receive $500,000 in federal funding to support environmental cleanup projects and infrastructure initiatives. 
Representative John W. Mannion said, “This funding will provide the City of Utica with additional resources to turn vacant sites into safe, productive spaces. This brownfield grant will protect public health, create new opportunities for growth, and strengthen our neighborhoods. I will continue working with our local leaders to ensure our communities get the support they deserve, and I look forward to seeing this project drive lasting change in the region.” 
The City of Utica will use the award to conduct assessments, cleanups, and revitalize polluted brownfield areas. These investments will support the local economy, support redevelopment, and protect public health for Utica residents. Utica plans to conduct over a dozen site assessments and hold almost 20 community meetings throughout the process. 
The funding was awarded by the Environmental Protection Agency through the Brownfields Multipurpose, Assessment, Revolving Loan Fund, and Cleanup Cooperative Agreements. The program provides federal resources to address sites contaminated by hazardous substances, pollutants, or contaminants and petroleum. 
# # #

ST. GEORGE , Utah – A Weber County, Utah, man was sentenced to 120 months’ imprisonment today after he manipulated a child into taking sexually explicit photos and videos and sending them to him over the course of six months.

The sentence, imposed by U.S. District Court Judge Ann Marie McIff Allen, comes after Tyler Justin Pitt, 28, of Ogden, Utah, pleaded guilty on February 23, 2026, to coercion and enticement, and receipt of child pornography. In addition to his term of imprisonment, he was sentenced to a lifetime of supervised release.

According to court documents and statements made at Pitt’s change of plea and sentencing hearings, between January 2024 and July 2024 Pitt systematically groomed and exploited a child he met on Snapchat to produce child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and send to him. In many of Pitt’s messages to the victim, he discussed his intention to sexually abuse the victim and repeatedly asked the victim for nude photos and videos. Pitt also sent nude photos and videos of himself to the victim.

On August 28, 2024, a search warrant was executed on Pitt’s residence. During the search, law enforcement seized Pitt’s electronic devices, including his iPhone and found his communication with the victim. Based on Pitt’s phone contents, Pitt’s interaction with the victim was not a singular incident but instead part of a larger pattern of child exploitation offenses. Law enforcement found additional exchanged images and videos with numerous females. In addition to Snapchat, Pitt used Omegle, WhatsApp, and Discord to exchange these messages and videos. Pitt’s cellphone also had 22 images of child sexual abuse material, not depicting the victim, which he appeared to receive over X/Twitter. These sexually explicit photos of minors included depictions of prepubescent children. Pitt’s phone also included multiple search terms indicative of child sexual abuse material.

“My office’s priority, along with this administration, is the safety of our communities, especially children, and to remove child predators like Pitt from society,” said U.S. Attorney Melissa Holyoak of the District of Utah. “Anyone who preys on the most vulnerable among us will be investigated by our federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement partners and aggressively prosecuted.”

“My office’s priority, along with this administration, is the safety of our communities, especially children, and to remove child predators like Pitt from society,” said U.S. Attorney Melissa Holyoak of the District of Utah. “Anyone who preys on the most vulnerable among us will be investigated by our federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement partners and aggressively prosecuted.”

“Children deserve to grow up safe. In this case, a child will have to carry the lasting impact of Mr. Pitt’s actions,” said Special Agent in Charge Robert Bohls of the Salt Lake City FBI. “The FBI and our partners will use every available resource to protect children and pursue those who try to exploit them."

“Children deserve to grow up safe. In this case, a child will have to carry the lasting impact of Mr. Pitt’s actions,” said Special Agent in Charge Robert Bohls of the Salt Lake City FBI. “The FBI and our partners will use every available resource to protect children and pursue those who try to exploit them."

The case was investigated jointly by the St. George City Police Department, Washington County Sheriff’s Office, and the FBI Salt Lake City Field Office, St. George Resident Agency.

Assistant United States Attorney Christopher Burton of The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Utah prosecuted the case.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC .

Media Note

Office of the Spokesman

October 7, 2026

The following is the text of a joint statement by the United States of America and the Hellenic Republic on the occasion of the sixth U.S.-Greece Strategic Dialogue.

Begin text:

On October 7, 2026, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Greek Minister of Foreign Affairs George Gerapetritis presided over the 6th round of the U.S.-Greece Strategic Dialogue and held discussions on a wide area of global issues. The two sides reaffirmed their steadfast, long and deep bilateral relations in the context of shared democratic values and Greece’s role as an active NATO ally. Anchoring their discussions in shared priorities, both sides committed to deepen defense ties, bolster trade and investment, and promote cultural ties.

DEFENSE AND SECURITY COOPERATION

Greece and the United States reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthen their longstanding defense and security cooperation. The United States and Greece announced $4 billion in Foreign Military Sales in support of Greece’s long-term defense plan to deepen our interoperability, and to explore future opportunities for defense industrial base cooperation, including on innovative technologies. They finalized Greece’s participation in the U.S. National Guard Bureau’s State Partnership Program with Florida, and enhanced interoperability through the provision of Stryker vehicles to Greece. Both sides reaffirmed the strategic value of our defense cooperation in support of bilateral and NATO security objectives. They expanded law enforcement and counterterrorism cooperation and reaffirmed their commitment to address illegal migration.

ECONOMIC AND TRADE COOPERATION

Greece and the United States reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening two-way trade and investment. They recognized the importance of economic security and intend to partner to strengthen investment screening and protect critical infrastructure procurements. With Greece’s status as a Pax Silica signatory, the two sides welcomed growing cooperation in super intelligence, high-performance computing, cybersecurity, and advanced technologies. They highlighted deepening energy ties, building on the November 2025 P-TEC ministerial, the Vertical Gas Corridor, and hydrocarbon exploration. They underscored the significance of maritime collaboration and signed an agreement on certification for U.S. seafarers on Greek vessels.

CULTURAL TIES

The governments also signed an extension of their Cultural Property Agreement, reaffirming their commitment to protect cultural heritage and combat illicit trafficking networks. In addition, they announced the United States’ first project in Greece under the Ambassadors Fund for Cultural Preservation to highlight shared democratic traditions.

End Text.

WASHINGTON, D.C.— As the Trump Administration prepares propaganda signage to adorn the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History, Representative Jamie Raskin (MD-08) introduced legislation to ensure future generations learn about President Donald Trump’s commitment to censoring, whitewashing and fictionalizing American history. The Preserving and Remembering the History of Trump and other Tyrants Act directs officials from the Smithsonian Institution to collect and preserve artifacts reflecting the rise of governmental propaganda, corruption, and authoritarianism during the Trump presidencies as the basis for a permanent exhibition in the National Museum of American History.
Last month, the Department of the Interior—under orders from President Trump—created propaganda signage to place outside of the National Museum of American History, warning visitors of curators’ “personal, radical ideologies.” Preserving these signs will educate Americans on how authoritarians attempt to control media, government and culture.
“Unlike President Trump’s project of censoring, whitewashing and fictionalizing American history, my legislation will forever preserve his manifestations of authoritarian narcissism and his propagandistic assault on American history and American democracy,” said Rep. Raskin. “To avoid repeating this descent into authoritarianism, we must study this corrupt President’s actions and allow the public to learn about the numerous tools he deployed while attempting to remake American history in his own image and according to his own autocratic and white nationalist beliefs.”
The legislation directs officials from the Smithsonian Institution to preserve the banners bearing President Trump’s face that are currently displayed outside of certain federal agencies; still images and videos from the media; personal narratives of American citizens who resisted and opposed the rise in authoritarianism in the United States; and other artifacts that the Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution determines to have historical significance. The legislation also directs officials from the National Park Service to remove any signage that was erected near the National Museum of American History without the consent of Congress.
Rep. Raskin has drawn on his expertise as an American constitutional scholar as he speaks out against the Trump Administration’s authoritarian tactics. This month, he introduced a Resolution condemning President Trump and MAGA’s campaign of book bans and censorship and advocating for the American freedom to read and think freely.

NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA – LEVIN YULIEN ESCOTO-SOLIS (“ESCOTO-SOLIS”), age 38, a Honduran national, was indicted on October 2, 2026, for illegal reentry of a removed alien, in violation of Title 8, United States Code, Sections 1326(a) & (b)(1), announced U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle.

According to the indictment, on or about September 15, 2026, in the Eastern District of Louisiana, ESCOTO-SOLIS , an alien, was found in the United States after having been deported and removed therefrom on or about April 13, 2012, without the approval of the Attorney General of the United States or his designated successor, the Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security, having expressly consented to the defendant’s reapplication for admission into the United States.

If convicted, ESCOTO-SOLIS faces a maximum penalty of up to ten (10) years of imprisonment, up to a $250,000 fine, up to three (3) years of supervised release, and a $100 mandatory special assessment fee.

U.S. Attorney Courcelle reiterated that an indictment is merely a charge and that the guilt of the defendant must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt.

U.S. Attorney Courcelle praised the work of the Department of Homeland Security and United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement, in investigating this matter. Assistant United States Attorney Lorcan L. Connick of the General Crimes Unit is handling the prosecution.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

Congresswoman Simon, Colleagues Introduce Bipartisan Resolution Honoring Landmark Olmstead Court Decision Supporting Americans with Disabilities on 27th Anniversary
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Simon (CA-12) alongside Reps. Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06), Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA-01), Mary Gay Scanlon (D-PA-05), Mike Lawler (R-NY-17), and Tom Kean (R-NJ-07) introduced a bipartisan resolution commemorating the 27th anniversary of the landmark Supreme Court decision, Olmstead v. L.C.. The Olmstead decision prohibits the unnecessary institutionalization of people with disabilities and ensures Americans with disabilities can live full, independent lives and categorized the unjustified institutionalization of people with disabilities as discrimination under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). As the Olmstead decision comes under attack from the Trump Administration, this bipartisan resolution reaffirms the right that people with disabilities have to live, work, and participate in their own homes and communities with independence and dignity.
As the first congenitally blind Member of Congress, Congresswoman Simon is committed to defending the disability community from attacks by the Trump Administration and advancing policies that expand accessibility. Congresswoman Simon recently condemned the Trump Administration’s Department of Justice and Department of Health and Human Services’ move to dispute the Olmstead integration mandate and undermine the key protections outlined by the Olmstead decision.
"Community-based services and supports work. They are more cost-effective, produce better health and quality-of-life outcomes, and honor people with disabilities’ autonomy and self-determination. The consequences of weakening the integration mandate would be profound and impact millions of Americans’ ability to access home and community-based services that allow them to remain among their families, maintain employment, pursue education, and participate in civic life," said Congresswoman Simon. "That's why as the first congenitally blind Member to serve in Congress, I am proud to join my colleagues to reaffirm our bipartisan commitment to the Olmstead decision and fight any attempts to diminish the civil rights of the disability community."
"It is essential that people with disabilities continue to have the right to live, work, and thrive in their own communities with dignity," said Congresswoman Dingell. "This bipartisan resolution reaffirms that we will not allow hard won progress to be rolled back, and that we will continue to protect and support the rights enshrined by the Olmstead decision for every person whose lives it has changed for the better."
"Although the Olmstead decision was issued more than twenty‑five years ago, its significance remains just as strong today. I am pleased to join my colleagues in introducing this resolution, reaffirming our commitment to ending discrimination based on disability," said Congressman Kean.
"For 27 years, the Supreme Court’s decision in Olmstead v. L.C. has informed the advancement of policies to empower individuals with disabilities to live and work independently in our communities," said Congresswoman Scanlon. "Recent attempts to undermine the Olmstead integration mandate and roll back those policies raises new opportunities for discrimination against our friends and neighbors with disabilities, and harms the larger community. I’m proud to join my House colleagues in recognizing Olmstead’s anniversary and recommitting ourselves to protecting community integration for the good of all."
"Olmstead affirmed a fundamental principle: every American deserves the freedom and opportunity to build a full life in the community they call home. As Co-Chair of the Bipartisan Disabilities Caucus, that principle has always been at the heart of my work to break down barriers, strengthen independence, and ensure all Americans with disabilities have the resources, support, and opportunities they need to thrive. Twenty-seven years later, our responsibility is not simply to recognize the progress Olmstead made possible, but to protect it, build upon it, and ensure that progress is never reversed," said Congressman Fitzpatrick.
The resolution is endorsed by the Caring Across Generations, United Spinal, ANCOR, Autism Self Advocacy Network, National Council on Independent Living, American Association of People with Disabilities, and the National Disability Rights Network.
A copy of the resolution can be found HERE.

Developed as a Partnership Between Wichita Northwest High School Students and the Drug Free Communities Support Program
WICHITA, KS – Today, the Director of the Office of National Drug Control Policy, or “Drug Czar,” Sara Carter and Senator Roger Marshall (R-KS) announced a new partnership between the Drug Free Communities Support (DFC) program and Wichita Northwest High School to develop the first youth-led primary prevention toolkit. This toolkit will guide primary prevention efforts throughout the nation by providing evidence-based best practices recommendations adapted to the best suit today’s youth. The toolkit is expected to be released around the back-to-school season in 2027.
“The DFC program has been successful because it empowers local leaders- those who know their communities best- with federal resources to make a difference in the lives of countless young Americans. Among those leaders, and some of our most powerful advocates, are youth themselves,” said Drug Czar Sara Carter. “The students developing this toolkit know better than anyone the pressures their peers face, and how to best overcome them. I look forward to the release of their work.”
“We don’t want the next generation to inherit the drug crisis we are fighting today. We need to empower young people to take this crisis on head-on because they know what their friends and classmates are facing,” said Senator Marshall. “I appreciate Director Carter and ONDCP for putting young people at the center of this effort and giving them the tools to lead. It’s great to see a Kansas school setting an example and empowering students to take ownership in this fight.”
“We are excited that students of our district were selected to help create this national toolkit, giving young people a voice in shaping youth engagement efforts nationwide,” said Superintendent Kelly Bielefeld.
Primary prevention is a cornerstone of President Donald J. Trump’s 2026 National Drug Control Strategy, which governs the Administration’s approach to defeating the drug crisis. This latest partnership comes as the most recent reports indicate drug use among students is now at a near-record low, now the lowest since 1992 and the second-lowest since reporting began.
The White House Office of National Drug Control leads and coordinates U.S. drug policy, develops and implements the President’s the National Drug Control Strategy, and supports communities through the Drug Free Communities Support (DFC) and High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (HIDTA) programs.
title: Drug Czar Sara Carter, Senator Roger Marshall Announce First Ever Youth-led Primary Prevention Toolkit
