text:
BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
A PROCLAMATION
More than five centuries ago, Christopher Columbus embarked westward across uncharted waters and discovered the New World — bringing with him the rich traditions of Western civilization and paving the way to the birth of the American Nation less than three centuries later. Today, we honor his life of valor, adventure, and ingenuity. We cherish his memory and pledge to safeguard his story. Above all, we remember with gratitude that the triumph of freedom and the glory of our Republic are the fruits of his faith and unrelenting devotion.
In August of 1492, Columbus departed the shores of Spain to chart a new trade route to Asia. With his crew of about 90 men aboard the Niña, the Pinta, and the Santa María, for more than 2 grueling months, he pressed onward across the vast and unforgiving Atlantic Ocean — braving violent storms and treacherous waters. Through every trial, Columbus never wavered, holding his crew to the mission when most others would have turned back.
When Columbus and his crew made landfall on the islands of the present-day Bahamas, they first believed they had reached the shores of Asia. Instead, their voyage redrew the map of human possibility and opened a new chapter in the history of exploration. They unleashed a bold new age of discovery that expanded the horizons of knowledge, carried the splendors of the Western world across an ocean, and set in motion the forces that would culminate in the miracle of July 4, 1776. When they arrived, as a sign of devotion to God and respect to Ferdinand and Isabella of Spain, Columbus raised a mighty cross in the newly discovered land as a sign that “Your Highnesses hold this land for your own, but chiefly as a sign of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Ever since, this spirit of adventure has coursed through the veins of generations of patriots — from the brave settlers who established the first colonial foothold at Jamestown to the daring pioneers who pushed westward and tamed the frontier.
Today, we reaffirm that Christopher Columbus is a legend whose vision, fortitude, and perseverance unleashed a dynamic of history that led to the creation of the greatest, freest, and most just Nation in history. We are forever indebted to his courageous voyage, and we will never allow his legacy to be erased by radical extremists. For this reason, earlier this year, I was proud to install a statue of Christopher Columbus on the White House grounds — an exact replica of the statue that stood for more than three decades in Baltimore, Maryland, from its dedication by President Ronald Reagan in October 1984 until rioters tore it down and threw it into Baltimore Harbor on July 4, 2020. Now placed at the White House, this magnificent monument stands as a testament to the resilient legacy of one of history’s greatest heroes.
Columbus Day also holds special significance for our incredible Italian-American citizens. Like Columbus, they have embodied a steadfast love of country and faith in God, and they continue to strengthen our communities and propel our country to even greater heights.
In 1892, on the occasion of the 400th anniversary of Columbus’ epic voyage, Pope Leo XIII published an encyclical hailing “the greatness of his mind and heart,” which “can be compared to but few in the history of humanity.” The Pope continued: Columbus “looked for a something greater and higher than did these others.” Today, as we celebrate the anniversary of Christopher Columbus’ arrival in the New World, we honor his unrivaled greatness. We embrace our duty to prove worthy of the inheritance he left us, to match his courage with our own, and to never abandon, forsake, or forget the beauty of our faith, the glories of our culture, and the stories of our heroes.
In commemoration of Christopher Columbus’ historic voyage, the Congress, by joint resolution of April 30, 1934, and modified in 1968 (36 U.S.C. 107), as amended, has requested the President proclaim the second Monday of October of each year as “Columbus Day.”
NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, do hereby proclaim October 12, 2026, as Columbus Day. I call upon the people of the United States to observe this day with appropriate ceremonies and activities. I also direct that the flag of the United States be displayed on all public buildings on the appointed day in honor of the great Christopher Columbus and all who have contributed to building our Nation.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this seventh day of October, in the year of our Lord two thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the United States of America the two hundred and fifty-first.
DONALD J. TRUMP
title: Columbus Day, 2026

ALEXANDRIA, Va. – The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia, in partnership with the FBI Washington Field Office and the Cybercrime Division of France’s Parquet de Paris, announced today the seizure of two websites as part of a coordinated law enforcement action taken against the dissemination of child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and the non-consensual publication of intimate images.

According to the seizure warrant, the United States obtained court authorization to seize two domains associated with NudeLeaksTeens (NLT), which advertised for sale leaked ( i.e., hacked and stolen), sexually explicit images and videos depicting young women and girls. Law enforcement’s investigation of NLT revealed that despite website warnings against CSAM, the site also offered for sale sexually explicit images and videos of children.

NLT advertised and sold its content in “albums” and “collections.” While the content of albums and collections varied, many included personal identifying information of victims, pictures of victims in various stages of undress, and pictures of victims engaged in sexually explicit conduct. Some of the victims have been identified and confirmed to be minors at the time the visual depictions were created. NLT also advertised a collection named for the website, “Nudeleaksteens Collection,” which it boasted contained “6200 private nude files leaked of teenagers or adults (mostly American) from hacked snapchats, Instagram, tiktok, facebook accounts[.]” This collection also contained CSAM.

French law enforcement simultaneously arrested a 25-year-old man living in Northern France who is suspected to have been the main administrator of NLT.

Theophani K. Stamos, First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia; Darren Cox, Assistant Director in Charge of the FBI Washington Field Office; and Charles “Andy” Penn, Arlington County Chief of Police, made the announcement.

The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs provided significant assistance.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys April Russo, Lauren Halper, and Meredith Clement are representing the United States.

Victims of the non-consensual publication of intimate images on NLT or elsewhere online are encouraged to file a report with the FBI at ncii.ic3.gov.
title: International law enforcement operation leads to seizure of websites used to traffic child sexual abuse material and non-consensual intimate images

BROOKLYN, NY – Earlier today, Zohar Pinhasi, also known as “Zack Silver” and “Zack Green,” was arraigned on wire fraud charges for allegedly defrauding clients of his ransomware remediation company, MonsterCloud LLC (MonsterCloud). Pinhasi, a national of the United States and Israel, was indicted by a grand jury in the Eastern District of New York on September 23, 2026. The proceeding was held in federal court in Brooklyn before United States Magistrate Judge Peggy Cross‑Goldenberg.

Joseph Nocella, Jr., United States Attorney for the Eastern District of New York; A. Tysen Duva, Assistant Attorney General, head of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division; and James C. Barnacle, Jr., Assistant Director in Charge, Federal Bureau of Investigation, New York Field Office (FBI), announced the charges.

“As alleged in the indictment, by falsely claiming to decrypt ransomware without paying off the ransomers, the defendant re-victimized his clients while extracting a hefty profit for himself,” stated United States Attorney Nocella. “Our Office will vigorously prosecute ransomware attackers who prey on Americans from across the world and those who cynically profit from their criminal activity.” Mr. Nocella thanked the Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs for its assistance.

“The defendant is charged with offering an alternative to ransom payments, but instead is alleged to have victimized the victim again and committed additional fraud, harming the victim again,” stated Assistant Attorney General Duva. “This prosecution underscores the Department’s commitment to protecting ransomware victims, regardless of how these cyber ransoms occur.”

"As alleged, Zohar Pinhasi claimed to fix ransomware while never remediating the underlying threat. Instead, he turned the victim's crisis into his own profit center. This deception is unacceptable, and the FBI is committed to ensuring accountability for those who choose to victimize the very people who trusted them for help," stated FBI Assistant Director in Charge Barnacle.

The charges relate to Pinhasi’s claimed ability to decrypt ransomware without paying cybercriminals, purportedly using “proprietary tools” and “advanced decryption techniques” on behalf of distressed business owners who came to his company, MonsterCloud, for help after being victimized by cybercriminals. In fact, Pinhasi allegedly used a portion of his clients’ fees to pay off the ransomware attackers, and then kept the rest, often extracting a substantial markup. As alleged in the indictment, Pinhasi claimed to prospective clients that MonsterCloud offered a principled alternative to paying off ransomware attackers. MonsterCloud’s website cautioned clients not to pay the ransom, and proclaimed that “our team specializes in helping businesses recover their data without succumbing to ransom demands.” MonsterCloud supposedly did this using “advanced decryption techniques and cutting-edge technology.”

Instead, as alleged, Pinhasi had no special technology to decrypt data. Rather, Pinhasi contacted and paid the cybercriminals who had victimized MonsterCloud’s client, in exchange for a decryption key that MonsterCloud employees then used in an attempt to decrypt the client’s files. Pinhasi typically charged MonsterCloud’s clients a fee that was substantially higher than the ransom that MonsterCloud secretly paid. For example, in August 2023, Pinhasi made a ransom payment of approximately $8,200 to a cybercriminal and charged the client approximately $150,000.

MonsterCloud’s website included “testimonials,” including some from paid spokespersons. As alleged, in May 2019, one such spokesperson contacted Pinhasi to ask whether MonsterCloud truly had any proprietary software to decrypt encrypted data. Pinhasi responded: “Monstercloud doesn’t hold any Proprietary technology [to] decrypt the ransomware data.”

Over the course of the scheme, Pinhasi allegedly charged clients more than $19 million, and paid more than $8 million in ransom payments.

The charges in the indictment are allegations, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. If convicted, the defendant faces a maximum sentence of up to 20 years in prison.

The government’s case is being handled by the Office’s National Security and Cybercrime Section. Assistant United States Attorneys Alexander Mindlin and Lindsey Oken are in charge of the case, along with Senior Trial Attorneys Brian Mund and Vasantha Rao of the Department of Justice’s Computer Crimes and Intellectual Property Section. Assistant United States Attorney Laura Mantell is handling forfeiture matters.

The Defendant :

ZOHAR PINHASI (also known as “Zack Silver” and “Zack Green’) Age: 50 Hollywood, Florida

E.D.N.Y. Docket No. 26-CR-271 (RER)
title: Owner of Florida Ransomware Remediation Company Charged with Defrauding Clients

RAPID CITY - United States Attorney Ron Parsons announced today that U.S. District Judge Camela C. Theeler has sentenced a Box Elder, South Dakota, man convicted of Receipt of Child Pornography. The sentencing took place on October 5, 2026.

Zachary Wylie, 20, was sentenced to five years in federal prison, followed by five years of supervised release, and ordered to pay $95 in restitution and a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund. Forfeiture of a Google Pixel cell phone was also ordered.

Wylie was indicted for the charge by a federal grand jury in March 2025. He pleaded guilty on June 29, 2026.

Between June and December 2024, the internet-based messaging application Kik generated multiple CyberTips based on Wylie’s viewing, downloading, and receiving sexually explicit visual depictions of minors. The CyberTips were routed to the South Dakota Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force for investigation. Each of the CyberTips contained information identifying Wylie as the user of each of the relevant Kik accounts. In January 2025, law enforcement investigators executed a search warrant on Wylie’s residence and seized multiple electronic devices. Wylie admitted he had been viewing child pornography online for many years and was doing so right before law enforcement arrived at his residence. The contents of his Kik accounts contained more than 30 videos of child pornography. They also contained messages in which Wylie discussed trading child pornography and encouraging minors to engage in sexually explicit activity over video chats so he could watch them.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse, launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the DOJ’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children, as well as identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc .

This case was investigated by the South Dakota Division of Criminal Investigation’s Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Task Force, the Box Elder Police Department, and the Pennington County Sheriff’s Office. Former Assistant U.S. Attorney Heather Knox prosecuted the case.

Wylie was immediately remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service.
title: Box Elder Man Sentenced to Five Years in Federal Prison for Receiving Child Pornography

Athens, Greece

October 7, 2026

FOREIGN MINISTER GERAPETRITIS: Dear Secretary, dear colleagues, it is a great pleasure to welcome and your delegation to Athens for the sixth round of the Greece-U.S. Strategic Dialogue. Your presence here speaks to the enduring strength of our relationship and to the importance both our countries attach to its future.

Since the launch of the Strategic Dialogue back in 2018, our cooperation has grown steadily in scope and ambition, encompassing defense, energy, infrastructure, digital technologies, law enforcement, maritime affairs, and the close ties between our peoples. The three agreements signed today are tangible evidence of that progress. Our partnership has never been stronger, deeper, or more consequential. It rests on shared values and a common determination to advance peace, stability, security, and prosperity for our peoples, for our regions, and beyond.

We meet at a time of profound geopolitical change. The ongoing war in Ukraine, instability in the Middle East, threats to maritime security in the Red Sea, and the resurgence of a revisionist rhetoric demand resolve, coordination, and a clear sense of purpose. In this uncertain environment, Greece remains a reliable ally and an anchor of stability in the Eastern Mediterranean. During the 2025-‘26 term on the United Nations – of the Security Council – and as we prepare to assume the presidency of the Council of the European Union second semester of 2027 – we bring that same sense of responsibility to our work. Respect for international law is a guiding principle for our foreign policy and an essential condition for lasting peace.

Greece’s geography places us at the meeting point of three continents. Our history, our longstanding relationships across the region, and the enduring influence of Hellenism allow us to engage with a wide range of partners in good faith and with credibility. This gives Greece a particular responsibility and a practical capacity to connect countries, facilitate dialogue, and build understanding. It also gives our partnership strategic value. Strengthening Greece’s role strengthens the security of the wider region and advances interests we share with the United States.

The Strategic Dialogue allow us to translate this convergence into concrete action. Today, we have an opportunity to carry that world forward across its core pillars. Our defense cooperation has reached unprecedented levels. The Mutual Defense Cooperation Agreement has deepened our strategic partnership and strengthened our capacity to address common security challenges.

Alexandroupolis exemplifies the value of this cooperation. A sovereign Greek port and a vital logistical hub for the United States, it contributes directly to the security of nations – of NATO’s eastern flank. Greece’s consistently high defense expenditure and longstanding contribution to the Alliance reflect a simple conviction: Collective security requires every Ally to shoulder its responsibilities. We are committed to further strengthening our defense cooperation, including through procurement, industrial partnerships, and advanced technologies. Our growing collaboration in law enforcement and counterterrorism is equally important to the security of our citizens.

On energy, Greece is emerging as a vital hub for Southeastern and Central Europe infrastructure, such as the Alexandroupolis FSRU. Together with our leading role in the Vertical Corridor, this diversifying supply is strengthening resilience and giving our neighbors greater energy security. The growing engagement of U.S. energy companies, including Severn and ExxonMobil, underscores confidence, increases potential, (inaudible) the opportunities our partnership offers.

Our maritime strength are the third strategic dimension. With Greek-owned vessels accounting for almost one-fourth of global energy shipping capacity globally, Greek shipping plays a pivotal role in connecting energy producers with consumers and sustaining transatlantic energy flows. The transformation of the Greek economy has opened a new chapter in our bilateral relationship. Renewed growth and investment confidence are creating opportunities for American businesses to participate in Greece’s progress.

Investment by leading U.S. technology companies in data centers’ digital infrastructure is helping to establish Greece as a regional center for innovation. Our ambition is to build on this momentum through partnerships that create skilled jobs, support research, and bring new opportunities to the next generation.

At the heart of this relationship, however, are our people. The Greek American community has helped shape America while sustaining a close and abiding connection with Greece. Its achievements in business, science, public service, and the arts are a source of pride for both our nations. Greek Americans have made Greece’s heritage part of America’s success. They embody a relationship rooted in the ideals of liberty, democracy, and the rule of law, ideals that inspired America’s Founding Fathers and continue to give our partnership purpose. Our expanding education and cultural exchanges carry this connection forward, allowing young Greeks and Americans to learn from one another and to build relationships of their own.

Mr. Secretary, I look forward to our discussions today and to the practical results that we deliver. We have a strong foundation and a clear sense of what we can achieve. Today’s discussion will help us turn that shared ambition into practical results. Our alliance draws strength – draws strength from all we have achieved together. Its promise lies in what we choose to do next. Thank you.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, thank you. Thank you for this opportunity to be here today for the sixth time a U.S. secretary of state gathers with their counterparts in Greece for this Strategic Dialogue. And I’m happy to be here in Greece for that dialogue. It’s my first trip to the country ever; I didn’t even have a chance to come as a senator. And so I’m happy to be here and to be a part of this Strategic Dialogue.

I want to begin by saying that I hope our presence here today and our work that we’re about to do – and continue to do together – highlights something very important, and that is how critical the historic alliance between Greece and the United States is. And this is especially true now at a time of great global uncertainty, whether it’s the war between Russia and Ukraine, whether it’s what’s happening in the Middle East, whether it’s – meaning in the Straits of Hormuz and, increasingly now, in the Red Sea because of the Houthis in Yemen and Saudi Arabia.

At a time of extraordinary global tumult and global instability, we need anchor partners rooted in a common history. And that is what Greece has meant for the United States and, I hope, what the United States has meant for Greece and what we will continue to mean for each other. This strong partnership, it’s a relationship that spans a variety of fronts – obviously defense and security, our mutual defense and security as allies and partners, but it extends to trade, to investment, to energy. There literally is no – it’s a cultural exchange. There are literally no areas of our societies or of our countries that are not part of the U.S.-Greece relationship, and we seek to build and expand on every single one of them.

Let me begin by saying what is obvious to everyone but should continue to be obvious: Greece is an indispensable NATO partner, an indispensable NATO Ally. It is a pillar of stability in this region, it is a pillar of the U.S.’s presence in this region, and it is a pillar of how we secure our national interest as well as Greece’s in the region. So we are thrilled – part of that, some of the things that aren’t heavily perceived but we’ll be able to be a part of announcing again later today, is we’re thrilled that Greece joins the

U.S. National Guard Bureau of State Sponsorship [1] Program, and they’re doing so with the guard from my home state of Florida. It’s another milestone in our deepening defense relationship.

The U.S.-Greece Economic Security Declaration commits both nations to continue to work with likeminded allies as well to develop secure supply chains. That includes – including critical mineral productions, again another area of very strong cooperation in which our mutual interests are aligned but also in which we’re taking concrete action.

Our energy relationship is reaching new heights, and it continues to expand and grow, and it’s something we’re going to be building on. The Vertical Gas Corridor expansion has cemented in Greece, has cemented Greece as an energy hub and as a secure energy hub, and has facilitated increase in U.S. LNG exports to Europe. That’s something we continue to build on.

Our bilateral relationship as countries, of course, at the end, is founded not just in a common history but in enduring ties of family, of culture, of religion, of a shared heritage. As I’ll speak about later today in what I think is a pretty historic setting, from what I read – (laughter) – it – we are indebted to ancient Greece for its role in shaping not just our country but, frankly, our civilization.

And we – so we’re here today to remember the past because that’s the foundation upon which our relationship is built, but also to focus on the future, because we have incredible things that we can do together. And I’m very grateful to be a part of this, to be – excited to be a part of the Strategic Dialogue and happy to be here on my first visit to Greece but hopefully not my last.

[1] Partnership

Congressman Brad Sherman Marks Three Years Since October 7th Attack on Israel
Washington, D.C. — Today, Congressman Brad Sherman (CA-32), Co-Chair of the House Israel Allies Caucus, Ranking Member Emeritus of the Middle East Subcommittee, and senior member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, issued the following statement marking three years since Hamas’s October 7th, 2023 terrorist attack on Israel:
“Three years ago today, Hamas terrorists launched a barbaric and unprovoked attack against Israel, murdering more than 1,200 innocent men, women and children, including Americans, and taking some 250 people hostage in the deadliest day for the Jewish people since the Holocaust.
Today, we must continue to remember those who were murdered, honor their memories, stand with the survivors and families whose lives were forever changed, and recommit to ensuring that Hamas and any like-minded terrorist entity can never be allowed to govern again.
Last October, after more than two agonizing years of captivity, the remaining twenty living hostages held in Gaza finally returned home. Their release brought enormous relief, but it did not erase the suffering inflicted upon the hostages and their families, nor diminish our obligation to ensure that every terrorist organization that participated in the October 7th attack is held accountable.
The acts of brutality committed on that day – including rape and torture – should have inspired global solidarity. Instead, 3 years later, we are witnessing the return of extreme vilification of the Jewish people and the Jewish state, including through the manufactured and libelous accusation of genocide.
The United States must reject this disinformation campaign and remain steadfast in supporting Israel’s security. Hamas can never again carry out such an attack and Gaza must be governed not by terrorists, but by legitimate leadership committed to peace. This is critical to ending the tragic cycle of violence and finally allowing innocent Israelis and Palestinians to live in security.
The U.S.–Israel partnership has endured because of our shared democratic values and common determination to confront terrorism and pursue lasting security and peace. We must stand up to the antisemitism and coordinated disinformation that threatens this alliance. On this solemn anniversary, we remember the victims of October 7th and reaffirm our commitment to building a future of greater peace and security for Israelis, Palestinians, and the region.”
Since the October 7th attack, Congressman Sherman has led and co-sponsored numerous measures to support Israel’s security and hold Hamas and other terrorist organizations accountable, including legislation to sanction the Popular Resistance Committees for their participation in the October 7th massacre, strengthen Israel’s missile-defense capabilities, and counter the flow of Iranian funds to terrorist proxies.
###

DOJ’s National Fraud Enforcement Division established to prosecute those who steal or fraudulently misuse taxpayer dollars
A 42-year-old woman has been ordered to federal prison for her role in a multimillion-dollar pandemic loan fraud conspiracy.
Trenikia Lashae Banks pleaded guilty Sept. 22, 2025.
U.S. District Judge Kenneth M. Hoyt ordered Banks to serve 18 months in federal prison to be followed by three years of supervised release. Banks was also ordered to pay more than $400,000 in restitution to the Small Business Administration. In handing down the sentence, Judge Hoyt cited the aggravated nature of the crime and Banks’ lack of moral fortitude. He emphasized there is no such thing as “free money” and described her conduct as intentional, not a mistake.
In 2020 and 2021, Banks and Shawn Nicholas Young conspired with approximately 70 others to submit fraudulent applications for funds through the Paycheck Protection Program and Economic Injury Disaster Loan funds intended to help small businesses during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Young submitted more than 100 loan applications from his Missouri City residence, including one for his fake business All Day Money Crew LLC.
The group attempted to obtain more than $14 million in pandemic loan funds and successfully received approximately $4.5 million.
Through Young, Banks obtained three pandemic loans for fake businesses in her name and paid him kickbacks from the proceeds. She also falsified documents at Young’s request for submission with 15 loan applications for other co-conspirators. Young paid Banks to falsify the documents even when the loan applications were unsuccessful.
Banks was permitted to remain on bond and voluntarily surrender to a Federal Bureau of Prisons facility to be determined in the near future.
Young, 43, Missouri City, also pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud for his role in the scheme and is set for sentencing Feb. 9, 2027.
Federal Housing Finance Agency - Office of Inspector General, Treasury Inspector General for Tax Agency, SBA - OIG, Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation - OIG, and Immigration and Customs Enforcement Homeland Security Investigations conducted the investigation, with the assistance of Fort Bend County Sheriff’s Office and Harris County Constable’s Office Precinct 1.
Assistant U.S. Attorney Stephanie Bauman prosecuted the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division which is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within federal benefit programs.
title: Houston Resident Sentenced in $14 Million Pandemic Loan Fraud Conspiracy

Budzinski Celebrates Nearly $145,000 AmeriCorps Seniors Grant for Dove, Inc.
DECATUR, IL — Today, Congresswoman Nikki Budzinski (IL-13) visited Dove, Inc. in Decatur to celebrate the organization receiving nearly $145,000 through the AmeriCorps Seniors Retired and Senior Volunteer Program (RSVP). During her visit, Budzinski met with Dove staff and senior volunteers to hear how the federal investment is helping adults 55 and older give back and support their neighbors across the 13th District.
Dove, Inc. has sponsored the RSVP program since 1976, connecting adults 55 and older with meaningful volunteer opportunities that address needs in their own communities. On June 30, Dove was awarded $144,731 through the FY26 AmeriCorps Seniors RSVP grant competition. The program provides funding to organizations that engage older adults as volunteers to address critical local needs and strengthen communities.
“People who want to give their time and talents to their communities should have every opportunity to do so, no matter their age,” said Congresswoman Budzinski. “Dove understands the incredible value that older adults bring to our communities and this investment will help connect even more seniors with meaningful opportunities to serve their neighbors across Macon and DeWitt Counties. I’m proud to support AmeriCorps Seniors and the organizations like Dove that make a difference every day across Central Illinois.”
Throughout her time in Congress, Budzinski has supported federal investments that create meaningful opportunities for older Americans to serve their communities, strengthen local organizations, and provide critical support to families and neighbors in Illinois.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Small Business Administration Inspector General and Pandemic Response Accountability Committee (PRAC) Chairman William W. Kirk welcomed Treasury’s announcement of expanded fraud prevention and payment verification safeguards, emphasizing the importance of a whole-of-government approach to protecting taxpayer dollars. Treasury reported expanding access to Do Not Pay data and screening approximately $3.7 trillion in federal payments during fiscal year 2026.
“Protecting taxpayer dollars requires us to identify fraud risks before funds go out the door,” said Kirk. “Treasury’s announced progress represents an important step in moving from ‘pay and chase’ to prevention. As SBA Inspector General and PRAC Chairman, I support this governmentwide effort and am committed to ensuring our oversight work helps agencies strengthen safeguards, identify risks early, and prevent losses.”
SBA OIG’s oversight of pandemic assistance programs illustrates the importance of early screening and effective follow-through. In its management alert on Paycheck Protection Program recipients identified through Treasury’s Do Not Pay data, SBA OIG collaborated with Treasury’s Do Not Pay Business Center to identify loans to potentially ineligible recipients and recommended stronger screening before awards and payments.
The PRAC’s Blueprint for Enhanced Program Integrity reinforces complementary principles, including strong internal controls, access to data, verification of applicant identity and eligibility, and coordinated oversight across government. These principles support efforts to prevent fraud while ensuring assistance reaches eligible recipients.
“Our contribution is to turn oversight findings into fraud prevention,” Kirk said. “By sharing lessons learned, identifying vulnerabilities, and working across organizational boundaries, inspectors general and the PRAC help strengthen the government’s defenses against fraud. We welcome Treasury’s reported progress and will continue doing our part alongside our federal, state, and local partners.”
According to Treasury, approximately 99 percent of federal programs can now access the Do Not Pay data sources for which they are legally authorized, compared with approximately 4 percent at the end of fiscal year 2025. Treasury also reported screening more than 1.1 billion federal payments totaling approximately $3.7 trillion during fiscal year 2026.

Fast Facts
The Department of Defense relies on GPS for military operations. But it's vulnerable to interference and jamming. DOD's decades-long efforts to strengthen GPS are behind schedule and over budget.
DOD has explored ways to get navigation data to the battlefield if GPS service is disrupted. For example, it's developing navigation receivers that use non-GPS satellites, as well as automated observations of the sun, moon, and stars. But these efforts vary in scale and are currently fragmented across the military services.
Better coordination could help DOD's efforts stay on track and within budget.
Our recommendations address this.
Two people in camouflage clothing pointing at a tablet while viewing a map and a phone on a table
Highlights
What GAO Found
The Department of Defense’s (DOD) efforts to modernize GPS continue to face delays. In response, DOD is developing new complementary sources of positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) data to mitigate GPS threats. In 2026, after years of delays, DOD canceled the Next Generation Operational Control System ground control system and began modernizing the existing GPS Operational Control Segment. Among other effects, this creates risks for the launch, checkout, and operation of new GPS satellites. Given ongoing threats to GPS, DOD is operating and continuing development of (1) satellite-based PNT systems, (2) non-satellite-based PNT systems, and (3) backup timing solutions.
Operational Illustration of Threats to GPS and Complementary Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Systems
The Air Force continues to make progress developing modernized GPS military code (M-code) receiver cards, but challenges remain with fielding and integration. For example, the M-code aviation receiver programs continue to encounter development and integration challenges. In response, the Navy is developing an interim solution for its aircraft to use M-code. On the other hand, the Army and Navy are fielding M-code capable and multi-PNT receivers in ground vehicles, ships, and Army aircraft. All the military services are also pursuing integration of complementary PNT data into multi-PNT receivers.
Challenges with aligning multiple, fragmented PNT efforts across the military services impact DOD’s ability to ensure that M-code and PNT efforts are completed promptly. Congress mandated a PNT Oversight Council to oversee the portfolio. While the council can make budget-related recommendations to the services, the services are responsible for their own budgets. The PNT enterprise could benefit from consolidating and aligning efforts among the services. DOD has taken some steps to consolidate multiple PNT efforts, such as combining aircraft PNT receivers and M-code receiver card efforts into a single Air Force managed joint program office. Benefits of consolidation could include synchronization of schedules and better strategic alignment of funding.
Why GAO Did This Study
The U.S. military and civilians depend daily on accurate PNT data provided by GPS operated by the Space Force on behalf of DOD. DOD has worked for decades to modernize its GPS, including the use of a new signal—called M-code—and other features to counter evolving threats. Challenges have delayed these efforts. The military services have also started developing and fielding complementary PNT systems to ensure the availability of this foundational military capability.
Congress included a provision in law for GAO to report on DOD’s GPS modernization efforts and development and fielding of complementary PNT efforts. This report (1) addresses the progress DOD has made in modernizing GPS and providing complementary PNT data to the warfighter; (2) discusses the status of DOD efforts to develop and field modernized PNT receivers; and (3) assesses the extent to which DOD has taken steps to oversee the PNT portfolio, and what challenges it is facing.
To conduct this work, GAO reviewed documentation from GPS modernization and complementary PNT programs and efforts and interviewed relevant officials from DOD and the military departments.
Recommendations
GAO is making three recommendations for DOD to ensure that each of the three military departments assesses where consolidation of its GPS modernization and complementary PNT efforts would ensure better strategic alignment between DOD and the military departments and develop plans to consolidate efforts. DOD concurred with GAO’s recommendations.
title: Precision Navigation Systems: Challenges Remain with Fielding New Capabilities

Georgia's Congressional Democrats Push Back on State Board’s 'Unsubstantiated Claims' in DOJ Letter
ATLANTA, GA — Today, four of the five members of the Georgia U.S. House of Representatives Democrat delegation and Rep. Joe Morelle of New York, the Ranking Member of the Committee on House Administration that oversees federal elections, sent a letter to the Georgia State Election Board pushing back on its Sept. 30 letter to the Department of Justice seeking their intervention in the state’s voting machines ahead of the November midterms elections, which are now in just 27 days.
“We are greatly alarmed by the mischaracterizations, and clear partisan motivations, that underlie the “Formal Request” letter you submitted to the U.S. Department of Justice on September 30, 2026. This letter, which plainly misstates the requirements of federal law — and which requests the Attorney General take action exceeding the power of the Department of Justice — is a clear attempt to sow public mistrust in the security of American elections. We demand that the Georgia State Election Board (“SEB”) clarify to the voters of Georgia that the tested and certified voting systems in use in the state, which have been used for three federal elections, are legal, secure, and safe.”
Read the full letter HERE and below.
Georgia State Election Board
2 Martin Luther King Jr. Drive SE
Floyd West Tower
Suite 324
Atlanta, Georgia 30334
Dear Mr. Mills:
We are greatly alarmed by the mischaracterizations, and clear partisan motivations, that underlie the “Formal Request” letter you submitted to the U.S. Department of Justice on September 30, 2026. This letter, which plainly misstates the requirements of federal law—and which requests the Attorney General take action exceeding the power of the Department of Justice—is a clear attempt to sow public mistrust in the security of American elections. We demand that the Georgia State Election Board (“SEB”) clarify to the voters of Georgia that the tested and certified voting systems in use in the state, which have been used for three federal elections, are legal, secure, and safe.
There is absolutely no ambiguity on this point: The voting system used by Georgia voters complies with state and federal law. Your unsubstantiated claim that Georgia’s voting system is “inconsistent” with the requirements of the Help America Vote Act (“HAVA”) is deeply troubling; one would expect that someone in your position would have some basic understanding of applicable federal election law. HAVA mandates that the United States Election Assistance Commission (“EAC”) “provide certification, decertification, and recertification of voting systems, as well as the accreditation of voting system testing laboratories.” The EAC also issues Voluntary Voting System Guidelines (“VVSG”), which cover “pre-voting, voting, and post-voting operations consistent with the definition of a voting system in HAVA Section 301(a).” And, as you should know, a state’s voting devices and software “must meet [VVSG specifications] in order to receive certification from the EAC.” Of course, Georgia’s voting system has undergone the EAC’s thorough testing process, as evidenced by the fact that the EAC has certified Georgia’s voting system, as required by Georgia’s statutory and regulatory regime.
The intent of your letter is clear—to serve as a pretext for undermining public confidence in Georgia’s election results this November. Americans should know that the State Election Board does not administer Georgia’s elections. That responsibility rests with the Secretary of State and the Secretary of State’s Elections Division. The SEB has important statutory oversight and rulemaking responsibilities, but those responsibilities should not be conflated with the actual administration and certification of Georgia elections. Nor should any erroneous SEB communication to the Department of Justice concerning Georgia’s elections be understood as anything more than partisan political actors’ attempt to justify future attempts to overturn a free and fair American election—an extraordinarily serious, and cynical, misuse of official communication.
Public confidence in elections depends in substantial part upon public officials communicating accurately, responsibly, and within the scope of their statutory authority—and without incompetently, or intentionally, mischaracterizing the law. Georgians have used the state’s voting system for three straight federal elections—elections won by both Republicans and Democrats. And Georgia has one of the most rigorous, robust post-election audit regimes in the country—this is how we know that Georgia’s elections are free, fair, and secure. You should therefore promptly clarify the record, correct any inaccurate characterization of HAVA or Georgia’s voting-system requirements, and make clear that Georgia’s elections are administered by the Secretary of State and conducted using voting systems that have satisfied the certification requirements established by state and federal law.
Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.
Sincerely,
Reps. Joe Morelle (NY-25), Sanford D. Bishop, Jr. (GA-02), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Nikema Williams (GA-05), Everton Blair (GA-13).
###
title: Georgia's Congressional Democrats Push Back on State Board’s 'Unsubstantiated Claims' in DOJ Letter

CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas – A 28-year-old Corpus Christi resident has been found guilty of transporting illegal aliens.

The jury deliberated for approximately two hours before convicting Jose Manuel Gomez following a two-day trial.

On July 2, Gomez drove a white Ford F-250 hauling a cattle trailer to the Border Patrol checkpoint near Falfurrias.

The jury heard that following a K-9 alert, authorities discovered eight illegal aliens hidden behind bales of hay.

Gomez claimed a friend asked him to move cattle and directed him to the trailer. He also claimed he did not know who owned it.

The investigation revealed the trailer had been sold on Facebook Marketplace to a buyer using the same phone number as Gomez’s wife.

The seller testified that Gomez, his wife, and their children arrived in a white F-250 to pick up the trailer in Melvin, Texas.

The jury also heard that Border Patrol checkpoint cameras captured the same white F-250 hauling the trailer approximately one week before the smuggling incident and again on the day of the offense.

U.S. District Judge Nelva Gonzalez Ramos presided over the trial and set sentencing for Jan. 6, 2027. At that time, Gomez faces up to 20 years in federal prison and a possible $250,000 maximum fine

Border Patrol and Brooks County Sheriff’s Office conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Zachary Bird and Ashley Martin are prosecuting the case.
title: Rio Grande City man convicted for transporting illegal aliens in cattle trailer

BOSTON –Two men have been indicted by a federal grand jury for allegedly conspiring to distribute fentanyl in Worcester County.

Richard Molina-Ovalle, 36, of Worcester and Jose Molina-Ovalle, 27, a Dominican national unlawfully residing in Worcester, were charged in an indictment with conspiracy to distribute 400 grams or more of fentanyl and related charges. Jose Molina-Ovalle was also charged with being an Alien in Possession of Firearms and Illegal Reentry of an Alien among other offenses.

Richard Molina-Ovalle was previously arrested and charged in September 2026 and was released on conditions. He is scheduled to be arraigned in federal court in Boston on Oct. 13, 2026. Jose Molina-Ovalle was arrested in the Bahamas on Sept. 24, 2026.

According to the charging documents, on Sept. 10, 2026, Richard Molina-Ovalle was observed outside of an alleged co-conspirator’s residence in Leominster, with more than 400 grams of fentanyl in his vehicle. Approximately 31 grams of fentanyl, in addition to drug packaging materials were allegedly seized from Richard Molina-Ovalle’s apartment in Worcester during a subsequent search.

Jose Molina-Ovalle allegedly served as Richard Molina-Ovalle’s drug supplier. It is further alleged that a search of Jose Molina-Ovalle’s residence in Worcester resulted in the recovery of approximately 4.5 kilograms of fentanyl, one kilogram of cocaine, cutting agents, a large amount of U.S. currency, scales, blenders and drug packaging materials. Numerous firearms were also allegedly seized from Jose Molina-Ovalle’s residence, including: a Glock 21 .45 caliber pistol; a Glock 27 .40 caliber pistol; a Smith and Wesson .380 caliber pistol; a 12-gauge shotgun; and an Anderson Arms AR-15 rifle.

The charge of conspiracy to distribute 400 grams or more of fentanyl provides for a sentence of no less than 10 years in prison and up to life in prison, at least five years of supervised release and a fine of up to $10 million. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case.

DALLAS — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced today that AMAX Engineering Corporation, an AI data center engineering firm, has agreed to pay $2.48 million to resolve allegations that the company violated the False Claims Act by applying for and receiving a loan that it was not eligible for in the Small Business Administration’s Paycheck Protection Program.

AMAX applied for and received a second draw PPP loan in 2021 which was later forgiven in full. However, the government contended that AMAX was not a qualified small business eligible for the loan, because it and related entities collectively exceeded the applicable size standard.

The settlement resolved a lawsuit filed under the qui tam or whistleblower provision of the False Claims Act, which permits private parties to file suit on behalf of the United States and share in a portion of the government’s recovery. The qui tam lawsuit is case number 3:25-CV-3100-N in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas, and the qui tam relator, Blockquote, Inc., will receive $248,000 in connection with the settlement.

“My office continues to aggressively investigate and pursue companies that received PPP funds they were not eligible for,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “The PPP was purposely limited to qualifying small businesses, meaning that every PPP dollar taken by a larger, ineligible company during the pandemic was a dollar that should have gone to the small businesses of Main Street America that Congress was trying to help. We are determined to hold those companies accountable and recover those taxpayer dollars.”

“My office continues to aggressively investigate and pursue companies that received PPP funds they were not eligible for,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “The PPP was purposely limited to qualifying small businesses, meaning that every PPP dollar taken by a larger, ineligible company during the pandemic was a dollar that should have gone to the small businesses of Main Street America that Congress was trying to help. We are determined to hold those companies accountable and recover those taxpayer dollars.”

Congress created the PPP in March 2020, as part of the Coronavirus Aid, Relief and Economic Security Act to provide emergency loans to small businesses suffering economic hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Whether an applicant qualified for a PPP loan depended on various factors, including employee-count size standards for applicants.

The matter was handled by Assistant U.S. Attorney Najib Gazi, together with Attorney Amber Perez, Office of General Counsel for the Small Business Administration.

This year, the Trump Administration launched the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud and the National Fraud Enforcement Division to enhance the Administration’s war on fraud, waste, and abuse in federal programs. When unscrupulous actors exploit these programs for their own financial gain, they defraud the government, harm the people these programs are designed to aid and protect and undermine American businesses that play by the rules. The Civil Division’s False Claims Act enforcement plays a critical role in combatting such fraudulent schemes, recovering billions of dollars for the American taxpayers, and holding wrongdoers accountable. False Claims Act matters will continue to be on the forefront of the battle against fraud, and the Civil Division’s False Claims work will support and advance the mission of the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud and the National Fraud Enforcement Division.

The civil claims settled by the agreement are allegations only, and there has been no determination of civil liability.

title: AI data center engineering firm settles PPP lawsuit for $2.48 million

As Colorado begins mailing ballots for the November election, Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen (CO-07) is demanding answers from the U.S. Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) regarding reported deployments of armed and unarmed guards at Colorado postal facilities.The deployments follow repeated Trump administration efforts to restrict mail voting, sow confusion, and undermine confidence in our elections—raising urgent concerns about whether voters will face intimidation simply for casting a ballot. In the 2024 general election, more than 92% of Colorado voters cast their ballots by mail—making reliable delivery and intimidation-free access essential for the state to conduct this and future elections. 
“Coloradans should be able to cast their ballots without fear or intimidation. Deploying armed guards at postal facilities just as voting begins demands an explanation and urgent action,” said Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen. “We need clear answers about why these guards are here, what authority they have, and how voters and election mail will be protected. Coloradans deserve confidence that their ballots will be delivered and their voices heard. Voter intimidation is an attack on our democracy, and here in Colorado, we will fight to ensure every vote is counted.”
Armed guards have reportedly been deployed at postal facilities even though USPIS says no credible security or operational threat prompted the increased presence. A memo distributed to the American Postal Workers Union says guards will monitor entrances and parking lots, verify IDs, and report purportedly suspicious activity at public Post Offices and restricted mail-processing plants. USPIS calls this a longstanding security plan, but has not explained why these deployments are happening now, identified the affected facilities, or detailed safeguards to prevent voter intimidation and interference with election mail.
In the letter to Chief Postal Inspector Barksdale, Pettersen writes, “Postal workers have a crucial responsibility to deliver election mail safely and on time. We support appropriate measures designed to protect them and their ability to carry out this responsibility. At the same time, the presence of armed guards at facilities where voters may deposit ballots runs the real risk of making voters feel intimidated. Federal law prohibits voter intimidation, which is defined as the use of threats, coercion, or attempts to intimidate for the purpose of interfering with the right of another person to vote or to vote for the person of their choosing. Voters should feel assured that they can send their ballots without being questioned, monitored, or deterred by armed guards.” 
Congresswoman Pettersen demands that USPIS disclose:
    - Who authorized the deployments,
- Which Colorado facilities are affected, and 
- Whether guards can demand identification, restrict public access, inspect ballots, or influence whether election mail is accepted and delivered. 
- She also asks whether the White House, the Department of Justice, or the Department of Homeland Security had any role in the decision.
Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen has consistently defended Coloradans’ access to secure, accessible elections. She introduced an amendment to protect eligible voters from disenfranchisement under the SAVE Act and opposed a Republican budget resolution that included $10 billion for election grants tied to SAVE America Act voter-ID requirements. Building on her work in the state legislature to strengthen Colorado’s mail-ballot system, she has also pressed USPS to ensure timely ballot delivery, particularly for rural communities, and pushed back against federal efforts to restrict mail voting.
The full text of the letter can be found HERE and below.
Dear Chief Postal Inspector Barksdale,
 
We write in response to recent reporting that the United States Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) has deployed armed and unarmed guards to postal facilities in Colorado and across the country just as millions of Americans are preparing to cast their ballots by mail ahead of the 2026 General Midterm Elections. 
 
In a memo distributed to the American Postal Workers Union, the USPIS has indicated that the guards will monitor entrances and parking areas, verify IDs, and observe and report purportedly suspicious activity in and around key postal facilities, including both Post Offices – which are open to the public – and US Postal Service processing plants – which are not open to the public. These deployments come despite the agency’s repeated assurances that no credible security or operational threat has necessitated the heightened presence, with USPIS characterizing this initiative as part of a longstanding, multiyear security plan. Yet the agency has provided little public information for the timing of this deployment, failed to identify which facilities will be affected, and offered no detail regarding the safeguards that will be implemented to ensure that the presence of law enforcement personnel does not disrupt, intimidate, or otherwise interfere with postal workers, election officials, or votes during a critical period of the election cycle. 
 
Postal workers have a crucial responsibility to deliver election mail safely and on time. We support appropriate measures designed to protect them and their ability to carry out this responsibility. At the same time, the presence of armed guards at facilities where voters may deposit ballots runs the real risk of making voters feel intimidated. Federal law prohibits voter intimidation, which is defined as the use of threats, coercion, or attempts to intimidate for the purpose of interfering with the right of another person to vote or to vote for the person of their choosing. Voters should feel assured that they can send their ballots without being questioned, monitored, or deterred by armed guards.
 
This issue is particularly poignant for Colorado, where over 90% of voters cast their ballots by mail. Colorado’s 2024 General Election Fact Sheet shows that every audit demonstrated a 97% rate of statistical certainty that voting tabulation equipment worked correctly, demonstrating the strength and soundness of Colorado’s election security system which has multiple layers of physical and network security measures designed to prevent unauthorized access and ensure accurate vote counts. Leading up to the 2026 General Midterm Election, the United States Postal Service (USPS) has disseminated best practices for voting by mail, which includes guidance that if and when feasible, voters should deliver their mail-in ballot to a postal facility or USPS retail facility to receive same-day stamping. The presence of armed and unarmed guards already deployed at postal facilities is not a hypothetical concern; it is a reality that voters and postal workers are confronting right now. Deploying armed and unarmed personnel at key mail-processing and ballot-return locations during an election, without a clear and compelling public justification, risks intimidating voters, discouraging ballot return, and eroding public confidence in both the Postal Service and the integrity of the electoral process.
As such, we request answers to the following questions to help us understand the circumstances surrounding this deployment and its potential impact on voter access:
    - When was the decision to deploy additional guards made, who approved it, and what prompted the deployment at this time?
- How many armed and unarmed guards have been deployed nationwide and in Colorado? At which facilities, and for what anticipated duration?
- What are the guards’ duties and limits of authority? May they ask members of the public for identification, inspect mail or ballots, direct postal employees, restrict access to facilities, or interact with election officials?
- What steps has USPIS taken to consult postal workers, their unions, state and local election officials, and USPS election mail personnel about the deployment and its potential effect on ballot processing?
- Has USPIS received any request, direction, or input concerning this deployment from the White House, the Department of Justice (DOJ), the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), or any other federal agency? 
- Will these guards have any role or authority in determining whether election mail is accepted, processed, or delivered?
- What specific steps has USPIS taken to ensure that the presence and conduct of these guards do not intimidate voters or discourage them from mailing their ballots?
 
Coloradans deserve certainty that every eligible voter can return a ballot free from intimidation, disruption, or interference, and that every piece of election mail will be handled and delivered securely and on time. Postal workers, election officials, and voters alike are entitled to clear assurances regarding the scope, purpose, and conduct of these deployments of armed and unarmed guards. In light of the urgency and significance of these concerns, we request a prompt and comprehensive response no later than October 16th, 2026.
 
Sincerely, 
Brittany Pettersen
Member of Congress
title: Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen Demands Answers on Armed Guards Trump Admin Has Reportedly Deployed to Ballot Drop Off Facilities As Colorado Begins Mail-In-Voting

Italian Alien Charged With Voting in 2024 General Election and Lying About It
TAMPA, Fla. —U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services provided critical assistance in the investigation that led to a federal indictment charging Andrea Catanese, 60, an Italian national, with voting by an alien, attempting to unlawfully procure naturalization, and making a false statement in connection with naturalization. If convicted on all counts, Catanese faces a maximum penalty of 10 years in federal prison. U. S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement.
According to the indictment, Catanese voted in the 2024 general election despite not being a U.S. citizen. The indictment further alleges that Catanese later falsely stated on a Form N-400, Application for Naturalization, that he had never voted in a federal election and repeated that false statement to a USCIS official reviewing the application.
An indictment is merely a formal charge that a defendant has committed one or more violations of federal criminal law, and every defendant is presumed innocent unless, and until, proven guilty.
This case was investigated by U.S. Immigration and Custom Enforcement’s Homeland Security Investigations with assistance from USCIS and the Pasco County Supervisor of Elections. It will be prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Mark E. Andreu.

CAMDEN, N.J. – A Middlesex County woman admitted to sexually abusing an individual in federal custody, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced today.

Jordan Pensak, 27, a corrections officer at Federal Correctional Institution Fort Dix (Fort Dix), pleaded guilty before U.S. District Court Judge Edward S. Kiel in Camden federal court to an Information which charged her with sexual abuse of an individual in federal custody. The sentencing date is scheduled for February 10, 2027.

According to statements made in court and documents filed in the case:

Pensak had a consensual sexual relationship with an inmate at Fort Dix, a low-security federal correctional institution in Burlington County, and had sex with him in January 2026. Pensak and the inmate also exchanged sexually explicit photographs and messages over social media and electronic applications, facilitated by the inmate’s use of two contraband cell phones while in custody at Fort Dix. Pensak admitted to having a sexual relationship with the inmate in text messages sent to multiple individuals, including family members of the inmate. In one of those communications Pensak raised concerns that she might be pregnant with the inmate’s child.

U.S. Attorney Frazer credited special agents of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy; and the Department of Justice, Office of the Inspector General, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Timothy Edminston, with the investigation.

Congresswoman Schrier, Senator Bennet Demand Answers on Childhood Vaccines EO, Measles Deaths, & Delayed Vaccine Access
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Yesterday, Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) and Senator Michael Bennet (D-CO) led 25 colleagues in a letter to Dr. Erica Schwartz, the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to call out efforts to reject settled vaccine science and demand answers about the CDC’s efforts to implement President Trump’s childhood vaccine Executive Order (EO), underreport measles-associated deaths, and delay access to childhood immunizations.
“[...] As the United States is experiencing the largest measles outbreak in 35 years, President Trump issued an Executive Order (EO) aimed at dismantling core immunization guidelines, and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) issued a Request for Information (RFI) to lay the groundwork for fundamentally restructuring the routine childhood immunization schedule. At the same time, reports indicate the CDC, under your leadership, excluded verified state-reported measles-associated deaths in Pennsylvania from the public mortality count. All of this is happening while the CDC delayed access to fall respiratory virus vaccines through the Vaccines for Children (VFC) program. We are deeply concerned by this administration’s persistent efforts to reject settled science. As CDC Director, you bear a responsibility to uphold scientific integrity, and we write seeking answers on how the CDC will respond to the EO and the RFI, and how you will honor the pledge you made to ensure that the CDC leads with evidence-based public health,” began the lawmakers.
The United States is facing a decline in childhood immunization rates. Recently, the CDC reported that 280,000 kindergartners did not complete their measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine series. This comes as the Trump Administration has actively worked to lower the number of recommended immunizations, break up safe and effective combination shots, and promote legal action against states unaligned with such efforts.
Additionally, the CDC has a long-standing agency precedent and prides itself on “objective data collection and reporting.” At the beginning of September, numerous reports exposed that four measles-associated deaths verified and reported by the Pennsylvania Department of Health were excluded from the CDC’s public outbreak tracker for weeks, even as internal CDC systems continued to track these fatalities. This omission breaks with agency standards, and raises serious questions about the CDC’s willingness to resist political pressure over settled science.
“The health of American children and families depends on a CDC Director who is willing to follow the science, even when it may be politically inconvenient. We look forward to your response and to seeing whether the CDC under your leadership honors the commitments you made at your confirmation hearing,” concluded the lawmakers.
The text of the letter is available HERE.

BLM Timber Sales Generate Nearly $30 Million, Support American Jobs in Third Quarter
Organization:
Media Contact:
WASHINGTON – The Bureau of Land Management generated $29.8 million in revenue from timber sales during the third quarter of 2026, supporting American jobs and increasing domestic timber supply.
During July, August, and September, the BLM sold about 121 million board feet of timber across 5,300 acres in Oregon, Washington, Wyoming, and Idaho. That amount of lumber is enough to build about 7,600 homes. The sales support local economies with well-paying jobs in logging, milling, and construction.
“I’ve met the people whose livelihoods depend on this work, from foresters in the woods to employees at local mills,” said BLM Director Steve Pearce. “These timber sales have a real impact in rural communities, and that’s something that goes well beyond the numbers in a quarterly report.”
The BLM plans to hold nine timber sales in October 2026 to offer about 46 million board feet of timber across more than 1,200 acres.
The BLM manages 58 million acres of forests—including 2.4 million acres in western Oregon. The bureau is committed to supplying a reliable, secure, and resilient domestic supply of timber. BLM forestry supports economic security, reduces risks from wildfire, conserves fish and wildlife habitat, and decreases costs of energy production. Local communities rely on jobs that come from BLM forests, and timber from public land feeds local industry.
More than 20% of BLM-managed lands are forest and woodland ecosystems. The BLM ensures the health and resilience of these public forest lands as well as the availability of traditional forest products, such as timber.
The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.

BILLINGS – A Billings man who was selling illicit drugs from his motel room was sentenced today to six years and six months in prison, followed by four years of supervised release, First Assistant U.S. Attorney Mark Steger Smith said.

Shawn Leon Anderson, 53, pleaded guilty in June 2026 to possession with intent to distribute controlled substances.

U.S. District Judge Susan P. Watters presided.

The government alleged in court documents that law enforcement learned in July 2023 that Anderson was selling illicit drugs from a Billings Rodeway Inn motel room. Agents arranged for an informant to buy from Anderson. Investigators searched the motel room and found just under a pound of fentanyl in the form of thousands of pills, roughly three-quarters of a pound of methamphetamine, 20 grams of cocaine, and $4,753 in cash.

Anderson told agents he used the motel room to sell drugs so that he didn’t draw attention to his residence in Billings. He said for the last three months he had been acquiring illicit drugs once or twice a month to sell to users.

The U.S. Attorney’s Office prosecuted the case. The Montana Division of Criminal Investigation and the DEA conducted the investigation.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities.

NIH joins effort to build SI-ready data for predictive models of human biology
Wednesday, October 7, 2026
NIH joins effort to build SI-ready data for predictive models of human biology
NIH-led Bio Genesis Mission will leverage existing biomedical data resources to accelerate SI-enabled discovery and improve human health.
The National Institutes of Health (NIH) is coordinating with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), Biohub and other partners to develop the data and resources needed to develop Super Intelligence (SI) models that can better predict how cells and biological systems respond to disease and potential interventions. Through its Bio Genesis Mission, NIH will bring together existing biomedical datasets, national data infrastructure, and research programs to help build SI-ready resources for the broader scientific community.
Developing predictive models of biology requires enormous amounts of high-quality, SI-ready data capturing how cells respond to interventions across different cell types and conditions. NIH’s extensive investments in biomedical research provide a foundation for this work; resources include national biomedical repositories catalogued by NIH’s National Library of Medicine (NLM) and the National Center for Biotechnology Information, as well as NIH Common Fund programs that are already developing coordinated biological atlases, shared data standards and SI-ready biomedical datasets.
“By combining resources and expertise, we can accelerate the development of universal cell models with sufficient biological complexity to predict how any cell responds to an intervention,” said Nicole Kleinstreuer, Ph.D., NIH Deputy Director for Program Coordination, Planning, and Strategic Initiatives (DPCPSI). “The return from these models could be broad and profound, resulting in substantially faster timelines for medical breakthroughs as compared with attempting to attain the same results through laboratory experiments alone.”
NIH will coordinate with Biohub to help standardize appropriate datasets for SI model training. Training these models requires obtaining measurements of how cells respond to intervention across many more cell types and conditions than have yet been studied, and building technologies for studying cells at scales and speeds that current instruments cannot capture.
“An accurate predictive model of biology could dramatically accelerate scientific discovery by enabling scientists to perform experiments digitally. The insights that come from this could unlock a far greater understanding of disease and open up completely new paths for cures,” said Biohub Head of Science, Alex Rives. “Because of this potential, the creation of a virtual cell is one of the most important challenges for the next era of science. It will require coordinated data generation efforts at a national and international scale, which is why these partners are coming together. We invite the worldwide scientific community to join us in this project.”
The joint effort aligns with the Predicting Living Systems National Science and Technology Challenge and seeks to make high-quality biological data more useful to researchers developing predictive models of living systems. These models could ultimately help scientists explore biological questions computationally, identify promising drug targets and interventions, and prioritize the most promising ideas for laboratory and clinical testing, accelerating the translation of biomedical discoveries into better health for all Americans.
About the National Institutes of Health (NIH): NIH, the nation's medical research agency, includes 27 Institutes and Centers and is a component of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. NIH is the primary federal agency conducting and supporting basic, clinical, and translational medical research, and is investigating the causes, treatments, and cures for both common and rare diseases. For more information about NIH and its programs, visit www.nih.gov.
NIH…Turning Discovery Into Health®
title: NIH joins effort to build SI-ready data for predictive models of human biology

Grant Extends Microloans and Business Support for Refugee Entrepreneurs
BUFFALO, N.Y. – Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26) today announced a $62,500 federal grant from the Office of Refugee Resettlement for the Westminster Economic Development Initiative (WEDI), extending its Refugee Microenterprise Development project through September 2027. The award will fund the project’s upcoming year, continuing WEDI’s microloans and business-development support for refugees and other eligible newcomers who are starting and growing small businesses in Western New York.
“Refugees and new Americans bring ambition, skill, and strong determination to build a better future for themselves and their family, and a small business is one of the best ways to help them put down roots here in Buffalo,” said Congressman Kennedy. “WEDI has spent years supporting these entrepreneurs with the capital and guidance they need to start a successful business. I’m thrilled to see this funding carry that work forward, and I know that WEDI will use it to make sure that Buffalo continues to live up to its reputation as the City of Good Neighbors.”
“At WEDI, we see every day what can happen when talented, determined entrepreneurs have access to the right resources and capital,” said WEDI Interim Executive Director Courtney Yonce-Swain. “This funding from the Office of Refugee Resettlement has helped us support more than 100 businesses since 2022, giving refugee entrepreneurs greater opportunity to start, stabilize, and grow their businesses. We are incredibly grateful for this additional support and for the opportunity to continue investing in entrepreneurs who strengthen their families, their neighborhoods, and the Western New York economy"
WEDI first received this award in 2022. Through March 31, 2026, the most recent reporting period, it has helped 105 businesses, including more than $94,000 in microloans for start-up, stabilization, and expansion. Founded in 2007, WEDI is a certified Community Development Financial Institution and also operates the West Side Bazaar, a small business incubator on Niagara Street.

MADISON, WIS. – Chadwick M. Elgersma, United States Attorney for the Western District of Wisconsin, announced that Tavares D. Jones, 50, Sun Prairie, Wisconsin, was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge William M. Conley to 1½ years in federal prison for violating the Sex Offender Registration and Notification Act. Jones pleaded guilty to this charge on August 25, 2026. His prison sentence will be followed by five years of supervised release.

In 1999, Jones committed a sex offense involving a minor in Chicago, Illinois. After serving his prison sentence, he moved to Wisconsin and failed to register as a sex offender for more than five years. For part of this time, he lived in a Sun Prairie residence that also violated the terms of his bond conditions in a pending state case. A minor lived in that home.

Explaining the sentence, Judge Conley said Jones’s failure to register presented a “serious public safety concern.” The judge further explained that Jones’s desire to avoid the collateral consequences of registering as a sex offender did not excuse the crime.

The charge against Jones was the result of an investigation conducted by the U.S. Marshals Service. Assistant U.S. Attorney Megan Stelljes prosecuted this case.

This investigation was a part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat child sexual exploitation and abuse. Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc.
title: Sun Prairie Man Sentenced to 1½ Years for Failing to Register as a Sex Offender

Introduces Bipartisan Resolution to Remember 10/7, Combat Terror

TENAFLY, NJ — Today, Wednesday, October 7, 2026, on the third anniversary of the October 7th terrorist attack on Israel, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) joined local leaders, community members, and the family of former hostage Edan Alexander on Edan Alexander Way in Tenafly to remember the victims, honor the hostages and their families, and announce new efforts to combat terror.
