FORT WORTH, Texas — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced that an Afghan citizen residing in Fort Worth pleaded guilty Oct. 6 to transmitting a threatening communication in interstate commerce after threatening to conduct a suicide attack.

Mohammad Dawood Alokozay, a 32-year-old Afghan national, was charged by federal complaint on Nov. 30, 2025, with transmitting a threatening communication in interstate commerce related to threats he made during a social media livestream, which was recorded and posted to multiple social media accounts.

“Threats of suicide bombing are not jokes or momentary outbursts, they are federal crimes,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “The United States has zero-tolerance for any threat to engage in a suicide attack or mass casualty event. We will respond swiftly and decisively to ensure that anyone who engages in this type of behavior faces serious federal consequences.”

“Threats of suicide bombing are not jokes or momentary outbursts, they are federal crimes,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “The United States has zero-tolerance for any threat to engage in a suicide attack or mass casualty event. We will respond swiftly and decisively to ensure that anyone who engages in this type of behavior faces serious federal consequences.”

“The FBI takes online threats of violence seriously and will work with our law enforcement partners to hold individuals accountable for threatening the safety of others. I want to thank the members of the public who came forward to report the defendant’s video. Their timely action contributed to our ability to quickly identify the defendant and secure this guilty plea. We continue to urge the public to report threatening communications to law enforcement," said FBI Dallas Special Agent in Charge R. Joseph Rothrock.

According to court documents, on Nov. 23, 2025, Alokozay participated in an online video chat group with several individuals, including Victim 1, who is also from Afghanistan. Alokozay and the others exchanged highly offensive insults based on longstanding tribal animosity. Alokozay threatened to conduct a "suicide attack" against Victim 1 and the others using a "suicide bomb." Portions of the exchange were recorded and uploaded to the social media platform TikTok.

Federal agents and local partners quickly identified and located Alokozay and executed a search warrant at his residence and on his mobile phone to confirm he had no bomb‑making materials and concluded that the defendant did not intend to carry out an attack. Alokozay admitted in court documents that he knowingly transmitted a threat to injure another person through interstate and foreign commerce.

Alokozay pleaded guilty before U.S. Magistrate Judge Jeffrey L. Cureton on Oct 6. He faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison, a fine of up to $250,000, and up to three years of supervised release. A sentencing date will be set by the Court.

The FBI Dallas, Fort Worth Resident Agency conducted the investigation with assistance from Homeland Security Investigations Dallas, the Texas Department of Public Safety and the Fort Worth Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Vincent Mazzurco from the National Security-Cybercrime section is prosecuting the case.

title: Afghan national pleads guilty to federal charge after online suicide attack threat

Las Vegas Man Sentenced to 40 Months in Prison for Distributing Methamphetamine and Heroin

LAS VEGAS – A Las Vegas man who admitted to selling methamphetamine and heroin was sentenced today by Chief United States District Judge Andrew P. Gordon to 40 months in prison followed by 3 years of supervised release. The government recommended a sentence of 60 months in prison.

“Our office remains fiercely committed to removing dangerous drug traffickers from our communities,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “This sentence sends a clear, definitive message that individuals who profit from fueling addiction in Nevada will be held fully accountable under federal law.”

“While methamphetamine remains one of the deadliest drugs, heroin has not gone away,” said David S. Olesky, Special Agent in Charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration Los Angeles Field Division, which covers Nevada. “These two highly destructive drugs threaten the health and safety of our community. The DEA stands united with our law enforcement partners in pursuing drug traffickers whose poison brings harm to Americans. Today’s sentencing proves that no drug criminal—regardless of their role in the supply chain—is above the law.”

Between August 2024, and October 3, 2024, Juan Carlos Barrera-Cortez, also known as “Rafael,” and co-conspirators Jesus Lomeli-Lopez and Eduardo Perez were part of a conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine and heroin in Las Vegas. As part of the drug conspiracy, Lomeli-Lopez would accept the drug orders by phone from customers, and he and Barrera-Cortez would then meet with the customers to sell the methamphetamine and heroin. Perez would provide Barrera-Cortez and Lomeli-Lopez with the drugs to sell the customers. Over the course of the conspiracy, Barrera-Cortez distributed approximately 3.4 pounds of methamphetamine, and approximately 8.951 grams of heroin. Methamphetamine is a Schedule II controlled substance, and Heroin is a Schedule I controlled substance

Barrera-Cortez pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine and heroin. Lomeli-Lopez pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine and heroin. He was sentenced to five years in prison. Perez is awaiting a jury trial set to begin on January 25, 2027.

First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada and Special Agent in Charge David Olesky for the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Los Angeles Field Division, which oversees Nevada, made the announcement.

The DEA investigated the case. Assistant United States Attorney Joshua Brister prosecuted the case.

###
title: Las Vegas Man Sentenced to 40 Months in Prison for Distributing Methamphetamine and Heroin

LITTLE ROCK—The two men responsible for distributing fentanyl to an individual who later died will now spend decades in federal prison. Today, Erick Williams, 49, of Pine Bluff, was sentenced to 240 months, or 20 years, in prison, followed by three years of supervised release. Earlier, Cortell Randolph, 48, of North Little Rock, the man who provided the fentanyl directly to the victim, was sentenced to 292 months in federal prison, also followed by three years of supervised release. Jonathan D. Ross, United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Arkansas, announced the sentences, which were both handed down by Chief United States District Judge Kristine G. Baker. There is no parole in the federal system.

A federal grand jury indicted Williams and Randolph on August 1, 2023, in the three-count Indictment that involved a fentanyl conspiracy that resulted in the death of an individual identified in court documents as A.M. In addition to the conspiracy count that charged both defendants, Randolph was also charged with the actual distribution of fentanyl that resulted in the death and for being a felon in possession of a firearm.

Randolph pleaded guilty to distributing the fentanyl that resulted in A.M.’s death and was sentenced to more than 24 years on June 27, 2024. Williams subsequently pleaded guilty to the fentanyl conspiracy charge on November 7, 2025, and was sentenced today.

Following the overdose death of A.M. at a hotel in Little Rock on June 28, 2023, the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and Little Rock Police Department (LRPD) began an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the death. The investigation revealed that while at a drug rehab facility, A.M. received the phone number for Randolph from an associate who knew that Randolph sold fentanyl. During the evening of June 27, 2023, Randolph sold fentanyl to A.M., who used it and died as a result.

The following day, law enforcement apprehended Randolph when he arrived at the same hotel intending to sell more fentanyl. Randolph had fentanyl and scales in his possession. After Randolph was taken into custody, officers learned that Randolph had been obtaining fentanyl from Williams, including the fentanyl that Randolph sold to A.M. The DEA and LRPD then determined that Williams was staying at a different hotel in Little Rock and took him into custody at that hotel when he exited his room. Williams also had fentanyl in his possession when arrested.

The investigation was conducted by the Drug Enforcement Administration with assistance from the Little Rock Police Department. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Chris Givens.

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) released the fourth and final installment of $3.3 million in previously approved funding for the Disaster Case Management Program (DCMP), completing the release of federal funding previously awarded to support survivors of the January 2025 Eaton and Palisades Fires

On September 30, 2026, following sustained pressure from Reps. Chu and Sherman and Sens. Schiff and Padilla, FEMA released the second and third installments of DCMP funding, totaling $6.6 million, on the same day the program was set to face a major funding cliff.

Rep. Chu, who has led congressional efforts to secure federal disaster assistance, tax relief, and long-term recovery resources for Eaton Fire survivors, repeatedly pressed FEMA to release the outstanding DCMP funds. She has also urged FEMA to approve California’s separate request for supplemental funding needed to sustain the program and ensure survivors can continue receiving case management services.

Rep. Chu released the following statement:

“I am relieved that FEMA has finally released the full amount of previously approved funding for the DCMP. This money was already approved and set aside for survivors. There was no reason to withhold it and jeopardize critical recovery resources for thousands. Now, Californians can keep getting help navigating temporary housing and loan assistance without fear of being left to fend for themselves mid-process. And hundreds of case managers can keep supporting survivors without worrying about losing their jobs. However, FEMA must do the right thing and approve the State of California’s appeal for additional supplemental funding to sustain DCMP through the full 24-month timeframe that FEMA itself approved.

Further, President Trump must still fully fund Governor Newsom’s disaster supplemental request with no strings attached so our communities get the full federal recovery support they have waited far too long to receive. I will keep fighting until every survivor gets every dollar they are owed to rebuild and recover.”
title: Rep. Chu Commends FEMA Release of Final Installment of Wildfire Survivor Case Management Funding

Rep. Frankel Introduces Bipartisan Resolution Marking Three Years Since October 7 Terrorist Attacks on Israel
West Palm Beach, FL — Today, to mark three years since the October 7 terrorist attacks on Israel, Rep. Lois Frankel (D-FL-22) joined colleagues in introducing a bipartisan resolution condemning Hamas’s horrific atrocities, honoring the victims and hostages, and calling for the complete disarmament of Hamas and an end to ongoing conflict in Gaza.
On October 7, 2023, Hamas and its accomplices stormed Israel, brutally murdering more than 1,200 people, committing horrific acts of sexual violence, and abducting 251 hostages, including Americans and citizens of more than 40 countries.
The resolution honors those murdered, the hostages, and their families; welcomes the return of the hostages; reaffirms Israel’s right to self-defense and long-term security; and supports a durable cease-fire and full implementation of the framework to end the war—including Hamas’s disarmament, increased humanitarian assistance and reconstruction for Gazans, and future governance in Gaza without Hamas. It also condemns the rise in antisemitism in the United States and around the world.
“Three years later, the horror of October 7 remains seared into our hearts,” said Rep. Frankel. “We remember those who were murdered, honor the survivors and hostages and their families, and stand firmly against antisemitism and terrorism. Now we must build a future where Hamas is disarmed, Israel is safe and secure, and Palestinians and Israelis can live in peace and dignity.”
The bipartisan resolution is led by Reps. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-05), Lois Frankel (D-FL-22), Joe Wilson (R-SC-02), and Young Kim (R-CA-40).

The Federal Trade Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture launched a joint public inquiry regarding issues affecting agricultural equipment manufacturing and distribution markets, including potential anticompetitive conduct.
The joint request for information is a part of the FTC’s ongoing work to preserve competition in the agricultural sector. This work includes the FTC’s recent settlement, joined by twelve states, enjoining Corteva Inc.’s alleged anticompetitive conduct in pesticides markets, as well as the FTC’s settlement, joined by five states, of an antitrust action challenging repair restrictions imposed by farm equipment manufacturer Deere & Company. The settlement with Deere ensures that farmers can enjoy the right to repair their own John Deere tractors and farm equipment.
The joint RFI seeks to address the growing number of complaints received by USDA that farmers across the country face other barriers to acquiring agricultural equipment and the services required to keep equipment operating.
The FTC and the USDA encourage members of the public, including farmers, independent repair providers and current and former employees of agricultural equipment manufacturers and dealers, to comment on any issues or concerns that are relevant to this topic, including:
- Any relevant business models, policies, agreements or contractual terms
- Any firsthand experiences or documented cases of restrictions, penalties or retaliation
- Broader competitive implications—how these practices may impact pricing, market entry, innovation, farmer welfare or rural economic resilience
This information will help both the FTC and USDA ensure that the marketplace for agricultural equipment remains fair and that farmers can continue to put food on Americans’ tables.
Comments can be submitted at Regulations.gov and must be received no later than December 7, 2026, by 11:59 p.m. The information will be used by the FTC and USDA to inform enforcement and regulatory priorities and future actions.
The Federal Trade Commission works to promote competition and to protect and educate consumers. The FTC will never demand money, make threats, tell you to transfer money, or promise you a prize. You can learn more about how competition benefits consumers, file an antitrust complaint, or comment on a proposed merger. For the latest news and resources, follow the FTC on social media, subscribe to press releases and read our blog.
title: FTC and USDA Seek Public Comment on Agricultural Equipment Manufacturing and Distribution Market Practices

WASHINGTON – Abdul Fields, 30, a previously convicted felon residing in the District, was sentenced today in U.S. District Court to 180 months in federal prison in connection with a March 2025 street shooting and a separate November 2025 incident in which he possessed a loaded ghost gun, both while he was on supervised release for a prior manslaughter conviction, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

“Despite multiple prior convictions, Abdul Fields persistently and dangerously armed himself, endangered the community, and demonstrated a clear disregard for the law,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “Today’s sentence reflects the seriousness of his conduct and our commitment to protecting the residents of the District from violent gun offenders.”

“Despite multiple prior convictions, Abdul Fields persistently and dangerously armed himself, endangered the community, and demonstrated a clear disregard for the law,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “Today’s sentence reflects the seriousness of his conduct and our commitment to protecting the residents of the District from violent gun offenders.”

Fields pleaded guilty on June 3, 2026, before U.S. District Judge Richard J. Leon to assault with a dangerous weapon and to possession of a firearm during a crime of violence, both in violation of D.C. Code, as well as unlawful possession of ammunition by a felon, a federal offense. In addition to the 180‑month prison term, Judge Leon ordered Fields to serve three years of supervised release.

According to court documents, Fields carried out two illegal firearms offenses within six months while he was on supervised release for a prior voluntary manslaughter conviction.

On March 24, 2025, about 12:26 a.m., Fields was in the crosswalk at the busy intersection of New York Avenue and North Capitol Street NW when he pulled out a pistol and fired it at the driver’s side of a passing vehicle. ShotSpotter detected the gunfire, and CCTV footage captured him pulling the firearm from his coat pocket and discharging a round as the vehicle made a routine right turn.

Ninety seconds later, Fields entered the nearby Tyler House Apartments, where he was living under GPS monitoring. Police recovered a nine-millimeter casing in the middle of the crosswalk and later linked it, through NIBIN analysis, to a ghost gun found in Fields’ residence during the execution of a search warrant.

On November 19, 2025, MPD officers arrested Fields on an outstanding warrant for simple assault after spotting him outside Tyler House Apartments. During a search incident to arrest, officers recovered a loaded ghost gun – an untraceable, privately manufactured firearm without a serial number -- tucked into his waistband.

Fields attempted to reach for the gun, struggled with officers, and headbutted one of them during the encounter. Moments after the gun was recovered, Fields told officers, referencing the recovery of the firearm, “S**t I’ll be back. That s**t ain’t nothing.” When the officer responded, “You’re a felon too,” Fields replied, “I don’t give a f**k. Eat my d**k…I’m superman.”

The firearm, which lacked a serial number, was loaded with one round in the chamber and 11 additional rounds in the magazine.

Fields’ convictions in this case mark at least his third and fourth gun related offenses since 2013. His criminal history includes a 2013 armed robbery and the 2014 killing of Donta Thrower behind Tyler House Apartments, for which he served more than eight years in prison. After his release in February 2024, Fields repeatedly violated supervision and continued to arm himself with illegal firearms.

This case was investigated by the Metropolitan Police Department, and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives - Washington Field Division.

The matter was prosecuted under the Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful initiative by Assistant U.S. Attorney Travis Wolf.

Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful supports President Trump's Executive Order that cracks down on gun violence, prioritizes federal firearms violations, pursues tougher penalties, and seeks detention for federal firearms violators.

He was arrested after he was caught in public with his pants off, fully exposing himself, in a residential neighborhood near a park with residents, including children, in the area.
“It’s unbelievable that Janelle Stelson would employ an illegal alien to work on a Congressional campaign, let alone a pervert who exposed himself in public,” said ICE Deputy Director Charles Wall.“Every single day, the men and women of DHS are working hard to target and remove dangerous illegal aliens like this sicko from our communities. The Trump Administration will always put the safety of the American people first.”
Igbojekwe was lawfully admitted to the United States in June 2017. After his authorized period expired in November 2019, he illegally remained in the United States. He was granted deferred action by the Biden Administration in September 2021.

ALBANY, Ga. – Two South Georgia residents are facing up to life in federal prison after admitting to distributing methamphetamine in the Valdosta, Georgia, community.

“Repeat felons who continue distributing deadly, addictive illegal drugs in the Middle District of Georgia will face federal prosecution, where there is no parole,” said U.S. Attorney William R. “Will” Keyes. “We are working closely with our law enforcement partners at every level to identify these cases, and hold repeat offenders accountable.”

“The investigators in this case did an excellent job, and their dedication helps protect the citizens of Lowndes County,” said Lowndes County Sheriff Ashley Paulk. “We are grateful for the strong partnership we share with our federal, state, and local partners, which strengthens our efforts to keep this community safe.”

Melissa Lynn James, 41, of Naylor, Georgia, pleaded guilty on Oct. 7, and Ryan Daniel Williams, 28, also of Naylor, pleaded guilty on Oct. 6, both to one count of possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine before Senior U.S. District Judge W. Louis Sands. James and Williams face a mandatory minimum of 10 years in prison, up to a maximum sentence of life in prison, to be followed by at least five years of supervised release, and a maximum fine of $10 million. There is no parole in the federal system.

According to court documents and statements made in court, a Lowndes County Sheriff’s Office investigator received a tip from a concerned citizen in November 2025 that Williams was distributing methamphetamine in the community. Williams, who has prior state convictions for methamphetamine possession, possession of a firearm by a convicted felon, and burglary, was a fugitive at the time, wanted for a probation violation out of Glynn County, Georgia. Investigators conducted a controlled purchase of methamphetamine from Williams and James on Nov. 4, 2025, at the Big Foot Truck Stop on West Hill Avenue in Lowndes County. Williams attempted to flee when officers approached, throwing a bag containing 11 grams of methamphetamine, but he was quickly apprehended. James, who was in the passenger seat of the car, moved into the driver’s seat but stopped when ordered by deputies.

During a search of the car, officers found four plastic baggies containing a total of 81 grams of methamphetamine, along with a digital scale with methamphetamine residue, and James’s iPhone. A lawful search of James’s home, where Williams was staying, recovered additional methamphetamine, including two zip-lock bags in James’s bedroom containing approximately 854 grams of methamphetamine, a digital scale with methamphetamine residue, and a glass smoking pipe. In addition, officers found 151 grams of methamphetamine in plain view on the kitchen counter. Investigators also recovered text conversations on James’s iPhone between James and individuals seeking to purchase methamphetamine.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

The Lowndes County Sheriff’s Office is investigating the case, with assistance from the District Attorney’s Office for the Southern Judicial Circuit.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Sonja Profit is prosecuting the case for the Government.
title: Two South Georgia Residents Face Life in Prison for Meth Distribution
Grand Jury Indicts Wichita Man for Trafficking Methamphetamine

WASHINGTON – Jerrad Anthony Childs, 27, of the District of Columbia, was sentenced today in U.S. District Court to 72 months in prison in connection with a fentanyl and crack cocaine trafficking operation out of a Southeast Washington apartment that involved seven firearms and body armor, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

“Child’s apartment was stocked like an arsenal, with seven firearms, hundreds of rounds of ammunition and body armor, all to protect a drug operation that was pumping fentanyl and crack cocaine into our neighborhoods,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “This office will continue dismantling armed drug‑trafficking networks and holding the people who run them accountable.”

“Child’s apartment was stocked like an arsenal, with seven firearms, hundreds of rounds of ammunition and body armor, all to protect a drug operation that was pumping fentanyl and crack cocaine into our neighborhoods,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “This office will continue dismantling armed drug‑trafficking networks and holding the people who run them accountable.”

Childs, aka “heavyglocksosa,” pleaded guilty on April 22, 2026, before U.S. District Judge Loren L. AliKhan to one count of possession with intent to distribute fentanyl, crack cocaine and cocaine, and to one count of possessing a firearm during and in relation to a drug trafficking crime. In addition to the 72-month prison term, Judge AliKhan ordered Childs to serve five years of supervised release. Federal prosecutors had requested a prison sentence of 124 months.

According to court papers, on Oct. 7, 2025, law enforcement executed a search warrant at an apartment in the 3900 block of 1st Street SE, a residence used by Childs.

Inside the apartment, law enforcement recovered seven firearms, including several semi-automatic pistols and a rifle with an obliterated serial number, along with 296 rounds of ammunition and tactical body armor.

Investigators also seized about 168 grams of fentanyl, 40 grams of crack cocaine, and 10 grams of cocaine, along with $18,581.99 in cash.

Childs admitted that he possessed the drugs with intent to distribute them and that he used and possessed the firearms in furtherance of that drug trafficking.

The investigation was conducted by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and the Metropolitan Police Department.

The matter was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney George Eliopoulos of the Violent Crime and Narcotics Trafficking Section.

EUGENE, Ore.—A Bend, Oregon, man was sentenced to federal prison today for robbery and use of a firearm during a crime of violence.

Russell Ian Boggess, 43, was sentenced to 125 months in federal prison and 5 years’ supervised release.

According to court documents, on July 23, 2024, Boggess robbed a cannabis dispensary in Bend at gunpoint. Boggess was armed with a 9mm handgun, carried a bag, and wore a bandana covering his face. He pointed his gun at an employee and demanded the employee give him marijuana stored behind the counter. While pointing the gun near the employee, Boggess tried to fire the gun twice, but it jammed both times. Boggess then walked behind the counter and took the marijuana himself. Boggess pistol whipped the employee when the employee attempted to call 911.

Officers from the Bend Police Department (BPD) responded to the scene within minutes of the robbery and took Boggess into custody. BPD recovered the gun containing a 34-round magazine. The gun was later test fired and was found to be operational.

On September 19, 2024, a federal grand jury in Eugene returned a 3-count indictment charging Boggess with interference with commerce by threats or violence, felon in possession of ammunition, and use and carry of a firearm during and in relation to a crime of violence.

This case was investigated by FBI and BPD. It was prosecuted by Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Matthew Nelson and Assistant U.S. Attorney William McLaren.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities.
title: Bend Man Sentenced to Federal Prison for Armed Robbery

SIOUX FALLS - United States Attorney Ron Parsons announced today that U.S. District Judge Karen E. Schreier has sentenced a Sioux Falls, South Dakota, man convicted of Conspiracy to Distribute a Controlled Substance. The sentencing took place on October 5, 2026.

Shawn Willis, 35, was sentenced to 11 years in federal prison, followed by five years of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund.

Willis was indicted for Conspiracy to Distribute a Controlled Substance by a federal grand jury in October 2025. He pleaded guilty on July 23, 2026.

Sioux Falls Police Department officers encountered Willis after he was found passed out behind the wheel of a running vehicle. Officers eventually searched the vehicle and found approximately 350 grams of methamphetamine and a pistol. Investigators discovered that Willis was part of a methamphetamine distribution organization that obtained methamphetamine from Omaha and California and then distributed it in Sioux Falls. Investigators determined that Willis was responsible for distributing over two pounds of methamphetamine during his involvement in the conspiracy.

This case was investigated by the Sioux Falls Police Department, Sioux Falls Area Drug Task Force, and Homeland Security Investigations. Assistant U.S. Attorney Mark Hodges prosecuted the case.

Willis was immediately remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service.
title: Sioux Falls Man Sentenced to 11 Years in Federal Prison for Conspiracy to Distribute Methamphetamine

Last Friday, U.S. Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02) commented on the news that Canada is fast-tracking a new oil pipeline project that would increase oil tanker traffic in Larsen’s district: 
“This project is not ready for prime time, and speeding up the review process will only make that worse,” said Rep. Larsen in the Washington State Standard. “Canada’s plan to fast track this new oil pipeline project puts sensitive marine habitats at risk and raises the chance of a devastating spill occurring before the U.S. and Canada can put updated plans in place.” 
On July 2, the Government of Alberta announced a proposed new oil pipeline from Alberta to the Pacific Ocean that would transport 1 million barrels per day to an export terminal at Roberts Banks in British Columbia. Last Thursday, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney designated the pipeline, now known as the Pacific Link, as a project of national interest, enabling a speedier regulatory review that could see pipeline design and construction underway by next fall. The new pipeline will increase tanker traffic in Haro Strait and Boundary Bay in the Salish Sea, and with it the risks for catastrophic oil spills impacting sensitive marine environments.  
“The people I represent have serious concerns about this new pipeline and how it could harm the Salish Sea,” continued Rep. Larsen. “They deserve answers to their questions and updated spill response plans that account for more oil tanker traffic, and I will keep fighting to get them both." 
Last month, Rep. Larsen’s staff observed a joint exercise between the U.S. Coast Guard and the Canadian Coast Guard designed to simulate response efforts and coordination between the two countries in the event of an oil spill in shared waters. 
“This type of collaboration across the border between the U.S. and Canada is even more critical because of Canada’s plans to ship more oil in the Salish Sea with the proposed new Alberta to B.C. pipeline,” said Rep. Larsen. “I have concerns about the potential impacts of this proposed pipeline, including on tanker traffic in the Salish Sea, and I am glad that my staff could observe the exercise to ensure that there are relationships and procedures in place that benefit both countries in the event of a disastrous spill.” 
Rep. Larsen is the top Democrat on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, which has oversight authority over the U.S. Coast Guard. In July, Rep. Larsen sent a letter to Admiral Kevin E. Lunday, Commandant of the Coast Guard, to insist that the Coast Guard review and update its oil spill preparedness plans in light of the new proposed pipeline. Larsen also pressed Coast Guard officials on their awareness of the new Canadian pipeline and how it would implicate existing oil spill prevention plans at a committee hearing. A video clip from that hearing can be found here, and the recording of the entire roundtable can be found here. 
The Washington State Standard article is available here and below.  
A proposed Canadian oil pipeline to a supertanker terminal at the Port of Vancouver in British Columbia is raising hackles among Washington state’s political leaders.  
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Thursday designated the West Coast Oil Pipeline, now known as the Pacific Link, as a project of national interest. That enables a speedier regulatory review that could see pipeline design and construction under way by next fall. 
In response, Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson on Friday sounded alarms about increased oil spill risk to the Salish Sea in his first public comments on the massive project. 
It would run from the Edmonton region to a new export terminal capable of handling supertankers proposed for Port of Vancouver’s Roberts Bank in British Columbia just north of the U.S. border. Oil could flow through by the early 2030s. 
Once operating, many more oil-filled vessels traveling from the port would pass by the San Juan Islands and Olympic Peninsula on their way to Asia. Project critics fear a spill could easily reach north Puget Sound, the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Washington’s outer coast, threatening sensitive ecosystems and killer whale habitat.  
Ferguson said Friday that he was “disappointed” at the decision because resources needed to respond to a major spill are insufficient today. 
“If a project of this scale is going to proceed, it needs to come with a corresponding commitment to also increase our region’s capacity to prevent and respond to a catastrophic spill,” he said in a joint statement with Casey Sixkiller, director of the state Department of Ecology. 
“If this project proceeds, it is critical that the Canadian government make detailed commitments to safeguard our shared marine waters and fill these gaps in our response capabilities,” he and Sixkiller said in the statement. 
San Juan County council members, northern Washington tribal representatives and others have been pushing Ferguson since July to speak out and engage with the Canadian provincial and federal governments about the crude pipeline and tanker traffic. 
On Tuesday, Ferguson met with Mark Wiseman, Canada’s ambassador to the U.S. in Seattle. It is not known if the two discussed the pipeline and Ferguson’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the meeting. 
Sixkiller dispatched a lengthy letter to Canadian Intergovernmental Affairs Minister Dominic LeBlanc in mid-September in a vain bid to forestall the fast-tracking of the Alberta pipeline permitting. 
U.S. Rep. Rick Larsen of Everett, whose 2nd Congressional District includes the state waters through which the supertankers would travel, was equally vexed. Many questions about the project and oil spill response need answers, he said. 
“This project is not ready for prime time, and speeding up the review process will only make that worse,” he said in an email. “Canada’s plan to fast track this new oil pipeline project puts sensitive marine habitats at risk and raises the chance of a devastating spill occurring before the U.S. and Canada can put updated plans in place.” 
The project comes as Canada looks to strengthen its economic ties beyond the U.S. and as Carney has said the nation is seeking to become an “energy superpower.” 
Smith has said the province chose a southern pipeline route that ends on the shores of the Salish Sea because it can take advantage of the existing Trans Mountain Pipeline corridor as well as established relationships with First Nations. 
Northern Washington tribes, including the Lummi, Samish, Swinomish and Makah, strongly opposed a previous Canadian pipeline expansion. The tribes argue that the large increase in vessel traffic endangers their treaty rights and threatens vital fisheries. 
Maithili Devadas of the Georgia Strait Alliance, an environmental group in British Columbia fighting the export terminal proposed at Roberts Bank, panned Carney’s announcement. 
“It would be reasonable to expect that a project with the potential to shape the environmental, economic, and social future of a region for decades to come would face an especially rigorous level of scrutiny. Instead, this project is being fast-tracked without any concern for its long-term impacts on ecosystems, communities and the people who depend on them,” she wrote in an update to supporters Friday.
title: Larsen: New B.C. Oil Pipeline is “Not Ready for Prime Time”

text:
Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03), a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, released a discussion draft of the Clear Liability for Artificial Intelligence Misconduct (CLAIM) Act. The legislation would give those harmed by AI agents a clear path to recovery by holding developers responsible when their systems engage in conduct that would be unlawful if committed by a person.
 
“When someone breaks the law and hurts you, you can take them to court. That shouldn't change just because the wrongdoer is an AI agent,” said Congresswoman Trahan. “Developers have already built systems capable of acting on their own and causing real damage. The CLAIM Act makes sure they answer for what their systems do.”
Specifically, the CLAIM Act:
    - Holds developers liable for AI misconduct. If an AI system injures a third party through conduct that would constitute negligence, an intentional tort, or a crime if committed by a person, the developer is liable. Liability does not apply where the user or a company that modified the system intended the conduct or was negligent.
- Resolves uncertainty around AI and intent. Courts would presume an AI system acted with the state of mind a person taking the same actions would have had. Developers could not argue that AI is incapable of intent.
- Establishes a federal cause of action. Injured parties may bring claims in federal or state court.
- Preserves state law. The bill sets a federal floor and does not preempt any state law. Existing state claims and state AI laws remain fully available.
The risks the CLAIM Act addresses already exist. In July, AI agents undergoing an evaluation by OpenAI escaped their test environment and hacked into Hugging Face, another AI company. No one instructed them to do so. Leading experts have called the incident a warning shot for a future of increasingly capable AI agents acting outside their users’ control.
Under current law, third parties harmed by a misaligned AI agent face significant hurdles. Many serious harms, including hacking and fraud, require proof of intent, and courts have not settled whether an AI system’s conduct can meet that standard. Negligence and product liability claims typically require showing that a company failed to take a specific precaution or ignored a safer design. Because AI alignment remains an unsolved technical problem, developers can argue the harm occurred despite their best efforts, leaving injured parties without a remedy.
The CLAIM Act complements the bipartisan FRONTIER Act, which Trahan introduced with Rep. Jay Obernolte (R-CA) to address catastrophic risks from the most advanced AI models. FRONTIER establishes transparency, independent verification, and incident reporting requirements. The CLAIM Act adds a robust liability regime that rewards developers who invest in making their systems safer.
Trahan is releasing the CLAIM Act as a discussion draft and welcomes feedback from experts, industry, advocates, and the public. In addition to comments on the draft legislation, the office welcomes answers to important questions related to the CLAIM Act and AI liability located HERE.
Comments can be submitted to MA03Leg@mail.house.gov.
A copy of the bill text can be accessed HERE.
A one-pager is available HERE.
title: Trahan Unveils CLAIM Act Discussion Draft to Hold AI Developers Accountable for Harms Caused by Their Agents

Board Chairman and Co-Owner of Puerto Rican Bank Sentenced in Multimillion-Dollar Wire Fraud Conspiracy
The former board chairman and co-owner of Nodus International Bank (Nodus Bank), a Puerto Rican International Banking Entity, was sentenced today to 62 months in prison, three years of supervised release, and to pay forfeiture of approximately $13.6 million, which represents the value of the proceeds he derived from the wire fraud conspiracy. Juan Francisco Ramirez, 60, of Miami, Florida, led a scheme to fraudulently obtain more than $23.6 million from Nodus Bank.
“This defendant abused the trust of his bank’s depositors, and when the bank went under, innocent people lost their savings,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “The Criminal Division won’t stand for it. We will use every resource at our disposal to protect this country’s financial system and the decent, hardworking people who rely on it.”
“Ramirez was entrusted to lead a bank. Instead, he looted it. He secretly steered millions of dollars in bank funds to benefit himself and his associates, causing nearly $24 million in losses and contributing to the bank’s collapse,” said U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida. “Today, he was sentenced to 62 months in federal prison and ordered to forfeit more than $13 million. This sentence sends a clear message: those who abuse positions of trust to enrich themselves will be held accountable.”
“Financial frauds can be complicated, but the law is simple: do your business honestly and protect your depositors, or you will be brought to justice,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Charles Miller of the IRS Criminal Investigation Florida Field Office. “IRS Special Agents, alongside our partners, will keep bringing transparency to complex financial crimes and protecting confidence in our banking system.”
In September 2025, Ramirez pleaded guilty to an information charging one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud.
According to court documents, Ramirez conspired with others to siphon money from Nodus Bank. Ramirez and a co-conspirator concealed from other Nodus Bank board members and executives, and the bank’s regulator — the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Institutions of Puerto Rico (OCIF) — that certain investments or loans were for the benefit of Ramirez and a co-conspirator, in violation of Puerto Rican law and Nodus Bank policy regarding insider transactions.
From 2017 to 2023, Ramirez conspired with others to invest more than $11 million of Nodus Bank’s funds in a Miami-based lender so that it could loan those funds to Ramirez and a co-conspirator for their own benefit. Ramirez and his co-conspirators knew that these transactions were illegal and took steps to conceal their prohibited nature by having the bank make sham investments in the lending entity.
Between January 2018 and September 2021, Ramirez and a co-conspirator fraudulently induced Nodus Bank’s board and comptroller to agree to, or facilitate, the purchase of at least 47 promissory notes totaling approximately $25.3 million from Miami-based finance company that Ramirez and the co-conspirator jointly owned. These promissory notes purported to fund loans to legitimate individuals or businesses, but in fact Ramirez and the co-conspirator used the loan proceeds for their own benefit, including to make personal investments in third-party companies, pay personal mortgages, or cover personal credit card expenses.
In early March 2023, OCIF notified Nodus Bank of its intention to place the Bank into liquidation, and later that month Nodus Bank agreed to enter into a voluntary liquidation. On April 28, 2023, knowing that the liquidation process would commence imminently and without authorization from OCIF, Ramirez and a co-conspirator caused Nodus Bank to purchase from their Miami-based finance company a loan portfolio totaling approximately $26 million. Most of these loans were delinquent, nonperforming, and otherwise uncollateralized. Ramirez and a co-conspirator caused Nodus Bank to accept the loan portfolio as payment of their Miami-based finance company’s debt arising from the 47 promissory notes that Nodus Bank had purchased during 2018 to 2021. This resulted in a direct benefit to the finance company — and Ramirez and his co-conspirator — by relieving the finance company of its debt to the bank.
Ramirez’s actions caused Nodus Bank to lose at least $23,613,371.
IRS-CI investigated the case with support from OCIF and Treasury Executive Office for Asset Forfeiture.
Trial Attorneys Javier Urbina and Samir Paul of the Criminal Division’s Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section (MNF) and Assistant U.S. Attorney Felipe Plechac-Diaz for the Southern District of Florida are prosecuting the case.
This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Miami comprises agents and officers from IRS Criminal Investigation with the prosecution being led by Bank Integrity Unit of MNF and by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Florida.
MNF’s mission is to take the profit out of crime, eliminate drug cartels, and protect the U.S. financial system. MNF pursues criminal prosecutions and criminal and civil asset recovery actions involving: financial facilitators who launder profits for criminals; financial institutions and their officers and employees whose actions threaten the U.S. financial system and financial institutions; international money launderers who support transnational organized crime; and the top command and control of international drug trafficking organizations.
MNF’s Bank Integrity Unit investigates and prosecutes banks and other financial institutions, including their officers, managers and employees whose actions threaten the integrity of the individual institution or the wider financial system.
title: Board Chairman and Co-Owner of Puerto Rican Bank Sentenced in Multimillion-Dollar Wire Fraud Conspiracy

MATSUI, SACRAMENTO COUNTY ANNOUNCE $1 MILLION IN FEDERAL FUNDING FOR FLORIN ROAD SAFE STAY COMMUNITY
SACRAMENTO, CA — Today, Congresswoman Doris Matsui (CA-07) held a press conference with Sacramento County leaders and Five Keys to announce $1 million in federal funding for the Florin Road Safe Stay Community.
The federal investment will support the installation of modular sanitation facilities to replace the site’s current mobile units, as well as the creation of permanent outdoor gathering space for guests and their pets. These improvements will help strengthen day-to-day operations and make the site more stable, functional, and supportive for the people it serves.
“This investment will build real restrooms and showers to replace temporary ones and create permanent outdoor space where folks can spend time together,” said Congresswoman Matsui. “Clean, reliable restrooms are a matter of basic dignity, and they keep people healthy. A place to sit outside with a neighbor or a case manager is where trust starts. And trust is what gets someone to say yes to the next step.”
Sacramento County’s latest point-in-time count found more than 7,400 people experiencing homelessness, while also showing more people in shelters than ever before. The Florin Road Safe Stay Community opened three years ago and provides private cabins, meals, showers, laundry, pet accommodations and on-site case management to help people experiencing homelessness move toward permanent housing.
“This infusion of critical funding comes at a pivotal moment in Sacramento County’s mission to continue its success in addressing homelessness in impactful and unique ways,” said District 2 Sacramento County Supervisor Patrick Kennedy. “We’re grateful to Congresswoman Matsui’s tenacity in working for Sacramento, working for the important work of addressing homelessness when funding is rapidly dwindling and we’re grateful for her continued advocacy in Washington.”
“At Florin Safe Stay, we are providing people with something critically important: a safe place to begin again,” said Heather Calomese, president and CEO of Five Keys. “But shelter is not the finish line. It is a bridge from the street to safety, from crisis to stability, and ultimately, from homelessness to a place to call home. Every person who walks through our doors deserves to be treated with dignity, to be seen and to have a real pathway forward.”
The Florin Road Safe Stay Community is operated by Five Keys in partnership with Sacramento County. The $1 million in federal funding is part of Matsui’s ongoing work to deliver federal resources directly to Sacramento-area projects that address local needs.

BUFFALO, N.Y. – U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Welded Tube USA, Inc. has agreed to pay $1,500,000 to resolve allegations that it improperly obtained a Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loan from the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA), which it was not eligible to receive. This action is part of the Trump Administration’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud.

The PPP loan program, enacted in March 2020, provided emergency financial assistance to small businesses during the COVID-19 pandemic. The program allowed eligible small businesses to receive loans guaranteed by the federal government. Regulations provided various eligibility requirements for the PPP, including limitations on the applicants’ number of employees, including employees of the applicants’ foreign affiliates. Specifically, applicants for second draw PPP loans were required, generally, to have 300 or fewer employees.

The United States contends that Welded Tube obtained a forgiven PPP loan that it was not eligible for because it exceeded the size restrictions for a second draw PPP loan. In 2021, when Welded Tube obtained a second draw PPP loan, it was a wholly owned subsidiary of Welded Tube of Canada Corp., a Canadian company. Welded Tube of Canada Corp. and its affiliates collectively had over 300 employees at the time of Welded Tube’s PPP loan.

“We continue to work tirelessly to recover taxpayer dollars that were improperly obtained by ineligible entities,” said U.S. Attorney DiGiacomo. “Through our affirmative civil enforcement efforts, we recovered over $10 million during the 2026 fiscal year related to PPP fraud.”

On April 7, 2026, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

This matter was handled by Assistant U.S. Attorney Jonathan W. Ferris and Investigator Margaret McFarland.

The claims resolved by the settlement are allegations only; there has been no determination or admission of liability.

Editor’s Note: This advisory was updated on Oct. 15, 2026, to reflect the revised spacecraft docking timeline.

NASA and SpaceX are targeting 6:33 a.m. EDT, Tuesday, Oct. 13, for the next launch to deliver science investigations, supplies, and equipment, including the final set of International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Arrays, to the space station. This is the 35th SpaceX commercial resupply services mission to the orbital complex for NASA.

NASA also will host a media teleconference on Thursday, Oct. 8 that will preview the cargo resupply flight, as well as provide a post-splashdown update for the agency’s SpaceX Crew-12 mission, which will have returned to Earth from the space station Thursday morning.

Loaded with more than 6,300 pounds of supplies, a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft on a Falcon 9 rocket will lift off from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Dragon will dock autonomously around 10:30 a.m. on Thursday, Oct. 15, to the space-facing port of the station’s Harmony module.

NASA’s live launch and docking coverage will stream through a variety of platforms. Learn where to watch online:

https://www.nasa.gov/live

In addition to the solar arrays, the Dragon spacecraft will deliver hardware to manufacture artificial retinas in microgravity to help restore vision on Earth and 3D heart tissues models to advance large‑scale drug testing on future missions. The spacecraft will carry materials to study how a new type of glass forms in microgravity and brain organoids that could reveal treatment targets for neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, and multiple sclerosis.

The Dragon spacecraft is scheduled to remain at the space station until mid-November when it will depart the orbiting laboratory and return to Earth with time-critical research and cargo, splashing down off the coast of California.

NASA’s mission coverage is as follows (all times Eastern and subject to change based on real-time operations):

Members of the public can register to attend this launch virtually. NASA’s virtual guest program for this mission also includes curated launch resources, notifications about related opportunities or changes, and a stamp for the NASA virtual guest passport following launch.

Wyden, Merkley, Bonamici, Salinas, Hoyle, Dexter Announce $4.3 Million to Support Public Safety Across Oregon
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley, along with U.S. Representatives Suzanne Bonamici, Andrea Salinas, Val Hoyle, and Maxine Dexter, today announced more than $4.3 million in federal awards to support public safety programs across Oregon.
“It is absolutely essential to ensure communities across Oregon are safe, and young people are able to get the support they need in times of crisis,” Wyden said. “These federal grants will help support local police agencies, youth support programs and resources for foster youth. I’ll keep fighting to secure the federal resources Oregon communities need to thrive and stay secure.”
“Every Oregon community needs the resources to keep young people safe, support children who have experienced abuse and neglect, and build stronger relationships between families and those who serve them,” said Merkley, who helped secure funding for these community-initiated projects as a senior member of the Senate Appropriations Committee. “These federal investments will expand mentorship and opportunities for young people, ensure children have access to critical advocacy and medical services, and strengthen public safety infrastructure in several communities across the state. I’ll keep fighting to bring these federal resources home to Oregon and support the local organizations working every day to make our communities safer.”
“Beaverton’s Behavioral Health Court is doing important work to help people with mental health challenges who encounter the justice system and put them on a path to recovery,” said Bonamici. “I’m grateful this grant will support this initiative, improve lives, and make our communities safer.”
“Investments in emergency response capabilities strengthen our communities,” said Hoyle. “This funding for the Cottage Grove Police Department will replace aging equipment and bolster our emergency preparedness, prioritizing public safety and making it easier for officers to do their jobs.”
“Every child deserves to be safe, cared for, and heard. I’m thrilled to have helped secure over $2 million to protect children across Oregon. Because of this funding, children who have experienced abuse or neglect will not have to navigate some of the hardest moments of their lives alone. They will have an advocate in their corner and a safe place to turn to when they need emotional or medical support. I’m proud to see these federal dollars coming home to support the people doing this vital work in our communities,” Salinas said.
“Our young people deserve to grow up safe, supported and hopeful about their future,” said Dexter, M.D. “I fought hard to bring this $1 million investment to Gresham because children deserve opportunities to succeed. This funding will connect them with mentors, workforce readiness and programs that prevent and reduce involvement in violent crime and strengthen public safety efforts for youth and families in East Multnomah County. Investing in our children makes Oregon stronger.”
The $4.3 million in federal awards from the Department of Justice’s Byrne Discretionary Community Project Grants program will be distributed as follows:
- $1.05 million to the City of Gresham to expand the East Multnomah Outreach Prevention Intervention initiative to prevent and combat juvenile delinquency, reduce youth involvement in violent crime, and strengthen coordinated public safety efforts for youth and families in East Multnomah County.
- $1 million to Liberty House in Salem to increase medical clinic services to children who are victims of abuse or neglect in Marion and Polk Counties.
- $1.03 million to the Oregon CASA Network in Salem to support its work to provide foster children the advocacy and support of an assigned Court Appointed Special Advocate.
- $500,000 to the City of Beaverton to support the Behavioral Health Court program that targets defendants with criminal cases in the Beaverton Municipal Court who are the top utilizers of legal, jail or emergency room services living in the Beaverton area.
- $800,000 to the City of Cottage Grove to support modernizing the Cottage Grove Police Department fleet and communications infrastructure to facilitate a department-wide transition to community-oriented policing practices.
“This funding will support Court Appointed Special Advocate programs across the state in recruiting and retaining volunteers who provide advocacy, encouragement, and a sense of stability to children impacted by abuse and neglect,” said Stephanie Brown, State Director, Oregon CASA Network. “Our advocates are in every corner of the state, getting to know the unique needs of each child they serve, and advocating for them in court, in school, and in the community. We appreciate the efforts of our elected officials to make this valuable investment in Oregon’s future which will help many of the state’s most vulnerable reach their full potential.
“Recovery takes time, care and support," said Beaverton Mayor Lacey Beaty. "Our Behavioral Health Court team understands that and helps participants get treatment and rebuild their lives. I’m proud of the work Judge Britton and her team do every day, and grateful to Senator Wyden and Congresswoman Salinas for supporting it. This investment will make a real difference for our neighbors and the safety of our community.”
title: Wyden, Merkley, Bonamici, Salinas, Hoyle, Dexter Announce $4.3 Million to Support Public Safety Across Oregon

CONCORD – During the federal fiscal year that ended on September 30, 2026, the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of New Hampshire obtained both civil and criminal judgments to recover more than $8.3 million in funds for crime victims and taxpayers, U.S. Attorney Erin Creegan announces.

“While we seek to impose penalties on criminals through convictions and prison sentences, both the criminal and civil divisions of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Hampshire are also hard at work every day seeking financial accountability for bad actors who commit crimes and defraud the public,” said U.S. Attorney Creegan. “These judgments show in real terms that crime and fraud hurt all of us, and they do not pay. Seeking and obtaining these financial judgments fulfills one of our primary responsibilities in the U.S. Attorney’s Office, which is to recover dollars for the public fisc, especially those illegitimately gained through unlawful means.”

Specifically, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Hampshire obtained civil judgments totaling $1,500,000.00, and criminal judgments totaling $6,812,837.21. Civil judgments represent amounts owed to the United States arising from civil penalties, debts to federal agencies, and other monetary obligations, while criminal judgments may include restitution owed to victims, criminal fines, and other court-ordered monetary penalties.

Total collections during FY 2026 for all outstanding civil and criminal judgments in the district amounted to $5,542,260.87. These funds were recovered in part through the efforts of the office’s Financial Litigation Program. The Financial Litigation Program actively monitors cases in which restitution, criminal fines, and civil penalties have been ordered to identify available assets and potential sources of recovery and to maximize collections on behalf of the United States and victims of crime. These recoveries were achieved through a combination of voluntary payments and federal collection and enforcement mechanisms, including the Treasury Offset Program, Bureau of Prisons’ Inmate Financial Responsibility Program, agency offsets of federal benefits, and enforcement actions such as wage or bank garnishments.
title: U.S. Attorney’s Office Obtains Civil and Criminal Judgments to Recover more than $8 Million for Crime Victims and Taxpayers During the 2026 Federal Fiscal Year

ANCHORAGE, Alaska – A former Anchorage defense attorney was sentenced yesterday to 20 years in prison for possessing fentanyl and methamphetamine with the intent to distribute the drugs in Alaska.

According to court documents, Justin Facey, 46, facilitated a drug trafficking organization run by a California prisoner, Heraclio Sanchez-Rodriguez, who was indicted on federal drug trafficking and murder charges in October 2023. To date, over 60 defendants have been charged in connection with the Sanchez-Rodriguez drug trafficking organization.

Facey continued to engage in drug trafficking after the indictment of Sanchez-Rodriguez and other defendants. Between April 2024 and 2025, he utilized his residence to distribute and use controlled substances, including fentanyl and methamphetamine. Facey also possessed multiple firearms in furtherance of his drug trafficking crimes. Facey was suspended from practicing law on February 24, 2025. Prior to suspension, Facey was a practicing defense attorney in Anchorage.

On May 20, 2025, Facey was indicted by a federal grand jury on one count of maintaining a drug-involved premises, one count of possession of firearms in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime, and one count of possession of firearms by a prohibited person. On July 17, 2025, a federal grand jury returned a superseding indictment adding one count of possession of a controlled substance with intent to distribute and one count of possession of methamphetamine with intent to distribute with a minor present. On June 22, 2026, Facey pleaded guilty to one count of possession with intent to distribute fentanyl and methamphetamine.

In handing down the sentence, the Court emphasized that Facey fell far short of his professional responsibility to seek justice, and that he dehumanized and exploited vulnerable women in the course of his drug trafficking.

“Mr. Facey egregiously betrayed his community while taking advantage of his clients and neglecting his ethical responsibilities,” said U.S. Attorney Scott E. Bradford for the District of Oregon. “Facey used his position to promote and personally assist a large-scale drug trafficking organization that endangered Alaskans and other communities. This sentence is a conclusion of a multi-year investigation and demonstrates that anyone who chooses profit over human life will be held accountable.”

“Mr. Facey was driven by greed and power and bragged about being an attorney for the cartel, while he victimized his clients, trafficked fentanyl and meth, and solicited sex in exchange for drug debts,” said Robert A. Saccone, Special Agent in Charge, DEA Seattle Field Division. “He betrayed his oath to uphold the law and spread poison in his community. Through Fentanyl Free America, DEA and our law enforcement partners are disrupting the fentanyl supply chain, reducing its availability, and saving American lives.”

“Mr. Facey used his position as an attorney to fuel a drug trafficking organization operating within Alaska, eroding the public’s trust and safety in the process,” said Special Agent in Charge Matthew Schlegel of the FBI Anchorage Field Office. “This sentencing demonstrates that no one, regardless of position or status, is above the law. The FBI, alongside the DEA and our law enforcement partners, will continue to investigate and hold accountable those who engage in drug trafficking activities.”

The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Alaska has been recused from this case with the exception of certain personnel. Assistant U.S. Attorney Steven D. Clymer from the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of New York has been appointed as Special Attorney to the United States Attorney General to assist with this and other recused cases. He reports to and acts under the direction of the Deputy Attorney General, or his delegee, or U.S. Attorney Bradford in these cases. Special Attorney Clymer supervises personnel from the District of Alaska who have been exempted from the recusal.

The DEA Anchorage District Office and FBI Anchorage Field Office, with assistance from the Anchorage Police Department, investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Adam Alexander and Jennifer Ivers prosecuted the case.

This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Region One comprises agents and officers from Federal Bureau of Investigation; U.S. Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Homeland Security Investigations – Seattle; the United States Attorney’s Office(s) for the Districts of Alaska, Idaho, Oregon, Eastern Washington, and Western Washington; the Drug Enforcement Administration; Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives; U.S. Marshals Service; Internal Revenue Service - Criminal Investigation Division; U.S. Postal Inspection Service; U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP); CBP – Office of Field Operations; CBP – Air & Marine Operations; U.S. Border Patrol; U.S. Coast Guard, Coast Guard Investigative Service; and Transportation Security Administration, Law Enforcement/Federal Air Marshal Service, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Alaska.

David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, announced that AMEER NASIR, 25, of Trumbull, was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge Kari A. Dooley in Bridgeport to 24 months of imprisonment and three years of supervised release for defrauding Amazon.com, Inc. (“Amazon”) of more than $3.5 million.

According to court documents and statements made in court, Amazon Logistics, an Amazon subsidiary, contracts with various interstate trucking businesses to transport both empty trailers and trailers containing heavy loads of freight between cities and between warehouses and fulfillment centers operated by Amazon. Nasir registered 23 trucking businesses with Amazon Logistics. One of the accounts was created in the name of Nasir’s business, Pak Express Transport, LLC, and others were created under false names or by fraudulently using the names and identifying information of other trucking or transportation companies without the knowledge of the operators of those companies. Between approximately December 2019 and February 2021, Nasir used these accounts to sign up for more than 1,000 transportation assignments with Amazon Logistics, manipulated information in Amazon Logistics’ transportation management system to misrepresent that he had completed trailer movements when he had not, and submitted fraudulent invoices to Amazon Logistics that were subsequently paid. Through this scheme, Nasir defrauded Amazon of more than $3.5 million.

Nasir was arrested on May 8, 2025. On March 6, 2026, he pleaded guilty to wire fraud.

Judge Dooley ordered Nasir to pay restitution of $3,547,090.93.

Nasir, who is released on a $300,000 bond, is required to report to prison on November 12.

This matter was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation with assistance from Amazon. The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Elena L. Coronado.
title: Trumbull Man Sentenced to Federal Prison for Defrauding Amazon of More Than $3.5 Million

Atlanta – Garry Haggins, Jr., a convicted drug dealer who served more than a decade in federal prison, was arraigned earlier today on new charges related to his alleged trafficking of approximately 42 kilograms of methamphetamine.

“Drug trafficking threatens the safety and stability of our community,” said U.S. Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg. “My office will continue to work closely with our law enforcement partners to pursue and punish criminals who distribute deadly narcotics.”

“This case is a clear example of the strength of law enforcement partnerships,” said Michael J. Connolly, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the DEA Atlanta Field Division. “Investigators across agencies worked together to track down a convicted felon facing federal charges for trafficking more than 40 kilograms of methamphetamine. That collaboration was critical to ensuring this defendant could no longer evade justice.”

According to U.S. Attorney Hertzberg, the charges, and other information presented in court: In 2009, Garry Haggins, Jr. was convicted of conspiracy to distribute cocaine and cocaine base in the Southern District of Florida and was sentenced to 135 months’ imprisonment. On April 9, 2026, Drug Enforcement Administration agents observed Haggins drive to a parking lot in Ellenwood, Georgia, park next to another vehicle, remove two bags from that vehicle, place those two bags in his vehicle, and quickly depart. Georgia State Patrol troopers later observed Haggins’s vehicle traveling at a high rate of speed. During a subsequent traffic stop, troopers attempted to detain Haggins, but he allegedly resisted and fled the scene, successfully evading capture. A search of Haggins’s vehicle allegedly uncovered approximately 42 kilograms of off-white crystal shards that tested positive for methamphetamine.

On September 18, 2026, after months as a fugitive, Haggins was arrested in Oklahoma and transferred to federal custody.

Today, Garry Haggins, Jr., 43, of Thomasville, Georgia, was arraigned in federal court in Atlanta on an indictment that charged him with possession with the intent to distribute methamphetamine. Haggins was ordered detained in the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service pending further proceedings.

Members of the public are reminded that the indictment only contains charges. The defendant is presumed innocent of the charges, and it will be the government’s burden to prove the defendant’s guilt beyond a reasonable doubt at trial.

This case is being investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration, with valuable assistance provided by the Georgia State Patrol and the Henry County Police Department.

Assistant United States Attorney Edward C. Robinson Jr. is prosecuting the case.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

The U.S. Attorney’s Office in Atlanta recommends parents and children learn about the dangers of drugs at the following web site: www.justthinktwice.gov .

For further information please contact the U.S. Attorney’s Public Affairs Office at USAGAN.PressEmails@usdoj.gov or (404) 581-6185. The Internet address for the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia is http://www.justice.gov/usao-ndga .
title: After Months on the Run, Felon Faces Federal Charges for Trafficking More than 40 Kilograms of Methamphetamine

U.S. Marshals Participate in Operation 10/90 Targeting Violent Offenders in Dallas, TX
For immediate release
Christopher McCarty, Deputy U.S. Marshal
Dallas, TX – The United States Marshals Service (USMS) – North Texas Fugitive Task Force (NTFTF) partnered with the Dallas Police Department to conduct Operation 10/90, an operation focused on targeting the 10 percent of the population who commit crimes against the other 90 percent – the law-abiding citizens within the Dallas communities.
Operation 10/90 was centered on the South Central Division of the City of Dallas, which was chosen based on crime data and feedback from members of the community.
The operation ran from September 1 to September 30, 2026, yielding over 100 arrests; of which 72 were felonies, 10 seized firearms, 2 case referrals to the Northern District of Texas United States Attorney’s Office, and 345 traffic citations as a result of the surge.
One of the many noteworthy arrests made during the operation occurred on September 4, 2026, when the NTFTF partnered with the Dallas Police Department’s South Central Patrol Division to safely apprehend Mysiah Clark, 19, who was already on-bond via a court-ordered ankle monitor as a result of a murder charge in Dallas. He cut off his ankle monitor and allegedly committed a second murder in Forney, Texas.
The operation concluded with a press conference on October 6th, 2026, at the Dallas Police Department Headquarters. The presser highlighted the 20+ year fruitful partnership between the North Texas Fugitive Task Force and the Dallas Police Department.
Sean Malecha, Acting United States Marshal for the Northern District of Texas, stated “The U.S. Marshals Service and its partners stand between the 10 and 90 percent daily, leveraging relationships, resources, and its vast investigative network to find and apprehend the 10 percent wherever they may hide.”
