BOSTON – A Brockton, Mass., man who recently worked as a caregiver for disabled adults in a group home, has been arrested and charged with attempted sex trafficking of a child. The defendant allegedly responded to an advertisement posted by undercover law enforcement for sexual intercourse with an under-age girl.

Jonathan Durocher, 34, was charged with one count of attempted sex trafficking of a child. Durocher was arrested this morning and, following an initial appearance in federal court in Worcester, was released on various conditions, including location monitoring and the requirement that he not have any unsupervised contact with any child younger than 18 years old.

According to court filings, Durocher was arrested as part of a federal law enforcement effort to address human trafficking and the sexual exploitation of children before, during, and after the World Cup matches held in the Boston area in June and July 2026.

Specifically, on June 15, 2026, Durocher allegedly responded to an advertisement posted by law enforcement on a website commonly used for prostitution services. The ad featured images of a young woman or girl and included a link to a phone number operated and monitored by an undercover officer.

Durocher allegedly began exchanging text messages with the undercover officer, who told Durocher that the girl was underage, “beautiful,” and “experienced.” “You good her being young?” the officer asked Durocher, who allegedly responded, “Yeah.” Later that day, Durocher allegedly arrived at the agreed upon meeting location and paid the undercover officer $100. When the officer asked whether Durocher had brought a condom, he allegedly replied that he did not. Durocher was taken into custody. According to court documents, Durocher told officers that worked as a caregiver at Bamsi Home, a residential group home in Brockton. The home serves adults who need daily living assistance because of their developmental disabilities, brain injuries, or other medical needs.

The charge of attempted sex trafficking of a child provides for a sentence of no less than 10 years and up to life in prison, at least five years and up to a lifetime of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Boston Division made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the Massachusetts State Police; and the Boston, New Bedford, and Brockton Police Departments. Assistant U.S. Attorney Amanda Beck is prosecuting the case.

The details contained in the charging document are allegations. The defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in the court of law.
title: Brockton Man Arrested for Attempted Sex Trafficking of a Child

CNO Strengthens Global Maritime Partnerships at 15th Trans-Regional Seapower Symposium
VENICE, Italy – Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle joined senior naval leaders from around the world at the 15th Trans-Regional Seapower Symposium in Venice, Italy, Oct. 6-7, underscoring the importance of international partnerships, maritime security and innovation in addressing shared challenges at sea.
VENICE, Italy – Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle joined senior naval leaders from around the world at the 15th Trans-Regional Seapower Symposium in Venice, Italy, Oct. 6-7, underscoring the importance of international partnerships, maritime security and innovation in addressing shared challenges at sea.
Hosted by the Italian Navy, the symposium brought together the heads of nearly 80 navies from around the world, along with experts from industry, academia, science and technology, to examine how regional maritime challenges increasingly produce global consequences.
Caudle said the symposium provides an important forum for building the relationships needed to confront challenges that transcend national boundaries.
“For 30 years, this symposium has brought naval leaders together here at Venice’s historic Arsenal, a place with centuries of maritime history behind it,” said Caudle. “The challenges we face at sea don’t stop at national borders, and no nation, no matter how capable, can address them alone.”
The 2026 symposium, themed “From Regional Waters to Global Influence: generating effects across the midland seas of the world,” focused on the relationship between regional security challenges and the broader global maritime system. Discussions examined how events in strategically important seas, straits and waterways can affect international trade, economic security, freedom of navigation and global stability.
Caudle participated in the working session “Future Seas: Industrial Scale, Decisive Mass and Innovation, and Securing the Maritime Domain,” joining fellow maritime leaders from Australia, France, Great Britain and Italy to discuss how navies must adapt their forces, industrial capacity and approach to innovation to meet rapidly evolving threats.
The discussion highlighted the growing importance of unmanned systems, autonomy, resilient logistics, advanced manufacturing and closer cooperation between navies and their industrial and technological partners.
For the U.S. Navy, Caudle emphasized that capability and capacity depend not only on what a navy can field, but also on its ability to sustain operations alongside allies and partners around the world.
“We have to be able to pull into [ports] and get the same kit that I can get in the United States,” said Caudle. “We need these solutions to be staged all around the world. That’s how our navies get force multiplication.”
Caudle said achieving that level of interoperability requires relationships and cooperation to be established well before they are tested in a crisis.
“Relationships and cooperation has to begin long before a crisis, not during one,” Caudle said.
The symposium’s other working sessions explored global and regional geopolitical dynamics, maritime regional security, the role of navies in protecting sea-based flows, the changing strategic environment in the Arctic and the leadership skills required to prepare future maritime commanders and Sailors for increasingly complex operating environments.
The gathering comes as naval leaders confront security challenges that increasingly connect once-distinct geographic regions. Disruption or instability in one maritime chokepoint can rapidly affect shipping, supply chains and economies thousands of miles away, making cooperation among maritime nations increasingly important.
Caudle also stressed that responding to those challenges requires navies to make deliberate choices about readiness while maintaining the ability to regenerate forces as operational demands change.
“We can’t surge everywhere indefinitely, so we have to make big decisions on readiness, said Caudle. “You have to not only build and certify those forces, but you have to be able to regenerate them and do that in timing and tempo as the situation demands.”
Throughout the symposium, Caudle engaged with fellow heads of navy and maritime leaders to reinforce relationships and discuss opportunities for greater cooperation and interoperability.
He said future naval forces must also be flexible, sustainable and capable of combining traditional platforms with emerging technologies to generate greater combat power.
“Together, we have to be adaptable. We have to be tailorable. There’s got to be a high-low mix. It’s got to be sustainable in forward places and force multiplied through robotic and autonomous systems. That’s why I’m investing so hard to build my endurance in directed energy and containerized payloads,” said Caudle.
The Trans-Regional Seapower Symposium traces its history to 1996, when the Italian Navy established what was then known as the Regional Seapower Symposium as a forum for multinational naval dialogue and cooperation. It has since grown from delegations representing 23 countries at its first gathering to approximately 70 navies today.
Caudle also continues a longstanding tradition of U.S. Chiefs of Naval Operations participating in the Venice symposium.
Former CNO Adm. Michael Mullen attended in 2006, followed by Adm. Gary Roughead in 2008, Adm. Jonathan Greenert in 2012 and Adm. John Richardson in 2015. Adm. Mike Gilday participated in both the 2019 Regional Seapower Symposium and the 2022 Trans-Regional Seapower Symposium, and Adm. Lisa Franchetti attended the 14th T-RSS in 2024.
Caudle’s participation makes him the seventh U.S. Chief of Naval Operations to attend the symposium and marks the eighth CNO appearance at the forum since 2006.
The symposium has evolved alongside the maritime environment it was created to address, expanding beyond its original regional focus to examine the increasingly interconnected nature of global maritime security.
Three decades after the first gathering in Venice, Caudle said its fundamental purpose remains unchanged: bringing naval leaders together before they are called upon to confront a crisis together.
He said those relationships strengthen deterrence by giving navies the trust and familiarity necessary to operate effectively alongside one another.
“We train together, we exercise together, we operate together,” Caudle said. “And we build the trust that allows us to act together when it matters most.”
title: CNO Strengthens Global Maritime Partnerships at 15th Trans-Regional Seapower Symposium

RELEASE: Gottheimer Introduces Bipartisan Resolution Honoring Flydubai Flight 1073 Heroes
Condemns Attempted Terrorist Attack
Resolution Honors Captain, Crew, Passengers Who Saved All Lives
Calls for a Full Investigation
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Tuesday, October 6, 2026, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), Congressman Michael McCaul (TX-10), and Congressman Don Bacon (NE-2) introduced a bipartisan resolution honoring Captain Smit Machchhar and the crew and passengers of Flydubai Flight 1073, and condemning the attempted terrorist attack on the flight.
“Captain Machchhar is a hero. While gravely wounded, he fought off a terrorist attack and saved every soul on that plane, including 27 children and four Americans,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “Congress must honor his extraordinary courage, and we must be clear that this was an act of terrorism and an attack on the safety of international air travel. I’m proud to lead this resolution with Congressman McCaul and Congressman Bacon, and we wish Captain Machchhar and everyone injured a full recovery.”
“I’m proud to co-lead this resolution, which condemns the attempted terrorist attack, calls for a full investigation, and honors the brave crew and passengers. The world owes a debt of gratitude to these heroes — especially Captain Smit Machchhar, who sustained injuries fighting the attacker and still managed to unlock the cockpit door and allow others to land the plane,” said Congressman Michael McCaul (TX-10). “Were it not for his extraordinary courage, this story could have ended in horrific tragedy. I wish Captain Machchhar, the crew, and all the passengers healing and strength as we await a comprehensive investigation into this harrowing incident.”
On September 30, Flight 1073 departed Dubai for Tel Aviv carrying approximately 174 passengers and six crew, including 4 U.S. citizens and 27 children. Midway through the flight, the first officer attacked the captain with the aircraft’s emergency crash axe and tried to seize the controls, sending the plane plunging more than 14,000 feet in under 30 seconds. Despite grave injuries, Captain Machchhar, a citizen of India, fought off the attack and unlocked the cockpit door so off-duty pilots could enter and land the plane, and so crew and passengers could restrain the first officer. The aircraft landed safely in Saudi Arabia with everyone accounted for. On October 3, the Attorney General of the United Arab Emirates announced that the investigation had determined the first officer attempted to carry out a terrorist act.
The resolution:
- Honors Captain Machchhar for extraordinary courage in protecting every soul aboard his aircraft;
- Commends the off-duty pilots, cabin crew, and passengers who secured the flight deck and brought the aircraft safely down;
- Wishes Captain Machchhar and all who were injured a full recovery;
- Condemns the attack as an act of terrorism and an attack on the safety of international civil aviation;
- Calls for a full and expeditious investigation by Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, and for the United States and Israel to be kept fully informed.
###
title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Introduces Bipartisan Resolution Honoring Flydubai Flight 1073 Heroes

SAN ANTONIO – A San Antonio woman was sentenced in federal court to 53 months in prison for aiding or assisting in the filing of a false tax return, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas.

According to court documents, Natasha Sheree Banks-Brown, 45, owned and operated a tax preparation business named “Tasha’s Total Tax Service,” beginning in 2016. In December 2020, IRS Criminal Investigations began investigating an increasing number of questionable tax returns prepared by Banks-Brown.

The investigation revealed that Banks-Brown filed individual tax returns on behalf of her clients which included false and fraudulent deductions and credits which significantly increased their tax refunds. Banks-Brown never quoted a specific price for her services and said that she would take her fee out of the return. As part of her fraudulent scheme, she used tax preparation software that allowed her to designate returns to be deposited into a bank account she controlled. The client would then receive a portion of the return via a transfer from Banks-Brown’s bank account to the client’s account, with Banks-Brown keeping a percentage as her fee. Multiple clients testified at trial that they were unaware of her actions and were never given the opportunity to review the return in detail before signing. Evidence introduced at trial indicated that Banks-Brown filed close to 1,200 tax returns between 2017 and 2021 that resulted in over $8 million dollars of refunds.

Banks-Brown was indicted on April 3, 2024, and arrested April 16, 2024. She was found guilty of all 11 counts after a four-day jury trial on April 10, 2026. In addition to the 53-month prison sentence, U.S. District Judge David Ezra ordered Banks-Brown to pay $3,824,887 in restitution and $1,100 in special assessments.

“Tax professionals like the defendant in this case take advantage of the intimidating and complex nature of the tax system, using their clients as unwitting pawns for personal gain. Unfortunately, this type of scheme is relatively common, and this sentence should serve as a warning that promises of inflated tax refunds can be too good to be true,” said U.S. Attorney Simmons. “Now, Natasha Banks-Brown is paying the price with a nearly five-year stay in federal prison for abusing the trust of the clients she victimized and for stealing from the American taxpayer. This office and our prosecutors remain focused on these cases from investigation through sentencing because every one of us cares about doing the next right thing and delivering justice for our fellow Americans.”

“Banks-Brown is a financial predator who used the tax refunds of her clients to feed her greed. We are talking about someone who repeatedly scammed her clients and her country. Thanks to the jury who convicted her, the special agents that investigated the case and the U.S. Attorney’s Office, we returned the favor and took her freedom along with her money,” said Special Agent in Charge Christopher J. Altemus Jr., of IRS-CI's Texas Field Office. “She is everything we warn you to avoid. Criminal return preparers like Banks-Brown promise you riches and steal from us all.”

IRS-CI investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Justin Chung and Ryan Groomer prosecuted the case.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

###
title: San Antonio Tax Preparer Sentenced to Federal Prison for Filing False Tax Returns, Over $3.8 Million in Restitution

Last night, President Donald J. Trump signed an Executive Order that immediately cuts diesel costs by authorizing highway use of tax-free dyed diesel and deferring the federal diesel excise tax through the end of the year. The decisive action — expected to save drivers as much as $100 per fill — puts real money back in the pockets of farmers, ranchers, truckers, loggers, and working families at the exact moment harvest demands it most.
Here’s what they’re saying:
President Donald J. Trump: “Today, I am announcing another unprecedented step to bring down costs. For many years, farm vehicles, construction equipment, and other off-road vehicles have used what is known as ‘red dye’ diesel… which is exactly the same as normal diesel, but is sold tax-free for off-road vehicles and big trucks… Tonight, I am going to sign a historic Executive Order to officially waive the off-road requirement and allow anyone to purchase tax-free red dye diesel for any reason.”
Vice President JD Vance: “Another example of President Trump acting quickly to tackle an urgent issue. In this administration, we’re fighting every day to help hard working Americans, especially our farmers.”
White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles: “President Trump signed an Executive Order right here in Nebraska to lower diesel costs for American farmers, truckers, and workers. By expanding access to red-dyed diesel and providing federal tax relief, President Trump is once again taking decisive action to put money back in the pockets of hardworking Americans. Promises made. Promises kept.”
Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins: “President Trump is the most pro ranching and farming president in our lifetime. Energy dominance is at the core of putting farmers and ranchers first. This administration has unleashed American energy dominance, and we are now the largest energy producer in the world as a result. While the Administration has structurally changed the energy sector to secure the long-term future of agriculture, we are now taking steps to deal with short term pressures impacting our American farmers. Thank you, President Trump for signing today’s Executive Order enacting enforcement discretion on on-road use of dyed diesel, which will better enable our farmers to deliver America’s harvest during this critical time. And I want to thank Vice President Vance for his help shepherding it to the end.”
American Farm Bureau Federation President Zippy Duvall: “We thank President Trump for recognizing that what happens at the fuel pump directly affects what happens on the farm and therefore at dinner tables across America. Allowing dyed diesel fuel to be used over-the-road will bring welcome relief for farmers because every cent per gallon matters when you’re running a fleet of grain trucks or hauling cattle hundreds of miles. As we detailed in a letter to the president last week, this effort will bring much needed price relief for farmers as they work to complete harvest across the U.S. The federal highway diesel tax is currently more than 24-cents per gallon, so it’s a big deal to farmers to be able to use tax exempt diesel more broadly to get their harvest to market. We appreciate that the president listened to farmers and responded.”
American Soybean Association Vice President Dave Walton: “As U.S. soybean farmers move the 2026 harvest to market, ASA thanks President Trump for his Executive Order that seeks to address high fuel costs impacting our bottom lines. This policy will align with actions taken by many soybean-producing states already, and ASA is encouraged by the administration’s continued focus on agricultural affordability.”
Missouri Gov. Mike Kehoe: “Last week, I signed an executive order taking targeted action to help address the unique fuel and transportation needs of harvest season in Missouri. President Trump’s action yesterday provides commonsense flexibility to lower transportation costs and keep agriculture moving across the entire nation. When we can reduce unnecessary costs for our farmers, that ultimately benefits families across our state and nation.”
Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry: “Thank you, President @realDonaldTrump! I declared a State of Emergency so our farmers could use the dyed diesel fuel they already had on hand—and now, thanks to YOU, that relief is going nationwide! This is a HUGE WIN for America’s farmers, truckers, and hardworking families. Lower costs and real relief for the people who keep this country moving.”
Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee: “On Friday, I directed TN state departments to suspend enforcement of dyed diesel restrictions through the end of October to provide relief for farmers & foresters during harvest season. Thank you, @RealDonaldTrump, for standing with the Tennesseans who feed & fuel our country.”
Nebraska Gov. Jim Pillen: “This action expands on state efforts I enacted by executive order just a few weeks ago. This will greatly assist farmers who are dealing with extraordinarily high diesel prices, impacting everything they do – from field operations to transportation of their products and livestock. I appreciate that President Trump signed his order today in Nebraska. Agriculture is the tip of the spear in our great state, and we need to continue to do all that we can to feed the world and save the planet. President Trump knows that and we appreciate his support.”
Mississippi Gov. Tate Reeves: “President Trump has announced he is signing an executive order that will defer the federal excise tax on dyed diesel and allow for highway use. Because of the EO signed by @POTUS, I have spoken with Commissioner @TindellSean and he plans to direct the Commercial Transportation Enforcement Division of the Mississippi Department of Public Safety to not enforce the dyed diesel prohibition on highways. Thanks to this executive order and Commissioner Tindell’s swift action, much-needed relief will be delivered to our nation’s farmers, truckers, ranchers and loggers, as well as a wide range of other industries that rely on diesel. This will have positive ripple effects on America’s economy and your wallet. I’d like to thank President Trump and his administration for working quickly to provide this relief.”
Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds: “Today, in line with President Trump’s executive order, I suspended state penalties for using dyed diesel to transport certain ag products on public roads. This will lower costs for farmers through the harvest and beyond by opening access to tax-free fuel.”
South Dakota Gov. Larry Rhoden: “In response to these extraordinary times, President Trump has ordered a suspension of enforcement of the federal dyed diesel fuel for taxpayers on highways and public roads. Therefore, I am directing the Department of Public Safety to adjust enforcement priorities regarding the use of dyed diesel fuel. Many farmers maintain on-site supplies of dyed diesel fuel for nontaxable, off-road use. By taking this action, we will provide meaningful relief to South Dakota farmers. Similarly, President Trump’s order will allow all taxpayers to realize meaningful savings from using dyed diesel.”
North Carolina Gov. Josh Stein: “Last week I took action to help provide some relief at the pump for North Carolina’s farmers, and I asked the IRS to step in to pause enforcement of the red-dyed diesel tax at the federal level. I am pleased to see farmers across the country will now get this same relief. Let’s keep working at every level of government to help people keep more money in their wallets.”
Tennessee Commissioner of Agriculture Andy Holt: “Governor Lee’s directive, coupled with President Trump’s federal executive order, provides timely relief for Tennessee farmers, forest product producers and timber harvesters facing high diesel costs during harvest season. Agriculture and forestry are essential to Tennessee’s economy, and this temporary flexibility will help keep producers working, products moving, and rural communities supported. We appreciate Governor Lee’s leadership, President Trump’s action, and Secretary Rollins’ support for American agriculture.”
Kentucky Commissioner of Agriculture Jonathan Shell: “Huge win for Kentucky farmers. President Trump signed an executive order expanding access to tax-exempt red-dyed diesel. With harvest underway and high fuel costs weighing on farm families, this will provide immediate relief and help lower costs. Thank you President Trump for standing with our farmers.”
Mississippi Commissioner of Agriculture and Commerce Andy Gipson: “A HUGE thank you to President Trump and Governor Reeves for taking action to allow red-dyed off-road diesel fuel. A huge help to our farmers, loggers and truckers here in Mississippi and across America.”
Alabama Farmers Federation President Jimmy Parnell: “We appreciate President Trump joining Gov. Kay Ivey in allowing dyed diesel fuel to be used without penalty for highway use. With about a dozen states easing enforcement of off-road diesel rules, President Trump’s executive order provides consistency across the country and ensures farmers and timber producers will not be penalized when they cross state lines to market their products.”
Louisiana Farm Bureau President Richard Fontenot: “Anything helps, especially as we work to get the crops out of the fields. I’m appreciative of the governor’s (and president’s) efforts to give us any relief during this time.”
Tennessee Farm Bureau Federation: “We join American Farm Bureau President @ZippyDuvall in applauding the executive order signed by President Trump to suspend enforcement of dyed diesel fuel restrictions for agricultural operators, giving farmers a break.”
Sen. Tom Cotton: “Allowing on-road use of red diesel will give Arkansas farmers much-needed relief. This is a welcome step by the administration that I’ve long called for.”
Sen. Chuck Grassley: “Thx to Pres Trump for listening to farmers & temporarily allowing off-road dyed diesel for highway use Lowering costs for FARMERS DURING HARVEST”
Sen. Bill Hagerty: “@POTUS is taking action to lower diesel prices, cutting costs for Tennessee farmers who keep food moving from the farm to families’ dinner tables.”
Sen. Roger Marshall: “Temporary expanded use of dyed diesel allows producers to utilize more fuel options during harvest and lightens the cost of production for farmers and ranchers at a crucial time. Thanks to the White House for listening to farmers. We still have more work to do.”
Sen. Mike Rounds: “Following my letter last week, I’m pleased to see that the President is taking steps to lower fuel prices, including a review of certain taxes on diesel. This is an opportunity to offer real relief to South Dakotans who continue to pay higher prices at the pump, particularly farmers and ranchers who are in the middle of harvest. We’ll continue to work on addressing the high cost of living impacting our state.”
Rep. Mark Alford: “@POTUS just signed an order letting truckers and farmers run tax-free dyed diesel on the highway through year’s end — no interest, no penalties. That puts real money back in the pockets of the folks who haul our freight and grow our food.”
Rep. Tim Burchett: “A few weeks ago, I called on @POTUS to take action on diesel prices. Last night, President Trump signed an Executive Order to put money back in the pockets of American farmers, truckers, and workers.”
Rep. Don Davis: “It’s a much needed Executive Order that provides temporary relief for farmers and working families facing record fuel costs.”
Rep. Russell Fry: “No one cares more about affordability than President Trump and Congressional Republicans.”
Rep. Ashley Hinson: “High diesel prices are hurting our truckers, farmers, and all Iowans, and this executive order is a step in the right direction to deliver relief. We should be using every tool available to lower fuel prices and provide flexibility for Iowa farmers during harvest season. I’ll continue to push for bipartisan policies that lower costs at the pump and the checkout line.”
Rep. Rich McCormick: “A farmer can’t wait for prices to come down. The crop is in the field right now. This week @POTUS signed an order that temporarily allows tax-free dyed diesel to be used on the highway. The federal diesel tax is deferred through the end of the year, with no interest and no penalties. That’s about $60 on a 250-gallon fill, and more where states follow suit. It’s temporary, and it’s not the whole answer. But for the families who feed America, it is real relief at a critical time. The long-term fix is more supply and more refining capacity. That is the work still ahead.”
Rep. Zach Nunn: “This is a good first step and it will deliver real relief for farmers facing record diesel prices in the middle of harvest.”
Rep. Jason Smith: “I applaud President Trump’s executive order today to provide immediate relief by deferring the excise tax for on-road use of dyed diesel until the end of the year. This is a much-needed step to lessen the burden that increased fuel prices have had on farmers, ranchers, and the entire agricultural community. This executive order is only a first step — it is crucial to provide lasting relief for the hardworking Americans who feed, fuel, and clothe our nation.”
Rep. Greg Steube: “President Trump is delivering relief for America’s farmers and truckers. My RED Fuel Act is sitting in Congress waiting to make this relief permanent. House Leadership needs to bring us back to D.C. and pass it!”
title: WHAT THEY ARE SAYING: President Trump Delivers Immediate Diesel Relief, Saving Americans Up to $100 Per Fill

Secretary Turner and Labor Secretary Sonderling Tour the 'Big Green House' by Structural Building Components Association
COLORADO - U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) spotlighted multiple housing innovations and resources from the Rocky Mountain region during the sixth annual Innovative Housing Showcase, held September 22-24 on the National Mall. This year’s theme, “Made in America,” highlighted American ingenuity and innovative approaches to expanding housing affordability and homeownership.

HUD’s “Made in America” Showcase spotlighted American builders, manufacturers, and innovators’ modern technologies and creative housing solutions that are expanding housing supply, lowering construction costs, and putting affordable homeownership back in reach for hardworking Americans. The Showcase featured a variety of full-scale housing models including manufactured, 3D printed, and modular homes built by American companies from across the nation.

Resources from Building America – National Laboratory of the Rockies (Colorado) that describe the U.S. Department of Energy's Building America program and existing technical assistance programs to support cost-effective housing construction technologies.

President Trump Admits He Used Taxpayers’ Money for Political Ads
WASHINGTON – After President Trump personally directed that taxpayer funding be used for a series of political ads, he has reportedly reversed course. Instead, he is opting to pay for the spots with his donors’ money, through his political action committee (PAC). House Appropriations Committee Ranking Member Rosa DeLauro (D-CT-03) issued the following statement on the president’s abrupt about-face:
“While I am glad it seems the American taxpayer will no longer be robbed to pay for presidential propaganda, their money should never have been stolen in the first place.
“By choosing to now fund these ads through his MAGA Inc. super PAC, President Trump is admitting a reality he previously denied: these are not public service announcements, they are political ads meant to boost his party’s chances in the upcoming elections.
“At minimum, the money this administration stole from the taxpayers to pay for these ads should be returned to the Treasury, and the president’s top aides who facilitated this theft must be held accountable.”

The Department of the Air Force Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Command, Control, Communications and Battle Management is seeking civilian candidates during a month-long digital hiring event, featuring careers focused on modernizing command and control systems across the defense enterprise.
Interested candidates must submit resumes and supporting documentation through the official application portal at afciviliancareers.com/C3BM between Oct. 5 and Nov. 5.
The PAE’s mission is to deliver an integrated DAF Battle Network, the system-of-systems connecting sensor, effector and logistics systems providing better situational awareness, faster operational decisions and decisive direction to the force.
“These positions play a decisive role in delivering the capabilities warfighters depend on,” said Kate Nelson, DAF PAE C3BM director. “If you’re ready to do hard things, and make a real difference in national security, you’re who we’re looking for.”
Within C3BM, civilian professionals work across several high-demand career fields, with positions available at Hanscom Air Force Base; Robins AFB, Georgia; and Wright-Patterson AFB, Ohio. Available positions include acquisition program management, acquisition test management, contracting, financial management, engineering, science, information technology, logistics and security.
Program and test managers lead cross-functional acquisition strategies balancing cost, schedule and performance, while engineers, scientists and IT specialists design resilient architectures, networks and data integration frameworks.
Contracting and financial specialists secure industry partnerships and execute critical resources, while logisticians and security specialists oversee life-cycle support and protect vital defense technologies.
Unlike traditional in-person job fairs, the digital hiring event is conducted entirely through an online intake process. Selected candidates will participate in virtual interviews conducted on an ongoing basis throughout the open announcement window.
Applicants must submit a resume of no more than two pages detailing professional experience and contact information. Submissions should also include unofficial or official college transcripts, an SF-50 for current or former federal employees, and a DD Form 214 (member copy 2 or 4) for military veterans, if applicable.
C3BM is the integrating entity for command, control, communications and battle management within the department, aligning technical architecture and acquisition authorities to execute its efforts to streamline the delivery of decision advantage capabilities. To drive rapid capability delivery and cut through bureaucratic hurdles, C3BM leadership anchors the workforce around three operational core values: Ruthless Focus, Violent Execution and Extreme Teaming.
“Our core values transform every challenge you face. We’re not ordinary around here,” Nelson said. “Come be extraordinary.”
C3BM professionals oversee major modernization programs, including deployable communications infrastructure, cloud-based tactical applications, and the software pipelines that accelerate programs such as the Advanced Battle Management System. Their efforts ensure warfighters receive capabilities at the speed of relevance.
Successful applicants will join the 170,000-member Air Force Civilian Service, receiving comprehensive federal civil service benefits, continuing education opportunities and specialized career progression across national defense programs.
title: C3BM seeks civilian talent to advance DAF Battle Network

U.S. Representative Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24), U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA) and Adam Schiff (D-CA), and House Natural Resources Committee top Democrat Jared Huffman (D-CA-02), led 30 of their colleagues in calling on House and Senate Armed Services Committee leaders to reject the Hunt Amendment’s provision (Section 2835) in the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), which would grant unprecedented eminent domain authority to the federal government to benefit Sable Offshore Corporation.
 “The NDAA has long served as a bipartisan vehicle to strengthen our national security and support our servicemembers. However, we are deeply concerned by the inclusion of Section 2835, which would grant extraordinary eminent domain authority to the federal government to circumvent established environmental protections for the benefit of a single private company. Given the sweeping implications of this provision, we believe this policy rider does not belong in the NDAA and, therefore, should be removed from the final conference agreement,” wrote the lawmakers. 
 The lawmakers explain how this provision would jeopardize the California coastal economy and do little to strengthen our nation’s energy security. 
“California’s coastal economy supports roughly 511,000 jobs and generates over $51.3 billion in GDP from marine-economy activities — largely in tourism and recreation. Another oil spill from a corrosion-prone pipeline that has spilled before would jeopardize the economic security of everyday Americans that rely on our coastal economy for their livelihoods,” the lawmakers continued. “In addition, there is no evidence that this provision would meaningfully advance our nation's energy security. Recent spikes in gasoline prices driven by market uncertainty surrounding the war in Iran underscore that global oil markets—not a single offshore project—continue to dictate prices at the pump.”
The letter goes on to highlight the unprecedented nature of Section 2835, which would grant the federal government extraordinary powers to seize property for the sole benefit of a single private organization. 
“The NDAA should not be used to circumvent established permitting processes or create special authorities for individual projects that have failed to secure the approvals required under existing law. The federal government's power of eminent domain is among its most significant authorities and should be exercised only when there is a clear and compelling public purpose—not to resolve private infrastructure disputes or increase the profitability of a single company—at the expense of communities who have to live with the consequences of an oil spill,” said the lawmakers. 
The full letter is available HERE.
Joining Carbajal, Padilla, Schiff, and Huffman the letter is co-signed by U.S. Representatives Maxine Waters (D-CA-43), Dave Min (D-CA-47), Julia Brownley (D-CA-26), Lou Correa (D-CA-46), Mike Thompson (D-CA-04), Brad Sherman (D-CA-32), Zoe Lofgren (D-CA-18), Nancy Pelosi (D-CA-11), John Garamendi (D-CA-08), Gil Cisneros (D-CA-31), Ted Lieu (D-CA-36), Derek Tran (D-CA-45), Mike Levin (D-CA-49), Juan Vargas (D-CA-52), Judy Chu (D-CA-28), Jimmy Panetta (D-CA-19), Laura Friedman (D-CA-30), Robert Garcia (D-CA-42), Lateefah Simon (D-CA-12), Kevin Mullin (D-CA-15), Mark Takano (D-CA-39), Ami Bera, M.D. (D-CA-06), Ro Khanna (D-CA-17), Scott Peters (D-CA-50), Doris Matsui (D-CA-07), Pete Aguilar (D-CA-33), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-CA-37), George Whitesides (D-CA-27), Luz Rivas (D-CA-29), and Sara Jacobs (D-CA-51). 
Background
Sable Offshore acquired the Santa Ynez Unit from ExxonMobil in 2024. The pipeline had been out of service since the 2015 Refugio oil spill. In March 2026, Energy Secretary Chris Wright invoked the Defense Production Act and ordered Sable to restore pipeline operations. 
Carbajal has been a leader in opposing the Sable pipeline’s forced restart. 
In September 2026, Carbajal led a bicameral group of colleagues in filing an amicus brief in California v. Wright to challenge the Trump Administration’s use of the Defense Production Act (DPA) to facilitate the restart of the Sable Offshore oil pipeline system along the California Central Coast. The brief argues that the Administration has failed to identify a legitimate national defense need for Sable’s crude oil and that the DPA order does not satisfy the statutory requirements for invoking this extraordinary authority.
In July 2026, Carbajal spoke on the House floor against the NDAA’s Hunt amendment, which would grant the federal government unprecedented access to California-owned public lands associated with the Santa Ynez Unit and Las Flores Pipeline System.
 In May 2026, Carbajal, Schiff, and members of the California congressional delegation launched an inquiry into Sable’s efforts to restart oil drilling off the California coast and demanded answers on the company’s collaboration with the Trump administration to invoke the DPA in relation to this project.
Last year, Carbajal, Schiff, Padilla, and members of the California congressional delegation demanded answers from the Trump administration on its involvement in Sable’s attempts to restart the pipeline.
title: Carbajal, Padilla, Schiff, Huffman Lead Colleagues in Urging Removal of Hunt Amendment from Annual Defense Bill

Reps. Cisneros, Castro Honor Hispanic and Latino Storytellers
WASHINGTON D.C. — Congressman Gil Cisneros (CA-31) and Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20) introduced a resolution to honor and celebrate the cultural impacts of Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming.
Hispanics and Latinos represent 21% of the total population of the United States but Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming account for less than 7% of on-screen roles and less than 5% of off-screen roles. However, television series and films featuring Hispanic and Latino talent consistently rank among the most-watched and financially successful productions.
El Cine, the Hispanic Heritage Foundation, the Latino Film Institute, the League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC), the National Association of Latino Independent Producers (NALIP), the National Hispanic Foundation for the Arts (NHFA), and the National Hispanic Media Coalition (NHMC) signed on as supporting organizations.
“Latinos and Hispanics represent some of the biggest stars and the most important stories of the century. The time when actors like Rita Hayworth, Anthony Quinn or Martin Sheen had to change their names has given way to mainstream stars like Selma Hayek, Eva Longoria, Diego Luna, and Selena Gomez,” said Congressman Cisneros. “Hispanic and Latino storytellers have enriched our media with diverse stories, artistic excellence, and economic growth and they deserve recognition for their talent. I’m proud to introduce this resolution to celebrate and honor the success of Hispanics and Latinos in film, television, and streaming and recognize their past, present, and future contributions to the United States.”
“Latino artists have helped shape American film and television for generations, and Latinos are one of the largest and fastest-growing audiences in this country,” said Congressman Castro. “Yet we are still underrepresented on screen and in the writing rooms and leadership roles where decisions are made. Latino film festivals across the country are doing important work to support Latino storytellers, and the industry should invest in that talent. I'm proud to join Congressman Cisneros in recognizing these contributions and calling for more Latino representation on and behind the big screen.”
“One of the biggest dangers our culture faces is erasure,” said Mariana Da Silva, Founder of El Cine. “We are taught to hide parts of ourselves, our language, our histories, and the stories that make us who we are. At El Cine, we create space for those stories to be seen, heard, and passed on. Latin culture is American culture. We’re proud to support this resolution because recognizing our contributions also means making room for the next generation to tell their stories without having to hide who they are.”
“Fifty-nine percent of Latino adults went to a movie theater last year, more than any other group,” said Juan Proaño, Chief Executive Officer of LULAC. “Latinos are the profit margin of this industry. Yet we hold just 5 percent of the roles on screen, 2.8 percent of the lead roles, and one half of one percent of the writing credits, and 44 percent of top films have no Latino speaking character at all. LULAC is proud to support Congressman Cisneros's resolution, which honors the artists who opened doors and calls on the industry to reflect the audiences who sustain it. When we tell our own stories, the whole country sees itself more clearly.”
“Thirty years ago, Jimmy Smits, Sonia Braga, Esai Morales, Merel Julia and I founded the National Hispanic Foundation for the Arts (NHFA), when Latinos were one in ten Americans and almost nowhere on screen,” said Felix R. Sánchez, Chair and Co-founder of NHFA. “Today we are one in five, and we hold fewer than three of every hundred lead roles in Hollywood's top films. The country changed, the screen has not.”
“Latino Americans are intertwined in the fabric of the United States – including in film, television, and streaming,” said Brenda Victoria Castillo, President and CEO of National Hispanic Media Coalition (NHMC). “With the highest per capita consumption in entertainment, representing 24% of film ticket sales, 29% of daily mobile television viewers, and 24% of streaming subscribers, it's no wonder that our stories resonate, inspire, and are central to modern American culture. NHMC thanks Congressmen Cisneros and Castro for recognizing our community and continuing to be allies to increase Latino representation in media.”
“From a fifth grader's first film to a fellow's first credit to a festival premiere, Latino Film Institute is building the workforce of American film, television, and streaming,” said Axel Caballero, Chief Executive Officer of the Latino Film Institute. “And we are preparing it for what comes next: new kinds of stories, told on platforms that are still taking shape. Through YCP, our fellowships, and LALIFF, that talent is being readied and celebrated. We thank Congressman Cisneros, Congressman Castro, and all the cosponsors, and LFI is proud to support this resolution.”
Read the full text of the resolution here
Rep. Cisneros is a member of the House Committee on Small Business, the Ranking Member on the Subcommittee on Contracting and Infrastructure, and on the Subcommittee on Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations. He is a member of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and serves on its leadership team as the Freshman Representative.
###
title: Reps. Cisneros, Castro Honor Hispanic and Latino Storytellers

ICYMI: Congresswoman Nikema Williams Urges HUD to Implement Whole Home Repairs Law
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) joined U.S. Senator John Fetterman (D-PA) and U.S. Senator Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) in a letter to U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Secretary Scott Turner urging an establishment of a Whole Home Repairs program through the Office of Lead Hazard Control and Healthy Homes.
The Members wrote:
“Almost 7 million Americans live in homes that are in need of significant repair, with deficiencies including leaky roofs, faulty wiring, and mold. This is an issue that disproportionately affects America’s seniors, many of whom would like to downsize but do not want to sell the home at a steep discount due to the updates required. As we saw in Commonwealth of Pennsylvania’s successful Whole Home Repairs program, providing grants for repairs allowed seniors to sell larger homes to growing families.”
The Whole-Home Repairs Act was signed into law with the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act. The Whole Home Repairs pilot program will provide renovation and repair grants to homeowners and small landlords. This will help ensure America’s aging homes do not fall out of the housing supply.
The Members continued:
“The language in the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act authorizes you to operate a Whole Home Repairs program through 2031. We want to show the nation that repairing America’s crumbling homes is not a red or blue issue. Creating greater access to housing is an American issue. Any delays will mean millions of American families may never realize the benefit of this program. We were proud to help the Whole Home Repairs bill become law, and we stand ready to support you in making it a reality for Americans.”
Read the full text of the letter here.

U.S. Marshals Assist in Months-Long Horry Co. Operation That Leads to 10 Arrests
For immediate release
Office of Public Affairs
Usms.mediadesk@usdoj.gov
Washington, DC – A months-long, multiagency operation targeting illegal narcotics and violent criminals in and around Horry County, South Carolina, ended Sept. 30 with 10 arrests and the seizure of significant quantities of narcotics, firearms and money.
U.S. Marshals Service (USMS) Special Operations Group (SOG) and Carolinas Regional Fugitive Task Force (CRFTF) assisted in the operation, which included Horry County Police, Homeland Security Investigations, South Carolina Law Enforcement Division, and the Horry County Sheriff’s Office.
Of the 10 people arrested, eight face pending drug charges, one faces a pending weapons charge, and one a pending obstruction charge.
The investigation remains active and ongoing.
The USMS Carolinas Regional Fugitive Task Force began operations in January 2018. The CRFTF has partnership agreements with 87 state and local agencies, as well as three federal agencies, and operates throughout North Carolina and South Carolina. The CRFTF has apprehended more than 9,000 fugitives since its inception and is always striving to make communities safer.
The Special Operations Group is a specially trained, rapidly deployable law enforcement element of the U.S. Marshals Service, capable of conducting complex and sensitive operations throughout the globe intended to further the rule of law. SOG leverages these enhanced capabilities in support of the Marshals Service mission and the Department of Justice to protect, defend, and enforce the federal judicial system.
title: U.S. Marshals Assist in Months-Long Horry Co. Operation That Leads to 10 Arrests | U.S. Marshals Service

Rep. Chu, Tri-Caucus Leaders Demand HHS Withdraw Harmful English-Only Head Start Proposal
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28), Chair Emerita of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus (CAPAC), CAPAC Chair Grace Meng (NY-06), Congressional Hispanic Caucus (CHC) Chair Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Congressional Black Caucus (CBC) Chair Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Rep. Marilyn Strickland (WA-10), and Rep. Juan Vargas (CA-52) sent a letter to Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary 
Head Start is a critical program that provides high-quality early childhood education and comprehensive support services for low-income children and their families. While the Members urge HHS to withdraw the proposed rule in its entirety, their letter focuses specifically on its harmful changes to language-access protections. Nearly 40 percent of children enrolled in Head Start are dual-language learners, representing almost 290,000 children nationwide, and 30 percent of enrollees come from families whose primary home language is not English.
In the letter, the Members explain that dual-language instruction helps children learn English and prepare for school:
“We share the goal of ensuring that every Head Start child develops strong English-language skills. But requiring English-only instruction is not supported by the evidence and risks undermining that very goal. For many children, Head Start is their first experience in a classroom. Providing an environment in which young children can understand, communicate, and participate supports their ability to learn and successfully transition into school.
The Members also warn that the proposed rule conflicts with Congress’s explicit directives in the Head Start Act:
“Congress directed the Secretary to establish standards ensuring that children with limited English proficiency make progress toward acquiring English while simultaneously making meaningful progress in other developmental domains, including through “culturally and linguistically appropriate instructional services” (42 U.S. Code § 9836a(a)(1)(B)(x)). Congress further directed the Secretary, when revising Head Start standards, to ensure that revisions do not eliminate or reduce the quality, scope, or types of educational, parental-involvement, health, or other services required under longstanding Head Start standards (42 U.S.C. § 9836a(a)(2)(C)). And the Head Start Act explicitly requires agencies to ensure teachers receive literacy training “in methods to promote vocabulary development and phonological awareness (including phonemic awareness) in a developmentally, culturally, and linguistically appropriate manner and support children’s development in their native language” (42 U.S. Code § 9843(d)(2)(B)). Eliminating longstanding language-access protections appears directly at odds with these congressional directives, and the Department has not adequately explained how its proposal can be reconciled with them.”
The Members detail how eliminating bilingual staffing requirements could undermine parents’ ability to participate in their children’s education and jeopardize accurate developmental screenings and assessments:
“Congress recognized that informed and engaged parents are essential to children’s success and required Head Start programs to conduct family needs assessments and communicate with parents, to the extent practicable, in a language they understand (42 U.S. Code § 9836(d)(2)(J)(vii); 42 U.S. Code § 9836(d)(2)(K); 42 U.S. Code § 9836a(f)(2)). Eliminating language-access staffing requirements without providing an adequate alternative could make it more difficult for parents to understand their children’s progress, participate in their education, communicate with teachers and staff, and access the comprehensive services Head Start provides.
We are particularly concerned about the consequences for developmental screenings and assessments. The Head Start Act requires measures used by Head Start programs to be developmentally, linguistically, and culturally appropriate; valid and reliable in the language in which they are administered; administered by appropriately trained staff; and accompanied by appropriate accommodations for children with limited English proficiency (42 U.S. Code § 9836a(b)(2)). These protections are critical. A screening or assessment administered in a language a young child does not sufficiently understand risks mistaking normal second-language development for a developmental delay or, conversely, failing to identify a genuine disability or developmental concern. Either outcome could delay appropriate early intervention at precisely the age when it can make the greatest difference.”
Finally, the Members warn that the proposal would impose significant disruption and costs on Head Start providers while weakening services for hundreds of thousands of children:
“The scale of the disruption caused by the proposed rule’s language-access changes would be substantial. Almost 290,000 dual-language learners nationwide could be affected […] Although the proposal is titled Reducing Federal Burden for Head Start Programs, affected programs could be forced to change curricula, replace classroom materials, and retrain or replace teachers, resulting in an estimated $99 million in costs.”
“HHS should not reverse decades of evidence-based practice, impose new costs on providers, and weaken language-access protections for hundreds of thousands of children without a compelling evidentiary or legal basis for doing so. Accordingly, we strongly urge HHS to withdraw the proposed English-only instruction requirement and retain the longstanding language-access protections that allow Head Start programs to effectively serve dual-language learners and their families. Congress expressly directed Head Start to support English-language acquisition through culturally and linguistically appropriate services, and HHS should uphold, not undermine, that mandate.”
Read the full letter HERE.
title: Rep. Chu, Tri-Caucus Leaders Demand HHS Withdraw Harmful English-Only Head Start Proposal

HOUSTON – A 66-year-old Houston physician is accused of participating in a scheme that fraudulently billed the federal government millions of dollars for medical services that were never provided.

Authorities have now taken Dr. Joseph A. Montes into custody. He made his initial appearance before U.S. Magistrate Judge Christina Bryan at 10 a.m. today.

A federal grand jury returned a 12-count indictment Sept. 30, which is now unsealed. It alleges that between 2020 and 2022, Montes and others submitted false and fraudulent claims to the Department of Health and Human Services’ Health Resources and Services Administration for office visits that were never provided.

According to court documents, Montes owned and operated two Houston clinics: Joseph A. Montes MD & Associates, P.A. and Montes Medical PLLC. He allegedly allowed co-conspirators to operate pop-up COVID-19 testing sites under his name. Patients visited the sites for nasal swab testing, while the co-conspirators allegedly billed HSRA for office visits.

The indictment further alleges Montes’s clinics submitted thousands of impossible claims. On approximately 29 dates, they submitted more than 3,000 claims for evaluation and management services. On Dec. 1, 2021, they allegedly submitted more than 9,000 claims in a single day—roughly one patient visit every nine seconds over a 24-hour period.

From 2020 to 2022, Montes and others allegedly billed HSRA approximately $30 million, of which HSRA paid approximately $20 million.

Montes allegedly used proceeds from the scheme to make expensive purchases at a luxury car dealership and Tiffany & Co.

If convicted, Montes faces up to five years in federal prison for the conspiracy charge, 20 years for each wire fraud count, and 10 years for each money laundering count. He also faces a possible $250,000 maximum fine.

FBI – Houston, DHHS - Office of Inspector General, and Texas Attorney General’s Office Medicaid Fraud Control Unit conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Kathryn Olson is prosecuting the case.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division which is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste and abuse within federal benefit programs.

An indictment is a formal accusation of criminal conduct, not evidence. A defendant is presumed innocent unless convicted through due process of law.
title: Local physician indicted in $30 million COVID-19 fraud scheme

text:
PHILADELPHIA – United States Attorney David Metcalf announced that Tenia A. Thompson, 51, of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, was arrested and charged by indictment with 17 counts of wire fraud, two counts of bank fraud, one count of filing a false tax return, and 49 counts of aiding the filing of a false tax return, arising from a scheme to defraud the Small Business Administration (“SBA”), multiple SBA-approved lenders participating in the Paycheck Protection Program (“PPP”) and Economic Injury Disaster Loan (“EIDL”) program — both established as part of the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (“CARES”) Act, a federal law enacted in March 2020 — and the Internal Revenue Service (“IRS”).

The indictment alleges that, from approximately April 2020 through June 2024, Thompson, the owner and operator of a financial services and tax preparation business called “Thompson Business and Tax Solutions” and “TBTS Taxes,” (collectively, “TBTS”) prepared false tax returns for individuals and businesses and helped them apply for and obtain COVID-19 disaster-related loans and tax benefits to which the clients were not entitled. After fraudulently obtaining these loans and tax benefits for them, Thompson charged the clients exorbitant fees.

As alleged, the defendant engaged in this fraudulent activity on behalf of more than 100 clients, generating at least $12 million in fraudulent loan proceeds, at least $5 million in fraudulent tax benefits, and at least $2.2 million in fees for herself. Moreover, Thompson fraudulently attempted to obtain tens of millions of dollars in additional tax benefits on behalf of her clients, but the IRS rejected most of these claims.

If convicted, the defendant faces a maximum possible sentence of 20 years in prison for each count of wire fraud, 30 years in prison for each count of bank fraud, and three years in prison for each tax count. In addition, she would face up to three years of supervised release, a fine of $18,750,000, and additional financial penalties.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

This case was investigated by the FBI, Amtrak Office of Inspector General, IRS Criminal Investigation, and the SBA Office of Inspector General. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Louis D. Lappen and S. Chandler Harris.

The charges and allegations contained in the indictment are merely accusations. Every defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty in court.
title: Philadelphia Woman Indicted for Sprawling Scheme to Defraud the Government Through Bogus Pandemic Loan Applications, False Tax Returns

Congresswoman Lee Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Protect High-Risk Faith-Based and Community Organizations
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Susie Lee (NV-03) and María Elvira Salazar (R-FL) introduced the bipartisan Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act, which would make it easier for nonprofit organizations at high risk of terrorist attack to access federal grant funding for target hardening and physical security enhancements.
“We can all agree that our children should be able to go to school and that families should be able to worship without fear. As hate crimes rise throughout the country, nonprofit organizations, churches, synagogues, mosques, and religious schools are diverting their scarce resources away from serving their communities to pay for security cameras, guards, and emergency trainings,” said Congresswoman Lee. “No organization should be forced to choose between keeping their members safe or their financial stability. This commonsense, bipartisan bill will help nonprofit organizations fund security improvements and overall preparedness, so they can keep those they serve safe amid increased violence and harassment.”
“Every American should be able to worship without fear. When a church, synagogue, or other place of worship is approved for a federal security grant, it should be able to spend the money to improve security immediately. The Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act gets security dollars out the door faster and helps protect our communities,” said Congresswoman Salazar.
Congress created the Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP) in 2004 to help nonprofit organizations prevent, prepare for, respond to, and recover from terrorist or extremist attacks. The program funds target hardening, physical security improvements, and related preparedness activities for nonprofits at high risk of terrorism or hate-motivated violence.
Under current law, nonprofit organizations selected to receive an NSGP grant through a competitive application process must pay out of pocket for approved critical security upgrades and then wait months—or even years—to be reimbursed. This places these organizations in an impossible situation: cut into their limited budgets to ensure the safety of those they serve without any idea of when they might see that money or forgo critical security upgrades to ensure they can continue their work unabated.
The Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act would amend the current law to require that NSGP awards be issued to approved nonprofits in advance, rather than as a reimbursement for costs already incurred. By allowing advance payments, FEMA could better support approved nonprofits that lack upfront capital, speed implementation of needed security measures, and strengthen protection for vulnerable communities.
“Synagogues and nonprofit are paying out of pocket for essential security, then waiting months or years to get their money back,” said Jonathan Greenblatt, ADL CEO and National Director. “Providing funding upfront to institutions already approved for security grants would help ease that financial burden and allow them to make critical security improvements sooner. We thank Representatives Susie Lee and María Elvira Salazar for advancing this commonsense solution to get security dollars where they’re needed, when they’re needed.”
“According to American Jewish Committee’s (AJC) State of Antisemitism in America 2025 Report, 28% of American Jews say that at least one Jewish institution they are affiliated with has been a target of antisemitic incidents in the last five years. As threats against Jewish institutions continue to rise, we applaud Representatives Susie Lee and María Elvira Salazar for introducing the Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act,” said Julie Rayman, AJC’s Senior Vice President of Policy and Political Affairs. “By removing a financial barrier that can delay or prevent needed security upgrades, this legislation will help at-risk institutions better protect the communities they serve.”
“Counties are on the front lines of keeping communities safe, but too often they are left filling the gap when nonprofits can’t afford to pay upfront for critical security upgrades,” said National Association of Counties Executive Director Matthew Chase. “The Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act would allow approved nonprofits to receive funding upfront, helping them strengthen security sooner rather than delaying upgrades due to lack of capital. That means safer facilities, stronger coordination with local law enforcement and more resilient communities. Counties urge Congress to advance this bipartisan legislation quickly.”
“The Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP) is an important resource for houses of worship to better secure themselves against acts of hate and prepare for all kinds of emergencies, but the logistical burdens of the process can pose barriers to applicants. This important proposal to disburse funds up front rather than requiring a reimbursement-based model removes one such major hurdle. With these kinds of improvements, as well as timely and apolitical execution by the Department of Homeland Security, NSGP can continue to serve more of our nation's most vulnerable communities in a time of increased threats.” – Mannirmal Kaur, Senior Federal Policy Manager, The Sikh Coalition.
The Nonprofit Security Grant Program Funding Improvement Act is endorsed by Jewish Nevada, American Jewish Committee (AJC), Anti-Defamation League (ADL), Jewish Federations of North America (JFNA), National Association of Counties (NACO), Secure Community Network, and The Sikh Coalition.
More information on the bill is here.
title: Congresswoman Lee Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Protect High-Risk Faith-Based and Community Organizations

HONOLULU – United States Attorney Ken Sorenson announced that Isaiah Okudara, 39, of Maui, pled guilty on October 2, 2026 to one count of possession with the intent to distribute methamphetamine and cocaine. Sentencing is scheduled for February 10, 2027 before United States District Judge Shanlyn A.S. Park.

According to court records, Okudara admitted to mailing three parcels collectively containing 8.5 kilograms of methamphetamine and 6 kilograms of cocaine from San Diego, California to Kahului, Hawaii, on February 12, 2025. Okudara also admitted he intended to distribute the drugs to others.

Okudara faces at least 10 years and up to life in prison, a fine of up to $10,000,000, plus a term of supervised release.

The FBI and the Maui Police Department investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Jeannette Graviss is prosecuting the case.

This case is part of Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN), the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities.
title: Maui Man Admits to Mailing Packages of Methamphetamine and Cocaine from California to Maui

PLANO, Texas – The Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative was established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States.
In the Eastern District of Texas, five defendants were sentenced to a total of 1,105 months in federal prison during the month of September as part of the Homeland Security Task Force, announced U.S. Attorney Jay R. Combs. Additionally, two Chinese nationals were arrested, and another four defendants were extradited from Guatemala to the United States to face drug trafficking violations in the Eastern District of Texas.
On September 2, 2026, Jose Luis Gonzalez, Jr., 24, of Dallas, was sentenced to 108 months in federal prison for trafficking at least 50 kilograms of cocaine from Mexico to the United States for further distribution.
On September 2, 2026, a Beaumont man was sentenced to 40 years in federal prison for drug trafficking violations in the Eastern District of Texas. Darrell Joshua Bendy, 42, was convicted at trial of trafficking between 20-30 kilograms of methamphetamine in the Eastern District of Texas.
On September 9, 2026, U.S. Attorney Jay R. Combs announced the arrests in China of Lisa Xing, 36, and Zhanwen Song, 38, Chinese citizens. Xing and Song were named in a six-count superseding indictment returned by a federal grand jury in the Eastern District of Texas, charging them with drug trafficking and money laundering violations. If convicted they face between 10 years and life in federal prison. It is important to note that a federal indictment is not evidence of guilt, and all defendants are considered innocent until proven guilty.
On September 15, 2026, 53-year-old Mozambican, Norolamin Gulam was sentenced to 135 months in federal prison and ordered to pay a money judgment in the amount of $7.5 million for conspiracy to commit money laundering. Gulam was identified as the leader of a transnational money laundering organization with connections and ties throughout Europe, Africa, Southeast Asia, the United States, and Central and South America. Gulam used multiple businesses and real estate ventures to launder multi-million dollar amounts of drug proceeds. It is believed Gulam was responsible for laundering a minimum of $500 million in U.S. currency.
On September 17, 2026, Pamela Esquivias, 25, of Maricopa, Arizona, was sentenced to 262 months in federal prison, while Aaron Jay Perez, 29, of Dallas, received 120 months in federal prison. The two were charged with federal drug trafficking violations as the result of an investigation into the overdose death of a 16-year-old girl in Flower Mound.
On September 24, 2026, U.S. Attorney Jay R. Combs returned from an unprecedented visit to Guatemala where he was part of a Department of Justice delegation that met with the President of Guatemala, their Attorney General, and Secretary of the Interior. Following the meetings, U.S. Attorney Combs boarded a DEA prisoner transport plane and accompanied four indicted individuals from Guatemala to the United States, including Juan Carlos Cruz Ovalle. Ovalle was indicted in 2018 and is alleged to have trafficked multi-ton quantities of cocaine from Guatemala for distribution to the United States. It is important to note that a federal indictment is not evidence of guilt, and all defendants are considered innocent until proven guilty.
HSTF Dallas comprises agents and officers from the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Dallas Field Office; U.S. Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Homeland Security Investigations - Dallas (ICE-HSI); Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Dallas Field Division; Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) Dallas Field Division; Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigations (IRS-CD; United States Postal Service, United States Postal Inspection Service (USPIS); Transportation Security Administration, Federal Air Marshal Service (FAMS); United States Secret Service (USSS); Department of State, Bureau of Diplomatic Security (DSS); TEXOMA HIDTA; and U.S. Marshals Service (USMS) Eastern District of Texas. HSTF Houston comprises agents and officers from the FBI; U.S. Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Homeland Security Investigations - Houston (ICE-HSI); Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA); Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF); Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigations (IRS-CI); and U.S. Marshals Service (USMS) Eastern District of Texas; Texas Department of Public Safety; Jefferson County Sheriff’s Office; Beaumont Police Department; Port Neches Police Department; Harris County Sheriff’s Office; Vidor Police Department; and the Orange County Sheriff’s Office.
For more information about the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Texas, please visit: https://www.justice.gov/usao-edtx.
title: Eastern District of Texas prosecutes multiple defendants as part of Homeland Security Task Force investigations in September 2026

Castro Challenges Trump To Visit Dilley Trailer Prison During San Antonio Visit
SAN ANTONIO, TX —Today, Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20) renewed his invitation to President Donald Trump to visit the Dilley Trailer Prison during his visit tomorrow in San Antonio, Texas.
“Donald Trump will be in San Antonio tomorrow. I invite him to visit the Dilley Trailer Prison and see for himself the trauma he is inflicting on children and babies, some as young as two months old.”
Castro first challenged the President to see firsthand the conditions facing children at the only family detention center in the country at a march protesting ICE’s proposed detention center in San Antonio. Transcript below:
“President Trump, you're coming to San Antonio. I would invite you to go to Dilley to see what Stephen Miller, who sits with you at the White House, has done to these children. To see the lifelong lasting trauma he's caused to these kids, to see what he's doing in the name of Americans. And I would say, because I would bet that the President has never been into a detention center, that he's certainly not been into a detention center, this trailer prison, where kids are held. Let me say this: the President of the United States is the leader of the country, the leader of the free world. If you can't stand there and go inside and look into the eyes of these kids and tell them that despite the fact they've done nothing wrong, that they belong there just because of where they were born, just because of the color of their skin, just because of the language that they speak, then you don't deserve to be President of the United States.”
“Presidente Trump, vas a venir a San Antonio. Yo te invito a ir a Dilley para ver lo que Stephen Miller, que se sienta contigo en la Casa Blanca, les ha hecho a estos niños. Para ver el trauma duradero que les ha causado a estosniños, para ver lo que está haciendo en nombre de Estados Unidos. Y yo diría esto, porque apostaría a que el presidente nunca ha estado dentro de un centro de detención. Que ciertamente nunca ha estado dentro de un centro de detención, esta prisión de tráileres, donde tienen detenidos a niños. Déjenme decir esto: el Presidente de los Estados Unidos es el líder del país, el líder del mundo libre. Si no puedes estar ahí, entrar y mirar a estos niños a losojos y decirles que, a pesar de que no han hecho nada malo, pertenecen allí simplemente por el lugar donde nacieron, simplemente por el color de su piel, simplemente por el idioma que hablan, entonces no mereces ser Presidente de los Estados Unidos.”
###
title: Castro Challenges Trump To Visit Dilley Trailer Prison During San Antonio Visit
