SPRINGFIELD, Mo. – Roy Dean Faux, 53, of Rockaway Beach, Mo., was sentenced in federal court, for receiving and distributing child pornography.

Faux was sentenced by U.S. District Court Judge Stephen R. Bough to 262 months in federal prison without parole, followed by a 10-year term of supervised release.

According to court documents, Faux, a prior convicted sex offender, who pleaded guilty on Dec. 15, 2025, used cellular devices to receive files of child pornography. Law enforcement’s investigation discovered Faux was utilizing social media applications to solicit the files of child pornography from other users.

Faux, who was already required to register as a sex offender, will continue to be required to register as a sex offender upon his release from prison and will be subject to federal and state sex offender registration requirements, which may apply throughout his life.

This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Ami Harshad Miller. It was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations, the Southwest Missouri Cyber Crimes Task Force, and the Taney County Sheriff’s Office.

Project Safe Childhood

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the United States Attorneys' Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.usdoj.gov/psc . For more information about Internet safety education, please visit www.usdoj.gov/psc and click on the tab "resources."
title: Former Rockaway Beach Man Sentenced to 21 Years for Receipt and Distribution of Child Pornography

text:
SAN DIEGO – Troy Clinton Van Sickle, a resident of Temecula, pleaded guilty in federal court today, admitting that he stole more than $1.8 million from two elderly women he claimed to be romantically interested in, and then obstructed federal law enforcement efforts to investigate the fraud scheme.

According to his plea agreement, Van Sickle targeted a wealthy divorced woman in Los Angeles and cultivated what appeared to be a romantic relationship in order to gain access to her finances. Van Sickle concealed his criminal history, which included convictions for fraud, theft, extortion, and perjury, and instead portrayed himself as a trustworthy and successful businessman.

After gaining the victim’s confidence, Van Sickle claimed he was facing financial hardship and needed money from the victim to pursue business deals and investment opportunities. He promised to repay the funds promptly and share future profits.

But it was all a lie. Van Sickle did not intend to repay the woman. He admitted that he used her money to enrich himself and others and to pay for personal expenses, including to make payments on luxury cars, gamble at casinos, and send money to other women.

According to his plea agreement, Van Sickle created a fake miniature replica car company and provided the woman a fake multi-million-dollar contract between the company and Lotus Cars to give the impression that his company was legitimate. The woman sent the contract to her financial advisor and wired $150,000 to Van Sickle to fund the purported agreement. Van Sickle then used the money to make a payment on a 2022 Ferrari SF90 Stradale that he purchased the month before for $734,000.

According to court documents, Van Sickle was on federal supervision for a prior fraud conviction at the time of the criminal offense. He had been ordered to pay $250,000 in restitution to nine victims of that offense and was required to truthfully and accurately report his financial resources to his probation officer.

To conceal the offense and avoid paying restitution, Van Sickle submitted a false financial packet signed under penalty of perjury to his probation officer that did not include the money he received from the woman, the luxury cars he had purchased and sold, and his gambling winnings and losses.

Upon learning that the Federal Bureau of Investigation had contacted the woman to discuss the money she had wired him, Van Sickle manipulated and exploited her to delete text messages, lie to law enforcement, and sign a false and fraudulent promissory note to make the wired proceeds appear simply as a lump-sum loan payable over a 10-year period. Van Sickle also directed the woman to sign a false statement to make it appear as though Van Sickle had already made a $140,000 payment to her through the note. Van Sickle disclosed the purported loan to his probation officer, along with the false promissory note and statement, and lied that he had already made a $140,000 payment to the woman.

According to his plea agreement, Van Sickle also targeted a woman in San Diego and lured her into a similar supposed romantic relationship in order to gain access to her finances and steal her money. He spent the money he received on luxury cars, gambling, and other women, and never intended to repay the woman.

Between 2022 and 2024, Van Sickle received more than 30 money transfers from the women totaling more than $1.8 million. He has not repaid any money to date. He admitted in his plea agreement that he knew the women were vulnerable victims due to their age, health, and trusting nature.

Van Sickle is next scheduled to appear before U.S. District Judge Ruth Bermudez Montenegro for sentencing on January 15, 2027. He is also scheduled to appear before U.S. Magistrate Judge Michael S. Berg for preliminary revocation of supervised release on October 20, 2026.

This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Patrick C. Swan.

DEFENDANT Case Number : 26-cr-1774-RBM

Troy Clinton Van Sickle Age: 55 Temecula, California

SUMMARY OF CHARGES

Wire Fraud – Title 18, U.S.C., Section 1343

Maximum penalty: Thirty years in prison and $250,000 fine

Money Laundering – Title 18, U.S.C., Section 1957

Maximum penalty: Ten years in prison and $250,000 fine

False Statement – Title 18, U.S.C., Section 1001(a)(2)

Maximum penalty: Five years in prison and $250,000 fine

INVESTIGATING AGENCIES

Federal Bureau of Investigation

Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation
title: Ten-Time Convicted Scammer Pleads Guilty to $1.8 Million Romance Fraud Scheme Targeting Two Elderly Women

text:
WASHINGTON — Karon Olufemi Blalock, 32, of Alexandria, Virginia, was sentenced today in U.S. District Court to 128 months in federal prison for his role in a transcontinental narcotics trafficking conspiracy that smuggled tens of thousands of fentanyl pills from California to the D.C. area, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

“Let me be crystal clear: When you flood our communities with a poison as deadly as fentanyl, you are waging war on the people who live here,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “This sentence is about accountability, and it is a message to every narcotics trafficker. The days of exploiting our neighborhoods for profit at the cost of human lives are over.”

text:
Fast Facts
It can be hard for people living in rural areas to get the health care they need. In 2025, a federal law established the Rural Health Transformation Program to fund state activities—like recruiting clinicians to rural areas.
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services administers the program, which will provide up to $50 billion to states over 5 years. In its first year, CMS gave $10 billion to 50 states.
This Q&A report looked at what CMS did to implement the program and its plans to monitor states’ activities. For example, CMS plans to communicate with states to discuss progress and conduct audits and site visits.
Person using a stethoscope on an elderly person
Highlights
What GAO Found
The Rural Health Transformation program provides funding for states to conduct rural health activities, such as recruiting clinicians to rural areas and providing training and technology to improve care delivery in rural hospitals. In the latter half of 2025, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) completed a number of early key actions to implement the Rural Health Transformation program. These actions included the release of the notice of funding opportunity—which provided details on program goals and requirements—and initial funding awards to all 50 states totaling $10 billion. The initial allotment of state funding ranged from $147 million for New Jersey to $281 million for Texas. CMS and merit reviewers assessed state applications based on a variety of factors—such as rural characteristics (e.g., total area in square miles and percent of population in rural areas) and the strength of states’ proposed initiatives. As a result, funding amounts variedacross states.
Rural Health Transformation Program Funding, by State, Budget Period 1 (December 29, 2025, Through October 30, 2026)
CMS plans on conducting a range of activities to monitor states’ activities and use of program funding. These monitoring activities include communicating with states to discuss progress and challenges, reviewing information states submit, and conducting audits and site visits. GAO found that its planned activities are generally consistent with selected requirements related to monitoring of federal awards. For example, CMS plans to measure awardee performance to show achievement of program goals and objectives, and hold webinars to share lessons learned, improve program outcomes, and foster the adoption of promising practices.
CMS plans to allot up to $40 billion of the remaining program funds to states over the next 4 years based on their demonstration of satisfactory progress toward approved initiatives (e.g., progress toward planned milestones), among other activities. If states do not comply with the terms and conditions of their notices of award, CMS may withhold, reduce, or recover a portion of states’ program funding. The authorizing legislation of the Rural Health Transformation program limits states’ ability to appeal or challenge any funding changes made by CMS. However, officials said issues related to appeals or challenges of funding changes may depend on the specific facts and circumstances, and they are in the process of determining how the agency will handle any such disputes or challenges.
Why GAO Did This Study
In July 2025, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act established the Rural Health Transformation program to provide funding allotments to states for specified rural health activities. It will fund up to $50 billion to states over 5 years. The program is administered by CMS as cooperative agreements with states. Federal law provided CMS with broad discretion to determine funding allotments to states.
Among other topics, this report describes CMS’s initial steps to establish the program, examines CMS’s plans to monitor states’ activities, and describes CMS’s approach for determining states’ future funding allotments.
To conduct this work, GAO reviewed CMS documentation on Rural Health Transformation program implementation and monitoring. GAO also interviewed CMS officials and representatives from two rural health stakeholder groups and one state government stakeholder group selected among those with national membership.
For more information, contact Leslie V. Gordon at GordonLV@gao.gov.
title: Rural Health Transformation Program: Early Implementation Actions and Monitoring Plans

Former Federal Employee Pleads Guilty to Defrauding the Federal Government of Approximately $194 Million
David J. Rush, 49, of Ashburn, Virginia, pleaded guilty today to executing a scheme to defraud the federal government relating to the misuse of his government position, resulting in a loss of approximately $194 million.
“Federal employees are entrusted with serving the American people, not themselves,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “The Trump Administration is committed to rooting out waste, fraud, and abuse in the federal government, including by prosecuting those who foolishly defraud American taxpayers.”
“Following an internal investigation that identified potential crimes, CIA immediately referred this matter to the FBI,” said CIA Director John Ratcliffe. “David Rush abused his position and betrayed the public trust and should be held fully accountable for his actions. We appreciate our law enforcement partners in the FBI and Department of Justice for securing this outcome. The Agency is committed to ensuring that those entrusted with our Nation’s secrets are held to the absolute highest standard.”
“By his own admission, David Rush defrauded the government of hundreds of millions of dollars, and then misused those funds for extravagant purchases,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “Rush betrayed his oath, his co-workers, and the American people and he will now face justice for his actions. This plea demonstrates the FBI’s commitment to protecting the public’s trust; and that no government position, security clearance, or access to government resources places anyone above the law.”
“Our Intelligence Community must have the trust of the American people to operate effectively in a Nation committed to transparency and the rule of law,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “Rush repeatedly betrayed that trust. He defrauded the United States out of approximately $194 million in real estate, jewelry, and other valuable property, including 298 gold bars. Worse, his self-serving actions threatened to erode public confidence in the intelligence services that must strive in secret to keep America safe. Thankfully, the efforts of the Department of Justice, its partners in law enforcement, and the Intelligence Community exposed Rush’s crimes. Today’s plea marks an important step in bringing Rush to justice.”
“The United States entrusted Davis Rush with the resources to protect our nation and its people, and for sheer avarice he chose to betray that trust for personal enrichment,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Theophani K. Stamos for the Eastern District of Virginia. “He robbed his country, not just of its treasury, but also of its faith. This office is committed to prosecuting those who undermine the security of the United States.”
According to court documents, Rush was employed in a senior executive-level position with a federal agency and held a Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) security clearance. He reached that position, in part, by lying about his education and military experience. Rush used his position of extraordinary public trust to create fictitious government authorities – including a fabricated Special Access Program – to obtain U.S. government funds for his personal benefit. Once he received the funds, Rush acquired gold bars and directed approximately $145 million in wire transfers that he ultimately used to purchase luxury real estate, watches, and at least one car. As a result of his scheme, Rush fraudulently obtained approximately $193,590,400 in U.S. government funds.
Cash and gold bars recovered in search of Rush's residence
On May 19, 2026, the FBI searched Rush’s residence and recovered 298 gold bars, approximately $2,106,550 in cash, €104,795, and numerous luxury watches. Rush had obtained the gold bars at an approximate cost to the government of $46 million. Pursuant to the plea agreement, Rush has agreed to forfeit the gold bars and currency found at his home, the fraudulently obtained properties, 30 watches (many of which were Rolexes), and two 2026 BMW Alpina vehicles, at least one of which is valued at approximately $172,000.
Rush is scheduled to be sentenced on Jan. 28, 2027. He faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison, three years of supervised release, forfeiture, restitution, and a fine. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
The case is prosecuted by Trial Attorneys Kevin C. Hakala and Kathryn D. DeMarco of the Justice Department’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section and Assistant U.S. Attorneys Raizza K. Ty, Gavin R. Tisdale, and Anthony T. Aminoff for the Eastern District of Virginia.
The U.S. Navy’s Naval Criminal Investigative Service also provided valuable assistance to the investigation.
The Department of Justice’s investigation is continuing. The Director of National Intelligence has requested that the Inspector General for the Intelligence Community initiate an investigation.
Related court documents and information are located on the website of the District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia or on PACER by searching for Case No. 1:26-cr-00185.

DENVER (KMGH) — Congress passed new protections for those looking for love on online dating apps.
The Romance Scam Prevention Act, passed on Sept. 24, will warn users about a potential scammer's intent before they fall too hard.
Colorado Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen, a co-sponsor of the bill, says this is an important first step in holding dating apps accountable.
“These are people who are showing up vulnerable, looking for love and connection, and being exploited at a surprisingly high rate. This is just making sure that they're (dating apps) doing their due diligence. Truly, the bare minimum of notifying their customers when they're deactivating an account because of fraudulent activity,” Pettersen said.
The law will require all online dating services to provide a “fraud ban notification” to users who have been in contact with someone the online dating service removed for fraudulent activity.
The notification would also warn them not to send money or share personal financial information with another member.
“Every single year, there's been over a billion dollars of losses from people who have been taken advantage of using dating apps, and when you think about the stigma that people feel when they've been taken advantage of, there's actually a significant underreporting,” Pettersen said.
Social media companies will be required to send fraud ban notifications to users within 24 hours of a member being banned, or within 3 days if law enforcement requests a delay.
The Romance Scam Prevention Act passed the Senate and will become law today unless President Donald Trump vetoes it.
This is Congresswoman Pettersen’s sixth bill signed into law during the current Trump Administration.
title: Congress passes landmark law to protect online daters from romance scams

Social Security Administration Refuses to Provide Services for Foster Care Youth, Horsford and Cortez Masto Demand Answers
For Immediate Release
October 6, 2026
Social Security Administration Refuses to Provide Services for Foster Care Youth, Horsford and Cortez Masto Demand Answers 
NORTH LAS VEGAS – Congressman Steven Horsford (NV-04) and Senator Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV) sent a joint letter to the Social Security Administration, calling on the agency to process pending applications submitted by Clark County Family Services (CCFS) to obtain Social Security Cards for youth in foster care. The letter comes after months of unanswered attempts by CCFS, County Commissioners, and both Rep. Horsford’s and Sen. Cortez Masto’s offices to work with SSA to rectify the issue. 
In December 2025, SSA notified CCFS that Social Security number applications required certain accompanying documentation to be physically certified by the custodian of record. For children in foster care, the custodian of record is the State of Nevada, which has operated digitally since 2010 when the Eighth Judicial District Court of Nevada mandated electronic filing for civil and family cases. This discrepancy between state law and federal agency policy makes it nearly impossible for CCFS to comply with SSA’s rule.
“Once again, the people are caught up in bureaucracy,” said Rep. Horsford. “Our priority is ensuring people have access to the services they are entitled to and can live their lives to the fullest. Our foster youth are among the most vulnerable in our community and SSA’s unwillingness to acknowledge our local laws shows this Administration’s regard for Nevadans.”
Over 1,300 foster youth in Clark County are currently unable to receive their Social Security Cards, severely restricting their livelihoods and quality of life.
“Without Social Security numbers, these youth can’t receive federal healthcare coverage, secure permanent placement in loving families, or even get their first job,” said Sen. Cortez Masto. “The Trump Administration must immediately process outstanding Social Security number applications and work with Clark County to remedy these documentation issues, so Nevada’s foster children don’t have to proceed any longer with their lives on pause.”
Since the initial notice in December, CCFS has provided documentation from the State of Nevada to SSA consistent with the state’s mandated electronic records and has offered to obtain any necessary information from the state to authenticate these records that may be used in other states. To date, there has been no response from SSA to this request.
“Clark County is grateful to the leadership of Senator Cortez Masto and Congressman Horsford as they work on our behalf to address this pressing issue which is impacting over 1,300 children in our care,” said Kevin Schiller, Clark County Manager. “Our most sacred responsibility is ensuring our most vulnerable children are cared for and we are being inhibited from doing this in the current state with the Social Security Administration.”
The full text of the letter can be found HERE.

WASHINGTON – Arnold Kevin Dussol, 39, of Leesburg, Virginia, pleaded guilty today in U.S. District Court in connection with unlawfully possessing a loaded firearm while hiding in a Northwest storage facility, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. Dussol pleaded guilty before Judge Amy Berman Jackson to one count of unlawful possession of a firearm. Judge Berman Jackson scheduled sentencing for February 19, 2027.

According to the government’s evidence, on March 30, 2026, law enforcement responded to reports from a victim stating that Dussol had threatened to kill her current boyfriend and that he possessed a firearm. Officers used location information and access instructions Dussol had sent the victim to locate a secure storage facility on 7th Street NW.

Inside the storage area, officers found Dussol hiding behind the door of an unlocked locker. He was dressed in all black and wearing a purple satchel consistent with the victim’s description.

Inside that satchel, investigators recovered a loaded 9mm handgun with one round in the chamber and six rounds in the magazine. A subsequent search revealed a small bag containing a white rock substance that field‑tested positive for methamphetamine.

Dussol has multiple prior felony convictions, including extortion, felony weapon possession, first‑degree assault, and felony drug distribution, and therefore was prohibited from possessing a firearm or ammunition at the time of his arrest.

This case was investigated by the Metropolitan Police Department with valuable assistance from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives Washington Field Office.

The matter was prosecuted under the Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful initiative by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Josh Satter and Lauren Ibanez.

Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful supports President Trump’s Executive Order that cracks down on gun violence, prioritizes federal firearms violations, pursues tougher penalties, and seeks detention for federal firearms violators.

ASHEVILLE, N.C. – A prior South Carolina drug trafficker was sentenced to 22 ½ prison today for trafficking methamphetamine and firearms throughout Cleveland and Rutherford Counties, announced Russ Ferguson, U.S. Attorney for the Western District of North Carolina.

Ronald Keith Goode, 53, of Mooresboro, North Carolina, was sentenced today to 270 months in prison followed by five years of supervised release for selling methamphetamine and firearms. In October 2025, Goode pleaded guilty to distribution of methamphetamine, possession of a firearm in furtherance of drug trafficking and possession of a firearm by a felon.

According to court documents, in February 2025, law enforcement in Rutherford and Cleveland Counties identified Goode as a methamphetamine and gun trafficker. During the investigation, law enforcement determined that Goode would transport large quantities of methamphetamine from the Atlanta area into Rutherford and Cleveland Counties. Between March and May 2025, an undercover agent met with Goode at Goode’s residence in Mooresboro multiple times, and purchased a total of approximately 998.01 grams of pure methamphetamine and 12 firearms. During one of the drug buys, the undercover agent observed four separate pound-sized bags containing methamphetamine (approximately two kilograms). Goode also talked about receiving as much as 10 kilograms of methamphetamine from his source of supply.

Court records also show that, when Goode was arrested on July 2, 2025, law enforcement searched his property in Mooresboro and seized from a shed located on the property a loaded Glock 27, .40 caliber pistol with 26 rounds of ammunition, a loaded Marlin, model 60W, .22 LR rifle with five rounds of ammunition, an unloaded Masterpiece Arms Defender 9mm pistol, two magazines, 93 rounds of ammunition, a ballistic vest, a digital scale, and small amount of white powder. Law enforcement also seized from Goode’s residence two loaded pistol magazines with three rounds of ammunition and a large digital scale.

“Nearly a kilogram of methamphetamine and a dozen firearms were just the beginning of what investigators uncovered in this case,” said U.S. Attorney Russ Ferguson. “Goode was a repeat trafficker who continued to bring dangerous drugs and guns into our communities. Today’s sentence makes clear that chronic offenders will face serious consequences in the federal system.”

“Drug dealing and firearms trafficking is a deadly combination that puts communities at risk,” said ATF Special Agent in Charge Alicia Jones. “ATF and our law enforcement partners make shutting these illegal networks down and holding traffickers accountable a top priority.”

Goode has prior convictions for trafficking methamphetamine in South Carolina, and he is prohibited from possessing firearms.

This investigation was led by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives along with the Rutherford County Sheriff’s Office, and the Cleveland County Sheriff’s Office.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Christopher Hess of the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Asheville prosecuted the case.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, Assistant Director in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (“FBI”), James C. Barnacle, Jr., and Chief of Police for the Town of Haverstraw, New York, John Gould Jr., announced today the unsealing of an Indictment charging JAQUEY WILKES, a/k/a “BQ,” and TYRONE STEWART, a/k/a “Ty,” with robbery, firearms offenses, and murder in connection with the March 5, 2023 fatal shooting of Eric Quinones in the parking lot outside of his home in Pomona, New York. WILKES, STEWART, and a third individual, LEROY SIMPSON, a/k/a “Unc,” were also charged with narcotics conspiracy in connection with the drug transaction that preceded the robbery and murder. All three defendants were presented this afternoon before U.S. Magistrate Judge Victoria Reznik. The case is assigned to U.S. District Judge District Judge Philip M. Halpern.

“This Office and our law enforcement partners continue to work tirelessly to keep the residents of this District safe,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “As alleged, Jaquey Wilkes and Tyrone Stewart robbed and murdered Eric Quinones outside of his home during a drug deal orchestrated by Leroy Simpson. We will relentlessly pursue those who plague our community with drug and gun violence and will hold them accountable for their crimes.”

“Today’s charges underscore the FBI’s resolve to hold violent offenders who terrorize our communities accountable for their actions,” said Assistant FBI Director James C. Barnacle, Jr. “As alleged, the defendants orchestrated a drug‑related robbery that culminated in a tragic and senseless murder. The FBI will continue to pursue these offenders until they are held fully accountable. We extend our gratitude to our partners at the Haverstraw Police Department and the United States Attorney’s Office for their dedication and coordination throughout this investigation.”

“This indictment is the result of an intensive investigation and the unwavering commitment of our detectives and law enforcement partners to seek justice for the victim and his family,” said Chief of Police for the Town of Haverstraw, John Gould Jr. “From the outset, the Town of Haverstraw Police Department remained committed to following the evidence wherever it led and ensuring that those allegedly responsible for this violent crime were held accountable. I want to commend the dedicated members of the Town of Haverstraw Police Department Detective Division, the FBI, the United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York, and the Rockland County District Attorney’s Office for their collaboration and persistence throughout this investigation. This case demonstrates the importance of strong partnerships among local, federal, and county law enforcement agencies and sends a clear message that acts of violence in our community will be investigated relentlessly, regardless of how much time has passed.”

As alleged in the Indictment, and based on statements made in public court proceedings:

On or about March 5, 2023, WILKES and STEWART robbed Eric Quinones at gunpoint in the parking lot outside of the Manors Apartments in Pomona, New York. WILKES and STEWART stole from Quinones, without limitation, narcotics and a firearm. In the course of that robbery, WILKES and STEWART brandished firearms and shot Quinones, resulting in his death. SIMPSON conspired with WILKES and STEWART to orchestrate the narcotics transaction that preceded Quinones’s robbery and murder.

* * *

WILKES, 29, of Nyack, New York, and STEWART, 35, of Nyack, New York, are each charged with Hobbs Act Robbery, which carries a maximum term of twenty years in prison; Firearms Use, Carrying, and Possession, which carries a mandatory minimum term of 10 years in prison and a maximum term of life in prison, and; Murder Through Use of a Firearm, which carries a maximum term of life in prison or death. WILKES, STEWART, and SIMPSON, 33, of Pomona, New York, are also charged with Narcotics Conspiracy, which carries a maximum term of twenty years in prison.

The statutory minimum and maximum potential sentences in this case are prescribed by Congress and provided here for informational purposes only, as any sentencing of the defendants will be determined by the judge.

Mr. McDonald praised the outstanding investigative efforts of the FBI Westchester County Safe Streets Task Force, Town of Haverstraw Police Department, Rockland County Sheriff’s Office, and Orangetown Police Department and thanked the Rockland County District Attorney’s Office for its assistance in this investigation.

The case is being prosecuted by the Office’s White Plains Division. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kathryn Wheelock and Ioannis Drivas are in charge of the prosecution.

The charges in the Indictment are merely accusations and the defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.

USDA Announces $180 Million Seed Sovereignty Initiative to Strengthen U.S. Agricultural Security
(WASHINGTON, D.C., October 6, 2026) – Today, U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins announced a $180 million investment to launch the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Seed Sovereignty Initiative, a major effort to both strengthen U.S. agricultural security by protecting the plant genetic resources that underpin American agriculture and enable breakthroughs in U.S. agricultural innovation.
This initiative will provide much-needed investments in USDA’s Agricultural Research Service (ARS) National Plant Germplasm System (NPGS), which houses more than 600,000 accessions representing over 16,000 species. Using this funding, USDA will sequence collections of major crops to unlock the tremendous potential of the plant genetic resources the United States holds and identify critical gaps.
“Since President Trump returned to office, he has made it clear that we are putting American farmers first. For too long, the future of our crops and our seeds has not been a priority. That changes today, because we cannot afford to depend on foreign adversaries for next year’s crop,” said Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins. “Today’s announcement is another example of this administration focusing on the inputs our agriculture industry depends on and ensuring a future where our farmers are the most productive in the world.”
Foreign competitors are actively acquiring and sequencing plant genetic resources from around the world. Meanwhile, the United States has not yet capitalized on the genetic information within U.S. collections, which is not fully sequenced. The Seed Sovereignty Initiative will help close that knowledge gap and reduce the risk of future foreign dependence.
“America’s agricultural resources are a strategic national asset,” said Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. “We need to survey our domestic resources, understand where we are vulnerable, and ensure the United States never has to rely on foreign competitors for critical agricultural resources.”
Over two years, USDA will characterize and sequence numerous NPGS collections and use advanced technologies, including super intelligence, to identify valuable traits. This work will help USDA and American researchers respond more quickly to emerging pests and diseases and support the development of new crop varieties to benefit U.S. farmers and consumers.
“The National Plant Germplasm System contains tremendous untapped potential for American agriculture,” said Dr. Scott Hutchins, USDA Under Secretary for Research, Education, and Economics and Chief Scientist. “Modern sequencing will allow us to unlock that potential and put it to work for American farmers, providing them a strong advantage.”
The Seed Sovereignty Initiative will move USDA from preserving America’s agricultural genetic resources to fully understanding and strategically using the resources to strengthen American agriculture.
USDA is also expanding its existing Memorandum of Understanding with the U.S. Department of Justice to strengthen competition in agricultural input markets, with a continued robust emphasis on seeds. The expanded partnership will help ensure American farmers have greater transparency, stronger competition, and more choices in the seed marketplace.
###
title: USDA Announces $180 Million Seed Sovereignty Initiative to Strengthen U.S. Agricultural Security

text:
Fast Facts
The government contracts with private companies, known as plan sponsors, to provide Medicare Part D prescription drug coverage. These plan sponsors work with pharmacy benefit managers to pay pharmacies for drugs.
Some plan sponsors are "vertically integrated"—under common ownership with pharmacy benefit managers and pharmacies.
We found that for some of the largest vertically integrated sponsors, about 25% of Part D prescriptions were dispensed by pharmacies they owned, often mail-order pharmacies. And these sponsors often charged beneficiaries less for prescriptions at their own pharmacies, encouraging beneficiaries to use those pharmacies.
Prescription drug bottles in a line on a shelf
Reissued with Revisions Oct 06, 2026
Revised October 6, 2026 to correct the percentages in the second sentence of the Highlights Page. The corrected sentence should read “GAO found that, for four large Part D plan sponsors, the pharmacies they owned accounted for about 28 percent of the Part D drugs they provided to their enrollees (drug utilization) and about 24 percent of the total payments to pharmacies in 2023 (see figure).”
Highlights
What GAO Found
The insurance plan sponsors that provide Medicare Part D drug coverage have increasingly become vertically integrated—that is, under common ownership—with pharmacy benefit managers and pharmacies. GAO found that, for four large Part D plan sponsors, the pharmacies they owned accounted for about 28 percent of the Part D drugs they provided to their enrollees (drug utilization) and about 24 percent of the total payments to pharmacies in 2023 (see figure). Payments included both reimbursement from plan sponsors and cost sharing paid by or on behalf of beneficiaries. When these vertically integrated plan sponsors’ own pharmacies provided drugs to their enrollees, they primarily did so through mail-order pharmacies. In contrast, other (non-owned) pharmacies primarily provided drugs through retail pharmacies.
Percentage of Drug Utilization and Payments at Owned and Non-Owned Pharmacies for Four Selected Medicare Part D Plan Sponsors, 2023
When these plan sponsors paid pharmacies for a 30-day supply of the 100 most commonly used prescription drugs, payments and cost sharing for at least 94 percent of these drugs were lower for owned pharmacies than for non-owned pharmacies. These 100 drugs with the highest total utilization in 2023 were primarily generic drugs, and average payments to owned and non-owned pharmacies for a 30-day supply of most were $10 or less. Lower cost sharing at plan sponsors’ own (primarily mail-order) pharmacies gives beneficiaries a financial incentive to use these pharmacies instead of non-owned (primarily retail) pharmacies, though beneficiaries may consider other factors when choosing a pharmacy to fill a prescription.
Payments to pharmacies and cost sharing were also generally lower at owned pharmacies for the 100 drugs with the highest total payments in 2023, which were primarily brand-name drugs. For some of these drugs, however, payments or cost sharing were higher at owned pharmacies. For example, cost sharing across the four selected plan sponsors was up to about $340 higher at owned pharmacies for about half of the 20 drugs with the highest payments per 30-day supply.
Why GAO Did This Study
Medicare Part D spent $150 billion on prescription drug coverage for 54 million beneficiaries in 2025. Vertically integrated plan sponsors may encourage beneficiaries to fill prescriptions at—or utilize—their own pharmacies, a practice known as steering.
GAO was asked to review vertical integration among Part D plan sponsors, pharmacy benefit managers, and pharmacies. This report describes drug utilization at and payments to selected vertically integrated Part D plan sponsors’ own pharmacies compared to non-owned pharmacies, among other issues.
GAO selected four vertically integrated Part D plan sponsors from among the 15 plan sponsors with the largest Part D enrollment in 2023. These four large, vertically integrated plan sponsors accounted for over 40 percent of total Part D enrollment in 2023. GAO analyzed the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Part D utilization and payments data for 2023 (the data most recently available at the time of GAO’s analysis). Our results for the four selected plan sponsors for 2023 are not generalizable to other plan sponsors or years. For example, Part D benefit changes since 2023 could have affected plan sponsors’ Part D drug utilization and payments at owned and non-owned pharmacies.
For more information, contact John Dicken at dickenj@gao.gov.
Reissued with revisions on Oct. 6, 2026

ALEXANDRIA, Va. – David J. Rush, 49, of Ashburn, pled guilty today to executing a scheme to defraud the federal government relating to the misuse of his government position, resulting in a loss of approximately $194 million.

“Federal employees are entrusted with serving the American people, not themselves,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “The Trump Administration is committed to rooting out waste, fraud, and abuse in the federal government, including by prosecuting those who foolishly defraud American taxpayers.”

“The United States entrusted Davis Rush with the resources to protect our nation and its people, and for sheer avarice he chose to betray that trust for personal enrichment,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Theophani K. Stamos for the Eastern District of Virginia. “He robbed his country, not just of its treasury, but also of its faith. This office is committed to prosecuting those who undermine the security of the United States.”

“Following an internal investigation that identified potential crimes, CIA immediately referred this matter to the FBI,” said CIA Director John Ratcliffe. “David Rush abused his position and betrayed the public trust and should be held fully accountable for his actions. We appreciate our law enforcement partners in the FBI and Department of Justice for securing this outcome. The Agency is committed to ensuring that those entrusted with our Nation’s secrets are held to the absolute highest standard.”

“By his own admission, David Rush defrauded the government of hundreds of millions of dollars, and then misused those funds for extravagant purchases,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “Rush betrayed his oath, his co-workers, and the American people and he will now face justice for his actions. This plea demonstrates the FBI’s commitment to protecting the public’s trust; and that no government position, security clearance, or access to government resources places anyone above the law.”

“As a former military service member and senior government official, Rush understood the gravity of the oaths he swore to protect the United States and its national security interests,” said Assistant Director in Charge Darren B. Cox of the FBI Washington Field Office. “Yet he chose to violate those commitments for his own personal enrichment. Rush manipulated security protocols designed to safeguard the nation’s most sensitive information, placing colleagues, operations, and lives at risk. The FBI remains resolute in its mission to defend the United States against criminal and national security threats, including— and especially—those that arise from within.”

“Our Intelligence Community must have the trust of the American people to operate effectively in a Nation committed to transparency and the rule of law,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “Rush repeatedly betrayed that trust. He defrauded the United States out of approximately $194 million in real estate, jewelry, and other valuable property, including 298 gold bars. Worse, his self-serving actions threatened to erode public confidence in the intelligence services that must strive in secret to keep America safe. Thankfully, the efforts of the Department of Justice, its partners in law enforcement, and the Intelligence Community exposed Rush’s crimes. Today’s plea marks an important step in bringing Rush to justice.”

According to court documents, Rush was employed in a senior executive-level position with a federal agency and held a Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) security clearance. He reached that position, in part, by lying about his education and military experience. Rush used his position of extraordinary public trust to create fictitious government authorities – including a fabricated Special Access Program – to obtain U.S. government funds for his personal benefit. Once he received the funds, Rush acquired gold bars and directed approximately $145 million in wire transfers that he ultimately used to purchase luxury real estate, watches, and at least one car. As a result of his scheme, Rush fraudulently obtained approximately $193,590,400 in U.S. government funds

On May 19, the FBI searched Rush’s residence and recovered 298 gold bars, approximately $2,106,550 in cash, €104,795, and numerous luxury watches. Rush had obtained the gold bars at an approximate cost to the government of $46 million. Pursuant to the plea agreement, Rush has agreed to forfeit the gold bars and currency found at his home, the fraudulently obtained properties, 30 watches (many of which were Rolexes), and two 2026 BMW Alpina vehicles, at least one of which is valued at approximately $172,000.

Cash and gold bars recovered in search of Rush's residence

Rush is scheduled to be sentenced on Jan. 28, 2027. He faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison, three years of supervised release, forfeiture, restitution, and a fine. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Raizza Ty and Gavin R. Tisdale of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia and Trial Attorneys Kevin C. Hakala and Kathryn D. DeMarco of the Justice Department’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section are prosecuting the case.

The Department of Justice's investigation is continuing. The Director of National Intelligence has requested that the Inspector General for the Intelligence Community initiate an investigation.

Related court documents and information are located on the website of the District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia or on PACER by searching for Case No. 1:26-cr-185.

During Fire Prevention Week, my Administration honors the memory of America’s courageous firefighters and first responders for their extraordinary service and sacrifice. We are reaffirming our commitment to strengthening fire prevention and emergency response across the Nation. I encourage every American to take simple steps to protect their homes, families, and communities from preventable fires.
Fire safety begins at home. Every family can take precautions to prevent fires, and to better protect themselves and their loved ones. These can include mapping out a home escape plan, testing smoke and carbon monoxide alarms every month, replacing the worn wiring and overloaded outlets that spark so many household fires, or practicing safe charging habits that minimize the potential of fires from ubiquitous electronic devices. These commonsense steps can save lives by preventing fire or by ensuring families are prepared in the event of an emergency.
My Administration remains committed to protecting American lives from the threat of fires and improving our country’s ability to prevent and respond to them. Last year, I signed an Executive Order to streamline Federal wildfire response, strengthen local preparedness, and put modern technology to work detecting and fighting fires. We are also working to establish the United States Wildland Fire Service to better coordinate Federal wildfire programs and respond more effectively when fires break out.
This week, we also honor America’s extraordinary firefighters, first responders, emergency personnel, and volunteers who selflessly respond whenever the alarm sounds. Their determination to aid fellow Americans in distress embodies the highest American ideals of heroism, courage, and service to others. Together, we recommit to preventing fires, protecting our communities, and building a Nation more prepared, more ready, and more resilient than ever before.
title: Presidential Message on Fire Prevention Week

Duke University, located in North Carolina’s Fourth Congressional District, was a recipient of a Teen Pregnancy Prevention grant in 2023.
In July, 79 members of the Democratic Women’s Caucus (DWC) and the Democratic Caucus, sent a letter to the Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, demanding the reversal of the Trump Administration’s cancellation of 53 active Teen Pregnancy Prevention Program (TPP) grants that the Department claimed were no longer aligned with the agency’s priorities.
Recent decisions by the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia blocked HHS from establishing new grants with new funding conditions. 92 members of Congress, including Rep. According to court documents, on January 2, 2026, Daphne Police Department officers responded to a room at the Eastern Shore Motel following a report of domestic violence. When officers arrived, they observed a woman crying and appearing to be in distress. Wooten became combative with officers, prompting one officer to deploy a taser. The taser probes did not incapacitate Wooten, and he pulled the probes from his body with his hands. After a struggle, several officers were able to gain control of Wooten and place him under arrest.

During the arrest, officers recovered a loaded handgun from Wooten’s right pants pocket. Officers also observed marijuana in the motel room. The room was secured while officers obtained a search warrant. A subsequent search revealed marijuana and a used marijuana grinder on the bedside table.

The firearm recovered from Wooten was a Hi-Point Model C9 9-millimeter handgun. The serial number on the bottom of the firearm’s frame, in front of the trigger guard, had been damaged. The surrounding plastic showed signs that someone had attempted to obliterate the serial number, apparently using a file or similar tool. Upon closer examination, agents were able to identify the firearm’s serial number.

Federal law prohibits convicted felons from possessing firearms. At the time he possessed the firearm, Wooten had two prior felony convictions: a conviction for Breaking and Entering a Vehicle in the Circuit Court of Baldwin County, Alabama, arising from conduct on or about June 17, 2025, and a conviction for Robbery in the Third Degree in the Circuit Court of Baldwin County, Alabama, arising from conduct on or about August 29, 2014.

U.S. Attorney Sean P. Costello of the Southern District of Alabama made the announcement.

The case was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and the Daphne Police Department.

Assistant U.S. Attorney George F. May prosecuted the case on behalf of the United States.

MIAMI – A convicted felon and gang leader has been sentenced to federal prison for illegally possessing firearms and conspiring to smuggle synthetic drugs into jail while awaiting trial.

U.S. District Judge Melissa Damian sentenced Michael Ridley, 34, of Fort Lauderdale, to 90 months in prison after he pleaded guilty to possessing firearms as a convicted felon, attempting to possess contraband in prison, and conspiring to possess with intent to distribute a controlled substance.

“Michael Ridley was a convicted felon and gang leader who illegally armed himself, flaunted firearms on social media, and then, after his arrest, tried to continue his criminal activity from inside jail by conspiring to smuggle liquid synthetic drugs into the facility,” said U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida. “This seven-and-a-half-year federal prison sentence reflects a simple reality: gang leaders who possess illegal guns and continue directing criminal activity from behind bars will be held accountable.”

According to court records, on June 12, 2025, Ridley posted a social media video showing him with two handguns at a shooting range. The video included the notation “TTB (Train to Bag),” a reference to a homicide victim’s body being placed in a bag and removed from a crime scene. Following the posting, law enforcement obtained a criminal complaint charging Ridley with unlawfully possessing the firearms while at the range.

Ridley was arrested on July 23, 2025. At the time of his arrest, law enforcement found him in possession of a firearm that had previously been reported stolen and an attached extended magazine.

Following his arrest, the U.S. sought Ridley’s pretrial detention. Ridley was a leader of the Eastside Gangsta Bloods (EGB), which operates as part of the larger United Blood Nation (UBN). The court ordered Ridley detained, and he was held as a federal detainee at two separate facilities in Broward County.

While detained, Ridley conspired with outside accomplices, including other gang members, to smuggle narcotics into the jail disguised as legal mail addressed to him. The method, commonly referred to as “paper dope,” involves saturating ordinary sheets of paper with liquid synthetic drugs.

At sentencing, the government presented evidence that Ridley possessed more than a dozen firearms and held a leadership position within EGB.

U.S. Attorney Reding Quiñones and Special Agent in Charge Brett D. Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office made the announcement.

FBI Miami investigated the case, with assistance from the Broward County Sheriff’s Office.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Julia Vaglienti prosecuted the case.

This prosecution is a part of the U.S. Department of Justice’s Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) program. PSN is the centerpiece of the Department’s violent crime reduction efforts. PSN is an evidence-based program proven to be effective at reducing violent crime. Through the PSN program a broad spectrum of law enforcement and community stakeholders work together to identify the most pressing violent crime problems in the community and develop comprehensive solutions to address them. As part of this strategy, PSN focuses enforcement efforts on the most violent offenders and partners with locally based prevention and reentry programs to reduce violence crime and gun violence, and to make our local neighborhoods safer for everyone.

Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Southern District of Florida at www.flsd.uscourts.gov or at http://pacer.flsd.uscourts.gov , under case numbers 25-cr-60177.

It has arrested and arbitrarily detained hundreds of Palestinian healthcare workers, including at least 16 physicians who continue to be held in inhumane conditions. Among them is Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, whom the Israeli government has arbitrarily detained since 2024 and tortured to the point of near-death after previously murdering his son and brutally attacking his hospital,” said the Members.
“Israel’s systematic annihilation of medical facilities and healthcare workers is not an accident or unfortunate consequence of war; it is an intentional policy designed to further occupation, apartheid, and genocide against the Palestinian people. We demand the immediate release of Dr. Abu Safiya and all other arbitrarily detained healthcare workers and Palestinian prisoners. And we demand an end to U.S. arms transfers to Israel, including the Trump Administration’s latest $2.8 billion sale of bombs. Congress must block this sale and pass the Block the Bombs Act to finally end our government’s shameful complicity in Israel’s mass atrocities.”
Congressman García also recently led a letter condemning the violence by Israeli settlers, police and military in the village of al-Mughayyir in the occupied West Bank, and called for the release of Marwan Barghouti who has been detained and tortured in Israeli prison for over 20 years.

October 6, 2026
WATCH: Pressley, Wu, Breadon Condemn USPS Service Cuts and Proposed Closure of Allston Post Office
Proposal for Allston Branch Also Coincides with USPS Announcement to “Temporarily” Close USPS Field Corner Office Later This Month
Today, Pressley Joined Markey, Mass. Colleagues Demanding USPS Cease Campaign of Post Office Closures in the Commonwealth
ALLSTON – Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07) joined Boston Mayor Michelle Wu, Boston City Council President Liz Breadon, and elected officials at a rally to condemn the United States Postal Service’s (USPS) actions to reduce service for residents across the city and plans to permanently close the Allston Post Office. The City of Boston also sent USPS leadership a letter notifying them of the City’s strong opposition to the agency’s reversal of its prior commitment to restore postal services in Allston.
If closed, 87,000 residents of Allston-Brighton will be served by one post office location in Brighton. This proposal also coincides with USPS announcing this week that it will, purportedly temporarily, close the USPS Fields Corner branch later this month.
“The USPS belongs to all of us and is a vital lifeline for folks in Allston who depend on it for everything from daily medications and Social Security checks to mail-in ballots and staying connected to loved ones,” said Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley. “That’s why we’re not letting them off the hook while they go back on their word and rip away this essential resource by permanently closing the Allston branch. I’m proud to stand with Mayor Wu and Councilor Breadon and our colleagues to fight back.”
“The reversal of the Post Office’s prior commitments to reopen the Allston USPS branch is an abdication of responsibility not only to Boston, but to all families,” said Mayor Michelle Wu. “This post office serves grandparents buying stamps to mail birthday cards to their grandchildren, parents sending care packages to students away at college, and residents and small businesses who rely on this location to conduct business. I thank Councilor Breadon for her work and leadership in bringing our community together as we continue to urge United State Postal Service leaders to keep their word and prevent the permanent closure of this vital resource for our community.”
“USPS’s proposal to permanently close the Allston Post Office is an unacceptable reversal of a promise made to our community by USPS,” said Boston City Council President Breadon. “For the past seven years, the 87,000 residents of Allston-Brighton have been served by only one post office location; Newton, which has a population of 88,000, has 10. Our neighborhood will continue to fight for the reestablishment of the Allston Post Office, fair treatment from USPS, and the fulfillment of commitments made.”
At today’s rally, the elected officials invited Allston residents to join them in contesting the closure. This proposal also coincides with USPS announcing last week that it will, purportedly temporarily, close the USPS Fields Corner branch later this month. People interested in submitting public comments can email allstonpostoffice@boston.gov. People should include their name and home address with their comments. The deadline for this initial period is Sunday, October 11 and there will be future opportunities for residents to engage on this issue in the coming months.
Congresswoman Pressley, Mayor Wu, and City Council President Breadon were joined at the press conference today by Scott Hoffman, National Business Agent, American Postal Workers Union; Tony D’Isdoro, President Allston Civic Association; George Huynh, Executive Director VietAID; State Senator Will Brownsberger; State Representative Kevin Honan; City Councilor-At-Large Ruthzee Louijeune; City Councilor-At-Large Erin Murphy; City Councilor-At-Large Henry Santana; City Councilor John FitzGerald, District 3; and President Mark Sideris, Watertown.
“The USPS has asked the Allston community to engage in a charade that operational performance will be enhanced by the permanent closing of the Allston Post Office,” said Tony D’Isidoro, President of the Allston Civic Association. “They’re not fooling anyone! This new business model will fail because it will not be applied fairly across the country.”
“Every day, we see how much our neighbors rely on the post office to apply for benefits, renew passports, update their address, receive important documents, and send packages home to family. For seniors and residents who don’t drive or are more comfortable in their own language, a nearby post office is a lifeline,” said George Huynh, Executive Director of Vietnamese American Initiative for Development (VietAID). “Allston has gone seven years without one. Fields Corner is now facing the same uncertainty, and we cannot afford to wait seven years. We urge USPS to commit to a clear timeline for a permanent location in Fields Corner and to restore the post office here in Allston. Every neighborhood in Boston deserves a post office close to home.”
“It’s bad enough that the Post Office degrades service levels, but here they want to take the post office away lock, stock, and barrel,” said Scott Hoffman, National Business Agent, American Postal Workers Union. “It’s a slippery slope type condition if we let them pull a post office after making promises to the community and to workers, then all is lost. This is a brazen move.”
Footage from the press conference is available here.
Photo Credit: Boston Mayor’s Office
In early September 2026, the United States Postal Service (USPS) announced its intent to study the permanent closure of the Allston Post Office Branch. This proposal has sparked concern and frustration among residents and elected officials. If closed, all 87,000 residents of Allston-Brighton will be served by only one post office location in Brighton.
The Allston Post Office Branch was previously located at 47 Harvard Avenue in Allston. Due to structural issues with its building, USPS suspended service at this location in 2019. In 2021, the former Allston Post Office site was purchased by Boston-based real estate firm Eden Properties. A mixed-used residential project was later approved for the site and is currently under construction. As part of this redevelopment, Eden Properties worked with USPS to reestablish the Allston Post Office Branch in a ground-floor commercial space designed for use by the post office.
In June 2025, USPS sent a letter to Mayor Wu stating its final decision to relocate and reestablish the Allston Post Office. In early September 2026, however, Allston residents received notification via letter from USPS announcing its intent to permanently close the Allston Post Office Branch.
A transcript of the Congresswoman’s remarks is available below and the full video is available here.
Transcript: Rep. Pressley Condemns USPS Plan to Close Allston Branch
October 5, 2026
Allston, MA
In serving on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, I was conducting a lot of oversight in the fight to send Postmaster DeJoy on his way. And I thought when we did that that we might be getting on a path to what the people deserve, and certainly the dedicated postal workers deserve. Instead, we find ourselves here.
But the reason why, in the midst of this, I still have hope, is because I believe in the power of pressure.
I believe in the power of organizing. I believe in the power of solidarity.
I was looking at Representative Honan and remembering the fight to save our branch libraries when we all came together and understood that they are a public good, a lifeline to and for the community, and so this is that same kind of fight. This is about livelihoods. This is about lives. This is about commerce. This is about connectivity. So that’s what brings us all here today.
I’m so grateful for the leadership of everyone who has been named and who has not been named, I’m so grateful to our mayor for convening us, and certainly grateful to our Council President, President Breadon, who has been indefatigable, and that is what we need to be in this fight.
Folks were shuddering a little bit. Maybe it’s a little chilly. It’s hot one second, cold the next. Yeah, welcome to perimenopause.
But the point is, the point is, you might be a little uncomfortable, but deal with it, so that we are never complacent in our advocacy.
I grew up in a family of proud letter carriers, postal workers, nurses, first responders. That was how we built the middle class. These good union jobs. They take pride in that work, no matter the weather, no matter the season, no matter the ingratitude, so that’s what brings us here today.
So I thank you all for showing up, for giving a damn, to show your support for reopening your neighborhood’s post office, which has been closed since 2019.
It is a shame, and the reason why we have to agitate, resist, and give our feedback, we see this is a very slippery slope because they’re trying to bring the same pain to Dorchester, which is why solidarity is so essential in this moment.
But everyone here, your advocacy, your love of community is inspiring. Now, while this injustice has gone on for too long, you refuse, you accept it as an inevitability, and let it be quietly swept under the rug.
So again, I say thank you to everyone, and especially to Scott Hoffman and all of our brothers and sisters at the American Postal Workers Union, who stand up every day for their members, as well as service and reliability for our neighbors.
For the past seven years, Allston residents have gone without retail post office services and had to travel to Brighton, to Brookline, or Cambridge to do their daily business. In that time, USPS has made commitments to my office, my colleagues’ offices, and the folks living in this community that they were searching for a new location and would indeed reopen.
There have been ups and downs, but finally, finally, it appeared we were close to having the branch reopen. A lease had been agreed to, construction plans were in place with the developer. Now we are told that this plan is to keep this branch permanently closed.
This is unconscionable. This is unacceptable.
With last week’s announcement of the quote-unquote “temporary” closure of the Fields Corner Post Office, I find it hard to believe that this is just a coincidence. And to be clear, these efforts to close our local branches are all part of a coordinated campaign.
Y’all are tired of me saying it as the co-founder of the Stop Project 2025 Task Force, but it was all laid out. It was not a blueprint. It was a playbook. They want to privatize the USPS. They want to privatize these essential services that our constituents need every single day.
The USPS has been serving our communities for 250 years, delivering our mail, our checks, our prescriptions, and our ballots.
The dedicated carriers who are out on our sidewalks six days per week are members of our community. They know our neighbors, and they are the way folks most often interact with the federal government.
These services are not nice to haves—they are must haves. And you, along with every other community, has come to depend upon them and rightly deserve them.
These efforts to degrade and undermine the postal service are intended to exhaust you and your neighbors, so that you’ll give up and do your business somewhere else. Hell no, we won’t go. But the services provided by USPS are a public good and should not be left to billionaires and for-profit private corporations to play games with.
Today, I’m proud to stand with Allston and everyone here, calling for the Postal Service to keep their word to this community.
They must reverse the decision, work to reopen the Austin branch, and restore daily service.
If they intend to follow through with this closure plan, they must give the community a way to have their voice heard, not simply hold a midday Zoom meeting when folks are at work or at school.
The 87,000 Allston-Brighton residents, our neighbors in Fields Corner, folks in Somerville, Grove Hall, and Mission Hill all need and should have an accessible and conveniently located post office to do their business.
So we will not stop advocating for what you deserve.
Again, I believe in the power of pressure, of organizing, and of solidarity.
We will not stop fighting the Republican campaign, because they are the architects of this, to privatize the postal service, and we will not stop fighting until Allston has a post office again.
And now, as someone who comes from a long line of letter carriers, it is my privilege to introduce a man who fights for better service for our friends and neighbors every single day, national business agent for the American Postal Workers Union, Scott Hoffman.
—
Throughout her time in Congress, Congresswoman Pressley has championed for federal resources to support the United States Postal Service and its employees.
- In December 2024, in a House Oversight Committee hearing, Rep. Pressley discussed the essential role that the United States Postal Service (USPS) plays in our communities and questioned USPS Postmaster General Louis DeJoy about the widespread delays and service failures that have severely impacted her constituents in the Massachusetts 7th.
- In October 2024, Rep. Pressley joined postal workers from the American Postal Workers Union (APWU) for a rally in Boston to sound the alarm about the United States Postal Service’s (USPS) substandard performance and service to communities.
- In August 2024, Rep. Pressley joined Senator Markey on a letter urging USPS to re-open postal facilities and improve service, spotlighting a larger statewide problem with postal service in Massachusetts.
- On December 16, 2022, Rep. Pressley joined Reps. Lynch and Raskin in leading their colleagues on a letter urging the extension of COVID-19 workers’ compensation benefits for postal workers.
- On February 25, 2021, Rep. Pressley called for postal banking to advance racial and economic justice during a House Committee on Oversight hearing.
- On February 19, 2021, Rep. Pressley urged President Biden in a letter to replace Postmaster General Louis DeJoy and appoint a diverse United States Postal Service Board of Governors.

- On August 21, 2020, Rep. Pressley and Rep. Payne lead their colleagues in a letter pushing party leadership to stand firm on postal service funding.
- On August 25, 2020, Rep. Pressley questioned Postmaster General Louis DeJoy and the United States Postal Service Board of Governors Chairman Robert Duncan about the harmful impact policy changes at USPS had on the workforce during a House Committee on Oversight hearing.

Pensacola, Florida – Hunter Drake Lovett, 30, of Pace, Florida, pleaded guilty in federal court to felony theft of government property. The plea was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida.

U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “This defendant thought he could enrich himself by stealing signs from our national parks that were paid for with U.S. taxpayer money, but thanks to the excellent investigative work by our federal law enforcement partners and this successful prosecution by my office, he now faces justice for his crimes.”

Court documents reflect that, in August 2026, state law enforcement and federal agents executed a search warrant on the defendant’s storage unit in Shalimar, Florida. Inside the storage unit, agents found hundreds of signs that were stolen from state and federal properties in the Northern District of Florida, Middle District of Alabama, Southern District of Alabama, Middle District of Georgia, and Southern District of Mississippi. Agents utilized GPS data from the defendant’s work vehicle to confirm that he was within close proximity to multiple sign locations at the times the thefts occurred, including the Eufaula National Wildlife Refuge and Conecuh National Forest. The defendant would then sell or attempt to sell the stolen signage to antique malls, flea markets, or via social media for profit. The signs that the defendant stole from the U.S. Forest Service and U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service totaled $7,326.79.

Lovett faces up to 10 years’ imprisonment.

The case was investigated by the United States Fish & Wildlife Service and United States Forest Service with assistance from the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services Office of Agricultural Law Enforcement, Eufaula (Alabama) Police Department, and Florida Forest Service. Assistant United States Attorney Brooke D. Lindsay is prosecuting the case.

Lovett’s sentencing is scheduled for December 22, 2026, at 10:00 a.m., at the United States Courthouse in Pensacola before United States District Judge T. Kent Wetherell, II.

The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl .

Pappas Meets with NH CAP Leaders on Rising Energy Costs and LIHEAP
Yesterday Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01) hosted a roundtable with leaders of New Hampshire Community Action Partnership agencies for a discussion on the impact of rising energy costs on Granite Staters and the importance of the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP).
New Hampshire households could pay $2,300 for home heating oil this winter because of President Trump’s war with Iran, a 31% increase. The cost of groceries rose 2.9 percent overall this year, and families paid $310 more for food during President Trump's first year in office compared to 2024. In total, American families have spent over $3,800 more on goods and services since President Trump took office.
“Electricity prices are up, natural gas and home heating oil prices are up, and diesel fuel is hitting record highs. Granite Staters don’t need federal data to tell them this: they are feeling it with every electric and gas bill. As we enter the colder months, tackling the rising cost of energy could not be more urgent,” said Congressman Pappas. “My new legislation would lower energy costs by increasing federal support for heating assistance, expanding eligibility to more families, and lowering gas and diesel costs. I will continue fighting to lower costs for families and put more money back in their pockets.”
Pappas recently introduced three new bills to lower energy costs.
The LIHEAP Act would expand the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP), one of the most successful programs aimed at reducing energy costs for working families.
The American Homes First Act would increase funding for LIHEAP by redirecting $1 billion from President Trump’s ‘Board of Peace’ slush fund.
The Consumer Fuel Prices Relief Act would provide federal fuel tax relief until the end of September 2027 by pausing the gas tax, the diesel tax, and the aviation fuel tax, while ensuring the benefit is immediately passed on to consumers in full. The legislation builds on his bicameral Gas Prices Relief Act of 2026, introduced in March, which would have suspended the federal gas tax through October 1, 2026. The legislation safeguards and maintains funding for roads, bridges, and gas spill remediation, and holds corporations accountable if they fail to pass along savings to individual consumers.
Background:
LIHEAP helps low-income individuals and families pay for heating and cooling and mitigates the impacts of rising energy costs and extreme weather events. Across the nation, LIHEAP helps nearly 6 million households afford their energy bills, including nearly 30,000 households in New Hampshire, but Secretary Kennedy’s decision last year to fire all LIHEAP staff and President Trump’s repeated efforts to fully defund the program have put this assistance at risk. 
In September 2026, Pappas led 116 of his Congressional colleagues across the aisle in urging for LIHEAP funds to be delivered to states as soon as possible, and no later than November 1st. He previously led 89 of his Congressional colleagues in calling for the protection of LIHEAP and the rehiring of all HHS staff who manage the LIHEAP program that were fired in April 2025, and has repeatedly led bipartisan calls for the Trump administration to distribute LIHEAP funds in a timely manner.
Pappas is a fierce advocate for efforts that lower energy costs for Granite Staters and programs that help low-income families pay their bills. He has previously introduced, cosponsored, or called for the passage of the following legislation:
- Pappas leads the bipartisan Energy Burden Tax Credit Act, which would provide a refundable tax credit to families struggling with high energy costs, saving households hundreds of dollars a year on energy.
- Pappas leads the bipartisanInvesting in State Energy Act, which would ensure funds from the Weatherization Assistance Program and State Energy Program are distributed without delay to state agencies and local partners that implement these cost-saving energy initiatives.
- Pappas leads the bipartisan Transmission Facilitation Program Reauthorization Act, which would reauthorize funding for DOE’s program providing states and municipalities with federal support for projects developing new transmission lines or upgrading existing transmission lines, helping accelerate project timelines and increase grid capacity.
- Pappas leads the Heroes Home Energy Savings Act, which would reauthorize and increase funding for the Weatherization Assistance Program Enhancement and Innovation Grant to spur innovation in weatherization and provide active-duty and reserve military families with grants to help lower their energy costs.
- Pappas leads the bipartisan Bolstering Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve Act, which would require the Department of Energy (DOE) to conduct a long-range strategic review of the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve (NEHHOR) and report to Congress on opportunities to strengthen it.
- He supports the bipartisan Banning Oil Exports to Foreign Adversaries Act, which would prohibit the sale or export of our nation’s Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPR) to foreign adversaries including China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea, closing a dangerous loophole that threatens U.S. energy and national security
- He supports the Energy Independence and Affordability Act, which would reinstate clean energy tax credits established by the Inflation Reduction Actand repealed by Republicans last year. These credits would help individuals, families, small businesses, and manufacturers save money on clean energy, including purchasing clean vehicles or making upgrades such as installing rooftop solar.
- He supports the bipartisan Weatherization Enhancement and Readiness Act of 2025, which would reauthorize and improve the Weatherization Assistance Program and guarantee the program can continue to provide weatherization services to tens of thousands of homes every year, saving households hundreds on their energy costs.
- He supports the bipartisan LIHEAP Staffing Support Act, which would set a minimum staffing level within HHS to administer LIHEAP.
