USITC Institutes Section 337 Investigation of Certain Mobile Electronic Devices and Components Thereof
The U.S. International Trade Commission (Commission or USITC) voted to institute an investigation of certain mobile electronic devices and components thereof. The products at issue in the investigation are described in the Commission’s notice of investigation.
The investigation is based on a complaint filed on behalf of trinamiX Sensing LLC of Austin, Texas and trinamiX GmbH of Ludwigshafen am Rhein, Germany on September 3, 2026. The complaint was supplemented on September 17, 2026. The complaint, as supplemented, alleges violations of section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930 based upon the importation into the United States, the sale for importation, and the sale within the United States after importation of certain mobile electronic devices and components thereof that infringe certain claims of the patents asserted by the complainants. The complainants request that the USITC issue a limited exclusion order and cease and desist orders.
The USITC has identified the respondent in this investigation as Apple Inc. of Cupertino, California.
By instituting this investigation (337-TA1525), the USITC has not yet made any decision on the merits of the case. The USITC’s Chief Administrative Law Judge will assign the case to one of the USITC’s administrative law judges (ALJ), who will schedule and hold an evidentiary hearing. The ALJ will make an initial determination as to whether there is a violation of section 337; that initial determination is subject to review by the Commission.
The USITC will make a final determination in the investigation at the earliest practicable time. Within 45 days after institution of the investigation, the USITC will set a target date for completing the investigation. USITC remedial orders in section 337 cases are effective when issued and become final 60 days after issuance unless disapproved for policy reasons by the U.S. Trade Representative within that 60-day period.

COLUMBUS and CLEVELAND, Ohio – United States Attorney Dominick S. Gerace II for the Southern District of Ohio and United States Attorney David M. Toepfer for the Northern District of Ohio announced today arrests in three voter fraud cases for allegations involving voting in an election that included candidates for the office of President, Vice President, Member of the Senate, and Member of the House of Representatives.

In the Southern District of Ohio, a criminal complaint was filed charging Cary Ann Patterson, 59, a citizen of the United Kingdom with lawful permanent resident status, with illegally voting in a federal election as an alien. Voters in federal elections must be U.S. citizens, and the complaint alleges that Patterson voted on Nov. 5, 2024. According to court documents, in 2005, the Gallia County Board of Elections received a voter registration card for Patterson in which “Yes” was marked in response to the question, “Are you a U.S. citizen?” Based on Gallia County Board of Elections records, Patterson allegedly voted in at least 10 elections as a non-citizen.

In the Northern District of Ohio, Arshed Zuberi, 69, a Pakistani national with lawful permanent resident status, has been charged by criminal complaint with illegally voting in a federal election as an alien. He allegedly registered to vote in September 2015 and August 2016. On voter registration forms, Zuberi’s signature appears next to the declaration “I declare under penalty of election falsification I am a citizen of the United States.” Voting records from the Cuyahoga County Board of Elections show that he voted in at least six elections.

A criminal complaint has also been filed in the Northern District of Ohio charging Eliza M. Moss, 63, a citizen of the Philippines with lawful permanent resident status, with unlawfully voting in a federal election as an alien. According to state of Ohio and Ashtabula County voting records, Moss registered to vote in September 2004 and in February 2023. On voter registration forms, her signature appears next to the declaration “I declare under penalty of election falsification I am a citizen of the United States.” Moss allegedly voted in several primary and general elections. According to the criminal complaint, Moss told investigators that the person who helped fill out her registration told her that she could vote despite not being a citizen.

Unlawfully voting in a federal election as an alien is punishable by up to 12 months in prison.

Dominick S. Gerace II, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Ohio; David M. Toepfer, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Ohio; and Acting Special Agent in Charge Jeremy Pierczynski, Homeland Security Investigations Detroit announced the charges. Executive Assistant United States Attorney Christy L. Muncy for the Southern District of Ohio and Assistant United States Attorney Robert Corts for the Northern District of Ohio are representing the United States in these cases.

Criminal complaints merely contain allegations, and defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law.

BISMARCK – United States Attorney Nicholas W. Chase announced that Zachary Paul Femling, age 34, from Fargo, North Dakota, pleaded guilty before United States District Court Judge Daniel L. Hovland to a felony charge of Theft of Government Property for stealing $52,176 from the Social Security Administration.

According to court documents, from August 10, 2021, to January 31, 2026, Femling falsely obtained his deceased relative’s Social Security Administration Disability Insurance Benefits. During the four-and-a-half-year period, Femling did not inform the Social Security Administration of his relative’s death and stole a total of $52,176.

Sentencing in this case is scheduled for January 11, 2027, at 9:00 a.m. in Bismarck before District Judge Daniel L. Hovland.

This case was investigated by the Social Security Administration—Office of Inspector General and prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Jonathan J. O’Konek.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

PHILADELPHIA – FEMA is proposing updates to the Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) for Howard County, Maryland. Community partners are invited to participate in a 90-day appeal and comment period.
The updated maps were produced in coordination with local, state and FEMA officials. Significant community review of the maps has already taken place, but before the maps become final, community partners can identify any corrections or questions about the information provided and submit appeals or comments.
The 90-day appeal period began on September 29, 2026. Residents, business owners and other community partners are encouraged to review the updated maps to learn about local flood risks and potential future flood insurance requirements. They may submit an appeal if they perceive that modeling or data used to create the map is technically or scientifically incorrect.
- An appeal must include technical information, such as hydraulic or hydrologic data, to support the claim.
- Appeals cannot be based on the effects of proposed projects or projects started after the study is in progress.
- If property owners see incorrect information that does not change the flood hazard information—such as a missing or misspelled road name in the Special Flood Hazard Area or an incorrect corporate boundary—they can submit a written comment.
The next step in the mapping process is the resolution of all comments and appeals. Once they are resolved, FEMA will notify communities of the effective date of the final maps.
Submit appeals and comments by contacting the County’s Stormwater Management Department. The preliminary maps may be viewed online at the FEMA Flood Map Changes Viewer,
For more information about the flood maps, contact a FEMA Map Specialist by telephone; toll free, at 1-877-FEMA-MAP (1-877-336-2627) or by email at FEMA-FMIX@fema.dhs.gov.
Most homeowner’s insurance policies do not cover flooding. There are cost-saving options available for those newly mapped into a high-risk flood zone. Learn more about your flood insurance options by talking with your insurance agent and visiting https://www.floodsmart.gov.
Howard County Flood Mapping Milestones
- September 30, 2024 — Flood Risk Review Meeting to review draft flood hazard data.
- August 1, 2025 — Preliminary Flood Insurance Rate Map released.
- August 21, 2025 — Community Coordination and Outreach Meeting to review Preliminary Flood Insurance Rate Map and discuss updates to local floodplain management ordinance and flood insurance.
- September 29, 2026 — Appeal Period starts.
- September 2027* — New Flood Insurance Rate Map becomes effective and flood insurance requirements take effect. (*Timeline subject to change pending completion of the appeal review process.)
If you have any questions, please contact FEMA Region 3 Office of External Affairs at (215) 931-5597 or at femar3newsdesk@fema.dhs.gov.

Follow FEMA online, on X @FEMA or @FEMAEspanol, on FEMA's Facebook page or Espanol page, on Truth Social and FEMA's YouTube account.
For preparedness information, follow the Ready Campaign on X at @Ready.gov, on Instagram @Ready.gov or on the Ready Facebook page.

Dân Biểu Derek Trần giới thiệu dự luật giảm chi phí nhà ở cho các gia đình Nam California
Dự luật mới đề nghị khoản tín dụng thuế dành riêng cho người thuê nhà nhằm giảm gánh nặng trước chi phí sinh hoạt ngày càng tăng tại California
WASHINGTON, DC – Dân Biểu Liên Bang Derek Trần (CA-45) giới thiệu Dự Luật Hỗ Trợ Chi Phí Sinh Hoạt Nhà Ở cho Người Thuê Nhà (COST) Act, để hỗ trợ cư dân tại Nam California đang phải đối mặt với chi phí nhà ở ngày càng tăng. Dự luật thiết lập các khoản tín dụng thuế dành cho người thuê nhà, tiếp nối nỗ lực của Dân Biểu Derek nhằm giúp người dân có thêm cơ hội tiếp cận nhà ở với chi phí hợp lý.
“Chi phí nhà ở trên cả nước, đặc biệt tại Nam California, đã tăng đến mức báo động. Nhiều gia đình phải chật vật mới đủ tiền trả tiền thuê nhà, chưa nói đến việc tiết kiệm cho tương lai,” Dân Biểu Derek Trần cho biết. “Dự luật này sẽ mang lại sự hỗ trợ thiết thực và kịp thời cho những người thuê nhà đang gặp khó khăn, giúp họ trang trải tiền thuê nhà, có thêm ngân sách cho các chi phí sinh hoạt hằng ngày, hoặc thậm chí dành dụm để mua nhà. Tôi tự hào dẫn đầu nỗ lực này vì các gia đình khắp nước Mỹ.”
Các gia đình tại Nam California phải đối mặt với mức chi phí nhà ở thuộc hàng cao nhất cả nước. Tại Orange County, tiền thuê nhà trung bình hiện vượt $3,200 mỗi tháng, tăng gần 40% kể từ năm 2017.
Dự luật đề nghị một khoản tín dụng thuế hoàn lại ở mức căn bản 8% dành cho các gia đình có tổng thu nhập từ $150,000 trở xuống, với mức hỗ trợ tối đa $333 mỗi tháng cho mỗi gia đình, tương đương $4,000 mỗi năm. Riêng tại Địa Hạt 45 của California, hơn 75,000 gia đình có thể được hưởng lợi từ chính sách này.
Trong khi những giải pháp khác nhằm giảm chi phí nhà ở có thể cần nhiều thời gian để thực hiện, dự luật này sẽ trực tiếp giúp người thuê nhà có thêm tiền để trang trải thực phẩm, thuốc men, chi phí chăm sóc trẻ em, và các nhu cầu thiết yếu khác.
Nỗ lực lập pháp này tiếp nối những hoạt động của Dân Biểu Derek Trần nhằm giải quyết vấn đề nhà ở trong khu vực:
- Dân Biểu Derek Trần đã vận động thành công $250,000 ngân sách liên bang để hỗ trợ xây dựng 2,700 căn nhà ở giá phải chăng lâu dài khắp Orange County.
- Dân Biểu Derek đồng bảo trợ Dự Luật Saving the American Dream Act, nhằm thành lập một lực lượng đặc nhiệm liên cơ quan để giải quyết cuộc khủng hoảng nhà ở, và Dự Luật Affordable Housing Credit Improvement Act, hỗ trợ tài chính cho việc xây dựng thêm các khu nhà ở nhiều căn.
- Ngoài ra, Dân Biểu Derek đã bỏ phiếu ủng hộ Dự Luật 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, được ký thành luật vào Tháng Bảy, 2026, đẩy nhanh tiến độ xây dựng nhà ở và giảm bớt các thủ tục hành chính không cần thiết.
Toàn văn dự luật có thể được xem TẠI ĐÂY.

WASHINGTON – Cierra Charity Lee, 21, of the District of Columbia, was sentenced today in U.S. District Court to 102 months in federal prison for her role in the brutal kidnapping and armed robbery of two women she lured to a Southeast residence under the promise of a babysitting job, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

“This was a calculated ambush engineered to silence a rape victim and bury the truth,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “These defendants used deception, weapons, and terror in an attempt to obstruct justice. Today’s sentence is a reminder that intimidation will never triumph over accountability, and that those who target victims to protect predators will face the full force of the law.”

“This was a calculated ambush engineered to silence a rape victim and bury the truth,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “These defendants used deception, weapons, and terror in an attempt to obstruct justice. Today’s sentence is a reminder that intimidation will never triumph over accountability, and that those who target victims to protect predators will face the full force of the law.”

Lee pleaded guilty on April 30, 2026, to kidnapping and armed robbery. Her co‑defendants, Robynn Danielle Bynum, 19, and Kayvon Edwards, 22, previously pleaded guilty to the same charges. In addition to the 102-month prison term, Judge Christopher R. Cooper also ordered Leed to serve five years of supervised release. Federal prosecutors had requested a 168-month prison sentence for Lee.

According to court documents, on the night of Oct. 20, 2025, two female victims arrived at a residence near Suitland Parkway and Stanton Road SE after Lee offered to hire them for a babysitting job. When the victims entered the home’s basement, co‑defendant Robynn Bynum emerged from a back room and stabbed Victim 1 repeatedly in the back while injuring Victim 2, who attempted to intervene. Lee helped restrain both victims, binding their hands with duct tape and taking their phones, car keys, and other property.

While the victims bled and remained bound in a bathroom, Lee questioned Victim 1 about a pending rape case against Lee’s boyfriend, co‑defendant Kayvon Edwards, who was then incarcerated in Prince George’s County.

Through a series of monitored jail calls, investigators determined that Edwards orchestrated the kidnapping and attack in an effort to prevent Victim 1 from testifying. On those calls, Edwards directed Lee to restrain Victim 1, ensure she could not flee, and silence her as a witness. Lee assured Edwards that Victim 1 would drop the charges and not appear in court.

Lee and Bynum forced the victims into Victim 1’s vehicle, duct-taped their eyes, and attempted to drive them out of the District, telling them they would be abandoned in Pennsylvania to prevent their appearance in court. After striking something and flattening a tire, Lee and Bynum fled the scene, leaving the victims bound and injured in the car. Eventually, the victims freed themselves and sought help.

MPD officers found the victim’s car parked in the 3200 block of M St. and saw blood stains and pieces of duct tape on the back seat. They also noticed that the front passenger tire was flat.

Emergency responders transported both victims to GW Hospital, where Victim 1 was treated for multiple stab wounds requiring trauma‑level care. Victim 2 was treated for lacerations to her wrist and elbow.

On November 5, 2025, police arrested all three defendants. Upon a review of Lee’s phone, law enforcement found that the device’s web history contained the following searches:

• October 7, 2025, at 2:48:31 p.m.: in dc how long can you get for kidnapping

• October 7, 2025, at 2:48:32 p.m.: dc kidnapping cases

• October 21, 2025, at 1:54:21 a.m.: how much can you get for kidnapping in dc

• October 21, 2025, at 7:49:14 a.m.: md case search

• October 21, 2025, at 8:10:26 a.m.: how much time can you get for aggravated assault

• October 21, 2025, at 11:30:26 a.m.: what does concluded held mean in court

• October 22, 2025, at 12:47:10 a.m.: how to see if you got a warrant

Bynum is scheduled to be sentenced Jan. 21, 2027. Sentencing for Edwards is pending.

This case was investigated by the FBI’s Washington Field Office and the Metropolitan Police Department. It is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Joshua Satter.

Justice Department and USDA Reaffirm and Expand their Partnership to Protect Competition in Agricultural Inputs
Attorney General Todd Blanche and Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins have agreed to a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU), building on the joint progress of the Department of Justice and Department of Agriculture to strengthen competition for agricultural inputs. Under the MOU, the agencies will expand their strong cooperation with respect to food and agricultural inputs, such as feed, fertilizer, fuel, seed, equipment, pesticides, among other essential goods.
The Justice Department is committed to vigorously investigating and bringing appropriate action to stop anticompetitive conduct that harms American famers and families. The new MOU deepens the Justice Department’s close partnership with the USDA to protect American farmers from unlawful conduct and to promote a more affordable and resilient food supply chain.
The new MOU, signed by Attorney General Blanche and Secretary Rollins on Oct. 5, reflects the high priority of agricultural input competition to both agencies. The MOU amends and restates a prior working-level MOU entered into by the Justice Department’s Antitrust Division in September 2025.
Anyone with information about anticompetitive conduct in agricultural industries or any other violations of the antitrust laws is encouraged to contact the Antitrust Division’s Citizen Complaint Center at 1-888-647-3258 or antitrust.complaints@usdoj.gov. Information about anticompetitive practices in livestock and poultry markets can also be submitted to the USDA’s and Justice Department’s Agricultural Markets Enforcement Partnership at www.farmerfairness.gov.
title: Justice Department and USDA Reaffirm and Expand their Partnership to Protect Competition in Agricultural Inputs

Tallahassee, Florida – Malcolm Akeem Holloway, 22, of Tallahassee, Florida, pleaded guilty in federal court to possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. The plea was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida.

U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “Our state and federal law enforcement partners are committed to removing dangerous, serial offenders, like this defendant, from our streets to keep our communities safe, and my office will continue to aggressively prosecute those criminals to the fullest extent of the law. The safety of our communities is not negotiable, and we must incapacitate chronic offenders, like this defendant, through robust criminal prosecutions and strict incarceration.”

Court documents reflect that, in March 2026, the Tallahassee Police Department was conducting surveillance when they observed the defendant carrying a backpack. They watched the defendant get into the front passenger seat of a vehicle that was subsequently stopped for multiple traffic infractions. A law enforcement K9 alerted to the presence of illegal contraband, which prompted a search of the vehicle. The backpack contained clothing matching the defendant’s size, a loaded FN 9 millimeter pistol which had been previously reported stolen, and two plastic shopping bags containing a combined total of 65 taped, hand-rolled cigarettes packaged in a manner typical for the introduction of contraband into correctional facilities.

A review of material from the defendant’s Instagram account from December 30, 2025, to March 2, 2026, found multiple instances of the defendant posing with various firearms.

The defendant was prohibited from possessing firearms because of prior state convictions for possession of a firearm by a delinquent, carrying a concealed firearm, three counts of possession of a firearm by a convicted felon, and possession of a machinegun. Most recently, the defendant had been to prison for three years and was released on December 8, 2025, approximately three months before his arrest.

Holloway faces up to 15 years in prison.

Sentencing is scheduled for December 11, 2026, at 10:00 am, in the United States Courthouse in Tallahassee before United States District Judge Mark E. Walker.

The case involved an investigation by Homeland Security Investigations and the Tallahassee Police Department, with assistance from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney James A. McCain.

This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF comprises agents and officers from multiple agencies with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida.

The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl .

SEC to Host Virtual National Compliance Outreach Seminar for Investment Companies and Investment Advisers
Washington D.C., Oct. 6, 2026 —
The Securities and Exchange Commission’s Compliance Outreach Program announced today that it will host a virtual national seminar for investment companies and investment advisers on November 19, 2026. The purpose of the event is to help chief compliance officers and senior personnel at investment advisory firms and investment companies enhance their compliance programs to protect investors.
The conference will include panel discussions on:
- Information security and operational resiliency
- Registered investment adviser topics
- Private fund adviser topics
- Registered investment company topics
- Effectiveness of compliance programs
- Briefings on current issues
View the full agenda. To submit questions for the panel, either in advance or during the event, use the links provided in the agenda.
Advance registration is not required. A link to the live webcast will be made available the morning of November 19 on SEC.gov.
The SEC's Divisions of Examinations and Investment Management, and the Asset Management Unit of the Division of Enforcement, jointly sponsor the compliance outreach program. The program promotes open communications and coordination among securities regulators and the industry on mutual fund, investment adviser, and broker-dealer compliance issues.
Please visit the SEC's compliance page for additional compliance-related resources.

Washington, D.C. — Rep. Robert Garcia, Ranking Member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, demanded answers from Jared Kushner, founder and Chief Executive Officer of Affinity Partners, on the apparent conflict of interest regarding the hundreds of millions of dollars his corporation has invested in Israeli firm Phoenix Financial, which is invested in Israeli military companies. Kushner simultaneously has a special envoy role in President Trump’s Middle East conflict, serving as a key envoy in the region; a status which allows him to dodge financial disclosure requirements.
“Jared Kushner is helping negotiate Middle East policy for his father-in-law, even as his firm is the top investor in Phoenix Financial. Phoenix Financial holds up to $456 million in companies that supply Israel’s military, including its largest arms manufacturer. Kushner’s apparent conflicts of interest throughout the region pose serious security threats, which must be investigated,” said Ranking Member Robert Garcia.
In the letter to Jared Kushner, Ranking Member Robert Garcia wrote, “Oversight Democrats are investigating the unprecedented and dangerous ways in which President Trump and his family have profited directly from their access to power. Public reporting has revealed that while you have been acting as a key envoy in the Middle East, including a purported attempt to negotiate a ceasefire to end the conflict in Gaza, your firm, Affinity Partners, is the largest shareholder in an Israeli company with more than $456 million invested in nine companies that supply Israel’s military, including its largest arms manufacturer. Your dual role as your father-in-law’s Middle East and Gaza negotiator while investing in a company that makes profits investing in arms manufacturing presents significant conflicts of interest, all while you avoid disclosing your financial entanglements to Congress or the American people. Since you continue to conduct foreign policy on behalf of the Trump Administration while having raised billions of dollars in capital provided to Affinity Partners by Gulf monarchies, I request detailed information about your business dealings in the Middle East to understand whether your significant financial gains have come at the cost of Americans’ safety and security.”
In March 2026, Ranking Member Robert Garcia demanded answers from the White House following reports that Jared Kushner had been soliciting billions of dollars from Middle Eastern state sovereign wealth funds for his private equity firm, Affinity Partners, while simultaneously co-leading the Trump Administration’s negotiations in the Middle East.
In August 2025, Ranking Member Garcia sent letters to President Trump’s son-in-law, Michael Boulos, his associate James Frangi, and Saudi businessman Abdulelah Allam following reports that Mr. Boulos received $100,000 for leveraging his ties to President Trump to help Mr. Allam recover assets seized by the Saudi government. This letter was part of the Oversight Democrats’ broader oversight of Trump’s family members, including Jared Kushner, whose private equity firm, Affinity Partners, received billions in foreign funding from the sovereign wealth fund of Saudi Arabia shortly after Kushner left the White House following the first Trump Administration.
In 2024, Ranking Member Garcia and Ranking Member Jamie Raskin urged Chairmen James Comer and Glenn Grothman to hold a hearing regarding Kushner’s apparent influence peddling and quid pro quos for actions he undertook to reshape U.S. foreign policy in the Middle East and beyond, as senior adviser in President Trump’s first Administration, following reports that Kushner was close to finalizing investments in Albania and Serbia and leveraged relationships he built during his time as a senior adviser in his father-in-law’s White House.

Former TD Bank Employee Pleads Guilty to Accepting Bribes, Laundering $4.8 Million to Colombia
Gerardo Aquino, 40, of Hollywood, Florida, pleaded guilty to accepting bribes and laundering more than $4.8 million to Colombia while employed by TD Bank.
“The Criminal Division is at the vanguard of protecting the security of the U.S. financial system, including against bank insiders,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Gerardo Aquino abused his position of trust at TD Bank and enriched himself in the process. Bank insiders who facilitate money laundering and illegal activity for criminal organizations play a critical role for that organization and abuse our financial system. When that happens, these insiders will be investigated and prosecuted.”
“From inside TD Bank, Aquino facilitated the laundering of millions of dollars in exchange for bribes,” said U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer for the District of New Jersey. “By enabling crime instead of preventing it, Aquino provided a soft entry point into our banking system for malevolent actors. The U.S. Attorney’s Office will continue to hold financial institutions and their employees accountable when they break the law and undermine the integrity of our financial system.”
“This guilty plea demonstrates that corrupt financial insiders are just as critical to criminal networks as those who move drugs or incite violence,” said Associate Chief of Operations Greg Millard of the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). “By exploiting his position at a financial institution, accepting bribes, and helping funnel millions of dollars to Colombia, Gerardo Aquino enabled the movement of illicit proceeds and undermined the integrity of the U.S. financial system. DEA and our partners will continue to identify, investigate, and hold accountable the facilitators who help transnational criminal organizations profit from their crimes.”
“Financial institutions and their employees serve as an important line of defense in protecting the integrity of our financial system,” said Special Agent in Charge Jenifer L. Piovesan of IRS Criminal Investigation’s Newark Field Office. “When someone abuses that position of trust to facilitate money laundering and move millions of dollars in illicit proceeds, they undermine the very system they are entrusted to protect. IRS Criminal Investigation and our law enforcement partners will continue to follow the money, expose those who enable criminal activity, and hold financial facilitators accountable.”
“The guilty plea in this case holds Mr. Aquino accountable for accepted bribes and abusing his trusted position at TD Bank to facilitate the laundering of millions of dollars out of the United States to Colombia,” said Special Agent in Charge Patricia Tarasca of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation Office of Inspector General (FDIC-OIG), New York Region. “The FDIC OIG is pleased to join our law enforcement partners in announcing today’s guilty plea, and we remain committed to investigating financial crimes that threaten to undermine the safety and soundness of our Nation’s financial system, including those crimes involving bank insiders.”
According to court filings, Aquino accepted bribes and exploited his position as a bank employee to help launder illicit funds to Colombia. From April 2022 to November 2023, Aquino opened fraudulent accounts, issued hundreds of debit cards to co-conspirators, and unblocked debit cards that TD Bank had restricted due to potential fraud. The bank accounts and debit cards were then used to funnel approximately $4.8 million out of the United States. As part of this scheme, Aquino opened 86 individual customer accounts using the same exact commercial address in Miami. Those accounts alone were used to launder over $3 million in illicit funds to Colombia. In exchange, Aquino received more than $8,000 in bribes — paid in cash and through a peer-to-peer digital payment network.
Aquino pleaded guilty to a two-count information charging him with conspiring to launder monetary instruments and receipt of bribes by a bank employee. The charge of money laundering conspiracy carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison. The charge of receipt of bribes by a bank employee carries a maximum penalty of 30 years in prison. Aquino’s sentencing has been set for March 23, 2027. A federal judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
The Drug Enforcement Administration, IRS Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI), and FDIC-OIG are investigating the case. The Justice Department also thanks the Morristown Police Department for their assistance with the investigation.
Trial Attorneys D. Zachary Adams and Chelsea Rooney of the Criminal Division’s Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture (MNF) Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Marko Pesce for the District of New Jersey are prosecuting the case.
MNF’s mission is to take the profit out of crime, eliminate drug cartels, and protect the U.S. financial system. MNF pursues criminal prosecutions and criminal and civil asset recovery actions involving: financial facilitators who launder profits for criminals; financial institutions and their officers and employees whose actions threaten the U.S. financial system and financial institutions; international money launderers who support transnational organized crime; and the top command and control of international drug trafficking organizations.
MNF’s Bank Integrity Unit investigates and prosecutes banks and other financial institutions, including their officers, managers, and employees whose actions threaten the integrity of the individual institution or the wider financial system.
This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of U.S. law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States.

Jamie McDonald, the United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, announced today that MICHAEL SMITH was sentenced to 18 months in prison for his role in a scheme to defraud music streaming platforms and musicians of royalty payments. On March 19, 2026, SMITH pled guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud before U.S. District Judge John G. Koeltl, who imposed today’s sentence.

“Michael Smith exploited super intelligence technology to generate a fraud,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “By flooding music streaming platforms with automated bots in the place of consumers, and fake songs in the place of creativity, Smith robbed millions in royalty payments from genuine artists and their fans. This Office is committed to ensuring the integrity of all markets, and protecting the public from those who use super intelligence for fraud.”

According to the charging documents and statements made in public filings and public court proceedings:

Music can be streamed through platforms such as Amazon Music, Apple Music, Spotify, and YouTube Music (the “Streaming Platforms”). Each time a song is streamed through one of the Streaming Platforms, the songwriter who composed the song, the musician who performed it, and in certain cases other rights holders, are entitled to small royalty payments. Royalty payments are made proportionately to musicians and songwriters from a pool of funds. As a result, streaming fraud diverts funds from musicians and songwriters whose songs were legitimately streamed by real consumers to those who use automation to falsely create the appearance of legitimate streaming.

SMITH’s streaming fraud lasted from 2017 to 2024 and he executed it in three steps. First, SMITH created thousands of fraudulent accounts on the Streaming Platforms (the “Bot Accounts”) that he could use to stream songs. Second, he used software to cause the Bot Accounts to continuously stream purported songs that he owned, which were generally created using super intelligence. Third, Smith collected royalties based on the fraudulent streams he orchestrated his own Bot Accounts to conduct.

SMITH spread his automated streams across thousands of songs to avoid anomalous streaming as to any single song, which would likely cause the Streaming Platforms to discover his scheme. At times SMITH was using as many as 10,000 Bot Accounts at once to fraudulently stream music, and he used fake email accounts and fraudulently-obtained debit cards to create the Bot Accounts. As SMITH explained it in an email, he needed “a TON of songs fast” in order to circumvent the “anti fraud policies” of the Streaming Platforms. To obtain the necessary number of songs for his scheme to succeed, SMITH turned to super intelligence, which he used to create hundreds of thousands of AI-generated songs for which he could manipulate the streams.

SMITH’s hundreds of thousands of AI-generated songs were streamed by his Bot Accounts billions of times. For example, in April 2023, the entire catalogue of Taylor Swift received 9.3 million streams on YouTube Music from family plan streams, while in the same month, Smith’s Bot Accounts used family plans to fraudulently stream his AI-generated music 80.9 million times. Smith’s Bot Account streams allowed him to fraudulently obtain more than $8 million in royalties from the Streaming Platforms.

* * *

In addition to the prison term, SMITH, 54, of Cornelius, North Carolina, was sentenced to two years of supervised release and ordered to pay $8,091,843.64 in forfeiture.

Mr. McDonald praised the outstanding work of the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

The case is being prosecuted by the Office’s Complex Frauds and Cybercrime Unit. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Nicholas W. Chiuchiolo and Kevin Mead are in charge of the prosecution.
title: North Carolina Man Sentenced To 18 Months In Prison For Super Intelligence-Assisted Music Streaming Fraud

Rep. Carson Seeks Answers on Canceled Naturalization Ceremonies
WASHINGTON, DC—This week, Congressman André Carson (IN-07) led 26 Members of Congress in seeking answers from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) about repeated cancelations of naturalization ceremonies.
In Indianapolis, USCIS canceled at least three naturalization ceremonies since July, citing a “lack of candidates.” But field offices report they have pending naturalization applications that are awaiting action from USCIS.
“Citizenship is a life-changing milestone, and people who have spent years following the law deserve a government that honors its commitments,” said Rep. Carson. “Canceling naturalization ceremonies without a clear explanation leaves families in Indianapolis in limbo and undermines trust in the process. These families deserve more than canceled ceremonies and unanswered questions. USCIS must explain these cancellations and ensure eligible applicants can take their oath without unreasonable delay. I will keep pressing this administration for answers and accountability.”
“We are concerned that lawful permanent residents are experiencing delays in the final stages of their naturalization across the country,” the lawmakers state in the letter. “Applicants who have spent years complying with immigration requirements should not face unexplained or unreasonable delays after becoming eligible for citizenship because of the political or ideological whims of a particular administration. These delays prevent lawful permanent residents from fully exercising the rights and responsibilities of citizenship, including voting, obtaining a U.S. passport, pursuing certain employment opportunities, and petitioning for family members. Congress has made it clear that the fair and timely processing of eligible citizenship applicants is a priority.”
Rep. Carson and his colleagues requested a response from USCIS by October 7, 2026, including the number of pending naturalization applications, how long those applications have been pending, and how many applicants have completed naturalization interviews but are still awaiting final decisions.
The full letter is HERE.

AIDS Healthcare Foundation Agrees to Pay $1.44M to Settle False Claims Act Allegations
AIDS Healthcare Foundation, a non-profit organization based in Los Angeles, California, has agreed to pay $1.44 million to resolve allegations that it violated the False Claims Act by submitting or failing to delete false or invalid diagnosis codes in order to increase payments that it received from the Medicare Advantage program.
“The government relies on Medicare Advantage participants to submit accurate, substantiated diagnosis codes that are adequately documented in a medical record to ensure proper payment,” said Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate of the Justice Department’s Civil Division. “The Justice Department will continue to protect the public fisc and hold accountable those who receive inflated payments by knowingly providing or failing to correct false information.”
“The integrity of our federal healthcare programs, including Medicare Advantage, must be preserved,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli for the Central District of California. “We will not tolerate companies undermining the interests of Medicare patients for financial gain.”
“Medicare Advantage organizations have a responsibility to ensure the accuracy of diagnosis codes they submit for payment. When entities fail to correct information they know is wrong, they undermine the integrity of a program millions of seniors rely on,” said Acting Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Miranda L. Bennett of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS‑OIG). “HHS‑OIG will continue to safeguard taxpayer funds by holding organizations accountable when their failures inflate federal payments and compromise program trust.”
Under the Medicare Advantage (MA) Program, also known as Medicare Part C, Medicare beneficiaries may opt out of traditional Medicare and enroll in private health plans offered by insurance companies known as Medicare Advantage Organizations, or MAOs. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) pays the MAOs a fixed monthly amount for each Medicare beneficiary enrolled in their plans. CMS adjusts these monthly payments to account for various “risk” factors that affect expected health expenditures for the beneficiary. In general, CMS pays MAOs more for sicker beneficiaries expected to incur higher healthcare costs and less for healthier beneficiaries expected to incur lower costs. To calculate the payment amounts, CMS uses a health-based risk adjustment model — the Hierarchical Conditions Category (HCC) model — that takes into account diagnoses reported by healthcare providers. In general, the more severe the diagnosis or costly the associated treatment, the higher the risk score and the higher the corresponding payments to the MAO. Diagnosis codes submitted to CMS must be supported by the beneficiaries’ medical records and be accurate, complete, and truthful, based on the best knowledge, information, and belief of the MAO making the submission.
AIDS Healthcare Foundation (AHF) provides care and services to HIV patients in the United States and other countries. AHF’s Managed Care Division (doing business as Positive Healthcare Partners) operated special needs MA plans for Medicare beneficiaries who have HIV and lived in Florida, Georgia, or California.
The settlement announced today resolves allegations that, for payment years 2017 to 2023, AHF failed to timely investigate and delete diagnosis codes that were either inaccurate or not documented in medical records. Beginning in around 2017, AHF’s risk adjustment coders conducted chart reviews to identify inaccurate or unsupported diagnosis codes for deletion. As part of this process, AHF’s risk adjustment coders maintained “Delete Research” spreadsheets, which listed diagnosis codes they identified as potentially lacking support in the medical record but needing further research. Although AHF knew that it was required to investigate and delete inaccurate and unsupported diagnosis codes within 60 days, AHF failed to timely investigate and delete the codes. AHF did not delete most of the inaccurate or unsupported diagnosis codes in the “Delete Research” spreadsheets until 2024 or 2025 — well after AHF was on notice that the codes potentially lacked support and only after being notified of the United States’ investigation.
The United States further alleges that, for payment year 2017, AHF knowingly submitted diagnosis codes for HIV (ICD-10 B20) where the diagnosis was not documented in any medical record for a face-to-face visit, in violation of CMS requirements that all diagnosis code submissions must be documented as a result of a face-to-face visit.
The civil settlement resolves claims brought under the qui tam or whistleblower provisions of the False Claims Act by Donna Irons, a former risk adjustment coder at AHF. Under the qui tam provisions, a private party can file an action on behalf of the United States and receive a portion of any recovery. The qui tam case is captioned United States ex rel. Irons v. AIDS Healthcare Foundation d/b/a Positive Healthcare Partners, Civil Action No. 23-cv-2160 (C.D. Cal.). Ms. Irons will receive $259,200 as her share of the federal recovery.
AHF received credit under the Department of Justice’s guidelines for taking disclosure, cooperation, and remediation into account in False Claims Act resolutions, Justice Manual § 4-4.112. In addition to cooperating in the government’s investigation and enhancing its compliance program, AHF proactively remediated its conduct during the course of Department’s investigation by submitting deletes for diagnosis codes that, based on review of medical records, were not supported.
The resolution obtained in this matter was the result of a coordinated effort between the Justice Department’s Civil Division, Commercial Litigation Branch, Fraud Section and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California, with assistance from the Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General.
The investigation and resolution of this matter illustrate the government’s emphasis on combating healthcare fraud. One of the most powerful tools in this effort is the False Claims Act. Tips and complaints from all sources about potential fraud, waste, abuse, and mismanagement, can be reported to the Department of Health and Human Services at 800-HHS-TIPS (800-447-8477).
This year the Administration launched the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud and the National Fraud Enforcement Division to enhance the Administration’s war on fraud, waste, and abuse in federal programs. When unscrupulous actors exploit these programs for their own financial gain, they defraud the government, harm the people these programs are designed to aid and protect, and undermine American businesses that play by the rules. The Civil Division’s FCA enforcement plays a critical role in combatting such fraudulent schemes, recovering billions of dollars for the American taxpayers, and holding wrongdoers accountable. FCA matters will continue to be on the forefront of the battle against fraud, and the Civil Division’s FCA work will support and advance the mission of the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud and the National Fraud Enforcement Division.
Trial Attorney Tiffany L. Ho of the Civil Division’s Commercial Litigation Branch, Fraud Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney S. Desmond Jui for the Central District of California handled this case.
The claims resolved by the settlement are allegations only and there has been no determination of liability.
title: AIDS Healthcare Foundation Agrees to Pay $1.44M to Settle False Claims Act Allegations

Fast Facts
The federal government spent $793 billion in 2025 on contracts with federal contractors, which employ over a million American workers. Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 requires certain contractors to take steps to employ people with disabilities.
The Department of Labor is tasked with overseeing how contractors implement this law in their workplaces. But since 2025, it has suspended much of its oversight. Contractors could also benefit from additional guidance from DOL.
We recommended that DOL resume oversight activities and provide contractors with additional guidance, such as a list of best practices for Section 503 compliance.
Highlights
What GAO Found
Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (Section 503) requires certain federal contractors to take proactive steps to employ people with disabilities. The Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP) within the Department of Labor (DOL) oversees contractors’ compliance with Section 503. Since January 2025, DOL has reduced its oversight activities. For example, DOL has suspended audits of selected contractors, which were a key tool for monitoring compliance. From fiscal years 2017 through 2025, 532 audits found Section 503 violations. Without resuming audits, DOL has less assurance that contractors are supporting employment of people with disabilities. Further, DOL has reduced OFCCP’s workforce in response to changes in its activities (see fig.). However, these changes were not informed by strategic workforce planning consistent with key principles for such efforts. DOL has made changes to Section 503 regulations that could further impact OFCCP’s activities. Engaging in strategic workforce planning would help DOL ensure that OFCCP’s workforce composition meets its needs.
Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs Workforce, FY 2017–2026
Federal contractors face a range of challenges complying with Section 503. Selected stakeholders identified challenges in three key areas:
- conducting outreach to and recruiting people with disabilities,
- retaining and advancing people with disabilities, and
- demonstrating compliance with Section 503.
Stakeholders also said that DOL could provide additional guidance to help contactors comply with the law. For example, information on how to provide reasonable accommodations and a list of best practices for Section 503 compliance could help contractors better understand how to support employees with disabilities.
Why GAO Did This Study
In fiscal year 2025, the federal government spent about $793 billion on contracts with federal contractors—which employ over 1 million U.S. workers. Section 503 prohibits federal contractors from discriminating in employment against people with disabilities. It also requires certain contractors to take proactive steps to employ and advance in employment people with disabilities.
GAO was asked to review the implementation and oversight of Section 503. This report addresses (1) the extent to which DOL monitors Section 503 compliance and plans for its workforce needs, and (2) what challenges, if any, contractors face in complying with Section 503 and the extent to which DOL has provided resources to assist contractors.
GAO analyzed OFCCP enforcement data and DOL human resources data, and reviewed DOL documents. GAO conducted interviews and discussion groups with DOL officials as well as representatives of contractors, consultants who assist contractors with compliance, academic researchers, and other stakeholders who were familiar with Section 503 compliance or supporting employment of people with disabilities. GAO also conducted a nongeneralizable survey of representatives of contractors.
Recommendations
GAO is making eight recommendations, including that DOL resume compliance audits, conduct strategic workforce planning for OFCCP, and provide additional information to help contractors provide reasonable accommodations to employees with disabilities and comply with Section 503. DOL agreed with six of the recommendations and neither agreed nor disagreed with the other two.
title: Disability Employment: DOL Should Enhance Monitoring and Guidance for Federal Contractors

Rep. Subramanyam Announced $1.5 Million Federal Funding for Oak Hill
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Representative Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10) announced an award of $1.5 million in federal grants for the mansion and outbuildings of the fifth President of the United States, James Monroe. Oak Hill, located in Loudoun County, has been preserved for hundreds of years and provides the local community and visitors access to American history and educational programming. Earlier this year, the Virginia General Assembly approved Governor Spanberger’s budget amendment to designated Oak Hill as a State Park. That amendment was championed by Senator Russet Perry and Delegate John McAuliff.
“Oak Hill is an important part of our history and has survived hundreds of years. This funding will ensure it can continue to live on for generations. I am proud that federal funding will help maintain and preserve this historical landmark. I look forward to seeing people of all ages in our community and across the world visit Oak Hill for many years to come,” said Congressman Suhas Subramanayam.
“For more than two years, we fought in Richmond to make Oak Hill a state park and protect more than 1,200 acres of Loudoun County and President Monroe’s historic home. We got it done, and now the work is making sure Oak Hill has what it needs to thrive for the long term. This $1.5 million in federal funding will help us do that, and I’m grateful to Congressman Subramanyam for securing these resources and being a partner in Oak Hill’s future. I’m looking forward to continuing this work and getting Oak Hill State Park open to the public,” said Senator Russet Perry.
"Oak Hill will be an enormous investment in the quality of life and conservation of Western Loudoun by opening up over 1,200 acres of farm and forestland for recreational use. The new funding secured by Congressman Subramanyam and State budget language provided by Gov. Spanberger ensures this land and history will be treasured by generations to come," said Delegate John McAuliff.
“Oak Hill stands as a powerful reminder of our nation’s founding story, and these grants ensure that story will be preserved for generations to come. We’re grateful to Rep. Subramanyam and our federal partners at the National Park Service for recognizing what this site means – not just to Loudoun County, but to the story of our nation as we mark 250 years of independence,” said Heather Richards, Mid-Atlantic Vice President, The Conservation Fund.
Of the $1.5 million in grants for preservation and restoration, $750k from Save America’s Treasures and $750k from Semiquincentennial grants. View the NPS announcements of funding here and here.
###
title: Rep. Subramanyam Announced $1.5 Million Federal Funding for Oak Hill

Southeast Housing Innovations Spotlighted at HUD’s Innovative Housing Showcase
October 6, 2026
Secretary Turner Visits Purple Heart Homes’ Modular House
GEORGIA - U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) spotlighted housing innovations from the Southeast region during the sixth annual Innovative Housing Showcase, held September 22-24, on the National Mall. This year’s theme, “Made in America,” highlighted American ingenuity and innovative approaches to expanding housing affordability and homeownership.
“Under President Trump’s leadership, HUD is taking an all-the-above approach to address housing affordability,” said Secretary Turner. “This year’s Innovative Housing Showcase demonstrated how American companies are taking unique approaches to build more homes and encourage the American Dream of homeownership. HUD is working alongside local communities and private industry to unlock more housing and further opportunity for the American people.”
HUD’s “Made in America” Showcase spotlighted American builders, manufacturers, and innovators’ modern technologies and creative housing solutions that are expanding housing supply, lowering construction costs, and putting affordable homeownership back in reach for hardworking Americans. The Showcase featured a variety of full-scale housing models including manufactured, 3D printed, and modular homes built by American companies from across the nation.
Examples from the Southeast Region
A tabletop exhibit on pioneering pneumatic spray technology for ultra-high-performance concrete from Florida International University (Florida).
Singleton Designs, LLC’s (Georgia) "Boxes System-Built," a new design concept for residential construction incorporating "Boxes,” which are rough-framed structures that include floors, walls, roofs, exterior sheathing, roof decking, exterior windows, and doors that are constructed offsite and installed onto a site-built foundation.
A cross-section of one of Lagom Development’s (Georgia) Structural Insulated Panels that showed the panel’s construction and insulation materials.
Examples of Super Intelligence-powered technologies from the Oak Ridge National Laboratory (Tennessee) that improve productivity, affordability, safety, and quality in residential building construction.
A modular home from Purple Heart Homes (North Carolina) that featured energy-efficient closed-cell spray foam insulation as well as maintenance-friendly exteriors with all vinyl products and a metal roof.
A Tiny Home from Duke Energy Corporation (North Carolina) with nanogrid technology that mixes power sources to make homes more cost-effective.
Follow @SecretaryTurner on X, FB, and Instagram.
title: Southeast Housing Innovations Spotlighted at HUD’s Innovative Housing Showcase

ICYMI: OPM Director Kupor Discusses American Leadership in Super Intelligence on Fox Business
WASHINGTON, DC – US Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Director Scott Kupor joined Varney & Co. on Fox Business for his first television appearance since President Trump announced his appointment as Vice Chair of the White House Super Intelligence Task Force. Kupor discussed the President’s vision for maintaining American leadership in superintelligence, protecting national security, and holding industry accountable while advancing innovation.
On advancing President Trump’s vision for American leadership in super intelligence:
“We are going to do exactly what the President has talked about, which is we all recognize that leading in super intelligence is the most important economic issue, security issue, for the country. And the President has asked us to do that. At the same time, the President recognizes that, yes, there are risks. Like any new technology, there’s new things we have to figure out. We have to figure out the energy cost, water cost, utilities, all these other things, security, of course.”
On developing a comprehensive plan to advance innovation and address risks:
“So the main thing for the task force to do will be to come back to the President with a comprehensive plan that balances those two issues and make sure that we have the precondition that will allow the U.S. to continue to win, which we are and we will continue to do so. And also make sure that all the other players in the ecosystem recognize and understand how do we address and how do we appropriately handle issues that may arise in the course of this development in the technology.”
On independent oversight and accountability for industry commitments:
“So, this is not just a bunch of engineers sitting around and grading themselves. This is actually them going outside to a third-party auditor, that auditor reporting to an independent committee of the board. It actually has real legal teeth in a way that I think people who haven’t been on a public company board before, they don’t quite appreciate and understand. I think this was the genius of what the President was able to get these industry leaders to commit to, is something that truly does have teeth.”
On protecting American innovation while enforcing existing laws:
“One of the key members of the task force is Andrew Ferguson, the head of the FTC. There are lots of things, obviously, the FTC can do. The President has mentioned the DOJ has lots of existing rules and regulations. So, nobody is going to get a free pass here. The question, though, is do you want to make sure you don’t introduce a regulatory scheme that will slow down or impact the ability of the inventiveness of this country to win what is an incredibly important technology. And I think the President is trying to strike the right balance here.”
On touring the new White House ballroom with President Trump:
“The President did a great job. He literally told us down to the thickness of the glass and the strength of the steel there. It looks awesome. It’s going to be fantastic. It has been well reported and not only adds to the functionality of the White House but obviously creates an entirely robust security infrastructure that’s been long needed. So, it was a great tour. It’s very clear that the President is a builder.”
title: ICYMI: OPM Director Kupor Discusses American Leadership in Super Intelligence on Fox Business

NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland is seeking Phase 1 proposals for the design and construction of the Aerospace Power Systems Laboratory. The principal purpose of this procurement is to deliver a laboratory facility to support the testing and development of power systems, with associated site work, infrastructure, and systems.

The laboratory will provide modern test facilities to advance power research and enable NASA to meet current and future mission needs. Glenn’s expertise in power is crucial to the Artemis program , the Moon Base , and the exploration of Mars and beyond.

Proposals submitted in response to this solicitation are due no later than Oct. 30, 2026, at 1 p.m. EST.

NASA will conduct this acquisition as a full and open competition. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 236220, and the small business size standard of $45 million.

The anticipated contract award date is Dec. 16, 2026. The contract will be performed on-site at NASA Glenn and off-site at the contractor’s facilities.

Proposals for this solicitation are required to be submitted through NASA’s Enterprise File Sharing and Sync Box (EFSS Box), a FedRAMP Moderate certified platform.

All questions regarding this request should be submitted electronically, in writing, to John Christel, contracting officer, at john.a.christel@nasa.gov on or before Oct. 12, 2026. Offerors are encouraged to submit questions as soon as possible for consideration.

For more information about NASA and agency programs, visit:

https://www.nasa.gov

-end-

Kristen Parker Glenn Research Center, Cleveland 216-990-4386 kristen.m.parker@nasa.gov
title: NASA Glenn Invites Phase 1 Proposals for Aerospace Power Systems Laboratory

SANTA ANA – A previously deported illegal alien has been charged in a federal criminal complaint alleging he attempted to smuggle illegal aliens into Southern California and unlawfully reentered the United States after removal, the Justice Department announced today.

Jose Miguel Castro‑Duenas, 44, a Mexican national who also uses the name Luis Enrique Santoyo‑Orozco, is charged with attempted transportation of illegal aliens and illegal reentry.

He was arrested on October 3, 2026, in Newport Beach and remains in federal custody. He made his initial appearance in U.S. District Court in Santa Ana on October 5 and was detained. A post-indictment arraignment was set for November 9, 2026.

“This case reflects a brazen assault on the rule of law and the sovereignty of the United States, where a previously deported illegal alien smuggler unlawfully reentered our country and resumed smuggling operations in one of our coastal communities,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli. “We will not tolerate repeated violations of federal law or attempts to exploit our coastline as an entry point for illegal smuggling activity.”

According to an affidavit filed with the complaint, Border Patrol agents had observed a white Honda Pilot near Newport Beach Harbor on multiple dates linked to maritime smuggling activity. On October 3, 2026, agents located the vehicle again and contacted the driver, who identified himself as Castro‑Duenas. Agents determined he was an illegal alien with no lawful immigration documents and detained him.

In a post‑arrest interview, Castro‑Duenas admitted he is a Mexican citizen who unlawfully reentered the United States by boat near San Diego around September 5, 2026. He further admitted he had been previously deported in 2008 following a 2007 federal conviction for alien smuggling, for which he served approximately 13 months. He confirmed he had not received permission from federal authorities to reenter the United States.

Castro‑Duenas also admitted he was working as a smuggler for a criminal organization. He told agents he owed the organization $18,000 for his own illegal entry and that each smuggling pickup reduced his debt by $1,000. He said the organization provided him with the Honda Pilot and a cell phone used to coordinate smuggling activity. He stated that he was at Newport Beach Harbor on the morning of October 3 because he had been instructed to pick up individuals arriving by boat that day. He also admitted he had completed at least two prior smuggling pickups at the same location.

That same morning, U.S. Customs and Border Protection Air and Marine Operations and the U.S. Border Patrol interdicted a boat off Newport Beach Harbor carrying 14 Mexican nationals, none of whom had lawful status to enter or remain in the United States.

A criminal complaint merely contains allegations. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

If convicted, Castro‑Duenas would face a total statutory maximum sentence of 12 years in federal prison.

Homeland Security Investigations and the U.S. Border Patrol are investigating this matter.

Assistant United States Attorney Rosalind Wang of the Orange County Office is prosecuting the case.
title: Previously Deported Illegal Alien Charged with Attempting to Smuggle Illegal Aliens Through Newport Beach Harbor

Today, Congresswoman Janelle Bynum (OR-05) announced that the Scio Rural Fire Protection District has received a $1.19 million federal grant from the Federal Emergency Management Agency to support firefighter safety and fire prevention. Congresswoman Bynum advocated for the funding by writing a letter to FEMA in support of Scio Rural Fire’s grant application.
“When you call 911, you shouldn’t have to wonder if there are enough firefighters to answer,” said Rep. Bynum. “This $1.19 million is a big deal for Scio, Jefferson, and the communities they serve. It means more support for the people running toward emergencies and a stronger response when our neighbors need help most. This is exactly what bringing federal dollars home should look like.”
"These grants are a significant opportunity and an important first step in building the capacity our Fire & Life Safety Division needs," said Albany Fire Chief Chris LaBelle. "A community our size, with the growth and unique industries we have, requires a more proactive approach to risk reduction. This position moves us in that direction and supports our mission to Prevent and Protect from Harm."
"Redmond Fire & Rescue would like to thank Senators Merkley and Wyden and Congresswoman Bynum for their support,” said Redmond Fire Chief Ryan Herrera. "With members of our organization having navigated a past cancer diagnosis, and with the recent passing of Firefighter/Paramedic Michael Kienzle from a Line-of-Duty cancer, this funding marks another meaningful step forward in our commitment to carcinogen reduction and improving the long-term health and safety of our firefighters."
"As costs continue to rise faster than available revenue, small fire districts like ours face difficult choices about how to best use limited resources. Recruiting, training, and retaining volunteer firefighters can too often be delayed as we focus on meeting the immediate costs of providing emergency services,” said Scio Fire Chief Kevin White. "This grant is an important investment in the future of our department and our community. It will strengthen our efforts to recruit and retain volunteers, grow our membership, and ensure we have the people and resources needed to provide the high-quality emergency services our community depends on. We are grateful for this support and the opportunity to build a stronger, more sustainable fire department."
FEMA awarded the funding through its Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) Grant Program, which helps fire departments hire additional firefighters and strengthen recruitment and retention efforts.
FEMA also issued funding under the SAFER Grant Program to the following areas:
- More than $2.3 million to Boise Fire Department in Boise, Idaho
- More than $1.7 million to South Kitsap Fire and Rescue in Port Orchard, Washington.
- More than $1.7 million to Spokane County Fire District 9 in Mead, Washington.
- More than $1.1 million to Umatilla Rural Fire Protection District in Umatilla, Oregon.
- $1 million to North Whidbey Fire and Rescue in Oak Harbor, Washington.
###
title: Bynum Secures Over One Million for Scio Rural Fire

Rep. Gillen Announces More Than $500,000 in New Federal Funding for Nassau County Fire Departments
GARDEN CITY, NY — Today, Congresswoman Laura Gillen (NY-04) announced that four fire departments in New York’s Fourth Congressional District have been awarded more than $500,000 total in federal funding for improved equipment, training and recruitment. Three departments were awarded Assistance to Firefighters Grants (AFG), including the Inwood Fire Department for emergency vehicle acquisition as well as the Bellerose Terrace Fire Department and the Lawrence-Cedarhurst Fire Department for operations and safety. Stewart Manor Village received funding through the Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) grant to help recruit and retain more volunteer firefighters.
“Firefighters across Long Island put their lives on the line every day to protect our families and communities. They should have the resources of a modern firefighting force,” said Rep. Gillen. “I’m proud to help secure more than $500,000 in federal funding for Nassau County fire departments to support critical equipment, vehicle and recruitment needs. I will continue working with our local fire departments to deliver federal dollars and ensure they have the tools and support they need to keep our communities safe.”
“The chiefs, officers and members of the Lawrence-Cedarhurst Fire Department thank Congresswoman Gillen very much,” said Chief Joseph McHugh, Lawrence-Cedarhurst Fire Department. “This will help keep our members safe and take a big financial burden off of us.”
- The Inwood Fire Department received $220,476 through the AFG program to assist with the purchase of new vehicles for the department.
- The Stewart Manor Village Fire Department received $119,500 through the SAFER program to help recruit and retain trained volunteer firefighters.
- The Bellerose Terrace Fire District received $96,666 through the AFG program to help support the operations and safety of their department.
- Lawrence-Cedarhurst Fire Department received $72,857 through the AFG program to help support the operations and safety of their department.
During the FY25 grant application process, Rep. Gillen urged all departments in New York’s Fourth Congressional District to apply for funding through the AFG and SAFER programs and wrote letters of support. As a member of the bipartisan Congressional Fire Services Caucus, Rep. Gillen has also pushed for increased funding for the AFG and SAFER Programs to help ensure Long Island fire departments have the federal resources to improve emergency response and support their firefighters.
The AFG program, administered by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), provides funding to local fire departments to help obtain needed equipment, protective gear, vehicles and training. The SAFER grant is a federal program administered by FEMA that provides direct funding to local fire departments and volunteer firefighter organizations to help increase or maintain the number of trained firefighters.
###
title: Rep. Gillen Announces More Than $500,000 in New Federal Funding for Nassau County Fire Departments

As part of its nationwide initiative to crack down on “Pass the Trash” practices, the U.S. Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights (OCR) today opened investigations into various school districts based on allegations of staff-on-student sexual misconduct. OCR will determine whether the districts’ handling of alleged sexual harassment, including sexual assault, by district teachers, administrators, and other school personnel violated Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 (Title IX).
OCR launched a directed investigation into the New York City Department of Education for its alleged systemic and disturbing pattern of enabling abuse in schools. According to reporting, nearly two thousand complaints filed under the state’s Child Victims Act accuse a school, educator, or staff member of sexual abuse. What is most chilling is that instead of protecting the students to ensure these incidents would never happen again, the schools allegedly allowed the accused to evade punishment and resign. Or, even worse, New York City allegedly let educators named in complaints remain in their job, even after a settlement.
Additionally, OCR is opening an investigation into Jefferson County Public Schools, which has faced intense scrutiny and parent-led protests regarding systematic staff misconduct, including at least four recent staff arrests for sexually assaulting students on campus.
OCR is opening additional investigations into school districts in California, Georgia, North Carolina, Missouri, Texas, and Virginia, alleging that the districts failed to respond as required to reports of staff-on-student sexual misconduct allegations. These investigations will examine reports across these districts that include allegations that a teacher touched the private parts of young elementary school girls in the classroom; a paraprofessional assigned to work with a student with a disability sexually harassed the student in question; a coach groped female student athletes; a staff member groomed a middle school student; and more unsettling accounts.
“Sexual misconduct in schools, especially by the adults entrusted with students’ care, is insidious. Schools have a duty to protect students from sexual harassment in schools and to respond appropriately when sexual misconduct occurs, especially when the predatory behavior is committed by school staff,” said Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights Kimberly Richey. “Parents and families should be able to send their kids to school without fear that they will be targeted by school staff. By opening these investigations, our message is clear: we will always protect our children so parents should never have to wonder if their kids are safe at school.”
Background
The Office for Civil Rights enforces Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972, which prohibits discrimination on the basis of sex in education programs and activities receiving federal financial assistance. Title IX requires schools with knowledge of sexual harassment or sexual assault to respond promptly and in a manner that is not deliberatively indifferent.
The Elementary and Secondary Education Act (ESEA) also requires states and school districts receiving federal funds to maintain policies that prohibit school employees, contractors, agents, and educational agencies from assisting individuals believed to have engaged in sexual misconduct involving a student in obtaining new employment with another educational institution. These protections are intended to prevent the practice commonly known as “passing the trash.”
The U.S. Department of Education will vigorously enforce ESEA and Title IX to ensure schools fulfill their legal obligations, protect students from sexual misconduct, and provide every child with a safe learning environment. Institutions that fail to comply with federal law may face enforcement action, including the potential termination of federal financial assistance.
Anyone who believes that a school, school district, or state educational agency has failed to comply with ESEA or Title IX may file a complaint with OCR. Information about filing a complaint is available on OCR’s website.
title: U.S. Department of Education Launches Multiple Investigations Based on Reports of Staff-on-Student Sexual Misconduct
