Ambassador Mike Waltz
U.S. Representative to the United Nations
New York, New York
AS DELIVERED
Danny, thank you for your kind words. It’s so good to be with you all again.
I just had the opportunity to meet Eliya and Ziv just outside, and I want to start today with talking about you all. What you two endured is just—I think it’s completely unimaginable to any normal human being.
And Eliya, there is one part of your story—I hope I’m pronouncing your name right. My Hebrew’s not the best—but it’s one in your story that I haven’t able to get out of my head that the night before you were released after 505 days in captivity, chained, starved, tortured, believing that the love of his life, Ziv, had been murdered because that’s the psychological torture that the terrorists impose on people. The night before, Hamas tried to make him record one of their propaganda videos, saying all was well, he had been treated magnificently, that it was all fine. He refused. He held firm. He said no.
And the next day, as they were finally handing him over, Hamas tried to turn his release again into a propaganda moment. They put him on a stage, surrounded him with cameras, told him to raise his hands for the spectacle. He refused again.
Eliya, we salute you. I salute you. You are a proud, strong Jew. You’re undefeated. You stood strong, man, and I’m deeply—deeply admirable. And I admire you.
Ziv, when all that’s happening underground, you were living through your own nightmare. You survived the music festival, one of peace and hope and fun, underneath the bodies of people who had been murdered. You watched Eliya being taken away, not knowing whether you would ever see him again.
At 505 days, neither of you knew what had happened to the other, and thankfully, we now obviously know how it ends. Both were freed just a few weeks ago, as Danny just celebrated with you, that you both got married. And from what I hear about your wedding, it was beautiful, and you used it to celebrate new life and to honor those that can no longer celebrate life.
And there’s others—that I think their stories should be heard, and we should take these opportunities and these moments to tell their stories. Ziv’s nephew, Amit, who was murdered at the Nova Festival. And like Aner, who protected God knows how many innocents. Do you know how they protected them? By picking up and throwing Hamas’ hand grenades that they were throwing at a civilian crowd at a music festival. They picked them up and threw them back. Not once, not twice—seven times. I mean, that’s a medal of honor. That’s multiple in our system. Sadly, it was the eighth grenade that Hamas threw at these civilians that killed him.
Folks, I’ve had the honor over these last few years of getting to know many of these hostages and their desperate, desperate families, hearing many of these stories firsthand. The one thing that struck me as a veteran again and again is their extraordinary ability to kind of hold two things at once: to carry the memory of this immense loss, the suffering and pain, but at the same time moving forward and living such beautiful lives, building families, going back to work, telling your stories through art and through love and through peace.
I want to recognize Oriya Berlin, who’s also here today for her unbelievable courage. She finished her IDF training on October 5, a brand new recruit, just two days on the job, when Hamas attacked her base. She was wounded in combat. Obviously survived, but what I found so admirable: she didn’t go home, she didn’t rest, she didn’t stay in the hospital, she went back to her duty, she stood with her fellow brothers and sisters in arms. Thank you, Oriya, for your bravery, and I salute you too.
I have to commend someone else who you just saw, Alon Ohel. Alon didn’t just kind of magically arrive on the USS Nimitz. He was facilitated by and helped by my good friend Ambassador Jeff Bartos, who, as many of you know, and is here for us and a real fighter for the U.S.-Israel relationship.
Alon was taken from the same shelter as Eliya, and for much of their captivity, they were held together underground. To go from that to a year later, standing on the deck of the USS Nimitz, just as it returned on its last voyage from combat operations in the Middle East against the Iranian regime on America’s 250th in front of the Statue of Liberty in New York Harbor to sing that song with another great friend and fighter for the U.S.-Israel relationship, John Ondrasik of Five for Fighting, was a surreal and amazing, just an amazing experience.
Here is a young man who spent 738 days in Hamas captivity. He had been held underground, away from his family, away from daylight, away from his piano that he loved, been such a huge part of his life. To see him playing on that deck was just an absolute beautiful symbol of freedom, and it struck me then, like how much it changed in just a year.
A year ago, 48 hostages underground, including two Americans, held in those Hamas terror tunnels. Their families were still waiting, calling us, begging for something to change, they were fighting every day.
And now today, for the first October 7 commemoration since that terrible morning, every hostage out, the living are back with their families, those who were sadly murdered are home for a proper burial. Even Hadar Goldin and Oron Shaul, who have been held by those depraved terrorists since 2014, were out and back home, which no one said was possible.
President Trump thought it was possible, and he told his envoys, he told me, he told Secretary Rubio, he told Steve and Jared to never stop pushing until we got them home—and we did.
And I just can’t tell you how amazing it was. I can tell you this: firsthand from the moment we started transition in my previous role as National Security Advisor, from that first day, he was talking about these hostages. They were always top of mind for the President and his charge to all of us, I can tell you, he was like, “I don’t want to see you guys again until we get them home.”
But that wasn’t the end of the job. The President was determined, and is still determined, that we do not go back to that cycle of violence. That we don’t go back to that old cycle where Hamas rearms, Iran feeds its proxies with weapons and money, then we have another war, we have another attack, we have another generation of Israelis and Palestinians who pay the price.
Colleagues, October 7 can never ever happen again, and it will not ever happen again, and certainly not under this President’s watch. And that’s why he fought so hard and put together and put forward his 20-Point Peace Plan.
He then charged us to do what seemingly was another impossible task to bring that plan to the UN of all places. Well, you know what? We got it done. Resolution 2803 passed through the UN Security Council 13-0. The UN endorsed that plan. It provides a framework for what? A Gaza without Hamas rule, a demilitarization of the Strip, an international stabilization force and a path towards reconstruction and peaceful coexistence.
It’s not guaranteed to work, folks. But what everything we’ve tried in the past was guaranteed to fail and had failed. And so, the terrorist aimed to isolate Israel and destroy any hope for peace.
Let’s take stock just for a minute of all the things that the media and the experts said couldn’t be done. The biggest thing that they said couldn’t be done was the Abraham Accords.
Look, folks, October 7, completely, and I think irreversibly has backfired on Iran and all of their terrorist proxies.
The Shia Crescent that Iran spent decades and billions building has shattered. Assad is gone. Syria is no longer Iran’s pawn. Lebanon is actually talking to Israel to break free from Hizballah. Iraq is turning westward. All of these things, you never know this by reading any of the headlines. But most importantly, Hamas, its friends, and its backers are in shambles.
And meanwhile, despite all of the experts that said it was impossible that the Abraham Accords would never survive all of these tests and conflict—meanwhile, the Abraham Accords are actually expanding.
You wouldn’t know that, but today, right now as we speak, Iron Dome technology is protecting cities like Abu Dhabi and Dubai. I mean, that folks, just was completely unthinkable. Israelis and Arabs are standing shoulder to shoulder to defend the region from Iranian attacks.
And just as recently as this month, Danny and I were able to host the Foreign Minister of Israel and the Foreign Minister of Morocco together as they expanded their relationship. They upgraded their embassies. They have direct flights. They’re upgrading their trade and tourism. They’re establishing new avenues for investment.
So, folks, my bottom line is—and I know I went a little long, but I think it’s so important for everyone to hear: have hope. Peace is possible. America will stand with the Jewish people. The terrorists are on their back foot. Be strong, be resilient, be wise, and know that what you’re doing is right. Stand with your moral compass, and know that this administration, the United States of America, stands with you.
Thank you. It’s good to be with you.
###
title: Remarks at a UN High-Level Event Marking Three Years Since the October 7th Attack Against Israel

SEC Seeks Final Judgment Against Former Western Asset Co-CIO Ken Leech in Cherry Picking Case
Washington D.C., Oct. 6, 2026 —
The Securities and Exchange Commission today moved for entry of a final judgment by consent against Stephen Kenneth Leech II, the former co-chief investment officer of registered investment adviser Western Asset Management Company LLC, whom the SEC previously charged with a multi-year cherry-picking allocation scheme.
As alleged in the SEC’s November 2024 complaint, from at least January 2021 through October 2023, Leech placed trades and then routinely delayed allocations until near or after futures markets set daily settlement prices, allowing him to observe price movements and disproportionally allocate hundreds of millions of dollars in realized and unrealized first‑day gains to favored portfolios and a similar amount of realized and unrealized first‑day losses to disfavored portfolios.
Without admitting the allegations in the SEC’s complaint, Leech consented to entry of a final judgment, subject to court approval, that would order him to pay a $3 million penalty, impose an officer-and-director bar and permanently enjoin him from violating antifraud provisions of federal securities laws. Leech also agreed to a forthcoming associational bar against him.
In June 2026, the Commission instituted settled public administrative proceedings against Western Asset, ordering the firm to pay a $100 million civil penalty and establishing a Fair Fund to distribute money to affected investors in the disfavored portfolios.
“The conduct by Leech and Western Asset was an egregious breach of fiduciary obligations to their clients,” said Brent Wilner, Associate Director of the SEC’s Los Angeles Regional Office. “Together, the resolution with Leech, if approved by the court, and the SEC’s prior settlement with Western Asset will return $103 million and provide meaningful relief to harmed investors, and reinforce that advisers must put clients first, every time.”
Also in June 2026, Leech pleaded guilty in U.S. District Court in the Southern District of New York to obstruction of justice charges related to false and misleading testimony he provided to the SEC during its investigation; sentencing will take place in the coming weeks.
The SEC acknowledges the assistance of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York and the FBI.
###
Last Reviewed or Updated: Oct. 6, 2026
title: SEC Seeks Final Judgment Against Former Western Asset Co-CIO Ken Leech in Cherry Picking Case

Neal, Wyden Object to Treasury’s Proposed Boost for Private School Tax Credits
New provision continues Trump’s pattern of ignoring clear Congressional mandates in an effort to benefit the wealthy and well-connected
WASHINGTON, DC— House Ways and Means Committee Ranking Member Richard E. Neal (D-MA) and Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden (D-OR) today objected to the Treasury Department’s recently issued proposed regulations on new Internal Revenue Code section 25F that further Republican attempts to undermine public school systems by directing taxpayer money toward private and religious schools.
In a letter to Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent, Ranking Members Neal and Wyden called out the Administration’s actions as a blatant attempt to circumvent the clear rules established by Congress to funnel even more taxpayer funds away from public education and use it to subsidize the private school education of children from wealthy families. Treasury’s baseless interpretation of federal statute would allow married couples filing jointly to potentially claim double the credit that is authorized under the law.
“This interpretation is wildly inconsistent with the longstanding treatment of other provisions that use identical or near-identical language,” Neal and Wyden wrote. “This throws doubt upon Treasury’s interpretation of many provisions of the Code, creates a great deal of uncertainty in the administration of our tax laws, and could balloon the deficit,” Neal and Wyden noted, adding that it could increase the cost of the credit by an additional $150 billion over the next decade.
The Democratic Committee leaders closed by demanding the Administration provide written answers and explanations to how the new interpretation of the law will impact taxpayers, how it came to be and was coordinated internally, which other tax provisions taxpayers might take a return position that is different from previously listed guidance based on new interpretations, and other pressing matters.
Read the full letter to Secretary Bessent HERE.
###

WASHINGTON – The Department of Veterans Affairs announced today $16 million in new grants to 91 community-based organizations across the country that provide adaptive sports programs for Veterans and service members with disabilities.
Adaptive sports programs give Veterans opportunities to build independence, well-being, and quality of life through a variety of competitive and recreational activities. These activities, such as archery, hunting, fishing, skiing, cycling, various wheelchair sports, and many others, enable Veterans to rehabilitate through recreation and encourage an active and healthy lifestyle.
View the complete list of grant awardees.
“Adaptive sports provide Veterans important opportunities to showcase their incredible resilience while improving their physical health and mobility,” said VA Secretary Doug Collins. “These grants will help thousands of Veterans across the country create meaningful connections through recreation and competition.”
VA has awarded more than $150 million to expand access to adaptive sports nationwide since the establishment of the Adaptive Sports Grant Program.
The grants announced today are the latest in a long line of VA accomplishments during the second Trump Administration. Since Jan. 20, 2025, VA has:
- Enrolled more than 290,000 new Veterans in VA healthcare in 2026
- Opened 43 new VA healthcare facilities since Jan. 20, 2025, expanding healthcare access for Veterans around the country
- Completed a record high 82,083,918 direct care appointments in fiscal year 2025, up 4.1% from FY 2024
- Completed a record high 59,989,662 community care appointments in FY 2025, up 12% from FY 2024
- Offered Veterans more than 3.2 million appointments outside of normal operating hours since Jan. 20, 2025, giving Veterans more timely and convenient options for care
- Committed nearly $5 billion in FY26 to modernize, repair and improve healthcare facilities, the largest non-recurring maintenance investment in VA’s history
title: VA awards $16M in grants for adaptive sports programs

Krishnamoorthi and Vindman Introduce LESSONS from Ukraine Act to Apply Ukraine’s Battlefield Innovations to U.S. Military
WASHINGTON — On Monday, Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), a senior member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and Congressman Eugene Vindman (VA-07), a 25-year Army veteran, introduced the Learning Effective Strategies and Systems Optimization for National Security (LESSONS) from Ukraine Act, legislation requiring the Pentagon to study and apply lessons from Ukraine’s battlefield innovations to U.S. military doctrine and training.
“During my visit to Ukraine, I saw firsthand how the Ukrainians are rapidly adapting to a battlefield where drones and electronic warfare are changing how wars are fought,” Congressman Krishnamoorthi said. “The LESSONS from Ukraine Act will make sure our military learns from what Ukraine has discovered through years of defending itself against Putin’s invasion, from countering drone swarms and operating through electronic warfare to sustaining weapons production under attack. We need to put those lessons to work to strengthen our own military, protect our servicemembers, and ensure we are prepared to deter aggression across the world.”
“Ukraine’s defense against Russia has shown just how rapidly modern warfare is evolving. I saw that firsthand during my trip to Ukraine last month, where drones, electronic warfare, cyber operations, and defense manufacturing are reshaping the battlefield in real time,” said Vindman. "As a 25-year Army veteran, I know our military must constantly learn, adapt, and innovate to maintain our strategic advantage and protect our service members. The LESSONS from Ukraine Act will ensure the Department of Defense learns from Ukraine’s hard-earned experience and applies those lessons to our doctrine, training, and capabilities so our military is prepared for the threats of tomorrow.”
The LESSONS from Ukraine Act would require the Secretary of Defense to report to Congress within 120 days on lessons the U.S. military can draw from the Russia-Ukraine War, including the use of drones and other unmanned systems, electronic and cyber warfare, air defense, operations without GPS or satellite communications, battlefield medicine, and Ukraine’s efforts to expand and decentralize weapons production. The Pentagon would also be required to develop a plan and timetable for incorporating those lessons into U.S. military doctrine and training. Congressman Krishnamoorthi first announced the legislation following an August official visit to Ukraine, where he visited a Ukrainian drone production facility and met with officials about the battlefield and Ukraine’s rapidly evolving defense innovations.
The text of the legislation is available here.
title: Krishnamoorthi and Vindman Introduce LESSONS from Ukraine Act to Apply Ukraine’s Battlefield Innovations to U.S. Military

text:
Fast Facts
Over the last several years, applying for a mortgage meant homebuyers would be bombarded with marketing calls and texts. That's because credit reporting agencies sold their information to lenders and brokers who used it to send competing offers.
Although these offers could help homebuyers shop for a mortgage, many were overwhelmed and annoyed by their high volume and at times confused over who was sending them.
New restrictions went into effect in March 2026 limiting who can buy this information. This could reduce unwanted solicitations while still allowing buyers to comparison shop for mortgages, e.g., by using online tools or referrals.
Hand holding a smartphone with incoming call from spam caller on the screen.
Highlights
What GAO Found
When homebuyers apply for a mortgage, lenders request their credit reports from credit reporting agencies. These agencies may then sell the homebuyers’ contact and credit information to other lenders and brokers, which use it to send competing loan offers. Before recent legislation, credit reporting agencies could, without the homebuyer’s consent, provide this information to those that did not have an existing relationship with the homebuyer (see figure). Thus, homebuyers could receive dozens of mortgage solicitations by phone or text in a short period.
Example of the Mortgage Trigger Lead Marketing Process
According to industry stakeholders, the primary benefit of trigger leads is that they can encourage homebuyers to comparison shop for loans and potentially save money. But this benefit may be limited: Recent federal survey results suggest that no more than 3.5 percent of homebuyers may have obtained a loan through competing offers based on trigger leads. One lender said homebuyers have ways to compare lenders before applying for a mortgage, so offers based on trigger leads generated later in the homebuying process may be less useful.
Trigger leads resulted in a high volume of unwanted marketing solicitations and posed other drawbacks for some homebuyers, according to consumer advocates and industry stakeholders:
- A high volume of solicitations can overwhelm and confuse homebuyers, and aggressive tactics can annoy them.
- Broad dissemination of homebuyers’ information could expose them to misleading or deceptive practices.
- Homebuyers may view the sale of their personal information and resulting marketing solicitations as an invasion of privacy.
In 2025, the Homebuyers Privacy Protection Act restricted credit reporting agencies’ ability to provide residential mortgage trigger leads to parties that have an existing relationship with or consent from the homebuyer. Because these restrictions took effect in March 2026, not enough time has passed to determine their effects on homebuyers. If effectively implemented, these restrictions could limit access to trigger leads and reduce the volume of solicitations homebuyers receive while preserving opportunities to comparison shop.
Why GAO Did This Study
Each year, millions of homebuyers apply for a mortgage, and some receive marketing calls and texts from other lenders and brokers with competing offers based on trigger leads. The volume of these mortgage solicitations prompted the enactment of the Homebuyers Privacy Protection Act in 2025.
The act includes a provision for GAO to assess the value of trigger leads for homebuyers. This report examines (1) the potential benefits of trigger leads, (2) drawbacks associated with them, and (3) how the act’s restrictions may affect those benefits and drawbacks.
GAO reviewed federal and state laws, searched for and reviewed relevant literature, and analyzed 2022–2024 responses to the National Survey of Mortgage Originations. In addition, GAO obtained information from or interviewed officials of credit reporting agencies, consumer groups, mortgage lenders (banks, credit unions, and nonbanks), industry associations, the association for state banking regulators, and a state regulatory agency. GAO also analyzed the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau’s (CFPB) consumer complaints database and used artificial intelligence to identify complaints related to mortgage solicitations, and interviewed officials from CFPB and the Federal Trade Commission.
For more information, contact William W. Colvin at colvinw@gao.gov.
title: Mortgage Lending: Newly Enacted Restrictions May Help Curb Unwanted Solicitations While Preserving Comparison Shopping

MOBILE, AL – Robert Davian Grijalva of Loxley, Alabama, who has been in custody since 2025, was sentenced today by Chief United States District Court Judge Jeffrey U. Beaverstock to time served for making an interstate threat.

According to court documents, Grijalva, 19, conveyed a threat by Instagram message to a victim stating that he would “blow yo head off.” The message also contained an emoji of a devil and a drop of blood.

“Threats to kill or commit violence, including threats made over the internet, are unacceptable and will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law,” said U.S. Attorney Sean P. Costello.

“Threats of violence, whether online or otherwise, create real fear in our communities. Robert Grijalva’s conviction underscores the seriousness of these actions and the FBI’s ongoing work to safeguard those who are targeted,” said Christopher R. Flowers, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI Mobile Division. “We will continue to investigate threats wherever they originate and ensure those responsible are held accountable.”

In addition to the sentence, the Court imposed certain conditions on Grijalva including mental health evaluation and treatment, drug and alcohol monitoring, and no contact with the victim.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation investigated the case, and Assistant U.S. Attorney Gaillard Ladd prosecuted the case on behalf of the United States.

You can report threats to the online through the Official FBI Tips Portal at www.tips.fbi.gov or by calling 1-800-CALL-FBI (1-800-225-5324).
title: Loxley Man Sentenced For Making Interstate Threats

Executive Order 14435
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered:
Section 1. Purpose and Policy. Farmers and truckers are essential to the American way of life. Restricted global diesel supply has led to rising prices, and these key industries have been particularly hard hit. While my Administration has already undertaken historic efforts to ensure fuel affordability for our citizens, it is clear that further temporary relief is necessary.
To that end, today I am directing the Secretary of the Treasury (Secretary) to use his authority to defer certain diesel fuel tax payment obligations and to provide penalty relief to the extent permitted by law. I am also directing the Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of Transportation to facilitate implementation of this policy. This targeted action will put money directly in the pocket of American farmers, truckers, and workers, to support their vital service to our Nation.
Sec. 2. Deferring Certain Payments of Excise Tax Liability and Providing Penalty Relief. (a) Within 5 days of the date of this order, the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of War, as appropriate, shall determine whether relief is authorized under 26 U.S.C. 7508A, including whether a qualifying event has occurred and which taxpayers have been affected by that event. If the Secretary makes those determinations, the Secretary shall, to the extent authorized by law, defer payment by those taxpayers of the taxes imposed by 26 U.S.C. 4041(a)(1)(A) or by 26 U.S.C. 4041(b)(1)(B) and that are incurred during the period of October 5, 2026, through December 31, 2026.
(b) Amounts deferred pursuant to the Secretary’s exercise of authority described in subsection (a) of this section shall, to the extent authorized by law, be deferred without any penalties, interest, additional amount, or addition to the tax.
(c) Within 5 days of the date of this order, the Secretary shall direct the Internal Revenue Service to announce that it will not impose a penalty under 26 U.S.C. 6715 (a)(1) or 26 U.S.C. 6715 (a)(2), when dyed diesel fuel is sold for use or used on the highway during the period of October 5, 2026, through December 31, 2026. The announcement shall also address relief from penalties for failure to make semimonthly deposits of that tax.
Sec. 3. Implementing Guidance. The Secretary shall issue guidance implementing this order. The guidance shall identify the specific relief being granted and any conditions on such relief; the legal basis for relief, covered taxpayers, persons, locations, acts, liabilities, and deadlines; the beginning and ending dates of each applicable period; the date by which postponed taxes must be paid.
Sec. 4. Tax Forgiveness. The Secretary shall explore avenues, including legislation, to eliminate the obligation to pay the amounts deferred pursuant to the Secretary’s exercise of authority described in section 2 of this order.
Sec. 5. Prioritizing Fuel Compliance Resources. The Secretary shall assess how the Internal Revenue Service should allocate resources to inspections of vehicle fuel tanks and fuel sampling during the period of any relief provided under section 2 of this order, and shall publicly announce that determination.
Sec. 6. Maintaining Safety and Efficiency on America’s Highways. The Secretary of Transportation, acting through the Administrator of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (Administrator), shall:
(a) engage with State governments, relevant industry leadership as determined by the Administrator, and relevant labor organizations as determined by the Administrator to encourage safe and expedient coordination between the Federal Government and these various stakeholders in furtherance of the policies of this order; and
(b) continue all compliance enforcement measures, including audits, inspections, and monitoring programs, as provided for by law.
Sec. 7. Promoting Diesel Access for Farmers. The Secretary of Agriculture shall further the priorities of this order, including by:
(a) coordinating with agricultural cooperatives, rural fuel distributors, farm supply organizations, and other agricultural stakeholders, as determined by the Secretary of Agriculture, to ensure adequate distribution of dyed diesel for their use in high-demand areas; and
(b) encouraging corresponding State action to further the policies of this order.
Sec. 8. Engaging State Governments. The Director of the White House Office of Intergovernmental Affairs shall engage with States to further the policies of this order, taking appropriate action to encourage States to adopt policies that correspond to the Secretary’s exercise of authority described in section 2 of this order, in accordance with applicable law.
Sec. 9. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect:
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; or
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.
(b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.
(c) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.
(d) The costs for publication of this order shall be borne by the Department of Agriculture.
DONALD J. TRUMP
THE WHITE HOUSE,
October 5, 2026.
title: Emergency Tax Relief on Diesel Fuel

Region VI Administrator Ashlea Quinonez and Team Visit Uplift’s Microhome
TEXAS - U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) spotlighted multiple housing innovations from the Southwest region during the sixth annual Innovative Housing Showcase, held September 22-24 on the National Mall. Hoyer, Comptroller Lierman Visit Nonprofit Organizations Across Maryland's Fifth Congressional District
WASHINGTON, DC – This week, Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) and Maryland Comptroller Brooke E. Lierman visited nonprofit organizations in Prince George's and Charles Counties to discuss each group's commitment to serving Southern Marylanders within their communities.
"Maryland's Fifth Congressional District is home to a multitude of nonprofit organizations that deliver critical resources and create opportunities for the region. From Westbrook Horse Farm to LifeStyles of Maryland, each advocate and organization we met with has an invaluable role in shaping the lives of Marylanders. I enjoyed seeing their work up close and discussing their contributions to our communities. I thank each organization for welcoming us, and I will continue to support their efforts during the remainder of my term in Congresss," said Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05).
“The three organizations we visited – all nonprofits but each doing work in its own way - play an essential role in strengthening our communities, supporting Marylanders in need, and creating opportunities for individuals to build better futures,” said Comptroller Brooke E. Lierman. “I am grateful for the dedicated people behind these organizations and the difference they make across our state. From supporting young people to helping individuals find stable housing, to supporting economic development and job creation, the work of these organizations makes Maryland a better place for everyone.” 
Congressman Hoyer and Comptroller Lierman with Brian Westbrook and his father, Roy Westbrook at the Westbrook Farm.
Starting off in Prince George's County, Congressman Hoyer and Comptroller Lierman visited the Westbrook Horse Farm in Upper Marlboro, Maryland. Owned and operated by Brian Westbrook, former NFL player and founder of The Brian Westbrook Foundation, the farm's programming provides hands-on skills training, riding lessons, and mentorship for youth to teach them responsibility and instill a greater sense of purpose in their lives. Today, the NLRB announced the appointment of Jamal M. Allen as the Associate General Counsel in the NLRB’s Ethics Office and the Agency’s new Designated Agency Ethics Official (DAEO).

In his role, he will advise senior leadership on ethical issues and will manage the Ethics Office, which is responsible for providing comprehensive guidance in response to ethics questions. The office also provides a wide array of training products and resources, which interpret and explain both legal and government ethics topics and obligations.

Jamal began his career with the NLRB in Region 16 as a Field Attorney in the San Antonio Resident Office from 2001 to 2007, and then in the Houston Resident Office from 2008-2013. Jamal joined the Agency’s legal ethics staff in July 2013 as Special Ethics Counsel and then Independent Special Ethics Counsel. Since 2017, Jamal had served as the Agency’s Alternate Designated Agency Ethics Official where he assisted the DAEO in running the day-to-day legal and government ethics program for the NLRB.

“Jamal Allen has long demonstrated exceptional integrity, judgment, and dedication to the mission of this Agency,” said General Counsel Crystal Carey. “His leadership of the Ethics Office will strengthen our commitment to ethical excellence and ensure that our employees receive the guidance and support they need to uphold the highest standards of public service.”

“Agency employees rely on the Ethics Office to ensure that they serve the American people with the utmost integrity,” said Chairman James Murphy. “I have every confidence that Jamal Allen will lead that Office with sound judgment and candor, upholding the Agency’s strong ethical culture at every level.” Jamal received a Juris Doctorate from the University of Texas School of Law where he was a Robert S. Strauss Scholar and a Bachelor of Arts cum laude in government from the University of Texas at Austin.

Established in 1935, the National Labor Relations Board is an independent federal agency that protects employees from unfair labor practices and protects the right of private sector employees to join together, with or without a union, to improve wages, benefits and working conditions. The NLRB conducts hundreds of workplace elections and investigates thousands of unfair labor practice charges each year.
title: Jamal M. Allen Appointed Associate General Counsel in the Ethics Office and the Agency’s Designated Agency Ethics Official (DAEO)

CLEVELAND and COLUMBUS, Ohio –United States Attorney David M. Toepfer for the Northern District of Ohio and United States Attorney Dominick S. Gerace II for the Southern District of Ohio announced arrests in three voter fraud cases for allegations involving voting in an election that included candidates for the office of President, Vice President, Member of the Senate, and Member of the House of Representatives.

In the Southern District of Ohio, a criminal complaint was filed charging Cary Ann Patterson, 59, a citizen of the United Kingdom with lawful permanent resident status, with illegally voting in a federal election as an alien. Voters in federal elections must be U.S. citizens, and the complaint alleges that Patterson voted on Nov. 5, 2024. According to court documents, in 2005, the Gallia County Board of Elections received a voter registration card for Patterson in which “Yes” was marked in response to the question, “Are you a U.S. citizen?” Based on Gallia County Board of Elections records, Patterson allegedly voted in at least 10 elections as a non-citizen.

In the Northern District of Ohio, Arshed Zuberi, 69, a Pakistani national with lawful permanent resident status, has been charged by criminal complaint with illegally voting in a federal election as an alien. He allegedly registered to vote in September 2015 and August 2016. On voter registration forms, Zuberi’s signature appears next to the declaration “I declare under penalty of election falsification I am a citizen of the United States.” Voting records from the Cuyahoga County Board of Elections show that he voted in at least six elections.

A criminal complaint has also been filed in the Northern District of Ohio charging Eliza M. Moss, 63, a citizen of the Philippines with lawful permanent resident status, with unlawfully voting in a federal election as an alien. According to state of Ohio and Ashtabula County voting records, Moss registered to vote in September 2004 and in February 2023. On voter registration forms, her signature appears next to the declaration “I declare under penalty of election falsification I am a citizen of the United States.” Moss allegedly voted in several primary and general elections. According to the criminal complaint, Moss told investigators that the person who helped fill out her registration told her that she could vote despite not being a citizen.

Unlawfully voting in a federal election as an alien is punishable by up to 12 months in prison.

Dominick S. Gerace II, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Ohio; David M. Toepfer , United States Attorney for the Northern District of Ohio; and Acting Special Agent in Charge Jeremy Pierczynski, Homeland Security Investigations Detroit announced the charges. Executive Assistant United States Attorney Christy L. Muncy for the Southern District of Ohio and Assistant United States Attorney Robert Corts for the Northern District of Ohio are representing the United States in these cases.

Criminal complaints merely contain allegations, and defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law.

LAFAYETTE – On September 25, 2026, the United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Louisiana charged Christopher Peck , 56, of La Center, Kentucky, by criminal complaint with Production of Visual Depictions Involving the Sexual Exploitation of Minors. If convicted, Peck faces a mandatory minimum of 15 years and up to 30 years in federal prison.

As alleged in the criminal complaint, foreign authorities notified the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) in September 2026 after reviewing an encrypted online conversation between a suspect the foreign authorities were investigating and an individual with a username the FBI later linked to Peck. The complaint alleges that Peck told the foreign suspect that he was actively abusing a 10-year-old girl and that he was using a spiked drink to facilitate the abuse. Peck then allegedly sent several photos of the minor victim being sexually abused that were taken in a hotel room. Law enforcement identified the minor victim as residing in Louisiana. The complaint further alleges that Peck rented a hotel room in Louisiana that matched the timeframe in which the images were transmitted, April 2026. Peck was arrested in Kentucky on September 29, 2026.

U.S. Attorney Zachary A. Keller for the Western District of Louisiana made the announcement.

The FBI and the New Zealand Police division of Online Child Exploitation Across New Zealand (OCEANZ) investigated this case. It is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Jessica D. Cassidy, with assistance from Paralegal Specialist Denise Duhon.

This case was prosecuted as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by the U.S. Attorneys' Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. Learn more at https://www.justice.gov/psc/about-project-safe-childhood.

A criminal complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

You may find a copy of this press release (and any updates) on the website of the United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Louisiana at www.justice.gov/usao-wdla. Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Western District of Louisiana at www.lawd.uscourts.gov or at https://www.lawd.uscourts.gov/cmecf-pacer. LAREDO, Texas – A 29-year-old former Webb County sheriff’s deputy will serve federal prison time for sexually assaulting and violating the civil rights of a woman.

Ignacio Rodriguez IV pleaded guilty April 23.

U.S. District Judge Marina Garcia Marmolejo ordered Rodriguez to serve 240 months in federal prison to be immediately followed by five years of supervised release. At the hearing, the court heard testimony that the victim and her passenger, who had been pulled over by Rodriguez, repeatedly said they wanted to go home, but Rodriguez told them, “No, you have to convince me,” before directing them to a desolate area. In handing down the sentence, the court noted Rodriguez’s conduct was brazen, calculated, and extremely cruel.

“When a law enforcement officer commits sexual violence under the color of law, the harm reaches far beyond a single victim,” said U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz. “It erodes community trust and undermines what it means to wear the uniform. Rodriguez’s abusive and predatory actions here were not only illegal, but immoral and disgusting.”

“When a law enforcement officer commits sexual violence under the color of law, the harm reaches far beyond a single victim,” said U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz. “It erodes community trust and undermines what it means to wear the uniform. Rodriguez’s abusive and predatory actions here were not only illegal, but immoral and disgusting.”

Rodriguez was a deputy with the Webb County Sheriff’s Office when he committed the offenses.

On Sept. 1, 2024, Rodriguez observed a vehicle traveling into oncoming traffic and conducted a traffic stop. He ordered the driver and a female passenger to exit the vehicle and stand near his marked patrol unit. Rodriguez then turned off his body-worn camera.

The passenger began recording portions of the interaction on her cell phone. The recording captured both women asking Rodriguez to let them go and Rodriguez repeatedly telling them they needed to “convince him.” He then took the driver’s cell phone and instructed the women to follow him to a nearby street.

Once there, the passenger remained in their vehicle while Rodriguez took the victim into his marked patrol unit, when he forced her to perform oral sex and groped her breast without her consent.

Rodriguez will remain in custody pending transfer to a Federal Bureau of Prisons facility to be determined in the near future.

The FBI and the Laredo Police Department conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Leslie Ann Cortez and Brandon Scott Bowling prosecuted the case.
title: Former sheriff’s deputy sentenced for sexually assaulting woman after traffic stop

Trump’s Transportation Department Celebrates $413 Million Investment to Upgrade Rail Safety Across Florida, Build New Multimodal Station for the Space Coast
Instead of funding California’s train to nowhere, President Trump & Secretary Duffy are fixing over 900 highway-rail grade crossings throughout the Sunshine State
COCOA, FL – The U.S. Transportation Department’s Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) today joined the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) to celebrate $413 million in federal funding for essential rail safety upgrades across the Sunshine State and the construction of a new multimodal station in Cocoa. The state of Florida is providing an additional $100 million to support the projects.
The federal package will provide:
- $356 million for Florida DOT to deploy safety upgrades – which include new high-tech signage, lighting, and physical barriers – to 910 highway-rail grade crossing locations to better protect passengers, motorists, and pedestrians.
- $57 million for the City of Cocoa to build a new Brightline in-line rail station, multi-use access road, and new segment of double-track.
The $356 million in federal support from the FRA is a key pillar of Secretary Duffy’s “Golden Age of Rail” package announced in August. Roughly $2 billion of this grant package is funding Secretary Duffy saved the American people by canceling Gavin Newsom’s disastrous high-speed train to nowhere.
FRA Administrator David Fink joined FDOT Secretary Jared W. Perdue, P.E., U.S. Congressman Mike Haridopolos, railroad industry leaders, and local and state officials in Brevard County today to share details about the safety upgrades as well as plans for the new Brightline Cocoa station.
"Defunding California’s train to nowhere is producing tangible safety upgrades and real infrastructure projects that will benefit millions of Floridians for years to come,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “President Trump is delivering transformational results for the Sunshine State, and we’re just getting started.”
“This is a monumental leap in rail safety for the state of Florida, and it was only made possible by President Trump and Secretary Duffy,” said FRA Administrator David Fink. “By investing these dollars where they matter most, President Trump and Secretary Duffy are ushering in a Golden Age of Rail that will make Florida’s rail corridors safe, modern, and more efficient.”
“Here on the Space Coast, we continue to build for the future,” said U.S. Congressman Mike Haridopolos. “This new station will make it easier for people to travel to and from the Space Coast while supporting our growing community. It is expected to have up to a $350 million annual economic impact and support 3,500 jobs, bringing even more opportunity to our region. Thank you to the FRA, FDOT, and our local partners for working together to make rail travel safer and more accessible for Floridians.”
Additional Information:
Of the railroad crossing enhancements to be installed at over 900 locations across Florida, nearly a quarter of the sites will be in Central Florida – in Brevard, Orange, Osceola, Seminole, and Volusia counties.
The types of safety features to be added include:
- Upgrades of pedestrian-activated warning systems at pedestrian rail crossings, including lights, gates, and audible warnings for pedestrians.
- Refinement and enhancement of pavement markings to ensure only rail-related markings are used (including Dynamic Envelopes). Raised reflective markers and solid lane lines will provide motorists, pedestrians, and bicyclists with clear, consistent visual cues.
- Installation of overhead-mounted signals to enhance motorists’ awareness of rail crossings.
- Enhanced lighting to heighten the visibility of rail crossings for pedestrians and motorists.
- Installation of LED-enhanced “DO NOT STOP ON TRACKS” signage at high-speed rail crossings to reinforce safe driving behaviors for motorists.
- Addition of “ANOTHER TRAIN COMING” warning signs at locations with at least two tracks to help prevent potential conflicts with pedestrians and vehicles with an unexpected additional train.
- Installation of physical barriers such as double gates to further deter vehicles from going around rail crossing gates.
###
title: Trump’s Transportation Department Celebrates $413 Million Investment to Upgrade Rail Safety Across Florida, Build New Multimodal Station for the Space Coast

PHILADELPHIA – FEMA is proposing updates to the Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) for Mecklenburg County, Virginia and Incorporated Areas. Community partners are invited to participate in a 90-day appeal and comment period.
The updated maps were produced in coordination with local, state and FEMA officials. Significant community review of the maps has already taken place, but before the maps become final, community partners can identify any corrections or questions about the information provided and submit appeals or comments.
The 90-day appeal period began on September 30, 2026. Residents, business owners and other community partners are encouraged to review the updated maps to learn about local flood risks and potential future flood insurance requirements. They may submit an appeal if they perceive that modeling or data used to create the map is technically or scientifically incorrect.
- An appeal must include technical information, such as hydraulic or hydrologic data, to support the claim.
- Appeals cannot be based on the effects of proposed projects or projects started after the study is in progress.
- If property owners see incorrect information that does not change the flood hazard information—such as a missing or misspelled road name in the Special Flood Hazard Area or an incorrect corporate boundary—they can submit a written comment.
The next step in the mapping process is the resolution of all comments and appeals. Once they are resolved, FEMA will notify communities of the effective date of the final maps.
Submit appeals and comments by contacting your local floodplain administrator. The preliminary maps may be viewed online at the FEMA Flood Map Changes Viewer,
For more information about the flood maps, contact a FEMA Map Specialist by telephone; toll free, at 1-877-FEMA-MAP (1-877-336-2627) or by email at FEMA-FMIX@fema.dhs.gov.
Most homeowner’s insurance policies do not cover flooding. There are cost-saving options available for those newly mapped into a high-risk flood zone. Learn more about your flood insurance options by talking with your insurance agent and visiting https://www.floodsmart.gov.
Mecklenburg County Flood Mapping Milestones
- July 12, 2023 — Flood Risk Review Meeting to review draft flood hazard data.
- August 28, 2025 — Preliminary Flood Insurance Rate Map released.
- October 9, 2025 — Community Coordination and Outreach Meeting to review Preliminary Flood Insurance Rate Map and discuss updates to local floodplain management ordinance and flood insurance.
- September 30, 2026 — Appeal Period starts.
- October 2027* — New Flood Insurance Rate Map becomes effective and flood insurance requirements take effect. (*Timeline subject to change pending completion of the appeal review process.)
If you have any questions, please contact FEMA Region 3 Office of External Affairs at (215) 931-5597 or at femar3newsdesk@fema.dhs.gov.
###
FEMA’s mission is helping people before, during and after disasters.
Follow FEMA online, on X @FEMA or @FEMAEspanol, on FEMA's Facebook page or Espanol page, on Truth Social and FEMA's YouTube account.
For preparedness information, follow the Ready Campaign on X at @Ready.gov, on Instagram @Ready.gov or on the Ready Facebook page.

Neal (D-MA) and Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden (D-OR) today objected to the Treasury Department’s recently issued proposed regulations on new Internal Revenue Code section 25F that further Republican attempts to undermine public school systems by directing taxpayer money toward private and religious schools.

PATERSON, NJ – Tonight, U.S. Representative Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09) celebrated the release of Martin Soto, a resident of the Ninth Congressional District who was held in ICE custody for several months.
“I am so overjoyed that Martin Soto is finally freed from ICE custody,” stated Rep. Nellie Pou, a member of the House Committee on Homeland Security. “Martin was undeniably targeted and mistreated, being moved from Delaney Hall to the Elizabeth Detention Center and held in solitary confinement. ICE remains out of control in our state and we must continue to oppose its rampant abuses. “I am so happy Martin is finally being released from ICE custody,” said Gabby Soto, wife of Martin Soto. “I want to thank Congresswoman Nellie Pou for all of her work on his case. Her efforts were critical to us finally reaching this moment.”

text:
WTAS: New Regulations Make It Easier to Find, Compare, and Report Healthcare Pricing and Coverage Information
WASHINGTON, D.C.—OCTOBER 6, 2026—The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), through the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), on Monday announced that Americans will have access to more reliable, accessible, and actionable information about what their health coverage includes and what they are likely to pay before receiving care under new regulations that strengthen federal healthcare price transparency requirements. The actions taken today to create a more transparent healthcare marketplace also ensure employers can make more informed decisions; researchers can better understand healthcare markets; and innovators can build better tools.
Here is how government officials, medical professionals, advocates, the media, and others are responding:
Government Officials:
- Rep. Davidson via X: “When patients can compare prices, health plans and providers have to compete for their business, and that competition brings costs down. This final rule puts Americans in charge of choosing the health care that works best for them and their families.”
- Rep. Harshbarger via X: “For too long, the corporations that pay for our care have gone to great lengths to hide costs and bury patients in complexity. For the first time, insurers will have to attest that their pricing data is accurate and complete. Transparency drives competition, and competition lowers costs. That's a win for patients, employers, and taxpayers!”
- Rep. Fine via Newsmax: “I think it's going to be a massive help,’ Fine said. ‘When people are getting an X-ray or they're going to get a shot or some other service, they don't realize that the 10 providers in their community could charge massively different prices. If you're willing to drive an extra mile down the street to save a nickel a gallon on gas, you certainly ought to know if a procedure is going to cost $50 or $100 less at one place or another.”
- White House via X: “The Trump Administration is putting Americans first with healthcare price transparency, ensuring healthcare price data is clear and reliable. @HHSGov is making healthcare transparency useful for patients. Americans should know exactly how much their healthcare options cost.”
- White House Rapid Response via X: “@DrOzCMS: ‘Our rule is going to empower all these transparency sites in the room today to sync up and deliver a one-stop shop for cost comparison — using data that has always been out there but has purposely been obfuscated.’”
- White House Rapid Response via X: “@SecKennedy: In his first term, President Trump succeeded in demanding healthcare price transparency — but the industry took evasive action to obscure the process. Today, we are fixing that so Americans know exactly what their healthcare procedure will cost.”
- Department of Labor via X: “The American People have a right to compare healthcare prices and thanks to @POTUS — now they can. CHOICE DRIVES COMPETITION — it’s the opposite of Socialism — IT IS THE AMERICAN WAY. Together with @HHSGov, @USTreasury, and @CMSGov — we are delivering on healthcare transparency so ALL AMERICANS can make the best choices for themselves and their families.”
- Republican Study Committee via X: “President Trump started the fight for healthcare price transparency in his first term, and now @SecKennedy and @DrOzCMS are finishing what he started by giving American families the CLEAR, ACCURATE, and ACTIONABLE prices they need to make the best decisions for their health.”
- Republican Study Committee via X: “For too long, Big Healthcare overcharged vulnerable patients and kept Americans in the dark about what their care would cost. Thanks to the leadership of @CMSGov, new transparency rules will cut bloated pricing files by roughly 70%, strip out useless and duplicative data, and make personalized cost estimates far easier to access. America FIRST means American patients FIRST, and the Trump administration is keeping that promise.”
- Pennsylvania State Senator Dawn Keefer via X: “A win for health care transparency! The federal govt is strengthening price transparency so patients can compare costs. That's a step in the right direction! One we should build on here in PA.”
Medical Professionals & Academics:
- Katy Talento, epidemiologist and former White House Health Policy Advisor, via X: “Announcements of more robust requirements to end secret health care prices. Closing some loopholes, requiring plans to attest that the prices are accurate, allowing patients to get REAL price info by phone in advance. And much more. Amen. Thanks @HHSGov @USDOL @USTreasury @FTC”
Advocates & Organizations:
- Patient Rights Advocate Founder and Chairman, Cynthia A. Fisher, via The Center Square: “…[A] transformative step to lower health care costs, stop overcharges, and hold insurers and hospitals accountable... added requirement of executive attestation that published prices and other information are true, accurate, and complete as of the date in the machine-readable file is a breakthrough for compliance… Real price transparency means patients can shop for better care at lower prices and employers can demand a better deal.”
- America First Works via X: “@SecKennedy announces more TRANSPARENCY in healthcare costs: ‘If you went to a car dealer and you said, 'How much does that cost?' and they said, 'We're not going to tell you until after you make the purchase,' you wouldn't do it—but that's how the healthcare system in this country [worked].’”
- American First Policy Institute via X: “@SecKennedy: Americans deserve healthcare price transparency, and to know exactly what their procedure will cost.”
- Patient Rights Advocate via X: “@AFergusonFTC hits it out of the park: ‘Arming consumers with the knowledge they need to shop around will foster competition and drive down healthcare costs.’”
- Patient Rights Advocate via X: “@Sonderling47 explains how price transparency is critical to lowering healthcare costs for employers and employees: ‘When workers and employers can compare prices, providers have to compete for their business... putting more money back in your pocket.’”
- Patient Rights Advocate via X: “@CMSGov’s Peter Nelson announces the upcoming schema for the Prescription Drug File, requiring insurers to post exactly what they pay for prescription drugs. This long-overdue step is essential to helping patients better understand and lower their drug costs!”
- Patient Rights Advocate via X: “@SecKennedy nails it: ‘One lesson from the first generation transparency requirement is that publishing enormous quantities of data does not necessarily produce useful information.’ The new Transparency in Coverage final rule requires health plans to publish the data actually needed to deliver clear and upfront prices to patients.’”
- Patient Rights Advocate via X: “The final Transparency in Coverage rule announced today is a significant step toward holding insurers accountable and securing actual, upfront prices in dollars and cents for consumers. As @SecKennedy said, ‘The American people pay for this care system, and they have the right to know the prices. The prices do not belong to the hospitals. They don’t belong to the insurance companies. They belong to the American people and the consumers.’”
- Patient Rights Advocate via X: “The @FTC is cracking down on hidden hospital prices, warning 24 large hospital systems to disclose their prices upfront or be taken to court. As @AFergusonFTC said, ‘We demand nothing less than radical transparency.’”
- Independent Women via press release: “Independent Women applauds new regulations finalized by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), under the leadership of HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. and CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz, respectively, that will strengthen federal healthcare price transparency requirements, empower employers to make informed decisions, equip researchers to more effectively understand healthcare markets, and incentivize innovators to develop better tools.”
- Independent Women Director of the Center for Better Health, Dr. Monique Yohanan, via press release: “Healthcare is one of the only places Americans are expected to buy first and learn the price later…Price transparency is one of the most powerful tools we have to make healthcare more affordable.”
- State Financial Officers Foundation via X: “Transparency only works if the data is actually usable. Today’s move toward real dollar prices, standardized reporting and greater accountability is meaningful progress for employers, patients and taxpayers trying to understand what healthcare actually costs.”
- MAHA Action via X: “Dr. Oz says UnitedHealthcare patients in New York City can be charged anywhere from $350 to $3,000 for the same MRI. And he says this is not unique to one insurer, but part of a broader pricing problem seen across the healthcare system. Now, he and RFK Jr. are taking action to make those prices far easier for patients to see and compare. ‘And if you actually look at the numbers, it’s stunning.’ ‘In the city that I practiced medicine in for much of my life, New York City, the difference between an MRI scan across UnitedHealthcare insured policies, so just one insurance company, one procedure, $350 to $3,000.’ ‘On the same island if you’re insured by the same company.’ ‘The bottom line is our rule is going to empower all these transparency sites in the room today to sync up and deliver a one stop shop for cost comparison using the data that is out there, has always been out there, but has purposely been obfuscated.’”
- MAHA Action via X: “‘Hip replacement in Boston costs $17,900 at one hospital, and at a nearby hospital, it costs $74,000 for the exact same surgery.’ ‘Researchers have found MRI prices varying as much as ninefold within a single city.’ RFK Jr. says Big Insurance has created a system where Americans can pay wildly different prices for the exact same care while the real cost stays hidden. ‘And one analysis found that 60% of insurer negotiated hospital rates were higher than the hospital’s own cash price.’ ‘The insurance company, who is supposed to be negotiating for all of its members and beating down the price, has actually negotiated a price that is higher than if you just walked into that hospital off the street and asked for that procedure.’ ‘So, the whole system was corrupt.’ ‘It was crooked.’ ‘Markets cannot discipline prices that they cannot see.’”
- MAHA Action via X: “RFK Jr. and Dr. Oz are making healthcare, and insurance executives put their names behind the pricing data they release. No more hiding behind manipulated numbers and misleading data. ‘We are also requiring health plans and insurers to attest that pricing data they publish is true, accurate, and complete.’ ‘And to identify the senior official at that company who is responsible for that data and for those statements.’”
- American Hospital Association via Spectrum News: “…[A]n important step toward greater accountability across the healthcare system by shining more light on health plan pricing information. Hospitals have spent years making detailed pricing information public, and we welcome efforts to bring greater transparency to health plan data. This includes making personalized cost information easier to access, which is critical to helping patients make informed health care decisions.”
- Erisa Industry Committee President and CEO, James Gelfand, via press release: “Employers buy health care for their workers, and for too long the prices have been hidden or buried…The first round of price data opened the books. This rule makes the data usable by a general audience. For large employers that provide coverage to tens of millions of workers and their families, better data means we can spot when one hospital charges more than another for the same procedure, negotiate harder, build better networks, and cut waste that drives up costs for employers and employees alike.”
- Purchaser Business Group on Health CEO, Elizabeth Mitchell, via Healthcare Dive: “We believe that these new rules are going to make a really significant difference, this has the potential to meaningfully address the affordability crisis in the commercial market.”
- State Financial Officers Foundation CEO, OJ Oleka via The Center Square: “…[R]eal dollar prices, standardized reporting, and greater accountability is meaningful progress for employers, patients, and taxpayers trying to understand what healthcare actually costs… Accountability and transparency go hand in hand, but transparency only works if the data is actually usable.”
- David Kochel, campaign strategist via The Center Square: “[T]he Trump Administration is taking action on healthcare price transparency ahead of the midterm elections, showing Republicans are willing to lean forward on an issue that hits Americans’ wallets every day. Real prices give patients the freedom to choose lower-cost, high-quality care and give employers the power to audit spending, negotiate better deals, and hold insurers accountable…The administration's work on price transparency puts power in the hands of patients and employers to stop overcharges, demand a better deal, and keep more of their hard-earned money."
- Families USA Executive Director, Anthony Wright, via press release: “Cleaner, more useable pricing data from insurers will help employers, researchers and other purchasers see what health care actually costs.”
- Save Our States Executive Director, Trent England, via The Center Square: “That it has taken this long to guarantee patients and employers actual prices is absurd…Fortunately, President Trump is standing strong for common-sense and putting the American people ahead of hospital and insurance executives and other insiders…With real price transparency, patients can plan ahead, find the best care at the best price, fight overcharging, and avoid price gouging and surprise bills…Employers can finally see the receipts and use real pricing data to negotiate better deals, lowering healthcare costs for employees and freeing up resources for higher wages, more jobs, and better returns for investors, including pensioners and retirees…All this is long overdue.”
- Andrew Bremberg, Former Director of the Domestic Policy Council via The Center Square: “…[R]equiring insurance executives to attest that their machine-readable files are true, accurate, and complete will unleash actual transparency and accountability… These commonsense reforms are a testament to President Trump's commitment to 'maximum transparency' and shifting the power from the big business of healthcare to the American people.”
Media & Influencers:

PLANO, Texas – The Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative was established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States.

In the Eastern District of Texas, five defendants were sentenced to a total of 1,105 months in federal prison during the month of September as part of the Homeland Security Task Force, announced U.S. Attorney Jay R. Combs. Additionally, two Chinese nationals were arrested, and another four defendants were extradited from Guatemala to the United States to face drug trafficking violations in the Eastern District of Texas.

On September 2, 2026, Jose Luis Gonzalez, Jr. , 24, of Dallas, was sentenced to 108 months in federal prison for trafficking at least 50 kilograms of cocaine from Mexico to the United States for further distribution.

On September 2, 2026, a Beaumont man was sentenced to 40 years in federal prison for drug trafficking violations in the Eastern District of Texas. Darrell Joshua Bendy , 42, was convicted at trial of trafficking between 20-30 kilograms of methamphetamine in the Eastern District of Texas.

On September 9, 2026, U.S. Attorney Jay R. Combs announced the arrests in China of Lisa Xing, 36, and Zhanwen Song, 38 , Chinese citizens. Xing and Song were named in a six-count superseding indictment returned by a federal grand jury in the Eastern District of Texas, charging them with drug trafficking and money laundering violations. If convicted they face between 10 years and life in federal prison. It is important to note that a federal indictment is not evidence of guilt, and all defendants are considered innocent until proven guilty.

On September 15, 2026, 53-year-old Mozambican, Norolamin Gulam was sentenced to 135 months in federal prison and ordered to pay a money judgment in the amount of $7.5 million for conspiracy to commit money laundering. Gulam was identified as the leader of a transnational money laundering organization with connections and ties throughout Europe, Africa, Southeast Asia, the United States, and Central and South America. Gulam used multiple businesses and real estate ventures to launder multi-million dollar amounts of drug proceeds. It is believed Gulam was responsible for laundering a minimum of $500 million in U.S. currency.

On September 17, 2026, Pamela Esquivias , 25, of Maricopa, Arizona, was sentenced to 262 months in federal prison, while Aaron Jay Perez, 29, of Dallas, received 120 months in federal prison. The two were charged with federal drug trafficking violations as the result of an investigation into the overdose death of a 16-year-old girl in Flower Mound.

On September 24, 2026, U.S. Attorney Jay R. Combs returned from an unprecedented visit to Guatemala where he was part of a Department of Justice delegation that met with the President of Guatemala, their Attorney General, and Secretary of the Interior. Following the meetings, U.S. Attorney Combs boarded a DEA prisoner transport plane and accompanied four indicted individuals from Guatemala to the United States, including Juan Carlos Cruz Ovalle. Ovalle was indicted in 2018 and is alleged to have trafficked multi-ton quantities of cocaine from Guatemala for distribution to the United States. It is important to note that a federal indictment is not evidence of guilt, and all defendants are considered innocent until proven guilty.

HSTF Dallas comprises agents and officers from the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Dallas Field Office; U.S. Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Homeland Security Investigations - Dallas (ICE-HSI); Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Dallas Field Division; Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) Dallas Field Division; Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigations (IRS-CD; United States Postal Service, United States Postal Inspection Service (USPIS); Transportation Security Administration, Federal Air Marshal Service (FAMS); United States Secret Service (USSS); Department of State, Bureau of Diplomatic Security (DSS); TEXOMA HIDTA; and U.S. Marshals Service (USMS) Eastern District of Texas. HSTF Houston comprises agents and officers from the FBI; U.S. Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Homeland Security Investigations - Houston (ICE-HSI); Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA); Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF); Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigations (IRS-CI); and U.S. Marshals Service (USMS) Eastern District of Texas; Texas Department of Public Safety; Jefferson County Sheriff’s Office; Beaumont Police Department; Port Neches Police Department; Harris County Sheriff’s Office; Vidor Police Department; and the Orange County Sheriff’s Office.

For more information about the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Texas, please visit: https://www.justice.gov/usao-edtx .

EPA to host Open House on Final Design Plans for New Rail Spurs on October 21, 2026
BOSTON, MASS. (Oct. 6, 2026) – U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) will host an Open House on October 21, 2026 from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. at the Berkshire Scenic Rail Museum located at 10 Willow Creek Road in Lenox, Massachusetts. EPA and General Electric (GE) will provide the public with information and answer questions about the Final Design Plan for the new Rail Loading Areas on the Site. The spurs will be located off Utility Drive in Pittsfield, and the other is adjacent to Woods Pond in Lenox.
"Local, state, and Tribal partners have all reviewed and contributed feedback that shaped this final plan," said EPA New England Regional Administrator Mark Sanborn. "Residents' perspectives are essential as we move forward together to restore clean water and healthy soil across the Berkshire community."
On September 21st, 2026, GE submitted the Final Design Plan for Rail Transload Areas in Reaches 5 and 6 (Revised Baseline Restoration Report, Cultural Resource Survey Addendum and Transmittal Letter Attached) (pdf) to EPA for review and approval.
EPA is requesting public input on this document be sent to R1Housatonic@epa.gov by Friday, November 6th, 2026.
For more information about the Plans and site, please visit: https://www.epa.gov/ge-housatonic.
