RELEASE: Rep. Friedman Leads Los Angeles Delegation and Entertainment Unions in Push for National Film Tax Credit
Bipartisan Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act brings production jobs back to the U.S.
Levels international playing field against 65 countries that offer incentives America does not match
Above: Friedman and entertainment union members rally for the national film tax credit.
GLENDALE, CA – Today, October 6, 2026, U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) led Members of the Los Angeles congressional delegation, and the major unions representing film and television workers at the Alex Theatre in a new push for the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act. This bipartisan legislation creates a national film tax credit on qualified labor expenses to bring production jobs back home.
A recording of the rally can be found here and here.
For decades, the United States has offered no national filming incentive, leaving American crews to compete against roughly 65 countries that do. The result has been hundreds of thousands of lost jobs for the drivers, grips, electricians, carpenters, caterers, and crew members.
WHAT THE BILL DOES:
- A 20% credit on American labor expenses. Feature films, television pilots, and television seasons that cost more than $1 million qualify if at least 75% of their principal photography days happen in the United States.
- Bonus credits that reward hiring where it is needed most. Productions can earn an additional 5% each, up to a 30% total credit, for shooting at least 30% of their days in a rural opportunity zone or a federally declared disaster area, for independent productions, for spending at least $10 million in qualified wages across 10 or more states, and for increasing domestic production relative to what a company shoots abroad.
- Includes post-production and visual effects work. Domestic post-production and VFX qualify as long as at least 75% of those costs are incurred in the United States, with the same 5% bonuses available.
- Usable by independent producers, not just major studios. The credit is transferable, meaning a producer who doesn't owe enough in federal taxes to use it can sell it to a company that does and get the cash up front.
- Takes effect quickly. The credit applies to productions that begin in taxable years starting after December 31, 2026.
- A one-pager with more details can be found here.
“When a production leaves this country, the stars still work. The crew is who gets left behind,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30). “65 countries offer incentives we don’t match, and no single state can outbid a foreign government on its own. Our bipartisan bill is built on labor costs, which means it only pays off when American workers get hired. These are good paying union jobs with benefits and pensions, and I won’t stop fighting until they come home.”
“You won’t see the carpenters, electricians and camera crews on screen, but they are the backbone of the film industry,” said Congresswoman Linda T. Sánchez (CA-38). “Many live in my district and have watched their jobs move overseas as other countries use incentives to lure production away. Our bipartisan bill will level the playing field to bring good-paying union jobs back to Southern California and keep them here.”
"Southern California has been the heart of America’s film and television industry, but today, too many productions are leaving the United States for countries offering better incentives," said Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28). "That’s why I’m proud to co-lead the bipartisan Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, which would provide a long-overdue federal tax credit to incentivize production here in the United States. Our creative workforce is the backbone of this industry. It's time we must invest in them and bring American film and television production back home.”
“Movie magic is central to the California story, and we need to keep it that way,” said Rep. Pete Aguilar (CA-33). “Our state is losing good-paying, union jobs because filming in this country has become far too expensive. The bipartisan Motion Picture, Television and Entertainment Revitalization Act will bring jobs back to America, boost wages for workers and keep productions at home.”
“California is the heart of film and television production, in large part because of the workers and technicians who bring the magic to life,” said Representative Tran (CA-45). “Yet the U.S. is rapidly losing jobs in this industry to competitors overseas. When productions relocate outside the U.S., it’s the American-based crews that suffer the most. California’s workforce deserves better. This bill incentivizes American-based productions, strengthens California’s production workforce, and brings jobs back to the U.S.—where they belong.”
“Southern California is the birthplace of the modern film and television industry. From the movies and television shows that have entertained audiences around the world to the hardworking people behind them, this industry is a vital part of our community and economy,” said Congressman Lieu (CA-36). “We can’t let the United States’ film industry lose ground to foreign competitors. I am pleased to be an original co-sponsor of the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act. It’s time to strengthen our domestic film industry and protect American jobs.”
“American performers and entertainment workers should not have to leave the country to find work in an industry that was built here. Film and television are more than entertainment — they are a major American industry that supports hundreds of thousands of good-paying union jobs and generates significant economic activity in communities across the country. For decades, foreign governments have recognized the economic value of production and successfully used incentives to attract these jobs overseas. States across the country have shown what targeted incentives can do to attract and retain production, and a federal incentive would build on those efforts and give the United States a stronger tool to compete. The Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act is an investment in American workers, American industry and American communities. SAG-AFTRA is proud to stand with Congresswoman Friedman and our labor partners in support of this important legislation,” said SAG-AFTRA National Executive Director and Chief Negotiator Duncan Crabtree-Ireland.
“The Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act will benefit entertainment industry workers, as well as the supporting businesses and local economies that rely on a robust domestic entertainment industry. Lawmakers have an opportunity to invest in an important American industry and preserve middle-class jobs, by passing the first-ever federal film and television tax incentive program,” said WGAW Secretary-Treasurer Peter Murrieta.
"Let’s not overthink this. The world is a complicated place, but this legislation is a no-brainer. It's going to get people back to work, and everyone just wants an opportunity to work in the industry they love in this country. Everyone will benefit from this – Republicans, Democrats, workers, audiences -- because our industry touches everyone," said Mike Farah, an Emmy-winning producer and a President of the Producers Guild of America.
“I’ve worked aggressively with labor and entertainment industry leaders, and together we've already expanded state-level tax incentives and reduced filming fees locally. A federal tax credit is critical so our local incentives remain competitive with countries that offer larger benefits and have drawn productions out of the United States,” said Mayor Bass. “I want to thank the bipartisan leadership of Representatives Laura Friedman, Brian Jack, Linda Sánchez, and Nathaniel Moran and Senators Adam Schiff and Tim Scott for understanding the importance of investing in an industry that is so critical to Los Angeles and the country. As a former Member of Congress, I'll continue leveraging my relationships in Washington to ensure this bill is passed into law.”
U.S. Representative Laura Friedman (CA-30) was joined by Senator Adam Schiff (CA), U.S. Representatives Linda Sánchez (CA-38), Maxine Waters (CA-43), Judy Chu (CA-28), Pete Aguilar (CA-33), Ted Lieu (CA-36), David Min (CA-47), and Derek Tran (CA-45), Glendale Mayor Ardy Kassakhian, IATSE International Vice President and Director of the Motion Picture and Television Department Mike Miller, SAG-AFTRA National Executive Director and Chief Negotiator Duncan Crabtree-Ireland, WGAW Secretary-Treasurer Peter Murrieta, DGA Associate National Executive Director and Western Executive Director Rebecca Rhine, Teamsters At-Large Vice President and Motion Picture Division Director Lindsay Dougherty, LiUNA Business Manager Alex Aguilar, Jr., and producer and three-time Emmy winner Mike Farah.
Below: Friedman and entertainment union members rally for the national film tax credit.

LAREDO, Texas – A 44-year-old man has pleaded guilty to perjury.

Jose Alfredo Zapata admitted he lied to law enforcement and multiple judges during his previous prosecution for smuggling illegal aliens.

On Sept. 3, 2022, Zapata drove a blue Ford Expedition hauling a trailer to a U.S. Border Patrol checkpoint in Laredo. He identified himself as E.S. and claimed to be a U.S. citizen traveling home to San Antonio.

Following a K-9 alert, authorities discovered 19 illegal aliens concealed in a compartment near the top of the trailer.

Zapata admitted to smuggling the illegal aliens and stated he expected to be paid $2,000 to transport the trailer to San Antonio.

Two of the illegal aliens admitted they had paid a human smuggling organization to transport them into the United States.

Between Sept. 6, 2022 and Jan. 18, 2023, Zapata repeatedly identified himself as E.S. and provided that individual’s identifying information during court proceedings and the investigation. The false information included the victim’s date of birth, address, driver’s license number, and Social Security number.

U.S. Magistrate Judge Diana Song Quiroga accepted the plea and set sentencing for December 29, 2026. At that time, Zapata faces up to five years in federal prison and a possible $250,000 maximum fine.

Zapata has been and will remain in custody pending sentencing.

FBI Laredo conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Anthony Franklyn is prosecuting the case.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigrants, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations, and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.
title: San Antonio human smuggler admits lying about identity during federal prosecution

This press release has been updated to more accurately report the sex of the school shooter in Tumbler Ridge.

Seattle – A 30-year-old Bellingham, Washington resident, James Cody Bryant, was arrested today on a criminal complaint charging conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country for Bryant’s role in a February 10, 2026, school shooting in British Columbia, Canada. Bryant was in frequent communication with school shooter Jesse Van Rootselaar in the six months leading up to the school shooting that killed six people and seriously injured others. The criminal complaint details several different ways Bryant encouraged and aided Van Rootselaar’s plan including agreeing to broadcast the attack.

“The Tumbler Ridge Secondary School shooting was a horrific tragedy for that small community and for all of Canada. Indeed, here in the Pacific Northwest we felt the pain of those families devastated by this violence,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Neil Floyd. “It is even more profoundly disturbing to learn that a resident of Western Washington had a role in the attack and took steps – providing counsel, technical advice, and money to the shooter planning such a tragedy.”

“On behalf of the FBI, I want to express heartfelt sympathy for the victims of this tragedy and their loved ones,” said W. Mike Herrington, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI Seattle field office. “No investigation can undo the fear and suffering caused by the horrific events of this February or bring these individuals back to their families, school, or community. We mourn with you. We hope the charge announced today demonstrates our commitment to pursue justice for the victims who lost their lives, or were injured, in this shocking act of violence. As part of that commitment, FBI Seattle remains dedicated to working with our law enforcement partners to hold this conspirator accountable for assisting in this terrible affair.”

“We remain mindful that no investigative milestone can undo the harm caused that day, but we hope it reflects our ongoing commitment to seeking answers and pursuing all available evidence,” says Assistant Commissioner Elija Rain, Acting Commanding Officer, BC RCMP. “I would like to thank the FBI Seattle and the United States Attorney's Office for the Western District of Washington for their partnership, professionalism, and commitment throughout this complex investigation. Their cooperation and expertise have been invaluable in advancing the work across jurisdictions and ensuring that all available evidence could be thoroughly examined.”

According to the RCMP Van Rootselaar was a male. Van Rootselaar had been transitioning and identified as female on official government identification and on law enforcement reports.

On February 10, 2026, Jesse Van Rootselaar killed two relatives and then drove to the Tumbler Ridge Secondary School where Van Rootselaar shot and killed five children ages 12 and 13 and killed an educational assistant. Van Rootselaar used an improvised explosive device to damage the school and tried to get into other classrooms by firing through locked doors. Van Rootselaar exchanged gunfire with police and ultimately committed suicide.

Shortly after the shooting, law enforcement learned Van Rootselaar had been in frequent communication with someone via the platform Discord. That person was identified as Bryant. According to the criminal complaint, Bryant and Van Rootselaar began communicating over Discord no later than August 2025, about Van Rootselaar’s plan to kill multiple people in a shooting in Canada. Numerous conversations between Bryant and Van Rootselaar are detailed in the criminal complaint. During these conversations, Bryant allegedly agreed to assist Van Rootselaar in a variety of ways: Bryant agreed to record and broadcast Van Rootselaar’s live stream of the murders; on multiple occasions, Bryant assisted Van Rootselaar in testing the livestreaming equipment to ensure it was functioning and would provide a viewable image of the planned killings; Bryant provided tactical advice on how to increase the carnage and what firearms to use; Bryant sent money to Van Rootselaar to purchase various items the shooter wanted in connection with the school attack, including a lighter that would be used to construct an explosive device detonated during the attack; mere moments before the shooting, Bryant confirmed that Bryant was receiving the livestream; and at various times Bryant advised Van Rootselaar about keeping the murder plot secret by deleting their messages and using Virtual Private Networks (VPN) for streaming the video of the shooting.

At various times leading up to the attack, Bryant assured Van Rootselaar that Bryant would not turn the shooter in to law enforcement and would be there to handle the live streaming. In various conversations between August and the February shooting, Bryant tried to talk Van Rootselaar out of doing the attack. But ultimately, Bryant did not contact law enforcement and agreed to handle the live streaming just minutes before the attack. Even after Van Rootselaar had killed two family members, there was time to intervene before the school shooting. Van Rootselaar could not get the family car started to head to the school. Bryant gave advice about how to get the engine to turn over, allowing the shooter to put the school shooting plan in motion.

Conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country is punishable by up to life in prison.

The charges contained in the criminal complaint are only allegations. A person is presumed innocent unless and until he or she is proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

The case was investigated by the FBI with assistance from Homeland Security Investigations and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP).

The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Todd Greenberg with assistance from the Justice Department’s National Security Division.
title: Bellingham resident charged with conspiring to commit murder in connection with school shooting in Tumbler Ridge, B.C.

Rep. Crockett Investigates Police Use of Force Against Students in Texas Schools
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Jasmine Crockett (TX-30) sent a letter to Governor Greg Abbott, Attorney General Ken Paxton, and Education Commissioner Mike Morath demanding answers and accountability over the use of excessive force against children in Texas public schools.
“Texas is failing our kids. Our children deserve to go to school in an environment that fosters learning and growth, not environments where ordinary student behavior can end with a child in handcuffs, hogtied, shocked with a Taser, or pepper-sprayed.”
Crockett expressed concern regarding the expansive presence of police in school, putting Texas students in unnecessary contact with the criminal system, further opening the door to the school-to-prison pipeline.
In her letter, Crockett highlights how officers using excessive force to respond to student behavior could ordinarily be addressed through school discipline. The letter cites a New York Times investigation documenting more than 2,600 school-based use-of-force incidents across Texas from January 2022 through December 2025.
Crockett is demanding answers regarding police involvement in routine student discipline, incident reporting, accountability for police misconduct, and potential changes to state law training.
“The number of “incidents” is alarming. Our kiddos should not be treated like criminals. They are the future of this country, and we owe it to them to protect them from cruel and abusive behavior. I am urging our Texas leaders to exercise immediate oversight and ensure accountability for these horrific reported actions. This is unacceptable, and it has to stop.”
The full letter can be found here.
title: Rep. Crockett Investigates Police Use of Force Against Students in Texas Schools

Memphis, TN – Edmund Ford, Jr. , 47 , was sentenced to 24 months’ imprisonment today for evading taxes in 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, and 2022. The unreported income was derived from grant funds awarded to non-profits by the Shelby County Commission. United States Attorney D. Michael Dunavant, of the Western District of Tennessee, announced the sentence today.

According to court documents and in-court statements, while serving as a Shelby County Commissioner, Ford failed to declare $310,743 in gross income to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) during tax years 2018 to 2022, causing losses to the IRS in the amount of $110,604. The source of Ford’s unreported income was non-profit organizations which had received grants from the Shelby County Commission.

In many cases, Ford sponsored the grants and voted in favor of awarding the grants to the grantees that would in turn use a portion of the grant funds to purchase computer equipment from a business Ford controlled called E&J Computer Services and Repair. After a Commercial Appeal article in 2021 calling attention to one such grant arrangement, Ford began using more sophisticated means to disguise grant-related income including intermediary accounts and the use of cash. Ford was confronted by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and IRS-Criminal Investigation in May 2023, where he falsely minimized his involvement in E&J Computer Services and Repair.

On February 2, 2026, Ford pled guilty to five counts of tax evasion, a violation of 26 U.S.C. § 7201. Ford served as a Shelby County Commissioner beginning in 2018 and continuing until his guilty plea in this case. As part of the plea agreement, Ford resigned his position from the Shelby County Commission and agreed that by function of State law, he would be forever disqualified from seeking or holding any public office in the State of Tennessee or any political subdivision.

On October 6, 2026, District Judge Thomas L. Parker sentenced Ford to 24 months in prison, followed by two years of supervised release. There is no parole in the federal system. The Court will provide an order of restitution at a later date.

While pronouncing the sentence today, the Court underscored that the source of the undeclared income was Ford’s “corrupt” conduct involving the administration of County grants. The Court further emphasized that the funds that Ford failed to report as income and pay tax on were public funds derived from tax revenues others had paid. The Court also applied a sentencing enhancement for over $10,000 in income derived from criminal conduct related to the illegal structuring of payments from grantees to Ford. As part of the sentencing hearing, the Court reviewed approximately 52 letters of support for Ford and expressed frustration with multiple letters written by current elected officials on Shelby County or City of Memphis official letterhead.

U.S. Attorney Dunavant said, “Ford used his elected public office to unjustly enrich himself at the expense of taxpayers and then doubled down on the dishonesty by intentionally defrauding the IRS. These are indeed bold and arrogant actions that have no place in public service, and which have rightly earned him a prison sentence as just punishment. Ford clearly had the ability and intention to brazenly continue the same criminal conduct in the future, and this successful federal prosecution and sentence has now ensured that he will be held accountable and permanently removed from public service.”

“Bribery and tax evasion undermine the fairness and transparency our communities depend on,” said Special Agent in Charge Donald “Trey” Eakins, IRS Criminal Investigation’s Charlotte Field Office. “Today’s sentence shows our commitment to ensuring no one is above the law. We will continue to work with our law enforcement partners and the U.S. Attorney’s Office to stop public corruption and deception in our communities.”

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and IRS-Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI) investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Lynn Crum and Scott Smith prosecuted this case on behalf of the government.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

###

For more information, please contact our Media Relations Team at USATNW.Media@usdoj.gov . Follow the U.S. Attorney’s Office on Facebook or on X at @WDTNNews for office news and updates
title: Former Shelby County Commissioner Edmund Ford, Jr. Sentenced to Two Years in Prison for Tax Evasion

Connecticut Congressional Delegation and Governor Lamont Announce Disaster Declaration from U.S. Small Business Administration for Homeowners, Renters, and Businesses Impacted by September Flooding
Declaration Enables Impacted Individuals, Families, Businesses, and Nonprofits to Apply for Low-Interest Loans to Aid in Their Recovery
Hartford, CT – Today, members of the Connecticut Congressional delegation joined Governor Ned Lamont to announce a disaster declaration from the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) for Fairfield County and the contiguous counties of New Haven County and Litchfield County in response to the flash flooding event that impacted the region on September 13, 2026. The approved declaration means that homeowners, renters, businesses, and nonprofits in the impacted counties can apply for low-interest loans from the SBA to aid in their recovery.
“This declaration makes low-interest loans available to homeowners, renters, businesses, and nonprofits so they can recover and rebound from these flash floods,” Governor Lamont said. “I am glad that we’ve been able to secure this funding and encourage anyone who was impacted by this storm to look into this assistance and determine whether it can help you in the recovery process.”
“As communities continue to recover from severe flooding that hit our state last month, I am glad that the Small Business Administration granted our request for a disaster declaration," said Congressman John B. Larson. "This declaration is a crucial step forward, so small businesses, local organizations, and homeowners can get the help they need to repair and rebuild after incurring damage—including in Litchfield County. Our delegation will keep working with the governor and state leaders to ensure the federal government is responsive to the towns and cities that were impacted by this storm.”
“This disaster declaration is a strong step toward bringing federal aid to Connecticut following severe floods last month. This step allows Connecticut state agencies to work with federal partners like the SBA to continue recovery efforts and potentially unlock more federal assistance to rebuild local businesses. I am grateful to the SBA for their swift response to Governor Lamont and our delegation’s request,” said Senator Richard Blumenthal.
“Connecticut communities were hit hard on September 13 by sudden and intense flooding. I encourage all small business owners in the counties covered by this disaster declaration to take advantage of the available assistance from the Small Business Administration,” said Congressman Joe Courtney.
“Extreme weather events like flash flooding are damaging our communities more often and more unexpectedly. I am glad that federal support is on its way through this SBA disaster declaration for the businesses, residents, and communities that were impacted by devastating flash floods last month. I will continue to fight for federal resources so that Connecticut has the support necessary rebuild after disasters like this one,” said Congresswoman Rosa DeLauro.
“I’m glad the federal government is stepping up to assist Connecticut residents and businesses, especially those in Fairfield County, in recovering from last month’s flooding. I encourage anyone whose residence or business was impacted by the severe weather to look into these resources. I will continue fighting alongside the rest of Connecticut’s Congressional delegation to bring home the federal support our constituents need to rebound,” said Congressman Jim Himes.
“Extreme weather continues to impact our state. I am pleased to see the U.S. Small Business Administration approve federal assistance for parts of the Fifth District and our state. These federal resources will help alleviate the financial losses of business leaders and homeowners from the recent flooding,” said Congresswoman Jahana Hayes.
The following groups may be eligible for low-interest SBA disaster loans:
- Homeowners: Up to $500,000 to repair their primary residence.
- Homeowners and renters: Up to $100,000 to repair or replace damaged or destroyed personal property.
- Business owners: Up to $2,000,000 for the replacement of real property, inventories, machinery, equipment, and other physical losses.
- Businesses and nonprofits: Economic Injury Disaster Loans of up to $2,000,000 to provide necessary working capital until normal operations resume after a disaster.
“We know there are people with uninsured losses. These low-interest SBA loans are a means for people to rebuild and recover from the flooding. Additionally, our Volunteer Organizations Active in Disaster—independent faith-based and nonprofit groups—remain engaged in helping people needing cleanup,” saidConnecticut Department of Emergency Services and Public Protection Commissioner Ronnell A. Higgins.
How to apply for low-interest SBA disaster loans
Under this declaration, the application deadline for physical damage loans is December 1, 2026, and the application deadline for economic injury loans is July 2, 2027.
Applications may be submitted to the SBA through the following methods:
- In-person: A temporary, in-person SBA Disaster Loan Outreach Center will open at the Margaret E. Morton Government Center at 999 Broad Street in Bridgeport beginning October 7, 2026.
  - It will operate Mondays through Fridays from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; Saturdays from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.; and it will be closed on Sundays.
  - Due to prior engagements, it will have adjusted hours of 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. on October 9, 2026; and 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on October 20 and 21, 2026.
  - It will be closed on October 12, 2026, due to the Columbus Day holiday.
  - It is expected to permanently close at 4:00 p.m. on October 21, 2026.
- Online: The MySBA Loan Portal at provides applicants with the ability submit applications online, view loan details, check balances, make payments, and access statements.
For further assistance, applicants can contact the SBA’s Customer Service Center by email at disastercustomerservice@sba.gov or by phone at 1-800-659-2955. For people who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability, dial 7-1-1 to access telecommunications relay services.

Jacksonville, FL – The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Florida has reached an agreement with Central Florida Pain Management (CFPM) to resolve allegations that the medical practice violated Title III of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) by failing to provide auxiliary aids and services to a patient with communication disabilities. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement.

“ADA enforcement is a significant feature of our district’s civil rights practice,” said U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe. “This settlement sends a firm message to our communities that disabled persons will be protected from practices that violate this important body of federal statutes.”

“ADA enforcement is a significant feature of our district’s civil rights practice,” said U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe. “This settlement sends a firm message to our communities that disabled persons will be protected from practices that violate this important body of federal statutes.”

The U.S. Attorney’s Office opened an investigation into CFPM after receiving a complaint from an individual who is legally blind (“Complainant”). The Complainant alleged that, on or about November 19, 2024, CFPM staff denied his request for assistance with completing medical history documentation on a digital tablet when he came for his new patient appointment. The Complainant alleged that, without this assistance, he could not complete the documentation before the appointment, which CFPM required him to do. Further, the Complainant alleged that because he was unable to complete the documentation, CFPM prohibited him from attending his new patient appointment, as scheduled, and required him to reschedule his appointment. As a result of CFPM’s failure to provide auxiliary aids and services, the Complainant was denied the opportunity to access CFPM’s health care services.

Title III of the ADA requires public accommodations, including professional offices of health care providers, to take such steps as may be necessary to ensure that no individual with a disability is excluded, denied services, segregated, or otherwise treated differently than other individuals because of the absence of auxiliary aids and services. Under the terms of the settlement agreement, CFPM must: adopt a written effective communication policy that specifies its office’s obligations to provide auxiliary aids and services pursuant to Title III of the ADA; implement effective communication training for all employees regarding their obligations to provide auxiliary aids and services pursuant to Title III of the ADA; maintain a log documenting all requests CFPM receives for auxiliary aids and services, as well as how it handled those requests; report any complaints received alleging CFPM violated Title III of the ADA to the United States; and pay the Complainant $2,000 in compensatory damages.

Assistant United States Attorney Mai Tran represented the United States in this case.

For more information on the ADA, visit www.ada.gov or call the Department of Justice’s toll-free ADA Information Line at (800) 514-0301 (Voice) or (833) 610-1264 (TTY). Accessibility specialists are available to answer questions from individuals, businesses, and state or local governments. All calls are confidential.

Individuals who believe they may have been victims of discrimination may contact the Civil Rights Unit of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Florida by calling our Civil Rights Hotline at (813) 274-6095 or emailing us at USAFLM.Civil.Rights@usdoj.gov . To fill out our civil rights complaint form, please visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-mdfl/civil-rights-complaint-form .
title: Settlement Agreement Reached with Central Florida Pain Management to Improve Services to Patients with Communication Disabilities

“The Grande Arbor” Manufactured Home by Cavco Homes and UMH Properties
CALIFORNIA - U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) spotlighted multiple housing innovations and resources from the West Coast during the sixth annual Innovative Housing Showcase, held September 22-24 on the National Mall. This year’s theme, “Made in America,” highlighted American ingenuity and innovative approaches to expanding housing affordability and homeownership.

HUD’s “Made in America” Showcase spotlighted American builders, manufacturers, and innovators’ modern technologies and creative housing solutions that are expanding housing supply, lowering construction costs, and putting affordable homeownership back in reach for hardworking Americans. The Showcase featured a variety of full-scale housing models including manufactured, 3D printed, and modular homes built by American companies from across the nation.
Examples from the West Coast Region
A fully furnished, enterable tiny home, manufactured using Azure Printed Home's (California) proprietary factory-based 3D printing technology and advanced modular construction.

CHICAGO — A felon has been sentenced to 15 years in federal prison for illegally possessing a handgun and using it to fatally shoot a man in Chicago.

LEVION THOMAS illegally possessed the handgun on March 20, 2023, when he sold it to an undercover law enforcement officer. As a previously convicted felon, Thomas was prohibited by federal law from possessing a firearm.

Two weeks earlier, Thomas used the same gun to fatally shoot Troy Pouncey in the 7100 block of South Calumet Avenue in Chicago. The fatal shooting occurred in the afternoon next to a children’s playground in nearby William Meyering Park.

Thomas, 31, of Chicago, pleaded guilty in 2024 to a federal charge of illegal firearm possession. On Oct. 1, 2026, U.S. District Judge Thomas M. Durkin sentenced Thomas to 15 years in federal prison.

The sentence was announced by Andrew S. Boutros, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois; Christopher Amon, Special Agent in Charge of the Chicago Division of the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives; and Fred Waller, Interim Superintendent of the Chicago Police Department.

“Thomas’s gun possession and sale were serious, but this case presents unique aggravating circumstances because Thomas used the firearm that he sold to murder someone,” Assistant U.S. Attorneys Julia K. Schwartz and Jessica R. Ecker argued in the government’s sentencing memorandum. “Too many people in this city believe that they can unlawfully possess firearms with impunity. This needs to stop.”

“The defendant knew he was prohibited from possessing a firearm, yet chose to arm himself and use that firearm to take another person’s life," said ATF SAC Amon. "Through the National Integrated Ballistic Information Network (NIBIN), agents were able to connect the firearm recovered from the defendant to a murder committed two weeks earlier, providing a critical link in the investigation. The statutory maximum 15-year federal prison sentence imposed in this case reflects the seriousness of the defendant’s actions and the consequences of illegally possessing a firearm as a convicted felon. ATF will continue to work with our law enforcement partners to aggressively investigate offenders who illegally possess firearms and use them to threaten the safety of our communities.”
title: Felon Sentenced to 15 Years in Federal Prison for Illegally Possessing Handgun and Using It To Fatally Shoot Man in Chicago

DALLAS — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced that a Mexican citizen was sentenced to 480 months in federal prison for his role in a methamphetamine trafficking conspiracy involving nearly four kilograms of high‑purity methamphetamine.

Luis Manuel Abarca‑Torres, a.k.a. “Güero Menso,” pleaded guilty to conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute and to distribute 50 grams or more of methamphetamine on July 29, 2025. Judge Brantley Starr imposed the decades long sentence on Sept. 30.

“Four kilograms of nearly pure methamphetamine poised for distribution is not just a drug transaction, it’s a direct threat to every family in North Texas,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “This defendant helped funnel extraordinarily dangerous narcotics into our community, and thanks to the relentless work of our Homeland Security Task Force that pipeline is now shut down. This 40‑year sentence sends a clear message: traffickers who target North Texas will face severe consequences.”

“Four kilograms of nearly pure methamphetamine poised for distribution is not just a drug transaction, it’s a direct threat to every family in North Texas,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “This defendant helped funnel extraordinarily dangerous narcotics into our community, and thanks to the relentless work of our Homeland Security Task Force that pipeline is now shut down. This 40‑year sentence sends a clear message: traffickers who target North Texas will face severe consequences.”

“This sentence sends a message to drug traffickers who poison our communities with dangerous drugs and line the pockets of criminal organizations,” said Joseph B. Tucker, Special Agent in Charge of the DEA Dallas Field Division. “This sentence of 480 months will hold Mr. Torres accountable for the poison that found its way into our neighborhoods by his hand. No amount of drugs is acceptable in our neighborhoods, and those that are responsible for the distribution of poison in the form of drugs in our communities will face justice sooner or later. The DEA will never cease its efforts to rid these drugs from the streets of North Texas.”

Courtroom filings reveal that between June 21, 2022, and June 30, 2022, Torres arranged to supply an undercover officer four kilograms of methamphetamine in exchange for $10,000 U.S. Dollars. During this time frame, Torres told the undercover officer that a Dallas based distributor would contact the undercover officer and tell the undercover officer that they were calling on Torres’ behalf by identifying Torres as “Guero.”

Co-defendant Adriana Melendez Calvillo met the undercover officer at a McDonald’s located at 7305 Airport Freeway, in Richland Hills, Texas and delivered 3.953 kilograms of methamphetamine to the undercover officer. The methamphetamine had a purity of 97%. Calvillo was sentenced on Nov. 20, 2024, to 480 months confinement on drug charges and 240 months confinement on money laundering charges.

Courtroom filings related to co-defendant Ignacio Manzo Cardenas, who was sentenced on Oct. 29, 2025, to a term of 440 months confinement on drug charges and 240 months confinement on money laundering charges, reveal that on Oct. 25, 2022, agents conducted a search at an address located in Reno, Texas. During the search agents located over 24 kilograms of crystalized methamphetamine. The methamphetamine had a purity of 99%. The search also revealed evidence of a methamphetamine conversion lab with different amounts of methamphetamine being located in liquid and crystalized form.

The search also revealed multiple drug ledgers that showed hundreds of kilograms of methamphetamine had been received and disbursed from the location. Those same ledgers also contained evidence regarding money deliveries.

Courtroom testimony from Melendez’s sentencing hearing revealed shipments of drugs and proceeds in this case are linked to the Cártel de Jalisco Nueva Generación. On Feb. 20, 2025, the U.S. Department of State designated the CJNG, which has contacts across the Americas, Australia, China, and Southeast Asia, as a Foreign Terrorist Organization. The CJNG has previously attacked the Mexican military and police with military grade weaponry, the use of drones to drop explosives on Mexican law enforcement and assassinations or attempted assassinations of Mexican officials.

Abarca-Torres is the 12th defendant sentenced in this investigation that involved a total of 13 defendants in two separate cases. All told, Abarca-Torres was held accountable for 396,769 kilograms (calculated as converted drug weight) for trafficking methamphetamine and heroin. One defendant remains unapprehended.

The following defendants have been previously sentenced in this case:

Adriana Melendez Calvillo was sentenced to a term of 480 months imprisonment for conspiring to possess with intent to distribute methamphetamine and 240 months imprisonment on money laundering

Ignacio Manzo Cardenas was sentenced to a term of 440 months confinement for conspiring to possess with intent to distribute methamphetamine and 240 months confinement for laundering of monetary instruments with individuals

Omar Gilliam was sentenced to a term of 270 months confinement for conspiring to possess with intent to distribute methamphetamine

David Garcia was sentenced to 121 months imprisonment for conspiring to possess with intent to distribute methamphetamine

Fatima Garcia was sentenced to a term of 108 months imprisonment for conspiring to possess with intent to distribute methamphetamine and money laundering charges

Juan Pablo Guerra was sentenced to a term of 62 months imprisonment for conspiring to possess with intent to distribute 100 grams or more of heroin

Gerardo Campos Garcia was sentenced to a term of 27 months imprisonment for conspiring to launder monetary instruments; and

Hilario Zamago was sentenced to a probation term of one year for using a communication facility to facilitate a drug felony.

As part of Torres’ agreement to plead guilty in this case, the Government agreed to dismiss charges in case number 3:23-CR-177-N. In that case the following sentences have been pronounced:

Oscar Alonso Dominguez Rodriguez was sentenced to 240-months confinement for possession of methamphetamine with intent to distribute

Guadalupe Ramirez was sentenced to 97-months confinement for Laundering Monetary Instruments

Franklin Jose Cruiz Arguijo was sentenced to 70-months confinement for conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute methamphetamine

The Drug Enforcement Administration, Dallas Division conducted the investigation with assistance from the IRS-Criminal Investigation, Texas Field Office. Assistant U.S. Attorneys George Leal, Joseph T. Lo Galbo and Abby Policastro prosecuted the case.

This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of U.S. law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Dallas comprises agents and officers from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Bureau of Alcohol, Firearms, Tobacco, and Explosives, Department of Homeland Security Investigations, United States Marshals Service, Internal Revenue Service, United States Postal Inspection Service, and United States Secret Service in partnership with the Texas Department of Public Safety, City of Dallas Police Department, the Dallas County Sheriff’s Office and other local law enforcement entities.

NEWARK, N.J. – Gerardo Aquino, 40, of Hollywood, Florida, pleaded guilty to accepting bribes and facilitating the laundering of more than $4.8 million to Colombia while employed by TD Bank, N.A., U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced.

Aquino, 40, pleaded guilty today before the Honorable Esther Salas in Newark to a two-count Information charging him with conspiring to launder monetary instruments and receipt of bribes by a bank employee. He is scheduled to be sentenced on March 23, 2027.

“The Criminal Division is at the vanguard of protecting the security of the U.S. financial system including against bank insiders,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Gerardo Aquino abused his position of trust at TD Bank and enriched himself in the process. Bank insiders who facilitate money laundering and illegal activity for criminal organizations play a critical role for that organization and abuse our financial system. When that happens, these insiders will be investigated and prosecuted.”

“From inside TD Bank, Aquino facilitated the laundering of millions of dollars in exchange for bribes. By enabling crime instead of preventing it, Aquino provided a soft entry point into our banking system for malevolent actors. The U.S. Attorney’s Office will continue to hold financial institutions and their employees accountable when they break the law and undermine the integrity of our financial system.” - U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer

“From inside TD Bank, Aquino facilitated the laundering of millions of dollars in exchange for bribes. By enabling crime instead of preventing it, Aquino provided a soft entry point into our banking system for malevolent actors. The U.S. Attorney’s Office will continue to hold financial institutions and their employees accountable when they break the law and undermine the integrity of our financial system.”

- U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer

“This guilty plea demonstrates that corrupt financial insiders are just as critical to criminal networks as those who move drugs or incite violence,” said Associate Chief of Operations Greg Millard of the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). “By exploiting his position at a financial institution, accepting bribes, and helping funnel millions of dollars to Colombia, Gerardo Aquino enabled the movement of illicit proceeds and undermined the integrity of the U.S. financial system. DEA and our partners will continue to identify, investigate, and hold accountable the facilitators who help transnational criminal organizations profit from their crimes.”

“The guilty plea in this case holds Mr. Aquino accountable for accepted bribes and abusing his trusted position at TD Bank to facilitate the laundering of millions of dollars out of the United States to Colombia,” said Special Agent in Charge Patricia Tarasca of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation Office of Inspector General (FDIC-OIG), New York Region. “The FDIC OIG is pleased to join our law enforcement partners in announcing today’s guilty plea, and we remain committed to investigating financial crimes that threaten to undermine the safety and soundness of our Nation’s financial system, including those crimes involving bank insiders.”

“Financial institutions and their employees serve as an important line of defense in protecting the integrity of our financial system,” said Jenifer L. Piovesan, Special Agent in Charge of IRS Criminal Investigation’s Newark Field Office. “When someone abuses that position of trust to facilitate money laundering and move millions of dollars in illicit proceeds, they undermine the very system they are entrusted to protect. IRS Criminal Investigation and our law enforcement partners will continue to follow the money, expose those who enable criminal activity, and hold financial facilitators accountable.”

According to documents filed in this case and statements made in Court:

Aquino accepted bribes and exploited his position as a bank employee to help launder illicit funds to Colombia. From April 2022 to November 2023, Aquino opened fraudulent accounts, issued hundreds of debit cards to co-conspirators, and unblocked debit cards that TD Bank had restricted due to potential fraud. The bank accounts and debit cards were then used to funnel approximately $4.8 million out of the United States. As part of this scheme, Aquino opened 86 individual customer accounts using the same exact commercial address in Miami. Those accounts alone were used to launder over $3 million in illicit funds to Colombia. In exchange, Aquino received more than $8,000 in bribes — paid in cash and through a peer-to-peer digital payment network.

The charge of money laundering conspiracy carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison and a fine of $500,000 or twice the amount involved in the offense, whichever is greater. The charge of receipt of bribes by a bank employee carries a maximum penalty of 30 years in prison and a fine of $1,000,000 or three times the amount involved in the offense, whichever is greater.

U.S. Attorney Frazer credited special agents and task force officers of the Internal Revenue Service-Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI), Newark Field Office, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Jenifer L. Piovesan, and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation-Office of Inspector General (FDIC-OIG), New York Region, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Patricia Tarasca, with the investigation. U.S. Attorney Frazer also thanked the Morristown Police Department for its assistance with the investigation.

This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of U.S. law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Marko Pesce, Deputy Chief of the Criminal Division for the District of New Jersey and Trial Attorneys D. Zachary Adams and Chelsea Rooney of the Bank Integrity Unit of the Criminal Division’s Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section are prosecuting the case.

The Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section's (MNF) mission is to take the profit out of crime, eliminate drug cartels, and protect the U.S. financial system. MNF pursues criminal prosecutions and criminal and civil asset recovery actions involving: financial facilitators who launder profits for criminals; financial institutions and their officers and employees whose actions threaten the U.S. financial system and financial institutions; international money launderers who support transnational organized crime; and the top command and control of international drug trafficking organizations.

MNF’s Bank Integrity Unit investigates and prosecutes banks and other financial institutions, including their officers, managers and employees whose actions threaten the integrity of the individual institution or the wider financial system.

Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Announces Five Actions to Accelerate Commercial Space Licensing
Proposed rules represent the USDOT SPACE Task Force’s first pillar to cut red tape & supercharge American space dominance
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy today announced that the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is proposing five rules to streamline and modernize the commercial space launch and reentry regulations. The rules were developed in concert with the recently launched the USDOT Space Policy Administration, Coordination, and Execution (SPACE) Task Force.
Key changes to the Part 450 commercial space licensing process include:
- Allowing operators to submit launch applications electronically
- Providing greater flexibility to demonstrate an equivalent level of safety
- Combining three required safety analyses into a single submission
- Eliminating duplicative safety analyses when a safety requirement is already addressed through other approved methods.
What we’re doing: The proposed rules would make the Part 450 licensing process more efficient, less burdensome, and more flexible for operators while maintaining the FAA’s safety standards.
Why it matters: Simplifying these critical rules will ensure American space operators can continue leading the world in commercial launch growth while maintaining the FAA’s highest safety standards. These actions also support President Trump’s space policy goals in his Enabling Competition in the Commercial Space Industry Executive Order and National Space Transportation Policy to enhance American greatness in space by enabling a competitive launch marketplace and substantially increasing commercial space launch cadence to 1,000 per year by 2030.
“We can’t unlock the final frontier if we let red tape hold American innovators back from leading the way,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “By making simple, common-sense changes to modernize the commercial licensing processes, we can strengthen the United States’ position as a powerhouse for commercial space transportation while maintaining the highest safety standards in the world.”
“The SPACE Task Force is moving quickly to execute on President Trump’s vision to achieve America’s continued superiority in space,” said U.S. Under Secretary for Transportation Ryan McCormack. “The commercial space industry is moving at lightning speed, and our regulations need to keep pace. I’m proud of the work the Task Force has already done to hit the ground running and create the conditions that will revolutionize America’s commercial space industry.”
“These proposed rules are just the beginning of the FAA’s effort to reduce unnecessary burdens on the U.S. commercial space industry,” said Acting Deputy FAA Administrator Liam McKenna. “These changes will give operators greater flexibility and make the licensing process more efficient, while ensuring the safety of the National Airspace System remains our top priority.”
Reminder:
The U.S. was responsible for 217 of the 329 commercial space launches worldwide in 2025 and we expect to see that number will soar to 10,000 FAA-licensed launches and reentries a year by 2035.

text:
Rep. Vasquez Urges Administration to Halt Rule Change Expanding Vehicle Access and Increasing Risks on Public Lands
The proposed revision of the 2005 Travel Management Rule poses serious risk to conservation and safety on public lands
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On October 6, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) sent a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Under Secretary Michael Boren and U.S. Forest Service (USFS) Chief Tom Schultz strongly opposing the Administration’s proposed rule expanding vehicle access to public lands and trails that are already facing maintenance backlogs. Vasquez was joined by 28 of his House and Senate colleagues in his call to keep the 2005 Travel Management Rule in place.
“New Mexicans deserve public lands that are safe and well-managed. Ending the long-established Travel Management Rule would put public safety at risk and open the door to damage that will take generations to undo,” said Vasquez. “Hikers, hunters, and ranchers alike shouldn’t have to worry about more folks driving through the spaces they use for recreation and grazing. Instead of opening more of our public lands to vehicle access in places where access already exists, the Forest Service should focus on maintaining existing trails and roads. This broad reversal is unnecessary."
The USFS and the Bureau of Land Management have separate but similar rules requiring our public land agencies to provide clear, consistent guidance for how public lands are used, including where motorized vehicles, including cars and ATVs, can travel. For those who enjoy our public lands, whether on foot or on wheels, these rules help keep trails open, accessible, and responsibly managed. They also require public input before designating routes, produce Motor Vehicle Use Maps that show visitors where they can go, give rangers clear standards to enforce, and allow exceptions for emergency, military, and law enforcement vehicles.
Changing the 2005 rule, as proposed by USDA, could endanger public safety, reduce quality access to our public lands, and degrade the quality of trails, lands and waters that support our nation’s wildlife and outdoor recreation economy.
The letter demands that any revisions to the 2005 Travel Management Rule preserve the following core principles:
- Maintain the current default of keeping routes and areas closed to motorized use unless expressly designated as open.
- Carry forward criteria that guide local land management decisions and protect critical public land values, including soil, watersheds, vegetation, and wildlife habitat, as well as reduce conflicts between public land uses such as camping, hiking, hunting, and grazing.
- Travel management decisions should continue to be informed by robust public engagement and local input.
- The agencies must retain the ability to protect fish and wildlife habitat, riparian areas, water quality, and cultural resources.
- The agencies should continue to clearly identify where motorized travel is permitted.
- The agencies should consider the long-term cost of properly maintaining, staffing, and administering their transportation system before adding new routes or expanding access.
“This is yet another egregious attack in the systematic dismantling of public lands management of our national forests,” said Paul Sanford, director for equitable access policy advocacy at The Wilderness Society. “Travel management provides the basic guardrails that let hikers, hunters, anglers, and riders share the same forest without chaos; removing those guardrails threatens the freedom of all public lands users to safely enjoy our national forests the way they choose. Paired with the proposed repeal of the Roadless Rule, this destructive agenda sells out future generations’ enjoyment of our forests in order to hand them over for corporate profits.”
“We’re grateful to see Congressional Leaders pushing back on federal agency proposals to gut travel management regulations and prioritize off-road vehicles at the expense of wildlife, cultural sites, desert waterways and other recreationists, proposals that will make visiting Utah’s canyon country worse for everyone,” said Laura Peterson, Senior Attorney at the Southern Utah Wilderness Alliance (SUWA). “The Trump Administration’s vision for public lands is not about balance or reasonable access, it is about blanketing landscapes with off-road vehicle routes, transforming quiet, wild places into motorized playgrounds.”
"We stand with Rep. Vasquez and his urgent request to keep the Travel Management Rule intact,” said Taylor Rush, government relations representative at Defenders of Wildlife. "For more than two decades, this rule has protected our cherished wildlife, outdoor recreationists, clean water supply and local communities from the harmful impacts of unmanaged motorized vehicle use. Weakening the framework used to reduce habitat damage and social conflict would result in dangerous degradation of our wild places and wildlife."

title: Rep. Vasquez Urges Administration to Halt Rule Change Expanding Vehicle Access and Increasing Risks on Public Lands

JACKSONVILLE, Fla. — U.S. Customs and Border Protection’s Air and Marine Operations marked the final operational flight of its last P-3 Airborne Early Warning aircraft Sept. 30, 2026, at the National Air Security Operations Center in Jacksonville.
For decades, Jacksonville-based P-3 AEW aircraft supported the nation’s border security mission by conducting wide-area aerial surveillance over the Caribbean, the Gulf of America and transit zones across Central and South America.
Known by flight crews as the “Dome,” the P-3 AEW paired the long-range capabilities of the Lockheed P-3 aircraft with radar, communications and command-and-control systems. Operating from NASOC Jacksonville and NASOC Corpus Christi, Texas, the aircraft functioned as an airborne command center. It tracked multiple air and maritime targets and supported complex operations to stop illicit activity with partners, including Joint Interagency Task Force South.
“The P-3 AEW platform carried out a critical mission for decades,” said a NASOC Jacksonville aircrew member. “It's crews monitored millions of square miles of air and maritime approaches, helping identify airborne threats, counter illicit drug trafficking and disrupt networks facilitating illegal migration before they reached U.S. borders.”
During their service, Jacksonville-based P-3 AEW aircraft logged tens of thousands of flight hours supporting counter-narcotics and border security missions. NASOC Jacksonville crews also deployed in support of domestic and international emergency response operations, including humanitarian relief and emergency communications coordination after major natural disasters in the Caribbean.
Although the P-3 AEW aircraft are retiring from AMO’s active inventory, the P-3 Long Range Tracker will continue to operate and support AMO’s maritime domain awareness, detection, monitoring and interdiction missions. The experience and technical expertise of P-3 AEW aircrews, maintenance specialists and flight engineers also will continue to support AMO’s aviation mission.
As AMO modernizes its fleet, it will add C-130J aircraft to help sustain long-range operational capabilities and mission readiness.
AMO safeguards the nation by anticipating and confronting threats through aviation and maritime law enforcement expertise, innovative capabilities and partnerships at the border and beyond. AMO is an operational component of CBP. It works alongside federal, state and international partners to disrupt smuggling operations and safeguard national security.
title: CBP retires aircraft following final operational flight

The Federal Trade Commission announced it is sending more than $100,000 in redress payments to consumers deceived by online marketplace GOAT. The refunds are part of a settlement over allegations the company failed to honor its refund policies and violated an FTC rule requiring companies to have reasonable shipping practices.
In a 2024 complaint, the FTC alleged that GOAT, an online marketplace for sneakers, apparel and accessories, failed to mail some priority processing orders as fast as promised and did not offer buyers the option of agreeing to the delay or cancelling the order and receiving a prompt refund, as required by the FTC’s Mail, Internet or Telephone Order Merchandise Rule.
The FTC also alleged that while GOAT offered “Buyer Protection” for consumers that received deficient products, it did not put a system in place to honor this policy. Despite promising full refunds for products found to be inauthentic, incorrect or otherwise not as described, the company frequently denied those refund requests, only provided partial refunds or issued in-store credits.
In 2025, GOAT directly refunded more than $736,000 to affected customers as part of a settlement with the FTC. Today, the FTC is sending checks or PayPal payments to 6,205 customers who have not yet received a payment. Most consumers will receive a check in the mail. Check recipients should cash their checks within 90 days, as indicated on the check. PayPal recipients should redeem their PayPal payments within 30 days.
Consumers who have questions about their payment should contact the refund administrator, JND Legal Administration, at 1-888-970-2410, or visit the FTC website to view frequently asked questions about the refund process. The Commission never requires people to pay money or provide account information to get a payment.
The Federal Trade Commission works to promote competition and protect and educate consumers. The FTC will never demand money, make threats, tell you to transfer money, or promise you a prize. Learn more about consumer topics at consumer.ftc.gov, or report fraud, scams, and bad business practices at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. Follow the FTC on social media, read consumer alerts and the business blog, and sign up to get the latest FTC news and alerts.
title: FTC Issues Redress Payments to Consumers Impacted by GOAT’s Deceptive Shipping, Refund Policies

LOWELL, MA – Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03), Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) and Congressman Stephen F. Lynch (MA-08) led 24 of their colleagues from Northeastern states in pressing the Department of Energy (DOE) to take immediate action to address the rapidly rising cost of heating oil, which has surged around 60 percent since the start of President Trump’s war in Iran. In their letter, the lawmakers urged the DOE to support an immediate end to the war and prioritize lowering energy costs for the winter, warning that rising prices will force families to choose between heating their homes and paying for basic necessities. 
“Heating oil costs for the upcoming winter are projected to reach record levels, and families throughout the northeastern United States will likely bear the brunt of these costs,” wrote the lawmakers.
The President’s war in Iran has played a large part in driving up the price of heating oil. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has pushed crude oil from $72 to over $100 a barrel, causing a massive increase in heating oil costs in the United States. American families that rely on heating oil are projected to pay about $600 more to keep their homes warm this winter than last year.
In addition to increasing the cost of heating oil, the Trump administration has made or attempted to make heating costs for the upcoming winter even higher by: 
    - Attempting to eliminate the $4 billion Low-Income Heating Assistance Program (LIHEAP) that supports families with high energy bills.
- Effectively increasing taxes on solutions to the heating cost crisis by eliminating four tax credits and deductions that supported residential and commercial building energy efficiency upgrades.
- Cutting more than $20 billion in clean energy and grid modernization funding for hundreds of energy projects across the country that would have decreased costs for families. 
“As Americans face immense difficulty with keeping the heat on, the administration appears to be cutting off all avenues for meaningful relief, handing out tax cuts to billionaires, spending tens of billions of dollars on an unnecessary foreign war, and jacking up costs for struggling families,” the lawmakers continued. 
“To address these costs for American families, we urge you to reverse course on the senseless war in Iran, undo the administration’s cuts to clean energy and grid modernization programs, work with Congress to repeal the tax increases imposed on energy efficiency upgrades and other ways to lower heating costs, and end the administration’s attacks on LIHEAP,” the lawmakers concluded. 
The lawmakers were joined by Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ed Markey (D-Mass.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Peter Welch (D-Vt.), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.); and Representatives Gabe Amo (D-R.I.), Jake Auchincloss (D-Mass.), Becca Balint (D-Vt.), Joe Courtney (D-Conn.), Rosa DeLauro (D-Conn.), Maggie Goodlander (D-N.H.), Bill Keating (D-Mass.), Seth Magaziner (D-R.I.), John Mannion (D-N.Y.), Gregory Meeks (D-N.Y.), Grace Meng (D-N.Y.), Seth Moulton (D-Mass.), Richard Neal (D-Mass.), Chris Pappas (D-N.H.), Chellie Pingree (D-Maine), Paul Tonko (D-N.Y.), and Nydia Velázquez (D-N.Y.).
A copy of the letter sent today can be accessed  HERE.

title: Trahan, Warren, Lynch, Lead Demands to Trump Administration to Provide Relief for Skyrocketing Winter Heating Bills Amid Iran War

CLEVELAND – An Ohio business owner has been charged with embezzling his employees’ retirement contributions and operating Ponzi and mortgage fraud schemes that mainly affected victims throughout Greater Cleveland.

A federal grand jury returned an indictment charging Seku N. Shabazz, formerly known as Jason Brooks, 54, of Cleveland, with the following:

Embezzlement from an Employee Benefit Plan - maximum 5 years in prison.

7 Counts of Wire Fraud – maximum 20 years in prison per count.

3 Counts of Engaging in Monetary Transactions in Criminally Derived Property – maximum 10 years in prison per count.

2 Counts of Aggravated Identity Theft – maximum 2 years in prison.

“We will not tolerate the actions of those who obtain money from others through fraudulent schemes, ” said U.S. Attorney David M. Toepfer for the Northern District of Ohio. “My office will aggressively prosecute anyone who intentionally engages in dishonest practices that rob people of their hard-earned money and ensure that they face justice.”

“We will not tolerate the actions of those who obtain money from others through fraudulent schemes, ” said U.S. Attorney David M. Toepfer for the Northern District of Ohio. “My office will aggressively prosecute anyone who intentionally engages in dishonest practices that rob people of their hard-earned money and ensure that they face justice.”

“Mr. Shabazz abused his position to embezzle hard-earned retirement dollars from trusting employees in an organization he helped form,” said FBI Cleveland Special Agent in Charge Joshua DelManzo. “His tactics not only impacted the employees of the business, but also the Ponzi scheme and investment fraud victims. The FBI will continue to pursue fraudsters who choose personal gain over faithful stewardship of the funds in their care.”

“This case underscores the importance of strong oversight and accountability in protecting Ohioans’ hard‑earned money,” said Ohio Department of Commerce Director Sherry Maxfield. “Ohioans deserve transparency, qualified professionals they can trust, and a fair, secure environment for their investments. We remain firmly committed to upholding these standards, strengthening the safeguards that keep our communities safe, and holding those individuals accountable who attempt to exploit the trust that Ohioans have placed in them.”

“When those entrusted with safeguarding workers' retirement savings betray that trust for personal gain, EBSA will hold them accountable,” said L. Joe Rivers, Regional Director of the Employee Benefit Security Administration, Cincinnati Regional Office. “This indictment sends a clear message that stealing employees' hard-earned 401(k) contributions is a serious federal crime, and EBSA will continue working with our law enforcement partners to protect the retirement security of American workers.”

According to allegations in the indictment, Shabazz carried out a series of interrelated frauds to obtain funds from various individuals and entities. He then used the money to fund his lifestyle and maintain the illusion of success.

Shabazz was a licensed investment advisor who was the president and chief executive officer of a wealth management and financial advisory firm. Although he withheld employee retirement savings contributions, he did not remit them into the company’s plan and failed to pay the required employer matching contributions. He instead used the money to make other business and personal expenditures, including to pay for his memberships to a yacht club and a private business and social club.

Once he exhausted his employees’ retirement funds, Shabazz allegedly began operating an investment fraud Ponzi scheme. He solicited individuals to loan him money so he could raise capital to make mortgage loans to real estate companies, developers, and other entities. Shabazz misled and lied to investors to obtain more than $1.2 million and used the money to fund his lifestyle and at times make some payments to earlier investors and other creditors.

In yet another financial scheme, Shabazz used the identity of two individuals to give the false appearance that he controlled their company, and therefore, owned their residence. Through this misrepresentation and identity theft, he obtained a mortgage loan for over $220,000 secured by their residence and then used a portion of those funds to repay approximately $97,000 owed to the 401(k) plan participants. The owners only learned of the mortgage when they received a notice of foreclosure.

The sentence will be determined by the court after a review of factors unique to this case, including the defendant’s prior criminal record, if any, his role in the offense, and the characteristics of the violations.

This investigation was conducted by the FBI Cleveland Division, the Ohio Department of Commerce–Division of Securities, and the U.S. Department of Labor–Employee Benefits Security Administration.

Assistant United States Attorney Megan R. Miller for the Northern District of Ohio is leading the prosecution.

An indictment is only a charge and is not evidence of guilt. Defendants are entitled to a fair trial in which it will be the government’s burden to prove guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.

If you believe you may have been a victim in this matter, please contact the FBI Cleveland Office at 216-522-1400.
title: Ohio Man Indicted for Stealing Employee 401(k) Funds and Client Investments, and Using Others’ Identities to Obtain a Home Loan

LAS VEGAS – A Las Vegas man who admitted to conspiring with others to distribute methamphetamine was sentenced today by United States District Judge Cristina D. Silva to 96 months in prison, to be followed by 3 years of supervised release. The government recommended a sentence of 108 months in prison.

“Our office continues to demonstrate that ultimate objective of this administration is not the temporary containment or mere management of a narcotics epidemic, but absolute victory over the illicit drug networks poisoning our communities,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “We will use every tool at our disposal to eliminate the supply, enforce maximum prosecution, and restore safety to American neighborhoods.”

“As reported by the Centers for Disease Control, Methamphetamine ranks as the second-most frequent cause of drug overdose deaths and poisonings in the United States, tracking closely behind fentanyl,” said David S. Olesky, Special Agent in Charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration Los Angeles Field Division, which covers Nevada. “Securing convictions for drug criminals is essential to halting the flow of destructive drugs into our communities. The DEA and our law enforcement partners and prosecutors remain steadfast in our commitment to keep communities safe from dangerous drugs, like methamphetamine, by reducing demand, holding accountable the drug distributors and their networks, and addressing the precursor chemical supply chains. The goal is to save lives.”

Ismael Preciado-Granados conspired with others to distribute methamphetamine in Las Vegas. From March 5, 2024, to April 17, 2024, Preciado-Granados arranged for his co-conspirators to deliver and sell methamphetamine to other individuals. In total, between 1.5 and 4.5 kilograms of methamphetamine were sold.

Preciado-Granados pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute a controlled substance-methamphetamine.

The DEA investigated the case. Assistant United States Attorney Joshua Brister investigated the case.
