COLUMBUS, Ohio – Samuel A. Griffith, 35, of Ashville, Ohio, was sentenced in U.S. District Court today to 270 months in prison. As part of the case against Griffith, investigators seized 18 firearms, tens of thousands of dollars in cash and bulk amounts of narcotics from his Hilliard hotel room in October 2025.

According to court documents, in October 2025, Griffith sold fentanyl, methamphetamine and cocaine from a hotel room at the Red Roof Inn in Hilliard. When agents executed a search warrant in the hotel room, they discovered more than four kilograms of methamphetamine, more than a kilogram of fentanyl, a partial kilogram of cocaine, numerous firearms and nearly $40,000 in cash.

Griffith has prior felony convictions for robbery, aggravated possession of drugs and having weapons under disability. As a previously convicted felon, he is prohibited from possessing firearms and ammunition.

Griffith pleaded guilty in April to six federal drug and gun crimes. Specifically, he pleaded guilty to distribution of 50 grams or more of methamphetamine, distribution of 40 grams or more of fentanyl, possession with intent to distribute 400 grams or more of fentanyl, possession with intent to distribute 50 grams or more of methamphetamine, possession with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of cocaine and illegally possessing a firearm as a felon.

Dominick S. Gerace II, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Ohio; Jorge Rosendo, Special Agent in Charge, U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives (ATF); Fairfield County Sheriff Alex Lape; Ohio State Highway Patrol Superintendent Col. Charles A. Jones and Columbus Police Chief Elaine Bryant announced the sentence imposed today by U.S. District Judge Michael H. Watson. Assistant United States Attorney Kevin W. Kelley is representing the United States in this case.

# # #
title: Pickaway County man sentenced to more than 22 years in prison for federal gun, drug crimes involving multiple kilograms of narcotics seized from Hilliard hotel

Pensacola, Florida – James Michael Olshefskie, 55, of Pensacola, Florida, was sentenced to two years in federal prison for possession of ammunition by a convicted felon and possession of two unregistered firearm silencers. The sentence was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida.

U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “This repeat offender clearly didn’t get the message that the Northern District of Florida will not tolerate violations of federal law after his last conviction, so my office is more than happy to return him to federal prison to make that point abundantly clear. The safety of our communities is not negotiable, and my office will aggressively enforce the law to keep our streets crime-free.”

On September 11, 2025, United States Probation Officers visited the defendant at his residence in Pensacola, Florida, as part of his federal post-conviction supervision. The defendant was on federal supervised release for a 2024 federal felony firearm conviction, and was therefore prohibited from possessing firearms or ammunition. During their visit, probation officers found ammunition and firearm silencers in the defendant’s bedroom.

The case involved an investigation by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Jeffrey M. Tharp.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities .

The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl .

Tampa, FL – Javion Ward (22, Fort Myers) has been sentenced by U.S. District Judge Steven Merryday to 28 years in federal prison for conspiracy to commit Hobbs Act robbery and possessing a firearm in furtherance of a crime of violence. The court also ordered Ward to forfeit the firearm used in the robberies. Ward pleaded guilty on June 25, 2026. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement.

According to court documents, in September 2025, Ward personally robbed five convenience stores and aided a co-conspirator in attempting to rob a sixth store. The robberies took place in Hillsborough, Sumter, Manatee, and Sarasota counties, all in close proximity to I-75. During each robbery, Ward entered the store armed with a firearm and demanded money from the clerk. On September 16, 2025, Ward entered a convenience store in Tampa, brandished a pistol, demanded money, and obtained about $600. In the early morning hours of September 19, 2025, Ward robbed four more stores—in Gibsonton, Ellenton, Nokomis, and North Port—where each time Ward entered with a firearm and demanded cash. In Gibsonton, Ward jumped over the counter to attempt to access the safe. In Ellenton, he threatened to pistol whip the employee if they did not move faster.

This arrest was the result of an investigation led by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, with assistance from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, the Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office, the Tampa Police Department, the Sumter County Sheriff’s Office, the Manatee County Sheriff’s Office, the North Port Police Department, the Fort Myers Police Department, and the Venice Police Department. It is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Michael R. Kenneth.

text:
BOSTON – A Brockton man pleaded guilty today to making false statements to law enforcement regarding his transfer of 24 firearms he had purchased. More than half of the firearms surfaced at various crime scenes across the Northeast including a Boston homicide.

Klordenzsky Senecharles, 29, pleaded guilty to one count of false statements. U.S. District Court Judge Angel Kelley scheduled sentencing for Jan. 20, 2027. Senecharles was arrested and charged in April 2026 . He was released on pretrial conditions.

Between March 2020 and May 2021, Senecharles purchased a total of 28 firearms and later sold four of them. Of the 24 firearms still registered to Senecharles, 13 firearms were recovered in connection with criminal activity, including a Feb. 26, 2024 homicide in Boston. Senecharles told law enforcement that he had sold 21 of the 24 firearms to various Massachusetts registered firearms dealers. The firearms dealers reported that they had no record of purchasing any of the 21 firearms from Senecharles.

The charge of making false statements provides for a sentence of up to five years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Thomas Greco, Special Agent in Charge of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the United States Marshals Service. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Meghan C. Cleary and Colin T. Missett of the Criminal Division are prosecuting the case.
title: Brockton Man Pleads Guilty to Making False Statements to Law Enforcement About Firearms Recovered at Crime Scenes

Washington, D.C. — Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) — the only Virginian on the U.S. House Agriculture Committee — joined Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (Va.-04) in sending a letter to Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins opposing the Trump Administration’s proposal to rescind the Roadless Area Conservation Rule, commonly referred to as the “Roadless Rule.”
Since its implementation in 2001, the Roadless Rule has protected 45 million acres of forest lands across the country, including nearly 394,000 acres in the Commonwealth of Virginia. Under the Trump Administration, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) and Forest Service filed a proposal in August of this year to repeal the Roadless Rule, which could have devastating impacts on water quality, biodiversity, economic development and more for these regions.
The letter was also signed by U.S. Senators Mark Warner (D-Va.) and Tim Kaine (D-Va.), and U.S. Representatives Bobby Scott (Va.-03), Don Beyer (Va.-08), Suhas Subramanyam (Va.-10) and James Walkinshaw (Va.-11).
“This proposal would strip protections from approximately 84% of Virginia’s roadless areas, opening these lands to road construction, logging, and other industrial activities. The consequences for Virginia’s environment, economy, and public health would be severe, falling squarely on the families and communities we represent,” wrote the lawmakers. “With more roadless acres than any other state east of the Mississippi River, Virginia has an outsized stake in decisions regarding the Roadless Rule. Once lost, these ecosystems and the countless benefits they provide to clean air, clean water, and climate resilience cannot be easily restored, if at all.”
The letter outlines the risks this rescission would pose to Virginia by jeopardizing Virginia’s drinking water and ecosystems, threatening economic activity driven by recreation and tourism activities, increasing wildfire risk and straining public resources.
“For 25 years, the Roadless Rule has demonstrated that protecting America’s national forest lands is both effective and widely supported. Rescinding the Roadless Rule would ignore this overwhelming public consensus while undermining Virginia’s drinking water, biodiversity, local economies, and public safety,” the lawmakers concluded. “We urge the Department to withdraw this dangerous proposal and maintain the Roadless Area Conservation Rule of 2001 in its entirety.”
Read the full letter text here.
###
title: Vindman Stands Up for Roadless Rule to Protect Virginia’s Natural Resources, Local Economies

WASHINGTON – Charles Dixon, 47, a previously convicted felon residing in the District, was sentenced today to 33 months in federal prison for his role in a fentanyl trafficking conspiracy operating out of Southeast D.C., announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

Dixon pleaded guilty on June 30, 2026, before U.S. District Judge Trevor N. McFadden to one count of conspiracy to distribute fentanyl. In addition to the 33-month prison term, Judge McFadden ordered Dixon to serve five years of supervised release.

According to court documents, between October 2024 and September 2025, Dixon worked with co‑defendants to distribute counterfeit M30 oxycodone pills containing fentanyl in the area of the 2000 block of 19th Place SE.

Dixon supplied the fentanyl pills to his coconspirators for redistribution, including 96 pills used in an April 2025 controlled buy and another 163 pills supplied for a July 2025 purchase. A search of Dixon’s residence in October 2025 yielded additional fentanyl pills and a firearm with an extended magazine.

Dixon has 10 prior convictions, including at least one prior felony including a 2001 gun offense, according to court filings.

This case was investigated by the FBI Safe Streets Task Force, with assistance from the Drug Enforcement Administration Washington Field Office.

The matter was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Iris Y. McCranie and Kate Naseef of the Violent Crime and Narcotics Trafficking Division.

This case is part of the Department of Justice’s broader efforts to combat fentanyl trafficking and drug related violence in the District of Columbia. Fentanyl remains one of the deadliest substances circulating in the illegal drug supply, and counterfeit pills containing fentanyl pose extreme risks to unwitting users and the community at large.

text:
Davids Helps Launch Bipartisan Agenda to Cut Red Tape, Boost Local Economies, Lower Everyday Costs for Kansas Families
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Yesterday, Representative Sharice Davids, a member of the Build America Caucus, helped announce the Build More Agenda — a major bipartisan policy platform designed to fix federal gridlock, strengthen local economies, create jobs, and lower everyday prices for hardworking families. By streamlining approval processes for energy, housing, and infrastructure, the roadmap directly targets the bureaucratic delays that slow down construction, drive up utility and housing costs, and prevent critical projects from getting built.
“Kansans don’t want D.C. talking points — they want lower utility bills, homes they can actually afford, and roads that aren't falling apart,” said Davids. “The problem isn't a lack of good ideas; it's the bureaucratic red tape slowing projects down for years. I’m supporting the bipartisan Build America Caucus’ new agenda because it would help cut through government gridlock and start building these projects now, not a decade from now.”
The bipartisan Build America Caucus was established to give pro-growth, pragmatic policymaking a permanent foothold in Congress. Over the past year, the Caucus helped negotiate and pass major bipartisan housing reform legislation and led bipartisan efforts to deliver permitting certainty for energy and infrastructure projects. Spanning seven core policy areas and over 60 legislative proposals, the Build More Agenda builds on those successes, establishing a comprehensive framework to spur domestic production, bring manufacturing home, create good-paying jobs, and lower the cost of living for Kansans.
“Not enough homes or energy, shortages of doctors and daycares, cures that take too long to reach patients, and infrastructure projects that drag on for decades. That’s what life in America looks like today because we’ve lost the ability to build the things we need,” said CaucusCo-Chairs Harder and Maloy. “We used to believe that America was the only place in the world where the boldest dreams could be realized, and we need a new politics of action to restore that national ambition and trust in government. The Build America Caucus was founded a little over a year ago with that goal in mind, and the Build More Agenda is our bipartisan roadmap to make growth and prosperity the cornerstone of American life once again.”
The solution to systemic dysfunction is to build our way to prosperity:
- Lowering Housing Costs: With the nation facing a shortage of five million homes, the agenda reduces regulatory delays, unlocks new project financing, and fully implements the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act to expand homeownership options and bring housing prices back within reach for young families and working Kansans.
- Cutting Healthcare Costs & Red Tape: We spend more on healthcare than any other nation, but that care is unaffordable, inaccessible, and archaic. It reallocates physician training investments and slashes mountain-high administrative paperwork, so doctors spend time on patient outcomes rather than bureaucracy — cutting health system waste and lowering out-of-pocket prescription drug costs.
- Cheaper, Reliable Energy: Electricity rates have jumped more than 30 percent in recent years. The platform fixes broken permitting rules, so grid upgrades and energy projects don't take longer to approve than to actually construct, bringing down monthly electricity bills for households and small businesses.
- Building Infrastructure Faster: It establishes dedicated fast-track approvals and smarter federal funding models to ensure roads, bridges, and water systems are completed on schedule and under budget — ending costly construction delays that waste taxpayer dollars.
- Accelerating Medical Cures: America is losing its scientific edge because our scientists spend half their time on paperwork and research dollars aren’t geared toward modern discovery. It saves American medical researchers over one million hours a year spent on bureaucratic paperwork, redirecting resources toward breakthrough science and AI technology to accelerate cures for cancer, Alzheimer's, and chronic conditions.
- Expanding Childcare & Workforce Pipelines: It strengthens workforce development programs that directly match workers to high-paying local jobs, while expanding accessible childcare options so parents can stay in the workforce without breaking their household budgets.
- Modernizing Government to Save Taxpayer Dollars: It cuts redundant D.C. red tape, updates archaic federal technology systems, and builds a skill-focused public workforce that manages taxpayer funds efficiently.
Read the full agenda here. Read a section-by-section here.
“America knows how to build, we just have to get out of our own way and start doing it,” said Rep. Janelle Bynum (D-OR-05). “More homes, better roads and bridges, new technology, and good jobs – this agenda is about turning big ideas into things people can actually see and feel in their communities. I’m ready to roll up my sleeves and help get it done.”
“Americans are tired of Washington making it harder and more expensive to build, innovate, and grow,” said Rep. Buddy Carter (R-GA-01). “The Build More Agenda brings Republicans and Democrats together around commonsense solutions to cut red tape, lower costs, strengthen American energy, improve access to healthcare, and get critical projects built. I’m proud to work with the Build America Caucus to turn good ideas into real results for the American people.”
“The Build More Agenda reflects what we can accomplish when we work across the aisle to tackle challenges facing American families and businesses,” said Rep. Gus Bilirakis (R-FL-12). “I’m proud to join my colleagues in the bipartisan Build America Caucus to advance practical solutions that cut unnecessary red tape, lower costs, and help America build faster and smarter. By modernizing infrastructure and creating opportunities for American workers and manufacturers, we can strengthen our economy, make taxpayer dollars go further, and deliver lasting results for our communities.”
“America used to pride itself on accomplishing big things — winning world wars, sending man to the moon, or discovering the next medical breakthrough,” said Rep. Scott Peters (D-CA-50). “Today, our challenges have not gone away, but our capacity to achieve great things has. Our constituents are counting on us to put politics aside and invest in our country’s future to make their lives better. The bipartisan Build More Agenda includes ways to do exactly that: lower costs, create good-paying jobs, strengthen communities, and restore America as a global leader in progress and innovation.”
“Folks in Western and Southern Colorado know how to build things, create jobs, and get things done,” said Rep. Jeff Hurd (R-CO-03). “Too often, Washington just gets in the way. The Build More Agenda is about cutting unnecessary red tape so we can produce more American energy, build the housing and infrastructure our communities need, and bring down costs for working families. Republicans and Democrats aren’t going to agree on everything, but we ought to be able to agree that it shouldn’t take years of paperwork and bureaucracy to build something in this country.”
“A housing shortage is a tax on working people, and they pay it every month in rent,” said Rep. Ritchie Torres (D-NY-15). “For decades, we have piled on rules and caps that make it slower and costlier to build homes, and few places have paid a higher price than the Bronx. The surest way to bring down the cost of housing is to bring up the supply of housing. The Build More Agenda is built on that principle, because a pro-growth agenda is a pro–working class agenda. Progress should be measured not by how many projects we regulate but by how many we deliver.”
“Congress passed a housing abundance bill this term,” said Rep. Jake Auchincloss (D-MA-04). “It's seriously debating a bipartisan energy abundance bill. Build America has momentum in its mission to lower prices by building more, faster & better – next up are unlocks to lower prices in medicine, transportation, and childcare.”
“As a senior member of the Housing, Transportation, and Urban Development Subcommittee, I’m proud to be a member of the bipartisan Build America Caucus. My constituents tell me every day they want to see their representatives in Washington take actions that will make their lives better – lower the cost of housing, healthcare, and energy,” said Rep. Mike Quigley (D-IL-05). “At a time of deep political division, we have the unique opportunity to come together as Democrats and Republicans to lower costs and solve the housing crisis.”
“Whether it’s rebuilding a bridge over I-95 in record time or passing landmark housing legislation, we know that government can still get things done, if rarely,” said Rep. Jim Himes (D-CT-04). “I’m in the Build America Caucus because this group of lawmakers fundamentally believes government needs to get things done — not as the exception, but as the rule. Our agenda reflects that belief, and I look forward to working with my colleagues to turn our group’s governing principle into law.”
What they’re saying about the Build More Agenda:
“For too long, we’ve treated a four-year college degree as the default path to a good career. The Build America Caucus’s push to get more apprenticeships and higher-quality workforce training programs off the ground is a critical step forward. If we want to build more in America, we need to make it easier for more Americans to learn how to do the building,” said Zach Boren, Senior Vice President, Apprenticeships for America.
“Getting lawmakers from both parties to agree on what's holding the country back is no easy feat, and we applaud the Build America Caucus for assembling a genuinely bipartisan coalition around these questions. BPC Action has long argued that the problems on this list — the cost of building housing, the time it takes to approve energy projects, and a broken childcare system — are solvable ones. We look forward to working with the caucus and its members as they move from agenda to legislation,” said Michele Stockwell, President, BPC Action.
“Through their work with the Build America Caucus, Reps. Harder and Maloy have asked how we can build more of what Americans actually need and answered it across housing, childcare, energy, and more. We applaud this effort and its goal to build 5 million homes, add millions more new childcare slots, modernize the energy grid, and get infrastructure built faster. This comprehensive plan demonstrates that pragmatic, actionable solutions can still be ambitious. This Agenda, written by a Democrat from California and a Republican from Utah, also shows the strength of abundance solutions in building coalitions. I urge Congress to take action on these solutions,” said Derek Kaufman, President, Inclusive Abundance Action.
“The Build More Agenda is an innovative, bipartisan framework for creating a more abundant future in America. The priorities laid out in this agenda have the potential to make a massive difference in areas from science and innovation to housing, transportation, and energy. For example, we were thrilled to see X-Labs and metascience units highlighted as vehicles to accelerate scientific discovery and increase the return on investment for R&D. Similarly, the Agenda’s focus on reducing land use regulations, building transit at lower cost, and achieving energy abundance is crucial for letting America build again and innovate in the world of atoms,” said Alec Stapp, CEO, Institute for Progress.
“For the past year, the Build America Caucus has worked across the aisle to notch key policy wins, making it easier, cheaper, and faster to build in America. The Build More Agenda strengthens that foundation, with over sixty policy proposals covering seven different policy areas. NAIA looks forward to working with the Caucus to back the builders,” said the New America Industrial Alliance.
“Finding childcare that's both affordable and meets their family’s specific needs is nearly impossible for far too many American parents. This agenda from the Build America Caucus offers an innovative menu of reforms to identify and remove the barriers to a more abundant supply of childcare options that fit family preferences without sacrificing quality or safety,” said Josh McCabe, Director of Social Policy, Niskanen Center.
“The housing affordability crisis is the result of many different factors, and solving it requires an all-hands-on-deck approach. The Build America Caucus agenda delivers this, with solutions that make it easier and less expensive to build housing. Critically, it does the same for transportation infrastructure and buses, because abundant housing and effective transportation options work together to connect people to economic opportunity,” said Kimberly Burnett, Deputy Director of Housing and Transportation, Niskanen Center.
“America's healthcare affordability crisis is fueled by a scarce and consolidated supply side of the market. This agenda from the Build America Caucus rightly targets solutions that increase care availability and cut out the incentives that drive consolidation,” said Lawson Mansell, Senior Health Policy Analyst, Niskanen Center.
“We applaud the Build America Caucus for its energy agenda focused on more power and lower bills. Getting transmission right and having neighboring regions connected is how you build a grid Americans can afford,” said Sarah Iskander, Government Affairs Manager, Niskanen Center.
“Whether it's housing, transportation, energy, or infrastructure, the federal government needs the tools and capacity to deliver for the American people. Meeting those demands requires a government whose systems and processes make delivery possible, and right now ours is not built to keep pace with changes in the workforce, technology, and the public's needs. The Build America Caucus's policy agenda takes this challenge head-on, rightly recognizing state capacity as essential to unlocking a prosperous future for our country,” said Max Stier, President and CEO, Partnership for Public Service.
“Getting the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act into law was a major accomplishment, and Congressman Josh Harder and Congresswoman Celeste Maloy deserve a lot of credit for helping build the bipartisan coalition that got it done. Now we have to make it work. That means making sure HUD has the people and resources to implement the law well, while continuing the bipartisan work of finding the next set of solutions to get more homes built. The Build America Caucus’ Build More Agenda carries that work forward by keeping the focus on implementation and putting new ideas on the table. Up for Growth supports that direction, and we look forward to bringing our members and policy expertise to the work ahead,” said Mike Kingsella, Chief Executive Officer, Up for Growth.

REP LIEU JOINS REP. FRIEDMAN, LOS ANGELES DELEGATION, AND ENTERTAINMENT UNION IN PUSH FOR NATIONAL FILM TAX CREDIT
GLENDALE, CA – Today, October 6, 2026, Congressman Ted Lieu (D-Los Angeles County) joined U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (D-Los Angeles County), Members of the Los Angeles congressional delegation, and the major unions representing film and television workers at the Alex Theatre in a new push for the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act. This bipartisan legislation creates a national film tax credit on qualified labor expenses to bring production jobs back home.
For decades, the United States has offered no national filming incentive, leaving American crews to compete against roughly 65 countries that do. The result has been hundreds of thousands of lost jobs for the drivers, grips, electricians, carpenters, caterers, and crew members.
WHAT THE BILL DOES:
- A 20% credit on American labor expenses. Feature films, television pilots, and television seasons that cost more than $1 million qualify if at least 75% of their principal photography days happen in the United States.
- Bonus credits that reward hiring where it is needed most. Productions can earn an additional 5% each, up to a 30% total credit, for shooting at least 30% of their days in a rural opportunity zone or a federally declared disaster area, for independent productions, for spending at least $10 million in qualified wages across 10 or more states, and for increasing domestic production relative to what a company shoots abroad.
- Includes post-production and visual effects work. Domestic post-production and VFX qualify as long as at least 75% of those costs are incurred in the United States, with the same 5% bonuses available.
- Usable by independent producers, not just major studios. The credit is transferable, meaning a producer who doesn't owe enough in federal taxes to use it can sell it to a company that does and get the cash up front.
- Takes effect quickly. The credit applies to productions that begin in taxable years starting after December 31, 2026.
“Southern California is the birthplace of the modern film and television industry. From the movies and television shows that have entertained audiences around the world to the hardworking people behind them, this industry is a vital part of our community and economy,” said Congressman Lieu (CA-36). “We can’t let the United States’ film industry lose ground to foreign competitors. I am pleased to be an original co-sponsor of the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act. It’s time to strengthen our domestic film industry and protect American jobs.”
“When a production leaves this country, the stars still work. The crew is who gets left behind,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30). “65 countries offer incentives we don’t match, and no single state can outbid a foreign government on its own. Our bipartisan bill is built on labor costs, which means it only pays off when American workers get hired. These are good paying union jobs with benefits and pensions, and I won’t stop fighting until they come home.”
“Movie magic is central to the California story, and we need to keep it that way,” said Rep. Pete Aguilar (CA-33). “Our state is losing good-paying, union jobs because filming in this country has become far too expensive. The bipartisan Motion Picture, Television and Entertainment Revitalization Act will bring jobs back to America, boost wages for workers and keep productions at home.”
"Southern California has been the heart of America’s film and television industry, but today, too many productions are leaving the United States for countries offering better incentives," said Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28). "That’s why I’m proud to co-lead the bipartisan Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, which would provide a long-overdue federal tax credit to incentivize production here in the United States. Our creative workforce is the backbone of this industry. It's time we must invest in them and bring American film and television production back home."
“California is the heart of film and television production, in large part because of the workers and technicians who bring the magic to life,” said Representative Tran (CA-45). “Yet the U.S. is rapidly losing jobs in this industry to competitors overseas. When productions relocate outside the U.S., it’s the American-based crews that suffer the most. California’s workforce deserves better. This bill incentivizes American-based productions, strengthens California’s production workforce, and brings jobs back to the U.S.—where they belong.”
QUOTES
“American performers and entertainment workers should not have to leave the country to find work in an industry that was built here. Film and television are more than entertainment — they are a major American industry that supports hundreds of thousands of good-paying union jobs and generates significant economic activity in communities across the country. For decades, foreign governments have recognized the economic value of production and successfully used incentives to attract these jobs overseas. States across the country have shown what targeted incentives can do to attract and retain production, and a federal incentive would build on those efforts and give the United States a stronger tool to compete. The Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act is an investment in American workers, American industry and American communities. SAG-AFTRA is proud to stand with Congresswoman Friedman and our labor partners in support of this important legislation,” said SAG-AFTRA National Executive Director and Chief Negotiator Duncan Crabtree-Ireland.
“The Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act will benefit entertainment industry workers, as well as the supporting businesses and local economies that rely on a robust domestic entertainment industry. Lawmakers have an opportunity to invest in an important American industry and preserve middle-class jobs, by passing the first-ever federal film and television tax incentive program,” said WGAW Secretary-Treasurer Peter Murrieta.
"Let’s not overthink this. The world is a complicated place, but this legislation is a no-brainer. It's going to get people back to work, and everyone just wants an opportunity to work in the industry they love in this country. Everyone will benefit from this – Republicans, Democrats, workers, audiences -- because our industry touches everyone," said Mike Farah, an Emmy-winning producer and a President of the Producers Guild of America.
Rep. Lieu was joined today by U.S. Representative Laura Friedman (CA-30), Senator Adam Schiff (CA), U.S. Representatives Linda Sánchez (CA-38), Maxine Waters (CA-43), Judy Chu (CA-28), Pete Aguilar (CA-33), David Min (CA-47), and Derek Tran (CA-45), IATSE International Vice President and Director of the Motion Picture and Television Department Mike Miller, SAG-AFTRA National Executive Director and Chief Negotiator Duncan Crabtree-Ireland, WGAW Secretary-Treasurer Peter Murrieta, DGA Associate National Executive Director and Western Executive Director Rebecca Rhine, Teamsters At-Large Vice President and Motion Picture Division Director Lindsay Dougherty, LiUNA Business Manager Alex Aguilar, Jr., and producer and three-time Emmy winner Mike Farah.

SACRAMENTO, Calif. — Parampreet Singh, 60, of Davis, was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge John A. Mendez to 10 years in prison and ordered to forfeit $2 million for conspiring to distribute and possess with intent to distribute cocaine, heroin, opium, and ketamine, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced.

According to court documents, Parampreet Singh, was the leader and organizer of a conspiracy to coordinate drug deals involving cocaine, heroin, opium, and ketamine in Canada. He and co-defendants Ranvir Singh, 43, of Sacramento, Amandeep Multani, 38, of Roseville, and others arranged these transactions from California using encrypted cellphone apps. Between October 2020 and April 2021, they coordinated sales to undercover officers totaling approximately 10 kilograms of cocaine, 1.5 kilograms of opium, 2 kilograms of ketamine, and multiple samples of heroin, generating $637,600 in Canadian currency and $75,190 in U.S. currency, in deals in Canada and Sacramento.

In addition, between September 2020 and April 2021, Parampreet Singh and his co-defendants repeatedly offered to sell up to 100 kilograms of cocaine, up to 25 kilograms of heroin, up to 100 kilograms of opium, and up to 200 kilograms of ketamine.

The Drug Enforcement Administration conducted the investigation with assistance from Homeland Security Investigations, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the York Regional Police in Canada, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, and the Placer County Special Investigations Unit. Assistant U.S. Attorney David W. Spencer prosecuted the case.

Parampreet Singh pleaded guilty on Sept. 9, 2025. Multani pleaded guilty on Dec. 13, 2022, and agreed to cooperate fully with the United States. He was sentenced to time served on Dec. 10, 2025, after spending more than four years and eight months in custody.

On Oct. 15, 2025, a jury found Ranvir Singh guilty of conspiracy to distribute cocaine and ketamine and one count of distribution of cocaine. He is scheduled to be sentenced on Dec. 1, 2026. Ranvir Singh faces a maximum statutory penalty of life in prison and a $10 million fine. The actual sentence, however, will be determined at the discretion of the court after consideration of any applicable statutory factors and the Federal Sentencing Guidelines, which take into account a number of variables.

This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Sacramento is composed of agents and officers from Homeland Security Investigations, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Drug Enforcement Administration, Northern California High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area, Central Valley High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area, and the Sacramento County Sheriff’s Office with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of California.
title: Davis man sentenced to 10 years in prison and ordered to forfeit $2 million for a drug trafficking conspiracy in the United States and Canada

SPRINGFIELD, Mo. – A Guatemalan national illegally residing in the Taney County, Missouri area, was sentenced today in federal court for one count of Illegal Possession of a Firearm by an Illegal Immigrant, and Illegal Entry into the United States.

Edilberto Gonzalez-Barrera, 40, was sentenced today before District Court Judge Douglas Harpool for the offense of an illegal immigrant in possession of a firearm and illegally entering the United States. Gonzalez-Barrera was sentenced to 20 months imprisonment with the Federal Bureau of Prisons, and one year of post release supervision, and will be deported to his native country of Guatemala immediately upon his release from prison.

On March 29, 2026, officers with the Branson, Missouri Police Department responded to Cox Hospital in Branson, in response to a male who had come into the hospital for treatment of a gunshot wound. Officers learned that Mr. Gonzalez-Barrera, an individual who illegally entered the United States, had possessed a firearm, and as he was cleaning the firearm, it accidentally discharged, shooting the lower end of one of his fingers off. Upon determining that Mr. Gonzalez-Barrera was illegally within the United States, local law enforcement contacted agents with the Department of Homeland Security – Immigration Customs Enforcement. Agents responded and determined that Mr. Guzman-Guerra was illegally in the United States, as he was a citizen of Guatemala, without permission to enter or remain within the United States.

This case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Patrick Carney. It was investigated by the Department of Homeland Security-Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Removal Operations, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and the Branson, Missouri Police Department.

Operation Take Back America

This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.
title: Guatemalan National Sentenced for Illegal Possession of a Firearm by an Illegal Immigrant and Illegally Entering the United States

Mid-Atlantic Housing Innovations Spotlighted at HUD’s Innovative Housing Showcase
October 6, 2026
National American Indian Housing Council's Exhibit
WASHINGTON - U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) spotlighted multiple housing innovations and resources from the Mid-Atlantic region during the sixth annual Innovative Housing Showcase, held September 22-24 on the National Mall. This year’s theme, “Made in America,” highlighted American ingenuity and innovative approaches to expanding housing affordability and homeownership.
“HUD is prioritizing innovation to make housing more affordable for American families,” said Assistant Deputy Secretary for Field Policy and Management and Region III Administrator Joseph DeFelice. “The Innovative Housing Showcase spotlighted cutting-edge work by Mid-Atlantic companies, making housing easier to build and buy. Deregulation and strong public-private partnerships paired with advanced construction methods are key to making the American Dream a reality for more families across our region.”
HUD’s “Made in America” Showcase spotlighted American builders, manufacturers, and innovators’ modern technologies and creative housing solutions that are expanding housing supply, lowering construction costs, and putting affordable homeownership back in reach for hardworking Americans. The Showcase featured a variety of full-scale housing models including manufactured, 3D printed, and modular homes built by American companies from across the nation.
Examples from the Mid-Atlantic Region
Live installations and product samples of mortarless manufactured stone veneers from Evolve Stone (Virginia).
A Student Team Showcase from Housing Innovation Alliance (Pennsylvania) with designs produced by students who competed in the Housing Innovation Challenge.
Exemplary projects from the National American Indian Housing Council’s (Washington, D.C.) Tribal and Tribally Designated Housing Entity membership across Indian Country.
Follow @SecretaryTurner on X, FB, and Instagram.

text:
This Child Health Day, we renew our commitment to ensure the health and well-being of America’s children – our Nation’s future – so that they may live full, lasting, and happy lives free from the burden of health concerns.
As our children grow, we must protect their health and give them every opportunity to thrive. American children now face chronic health conditions and serious medical issues at rates far higher than in previous generations. With little explanation, we have witnessed sharp rises in the prevalence of obesity, diabetes, severe allergies, autism, autoimmune diseases, and mental health challenges such as anxiety and depression in our Nation’s youth. As President, I have a solemn duty to safeguard the health of the coming generation, and I will not rest until these conditions are understood and defeated and every child in America can grow up strong and whole.
For this reason, my Administration is confronting the chronic health crisis plaguing our Nation’s most vulnerable citizens by reversing the failed policies that have fueled America’s childhood disease epidemic and ensuring parents are informed with the Gold Standard Science to make the decisions for their children. Through the Make Our Children Healthy Again Strategy—an initiative launched by the Make America Healthy Again Commission—we have taken over 120 specific actions to halt the rise in childhood chronic diseases and discover the root causes of serious medical conditions by improving preventative care, getting artificial dyes out of our food, accelerating breakthroughs and cures, and encouraging physical activity and limited screen time for children.
While more work remains to fully reverse these concerning trends, in just the first year of my Administration, we experienced the lowest death rate in recorded in our country’s history. Our Nation’s future relies upon the health and leadership of the next generation, which is why I remain committed to ensuring that Americans and their children receive the best medical advice to keep them healthy and the best care in the world if they do get sick. Under my leadership, we are delivering a healthcare system that restores trust and truly puts the health of children and families first, and together, we will make American children healthy again for generations to come.
title: Presidential Message on Child Health Day

COLUMBIA, S.C. — Devron Jakell Duncan, 33, of Aiken, has been sentenced to 33 months in federal prison for possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. On Feb. 15, 2023, a University of South Carolina Police Officer was patrolling the Five Points area of Columbia. Around 2 a.m., the officer stopped a vehicle driven by Duncan. Duncan refused the officer’s commands to stay in the vehicle, pushed the officer, and ran. After apprehending Duncan, USCPD officers searched the area and found a loaded 9 mm pistol that Duncan had tossed. Further investigation revealed that Duncan’s girlfriend was the purchaser of the gun and had previously told law enforcement that Duncan stole the gun from her residence. Duncan has prior convictions for domestic violence, illegally possessing a firearm, and kidnapping, among other offenses. These offenses prohibit Duncan from possessing a firearm or ammunition. Chief United States District Judge Sherri A. Lydon sentenced Duncan to 33 months’ imprisonment, to be followed by a three-year term of court-ordered supervision. There is no parole in the federal system. This case is part of Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN), a nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. This case was investigated by Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and the University of South Carolina Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Todd Timmons prosecuted the case.

EPA Administrator Zeldin Proposes Approving Another Innovative Plan in Maricopa County to Help Manufacturing and Economic Growth While Ensuring Clean Air
WASHINGTON – Today while in Maricopa County, Arizona, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin announced the proposed approval of a second innovative air quality rule by Maricopa County to support Arizona’s continued economic expansion while maintaining clean air for the region. Administrator Zeldin was joined by U.S. Representative Andy Biggs (R-AZ-05) and a number of state and Maricopa County officials for the announcement. If finalized as proposed, the County’s Air Quality Rule 204, “Emission Offsets Generated by Voluntary Nonroad Engine Emission Reductions,” would allow key American industries, like high-tech manufacturing and power plants in the area, to use emission reduction credits (ERCs) from voluntary nonroad engine emissions reductions to build and expand production without increasing emissions.
In April 2026, EPA proposed approval of a similar Maricopa County rule covering ERCs from on-road vehicles. Through these proposals, the Trump EPA is proving once again that there does not have to be a binary choice between protecting the environment and growing the economy.
“State and local officials know what works for their communities better than anyone else,” said EPA Administrator Zeldin. “The Trump EPA is proud to work once again with Maricopa County to ensure economic growth while also protecting clean air. We can and will grow the American economy while fulfilling our core mission of protecting human health and the environment.”
“This is an important win for cleaner air, economic growth and the kind of practical problem-solving Arizona does best... We appreciate Administrator Zeldin and the EPA for moving this forward,” said Arizona Chamber of Commerce & Industry President and CEO Danny Seidel. “Protecting air quality and maintaining a strong economy do not have to be competing goals, and once again Arizona is showing the rest of the country how smart policy can advance both.”
“This plan demonstrates how a healthy environment and growing economy can work together. By incentivizing rather than punishing job creators, implementing Maricopa County’s Rule 204 will improve the quality of the air we breathe while enabling key industries to continue investing in our community,” said Maricopa County Board of Supervisors District 3 Chair Kate Brophy McGee. “I thank Administrator Zeldin and the EPA for working with Maricopa County and our business community on this innovative approach.”
“Today’s announcement is a victory for our environment, the economy, and common-sense regulation reform. Maricopa County has proven our residents don’t have to choose between a clean air and economic opportunity,” said Maricopa County District 2 Supervisor Thomas Galvin. “I’m grateful to EPA Administrator Zeldin, county officials, and business leaders who helped make this possible, and we will continue looking for ways to partner with the federal government to streamline regulation impacting Maricopa County homes and businesses.”
“Our industry understands both the importance of cleaner air and the cost of regulatory delay. Rule 204 creates a practical path that rewards companies for investing in cleaner equipment while expanding the tools available to support future growth,” said Arizona Rock Products Association Executive Director Steve Trussell. “That is the kind of balanced policy Arizona needs as we continue building the infrastructure and communities that power our economy.”
“The construction industry knows that time matters. Delays in permitting can mean delayed investment, delayed jobs and higher costs. Rule 204 shows that the EPA can help speed up the path to growth without compromising clean-air goals. This practical, results-oriented approach is a win for both Arizona’s economy and our environment,” said Willmeng Vice President of Economic Development & Infrastructure Jimmy Lindblom.
Portions of Maricopa County are currently designated as “Moderate” nonattainment for the 2015 Ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS). As a result, major stationary sources, including power plants and manufacturing facilities, must obtain a preconstruction permit from the Maricopa County Air Quality Department (MCAQD) and offset any increase in emissions, per Clean Air Act (CAA) requirements, to build or expand in this nonattainment area.
If today’s proposed rule is finalized, nonroad engine owners and operators that permanently reduce nitrogen oxide or volatile organic compound emissions will be able to trade those reductions as ERCs to stationary sources wishing to build or expand in the County’s nonattainment area. Historically, ERCs have only been generated and traded between stationary sources; however, EPA is proposing that Rule 204 meets statutory requirements under CAA section 173. The ERCs will enable key industries to meet the manufacturing and energy needs of the area while following all CAA requirements for a “Moderate” nonattainment area for the 2015 Ozone NAAQS. EPA does not expect this rule to increase emissions in the area.
Under the framework of cooperative federalism, the Trump EPA believes that its local and state regulatory partners are oftentimes best positioned to understand the unique needs of their regions. Rule 204 provides a market-based regulatory structure that meets the area’s economic and environmental needs. EPA is proud to work with Maricopa County and Arizona to promote prosperity while fulfilling the agency’s core mission of protecting human health and the environment.
The agency will hold a 30-day public comment period. EPA’s proposed approval of Rule 204 is available here.
Background
Under the CAA, EPA established the 2015 Ozone NAAQS at 70 parts per billion.  
On March 23, 2026, EPA finalized a determination not to reclassify the Phoenix-Mesa area from “Moderate” to “Serious” nonattainment under the 2015 NAAQS. Citing Section 179B of the CAA, EPA found that the Phoenix-Mesa area would have met federal ozone air quality standards by its August 3, 2024, deadline had it not been for emissions coming to the area from outside the U.S. The agency’s decision will ensure that manufacturers and citizens in the Phoenix-Mesa area are not punished for emissions out of their control.
title: EPA Administrator Zeldin Proposes Approving Another Innovative Plan in Maricopa County to Help Manufacturing and Economic Growth While Ensuring Clean Air

JACKSON, MS – A Meridian, Mississippi man pleaded guilty on October 5, 2026 to being a convicted felon in possession of a firearm.

According to court documents and statements made in open court, Anteiar Martin, 36, was found in possession of two firearms during the execution of a search warrant on July 30, 2020 at a residence in Meridian.

Martin pleaded guilty to an indictment alleging that he had violated Title 18, United States Code, Section 922(g)(1). He is scheduled to be sentenced on February 5, 2027 and faces a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

U.S. Attorney J.E. Baxter Kruger of the Southern District of Mississippi; and Special Agent in Charge Joshua Jackson of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) made the announcement.

The ATF and the East Mississippi Drug Task Force are investigating the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Amber Jones, Matthew W. Allen, Charles W. Kirkham, and Adam T. Stuart are prosecuting the case.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. REP. HOYLE CONDUCTS OVERSIGHT AT TACOMA ICE FACILITY
Eugene, OR – Today, Congresswoman Val Hoyle and her staff conducted an oversight visit at a United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility in Tacoma, Washington, where constituents are being detained. After the visit, Rep. Hoyle released the following statement:
"Constituents in my district are footing a nearly $1,500-per-person bill for illegal mass deportations," said Rep. Hoyle. "This is a cruel waste of resources and not what people voted for. Today in Tacoma, we were checking on community members to ensure they have legal representation, healthcare and access to food and information.”
If you have questions about immigration or know someone who is in detention, contact our office at (541) 465-6732 or hoyle.house.gov.
Background
People in Oregon’s Fourth Congressional District are spending $1,483 per person to fuel the Administration’s mass deportation campaign. Rep. Hoyle is committed to fighting for a system that honors due process and focuses enforcement on those who have committed violent crimes, not tearing away innocent people from their families, jobs and communities.
Some of her recent legislative actions include:
- Cosponsoring the VISIBLE Act and the Preventing Authoritarian Policing Tactics on America's Streets Act, which require federal law enforcement to have clear identification and stop unmarked arrests
- Cosponsoring the Dignity for Detained Immigrants Act and Stop Inhumane Conditions in ICE Detention Act, which mandates strict detention standards and protects people’s civil and human rights
- Cosponsoring the Access to Counsel Act, which ensures detainees can speak with legal counsel
- Cosponsoring the Immigration Court Due Process Protection Act, which ends the arrest of people for just showing up to their scheduled immigration court hearings
- Cosponsoring the DIGNIDAD (Dignity) Act, a comprehensive immigration reform package that would increase border security while expanding legal immigration
- Cosponsoring the DRAIN Act to repeal H.R. 1’s $75 billion slush fund to support the administration’s deportation agenda

CLEVELAND – A 36-year-old career offender has been sentenced for trafficking fentanyl and cocaine throughout Northeast Ohio.

Dustin Young, of Lorain, was sentenced by U.S. District Court Judge John R. Adams to 327 months (27.25 years) in prison after pleading guilty in May to:

Possession with Intent to Distribute Fentanyl

Possession with Intent to Distribute Cocaine

Possessing a Firearm in Furtherance of a Drug Trafficking Crime

Felon in Possession of a Firearm and Ammunition; prior convictions include Attempted Felonious Assault and Domestic Violence in 2023, and Felonious Assault and Unlawful Discharge of a Firearm into a Habitation in 2014.

He was also ordered to serve 10 years of supervised release after imprisonment.

According to court documents and evidence presented before the judge, federal agents were investigating suspected drug trafficking activity in Lorain County and Young was identified. On Jan. 30, 2026, investigators executed a search warrant at his home and seized three handguns, two rifles, approximately 34 grams of fentanyl and 36 grams of cocaine, more than 80 Bupreorphine Nalozone sublingual films, several fentanyl patches, digital scales, cellphones, and $3,325.00 in cash. Cocaine and fentanyl were discovered in kitchen oven mitts. Firearms were hidden throughout the residence, including one magazine with ammunition found in a baby basinet.

This case was investigated by the FBI Cleveland Division and the Lorain Police Department.

The prosecution was led by Assistant United States Attorney Scott C. Zarzycki for the Northern District of Ohio.
title: Fentanyl and Cocaine Trafficker Sentenced to 27 Years in Prison

On September 21, 2026, First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III traveled to Guatemala for a two-day conference along with a delegation from the Department of Justice (DOJ) to discuss with Guatemala President Bernardo Arévalo, Guatemala Attorney General Gabriel García Luna, and Guatemala Minister of the Interior Marco Antonio Villeda Sandoval collaborative ways to assist Guatemala in eradicating cartels from its country who traffic drugs and humans into the United States. The historic meeting was sponsored by the United States Embassy in Guatemala and was hosted by Chargé d’Affaires Jorgan Andrews, in coordination with the Office of Overseas Prosecutorial Development, Assistance and Training (OPDAT), which is a program within the DOJ's Criminal Division that helps foreign countries improve their criminal justice systems.

The delegation from the DOJ was led by Acting Assistant Attorney General Brian Skaret, Joint Task Force Alpha (JTFA) Director Jay Bauer, and Joint Task Force Vulcan (JTFV) Senior Advisor Gilberto Guerrer Jr. United States Attorneys representing border districts attended from the Southern District of California, District of Arizona, District of New Mexico, Western District of Texas, Northern District of Texas, Southern District of Texas, Eastern District of Texas, Southern District of Florida, along with representatives from the Drug Enforcement Administration, Federal Bureau of Investigation and Homeland Security Investigations assigned to the U.S. Embassy in Guatemala.

JTFA is a joint initiative by the DOJ and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) created to dismantle dangerous transnational human smuggling and trafficking networks. JTFV is a DOJ federal law enforcement initiative created to dismantle and destroy transnational gangs like MS-13 and has been expanded to target other violent networks like Tren de Aragua.

On September 22, 2026, First Assistant United States Attorney Sarcone traveled to the Presidential Palace and met with Guatemala President Bernardo Arévalo to discuss how the Mexican cartels have expanded into Guatemala. The meeting focused on the collaboration both countries will have moving forward to identify cartel members and stop the trafficking before it reaches U.S. borders. Later that day, First Assistant United States Attorney Sarcone spoke to the Guatemalan press at a press briefing, which was covered by many Guatemalan press outlets including Prensa Libre .

On September 23, 2026, at the Salon Amate Conference Center, First Assistant United States Attorney Sarcone gave a 15-minute PowerPoint presentation to illustrate the challenges faced in the Northern District of New York with the Akwesasne Mohawk Tribal lands and Canadian border, which is considered the most serious threat to national security of any border today in the United States of America. Sarcone stated, “Since taking over leadership in the Northern District of New York, I have made it a priority to fight back against transnational networks who think they can bring their crimes to this district. Building these strong foreign partnerships to fight transnational crime, corruption, and terrorism before it reaches U.S. soil is instrumental in this fight. This office will persistently pursue those who endanger human life through smuggling and trafficking activities and will continue to support our Guatemalan partners. This meeting shows the power of bringing together prosecutors, agents, and international partners to target and dismantle some of the most dangerous international criminal networks. My office will not stop until these groups are eliminated.”

John A. Sarcone III is the First Assistant United States Attorney for the Northern District of New York. United States Attorney’s Offices conduct most of the trial work in which the United States is a party. The Northern District of New York encompasses 32 counties in Northern and Central New York, covering more than 30,000 square miles, with over 300 miles of border with Canada.

Presidential Palace front row (l) to (r): Attorney General Gabriel Estuardo Garcia Luna, Ministry of Governance Marco Antonio Villeda Sandoval, President Cesar Bernardo Arevalo De Leon, Charge d’Affaires Jorgan K. Andrews, Acting Deputy Assistant Attorney General Brian Skaret, OPDAT Director Erik Peterson.

Middle row (l) to (r): First Assistant USA John Sarcone of NDNY, USA Timothy Courchaine of DAZ, USA Aaron Reitz of SDTX, USA Ryan Raybould of NDTX, USA Jay Combs of EDTX.

New York and New Jersey Housing Innovations Spotlighted at HUD’s Innovative Housing Showcase
October 6, 2026
Region II Administrator Jason Loughran and Senior Advisor Barbara Gruson Visit Assembly OSM's Modular Structure Models
NEW YORK - U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) spotlighted multiple housing innovations and resources from New York and New Jersey during the sixth annual Innovative Housing Showcase, held September 22-24 on the National Mall. This year’s theme, “Made in America,” highlighted American ingenuity and innovative approaches to expanding housing affordability and homeownership.
“HUD spotlighted several local companies at its Innovative Housing Showcase that are building new housing to expand homeownership opportunities for Americans,” said Region II Administrator Jason Loughran. “These affordable options show how our region can help meet the housing needs in New York and New Jersey and across our nation.”
HUD’s “Made in America” Showcase spotlighted American builders, manufacturers, and innovators’ modern technologies and creative housing solutions that are expanding housing supply, lowering construction costs, and putting affordable homeownership back in reach for hardworking Americans. The Showcase featured a variety of full-scale housing models including manufactured, 3D printed, and modular homes built by American companies from across the nation.
Examples from New York and New Jersey
A national map of American universities with offsite construction education programs, drawn from the Accrediting Body for Offsite Construction Education’s (ABOCE, New York) national census.
A scale model and graphical materials of two modular structures from Assembly OSM (New York), built on the company’s platform of predesigned, engineered building elements that assemble quickly and cost-effectively.
A tabletop exhibit introducing “.CTO – The File That Knows What Your House Is Made Of” from the Center for Offsite Construction at the New York Institute of Technology School of Architecture and Design (CFOC at NYIT, New York). The .CTO file describes an entire purchasable unit in one file.
A model print of a wall section built by automated formwork and robotics from Verustruct (New Jersey).
“The Grande Arbor,” a two-bedroom manufactured home from Cavco Homes and UMH Properties (New Jersey). This home is the first manufactured house built to the HUD code without a permanent steel chassis.
Follow @SecretaryTurner on X, FB, and Instagram.
title: New York and New Jersey Housing Innovations Spotlighted at HUD’s Innovative Housing Showcase

COLUMBUS, Ohio – Miguel Camarena-Salazar, 37, of Mexico, was taken into federal custody after being charged by a federal grand jury of felony reentry of a removed alien.

Camarena-Salazar is scheduled to appear in federal court today at 12:15pm for a detention hearing.

In February 2026, Camarena-Salazar was convicted of abduction in Delaware County, Ohio. Camarena-Salazar was sentenced to a term of imprisonment and is required to register as a sex offender under Ohio law. Earlier this month, a federal grand jury indicted Camarena-Salazar on the immigration offense before he finished his state prison sentence.

According to the federal indictment, Camarena-Salazar was previously removed from the United States on three prior occasions in August 2015, December 2015 and June 2016.

Illegally reentering the United States is a federal crime punishable by up to two years in prison.

Dominick S. Gerace II, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Ohio; and Jeremy Pierczynski, Acting Special Agent in Charge, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s (ICE) Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Detroit announced the charges. Assistant United States Attorney Justin C. Sheridan is representing the United States in this case.

An indictment merely contains allegations, and defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law.

# # #
title: Grand jury indicts Mexican illegal alien sex offender with illegally reentering United States

CONCORD – Webster resident Dale G. Stewart, 57, was sentenced today by Chief U.S. District Court Judge Samantha D. Elliott to 60 months in federal prison for building and detonating pipe bombs in Weare in April of 2023, U.S. Attorney Erin Creegan announces. Stewart was also sentenced to three years of supervised release following completion of his incarceration.

Stewart pleaded guilty in April to three counts of possessing an unregistered firearm, specifically a destructive device. According to the plea agreement and statements made in court, Stewart detonated two pipe bombs on Dustin Tavern Road and Sugar Hill Road in Weare, New Hampshire, on the evening of April 26 and on the morning of April 27, 2023. As part of the emergency response to these explosions, on the evening of April 27, 2023, law enforcement agents located and searched Stewart’s vehicle on South Stark Highway in Weare, where they recovered an undetonated pipe bomb, constructed of white PVC pipe, with glued end caps, wrapped in black electrical tape, with a green hobby fuse protruding from one of the end caps. The undetonated pipe bomb contained more than 4 ounces of an explosive material, consistent with the manufacturing of the two pipe bombs that Stewart had detonated earlier. During police questioning, Stewart indicated he built these destructive devices at his home in Webster.

“This defendant is a dangerous individual, who deployed and detonated explosives that could have taken the lives of many people, and who will now be serving years behind bars,” said Erin Creegan, U.S. Attorney for the District of New Hampshire. “We are grateful for the quick actions of the Weare Police and the partnership with the ATF and all state and federal agencies who brought Mr. Stewart to justice. We will continue to prosecute violent individuals who put the safety of our communities at risk.”

“Dale Stewart manufactured and detonated explosive devices across the Weare, New Hampshire area, unlawfully possessed additional firearms and explosive material, and tried to flee to avoid prosecution,” said Thomas A. Greco, Special Agent-in-Charge for the New England region of the federal Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF). “It is clear Stewart is a danger to our community, and today’s sentence is necessary to protect the public. This investigation required timely and efficient cooperation between ATF and partner agencies to identify, locate, and arrest Stewart. ATF is grateful for, and proud of, these partnerships which greatly enhance public safety across New Hampshire. We specifically recognize the contributions of New Hampshire Department of Insurance Fraud Unit Director Brendhan Harris, who was integral to this investigation, and who sadly passed away before the conclusion of this case.”

The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives; the Weare Police Department; and the Federal Protective Service led the investigation. Valuable assistance was provided by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the New Hampshire State Police, the Bow and Webster Police Departments, the State of New Hampshire Department of Insurance, and the U.S. Marshals Service. Assistant U.S. Attorney Cesar Vega prosecuted the case.
title: Webster Man Sentenced to Five Years in Prison for Building and Detonating Pipe Bombs in Weare in 2023

text:
Krishnamoorthi Demands Answers on FDA Move to Rewrite Vaping Approval Rules, Blasts Weakening of Scientific Standards
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional Caucus to End Youth Vaping, today demanded answers from Food and Drug Administration Acting Commissioner Kyle Diamantas over FDA’s September 28 announcement that it is considering new rulemaking to replace the 2021 regulations governing approval of new tobacco products, pressing the agency over whether the move could weaken the scientific standards manufacturers must meet.
Krishnamoorthi is also demanding to know whether FDA discussed potential changes with tobacco manufacturers, industry associations, or parties challenging the current rules before announcing its review, and is seeking communications between agency officials and Altria, Reynolds American, their subsidiaries and representatives, and other parties challenging the framework.
FDA announced its review less than four weeks after Altria subsidiaries NJOY and Helix Innovations sued the agency over the current Premarket Tobacco Product Application framework. FDA itself cited recent litigation challenging the framework, along with the widespread illicit tobacco market, in explaining its decision to consider replacing the rule.
“The widespread sale of illegal products is an enforcement problem,” Krishnamoorthi wrote. “It should not become a justification for lowering the evidentiary requirements manufacturers must satisfy before FDA authorizes their products.”
Krishnamoorthi also raised concerns about the review in light of FDA’s recent authorization of flavored e-cigarette products. In May, the agency authorized Glas products in mango and blueberry flavors despite FDA data indicating that fruit-flavored e-cigarettes are the most popular flavor among youth. The letter notes that the FDA Center for Tobacco Products did not require the manufacturer to demonstrate that the flavors provided an added benefit to adults attempting to transition from combustible products, and that former FDA Commissioner Marty Makary reportedly resigned in part amid political interference surrounding the authorization.
FDA then authorized additional JUUL products on August 28, including a JUUL2 menthol product.
“FDA acknowledged that the menthol product carries risks ‘including youth appeal,’ but concluded that its benefits to adults who smoke outweighed those risks,” Krishnamoorthi wrote. “Exactly one month later, FDA announced that it may replace the broader framework governing applications for new tobacco products.”
Krishnamoorthi concluded:
“The FDA’s job is to protect public health, not make it easier for tobacco companies to evade rigorous scientific review. The agency should crack down on companies selling illegal products, not use their lawbreaking as a rationale for weakening safeguards governing products seeking FDA authorization.”
Krishnamoorthi requested written responses by October 20, 2026, to the following questions:
- Which specific provisions of the 2021 PMTA rule is FDA considering changing or eliminating, and what evidence supports each potential change?
- Will FDA commit that any replacement framework will not lower the scientific evidentiary bar manufacturers must meet to demonstrate that marketing their products is appropriate for the protection of public health? If not, why not?
- Did FDA discuss potential changes to the 2021 PMTA rule with any tobacco product manufacturer, industry association, or party challenging the 2021 PMTA rule before announcing its review? Please identify each such entity and provide all communications since January 20, 2025, between FDA officials and those entities. Please also provide all communications since January 20, 2025, between FDA officials and Altria, Reynolds American, their subsidiaries or representatives, and any other party challenging the rule concerning the PMTA framework or potential changes to it.
- How does the existence of a widespread illicit market justify changes to the regulatory requirements governing products seeking lawful authorization? What connection has FDA identified between illegal sales and the scientific evidence manufacturers should be required to provide before receiving authorization?
- What additional enforcement actions will FDA take, in coordination with the Department of Justice and U.S. Customs and Border Protection, to remove unauthorized e-cigarettes from the U.S. market?
The full letter is available here.
Congressman Krishnamoorthi has led congressional efforts to combat youth vaping and hold tobacco companies accountable. In 2019, he launched the first congressional investigation into youth vaping, exposing JUUL’s marketing tactics and pushing legislation to ban flavored e-cigarettes and close the synthetic nicotine loophole. He has since led bipartisan efforts urging federal agencies to crack down on illegal flavored vapes and launched an investigation into illicit vaping products from China advertised to children. In 2025, Krishnamoorthi and Congresswoman Celeste Maloy (R-UT), his fellow co-chair of the Congressional Caucus to End Youth Vaping, called on FDA to strengthen enforcement as more than 6,000 flavored products remained on the market. Most recently, Krishnamoorthi helped introduce the bipartisan PROTECT Act to strengthen federal efforts to prevent and reduce youth e-cigarette use.
title: Krishnamoorthi Demands Answers on FDA Move to Rewrite Vaping Approval Rules, Blasts Weakening of Scientific Standards
