WASHINGTON – Melvin Green, 27, of the District of Columbia, was sentenced today in U.S. District Court to 60 months in prison in connection with his role in a 2023 kidnapping that later resulted in the deaths of two men, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

Green, aka “Fat Goat,” pleaded guilty on Jan. 5, 2026, before Judge Coleen Kollar-Kotelly to a charge of accessory after the fact kidnapping. In addition to the 60-month prison term, Judge Kollar-Kotelly ordered Green to serve three years of supervised release.

According to court papers, on June 6, 2023, Green and others traveled from the 4400 block of F Street SE to the Saint Yves nightclub on the 1200 block of Connecticut Ave. NW for a birthday celebration. After returning to F Street in the early morning hours of June 8, Green served as a lookout while his co-conspirators searched an unoccupied Mercedes SUV that was parked on F Street.

Shortly after 3:40 a.m., Green’s associates kidnapped the Mercedes’ owner, dragging him from the driver’s seat and capturing a second victim. The individuals removed the victims’ clothing and confined them inside the Mercedes to prevent them from fleeing. As the kidnapping unfolded, an individual passed a firearm to Green, who tucked the gun into his waistband and walked away.

Without Green, the individuals drove to a nearby area where they threatened and assaulted the victims at gunpoint. The individuals then drove one of the victims into Maryland. About 4:40 a.m., the group arrived at an apartment complex in Suitland, Maryland, where one of the victims had a residence and burglarized the victim’s apartment. An hour later, the group arrived at another of the victim’s apartments in Waldorf where the group staged an armed robbery.

About 5:45 a.m., surveillance cameras recorded three individuals engaging in a shootout with the victim. The shootout left the victim and one of the co-conspirators fatally wounded. About 6:45 a.m., first responders found the victim’s Mercedes engulfed in flames in Capitol Heights, Maryland.

This case was investigated by the FBI’s Washington Field Office’s Violent Crimes Task Force and Safe Streets Task Force, the Charles County Sheriff’s Office, the Metropolitan Police Department and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Maryland.

The matter was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys John Crabb Jr. and Anthony Scarpelli of the Violent Crimes and Narcotics Trafficking section of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia.

Ongoing Review Ensures Sanctions Remain Targeted, Effective, and Current
WASHINGTON—Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) took another major action in its sanctions modernization effort, announced by Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent in May. Today’s action removed from OFAC’s sanctions lists 125 individuals and entities, consistent with current economic, national security, and foreign policy priorities. OFAC also updated 22 list entries to facilitate and enhance compliance screening.
Those removed include deceased individuals, defunct companies, and list entries lacking sufficient information for robust compliance screening. As with any removal from its sanctions lists, and consistent with prior sanctions modernization actions, OFAC conducted interagency review to ensure that today’s removals would not harm U.S. foreign policy or national security interests.
PRIORITIZING SANCTIONS IMPACT AND SUCCESS
As Secretary Bessent has outlined, the goal of Treasury’s sanctions modernization effort is to ensure U.S. sanctions remain targeted, effective, and aligned with U.S. economic, foreign policy, and national security priorities. The Trump Administration is measuring the success of its sanctions in terms of effect, impact, and benefit—not just based on the number of names Treasury places on a list.
Today’s action is part of this broader effort to streamline sanctions for greater efficiency and effectiveness, including through the review of sanctions programs that no longer support U.S. national security priorities. For example, on September 18, OFAC removed sanctions on six individuals and entities designated pursuant to a 2021 Ethiopia-related national emergency and sanctions program, which was not renewed because the circumstances that led to the underlying national emergency have changed such that the United States no longer requires the Ethiopia sanctions program to advance U.S. interests.
Sanctions list entries without appropriate identifying information can hamper private sector screening efforts by producing false positive matches. These may require financial institutions and businesses to spend considerable time on manual review and detract from compliance investigations that are consistent with current national security priorities. Accordingly, alongside today’s delistings, OFAC’s list updates have added new identifiers and removed outdated ones; this will further reduce compliance screening burden.
MODERNIZING SANCTIONS RECONSIDERATION
The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate persons and add them to the SDN List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List when appropriate and consistent with the law.
For information on the process for seeking removal from an OFAC sanctions list, including the SDN List, please refer to How to Request Removal from an OFAC Sanctions List | Office of Foreign Assets Control. The recently released Reconsideration Portal enables persons and property on an OFAC sanctions list—or their authorized representatives—to submit delisting petitions and request certain information underlying their sanctions determinations.

title: Treasury Announces Third Round of Sanctions Removals, Updates in Modernization Initiative

CFTC Issues No-Action Letter for DCMs Regarding Converting Existing Perpetual-Style Broad-Based Security Index Futures into True Perpetual Futures
October 05, 2026
WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s Division of Market Oversight today announced it has issued no-action relief to designated contract markets seeking to convert their existing perpetual style broad-based security index futures contracts into true broad-based security index perpetual futures.
According to the letter, DCMs may remove expiration dates from their existing broad-based security index futures perpetual style futures contracts and implement these amendments to convert them into true broad-based security index perpetual futures contracts effective upon the satisfaction of certain customer protection and procedural conditions in the letter. These include soliciting feedback from market participants with open positions; providing advance notice and an opportunity to exit positions; offering appropriate risk disclosures; and ensuring that no other material contract terms are modified.
DCMs must also file the amendments under CFTC Regulations 40.5 or 40.6 and certify compliance with all conditions.
The no action positions in this letter expire on October 20, 2026.

BIRMINGHAM, Ala. – A Jefferson County man has been sentenced for his role in a conspiracy to kidnap an individual in exchange for payment of a drug debt, announced U.S. Attorney Phillip W. Williams Jr.

U.S. District Court Judge Anna M. Manasco sentenced Amarion Dewayne Jackson, 20, of Center Point, Alabama, to 235 months in prison followed by five years of supervised release. In April, Jackson pleaded guilty to conspiracy to kidnap and kidnapping.

Also in April, Jackson’s co-defendant, Korbyn Markeith Williams, 21, of Alabaster, Alabama, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to kidnap, kidnapping, and receipt of ransom money. Williams is set for sentencing on January 13, 2027.

“The U.S. Attorney’s Office will not tolerate those who bring violence and fear into our communities. This sentence sends a clear message: those who commit violent crimes will be prosecuted and held accountable for their actions,” said U.S. Attorney Williams. “We commend our law enforcement partners for their dedication and tireless efforts to ensure that the victim was recovered safely and that this dangerous defendant was brought to justice.”

“The FBI will not tolerate individuals who attempt to terrorize our communities through violence. The 235-month federal prison sentence and five years of supervised release imposed on Amarion Jackson for conspiracy to kidnap and kidnapping underscore our unwavering resolve,” said David R. Fitzgibbons, Special Agent in Charge, FBI Birmingham. “Those who plot or carry out acts designed to create chaos or instill fear will be met with an immediate, coordinated, and forceful law enforcement response. We are grateful for our law enforcement partners whose dedication ensures that dangerous offenders are identified, apprehended, and brought to justice. Our message is clear: if you threaten the safety of our communities, we will act swiftly and decisively.”

According to court documents, in January 2025, Jackson and Co-defendant Williams kidnapped a victim at gunpoint from his apartment located in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, after a third party failed to pay them for a narcotics transaction.

The victim was not involved in the drug deal. Jackson and Williams, who were both armed with pistols, threatened to kill the victim and demanded at least $5,000 for his safe return. Williams digitally received $1,000 of ransom from the victim’s family. An individual called 911 to notify law enforcement that one of the kidnappers stated that if they did not get paid, they would shoot the victim.

Later, an officer with the Bessemer Police Department responded to a call at a store in Bessemer of an armed kidnapping involving a white car. The officer located the vehicle and activated her emergency lights. Williams and Jackson, who were there to meet the victim’s family to receive the ransom money in cash, were arrested and the victim was recovered unharmed. In the vehicle, officers found pistols, ammunition, two black ski masks, and gloves.

FBI investigated the case along with the Tuscaloosa Violent Crimes Unit, the West Alabama Narcotics Task Force, and the Bessemer Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Daniel S. McBrayer prosecuted the case.

Today, Congresswoman Suzan DelBene (WA-01) announced that she is filing a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to force the Trump administration to release unseen information on the Wasteful and Inappropriate Service Reduction (WISeR) program, which pays private companies to use AI to review Medicare claims.
Since the program began in January in Washington and five other states, patients have been left in severe pain and unable to access care prescribed by their doctors. In June, DelBene announced that the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) ordered the company administering WISeR in Washington to submit a corrective action plan for delays in reviewing claims following an audit. Neither the audit nor the corrective action plan has been released to Congress or the public. DelBene previously requested information on the model's performance from the administration and then moved to require CMS to release these documents through an amendment during a House Ways & Means Committee markup. The majority of Ways & Means Republicans rejected the amendment by an 18-19 vote.
DelBene announced her latest move to force the release of these documents and hold the administration accountable in an op-ed in the Everett Herald.
“Washington seniors have borne the brunt of this experimental program’s malfunctions,” DelBene wrote. “From January to March, over half of the claims submitted in Washington were denied and far exceeded the 72-hour decision deadline. This triggered an internal CMS audit and corrective action plan. This shouldn’t come as a surprise because the program pays these private companies for every claim they deny, which incentivizes them to reject more care.” 
“The audit and corrective action plan have never been released, which would further help inform lawmakers, health care providers, and patients about how WISeR is failing to function,” DelBene continued. “This stonewalling must end. That’s why I am filing a new FOIA request for these specific documents in addition to the audits and corrective action plans of any other private company participating in WISeR.” 
This effort follows a bombshell report from the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EEF) on the failures of WISeR that detailed widespread delays and denials, rushed implementation, and incentives for private companies reviewing claims to deny care. EFF obtained access to the documents uncovered in the report through a FOIA request and lawsuit. The report also revealed that the administration plans to expand WISeR to cancer treatments and other types of care despite clear, documented evidence of the program’s flaws. 
DelBene introduced legislation last November to repeal WISeR and has led multiple other legislative efforts to stop the program.
Read DelBene’s op-ed here. The text of the FOIA request can be found here.
title: DelBene Moves to Force Trump Administration to Release Files on AI Medicare Experiment

Rep. Neguse Leads Colleagues in Letter to State Department Urging Additional Support for Nepal Floods Response
Washington, D.C. — Today, Colorado Congressman Joe Neguse, Co-Chair of the Bipartisan Congressional Nepal Caucus, led a dozen colleagues in a letter to the United States Department of State, urging they provide additional aid to Nepal as the country recovers from devastating floods in the Trishuli River region.
In late August, a glacier collapse on the Nepal-China border, caused catastrophic flooding, destroying homes, workplaces, roads, bridges, and energy infrastructure. The floods killed 1,450 people and nearly 6,000 people are still missing, including 90 Americans.
In their letter, Neguse and his colleagues noted that the United States has been a longstanding partner in Nepal’s development and called on the State Department to provide much needed support and stability to the country as it recovers and eventually rebuilds.
Full text of the letter is available HERE and below.
It was signed by André Carson (IN-07), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), James McGovern (MA-02), Janice Schakowsky (IL-09), Tom Suozzi (NY-03), Emilia Sykes (OH-13), Dina Titus (NV-01), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Marc Veasey (TX-33), and Nydia Velázquez (NY-07).
October 1, 2026
The Honorable Marco Rubio
Secretary of State
U.S. Department of State
2201 C Street NW
Washington, DC 20520
Dear Secretary Rubio,
We write to respectfully request your administration provide further assistance to aid Nepal in its recovery efforts following the devastating floods in the Trishuli River region. Given the scale of this tragedy, we implore your department to act swiftly.
As you know, this unprecedented disaster has claimed at least 1,300 lives, with an estimated 5,000 people still missing—including 90 American citizens. Further, the destruction has left many in the region without access to clean drinking water, food, shelter, and other basic services, including thousands of children. As Nepal continues to recover, the U.S. is uniquely positioned to provide critical infrastructure support and essential supplies to aid these efforts.
The U.S. has been a longstanding partner in Nepal's development, supporting improvements in public health, education, infrastructure, and industry. Continued U.S. assistance would provide much needed stability to the country and help it to rebuild at this critical time.
As such, we urge the Department of State to work to assist search and rescue efforts across Nepal and to provide additional assistance to the country to ensure a speedy recovery.
Sincerely,
###
title: Rep. Neguse Leads Colleagues in Letter to State Department Urging Additional Support for Nepal Floods Response

FAA Funds Drone Research to Support Safe Integration
WASHINGTON, D.C. — The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) today announced it awarded $12 million to 19 companies for drone research and testing projects that will help safely expand drone operations in the National Airspace System.
These awards were made through the Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) Program. The program funds companies working with FAA-designated UAS Test Sites to test and evaluate technologies that support safe drone integration.
The awards advance the Unleashing American Drone Dominance Executive Order by supporting the full use of FAA UAS Test Sites to develop, test, and scale American drone technologies.
“The UAS Broad Agency Announcement Program gives us another way to directly work with industry and our test site partners on technologies that are critical to safe drone integration,” said FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford. “The research supported through this program will give us better data, help us identify and understand operational challenges, and inform how we safely integrate these aircraft into the National Airspace System.”
Companies and projects under the program include:
- General Atomics — ground systems to help drones avoid other aircraft
- NAVMAR — systems to help large drones fly safely
- SPS Aerial Remote Sensing — a test of drone visibility technology
- ANRA Technologies — tools to connect air taxi operations, vertiports, and flight procedures
- Devorto Corporation — long-range cargo drone service
- ANRA Technologies — tools to give drones a common altitude reference
- DroneUp LLC — a secure way to verify drone identity and approval to fly
- SPS Aerial Remote Sensing — a sensor system for drone traffic management and counter-drone operations
- SPS Aerial Remote Sensing — tools to measure sensor performance
- OneRadio Corporation — testing passive radar to help drones avoid other aircraft
- Censys Technologies Corp — testing satellite communications for long-range drone flights
- Frequentis USA — a drone technology demonstration
- ANRA Technologies — tools to connect drone traffic systems with traditional air traffic systems at airports
- ANRA Technologies — AI tools to identify different types of drones
- Skydweller — onboard systems to help large drones avoid other aircraft
- Aerial Vantage — tools to manage reserved airspace for drones in cities
- Lighthouse Avionics Inc. — surveillance tools for long-range drone routes
- ResilienX, Inc. — software to coordinate drone missions and resources
- Oklahoma State University — drone visibility technology under the Aero Aware project
There are currently nine FAA-designated UAS Test Sites:
- Alaska Center for Unmanned Aircraft Systems Integration, Alaska
- Northern Plains UAS Test Site, North Dakota
- New Mexico State University UAS Test Site, New Mexico
- State of Nevada UAS Test Site, Nevada
- New York UAS Test Site, New York
- Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi Autonomy Research Institute, Texas
- Mid-Atlantic Aviation Partnership, Virginia
- Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma, Oklahoma
- Indiana Economic Development Corporation, Indiana
More information is available on the FAA’s UAS Broad Agency Announcement Program webpage.
title: FAA Funds Drone Research to Support Safe Integration

NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA – A recently unsealed superseding indictment charged three men, HECTOR MARQUEZ MARQUEZ (“MARQUEZ”) , age 22, a resident of the Republic of Mexico, TONTA OCTAVE (“OCTAVE”), age 48, of Vacherie, Louisiana, and LAMONT WILLIAMS (“WILLIAMS”) , age 50, of New Orleans, with conspiracy to distribute, and possess with intent to distribute, over 5 kilograms of cocaine, in violation of 21 U.S.C. §§ 841(a)(1), (b)(1)(A) and 846, announced U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle. WILLIAMS and MARQUEZ are also each charged with possession with intent to distribute 5 kilograms of cocaine, in violation of Title 21, United States Code, Sections 841(a)(1) and 841(b)(1)(A).

MARQUEZ faces a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment of 10 years up to life imprisonment, a fine of up to $10,000,000, a term of supervised release of not less than 5 years and a $100 mandatory special assessment fee. WILLIAMS and OCTAVE each face a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment of 15 years up to life imprisonment, a fine of up to $20,000,000, a term of supervised release of not less than 10 years and a $100 mandatory special assessment fee per charged count.

U.S. Attorney Courcelle reiterated that the superseding indictment is merely a charge and that the guilt of the defendant must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt.

The case was investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration, Department of Homeland Security, Homeland Security Investigations, the St. John’s Parish Sheriff’s Office, the St. Charles Parish Sheriff’s Office and the Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries, Enforcement Division. Assistant United States Attorney Rachal Cassagne of the Narcotics Unit oversees the prosecution.

This case is brought pursuant to the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF New Orleans comprises agents and officers from the Department of Homeland Security, Federal Bureau of Investigations, Drug Enforcement Administration and Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Louisiana.

Rep. Gabe Vasquez Sends Letter to FAA Demanding Reversal of Decommissioning of Critical Air Safety Technology
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) partnered with Rep. Stansbury and Rep. Leger Fernández to urge the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to not decommission critical air safety technology used by the Double Eagle Airport II (DEII) in Albuquerque. The FAA recently initiated a study to decommission the Instrument Landing System (ILS) at the Double Eagle Airport without providing answers regarding the recent airspace closure and plane crash incidents in and around New Mexico airspace. Pilots in New Mexico use both ILS and GPS to land due to the unique challenges posed by flying commercial aircraft near military bases.
“We respectfully urge the FAA to maintain use of this critical technology given the unique demands of New Mexico that require aviation redundancy to maintain public safety and to provide our office with a briefing on airspace safety,” wrote the members. “In light of this change, the recent crash outside Ruidoso and other recent aviation incidents involving navigation technology issues, more information is needed before moving forward.”
The FAA recently began a study to determine whether ILS technology should be decommissioned at the DEII, which conducts tens of thousands of flights annually. ILS is a ground based guidance system for aircrafts typically used when pilots are unable to find the runway. It complements modern GPS-enabled navigation that only provides lateral guidance to the runway. While GPS-enabled navigation works in most conditions, New Mexico has its own set of unique airspace challenges due to nearby military bases that force a need for both ILS and GPS.
“The FAA has still not provided sufficient answers regarding the recent airspace closure in El Paso and plane crash in Ruidoso – and has still not shown that it is improving coordination with other agencies or ensuring that my constituents’ are safe,” said Vasquez. “In light of their recent failures, the public must have a lot more information before the FAA orders decommissioning any navigation safety tools or resources for our pilots.”
“DEII plays a critical role in our region’s aviation system as a reliever airport for the Sunport and an important facility for flight training and public safety operations. Maintaining ILS capability is essential to ensuring the airport can continue to serve these functions safely and effectively, particularly when reliable navigation is needed most,” said Manny Manriquez, Director of Aviation, City of Albuquerque.
Read the full letter HERE.
Rep. Vasquez continues to lead Congressional oversight efforts following multiple aviation incidents affecting southern New Mexico, including:
- Demanding answers from the Department of Defense and Department of Transportation on their coordination with each other to keep our skies safe.
- Securing an NTSB briefing on July 14 after demanding greater transparency and answers about the deadly Ruidoso plane crash.
- Pressing the FAA and Department of Defense for accountability following the February closure of El Paso airspace.
- Successfully secured passage of an amendment to the FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act requiring the Department of Defense to improve coordination with the FAA before testing military technologies that could impact civilian aviation.
###
title: Rep. Gabe Vasquez Sends Letter to FAA Demanding Reversal of Decommissioning of Critical Air Safety Technology

Media Note

Office of the Spokesman

October 5, 2026

The text of the following statement was released by the Governments of the United States of America and Japan.

Begin Text

Assistant to the President and Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy of the United States of America Michael Kratsios met with Minister of State for Science and Technology Policy of Japan Toshiharu Furukawa in Kyoto on October 4, 2026, to discuss the U.S.-Japan bilateral science and technology relationship and progress on the Memorandum of Cooperation Regarding the Technology Prosperity Deal Between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of Japan signed on October 28, 2025.

Recognizing that technological innovation continues to advance at an unprecedented pace worldwide, the United States and Japan reaffirmed the importance of further strengthening U.S.-Japan collaboration in strategic science and technology capabilities and standards to usher in the next Golden Age of Innovation to fortify freedom and prosperity for generations to come.

Both sides noted the following progress in strengthening U.S.-Japan science and technology cooperation:

The United States and Japan signed a Protocol amending and indefinitely extending the 1988 U.S.-Japan Agreement on Cooperation in Research and Development in Science and Technology with updated intellectual property protections, on October 2, 2026.

Separately, the United States and Japan committed to deepening cooperation, including through enhanced dialogue on Super Intelligence (SI) [1] , to work toward best practices for SI industry standards development as well as to advance a secure innovation ecosystem for trusted SI development and deployment.

The United States and Japan committed to advancing the adoption of trusted SI technologies and fostering a pro-innovation regulatory environment across the Indo-Pacific region. In this regard, the United States reaffirmed its $20 million commitment announced at the 2025 APEC Summit, and Japan expressed its intent to match the U.S. commitment.

In June 2026, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) and Japan’s Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) and Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) entered into a historic $1 billion strategic partnership, making Japan the first international partner in President Trump’s Genesis Mission. Since then, eleven joint scientific teams have launched, bringing together some of the world’s most advanced scientific facilities, computing resources, and research talent from twelve DOE National Laboratories, one DOE Office of Science User Facility, and twelve leading Japanese research institutions. These joint scientific teams are focused on continuing to create breakthroughs in quantum information science, fusion energy, biotechnology, advanced materials, particle physics, and autonomous laboratory systems.

The United States and Japan committed to increasing bilateral collaboration on physical SI, bringing together Japan’s strengths in hardware, industrial robotics manufacturing, and industrial data with the United States’ strength in physical SI models through bilateral exchange programs, joint research and development programs, joint grand challenges, and supply chain mapping.

In June 2026, U.S. Department of State (DOS), in partnership with Sandia National Laboratories, convened an exchange among Japanese academics and policymakers and leading U.S. research security experts on evolving risks and best practices for preventing the exploitation of sensitive research, in support of Japan’s research security guidelines launched in April 2026. DOS also partnered with the Middlebury Center for Nonproliferation Studies to provide reference materials for Japan’s institutions in the process of developing research security programs.

The U.S. National Telecommunications and Information Administration and Japan’s Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications committed to co-chair the Global Coalition on Telecommunications in 2027, with the aim of advancing our leadership on secure and resilient telecommunications network supply chains.

Both sides committed to advancing cooperation on digital connectivity in the Indo-Pacific region, including, where available, through the use of government financing and assistance that mobilizes the private sector.

Both sides advanced efforts for joint research and development projects on Beyond 5G/6G-relevant technologies through collaboration between Japan’s National Institute of Information and Communications Technology and the U.S. National Science Foundation.

Both sides welcomed Japan’s Rakuten Group and the U.S.-based AST SpaceMobile cooperation for the development and deployment of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite infrastructure.

Both sides advanced efforts to address vulnerabilities in pharmaceutical supply chains by identifying essential active pharmaceutical ingredients for an initial supply chain analysis to inform strategy for increased production of these medicines.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration and Japan’s Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency established an information-sharing platform on advanced manufacturing.

Recognizing that research cooperation in biotechnology is a key driver of resilient and secure innovation systems, the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, part of the U.S. National Institutes of Health, and the Japan Agency for Medical Research and Development advanced efforts to develop a joint Call for Proposals to establish collaborative biomedical research opportunities with the goal of increasing the range of available therapeutics and associated technologies.

Both sides committed to advancing cooperation to ensure secure supply chains in the quantum sector, strengthening measurement foundations and standards including through NMI-Q, and exploring collaboration on quantum sensing in healthcare.

U.S.-Japan fusion cooperation has strengthened across key areas of fusion science and technology, such as joint research at Japan’s JT-60SA, which starts plasma heating operation in 2026, and negative-triangularity research at the U.S. DIII-D National Fusion Facility. U.S.-Japan public-private partnerships are also accelerating progress toward commercial fusion, including a partnership between DOE’s Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) and Japan’s Kyoto Fusioneering, focused on fusion fuel-cycle and blanket development, which is establishing a new test facility, the UNITY-3, at ORNL and providing U.S. researchers access to the UNITY-1 in Japan.

On August 30, the U.S. National Aeronautics and Space Administration and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) celebrated the launch of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, confirming their commitment to strengthening their partnership in civil space. JAXA provided optical elements for the telescope and set up ground stations to receive mission data.

The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration and Japan’s National Space Policy Secretariat signed a Memorandum of Cooperation on Alignment of Launch and Re-entry Regulations on August 31 to advance interoperability for the two countries’ respective commercial space transportation industries.

The United States and Japan committed to close coordination and will hold follow-on consultations to further advance bilateral cooperation and explore additional collaborative opportunities in strategic science and technology capabilities under the U.S.-Japan Technology Prosperity Deal.

End Text

[1] In Japan, ‘super intelligence’ refers to ‘artificial intelligence.’

CHICAGO - Ohio homeowners and renters in Clermont, Franklin, Hamilton, Licking, Morgan, Muskingum, and Perry counties with uninsured damage to their primary home, personal property loss or disaster-related emergency needs due to the August storms, tornadoes and flooding may apply for FEMA assistance.
You should first file an insurance claim:
If you have homeowners, renters, or flood insurance, file a claim before applying for FEMA assistance. FEMA cannot duplicate benefits for losses covered by insurance. If your policy does not cover all your disaster expenses, you may be eligible for federal assistance.
FEMA Assistance:
FEMA may be able to help if you are displaced, have serious needs, need temporary lodging, require basic home repair costs, lost personal property or have other uninsured disaster-caused needs. The fastest way to apply is online at DisasterAssistance.gov or the Spanish language DisasterAssistance.gov/es.
You will need to provide the following information:
- Your contact information (phone number, current mailing address, email address, and damaged home address).
- Your Social Security number.
- A general list of damage and losses.
- Annual household income.
- Banking information if you choose direct deposit.
- If insured, the policy number or the agent and/or the company name.
If you need more information or additional help, call the FEMA Helpline at 1-800-621-3362 for assistance in multiple languages. If you use a relay service, captioned telephone or other service, give FEMA your number for that service. To view an accessible video on how to apply, visit What You Need to Know Before Applying for FEMA Assistance.

WASHINGTON – Two members of MS-13, a violent transnational criminal organization, were found guilty on Friday in U.S. District Court for conspiring to participate in racketeering activity, including murder and other charges stemming from their roles in killings and drug trafficking in the Washington, D.C. area, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

“These two MS-13 leaders ran a violent criminal enterprise fueled by murder, violence, and drug trafficking,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “One of these defendants even ordered hits from inside a prison in El Salvador. By the time these criminals get out of prison, they’ll be too old to think about murder and mayhem.”

“These two MS-13 leaders ran a violent criminal enterprise fueled by murder, violence, and drug trafficking,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “One of these defendants even ordered hits from inside a prison in El Salvador. By the time these criminals get out of prison, they’ll be too old to think about murder and mayhem.”

Moises Humberto Rivera-Luna, 56, of El Salvador, and Tokiro Rodas-Ramirez, 44, a dual citizen of Honduras and El Salvador, had been extradited to the United States to face these charges. Rivera-Luna was found guilty of RICO conspiracy, including murder and drug trafficking. Rodas-Ramirez was found guilty of RICO conspiracy, including murder and drug trafficking, as well as discharging a firearm during a crime of violence.

Joining U.S. Attorney Pirro in the announcement of the verdict were Homeland Security Investigations Washington, D.C. Acting Special Agent in Charge Kai Wah Chan, and Interim Chief Jeffery W. Carroll of the Metropolitan Police Department.

“This conviction marks the conclusion of a long, arduous journey towards justice. Rivera-Luna and Rodas-Ramirez have finally been found guilty of running a violent enterprise that committed horrific crimes in our communities. From murder to drug trafficking, their chapter of MS-13 terrorized innocent residents throughout the District. HSI special agents and our law enforcement partners used their skills, resources, and authorities to work to bring them to justice,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Kai Wah Chan of Homeland Security Investigations Washington, D.C.. “HSI leverages our international footprint to dismantle transnational criminal organizations at home and abroad to keep our communities safe.”

According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, MS-13 operates in the United States and Central America. The gang engages in racketeering activity, including murder, narcotics distribution, extortion, robberies, obstruction of justice, and other crimes. The gang has numerous rules. The primary rules are (1) kill rival gang members on sight, and (2) do not cooperate with law enforcement.

Rivera-Luna, aka “Viejo Santos,” was an MS-13 leader in prison in El Salvador. From prison, Rivera-Luna directed the activities of the Normandies, an MS-13 clique that operated in El Salvador and the Washington, D.C. area. Members of the Normandie clique would collect money through membership dues, extortion of legitimate and illegitimate businesses, and narcotics distribution to purchase guns and other weapons for the gang and to support imprisoned leaders and members, including Rivera-Luna.

While he was in prison, Rivera-Luna authorized kill orders on two MS-13 members for breaking MS-13 rules. At Rivera-Luna’s direction, MS-13 members stabbed to death Victim 1 on Nov. 6, 2008, in Northwest Washington, D.C. MS-13 members stabbed Victim 1 at least 20 times. Rivera-Luna also ordered the slaying of a second victim. On March 31, 2010, Victim 2 was found shot to death at a park in Montgomery County, Maryland, after he brought a knife to an MS-13 meeting, which was a violation of MS-13’s rules.

The government’s evidence demonstrated that Rodas-Ramirez, aka “Perverso,” was the second-in-command of the Normandie clique in the Washington metropolitan area. Rodas-Ramirez participated in a murder and assault involving suspected rival gang members. On April 7, 2008, Rodas-Ramirez was driving his vehicle in the D.C. area with other MS-13 members, when they saw a suspected rival gang member. Rodas-Ramirez stopped his vehicle while another MS-13 member exited and shot Victim 3 multiple times. A Metropolitan Police Officer happened to be near the shooting and was able to respond immediately and provide care to Victim 3, who survived.

On July 29, 2008, about three months later, Rodas-Ramirez and other MS-13 members found another suspected rival gang member, Victim 4, at an apartment complex in Riverdale, Maryland. They believed Victim 4 was a member of a rival gang that threatened Rodas-Ramirez’s girlfriend’s sister. MS-13 members followed Victim 4, who was riding a bicycle, and shot him multiple times; Victim 4 died of his injuries.

Rodas-Ramirez was arrested on March 18, 2022 and extradited from Honduras on Aug. 12, 2022. Rivera-Luna was arrested pursuant to the extradition request on Aug. 28, 2022. Because he was serving a prison sentence in Guatamala at the time, Rivera-Luna was extradited on March 4, 2025.

Rivera-Luna, who was convicted of RICO conspiracy, is scheduled to be sentenced on Jan. 7, 2027.

Rodas-Ramirez, who was convicted of RICO conspiracy, assault with a dangerous weapon in aid of racketeering, and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a violent crime, is scheduled to be sentenced on Jan. 7, 2027.

A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

The case was investigated by HSI-Washington D.C. and the MPD. Assistance was provided by the Montgomery County and the Prince George’s County, Maryland, Police Departments, the Police Departments of Fairfax and Herndon Counties in Virginia, the FBI, and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia. The Governments of Guatemala and Honduras provided critical assistance.

This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Nihar Mohanty of the Violent Crime and Narcotics Trafficking Section and Mark Levy of the Federal Major Crimes Section in the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia.

The Criminal Division’s Office of International Affairs provided significant assistance in securing the arrests and extraditions of Rivera-Luna and Rodas-Ramirez from Guatemala and Honduras, respectively.

This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion.

The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children.

The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Washington D.C. comprises agents and officers from numerous federal agencies with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia.

MEDFORD, Ore.—A Medford, Oregon, man pleaded guilty today to distributing fentanyl and admitted that it caused the death of another person.

Richard Scott Samuels, 60, has pleaded guilty to an indictment charging possession with the intent to distribute fentanyl, announced the U.S. Attorney Scott E. Bradford for the District of Oregon.

According to court documents, a death was reported on May 15, 2025, and on August 6, 2025. Both were determined to be deaths due to a fentanyl overdose. Law enforcement investigated these deaths and learned that Samuels was alleged to be the supplier of the fentanyl that both the deceased had used.

On September 4, 2025, law enforcement arrested Samuels and seized from his person and residence, a phone, $5,332 cash, a handgun, and multiple drugs in approximate amounts; 283g fentanyl, 92g of heroin, 5g of meth, and 5g of cocaine.

On November 6, 2025, a federal grand jury in Medford returned an indictment charging Samuels with possession with intent to distribute fentanyl and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime.

Samuels faces a maximum sentence of 40 years in prison, a $5,000,000 fine and four years of supervised release. He will be sentenced on December 17, 2026, before a U.S. district court judge.

As part of the plea agreement Samuels has agreed to forfeit any criminally derived proceeds and property used to facilitate his crimes identified by the government prior to sentencing.

This case was investigated by the FBI and Medford Area Drug and Gang Enforcement. It is being prosecuted by AUSA Sara Shaw.

AUSTIN, Texas – A federal jury in Austin convicted an Indian national for two counts related to wire fraud and money laundering, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas.

According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Bhavesh Kumar Thakkar, 45, was in the United States on a spousal visa. From at least September 2022 and continuing until Sept. 17, 2025, Thakkar conspired in a fraud scheme with co-defendants Rakesh Barot, Dhruv Rajeshbhai Mangukiya and Kishan Rajeshkumar Patel.

In his role, Thakkar served as a U.S.-based coordinator for the receipt and laundering of fraud proceeds in the form of cash and gold obtained from elderly victims across the country. The fraud proceeds were obtained by call center scammers based in India. He also personally received some of those funds from couriers such as Mangukiya and Patel. The funds were shipped to Los Angeles and New York before being laundered overseas. Thakkar was directly connected to over $150 million in fraud proceeds scammed from elderly victims across the United States.

“Foreign actors, both abroad and here in the United States, cannot be allowed to target Americans, especially our most vulnerable citizens,” said U.S. Attorney Simmons. “Many victims lose a significant portion of their life savings to these scammers, leaving victims vulnerable and hopeless. When we find them, we will do all we can to take from them the same sense of freedom and comfort they stole from their victims.”

“Protecting our elderly citizens from those who would defraud them out of their hard-earned money is a high priority for the FBI,” said FBI San Antonio Division Special Agent in Charge Daniel Faith. “This defendant was found guilty of working with others to scam a large number of vulnerable senior citizens out of millions of dollars. We’re grateful to all of our partners in this case, including numerous FBI Field Offices, Indian authorities via our Legat New Delhi and the Granite Shoals Police Department.”

In 2025, Mangukiya and Patel were sentenced to 97 months and 63 months in federal prison, respectively. Barot pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering and is awaiting sentencing.

The FBI and the Granite Shoals Police Department investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Keith Henneke and Brandy Gann are prosecuting the case.

Tacoma – Three residents of the South Sound region have now been sentenced to federal prison for their post office burglary scheme, announced Acting U.S. Attorney Charles Neil Floyd. Paula Jean Gamboa, 38 of Federal Way, Washington, was the last of three defendants sentenced today to 18 months in prison. Burglary ringleader Justin Tate, 37, of Tacoma, was sentenced in April 2026 to 50 months in prison and Gregory Foster, 60, of Port Orchard, Washington, was sentenced in May 2026 to two years in prison. The three were indicted by a federal grand jury in May 2025.

U.S. District Judge Benjamin H. Settle noted that crimes related to identity and mail theft are “tremendously disruptive to people’s lives,”

while also reflecting on the emotional harm suffered by victims. He ordered each of the defendants be on supervised release for three years following prison. Tate was ordered to pay $10,785 in restitution.

According to records in the case, Tate led the burglary crew that targeted post offices in the Puget Sound region. The break-ins spanned Kitsap, Thurston, Pierce, King, and Island Counties. The thieves kept cash and other valuables from the stolen mail. Tate went on to use identity and financial documents obtained from victims’ mail to commit bank fraud. The specific burglaries are these:

July 4, 2024, Tate and Foster break into the Olalla Post Office wearing face masks to obscure their identities.

July 8, 2024, Tate and Foster attempt to enter the restricted area of the Littlerock Post Office – they disconnect the security camera

but cannot breach a metal shutter into the restricted area.

but cannot breach a metal shutter into the restricted area.

July 9, 2024, Tate and Gamboa enter the Fox Island Post Office and steal mail from various post office boxes.

July 15, 2024, Foster breaks a window and enters the Anderson Island Contract Post Office and steal $3,000 in stamps, $100 in cash and about 100 postal money orders.

July 24, 2024, Tate enters the Vashon Island Post Office and steals mail from multiple post office boxes.

July 27, 2024, Tate and Foster force their way through the back door of the Snoqualmie Post Office and steal mail.

July 30, 2024, Tate and Gamboa steal mail from boxes inside the Preston Post Office.

July 31, 2024, Tate and Gamboa break into the Clinton Post Office on Whidbey Island and steal mail from post boxes and from a mail drop box.

Ringleader Justin Tate pleaded guilty to conspiracy and two counts of bank fraud. Tate opened a bank account in the name of one of the victims and then transferred or attempted to transfer more than $3,500 for his own use. He attempted to deposit more than $13,000 in fraudulent checks. Tate also ran up $7,200 in point-of-sale charges with a stolen debit card. Tate and Gamboa would go to area casinos after the burglaries to launder the stolen funds.

Gamboa was the last to be sentenced because she repeatedly fled pretrial supervision and custody. In asking for a 21-month sentence, prosecutors wrote to the court, “Gamboa’s crimes were carried out with little regard not only for the United States property they destroyed, but for the victims whose privacy was violated through these illegal activities. Arms full of mail representing hundreds of Washington citizens were swept up, to be opened and rifled through later – all so Gamboa and her co-conspirators could pocket their contents. Bank cards, checks, registrations, social security documents were taken and used by the defendants.”

The case was investigated by the U.S. Postal Inspection Service (USPIS). The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Victoria Cantore.

Davids Celebrates Opening of KCKCC Downtown Center, Highlighting Her Secured Investment for Workforce Training
KANSAS CITY, KS — Today, Representative Sharice Davids joined Kansas City Kansas Community College (KCKCC) leadership, local officials, and community partners for the official dedication of the new downtown Community Education, Health and Wellness Center. During the ceremony, Davids highlighted nearly $2 million in federal funding she secured to outfit KCKCC’s Automated Engineering Technology Program with state-of-the-art training equipment.
"If we want a future that is 'Made in Kansas,' we have to give our students the tools to actually build it right here at home," said Davids. "This new Downtown Center is a direct pipeline to good-paying jobs. I was proud to work across the aisle to deliver federal investments so KCKCC students can train on the exact, state-of-the-art automation systems used in high-tech manufacturing and defense today. This is about bypassing D.C. politics, setting our workers up to succeed, and keeping our local economy moving forward."
The $1.9 million secured by Davids equips KCKCC’s Automation Engineering Technology program with real-world machinery, preparing students directly for high-demand, high-wage roles in advanced manufacturing and logistics. By training on the exact, state-of-the-art automation systems used across modern industrial and defense sectors, students will gain the hands-on experience needed to transition seamlessly from the classroom straight into high-paying local careers.
Located in eastern Wyandotte County, the Downtown Center serves high school students from KCK Public Schools completing dual-enrollment degrees, adult learners obtaining GEDs or ESL certifications, and individuals entering specialized technical fields. The new facility, a public-private partnership between KCKCC, Swope Health, and Community America Credit Union, offers holistic education, healthcare, and career training services.
Overall U.S. manufacturing performance in 2026 has slowed compared to the rapid growth seen coming out of the pandemic in 2021 and 2022. Economic experts point to a growing technical skills gap as a primary roadblock holding back further domestic expansion. To bring critical supply chains back home, local companies urgently need workers trained on modern, automated systems. Investments like Davids’ directly bridge this gap, equipping Kansas workers with the hands-on skills required to drive the next wave of American manufacturing.

Reps. Carter, Matsui Introduce the 988 Crisis Workforce Response Act for Suicide Prevention Month
WASHINGTON, D.C. – In honor of Suicide Prevention Month, Congressman Troy A. Carter Sr. (D-LA) and Congresswoman Doris Matsui (D-CA) introduced the 988 Crisis Workforce Response Act. This legislation builds on existing behavioral health workforce training programs at the Health Resources & Services Administration (HRSA and Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) to include trained crisis professionals, improving recruitment and retention efforts for these critical members of the behavioral health care team.
“America is not only experiencing a mental health crisis – but a severe mental health workforce shortage,” said Congressman Carter. “Every year, millions of Americans rely on the 988 Crisis Line to connect them to care, to specialists, and to hope. But without a properly trained and substantial workforce, individuals with mental health needs aren’t getting the care they deserve. This commonsense legislation will ensure that our behavioral health professionals have the support and resources necessary to continue providing care to those who need it.”
“When someone calls 988, they are often reaching out on one of the hardest days of their life. We need to make sure there is a trained professional ready to answer that call and help them through what comes next,” said Congresswoman Matsui. “I’m proud to partner with Congressman Carter on this impactful legislative effort to build the behavioral health workforce communities need and turn 988 from a number people can call into a system that can truly respond when someone is in crisis.”
Background
Nationwide, 137 million Americans live in a Mental Health Professional Service Area, and many states specifically report they have a shortage of crisis care providers. Without dedicated recruitment and retention programs, we will continue to fall short of the workforce needs for a robust crisis care continuum.
The 988 Crisis Response Workforce Act builds on existing behavioral health workforce training programs at the Health Resources & Services Administration (HRSA) and Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) to include trained crisis professionals, improving recruitment and retention efforts for these critical members of the behavioral health care team.
Specifically, this bill:
- Directs the Secretary to collect data on the availability and shortage of crisis response professionals and facilities.
- Creates a $10 million pilot program to train professionals who provide crisis management services, including those delivered at crisis call centers, as part of a mobile crisis response team, or through a crisis receiving and stabilization program, as part of the Minority Fellowship Program,
- Authorizes $10 million to add crisis workforce training programs as part of the Behavioral Health Workforce Education and Training program.
The 988 Crisis Workforce Response Act was included in a larger 988 package – the 988 Implementation Act, which was introduced earlier this month. The 988 Implementation Act is cosponsored by Congressmembers Doris Matsui (CA-07), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Troy Carter (LA-02), Lori Trahan (MA-03), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Dan Goldman (NY-10), Don Beyer (VA-08), Jennifer McClellan (VA-04), Becca Balint (VT-AL), and Kim Schrier (WA-08). The comprehensive legislative package will provide states with federal resources to build the crisis response infrastructure behind the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.
Read the full bill text here.

Rep. Norma Torres Secures $25 Million For State Route -71 Gap Closure Project in Pomona
Torres previously urged the Department of Transportation to support the project, which will reduce congestion, improve safety, and strengthen a critical freight corridor
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Norma Torres (CA-35), a member of the Appropriations Subcommittee that oversees all federal transportation funding, announced that the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LA Metro) will receive $25 million in federal funding from the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) for Phase 2 of the State Route 71 (SR-71) Gap Closure Project in Pomona.
The funding, awarded through the DOT’s Fiscal Year 2026 Nationally Significant Multimodal Freight and Highway Projects (INFRA) Grant Program, will help upgrade the existing four-lane expressway between Interstate 10 (I-10) and Mission Boulevard into an eight-lane freeway. The project will add one high-occupancy vehicle lane and one mixed-flow lane in each direction, construct auxiliary lanes, replace aging railroad bridges, install soundwalls, and construct an ADA-compliant pedestrian overcrossing at 9th Street.
Congresswoman Torres previously wrote to U.S. Department of Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy in support of LA Metro’s application, emphasizing the project’s importance to commuters, public safety, the regional economy, and the movement of goods throughout Southern California.
“Anyone who drives the 71 knows how badly these improvements are needed,” said Congresswoman Torres. “I urged the Department of Transportation to support this project because families in Pomona and across the Inland Empire deserve safer roads, shorter commutes, and infrastructure that can keep up with our growing region. This $25 million investment will help eliminate a major bottleneck, improve the movement of goods, and strengthen a corridor that our communities and economy depend on every day. I am thrilled to see federal dollars coming home to move this critical project forward.”
“Metro is pleased to be receiving a $25 million INFRA grant from the U.S. Department of Transportation for the State Route 71 Gap Closure Project,” said Metro CEO Stephanie Wiggins. “We are grateful for the remarkably strong support for this project from Congresswoman Norma Torres, a senior member of the House Committee on Appropriations, Subcommittee on Transportation, Housing and Urban Development. This Measure M voter-approved project will significantly reduce congestion and travel times, improve safety and connectivity – all while enhancing the movements of goods and people across our region. I welcome this infusion of federal funding that will help complete this project and express my appreciation to the local, state, and federal stakeholders whose collaboration are making this project a reality.”
The SR-71 corridor connects communities across Los Angeles, San Bernardino, and Riverside counties and serves as an important route for commuters and freight movement. Phase 2 will address approximately two miles between I-10 and Mission Boulevard and help create consistent improvements along SR-71 from SR-91 to I-10.
The INFRA program provides competitive federal funding for highway and freight projects of national and regional significance that improve the safety, efficiency, and reliability of moving people and goods.
###
title: Rep. Norma Torres Secures $25 Million For State Route -71 Gap Closure Project in Pomona

LAS VEGAS – A Las Vegas man was sentenced today to 33 months in prison for engaging in the business of dealing firearms without a Federal Firearms License and for distributing fentanyl pills. The government recommended a sentence of 33 months in prison.

“The intersection of unlicensed firearms trafficking and illicit narcotic distribution represents one of the most severe threats to public safety in our communities,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “This case highlights the critical importance of coordinated law enforcement efforts to disrupt criminal networks before they can inflict further harm. Our office remains firmly committed to working alongside federal and local partners to hold individuals accountable who traffic in weapons, distribute deadly substances, and attempt to obstruct the justice system. We will continue to use every tool at our disposal to remove these compounding threats from our streets and protect the public.”

“The suspect in this case sold multiple firearms without a Federal Firearms License (FFL), as well as, distributed narcotics,” said Assistant Special Agent in Charge Alex Buenaventura, San Francisco Field Division, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF). “Individuals who choose to operate in criminal activity will be prosecuted. This case serves as an example of that. ATF is grateful to have worked with our partners on this investigation to bring this dangerous conduct to justice.”

According to court documents, between October 4, 2024, and December 20, 2024, Ty’Shaun Meeks sold an AR-556 with a 30-round capacity empty magazine; a 100-round capacity empty drum style magazine; a 9mm caliber firearm with an 18-round capacity empty magazine; two machinegun conversion devices; a .40 caliber firearm with an empty 10-round capacity magazine; and a 9mm caliber firearm with an empty 24-round capacity magazine. He did not have a Federal Firearms License to sell firearms. Additionally, Meeks sold approximately 1,000 fentanyl pills in exchange for cash.

Meeks pleaded guilty to one count of engaging in the business of dealing or manufacturing firearms without a license and one count of distribution of a controlled substance. In addition to his prison sentence, United States District Judge Cristina D. Silva ordered Meeks to serve 4 years of supervised release.

The ATF investigated the case. Assistant United States Attorney Joshua Brister prosecuted the case.

text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. – Four individuals have been charged in an eight‑count federal indictment for their roles in a multistate bank-fraud and money-laundering scheme involving stolen and altered checks issued by a multinational corporation.

Cory L. Sims, Jr., of Bridgeport, Conn.; Dondre O. Daniels, of Bridgeport and Tampa, Fla.; Christian M. Hill, of Kansas City, Mo.; and Makhia L. Duncan, of Des Moines, Iowa, were charged in an indictment returned under seal by a federal grand jury in Kansas City. The indictment was unsealed following Hill’s initial court appearance. Daniels and Duncan were subsequently taken into custody. Sims remains at large.

According to the indictment, the defendants unlawfully obtained checks issued by the corporation to pay its vendors. The indictment alleges that the defendants altered those checks by removing the names of the intended payees and replacing them with their own names or with the name of an identity‑theft victim. The altered checks then were deposited into accounts controlled by the defendants, who subsequently withdrew or transferred the unlawfully obtained funds.

The indictment alleges that Sims and Daniels deposited multiple altered checks into bank accounts opened either in Sims’ name or in the name of an identity‑theft victim. Daniels allegedly made ATM withdrawals in several cities using bank cards linked to those accounts. According to the indictment, Sims and Daniels then laundered the fraud proceeds through cash withdrawals, transfers, payments to Daniels’s business, and electronic transactions.

Hill is alleged to have obtained and deposited an altered check into his personal account, then withdrawn and laundered more than $45,000 in fraud proceeds. Duncan is alleged to have deposited a separate altered check into his personal account, later withdrawing and laundering more than $34,000 through subsequent transactions.

The indictment charges Sims with conspiracy to commit money laundering; Daniels with bank fraud, conspiracy to commit money laundering, and aggravated identity theft; Hill with bank fraud and two counts of money laundering; and Duncan with bank fraud and one count of money laundering. The indictment also seeks forfeiture of the proceeds of the offenses.

Bank fraud is punishable by up to 30 years in federal prison. Conspiracy to commit money laundering carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison. Money laundering carries a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison. Aggravated identity theft carries a mandatory two‑year consecutive sentence.

The charges contained in the indictment are simply accusations, not evidence of guilt. Evidence supporting the charges must be presented to a federal trial jury, whose duty is to determine guilt or innocence.

This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney James Kirkpatrick. It has been investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation.
title: Four Charged in Multistate Bank Fraud and Money-Laundering Scheme

BOSTON – A Fitchburg, Mass. man was sentenced today in federal court in Worcester for his role in a fraud scheme that used the stolen identities of more than 100 individuals to obtain $440,000 in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits from Massachusetts and Rhode Island. The defendant and his alleged co-conspirators also fraudulently obtained over $700,000 in Pandemic Unemployment Assistance (PUA) benefits from Massachusetts, New York, Pennsylvania, Ohio Washington and Nevada.

Raul Fernandez Vicioso, 38, was sentenced by U.S. District Court Judge Margaret R. Guzman to two years in prison, to be followed by three years of supervised release. The defendant was also ordered to pay $1.1 million in restitution and $1.1 million in forfeiture. In March 2026 , Raul Fernandez Vicioso pleaded guilty to Conspiracy to Commit SNAP Fraud, Conspiracy to Commit Wire Fraud, SNAP benefit Fraud, Aiding and Abetting and Money Laundering.

The defendant was charged on Feb. 3, 2026 along with three co-conspirators –Roman Vequiz Fernandez, 32, a Venezuelan national living in Leominster, Mass.; Coralba Albarracin Siniva, 24, a Venezuelan national living in Leominster, Mass.; and Joel Vicioso Fernandez, 42, of Fitchburg, Mass.

Raul Fernandez Vicioso and his alleged co-conspirators purchased and used the stolen personal information of over 100 real people from multiple states to fraudulently obtain SNAP benefits. The stolen identities were used to create 24 “households” in SNAP applications. All of these applications, submitted in the names of over 100 people, were listed as living in two single-family apartments in Providence, R.I. A number of the stolen identities from Connecticut, Florida, Kentucky, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania and Puerto Rico were used to fraudulently obtain SNAP benefits in Massachusetts and Rhode Island.

Raul Fernandez Vicioso used his own personal information to create fraudulent SNAP benefit accounts that were found commingled among the victim identities in the applications. In support of the fraudulently submitted SNAP applications, the defendants and their co-conspirators allegedly provided images of counterfeit passports and passport cards, with metadata that indicated the images were taken inside or within the immediate vicinity of El Primo Restaurant – a restaurant operated by Raul Fernandez Vicioso in Leominster, Mass.

The defendants and their co-conspirators allegedly used the fraudulent SNAP benefits cards to purchase large quantities of expensive bulk food items (such as multiple-pound packages of chicken, beef and pork) at various local wholesalers and food markets to stock El Primo Restaurant at no expense. With their supplies obtained for free through fraudulent SNAP benefits, they sold menu items at El Primo Restaurant at a complete profit, later wiring the fraud proceeds to individuals living in Venezuela and the Dominican Republic, among other places.

According to the charging documents, between April 2020 and December 2021, the defendants and their co-conspirators further enriched themselves by over $700,000 by submitting fraudulent applications and supporting documents for PUA in Massachusetts, New York, Pennsylvania, Ohio and Nevada. The fraudulent PUA benefits were issued in the names of Raul Fernandez Vicioso and in the names of suspected identity theft victims, including identities common to the related the SNAP benefit fraud. At least 29 different identities were allegedly used in PUA applications in six different states – all of which listed the address for El Primo Restaurant as the residential address.

Bank records obtained during the investigation detail approximately $276,021 in fraudulent PUA benefits deposited into bank accounts held in the names of the El Primo Restaurant, Raul Fernandez Vicioso and other alleged co-conspirators. Other fraudulent PUA benefits were allegedly issued to prepaid cards in the identities of the various individuals which were applied for using known addresses and telephone numbers of the subjects.

During searches of Raul Fernandez Vicioso’s residence and El Primo Restaurant, fraudulently obtained Massachusetts and Rhode Island EBT cards, fraudulent documents bearing a Providence address involved in the alleged scheme, printed ledgers and handwritten lists of more than 100 identities and SNAP-related mailings were recovered.

Fraud, waste or abuse can be reported to the Council of the Inspectors General for Integrity and Efficiency: https://www.oversight.gov/where-report-fraud-waste-abuse-or-retaliation .

The charge of conspiracy to commit SNAP fraud provides for a sentence of up to five years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of $250,000. The charge of conspiracy to commit wire fraud provides for a sentence of up to 20 years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of $250,000 The charge of illegal acquisition or use of SNAP benefits provides for a sentence of up to five years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of $250,000. The charge of money laundering provides for a sentence of up to 20 years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of $500,000 or twice the amount involved in the transaction, whichever is greater. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Charmeka Parker, Special Agent in Charge of the U.S. Department of Agriculture - Office of Inspector General, Northeast Region; Anthony P. D’Esposito, Inspector General, Department of Labor, Office of Inspector General; Thomas Demeo, Special Agent in Charge of the Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigation, Boston Field Office; and Jeff Grimming, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations in New England made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the Social Security Administration - Office of Inspector General; U.S. Department of Homeland Security - Office of Inspector General; U.S. Postal Inspection Service; U.S. Department of State - Diplomatic Security Service; Rhode Island Office of Internal Audit - Fraud Detection & Prevention Unit; Massachusetts State Police; the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Rhode Island; and the Fitchburg and Leominster Police Departments. Assistant U.S. Attorney Danial Bennett of the Worcester Branch Office is prosecuting the case.

On March 26, 2026 , United States Attorney Leah B. Foley announced the creation of the Benefit & Voter Fraud Team, a district-wide initiative established in response to the rampant fraud being uncovered across Massachusetts. Members of the public are encouraged to report suspected benefit fraud in Massachusetts by calling 1-855-SCAM-MA-1 (855-722-6621).

On April 7, 2026, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division . The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

The details contained in the charging document are allegations. The remaining defendants are presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in the court of law.
title: Lead Defendant in Multi-State SNAP and PUA Fraud Conspiracy Sentenced to Two Years in Federal Prison

RAPID CITY - United States Attorney Ron Parsons announced today that U.S. District Judge Camela C. Theeler has sentenced a Rapid City, South Dakota, man convicted of Possession of a Firearm by a Prohibited Person. The sentencing took place on September 28, 2026.

Avery Hawk Wing, 36, was sentenced to three years and 10 months in federal prison, followed by three years of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund. Forfeiture was also ordered.

Hawk Wing was indicted by a federal grand jury in October 2024. He was found guilty on July 2, 2026, following a three-day jury trial in federal district court in Rapid City.

Evidence at trial showed Hawk Wing handled a rifle that was in a tote bag that belonged to him. Hawk Wing told law enforcement that he touched the firearm when going through his tote bag. Unsurprisingly, forensic examination revealed Hawk Wing’s DNA on several locations of the firearm, consistent with him handling the firearm. Hawk Wing was previously convicted of a felony crime punishable beyond a year in prison and, as a result, is prohibited from possessing firearms.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities .

This case was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and the Rapid City Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Benjamin Schroeder prosecuted the case.

Hawk Wing was immediately remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service.

United States Attorney Lesley A. Woods announced that on September 30, 2026, Brian Baldonado-Belmontes, 24, a Mexican man unlawfully in the United States, was sentenced to 30 months in prison for unlawfully possessing a firearm. Because Baldonado-Belmontes is a citizen of Mexico and was unlawfully in the United States, it was illegal for him to possess a firearm.

On March 22, 2026, the Omaha Police Department monitored a social media account belonging to a juvenile, which appeared to show the juvenile discharging a rifle in Omaha. After officers discovered the area of the shooting, they found approximately 23 spent .22 caliber cartridge cases and two live .22 caliber rounds. They also found a truck that had been struck by bullets about six times. While officers were processing the scene, Baldonado-Belmontes approached officers and admitted that he shot the truck. He later admitted that he shot the truck while riding as a passenger in the juvenile’s vehicle. He advised officers that the firearm was at his residence in Bellevue. Officers went to the residence and recovered the firearm, which was a Smith and Wesson, M&P 15-22, .22 caliber rifle. Attached to the rifle was a magazine, marked for 25 round capacity of .22LR ammunition.Just a few feet from the rifle, officers located an extended magazine for 9 mm ammunition.

This case was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, the Omaha Police Department, and the Bellevue Police Department.
title: Mexican Man Illegally in the United States Sentenced to 30 Months for Possessing a Firearm

HUNTINGTON, W.Va. – Roger Lee Townson, 58, of Huntington, was sentenced today to three years of federal probation for possession of a firearm by a prohibited person.

According to court documents and statements made in court, on March 25, 2025, law enforcement officers executed a search warrant at a garage behind Townson’s residence. Officers ordered the residence’s occupants, including Townson, to exit the house and asked Townson if there were any firearms inside. Townson told officers he had a firearm in his bedroom and allowed officers to enter the residence to secure it. Officers found a Glock model 43 9mm pistol in the bedroom.

Federal law prohibits a person with a prior felony conviction or a conviction for a misdemeanor crime of domestic violence from possessing a firearm or ammunition. Townson knew he was prohibited from possessing a firearm because of his prior convictions for forgery in Cabell County Circuit Court on March 10, 2000, and for domestic battery in Cabell County Magistrate Court on June 14, 2010.

United States Attorney Moore Capito made the announcement and commended the investigative work of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) and the Huntington Police Department.

United States District Judge Robert C. Chambers imposed the sentence. Assistant United States Attorneys Lesley C. Shamblin and Sarah N. Hudson prosecuted the case.
