RAPID CITY – U.S. Attorney Ron Parsons announced today that U.S. District Judge Camela C. Theeler has sentenced a Mexican man convicted of Illegal Reentry after Deportation. The sentencing took place on September 18, 2026.

Marco Jimenez-Sanchez, 38, was sentenced to time served. He will be deported back to Mexico.

Jimenez-Sanchez was indicted for Illegal Reentry after Deportation by a federal grand jury in June 2026. He pleaded guilty on September 18, 2026.

Jimenez-Sanchez is an alien and Mexican national. He has been deported from the United States on multiple occasions. On May 21, 2026, in Box Elder, SD, Ellsworth Air Force Security Forces and Box Elder Police Department were dispatched after Jimenez-Sanchez was observed crossing a fence into a restricted construction area. Jimenez-Sanchez was not on the list of employees allowed in the restricted area. It is a federal felony for an alien to be present in the United States after deportation and without permission for reentry.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. Operation Take Back America streamlines efforts and resources from the Department’s Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Forces (OCDETFs) and Project Safe Neighborhood (PSN).

This case was investigated by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security Immigration and Customs Enforcement and the Box Elder Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Benjamin Schroeder prosecuted the case.

MADISON, WIS. – Chadwick M. Elgersma, United States Attorney for the Western District of Wisconsin, announced that four more defendants were sentenced by U.S. District Judge William M. Conley for their roles in a large drug trafficking organization operating in Madison.

Treagir Sander, 27, La Crosse, Wisconsin, was sentenced on September 15, 2026, to 78 months in federal prison for conspiring to distribute 50 grams or more of methamphetamine and 40 grams or more of fentanyl. The prison term will be followed by 5 years of supervised release. Sander pleaded guilty to the charge on June 26, 2026.

Alisha Lavine, 36, Sun Prairie, Wisconsin, was sentenced on September 16, 2026, to 36 months in federal prison for conspiring to distribute fentanyl and 50 grams or more of methamphetamine. The prison term will be followed by 4 years of supervised release. Lavine pleaded guilty to the charge on July 14, 2026.

Kyle Haag, 40, Madison, Wisconsin, was sentenced on September 22, 2026, to 75 months in federal prison for conspiring to distribute fentanyl and 50 grams or more of methamphetamine. The prison term will be followed by 5 years of supervised release. Haag pleaded guilty to the charge on July 6, 2026.

Waylon Degenhardt, 44, Boscobel, Wisconsin, was sentenced on October 1, 2026, to 24 months in federal prison for conspiring to distribute methamphetamine and fentanyl. The prison term will be followed by 3 years of supervised release. Degenhardt pleaded guilty to the charge on July 7, 2026.

In early 2024, law enforcement began investigating members of a drug trafficking organization operating in Dane County led by Jamar Purnell. During the investigation, officers worked with confidential informants to purchase significant quantities of drugs. Officers seized drugs and firearms during search warrants executed at residences and vehicles associated with the organization.

Sander, Lavine, Haag, and Degenhardt were identified as drug distributors for the Purnell drug trafficking organization. Investigators determined that Sander and Haag sold around a kilogram of methamphetamine and substantial quantities of fentanyl. Lavine and Degenhardt also sold methamphetamine and fentanyl but at lower amounts than Sander and Haag.

Jamar Purnell, 49, Chicago, Illinois, was previously sentenced by Judge Conley to a total sentence of 20 years in federal prison for conspiring to distribute 500 grams or more of methamphetamine and 400 grams or more of fentanyl and for possessing a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime.

Keean Moore, 49, Chicago, Illinois, was previously sentenced by Judge Conley to 11 years in federal prison for conspiring to distribute 500 grams or more of methamphetamine and fentanyl.

Jimmie Leuaxay, 33, Madison, Wisconsin, was previously sentenced by Judge Conley to a total sentence of 15 years in federal prison for conspiring to distribute 500 grams or more of methamphetamine and fentanyl and for possessing firearms in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime.

James Dubois, 31, Madison, Wisconsin, was previously sentenced by Judge Conley to 66 months in federal prison for conspiring to distribute methamphetamine and 40 grams or more of fentanyl.

James Land, 37, Madison, Wisconsin, was previously sentenced by Judge Conley to 6 years in federal prison for conspiring to distribute 50 grams or more of methamphetamine and 40 grams or more of fentanyl.

Keean Moore Jr., 26, Madison, Wisconsin, was previously sentenced by Judge Conley to 5 years in federal prison for distributing 50 grams or more of methamphetamine and possessing a firearm as a felon.

Travis Corrado, 46, Madison, Wisconsin, was previously sentenced by Judge Conley to 5 years in federal prison for conspiring to distribute 50 grams or more of methamphetamine and 40 grams or more of fentanyl.

Shavarim Wicks, 48, Chicago, Illinois, was previously sentenced by Judge Conley to 5 years in federal prison for conspiring to distribute 500 grams or more of methamphetamine and 40 grams or more of fentanyl.

A total of sixteen individuals were charged in connection with this drug trafficking organization. Dajuea Purnell, Yasir Stackhouse, and William Marshall have entered guilty pleas for their involvement in drug trafficking and will be sentenced in the coming months. The case against Anthony E. Hohenstein is still pending, and he is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.

The charges against Sander, Lavine, Haag, and Degenhardt were the result of an investigation conducted by the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration, ATF Madison Crime Gun Task Force, Wisconsin Department of Justice Division of Criminal Investigation, Dane County Narcotics Task Force, Lake Winnebago Area Metropolitan Enforcement Group, Wisconsin State Patrol, and Madison Police Department. The ATF Madison Crime Gun Task Force consists of federal agents from ATF and Task Force Officers from state and local agencies throughout the Western District of Wisconsin. Assistant U.S. Attorney Steven P. Anderson prosecuted this case.

This prosecution is part of the U.S. Department of Justice’s Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) Program initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of federal law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States.

BLM Celebrates Responsible Mining, Community Outreach, and Public Land Stewardship Award Winners
Organization:
Media Contact:
WASHINGTON –The Bureau of Land Management is recognizing hardrock mineral operators for their superior efforts toward Unleashing American Energy during the 18th annual Mineral Development Awards ceremony, hosted by the National Mining Association. These awards commend operators who have made exemplary contributions to the development of hardrock minerals.
“Hardrock minerals play a critical role in supporting America’s energy security and economic strength, and the BLM is proud to recognize operators who show what responsible development on public lands looks like,” said BLM Director Steve Pearce. “These operators restore the ground they work, invest in local communities, and help ensure domestic mineral production continues to benefit our nation. Their leadership reflects the balance we strive for every day: good stewardship, solid partnerships, and development that supports families and local economies.”
Award winners were chosen in the following categories:
Hardrock Mineral Leadership Award recognizes achievements demonstrating continuous or repeated efforts to successfully meet or exceed federal, state, or local requirements with minimal oversight. The 2026 winner is Nevada Gold Mines for its reclamation efforts at the Rain Mine in Nevada.
Hardrock Mineral Community Outreach and Economic Security Award recognizes the successful coordination of projects with local and regional stakeholders, including those projects that contribute to quality of life or demonstrate concern for the long-term health of the local community. The 2026 winner is Alaska Resource Education for its work in community outreach and education about the mining sector to the public.
Hardrock Mineral Small Operator Award recognizes operators or organizations with fewer than 15 employees who have demonstrated continuous or repeated efforts to successfully meet or exceed federal, state, or local requirements with minimal oversight. The 2026 winner is Valdez Creek Mining for its removal of 230 tons of solid waste and derelict equipment left behind by previous operators in the areas at Valdez and White creeks in Alaska.
Mine Legacy Steward Award recognizes partnership activities that assist in addressing hardrock abandoned mine land features across the American West. The 2026 winner is American Gilsonite Company for its efforts in reclaiming legacy mining disturbance at the Cowboy Mine in Utah.
The Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement also recognized two companies for their superior efforts with 2026 Excellence in Surface Coal Mining Reclamation Awards during the ceremony.
Hardrock minerals are nonfuel minerals— such as gold, copper, iron, gypsum, limestone, and salt— that are mined from solid rock formations rather than fluids or energy resources. Mining on BLM-managed public lands for materials not used for energy contributes nearly $14 billion annually to the U.S. economy. For additional information visit the BLM’s solid minerals program website.
The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.
title: BLM Celebrates Responsible Mining, Community Outreach, and Public Land Stewardship Award Winners

LOS ANGELES – A now-imprisoned fraudster was sentenced today to 78 months in federal prison for hiring several now-convicted off-duty former Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department (LASD) deputies to violate his perceived adversaries’ civil rights, stealing more than $37 million from Meta Platforms Inc. by fraudulently gaining access to its business manager accounts and their lines of credit, and for cheating on his taxes.

Adam Iza, 26, a.k.a. “The Godfather,” who formerly resided in Beverly Hills and Newport Beach, was sentenced by United States District Judge Percy Anderson, who also ordered him to pay $23,402,766 in restitution.

Iza pleaded guilty in January 2025 to one count of conspiracy against rights, one count of wire fraud, and one count of tax evasion.

He has been in federal custody since September 2024, and today’s sentence runs concurrent to a 15-year federal prison sentence received last month in Connecticut for his involvement in an attempted robbery of Bitcoin the month prior to his arrest.

According to Iza’s plea agreement in his Los Angeles federal criminal case, from August 2021 to April 2022, he hired off-duty LASD deputies to provide him with personal security. Iza knowingly and intentionally conspired with these corrupt sheriff’s deputies to obtain confidential law enforcement information, personally identifiable information (PII) about individuals with whom Iza had financial and other disputes, and court-authorized search warrants to track down and harass his victims. While using the sobriquet “The Godfather,” Iza also enlisted the corrupt deputies to intimidate and threaten these victims.

In total, five now-former LASD deputies whom Iza employed now stand convicted of federal crimes:

Eric Chase Saavedra, 42, of Chino, a former LASD deputy and a former federal task force officer, was sentenced on September 28 to 21 months in federal prison after pleading guilty in February 2025 to one count of conspiracy against rights and one count of making and subscribing to a false tax return. Saavedra founded a company – Saavedra & Associates LLC – that provided security to Iza and hired LASD deputies to do so. Among other crimes, Saavedra used his powers as a sworn law enforcement officer to improperly obtain court-authorized search warrants related to intimidating, threatening, and harassing Iza’s adversaries.

Michael David Coberg, 45, of Eastvale, is serving a 63-month federal prison sentence for helping Iza extort a rival and arranging the sham illegal drug possession arrest of another adversary in Paramount in 2021. Judge Anderson sentenced Coberg on March 16.

Scott Allen Simpkins, 34, of Brea, was sentenced on July 13 to 18 months in federal prison for obstructing a federal investigation into Iza’s extortion of $25,000 from a party planner at Iza’s Bel Air mansion.

David Anthony Rodriguez, 45, of La Verne, was sentenced on July 20 to one year in federal prison and who had worked for Iza as a private security guard, pleaded guilty to submitting a false search warrant application to a state court judge on behalf of a different client.

“Individuals with substantial financial resources must understand that they cannot purchase access to confidential databases, investigative tools, warrants, arrests, badges, or firearms for use in private disputes,” prosecutors argued in a sentencing memorandum.

In an unrelated scheme, from December 2020 to September 2024, Iza fraudulently gained access to Meta business manager accounts and their associated lines of credit. He then sold access to the compromised accounts and lines of credit to various advertising companies, making substantial profits in the process.

From 2020 through 2022, Iza received approximately $37 million associated with the sale of access to the Meta advertisement accounts into his companies’ bank accounts from domestic and international payors. As a result, Meta clients were billed for, and paid for, advertising expenditures they did not incur. When Meta or Meta clients discovered the fraudulent billing, Meta refunded its clients, thereby suffering the loss.

Iza admitted in his plea agreement that from 2020 through 2023, he received at least $36,360,844 in gross income from his scheme to defraud Meta, causing a total loss to the IRS of $13,286,152. Iza knowingly failed to file corporate tax returns during this time. He further evaded the payment of federal taxes by concealing his ownership of his company, Zort, including his communications with advertising clients, getting a co-schemer to use the money to acquire personal items for Iza and himself, and by transferring his corporate income to cryptocurrency custodians.

Relatedly, Iris Rabaya Au, 37, of Irvine, was sentenced on September 21 to 18 months in federal prison and was ordered to pay $1,484,343 in restitution and to forfeit a fleet of luxury and high-performance cars, designer handbags, and three “Godfather” sculptures, among other assets.

Au pleaded guilty in March 2025 to one count of subscribing to a false tax return. She failed to report more than $2.6 million in ill-gotten gains she obtained via Iza’s criminal activities.

The FBI and IRS Criminal Investigation investigated this matter. The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department has assisted.

Assistant United States Attorney Maxwell K. Coll of the National Security Division prosecuted this case.
title: Self-Proclaimed ‘Godfather’ Sentenced to Over 6 Years in Prison for Fraud, Tax Evasion, and Using LASD Deputies to Torment His Opponents

HUNTINGTON, W.Va. – Marlon Leftwich, 46, of Huntington, was sentenced today to 20 years and six months in prison, to be followed by 20 years of supervised release, for production of child pornography. Leftwich must also register as a sex offender. The Court will determine restitution at a later date.

According to court documents and statements made in court, on June 24, 2025, law enforcement officers executed a search warrant at Leftwich’s residence and seized numerous electronic devices including a cell phone and SD memory card. A forensic review found approximately four files on the memory card and approximately 666 files on the cell phone, of images and videos depicting sexual abuse and exploitation of children.

As part of his guilty plea, Leftwich admitted that the child pornography included a video of him persuading a five-year-old minor female to engage in sexually explicit conduct with him at his Huntington residence while he recorded the conduct using a cell phone. Leftwich further admitted that he recorded the child sexual abuse material on or about January 1, 2016, and transferred the video file to the memory card.

“This defendant inflicted an unspeakable horror upon a five-year-old child, and today’s sentence brings nearly a decade of delayed justice to an end. Through the hard work of our prosecutors in the Southern District of West Virginia and our partners in the FBI, he will now serve a prison sentence that protects our community from further harm,” said United States Attorney Moore Capito. “Those who prey on children should make no mistake: this office will pursue them, prosecute them, and fight to put them behind bars. Protecting children is one of our highest responsibilities, and we will continue our relentless efforts to hold those who exploit them accountable.”

Capito made the announcement and commended the investigative work of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI).

United States District Judge Robert C. Chambers imposed the sentence. Assistant United States Attorney Gabriel Price prosecuted the case.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc .

A copy of this press release is located on the website of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of West Virginia. Related court documents and information can be found on PACER by searching for Case No. 3:25-cr-132.

Congressman Menefee Announces Major Constituent Casework Milestone
HOUSTON, TX — Today, Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) announced that his casework team has closed more than 500 constituent cases since he took office. This milestone reflects eight months of delivering results for the people of Texas’s 18th Congressional District. After TX-18 went more than 330 days without representation in Congress, this accomplishment is a clear sign that our district is back to having a strong, responsive office working for the people.
“Helping constituents navigate the bureaucracy of the federal government and alleviating their hardships is my top priority,” said Rep. Menefee. “We built this office from the ground up. Every call answered and every case closed is a step closer to delivering on the promise I made to the people of the 18th. From Veterans’ benefits to visa assistance, we’re going to keep showing up and helping folks get the help they need.”
Since taking office, Congressman Menefee's team has:
- Closed more than 500 constituent cases out of the nearly 1,000 opened.
- Recovered more than $1 million in eligible and/or delayed funds for constituents.
- Successfully closed cases involving immigration, expedited passports, Veterans’ benefits, Social Security, Medicare, the Department of Education, the IRS, OPM, and the U.S. Postal Service.
- Delivered more than 7,000 congressional recognitions throughout the District, celebrating the people and businesses that shape TX-18.
Constituents who need assistance with a federal agency can call 713-655-0050 or visit our website at Menefee.House.Gov.

Coast Guard completes $132.5 million Pier November rebuild at Base Charleston
The U.S. Coast Guard completed a $132.5 million rebuild of Pier November at Base Charleston, South Carolina, delivering critical waterfront infrastructure that expands the Service’s capacity to support cutters, crews and operations in the Southeast and beyond.
The new 1,190-foot-long, 80-foot-wide pier can accommodate up to five major cutters, increasing Base Charleston’s capacity and providing modern infrastructure designed to support current and future Coast Guard operations. This project was funded, in part, by an historic investment through the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Of the nearly $25 billion provided through this act – the largest capital investment in Coast Guard history – the Service has been delivering on that investment by ordering approximately $19 billion in assets, capabilities, and infrastructure.
“Pier November will be home to new major Coast Guard cutters currently being constructed that will strengthen the Coast Guard’s ability to secure America’s borders and maritime approaches far at sea,” said Adm. Kevin Lunday, Commandant of the Coast Guard. “Base Charleston is critical to our operations and will be home to one of the largest concentrations of Coast Guard personnel, assets, and capabilities.”
The project included demolition and replacement of the existing Pier November, repairs to collapsed bulkheads, dredging and shoreside utility improvements. Construction crews also addressed remnants of previous pier repairs discovered during the project. The work was completed 60 days ahead of schedule.
The Coast Guard’s Facilities Design and Construction Center managed the project as part of a broader effort to expand and modernize Base Charleston. Additional work includes demolition and reconstruction of Pier Mike and construction of new engineering, multifunctional and medical facilities. Together, these investments will expand Base Charleston’s capacity and strengthen its ability to support critical Coast Guard missions. This project was initially funded by the Fiscal Year 2019 Hurricane Supplemental with the removal of previous pier repairs funded through the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
For media inquiries, contact mediarelations@uscg.mil.

About the U.S. Coast Guard
With more than 95,000 miles of shoreline, 25,000 miles of navigable rivers and 4.5 million square miles of U.S. exclusive economic zone, the U.S. Coast Guard defends the Nation, protects the marine transportation system, regulates and safeguards ports and waterways, leads the Nation in maritime drug interdiction and secures the maritime border. As a member of the joint force, a law enforcement organization, a regulatory agency and a member of the U.S. intelligence community, the Coast Guard employs a unique mix of authorities to ensure the safety and integrity of the maritime domain to protect the economic and national security of the nation. More than 76,000 members of the Coast Guard operate a multi-mission, interoperable fleet of more than 220 cutters, 185 fixed and rotary-wing aircraft, 1,300 boats and its own dedicated cyber command to protect critical maritime infrastructure.
More information about the U.S. Coast Guard can be found at www.uscg.mil. Follow @USCG on X and Instagram, like us on Facebook, subscribe on YouTube and follow on LinkedIn—connect with us.

text:
OKLAHOMA CITY – As October marks Domestic Violence Awareness Month, United States Attorney Robert J. Troester highlights the successful partnerships and impact of Operation 922, a local Project Safe Neighborhoods initiative in the Western District of Oklahoma to hold violent domestic abusers accountable for violation of federal firearms laws.

“You cannot have safe neighborhoods without first having safe homes,” said U.S. Attorney Robert J. Troester. “When domestic violence escalates to involve firearms, the likelihood of death for the abuse victim or responding law enforcement increases exponentially. Simply put, Operation 922 is a targeted strategy to save lives by holding domestic abusers accountable for violation of federal laws before their violence escalates.”

“Operation 922 demonstrates the life-saving impact that comes from bringing law enforcement agencies together to address the intersection of domestic violence and firearms,” said ATF Special Agent in Charge Brian Garner. “When a violent domestic abuser is prohibited from possessing a firearm, identifying and removing that firearm can prevent further violence and potentially save a life. ATF is proud to work alongside our federal, state, local, and tribal partners to hold these offenders accountable and to ensure that firearms do not become tools of intimidation, control, or further violence in our communities.”

“The Oklahoma City Police Department has long shared a strong partnership with the United States Attorney’s Office, out of the Western District of Oklahoma,” said Oklahoma City Police Chief Ron Bacy. “Together we investigate and prosecute violent crimes, particularly those involving domestic violence, especially given the staggering domestic violence statistics in our state. This collaboration includes our joint efforts through the Operation 922 initiative.”

“Palomar is proud to have partnered with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Oklahoma since the beginning of Operation 922. Together, we have helped protect hundreds of women and children from violence, hold dangerous offenders accountable, and make our community safer,” said Palomar Chief Visionary Officer & Founder Kim Garrett-Funk. “We commend Bob Troester and his team for their leadership and unwavering commitment to justice. We are honored to stand alongside partners who share our belief that every person deserves to live free from violence and fear.”

The Problem

According to a 2025 report , Oklahoma ranks among the top in the nation for women murdered by men in domestic disputes. The danger from domestic abuse, however, extends beyond the home; one of the leading causes of firearms-related fatalities for police officers is responding to domestic abuse calls . Moreover, domestic violence is not limited to specific geographic areas but exists in all neighborhoods (wealthy and poor) and in all communities (metropolitan and rural).

The Strategy

Launched in 2018, Operation 922 brings law enforcement and prosecutors together with a clear direction and common purpose: holding violent domestic abusers accountable. Operation 922 prioritizes the prosecution of violent domestic abusers primarily using federal firearms laws, most of which are found in 18 U.S.C. § 922, from which this initiative takes its name.

All told, Operation 922 has used more than 20 federal statutes to target these violent offenders. Common federal charges include, but are not limited to, illegal possession of a firearm or ammunition by a person (1) previously convicted of a felony offense, (2) previously convicted of a misdemeanor crime of domestic violence, (3) under current felony indictment, or (4) subject to an active domestic violence related Victim Protective Order, and (5) making false statements to federally licensed firearms dealers. Given the focus on violent abusers, federal prosecutors often seek the defendant’s pre-trial detention after arrest, in part to limit the abuser’s ability to return to the home and exert control and intimidation over victims while trial is pending. Similarly, federal prosecutors often seek substantive prison sentences after conviction with Operation 922 offenders averaging 76 months in prison.

The Partnerships

Operation 922 is a collaboration of federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement and prosecutors across the Western District of Oklahoma. To date, cases have originated in 26 different counties—well over half the counties in the district.

From its inception in 2018, Operation 922 has maintained a pivotal partnership with Palomar, Oklahoma City’s Family Justice Center. Palomar brings together multi-disciplinary resources under one roof to meet the specific and multiple areas of need experienced by the victims of domestic abuse. This partnership is critical to provide the necessary victim services and support to those suffering from abuse.

Results Since 2018

Since 2018, Operation 922 has had phenomenal results:

433 defendants have been charged More than 96% have already pleaded guilty or been convicted at trial. More than 90% have already been sentenced, receiving average federal prison sentences of 76 months.

More than 96% have already pleaded guilty or been convicted at trial.

More than 90% have already been sentenced, receiving average federal prison sentences of 76 months.

More than 33% were identified known gang members.

Law enforcement has seized from these defendants: 606 firearms, and 18,068 rounds of ammunition.

18,068 rounds of ammunition.

The following press releases over the past two years are examples of the breadth of Operation 922’s impact:

Oklahoma City Man Receives Statutory Maximum Sentence for Illegally Possessing Ammunition Connected to Shooting of Unarmed Man – (September 15, 2026)

Oklahoma City Felon Sentenced to Twelve Years in Federal Prison after Pointing a Firearm at Three People Inside Vehicle - (July 13, 2026)

Alva Man to Serve Six Years in Federal Prison for Firearm Possession after Threatening and Strangling Woman - (June 8, 2026)

Lawton Man in Illegal Possession of 11 Firearms while Subject to a Protective Order is Sentenced to Serve 57 Months in Federal Prison - (June 3, 2026)

Oklahoma City Man with Violent Criminal History Sentenced to 12 Years for Firearm Offense - (April 22, 2026)

Lawton Man Sentenced to Nine Years in Federal Prison for Gun Charge after Shots Fired during Domestic Dispute - (March 6, 2026)

Oklahoma City Man Sentenced to Serve More Than Three Years in Federal Prison for Illegal Firearm Possession - (January 22, 2026)

Oklahoma City Man Sentenced to Serve 55 Years in Prison Following Retrial after Shooting Woman in Metro Parking Garage - (January 14, 2026)

Oklahoma City Man Sentenced to Federal Prison for Illegal Firearm Possession Following Shooting - (January 7, 2026)

Oklahoma City Man Lands in Federal Prison for Possessing Firearm While Subject to Protective Order - (November 25, 2025)

Canadian County Man to Serve Decade in Federal Prison following Domestic Violence Incident with Pregnant Woman Involving Firearms - (June 4, 2025)

Illegal Firearm Possession Lands Oklahoma City Man in Federal Prison for Six Years Following Domestic Calls to Law Enforcement - (May 21, 2025)

Oklahoma City Man Sentenced to Serve More Than Four Years in Federal Prison for Illegal Ammunition Possession after Attacking Woman at Club and Her Home - (May 9, 2025)

Oklahoma City Man Sentenced to Serve Six Years in Federal Prison after Domestic Violence Call Leads to Illegal Firearm and Ammunition Possession Conviction - (April 24, 2025)

Road Rage Shooting Lands Oklahoma County Man in Federal Prison for More Than Seven Years for Illegal Firearm Possession - (March 18, 2025)

Training Beyond Western Oklahoma

Since 2018, the U.S. Attorney’s Office has trained more than 2,500 federal, state, local, and tribal officers and prosecutors nationwide on Operation 922. More than half of that training has taken place in Oklahoma. Western District of Oklahoma prosecutors have also provided national training to other U.S. Attorney’s Offices who have used Operation 922 as a model for a similar strategy in their districts.

For more information about Project Safe Neighborhoods, visit justice.gov/psn . More information about the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Oklahoma is available at justice.gov/usao-wdok .
title: Western District of Oklahoma's "Operation 922" Domestic Violence Initiative Continues to Save Lives

United States Attorney Lesley A. Woods announced that on September 30, 2026, Marvin Amilcar Cermeno-Perez, 28, a Guatemalan man unlawfully in the United States, was sentenced to 70 months in prison for possessing with intent to distribute cocaine, carrying a firearm during and in relation to a drug trafficking crime, and illegal reentry of a removed alien.

On October 6, 2025, Omaha police officers stopped Cermeno-Perez’s vehicle in Omaha. Officers searched the vehicle and located marijuana and approximately 25 small zip lock bags, collectively containing about 11.3 grams of cocaine. Officers also located a Taurus, model TX, .22 caliber pistol in the center console. Cermeno-Perez admitted to possessing the firearm and purchasing the cocaine, which he intended to distribute. Because Cermeno-Perez was unlawfully in the United States, he was not permitted to possess firearms. Before illegally reentering the United States, Cermeno-Perez was removed to Guatemala in 2019.

This case was investigated by United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and the Omaha Police Department.
title: Guatemalan Man Illegally in the United States Sentenced to 70 Months for Immigration, Drug, and Firearm Offenses

BINGHAMTON, NY – Representative Josh Riley (NY-19) is demanding answers from Verizon about notices the company has sent to residents across Upstate New York warning that their copper landline telephone service may soon be shut off. These notices followed Verizon’s September 9, 2026 application to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) seeking approval to discontinue this service as soon as November 30, 2026.
In a letter to Verizon CEO Dan Schulman, Riley expressed concern that alternatives to copper landline service, such as fiber and wireless networks, are not a reliable solution for Upstate New York communities. In many rural areas, the landline is how people call 911, how medical alert and monitoring devices work, and how families stay connected. Unlike the alternatives, traditional landlines keep working during a blackout, and in rural New York, blackouts are frequent and can last for days.
“For many Upstate New Yorkers, discontinuing copper landline service would mean losing the only phone service they can count on,” Riley said. “Rural communities present real challenges, but rather than rising to meet them, Verizon appears to be walking away from us. Upstate New Yorkers should not be forced to pay the price in new equipment, higher monthly bills, or fears about whether their phone will work in an emergency.”
In the letter, Riley demanded Verizon provide the following information to his office:
- The number of residential and business customers in New York’s 19th Congressional District whose copper landline service could be discontinued under Verizon’s application, broken down by county.
- A full list, by county, town, and ZIP code, of every area in New York’s 19th Congressional District where Verizon is seeking to discontinue copper landline service. For each area, indicate whether affected customers currently have access to an alternative voice service, such as fiber or wireless, or whether they will have no alternative option available.
- For each affected customer, the specific alternative service that will be available, and how Verizon has confirmed that it is fully operational at that customer’s location.
- Whether Verizon will commit not to discontinue service to any customer until a working alternative has been confirmed at that customer’s location, and what will happen to customers for whom no reliable alternative exists.
- The financial impact on affected customers, including whether they will be protected against rate increases after switching to a new service, and whether Verizon will cover all necessary equipment, installation and setup costs.
- How replacement services will function during power outages, and how Verizon will ensure uninterrupted access to 911 and other emergency services.
- The steps Verizon will take to engage affected customers, county emergency management offices, and local governments before any service is discontinued, including whether Verizon will commit to holding public meetings in affected communities.
- Why Verizon believes a November 30, 2026 timeline gives customers sufficient time to transition, and whether it will agree to extend that timeline.
You can read the full letter HERE.
###
title: RILEY DEMANDS ANSWERS FROM VERIZON OVER RURAL LANDLINE SHUTOFFS

The U.S. Department of Energy today announced its intent to deploy Defense Production Act funding to develop a second high-voltage connection between Southcentral and Interior Alaska, strengthening grid infrastructure essential to national defense.
October 5, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy today announced its intent to deploy Defense Production Act (DPA) funding to develop a second high-voltage connection between Southcentral and Interior Alaska, strengthening grid infrastructure essential to national defense. The Alaska Energy Authority’s Beluga-Healy Transmission Project combines up to $150 million in DPA funding with $268 million in non-federal funding, representing a planned total investment of $418 million in Alaska’s grid. 
Approximately 223 miles of new transmission line connecting Beluga and Healy will be built. Once complete, grid operators will have an additional pathway to move power between Alaska’s most densely populated communities and major military installations–lowering electricity costs and strengthening grid reliability for approximately 75% of Alaska’s population.
Thanks to President Trump and the passage of the Working Families Tax Cut, $1 billion in federal funding has been appropriated for energy-related projects deemed critical to national security. Presidential Determination No. 2026-10 identifies transmission lines and conductors, substations, and power-control and protection equipment as essential to national defense.
“Supporting improvements to Alaska’s transmission infrastructure with Defense Production Act funds reflects the Trump Administration’s commitment to strengthening national security, improving grid reliability, and lowering electricity costs,” U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright said. “Thanks to Senator Sullivan, I received an extensive briefing from the Alaska Energy Authority during my recent visit to Anchorage in August. This meeting, combined with briefings from Alaska Command, confirmed the need to support an expansion of Alaska’s energy infrastructure. This project will not only support the major U.S. military expansion currently underway in Alaska, but also mining and other resource development critical to our national security.”
“Alaska’s weather is unforgiving, and its grid needs another way to keep power moving,” said Office of Electricity Assistant Secretary Katie Jereza. “Beluga-Healy will provide that critical second route, helping protect communities from disruptions and meet growing demand.”
The current project has a preliminary planning estimate of approximately $418 million. This project reflects the Trump Administration’s focus on delivering critical energy infrastructure while protecting taxpayer dollars and ratepayers.
title: Energy Department Announces Alaska Railbelt Transmission Project to Receive Defense Production Act Funding, Securing Alaska Military Installations and Local Communities

CONCORD – Nashua resident Alexander Diandro Cruz, 19, charged by criminal complaint for possession of a machine gun, was arrested yesterday and appeared in federal court today, U.S. Attorney Erin Creegan announces. Cruz is being detained following his appearance in court.

On September 24, 2026, Nashua Police encountered Cruz and found him in possession of a loaded Glock firearm equipped with a “switch” or machine gun conversion device. A machine gun must be lawfully registered to a possessor in the National Firearms Registration and Transfer Record, but Cruz is not lawfully registered to possess such a weapon.

The charging statute provides a sentence of no greater than 10 years in prison, 3 years of supervised release, and a fine of $10,000.

The details contained in charging documents are allegations. The defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

The Bureau of Alcohol Tobacco Firearms and Explosives and the Nashua Police department are leading the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Charles Rombeau is prosecuting the case.
title: Nashua Man Charged With Possessing Unregistered Machine Gun Conversion Device

Fairfax, VA – Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04), House Administration Committee Ranking Member Joe Morelle (NY-25) and members of Virginia’s Democratic Congressional delegation held a public shadow hearing on Thursday in Fairfax to confront the Trump Administration’s attacks on voting and detail efforts to defend every eligible American’s right to cast a ballot and have it counted.
Panelists outlined litigation, voter education and safeguards countering interference, intimidation and misinformation.
The hearing examined the Administration’s attempted overhaul of mail-ballot processing, federal demands for sensitive voter information and concerns about armed immigration agents at polling places. The experts explained how litigation blocked the mail-voting rule and detailed ongoing efforts to protect voter privacy and prevent intimidation.
In his remarks and responses to lawmakers, Fairfax County Board of Supervisors Chairman Jeff McKay outlined safeguards against duplicate voting, secured ballot drop boxes and the county’s use of paper ballots and scanners without internet connectivity. The discussion emphasized that protecting election integrity and ensuring access to the ballot go hand in hand.
“My own family struggled, fought, bled and in some cases died for the right to vote,” said Congresswoman McClellan. “We have seen repeated efforts by the Administration to undermine the electoral process and the constitutionally protected right of millions to vote. Election integrity means protecting our election systems from foreign interference and unlawful voting, but it also means protecting every citizen’s right to vote, free of intimidation, free from discrimination. We cannot have an America that goes back to the days when propaganda, violence and voter suppression were used to keep all of the people from participating in their government.”
“Where the Trump Administration is sowing fear and confusion, we’re providing facts and defending the right to vote. We came together in Fairfax to make clear that every eligible American, no matter who they support, can cast a ballot with confidence,” said Congressman Walkinshaw. “I’m grateful to Ranking Member Morelle for joining us and proud to stand alongside my Virginia colleagues and the voting rights leaders doing this work every day. We will keep fighting to protect every vote and ensure the American people decide who represents them.”
“In this moment, there is nothing more urgent than protecting American democracy,” said Ranking Member Morelle. “The election is here and we are protecting Americans’ right to the ballot box. Every time the Trump Administration has tried to interfere with the integrity of the midterm elections, they have lost. Over the next month, we need to remain clear-eyed about the threats we continue to face. We will fight to protect American elections. Failure, quite simply, is not an option.”
“Over the last two years, the Trump Administration and the Supreme Court have levied various attacks against the right to vote,” said Congressman Bobby Scott, Ranking Member of the House Education and Workforce Committee. “Unfortunately, Congressional Republicans have been unwilling to take a stand against these actions. Democrats are fighting to defend everyone’s right to participate in our elections, and this hearing demonstrates the urgency of this fight.”
“Every eligible voter should be able to cast their ballot without fear, intimidation, or unnecessary barriers,” said Congressman Vindman. “Our democracy works when voters know their voices will be heard and their votes will be counted. I’m proud to stand with my Virginia colleagues, local election officials, and voting rights advocates to protect access to the ballot, safeguard voter privacy, and ensure every eligible Virginian can make their voice heard.”
“This Administration has threatened to cheat and exhaust every option to diminish our free and fair elections. In these unprecedented times, I am proud to stand together with my colleagues and voting rights organizations to protect the voices of all Americans. We will ensure every vote, regardless of party, gets counted this November. We will not be intimidated,” said Congressman Suhas Subramanyam.
The panel included Chairman McKay; Skye Perryman, President and CEO of Democracy Forward; Omar Noureldin, Senior Vice President for Policy and Litigation Strategy at Common Cause; Rev. Dr. Cozy Bailey, President of the Virginia State Conference NAACP; and Jessica Jones Capparell, Director of Government Affairs at the League of Women Voters of the United States.
The experts urged voters to check their registration, make a plan to vote and consult trusted election officials.
View photo gallery here.
Watch the full hearing: C-SPAN.
title: McClellan, Morelle and Virginia Democrats Fight Trump Administration’s Attacks on Voting, Pledge to Protect Every Vote

Seattle – A 36-year-old Carnation, Washington, man was sentenced today in U.S. District Court in Seattle to three years in prison for wire fraud, access device fraud, and aggravated identity theft for his two distinct fraud schemes to steal pandemic unemployment benefits and steal the home, bank assets, and stock portfolio of a deceased Seattle victim. Tyler Lee Berens pleaded guilty in July 2026. At today’s sentencing hearing, U.S. District Judge John H. Chun noted these were “addiction-fueled” crimes that were nonetheless serious and had wide-reaching ramifications on the government and the victim.

Berens conducted two fraud schemes between 2020 and 2024. Beginning in May 2020, Berens submitted false claims for pandemic unemployment benefits in 19 different states: Montana, New Jersey, Nevada, Kansas, South Dakota, California, Arizona, Utah, Vermont, Alabama, Washington, Minnesota, Rhode Island, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Idaho, Indiana, Delaware, and Colorado. He received a total of $148,206 from six of those states - Colorado, Kansas, Montana, Nevada, Rhode Island, and Washington. Berens also applied for and was approved for a Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loan of $17,500. His PPP application was false, and no loan funds were paid out.

Two years later, Berens launched a second fraud scheme to steal the Seattle home, bank accounts, and stock portfolio of a deceased elderly victim by posing as the victim’s authorized agent, impersonating the victim, and using the victim’s personal information. Berens made multiple attempts to steal a total of over half a million dollars’ worth of the victim’s assets.

Berens sent a real estate agent a forged power of attorney document and represented that he had the victim’s authorization to sell the victim’s home. Berens had even accepted an offer for the home, but fortunately the victim’s niece was alerted, stepped in, and reported the attempted fraud.

Berens was not deterred once caught in the real estate fraud. He accessed the victim’s bank accounts to try to transfer money from them and obtained a debit card for the victim’s checking account. After fraud restrictions were placed on the accounts, Berens attempted to get them removed by impersonating the deceased victim via email.

Finally, Berens took over the victim’s brokerage accounts and attempted to transfer money to himself and tried to liquidate over $235,000 worth of stocks. When, once again, fraud restrictions stopped the attempted transactions and cut off his access, Berens impersonated the deceased victim and tried to regain control of the accounts.

Berens was indicted in August 2025, and pleaded guilty to wire fraud, aggravated identity theft, and access device fraud on July 2, 2026.

In asking for the three-year prison sentence, prosecutors wrote to the court, “The $148,206.00 that went into Berens’ pocket was money siphoned away from people and businesses in desperate need of assistance during the pandemic. He deliberately exploited vulnerabilities in the government’s controls during an unprecedented and devastating period for his personal gain. As a result of his and similar schemes, the government continues to expend an inordinate amount of resources investigating and prosecuting COVID-19-related fraud.”

“For years, Mr. Berens sought to profit through a variety of schemes, taking advantage of pandemic-era assistance programs to receive benefits to which he was not entitled from six states, and also impersonating a deceased person to steal their assets," said W. Mike Herrington, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI Seattle field office. "The FBI and our partners will carefully follow the money to pursue those who steal funds, and identities, that rightfully belong to others.”

“Today’s sentencing demonstrates our commitment to holding accountable those who exploit vulnerable individuals and abuse federal programs, ensuring they face the consequences they deserve. Fraud is not a victimless crime, and my office will continue to pursue justice for those exploited and uphold the integrity of our financial and social systems,” said Anthony P. D’Esposito, Inspector General, U.S. Department of Labor.

Berens will be on three years of supervised release following prison and was ordered to pay $148,706 in restitution.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

The case was investigated by the FBI, the Social Security Administration Office of Inspector General (SSA-OIG), and the U.S. Department of Labor Office of Inspector General (DOL-OIG).

The case is being prosecuted by Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Jessica M. Ly.
title: Carnation, Washington, man sentenced to prison for COVID fraud scheme and attempts to steal from deceased Seattle victim

ADDRESSING AMERICAN DIESEL AFFORDABILITY: Today, President Donald J. Trump signed an Executive Order to temporarily allow off-road “dyed” diesel for highway use and defer the applicable Federal excise tax, lowering costs for Americans.
- The Order directs the Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Secretary of War, to defer payment of the Federal excise tax imposed for on-road use of dyed diesel fuel for the remainder of the year without interest or penalties, and to explore pathways to eliminate the obligation to pay the deferred taxes.
- The Order directs the Secretary of Transportation to coordinate with States, industry leadership, and labor organizations on access to dyed diesel.
- The Order directs the Secretary of Agriculture to ensure farmers’ access to dyed diesel in high-demand areas, and to encourage corresponding action by States.
- The Order directs the Director of the White House Office of Intergovernmental Affairs to encourage more States to adopt policies that correspond with the Secretary of the Treasury’s actions pursuant to this Order.
PUTTING MONEY BACK INTO THE POCKETS OF AMERICANS: President Trump is addressing fuel affordability for American consumers, farmers, truckers, and workers. The Administration has already undertaken historic efforts to ensure fuel affordability for Americans, and is taking this action to make available further temporary relief for Americans because of ongoing global conditions affecting the supply of diesel.
- Farmers and truckers are essential to the American way of life, feeding families, fueling communities, and sustaining the American people. As restricted global diesel supply, driven by the Russia-Ukraine war and a lack of refining capacity around the world, including Democrat-led States that chose to shut down their refineries in the name of “Green Energy” policies, has led to rising prices, further action is necessary to provide Americans with relief.
- This action will put money directly back in the pockets of American farmers, truckers, and workers, for example saving truckers over $100 per refill.
- Diesel is taxed based on its intended use. “On-road” or highway diesel is subject to state and federal excise taxes. Diesel used for off-road purposes, such as agricultural, construction, or heating, is not taxed. This off-road diesel is dyed red so that law enforcement can identify it to enforce penalties and back taxes for on-road use.
- The Administration, and State Governors, can exercise their enforcement discretion to halt inspections and waive the tax liability that users would face for on-road use of dyed diesel.
CUTTING COSTS THROUGH AMERICAN ENERGY DOMINANCE AND SUPPORTING AMERICA’S FARMERS AND TRUCKERS: The Trump Administration’s American energy dominance and economic policies are reducing costs and delivering real benefits to hardworking Americans across the country.
- Since Day One, President Trump and his Administration have fought to rescind the Biden Administration’s inflation-fueling energy regulations, eliminate red tape, and restore America’s position as the world’s leading energy producer. 
  - As a result, the United States has reclaimed its position as the world’s leading energy producer and exporter, driving economic growth, lowering costs for families, and bolstering our national security. Under President Trump’s leadership, American energy dominance is back.
- President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts delivered for America’s farmers and ranchers, putting their hard-earned money back in their pockets. This historic legislation modernized the farm safety net, expanded market access for farmers, and invested in rural economies. Additionally, the Trump Administration has delivered over $40 billion in direct aid to farmers since January 2025.
- Since President Trump returned to office, the Trump Administration has prioritized American truckers, replacing illegal immigrant truck drivers with American veterans. In that time, American truckers’ earnings have increased by over 7%.
- The Department of Transportation waived its hours of service rules, allowing truck drivers handling gasoline and diesel shipments to drive additional hours, lowering fuel costs for all Americans.
- In August 2026, President Trump announced the largest oil deal in world history with Venezuela, securing 65 billion barrels of oil to double America’s oil reserves, increase our oil supply, and lower gas prices for all Americans, long into the future.
- In October 2026, President Trump successfully negotiated with Europe to release 100 million barrels of refined diesel from its strategic reserves within the next four months. This will increase supply and bring diesel prices down for Americans.
title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Promotes Diesel Affordability

DENTON, Texas – Randall “Randy” D. Meshell took the oath of office today as Regional Administrator for FEMA Region 6, following his appointment by the Trump administration.
FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton arrived from Washington, D.C. to participate in the swearing in ceremony at the Denton, Texas, regional headquarters.
The Region 6 Administrator oversees FEMA operations supporting 68 federally recognized Tribal Nations and the states of Arkansas, Louisiana, New Mexico, Oklahoma and Texas.
“We are thrilled to welcome Regional Administrator Meshell who understands unique qualities and challenges of these States,” Administrator Hamilton said. “I look forward to working with him as FEMA continues to support communities across the country under President Trump’s leadership. This includes locally managed, state-led, and federally supported capacity building throughout the disaster lifecycle.”
Meshell most recently directed statewide preparedness as Division Chief for the Texas Division of Emergency Management (TDEM). He led the state’s efforts to strengthen local emergency planning, exercises, technological hazards and emerging threat preparedness.
Previously, he led the FEMA Region 6 National Preparedness Division. In that role, he managed security, intelligence, continuity of operations, training, exercises, grants and preparedness programs.
The Secretary of Homeland Security twice appointed him to Federal Coordination Teams for special regional security events, and he has managed responses to numerous major national disasters and emergencies.
Before FEMA, Meshell worked as a firefighter and assistant fire marshal. As a U.S. Army veteran, he deployed in support of Operation Noble Eagle and Operation Iraqi Freedom. Meshell earned a bachelor’s degree in criminal justice from Cameron University in Lawton, Oklahoma and is an alumnus of the FEMA Pinnacle program.
Follow us at x.com/FEMARegion6 and at linkedin.com/showcase/fema-region-6/ and like us at facebook.com/FEMARegion6/.
title: FEMA Appoints Randall D. Meshell as Regional Administrator for Region 6

Washington, DC – Legislation led Rep. Lucy McBath (D-Ga.) and Chairman of the U.S. House Education and Workforce Committee Tim Walberg (R-Mich.) has passed the Senate unanimously and is headed to the President’s desk to be signed into law. The bipartisan, bicameral Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act is led by Senators Jon Husted (R-Ohio) and Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.).
This bill directs the Department of Labor (DOL) to train its employees to identify human trafficking and refer suspected trafficking crimes to law enforcement. While DOL employees are on the ground conducting workplace inspections, they will be able to spot human trafficking behavior in real time.
“Human trafficking is a devastating crime that preys on the most vulnerable and robs victims of their freedom and dignity. We have a responsibility to ensure that those on the front lines in our communities and across the federal government have the tools necessary to help combat this crime and provide survivors with a path to safety. Strengthening training for Department of Labor employees is an important step toward recognizing the signs of human trafficking, protecting victims, and connecting them with the resources they need. I thank my colleagues for their support,” said McBath.
“Human trafficking is a national tragedy, and we need to do everything we can to stop it. This law will help ensure federal workers are equipped to spot the signs of human trafficking and refer suspected crimes to law enforcement. I’m proud this bill will be my fourth bill signed into law since I took office. This is a great example of the bipartisan work we can accomplish for the American people, and I look forward to the lives this law will help save,” said Husted.
“The fight against human trafficking should never be a partisan issue. Survivors and victims in Michigan and across the country are owed justice, accountability, and meaningful action to prevent these crimes from happening in the first place. Our bipartisan bill, the Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act, provides the Department of Labor with the necessary framework to address these unthinkable crimes head-on. I am proud to have worked alongside my colleagues to get this important legislation passed and look forward to seeing it signed into law,” said Slotkin.
“Human trafficking can hide in plain sight, and this bill will help more people recognize the warning signs. I’m glad the Senate unanimously passed my bill and sent it to President Trump’s desk. By giving Department of Labor employees the right training, we can help identify victims sooner and get potential cases to law enforcement,” said Walberg.
McBath and Walberg introduced the companion bill to the Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking in the House of Representatives, where it passed on March 3, 2026.
Full text of the bill is available here.
title: McBath Bill to Stop Human Trafficking Passes Senate, Heads to President’s Desk

EPA Implements Updated Cleanup Approach to Address Groundwater Contamination at Baird & McGuire Superfund Site
BOSTON (Oct. 5, 2026) – U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has selected an interim cleanup plan for groundwater at the Baird & McGuire Superfund Site located in Holbrook, Massachusetts.
After approximately 25 years of active site remediation, contaminant levels at the site have decreased, but groundwater remains impacted. In 2023, EPA began a Focused Feasibility Study (FFS) to evaluate additional cleanup options, and in 2026 selected a new cleanup approach based on the evaluations performed during the FFS.
"We've made real progress at the Baird & McGuire Site, but we need a different approach to address the groundwater contamination that remains," said EPA Regional Administrator Mark Sanborn. "This updated plan will move the cleanup forward and put us on a better path toward restoring the groundwater to drinking water standards."
The updated cleanup plan is based on past investigations, a pilot test, updated human health and ecological risk assessments, the 2026 FFS, and comments received on EPA's Proposed Plan during a 37-day public comment period. This cleanup plan is formally called an Interim Record of Decision Amendment for Operable Unit 1 (Groundwater and Surface Water).
EPA's interim cleanup plan includes:
- Treating polluted groundwater directly underground. This includes injecting sulfate into groundwater to help naturally break down harmful chemicals and to trap arsenic so it cannot spread.
- Additional cleanup options for reducing arsenic contamination may involve:
  - Cleaning groundwater using filters designed to remove arsenic, and/or
  - Underground treatment using air or a special barrier that helps capture arsenic until groundwater conditions improve.
EPA will continue to track groundwater and see whether pollution outside the treatment areas is decreasing enough for groundwater to achieve drinking water standards. EPA will also watch for any signs that contamination is spreading to the bedrock groundwater.
EPA will also continue to use groundwater use restrictions and engineered barriers that prevent people from using contaminated groundwater and keep activities from disturbing the pollution plume. These protective measures will remain in place until cleanup goals are met.
EPA estimates the interim cleanup plan including construction, operation, maintenance, and long-term monitoring will cost about $7.1 million.
More information
A copy of the interim cleanup plan, the Administrative Record supporting the cleanup plan, and other background information about the Baird & McGuire Superfund Site can be found at: www.epa.gov/superfund/baird
Background
The Baird & McGuire Superfund Site is located at 775 South Street in Holbrook, Massachusetts. Baird & McGuire Company, Inc. operated a chemical mixing and batching operation at the Site for approximately 71 years. Manufactured products included herbicides, pesticides, disinfectants, soaps, floor waxes, and solvents.
Operations from the facility resulted in contaminant releases to soil and groundwater. Site-related contamination includes various volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds (VOCs and SVOCs), pesticides, and arsenic.
Record of Decision Administrative Record:  
Baird & McGuire Interim Record of Decision Amendment Administrative Record
title: EPA Implements Updated Cleanup Approach to Address Groundwater Contamination at Baird & McGuire Superfund Site

PIERRE - United States Attorney Ron Parsons announced today that U.S. District Judge Eric C. Schulte has sentenced a Mission, South Dakota, man convicted of two counts of Assault with a Dangerous Weapon. The sentencing took place on September 28, 2026.

Daniel Hart, age 20, was sentenced to six years and seven months in federal prison on each count, with the sentence to be served concurrently, followed by three years of supervised release. Hart was further ordered to pay a $200 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund.

Hart was indicted in January 2026. He pleaded guilty on June 29, 2026.

The convictions stemmed from two separate incidents that occurred within the Rosebud Sioux Indian Reservation. On May 24, 2025, Hart and others assaulted a man with a machete and shod feet outside a gas station in Mission, South Dakota. The man sustained multiple injuries including lacerations to his left arm and scalp.

In a separate incident on December 6, 2025, a man was driving a vehicle in Mission when his vehicle was blocked in by another vehicle occupied by Hart. Hart exited his vehicle and approached the man’s vehicle on the driver’s side. Hart pointed a firearm through the driver’s side window and pulled the trigger, striking the man in the leg.

These matters were prosecuted by the U.S. Attorney’s Office because the Major Crimes Act, a federal statute, mandates that certain violent crimes alleged to have occurred in Indian country be prosecuted in federal court as opposed to State court.

These cases were investigated by Rosebud Sioux Tribe Law Enforcement Services. Assistant U.S. Attorney Abby VanDenBerg prosecuted the case.

Hart was immediately remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service.
title: Mission Man Sentenced to Over 6 Years in Federal Prison for Assault

SEC Coordinates with Global Financial Regulators to Raise Fraud Awareness During World Investor Week
Washington D.C., Oct. 5, 2026 —
The Securities and Exchange Commission, in coordination with other U.S. and global financial regulators, today issued a joint investor bulletin as part of World Investor Week (WIW). The bulletin encourages investors to be resilient in changing economic conditions and to be vigilant in the face of rising relationship investment and impersonation scams.
World Investor Week is a global effort by the International Organization of Securities Commissions to bring together regulators across six continents to raise awareness about the importance of investor education and investor protection. This year marks WIW’s tenth anniversary. The SEC, coordinating U.S. efforts, worked with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Securities Investor Protection Corporation, National Futures Association, and North American Securities Administrators Association to issue the joint Investor Bulletin.
“Investor protection is a core tenet of the SEC’s mission, and World Investor Week provides another important opportunity for U.S. financial regulators and international counterparts to raise awareness together and encourage investor resilience across the globe,” said SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins. “This week, as always, I urge investors to take advantage of the resources on the SEC’s Investor.gov website and to remain vigilant against potential scams.”
“Investors can use the principles of resiliency that the SEC and our partners highlight this week to help protect themselves against fraud and weather market volatility,” said John Moses, Director of the SEC’s Office of Investor Education and Assistance. “We encourage investors to visit Investor.gov, which provides free, accurate, unbiased information and financial planning tools to help individuals invest wisely and better protect themselves against investment fraud.”
The SEC’s WIW page highlights resources on investor education and protection.
###

title: SEC Coordinates with Global Financial Regulators to Raise Fraud Awareness During World Investor Week

MACON, Ga. – U.S. Attorney William R. “Will” Keyes and FBI Atlanta’s Supervisory Senior Resident Agent Robert Gibbs launched a renewed training initiative to empower older adults in the Middle District of Georgia on financial fraud and abuse, as crimes targeting this population continue to climb rapidly, with the FBI reporting a 37% increase in reported crimes in 2025 compared to the year prior.

U.S. Attorney Will Keyes and FBI Atlanta’s SSRA Robert Gibbs speak to residents of the Pruitt Health Active Assisted Living Community in Macon, Georgia, on Oct. 2, 2026.

“We want to support older adults as they take proactive steps to protect themselves from individuals who target them for financial fraud and abuse,” said U.S. Attorney William R. “Will” Keyes. “Under the direction of the National Fraud Enforcement Division, we are using every available tool to combat financial fraud, including specialized training designed to help older adults recognize the signs of financial crimes, safeguard themselves, and report suspected wrongdoing. This layered approach strengthens prevention efforts and ultimately helps reduce the victimization of older people.”

“Overall, while violent crime is dropping dramatically here in Georgia and across the nation, elder fraud continues to increase as criminals target some of our most vulnerable,” said Robert Gibbs, Supervisory Senior Resident Agent of FBI Atlanta's Macon office. “We want to provide older adults with every possible resource to protect themselves. It is important for victims to not be ashamed and report the crimes when they happen.”

“The U.S. Attorney and the FBI did an outstanding job explaining just how easily seniors can become targets of scams. Their message reassured our residents that there is no shame in being scammed, what matters is reporting it,” said Mary Hudson, the Assisted Living Administrator of Pruitt Place Peake Active Assisted Living Community. “I’m grateful for their commitment to sharing this program with our community and helping protect our seniors.”

U.S. Attorney Keyes and SSRA Gibbs spoke to residents at the Pruitt Place Peake Active Assisted Living Community in Macon on Friday, October 2. During the hour-long presentation and conversation, participants learned how to recognize warning signs of financial mistreatment, common tactics used in financial scams, and how to protect themselves from these crimes. According to the FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) data, in 2025 there were $7.7 billion in losses from over 200,000 victims. This is a 37% increase in complaints from 2024. For more information about these types of crimes, please visit https://www.fbi.gov/how-we-can-help-you/common-frauds-and-scams/elder-fraud .

For more information about how you can bring this training to older adult and senior living communities or community groups within the Middle District of Georgia, please contact Dion Lyons, Law Enforcement Coordinator with the U.S. Attorney’s Office, at dion.lyons@usdoj.gov or call (478) 733-9659.

This training is offered as part of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s efforts. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: U.S. Attorney’s Office Launches Renewed Training Initiative to Empower Older Adults to Combat Elder Financial Fraud and Abuse

New Regulations Make It Easier to Find, Compare, and Report Healthcare Pricing and Coverage Information
WASHINGTON, D.C.—OCTOBER 5, 2026—The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), through the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), today announced that Americans will have access to more reliable, accessible, and actionable information about what their health coverage includes and what they are likely to pay before receiving care under new regulations that strengthen federal healthcare price transparency requirements. The actions taken today to create a more transparent healthcare marketplace also ensure employers can make more informed decisions; researchers can better understand healthcare markets; and innovators can build better tools.
“Americans should know what their healthcare will cost before they receive it,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “President Trump directed us to bring real price transparency to healthcare, and HHS is delivering. These rules give patients clearer, more reliable information to compare costs, understand their coverage, and make informed decisions before they receive care.”
“Greater transparency drives competition, reduces price disparities, and helps lower healthcare costs, a key priority for the Trump Administration,” said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “At the heart of this rule is a simple idea: People should know what their health insurance will cover and what they will need to pay before receiving medical care, not after the bill arrives.”
Updates to the Transparency in Coverage (TiC) rules, finalized today by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), in partnership with the Departments of Labor and the Treasury (the Departments), build on the historic health care price transparency rules established during President Trump’s first term.
The final rules improve the underlying healthcare pricing data by reducing duplicative and unnecessary information, providing more context about in-network prices, increasing available out-of-network pricing information, and strengthening accountability for the completeness and accuracy of published data. Reporting frequency for pricing information will change from monthly to quarterly, maintaining meaningful transparency while lowering administrative burden.
The rules also require group health plans and health insurance issuers to provide consumers with personalized cost-sharing information by phone, in addition to existing online tools.
These improvements will help technology developers build better consumer tools, give consumers more reliable information when comparing costs before receiving care, and enable employers and researchers to better analyze healthcare markets, all of which will help drive competition across the healthcare industry.
“Transparency is a pillar of the Trump Administration’s efforts to drive better value in healthcare,” said Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling, “Today’s final rules will enhance the Transparency in Coverage (TiC) files already in existence, giving workers and employers alike a clearer view of their true healthcare costs.”
“Healthcare price transparency is common sense,” said FTC Chairman Andrew N. Ferguson. “But only President Donald Trump, with assists from Secretary Kennedy, Secretary Sonderling and Dr. Oz, decided to actually make it happen. Today’s announcements follow a basic but important principle: Consumers should always have as much information as possible.”
“Under President Trump’s leadership, this Administration is delivering on its commitment to strengthen transparency and accountability across America’s healthcare system,” said Deputy Secretary of the Treasury Francis Brooke. “This rule helps improve the standardization, accuracy, and accessibility of pricing disclosures to put Americans and their families in a better position to understand the cost of their health care coverage and make informed decisions about their own care.”
The Departments plan to begin development of the initial schema for the Prescription Drug File in November 2026 and will finalize it on or around May 2027. Plans and issuers will be expected to publish their Prescription Drug Files using this schema starting in December 2027 and monthly thereafter.
Today’s announcement builds on the original TiC regulations established during President Trump’s first term. This work allowed for continued refinement to TiC requirements that have improved the usability of pricing data, enabling developers to build more accurate tools for consumers, employers, researchers, and industry. Recent data have found that the top 25% of the most expensive healthcare service prices have dropped by 6.3% per year following the initial implementation of price transparency requirements on hospitals and health plans.
Today’s final rules support Executive Order 14221, Making America Healthy Again by Empowering Patients with Clear, Accurate, and Actionable Healthcare Pricing Information.
To view the final rules, visit: https://www.federalregister.gov/public-inspection/2026-20447/transparency-in-coverage
To read the CMS fact sheet, including implementation dates, visit: https://www.cms.gov/newsroom/fact-sheets/transparency-coverage-final-rules-cms-9882-f
Like HHS on Facebook, follow HHS on X @HHSgov, @SecKennedy, and sign up for HHS Email Updates.

title: New Regulations Make It Easier to Find, Compare, and Report Healthcare Pricing and Coverage Information
