text:
Weaponization Working Group Releases Report on Garland Memo That Chilled Parental Rights and Warned Parents Could Be Domestic Terrorists
Today, the Justice Department’s Weaponization Working Group issued a report detailing how Biden Administration officials at the Department of Justice explored avenues to prosecute parents and protestors who spoke to school boards and school officials during the Covid-19 pandemic.
Today’s report focuses on the production and circulation of an October 4, 2021 memorandum sent from Attorney General Merrick Garland to the Director of the FBI, the Assistant Attorney General for the Criminal Division, the Director of the Executive Office for U.S. Attorneys, and United States Attorneys.
On January 20, 2025, President Trump signed Executive Order 14147 to eliminate the political weaponization of federal agencies. To many Americans, Attorney General Garland’s memo embodied the misuse and weaponization of government power. This report fulfills the February 2, 2025 directive from Attorney General Pam Bondi to review the Memo and the report ordered by the President in EO 14147.
The report details how, despite being presented with very little evidence of actual violence or violent threats against school administrators and at school board meetings, Garland arrived at a memo which claimed, “in recent months, there has been a disturbing spike in harassment, intimidation, and threats of violence.”
The Working Group’s report makes clear that the ideological inspiration for the October 4, 2021 memo was a September 29, 2021 letter from the National School Boards Association to President Joe Biden in which the organization urged the federal government to consider that “these heinous actions” “could be equivalent to a form of domestic terrorism and hate crimes.”
The Working Group officially acknowledges what many Americans already assumed: that as Biden Administration actions chilled the exercise of parental and free speech rights, parents who lawfully exercised their parental rights and freedom of speech were often targeted by members of the educational establishment.
Among the most egregious findings, exhibits show that individuals in the Biden White House and Attorney General Garland’s advisors wanted to involve federal law enforcement and prosecutors in matters involving parents and school boards. Further, the Memo established a task force to find federal enforcement options for investigating and prosecuting parents and the FBI opened 25 “Guardian assessments” on parents. One FBI whistleblower disclosed that a mother was investigated because she “is a gun owner” and belonged to a “right-wing mom’s group.”
After thoroughly reviewing internal communications and investigative records, the Working Group found that more than a dozen DOJ and FBI personnel raised concerns with the Memo and its directive, including:
- “Stupid, stupid, stupid”
- “they might as well rename the damn thing the Anti-MAGA Task Force”
- “ridiculous,”
- “challenging from a First Amendment perspective”
- “potentially dangerous ground”
- “horrible”
- “confusing”
- “look[s] political”
- “a partisan exercise aimed at those who do not support the Administration”
- Would “tarnish reputation as an apolitical law enforcer”
- “very messy and political”
- “nothing remotely federal”
Despite internal pushback, emails show Attorney General Garland issued the Memo, influenced by White House officials. The Working Group confirms the Memo was the product of pressure exerted by the White House and wrongly weaponized the Department of Justice against parents.
The Trump Administration and Attorney General Todd Blanche have made securing parental and First Amendment rights a top priority. In addition to the investigative Report, the Department of Justice is taking the following steps:
- Parents and other participants at school board meetings who became the subject or target of an FBI Guardian assessment as a result of the Garland Memorandum will be offered the opportunity to review the Guardian.
- A disclaimer will be added to Guardian assessments associated with the Garland Memorandum. The majority of these Guardian assessments have been closed or discontinued, but this disclaimer will note that the Garland Memorandum raised serious constitutional concerns, and so any Guardian assessment resulting from it should be read with caution.
- The Department will review the files of anyone who was investigated under the Garland Memorandum to determine if their constitutional rights were violated. To the extent such a violation is found, the Department will issue a formal apology and institute internal controls as necessary to prevent repeating the violation.
- Through the Office of Community Oriented Policing Services, the Department is partnering with the National Association of School Resource Officers and awarding them $1.5 million to develop and deliver a series of training and technical assistance directly to our nation’s school resource officers. The goal of this grant is to increase the organization’s capacity to inform school employees regarding the rights of parents in our primary and secondary educational system.
- Through the Office of Justice Programs, the Department is prioritizing additional funding to provide resources and training to schoolteachers and staff about the First Amendment rights of parents and the rights of parents to direct and guide the upbringing and education of their children.
This report follows letters sent earlier today by Department of Justice and Department of Education leadership to all 50 state attorneys general on parental rights. The letters can be viewed here.
The Justice Department remains committed to defending Constitutionally protected civil liberties, especially the First Amendment rights of all Americans. Individuals with concerns about unconstitutional conduct are encouraged to come forward; the Department will evaluate such matters without fear or favor.
Read the full report here.
Press Release Number: 26-1138
title: Weaponization Working Group Releases Report on Garland Memo That Chilled Parental Rights and Warned Parents Could Be Domestic Terrorists

text:
RICHARD J. MESSINA, 54, of Trumbull, pleaded guilty today before U.S. District Judge Vernon D. Oliver in Hartford to an offense stemming from his participation in an embezzlement conspiracy involving Success Village Apartments, Inc., located in Bridgeport and Stratford.

The announcement was made by David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut; P.J. O’Brien, Special Agent in Charge of the New Haven Division of the FBI; Thomas Demeo, Special Agent in Charge of IRS Criminal Investigation in New England; and Justin Page, Acting Inspector in Charge of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Boston Division.

According to court documents and statements made in court, Success Village Apartments, Inc. (“SVA”) is a residential cooperative located in Bridgeport and Stratford. SVA comprises 96 separate buildings containing 924 residential units. Messina and Carmine Gentile own Umbrella Mechanical LLC (“Umbrella”), a New Jersey-registered company, and Messina owns RJM Mechanical (“RJM”), a Connecticut-registered Company, businesses that provided commercial and residential plumbing, heating, and air conditioning services. In approximately June 2022, Umbrella began providing plumbing services to SVA, including work on the piping and boilers that provided heat and hot water to SVA residents. In approximately July 2024, RJM began providing plumbing services related to heat and hot water to SVA. SVA’s general manager, Charles Pitcher, referred Messina and Umbrella to SVA as a plumbing contractor.

Between approximately June 2022 and September 2024, Messina, Gentile, Pitcher, and others, including an individual identified as “Person-2” in the Criminal Information charging Messina, engaged in an embezzlement conspiracy through which vendors, including Umbrella and RJM, would submit fraudulent invoices and requests for payment to SVA, either for work that was not performed or at artificially inflated prices that overstated the amount of money owed by SVA. Pitcher and Person-2 agreed that, in exchange for the vendors’ receipt of work and payments from SVA, the vendors would divert a percentage of the payments received from SVA to Pitcher and Person-2. Messina, Gentile, and their co-conspirators agreed that, in exchange for Umbrella’s and RJM’s receipt of work and payments from SVA, Umbrella and RJM would divert approximately 20 percent of those payments to Pitcher and Person-2.

Messina, Gentile, and others prepared and caused to be prepared fraudulent invoices and requests for payment to SVA that were not the result of a competitive bidding process, contained objectively unreasonable markups for certain goods and services, contained charges for goods and services that were not rendered, contained amounts to be billed to SVA that were chosen by Pitcher and Person-2, and were otherwise fraudulently inflated, including by not accounting for the money that was remitted to Pitcher and Person-2.

SVA paid Umbrella approximately $2,631,769.71 and RJM approximately $99,414.11 during the conspiracy, $546,000 of which was diverted to Pitcher and Person-2.

Messina pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, an offense that carries a maximum term of imprisonment of 20 years. As part of his plea agreement, he has agreed to a forfeiture money judgment in the amount of at least $750,000 and agreed to pay restitution in the amount of at least $1,500,000. He is released on a $100,000 bond pending sentencing.

Gentile and Pitcher previously pleaded guilty and await sentencing.

This ongoing investigation is being conducted by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigation Division, and the U.S. Postal Inspection Service. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Paul A. Riley.
title: Trumbull Man Admits Role in Success Village Apartments Embezzlement Conspiracy

Blair: New SNAP Cut Hits Georgia Families as 5 Million Americans Have Already Lost Food Assistance
Congressman's office stands ready to help GA-13 residents keep their benefits and navigate new federal rules
Media Contact:
Allison Phipps, Allison.Phipps@mail.house.gov ; Amya Enlow, Amya.Enlow@mail.house.gov
Washington, D.C. – Congressman Everton Blair (GA-13) warned today that the latest SNAP cut in H.R. 1, the Republican Reconciliation Law, is now in effect, and announced that his office will help constituents across the 13th District keep the food assistance they are eligible for.
As of October 1, Washington pays half of what it used to toward the cost of running SNAP, leaving states to cover 75% of administrative costs. Nationwide, that is more than $16 billion in lost funding. For Georgia, it means an estimated $43.7 million hole this year and up to $58.3 million every year after.
"When Washington cuts the people who process SNAP applications and then piles new paperwork on families, the result is predictable: longer waits, more mistakes, and eligible people losing food they qualify for," said Congressman Blair. "This is about a mother in Clayton County waiting weeks for a renewal, a senior in Rockdale who can't get anyone on the phone, a veteran in Henry County who loses benefits over a missed form. Georgia had to put up more than $46 million of its own money just to keep the lights on, and that is a patch, not a plan. Families in our district should not go hungry to pay for tax breaks for big corporations and the wealthiest Americans. I will keep fighting to reverse these cuts. In the meantime, if you have lost benefits, received a notice you don't understand, or aren't sure what the new rules mean for you, call my office. We will help you."
What this means for Georgia and the 13th District
About 1.4 million Georgians rely on SNAP, and roughly seven in ten Georgia SNAP households include a child. Fewer administrative dollars mean fewer caseworkers to process applications, determine eligibility, and answer questions at the moment new federal rules are making the program harder to navigate.
State lawmakers temporarily filled the gap with $46.4 million in FY 2027, plus $18.2 million for error-rate reduction. But relying on state funds to backstop federal cuts is not sustainable, and it puts schools, public safety, and other state and local services at risk. A second cost shift, forcing states to pay a share of SNAP benefits themselves, begins as soon as October 1, 2027.
According to USDA data, more than 5 million Americans, including about 2 million children, have lost SNAP since H.R. 1 was enacted in July 2025. More than 150,000 of them are Georgians.
Help for GA-13 residents
H.R. 1 also expanded SNAP work requirements. Many adults up to age 64, parents of teenagers 14 and older, veterans, people experiencing homelessness, and young adults leaving foster care must now document 80 hours a month of work, training, or volunteering to keep their benefits. Congressman Blair's office can help constituents:
- Understand whether the new rules apply to them and whether they qualify for an exemption
- Resolve delayed applications, renewals, and notices with the Georgia Division of Family and Children Services
- Connect with local food banks and community partners
Residents should watch their mail and their Georgia Gateway account for notices and respond by the deadline. For help, contact the district office at (770)-210-5073 or visit the website.

title: Blair: New SNAP Cut Hits Georgia Families as 5 Million Americans Have Already Lost Food Assistance

October 5, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Energy Dominance Financing (EDF) today announced a conditional loan commitment of up to $4.2 billion to finance nuclear uprates and modernization across Vistra’s nuclear fleet in Pennsylvania and Ohio. Today’s announcement will deliver more reliable American energy, strengthen the grid, lower costs, and meet growing power demand across the 13-state PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (PJM) region.
The investment advances President Trump’s Executive Order Reinvigorating the Nuclear Industrial Base, and marks another major step in restoring American nuclear leadership.
“President Trump promised to unleash an American nuclear renaissance, and the Energy Department is delivering,” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. “By getting more power out of the nuclear plants we already have, we can deliver more affordable, reliable, around the-clock energy for American families and businesses.”
The projects will preserve nearly 4 gigawatts (GW) of reliable baseload power—enough to power more than 3 million homes—and add 433 megawatts (MW) of new nuclear capacity, helping meet growing electricity demand in Pennsylvania, Ohio, and across the PJM region. The investments will support approximately 3,000 project-related jobs in engineering, construction, and planned outage work while preserving thousands of permanent, well-paying jobs.
“President Trump and Secretary Wright have set a clear direction for America’s nuclear future, and EDF is financing the projects that advance that mission,” said EDF Director Gregory A. Beard. “These investments will extend the life of existing reactors, increase nuclear generation, and deliver abundant, around-the-clock power to lower costs and power American prosperity for decades to come.”
Vistra’s planned investments at Beaver Valley in Pennsylvania and Davis-Besse and Perry in Ohio will produce more electricity from existing nuclear plants without requiring new transmission corridors or equivalent new generation resources, while supporting the plants’ operation for an additional 20 years beyond their existing licenses. EDF’s conditional loan commitment also includes an option to finance potential future uprates at Vistra’s Comanche Peak Nuclear Power Plant in Texas.
While this conditional commitment indicates DOE's intent to provide a loan, Vistra must satisfy certain technical, legal, environmental, and financial conditions before the Department enters into definitive financing documents and funds the loan.
title: Energy Department Announces $4.2 Billion Investment to Boost Nuclear Power and Help Lower Energy Costs in Pennsylvania and Ohio

text:
Anyone who defrauds American taxpayers will face the consequences
WASHINGTON -- Last week, a North Carolina woman was sentenced to three years in prison followed by four years of supervised release for defrauding FEMA following Hurricane Helene. She was also ordered to pay more than $30,000 in restitution for false claims. 
“Those who steal disaster assistance from survivors will be investigated, prosecuted and held accountable. This woman’s actions, including committing fraud while incarcerated, are a blatant betrayal of disaster survivors and American taxpayers,” said FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton. “Funds intended to help North Carolina families rebuild after Hurricane Helene were instead stolen for personal gain. Every dollar taken through deception is a dollar unavailable to help communities recover. FEMA remains committed to reducing risks, building capabilities to detect and prevent fraud, and ensuring those who exploit federal disaster programs face serious consequences.”
In February 2025, the woman filed an application for disaster assistance with FEMA for a dwelling she claimed was in Marion, North Carolina. She falsely claimed the residence was destroyed by Hurricane Helene in September 2024. In the application, the woman asserted she rented the property and that the damaged dwelling was her primary residence. Days later, she falsely amended her FEMA application’s residential status from renter to owner of the damaged dwelling. The next day, she falsely represented to a FEMA inspector that she owned the residential trailer that was destroyed, but not the land where the trailer was placed.  
In March 2025, the woman submitted a handwritten letter to FEMA attesting that the information she had provided was “true and correct”, falsely claiming that she had purchased the dwelling for $8,500 and that she had lived there for 25 years. She also falsely attested that all her important personal documents “got washed away by Hurricane Helene." During that month, FEMA paid the woman’s false claim and wired her more than $30,000. 
Contrary to her claims, the woman never lived at, rented or owned a residence or structure at that location, and no dwelling existed at that location at the time the storm struck the area. At the time Hurricane Helene hit Western North Carolina, the woman was an inmate with the North Carolina Department of Adult Corrections and outside of the effects of the storm. 
Under the leadership of President Trump, Vice President Vance and Secretary Mullin, FEMA continues to strengthen safeguards, support the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud and work closely with law enforcement partners to identify, investigate and prosecute those who defraud disaster assistance programs. FEMA remains committed to protecting taxpayer dollars and ensuring aid reaches the survivors who genuinely need it. 
Taking funds meant for disaster survivors is a serious crime. In Fiscal Year 2025, FEMA investigated over 2,000 fraud cases. The agency refers suspected fraud in its Individual Assistance program to the DHS Office of Inspector General and other law enforcement partners for investigation and potential prosecution, including cases involving organized criminal activity.   
President Trump’s Executive Order 14395 established the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, bringing together federal agencies to coordinate a national strategy to stop fraud, waste and abuse in federal benefit programs. FEMA is fully engaged in strengthening eligibility verification, enhancing pre-payment controls and ensuring disaster assistance is delivered quickly and securely to eligible survivors.
title: No Safe Harbor for Disaster Fraud: North Carolina Woman Sentenced to Prison for Defrauding FEMA After Hurricane Helene

CHICAGO — A man has been sentenced to two years in federal prison for willfully failing to pay child support for two children in the Chicago area.

From 2009 to 2017, EVAN MUSIKANTOW willfully failed to pay more than $1 million of child support (including interest) that the Circuit Court of Cook County ordered him to pay following a divorce. During those years, Musikantow paid only $3,000 towards child support, with most of that money having been remitted involuntarily via interceptions of Musikantow’s tax refunds by the State of Illinois.

A federal jury in Chicago last year convicted Musikantow, 60, of Scottsdale, Ariz., of the willful failure to pay court-ordered child support. On Oct. 1, 2026, U.S. District Judge John J. Tharp, Jr. sentenced Musikantow to two years in federal prison and ordered him to pay $1,092,561.80 in restitution.

The sentence was announced by Andrew S. Boutros, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois, and Thomas Ethridge, Special Agent-in-Charge of the Chicago Region of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General.

“Defendant ignored and otherwise dodged his duty to support his children despite the longstanding efforts of the Circuit Court of Cook County, the Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services, and the mother of the two children to get defendant to provide support,” Assistant U.S. Attorneys Edward G. Kohler and Edward A. Liva, Jr. argued in the government’s sentencing memorandum. “Defendant committed this continuing offense over a period of many years, apparently motivated to abandon his children’s financial support to chase his own lavish lifestyle.”
title: Man Sentenced to Two Years in Federal Prison for Willfully Failing To Pay Child Support

SAN ANTONIO – The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Texas and the Drug Enforcement Administration San Antonio Field Division announced the establishment of an Overdose Task Force aimed at investigating overdose cases in the San Antonio metropolitan area.

The Overdose Task Force was employed in support of a Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) operation on Oct. 1. Together, the task forces executed a search warrant on three residences near the 1000 block of Torreon Street after allegedly observing multiple hand-to-hand controlled substance sales. The exchanges allegedly occurred out of the homes as well as a vehicle regularly parked outside the residences. Eight individuals were encountered in total. Three individuals were arrested and charged via federal complaints. All three federally charged defendants are previously convicted felons.

Valerie Samaniego is charged with possession with intent to distribute 40 grams or more of fentanyl, which carries a sentence of five to 40 years in federal prison. Samaniego allegedly possessed 141 grams of a substance testing positive for fentanyl as well as a handgun, both hidden in the floors of a residence.

Alfredo Alejandro is charged with possession with intent to distribute 50 grams or more of methamphetamine mixture, which also carries a sentence of five to 40 years in federal prison. Alejandro was allegedly found in possession of 128 grams of methamphetamine, 71 grams of a heroin/fentanyl mixture, 131 grams of cocaine, and 165 grams of various unknown pills, as well as a short barrel shot gun and an AR style rifle. A criminal complaint also alleges that law enforcement officers encountered more than 100 small baggies, digital scales with narcotics residue, along with $3,000 cash at Alejandro’s residence, consistent with drug distribution.

Alejandro Reyes is charged with possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine, which carries a sentence of up to 20 years in federal prison. He was allegedly found in possession of 27.58 grams of methamphetamine and 29.01 grams of a heroin/fentanyl mixture. Reyes has allegedly been previously observed completing hand-to-hand narcotics transactions from his vehicle outside of a Torreon Street residence.

“The DEA’s Overdose Task Force, in collaboration with the Homeland Security Task Force, is allowing law enforcement entities across varying levels of government to combine their efforts against the fentanyl problem,” said U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Texas, Justin R. Simmons. “These task forces exist for local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies to collaborate in our shared mission, to eradicate crime in our community, and sweep dangerous drugs off our streets, ultimately protecting our families and enabling Americans to live their lives, enjoy the blessings of liberty, and pursue happiness.”

While the DEA San Antonio office has been investigating overdose cases in the area, the establishment of this new joint overdose task force will help dedicate federal, state, and local resources to overdose investigations and utilize several investigative resources and tools to bring those responsible for overdoses to justice.

“Fentanyl-related overdose deaths are declining nationally, but that does not mean our work is over,” said DEA San Antonio Division Special Agent in Charge Miguel A. Madrigal. “The DEA San Antonio Division will pursue those who devastate our communities by trafficking fentanyl and other illicit drugs, leaving families shattered and innocent lives lost. We have zero tolerance for those who profit from poisoning our communities, and we will continue working alongside our law enforcement partners to hold them accountable and protect the public.”

The Overdose Task Force includes state, local, and federal counterparts, including the DEA San Antonio Division, San Antonio Police Department, Bexar County Sheriff’s Office, UTSA Police Department, Texas Department of Public Safety, Immigration and Customs Enforcement Homeland Security Investigations, IRS Criminal Investigation and the FBI.

“This Task Force brings together local, state and federal partners to save lives, hold drug traffickers accountable, disrupt the supply of dangerous drugs, and connect those in need with resources,” said San Antonio Police Chief Jesus "Jesse" Salame.

The United States continues to face an unprecedented and evolving drug threat driven by illicit fentanyl, which is increasingly mixed with a dangerous array of synthetic substances emerging in the illicit market. These combinations are making an already deadly drug supply even more unpredictable and lethal.

Fentanyl-related deaths have declined over the past several years, yet fentanyl remains the leading cause of death among Americans aged 18-45 years old. Last year, DEA intensified its fight against the deadly threat of synthetic opioids with the launch of its Fentanyl Free America initiative. To submit a tip regarding a possible violation of controlled substances laws and regulations, visit https://www.dea.gov/submit-tip .

This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF comprises agents and officers from FBI; ICE HSI; DEA; ATF; U.S. Border Patrol; USMS; U.S. Postal Inspection Service; Department of Transportation; IRS Criminal Investigation; Texas Department of Public Safety; as well as local police departments and sheriff’s offices, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Texas.

A criminal complaint is merely an allegation and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

###
title: U.S. Attorney and DEA San Antonio Field Division Announce New Overdose Task Force to Combat Drug Related Overdoses

Coast Guard, partners rescue 4 from grounded vessel near Richmond, Calif.
U.S. Coast Guard Southwest District Phone: (206) 815-6689
SAN FRANCISCO — The Coast Guard and San Francisco Fire Department rescued four boaters after their vessel ran aground near Brickyard Cove in Richmond on Saturday.
Coast Guard Sector San Francisco command center watchstanders received notification from Richmond Fire Department personnel at 8:19 p.m. that a 25-foot pleasure craft had run aground on the break wall with four people aboard.
Watchstanders coordinated the launch of a Coast Guard Station San Francisco 29-foot Response Boat–Small and a Coast Guard Air Station San Francisco MH-65 Dolphin helicopter.
The Station San Francisco boatcrew arrived on scene at approximately 8:33 p.m. and reported all four individuals had sustained serious injuries. Two were transferred to Richmond Fire Department emergency medical services personnel and transported to a local hospital.
A San Francisco Fire Department boatcrew transferred a third individual to EMS personnel for transport to a local hospital.
The Coast Guard aircrew hoisted the fourth individual and transferred them to EMS at San Francisco International Airport.
The vessel remains hard aground on the breakwall and does not currently pose a hazard to navigation. Additionally, no pollution has been observed.
Coast Guard personnel are currently working with the vessel representative and Richmond and San Francisco Police Departments for potential salvage options.
“Strong partnerships are critical to an effective search and rescue response,” said Lt. Cmdr. Carey Lewis, incident management division chief at Coast Guard Sector San Francisco. “The swift coordination between the Coast Guard and our partners agencies helped ensure four people were safely rescued and quickly connected with higher level of care they needed.”
For more information follow us on Facebook, X and Instagram.

title: Coast Guard, partners rescue 4 from grounded vessel near Richmond, Calif.

text:
Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew N. Ferguson today sent letters to 24 of the nation’s largest healthcare services companies, reminding them of their legal obligation to provide patients with timely, accurate and complete pricing information for healthcare services, and that failing to do so can be an unfair or deceptive practice.
The letters sent today are part of the Trump FTC’s ongoing commitment to promote healthcare affordability and price transparency for consumers.
The letters highlight concerns that healthcare services companies may violate the FTC Act by failing to provide transparent price information, particularly for routine and non-emergency medical care scheduled in advance.
Healthcare is among the largest and most consequential expenses American families face, yet patients are routinely asked to commit to care without knowing what it will cost and with prices for the same service often differing dramatically from one facility to the next. When patients are not told the true price in advance, the letters explain, both consumers and competition suffer. This also means patients cannot comparison shop or make informed decisions, and providers that deal honestly and transparently are put at a competitive disadvantage.
The letters emphasize that the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services’ price transparency rules establish a critical baseline for ensuring that healthcare facilities provide pricing information. However, compliance with these CMS requirements does not mean that a healthcare facility has met its obligations under Section 5 of the FTC Act. The CMS rules do not create a safe harbor from FTC Act liability.
Because price is a material term, the letters state, clear and conspicuous disclosures are often needed. Failing to disclose the price of a healthcare service may be deceptive if the omission is likely to mislead consumers acting reasonably under the circumstances. And when a disclosure is made, it may still be deceptive if it is incomplete, such as when it omits physician or facility fees or covers only a portion of the expected course of care. This is so because patients may reasonably believe they have been told the total cost of their care. Inaccurate disclosures are likewise misleading.
Failure to provide transparent pricing may also be unfair under Section 5 if it causes or is likely to cause substantial injury that consumers cannot reasonably avoid and that is not outweighed by countervailing benefits to consumers or competition. For example, when price information is incomplete, inaccurate or not provided sufficiently in advance for scheduled services, consumers cannot compare competing healthcare providers’ services or make informed decisions. Nor do incomplete, inaccurate or untimely pricing disclosures (where that information is reasonably available to the healthcare provider in advance) provide any countervailing benefits to competition or consumers. On the contrary, this practice undermines competition by obscuring one of the most important dynamics of competition from consumer observation and comparison.
Chairman Ferguson urged the healthcare services companies to conduct a comprehensive review of their price disclosure practices and take swift corrective action as needed.
The FTC has prioritized investigating and prosecuting deceptive and unfair practices in the healthcare industry, including through Chairman Ferguson’s creation of the Healthcare Task Force earlier this year. Last week, the FTC sued online contact lens providers Lens.com for misrepresenting the price of contact lenses in search ads and on its website.
The Federal Trade Commission works to promote competition and protect and educate consumers. The FTC will never demand money, make threats, tell you to transfer money, or promise you a prize. Learn more about consumer topics at consumer.ftc.gov, or report fraud, scams, and bad business practices at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. Follow the FTC on social media, read consumer alerts and the business blog, and sign up to get the latest FTC news and alerts.
title: FTC Issues Letters Warning Hospitals Against Deceptive Pricing Practices

Nation’s Largest Law Enforcement Organization Endorses Figures’ Bill to Cover College and Trade School Costs for the Children of Police Officers
MONTGOMERY – Today, Congressman Shomari C. Figures announced that the National Fraternal Order of Police – the nation’s largest organization of sworn law enforcement officers – has endorsed his bipartisan bill, the Public Service Educational Assistance Act, to cover the cost of college and job training for the children of law enforcement officers, other first responders, educators, and social workers.
“Every day, our police officers put their lives on the line to keep our streets and communities safe,” said Figures. “They and their families make tremendous sacrifices for us, and we should be there to give back to them in any way that we can. That’s why I introduced this bipartisan bill to recognize the vital work of our law enforcement officers by investing in their families' future.”  
“Public servants are the backbone of America, serving in vital roles that ensure the safety and well-being of their communities every day. As law enforcement in America faces a critical recruitment and retention crisis, and as postsecondary education becomes more expensive and crucial in our modern world, it is vital that the Federal government ensures that our public servants have the necessary funding and opportunities to receive postsecondary education,” said Patrick Yoes, National President of the National Fraternal Order of Police. “On behalf of the more than 382,000 members of the Fraternal Order of Police, thank you both for your leadership on this important issue.” 
Figures’ bill establishes a federal education assistance program covering the full cost of postsecondary education and training opportunities – including those enrolled in trade schools and vocational programs – for the dependents of educators, first responders, and social workers who have completed at least 20 years of qualifying service.  
Congressman Figures is joined in introducing this legislation by Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ) and Representatives Jahana Hayes (CT-05) and Mike Ezell (MS-04).  
In addition to the National Fraternal Order of Police, this bill is also endorsed by the Federal Law Enforcement Officers Association, the National Association of Social Workers, the International Association of Fire Fighters, the National Association of Emergency Medical Technicians, and the Major Cities Chiefs Association.
title: Nation’s Largest Law Enforcement Organization Endorses Figures’ Bill to Cover College and Trade School Costs for the Children of Police Officers

text:
Congresswoman Schrier, WA Lawmakers, Colleagues Demand Transparency After U.S. Forest Service Coordinates with ICE on Public Lands
Letter follows Labor Day incident where individuals were arrested in the middle of the night while camping at Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, 4 of 5 are still being held at Tacoma NW ICE Detention Center
PNW records devastating 2026 wildfire season – Members voice concern USFS is misusing taxpayer funds by directing resources outside of USFS scope and mission
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) and Representatives Emily Randall (D, WA-06), Rick Larsen (D, WA-02), Suzan DelBene (D, WA-01), Jared Huffman (D, CA-02), Ranking Member of the House Natural Resources Committee, Adriano Espaillat (D, NY-13), Chairman of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, Andrea Salinas (D, OR-06), Adam Smith (D, WA-09), Val Hoyle (D, OR-04), Marilyn Strickland (D, WA-10), Suzanne Bonamici (D, OR-01), and Pramila Jayapal (D, WA-07) sent a letter to U.S. Forest Chief Tom Schultz demanding transparency regarding immigration enforcement activities on U.S. Forest Service (USFS) lands.
This letter comes after a shocking incident over Labor Day Weekend where U.S. Forest Service Law Enforcement Officers (LEO) coordinated with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents to arrest five men who were camping with their families in Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest.
As of October 1, 2026, four of the five men arrested still remain in detention at the Tacoma NW ICE Detention Center.
“As Members of Congress representing the Pacific Northwest and Democratic leadership of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, the House Natural Resources Committee, and the House Agriculture Committee, we are concerned that the U.S. Forest Service (USFS) is misusing taxpayer dollars by neglecting their mission and directing career staff to prioritize immigration enforcement on federal public lands. Particularly during a difficult wildfire season, we want to express our gratitude to the Forest Service for fighting wildfires in the Pacific Northwest and across the country,” wrote the members.
The U.S. Forest Service has undergone significant funding cuts and reorganizations efforts since the start of Trump’s second term. Since 2025, the USFS has lost nearly 6,000 workers through DOGE cuts and other factors, raising concerns about wildfire preparedness, forest health research, and public land management. Earlier this year, USFS announced consolidation efforts to shutter research and development facilities nationwide. USFS backtracked on their original proposal to close57 out of 77 research labs after public outcry. In September 2026, USFS announced they will be closing 23 labs.
The 2026 wildfire season is still underway, and Washington state has recorded one of the worst wildfire seasons to date with almost 900,000 acres being burned as of early September.
The members conclude the letter by demanding answers to the following questions by October 15, 2026:
Questions for the U.S. Forest Service:
- Which agency first identified those arrested as targets for investigation, when were they identified, and what information about the targets was used to justify the raid?
- Can you confirm that the law enforcement officers that first approached the families were employees of the USFS?

PHILADELPHIA – United States Attorney David Metcalf announced that four non-citizens residing in Philadelphia have been charged with illegally voting. Under both federal and state law, only U.S. citizens may vote in Pennsylvania.

Jamil Ahmad , 50, was charged by information with voting by an alien during the 2024 election. At that time, Ahmad was a citizen of Pakistan and a lawful permanent resident of the United States.

Nighat Jamil , 47, was charged by information with voting by an alien during the 2024 election. Jamil is a citizen of Pakistan and a lawful permanent U.S. resident.

Hacina Saadi , 48, was charged by information with voting by an alien during the 2024 election. Saadi is a citizen of France and an illegal alien.

Paulo Silva , 54, was charged by information with voting by an alien during the 2024 election. Silva is a citizen of Portugal and a lawful permanent U.S. resident.

The informations allege that the defendants, despite knowing that they were not United States citizens, knowingly voted in an election held in part for the purpose of electing a candidate for the office of President, Vice President, and Presidential elector.

“Our democracy belongs to the American people and no one else,” said U.S. Attorney Metcalf. “We will continue to prosecute every instance of non-citizen voting that we encounter.”

If convicted, the defendants each face a maximum possible sentence of a fine, one year in prison, or both.

These cases were investigated by Homeland Security Investigations and the FBI.

The charges and allegations contained in the informations are merely accusations. Every defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty in court.

WASHINGTON–The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) today hailed the 2026 update to the U.S. National Strategy for Financial Literacy, underscoring the agency’s commitment to helping Americans develop practical skills to make sound financial decisions, build greater financial security, and pursue economic opportunity.

“When Americans understand how our financial system works, they are better equipped to save for the future, protect themselves from fraud, and fully participate in the greatest economy in the world,” said Comptroller of the Currency Jonathan V. Gould.

2026 Update to the U.S. National Strategy for Financial Literacy

The Financial Literacy Strategy outlines FLEC’s goals for advancing financial literacy and education across the United States and identifies priority areas and actions to help Americans build the knowledge and skills to make informed financial decisions, achieve their financial goals, and enhance their financial well-being.

The Financial Literacy Strategy establishes four priority areas for FLEC:

Youth Financial Capability: Build a foundation of basic financial skills starting in childhood and young adulthood to improve financial outcomes for the next generation of Americans.

Saving and Investing: Increase Americans’ knowledge of saving and investing to build financial security and achieve their financial goals, including by promoting awareness of new savings and investment vehicles such as Trump Accounts for children.

Digital Financial Literacy: Improve Americans’ knowledge and decision-making skills to enable the safe and confident use of digital financial products and services.

Scams and Fraud Education: Equip consumers with the knowledge to recognize and avoid scams and fraud and the tools to mitigate the impact of potential losses.

The Financial Literacy Strategy also identifies best practices for delivering effective financial education, including providing actionable and timely education at key financial decision points, tailoring education to life stages and individual situations, reinforcing concepts over time, incorporating experiential and hands-on learning, supporting high-quality instruction, and evaluating program effectiveness.

The Financial Literacy Strategy was developed through consultation with FLEC-represented agencies, public input, and independent research on financial literacy and education.

The OCC provides financial education resources to help consumers make informed financial decisions and recognize and avoid fraud and scams, including through its Safe Money resources.

Read the full 2026 Update to the U.S. National Strategy for Financial Literacy here .

Financial Literacy and Education Commission

FLEC was established by the Financial Literacy and Education Improvement Act, Title V of the Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions Act of 2003. The commission provides a forum for represented federal entities to coordinate and collaborate to advance financial literacy and education and increase access to financial services for Americans.

Learn more about FLEC and financial literacy resources at MyMoney.gov .

Ruiz Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Fix Medicare Advantage Payments in Puerto Rico
Joined by Reps. Bilirakis, Soto, and Resident Commissioner Hernández
WASHINGTON, D.C. Today, Congressman Raul Ruiz, M.D. (CA-25), joined by Congressman Gus Bilirakis (R-FL), Congressman Darren Soto (D-FL), and Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández (D-PR), introduced the Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act. This bipartisan bill would correct a long-standing formula gap that underpays Medicare Advantage in Puerto Rico.
How it works 
Medicare Advantage plans receive a fixed monthly payment from the federal government for each senior they enroll. Part of that payment is based on the local cost of care, which is measured by the average geographic adjustment (AGA).  Puerto Rico's AGA is much lower than it should be. The formula relies on spending in traditional Medicare (fee-for-service), but very few beneficiaries in Puerto Rico use fee-for-service, since most are enrolled in MA. Basing the AGA on such a small population understates what care actually costs on the island, and MA plans receive a lower benchmark payment for each senior as a result. 
This bill would set Puerto Rico's AGA equal to that of the U.S. Virgin Islands, a territory with similar socioeconomic circumstances, so that payments reflect the true cost of delivering care.
The problem
- Over 650,000 Puerto Rico beneficiaries rely on Medicare Advantage, over 90 percent of all Medicare beneficiaries on the island.
- Puerto Rico receives about 40 percent less per beneficiary than the U.S. average.
- Benchmark rates run roughly 20 percent below those in the U.S. Virgin Islands.
- The payment gap has led to smaller provider networks and reduced benefits, and doctors and hospitals absorb lower reimbursements. This threatens the quality and availability of healthcare services in Puerto Rico.
"As an emergency physician, I know that when care is out of reach, seniors pay the price," said Congressman Raul Ruiz, M.D. "Puerto Ricans pay into Medicare on the same terms as every American, yet their Medicare Advantage plans are paid about 40 percent less. That gap has shrunk provider networks, cut benefits, and strained doctors and hospitals. This bill is a targeted, common-sense fix. I thank Representatives Bilirakis and Soto and Resident Commissioner Hernández for working with me to give seniors the fair coverage they have earned."
"Seniors deserve reliable access to the high-quality health care they have earned through Medicare, regardless of where they live," said Congressman Gus Bilirakis. "Medicare Advantage plays an important role in delivering care to beneficiaries across Puerto Rico, and we must ensure the program is funded fairly and sustainably so seniors can continue accessing the doctors, treatments, and benefits they rely upon. I'm proud to join Representatives Ruiz and Soto in introducing the bipartisan Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act to address longstanding disparities, strengthen access to care and provide greater stability for patients and providers."
“I am proud to join Reps. Bilirakis and Ruiz in introducing the bipartisan Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act to make geographic adjustments to Medicare Advantage benchmarks in Puerto Rico to match those of the U.S. Virgin Islands. This takes us closer to achieving full parity between the Island and the mainland. Puerto Ricans are American citizens, and they deserve access to the same healthcare benefits as all Americans." said Congressman Darren Soto.
“We are prioritizing the basics: ensuring that our seniors have access to the doctors and healthcare services they need. This year, we secured a significant increase in Medicare Advantage funding for Puerto Rico. Now, we are taking the next step to fix a longstanding funding disparity that has affected the Island for years,” said Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández.
“This legislation represents an important step toward addressing a longstanding structural challenge in Medicare Advantage payments in Puerto Rico. With approximately 96% of Medicare beneficiaries on the Island choosing Medicare Advantage, the methodology used to establish Puerto Rico’s benchmarks must reflect the reality of the market it serves. We thank Congressman Ruiz, Representatives Bilirakis and Soto, and Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández Rivera for coming together on a bipartisan solution that would use the U.S. Virgin Islands as a comparable geographic reference and help strengthen access to care for hundreds of thousands of beneficiaries in Puerto Rico. MMAPA strongly supports this effort and looks forward to continuing to work with Congress and CMS to advance a more stable and sustainable Medicare Advantage program for Puerto Rico”, said Solage De Lahongrais, President of the Medicaid and Medicare Advantage Products Association of Puerto Rico (MMAPA)
The legislation would create a self-adjusting link: if the U.S. Virgin Islands' adjustment changes, Puerto Rico's would move with it. It is a targeted fix for a formula that has never reflected the true cost of care on the island.
title: Ruiz Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Fix Medicare Advantage Payments in Puerto Rico

U.S. Forest Service and U.S. Endowment for Forestry and Communities announce the Forestry Analytics for Carbon Tracking (FACT) Data Platform
 
                    Transparent and accessible digital platform with standardized U.S. forest and harvested wood product carbon data
            
The Forest Service and U.S. Endowment for Forestry and Communities today announced the Beta launch of the Forestry Analytics for Carbon Tracking (FACT) platform, a science-based platform that addresses the growing challenge and need for reliable forest sector carbon data at no cost to users.
Landowners and businesses face increasing pressure to report and communicate carbon information, but existing data can be fragmented, inconsistent, and costly to aggregate. FACT compiles previously siloed public and private data into one free, accessible, and transparent place, strengthening the competitiveness of U.S. forest products in domestic and global markets.
“The Forest Service is committed to giving landowners access to information that supports active and effective forest management,” said Forest Service Chief Tom Schultz. “FACT demonstrates what is possible when the public and private sectors work together around transparent, standardized data.”
The FACT Beta launch serves as a working release and active improvement period during which the platform will continue to be optimized, functionality will evolve, and new information will be incorporated. Valuable input gathered during this stage will shape the platform ahead of its full Version 1 release, which is planned for summer 2027.
To explore the FACT Beta and test its tools, visit forestryanalytics.org.
FACT is being developed through a public-private effort led by the Endowment, the Forest Service, and the forest sector, with input from scientists, engineers, and practitioners. The effort is supported through a collaborative agreement including the American Forest Foundation, American Wood Council, Composite Panel Association, Decorative Hardwoods Association, Hardwood Federation, Hardwood Manufacturers Association, National Alliance of Forest Owners, National Hardwood Lumber Association, National Wood Flooring Association, and Woodpack Global.
“Forest and harvested wood product carbon data has been scattered across public and private sources for years, making it challenging for landowners, manufacturers, and researchers to work from a consistent foundation of information,” said Pete Madden, president and CEO of the Endowment. “FACT will make standardized, transparent data easier to access and use, strengthening the competitiveness of American forest products while supporting U.S. jobs and rural economies.”
FACT will complement tools and datasets people already use across the forest products value chain rather than replacing them. The platform is being designed to:
- Provide forest land managers with a standardized method to convert their forest inventories to carbon stocks and create small area carbon estimations.
- Give harvested wood product manufacturers the tools to determine and report the carbon impacts of their operations.
- Support the consideration of embodied and displaced carbon estimates in design and architectural applications.
- Advance research by identifying gaps in primary carbon data.
As forest carbon research advances and published Life Cycle Assessments and Environmental Product Declarations are updated, FACT will continue incorporating new information. This approach will allow the platform to evolve as science, data, and user needs change.
title: U.S. Forest Service and U.S. Endowment for Forestry and Communities announce the Forestry Analytics for Carbon Tracking (FACT) Data Platform

MOBILE, AL – Several defendants have recently been sentenced in federal court for illegally reentering the United States after having previously been deported. On August 27, Ricardo Hernandez-Martinez, 60, a Mexican national, was sentenced to 16 months in prison for illegally reentering the United States after a prior deportation. In a separate case, Walter Noel Castellon-Guerra, 39, a Guatemalan national, was sentenced to time served for the same charge on October 1, 2026.

According to court documents, on March 20, 2026, the Baldwin County Sheriff’s Office (BCSO) encountered Hernandez-Martinez during a traffic stop and requested assistance from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO). ERO responded and took Hernandez-Martinez into custody. ERO determined that Hernandez-Martinez had previously been removed from the United States on four occasions.

Hernandez-Martinez has multiple prior felony convictions, including two prior convictions for illegal reentry and a conviction for transporting an alien. He also has prior convictions for reckless driving, driving under the influence, providing a false name to law enforcement, and public intoxication. Following his federal sentence for his third illegal reentry offense, Hernandez-Martinez was ordered to be transferred to immigration authorities for deportation proceedings.

On July 22, 2026, the Saraland Police Department stopped a vehicle after determining that none of the occupants had a valid driver’s license. Saraland Police requested assistance from the United States Border Patrol (USBP), a component of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP). USBP responded and determined that Castellon-Guerra had previously been deported from the United States on two occasions. He was subsequently arrested for illegal presence in the United States. Castellon-Guerra was sentenced to time served and ordered to be transferred to immigration authorities for deportation proceedings.

In addition to these two recent sentencings, the following defendants were prosecuted and sentenced in federal court for illegally reentering the United States after previously having been deported:

Jose Luis Lara-Arteaga, 29, a Mexican national, was encountered by the Daphne Police Department on August 25, 2025, in response to a suspicious vehicle call. ERO reviewed information from the encounter and determined that Lara-Arteaga was unlawfully present in the United States and had previously been deported in 2018 following a felony conviction in Baldwin County Circuit Court for leaving the scene of an accident involving injuries. ERO arrested Lara-Arteaga in March 2026. He was subsequently convicted of illegal reentry and sentenced to time served. He was ordered to be transferred to immigration authorities for deportation proceedings upon his release.

Juan Rodrigo Gonzalez-Hernandez, 40, a Mexican national, was arrested by the Foley Police Department on January 23, 2026, for possession of drug paraphernalia. ERO responded to the jail and determined that Gonzalez-Hernandez had previously been deported from the United States in 2011 following a felony conviction in Baldwin County Circuit Court for possession of a controlled substance. Gonzalez-Hernandez was convicted of illegal reentry and sentenced to time served. He was ordered to be transferred to immigration authorities for deportation proceedings upon his release.

Agustin Eduardo Lucas-Gomez, 28, a Mexican national, was encountered by the Silverhill Police Department during a traffic stop on January 24, 2026. ERO responded and determined that Lucas-Gomez had been removed from the United States on three prior occasions. Lucas-Gomez also had prior convictions for DUI, driving without a license, and illegal entry. ERO arrested Lucas-Gomez, who was subsequently convicted of illegal reentry in federal court. He was sentenced to time served and ordered to be transferred to immigration authorities for deportation proceedings upon his release.

Deric Fiallos-Villalobos, 24, a Honduran national, was arrested by ERO on February 19, 2026, pursuant to a federal arrest warrant. Fiallos-Villalobos had previously been arrested by the Foley Police Department for third-degree domestic violence in June 2022. ERO determined that Fiallos-Villalobos had previously been deported from the United States in 2020 and did not have lawful permission to remain in the country. He was convicted in federal court of illegal reentry, sentenced to time served, and ordered to be transferred to immigration authorities for deportation proceedings upon his release.

Nelson Felipe Miralda-Avila, 37, a Honduran national, was encountered by the BCSO during a traffic stop on February 12, 2026. ERO assisted with the investigation and determined that Miralda-Avila had been removed from the United States on five prior occasions. He also had prior convictions for illegal reentry in 2013 and 2016. Miralda-Avila was convicted of illegal reentry for a third time and sentenced to eight months in prison. He was ordered to be transferred to immigration authorities for deportation proceedings upon his release.

Hector Saldivar-Orellana, 34, a Honduran national, was encountered by the BCSO during a traffic stop on March 13, 2026. The BCSO requested assistance from ERO, which determined that Saldivar-Orellana had previously been removed from the United States in 2010 following a felony conviction in Maryland for second-degree rape. Saldivar-Orellana was convicted of illegal reentry, sentenced to time served, and ordered to be transferred to immigration authorities for deportation proceedings upon his release.

Wilson Tabora-Henriquez, 34, a Honduran national, was stopped by the BCSO on March 18, 2026, for a traffic violation. ERO assisted with the stop and determined that Tabora-Henriquez had previously been deported from the United States on three occasions. Tabora-Henriquez also had a prior felony conviction in Maryland for second-degree assault. He was convicted of illegal reentry, sentenced to time served, and ordered to be transferred to immigration authorities for deportation proceedings upon his release.

Jose Ramos Chabarria, 49, a Salvadoran national, was stopped by the Summerdale Police Department during a traffic stop on March 18, 2026. Summerdale Police requested assistance from ERO, which determined that Chabarria had previously been deported from the United States six times. Chabarria also had a prior felony conviction in Texas for driving while intoxicated with three or more prior convictions. He was convicted in federal court of illegal reentry, sentenced to time served, and ordered to be transferred to immigration authorities for deportation proceedings upon his release.

Jesus Adolfo Mejia-Torres, 34, a Mexican national, was arrested by the Fairhope Police Department on April 5, 2026, for second-degree possession of marijuana. ERO responded to the jail and determined that Mejia-Torres had previously been deported from the United States in 2017. Prior to his removal, Mejia-Torres had been convicted of third-degree burglary in Baldwin County Circuit Court. Mejia-Torres was subsequently convicted in federal court of illegal reentry based on his unlawful presence in the United States at the time of his arrest. He was sentenced to four months in prison and ordered to be transferred to immigration authorities for deportation proceedings immediately upon his release.

Ignacio Aguilar-Gutierrez, 39, a Mexican national, was encountered by the BCSO during a traffic stop on May 20, 2026. Aguilar-Gutierrez was convicted of illegal reentry and sentenced to time served. He was ordered to be transferred to immigration authorities for deportation proceedings immediately upon his release.

The defendants were prosecuted in the Southern District of Alabama as part of the ongoing efforts of federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies to identify and prosecute individuals who illegally reenter the United States after having previously been deported.

All defendants were ordered to pay a $100 special assessment. Defendants remained in custody on their respective federal charges until sentencing. Those ordered to be transferred to immigration authorities will face further immigration proceedings following completion of their federal sentences.

U.S. Attorney Sean P. Costello of the Southern District of Alabama made the announcement.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Office of Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO), Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), U.S. Border Patrol (USBP), and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), investigated these cases with the assistance of state and local law enforcement partners, including the Baldwin County Sheriff’s Office, Daphne Police Department, Fairhope Police Department, Foley Police Department, Saraland Police Department, Silverhill Police Department, and Summerdale Police Department.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Justin D. Kopf prosecuted the cases on behalf of the United States.

In addition to repelling the invasion of illegal immigration, Operation Take Back America aim includes the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs) and protecting our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

Fast Facts
The Concrete Masonry Checkoff program helps masonry block producers pool fees they collect to support research, education, and promotion they can't do effectively by themselves. An industry board administers the program, and the Commerce Department oversees the board.
From 2023-25, the board collected over $27 million in fees and spent nearly $15 million, mostly on promotion. The board approved 27 performance metrics, each with a 5-year goal. The board reported being on track to meet most metrics, but Commerce hasn't developed written procedures to approve metrics in the future, which would improve oversight.
Our recommendation addresses this.
A mason builds a wall by laying a grey, precast concrete block on a mortared row.
Highlights
What GAO Found
The Concrete Masonry Checkoff (CMC) program is a federally authorized, industry-funded program that supports research, education, and promotion projects intended to strengthen the concrete masonry industry and expand markets for its products. The term checkoff refers to the way similar programs are funded—that is, through assessments. The CMC Board administers the program, which is funded through mandatory assessments on specified concrete masonry units sold. From 2023 through 2025, the board collected over $27 million in assessments and spent nearly $15 million of the funds, primarily on 17 national projects and 69 regional projects.
CMC Program Assessments and Projects, 2023–2025
Source: Concrete Masonry Checkoff (CMC) Board information. | GAO-27-108692
The CMC Board uses key performance indicators to track progress toward the program’s objectives. Projects fall within six focus areas, including marketing, research, and education. For each area, the board established output-oriented indicators and corresponding 5-year goals. For example, one research indicator is the number of new engineering courses focused on concrete masonry and has a 5-year goal of 50 courses. As of year-end 2025, the board reported meeting or exceeding five of its 27 goals and achieving at least 20 percent of the target for 10 additional goals in its first year. The board plans to issue its required independent evaluation of the program’s effectiveness in the first quarter of 2027.
The U.S. Department of Commerce is statutorily required to oversee the CMC Board’s compliance with applicable law and the accompanying order primarily through reviews, approvals, and monitoring. To set up its oversight structure, Commerce consulted with the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) because of its experience overseeing agricultural checkoff programs. Commerce reviews and approves the CMC Board’s projects, contracts, annual budgets, objectives, and performance metrics. It also monitors program and contract execution, reviews projects and marketing materials for prohibited activities (e.g., false or misleading advertising), and may investigate violations and assess civil penalties.
However, Commerce has not developed written procedures for approving the CMC Board’s annual program objectives and performance metrics. Commerce could do so using its current resources and thereby take advantage of a relatively low-effort opportunity to enhance its existing oversight controls. For example, such procedures could reduce the risk of inconsistent approvals and preserve organizational knowledge.
Why GAO Did This Study
The Concrete Masonry Products Research, Education, and Promotion Act of 2018 (the Act) directed Commerce to create the CMC program. After industry members approved the referendum to establish the program, Commerce put into effect a final order in 2021. The concrete masonry industry consists largely of small producers, and the checkoff program allows them to pool assessments for industry-wide research, education, and promotion. In 2023, the CMC Board estimated that about 260 concrete masonry producers operated in the United States.
The Act includes a provision for GAO to review the CMC program. This report addresses (1) assessments the CMC Board collected and spent from 2023 through 2025, (2) the extent to which the board has evaluated the program’s effectiveness, and (3) how Commerce has overseen the board’s compliance with the Act and accompanying order.
GAO reviewed CMC Board documents, including audited financial statements, policies and procedures, the strategic plan, and annual reports, including the results reported for key performance indicators. GAO compared Commerce’s oversight procedures and related documents against the Act, accompanying order, and federal internal control standards. GAO also interviewed Commerce, USDA, and CMC Board officials.
Recommendations
GAO recommends that Commerce develop written procedures for approving the CMC Board’s annual program objectives and performance metrics. Commerce had no comments.
title: Concrete Masonry Promotion Program: Commerce Could Enhance Its Oversight Controls

PHILADELPHIA –FEMA will evaluate the readiness through a Biennial Radiological Emergency Preparedness Exercise at the Susquehanna Steam Electric Station. The exercise will occur during the week of October 19, 2026, to assess and improve the ability of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania to respond to an emergency at the nuclear facility.
“These drills are held every other year to evaluate the government’s ability to protect public health and safety,” said Andre C. McCoy, Regional Administrator for FEMA Region 3. “We will assess commonwealth and local government emergency response capabilities within the 10-mile Emergency Planning Zone of the Susquehanna Steam Electric Station in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.”
Within 90 days, FEMA will send its evaluation to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) for use in licensing decisions. The final report will be available to the public approximately 120 days after the exercise.
FEMA will present preliminary findings of the exercise during a public meeting at 10:00 a.m. EST on Friday, October 23, 2026. Planned speakers include representatives from FEMA and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. The meeting will take place in-person at:
Courtyard by Marriott Wilkes-Barre Arena

U.S. Representative Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) and U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) introduced the Domestic Violence Survivors Alerted for Emergency (SAFE) Notice Act, new legislation to establish notification systems that would alert survivors of domestic violence offenses when their abuser attempts to purchase a firearm illegally. 
Loopholes in federal and state law can allow domestic violence offenders to purchase guns notwithstanding their criminal history – situations that can be life threatening for survivors. Even when offenders are unsuccessful, the fact they are trying to purchase a firearm illegally can be a warning sign for survivors. The Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act would help keep survivors safe by setting up systems to notify domestic violence survivors when an abusive partner has obtained or is trying to obtain a firearm illegally. 
“When a domestic violence survivor is rebuilding their life, safety and peace of mind are everything. We know that an abusive partner’s access to a firearm dramatically increases the risk of fatal violence. By ensuring survivors receive immediate alerts if an offender attempts to purchase a gun illegally, the Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act empowers victims with time-sensitive information that can save lives,” said Congresswoman Dingell.
“I spent years prosecuting domestic violence cases in Rhode Island, and I know the toll it can take on survivors as they rebuild their lives. Our legislation will help ensure survivors are made aware when the government has information about an abuser’s attempt to buy a firearm, so survivors and their loved ones can make decisions in the interest of their own safety and wellbeing,” said Senator Whitehouse.
Domestic violence offenders and protective order respondents are generally prohibited under federal and many state laws from purchasing firearms. However, that prohibition does not always stop offenders from trying to purchase firearms anyway. FBI data shows that almost 160,000 gun purchases were denied from 2018 to 2023 because of the purchaser’s domestic violence background. These situations can be life threatening for people in abusive situations, especially women. An abusive partner’s access to a gun significantly increases the risk of an intimate partner homicide.
The bicameral Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act would help ensure domestic violence survivors are notified when an abusive partner is trying to obtain a firearm illegally.
Specifically, the Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act would:
    - Direct the FBI to establish a notification system to alert survivors of federal domestic violence offenses when the offender attempts to purchase a firearm illegally. 
        
  - Permit survivors to register or de-register at will.
  - Provide key alerts about an offender’s attempted illegal firearm purchase, including if the sale went through or law enforcement has recovered the firearm.
  - Provide additional alerts about related events, such as a pardon that restores an offender’s ability to purchase firearms legally.
- Authorize grants for states to pilot state-run alert systems, so survivors can receive alerts related to protective orders and non-federal domestic violence offenses. 
        
  - Enable states to use funds to expand existing systems or set up new ones.
  - Require reports on the success of and challenges related to these pilot projects, including recommendations for expanding the projects to other states.
“Survivors often must make complex safety decisions in real time, and having timely information about an abusive partner’s attempt to obtain a firearm can be critical to that decision-making. The Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act would help ensure survivors have access to information that could allow them to take additional safety precautions, seek support, and make informed decisions for themselves and their families. The Hotline is grateful to Rep. Debbie Dingell and Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse for introducing this legislation and for their continued commitment to the safety and well-being of survivors of domestic violence,”
 said Katie Ray-Jones, Chief Executive Officer of the National Domestic Violence Hotline.
“The National District Attorneys Association is proud to support the Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act, which establishes a common-sense notification system to alert victims when offenders unlawfully attempt to acquire a firearm as well as other firearm-related updates. NDAA commends this victim-centered approach that promotes public safety,”
 said Nelson Bunn, Executive Director of the National District Attorneys Association.
The Domestic Violence SAFE Notice Act has been endorsed by the National Domestic Violence Hotline, National District Attorneys Association, Association of Prosecuting Attorneys, Survivor Justice Center, Jewish Women International, National Alliance of Trauma Recovery Centers, National Advocacy Center of the Sisters of the Good Shepherd, Congregation of Our Lady of Charity of the Good Shepherd (U.S. Region), the Rhode Island Coalition Against Domestic Violence, National Council of Jewish Women, Just Solutions, Futures Without Violence, Union for Reform Judaism, Ujima, National Network to End Domestic Violence, Maryland Coalition Against Sexual Assault, Sakhi for South Asian Survivors, National Organization for Victim Advocacy, Asian Pacific Institute on Gender-Based Violence, Lovelace Consulting Services, Inc., National Indigenous Women's Resource Center, Colorado Organization for Victim Assistance, National Crime Victim Law Institute, Yup'ik Women's Coalition, Life Span, Women of Reform Judaism, and Alliance of Tribal Coalitions to End Violence.
Bill text can be found HERE.
title: Dingell, Whitehouse Introduce Bill to Create Alert System to Notify Survivors of Illegal Gun Purchase Attempts by Domestic Abusers

The Department of War announced the directed-energy systems selected following the Joint Interagency Task Force 401's (JIATF-401) counter-unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) directed energy pilot program, marking the next phase of efforts to expand the operational use of high-energy laser (HEL) and high-powered microwave (HPM) capabilities across the homeland.
Systems selected for the pilot include:
AeroVironment Palletized High-Energy Laser system
Epirus Leonidas High-Powered Microwave system
Kord Firefly High-Energy Laser system
Boeing Compact Laser Weapon system
"High-energy lasers and high-powered microwave systems are tools that can be effectively used in a layered drone defense," said U.S. Army Brig. Gen. Matt Ross, director of JIATF 401. "This pilot program will test these capabilities in an operational environment so we can understand how best to integrate and sustain them to defend the homeland."
Directed by the Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act, the pilot will evaluate these systems' performance providing real-time data and feedback on the systems' requirements, costs, and best practices.
JIATF-401 is conducting this pilot program in close coordination with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), U.S. Northern Command and the Services. Earlier this year, JIATF-401 partnered with the FAA to conduct a safety risk assessment during a live-fire HEL demonstration at White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico. As a result of this testing, the FAA determined that the system posed minimal risk to the National Airspace System and established a framework for continued coordination.
"There is no silver bullet, or one size fits all solution to countering the threat of drones," Ross said. "Directed energy gives commanders another option within a layered defense, complementing existing counter-UAS capabilities with a scalable, safe, and effective way to respond to drone threats. This pilot program will give us vital information in a real-world environment so we can employ these systems to protect the homeland."
While these systems represent the first capabilities selected for the pilot program, the DoW and JIATF-401 will continue to evaluate additional directed-energy technologies. In December, the Department will host a directed-energy shoot-off at Dugway Proving Ground to assess additional high-energy laser and high-powered microwave systems to identify promising capabilities for future operational use.
title: Systems Selected for JIATF 401 Directed-Energy Counter-Drone Pilot Program
