Congresswoman Scholten Announces Her Inaugural Congressional Youth Advisory Council
18 students from Michigan’s Third District were selected to advise the Congresswoman on issues facing their generation
GRAND RAPIDS, MI – Congresswoman Hillary Scholten (D-MI-03) announced her inaugural Congressional Youth Advisory Council (CYAC) for the 2026-2027 school year. 18 students were chosen from a competitive pool of applicants across West Michigan. The students will serve a one-year term, meeting five times over the course of the school year and advising the office on key issues facing their generation.
“Young people bring an energy and thoughtfulness that shapes our political discourse in ways that can invigorate unique ideas. The policy we create in Washington impact not only their day-to-day lives right now, but also, critically, their future. These young people deserve a say in their representation as well, said Congresswoman Scholten. “This class of students embodies West Michigan through their work ethic, care for community, and commitment to public service.”
Throughout the academic year, members of the Congressional Youth Advisory Council participate in policy-focused sessions where student-led committees work together to identify and examine key issues facing their communities. They will work directly with Congresswoman Scholten and her team to turn their ideas into real, workable recommendations for her to consider. While each meeting focuses heavily on one main committee topic, the group also sets aside time to review other upcoming bills. This setup gives students a genuine chance to weigh in on federal legislation, share their perspectives, and make sure young voices have a direct line to Congress.
Meeting one will be an introductory overview to cover the foundations of the program, set expectations, and get everyone ready for the year ahead.
Meeting two will focus on economic policy, where the economy committee will take the lead, guiding a deep dive into the specific financial and economic issues the students want to focus on.
Meeting three will focus on education policy and the education committee will take the floor to explore different facets of the education system and brainstorm potential solutions.
Meeting four will focus on environmental policy. The environment committee will lead discussions on ecological issues and how federal policy can address them.
Meeting five will be an opportunity for the various committees to present their research and policy proposals. Congresswoman Scholten will take the proposals into consideration and the students will be able to answer questions based on their research.
“I’m honored to be part of Congresswoman Scholten’s inaugural Youth Advisory Council. This opportunity allows students like me to share their perspectives, learn more about public service, and contribute to conversations that affect our schools, communities, and future. I look forward to working with Congresswoman Scholten and other student leaders from across West Michigan to make a positive impact,” said Youth Council Member Patrick Latchana.
“I am deeply excited for this opportunity! It is extremely important to hear the voices of the youth, as they will be the next generation in government. Hillary Scholten’s Youth Advisory Council is a step towards making youth’s voices heard state and nationwide,” said Youth Council Member Emma Palmer.
This program reflects Congresswoman Scholten’s ongoing commitment to lifting up the next generation of West Michigan leaders and giving young people a seat at the table in the decisions that shape their future. Read more here.

Baltimore, Maryland – A Baltimore man learned his fate in federal court, stemming from a firearm incident in the parking lot of a convenience store.

U.S. District Court Judge Adam B. Abelson sentenced Demond Thompson, 23, to 52 months in prison, followed by three years of supervised release, for possession of a firearm and ammunition by a prohibited person. Thompson, a convicted felon who is prohibited from possessing firearms and ammunition, threw a loaded firearm across a populated parking lot of a convenience store when approached by police officers.

Kelly O. Hayes, U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the sentence with Special Agent in Charge Charles Doerrer, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives (ATF), and Commissioner Richard Worley, Baltimore Police Department (BPD).

According to court documents, on December 21, 2025, BPD detectives were looking for Thompson in connection with an arrest warrant for failure to register as a gun offender. Detectives located Thompson walking on the sidewalk and attempted to speak with him. Then Thompson fled southbound into a populated Northwest Baltimore shopping-center parking lot.

As law enforcement pursued Thompson on foot, he reached into his front waistband, took out a firearm, and threw it across the parking lot. The firearm then hit the ground and landed next to a truck as a civilian stood in the doorway of the vehicle. When the firearm fell, the magazine base plate broke, causing 17 live rounds of ammunition to scatter on the ground. Law enforcement subsequently captured and arrested Thompson.

U.S. Attorney Hayes commended the ATF and BPD for their work in the investigation. Ms. Hayes also thanked Assistant U.S. Attorneys Alexandria A. Bell and Jonathan S. Tsuei who prosecuted this federal case.

For more information on the Maryland U.S. Attorney’s Office, its priorities, and resources available to help the community, please visit justice.gov/usao-md .

Rep. Aguilar Announces Nearly $730,000 for El Sol Neighborhood Educational Center to Improve the Health and Well-Being of Inland Empire Residents
El Sol will use the grant to teach and connect people to healthcare
SAN BERNARDINO, CA – Today, Rep. Pete Aguilar (CA-33) announced a $728,610 federal grant for El Sol Neighborhood Educational Center to hire more Community Health Workers and reach more people in the Inland Empire who need help finding healthcare and social resources.
El Sol’s health workers build trust with residents, teach them about their health in ways that match their culture and language, figure out their health needs and find the right doctors and care. Additionally, health workers connect people to basic needs support like housing, food assistance, domestic violence shelters, transportation, Medicare, Medi-Cal and more.
“Everyone deserves to find a doctor that’s right for them or get help with food, housing and other needs,” said Rep. Pete Aguilar. “El Sol’s Community Health Workers help build a bridge between our neighbors and the healthcare and support they need. This grant will bring more of these workers to our communities so that people in the Inland Empire can be healthy, happy and successful.”
“This federal investment recognizes the vital role that community-based organizations play in reaching people where they are and building trust where it matters most,” said Alexander Fajardo, Executive Director, El Sol Neighborhood Educational Center. “At El Sol, we will use these resources to strengthen our community health worker workforce and expand our ability to connect individuals and families with health education, resources, and support. When we invest in trusted community organizations, we invest directly in the health and well-being of our communities.”
This funding comes from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services’ Mental Health & Substance Abuse Service Grants.

WASHINGTON, D.C.— Representative Jamie Raskin (MD-08) and Senator Brian Schatz (D-HI) introduced a resolution standing strong for the American freedom to read, write and learn. The lawmakers’ resolution condemns MAGA’s escalating campaign of book bans in school libraries and censorship targeting the Smithsonian Institution and other public museums, parks and facilities.
The lawmakers’ resolution specifically cites book bans issued by the Trump Administration, MAGA state legislatures, local libraries and schools across America. This year, federal officials, at the direction of President Trump, censored books and educational materials at the Smithsonian Institution and Department of Defense Education Activity schools.
“The freedom to read, write and think independently are all rights enshrined in the First Amendment to our Constitution,” said Rep. Raskin. "MAGA’s book bans and censorship campaigns seek to control the freedom of thought in schools, libraries and government, but we are fighting back against this authoritarian assault on free expression and American democracy.”
“Any attempt to ban books because someone has an ideological disagreement or doesn’t believe in capturing the full scope of history is un-American,” said Senator Schatz. “Freedom of expression is a founding principle of our country, and it's up to all of us to stand up against these attacks on this fundamental right.”
More than 12,000 individual books were banned in America between July 2025 and June 2026, according to a report by PEN America. This includes books like “The Bluest Eye” by Toni Morrison and “MARCH” by former Congressman and Civil Rights Movement hero John Lewis, Andrew Aydin and Nate Powell.
PEN America’s report captures the proliferation of MAGA book bans that specifically target books written by and about outsiders and individuals from marginalized backgrounds. Books with LGBTQ+ characters or themes face a disproportionate risk of being banned.
According to PEN America, from July 2025 to June 2026, 24 States across the country limited access to certain books, including—
- Texas, where at least 8,000 books in total have been banned or restricted in 45 school districts;
- Florida, where at least 3,000 books in total have been banned or restricted in 35 school districts;
- Ohio, where at least 115 books in total have been banned or restricted in one school district;
- Utah, where at least 100 books in total have been banned or restricted in five school districts; and
- Michigan, where at least 65 books in total have been banned or restricted in two school districts.
The resolution is endorsed by PEN America and the American Library Association (ALA); Authors Against Banned Books; Banned Books Week Coalition; Center for American Progress; EdTrust; EveryLibrary; Freedom to Learn Foundation; Florida Freedom to Read Project; Freedom to Read Project; Hatchette Book Group; Interfaith Alliance; JCRC of Greater Washington; Jewish Community Relations Council of Portland; Jewish Council for Public Affairs; Jewish Federation of Greater Rochester; Lee & Low Books ; Let Utah Read; Macmillan Publishing; National Coalition Against Censorship; National Council for Jewish Women; National Council of Teachers of English; National Education Association; Penguin Random House; PFLAG National; Red Wine and Blue Education Fund; Simon & Schuster; Texas Freedom to Read Project; and the Tucson Jewish Museum & Holocaust Center.

LEXINGTON, Ky. – A Lexington man, Victorian Valdimar Hardaway, 36, was sentenced to over 21 years in prison on Friday, October 2, 2026, by U.S. District Judge Robert Wier for armed drug trafficking and illegal firearm possession charges.

Hardaway was convicted in April 2026 of conspiring to distribute aggravated quantities of fentanyl and methamphetamine; distributing fentanyl; possessing with the intent to distribute fentanyl, oxycodone, and methamphetamine; possessing a firearm as a convicted felon; and possessing a firearm in furtherance of his drug trafficking crimes.

According to testimony at trial and items seized during a search warrant, Hardaway had large amounts of fentanyl and methamphetamine throughout the apartment where he was staying. Law enforcement recovered numerous items of drug paraphernalia, including a hydraulic press, baggies, cutting agents, a blender, more than $5,000 in bundled cash, and digital scales. Evidence revealed that Hardaway was a large-scale drug trafficker in the Lexington community selling substantial amounts of fentanyl, methamphetamine, and oxycodone. Hardaway also possessed firearms during drug transactions and another one in the bedroom where many drugs and paraphernalia was recovered. Further, Hardaway’s criminal history shows he is a convicted domestic violence aggressor.

Jason Parman, United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Kentucky; Jim Scott, Special Agent in Charge, DEA, Louisville Field Division; Phillip J. Burnett, Jr., Commissioner of the Kentucky State Police; and Chief Lawrence Weathers, Lexington Police Department, jointly announced the sentence.

The investigation was conducted by the DEA, KSP, and Lexington Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Ron Walker and Aubrey McGuire Girouard, as well as Paralegal Jennifer Short prosecuted the case on behalf of the United States.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities.

– END –
title: Lexington Man Sentenced for Armed Drug Trafficking and Illegal Firearm Possession Charges

LOS ANGELES – An Orange County woman has been arrested on a federal criminal complaint charging her with acting in the United States as an unregistered agent of the government of the People’s Republic of China (“PRC”), including by conducting surveillance of family members of a high-ranking Taiwanese government official, the Justice Department announced today.

Wanying Zhang, 34, a.k.a. “Heather Zhang,” of Irvine, was arrested on Sunday at Los Angeles International Airport, where she planned to board a flight to China. She is expected to make her initial appearance and be arraigned this afternoon in U.S. District Court in downtown Los Angeles.

“Protecting our national security means confronting foreign governments that engage in covert operations in our nation,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli. “Ms. Zhang acted at the direction of Chinese government officials to spy on the family of a senior Taiwanese official here in the United States. She violated our laws and will be held accountable in our courts. We will aggressively investigate and prosecute illegal foreign operations on American soil.”

“The central allegation here — that Zhang, at the behest of the People’s Republic of China, covertly surveilled relatives of a high-ranking foreign government official in the United States — is deeply troubling,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “The National Security Division and U.S. Attorney’s Offices, along with the FBI and other law enforcement partners, will remain vigilant against threats like this on our soil.”

“The complaint in this case lays bare a brazen plot directed by the Chinese government to conduct a covert surveillance mission on U.S. soil targeting close relatives of a Taiwanese government official,” said Assistant Director Roman Rozhavsky of the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division. “Wanying Zhang’s arrest for allegedly acting as an unregistered agent of the Chinese government makes clear how far China’s authoritarian regime will go to advance its goals. However, this case also demonstrates the FBI’s unwavering commitment to defending the sovereignty of our democratic allies and combating all attempts by the Chinese government — and any foreign adversary — to conduct transnational repression within our borders.”

According to the complaint, from June 2025 to September 2025, Zhang acted as an agent of the Chinese government without prior notification to the Attorney General of the United States, as required by federal law.

At the direction and control of Chinese government officials, Zhang coordinated with other individuals to promote the interests of China by, among other things, conducting surveillance on family members of a high-ranking Taiwanese government official at their residence in the United States.

In June 2025, Zhang traveled from Southern California to China, where she met with Chinese government officials and was tasked with conducting the surveillance in the United States.

On August 29, 2025, Zhang and another individual flew from John Wayne Airport in Orange County to Las Vegas. On September 1, 2025, they flew from Las Vegas to the state where the victim resides. On that date, she messaged a PRC government official that she was “Boarding now” and sent the PRC official a photograph of her boarding pass.

Upon their arrival, Zhang and the other individual rented a car and drove to the victim’s residence, where they conducted surveillance. Zhang sent the same PRC official the following message: “Saw him, young male, it’s the young one.” When this official asked her to join an audio call, she replied, “I am videorecording.”

Zhang also sent the same official the license plate numbers for the two vehicles parked in front of the victim’s home.

A criminal complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

If convicted, Zhang would face a statutory maximum sentence of 10 years in federal prison.

The FBI is investigating this matter.

Assistant United States Attorneys Amanda B. Elbogen and Colin S. Scott of the National Security Division and Justice Department Senior Counsel Scott M. Lara of the National Security Division’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section are prosecuting this case.
title: Irvine Woman Arrested on Federal Complaint Alleging She Acted as an Agent of China and Spied on U.S.-based Relatives of High-Ranking Taiwanese Government Official

ROCHESTER, N.Y.-U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Thomas D. O’Brien, 65, of Henrietta, NY, was arrested and charged by criminal complaint with the production and possession of child pornography. Because of a prior conviction involving the sexual abuse of a minor, the charges carry a minimum penalty of 15 years in prison, a maximum of 40 years, a lifetime period of supervised release, and a $250,000 fine.

According to the criminal complaint, in April 2026, the Monroe County Sheriff’s Office Sex Offense Coordinator contacted Homeland Security Investigations regarding O’Brien, who is a level two registered sex offender in New York State following his 1991 conviction for Sexual Abuse in the First Degree, which involved the sexual abuse of a nine-year-old male victim. As part of his sex offender registration requirements, O’Brien is required to submit change of address forms to the Sheriff’s Office each time he moves to a new residence, as well as information regarding his phone number, internet accounts and online identifiers. O’Brien completed a change of address form in October 2025, changing his address from Henrietta to Vietnam. In June 2026, O’Brien completed another form, changing his address from Vietnam back to Henrietta, as well as listing his Instagram and X accounts. According to the coordinator, O’Brien has engaged in a similar pattern of travel to Vietnam for several years.

In January, 2026, the National center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) received a CyberTip from Instagram stating that child pornography had been exchanged in a messenger chat room named “Tom & You Gay,” and that a user uploaded a file including child pornography to the “Tom & You Gay” chat. According to Instagram, the files were received by O’Brien’s Instagram account “bom4bym.” The Sheriff’s Office executed a search warrant on the files received by O’Brien and recovered an image and a video that included child pornography.

Another search warrant was executed by investigators on another Instagram account registered to O’Brien, which goes by the name “Tom & Jerry.” The search recovered nude images of O’Brien, images of a minor in a bathtub, and sexually suggestive images of minor boys. A chat conversation was also recovered indicating that O’Brien has a sexual interest in minor Vietnamese boys.

On June 4, 2026, on his return trip from Vietnam, HSI agents conducted a border search of O’Brien’s electronic devices at Chicago O’Hare International Airport, including a laptop and two cell phones, recovering nude images of minors. A subsequent forensic examination revealed that three of the four devices contained child pornography. On September 15, 2026, HSI and the Monroe County Sheriff’s Office executed a search warrant at O’Brien’s Henrietta residence and located photo albums containing hundreds of printed photographs, from approximately 2013, depicting apparent minors in various stages of undress, and nude minors, most of whom were of Asian descent.

Anyone with information regarding this defendant or this case is asked to contact the HSI Tipline at 1-866-347-2423.

The criminal complaint is the result of an investigation by Homeland Security Investigations, under the direction of Acting Special Agent-in-Charge Anthony Patrone and the Monroe County Sheriff’s Office, under the direction of Sheriff Todd Baxter.

The fact that a defendant has been charged with a crime is merely an accusation and the defendant is presumed innocent until and unless proven guilty.

Today, Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16) released the following statement after attending a community stakeholder meeting on the Fort Bliss data center project:
“Today, the Army and Carlyle Group held a meeting of El Paso community stakeholders to discuss the latest updates on the Fort Bliss data center.
"Since March, when my team and I first learned of this project, we have asked that the public and local representatives be kept in the loop and be allowed to voice their concerns and ask questions. I’m grateful to the Army and Carlyle for their continued engagement.
"I’ve consistently had a number of requests, including that they:
    - Move the data center far away from any neighborhood;
- Preserve our water;
- Use renewable energy for the electrical generation;
- Be transparent and accountable.
"Today we learned that the location of the data center has indeed been moved, but it is still too close to residential areas. Close proximity to homes is not acceptable, and I will continue to advocate for a different location.
"We also learned that their water use will likely be of brackish water that will be sent to the Kay Bailey Hutchison Plant for desalination, which I see as a positive development. And while the scale of the data center has also been reduced, they are still on track to utilize gas generation for their power needs. The gas generation for power remains an additional serious concern. We must protect our community’s air quality, and I will continue to push for the use of renewable energy.
"As more information becomes available, my team and I will continue to keep the community updated."
title: Congresswoman Escobar Statement on Fort Bliss Data Center Project Update

FRESNO, Calif. — Binghui Liu, 33, a citizen of China formerly residing in San Jose, pending an asylum application, pleaded guilty today to one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced.

According to court documents, between February 2024 and April 2025, Liu and other co-conspirators engaged in a scheme to launder proceeds from a government-impersonation fraud scheme. In this type of scam, individuals posing as a federal law enforcement officers or employees contacted victims and falsely claimed that criminal charges had been filed against them and that their bank accounts would be frozen. The scammers, operating both inside and outside the United States, including in India, instructed victims to withdraw their savings in cash and surrender the money “for safekeeping.” Victims were told that a federal official would arrive to collect the cash. The scammers used fake names, code words, and directed the victims to take pictures of themselves and the cash packaged for pickup.

In one case, an elderly victim was contacted by someone posing as a U.S. Marshal, who falsely claimed there was an arrest warrant and that the victim’s bank accounts were at risk of being frozen. The scammer instructed the victim to “protect” their funds by turning the money over to supposed Federal Reserve employees. They coached the victim on how to withdraw the cash, what to tell the bank, and how to package the money for pickup. Liu and other co‑conspirators then arrived, impersonating federal officials, to collect the cash. In total, the victim lost more than $700,000.

Liu served as a money launderer for other co-conspirators participating in the fraud scheme. Between March and April 2025, Liu took approximately $597,100 from 24 victims throughout California and Nevada. He used code words, fake names, and victims were told he was either a federal employee or law enforcement officer. On April 9, 2025, agents set up a sting operation. Liu arrived at the victim’s house and took what he believed was $20,000, but was in fake money. At no point was Liu a federal law enforcement officer or federal employee.

If you have information related to this case or believe you may be a victim, please submit a report at tips.fbi.gov or call 1-800-CALL-FBI (1-800-225-5324) or your local FBI office.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Cody S. Chapple and Arelis M. Clemente are prosecuting the case.

Liu is scheduled to be sentenced by U.S. District Judge Kirk E. Sherriff on Jan. 4, 2027. Liu faces a maximum statutory penalty of 20 years in prison and a $500,000 fine or twice the value of the property involved in the transaction, whichever is greater. The actual sentence, however, will be determined at the discretion of the court after consideration of any applicable statutory factors and the federal Sentencing Guidelines, which take into account a number of variables.
title: Chinese national pleads guilty to $597,000 money laundering conspiracy that took life savings from victims in California and Nevada

text:
CHICAGO — A federal jury in Chicago has convicted a man of trafficking methamphetamine to Illinois from California.

HUGO STEVEN DE LA CRUZ CORONA, 24, of San Jacinto, Calif., trafficked the meth on behalf of a Los Angeles-based drug trafficking organization that distributed narcotics throughout the country via the U.S. Postal Service. In October 2020, De La Cruz traveled to Chicago and attempted to pick up two parcels containing multi-pound quantities of meth that the organization had shipped from California. Unbeknownst to De La Cruz, law enforcement had intercepted both parcels and replaced the meth with sham drugs.

After a four-day trial in U.S. District Court in Chicago, the jury on Sept. 25, 2026, convicted De La Cruz of both drug charges against him. The convictions are punishable by a maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison. U.S. District Judge Manish S. Shah set sentencing for Jan. 20, 2027, at 1:30 p.m.

The convictions were announced by Andrew S. Boutros, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois; Nicholas Bucciarelli, Inspector-in-Charge of the Chicago Division of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service; Ryan Whalen, Special Agent-in-Charge of the Chicago Field Office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation; and Todd C. Smith, Special Agent-in-Charge of the Chicago Field Division of the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration. The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Chester Choi and Holly Lanchantin.

The federal investigation was part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. The task force in this investigation was comprised of agents from USPIS, FBI, and DEA, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Illinois.

Four other defendants, including the leader of the drug trafficking organization—MARCO TORRES, SR., 49, of Hesperia, Calif.—pleaded guilty prior to trial. Torres Sr. is awaiting sentencing; a status hearing in his case is set for Oct. 13, 2026, at 10:15 a.m. The three other defendants were sentenced to prison terms of six years, five years, and 14 months.
title: Federal Jury in Chicago Convicts Man of Trafficking Meth to Illinois From California

text:
FBI Hosts Special Agent Information Session
Please note: Due to the privacy of those looking to become FBI agents, the event itself is not open to media; however, the FBI is willing to facilitate media interviews with FBI personnel prior to the day of the event for any pre-coverage. Any media member looking to conduct an interview can contact FBI Public Affairs Specialist Dixon Land at media.kansascity@fbi.gov.
KANSAS CITY, MO—As the FBI continues to hire qualified special agents to its ranks, FBI Kansas City will be hosting special information session on October 28th from 5–7 p.m.
Interested candidates should fill out the form at forms.fbi.gov/field-offices/special-agent-information-session-kansas-city-missouri-october-28-2026. A direct link to the form is available at www.fbi.gov/kansascity. Questions about the session can be emailed to: KansasCityApplicants@fbi.gov. The event is free and those who attend are not required to apply for a position with the FBI.
Submission of the form does not guarantee entry into the session. Those who submit will be contacted by the FBI to obtain additional details for entry to the event, such as a simple background check. Space is limited and on a first-come, first-served basis. While there is not a deadline to apply prior to event, interested candidates are encouraged to fill out the form as soon as they can.
This session will cover the requirements to be an FBI special agent, the application process, pay and benefits, and a typical day in the life of a special agent. Additionally, attendees will have a chance to ask questions and meet current special agents. Attendees interested in pursuing a career as a special agent will have the opportunity to begin the application process during the event.
The requirements to become an FBI special agent include:
- Being a U.S. Citizen
- Age between 23-37 years old
- Possessing a valid driver’s license
- Having a bachelor’s degree
- Maintaining good standing on loans and taxes
- No felony convictions
The FBI is seeking individuals from a wide variety of backgrounds to fulfill our mission to protect the American people and uphold the constitution. Those interested in having a career with a purpose and a mission that matters are encouraged to attend.
title: FBI Hosts Special Agent Information Session

text:
FRESNO, Calif. — Ifeanyi Emmanuel Ugwu, 50, of Bakersfield, was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge Jennifer L. Thurston to one year in prison for illegally transmitting $5 million overseas to China and elsewhere while operating an unlicensed money transmitting business, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced.

According to court documents, between December 2020 and August 2023, Ugwu owned, operated, and served as chief executive officer of Franklin Finance Inc. Through this business, he opened and controlled 20 bank accounts across nine financial institutions, receiving approximately $5 million from more than 100 individuals in the United States. He then transferred the funds to individuals in China, Nigeria, and other countries. At no point did the company have the required licenses to operate a money-transmitting business.

Ugwu marketed his services as “money transfers … at black market rates,” misrepresenting the nature of his business to banks in order to open accounts, and provided bogus reasons for the transactions. His operation attracted fraudsters and enabled the theft of hundreds of thousands of dollars from American citizens.

Several of the individuals who sent Ugwu funds were victims of cybercrimes and fraud. Ugwu received and transferred approximately $580,000 in fraud proceeds from these victims, continuing to operate his unlicensed business by making various misrepresentations to individuals, banks, and other financial institutions to conceal his fraudulent activity.

The IRS Criminal Investigation and Homeland Security Investigations conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Cody S. Chapple prosecuted the case.
title: Bakersfield man sentenced to one year in prison for transferring $5M abroad through illegal money transmitting operation

With the close of Fiscal Year (FY) 2026, the U.S. Department of Education (ED) continued to deliver on its promise both to supercharge evidence-based literacy and the fundamentals of learning rather than pushing ideological indoctrination, and to break up the federal education bureaucracy and place more funding directly into the hands of local communities.
ED’s interagency agreements allowed over $3.4 billion of formula and competitive grants to flow through the partner agencies to states, students, families, and educators. And by leveraging the expertise and networks of partner agencies, ED significantly expanded the pool of applicants for federal grant competitions.
“This is truly proof of concept that our interagency partnerships are delivering for the American people by streamlining services, breaking up the federal education bureaucracy, better stewarding taxpayer resources, and demonstrating these programs are better situated in other federal agencies,” said U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon. “As we return education to the states, we are focusing our resources on the fundamentals – investing in literacy, expanding career training and apprenticeships, and delivering stronger support to students with disabilities. As a prime example, nearly 80 percent of new elementary and secondary education grants went directly to State Education Agencies or state-endorsed projects, ensuring federal dollars closely reflect local needs. When we zero in on these foundational needs and let states lead the way, students are better served.”
Key FY26 Milestones:
Expanding Career and Adult Education: The Office of Career, Technical, and Adult Education (OCTAE) delivered over 7,850 payments totaling $2 billion through DOL for career and technical education, adult literacy, and workforce preparation programs. These investments are building clear pathways to high-paying, high‑demand jobs.
Investing in Students and Community Innovation: The Office of Elementary and Secondary Education (OESE) routed nearly $500 million through DOL and HHS to strengthen literacy, expand charter school access, bolster American History and Civics education, and modernize state academic assessments.
- Career Pathways Exploration: $38 million to help states integrate career exploration into their career pathways and workforce readiness programs.
- Charter Schools Program – State Entities: $78 million to help open new charter schools and replicate and expand high-quality charter schools.
- American History and Civics – National Activities: $19.8 million to promote American history, civics and government, and geography instruction.
Improving Graduation Outcomes and Building a Stronger Workforce: The Office of Postsecondary Education (OPE) awarded 1,000 new grants totaling nearly $1 billion through DOL and HHS. For the first time, these awards prioritized Registered Apprenticeships, responsible Super Intelligence (SI), and short‑term, employment‑focused programs that improve earnings and help Americans build in‑demand skills.
Highlights include:
- Strengthening Institutions (SIP): $365 million to help institutions become self-sufficient and expand their capacity to serve low-income students by providing funds to improve and strengthen the institution's academic quality, institutional management, and fiscal stability.
- Rural Postsecondary and Economic Development (RPED): $44.5 million to help improve postsecondary enrollment, persistence, and completion among rural students. Its core strategy is to develop career pathways aligned with high-skill, high-wage, and in-demand industry sectors and occupations in rural regions.
Bolstering Support for Students with Disabilities: ED’s Office of Special Education and Rehabilitative Services (OSERS) directly awarded investments to support students with disabilities, including a record $144 million to states in IDEA funding to serve infants, toddlers, children, and youth with disabilities. Additionally, for the first time, states can use IDEA Part C early intervention funds to connect expectant parents of infants with disabilities to information and referrals before their child is born. ED and HHS continue to deepen their partnership, collaborating on best practices to support families and ensuring a continuum of services.
Supporting Child Care Resources: ED’s partnership with HHS leveraged HHS’ existing relationships with childcare providers, community organizations, and early childhood networks to reach new applicants, enhance the quality of technical assistance, and better connect federal support to low-income student parents and their children. As a result, the Child Care Access Means Parents in School program (CCAMPIS), the federal program that supports on-campus and community childcare for parents pursuing an education, received almost 300 applications, nearly double the 161 applications received in the last competition of the program.
Modernizing the Federal Student Aid System: In partnership with the U.S. Department of the Treasury, ED continues to streamline critical resources and help borrowers return to repayment. Most recently, ED and Treasury launched the new Defaulted Loans Support Center, a one-stop shop for borrowers to rehabilitation and consolidate their loans.
title: Fiscal Year 2026 in Review: Investing in Career Readiness, Improving Outcomes for Students, and Returning Education to the States

Gainesville, Florida – Roosevelt Allen Douglas II, 46, of Hawthorne, pleaded guilty in federal court to accessing with intent to view child pornography, receipt or attempted receipt of child pornography, and possession of child pornography. John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida, announced the plea today.

U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “Our law enforcement partners are relentless in their pursuit of predators using the internet to access and transmit child sexual abuse material, and my office will continue to aggressively prosecute these cases to ensure those criminals are kept locked away behind federal bars.”

Court documents reflect that on April 24, 2023, the defendant used his laptop to access a website that displayed child pornography for sale. After the defendant “previewed” the child pornography on the website, he sent money to an individual that was engaged in the business of receiving and laundering money for a child pornography distribution enterprise. After learning that the defendant had attempted to purchase child pornography on other occasions, law enforcement searched the defendant’s electronic devices, which contained multiple images of child sex abuse material.

Due to a prior conviction relating to sexual abuse or abusive sexual conduct involving a minor, Douglas faces 15 to 80 years’ imprisonment and up to life on supervised release.

Sentencing is scheduled before United States Chief District Judge Allen C. Winsor, in Gainesville, Florida on December 8, 2026, at 1:30PM.

The case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations, Federal Bureau of Investigation, and the Alachua County Sherriff’s Office. Assistant United States Attorney Adam Hapner is prosecuting the case.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC .

The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl .
title: Convicted Sex Offender Pleads Guilty to Federal Child Pornography Offenses

Coast Guard, Dominican Republic Navy rescue 61 alien migrants from sinking vessel
SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — The crew of the Coast Guard Cutter Winslow Griesser and two Dominican Republic Navy vessels rescued 61 alien migrants Monday morning from a grossly overloaded, sinking vessel in Atlantic Ocean waters off Dominican Republic.
All migrants aboard the sinking vessel were successfully rescued and transferred to Dominican Republic Navy rescue assets on-scene, their nationalities are yet to be determined.
“Thanks to the rapid response of the Coast Guard and Dominican Republic Navy rescue crews, 61 lives were saved from an overloaded, sinking vessel,” said Cmdr. Matthew Romano, Sector San Juan chief of response. "However, these dangerous and unlawful voyages are increasing, and our luck will eventually run out. Do not risk your life with ruthless smugglers. Choose safe, lawful migration pathways; if caught, you could face prosecution or immediate repatriation.”
At approximately 5:50 a.m., the crew of the Winslow Griesser detected a suspect, 30-foot makeshift vessel taking on water, approximately 12 nautical miles northwest of Cabo Cabron, Dominican Republic. Cutter Winslow Griesser spotted the makeshift vessel while transiting through Dominican Republic territorial waters under our joint nation bi-lateral agreement to help deter unlawful maritime migration.
Upon arriving alongside, the cutter crew confirmed the makeshift vessel was rapidly taking on water and immediately began embarking the passengers. Coast Guard watchstanders also deployed an MH-60T Jayhawk helicopter crew from Air Station Borinquen to provide overhead rescue support, while a Dominican Air Force aircraft also responded.
Shortly after, the Dominican Republic Navy patrol boats Capella CG-108 and Algenib Ll-169 arrived on scene to assist with the rescue. Together, the crews safely embarked all 61 survivors.
Just last week a similar migrant venture capsized, dumping more than 60 people into the waters of the Mona Pass. A multi-agency response, including the Coast Guard, Customs and Border Patrol Air and Marine Operations, Puerto Rico Police Joint Forces of Rapid Action FURA, and Dominican Navy assets, which rescued 49 of the migrants and recovered three deceased. Several remain unaccounted for.
Migrants interdicted at sea or apprehended ashore will not be allowed to stay in the United States or a U.S. territory. Furthermore, individuals who arrive unlawfully may be declared ineligible for legal immigration parole options and face repatriation to their country of origin or return to their country of departure.
The Coast Guard, along with its Operation Vigilant Sentry and Operation Bahamas, Turks and Caicos partners, maintains a continual presence with air, land and sea assets in the Florida Straits, Windward Passage, Mona Passage and Caribbean Sea in support of OVS. This multiagency and multilayered approach is designed to protect the safety of life at sea while preventing unlawful maritime entry to the United States and its territories.
This interdiction is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States.
HSTF San Juan comprises agents and officers from the following federal partners: FBI, ICE-HSI, CBP (OFO, AMO and Border Patrol), the U.S. Marshals Service for Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands, DEA, ATF, IRS, U.S. Coast Guard, U.S. Coast Guard Investigative Service, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, the Department of State, and the U.S. Secret Service, the Puerto Rico/U.S. Virgin Islands HIDTA, TSA, FAA, and the U.S. Attorney’s Offices for the Districts of Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands

For breaking news, follow us on X (formerly Twitter). For additional information, find us on Facebook and follow us on Instagram.
title: Coast Guard, Dominican Republic Navy rescue 61 alien migrants from sinking vessel

- For Immediate Release:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today announced a request for information (RFI) describing approaches the agency is considering for the design of early-phase clinical trials of ibogaine drug products and seeking public input on those approaches. The RFI seeks comments, data, and information on specific protocol elements relevant to ibogaine drug development, including dose selection and escalation, care setting, safety monitoring, eligibility criteria, stopping rules and safety oversight. This RFI marks the latest FDA action to advance President Trump’s April 2026 executive order on Accelerating Medical Treatments for Serious Mental Illness, which directed agencies to accelerate research into psychedelic medicine.
“Patients facing serious conditions that have not responded to existing treatments deserve rigorous scientific investigation of promising new approaches,” said Michael Davis, M.D., Ph.D., Director of the FDA Center for Drug Evaluation and Research. “With ibogaine, there are important scientific questions as well as serious safety concerns. We are seeking high-quality data and input that can help inform clinical research while putting patient safety first.”
The FDA is seeking comments, data and information in four primary areas:
- General study design, including appropriate patient populations;
- Dose selection and escalation, including the proposed use of small, sequential dose-ascending groups and a starting dose justified by available data and not exceeding 10 mg/kg;
- Safety considerations, including monitoring for cardiac and neurologic adverse events and other safeguards for clinical trials; and
- Ethical and oversight considerations, including informed consent and appropriate independent safety oversight.
The FDA recognizes the seriousness of the conditions and unmet needs that patients seeking ibogaine treatments face. The information received through this RFI may help the agency better understand the potential uses, benefits and risks of ibogaine drug products and inform approaches to drug development.
The FDA has been working across the federal government to support the responsible development of ibogaine drug products through careful evidence-based processes. In July 2026, the FDA issued its finalized guidance for industry, Psychedelic Drugs: Considerations for Clinical Investigations, which provides general considerations for sponsors developing psychedelic drugs. The FDA has also allowed an early-phase clinical study of noribogaine hydrochloride, a derivative of ibogaine, to proceed under an Investigational New Drug application as a potential treatment for alcohol use disorder.
As part of the whole-of-government approach to advance psychedelic drug development, HHS, through the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H), is funding a program to collect safety and efficacy data through early-phase clinical trials, and the National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA) is funding research on ibogaine for the potential treatment of opioid use disorder (OUD). Based on available data and the seriousness of the conditions, HHS is prioritizing two initial populations for federally supported research: adults with OUD and adults with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).
The public will have 45 days following publication in the Federal Register to submit comments, data or information to the docket. Stakeholders are encouraged to submit comments electronically at regulations.gov by searching for Docket No. FDA-2026-N-10429. Written/paper submissions may also be sent to: Dockets Management Staff (HFA-305), Food and Drug Administration, 5630 Fishers Lane, Rm. 1061, Rockville, MD 20852.
The comment period closes Friday, November 20, 2026. Late comments will not be considered.
###
The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation’s food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, radiation-emitting electronic products, and for regulating tobacco products.
title: FDA Seeks Public Input to Support Ibogaine Research

Congressional 4-H Caucus Leaders Introduce National 4-H Week Resolution
WASHINGTON – U.S. Representatives Sanford D. Bishop, Jr. (GA-02), Glenn “GT” Thompson (PA-15), Angie Craig (MN-02), and Andy Harris (MD-01), co-chairs of the bipartisan 4-H Caucus, introduced a resolution today to designate the week of October 4 through October 10 as "National 4-H Week.”
As the youth development program of the Cooperative Extension System of Land-Grant Universities, 4-H engages young people in hands-on projects in the critical areas of agriculture, health, science, and civic leadership. 4-H is the largest youth development organization in the country, with six million current members and 35 million alumni.
“Georgia is proud to be an early home for 4 H, starting in 1904, with programs reaching every county in our state and preparing young people to lead in agriculture, science, and civic life. I’ve had the pleasure to meet with National 4 H Council President & CEO Jill Bramble to discuss how 4 H continues to strengthen youth leadership nationwide. As an Eagle Scout, I know how essential positive role models and supportive environments are for young people, and 4 H delivers that every day. As Ranking Member of the House Agriculture Appropriations Subcommittee, I remain committed to investing in programs that uplift rural communities and build a stronger future for Georgia and our nation,” Rep. Bishop said.
“The work ethic and curiosity of each 4-H member I’ve met over the years is one of the reasons I feel so confident in the future of our country's agriculture industry. I am proud to introduce this bipartisan resolution to recognize the important work of 4-H members across the country, and encourage others to get involved as well,” Rep. Thompson said.
“The work that 4-H does to develop our youth into the next generation of leaders in agriculture and beyond is more important than ever. American agriculture has come under great pressure, and fostering a love of agriculture in young people is crucial for America’s future. I am proud to celebrate 4-H today and stand with them as they work to empower America’s youth,” Rep. Craig said.
“4-H gives young people in Maryland and across our nation the chance to experience agriculture firsthand. Representing farming communities across Maryland’s First District, I understand the hard work that farming requires and why it matters for young people to learn about agriculture and the work behind it. I’m proud to recognize National 4-H Week and the millions of young Americans who participate in 4-H,” Rep. Harris said.
“We are grateful for the bipartisan support of the Congressional 4-H Caucus and its recognition of the millions of young people who are building the skills and confidence to be ready for work and life. For nearly 125 years, 4-H and Cooperative Extension have helped young people discover what they’re capable of, explore career skills and opportunities, and become Beyond Ready for what comes next,” National 4-H Council President and CEO Jill Bramble said.
Read the full resolution here.
###
title: Congressional 4-H Caucus Leaders Introduce National 4-H Week Resolution

text:
CNO, MCPON Conduct All Hands Call at NAS Sigonella
SIGONELLA, Italy — Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle and Master Chief Petty Officer of the Navy John Perryman visited Naval Air Station Sigonella Oct. 5, meeting with Sailors, touring naval aviation assets and fielding questions during an All Hands Call attended by more than 500 Sailors.
The visit marked the pair’s first stop on a six-day trip to the U.S. European Command area of operations, providing an opportunity to hear directly from Sailors supporting naval operations in the region.
“The strength of our Navy starts with our Sailors,” said Caudle who takes pride in being called a “Sailors First CNO.” “Being here in Sigonella gives us an opportunity to see their work firsthand, hear what they need and understand how decisions made in Washington affect the people carrying out the mission.”
Caudle and Perryman met with Sailors and toured helicopters and a P-8 assigned to Commander, Task Force 67. They also visited Unmanned Patrol Squadron 19, getting a firsthand look at the personnel and aviation capabilities supporting the fleet.
“It was incredible to witness CNO and MCPON visit our Sailor’s workspaces, shake their hands, and talk to them” said Captain Frank Sanchez, commodore, Commander Task Force (CTF) 67.
“Our Sailors were looking forward to this visit and we’re beyond grateful for their dedication in making time to visit us.”
“Having our senior leaders here to see the great work our Sailors do every day and to see our warfighters operating forward to support combat operations across the area of responsibility is phenomenal,” said Capt. Daniel Martins, the commanding officer of Naval Air Station Sigonella.
During the All Hands Call, Sailors raised questions on career development, retention and operational demands, including deployment lengths and the war with Iran. The exchange gave the Navy’s senior uniformed leaders an opportunity to address concerns and hear perspectives from the deckplates.
“Our Sailors deserve leaders who listen and communicate clearly,” said Perryman. “Whether the question is about advancing in your career, the length of your next deployment or taking care of your family, those concerns matter. They affect your readiness, your future and your decision to continue serving.”
Caudle emphasized the connection between supporting Sailors and sustaining a combat-ready fleet.
“When we ask Sailors to operate forward and respond to demanding missions, we owe them the training, equipment and support to succeed,” said Caudle. “Their questions help us identify where we need to do better, and their professionalism gives us confidence in what this fleet can accomplish.”
Before departing Sigonella, Caudle and Perryman participated in a leadership lunch with the region’s senior military officers and civilian leaders.
“Taking care of Sailors is a responsibility at every level of leadership,” said Perryman. “We need to develop their skills, give them opportunities to lead and make sure they know their service is valued. That is how we build strong teams and keep talented people in our Navy.”
Caudle’s next stop is Venice, Italy, where he will participate in the Trans-Regional Seapower Symposium, joining international naval leaders for discussions on maritime security and cooperation.
title: CNO, MCPON Conduct All Hands Call at NAS Sigonella

BUFFALO, N.Y. - U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today Carwin D. Lidge, 27, of Amherst, NY, Jenny B. Alemany, 40, and Richard Law, 29, both of Buffalo, NY, were arrested and charged by criminal complaint with conspiracy to commit mail theft, which carries a maximum penalty of five years in prison and a fine of $250,000.

According to the criminal complaint, in October 2025, the U.S. Postal Inspection Service launched multiple investigations into the robberies of nine letter carriers in Erie and Niagara Counties for their specialized postal keys, which are used to access blue mail collection boxes.

On December 5, 2025, Niagara Falls Police officers and Postal Inspectors responded to the scene of a letter carrier who was robbed of her postal key on Forest Avenue. The letter carrier was approached by an unknown black male wearing a neck warmer pulled up to mask much of his face. The man had his hands in his front hoodie pocket and pointed the pocket toward the letter carrier, causing her to believe the individual had a weapon pointed at her. The man demanded, “give me that gold key,” which she understood to mean her postal key. She gave the man her key, and he then ran off. The stolen key could be used to gain access to all blue collection boxes located in the Niagara Falls area.

In the early morning hours of October 5, 2026, investigators were conducting surveillance of the La Salle Post Office in Niagara Falls, when inspectors received notification that the collection box outside the Main Street Post Office in Niagara Falls had been accessed. At approximately 2:35 a.m., law enforcement observed a silver-colored vehicle, with a burned-out driver side taillight, park near the La Salle Post Office. Two suspects exited the vehicle with a large black bag. Security surveillance video showed a third suspect seated in the front passenger seat. The first two suspects approached the collection box outside the La Salle Post Office, one suspect held back, appearing to act as a lookout, while the other suspect accessed the drive-up collection box. Security surveillance video captured the suspect as he appeared to use a key to open the lower employee access panel to the box and remove all of the mail from the white flat tub contained in the bottom of the box, loading all of the mail into a backpack. As the two suspects started heading back to their vehicle, Inspectors and Niagara Falls Police officers quickly moved in with vehicles and on foot. The two suspects briefly attempted to flee but were quickly apprehended along with the third suspect. La enforcement recovered the backpack full of mail and the postal key, which had been stolen from the postal carrier in December 2025.

The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Franz M. Wright. The complaint is the result of an investigation by the U.S. Postal Inspection Service, under the direction of Acting Inspector-in-Charge Justin Page, Boston Division and the Niagara Falls Police Department, under the direction of Chief Nick Ligammari.

The fact that a defendant has been charged with a crime is merely an accusation and the defendant is presumed innocent until and unless proven guilty.

WASHINGTON D.C. – Today, Rep. George Whitesides (CA-27) announced his cosponsorship of the bipartisan, bicameral Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act. The bill would create a national film tax credit to bring film and television production, and the crew, trades and small-business jobs that come with it, back to the United States.
“Our region is at the heart of film and television production, and we owe it to the hardworking crews who live in our area to bring American production home,” said Rep. Whitesides. “This bipartisan bill invests in the people, sound stages, movie sets, and scenery we have right here in our backyard, and gives productions an incentive to keep good-paying jobs in Southern California. I’ll keep fighting alongside this bipartisan coalition to make sure our local film economy is able to thrive.”
In 2019, Santa Clarita issued a record 576 film permits for 1,490 days of location filming, generating an estimated $35.9 million for the local economy. In 2025, the city issued 338 permits, generating an estimated $14.6 million, a drop of nearly 60%. Across the region permitted by FilmLA, which includes Palmdale and the unincorporated communities of north Los Angeles County, on-location shoot days fell 16% from 2024 to 2025, and television shooting ran 50% below its five-year average. Nationwide, more than 100,000 production jobs have disappeared since October 2022 as 65 countries now offer incentives to lure American productions overseas.
Under the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act:
- Feature films, TV pilots, and TV seasons costing more than $1 million earn a 20% credit on American labor costs if at least 75% of filming takes place in the U.S.
- Productions earn bonus credits of 5% each, up to 30% total, for filming in rural opportunity zones or disaster areas, for independent productions, for hiring across 10 or more states, and for bringing work home from overseas.
- Post-production and visual effects work done in the U.S. qualifies.
- The credit is transferable, so independent producers who don’t owe enough in taxes can sell it for cash up front.
- The credit applies to productions beginning in taxable years after December 31, 2026.
The legislation is led in the House by Representatives Laura Friedman (CA-30), Nathaniel Moran (TX-01), Linda Sánchez (CA-38), Brian Jack (GA-03), David Kustoff (TN-08), Judy Chu (CA-28), Mike Carey (OH-15) and Tom Suozzi (NY-03), and in the Senate by Senators Tim Scott (SC) and Adam Schiff (CA). It is endorsed by the American Federation of Musicians, ASCAP, Coalition for American Production, CreativeFuture, Directors Guild of America, FilmUSA, Independent Film and Television Alliance, IATSE, Motion Picture Association, Paramount, Producers Guild of America, SAG-AFTRA, Teamsters, Television Academy, Writers Guild of America East, and Writers Guild of America West.
###
title: Rep. Whitesides Pushes for a National Film Tax Credit to Bring Production Jobs Back to Santa Clarita and the Antelope Valley

PHOENIX – Last week, Representative Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) met with Marine Corps combat veteran Sergeant Alecsaiah Tree, whose combat-related compensation claim was delayed five months past the processing times after nearly two years without an update. Following concerted efforts by Ansari’s office, Sergeant Tree secured approval for Combat-Related Special Compensation with a 100 percent combat-related disability rating, retroactive to April 1, 2024.
“Sergeant Tree served our country for more than 11 years and was wounded while helping evacuate people from Afghanistan. He should not have had to wait this long for the compensation he earned,” said Rep. Ansari. “I’m glad my office was able to help him secure approval. Our responsibility to service members continues long after they leave the military, and I remain committed to helping Arizona veterans access the benefits and support they deserve.”
“After waiting nearly two years for an update, I’m grateful that Congresswoman Ansari’s office helped move my case forward,” said Sergeant Tree. “Having someone follow up and help me navigate the process made a real difference. Veterans should be able to get the benefits they earned without having to fight for them.”
Sergeant Tree was wounded in the August 26, 2021, attack at Abbey Gate during the military evacuation from Afghanistan. He contacted Rep. Ansari’s office after waiting 23 months for an update on his compensation request—five months beyond the agency’s stated processing timeframe. Ansari’s office contacted the Department of the Navy and worked to get Sergeant Tree’s claim processed.
Ansari with Sergeant Tree and his service dog, Zeus
AZ-03 residents in need of assistance with federal agencies are encouraged to reach out to Rep. Ansari’s office. Visit ansari.house.gov or contact her Phoenix office by phone at (602) 956-2285.
###
title: Ansari Secures Long-Delayed Combat-Related Compensation for Wounded Marine Veteran

The persons aboard the aircraft were:
Canadians:
Philip Gregory Childerhose
Thomas Henry Farquhar
Sarah Jane Paton
Jolene Beth Weir
Bermudians:
Marilyn Lavonne Bean
Sergio Wayne Lottimore
The Coast Guard is aware that a civilian vessel in the area located debris in the water associated with the aircraft.

Kaptur Announces Additional Federal Funds for Davis-Besse Nuclear Power Plant in Oak Harbor
DOE Loan to Increase Plant Power Generation by About 9 Percent for Northwest Ohio
Oak Harbor, OH – Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development, welcomed the Department of Energy’s announcement of a Federal loan of up to $4.2 Billion to Vistra Corp. to modernize three nuclear power plants, including the Davis-Besse Nuclear Power Plant in Oak Harbor, Ohio. The investment will increase reliable power generation and grid capacity across Northern Ohio. At Davis-Besse, the project is expected to add 80 Megawatts of generating capacity and extend the reactor’s operating life by 25 years.
“This Federal support is timely given rising demands on our electrical grid and the need for additional power to protect jobs and attract new and expanded manufacturing facilities, while also helping avoid further rate increases on residential ratepayers,” said Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09).
Kaptur emphasized the need for continued accountability and ratepayer protection following the plant’s history under its former owner, FirstEnergy, and the corruption associated with Ohio House Bill 6. She continues to advocate for her Ratepayer Justice and Commercial Power Accountability Act, which would seek to return funds improperly taken from ratepayers and prioritize future Federal investment in communities harmed by utility misconduct.
Kaptur also highlighted Federal investments in the region’s nuclear workforce. In April, the US Department of Energy awarded $19.2 Million to the University of Toledo for the Great Lakes Partnership to Enhance the Nuclear Workforce, under a new national nuclear workforce training program Congresswoman Kaptur created. The initiative, in partnership with Vistra, UToledo, the University of Michigan, Owens Community College, IBEW, and others, is a first of its kind industry commitment to develop workforce training and nuclear reactor safety credentials for current and future workers.
“These efforts are interconnected: delivering ratepayer justice, moving toward a new energy future, training a workforce focused on safety, and upgrading Davis-Besse to meet growing electricity demand,” Congresswoman Kaptur concluded.
The Vistra projects at Davis-Besse, the Perry nuclear facility in Ohio, and Beaver Valley in Pennsylvania are expected to preserve nearly 4 Gigawatts of reliable baseload power, add 433 Megawatts of new nuclear capacity, support approximately 3,000 project-related jobs, and preserve thousands of permanent jobs across the region. Davis-Besse, which began operating in 1977, was acquired by Vistra from FirstEnergy in 2024 and currently employs approximately 530 workers.
As Ranking Member of the Energy and Water Development Subcommittee, Congresswoman Kaptur continues to oversee DOE programs supporting power generation, grid modernization, nuclear safety, and ratepayer protection in Northern Ohio.
# # #
title: Kaptur Announces Additional Federal Funds for Davis-Besse Nuclear Power Plant in Oak Harbor

Doggett Statement on New GAO Report on Insurer-Owned Pharmacies
WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, U.S. Representative Lloyd Doggett (D-TX), Ranking Member of the House Ways & Means Health Subcommittee, released the following statement after a Government Accountability Office (GAO) report he requested found that large health insurers often give their own pharmacies better terms on lower-cost generic drugs:
“There is a real danger that consumers and taxpayers are being ripped off by giant health conglomerates. Three insurer-pharmacy benefit managers control 80% of prescription drug claims. This report is the first detailed study of these insurer-pharmacy contracts and exposes frequent preferential treatment for insurer-owned pharmacies. Americans are struggling with higher and higher costs for medications and other care. Congress must act to restrain health care monopolies and oligopolies.”
The GAO report can be found here.

ST. LOUIS – Three men who have been accused of involvement in a methamphetamine distribution conspiracy in Dent County, Missouri were arrested Monday.

William Wind, 59, Thomas Wind, 60, and David Gray, 58, were indicted in U.S. District Court in St. Louis on September 16 with one count of conspiracy to distribute and possess with the intent to distribute methamphetamine. The indictment alleges the drug conspiracy lasted from Jan. 1, 2025, to at least February 2026. Each man also faces one count of possession with the intent to distribute meth and Thomas Wind faces a charge of being a felon in possession of a firearm.

The indictment also seeks the forfeiture of three pistols and five rifles seized during the investigation.

Charges set forth in an indictment are merely accusations and do not constitute proof of guilt. Every defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty.

The FBI; the Rolla Area Drug Enforcement Task Force (RADE), which is comprised of officers from the Rolla Police Department, the Dent County Sheriff’s Office and the Phelps County Sheriff’s Office; the Salem Police Department; the Licking Police Department; the Texas County Sheriff's Department and Missouri’s Operation Relentless Pursuit, a coordinated, intelligence-led law enforcement initiative to locate and apprehend fugitives, assisted with the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Mohsen Pasha is prosecuting the case.

This investigation is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF St. Louis comprises agents and officers from the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE); Homeland Security Investigations (HSI); Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI); Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF); Untied States Marshal Service (USMS); Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA); Internal Revenue Service (IRS); and United States Postal Inspection Service (USPIS), with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Missouri.

Rep. Chu Introduces Resolution to Designate October 5th as National Beyond the Milky Way Day
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28) introduced a resolution to designate October 5, 2026, as “National Beyond the Milky Way Day,” commemorating the groundbreaking discovery that the Milky Way is just one of countless galaxies and celebrating the scientific research that fundamentally transformed humanity’s understanding of the universe.
The resolution recognizes a transformative breakthrough in astronomy made possible by American scientific leadership, the pioneering work of astronomers at Carnegie Science, and the world-class facilities at Mount Wilson Observatory in the San Gabriel Mountains.
On October 5, 1923, Carnegie Science astronomer Edwin Powell Hubble, working overnight at Mount Wilson Observatory, identified a Cepheid variable star in what was then thought to be the Andromeda Nebula. Using the period-luminosity relationship discovered by Harvard astronomer Henrietta Swan Leavitt, now known as Leavitt’s Law, Hubble was able to determine the star’s distance from Earth. His observations provided decisive evidence that Andromeda was not a nebula within the Milky Way, but an entirely separate galaxy far beyond its boundaries.
This discovery fundamentally transformed humanity’s understanding of the universe, establishing that the Milky Way was not the entirety of the universe, but just one galaxy among countless others in an unimaginably vast universe. It remains one of the most consequential discoveries in the history of astronomy.
“More than a century ago, right here in the San Gabriel Mountains, a groundbreaking discovery forever changed humanity’s understanding of our place in the universe,” said Rep. Chu. “I’m proud to honor the scientists and institutions whose pioneering work made that discovery possible. Their achievement is a powerful reminder of what we can accomplish when we invest in scientific research, discovery, and collaboration, and I will always fight to ensure America continues making those investments for generations to come.”
"Our founder, Andrew Carnegie, foresaw that investing in scientific research would pay dividends for all of humankind. Discovery science, like the astronomical breakthroughs pioneered by Edwin Hubble, have fed our collective hunger to understand our place in the universe and we continue to push the boundaries of discovery today," said Carnegie Science President John Mulchaey. "We are so grateful to Rep. Judy Chu for her tireless advocacy for science both here in Pasadena and nationwide. Her work enables the next generation of Hubbles and Leavitts to advance our knowledge of the natural world."
The resolution is co-sponsored by Reps. Zoe Lofgren (CA-18), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), and Ted Lieu (CA-36).
It is endorsed by Carnegie Science.
The full text of the resolution is available HERE.
title: Rep. Chu Introduces Resolution to Designate October 5th as National Beyond the Milky Way Day

SIOUX FALLS - United States Attorney Ron Parsons announced today that Chief District Judge Roberto A. Lange has sentenced a Rapid City man convicted of Possession of a Firearm and Ammunition by a Prohibited Person. The sentencing took place on September 28, 2026.

Patrick Riley Bettelyoun, 47, was sentenced to two years and six months in federal prison, followed by three years of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund.

Bettelyoun was indicted for Possession of a Firearm and Ammunition by a Prohibited Person by a federal grand jury in July 2025. He pleaded guilty on June 29, 2026.

Bettelyoun was convicted of a felony offense for possession of a controlled substance in Codington County, South Dakota, in 2022. In October 2024, Bettelyoun was on parole and absconded. Accordingly, an arrest warrant was issued and the warrant area task force found him in a vehicle in Sioux Falls and performed a traffic stop. During a search of Bettelyoun’s vehicle, law enforcement located a firearm, ammunition, methamphetamine, and fentanyl.

This case was investigated by the Sioux Falls Police Department and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives. Assistant U.S. Attorney Elizabeth Ebert-Webb prosecuted the case.

Bettelyoun was immediately remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service.
title: Rapid City Man Sentenced to Over 2 Years in Federal Prison for Possession of a Firearm and Ammunition by a Prohibited Person
