ABINGDON, Va. – Two individuals who conspired with others to execute a business email compromise scheme that stole more than $1.5 million from victims throughout the United States were recently sentenced in U.S. District Court in Abingdon.

Shelton, 57, of Wytheville, Virginia, and Olivia Oxley, 36, of Brooklyn, New York, both pleaded guilty in July last year to conspiracy to commit bank and wire fraud. For her role in the conspiracy, Oxley was sentenced to one year and one day of imprisonment followed by three years of supervised release. Shelton was sentenced to 300 hours of community service and five years of supervised release. Both were also ordered to pay restitution to four victims totaling over $1.5 million jointly and severally with their coconspirators. Neither Shelton nor Oxley were leaders of the scheme but instead facilitated the transfer of the fraudulent funds. Shelton and Oxley forwarded almost all of the fraudulently obtained proceeds to coconspirators overseas.

Zamar Tara McPherson, 49, of Boynton Beach, Florida, has also pleaded guilty to being part of the conspiracy and is awaiting sentencing.

“The Western District of Virginia will continue to prioritize scammer and fraudsters who prey on our citizens,” First Assistant United States Attorney Robert N. Tracci said today. “Special thanks to the FBI, Homeland Security Investigations, Virginia State Police, and all the state and local agencies who assisted in this investigation.”

According to court documents, McPherson, Shelton, Oxley, and others conspired to engage in a business email compromise scheme. The victims in this case had planned to send legitimate wire payments to certain payees. A member of the conspiracy created and utilized fictitious email accounts, however, and provided new account information for the wire payments to the victims. The victims were then defrauded into sending large sums of money to bank accounts belonging to McPherson, Shelton, and Oxley. McPherson, Shelton, and Oxley created and utilized personal and illegitimate business accounts at various financial institutions to facilitate these fraudulent wire transfer payments.

First Assistant United States Attorney Robert N. Tracci, Ian Kaufmann, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI’s Richmond Division and Homeland Security Investigations Washington, D.C. Acting Special Agent in Charge Kai Wah Chan made the announcement.

Several law enforcement agencies throughout the United States investigated the case, including Homeland Security Investigations Washington, D.C., St. Paul; Federal Bureau of Investigation; Eden Prairie, Minnesota Police Department; Virginia State Police; Middlesex County, New Jersey Prosecutor’s Office; and Palm Beach County, Florida Sheriff’s Office.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Corey Hall is prosecuting the case.
title: Pair Sentenced for Roles in Business Email Fraud Scheme

Secretary Kennedy Announces 8 Communities to Receive $96 Million Through New STREETS Program
WASHINGTON, D.C. — October 2, 2026 — U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. today announced in Houston, Texas the eight communities selected to receive funding through the new Safety Through Recovery, Engagement, and Evidence-based Treatment and Support (STREETS) program. Administered by the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), STREETS will provide $96 million over four years to help communities build coordinated systems of care for people who are homeless and have serious mental illness, substance use disorders, or co-occurring disorders.
“STREETS takes treatment directly to Americans living on our streets and connects them to the care and support they need to recover,” said Secretary Kennedy. “Under President Trump, we will no longer accept a system that manages human suffering instead of ending it. We are helping people reclaim their health, rebuild their lives, and achieve the dignity, purpose, and independence that come with recovery.”
Each of the eight selected communities will receive $3 million a year for four years. The selected communities are:
- Alcohol, Drug Addiction and Mental Health Services (ADAMHS) Board for Montgomery County (OH)
- Cherokee Nation (OK)
- City of Detroit, Health Department (MI)
- City of Houston, Health Department, Human Services Division (TX)
- City Of Huntington (WV)
- Miami-Dade County (FL)
- Robeson County (NC)
- Tangipahoa Parish Government (LA)
STREETS puts the Trump Administration’s Treatment First approach into action by bringing engagement and evidence-based treatment directly to people who are homeless and connecting treatment with recovery supports, housing, and other community services. Treatment is the starting point; recovery is the goal. The program emphasizes sustained engagement to improve health, promote stability and self-sufficiency, and reduce repeated homelessness and involvement with crisis systems.
“People who are homeless and struggling with serious mental illness or addiction should not have to navigate fragmented systems alone,” said SAMHSA Chief of Staff Timothy W. Westlake. “We are organizing systems around recovery instead of asking people in crisis to organize themselves around systems. STREETS brings treatment, recovery supports, housing, and community partners together to help people achieve lasting stability and greater independence.”
STREETS advances President Trump’s Executive Order on Ending Crime and Disorder on America’s Streets and the Great American Recovery, co-chaired by HHS Secretary Kennedy and White House Senior Advisor for Addiction Recovery Kathryn Burgum. STREETS also supports SAMHSA’s Strategic Priorities to advance evidence-based treatment approaches that prioritize recovery, self-sufficiency, and public safety while directly combating the devastating effects of addiction, mental illness, and homelessness in America.
“The Great American Recovery is building a national culture in which recovery is expected, supported, and celebrated,” said White House Senior Advisor Kathryn Burgum. “STREETS brings that mission directly to Americans in need by connecting Treatment First with sustained recovery support, housing, and a pathway toward stability, self-sufficiency, and renewed purpose.”
STREETS places special emphasis on rapid, comprehensive, and coordinated street-based engagement, treatment, and recovery support. Grantees will bring together local government, behavioral health and health care providers, housing partners, law enforcement, courts, first responders, and other community organizations to build coordinated systems of care that help people remain engaged in treatment and recovery, achieve greater stability and independence, and reduce repeated homelessness and crisis-system involvement.
If you or someone you know is struggling or in crisis, help is available. Call or text 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org. To locate a treatment facility or provider, visit FindTreatment.gov.
Credentialed media outlets may send requests for comment.

WASHINGTON – Demonte Gibson, 28, Tre’Quan Nelson, 26, and Asani Forte, 29, all of Washington, D.C., were found guilty today in D.C. Superior Court, related to a shooting on November 3, 2021, that killed 34-year-old Delonte King and injured several others, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

“Individuals who commit acts of violence against residents of the District have no place in our society,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “Today’s verdict takes violent offenders off our streets and contributes to a safer D.C. for everyone.”

“Individuals who commit acts of violence against residents of the District have no place in our society,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “Today’s verdict takes violent offenders off our streets and contributes to a safer D.C. for everyone.”

Gibson was found guilty of one count of first-degree murder while armed, one count of assault with intent to kill while armed, one count of malicious destruction of property, and one count of conspiracy.

Nelson was found guilty of one count of conspiracy to commit murder while armed.

Forte was found guilty of one count of conspiracy to commit murder while armed.

This is a retrial as the case resulted in a hung jury in April 2025. Superior Court Judge scheduled sentencing for Gibson on January 8, 2027.

According to the government’s evidence, at approximately 2:02 p.m., on November 3, 2021, members of the Metropolitan Police Department’s Third District responded to the report of a shooting in the 2800 block of 14th Street, NW. Upon arrival, the members located an adult male victim, Delonte King, unconscious and breathing, suffering from apparent gunshot wounds to the head and back. Shortly thereafter, a second adult male shooting victim, 64-year-old Allen Hillyer, was located in the 2900 block of 14th Street, NW. Mr. Hillyer was conscious and breathing but suffering from a gunshot wound to the arm. District of Columbia Fire & EMS units were summoned to the scene, and both victims were transported to area hospitals for treatment.

Later, two additional victims, who were not injured but suffered destruction of property, were inside their home when a bullet came through a third-floor bedroom window, located in Trinity Towers, right up the street from the shooting location. ShotSpotter did not alert to this incident, but later provided that approximately 25 rounds were from the reported location. Surveillance video showed all three defendants congregating together without masks in the area of the shooting and eventually, the defendants were arrested for the shooting spree. A search warrant of Gibson’s apartment uncovered guns and ammo (including head stamps that match some of the head stamps on shell casings found at the murder scene – 40 caliber) they also found a ski mask and purple brand jeans that appear to be identical to the ski mask and the jeans worn by Gibson during the homicide shooting.

Surveillance image of the three defendants in front entrance of 1443 Fairmont Street, NW

Gibson was arrested on February 27, 2023, Nelson was arrested on March 30, 2023, and Forte was arrested on April 25, 2023. All have been in custody since.

Joining the announcement was Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll of the Metropolitan Police Department.

This case was investigated by the Metropolitan Police Department.

The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Erin DeRiso.

PHOENIX, Ariz. – During the week of enforcement operations from Sep. 26 through Oct. 2, 2026, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Arizona brought immigration-related criminal charges against 374 individuals. Specifically, the United States filed 189 cases in which aliens illegally re-entered the United States, and the United States also charged 155 aliens for illegally entering the United States. In its ongoing effort to deter unlawful immigration, the United States filed 27 cases against 29 individuals responsible for smuggling illegal aliens into and within the District of Arizona. Protecting law enforcement officers is a key part of border vigilance, and federal prosecutors also charged one defendant for assaulting a Border Patrol Agent (BPA).

These cases were referred or supported by federal law enforcement partners, including U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s Enforcement and Removal Operations (ICE-ERO), ICE- Homeland Security Investigations (ICE-HSI), U.S. Border Patrol, the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), the FBI, the U.S. Marshals Service (USMS), and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF).

Recent matters of interest include:

United States of America v. Anita Lynn Torres. On Oct. 1, 2026, Anita Lynn Torres was charged by criminal complaint with Transportation of an Illegal Alien. On Sept. 29, 2026, a Pinal County Deputy observed a Ford Escape speeding on Interstate 10 and initiated a traffic stop. Torres was driving the vehicle and transporting two passengers. As the deputy and Torres walked to the deputy’s patrol vehicle, both passengers fled the Ford Escape. They were later apprehended. BPAs determined that one passenger is a citizen of El Salvador and the other a citizen of Mexico, and that both were unlawfully present in the United States. BPAs also learned that Torres recruited drivers to transport illegal aliens and knew her passengers were illegal aliens. [Case Number 26-MJ-6382]

United States of America v. Fred Jacob Lopez Jr. On Oct. 1, 2026, Fred Jacob Lopez Jr., was charged by criminal complaint with Transportation of an Illegal Alien. On Sept. 30, 2026, an Arizona Department of Public Safety Trooper stopped Lopez for speeding on Interstate 10. Lopez was transporting one passenger at the time. The Trooper learned that Lopez had an active federal arrest warrant for violating the supervised release conditions of his 2023 conviction for Transportation of Illegal Aliens for Profit. BPAs responded and determined that Lopez’s passenger was a citizen of Mexico, unlawfully present in the United States. [Case Number: 26-MJ-6388]

A criminal complaint is a formal accusation of criminal conduct. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

BUFFALO, N.Y. - U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Dustin Coffelt, 37, of Depew, NY, who was convicted of production and possession of child pornography, was sentenced to serve 30 years in prison by U.S. District Judge Lawrence J. Vilardo.

In July 2022, the Depew Police Department received a report that Coffelt sexually abused a 13-year-old girl (minor victim). Subsequent investigation determined that the alleged abuse may have been ongoing for several years and included communication over various social media applications and text messaging. On July 29, 2022, Coffelt provided a voluntary statement to detectives from the Depew and Cheektowaga Police Departments admitting to the sexual abuse and producing sexually explicit photographs of the minor victim. Coffelt also voluntarily provided his phone to the detectives and subsequent extraction of the device revealed numerous sexually explicit images of the minor victim, which constitute child pornography. Members of the Federal Bureau of Investigation subsequently arrested Coffelt on August 11, 2022.

The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Maeve E. Huggins and Sasha Mascarenhas. The sentencing is the result of an investigation by the Depew Police Department, under the direction of Chief James McNamara, the Cheektowaga Police Department, under the direction of Chief Brian Coons, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Allen D. Davis, II.

Esta función es fundamental para reforzar el liderazgo estadounidense en la exploración espacial, a medida que la NASA allana el camino hacia una presencia humana sostenida en la Luna.

El plazo para presentar solicitudes está abierto desde ahora hasta el lunes 12 de octubre. Los ciudadanos estadounidenses pueden presentar su solicitud en (información en inglés):

https://www.usajobs.gov/GetJob/ViewDetails/886788000

Las personas seleccionadas como directores de vuelo de la NASA dirigirán misiones tripuladas a la Estación Espacial Internacional, misiones Artemis a la Luna y, más adelante, las primeras misiones tripuladas a Marte. Los directores de vuelo dirigen equipos de controladores de vuelo, astronautas y socios comerciales e internacionales en la ejecución de misiones en tiempo real y en la gestión de riesgos. Durante los preparativos de una misión, los directores de vuelo colaboran con los equipos de ingeniería, seguridad y programas para garantizar que los planes operativos se ajusten a las capacidades de la nave espacial y a los objetivos de la misión.

“Estamos en un momento apasionante y decisivo, ya que seguimos dando soporte a las operaciones en la Estación Espacial Internacional mientras construimos la próxima etapa de los vuelos espaciales tripulados con las misiones de Artemis y Base Lunar, y nos preparamos para llegar más lejos que nunca”, dijo Emily Nelson, jefa de directores de vuelo en el centro Johnson. “Alcanzar estos ambiciosos objetivos requiere directores de vuelo que sean expertos en integración, capaces de reunir una amplia variedad de equipos y disciplinas en un esfuerzo de misión claro y unificado. Esta función esencial representa lo mejor de la innovación y el trabajo en equipo”.

Para ser considerados, los candidatos a director de vuelo deben ser ciudadanos estadounidenses y contar con una licenciatura de una institución acreditada en ingeniería, ciencias biológicas, ciencias físicas, informática o matemáticas. También necesitarán una amplia experiencia profesional afín y de responsabilidad creciente, que incluya la toma de decisiones críticas en entornos de alta presión y alto riesgo. Aunque muchos directores de vuelo de la NASA han sido antes controladores de vuelo en el control de misión, no es un requisito para presentar la solicitud.

La NASA prevé anunciar las selecciones antes de que termine el año. Los nuevos directores de vuelo recibirán una amplia formación en control de vuelo y sistemas de naves espaciales, así como en liderazgo operativo y gestión de riesgos. WASHINGTON, D.C. (October 1, 2026) – Today, Congressman Adam Smith (WA-09) and Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08) introduced the Immigrants in Nursing and Allied Health Act and the Internationally Trained Physicians Assistance Act, two bills to help immigrants enter the U.S. health care workforce and address the nation's growing shortage of health care providers. A 2022 study by the Migration Policy Institute found that 2.1 million college-educated immigrants are unemployed or underemployed, even as sectors like health care face mounting workforce shortages — including a projected shortfall of up to 48,000 primary care physicians by 2034, according to the Association of American Medical Colleges.

“We have thousands of skilled nurses, doctors, and health professionals in this country whose training and expertise are going to waste because their professional expertise is not recognized and they face numerous barriers to achieve the needed licensure. At the same time, our health care system is stretched thin and patients are waiting longer for care,” said Congressman Adam Smith. “This bill package helps immigrants put their skills to work and serve their communities and will rebuild the health care system.”

“Skilled doctors, nurses, and other health professionals should have the opportunity to put their training and expertise to work caring for patients,” said Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi. “Our legislation would help qualified immigrants overcome unnecessary barriers to entering the health care workforce while helping communities address critical provider shortages. When we make better use of the talent already in our communities, we strengthen our health care system and expand access to care.”

Statements of Support

“Across the U.S., communities face critical health workforce shortages, yet immigrant and refugee health professionals—who possess in-demand skills—remain underemployed. Communities need this talent, and recognizing it is an essential step. By streamlining licensure and addressing unnecessary barriers, we can meet urgent labor needs and improve access to quality care. We support efforts, including at the state and federal levels, to advance policies that promote community prosperity by ensuring that immigrants can fully contribute their training and skills to their local economy.” - Kit Taintor, Head of US Policy and Practice, World Education Services (WES)

“We are proud to support these bills, which will expand opportunities for immigrant professionals while helping address critical workforce shortages in the healthcare sector," said Alice Kang, President of Upwardly Global. "With demand for healthcare workers rising nationwide, we should be creating pathways that allow qualified immigrants and refugees to contribute their expertise. This legislation will strengthen our healthcare system, bolster the economy and support safer, more resilient communities. Upwardly Global will continue to stand with Rep. Smith in moving this work forward.”

"Many members of our team hold advanced education and expertise in medicine, nursing, and behavioral health. Yet they are unable to practice here due to costly additional education requirements and complex licensing procedures. At a time when we are confronted with a significant healthcare provider shortage—and as we work to diversify the healthcare workforce—it is critical to consider policies that create pathways for these highly skilled professionals to contribute to patient care,” said Tamara Cyhan Cunitz, MN, RN, Executive Director, Nashi Immigrants Health Board. “These bills introduced by Rep. Smith would expand opportunities for immigrant healthcare professionals to serve patients in our community and region. These measures would not only strengthen our workforce with qualified providers but also enable community members to receive care from clinicians who understand their language and cultural background.”

Background

The Immigrants in Nursing and Allied Health Act would help immigrants, regardless of previous health care experience, enter the nursing and allied health workforce by:

Creating grants for programs that provide training, licensing, certification, and case management for immigrants interested in entering the health care field; and

Opening eligibility for the National Health Service Corps (NHSC) to non-U.S.-citizen immigrants.

An estimated 200,000 nurses per year will need to be hired to meet increased demand and replace retiring nurses. This bill supports immigrants entering nursing or an allied health profession, including dental hygienists, dietitians, medical technologists, occupational therapists, physical therapists, respiratory therapists, and speech language pathologists.

A fact sheet about the Immigrants in Nursing and Allied Health Act can be found here. The bill text can be found here.

The Internationally Trained Physicians Assistance Act would help internationally trained physicians (ITPs) obtain a U.S. medical license by:

Incentivizing states to create temporary licensing programs allowing internationally educated immigrants with medical degrees to practice under supervision while completing the training and certification needed for a U.S. medical license;

Establishing guaranteed medical residency slots for ITPs to practice in predominantly medically underserved communities; and

Providing grants to help cover the cost of exam preparation, testing, certification, ESL classes, and case management for ITPs in need of financial assistance.

Apart from Canada, internationally trained physicians cannot immediately apply to sit for the U.S. Medical Licensing Exam (USMLE), and the cost of licensing, test preparation, and certification often puts a U.S. medical license out of reach, even for highly trained professionals. Many states have created alternative licensure pathways, but more must be done at the federal level to support these reforms nationwide to expand high-quality health care access.

A fact sheet about the Internationally Trained Physicians Assistance Act can be found here. The bill text can be found here.

Endorsements: International Medical Graduates Academy (TIMGA), Nashi Immigrants Health Board, Northwest Immigrant Rights Project, Sea Mar Community Health Center, Seattle Indian Health Board, Spring Institute for Intercultural Learning, Talent Beyond Boundaries, Upwardly Global, World Education Services (WES)

ROCHESTER, N.Y.-U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that a federal jury has convicted Akram Marseet, 42, a native of Libya living in Golden, Colorodo, with threatening to murder two Rochester Federal judges while they were engaged in the performance of their official duties. The conviction carries a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison.

“Today’s verdict reinforces a fundamental principle: threats against members of our judiciary will never be tolerated,” said U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo. “Judges deserve to carry out their work free from intimidation and threats of violence.”

According to testimony presented by the Government, Marseet was the plaintiff in a civil case in United States District Court for the Western District of New York. In January 2024, a federal judge dismissed Marseet’s case.

On January 10, 2024, the U.S. Marshals Service received a report that a direct threat was conveyed via a telephone call to the Clerks’ Office for the Western District of New York and included individuals protected by the Marshals Service. The caller identified himself as Akram Marseet, who stated a pending case number and began to discuss the details of his civil case. The clerk who took the call had spoken to Marseet several times in the past and recognized his voice. Prior to the phone call, Marseet also visited the clerk’s office on multiple occasions.

Marseet became very agitated during the phone conversation because his case was dismissed. He made several statements regarding two judges as being “dirty sons of (expletive)” and criminals. Marseet stated, “If I ever come across any of you, you will be dead sons of (expletive).”

The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Everardo A. Rodriguez and Katelyn M. Hartford. The verdict is the result of an investigation by the U.S. Marshals Service, under the direction of Marshal Charles Salina, the FBI, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Allen D. Davis, II, and the New York State Police, under the direction of Major Kevin Sucher.

Sentencing is scheduled for February 1, 2027, before Chief U.S. District Judge Brenda K. Sannes of the Northern District of New York, who presided over the trial of the case.

EVANSVILLE- Three co-conspirators have been sentenced to federal prison for orchestrating a multi-state bank fraud scheme that targeted federally insured financial institutions. Using stolen identities, sophisticated counterfeit documents, and chemically “washed” checks, the defendants carried out an organized effort to steal tens of thousands of dollars while attempting to defraud victims of more than $300,000 in total. This case was brought as part of the Trump Administration’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud.

According to court documents, between August 1 and September 16, 2025, the three defendants carried out—and attempted to carry out—approximately 30 fraudulent withdrawals at financial institutions across Indiana, Ohio, Virginia, Maryland, and Pennsylvania. Using stolen identities and counterfeit identification cards, the defendants successfully stole $58,800 and attempted to steal a total of $180,058.19.

As one example, on September 13, 2025, Jackson and Javier directed Cimino to enter a bank in Princeton, Indiana, and falsely identify herself as “M.B.” to withdraw funds from the victim’s account. Jackson and Javier supplied Cimino with counterfeit identification documents bearing M.B.’s name and Cimino’s photograph, including a counterfeit U.S. Army identification card. When bank staff requested additional verification, Cimino provided M.B.’s Social Security number and date of birth, which Jackson and Javier relayed to her through an earpiece. Cimino successfully withdrew $8,700 from the victim’s account.

On September 17, 2025, Javier shipped a package from Indianapolis to the Bronx, New York, via FedEx. Inside the package were seven counterfeit U.S. Army identification cards, seven counterfeit U.S. passport cards, and 14 stolen checks. The fraudulent identification cards featured Cimino’s photograph paired with the personal information of seven different victims.

The defendants also obtained stolen checks, chemically “washed” them to remove the original ink, and rewrote the checks payable to themselves for higher amounts. They then attempted to deposit the altered checks into bank accounts controlled by members of the conspiracy. Through this scheme, the defendants intended to steal an additional $149,286.45.

Samuel Javier is a citizen of the Dominican Republic whose visa has expired. At the time he entered his guilty plea, Javier acknowledged that he will be subject to removal from the United States upon completion of his sentence.

“These defendants didn’t hesitate to exploit stolen identities, counterfeit documents, and even fake U.S. Army identification cards to carry out their scheme. Pretending to serve in our nation’s military to steal from innocent Americans is not just fraud, it is an appalling act of deception that insults the men and women who wear the uniform with honor. Their conduct was deliberate, coordinated, and deeply harmful,” said Tom Wheeler, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Indiana. “Today’s sentences reaffirm our commitment to protecting Hoosiers by aggressively pursuing fraudsters and holding accountable those who weaponize deceit against our financial institutions.”

“Fraudsters can use sophisticated tactics and move across state lines, but they can’t hide from investigators who know how to follow the evidence,” said FBI Indianapolis Special Agent in Charge Timothy J. O’Malley. “This investigation is a good example of law enforcement agencies working together to identify a coordinated criminal scheme and bring those responsible to justice. We will continue to pursue criminals who target our financial institutions and steal from others for their own gain.”

The Federal Bureau of Investigation, Defense Criminal Investigative Service, and Indiana State Police investigated this case. The sentences were imposed by U.S. District Court Judge Matthew P. Brookman.

U.S. Attorney Wheeler thanked Assistant U.S. Attorneys Matthew B. Miller and Todd S. Shellenbarger, who prosecuted this case.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Representatives James Walkinshaw (Va.-11), Eugene Vindman (Va.-07), Bobby Scott (Va.-03), Don Beyer (Va.-08), Jennifer McClellan (Va.-04), and Suhas Subramanyam (Va.-10) released the following statement on the eighth anniversary of the murder of Jamal Khashoggi.

Eight years ago today, Virginia resident and journalist Jamal Khashoggi was brutally murdered inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul. His murder was an unconscionable attack on a journalist and a Virginia resident, and his family and the American people deserve the full truth about what happened and what followed.

That includes transparency about President Trump’s 2019 call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Congressman Vindman reviewed the transcript of that call while serving as a lawyer on the National Security Council, and we believe the American people deserve to see it for themselves.

As members of Virginia’s congressional delegation, we will continue pressing for the transparency and accountability that this case demands. If President Trump will not release the transcript now, we will force him to do it in the next Congress when Democrats are in charge.

Eight years is far too long to wait for answers. President Trump should declassify and release the transcript and give the Khashoggi family and the American people the truth they deserve.”

BACKGROUND

Jamal Khashoggi, a Washington Post journalist and U.S. resident, was murdered inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul in October 2018 — an assassination that drew global condemnation and raised serious questions about Saudi Arabia’s leadership and the Trump administration’s response.

In November 2025, Vindman demanded that the White House release the transcript of a “shocking” 2019 call that took place between President Donald Trump and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman following Khashoggi’s murder. Vindman reviewed this call while serving as a staff lawyer on Trump’s National Security Council.

That same month, he led 37 lawmakers in sending a letter to President Trump calling for the immediate release of the transcript. He also hosted a press conference alongside Hanan Elatr Khashoggi — Khashoggi’s wife — and U.S. Representatives Jamie Raskin (Md.-08) and Suhas Subramanyam (Va.-11) to urge President Trump to release the transcript of the call.

In October 2025, Congressman Walkinshaw and Senators Kaine and Warner introduced a bicameral resolution commemorating the seventh anniversary of Khashoggi’s murder and calling for accountability. The resolution also called for the Government of Saudi Arabia to release wrongfully detained individuals, respect the rights of Saudi citizens, and ensure the protection of the freedoms of assembly, association, and the press.

Khashoggi was a resident of Virginia’s 11th District, which was formerly represented by the late Congressman Gerry Connolly and is now represented by Walkinshaw.

BOISE – Jeremy Louis Prior, 41, was sentenced to 15 months in federal prison for assaulting a federal officer, U.S. Attorney Bart M. Davis announced today. Prior is a member of the Shoshone-Paiute Tribe of the Duck Valley Indian Reservation.

According to court records, on February 15, 2026, a Bureau of Indian Affairs officer responded to a request for assistance at a residence located on the Idaho side of the Duck Valley Indian Reservation. The calling party reported that Prior was under the influence and causing a disturbance at the residence. When the officer arrived, he attempted to locate and arrest Prior for an active tribal warrant. The officer eventually found Prior hiding in a closet. As the officer began to place Prior in handcuffs, Prior resisted and punched the officer in the face. Prior also kicked the officer.

Senior U.S. District Judge B. Lynn Winmill also ordered Prior serve three years of supervised release following his prison sentence.

U.S. Attorney Davis commended the work of the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) and Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), which led to the charge. Assistant U.S. Attorney Christopher A. Booker prosecuted the case.

WASHINGTON – Kenneth Coleman, 37, of Washington, D.C., was sentenced today to 240 months in prison for the murder of 24-year-old Jireh Martinez in November 2023, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

Coleman pleaded guilty to one count of second-degree murder while armed on July 13, 2026, before D.C. Superior Court Judge Danya Dayson. In addition to the 20-year prison sentence, Judge Dayson ordered Coleman to serve five years of supervised release.

According to court documents, on November 17, 2023, Coleman attempted to rob Mr. Martinez as Mr. Martinez returned home from a convenience store. Coleman pressed a gun into Mr. Martinez’s head and repeatedly demanded “give it to me.” Mr. Martinez dropped the store bag he was holding but otherwise just stood in place. After the eighth “give it to me,” Coleman pulled the trigger. Mr. Martinez crumpled to the ground, and Coleman walked away. When law enforcement reached Mr. Martinez, his only possession was a single dime.

Coleman was arrested on separate charges on February 9, 2024, and has been in custody ever since.

Joining the announcement was Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll of the Metropolitan Police Department.

In announcing the sentence, U.S. Attorney Pirro and Interim Chief Carroll commended the work of those who investigated the case from the Metropolitan Police Department. They also thanked Assistant U.S. Attorneys Jessica Keefer and William Lawrence, who prosecuted the case.

Tallahassee, Pensacola, & Gainesville, Florida — The Department of Justice’s Office on Violence Against Women has awarded more than $74 million in federal grants to support state, local, and Tribal governments in combatting domestic violence and sexual assault in FY2026. In recognition of Domestic Violence Awareness Month, United States Attorney John P. Heekin of the Northern District of Florida highlighted federal grants recently awarded to key stakeholder groups operating within the Northern District of Florida.

U.S. Attorney John P. Heekin said: “October is Domestic Violence Awareness Month, during which we reaffirm our commitment to providing the safety, dignity, and justice that victims of domestic violence deserve. Through these critical investments of federal grant monies, we strengthen our partnership with coalitions operating in my district to provide victim support services as we work toward building a future free from domestic violence and sexual assault.”

Grant funds authorized under this program may be used for coordinating state and territory victim services activities, or collaborating and coordinating with federal, state, territory, and local entities engaged in violence against women activities.

OVW State and Territory Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault Coalitions Program funds were awarded to the following entities within the Northern District of Florida:

Florida Council Against Sexual Violence, Inc., based in Tallahassee, Florida;

Florida Partnership to End Domestic Violence, Inc., based in Tallahassee, Florida

By understanding the signs of abuse and connecting victims to resources, we can all play a role in creating safer communities. For more information on domestic violence or to access resources, please visit https://www.justice.gov/ovw/domestic-violence .

Fast Facts
The U.S. Interagency Council on Homelessness—which coordinates federal efforts to address homelessness—consists of federal agency representatives (the Council) and a small staff.
In early 2025, the agency placed 11 of its 13 staff on paid administrative leave in response to an executive order to downsize federal agencies. A federal district court found that the agency's implementation of the order was unlawful and made performing its statutory duties impossible.
In early 2026, the agency returned staff to active status, but staff said they haven't received direction on their work from the Council. The agency has appealed the court's decision.
A person sleeping on a bench in a long trench coat and winter hats with bags as a pillow.
Highlights
What GAO Found
The U.S. Interagency Council on Homelessness (USICH) is an independent establishment in the executive branch that coordinates the federal response to homelessness. It consists of representatives from designated federal agencies (the Council) and a staff that has ranged from 10 to 18 full-time employees over the past decade.
USICH’s enabling legislation—the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act—requires it to maintain certain personnel and perform specified duties. These include providing technical assistance to state and local governments through five to 10 regional coordinators employed by the Council, reporting annually to the President and Congress on federal efforts to address homelessness, and developing a national strategic plan to end homelessness.
The act also established a termination date for USICH, which Congress has extended several times, most recently to October 1, 2028. The President’s most recent budget proposes to terminate USICH in fiscal year 2027.
USICH began making changes to its staffing and operations in early 2025, including in response to Executive Order 14238, Continuing the Reduction of the Federal Bureaucracy. In April 2025, 11 of USICH’s 13 employees were placed on paid administrative leave. In the same month, the General Services Administration terminated USICH’s office lease and recovered its equipment.
In November 2025, a federal district court found that USICH’s implementation of the executive order was unlawful. The court noted that the personnel reduction made it impossible for USICH to perform its statutory duties, among other things. The court set aside USICH’s prior actions to implement the order and barred it from doing so in the future. USICH has appealed the decision.
Selected Developments Affecting the U.S. Interagency Council on Homelessness (USICH), January 2025–September 2026
Eight of 11 USICH employees returned from paid administrative leave in mid-February 2026. The other three left USICH prior to employees’ return to active status. As of May 2026, USICH had 10 full-time employees and a part-time executive director. USICH staff told GAO that, since their return, they had not received direction from the Council or the executive director on homelessness policies or priorities to guide their work or help them perform USICH’s statutory duties and functions. The executive director stated that the Council should provide guidance before USICH drafts a strategic plan or undertakes policy initiatives.
Why GAO Did This Study
Several federal agencies administer programs to address homelessness, and USICH was created in 1987 to coordinate these efforts and reduce homelessness.
In early 2025, the President issued a series of directives to downsize the federal workforce and reorganize federal agencies. Among these, Executive Order 14238, issued in March 2025, directed seven federal entities—including USICH—to eliminate nonstatutory functions and to reduce statutory functions and associated personnel to the minimum required by law.
GAO was asked to review USICH’s statutory responsibilities and recent changes to its staffing and operations. This report describes (1) USICH’s responsibilities under the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act and (2) the status of its staffing and operations.
GAO reviewed the McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act, relevant executive orders, court documents, and appropriations acts. GAO also reviewed USICH documentation, interviewed USICH’s executive director and staff, and requested information from three Council member agencies.
For more information, contact Alicia Puente Cackley at CackleyA@gao.gov.
title: U.S. Interagency Council on Homelessness: Staff Placed on Administrative Leave Have Returned and Await Direction

HONOLULU – United States Attorney Ken Sorenson announced that Vaughn Ludwig, 50, of Kailua, Hawaii, was sentenced yesterday in federal court by United States Chief District Judge Derrick K. Watson to 70 months in prison followed by 4 years of supervised release after pleading guilty to conspiring to distribute and possess with intent to distribute fentanyl.

According to court records, Ludwig was part of a conspiracy from at least November 2024 to May 2025 to obtain fentanyl from a mainland supplier and then distribute it in Hawaii. At sentencing, Ludwig was held responsible for approximately 1.5 kilograms of fentanyl and over 200 grams of heroin. In his plea agreement, Ludwig admitted to distributing fentanyl and heroin from a hotel in Waikiki in the days leading up to his arrest on May 1, 2025.

In a separate case related to the same drug trafficking conspiracy, Louis Deguair was sentenced on July 13, 2026, to 37 months in prison followed by 5 years of supervised release for possessing with intent to distribute fentanyl. Charles Patrick Saikley also previously pled guilty in a separate case related to the same drug trafficking conspiracy and is pending sentencing on October 15, 2026, for possessing with intent to distribute fentanyl and methamphetamine.

The FBI investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Barbara Eucker prosecuted the case.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities.

BOSTON – Two Massachusetts men were sentenced yesterday in federal court in Boston for conspiring to damage a building on Harvard Medical School’s (HMS) campus using a large commercial firework.

Logan David Patterson, 19, of Plymouth, Mass. and Dominick Frank Cardoza, 21, of Bourne, Mass., each were sentenced by U.S. District Court Judge Angel Kelley to three years of probation and were ordered to pay restitution of $28,517 to Harvard Medical School. In April 2026 , both defendants pleaded guilty to one count each of conspiracy to damage, by means of an explosive. Patterson and Cardoza were arrested and charged in November 2025 .

At approximately 2:23 a.m. on Nov. 1, 2025, surveillance cameras located at Huntington Avenue and Longwood Avenue in Boston captured two males – later identified as Patterson and Cardoza – walking toward the HMS campus wearing face coverings and dark clothing. Surveillance video captured the defendants lighting what appeared to be roman candle fireworks at approximately 2:24 a.m.

At approximately 2:33 a.m., the defendants were seen climbing over a chain-link fence into a construction area surrounding the Goldenson Building and, minutes later, climbing scaffolding beside the building to access the roof. At approximately 2:45 a.m., campus police received a fire alarm alert from an explosion on the fourth floor of the Goldenson Building, which houses a research laboratory within HMS’s Department of Neurobiology. It was determined that the defendants detonated a large, commercial firework inside a wooden locker in the fourth-floor research laboratory.

Subsequent security footage captured the defendants visiting the fifth floor of the building before exiting via a first-floor emergency exit and fleeing in opposite directions; removing and discarding clothing items they had worn on the HMS campus; and returning to the nearby campus of Wentworth Institute of Technology, which they were visiting for Halloween social activities.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Boston Division made the announcement today. Assistant U.S. Attorney David M. Holcomb of the National Security Unit prosecuted the case.

MILWAUKEE – Yesterday, Ambassador Jamieson Greer released a statement following the G20 Trade Ministerial in Milwaukee, Wisconsin in his capacity as the Chair of the G20 Trade Ministerial.
“This week’s G20 Trade Ministerial in Milwaukee was a success. It is especially significant that the entire G20 was able to reach consensus on the statement on the weaponization of food through coercive trade actions,” said Ambassador Greer. “We also had constructive meetings on the sidelines regarding global diesel supplies which contributed to the anticipated release of more diesel into the global market. G20 Trade Ministers also had candid and productive discussions regarding eliminating forced labor in global supply chains, addressing structural excess capacity and production, and reforming the Most–Favored Nation principle (MFN).”
“In addition, I commend Mexico and Argentina in joining the United States in a statement on eliminating forced labor in global supply chains,” continued Ambassador Greer. “While I am disappointed that the G20 Trade Ministers did not reach consensus on this issue, I am hopeful that discussions on this topic will continue and that other economies will join us in taking increased action to combat forced labor in global supply chains. In addition, many G20 members expressed resolve to address structural excess capacity and production in key sectors of concern. I am disappointed that a handful of members rejected creating a pathway toward cooperative action. Finally, I’m encouraged that members across the development spectrum indicated that they see merit in considering how the MFN principle might be improved to address today’s global trade environment.”

Ranking Member Joe Morelle, Rep. James Walkinshaw Host Fairfax, Virginia Shadow Hearing on Election Security, Fighting Trump Administration’s Attacks on Voting
With voting underway, lawmakers and voting rights leaders gathered in Fairfax to defend mail-in voting, combat intimidation and protect election integrity
FAIRFAX, VA – Yesterday, Ranking Member Joe Morelle (NY-25), Committee on House Administration, and Congresswoman James Walkinshaw (VA-11) hosted a public shadow hearing with members of the Virginia delegation to confront the Trump administration’s attacks on voting and detail efforts to defend every eligible American’s right to cast a ballot and have it counted.
Experts at the shadow hearing included:
- Jeff McKay, Fairfax County Board of Supervisors Chairman
- Skye Perryman, President and CEO of Democracy Forward
- Omar Noureldin, Senior Vice President for Policy and Litigation Strategy at Common Cause
- Rev. Dr. Cozy Bailey, President of the Virginia State Conference NAACP
- Jessica Jones Capparell, Director of Government Affairs at the League of Women Voters of the United States
Experts outlined litigation, voter education and safeguards countering interference, intimidation and misinformation. The hearing examined the administration’s attempted overhaul of mail-ballot processing, federal demands for sensitive voter information, and concerns about armed immigration agents at polling places. Experts explained how litigation blocked the mail-voting rule and detailed ongoing efforts to protect voter privacy and prevent intimidation.
“In this moment, there is nothing more urgent than protecting American democracy,” said Ranking Member Morelle. “The election is here and we are protecting Americans right to the ballot box. Every time the Trump Administration has tried to interfere with the integrity of the midterm elections, they have lost. Over the next month, we need to remain clear-eyed about the threats we continue to face. We will fight to protect American elections. Failure, quite simply, is not an option.”
“Where the Trump administration is sowing fear and confusion, we’re providing facts and defending the right to vote. We came together in Fairfax to make clear that every eligible American, no matter who they support, can cast a ballot with confidence,” said Congressman Walkinshaw (VA-11). “I’m grateful to Ranking Member Morelle for joining us and proud to stand alongside my Virginia colleagues and the voting rights leaders doing this work every day. We will keep fighting to protect every vote and ensure the American people decide who represents them.”
“Over the last two years, the Trump Administration and the Supreme Court have levied various attacks against the right to vote,” said Congressman Bobby Scott (VA-02), Ranking Member of the House Education and Workforce Committee. “Unfortunately, Congressional Republicans have been unwilling to take a stand against these actions. Democrats are fighting to defend everyone's right to participate in our elections, and yesterday's hearing demonstrates the urgency of this fight.”
“My own family struggled, fought, bled and in some cases died for the right to vote,” said Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04). “We have seen repeated efforts by the Administration to undermine the electoral process and the constitutionally protected right of millions to vote. Election integrity means protecting our election systems from foreign interference and unlawful voting, but it also means protecting every citizen’s right to vote, free of intimidation, free from discrimination. We cannot have an America that goes back to the days when propaganda, violence and voter suppression were used to keep all of the people from participating in their government.”
“Every eligible voter should be able to cast their ballot without fear, intimidation, or unnecessary barriers,” said Congressman Eugene Vindman (VA-07). “Our democracy works when voters know their voices will be heard and their votes will be counted. I’m proud to stand with my Virginia colleagues, local election officials, and voting rights advocates to protect access to the ballot, safeguard voter privacy, and ensure every eligible Virginian can make their voice heard.”
“This Administration has threatened to cheat and exhaust every option to diminish our free and fair elections. In these unprecedented times, I am proud to stand together with my colleagues and voting rights organizations to protect the voices of all Americans. We will ensure every vote, regardless of party, gets counted this November. We will not be intimidated,” said Congressman Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10).
Ranking Member Morelle and the Committee on House Administration is charged with the oversight of federal elections, including considering proposals to amend federal election law and monitoring congressional elections across the U.S.

Santa Cruz, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) called on U.S. Postmaster General David Steiner to immediately halt the discontinuance feasibility study for the Brookdale Post Office, identify an alternative post office location in the community, and expand postal services to ensure that residents have timely and local access to their mail.

Postal services in Brookdale have been suspended since a fire severely damaged the community’s contract post office in December 2024. After residents waited nearly two years for the facility to reopen, with no apparent progress being made on repairs, the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) notified the community in September 2026 that it was conducting a feasibility study on permanently closing the location. USPS still has not proposed an alternative location or expanded service within Brookdale.

“Since the Brookdale Post Office burned down, the people of that community have waited for nearly two years in good faith while the USPS sat on its hands saying that they would reopen the facility,” said Rep. Panetta. “Then, out of the blue, the USPS made the haphazard decision to study whether it should shut down the post office without providing any postal service in Brookdale. Such an indiscriminate and arbitrary decision to shut down a local post office, without any plan to open up the existing one or attempt to provide postal services to existing Brookdale customers, is unreasonable, and we expect more out of our Postal Service. That is why I wrote this letter calling on the USPS to stop the study and start figuring out how it can provide postal services to the people of Brookdale.”

Brookdale residents do not receive home mail delivery and have historically relied on post office boxes and retail services at the local facility. Since the fire, residents have been forced to travel to neighboring communities, including Boulder Creek and Ben Lomond, to retrieve their mail and access basic postal services. In the mountain community of Brookdale, that burden is particularly significant for seniors, people with disabilities, working families, and residents without reliable transportation, especially during severe weather and other disruptions in the San Lorenzo Valley.

Rep. Panetta called on Postmaster General Steiner to:

Immediately halt the discontinuance feasibility study on the proposed permanent closing of the Brookdale Post Office;

Investigate potential alternative permanent post office locations in Brookdale;

Explore home delivery service for the residents of Brookdale;

Until home delivery is available, offer cluster box units or another mail pickup solution in Brookdale; and

Schedule a meeting with Rep. Panetta to discuss next steps.

Rep. Panetta has repeatedly pressed USPS leadership to restore postal services in Brookdale. In a February 2026 letter to the Postmaster General, he called on USPS to repair and reopen the facility with a clear project timeline and provide temporary postal service within the community in the interim. After USPS missed its promised May 1 reopening date, Rep. Panetta sent a May 2026 letter requesting that the USPS Inspector General review the agency’s management, communication, and decision-making, the adequacy of interim services, and the feasibility of restoring service through a temporary or alternative facility.

Full text of the letter is available here and below:

Dear Postmaster General:

I write to request your immediate action to end the discontinuance feasibility study for the Brookdale Post Office, to find a new post office location in Brookdale, California, and to expand appropriate postal services to serve this community. Since their contract post office burned down, my constituents have waited for nearly two years in good faith while the USPS deflected its responsibility to reopen the facility. The decision this month to consider discontinuing postal service in Brookdale, with no alternative services to your existing Brookdale customers, is unreasonable without any effort to find an alternative post office location or any other remedy for postal services and basic operations in the community.

In December 2024, a fire disabled service at the contract post office in Brookdale, a town I represent in California’s 19th District. Brookdale is a rural mountain community, and for nearly two years, residents waited in good faith for the USPS to restore service, traveling to other towns to receive basic postal services. This would be a burden under normal circumstances, and it is particularly challenging when residents face weather events or other impediments in the San Lorenzo Valley. For disabled, elderly, and mobility-impaired constituents, traveling out of their town presents an additional challenge, but Brookdale residents have done so patiently with the expectation that USPS would eventually restore a local post office. However, in September 2026, after years of deflections, the USPS announced a discontinuance feasibility study for the post office and took the extraordinary step of preemptively refusing to expand services in Brookdale or to consider a new post office location in the community.

Brookdale has never had home delivery, despite the fact that neighboring towns enjoy this basic service. Over time, residents have come to rely on boxes and retail services at the local post office. For years, these services were housed in a rented facility. When that facility suffered a catastrophic fire, the USPS spent years assuring residents and my office that they were waiting for the property owner to conduct necessary repairs. This rationale continued even after the property owner missed basic deadlines for the repairs. Instead of considering alternative locations for the post office, or my constituents’ requests for home delivery or cluster box units in Brookdale, the USPS took steps to discontinue service altogether.

Faced with this situation, I ask that you:

Immediately halt the discontinuance feasibility study on the proposed permanent closing for the Brookdale Post Office;

Investigate potential alternative permanent post office locations in Brookdale;

Explore home delivery service for the residents of Brookdale;

Until home delivery is available, offer cluster box units or another mail pickup solution in Brookdale;

Schedule a meeting with me to discuss next steps to ensure my constituents are being served.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. Restoring dependable postal operations is vital for my constituents, and these steps will help ensure the residents of Brookdale can rely on the United States Postal Service for years to come.

Sincerely,
title: Rep. Panetta Calls on USPS to Stop Feasibility Study to Close the Brookdale Post Office

WASHINGTON – Kurono Scutchings, 29, a previously convicted felon residing in the District of Columbia, was sentenced today to 50 months in prison in connection with his unlawful possession of a stolen semi-automatic pistol and more than 11 grams of cocaine base, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

“Kurono Scutchings had already been convicted of robbery, and yet he was again found in possession of a stolen firearm and possession with intent to distribute amounts of various narcotics in the District,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “Let this serve as a warning: those who choose a path of illegal firearms possession and possession of trafficking amounts of narcotics will face prosecution and federal prison.”

“Kurono Scutchings had already been convicted of robbery, and yet he was again found in possession of a stolen firearm and possession with intent to distribute amounts of various narcotics in the District,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “Let this serve as a warning: those who choose a path of illegal firearms possession and possession of trafficking amounts of narcotics will face prosecution and federal prison.”

Scutchings, aka “Kuron Scutchings,” pleaded guilty on May 6 before U.S. District Judge Dabney L. Friedrich to unlawful possession of a firearm and ammunition by a felon, and to unlawful possession with intent to distribute cocaine base. In addition to the 50-month prison term, Judge Friedrich ordered Scutchings to serve three years of supervised release.

According to court documents, on Aug. 24, 2025, officers from the Metropolitan Police Department’s Special Missions Unit, along with federal agents operating under the Federal Law Enforcement Surge Task Force, were on patrol in the 2900 block of Knox Place SE. Officers observed Scutchings speaking with another individual before moving to the driver’s seat of a parked vehicle as the officers approached.

When officers asked Scutchings what was in a clear plastic bag in his hand, he claimed it was marijuana but would not show them the contents. Scutchings then handed over the bag. It contained 11.46 grams of cocaine base. During a subsequent search, officers recovered an FN Five-Seven semi-automatic pistol, loaded with 20 rounds of 5.7x28mm ammunition, hidden in Scutchings’ compression shorts. The firearm had been reported stolen out of Prince George’s County, Maryland.

Officers also recovered 5.96 grams of methamphetamine and 1.49 grams of fentanyl from the vehicle’s center console.

Scutchings’ criminal history includes a 2020 D.C. Superior Court conviction for robbery, for which he had been sentenced to 30 months’ incarceration. Given his status as a felon, he was forbidden from possessing any firearm.

The investigation was conducted by the Metropolitan Police Department, with assistance from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, under the Federal Law Enforcement Surge Task Force.

The matter was prosecuted under the Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful initiative by Assistant U.S. Attorney Emory V. Cole. Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful is a law enforcement initiative in support of President Trump’s Executive Order to crack down on gun violence, prioritize federal firearms violations, pursue tougher penalties, and seek detention for federal firearms violators.

Rep. Andrea Salinas Celebrates Continued Funding for Landmark Women’s Healthcare Research
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Congresswoman Andrea Salinas (OR-06) celebrates the five-year extension of funding for the Study of Women's Health Across the Nation (SWAN). The National Institutes of Health (NIH) will award the study $44,456,682 to continue studying menopause and additional midlife factors that may contribute to women's health.
“Menopause affects every woman as they age, yet it has long been underresearched and underfunded, thus limiting our understanding of its impact on women's lives. Over the last three decades, SWAN researchers have made innovative breakthroughs in understanding how perimenopause and menopause can exacerbate mental health issues, bone loss, and sleep problems,” said Salinas. “Regardless, more research is needed to understand its connection to long-term, life-threatening conditions, including strokes and Alzheimer's disease. I am proud that SWAN will receive full funding for the next five years to continue strengthening our understanding of women's health and to equip providers with the training and education they need to deliver quality care to their patients.”
In December 2025, Salinas led thirty-three of her colleagues in sending a letter to the NIH urging continued funding for SWAN, a long-running, federally funded research study examining women’s health during midlife and menopause.
SWAN is an epidemiologic study that began in 1994 to research the health of women as they enter their midlife years. The study aims to educate women and providers about how midlife transitions can affect women's health and to continue scientific research for future breakthroughs.

Despite its growing significance to national security and the economy, the federal government does not adequately protect biotechnology infrastructure or sensitive biological data.

Washington, D.C. – Last week, U.S. Representatives Scott Peters (D-CA), Ro Khanna (D-CA), and Stephanie Bice (R-OK), as well as U.S. Senators Todd Young (R-IN) and Maggie Hassan (D-NH) introduced two bipartisan bills to protect biotechnology data and infrastructure from malicious actors.

The Protecting Biotechnology and Biomanufacturing as Critical Infrastructure Act and the Protecting Biological Data as Critical Infrastructure Act aim to recognize life science infrastructure and sensitive data as critical infrastructure, ensuring robust cybersecurity and cross-sector protection. The legislation directs Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to designate facilities and systems handling genetic and biometric information as critical and requires collaboration with industry stakeholders to develop coordinated security protocols.

Biotechnology infrastructure spans several critical sectors, including health, agriculture, and industry, yet current policy doesn't explicitly recognize or fully protect it. Biological data, which fuels research breakthroughs and often contains sensitive personal information, isn't treated as a strategic national resource either. Some federal efforts are underway, but they're scattered and leave major vulnerabilities.

“Biotechnology is a major driver of San Diego’s economy, employing 167,000 members of our community and generating $55.2 billion in economic output just last year,” said Rep. Peters. “America’s leadership in the sector is a strategic advantage we cannot take for granted. As technology advances and our adversaries grow more capable, American national security, public health, and competitiveness will continue to face more serious threats. Our legislation will strengthen America’s biotech ecosystem against cyber threats, supply chain disruptions, and other vulnerabilities. To maintain our leadership in biotechnology, we need to make sure that the United States remains a safe place to innovate.”

“Protecting biomanufacturing infrastructure and the most sensitive biological data of Americans is essential for our national security,” said Rep. Khanna. “These bipartisan bills will help ensure we are protecting this sector from physical and cyber threats while keeping America as the world leader in biotechnology.”

“Biological data is one of America’s most valuable strategic resources,” said Rep. Bice. “It is the foundation for new discoveries and an increasingly important driver of innovation at the intersection of AI and biotechnology. Recognizing biological data as critical infrastructure is a vital part of protecting sensitive data from those who could exploit it.”

In its April 2025 report to Congress, the National Security Commission on Emerging Biotechnology (NSCEB) assessed that malicious actors will increasingly target the biotechnology sector’s infrastructure and data. Critical biotechnology infrastructure, such as hospitals and agricultural facilities, have already faced numerous cyberattacks. Biological data are not currently treated or protected as a strategic national resource. Both bills reflect NSCEB recommendations.

A detailed summary of the bills can be found here.

Media Note

Office of the Spokesman

October 2, 2026

The text of the following statement was released by the Governments of the United States of America, Albania, Argentina, Australia, Austria, Bahrain, Belize, Bosnia, Bulgaria, Canada, Colombia, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Dominican Republic, Estonia, Federated States of Micronesia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Latvia, Liberia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Marshall Islands, Moldova, Montenegro, Morocco, New Zealand, North Macedonia, Norway, Palau, Panama, Paraguay, Poland, Portugal, Republic of Korea, Romania, San Marino, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, The Netherlands, Trinidad and Tobago, Ukraine, United Kingdom, and Yemen. Begin Text On September 27, 2025 (at 8:00 p.m. EDT), six United Nations Security Council resolutions (UNSCRs) – 1696 (2006), 1737 (2006), 1747 (2007), 1803 (2008), 1835 (2008), 1929 (2010) – returned into force pursuant to the completion of the snapback process. France, Germany, and the United Kingdom initiated this process in response to Tehran’s persistent and significant non-performance of its nuclear commitments under the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA). One year on, we, the Proliferation Security Initiative (PSI)-endorsing States listed above, affirm our commitment to the continued implementation of all relevant obligations enumerated in the reinstated UNSCRs. We further recall that the 2003 Statement of Interdiction Principles (2003), which all PSI participants have endorsed, affirms our adherence to all relevant international law and frameworks, including the UNSCRs. We further commit, consistent with our UNSCR obligations, to continue to take measures – consistent with relevant domestic and international authorities and related commitments – to prevent the supply, sale, or transfer to Iran of items, materials, equipment, goods, and technology that could contribute to proliferation-sensitive nuclear activities or the development of nuclear weapon delivery systems, as well as to uphold the restrictions on the supply, sale, or transfer of arms and related materiel to or from Iran. Our countries further reaffirm our commitment to ensuring sufficient domestic legal authorities and capabilities to address Iran’s proliferation-sensitive activities. More concretely, we commit to (1) undertake effective measures to prevent the direct or indirect sale, supply, and transfer to and from Iran of items from or through their territories that could contribute to weapons of mass destruction, their means of delivery (including UAVs), and related materials and items subject to the reinstated UNs arms restrictions; (2) adopt streamlined procedures to facilitate the rapid exchange between PSI partners of relevant information concerning Iran’s proliferation activities; (3) where needed, continue to keep our national legal authorities under review to ensure the effectiveness of our measures; and (4) take appropriate specific actions in support of interdiction efforts related to Iran’s proliferation activities. We welcome all national-level efforts to implement our UNSCR obligations, as well as relevant activities that support our objective of preventing Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon, such as those linked to Operation Economic Outcast. We urge all UN Member States to implement these resolutions and reiterate the international community’s longstanding concerns about Iran’s nuclear program. We will continue to coordinate our counterproliferation efforts to counter any attempts by Iran to undertake UNSCR-prohibited efforts to resume development of its nuclear or ballistic missile programs. We call on Iran to return to compliance with its nonproliferation obligations, and cooperate fully with the IAEA, and address the international community’s proliferation concerns.

End Text

Social Adult Day Care Owner Pleads Guilty to $65M Medicaid Fraud
A Brooklyn man pleaded guilty today to defrauding New York State Medicaid of approximately $65 million through claims for social adult day care services and home health care services that were not provided.
According to court documents, Ahsan Ijaz, 29, of Brooklyn, New York, was an owner of Happy Family Social Adult Day Care Center, Inc. and Family Social Adult Day Care Center Inc., social adult day care centers located in Brooklyn, and Responsible Care Staffing Inc., a home health care fiscal intermediary in Brooklyn. Over approximately seven years, Ijaz’s businesses paid cash kickbacks and bribes to Medicaid recipients to induce them to enroll with the businesses and billed Medicaid for services that were not provided, including when certain Medicaid recipients were not in the United States at the time of service. Ijaz is the 10th defendant to plead guilty in connection with the scheme.
Ijaz pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit health care fraud. He is scheduled to be sentenced on March 10, 2027 and faces a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division); U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr. for the Eastern District of New York; Acting Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Miranda L. Bennett of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG); Acting Special Agent in Charge Pete Gizas of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) New York; and Commissioner Jessica S. Tisch of the New York City Police Department (NYPD), made the announcement.
HHS-OIG, HSI New York, and NYPD investigated the case.
Deputy Chief Patrick J. Campbell and Trial Attorney Leonid Sandlar of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Health Care Fraud Section are prosecuting the case, with the assistance of Assistant U.S. Attorney Claire Kedeshian for the Eastern District of New York, who is assisting with forfeiture matters.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with HHS-OIG, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit.
