Brann for interstate transportation of stolen motor vehicles.

According to United States Attorney Brian D. Miller, Torres, Otero, and eight additional co-conspirators conspired with each other and others to transport stolen motor vehicles interstate and to receive, possess, conceal, store, sell, and dispose of stolen motor vehicles that had been transported interstate.

Torres, Otero, and their co-conspirators took the stolen vehicles—typically high-end, “muscle” type cars—across state lines to “car meetups” and “street takeovers,” at which the co-conspirators would take over a parking lot, intersection, road, or portion of a highway. The vehicles were then shown off in person at the meetups and on social media and driven in a reckless and dangerous manner, such as drifting and “burning out” the vehicles. Otero ran a prominent car meetup group out of Baltimore, Maryland.

The co-conspirators stole numerous vehicles across multiple states. For example, on October 3, 2023, Torres, Otero, and other co-conspirators traveled to a car dealership in Selinsgrove, Pennsylvania, to steal two 2017 Cadillac CTS-V’s, a 2016 Cadillac CTS-V, two 2019 Cadillac CTS-V’s, a 2018 Chevrolet Camaro, a 2019 Chevrolet Camaro, and a 2019 Chevrolet Corvette.

The defendants in this conspiracy have each been sentenced by Chief Judge Brann as follows:

Jose Otero Nieves, of Baltimore County, Maryland—96 months’ imprisonment.

Rafael Otero Nieves, of Baltimore County, Maryland—84 months’ imprisonment.

Nigel Criss, of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania—54 months’ imprisonment.

Ian Quintana Torres, of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania—54 months’ imprisonment.

Jesus Terrero, of Baltimore County, Maryland—36 months’ imprisonment.

Tyler Hoagland, of Howard County, Maryland—18 months’ imprisonment.

Shamar Morris, of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania—12 months’ imprisonment.

Raymond Steward, of Camden County, New Jersey—6 months’ imprisonment.

Robert Jones, of Prince George’s County, Maryland—6 months’ imprisonment.

Jumaane Wright, of Montgomery County, Pennsylvania—deceased.

In imposing the sentences, Chief Judge Brann noted the sheer volume of vehicles stolen by Torres and Otero—more than two dozen each—and the leadership roles each defendant played in the wide-ranging, multi-state conspiracy. For Otero, Chief Judge Brann also noted his significant criminal history, which includes a second-degree murder conviction.

The FBI Philadelphia’s Capital Area Resident Agency and Pennsylvania State Police, Central and Eastern Auto Theft Task Forces, investigated the case. Assistant United States Attorney Kyle A. Moreno prosecuted the case.

# # #
title: Final Two Defendants Sentenced in Interstate Auto Theft Conspiracy

text:
Every child is a gift from God, created in His image and likeness, bringing hope, love, and a future filled with promise to our Nation and the world. This Down Syndrome Awareness Month, I join millions of Americans in celebrating the lives, accomplishments, and contributions of people with Down syndrome and honor the families and communities who stand beside them each and every day.
Americans with Down syndrome enrich every life they touch, meeting the world with a sincerity and joy that make our classrooms brighter and our communities stronger. Their condition arises from a single extra chromosome, a small difference that can slow a child’s development and bring challenges to families who love and care for them. In recent decades, our Nation’s doctors and researchers have answered these challenges with remarkable scientific discoveries, and in so doing have greatly enhanced the quality of life for children and adults living with Down syndrome.
As President, I have taken action to protect every innocent life and empower young Americans, including those living with Down syndrome, to lead long, productive, and fulfilling lives. My Administration is leading the charge, advancing the research that delivers new treatments and opening every door for these individuals to pursue their dreams and thrive in their communities. The families, friends, and caregivers who pour their hearts into looking after children with developmental disabilities are some of the most extraordinary, caring, and generous Americans—ensuring the more than 5,000 babies born with Down syndrome every year can live their American Dream just like every other citizen.
My Administration will never waver in our devotion to the men, women, and children living with Down syndrome, and I will always fight to ensure that they, like every other American, can be proud to live in a country with a government and a society that upholds the dignity of every precious life and recognizes the beauty and humanity of every person. This month, and every month, we celebrate, love, and cherish the incredible Americans living with Down syndrome.
title: Presidential Message on Down Syndrome Awareness Month

text:
Black Unemployment Jumped to 7% in September, Up a Full Percentage Point and Nearly Double the 3.6% Rate for White Workers

Pressley Has Consistently Sounded the Alarm on the Pushout of Black Women from the Workforce, Warned of Harm to Economy at Large, and Demanded Federal Action

BOSTON – Today, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), a member of the House Financial Services Committee, condemned the latest jobs report, in which the unemployment rate among Black workers jumped to 7 percent in September, up a full percentage point from August and nearly double the 3.6 percent rate for white workers.

Congresswoman Pressley has consistently sounded the alarm on the pushout of Black women from the workforce, warned of the harm to the American economy at large, and demanded federal action to confront this crisis.

“The state of our economy is failing Black workers, families, and futures — and this is a damning reminder of that,” said Congresswoman Pressley in statement. “We need federal action to address this crisis. Secretary Bessent must release the report on the impact of Black unemployment, and the Federal Reserve must do its job to maximize employment for all.”

Rep. Pressley has repeatedly sounded the alarm on the rising number of Black women forced out of the workforce in the United States, called on the Federal Reserve to take action, and demanded Treasury Secretary Bessent analyze Black unemployment rates and release a report on the impact of Black unemployment on financial stability.

In September 2026, Congresswoman Pressley convened an urgent and timely discussion about the Black unemployment crisis in America and the pushout of Black workers, especially Black women, from the workforce.

In September 2026, Congresswoman Pressley reintroduced her historic resolution calling for a federal job guarantee to help the United States achieve the promise of full employment, establish a more resilient and inclusive economy, and begin to close racial and gender income gaps.

In July 2026, in a House Financial Services Committee hearing, Congresswoman urged Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh to address the alarmingly high Black unemployment rate and uphold the Federal Reserve’s mandate for maximum employment.

In May 2026, Rep. Pressley vehemently opposed Republican legislation that would strip the Federal Reserve’s mandate for maximum employment, emphasizing the Fed’s essential role in ensuring economic health, community well-being, and personal dignity in work especially under Trump’s unemployment crisis. During debate, Rep. Pressley combatted Republicans’ anti-worker legislation through four amendments affirming the importance of the Fed’s mandate for maximum employment.

In March 2026, Reps. Pressley and Summer Lee (PA-12) introduced the Better Labor Statistics Act, or the BLS Act, legislation that would codify the Bureau of Labor Statistics’ mandate to report unemployment data publicly, online, and at the first Friday of each month to ensure transparency and accuracy in unemployment data collection. The BLS Act would also codify the publication of unemployment data broken down by race and ethnicity, gender, geography, and industry.

In December 2025, Rep. Pressley and Congressional Black Caucus Chairwoman Yvette Clarke followed up to Rep. Pressley’s demands and wrote to Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell demanding a briefing for members of the Congressional Black Caucus on how the Federal Reserve is responding to this growing crisis.

In December 2025, Rep. Pressley, along with Co-Chairs of the Congressional Caucus on Black Women & Girls, Congresswomen Yvette D. Clarke (NY-09), Robin Kelly (IL-02), Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12), led 19 of their colleagues demanding the Department of Labor (DOL) take immediate action to address the rising unemployment crisis among Black women that has taken shape since the start of the second Trump Administration.

In November 2025, Rep. Pressley convened Black women, economists, civil rights leaders, and community members for an urgent discussion about the unemployment crisis facing Black women and its impact in Massachusetts and beyond.

In September 2025, Congresswoman Pressley convened a press conference with a coalition of Black women activists and civil rights leaders to continue sounding the alarm on the rising number of Black women forced out of the workforce in the United States.

In September 2025, Congresswoman Pressley wrote to Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell sounding the alarm on the rising unemployment rate for Black women in the United States and demanding the Fed take immediate action to uphold its mandate of maximum employment for all. The Congresswoman’s letter came amid the Trump Administration’s mass federal workforce layoffs and anti-DEI policies disproportionately impacting Black women and as Donald Trump attempted to seize control of the Fed by illegally firing Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook. A copy of the Congresswoman’s letter is available here.

###
title: BREAKING: Pressley Slams Latest Spike in Black Unemployment, Renews Demand for Federal Action

Pensacola, Florida – Shawn Steele, 52, of Pensacola, Florida, was sentenced to two years in federal prison for making false statements to federally insured institutions. This investigation is part of the Trump Administration’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud. The sentence was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida.

U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “Defrauding federally insured financial institutions by lying on loan applications has landed this fraudster in federal prison, and should be a warning to others looking to make a quick buck by ripping off a credit union.”

Between March 7, 2023, and June 30, 2023, the defendant obtained loans from Pen Air Credit Union and Central Credit Union of Florida for a Jeep Wrangler, a Ferrari 488 Pista, and a Cape Horn boat. The defendant submitted false pay stubs and provided false information when applying for the loans with the intent to influence the financial institutions’ loan decisions. Based on these false representations, the defendant was granted loans in the amounts of $98,120.07, $250,000 and $299,243.00.

“This sentence holds Shawn Steele accountable for his actions and the financial harm caused by his conduct,” said FBI Jacksonville Special Agent in Charge Jason Carley. “The FBI will continue to work with our law enforcement partners to investigate financial crimes and ensure those who commit fraud are held accountable.”

The sentence was the result of an investigation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Jeffrey M. Tharp.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl .

text:
Kimberly Cardella, 59, of Rensselaer, NY was arraigned September 18, 2026, in Albany, NY before U.S. Magistrate Daniel J. Stewart on multiple counts including bank fraud, theft of government property and aggravated identity theft. A federal grand jury indicted Cardella on September 3, 2026. The charges arise from a joint investigation involving the Social Security Administration’s Office of the Inspector General and the New York State Comptroller’s Office. According to the indictment, Cardella’s mother-in-law was a Social Security beneficiary and a NYS pensioner who passed away in 2009. Because neither the Social Security Administration nor the New York State and Local Retirement System had been made aware of the death, both agencies continued to fund the dead mother-in-law’s checking account. Cardella wrote checks for her personal use against that account, signing the checks in her mother-in-law’s name for nearly 17 years after the death. This caused a loss of more than $530,000.00 to the Social Security program and more than $138,000.00 to the NYS pension fund. This action is part of an ongoing effort of the Trump Administration’s Fraud Task Force aimed at eliminating fraud across the country.

First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III, Amy Connelly, Special Agent in Charge, Boston/New York Field Division, Social Security Administration Office of the Inspector General (SSA-OIG), and New York State Comptroller Thomas P. DiNapoli made the announcement.

First Assistant United States Attorney John Sarcone stated, “The fact that this defendant openly signed her own dead mother-in-law’s name on checks that did not belong to her, in effect adopting her mother-in-law’s identity to obtain public funds intended for those in genuine need, as alleged, is simply shocking. The fact that she continued this scheme for nearly seventeen years underscores the need for continued robust oversight and enforcement in our public benefits programs. Hat’s off to the SSA-OIG and the New York State Comptroller’s investigators who jointly investigated this case. My office stands ready to enforce laws against self-interested fraudsters like this who shamelessly convert public funds away from programs for the elderly and those who are truly in need.”

“Diverting more than half a million dollars in Social Security benefits is an egregious crime that directly harms the beneficiaries these programs are meant to support,” said Amy Connelly, Special Agent in Charge, Social Security Administration Office of the Inspector General, Boston–New York–Philadelphia Field Division. “Working alongside the U.S. Attorney’s Office and the New York State Comptroller’s Office, we will continue to pursue those who exploit federal and state benefit programs and ensure these vital funds remain protected for the individuals they are intended to serve.”

New York State Comptroller Thomas P. DiNapoli stated "Kimberly Cardella allegedly scammed the state and federal governments out of nearly $670,000 over a 17-year period by taking money meant for her deceased mother-in-law. Thanks to the work of my investigators and partners in the federal government, her brazen fraud has been exposed, and she will be held accountable."

The charges filed against Cardella carry a maximum sentence of 30 years in prison and a $1 million fine for bank fraud, 10 years for theft of government property, and a mandatory 2 years for aggravated identity theft; with additional fines of up to $250,000, and a term of supervised release of up to 5 years. Cardella may also be ordered to pay restitution to the United States of America and to New York State. In addition, the government is seeking forfeiture of $530,735.00 lost to fraud in this case. A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the statutes the defendant is convicted of violating, U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other factors. The charges in the indictment are merely accusations. The defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.

SSA-OIG and the NYS Comptroller’s Office are investigating the case. Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Arne Soldwedel is prosecuting the case.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Rensselaer Woman Indicted in $668,884 Social Security and NYS Pension Fraud Scheme

Krishnamoorthi and Menendez Demand Updated Federal Safety Guidance on Energy Drinks as Youth Consumption Surges
Lawmakers press HHS for updated research and guidance as nearly one in four high school seniors reports daily energy drink use
WASHINGTON — Congressmen Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) and Rob Menendez (D-NJ) today sent a letter to U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. calling on HHS to update federal research and guidance on high-caffeine energy drinks and conduct a comprehensive assessment of their consumption and health effects among school-aged children.
“Energy drink use among kids is at record levels, while caffeine-related emergency room visits among middle and high school students have roughly doubled,” said Congressman Krishnamoorthi. “These products can pose serious health risks to children, yet the federal government is still relying on outdated research and guidance. Our government needs to catch up and give parents, schools, and health care providers the information they need to keep kids safe.”
“Kids are consuming more caffeine than ever, and Sarah Katz’s tragic death exposed how dangerous poor labeling and hidden caffeine levels can be,” said Congressman Menendez. “We are calling on HHS to update federal caffeine guidelines, protect our children, and ensure parents and teachers have the information they need to keep children safe.”
Energy drink consumption among students is at or near record levels, with nearly one in four high school seniors now drinking energy drinks daily, up from about one in six four years ago. Many popular energy drinks contain as much as 200 milligrams of caffeine per serving, while the American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that adolescents ages 12 to 18 consume less than 100 milligrams of caffeine per day. The lawmakers also noted that emergency department visits by middle and high school students for adverse effects associated with caffeine roughly doubled between 2017 and 2023.
Despite that increase, much of the federal government’s research and guidance on energy drinks is more than a decade old. Current CDC guidance still relies in part on a 2013 SAMHSA report examining emergency department visits through 2011, while federal researchers have acknowledged significant gaps in research on how energy drinks affect children.
“Despite these risks, much of the federal government's research and guidance on energy drinks is more than a decade old,” Krishnamoorthi and Menendez wrote. “While caffeine-related emergency visits among middle and high school students doubled, federal guidance continues to rely on decades-old data that do not reflect today’s levels of consumption.”
The lawmakers also raised concerns about the lack of federal regulation specific to energy drinks. Federal law does not require these products to disclose how much caffeine they contain, and FDA guidance on energy drinks dates to 2014, is nonbinding, and sets no recommended caffeine limit for children or adolescents.
“Rising consumption, a rapidly expanding market, and outdated federal research and guidance specific to energy drinks raise serious questions about whether HHS has the information it needs to guide schools, parents, and health care providers,” Krishnamoorthi and Menendez wrote. “We strongly urge HHS and its agencies to update the federal government’s research on these products and provide clear guidance to protect children.”
Krishnamoorthi and Menendez requested that HHS, in coordination with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Food and Drug Administration, National Institutes of Health, and Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration, conduct a comprehensive assessment of energy drink consumption and its health effects among school-aged children and provide answers to the following questions:
- What research is HHS currently conducting or funding on energy drink consumption and its health effects among school-aged children, including interactions between energy drinks and prescribed stimulant medications?
- When will SAMHSA or another HHS component update its 2013 analysis with national estimates of energy drink-related emergency department visits, hospitalizations, and deaths among minors?
- Does FDA intend to evaluate or establish recommended limits on caffeine intake for children and adolescents? FDA has listed draft guidance on labeling caffeine content as a 2026 priority. When will that guidance be issued, will it recommend that manufacturers disclose caffeine content in milligrams, and does FDA intend to pursue binding labeling requirements?
- How is HHS tracking adverse events involving children and energy drinks, including cardiac events, reports submitted to FDA, and poison center data? What trends has the Department identified since 2020?
- Has HHS engaged with USDA on revisiting federal school nutrition standards that permit caffeinated beverages in high schools, given USDA’s 2016 commitment to continue monitoring FDA’s work on caffeine?
The lawmakers requested responses and the results of the assessment by October 14, 2026, and called on HHS to make the assessment publicly available so parents, schools, and health care providers can understand the risks these products pose and the steps being taken to address them.
The full letter is available here.
title: Krishnamoorthi and Menendez Demand Updated Federal Safety Guidance on Energy Drinks as Youth Consumption Surges

WASHINGTON, DC – Congresswoman Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09) praised the U.S. Senate approval of the Dennis John Benigno Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) Program Reauthorization Act, legislation to renew the federal government’s public health programs related to TBIs, including the national TBI surveillance program which is being named in honor of former New Jersey Congressman Bill Pascrell, Jr.

“Congressman Bill Pascrell spent decades fighting for Americans living with traumatic brain injuries and pushing our country to take this epidemic seriously,” said Congresswoman Pou. “But one major impetus for Bill taking on this fight was his close work with the Benigno family of Clifton who raised the profile of TBIs after a severe brain injury DJ suffered. Thank you to Senator Kim for advancing this legislation out of the Senate and making sure the bill honors both the legacies of Congressman Pascrell and Dennis John Benigno. We must get a TBI renewal across the finish line this year to continue the critical work to support survivors, expand research, and improve care for families across our country.”

In the Senate, this legislation was led by Sen. Andy Kim (D-NJ) and passed unanimously. In July 2026, the House advanced a similar measure authored by Congressman Frank Pallone (D-NJ-06) also naming the surveillance program for Congressman Pascrell.

“It was an honor to lead the Senate’s TBI reauthorization efforts to ensure these lifesaving programs continue as they have done since 1996, carrying forward Bill’s legacy of caring for those impacted by TBI’s in the process. I'm grateful my Senate colleagues came together in a bipartisan way to move this legislation forward, and hope to see it cross the finish line soon," said Senator Kim.

The namesake of the Senate-passed legislation stems from lifelong Clifton resident Dennis John “DJ” Benigno who passed away in January 2024. Benigno’s life was forever altered after being struck by a car at just fifteen, leaving him with a devastating brain injury that left him totally disabled.

“I am proud to see Dennis John’s legacy – bringing greater attention and resources to addressing the devastating consequences of traumatic brain injury – live on through this Senate-passed bill,” said DJ’s father, Dennis, who together with DJ’s mother, Rosalind, founded the Coalition for Brain Injury Research. “Our family knows firsthand how profoundly a traumatic brain injury can change a life and affect an entire family. It is our hope that continued federal focus and research on traumatic brain injuries (TBIs) will lead to meaningful advances in treatment and recovery, while bringing hope and aid to the many survivors and families affected by the devastating consequences of these injuries. We are deeply grateful for the work of the late Congressman Bill Pascrell and Senator Andy Kim, and for the continued advocacy of Congresswoman Nellie Pou.”

The Congressional Brain Injury Task Force, established in 2001, was created by Congressman Pascrell to confront TBI and the impact it has on the inflicted, their families, and their loved ones. Millions of veterans, accident victims, athletes and others have benefitted from the policies the task force has helped advance over the years.
title: Honoring Clifton’s Dennis John Benigno; The Fight for Traumatic Brain Injury Victims Lives On

Moulton Applauds Restoration of 988 “Press 3” Option for LGBTQIA+ Youth After Months of Pressure on Trump Administration
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Following the months of pressure on the Trump Administration, led by Congressman Seth Moulton (MA-06), the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline resumed its LGBTQIA+ Youth Specialized Services, known as the “Press 3” option, this week.
“Restoring the Press 3 option is long overdue, but I’m glad to see the Trump Administration finally heed our calls to bring back this critical affirming care for LGBTQIA+ youth,” said Congressman Moulton. “Congress provided the funding and the direction to keep this lifeline open long ago, and it’s disappointing that there was any lapse in service for the Press 3 option. I’ll keep working alongside my colleagues to make sure Press 3 is available to every young person who needs it.”
The Press 3 option launched nationally in 2022 and handled roughly 1.6 million contacts before the Trump Administration shut it down in July 2025. Congressman Moulton and a bipartisan group of colleagues sent a letter in February 2026 to Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and the Department of Health and Human Services demanding the immediate restoration of the Press 3 option.
On July 15, 2026, Congressman Moulton and several other colleagues held a press conference on Capitol Hill to renew the call for the Press 3 option to be restored. This followed the inclusion of $33.1 million in the FY2026 Appropriations law, along with a funding directive, requiring HHS to fund the line.
LGBTQIA+ youth face higher rates of serious depression and suicidal thoughts than their peers, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Congressman Moulton has emphasized that specialized crisis services like the Press 3 option are a proven way to reach young people at their most vulnerable moments.
If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988, or chat at 988lifeline.org.
###
title: Moulton Applauds Restoration of 988 “Press 3” Option for LGBTQIA+ Youth After Months of Pressure on Trump Administration

BOSTON – A Lynn man has been arrested and charged with allegedly receiving child sexual abuse material (CSAM).

Zachary Brodeur, 37, was charged by criminal complaint with one count of receipt of child pornography. Following an initial appearance in federal court in Boston on Sept. 29, 2026, the defendant remains detained in state custody on related charges.

According to the charging documents, Brodeur was identified in an online chatroom in which he engaged with a law enforcement agent posing as a 14-year-old boy.

It is alleged that during a subsequent search of Brodeur’s cell phone, approximately 138 videos depicting CSAM were located in the phone’s downloads folder. It is further alleged that the videos depicted minors between the ages of five and 11 years old. Brodeur was convicted as a Youthful Offender for rape of a child and possession of child pornography in Massachusetts state courts.

The charge of receipt of child pornography provides for a sentence of at least 15 years and up to 40 years in prison, at least five years and up to a lifetime of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Ted E. Docks, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Boston Division made the announcement. Valuable assistance was provided by the Lynn Police Department and the Scituate Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Catherine Conroy of the Major Crimes Unit is prosecuting the case.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse, launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the DOJ’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children, as well as identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc .

The details contained in the charging document are allegations. The defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in the court of law.
title: Lynn Man Arrested and Charged for Receipt of Child Pornography

Rep. Craig Secures Nearly $2.3 Million in Federal Funding for Rosemount Fire Department to Hire Additional Firefighters
The Lakeville, Shakopee and Woodbury Fire Departments also received federal grants
EAGAN, MN – Today, U.S. Representative Angie Craig announced that her office secured $2,290,047 in federal funding for the Rosemount Fire Department.
The funding, which came through the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s (FEMA) Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) grant program will be used to hire nine additional firefighters as the city continues to grow, ensuring that the department can have at least 24 firefighters on duty at all hours. Rep. Craig wrote a letter of support on behalf of the Rosemount Fire Department in June.
“I am excited to announce that the Rosemount Fire Department will receive critical federal funding to hire more firefighters and ensure the department has adequate staff as Rosemount continues to grow,” said Rep. Craig. “Every day, our firefighters run into danger to save lives, and I couldn’t be prouder to have helped secure this funding that will keep our firefighters and our communities safe.”
This week, FEMA also announced it has awarded grants to three additional fire departments in MN-02. The Lakeville Fire Department will receive $1,315,103 through the SAFER grant program. The Shakopee Fire Department will receive $81,818 and the Woodbury Fire Department will receive $55,680 through the Assistance to Firefighters (AFG) grant program.

title: Rep. Craig Secures Nearly $2.3 Million in Federal Funding for Rosemount Fire Department to Hire Additional Firefighters

BOSTON – A former Immigration Services Officer pleaded guilty yesterday in federal court in Boston to stealing more than $60,000 from a labor union over the course of five years.

Carol A. Aguja, 55, of Reading, Mass., pleaded guilty to wire fraud. U.S. Senior District Court Judge Nathaniel M. Gorton scheduled sentencing for Jan. 7, 2027. Aguja was charged in August 2026 .

Aguja was an Immigration Services Officer employed by the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS). Between approximately 2015 and August 2024, Aguja also served as Treasurer of the American Federation of Government Employees Local 38 (AFGE Local 38), a labor organization that represented USCIS employees who lived in Massachusetts, Rhode Island and New Hampshire.

Between 2019 and 2024, Aguja defrauded AFGE Local 38 by siphoning funds from the union bank account to pay for her own personal and non-union related expenses. As part of her fraud scheme, Aguja also paid union expenses out of her personal accounts and commingled union and personal funds to conceal her embezzlement. Specifically, Aguja used the AFGE Local 38 credit card to pay approximately $12,508 for personal expenses such as restaurant meals, bills, clothing and dance lessons. She also made 128 cash withdrawals totaling over $23,700 from the AFGE Local 38 account, and transferred over $25,000 from the AFGE Local 38 account to her personal accounts. Aguja falsified annual forms regarding the union finances that AFGE Local 38 was required to submit to the United States Department of Labor-Management Standards, in order to conceal her fraud.

The charge of wire fraud provides for a sentence of up to 20 years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of $250,000 or twice the gross gain or loss, whichever is greater, restitution, and forfeiture. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Jonathan Russo, District Director, U.S. Department of Labor, Office of Labor-Management Standards; and Inspector General Joseph V. Cuffari, Ph.D., U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Office of Inspector General made the announcement. Assistant U.S. Attorney Kristina E. Barclay of the Public Corruption & Special Prosecutions Unit is prosecuting the case.
title: Former Immigration Services Officer Pleads Guilty to Defrauding Union

Scott Statement on September Jobs Report
WASHINGTON – Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03), House Committee on Education and Workforce, released the following statement after the Bureau of Labor Statistics announced that the economy gained 29,000 jobs in September, and the unemployment rate increased from 4.1 percent to 4.2 percent.
“This Trump economy might be working for the wealthy and the well connected, but it clearly is leaving workers behind. CEO pay is skyrocketing, while for working people, it's a daily struggle just to cover groceries and rent. Workers’ wages are failing tokeep up with inflation, and the increasing cost of daily expenses are eating into workers’ paychecks. According to the Century Foundation, inflation-adjusted debt payments grew faster than income in recent years as working families have struggled to make ends meet.
“The jobs numbers show the same strain: Trump has added only 776,000 jobs between January 2025 and September 2026, while the Biden administration added 10.7 million within its first 20 months. Since President Trump returned to office, not one month has reached the average monthly job creation under the Biden administration. In fact, he has not even achieved 70 percent of Biden’s monthly average.
“And now, as a result of the ‘Big Ugly Bill’s’ cuts to the SNAP program, families are losing their food assistance. An estimated 4.5 million people have lost their SNAP benefits, including more than 1.5 million children. Across the country, people are feeling the impact. In North Carolina, demand at food pantries and food banks is up 20 percent this year, as SNAP enrollment has plummeted by more than 110,000 people since September 2025. In Kansas, one pantry reports distributing 50 percent more food than a year ago. In Oregon, pantry directors say they have gone from being a supplemental resource to the primary source of food, and many incoming families have never had to ask for help before. This is what happens when tax breaks for the wealthy are paid for by taking food off the tables of working families.
“That's why I, alongside my Democratic colleagues, am fighting to put working families first. Children cannot learn on an empty stomach, and parents cannot build a better life when they cannot afford groceries. We will keep pushing to protect school meals, strengthen job training, lower the cost of college, and make sure every worker can earn a living wage and retire with dignity.”

FLINT— Congresswoman Kristen McDonald Rivet (MI-08) and the mid-Michigan community have secured a commitment from the United States Coast Guard that the Saginaw River station will be returning to full staffing and capacity in 2027. The announcement follows more than a year of Congresswoman McDonald Rivet’s advocacy for a return to full operations.

“The Saginaw Coast Guard station getting its full funding is a big deal for mid-Michigan. It means stronger search-and-rescue operations, significantly shorter response times on the Saginaw Bay and Saginaw River, and less strain on local law enforcement so they can fully focus their efforts on the ground,” said Congresswoman Kristen McDonald Rivet. “This is what happens when everyday people use their voices, and I am deeply grateful to the hundreds of Michiganders and community leaders who joined together to make this happen.”

For over a year, Congresswoman McDonald Rivet has pushed the U.S. Coast Guard to restore full coverage at the station:

In July 2025, Congresswoman McDonald Rivet authored a provision requiring the Coast Guard to study the impact of reduced search-and-rescue operations at the Saginaw River station following the elimination of 24/7 operations in 2024.

In December 2025, the Congresswoman got that provision signed into law.

Also in July 2025, the Congresswoman advocated for restoring 24/7 coverage in a Transportation and Infrastructure Committee markup of the Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025.

In March 2026, at a Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee hearing with USCG Vice Commandant Admiral Thomas Allan Jr., Congresswoman McDonald Rivet emphasized how local first responders have had to make up for the Coast Guard’s cuts to search-and-rescue coverage.

In June 2026, Congresswoman McDonald Rivet again urged the Commandant of the United States Coast Guard to immediately restore a fully operational and fully staffed Saginaw River Station.

Later in June 2026, at a Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee hearing, the Congresswoman highlighted the consequences of short staffing to USCG Vice Admiral Douglas M. Schofield.
title: Rep. McDonald Rivet, Mid-Michigan Secure Return of Full Service to Saginaw River Coast Guard Station

NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA – BRYAN ROGERS (“ROGERS”) , age 21, of New Orleans, was sentenced on September 30, 2026, by United States District Judge Greg G. Guidry, after previously pleading guilty to being a felon in possession of a firearm, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Sections 922(g)(1) and 924(a)(8), announced United States Attorney David I. Courcelle.

ROGERS was sentenced to 36 months in prison, followed by three years of supervised release, along with payment of a $100 mandatory special assessment fee.

According to court documents, on May 18, 2025, Jefferson Parish Sheriff’s Office (“JPSO”) deputies encountered ROGERS during a traffic stop in Marrero, Louisiana. During the course of this traffic stop, law enforcement located a Glock Model 30 Gen4, .45 caliber semi-automatic pistol loaded with an extended magazine containing 20 rounds of ammunition under the front passenger seat of the vehicle ROGERS was operating at the time. The recovered firearm was previously reported as stolen to the New Orleans Police Department, according to court records. Through their investigation, law enforcement developed evidence establishing that ROGERS possessed the recovered firearm before JPSO initiated the traffic stop. ROGERS is a convicted felon and therefore federally prohibited from possessing firearms.

U.S. Attorney Courcelle praised the work of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives and the Jefferson Parish Sheriff’s Office in investigating this matter. Assistant United States Attorney Shannon Kippers of the General Crimes Unit is in charge of the prosecution.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities.

WASHINGTON—Representatives Lauren Underwood, Jen Kiggans (VA-02), and Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), introduced the Educating Future Nurses Act to expand clinical education and training opportunities for future Advanced Practice Registered Nurses (APRNs). As costs explode and our health care system confronts the historic crisis caused by Republicans’ Big Ugly Bill, fixing gaps in nursing education is critical to keeping health care affordable and accessible.

Underwood’s legislation would create permanent federal funding for hospitals to partner with schools of nursing and community-based care settings to address clinical training costs for graduate nursing students.

“In every corner of our country, nurses are doing critical work to support the health and well-being of our communities. We’re providing excellent clinical care, conducting important research, and carrying out the public health initiatives that keep our families safe and healthy,” said Rep. Underwood. “But our profession is under unprecedented attack, particularly for nurses who are looking to further their education. America needs more nurses, not fewer. Our legislation will strengthen graduate-level nursing education and make sure these dedicated professionals get more support for this vitally important training.”

“As a geriatric nurse practitioner and Congressional Nursing Caucus co-chair, I know that a strong nursing workforce starts with ensuring our future nurses have the training and resources they need to effectively care for their patients. Unfortunately, there are too many aspiring advanced practice nurses who face barriers from accessing the education required to complete their training. I’m proud to join my caucus co-chair, Congresswoman Underwood, to introduce the Educating Future Nurses Act to strengthen partnerships between our hospitals, nursing schools, and communities and expand clinical training opportunities for the next generation of nurses.” Said Rep. Kiggans.

"Health care costs are rising and more people are reliant on hospitals and emergency care,” said Rep. Bonamici."Our country is in desperate need of more nurses, including advanced practice nurses, but there are too many barriers to graduate education. As Co-Chair of the Congressional Nursing Caucus, I stand firmly behind the Educating Future Nurses Act and the opportunities it would create for nurses to advance in their careers and bolster the health care workforce."

“The Educating Future Nurses Act is an important step toward addressing our nation’s ongoing nursing shortage and ensuring that all Americans have access to high-quality healthcare,” said Dr. Julie Sanford, Chair of the Board of Directors of the American Association and Colleges of Nursing. “Enabling partnerships between hospitals and nursing schools is an innovative approach to expanding the nursing workforce."

“We applaud Congresswoman Underwood and our congressional champions for their continued support of nursing education,” said Dr. Deborah Trautman, President and Chief Executive Officer of the American Association of Colleges of Nursing. “By building on the success of the Graduate Nurse Education demonstration program, the Educating Future Nurses Act will have a profound impact on sustaining the nation’s Advanced Practice Registered Nursing workforce and access to care for all patients in need.”

The cost of clinical training has limited the number of APRN students that hospitals can accept. Funding from the Educating Future Nurses Act would help these hospitals accept APRN students, enabling them to train and work in geographically diverse areas, especially rural and underserved communities.

The legislation builds on a similar program created under the Affordable Care Act (ACA). The ACA’s Graduate Nurse Education Demonstration Program provided federal funding to hospitals to pay for the clinical training costs of APRNs.

The Educating Future Nurses Act has been endorsed by 30+ leading nursing organizations in Illinois and across the country, including the American Association of Colleges of Nursing and the American Association of Nurse Anesthesiology.

###
title: Underwood Introduces Bipartisan Legislation to Train More Nurses

Apprehended Venezuelan Tren de Aragua Leader on FBI’s 10 Most Wanted Fugitives List Appears in Nebraska Court Following Homeland Security Task Force Investigation
The Justice Department announced the apprehension of Anibal Alexander Canelon Aguirre also known as “Prometheus” and “The Engineer,” 50, of Venezuela. Anibal Alexander Canelon Aguirre was added to the FBI’s “Top 10 Most Wanted Fugitives” list in March of 2026. Canelon Aguirre was the first cyber criminal and the 540th individual to be added to the Top 10 Most Wanted Fugitives list.
“Since President Trump designated Tren de Aragua a foreign terrorist organization, the Department of Justice has charged nearly 350 of its members and associates with brutal violent crimes,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “The capture and arrest of Anibal Alexander Canelon Aguirre marks yet another success for the Homeland Security Task Force and Joint Task Force Vulcan. We will continue to break up narcoterrorist finance networks, prosecute violent criminals, and keep American neighborhoods safe.”
“Anibal Canelon Aguirre served as a key architect of sophisticated malware used to drain ATMs of cash across the United States — technology that helped fuel the criminal operations of the violent transnational organization Tren de Aragua (TdA),” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “His apprehension sends a clear message: the Criminal Division and our partners will pursue those who attack our financial institutions to support foreign terrorist organizations, wherever they reside across the world.”
“Anibal Alexander Canelon Aguirre is the 10th member of the Ten Most Wanted Fugitives List captured by this FBI since the beginning of the Trump administration – more than 2.5 times the total captured during the previous four years combined, and the first ever Cyber fugitive,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “Now Aguirre is back in the United States to face justice, thanks to brilliant work from the FBI’s Cyber Division and Critical Incident Response Group. This fugitive’s return to the United States is the latest in the FBI’s record success manhunting fugitives across the globe, with 107 foreign transfers of custody from 43 countries the last 18 months – an over 90% increase – showing this FBI is using super charged horsepower to chase down violent criminals no matter where they try to hide.”
“There is nowhere that a terrorist indicted in the District of Nebraska can safely hide from justice,” said U.S. Attorney Lesley A. Woods for the District of Nebraska. “We will never stop pursuing those who do harm to the United States for the financial benefit of criminal organizations that are in the full-time business of torture, murder, and trafficking human beings.”
“This case underscores the serious and evolving threat posed by transnational criminal organizations that use sophisticated financial and cyber-enabled schemes to fund violence and destabilize communities,” said Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Acting Executive Associate Director John A. Condon. “Canelon Aguirre is alleged to have developed technology that enabled criminals to target American financial institutions and generate illicit proceeds for a violent transnational organization. Through the Homeland Security Task Force, HSI and our federal, state, local, and international partners are combining capabilities to pursue the networks, facilitators, and leaders behind these crimes. No border, false identity, or digital disguise will shield those who threaten the safety and security of the American people.”
Canelon Aguirre was indicted by a federal grand jury in the District of Nebraska in December 2025, and is charged with the following counts:
Canelon Aguirre made his initial appearance on Oct. 2 before U.S. Magistrate Judge Michael D. Nelson and entered not guilty pleas to the counts charged. He will remain detained in the District of Nebraska while pending trial. Chief U.S. District Court Judge Brian C. Buescher and U.S. Magistrate Judge Ryan C. Carson are presiding over Canelon Aguirre’s case.
An ATM jackpotting attack is a type of cyberattack where criminals exploit vulnerabilities in an ATM by using malware to force the ATMs to dispense cash without debiting an account. Malware is an abbreviated term for “malicious software” and refers to software programs designed to damage or do other unwanted actions on a computer system. “Ploutus” is a specific type of malware designed to be used in ATM jackpotting to force an ATM to dispense cash.
Canelon Aguirre is alleged to be the developer of the Ploutus malware and one of the principal leaders of ATM jackpotting conspiracy. Ploutus malware consisted of, among other things, files that contained anti-analysis measures to hinder forensic review, specifically software protection utilities to prevent reverse-engineering and debugging. The malware also contained other files that served the function of deleting the malware from the system in an effort to conceal, create a false impression, mislead, or otherwise deceive employees of the financial institution from learning about the deployment of the malware on the ATM.
Canelon Aguirre’s indictment is part of a coordinated investigation and prosecution by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Nebraska in conjunction with the Department of Justice’s Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section (CCIPS) of the Department’s Criminal Division and Joint Task Force Vulcan along with the lead investigative agencies the FBI and HSI. This investigation and prosecution are focused on a widespread ATM Jackpotting conspiracy that has been tied to the designated foreign terrorist organization TdA. To date, 120 defendants have been charged in the District of Nebraska for their role in this conspiracy. Three of these defendants have been sentenced in the District of Nebraska:
The investigation has established extensive direct and indirect links between the indicted co-conspirators and TdA. According to court documents, TdA is a violent transnational criminal organization that originated as a prison gang in Venezuela in the mid-2000s. TdA has expanded its criminal network throughout the Western Hemisphere and established a presence in the United States. TdA’s criminal activities range from drug trafficking and firearms trafficking to commercial sex trafficking, kidnapping, robbery, theft, fraud, and extortion. TdA members also commit murder, assault, and other violent acts to advance the organization’s criminal activities. TdA has also developed an additional source of revenue stream through financial crimes that target financial institutions throughout the United States, including using ATM jackpotting to steal millions of dollars in cash. The investigation has revealed that the conspiracy has targeted or carried out ATM jackpotting attacks in 47 states, the District of Columbia, and several foreign nations.
On Sept. 30, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned Canelon Aguirre.
The Justice Department’s Judicial Attaché in Bogotá and Office of International Affairs, along with the U.S. Secret Service, have provided significant assistance in this matter.
This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Omaha comprises agents and officers from HSI, FBI, Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), U.S. Marshals Service (USMS), U.S. Postal Inspection Service (USPIS), and the IRS Criminal Investigation.
Joint Task Force Vulcan (JTFV) was created in 2019 to eradicate MS-13 and has now expanded to target TdA. JTFV is comprised of U.S. Attorney’s Offices across the country, including Southern and Eastern Districts of New York; Eastern and Western Districts of North Carolina; Western District of Virginia; Middle and Southern Districts of Florida; Eastern District of Texas; Western District of Oklahoma; Northern District of Indiana; District of Nevada; and the District of Arizona, as well as the Executive Office for U.S. Attorneys, and the Department of Justice’s National Security Division, Criminal Division, and the Office of Judicial Attaché and DEA partners in Bogotá, Colombia. Additionally, the FBI, HSI, ATF, USMS, and the Federal Bureau of Prisons are essential law enforcement partners with JTFV.
CCIPS investigates and prosecutes cybercrime and intellectual property (IP) crime in coordination with domestic and international law enforcement agencies, often with assistance from the private sector. Since 2020, CCIPS has secured the conviction of over 180 cyber and IP criminals, and court orders for the return of over $350 million in victim funds.
An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

ALBUQUERQUE – The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Mexico joins the Department of Justice, the Office on Violence Against Women and communities across New Mexico in recognizing October as Domestic Violence Awareness Month and reaffirming its commitment to protecting victims, holding offenders accountable and supporting the organizations that serve survivors.

“Protecting victims of domestic violence takes coordinated work from law enforcement, prosecutors, advocates and service providers.,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison. “These grants strengthen that work across New Mexico, and our office will continue doing its part to protect victims and pursue offenders under federal law.”

“Protecting victims of domestic violence takes coordinated work from law enforcement, prosecutors, advocates and service providers.,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison. “These grants strengthen that work across New Mexico, and our office will continue doing its part to protect victims and pursue offenders under federal law.”

As part of that effort, the Department of Justice recently awarded $106,581 to the New Mexico Coalition Against Domestic Violence and $236,484 to the New Mexico Coalition of Sexual Assault Programs, Inc. The two organizations are New Mexico’s designated statewide domestic violence and sexual assault coalitions.

“Domestic violence has a devastating impact that reaches far beyond an individual survivor—it affects children, families, communities, and generations,” said MaryEllen Garcia, CEO of New Mexico Coalition Against Domestic Violence. “During Domestic Violence Awareness Month, we honor the courage of survivors while also recognizing the extraordinary work happening every day across New Mexico. The New Mexico Coalition Against Domestic Violence is proud to stand alongside our statewide network of domestic violence providers, whose advocates show up every day with compassion, skill, and an unwavering commitment to survivor safety, dignity, and choice. Ending domestic violence requires all of us—advocates, law enforcement, prosecutors, courts, community partners, and neighbors—working together to build communities where survivors are supported, people who cause harm are held accountable, and everyone has the opportunity to live free from violence.”

It also highlights the role friends, relatives, coworkers and neighbors can play in recognizing abuse and helping victims connect with available resources.

The U.S. Attorney’s Office works with federal, Tribal, state and local law enforcement and prosecutors to enforce federal laws applicable to domestic violence, including federal firearms laws intended to keep firearms out of the hands of certain individuals prohibited from possessing them because of domestic violence convictions or qualifying protection orders.

The Department of Justice also supports victim services through grant programs administered by the Office on Violence Against Women and the Office for Victims of Crime. OVW identifies the New Mexico Coalition Against Domestic Violence and the New Mexico Coalition of Sexual Assault Programs, Inc. as the state’s designated domestic violence and sexual assault coalitions for fiscal year 2026.

In communities across our great Nation, domestic violence destroys families, harms innocent children, and leaves lasting pain in our neighborhoods. For America to be strong, children must feel safe in their homes, spouses and significant others must be respected, and it must be a universal truth that violence in any form is unacceptable. This National Domestic Violence Awareness Month, my Administration reaffirms its commitment to permanently ending domestic violence and ensuring every American can live free from the threat of violence.
For as many as 10 million Americans, the unrelenting fear of violence in our homes, places of work, and other social settings make it impossible to enjoy life and foster healthy relationships. Behind every one of these numbers is a fellow American robbed of the safety and peace that our Nation promises to all its people. As President, I will always uplift survivors of domestic violence and make certain that shelters, counselors, advocates, and hotlines have the resources they need to answer each and every call for help. Help is always within reach, and you are never alone. If you are in need of immediate and confidential support, call the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233.
This month, we commit that for our mothers, our fathers, our daughters, and our sons, we will end the scourge of domestic violence. My Administration remains steadfast in safeguarding the safety and security of the American People, giving law enforcement the tools and resources they need to prevent domestic violence, and ensuring that those who commit acts of violence are held accountable. Together, we will protect the innocent, defend the vulnerable, and build a safer and stronger America.

As temperatures begin to drop and fuel prices remain high due to the Iran War, Congressman Ryan is demanding that the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) distribute critical home energy funds without delay

Ryan co-sponsors the “Heating and Cooling Relief Act,” which would expand eligibility for LIHEAP and lower home energy costs for millions more households nationwide

Heating oil prices in New York state are up more than 70% from this time last year, with prices in the Hudson Valley averaging $6.22/ gallon

WASHINGTON, DC – As home heating oil prices continue to rise, Congressman Pat Ryan joined a bipartisan group of 116 members in calling on the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to take all necessary steps to ensure that the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) funds are distributed to the states as soon as possible and no later than November 1, 2026. Heating oil prices in New York state are up more than 70% from this time last year, with prices in the Hudson Valley averaging $6.22/ gallon.

Ryan is also a co-sponsor of the Heating and Cooling Relief Act, legislation to modernize LIHEAP, increase investments, and dramatically expand eligibility so that households earning up to 250 percent of the Federal Poverty Line or 80 percent of State Median Income can qualify to apply for assistance.

“With a history of repeated funding delays by HHS to states, we are especially concerned for households facing high energy prices this winter who rely on LIHEAP... It is of the utmost importance that the agency ensures funds are released as soon as possible and without congressional intervention throughout Fiscal Year 2027,” wrote the lawmakers.

“Since February, crude oil prices have significantly increased, topping significantly more than $100 per barrel at its peaks in April 2026 and recently on September 15, 2026. These price spikes impact home heating oil prices especially, as it is refined from crude oil,” they stated.

Emphasizing the importance of the speedy delivery of funds for families who rely on home heating oil, they continued, “Home heating oil will not be delivered without payment in full, up front, which can average $2,300 for just the winter season. For the many families that cannot afford these high costs, LIHEAP is a lifeline. If households don’t receive these funds on schedule, families will go without heat or be forced to make remarkably difficult decisions in order to afford it.”

LIHEAP helps low-income individuals and families pay for heating and cooling and mitigates the impacts of rising energy costs and extreme weather events. Across the nation, LIHEAP helps nearly 6 million households afford their energy bills, including nearly 30,000 in NY-18, but Secretary Kennedy’s decision last year to fire all LIHEAP staff last year has put this assistance at risk. Ryan has previously blasted the Trump Administration for threatening to eliminate federal funding for LIHEAP.

“Throughout the summer, families have struggled to fill up their gas tank because Trump’s war in Iran has sent gas prices skyrocketing. But it’s not just gas – it’s home heating oil too. As we head into fall and temperatures drop, Hudson Valley families are about to face higher heating bills on top of everything else. Thousands of families in our community rely on the LIHEAP program to keep their homes warm. The last thing these folks should be worrying about is whether they’ll get the support they’re counting on,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “We’ve seen this Administration’s attempts to cut LIHEAP before, and I refuse to allow any delays to leave Hudson Valley families out in the cold this winter. We’re making sure these funds get distributed to the New Yorkers who need them.”

Underscoring the continued concerns about LIHEAP’s capacity to operate without dedicated staff, the lawmakers wrote, “We urge you to ensure that necessary personnel and resources are in place to support LIHEAP's continued success and request a detailed response on staffing levels supporting the LIHEAP program, including but not limited to how many staff members work on the program full time and part time, as well as projected vacancies that must be filled to ensure continued success.”

“Once again we urge you to do everything possible to distribute LIHEAP funds to states and families expeditiously. Families should not have to choose between staying warm and affording other essential items like food, medication, or rent. We appreciate your attention on this urgent matter and stand ready to support the agency in assisting the American people,” they concluded.

Read the full letter to Secretary Kennedy here.

Ryan also co-sponsors the Heating and Cooling Relief Act, which would lower home energy costs for millions more households nationwide.

Specifically, the Heating and Cooling Relief Act would:

Substantially increase LIHEAP funding to ensure year-round assistance, including an additional $2 billion for emergency energy assistance and $1 billion in Just Transition Grants to help vulnerable households adapt to a changing climate;

Broaden eligibility so that households earning up to 250 percent of the Federal Poverty Line or 80 percent of State Median Income can qualify, while ensuring lower energy burdens for lower-income households and capping household energy burdens at 3 percent of monthly income;

Protect consumers from utility shutoffs, excessive late fees, and predatory energy practices that disproportionately impact vulnerable communities;

Expand emergency assistance, ensuring extreme heat and cold are recognized as qualifying emergencies and that states can provide vital cooling relief;

Increase funding for weatherization and home electrification, to help low-income households reduce energy costs, improve health and safety, and transition to clean, resilient energy systems;

Streamline enrollment and outreach, improving coordination with other federal programs and increasing access through automatic enrollment and simplified verification; and

Strengthen reporting requirements to better track affordability, equity, and climate resilience outcomes.

A man who distributed, received, and possessed child pornography was sentenced today to more than seven years in federal prison. Anthony Paul Harden, age 48, from Rockford, Iowa, received the prison term after a February 23, 2026, guilty plea to receipt of child pornography.

Evidence at court hearings in the case showed that in August 2025, law enforcement officers searched Harden’s home in Rockford. They seized four electronic devices that contained child pornography. Between May 2023 and July 2025, Harden received and possessed hundreds of images and videos of child pornography, including depictions of infants and sadistic and masochistic conduct. He also distributed child pornography to undercover law enforcement computers.

Harden was sentenced in Cedar Rapids by United States District Court Chief Judge C.J. Williams. Harden was sentenced to 90 months’ imprisonment and was ordered to make $3,000 in restitution to a victim in the case. He must also serve a five-year term of supervised release after the prison term. There is no parole in the federal system.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the United States Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.usdoj.gov/psc . For more information about Internet safety education, please visit www.usdoj.gov/psc and click on the tab “resources.”

Harden is being held in the United States Marshal’s custody until he can be transported to a federal prison.

The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Devra T. Hake and investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and Floyd County Sheriff’s Office.

LOS ANGELES – An illegal alien from Guatemala was sentenced today to 262 months in federal prison for leading one of the nation’s largest human smuggling organizations, a ring that smuggled approximately 20,000 illegal immigrants from Guatemala to the United States over a five-year span, held some of them hostage, and was responsible for a car accident that killed seven migrants, two of them young children.

Eduardo Domingo Renoj-Matul, 53, a.k.a. “Turko,” “El Jefe,” “Patrón,” and “El Gallo,” who most recently lived in the Westlake neighborhood near downtown Los Angeles, was sentenced by United States District Judge Cynthia Valenzuela, who also ordered him to pay $64,945 in restitution in connection with a November 2023 car accident resulting in the deaths of seven illegal immigrants – including two children ages 4 and 6 years old. An additional restitution hearing related to Renoj-Matul’s kidnapping victims will be scheduled at a later date.

Renoj-Matul pleaded guilty on March 6 to one count of conspiracy to bring aliens to the United States, transport aliens in the United States, and harbor aliens in the United States for private financial gain and one count of hostage taking. He has been in federal custody since February 2025.

“This criminal built an illicit money-making machine off the desperation of illegal immigrants,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli. “This case, which involved hostage taking, sexual assault, and children killed in a car accident, proves that smuggling aliens into our country is not a harmless crime. It is for the safety of our citizens and immigrants themselves that we zealously police and protect our borders.”

According to court documents, Renoj-Matul first worked for then acted as a leader in the smuggling organization and specialized in the smuggling of illegal aliens from Guatemala to the United States, the transportation and movement of those illegal aliens within the United States, and the harboring, concealing, and shielding of illegal aliens within the United States. This organization moved approximately 20,000 illegal aliens from 2019 through July 2024.

Associates in Guatemala who solicited illegal aliens to come to the United States accepted payment of between $15,000 and $18,000 for each illegal alien to be smuggled into the United States and coordinated the journey of the illegal aliens from Guatemala to the United States.

Mexican smuggling organizations who accepted Guatemalan illegal aliens in southern Mexico transported them through Mexico and then smuggled those illegal aliens across the U.S.-Mexico border.

In the United States, co-conspirators within the organization oversaw smuggling cells, teams of drivers who transported illegal aliens, and operators of stash houses where illegal aliens were held while they were within the United States.

Co-conspirators operated an illegal alien stash house located on James M. Wood Boulevard in the Westlake district of Los Angeles. Illegal aliens smuggled by the organization were brought to this house. After an illegal alien’s smuggling fee was paid, the illegal alien was transported by co-conspirators to another destination within the United States. If an illegal alien’s smuggling fees were not paid, Renoj-Matul and other co-conspirators would hold that person against their will at the Westlake house until their fee was paid.

In retaliation for one victim who had not paid her smuggling fees, Renoj-Matul held her against her will, “sexually assaulted her, forced her to work demeaning jobs, mistreated her, and threatened her family in an effort to extract payment of the smuggling debt,” prosecutors argued in a sentencing memorandum.

Other co-conspirators transported and coordinated the transport of illegal aliens for Renoj-Matul from Guatemala, through Mexico, to the United States and then throughout various destinations within the United States. Within the United States, co-conspirators drove illegal aliens to other destinations in vehicles provided by Renoj-Matul and others for a fee paid by the aliens.

Renoj-Matul directed that the transportation of proceeds from human smuggling be transported from Los Angeles to Phoenix to be given to the Mexican smuggling organization and pay the smuggling organization’s expenses.

Renoj-Matul arranging for co-conspirators to transport illegal immigrants to Alabama, Colorado, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Mississippi, New York, Tennessee, Virginia, and Washington, D.C.

He admitted in his plea agreement that at all relevant times, he acted for the purpose of private financial gain.

In 2024, after a third party reneged on paying a victim’s smuggling fees, co-conspirators in Guatemala and Renoj-Matul called the victim’s mother and threatened to harm the victim, including by warning the victim “would come home in a box” if her smuggling fees were not paid, according to court documents. For a two-month period from May 2024 to July 2024, the victim was held hostage at the house in the Westlake area of Los Angeles.

Renoj-Matul also held hostage another victim – an illegal immigrant from Guatemala –from April 2024 to July 2024. He knowingly and intentionally seized and detained, and threatened to kill, injure, and continue to detain the victim to compel third persons to pay smuggling fees to the hostage takers as an explicit condition for the victim’s release.

Relatedly, Cristóbal Mejia-Chaj, 51, of Westlake, was sentenced today by Judge Valenzuela to 33 months in federal prison. He pleaded guilty on March 25 to one count of conspiracy to bring aliens to the United States, transport aliens in the United States, and harbor aliens in the United States for private financial gain. His restitution hearing is scheduled for December 11.

José Paxtor-Oxlaj, 46, a co-defendant, was sentenced by Judge Valenzuela on July 31 to 78 months in federal prison and ordered him to pay $64,945 in restitution in connection with the fatal November 2023 car accident. Paxtor-Oxlaj is incarcerated in Oklahoma state prison in connection with that fatal crash. He pleaded guilty on April 13 to one count of conspiracy to bring aliens to the United States, transport aliens in the United States, and harbor aliens in the United States for private financial fain and resulting in death.

Helmer Obispo-Hernández, 43, a.k.a. “Xavi,” a lieutenant in the criminal organization, faces federal criminal charges in this case and is a fugitive.

Homeland Security Investigations’ (HSI) El Camino Real Financial Crimes Task Force, HSI’s Figueroa Initiative Gang and Human Trafficking Task Force, United States Border Patrol, and the Inglewood Police Department investigated this matter.

Assistant United States Attorneys Kelly Larocque of the Transnational Organized Crime Section and Lana Morton Owens of the National Security Division prosecuted this case.

Connecticut House Delegation Statement on Reports President Trump is Seeking to Ease Russian Sanctions
Today, Reps. John Larson (CT-01), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Rosa DeLauro (CT-03), Jim Himes (CT-04), and Jahana Hayes (CT-05) responded to reporting from the Atlantic that President Trump is entertaining a plan to ease sanctions on Russia:
“When we voted against the Senate’s sanction bill this month, we warned that stripping out the enforcement language would leave every decision about punishing Putin to a president who keeps siding with the Kremlin. It took less than two weeks and President Trump is entertaining a plan to ease sanctions on Russia.
“Just last week President Trump went to the United Nations and bragged about the ‘enormous new tariff authorities’ this bill handed him. So, the one part of the law he seems eager to enforce will needlessly raise costs on Americans by continuing his reckless trade policies, while the power he was given to cripple Putin’s war machine he is already looking to sign away.
“That is exactly why the House-passed bill, H.R. 2913, required the president to act on sanctions. Without that requirement, sanctions are dependent on President Trump’s will to impose them – and President Trump has shown us time and time again he would rather be a friend to Putin than hold him accountable.
“We will keep fighting for military assistance for Ukraine and real sanctions that no president can waive away as a favor.”
title: Connecticut House Delegation Statement on Reports President Trump is Seeking to Ease Russian Sanctions

Velázquez Slams SBA for Stonewalling GAO Probe Into DOGE Access to Sensitive Small Business Data
  
  
    
      Washington,
      October 2, 2026
    
    
    
    
  
  
  
  
  
  
    
      WASHINGTON —The Government Accountability Office (GAO) released a report examining DOGE teams’ access to federal agency systems and the safeguards agencies put in place to protect sensitive information.
As part of its review, GAO sought information from the Small Business Administration about which systems DOGE team members had access to and what controls were in place to protect those systems and data. SBA did not provide the requested information despite repeated efforts by GAO to obtain it.
“SBA’s refusal to provide GAO with basic information about DOGE’s access to agency systems is deeply troubling,” said Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez, Ranking Member of the House Small Business Committee. “The federal government has a responsibility to safeguard the personally identifiable information of our nation’s small business owners. Congress and the public have a right to know who had access to that sensitive information and whether proper safeguards were in place. This lack of cooperation is unprecedented. Independent oversight only works when agencies cooperate with it. SBA needs to stop stonewalling GAO and provide the answers America’s small businesses deserve.”
