HOUSTON – A 34-year-old woman has pleaded guilty to health care fraud and aggravated identity theft.

Tekiyah McLeod served as the registered agent for nLove Community Services LLC, which purported to provide mental health therapy services to Medicaid beneficiaries.

McLeod admitted billing Medicaid approximately $477,872 for mental health therapy services that were never provided, including services purportedly provided to herself. She also used a nurse practitioner’s name and National Provider Identifier to submit fraudulent claims without the practitioner’s knowledge or consent.

As a result of the fraudulent claims, McLeod received approximately $453,323 from Medicaid.

“Another day, another Medicaid fraudster brought to justice. Why are medical expenses so out of control in this country? In large part because of scammers like Tekiyah,” said U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz. “Her conduct is despicable, and I trust she’ll have time to dwell on that while in prison for ripping off the American taxpayer.”

“Another day, another Medicaid fraudster brought to justice. Why are medical expenses so out of control in this country? In large part because of scammers like Tekiyah,” said U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz. “Her conduct is despicable, and I trust she’ll have time to dwell on that while in prison for ripping off the American taxpayer.”

U.S. District Judge Keith Ellison accepted the plea and will impose sentencing Dec. 16. At that time, McLeod faces up to 10 years in federal prison for health care fraud and a mandatory consecutive sentence of two years for aggravated identity theft as well as a possible $250,000 maximum fine.

McLeod was permitted to remain on bond pending sentencing.

The FBI conducted the investigation with assistance from the Texas Attorney General’s Office – Medicaid Fraud Control Unit and the Virginia Office of the Attorney General – Medicaid Fraud Control Unit. Assistant U.S. Attorney Alexander Alum is prosecuting the case.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division which is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste and abuse within federal benefit programs.
title: Magnolia woman fraudulently bills Medicaid for nonexistent mental health services

This week, FEMA awarded more than $47.7 million in grant funding to fire departments, first responder organizations, and other institutions focused on firefighter safety and fire prevention in the Mid-Atlantic. These awards will enable agencies to get the equipment, staff and support they need to carry out their critical, life-saving missions. This week’s fire grant funding brings the total amount awarded to DC, Delaware, Maryland, Pennsylvania, Virginia and West Virginia this year to more than $95 million. Nationwide, FEMA awarded $648 million through its three fire grant programs.
“Firefighters and other first responders are everyday heroes, helping their neighbors and communities when they need it most,” said FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton. “Through this grant funding, FEMA is building the capability of these local organizations to respond to disasters and emergencies. By empowering fire departments to get the staff, training and equipment they need, FEMA is strengthening the resilience of American communities nationwide.”
FEMA is administering these funds through its three fire grant programs: the Assistance to Firefighters Grants, the Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response grant program, and the Fire Prevention and Safety grant program. Examples of awards issued this week include:
- Nearly $5 million to Anne Arundel County in Maryland to hire firefighters under the Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response grant program.
- More than $3.4 million to the City of Newport News in Virginia to hire firefighters under the Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response grant program.
- Nearly $3 million to the City of Philadelphia Fire Department to improve operations and safety through the Assistance to Firefighters Grants Program.
- Nearly $2.8 million to the City of Baltimore to improve operations and safety through the Assistance to Firefighters Grants Program.
- Nearly $1.5 million to the American National Red Cross in Washington, D.C. under the Fire Prevention and Safety grant program.
For information on all the awards issued this year, visit the fire grant program webpages on FEMA.gov: the Assistance to Firefighters Grants, the Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response grant program, and the Fire Prevention and Safety grant program.

As part of NASA’s ongoing Inspiration Tour, NASA astronaut Christina Koch will highlight America’s strengths in space exploration and aeronautics innovation at the Philadelphia Eagles vs. Los Angeles Rams game in Philadelphia on Sunday, Oct. 4.

A self-proclaimed Philadelphia sports fan, Koch is an explorer and engineer who spent a total of 338 days in space across two missions, including serving as a mission specialist for the agency’s Artemis II mission earlier this year. On April 1, Koch launched from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida aboard the Orion spacecraft on top of the agency’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket as part of Artemis II . Koch and her fellow crew members completed a historic lunar flyby, marking humanity’s return to the vicinity of the Moon for the first time in more than 50 years.

NASA team members will engage with fans at the agency’s Experience Zone, located outside the stadium from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. before the game. Fans can learn more about NASA’s return to the Moon through the agency’s Artemis program, enjoy interactive games, and capture photos at a selfie station and with a large, inflatable NASA logo.

With stops across the nation, NASA’s Inspiration Tour convenes academic, industry, and public sector stakeholders to connect the agency with the people, technologies, and organizations that drive American leadership in space.

The tour will culminate in MAX POWER, a public exposition of American air and space innovation, Saturday, Nov. 7, and Sunday, Nov. 8, on and near the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Held in honor of America’s historic 250th anniversary, the multi-day, family-friendly event will showcase the next-generation aircraft, spacecraft, autonomous vehicles, and technologies that will help define the future of transportation in air and space.

For more information about MAX POWER and the agency’s missions, visit:

https://www.nasa.gov/maxpower

WASHINGTON, D.C. and KYIV – The U.S.–Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund (URIF) today approved a number of new investments to advance the shared economic and strategic interests of the United States and Ukraine. These investments will help secure critical supply chains, strengthen Ukraine’s energy resilience, and develop its critical mineral sector.
“URIF’s first investment in March demonstrated that it was open for business. Today’s board approval of additional investments in Ukraine’s critical minerals and energy sectors signals investor support for Ukraine’s recovery and future prosperity,” said U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. “These investments represent the continued realization of the vision behind the novel agreement that Prime Minister Svyrydenko and I signed in April 2025 to establish URIF and give America a direct stake in Ukraine’s long-term peace and prosperity,”
“Today's Board meeting marks an important step forward for the U.S.-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund. These investments strengthen Ukraine's energy resilience, develop critical mineral resources, and support innovative Ukrainian companies. Together these projects are building the foundation for Ukraine's economic recovery and deepening the partnership between our countries,” said DFC CEO Ben Black.
“This round of investments shows the growing scope of the U.S.-Ukraine partnership, from energy and critical minerals to telecommunications and emerging technologies. For URIF, it is an important step in building a track record of investments that gives investors confidence in Ukraine. We want to see more Ukrainian companies develop through this partnership and create new opportunities for the Ukrainian economy,” said Oleksii Sobolev, Deputy Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine.
The joint U.S.-Ukrainian URIF board of directors approved the following today:
- Expanding Investment in Ukraine’s Critical Minerals: URIF will establish a joint investment platform with Ukrainian company BGV Group Management. The platform will seek to build a diverse portfolio of early-stage mining projects across Ukraine, supporting the development of Ukraine’s critical minerals sector. Its initial focus will be on identified assets of rare earths, beryllium and zirconium deposits. This platform aims to significantly scale up Ukraine’s critical mineral production, creating Ukrainian jobs and investment opportunities for U.S. and Ukrainian companies and international investors, while shoring up secure supply chains of these vital critical minerals for U.S. and allied markets.
- Restoring Heat and Power to Ukrainian Communities: URIF’s equity investment in a multi-site distributed combined heat and power (CHP) cogeneration platform will support the construction and operation of a series of community-scale energy hubs designed to restore electricity and heat supply damaged by the war. Once completed, the project is intended to provide heat and power to thousands of households, ensuring access to vital energy and heat in Ukraine as the conflict continues.
- Enhancing Ukraine’s Energy Security: URIF’s debt investment provides financing for DTEK’s 200 MW/400 MWh battery energy storage system across six sites in Ukraine. The system is operational, with enough capacity to supply electricity equivalent to approximately 600,000 Ukrainian homes for two hours and provide the country’s power grid with greater resilience and stability. The project is built by DTEK, Ukraine’s largest private energy company, and leverages American energy technology at the battery storage sites to provide backup power and enable faster grid restoration.
Today’s announcement comes one year after the United States and Ukraine established URIF’s initial capital base and launched the Fund’s operations, moving URIF from an institutional framework to capital deployment. The Fund made its first investment in emerging-technology company Sine Engineering in March of this year. In June, the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation signed a cooperation agreement with the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) to develop a political risk insurance framework that will catalyze and support private sector investment and capital mobilization in Ukraine in connection with URIF’s investments.
URIF is a joint U.S.–Ukrainian investment fund and a key pillar of the economic partnership between the Trump administration and the Government of Ukraine. The Fund harnesses American and Ukrainian talent, resources, and expertise to mobilize U.S. and aligned private capital and create strategic investment opportunities in Ukraine for the United States, its allies, multilateral development banks, and private investors. URIF focuses on investments that support Ukraine’s reconstruction, supply chain resilience, and the shared economic security and prosperity of Ukraine and the United States.
For more information and to submit a project proposal, please visit URIF’s website: https://urifinvest.com.
title: URIF Approves Additional Investments and Partnerships in Energy and Critical Minerals

EPA Notifies States of Potential Designations for the Biden EPA’s Flawed 2024 Air Quality Standard Following Appealed Court Order
EPA Press Office (press@epa.gov)
WASHINGTON — Today, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) notified all 50 states, the District of Columbia, five territories, and 67 Tribes of the agency’s intended approach for area designations under the Biden-era 2024 revised National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) for fine particulate matter (PM2.5) despite EPA’s belief the designations should not move forward. To assist in further analysis, EPA is providing an opportunity for states, territories, and Tribes to submit additional information within 30 days. The agency is also publishing a Notice of Availability in the Federal Register opening a 30-day public comment period for all Americans to provide feedback. These opportunities for further input represent a step toward complying with a court order issued by the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California requiring EPA to designate areas as attainment, unclassifiable, or nonattainment under the 2024 PM2.5 NAAQS by February 6, 2027.
Since day one, the Trump EPA has maintained the position that the Biden Administration’s 2024 PM2.5 NAAQS is unlawful on multiple grounds. In 2020, EPA concluded after the “thorough review” of available science required by the Clean Air Act (CAA) that the 2012 PM2.5 standard set by the Obama Administration protects public health with an “adequate margin of safety.” In 2021, however, the Biden Administration broke with fifty years of precedent by “reconsidering” and revising the standard without doing a thorough review required by law. The resulting 2024 PM2.5 NAAQS—which were set without fully considering the available science or taking into account the severe consequences a rushed revision would have on Americans—is the most stringent in history and approaching natural levels.
In a brief filed today with the U.S. Supreme Court, the United States joined a broad coalition of States and associations in urging the Justices to review the 2024 standard; once again acknowledging that the 2024 PM2.5 NAAQS did not comply with statutory requirements. In addition to the unlawful and scientifically unsound nature of the underlying standard, EPA is concerned that the court-ordered deadline leaves insufficient time to consider critical information relevant to particular areas.
Additionally, due to significant wildfires, concerns with the accuracy of air monitors, and the need to evaluate new data, EPA believes the designation timeline set by the court is unrealistic and could cause further harm. On September 2, 2026, EPA appealed the district court order imposing a rushed deadline for the agency to designate all areas by February 6, 2027. The agency requested, and the Ninth Circuit granted, expedited consideration of the case. However, while the appeals are pending, EPA is taking the actions required under the CAA to meet the court’s deadline. Absent further action by the judiciary, the agency intends to meet the current, court-ordered deadline for finalizing designations based on monitoring data from 2023-2025 and other relevant available information.
The Trump EPA has been committed to making every decision based on the best available science and the best reading of the law. A rushed decision to revise the NAAQS, as well as a rushed timeline for designating all areas of the nation under an unlawful standard, goes against these principles.
Details on the potential designations and EPA’s responses to initial area designations submitted by states, territories, and Tribes are accessible on the EPA designations webpage.
Background
Under the CAA, when EPA establishes a new or revised NAAQS, governors and other leaders submit initial designations for areas within their states or tribal area. Areas can be designated as attainment, meaning they meet the air quality standard; nonattainment, meaning they do not meet the air quality standard; or unclassifiable, meaning there is not enough monitoring data or other information to make a determination. If EPA intends to modify an initial area designation, the agency must notify that governor or respective leader at least 120 days before finalizing the designation. EPA is fulfilling this obligation today by notifying states, territories, and Tribes of potential modifications to their initial designations.
In November 2025, EPA confessed error before the D.C. Circuit, admitted that the 2024 PM2.5 NAAQS was unlawful, and urged the court to vacate the standard. The D.C. Circuit denied EPA’s motion, rejected similar arguments by a broad coalition of states and associations, and sided with intervenors who argued that the statute allows the agency to act outside statutory requirements and without considering relevant factors. States and industry petitioners have asked the Supreme Court to review and overturn the D.C. Circuit’s decision.
title: EPA Notifies States of Potential Designations for the Biden EPA’s Flawed 2024 Air Quality Standard Following Appealed Court Order

WACO, Texas – A federal jury in Waco convicted a former U.S. Army Soldier on nine counts related to the sexual abuse and exploitation of two minor victims, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas.

According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Jordan Anthony Pearce, 30, of Tuscaloosa, Alabama, began sexually abusing a minor female at his Fort Hood residence when the minor was 11 years old. The victim reported the abuse to a friend and later school and law enforcement officials. In April 2023, the victim spoke to a forensic interviewer at the Child Advocacy Center (CAC) in Bell County and stated that Pearce told her she would not be believed if she told anyone about the abuse.

Shortly after the first reports, a second minor female was taken to the CAC, where she also detailed how she had been sexually abused by Pearce at his residence and other locations when she was between the ages of 13 and 16 years old. A search of the second victim’s cell phone revealed text messages between Pearce and the minor along with a sexually explicit video Pearce had requested from the child victim.

Pearce was indicted on April 8, 2025, and arrested on May 30, 2025. A second superseding indictment charged Pearce with ten counts which included abusive sexual contact, transportation of a minor, sexual abuse of a minor, production of child pornography, distribution of visual depictions of sexual activities by a minor, and enticement of a minor. On Wednesday, a federal jury found Pearce guilty on all charges except for transportation of a minor.

The Department of the Army Criminal Investigation Division investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Mary Kucera and Mark Frazier are prosecuting the case. Donna Myrdahl, Brenda Wright and Marci’a Wilson provided valuable assistance with litigation support and trial preparation.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC .

Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05) yesterday introduced a package of bills designed to improve support for state and local election offices to improve voting access for Americans in future elections. The Accessible Voting Act will support state and local efforts to expand voter access, while the Dropbox Access Act will create a new standard by which localities must provide ballot dropboxes.

“Our democracy thrives when every eligible voter is able to participate, and these bills will remove barriers that all too often make it more difficult for Americans to cast their ballots. I’ve seen how expanding accessibility and access to ballot boxes has improved voter turnout and engagement in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania,” said Rep. Scanlon. “I’m proud to introduce these bills to advance more equitable and just voting policies for all Americans.”

The Accessible Voting Act, which Scanlon co-leads with Reps. Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Jamie Raskin (MD-08), and Lateefah Simon (CA-12), would support state and local election efforts through the establishment of the Office of Accessibility within the Election Assistance Commission (EAC). Specifically, the bill would ensure through the Office of Accessibility that state and local election officials are taking steps to obtain, deploy, and maintain voting systems, expand the number of options to cast a ballot in federal elections for older voters and voters with disabilities, and establish an online national resource center on accessible voting. The bill would also create a new state grant program through the Office of Accessibility for the improvement of accessible voting options, and reauthorize and expand grants through the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services to improve voter accessibility for older Americans and people with disabilities.

The Dropbox Access Act, co-led by Reps. Simon and Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), would require each state to provide county-level secure drop boxes where individuals may drop off their completed ballots for federal elections. Specifically, the bill would prevent states from restricting voters’ access to drop boxes by requiring counties to provide, at minimum, one drop box per 20,000 voting-age residents, ensure that drop boxes are available 24 hours a day beginning 45 days before each election, and create more accessible options near public transit and for individuals with disabilities or with limited English-language proficiency, and for voters living in rural communities and tribal lands.

Scanlon introduced the voting accessibility bills package as the Trump administration has issued a series of executive orders and legislative proposals apparently designed to suppress voter turnout ahead of November’s midterm elections. Those proposals largely have been rejected by the courts. According to Scanlon, “now more than ever, it’s important that our elections reflect the will of the people, and that we challenge efforts by the current administration to undermine our election integrity.”

Recently, Congresswoman Scanlon convened hearings in her congressional district, at Widener University, and at the U.S. Capitol, to counter efforts by the Trump administration to spread disinformation about elections and disenfranchise voters with voter roll purges and by restricting access to mail-in voting. At both hearings, Members of Congress heard from election protection experts on voter protection and election security. Those experts expressed confidence in the safeguards and resiliency of our elections, and the importance of expanding access to the ballot box. Recordings of those hearings are available here: at Widener University, Chester PA and in Washington, D.C.

“American democracy works best when all citizens can participate and vote, no matter where they’re from, what language they speak or whether they live with a disability,” said Rep. Raskin. “Our Accessible Voting Act strengthens access to the ballot box and addresses a wide range of systemic deficiencies, so no eligible voter is left alone to overcome barriers to casting a ballot.”

“Our elders fought for our voting rights with blood, sweat, and tears – and yet too many people, particularly older Americans and Americans with disabilities, still face barriers to voting such as inaccessible polling locations or access to voter information. Both the Accessible Voting Act and Dropbox Access Act will improve voter accessibility for requesting mail-in ballots, accessing voter registration info, and when showing up to the ballot box,” said Rep. Simon. “As the first congenitally blind Member of Congress, improving accessibility to ensure that all Americans can equally access resources and participate in society is a top priority of mine. I am proud to lead on these bills with Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon to ensure ALL individuals can equally participate in local and federal elections to make their rightful voices heard.”

“The ability for everyone to have their voice heard is central to our American ideals—yet too often people with disabilities face unnecessary barriers in both registering to vote and casting their ballots, preventing them from fully participating in our democracy,” said Rep. Dean. “This legislation will help improve registration processes and eliminate barriers to voting, including by reauthorizing grants to improve voting accessibility for older Americans and those with disabilities. By breaking down these barriers, our communities can be better represented by every voice. I'm thankful to partner with Congresswoman Scanlon and Congressman Raskin to pass these essential bills.”

“We should be making it more accessible for Americans to vote, not harder,” said Rep. Garcia. “But the Trump administration and its Republican allies continue to attack voting rights and put up new barriers to the ballot box. That is why I am proud to once again co-lead the Dropbox Access Act, a practical bill to make sure voters have fair, accessible options to return their ballots. We should be protecting the right to vote, not suppressing it.”

They were presented in D.C. Superior Court on October 1, where Judge Dorsey Jones found probable cause for their arrest and ordered them detained pending a preliminary hearing scheduled for October 19, 2026.

According to the arrest warrants, at around 4:15 a.m., on August 4, 2026, the victim, Xavier Fogle, was captured on CCTV footage pulling on door handles in the 1400 block of Clifton St. NW, where defendant Buchanan’s car was parked. Buchanan is then seen on CCTV footage walking out of his building neighboring Clifton St., getting into a verbal altercation with the victim, and then making a phone call. Call detail records from Buchanan’s phone show that the call was placed to Co-defendant Jenkins. Buchanan is then seen on CCTV footage getting into his white BMW sedan and driving in the direction where the victim was headed on foot. About a block away, Buchanan is seen on CCTV footage exiting his vehicle and seemingly receiving something—presumably a firearm—from Jenkins, who was exiting the same building as Buchanan and running to catch up with him after the phone call Buchanan is then seen on video taking the item, chasing the victim, in the 2600 block of 15th St. NW, and fatally shooting him twice in the back of the legs.

PITTSBURGH, PA – October 2, 2026 — Congresswoman Summer L. Lee (PA-12) alongside Rep. Chris Deluzio (PA-17) and Rep. Ro Khanna (CA-17), called on The University of Pittsburgh Medical Center (UPMC) to bargain in good faith with nearly 900 nurses, nurse practitioners, and midwives at UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital who have spent approximately eight months negotiating their first union contract.

In a letter to UPMC President and CEO Leslie Davis, the lawmakers raised concerns they have heard from workers and organizers about staffing levels, excessive workloads, and conditions that healthcare professionals say can make it harder to provide patients with the level of care they deserve.

The lawmakers specifically pointed to reports that nurses are routinely responsible for more patients than nationally recognized clinical standards recommend, including instances in which one labor and delivery nurse may be responsible for two or three patients even though professional staffing standards call for dedicated nursing care for a patient in active labor.

“For approximately eight months, nearly 900 health care professionals at UPMC Magee have been negotiating for a contract that reflects the critical role they play in caring for patients and families throughout western Pennsylvania,” the lawmakers wrote. “These workers have raised serious concerns about inadequate staffing, excessive workloads, and conditions that prevent them from consistently providing the level of care their patients deserve. UPMC has a responsibility to listen to these frontline professionals and work constructively to resolve their concerns without unnecessary delays.”

Contract negotiations between UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital, University of Pittsburgh Physicians, and SEIU Healthcare Pennsylvania began in January. UPMC reported that the parties held their 38th bargaining session on September 22 and have reached tentative agreements on several issues as negotiations continue.

These staffing concerns come as Allegheny County continues to face seriousracial disparities in maternal health. In 2023, the rate of preventable hospitalizations among Black women was 3.3 times higher than among White women in Allegheny County. The disparities are especially stark in Pittsburgh, where previous reports found that Black women were more likely to die during pregnancy than their peers in 97% of comparable U.S. cities.

Rep. Lee has made confronting the Black maternal health crisis a focus of her work in Congress, including pressing HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. during Black Maternal Health Week over threats to maternal health research and community-based programs, joining congressional efforts to expand access to midwifery care, and strongly supporting the Black Maternal Health Momnibus Act to invest in community-based care, strengthen and diversify the perinatal workforce, improve maternal health data collection, and expand maternal mental health support.

In their letter, Reps. Lee, Deluzio, and Khanna emphasized that safe staffing and workplace protections are critical to patient safety, retaining experienced healthcare workers, reducing exhaustion and burnout, and ensuring hospitals can respond effectively to emergencies.

“UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital is a vital institution that generations of western Pennsylvanians have relied upon for obstetric, neonatal, reproductive, and specialized health care,” the lawmakers wrote. “We will continue to monitor UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital actions closely and strongly encourage UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital, in accordance with the law, to bargain a fair contract in good faith with these workers.”

Workers at Magee have publicly advocated for staffing standards based on recommendations from national professional organizations. Those proposals include dedicated nursing care for patients who are laboring or being induced, as well as staffing standards for neonatal intensive care, postpartum care, emergency care, oncology, and other hospital units.

The full letter can be read HERE and letter text is below:

September 22, 2026

Dear Ms. Davis:

We write to urge the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center (UPMC) to bargain in good faith, as required by federal law, with the nurses, nurse practitioners, and midwives at UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital. As you know, workers have a right to organize and advocate for improvements in their wages and working conditions, as well as engage in protected concerted activity under Section 7 of the National Labor Relations Act (NLRA).

We have received troubling reports from our constituents and organizers that nurses are routinely assigned more patients than nationally recognized clinical standards recommend. Nurses have described situations in which a single labor and delivery nurse may be responsible for two or three patients, even though established standards call for a patient in active labor to receive dedicated nursing care.

For approximately eight months, nearly 900 health care professionals at UPMC Magee have been negotiating for a contract that reflects the critical role they play in caring for patients and families throughout western Pennsylvania. These workers have raised serious concerns about inadequate staffing, excessive workloads, and conditions that prevent them from consistently providing the level of care their patients deserve. UPMC has a responsibility to listen to these frontline professionals and work constructively to resolve their concerns without unnecessary delays.

Safe staffing and other workplace protections are fundamental to patient safety, retaining experienced nurses, protecting workers from exhaustion and burnout, and ensuring that hospitals remain prepared to respond to emergencies.

UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital is a vital institution that generations of western Pennsylvanians have relied upon for obstetric, neonatal, reproductive, and specialized health care. We will continue to monitor UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital actions closely and strongly encourage UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital, in accordance with the law, to bargain a fair contract in good faith with these workers.

Thank you for your attention to these issues.

Sincerely,

Summer Lee

USDA Website Gives Veterans Outdated SNAP Information as Partnership With VA Stalls
Press Contact
Mike Lavigne (Communications Director)
Elain Shubat (Deputy Communications Director/Digital Director)
WASHINGTON– According to a Government Accountability Office (GAO) report released yesterday, USDA’s website still suggests veterans are exempt from SNAP’s time limit—even though Republicans took away that protection, putting veterans at risk of losing food assistance. The report on veterans’ access to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) also found that USDA has produced no veteran-specific outreach materials in the past five years and that its food security workgroup with VA has not met since April 2025.
House Committee on Veterans' Affairs Ranking Member Mark Takano (CA-39) issued the following statement on the report:
“Republicans in Congress took away veterans' exemption from SNAP's time limit, and the Trump administration can't even update a webpage to tell them. Call it what it is: incompetence. The agency that is supposed to lead on veteran hunger hasn't held a meeting with VA since April 2025, and it didn't respond when GAO asked why the agreement hasn't been reviewed. Veterans earned better than this. Congress should restore their exemption, require USDA and VA to work together and report on their progress, and use our oversight to hold USDA to its promise to fix what it tells veterans.”
Background: SNAP is the federal program that helps low-income households buy groceries. Adults who can work and don't have children at home can receive it for only three months in any three-year period, unless they meet a work requirement or another exception. From September 2023 to July 2025, veterans were exempt from that limit. Trumps One Big Beautiful Bill ended the exemption, and veterans now face the same limit as other adults.
GAO found that USDA never updated its eligibility webpage to match. As of September, the page still suggests veterans may not be subject to the time limit. A veteran who reads it and believes it could count on benefits that end after three months. Stakeholders told GAO that veterans experiencing homelessness and veterans in rural areas can have a harder time meeting the work requirement, which makes the wrong information costlier for them. GAO also found that USDA has produced no veteran-specific SNAP outreach materials in the past five years, even though veterans’ groups told GAO they need them.
USDA and VA signed an agreement in September 2023 to work together on veteran food insecurity. That work slowed in April 2025 after key staff were “DOGEd” at USDA. Under the Trump administration, USDA, which leads the partnership, has not held a workgroup meeting since, and the agencies have not done the annual review the agreement requires. VA has kept screening veterans for food insecurity, reaching 4.4 million in fiscal year 2025, but the two agencies are not working together as planned. VA health officials told GAO they are trying to restart the partnership.
The GAO report recommends that USDA update its eligibility page, build SNAP outreach materials for veterans with VA, and put a formal collaboration mechanism in place with VA, and that VA do the same with USDA. VA concurred. USDA generally concurred and said an update to the page is underway.

Media Note

Office of the Spokesman

October 2, 2026

Today in Tokyo, the United States and Japan signed a protocol that extends and amends the U.S.-Japan Agreement on Cooperation in Research and Development in Science and Technology, also known as the U.S.-Japan Science and Technology Agreement. Assistant to the President and Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Michael Kratsios signed for the United States and Minister for Foreign Affairs Motegi Toshimitsu signed for Japan.

First signed in 1988, the Science and Technology Agreement provides a legally binding framework for scientific cooperation between the U.S. and Japanese governments. Under this framework, the United States and Japan have built countless links between their scientific communities.

The protocol extends the Agreement indefinitely, a sign of the deep trust and respect between the U.S. and Japanese governments. The extended and amended Agreement positions both countries to sustain and strengthen their cooperation, with a focus on critical and emerging technologies that improve the lives of both peoples.

The indefinite extension reaffirms the long-term U.S. and Japanese commitment to close partnership on science and technology, while advancing a secure, trusted innovation ecosystem that benefits both nations.

WASHINGTON – Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03), House Committee on Education and Workforce, released the following statement after the Bureau of Labor Statistics announced that the economy gained 29,000 jobs in September, and the unemployment rate increased from 4.1 percent to 4.2 percent.
“This Trump economy might be working for the wealthy and the well connected, but it clearly is leaving workers behind. CEO pay is skyrocketing, while for working people, it's a daily struggle just to cover groceries and rent. Workers’ wages are failing to keep up with inflation, and the increasing cost of daily expenses are eating into workers’ paychecks. According to the Century Foundation, inflation-adjusted debt payments grew faster than income in recent years as working families have struggled to make ends meet.
“The jobs numbers show the same strain: Trump has added only 776,000 jobs between January 2025 and September 2026, while the Biden administration added 10.7 million within its first 20 months. Since President Trump returned to office, not one month has reached the average monthly job creation under the Biden administration. In fact, he has not even achieved 70 percent of Biden’s monthly average.

Children cannot learn on an empty stomach, and parents cannot build a better life when they cannot afford groceries. We will keep pushing to protect school meals, strengthen job training, lower the cost of college, and make sure every worker can earn a living wage and retire with dignity.”

CLEVELAND – A Trumbull County man has been sentenced to federal prison for engaging in online activities that involved Child Sexual Abuse Materials (CSAM).

James Joseph Cataline, 47, of Hubbard, Ohio, has been sentenced to 282 months (23.5 years) in prison by U.S. District Judge Pamela A. Barker, after pleading guilty in May to:

Receipt of Visual Depictions of Minors Engaged in Sexually Explicit Conduct

Possession of Child Pornography, or Child Sexual Abuse Materials (CSAM)

Transferring Obscene Material to a Minor

Cataline was also ordered to serve 10 years of supervised release after imprisonment and pay $5,000 toward the Justice for Victims of Trafficking Act, which was established in 2015 to provide justice for victims of trafficking. A restitution hearing will be held Dec. 10.

According to court documents and evidence, from about December 2024 to November 2025, Cataline had a history of engaging with CSAM. Investigators also discovered that he was directly engaging with minors to solicit sexually oriented materials from them, including making video calls. Cataline shared explicit materials of himself with others who he believed were minors, but were in fact, undercover agents.

During a search warrant executed on his electronic devices, investigators found more than 120 images and videos on his laptop. Cataline’s cellphones contained more than 2,400 CSAM files including approximately 600 videos and 1,800 images. Several files involved prepubescent minors under the age of 12.

The investigation leading to the indictment was led by the FBI Youngstown Resident Agency, the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force, and the Mentor Police Department.

Tallahassee, Florida – Nathan Taylor Porter, 21, of Tallahassee, Florida, was sentenced after a federal conviction for two counts of possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. The sentence was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida.

U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “This felon’s repeated offenses demonstrated his brazen disregard for the law and posed a threat to the safety of our community. My office remains committed to safeguarding our citizens against the predations of dangerous criminals, like this defendant, and we will continue to aggressively prosecute these cases until our residents get the safe, crime-free streets that they deserve.”

A federal investigation revealed that on October 17, 2025, law enforcement located a loaded .40-caliber pistol in Porter’s backpack during a search. Porter admitted ownership of the firearm. At the time that Porter possessed the firearm, he was a convicted felon and was legally prohibited from possessing firearms or ammunition. While he was awaiting trial in state court for his unlawful firearm possession, Porter was caught with another firearm on March 14, 2026.

Porter was sentenced to 51 months’ imprisonment followed by three years of Supervised Release at the United States Courthouse in Tallahassee by District Judge Allen C. Winsor.

The case was jointly investigated by Homeland Security Investigations, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, the Tallahassee Police Department, and the Leon County Sheriff’s Office. Assistant United States Attorney Joseph A. Ravelo prosecuted the case.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

Washington, DC – Today, Congresswoman Julia Brownley (CA-26) joined Congressman Rick Larsen (WA-02) and Congressman Mark Veasey (TX-33) in introducing the America Votes Act, legislation to protect U.S. citizens who face disenfranchisement because of restrictive voter identification (ID) laws.
Despite claims that restrictive voter ID laws are necessary to prevent voter impersonation, there is no evidence of widespread voter fraud in the United States. Some state legislatures across the country continue to use excessively restrictive voter ID laws to target and deny certain Americans the right to vote. Restrictive voter ID laws disproportionately impact Black and transgender Americans, perpetuating the systematic disenfranchisement of certain groups in the United States.
In 2026, a total of 36 states require voters to show identification to cast a ballot, and 24 of those states require voters to present identification with a photograph. These identification requirements are in addition to those under federal law to register to vote.
The America Votes Act would establish new federal protections for registered voters to affirm their identity by submitting a sworn, written statement, even if they do not have a government-issued ID. Voters who sign a sworn, written statement can vote using a standard, non-provisional ballot. The legislation is modeled on a successful Washington state law that allows voters to affirm their identity by submitting a similar written statement along with their mail-in ballot.
The full text of the America Votes Act can be found here.
In addition to Brownley, the America Votes Act is cosponsored by Representatives Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Betty McCollum (MN-04), and André Carson (IL-07).

The Justice Department announced today the unsealing of an indictment charging Saleem Alzaq, as well as the arrests of Omar Adhami, Abdel Adhami, and Raed Yousef, for their involvement in paying, soliciting and collecting funds for Hamas. In a coordinated law enforcement operation in France, three of Alzaq’s associates, Faouzi Barika, Amel Oualid, and Nordine Barika were arrested by the French General Directorate for Internal Security.

“Anyone who finances or assists terrorist organizations responsible for the deaths of American citizens should expect to be prosecuted by the Department of Justice,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “For decades, members of Hamas have raised funding to carry out brutal terrorist attacks. Under the leadership of President Trump, the Department of Justice will continue pursuing terrorists who kill Americans, dismantling terrorist finance networks, and delivering justice for the families of victims.”

“The FBI will never forget the horrific attack on Israel by Hamas on October 7, 2023 – and we will never stop our efforts to cut off funding to Hamas terrorists,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “These subjects allegedly engaged in a conspiracy that extended beyond national borders to funnel money to Hamas and fuel violent attacks, using cryptocurrency to try to hide their criminal activity. Today's announcement shows the abilities of this FBI and our interagency partners to follow the money and shut down resources going to terrorists under the guise of charitable giving - disrupting over 4,000 Foreign Terrorist organizations and stopping 1,100 alleged terrorist actors here at home and around the world since last year. Special thanks to our FBI New York, New Orleans, and Tampa Field Offices, our Counterterrorism Division, as well as the Paris Legal Attaché's Office and French authorities for their outstanding work with us in this case.”

“Money is the lifeblood of terrorist organizations, and the arrests announced today disrupted a global financing network that was supplying Hamas with the funds needed to continue its campaign of destroying innocent lives,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg, “These coordinated investigations and arrests spanned multiple jurisdictions in the United States and across international borders, and demonstrate that we will use all of our capabilities to eradicate terrorism. I want to thank the FBI agents and federal prosecutors who worked together to dismantle this network, and I also want to thank Joint Task Force 10-7 for its leadership in seeking justice for the victims of the Hamas-led attack in Israel on October 7, 2023, that killed more than 1,200 men, women, and children. My thoughts are with all who are still suffering from the losses of that terrible day, and the National Security Division will never stop working to hold the perpetrators, and those who enabled them, accountable for their atrocities.”

“This Office and our law enforcement partners will root out and prosecute those who finance Hamas, no matter where they are located,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald for the Southern District of New York. “As alleged, Saleem Alzaq was the center of a Hamas financing network that operated around the globe, soliciting more than a million dollars from individual donors including here in the United States. The close cooperation of law enforcement and prosecutors’ offices to dismantle Alzaq’s alleged Hamas financing network demonstrates our commitment to depriving Hamas of the funding it relies on in Gaza and to commit terror attacks like the brutal October 7, 2023, massacre of more than a thousand innocent victims, including dozens of Americans.”

“According to the indictment and complaint filed in the Eastern District of Louisiana, Saleem Alzaq solicited financial donations on behalf of Hamas, a terrorist organization responsible for the commission of heinous attacks worldwide,” said U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle for the Eastern District of Louisiana. “Omar Adhami and Abdel Adhami are accused of providing Alzaq with resources intended to fund Hamas’ relentless reign of terror. The Department of Justice and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Louisiana are laser focused on the identification, prosecution, and eradication of terrorist networks, and the individuals who financially support these networks.”

“According to the indictment and complaint filed in the Eastern District of Louisiana, Saleem Alzaq solicited financial donations on behalf of Hamas, a terrorist organization responsible for the commission of heinous attacks worldwide,” said U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle for the Eastern District of Louisiana. “Omar Adhami and Abdel Adhami are accused of providing Alzaq with resources intended to fund Hamas’ relentless reign of terror. The Department of Justice and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Louisiana are laser focused on the identification, prosecution, and eradication of terrorist networks, and the individuals who financially support these networks.”

“Providing financial assistance and support to terrorist organizations like Hamas place the safety and security of everyone, anywhere in the world, at risk,” said U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe for the Middle District of Florida. “The diligence and cooperation exhibited by our domestic and international law enforcement partners during this investigation demonstrates our collective resolve to relentlessly pursue, disrupt, and prosecute those who engage in these illegal activities.”

“The NYPD’s counterterrorism work knows no borders,” said NYPD Commissioner Jessica S. Tisch. “Our intelligence analysts uncovered this international finance network and built the case that exposed more than $2 million being funneled to Hamas. Saleem Alzaq, a leader in Hamas’ military arm responsible for planning and carrying out terrorist attacks, and the other defendants allegedly solicited donations under the guise of humanitarian aid and then directed that money to Hamas. This is the kind of extraordinary counterterrorism work the NYPD does every day to disrupt threats before they reach New Yorkers, and I thank our law enforcement partners for helping us dismantle this network.”

According to the Alzaq indictment unsealed in the Southern District of New York, the Adhami complaints filed in the Eastern District of Louisiana, and the Yousef indictment filed in the Middle District of Florida:

Alzaq, 45, of Gaza, is a Hamas member in the Gaza Strip and a battalion deputy in the Izz al-Din al-Qassam Brigades (the Al-Qassam Brigades), Hamas’s armed wing responsible for planning and executing terrorist attacks. Alzaq serves in the Photography Department of the Al-Qassam Brigades’ Shujaiyya Brigade Media Office, a Hamas propaganda office. In this role, he has photographed Hamas events, including events led by senior Hamas leaders such as Ismail Haniyeh and Yahya Sinwar. He distributes these photographs and descriptions of Hamas events to others involved in the Hamas propaganda apparatus. He has also posted Hamas propaganda across multiple social media platforms, including posts glorifying deceased leaders of Hamas (such as Sheikh Ahmed Yassin, Haniyeh, and Sinwar); supporting Al-Qassam Brigades terrorists and glorifying Al-Qassam Brigades “martyrs;” and promoting and celebrating Hamas’s October 7, 2023, terrorist attacks against Southern Israel, in which more than 1,200 victims were murdered and more than 250 were taken hostage, including 46 American citizens.

Since at least about January 2020, Alzaq has operated an international Hamas fundraising network that collects donations from individuals around the world, including from individuals in the United States. Alzaq promotes this fundraising through social media campaigns purportedly providing humanitarian aid to people in Gaza, while the money is funneled to Hamas. Since January 2020, Alzaq has collected more than $1.7 million through purported charitable campaigns. Alzaq’s associates in France, Barika, Amel Oualid, and others assisted Alzaq in collecting and transferring money raised for Hamas.

Abdel Adhami, 35, and Omar Adhami, 33, both of Covington, Louisiana, donated funds to Alzaq’s Hamas financing network. Beginning in approximately February 2021, and continuing through approximately September 2026, Abdel Adhami allegedly contributed approximately $94,000 and Omar Adhami allegedly contributed approximately $11,000 to Hamas, a designated terrorist organization, knowing that the organization engaged in terrorist activities, and attempted to conceal their contributions to Hamas through wire transfers, and the use of intermediaries. Yousef, a resident of Lutz, Florida, provided almost $50,000 to Alzaq’s Hamas financing network.

Alzaq is charged with conspiring to provide material support to Hamas, a designated foreign terrorist organization, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; conspiring to violate the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; conspiring to commit money laundering, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; and conspiring to defraud the United States, which carries a maximum penalty of five years in prison.

Omar Adhami is charged with providing material support to a Foreign Terrorist Organization, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; conspiracy to provide material support to a Foreign Terrorist Organization, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; conspiracy to commit wire fraud, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; and conspiring to commit money laundering, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison.

Abdel Adhami is charged with providing material support to a Foreign Terrorist Organization, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; conspiracy to provide material support to a Foreign Terrorist Organization, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; conspiracy to commit wire fraud, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; and conspiring to commit money laundering, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison.

Raed Yousef, 56, of Lutz, Florida, is charged with one count of conspiring to provide material support to a foreign terrorist organization, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; five counts of attempting to provide material support to a foreign terrorist organization, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison on each count; one count of providing funds, goods, and services to a specially designated terrorist, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in federal prison; five counts of attempting to provide funds, goods, and services to a specially designated terrorist, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in person on each count; one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in federal prison; five counts of money laundering, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in federal prison on each count; and one count of passport fraud, which carries a maximum penalty of 5 years in federal prison.

The Alzaq case is being investigated by the FBI with the assistance of the New York Police Department (NYPD). Assistant U.S. Attorneys David A. Markewitz, Ben Arad, Sarah L. Kushner, Juliana N. Murray, and Keith Savino for the Southern District of New York are prosecuting the case, with assistance from Trial Attorneys Rob MacDonald and A.J. Dixon of the National Security Division’s Counterterrorism Section. The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs provided significant assistance.

The Adhami case is being investigated by the FBI New Orleans Field Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Greg Kennedy for the Eastern District of Louisiana is prosecuting the case.

The Yousef case is being investigated by the FBI. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Lindsey Schmidt and Michael Buchanan for the Middle District of Florida are prosecuting the case.

An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

MUSKOGEE, OKLAHOMA – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Oklahoma announced that Deaundray Chrisshawn Williams, age 36, of Okmulgee, Oklahoma, was sentenced to thirty-seven months in prison for one count of Felon in Possession of Firearm.

The charge arose from an investigation by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, the Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation, and the Okmulgee Police Department.

On September 23, 2025, Williams pleaded guilty to the charge. According to investigators, on December 15, 2024, law enforcement discovered Williams in possession of a revolver after having previously been convicted of a crime punishable by more than one year imprisonment.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America , PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities.

The Honorable John A. Woodcock, Jr., Senior Judge in the United States District Court for the District of Maine, sitting by designation, presided over the hearing in Muskogee, Oklahoma. Williams will remain in the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service pending transportation to a designated United States Bureau of Prisons facility to serve a non-paroleable sentence of incarceration.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Lewis M. Reagan represented the United States.

Brown, Casar Demand Answers on FBI’s Plan to Buy Mass Surveillance Systems, Including Flock Cameras
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Shontel Brown (OH-11) and Congressman Greg Casar (TX-35) sent a letter demanding answers and transparency from the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director Kash Patel on the FBI’s planned increase of mass surveillance systems, such as Flock.
Brown and Casar both serve on the House Committee on Oversight. Brown is Ranking Member on the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation, Casar is Ranking Member on the Subcommittee on Federal Law Enforcement.
In May 2026, the FBI issued a Request for Proposals (RFP) to acquire automatic license plate readers (ALPR) systems, including Flock and Motorola Solutions, that offer the ability to search for license plate information “and other descriptive data such as vehicle description information, time/date criteria, and geo-location criteria.” Flock and Motorola Solutions, whose ALPR systems are used by local police departments, likely possess the capabilities to satisfy this RFP. While the FBI already runs a License Plate Reader (LPR) program through the National Crime Information Center (NCIC) to facilitate LPR information sharing with and between its law enforcement partners, the FBI’s plan to obtain direct access to an extensive network of cameras—such as those operated by Flock and Motorola—would dramatically expand the license plate data currently held by the FBI and institute “near real time” surveillance of civilians.
The Members of Congress write: “The American people are clearly concerned about law enforcement having access to Flock data and about government surveillance more broadly. Entering into a contract that would give the nation’s largest law enforcement agency access to Flock data across the country would subvert the clear preference of the American people.”
The Oversight and Government Reform Committee Democrats are requesting information by October 16, 2026.
Read the full letter here.

Today, the Federal Trade Commission, joined by the Utah and Nevada Attorneys General, sued to stop a long-running deceptive pricing scheme run by contact lens retailer Lens.com Inc.
In a joint complaint, the FTC, Utah and Nevada allege that Lens.com, along with its owner Cary Samourkachian and an affiliated entity Speed Commerce LLC (together referred to as Lens.com), advertise artificially low prices for contact lenses but then charge consumers much higher prices through substantial, mandatory “Taxes & fees” charges.
Lens.com’s hidden fees routinely double the price it advertises for contact lenses, costing consumers hundreds of millions of dollars, the joint complaint alleges.
“Millions of Americans rely on contact lenses to perform their daily tasks,” said Christopher Mufarrige, Director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection. “Lens.com advertised one price for contact lenses but charged a substantially higher price at checkout, deceiving consumers about the cost of this healthcare necessity. The FTC’s joint action today with Utah and Nevada underscores the agency’s commitment to lowering healthcare costs for consumers by stopping deceptive businesses practices that raise prices and harm Americans.”
The complaint also alleges that this “Taxes & fees” charge is buried deep in the checkout process and is never clearly and conspicuously disclosed to consumers. According to the complaint, Lens.com has also used deceptive pricing practices in connection with its “AutoRefill” subscription plan, which automatically charges consumers for recurring shipments of contact lenses, the complaint alleges.
These deceptive pricing practices obscure the total price of contact lenses, preventing customers from determining what they will really pay and thus from being able to compare Lens.com’s prices against competitors’ prices, the complaint further alleges.
According to the joint complaint, Lens.com deceived consumers in the following ways:
- Lens.com prominently advertises eye-catching, artificially low prices in sponsored Google search ads and on its website, www.lens.com. In reality, the advertised prices bear little resemblance to what consumers ultimately pay for contact lenses because Lens.com imposes a mandatory, substantial “Taxes & fees” charge at checkout.
- Lens.com hides the “Taxes & fees” line item during the checkout process, hiding the line item below the viewable portion of the screen while encouraging consumers to click a prominent “Continue” button to proceed with the checkout process rather than scroll down. Consumers who click the “Continue” prompt never see the “Taxes & fees” line item at all.
- Lens.com also deceives consumers regarding the nature of the “Taxes & fees” charge. That label misleadingly suggests the charge includes state sales taxes. In fact, many states exempt contact lenses from state sales taxes or have no sales taxes at all, yet Lens.com uses the label “Taxes & fees” anyway.
- Lens.com uses these same deceptively low prices to induce consumers to enroll in AutoRefill, a negative option plan, and fails to clearly and conspicuously disclose the same hidden and misleading “Taxes & fees” charge before obtaining consumers’ billing information.
- Lens.com also fails to clearly and conspicuously disclose how to cancel the AutoRefill subscription and the deadline by which consumers must cancel to avoid incurring charges for a future shipment—burying that information outside of the AutoRefill purchase flow.
The FTC, Utah and Nevada allege these practices violate the FTC Act, the Restore Online Shoppers’ Confidence Act (ROSCA), the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (GLB Act), the Utah Consumer Sales Practices Act (Utah CSPA), the Utah Automatic Renewal Contracts Act (Utah ARCA) and Nevada Deceptive Trade Practices Act (Nevada DTPA).
The Commission vote authorizing the staff to file the complaint was 2-0. The FTC filed the complaint in the U.S. District Court for the District of Nevada.
NOTE: The Commission files a complaint when it has “reason to believe” that the named defendants are violating or are about to violate the law and it appears to the Commission that a proceeding is in the public interest. The case will be decided by the court.
The Federal Trade Commission works to promote competition and protect and educate consumers. The FTC will never demand money, make threats, tell you to transfer money, or promise you a prize. Learn more about consumer topics at consumer.ftc.gov, or report fraud, scams, and bad business practices at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. Follow the FTC on social media, read consumer alerts and the business blog, and sign up to get the latest FTC news and alerts.
title: FTC, States Sue Lens.com for Misrepresenting the Price of Contact Lenses in Search Ads and on Its Website

Washington, DC -- U.S. Representative Jim Himes (D-CT), Ranking Member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and Senator Mark R. Warner (D-VA), Vice Chairman of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, wrote to Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton regarding the upcoming midterm election, urging transparency to Congress and the public around possible foreign threats to the midterms.
“Career intelligence community (IC) analysts recently briefed the House Committee about the latest assessments regarding foreign threats to the upcoming midterms,” the lawmakers wrote. “These briefings, as well as additional briefings given to staff of both committees, provided valuable insight into how our intelligence professionals are monitoring potential attempts by our adversaries to influence or interfere in U.S. elections, and how such foreign malign activity compares to prior cycles. Between now and Election Day, it is critical the IC continue to inform policymakers, state and local election administrators, and the American people about threats to our elections.”
They continued, “While we have received the first in a series of statutorily required reports about foreign adversaries targeting this election, there are still several outstanding statutorily required products owed to the Committees. It is essential that the IC complete production of its remaining assessments in a timely manner, so that policymakers remain up-to-date regarding any emerging intelligence or shifts in the analytic line before the midterm elections. This process should include the declassification and public issuance of the Intelligence Community Assessment (ICA) about foreign threats to the 2024 presidential election. The lack of a public ICA contravenes the law and undercuts needed transparency about IC efforts to keep our elections secure from outside interference.”
In addition to these statutory requirements, the lawmakers requested a full interagency classified update for members before the election, a commitment to provide real-time notification about emerging threats to elections, and the responsible release of unclassified election assessments to keep the public informed about possible threats and other relevant context.
“A statement noting the absence of indications of significant foreign interference efforts is just as important as a statement exposing any such activities. Regardless, the American people should receive as much information as we can responsibly provide prior to the election,” they concluded. 
Read the full letter here.
title: Himes, Warner Push for Transparency on Election Security

EPA Finalizes Groundwater Cleanup Plan for Hopewell Precision Superfund Site in Dutchess County, New York
NEW YORK – The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has finalized the update to its original cleanup plan to address trichloroethylene, or TCE, contamination at the Hopewell Precision Superfund Site in Hopewell Junction, New York. The update to the plan will address groundwater that was contaminated by past industrial practices at the Hopewell Precision, Inc., facility, where solvents and chemicals were improperly managed in the past.
“Finalizing this cleanup plan is a major step forward for Hopewell Junction and a powerful investment in the community’s future,” said EPA Regional Administrator Michael Martucci. “By advancing this work, we are protecting clean water and air, strengthening public confidence, and delivering meaningful progress for residents today and for generations to come.”
The final cleanup plan is to rely on natural processes that are already reducing the levels of contaminants with a goal of meeting drinking water standards. This cleanup method is called monitored natural attenuation. EPA will regularly monitor and test the groundwater to ensure that natural processes—like biological or chemical reactions—are safely breaking down the contamination.
Former manufacturing operations contaminated groundwater at the site with volatile organic compounds, or VOCs. EPA is formalizing local municipal ordinances currently in place, which already require well testing for any water source outside the municipal system and allows the community to use water sourced from non-public systems for non-drinking purposes only. Residents were already connected to an alternative water supply, and specialized systems were installed on some homes to vent vapors that were seeping into the home from the groundwater.
EPA thoroughly reviewed and considered public comments submitted during the comment period before selecting the final cleanup plan.
The Record of Decision, EPA’s response to comments and supporting documents will be available on the Hopewell Precision Superfund site profile page.

PITTSBURGH, Pa. - A resident of North Braddock, Pennsylvania, has been indicted by a federal grand jury in Pittsburgh on charges of social security fraud, United States Attorney Troy Rivetti announced today.

The two-count Indictment named Daniel M. Wallar, 70, as the sole defendant, and was unsealed today upon Wallar’s arrest.

According to the Indictment, from June 3, 2019, until May 30, 2025, Wallar—who was named as the representative payee on another person’s Social Security benefit account—unlawfully converted such payments for purposes other than for the use and benefit of that individual. Wallar is charged at Count One with theft of public money and at Count Two with representative payee misuse.

As to Count One, the law provides for a term of imprisonment of up to 10 years, a fine of up to $250,000, or both. As to Count Two, the law provides for a maximum sentence of up to five years in prison, a fine of up to $250,000, or both. Under the federal Sentencing Guidelines, the actual sentence imposed would be based upon the seriousness of the offenses and the prior criminal history, if any, of the defendant.

Executive Assistant United States Attorney Carolyn J. Bloch is prosecuting this case on behalf of the government.

The Social Security Administration Office of the Inspector General conducted the investigation leading to the Indictment.

An indictment is an accusation. A defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.

NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA – JOSHUA PAUL FALGOUT (“FALGOUT”) ,age 32, of Houma, Louisiana, was charged on September 25, 2026 in a recently unsealed indictment with Receipt of Materials Involving the Sexual Exploitation of Minors, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Sections 2252 (a)(2), and (b)(1), announced U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle.

According to the indictment, beginning on a date unknown, and continuing until on or about March 26, 2026, FALGOUT knowingly received visual depictions of minors engaging in sexually explicit conduct.

FALGOUT faces a minimum of five (5) years up to a maximum of twenty (20) years in prison, followed by a term of supervised release for five (5) years up to life. A $100.00 mandatory special assessment fee and a fine of up to $250,000 are also applicable. If convicted, FALGOUT will be required to register as a sex offender.

U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle reiterated that the indictment is merely a charge and that the guilt of the defendant must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt.

U.S. Attorney Courcelle praised the work of Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Louisiana State Police in investigating this case. Assistant United States Attorney and Human Trafficking and Child Exploitation Task Force Leader Maria M. Carboni of the Public Integrity Unit is in charge of the prosecution.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC .

TRENTON, N.J. – Two more defendants have admitted to their roles in an $11 million conspiracy to defraud banks by depositing stolen checks and withdrawing the funds, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced.

The following individuals each pleaded guilty before U.S. District Judge Michael A. Shipp in Trenton federal court to a one-count Information charging them with conspiracy to commit bank fraud:

Raymond Wade, 43, of Morrisville, Pennsylvania, pleaded guilty on September 28, 2026. Sentencing is scheduled for December 17, 2026.

Dwayne Reddon, 40, of Trenton, New Jersey, pleaded guilty on September 29, 2026. Sentencing is scheduled for February 9, 2027.

Between July 21, 2026 and August 4, 2026, eight other individuals pleaded guilty for their roles in the same conspiracy. Charges remain pending against Wayne Bessant, 45, of Hamilton, New Jersey, and Ryan Small, 33, of Ewing, New Jersey.

According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court:

From March 2023 through June 2025, the Defendants conspired to deposit stolen checks—including U.S. Department of Treasury checks—at various banks in New Jersey and Pennsylvania. The conspirators impersonated the businesses or individuals listed as payees on the stolen checks, often by acquiring business documents in the names of the payees. Once the conspirators acquired fraudulent business documents or opened fraudulent bank accounts, they deposited the stolen checks and split the proceeds. In total, the conspirators deposited or attempted to deposit over 100 Treasury and commercial checks totaling over $11 million. Many of the Treasury checks were refunds issued as Employee Retention Credits, a program the Internal Revenue Service created during the COVID-19 pandemic to encourage businesses to retain employees.

The bank fraud conspiracy charge is punishable by a maximum potential penalty of 30 years in prison and also carries a fine of up to $1,000,000, twice the gross amount of any pecuniary gain that any persons derived from the offense, or twice the gross amount of any pecuniary loss sustained by any victims of the offense.

U.S. Attorney Frazer credited special agents with the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Newark-Trenton Resident Agency under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy; special agents with Homeland Security Investigations, Cherry Hill, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Michael S. McCarthy; special agents with the Internal Revenue Service – Criminal Investigation, Newark Field Office, under the direction of Jenifer L. Piovesan; special agents with Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration, Northeast Field Division, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Michael Carpenter; special agents with the Defense Criminal Investigative Service, Northeast Field Office, under the direction of Acting Special Agent in Charge Jessica Herrington; special agents with the U.S. Air Force – Office of Special Investigations, Detachment 307, Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst, New Jersey, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Rebecca B. Bates; and postal inspectors of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Philadelphia Division, under the direction of Inspector in Charge, Christopher Nielson, with the investigation leading to the guilty pleas.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

Anyone with information about allegations of attempted fraud involving COVID-19 can report it by calling the Department of Justice’s National Center for Disaster Fraud Hotline at 866-720-5721 or via the NCDF Web Form at: https://www.justice.gov/disaster-fraud/ncdf-disaster-complaint-form .

The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorney Benjamin D. Bleiberg and Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Alanna M. Jereb of the Economic Crimes Unit in Newark.

WASHINGTON, DC – Congressman Rob Menendez (NJ-08) and Congressman August Pfluger (TX-11) introduced the bipartisan Submarine Cable Security Policy Act of 2026, which would streamline the Federal Communications Commission (“FCC”) permitting process for undersea cables while carefully vetting projects for national security concerns.

“Submarine cables are critical to our economy and national security, carrying the internet and communications traffic that Americans rely on every day,” said Congressman Menendez. “I am proud to co-lead this bipartisan legislation with Rep. Pfluger to establish a clear and consistent permitting process, provide greater certainty for responsible projects, and ensure that cables with potential national security risks receive the scrutiny they deserve.”

“Our foreign adversaries are investing in the undersea cables that carry over 95% of our international data, and they're doing it to undermine our national and economic security. The United States Submarine Cable Security Policy Act of 2026 sets clear, consistent security standards so we can keep bad actors out of our critical infrastructure,” said Congressman Pfluger.

The legislation would standardize the U.S. licensing process for undersea cables, establish national security requirements, set FCC review timelines, allow certain applicants to use self-certification and expedited review, and provide additional scrutiny for projects that raise foreign adversary or other national security concerns.

Read the full bill text here.
title: Menendez Introduces Legislation to Establish Permitting Process for Undersea Cables and Protect National Security Interests
