NASA is seeking leaders for one of the most esteemed positions on Earth for human spaceflight: flight director in mission control at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. This role is critical to advancing American leadership in space exploration, as NASA paves the way for a sustained human presence on the Moon.

Applications for new flight directors are open now through Monday, Oct. 12. U.S. citizens can apply at:

https://www.usajobs.gov/GetJob/ViewDetails/886788000

Those chosen as NASA flight directors will lead human spaceflight missions to the International Space Station , Artemis missions to the Moon, and, eventually, the first human missions to Mars.

Flight directors lead teams of flight controllers, astronauts, and commercial and international partners in real-time mission execution and risk management. In preparation for a mission, flight directors collaborate with engineering, safety, and program partners to ensure operational plans align with spacecraft capabilities and mission objectives.

“We are working in an exciting, pivotal time as we continue supporting operations to the International Space Station while building the next phase of human spaceflight with Artemis and Moon Base missions, preparing to go farther than ever before,” said Emily Nelson, chief flight director at Johnson. “Accomplishing these ambitious goals requires flight directors who are expert integrators, bringing together a broad range of teams and disciplines into a clear, unified mission effort. This integral role exemplifies the best of innovation and teamwork.”

To be considered, flight director candidates must be U.S. citizens with a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in engineering, biological science, physical science, computer science, or mathematics. They also will need substantial related, progressively responsible professional experience, including time-critical decision-making experience in high-stress, high-risk environments. Although many NASA flight directors have previously been flight controllers working in mission control, it is not a prerequisite to apply.

NASA plans to announce selections by the end of the year. The new flight directors will receive extensive training in flight control and spacecraft systems, as well as operational leadership and risk management.

Learn more about NASA flight directors and the application process at:

go.nasa.gov/BeAFlightDirector

Oct. 2, 2026
The image is from a 16th-century painting titled ‘The Virgin and Child Enthroned’
WILLIAMSTOWN, MA — The Postal Service has released a new Christmas stamp featuring a depiction of the Madonna and Child from a painting in the collection of the Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute in Williamstown, MA. The stamp was issued today without a ceremony.
“This painting caught my eye because of the beautiful red folds in the Madonna’s dress and the unusual background,” said Greg Breeding, an art director for USPS. “I also love the ornate patterns behind Mary’s head, and the figures and symbols in the background intrigue me. There are more detailed background and context than we sometimes see in Madonna and Child paintings, and I find it unusually interesting and beautiful.”
Art history in the mail: The story behind the 16th-century painting now on a stamp
The stamp features a richly symbolic depiction of the Virgin Mary and the Christ child painted around the year 1500. Distinctive for its large central figure of Mary in red garments and an array of background details, the oil-on-panel painting, known by its modern title “The Virgin and Child Enthroned,” is in the collection of the Clark Art Institute.
Mary’s red garments are detailed with gold and jewels and she is wearing a jeweled band with pearls on her head — all signs of her exalted status. In her lap sits the Christ child dressed in white, resting one small hand on a decorated book of hours — a collection of prayers for different times of day.
Behind Mary is a brocade textile with gold and silver threads, dignifying her with its preciousness. Angels appear in the background to the viewer’s left, while on the right side, two small human figures at a rampart behold a Dutch city with scenes of daily life — a detail typical of Netherlandish painting — and the heavenly Jerusalem far beyond it. At Mary’s feet is an area rich in foliage believed to represent a walled garden.
Art historians have documented the numerous Christian symbols in this painting. The Christ child wears a necklace that includes a red carbuncle — an indicator of martyrdom — and a pearl, which symbolizes salvation. Pomegranates on the textile behind the figures suggest fertility and resurrection. According to the Clark Art Institute, other likely symbols include a small dog that stands for faith, a glimpse of plantains growing along the road to salvation, and strawberries as symbols of righteousness and good works. The walled garden has been interpreted as a symbol of Mary’s virginity.
This stamp continues a tradition of U.S. stamps featuring Madonna and Child paintings that began in 1966, four years after the debut of the first Christmas stamp. Madonna and Child stamps were issued nearly every year until 2009, with occasional departures to show other traditional Christmas imagery such as angels or Nativity scenes.
The Postal Service printed 185 million Christmas stamps that will be issued in booklets of 20. As Forever stamps, they will always be equal in value to the current First-Class Mail 1-ounce price. News of the stamps is being shared with the hashtag #MadonnaAndChildStamp.
Postal Products
Customers may purchase these stamps and other philatelic products through The Postal Store at usps.com/shopstamps, by calling 844-737-7826, by mail through USA Philatelic, or at Post Office locations nationwide. For officially licensed stamp products, shop the USPS Officially Licensed Collection on Amazon. Additional information on stamps, first-day-of-issue ceremonies and stamp-inspired products can be found at stampsforever.com.

Navy Announces Commissioning of the Future USS Ted Stevens
WHITTIER, Alaska — The U.S. Navy will commission its newest Flight III Arleigh Burke-class destroyer, USS Ted Stevens (DDG 128), on Saturday, Oct. 3, at 12 p.m. AKDT in Whittier, Alaska.
The commissioning of USS Ted Stevens delivers an immediate, decisive expansion in surface fleet lethality and global deterrence. Engineered to prevail in contested environments, the warship integrates the AN/SPY-6(V)1 Air and Missile Defense Radar and Aegis Baseline 10 combat system, establishing unparalleled Integrated Air and Missile Defense (IAMD) capabilities across simultaneous anti-air warfare and ballistic missile defense operational profiles.
The ship and its commissioning location honor the legacy of the late Senator Ted Stevens, who was a decorated Army Air Corps pilot in World War II, flying hazardous transport missions over "The Hump" in the China-Burma-India theater. Returning to Alaska following World War II, he became a champion of Alaska statehood. Stevens later served in the U.S. Senate from December 1968 until January 2009, where he served as the president pro tempore in the 108th and 109th Congresses and was the third U.S. Senator to hold the title of president pro tempore emeritus. In the Senate, Stevens promoted national security, worked to strengthen our military with modern weapons, new facilities, and improved pay and benefits. Selecting Whittier highlights Alaska's critical strategic geography and reinforces the Navy’s persistent operational readiness to secure vital high-latitude sea lanes and defend the homeland.
The ship’s sponsors are Mrs. Catherine Ann Stevens, Senator Stevens’ wife, and his daughters, Mrs. Susan Stevens Covich and Mrs. Lily Stevens Becker. In accordance with naval tradition, the sponsors will order the crew to “Man our ship and bring her to life!” As sponsors, they will represent the ship's enduring connection to the Stevens family throughout the vessel's operational lifetime.
From the North Pacific campaigns of World War II to current Arctic operations, the Navy and Alaska have maintained a shared commitment to defending the nation’s northernmost sea lanes. Today, the Navy maintains a persistent operational presence in Alaska by conducting high-latitude maritime security patrols, cold-weather warfare training, and joint-force exercises designed to project decisive naval power, secure critical sea lanes, and defend the homeland.
Following commissioning, USS Ted Stevens will transit to its homeport in Norfolk, Virginia, joining the operational fleet fully prepared to deploy in support of national defense priorities and global maritime security.
The commissioning of the USS Ted Stevens (DDG 128) underscores the Navy's commitment to building America’s Golden Fleet. For 250 years, American naval power has projected strength globally. That mission continues – and intensifies. We operate forward 24/7, 365 days a year. This operational tempo demands continuous capability delivery, and the Golden Fleet is our answer.
The commissioning ceremony will stream on the Defense Video Information Distribution Service (DVIDS) at https://www.dvidshub.net/webcast/38076. The live stream will begin at 11:50 a.m. EDT, and the ceremony will begin at 12:00 p.m. AKDT on Oct. 3.
Media may direct queries to the Navy Office of Information at (703) 697-5342.
More information on the Destroyer Program can be found at: https://www.navy.mil/Resources/Fact-Files/Display-FactFiles/Article/2169871/destroyers-ddg-51/.

text:
MIAMI – Former U.S. Congressman David Rivera was sentenced today to 10 years in federal prison for secretly acting as an unregistered agent of the Venezuelan government and laundering millions of dollars connected to that work.

U.S. District Judge Melissa Damian imposed the sentence after a federal jury convicted Rivera, 61, of conspiracy to violate the Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA), violating FARA, conspiracy to commit money laundering, and four counts of engaging in transactions in criminally derived property.

“Today’s sentence reinforces a simple rule: foreign influence in America cannot operate in the shadows,” said U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida. “If you act at the request, direction, or control of a foreign government and engage in covered political activity, you must comply with our disclosure laws. That can include conduct like arranging a meeting with policymakers, lobbying a government official, or promoting a foreign government’s message on social media.

“For a former Congressman from South Florida, this betrayal cuts especially deep. Rivera represented a community shaped by generations of families who fled communist oppression and came to this country seeking freedom. He knew that history. He knew what this community had endured. Yet the jury found that, for millions of dollars, he secretly used the access and relationships entrusted to him to advance the interests of the Maduro regime.

“Today’s sentence of 10 years is the consequence of that choice. In South Florida, we will aggressively enforce the laws that protect our country and our communities from covert foreign influence.”

“Today’s sentencing represents a meaningful step toward restoring public trust in the integrity of our democratic processes,” said Special Agent in Charge Brett D. Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office. “It also demonstrates the impact of federal partners working together and combining their investigative expertise. And no attempt to conceal unlawful conduct will remain beyond the FBI’s reach.”

“This case shows that laundering illicit funds in the United States will not go unchecked,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Charles E. Miller of the IRS Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI) Florida Field Office. “The partnership between IRS-CI and our law enforcement counterparts was vital in exposing this operation and protecting the integrity of the U.S. financial system.”

According to court records and evidence presented at trial, Rivera and co-defendant Esther Nuhfer obtained a $50 million contract with a subsidiary of Venezuela’s state-owned and state-controlled oil company, Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. (PDVSA), to advance the interests of the Venezuelan regime in the U.S. Without registering as foreign agents as required by law, Rivera and Nuhfer lobbied U.S. officials, including then-U.S. Senator Marco Rubio and U.S. Representative Pete Sessions, and arranged meetings between U.S. policymakers and high-ranking Venezuelan officials, including then-President Nicolás Maduro and then-Foreign Minister Delcy Rodríguez. Rivera and Nuhfer used coded language in text messages to describe their activities.

The evidence at trial further showed that Rivera deposited approximately $1.5 million in proceeds from the contract to his Florida state congressional campaign account between March 2017 and August 2018, among other personnel uses. Nuhfer used approximately $455,000 in proceeds to purchase a residence in Key Colony Beach.

Nuhfer, 52, who was convicted at trial of conspiracy to violate FARA, violating FARA, conspiracy to commit money laundering, and engaging in a transaction in criminally derived property, was previously sentenced to 60 months in federal prison.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Harold Schimkat and Roger Cruz, along with Trial Attorney David Ryan of the Justice Department’s National Security Division, are prosecuting the case.

FBI Miami and IRS-CI Florida Field Office are investigating the case. This investigation is supported by the Treasury Executive Office for Asset Forfeiture (TEOAF).

Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Southern District of Florida at www.flsd.uscourts.gov or at http://pacer.flsd.uscourts.gov , under case numbers 22-cr-20552.

###
title: Former US Congressman Sentenced to 10 Years in Federal Prison for Secretly Acting as Agent of Venezuelan Government

The Department of War today issued a memorandum to accelerate the lawful, safe, and effective employment of counter-unmanned aircraft systems (c-UAS) across the Department.
The memorandum, Accelerating Employment of Counter-Unmanned Aircraft Systems to Protect American Airspace Sovereignty, directs the Department of War to eliminate unnecessary barriers that delay c-UAS capabilities for forces, installations, and assets.
The policy requires approval authorities to treat delays as an operational risk; use relevant prior approvals, test data and risk mitigations to accelerate comparable decisions; and use interim, conditional, or time-bound approvals when testing supports low or manageable risk.
Any denial of requested c-UAS employment must be documented with a rationale and submitted to Joint Interagency Task Force-401 (JIATF-401). Every approval barrier must have a designated owner, timeline, and escalation path. If an approval authority does not act within 30 days, the requestor will notify the office of the Secretary of War.
The memorandum targets four barriers that have delayed fielding of c-UAS capabilities:
Authorities to operate: Within 30 days, the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer, working with the DoW Chief Information Officer (CIO) and other Department organizations, will establish a single Department-wide c-UAS process to reduce approval timelines for tested and validated systems from months to days or weeks.
Spectrum certification and frequency: The CIO will review the c-UAS spectrum-request process and recommend ways to accelerate approvals. The Department will support the Defense Innovation Unit’s Project Spectrum Strike, an automated, AI‑driven software to coordinate, authorize, and deconflict U.S. government radio spectrum use to incorporate c-UAS spectrum-management requirements.
Weapons safety: Services will not repeat a weapons safety review for the same system, configuration and use case unless a material change creates a new risk. JIATF-401 will synchronize c-UAS weapons safety reviews with the Unmanned Systems Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager.
Legal reviews: Required reviews for c-UAS weapons and weapon systems will be expedited, generally within 10 days after receipt of necessary information. Components will share completed reviews to support timely, consistent decisions.
The memorandum does not change existing policies or procedures governing operational c-UAS use, including activities under 10 U.S.C. § 130i, and does not authorize violations of law or compromises to public or Service member safety.
title: Department of War Accelerates Counter-UAS Employment to Defend American Airspace Sovereignty

Congressmen Goldman and Bentz Introduce the IMD CARE Act for Patients Suffering from Serious Mental Illnesses
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman Dan Goldman (D-NY) and Congressman Cliff Bentz (R-OR) introduced the IMD CARE Act, legislation which would expand Medicaid eligibility to include psychiatric care facility beds in excess of the current 16 bed limit for patients suffering from severe mental illness.
When the Social Security Act was enacted in 1965, it limited Medicaid funding to psychiatric facilities that had no more than 16 beds, resulting in a shortage of beds when the need for inpatient mental health care has grown.
The IMD CARE Act would amend the Social Security Act to establish a State Plan Amendment, allowing Institutions of Mental Diseases (IMDs) with more than 16 beds to receive Medicaid funding for all mental health patients.
Under current law, States that wish to receive federal Medicaid funding for IMDs with over 16 beds must submit a request for a waiver allowing them to receive Medicaid reimbursement for individuals needing psychiatric care.
These waivers are temporary, unstable, and require complex renewal negotiations.
The State Plan Amendment option included in the IMD CARE Act would provide predictable reimbursement structures, durable financing mechanisms, and greater continuity for patients and providers. States would be required to ensure a robust continuum of care including providing outpatient and community-based mental health care and wrap-around services. States would also be required to follow evidence-based clinical criteria for admitting and transitioning patients from institutional care.
The bill is endorsed by the National Association of State Mental Health Program Directors, National Association for Behavioral Health, Treatment Advocacy Center, National Shattering Silence Coalition, and Meadows Mental Health Policy Institute.
“Outdated Medicaid restrictions on long-term mental health care have left too many Americans in crisis without access to treatment,” Congressman Goldman said. “By allowing states more authority to expand their mental health services, we can reach more Americans who are stuck in a never-ending cycle of hospitals, jail, and the streets. This legislation is a critical step towards ensuring that everyone, regardless of income, can get the help they need with dignity.”
Said Congressman Bentz: “Studies show that a significant portion of the homeless and prison population suffer from severe mental illness. These people would benefit from the availability of proper treatment in our existing mental healthcare facilities. This bill would result in an increased number of beds and treatment available for mentally ill people. Without this improvement in how we deliver mental health services, those who need such treatment will continue to cost communities more in law enforcement and healthcare expenses. The circular progression of the mentally ill from the street to the hospital to the prison and back to the street must stop.”
“When someone on Medicaid is experiencing a mental health crisis, the program often won’t cover a psychiatric hospital bed. That’s because of a rule written in 1965,” said Scott Dziengelski, President and CEO of the National Association for Behavioral Healthcare. “A 60-year-old rule shouldn’t keep people from getting the care they need today. The IMD CARE Act takes an important step toward fixing that.”
Congressman Dan Goldman is committed to alleviating the mental health crisis in America. In 2025, he introduced the ‘Michelle Alyssa Go Act’ to increase the number of federal Medicaid-eligible in-patient psychiatric beds for individuals who are seeking treatment for both mental health and substance use disorders.
Full bill text here.

title: Congressmen Goldman and Bentz Introduce the IMD CARE Act for Patients Suffering from Serious Mental Illnesses

Coast Guard, partner agencies respond to an oil spill in Huntington Beach Harbor, California
U.S. Coast Guard Southwest District Phone: 206-815-6689
LOS ANGELES — The Coast Guard, California Department of Fish and Wildlife's Office of Spill Prevention and Response, Huntington Beach Fire Department, and Orange County Sheriff’s Harbor Patrol responded to an oil spill in Huntington Beach Harbor on Wednesday.
Coast Guard Sector Los Angeles-Long Beach command center watchstanders received a call at 2:10 p.m. Wednesday reporting a 40-foot pleasure craft that caught fire.
Huntington Beach Fire Department personnel arrived on scene and began firefighting efforts using extinguishing foam; however, the vessel subsequently sank at approximately 4 p.m. within its slip.
Due to an active discharge of diesel fuel, the Huntington Beach Fire Department personnel deployed containment boom and absorbent pads to contain the spill.
The Coast Guard Sector Los Angeles-Long Beach Federal On-Scene Coordinator activated the Oil Spill Liability Trust Fund and contracted an Oil Spill Response Organization to begin oil spill removal activities.
The vessel’s maximum potential fuel and oil capacity is estimated at 520 gallons. The actual amount discharged and the cause of the fire remain under investigation.
There have been no reports of injuries or wildlife impacts. Cleanup efforts are ongoing.
For more information follow us on Facebook, X and Instagram.

title: Coast Guard, partner agencies respond to an oil spill in Huntington Beach Harbor, California

PHILADELPHIA – United States Attorney David Metcalf announced today that Laboriel Serrano Fernandez, aka Ivan Serrano, 42, a Mexican national who entered the U.S. illegally and has been residing in Norristown, Pennsylvania, was arrested and charged by indictment with four counts of transferring unlawful identification documents.

The defendant made his initial appearance in federal court this afternoon before U.S. Magistrate Judge Elizabeth L. Toplin.

The indictment alleges that on multiple dates earlier this year, Serrano knowingly transferred false identification documents that appeared to be issued by and under the authority of the United States, knowing that such documents were produced without lawful authority.

“Selling fake identification documents is a serious crime that threatens our national security and puts all of us at risk,” said U.S. Attorney Metcalf. “My office will prosecute to the fullest extent anyone putting these fraudulent IDs into circulation.”

“The production and distribution of counterfeit government documents is a serious criminal activity that compromises our national security,” said HSI Philadelphia Special Agent in Charge Nathan Abel. “HSI remains committed to leveraging our investigative expertise to identify and dismantle the criminal networks that profit from this fraud.”

If convicted, the defendant faces a maximum possible sentence of 60 years in prison.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

The case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations and is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Eileen Castilla Geiger and Erin Fountaine.

The charges and allegations contained in the indictment are merely accusations. Every defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty in court.

WASHINGTON -- Rashim Johnson, 35, a previously convicted felon residing in Warsaw, Virginia, was sentenced today in U.S. District Court in Washington D.C. to 84 months in federal prison in connection with his illegal possession of a fully loaded Glock 19 handgun and a large quantity of methamphetamine while he was on supervised release for two serious felonies, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

Johnson pleaded guilty May 18, 2026, before Judge Amit P. Mehta to unlawful possession of a firearm and ammunition. In addition to the 84-month prison sentence, Judge Mehta ordered Johnson to serve three years of supervised release. Federal prosecutors had requested a 110-month prison term.

According to court papers, on Sunday, Aug. 10, 2025, about 12:13 a.m., Metro Transit Police Department units assigned to the United States Park Police Task Force were on patrol in an unmarked patrol cruiser near the 4800 Block of Sherrif Road NE.

Officers observed 10 to 15 people loitering in the middle of the street. The officers stopped and exited their vehicles wearing marked police uniforms. Johnson spotted the approaching officers and immediately fled in the opposite direction. An officer gave chase. As Johnson ran, the officer watched Johnson remove a black object from his waistband and toss it over a chain-link fence.

Johnson continued running across Kane Place NE. The officer drew his firearm and ordered the Johnson to the ground. Johnson surrendered. Only ten seconds elapsed between when the officer observed Johnson toss the gun and Johnson’s surrender. Police recovered the firearm, a nine-millimeter Glock 19 handgun with an obliterated serial number. The weapon was equipped with an extended magazine loaded with 31 rounds with one round in the chamber. It was also equipped with a flashlight mounted below the barrel.

Once Johnson was placed in handcuffs, police recovered 53.5 methamphetamine pills from his right pants pocket.

Johnson was prohibited from possessing any firearm due to his previous convictions for felony firearm possession, possession with intent to distribute PCP and LSD, and for second degree assault, all out of Prince George’s County, Maryland. Johnson also has additional convictions in Maryland for armed robbery, robbery with a deadly weapon, and use of a handgun in a crime of violence.

This case was investigated by Metro Transit Police Department units assigned to the United States Park Police Task Force.

The matter was prosecuted under the Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful initiative by Assistant U.S. Attorney Samuel M. Deau and Travis Wolf.

Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful supports President Trump’s Executive Order that cracks down on gun violence, prioritizes federal firearms violations, pursues tougher penalties, and seeks detention for federal firearms violators.

Following a brief foot chase, police recovered Johnson’s firearm, a nine-millimeter Glock 19 handgun with an obliterated serial number. The weapon was equipped with an extended magazine loaded with 31 rounds with one round in the chamber. It was also equipped with a flashlight mounted below the barrel.

BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
A PROCLAMATION
For 250 years, American workers have been the driving force behind our Nation’s strength, prosperity, and industrial might. Their skill, ingenuity, and determination have fueled our economy and carried American manufacturing to new heights. On National Manufacturing Day, we honor the men and women who make, build, and create in America — and we celebrate the extraordinary comeback of American manufacturing.
As President, my highest priority has been putting America First by restoring our Nation’s manufacturing and bringing back good-paying American jobs. I have imposed powerful tariffs to protect American workers and businesses from unfair trade practices, and as a result, we are seeing the greatest reshoring of American manufacturing in our Nation’s history, alongside a surge in demand for products Made in America. Since I returned to office, I have secured more than $11.2 trillion in United States and foreign investments across manufacturing, critical infrastructure, and technology sectors. Groundbreakings of new factories are surging with 112,000 new factory construction workers building since I returned to office. The factory construction jobs of today mean more good-paying manufacturing jobs for decades to come. These investments fuel job growth, innovation, and opportunity across every corner of our country.
I was also proud to sign the Working Families Tax Cuts Act into law — landmark legislation that makes the Small Business Tax Deduction permanent and allows American manufacturers to immediately expense 100 percent of their factory, machinery, equipment, and domestic research and development investments. At the same time, this historic law is putting more money back into the pockets of hardworking Americans and increasing take-home pay, including new provisions like No Tax on Overtime. After declining by nearly $850 under the previous administration, the real wage for the average manufacturing worker has surged by $2,500 annually since I took office. These efforts are driving a revival of American manufacturing and making our country the best place in the world to build, produce, and invest.
After years of failed policies that hollowed out our industrial base and left American workers behind, manufacturing is once again powering America’s economic resurgence. After years of decline, manufacturing employment is rising once again with 72,000 new manufacturing jobs added in 2026 so far. Today, we honor the generations of Americans who have built our country through their hard work, and we look proudly to the next generation, who will carry on our great tradition of American innovation and enterprise. Together, we will make American manufacturing bigger, better, and stronger than ever before.
NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, do hereby proclaim October 2, 2026, as National Manufacturing Day. I call upon all Americans to celebrate the entrepreneurs, innovators, and workers in manufacturing who are making our communities strong.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this second day of October, in the year of our Lord two thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the United States of America the two hundred and fifty-first.
DONALD J. TRUMP
title: National Manufacturing Day, 2026

Khanna, Krishnamoorthi, Quigley, Crockett, Johnson Demand Answers From White House Over Denial Of CNN, MS NOW Access During Xi State Dinner
WASHINGTON – Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA), Ranking Member of the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, alongside Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), Rep. Mike Quigley (D-IL), Rep. Jasmine Crockett (D-TX), and Rep. Henry Johnson (D-GA), demanded answers from White House Communications Director Steven Cheung regarding reports that journalists from CNN and MS NOW were denied access to the White House to cover President Donald Trump’s state dinner with General Secretary Xi Jinping in Washington last week.
The lawmakers sent a letter Thursday just days after a federal judge preliminarily ordered the Trump Administration to immediately restore White House press credentials for CNN, MS NOW, and Politico after the outlets challenged the Administration’s decision to revoke their White House passes. Federal Judge Timothy Kelly issued a temporary restraining order requiring the Administration to reinstate the outlets’ hard-pass credentials.
According to media reports, CNN and MS NOW journalists encountered restrictions while attempting to cover Xi’s arrival and state dinner. CNN reported that a reporter and producer were initially blocked from accessing the White House, while MS NOW reported that White House correspondent Laura Barrón-López was denied entry.
“These reports are deeply troubling not only given the context of the court’s temporary restraining order and First Amendment press freedom but also as a sign of the President’s use of anti-democratic tactics perfected by the very guest hosted at the White House,” the Members wrote.
The lawmakers expressed particular concern about the reported restrictions given that the state dinner was held for Xi, whose government has engineered one of the world’s most restrictive media environments. The PRC ranks third lowest globally for press freedom, and the CCP has instituted crippling censorship of independent journalism.
The Members also highlighted the contrast between the reported treatment of American news organizations and the access provided to PRC state-run media, including Xinhua, during Xi’s visit.
“In no way should a U.S. president or any other official attempt to squash the freedoms of American media outlets at a time when we should be condemning the limitations on the freedom of the press that the CCP supports at home and around the world,” the lawmakers continued.
The letter further notes that freedom of the press is a fundamental constitutional principle in the United States and distinguishes the American system of government from the authoritarian model employed by the CCP. As Judge Kelly wrote in his recent ruling, the free press “stands as one of the great interpreters between the government and the people.”
The Members are requesting answers from the White House on the following:
- On what grounds did the President, you, or the White House Office of the Press Secretary deny access to CNN and MS NOW reporters or producers at last week’s state dinner?
- What background checks and procedures were implemented to screen PRC state-run media outlets’ access to last week’s bilateral meetings between yourself and Xi Jinping?
- What is the Trump Administration’s strategy to hold the PRC and Xi Jinping accountable for their violations of basic human rights, including freedoms of speech, opinion, and expression?
Read the full letter to White House Communications Director Steven Cheung HERE.

BOSTON – A Lynn man with multiple prior criminal convictions was sentenced yesterday in federal court in Boston for unlawfully possessing firearms and ammunition.

Derrick J. Poe, 41, was sentenced by U.S. District Court Judge Brian E. Murphy to 40 months in prison, to be followed by three years of supervised release. In April 2026 , Poe pleaded guilty to one count of being a felon in possession of firearms and ammunition after being charged by criminal complaint in February 2026.

Between Dec. 2, 2025 and Dec. 18, 2025, Poe distributed crack cocaine to undercover law enforcement in three separate controlled purchases in Salem, Mass. Poe was arrested after the third controlled purchase. A subsequent search of Poe’s Lynn residence resulted in the recovery of suspected crack cocaine and other evidence of drug distribution as well as three firearms and ammunition. Two of the firearms were privately made polymer-80 pistols, bearing no serial numbers, which are commonly referred to as “ghost guns.” The third firearm was a Springfield Armory 9mm pistol that had been reported stolen from Columbus, Ohio:

Poe is prohibited from possessing firearms and ammunition due to multiple prior felony convictions, including in Alabama. These include a 2006 conviction for unlawful possession of a controlled substance and robbery as well as a 2012 conviction for receiving stolen property. Poe received concurrent 10-year and 20-year sentences for the 2006 drug and robbery offenses – sentences which were later suspended and he was ordered to serve four years in prison followed by four years of supervised probation. As for the 2012 receipt-of-stolen-property offense, Poe received a 69-month prison sentence that was suspended, with credit for time served, and was placed on probation for 60 months. In 2016, he was convicted in Massachusetts state court of possessing Class B drugs with intent to distribute.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Thomas A. Greco, Special Agent in Charge of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives, Boston Field Division made the announcement. Valuable assistance was provided by the Lynn and Salem Police Departments. Assistant U.S. Attorney Aidan Lang of the Major Crimes Unit prosecuted the case.

TOPEKA, KAN. – Nine defendants have been sentenced to prison terms for their part in an international drug trafficking ring that brought large amounts of methamphetamine into Kansas.

In 2022, the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and Riley County Police Department launched an investigation into a drug trafficking organization operating in the Manhattan and Salina area. Over time, law enforcement seized large quantities of methamphetamine during multiple traffic stops. As two examples, law enforcement seized 62.9 pounds of methamphetamine during one traffic stop and found 20 pounds after another traffic stop.

Through the course of the investigation, DEA agents concluded that Gonzalo Escobedo, 49, an illegal alien from Mexico, was acting as the local leader of the organization.

On multiple occasions, Escobedo instructed subordinates to pick up crystal methamphetamine and cocaine from suppliers in California and Arizona then return to Kansas for further distribution. Some co-conspirators also made trips to Mexico to bring back liquid methamphetamine that, once in Kansas, was then converted to crystal methamphetamine.

“Drug trafficking organizations with connections to international cartels reach far and wide, even to central Kansas,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser. “Often in these communities the drug operations will cross jurisdictions, which create barriers for law enforcement in identifying and disrupting the operation as a whole. When local and federal law enforcement agencies partner together, our communities receive a greater impact.”

According to court documents, the following defendants pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute and possess with intent to distribute methamphetamine. They were sentenced to the following prison terms:

• Gonzalo Escobedo, 49, was sentenced to 240 months, • Joseph K. Murdoch, 32, was sentenced to 240 months, • Manuel Meza, 31, was sentenced to 240 months, • Aaron Noonan, 32, was sentenced to 180 months, • Amanda Hubbard, 43, was sentenced to 180 months, • Julisa Esparza, 26, was sentenced to 180 months, • Shelbie Louise Durham, 29, was sentenced to 126 months, • Harley David Blair, 46, was sentenced to 121 months, and • Michael Anthony Jones, 51, was sentenced to 77 months.

The Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and Riley County Police Department investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Lindsey Debenham prosecuted the case.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

In an age of rapid digital advancement, cyberspace has emerged as the new frontier of American innovation, prosperity, and strength. As new technologies open doors to discovery and opportunity that were once unimaginable, a secure cyberspace is essential to ensuring that America continues to lead the world in finance, military power, emerging technology, and manufacturing. During National Cybersecurity Awareness Month, my Administration reaffirms our dedication to bolstering our Nation’s cybersecurity, protecting the American People, and unleashing the Golden Age of Cyberspace.
Every American relies on the digital world for information, economic opportunity, and the simple routines of daily life. Freedom and security in cyberspace, however, can never be taken for granted. For too long, adversaries and cybercriminals exploited our connected way of life to target our citizens, communities, and businesses without consequence. My Administration has put an end to this era of weakness.
As President, I signed an Executive Order to combat cybercrime, fraud, and predatory schemes and stop foreign criminal networks from preying on vulnerable Americans. In March, I released my Cyber Strategy for America—a bold vision for the future of American cybersecurity and innovation. My Administration is already putting this strategy into action through the creation of “GOLD EAGLE,” a partnership between the Federal Government and leading American companies to harness the power of American Super Intelligence to identify cybersecurity vulnerabilities at rapid speed and stay ahead of our adversaries, defend the American People from emerging threats, and safeguard the critical infrastructure vital to our national security and global competitiveness.
As we secure America’s digital future, we are also preparing the next generation to lead it. Through First Lady Melania Trump’s leadership on the Presidential Super Intelligence Challenge, we have inspired young Americans to embrace emerging technologies, develop new skills, and find solutions to challenges in their own communities. The First Lady’s Fostering the Future Together initiative also continues to empower students, parents, and educators to learn, grow, and thrive through the safe and innovative use of advanced technology. This month, I encourage every American to do their own part to stay safe online by creating strong passwords, keeping software up to date, and remaining vigilant against scams. Together, we can strengthen our Nation’s cybersecurity, safeguard the technologies that power our daily lives, and secure America’s place as the leader in the world’s digital age.

Yesterday, U.S. Representatives Rick Larsen (WA-02) and Mark Veasey (TX-33) reintroduced the America Votes Act to protect U.S. citizens who face disenfranchisement because of restrictive voter identification (ID) laws.

“As Trump and Republicans in Congress continue their unlawful attempts to suppress the right to vote, it is more urgent than ever to break down barriers to the ballot box,” said Rep. Larsen, a co-founder of the Congressional Voting Rights Caucus. “This bill builds on Washington state’s successful efforts to safeguard election integrity while getting rid of laws that disenfranchise citizens and prevent people from fully participating in democracy.”

“Voter ID laws are being sold as a solution to a problem that doesn't exist, and the people paying the price are eligible voters, especially in communities of color,” said Rep. Veasey, a founder and co-chair of the Congressional Voting Rights Caucus. “The America Votes Act protects every registered voter's right to cast a regular ballot by affirming their identity under oath. It's common sense, and it's time for Congress to act to protect the vote for all Americans.”

Despite claims that restrictive voter ID laws are necessary to prevent voter impersonation, there is no evidence of widespread voter fraud in the United States. Some state legislatures across the country continue to use excessively restrictive voter ID laws to target and deny certain Americans the right to vote. Restrictive voter ID laws disproportionately impact Black and transgender Americans, perpetuating the systematic disenfranchisement of certain groups in the United States.

In 2026, a total of 36 states require voters to show identification to cast a ballot, and 24 of those states require voters to present identification with a photograph. These identification requirements are in addition to those under federal law to register to vote.

The America Votes Act would establish new federal protections for registered voters to affirm their identity by submitting a sworn, written statement, even if they do not have a government-issued ID. Voters who sign a sworn, written statement can vote using a standard, non-provisional ­­ballot. The legislation is modeled on a successful Washington state law that allows voters to affirm their identity by submitting a similar written statement along with their mail-in ballot.

The full text of the America Votes Act is available here.

The America Votes Act is cosponsored by Representatives Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Betty McCollum (MN-04), André Carson (IL-07), and Julia Brownley (CA-26).

Larsen Fights to Protect Voting Rights

Rep. Larsen is a strong advocate for free and fair elections, expanding access to the ballot and Washington state’s vote-by-mail system. He has visited or plans to visit election offices in every county of Washington’s Second Congressional District to discuss the importance of safeguarding the right to vote with local officials ahead of this November’s elections.

Larsen first introduced the America Votes Act in 2012. The bill was included in the For The People Act, sweeping legislation to expand access to the ballot box, get dark money out of politics, end partisan gerrymandering and hold elected officials accountable to their voters. The For The People Act passed the House in 2021 but did not receive a vote in the Senate after Republicans blocked its passage.

###
title: Larsen Reintroduces Bill to Fight Discriminatory Voter ID Laws

At Kennedy’s Demand, DHS Finally Discloses Details of Batavia ICE Facility Expansion - New $17 Million Structure Will House Women Detainees

In a Response to Kennedy’s Letter Written in His Oversight Capacity, DHS's Own Numbers Show More Than 70% of Batavia Detainees Have No Criminal Record, Contradicting Administration's "Worst of the Worst" Claims

BUFFALO, N.Y. – Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26), a member of the House Committee on Homeland Security, today condemned the Trump administration's plan to build a new detention facility at the Buffalo Service Processing Center in Batavia at a cost to taxpayers of nearly $17 million funded by Trump and Congressional Republicans' Big Ugly Bill. He also exposed the administration's own admission that the vast majority of the people it is detaining in Western New York have no criminal record.

In a response to Kennedy's July 8 oversight letter, which arrived on September 29, 76 days past his July 15 deadline, the Department of Homeland Security disclosed that 72 percent of detainees at Batavia have no criminal record. Rather than defend the expansion as a public safety measure, DHS wrote that known criminal history "is not a prerequisite for immigration enforcement action." Secretary Markwayne Mullin instead pointed to the 2024 election, writing that the department intends to deliver "mass deportations."

"This administration told the American people it was going after the worst of the worst. Now they've admitted in writing that it isn't true. More than 70 percent of the people held in Batavia have no criminal record, and DHS says that doesn't matter," said Congressman Kennedy. "It took them more than two months to answer, and they still can't keep their story straight about what they're building. Meanwhile, the calls coming into my office tell the real story. Every single day we’re getting calls about people who are picked up by ICE while dropping their kids off at school or going to work. People that are here lawfully are feeling threatened and afraid. This administration must be held accountable.”

"Western New Yorkers are working hard to put food on the table, keep up with their utility bills, fill their gas tanks, and afford their medical bills. Our government should be focused on making life more affordable," Kennedy continued. "Instead, the Trump administration is spending nearly $17 million to enact its cruel and inhumane agenda.”

DHS's response contradicts itself. ICE's contract approval describes a "soft sided temporary detention facility," while DHS's answers refer to a "hard-sided" structure.”

The department also revealed that ICE plans to hold women at the new facility and that men could be held there as well "if the needs of the service dictate."

Kennedy's letter requested all records related to the decision to build the facility, including cost estimates and communications with contractors. DHS provided a single approval memo, with pricing details and the planned number of beds redacted. It said staffing levels for the facility are "still being discussed."

In July, Kennedy warned that the Trump administration has a pattern of rapidly building soft-sided tents and makeshift detention facilities without ensuring detainee health and safety, and demanded that DHS halt construction at Batavia. He will continue to press DHS for answers and to oppose the expansion of ICE detention in Western New York.

Read Congressman Kennedy’s oversight letter here.

Read Secretary Markwayne Mullin’s full response here.

WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Rob Menendez (NJ-08) and Congressman Jefferson Shreve (IN-06) introduced the bipartisan Stop SIM Box Scams Act, which would ban the hardware that enables scammers to disguise robocalls as local telephone numbers.

In 2025, Americans received approximately 29.6 billion scam robocalls and texts and lost nearly $2 billion to these scams. By masking international or out-of-state calls with local area codes, scammers exploit trust and dramatically increase answer rates among unsuspecting victims.

“Scammers shouldn’t be able to use our area codes to rip off our communities,” said Congressman Menendez. “Our legislation bans the deceptive devices that allow scammers to masquerade as our neighbors, cutting off a key tool for fraudsters and protecting working families.”

“That ‘local’ Indiana number on your phone may be a scammer calling from halfway around the world,” said Congressman Shreve. “I wrote this bill to stop scammers from using these machines to pose as our neighbors.”

The legislation targets “SIM boxes,” which are specialized devices that house hundreds of SIM cards at once, cycling through local phone numbers to help scam syndicates flood individuals with robocalls and text messages while evading law enforcement detection.

The Stop SIM Box Scams Act would prohibit manufacturing, importing, selling, leasing, advertising, owning, or operating SIM boxes. It would also direct the Federal Communications Commission to coordinate with federal law enforcement to block imports and prosecute people who use them.

Read the full bill text here.
title: Menendez, Shreve Introduce Legislation to Ban Scam Call Machines

U.S. Marshals-Led Operation Triple Beam-Prolific Results in 237 Arrests
Las Cruces – An intensive five-week-long joint federal, state and local operation led by the United States Marshals Service District of New Mexico, focused on violent fugitives, firearms, and narcotics-related offenders, has concluded.
Operation Triple Beam-Prolific commenced on August 24, 2026, and concluded on September 25, 2026. The operation brought together the Las Cruces Police Department and other federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies to apprehend violent fugitives and target firearm and narcotics offenders as part of a coordinated effort to reduce violent crime.
Led by the U.S. Marshals Southwest Investigative Fugitive Team (SWIFT), multiple federal, state and local law enforcement agencies concentrated their efforts on known violent offenders, resulting in 237 total arrests, 17 firearm seizures, 2 vehicles recovered, 54 grams of Cocaine seized, 403.4 grams of methamphetamine seized, and 110 grams of Fentanyl seized.
“The success of Operation Triple Beam–Prolific reflects the strength of the partnerships we have built across New Mexico. When local, state, and federal partners work together, we can identify violent offenders, take them off our streets, and remove illegal firearms and dangerous drugs from our communities. We will continue to be proactive, work together, and do everything we can to make New Mexico’s communities safer.” – David Barnett, U.S. marshal for the District of New Mexico.
"Operation Triple Beam-Prolific continues to demonstrate the power of a unified law enforcement effort in New Mexico," said Justin A. Garris, special agent in charge of the FBI Albuquerque Division. "When agencies come together, share information, and work toward a common goal, we can have a meaningful impact on the safety of the communities we serve."
“When federal law gives us an opportunity to change the consequences for someone committing serious crimes, we are going to take a hard look at that case," said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison. "Triple Beam puts more eyes on the people and conduct causing problems in our communities, and it gives my office more opportunities to step in where federal prosecution can matter. If there is an appropriate federal case to bring, we intend to bring it.”
“Homeland Security Investigations is proud to stand alongside our federal, state, and local law enforcement partners in protecting the communities we serve,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge of HSI El Paso Ryan G. McRae. “By combining our resources, expertise, and investigative capabilities, we can more effectively identify and disrupt criminal activity, hold dangerous offenders accountable, and strengthen public safety. These partnerships demonstrate what can be accomplished when law enforcement agencies work together toward a shared mission of keeping our communities 
safe.”
“The DEA was more than ready, willing, and able to assist our partners in the U.S. Marshal service with the narcotics arm of this operation,” said Robert ‘Eric’ Castañeda, special agent in charge of the El Paso Division. “The men and women of DEA El Paso stand united with all federal government agencies to pursue drug dealers who are foolish enough to attempt to remain in Southern New Mexico.”
“This successful operation has communicated to those who seek to harm others in our community that we will not tolerate violence and disorder. It also shows our citizens that law enforcement at all levels will work together to reduce crime and prevent victimization in our beautiful city. Thank you to our partners for standing alongside us to make Las Cruces safer.” - Las Cruces Police Chief Jeremy Story
“Our officers see firsthand the harm criminals cause in Las Cruces and across New Mexico. I thank the U.S. Marshals Service for leading this operation and every agency involved for their commitment to keeping our communities safe. These arrests show what we can accomplish together. The New Mexico State Police will continue to stand alongside our local, county, state and federal partners to protect the people who call New Mexico home.” said Matthew Broom, chief of the New Mexico State Police.
“This community is safer because of the dedicated work of the officers with our Probation and Parole Division’s Security Threat Intelligence Unit (STIU) and our law enforcement partners during Operation Triple Beam Prolific,” said Adult Probation and Parole Director Lupe Sanchez. “The actions of our STIU officers resulted in 27 arrests of justice-involved individuals on warrant status, the recovery of a firearm, and the seizure of illegal drugs. The New Mexico Corrections Department places a high priority on community safety and enforcement, while equally prioritizing rehabilitative services for justice-involved individuals through specialized programming and behavioral health services—both for those housed in the NMCD facilities and those under community supervision. I want to commend the dedicated work of our STIU officers and thank all participating law enforcement agencies who worked alongside us in this operation.”

This operation will allow our office to move forward, seek justice and pursue accountability.” - Doña Ana County District Attorney, Fernando R. Macias

NEWARK, N.J. – A Massachusetts man was convicted on September 28, 2026, for his role in a multi-year conspiracy to launder money that was stolen from victims across the United States as a part of a series of internet-enabled romance scams, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced.

Manaseh Mintah, 43, of Dracut, Massachusetts, was convicted of one count of money laundering conspiracy, three counts of money laundering, and one count of operating an unlicensed money transmitting business. Mintah was convicted following a two-week trial before U.S. District Court Judge Esther Salas in Newark federal court. Sentencing is scheduled for March 16, 2027.

“Cyber-enabled fraud schemes take advantage of vulnerable Americans, especially older Americans, stealing their hard-earned life savings and destroying families’ financial security. Transnational criminal networks may think that they can hide behind computer monitors, but our office, alongside our federal partners, will relentlessly track down these bad actors and the people who launder money on behalf of these criminal networks.” - U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer

“Cyber-enabled fraud schemes take advantage of vulnerable Americans, especially older Americans, stealing their hard-earned life savings and destroying families’ financial security. Transnational criminal networks may think that they can hide behind computer monitors, but our office, alongside our federal partners, will relentlessly track down these bad actors and the people who launder money on behalf of these criminal networks.”

- U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer

“Romance‑scam network operators believe themselves untouchable, hiding behind keyboards and laundering money through shell companies with impunity,” said FBI Newark Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy. “But reality hits hard when they hear a guilty verdict read out loud in a U.S. federal court. The FBI Newark Joint Organized Crime Task Force disrupts transnational groups to protect Americans who are being targeted and prevent them from losing their life savings to these malicious criminals.”

“Romance scams prey on the trust of vulnerable individuals and too often shatter their finances and lives. This verdict makes it clear that those who move illicit funds for fraudsters will be held accountable,” stated Special Agent in Charge Jenifer L. Piovesan, IRS Criminal Investigation, Newark Field Office. “IRS‑CI is dedicated to partnering with fellow law enforcement agencies to expose financial crimes that victimize our citizens.”

According to court documents and evidence presented at trial:

Mintah laundered money sent to him directly by victims of internet-enabled romance scams through numerous bank accounts opened in his own name, and also under the name of Dazionking LLC, a shell business entity that he formed to launder money. Mintah would then move these victim proceeds from the Dazionking accounts and his own personal account to coconspirators through wire transfers, cash withdrawals, and other means. As part of this scheme, Mintah received and transferred at least approximately $1.2 million, knowing that the transactions were for the purpose of disguising or hiding the proceeds of criminal activity.

The money laundering conspiracy charge and one of the money laundering charges carry a statutory maximum sentence of 20 years in prison. Two of the money laundering charges carry a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison. The operating an unlicensed money transmitting business charge carries a maximum sentence of 5 years in prison. The money laundering charges each carry a potential fine of up to $500,000 and the operating an unlicensed money transmitting business charge carries a potential fine of up to $250,000.

U.S. Attorney Frazer credited special agents of the FBI Newark Field Office, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy in Newark, New Jersey, and the FBI Cleveland Field Office, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Joshua J. DelManzo in Cleveland, Ohio, with the investigation leading to the conviction. U.S. Attorney Frazer would also like to thank special agents of IRS-Criminal Investigation, under the direction of Jennifer Piovesan in Newark, as well as special agents of the HSI Detroit Field Office, under the direction of Acting Special Agent in Charge Jeremy Piercynski in Cleveland, Ohio, for their assistance in the case.

The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Benjamin Levin, Chief of the Cybercrime Unit, and Sean Nadel of the Cybercrime Unit in Newark.

WASHINGTON – U.S. Representatives Jan Schakowsky (IL-09) and Mark Pocan (WI-02) on Thursday led a letter, signed by 71 Members of Congress, to Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) Robert F. Kennedy, Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) Markwayne Mullin, and the commissioners of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP), urging that the agencies ensure that Americans can continue to obtain genuine, non-controlled prescription medicines from outside the country.

New CBP procedures for international mail shipments, taking effect October 22, could disrupt 2.3 million Americans’ longstanding ability to obtain lower-cost prescription medicines from Canada and other countries for their personal use.

“For years, our constituents who have struggled with high prescription drug prices have obtained their medicines from pharmacies outside the United States, especially from Canada,” the members wrote.

“We support CBP’s goal of using better data to identify and intercept high-risk shipments. However, we are concerned that the new process could be implemented in a manner that prevents personal-use prescription medicines from being shipped to the United States or results in their routine refusal, including medicines Americans have long obtained from licensed pharmacies abroad,” the members continued. “Greater visibility should instead improve the government’s ability to distinguish dangerous products from lower-risk prescription medicines and preserve appropriate enforcement discretion.”

“We urge HHS, FDA, DHS, and CBP to delay any implementation of new procedures with respect to prescription medicines unless you can provide clear assurances that your agencies will not prevent genuine prescription medicines clearly intended for personal use and not appearing to present an unreasonable risk from entering the United States,” the members added.

“Americans should not lose access to affordable medicines simply because the government has better information about packages entering the country. We urge your agencies to use that information to focus enforcement on where the risks are greatest while preserving appropriate access to safe and affordable medicines for personal use,” the members concluded.

The letter is endorsed by the Campaign for Personal Prescription Importation, Just Care USA, National Association of Letter Carriers, Prescription Justice, and Social Security Works.

text:
CONCORD –Three men pleaded guilty this week in federal court to violating the Lacey Act , illegally hunting dozens of wild Bobcats in New Hampshire in order to ship the animals’ pelts to Canada, U.S. Attorney Erin Creegan announces.

Sherwood Dubrey, Jr., 48, and Randy Inman , 49, pleaded guilty to conspiring to violate the Lacey Act and Sherwood Dubrey Sr., 72, pleaded guilty to violating the Lacey Act before U.S. District Judge Joseph N. Laplante this week. The Court scheduled sentencing for each defendant in January 2027. Dubry Jr. and Inman face a maximum prison term of five years and no more than three years of supervised release; Dubrey Sr. faces a maximum prison term of one year and no more than one year of supervised release.

Enacted 126 years ago, the Lacey Act protects the nation’s wildlife resources by prohibiting wildlife violations that cross state or international borders. The bobcat ( Lynx rufus ) is a wild cat native to North America. In New Hampshire, it is unlawful to hunt or trap bobcats. To export a lawfully hunted bobcat pelt, the law requires that hunters obtain a tag under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (or CITES). Because hunting bobcats is illegal in New Hampshire, New Hampshire does not have an export program for bobcats and does not distribute CITES tags for bobcats. New York, which has a lawful bobcat hunting season, has an export program for bobcats and provides successful trappers or hunters of bobcats CITES tags.

According to the public record, Dubrey Jr. and Inman conspired to violate the Lacey Act by poaching Bobcats in New Hampshire, transporting them to New York where Dubrey Sr. obtained false CITES tags to make the bobcats appear as though they were killed in New York, then shipping them to Canada to be sold at a fur auction. Text messages and other evidence obtained through the investigation showed that for more than four years, Dubrey Jr. and Inman routinely killed bobcats in New Hampshire, including by using bait piles on their property and on state land to lure the bobcats to be shot. They then transported the poached bobcat pelts to New York to be falsely tagged and exported to Canada. In their messages, the defendants acknowledge that their bobcat poaching is illegal and discuss the details of the scheme. In one such message, Inman confirmed to Dubrey Jr. that he shot or choked out an illegally trapped bobcat; in another, Dubrey Jr. told his father that he did not want a legal bobcat hunting season in New Hampshire because that would create “competition.” Inman and Dubrey Jr. also used rifles with scopes that could capture videos and photographs of their illegal kills and sent those videos and images to others via text messages. In total, from 2018 to 2022, Dubrey Jr. and Inman illegally exported at least 41 poached bobcat pelts.

“The people of New Hampshire have enacted hunting laws that conserve our resources and define our sense of fair play,” said Erin Creegan, U.S. Attorney for the District of New Hampshire. “Baiting and poaching dozens of bobcats for profit disregards that democratic consensus and the duty of sportsmanship shown by New Hampshire’s hunters. Crossing state or international lines will not protect poachers from accountability for their actions.”

“This case began with the dedicated work of New Hampshire Fish and Game conservation officers and shows what we can accomplish together,” said Assistant Director Doug Ault, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Office of Law Enforcement. “Over four years, the defendants illegally killed at least 41 bobcats and falsified where the animals were taken so they could be sold on the international market. Their actions undermined the tagging system that wildlife managers, hunters, and trappers depend on to keep the fur trade legal and sustainable. Our message is clear—exploiting wildlife for profit has consequences, and we will work with our state partners to bring those responsible to justice.”

“We are grateful for the vital assistance provided by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service throughout this lengthy poaching investigation,” said New Hampshire Fish and Game Department Conservation Officer Lieutenant William Boudreau. “Protecting wildlife requires a united front, and the collaboration between our state conservation officers and federal agents was instrumental in bringing these violators to justice. Investigations into wildlife poaching do not end at the state line.”

The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Office of Law Enforcement and the New Hampshire Fish and Game Department led the investigation with valuable assistance from the Gilmanton Police Department, the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation, Environment Canada, the Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources Enforcement Branch, the Massachusetts Environmental Police, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Matthew T. Hunter prosecuted the case in coordination with Trial Attorney Mark Romley of the Justice Department’s Environmental Crimes Section.
title: Three Men Plead Guilty to Poaching More than 40 Bobcats and Exporting them to Canada

FBI Columbia Summer Heat 2.0 Numbers Surpass 2025 Results
FBI Columbia announced this week the successful conclusion of Operation Summer Heat 2.0, an FBI-led nationwide initiative to crush violent crime.
The FBI Columbia Field Office and its law enforcement partners executed 80 arrests and carried out 43 significant narcotics seizures, disrupting the distribution of more than 16 kilograms of cocaine, fentanyl, marijuana, and methamphetamine. They also recovered 40 firearms, removing dangerous weapons from violent individuals. Compared to last year, arrests surged by 156% and firearm seizures increased by 266%.
Summer Heat 2.0 launched in June and ran through September. During the three-month period, the FBI, along with law enforcement partners at the local, state, and federal level, carried out enhanced investigative activities that targeted violent crime across South Carolina. The FBI surged resources that helped dismantle gangs, removed dangerous drugs and weapons from the streets, and saved children from potential predators.
“This FBI continues to prioritize crushing violent crime by dedicating the resources and personnel to communities affected most by dangerous criminals,” said FBI Columbia Special Agent in Charge Anish Shukla. “Working hand-in-glove with our law enforcement partners is critical to tackling violent crime. We’re grateful for the partnerships that made Summer Heat 2.0 a success, and we all remain committed to ensuring South Carolina neighborhoods are safe from those who seek to plague them with poisonous drugs and violence.”
“We’re proud to partner with the FBI in their commitment to combat violent crime and make South Carolina safer,” said U.S. Attorney Bryan Stirling for the District of South Carolina. “We’ll continue working with agencies across our state to investigate and prosecute violent criminals, drug traffickers, and weapons dealers who seek to harm our communities.”
Operation Summer Heat 2.0 follows historic drops in crime across the U.S., according to the FBI’s 2025 UCR Summary of Reported Crimes in the Nation.

KANSAS CITY, Mo. – A Kansas City, Mo. man has pleaded guilty to a firearms violation.

Edward L. Vann, 44, pleaded guilty before U.S. District Judge Greg Kays to being a felon in possession of a firearm.

According to the plea agreement, Vann was found in possession of two semi-automatic handguns while parked outside a business on Independence Avenue in Kansas City, Mo., during the evening of Nov. 2, 2025. Both firearms were loaded, and one contained a machinegun conversion device that rendered it capable of fully automatic fire.

Under federal statutes, Vann is subject to a sentence of up to 15 years in federal prison without parole. The maximum statutory sentence is prescribed by Congress and is provided here for informational purposes, as the sentencing of the defendant will be determined by the court based on the advisory sentencing guidelines and other statutory factors. A sentencing hearing will be scheduled after the completion of a presentence investigation by the United States Probation Office.

This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys David Wagner and James Kirkpatrick. It was investigated by the Kansas City, Missouri Police Department.

Project Safe Neighborhoods

This case is part of Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN), a program bringing together all levels of law enforcement and the communities they serve to reduce violent crime and gun violence, and to make our neighborhoods safer for everyone. On May 26, 2021, the Department launched a violent crime reduction strategy strengthening PSN based on these core principles: fostering trust and legitimacy in our communities, supporting community-based organizations that help prevent violence from occurring in the first place, setting focused and strategic enforcement priorities, and measuring the results.

WICHITA, KAN. – An illegal alien from Mexico was sentenced to 24 months in prison for using a deceased person’s identity to receive benefits from federal and state public assistance programs.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

According to court documents, Simon Flores-Torres, 72, pleaded guilty to one count of aggravated identity theft.

In September 2024, Flores-Torres requested a U.S. passport in someone else’s name. He provided a Kansas driver’s license and Social Security card with the victim’s stolen information as part of the application. Suspicious because of prior applications using the same identity, the U.S. State Department and the Social Security Administration - Office of Inspector General (SSA-OIG) launched an investigation. They learned the identity belonged to an actual person who died in 2015.

Further investigation showed Flores-Torres used the victim’s information to fraudulently obtain $95,811 in Social Security benefits from the federal government, and $97,095 in Medicaid and $24,269 in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits from the state of Kansas. As part of his plea agreement, Flores-Torres must pay restitution to those entities.

“Realistically, it is incredibly difficult to avoid violating the law while living day to day in the United States as an illegal alien because one cannot legally drive without a license or legally work without authorization. As a result, identity theft is one of the most common types of cases we prosecute against illegal aliens. The perpetrators care more about gaining privileges their immigration status doesn’t afford them than about the harm they cause to victims,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser.

“Safeguarding Social Security programs supported by the American taxpayer is our mission. This case demonstrates our commitment to detecting identity related fraud and holding accountable those who attempt to exploit Social Security benefits,” said Corwin Rattler, Acting Special Agent-in-Charge, SSA OIG, Dallas–Kansas City Field Division. “We appreciate the joint effort and coordination of the Diplomatic Security Service, Homeland Security Investigations, and the Kansas Department of Revenue throughout this investigation.”

“This sentencing sends a strong message that schemes to defraud the Medicaid, SNAP, and Social Security Disability programs will not be tolerated,” stated Steven D. Anderson, Kansas Inspector General. “The Office of Inspector General will continue to work cooperatively with our law enforcement partners to aid in the identification and prosecution of individuals engaged in these types of crimes.”

An investigation showed Flores-Torres had also given the victim’s name during a prior arrest.

The Social Security Administration – Office of Inspector General (SSA-OIG), Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), Kansas Office of Inspector General, and Kansas Department of Revenue investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Aaron Smith prosecuted the case.

NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA – ROMALIS WILLIAMS (“WILLIAMS”) , age 33, a resident of New Orleans, Louisiana was sentenced on October 1, 2026 by United States District Judge Brandon S. Long after being found guilty by a jury of possession with the intent to distribute controlled substances, in violation of Title 21, United States Code, Sections 841(a)(1) and (b)(1)(C) and being a felon in possession of firearms, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Sections 922(g)(1) and 924(a)(8), announced U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle.

Judge Long sentenced WILLIAMS to 137 months in federal prison, six years of supervised release, and ordered WILLIAMS to pay a $200.00 mandatory special assessment fee.

On March 25, 2024, NOPD officers, while conducting routine surveillance observed WILLIAMS in the 8700 block of Green Street with a bulge on the right front side of his waistband. WILLIAMS proceeded to get onto a bicycle and ride down Green Street and, while doing so, kept adjusting an object in his waistband area. WILLIAMS then shoved his right hand deep into his pants as if he were attempting to hide an object. Officers believed WILLIAMS may have been in possession of a firearm concealed in his waistband and commanded WILLIAMS to stop his bicycle. WILLIAMS disregarded the command, dropped the bicycle, and ran from the officers. Officers chased WILLIAMS into the 1700 block of Joliet Street. WILLIAMS jumped several fences before being detained.

During the search of WILLIAMS ’ person, a distributable amount of fentanyl and methamphetamine were found in a clear plastic bag inside WILLIAMS ’ pants pocket. A stolen Springfield Armory Model XDM, 40 caliber pistol, was recovered from WILLIAMS ’ left pant leg. WILLIAMS , a convicted felon, is prohibited from possessing firearms.

The case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the New Orleans Police Department. It was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Brittany L. Reed of the Violent Crime Unit and Assistant United States Attorney Shannon Kippers of the General Crime Unit.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

Tampa, Florida – Andrea Catanese (60), an Italian national, has been charged by federal indictment with voting by an alien, attempting to procure naturalization unlawfully, and making a false statement related to naturalization. If convicted on all counts, Catanese faces a maximum penalty of 10 years in federal prison. U. S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement.

According to the indictment, Catanese, voted in the 2024 general election despite not being a citizen of the United States. The indictment further alleges that afterward, Catanese falsely stated he had never voted in a federal election on an Application for Naturalization and then made the same false statement to an immigration official who was reviewing the application.

An indictment is merely a formal charge that a defendant has committed one or more violations of federal criminal law, and every defendant is presumed innocent unless, and until, proven guilty.

This case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations, with assistance from the Pasco County Supervisor of Elections. It will be prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Mark E. Andreu.
title: Italian Alien Charged with Voting in 2024 General Election and Lying About it
