FORT WORTH, Texas — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas, Ryan Raybould, announced that a federal court sentenced Stephenville businessman Clayton Lloyd Iley, 41, to more than 13 years in federal prison for wire fraud and aggravated identity theft on Oct. 1. These offenses arose from a scheme wherein he illegally obtained credit cards and offered a scam loan program to victims.

“Clayton Iley’s conduct caused real financial and emotional harm to the victims he targeted, many of whom trusted him with their personal information and hard‑earned money,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “This sentence reflects our commitment to holding fraudsters accountable. Those who steal from members of our community, manipulate them with fabricated schemes and misuse their identities will face significant federal consequences.”

“Clayton Iley’s conduct caused real financial and emotional harm to the victims he targeted, many of whom trusted him with their personal information and hard‑earned money,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “This sentence reflects our commitment to holding fraudsters accountable. Those who steal from members of our community, manipulate them with fabricated schemes and misuse their identities will face significant federal consequences.”

“This 160-month sentence holds the defendant accountable for a multi-year fraud scheme that exploited members of our communities,” said FBI Dallas Special Agent in Charge R. Joseph Rothrock. “The FBI will continue to work in close coordination with our partners to identify, investigate, and disrupt fraud schemes that threaten the public.”

According to court records, Iley operated an insurance brokerage business named Clayton Texas Legacy Insurance Group, LLC from its headquarters in Cross Plains, Texas and offered home, auto, life, health, farm & ranch, and commercial insurance policies to the public.

Court documents show from January 2020 through May 2026, Iley used at least two entities he controlled, Texas Legacy Holdings and Enterprises, LLC and Spartan Global Security, LLC dba as “Black Eagle PMC” to conduct financial transactions. Texas Legacy Holdings operated as a holding company and was used to conduct financial transactions. Spartan Global purported to offer private security services, commercial security services, corporate security services, and private military contracting services. Iley defrauded victims by, among other things:

Falsely representing to victims that he could invest their funds in a “Bonded Note” loan program that was provided by the U.S. Department of Defense to private military contractors, when in reality, Iley knew the relevant loan program did not exist; during the relevant time period, Iley collected over $2 million based on this misrepresentation and used the funds to pay his own personal expenses and to execute other parts of his fraudulent scheme

Falsely represented to specific Texas Legacy Insurance clients that he would accept client funds and cause Texas Legacy Insurance to initiate requested insurance policies on their behalf, when in in reality, Iley knew he would accept their insurance premium payment funds, fail to open requested insurance policies, and instead intended use their funds to pay his own personal expenses and to fund the relevant fraudulent scheme

Provided victim personal identifying information (e.g., first name, last name, etc.) to financial institutions to fraudulently secure credit cards bearing the names of those specific victims without the knowledge or authority of each victim, then used the resulting credit cards deposit funds into Spartan Global bank accounts and claim the transactions were gross receipts for the business; and pay for his own personal expenses and exotic collector vehicles.

As part of his plea agreement, Iley agreed to forfeit property over 90 exotic collector vehicles obtained with funds from his fraudulent scheme. text:
ROANOKE, Va. – Four Maryland residents who conspired with Dr. Rotimi Iluyomade, an Annandale-based doctor convicted of distributing more than 7,000 oxycodone pills, 34,000 milliliters of hydrocodone-chlorpheniramine solution (also known as “Tussionex”), and 107,000 milliliters of promethazine-codeine solution (also known as “lean”) were sentenced today in federal court.

Yared Michael Tesfaye, a.k.a. “Yar” 29, of Montgomery Village, Maryland, was sentenced today to 60 months in federal prison.

Elhadj Malick Diallo, 32, of Silver Spring, Maryland, was sentenced to time served (approximately 13 months) in federal prison. Cameron Isaiah Lewis, 24, and Raymono Alfonzo Russell II, 25, both of Bowie, Maryland, were sentenced to 8 months and 10 months respectively.

All four defendants previously pleaded guilty to conspiracy to distribute and possess with the intent to distribute Schedule II controlled substances and to acquire promethazine-codeine solution by fraud.

“Any physician and anyone who conspires with a physician to facilitate the illegal distribution of drugs will be aggressively prosecuted in the Western District of Virginia,” First Assistant United States Attorney Robert N. Tracci said today. “I applaud the outstanding work of the FBI and the DEA in this case.”

“The defendants paid a doctor to issue fraudulent prescriptions for opioid medications and then trafficked those drugs to buyers across multiple states,” said Darren Cox, Assistant Director in Charge of the FBI Washington Field Office. “We are grateful to our federal, state, and local partners for their help in ensuring these defendants are held accountable for profiting from the illegal distribution of controlled substances.”

“Patient care is a privilege. Patient safety is a responsibility. When responsibility is betrayed through the unlawful prescribing of controlled substances, DEA and other law enforcement partners will act decisively and with one purpose: protecting American lives,” said DEA Special Agent in Charge Cindy Marx of the Washington Division.

According to court documents, in at least 2023 and 2024, Iluyomade and the co-conspirators entered into an agreement to distribute oxycodone pills, promethazine-codeine solution, and Tussionex to pharmacies in multiple states, including California, Colorado, Nebraska, Arizona, Missouri, Florida, Pennsylvania, Maryland, New Jersey, Delaware, Rhode Island, Georgia, Wisconsin, Texas, West Virginia, and in the Eastern and Western Districts of Virginia. At least 70 of the illegal controlled substance prescriptions were transmitted to and/or filled at pharmacies in the Western District of Virginia.

As part of the conspiracy, multiple individuals visited Iluyomade’s medical clinic to obtain fraudulent prescriptions. The individuals provided Iluyomade with lists of multiple “patients” addresses and identify information or different variations of names and false addresses, and requested prescriptions be sent to pharmacies throughout the United States for the “patients” on the lists.

Tesfaye was the first co-conspirator to visit Iluyomade at Crossover Medical Center in Annandale, Virginia to obtain fraudulent prescriptions. In addition to obtaining his own fraudulent prescriptions, he sold “slots” with Iluyomade to other co-conspirators that they used to obtain fraudulent prescriptions.

Lewis and Diallo traveled to various pharmacies to pick up fraudulent prescriptions written by Iluyomade, which they then distributed for profit, often posting pictures on social media to facilitate drug sales. Lewis and Diallo paid Iluyomade $300 per fraudulent prescription.

The investigation began on September 2, 2023, when Russell attempted to pick up a fraudulent prescription transmitted by Iluyomade at a pharmacy in Honaker, Virginia. Russell was arrested and a search of his vehicle revealed multiple controlled substance prescription bottles in various “patient” names, all from Iluyomade, filled at pharmacies in Roanoke, Radford, Tazewell, and Floyd, Virginia.

The Drug Enforcement Administration, Federal Bureau of Investigation, Virginia State Police, Russell County Sheriff’s Office, Salisbury, Maryland Police Department, Loudoun County Sheriff’s Office, Nebraska State Police, HHS-OIG, and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) are investigating the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Lena Busscher and Randy Ramseyer are prosecuting the case.
title: Four Sentenced for Conspiring with Annandale-Based Doctor to Illegally Distribute Oxycodone and other Controlled Substances

text:
BURLINGTON – The United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Vermont stated that Khadim Ndaiye, 29, of Senegal and previously of Brooklyn, New York, has been charged by criminal complaint with illegal entry into the United States. Ndaiye’s initial appearance in court is scheduled for this afternoon before United States Magistrate Judge Kevin J. Doyle in Burlington.

According to court records, on September 30, 2026, the U.S. Border Patrol detected an unlawful crossing of the international border between Canada and the United States in the vicinity of North Troy, Vermont. Agents responded to the area and observed tracks and indicators of people moving through the woods. After following the trail of sign, agents observed a man walking along a creek. As agents approached the man, he began to run and evaded them. Agents continued to search the area for hours, eventually locating a man consistent in appearance with one detected crossing the border. The man initially ran from agents but was apprehended shortly thereafter and later identified as Khadim Ndaiye. Ndaiye’s clothing was covered in brush and mud, indicating he had likely been in the woods for an extended period. Ndiaye’s fingerprints were used to identify him as a citizen of Senegal, who had previously been apprehended by U.S. Border Patrol in 2023 in Arizona while illegally entering. Consistent with border policies in 2023, Ndaiye was issued a notice to appear for immigration proceedings and released into the country. The recent fingerprint check by Border Patrol revealed that Ndaiye has an open bench warrant for his arrest, issued by New York County Criminal Court for charges related to felony attempted forcible rape stemming from a September 1, 2025 arrest. Immigration records reveal Ndiaye departed the United States on September 15, 2025, shortly after his New York arrest.

The United States Attorney’s Office emphasizes that the complaint contains allegations only and that Ndiaye is presumed innocent until and unless proven guilty. Ndiaye faces up to 6 months of imprisonment if convicted. The actual sentence, however, would be determined by the District Court with guidance from the advisory United States Sentencing Guidelines and the statutory sentencing factors.

First Assistant United States Attorney Jonathan A. Ophardt commended the investigatory efforts of the U.S. Border Patrol. “I am extremely grateful that Border Patrol Agents worked tirelessly to locate and apprehend Ndiaye after his alleged unlawful crossing. Ndiaye’s immigration history and pending criminal charges in New York State underscore the vital importance to securing our northern border with Canada. The United States Attorney’s Office remains committed to working closely with our federal law enforcement partners to ensure that those who evade our ports of entry are apprehended and prosecuted.”

The prosecutor is Assistant United States Attorney Eugenia A. P. Cowles. Ndiaye is represented by the Office of the Federal Public Defender.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.
title: Wanted Senegalese Man Arrested Illegally Crossing Border

Congressman Davis Helps Deliver New 100-Foot Ladder Truck to Williamston Fire Department
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Don Davis (NC-01) celebrated the delivery of a new 100-foot aerial ladder truck to the Williamston Fire Department, made possible in part by $1 million in community project funding he secured for the Town of Williamston. Congressman Davis secured the project for federal funding to help replace the department’s aging 1999 Pierce 75-foot ladder truck after nearly 30 years of service, and voted to approve it as part of H.R. 5371, Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act, 2026 (Public Law 119-37).
The $1 million investment, delivered through the USDA Rural Development Community Facilities program, helped fund the new custom-built 2026 E-ONE HR 100-foot tandem aerial ladder truck, designated Ladder 26. The Town of Williamston covered the remaining $500,000 for the apparatus. Ladder 26 expands the department’s vertical reach by 25 feet and strengthens its firefighting and emergency response capabilities.
“Behind the wheel of Williamston’s new ladder truck are firefighters who train, prepare, and put themselves in harm’s way to protect their neighbors,” said Congressman Don Davis. “I am proud to have voted and secured $1 million to help deliver this new apparatus, and grateful to the firefighters who answer the call when our community needs them most.”
Congressman Don Davis secured nearly $54 million in Fiscal Year 2026 Community Project Funding for eastern North Carolina through federal appropriations legislation he supported. The funding was included in the Senate amendment to H.R. 7148, Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026; H.R. 6938, Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026; and H.R. 5371, Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act, 2026.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11), a member of the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, today introduced the Federal Employee Records Relief Act, legislation to help former federal employees obtain missing personnel records, fix administrative errors and navigate their earned benefits. Missing or inaccurate records can delay retirement processing, complicate health coverage and interfere with future employment.

“Federal employees have suffered enough under the Trump administration’s mass firings and attacks on our civil service. They should not have to chase down missing paperwork to document their service and access the benefits they earned,” said Congressman Walkinshaw. “My bill would require the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) and federal agencies to help former employees get their records, fix errors and get clear answers about their benefits. These public servants deserve better.”

The bill would require OPM, working with former employing agencies, to provide personnel records, correct administrative errors and offer written benefits information and coordination assistance, including information about health coverage continuation options.

Federal employees who separated for any reason on or after January 20, 2025, including retirees, would have four years after enactment to submit requests.

“Too often, federal employees leave government service only to find themselves trapped in bureaucratic limbo, waiting months for agencies and OPM to correct records or process paperwork they need to collect benefits, secure loans, or move on to their next job. This commonsense legislation creates a clear, centralized, and time-limited process to fix those problems so former federal employees are not forced to keep paying the price for administrative failures that are beyond their control,” said the National Federation of Federal Employees.

“Mass firings and pressure campaigns to force out federal employees have thrown thousands of dedicated civil servants into chaos. Now many are left hanging, trapped by botched personnel records and processing delays that stand between them and their next job, their retirement, and the benefits they earned. The Federal Employee Records Relief Act will give these workers a clear path to correct their records and move forward with their lives. NTEU applauds Rep. Walkinshaw for his work on this bill and for standing up for federal employees and their families,” said Doreen Greenwald, National President, National Treasury Employees Union.

Original cosponsors include Reps. Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D.C.), Don Beyer (VA-08), Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05), Stephen F. Lynch (MA-08), Glenn Ivey (MD-04) and Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10).

Read the bill text here.

title: Walkinshaw Introduces Bill to Fix Personnel Record Errors Delaying Federal Workers’ Retirement and Benefits

CLEVELAND – A federal grand jury has indicted a 34-year-old man with possessing a deadly biological agent.

Brandon L. Baxter, of East Cleveland, was charged with Prohibitions with Respect to Biological Weapons and Possession of a Biological Toxin by a Restricted Person.

According to allegations in the indictment, Baxter was knowingly in possession of a biological agent, ricin, which is known to be lethal to humans. Baxter was previously convicted for being part of a terrorist collective that attempted to detonate explosives at the base of the Route 82 bridge in Macedonia, Ohio in 2012. Baxter is expected to appear for arraignment on Oct. 14, before U.S. Magistrate Judge Jonathan D. Greenberg.

U.S. Attorney David M. Toepfer for the Northern District of Ohio and FBI Cleveland Division Special Agent in Charge Joshua DelManzo made the announcement.

The investigation in this case is being conducted by the FBI Cleveland Division with assistance from the Cuyahoga County Sheriff’s Office, and the City of East Cleveland Police Department.

Assistant United States Attorney Duncan T. Brown is leading the prosecution for the Northern District of Ohio, along with Trial Attorney Ryan D. White of the National Security Division’s Counterterrorism Section.

If convicted, the defendant faces a maximum of 15 years in prison for both counts. The sentence will be determined by the court after a review of factors unique to this case, including the defendant’s prior criminal record, if any, the defendant’s role in the offenses, and the characteristics of the violations.

An indictment is only a charge and is not evidence of guilt. Defendants are entitled to a fair trial in which it will be the government’s burden to prove guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.
title: Ohio Man Charged for Possessing Dangerous Biological Weapon

Baltimore, Maryland – The U.S. Attorney’s Office announced, today, that a Maryland man is facing federal indictment in connection with child sex abuse crimes.

Charles Mark Wooters, 34, of Easton, is charged with one count of sexual exploitation of a child; transportation of child sex abuse material (CSAM); and receipt of CSAM; along with five counts of possession of CSAM.

Kelly O. Hayes, U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the indictment with Special Agent in Charge Jimmy Paul, FBI Baltimore Field Office, and Chief Alan Lowrey, Easton Police Department.

According to the indictment, in November 2025, Wooters allegedly uploaded more than two dozen CSAM files, depicting minors engaging in sexually explicit conduct, to an internet-based file storage account. Additionally, law enforcement found that Wooters possessed CSAM files on multiple electronic devices and an internet-based cloud storage account associated with his email address.

Wooters is facing a mandatory minimum sentence of 15 years and a maximum sentence of 30 years in federal prison for sexually exploiting a minor and a minimum of five years and a maximum of 20 years for transporting CSAM. He also faces a minimum of five years for receipt of CSAM, along with a maximum of 10 years for each count of possessing CSAM.

Actual sentences for federal crimes are typically less than the maximum penalties. A federal district court judge determines sentencing after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

This case is part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the United States Attorney’s Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit justice.gov/psc . For more information about Internet safety education, visit justice.gov/psc and click on the “Resources” tab on the left of the page.

U.S. Attorney Hayes commended the FBI and Easton Police Department for their work in the investigation. Ms. Hayes also thanked Assistant U.S. Attorney Maryam Zhuravitsky who is prosecuting the federal case.

For more information about the Maryland U.S. Attorney’s Office, its priorities, and resources available to help the community, please visit justice.gov/usao-md .

Landsman, Van Hollen, Mfume, Beyer Lead Letter to Protect Federal Workers
Cincinnati, OH – This week, Congressman Greg Landsman (D-OH), Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Congressman Kweisi Mfume (D-MD), and Congressman Don Beyer (D-VA) sent a letter to the Equal Opportunity Employment Commission (EEOC) opposing a proposed rule to overhaul the federal employee complaint process.
The EEOC is proposing a rule change to eliminate protections and strip federal employees of critical civil rights in discrimination complaints.
In response, Landsman, Van Hollen, Mfume, and Beyer – along with 79 colleagues – are calling on EEOC Chair Andrea Lucas to rescind the proposed rule.
The letter argues the change will make it harder for workers to challenge workplace discrimination or retaliation and weaken important protections and enforcement. It urges the EEOC to withdraw the proposed rule and work with Congress on reforms to make the federal-sector EEOC process fairer and faster.

text:
The Lawmakers Also Renewed Their Call for Trump to Release the Transcript of His 2019 Call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman Following Khashoggi’s Murder

Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Representatives Eugene Vindman (Va.-07), James Walkinshaw (Va.-11), Bobby Scott (Va.-03), Don Beyer (Va.-08), Jennifer McClellan (Va.-04), and Suhas Subramanyam (Va.-10) released the following statement on the eighth anniversary of the murder of Jamal Khashoggi.

“Eight years ago today, Virginia resident and journalist Jamal Khashoggi was brutally murdered inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul. His murder was an unconscionable attack on a journalist and a Virginia resident, and his family and the American people deserve the full truth about what happened and what followed.

“That includes transparency about President Trump’s 2019 call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Congressman Vindman reviewed the transcript of that call while serving as a lawyer on the National Security Council, and we believe the American people deserve to see it for themselves.

“As members of Virginia’s congressional delegation, we will continue pressing for the transparency and accountability that this case demands. If President Trump will not release the transcript now, we will force him to do it in the next Congress when Democrats are in charge.

“Eight years is far too long to wait for answers. President Trump should declassify and release the transcript and give the Khashoggi family and the American people the truth they deserve.”

BACKGROUND

Jamal Khashoggi, a Washington Post journalist and U.S. resident, was murdered inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul in October 2018 — an assassination that drew global condemnation and raised serious questions about Saudi Arabia’s leadership and the Trump administration’s response.

In November 2025, Vindman demanded that the White House release the transcript of a “shocking” 2019 call that took place between President Donald Trump and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman following Khashoggi’s murder. Vindman reviewed this call while serving as a staff lawyer on Trump’s National Security Council.

That same month, he led 37 lawmakers in sending a letter to President Trump calling for the immediate release of the transcript. He also hosted a press conference alongside Hanan Elatr Khashoggi — Khashoggi’s wife — and U.S. Representatives Jamie Raskin (Md.-08) and Suhas Subramanyam (Va.-11) to urge President Trump to release the transcript of the call.

In October 2025, Congressman Walkinshaw and Senators Kaine and Warner introduced a bicameral resolution commemorating the seventh anniversary of Khashoggi’s murder and calling for accountability. The resolution also called for the Government of Saudi Arabia to release wrongfully detained individuals, respect the rights of Saudi citizens, and ensure the protection of the freedoms of assembly, association, and the press.

Khashoggi was a resident of Virginia’s 11th District, which was formerly represented by the late Congressman Gerry Connolly and is now represented by Walkinshaw.

###
title: Vindman, Virginia Democrats Release Statement on 8th Anniversary of Jamal Khashoggi’s Murder

SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, amplió al sector hospitalario la discusión sobre el futuro de Medicaid en Puerto Rico durante su participación en la Convención de la Asociación de Hospitales, donde abordó los cambios que enfrenta el programa a partir de 2027 y la necesidad de que Puerto Rico llegue preparado a la próxima etapa de discusión en el Congreso.

El Comisionado Residente destacó que las decisiones que se tomen en Washington tendrán consecuencias directas sobre la estabilidad del sistema de salud, incluyendo la capacidad de los hospitales para sostener sus operaciones, retener profesionales de la salud y garantizar acceso a servicios de calidad para los pacientes.

“Nuestra prioridad es atender lo básico, y la salud es parte de eso. Trabajamos más allá de líneas partidistas para extender los fondos del Plan Vital.El 23 de septiembre reunimos en el Congreso a expertos, personal congresional y representantes del sector de la salud para discutir los retos que tenemos por delante, y el 25 de septiembre nos reunimos con la gobernadora y el grupo multisectorial en La Fortaleza para revisar los datos y afinar la propuesta que llevaremos a Washington. El 2027 está cada vez más cerca y queremos llegar a esa discusión preparados, con una agenda clara y con una propuesta sustentada en datos. En asuntos como este, la salud de los puertorriqueños no tiene colores políticos”, expresó el comisionado residente.

Durante su participación, el Comisionado Residente explicó que Puerto Rico enfrenta una estructura de Medicaid distinta a la de los estados, particularmente por el tope anual al financiamiento federal. Bajo la ley vigente, el porcentaje de participación federal también está programado para reducirse de 76% a 55% a partir del 1 de octubre de 2027, mientras que la asignación federal bajo la Sección 1108 enfrenta una reducción significativa al culminar las asignaciones temporeras.

Estos cambios coinciden en el tiempo y crean lo que se ha denominado el precipicio de Medicaid de 2027, un escenario que requiere atención y planificación antes de que comiencen a materializarse sus efectos.

Como parte de la discusión, el comisionado residente presentó la necesidad de evaluar una estructura de financiamiento más estable para el programa, incluyendo una propuesta para el próximo Congreso que eliminaría el tope de la Sección 1108 y permitiría que el financiamiento federal continúe respondiendo a los gastos elegibles de Medicaid, como ocurre en los estados, sujeto al límite estatutario aplicable al porciento de participación federal.

La conversación con el sector hospitalario también incluyó otros asuntos que inciden sobre la estabilidad del sistema de salud, entre ellos Medicare Advantage, la retención de profesionales, los hospitales y centros de salud 330, la salud mental, la prevención, la investigación, la salud materna y los servicios comunitarios.

El Comisionado Residente repasó además las gestiones que ha realizado durante los últimos meses para fortalecer la coordinación entre el gobierno de Puerto Rico, el sector de salud y los interlocutores en Washington. Entre estas se encuentran sus reuniones con funcionarios federales y congresistas, su testimonio ante el Comité de Energía y Comercio de la Cámara de Representantes, la coordinación de esfuerzos bipartidistas sobre Medicare Advantage y las reuniones recientes con la gobernadora y representantes del sector de salud para revisar datos y recomendaciones de política pública.

De cara al próximo Congreso, el comisionado residente señaló la importancia de que Puerto Rico llegue a Washington con información sólida sobre costos, utilización de servicios, necesidades de los pacientes y las condiciones que enfrentan los proveedores de salud.

La participación ante la Asociación de Hospitales forma parte de los esfuerzos de el Comisionado Residente para mantener la discusión sobre Medicaid y Medicare Advantage conectada con los hospitales, profesionales y demás sectores que sostienen diariamente el sistema de salud de Puerto Rico.

title: Comisionado Residente amplía la discusión del futuro de Medicaid al sector hospitalario

The Department of the Interior today announced the designation of Whittier, Alaska, as an American World War II Heritage City, recognizing the community’s extraordinary contributions to the nation’s World War II home front and its ongoing commitment to preserving that history.

“The Department of the Interior is honored to designate Whittier, Alaska as one of the 2026 American World War II Heritage Cities in recognition of its vital contributions to securing our Allied victory and steadfast dedication to preserving this important chapter in American history,” said Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum . “By recognizing this region, the Trump administration is reaffirming our nation's commitment to preserving the legacy of the United States' involvement in World War II and ensuring that the sacrifices, services and contributions of those who served and the communities that supported them will be remembered, both locally and nationally, for generations to come.”

Whittier’s nomination highlighted its vital strategic role in the defense of Alaska during World War II, when the U.S. Army transformed a remote site on Prince William Sound into a secret major military port and transportation hub. Chosen for its deep, ice-free harbor and the natural protection of surrounding mountains, Whittier provided a second, strategically located military port that relieved pressure on the more vulnerable commercial port of Seward and provided a more secure route for moving wartime supplies into Alaska.

Beginning in 1941, the U.S. Army constructed a railroad connection through the Chugach Mountains, including a tunnel through Mynard Mountain, as well as docks, warehouses, rail yards and other essential facilities to move troops, fuel, equipment and war materiel into Alaska. When the rail connection was completed in 1943, Whittier emerged as a principal entry point for military personnel and supplies supporting the defense of Alaska and the Aleutian Campaign.

“The community of Whittier would not exist if it were not for World War II and the U.S. Army's decision to utilize its strategic location. Today, the port of Whittier supports over 700,000 visitors and remains a major logistics hub for Alaska," said Kara Moriarty, Senior Advisor to the Secretary of the Interior for Alaska Affairs . “This designation appropriately recognizes how Alaskans, through military service, wartime construction and industrial production, strengthened the war effort and continue to defend our freedoms today.”

The community that developed from this massive wartime undertaking remains a tangible reminder of the scale, ingenuity and strategic importance of Alaska’s role in World War II. Today, Whittier’s preserved World War II structures, historical markers and local museum continue to interpret and honor this significant chapter in American history.

About the American World War II Heritage City Program

Administered by the National Park Service, the American World War II Heritage City Program was signed into law by President Donald J. Trump in March 2019 as part of the John D. Dingell Jr. Conservation, Management, and Recreation Act (S. 47). The program recognizes communities for their contributions to the World War II home front and helps preserve the history of U.S. involvement in the war. It authorizes the secretary of the interior to bestow the honorary designation on only one city or local jurisdiction in each state and territory.

Since 2020, designations have been made in 38 states and one territory, strengthening public understanding of the war’s local impacts and advancing preservation of historically significant sites.

Nominate Your City

Any city or other local jurisdiction in a state without an existing designation, is eligible for this recognition. Nominations must be submitted by the highest locally elected official.

Nominations will open in early 2027. For more information, including program information and nomination guidance, please visit the American World War II Heritage Cities Program webpage.

KANSAS CITY, KAN. – A former executive for International Brotherhood of Boilermakers, Iron Ship Builders, Blacksmith, Forgers and Helpers (Boilermakers Union) was sentenced to 16 months imprisonment and two years of supervised release. The sentence also included a ban from employment with a labor union or ERISA fund for 13 years for the defendant’s part in nearly a decade of egregious financial corruption and abuse of union funds.

According to court documents, Tyler Brown, 46, of Kansas City, Missouri, pleaded guilty to one count of racketeering conspiracy.

The Boilermakers Union is a labor union formerly headquartered in Kansas City, Kansas, with approximately 45,000 members consisting of skilled tradespersons.

Brown was employed by the Boilermakers Union in a variety of roles, including as Executive Director of Industrial Sector Operations, Special Assistant to the International President, and Chief of Staff. Brown reported directly to International President Newton Jones and carried out Jones' directives including those Brown knew to be illegal and contrary to the union’s constitution. Some of those actions include:

• Assisting in hiring Jones’ wife, son and other relatives as staff with substantially inflated salaries knowing they did little to no productive work • Preparing letters at Jones’ direction assigning union executives and guests to 100 lavish international trips that served no legitimate union-related purpose. Brown himself took more than 30 of such trips to destinations like Italy, London, Spain, Switzerland, Peru, and Thailand • As chief of staff, Brown prepared agenda packages for International Executive Council Docket meetings. Brown omitted expense reports for the International President and International Secretary-Treasurer to impede councilmembers from reviewing the information

Brown, who was a licensed attorney, surrendered his license to practice law in five states. Seven other defendants involved in the conspiracy will be sentenced at a later date.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and the U.S. Department of Labor investigated the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Faiza Alhambra and Jabari Wamble prosecuted the case.

###
title: Former Boilermakers executive headed to prison

The Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering (R&E), through the Office of the Assistant Secretary of War for Critical Technologies (CT), has announced an agreement to partner with the Central Intelligence Agency and In-Q-Tel (IQT), a not-for-profit strategic investor that has served the national security community since 1999.
The partnership gives the Department's research and engineering enterprise structured access to IQT's global technology-scouting platform and its portfolio of early-stage companies, with the explicit objective of compressing the timeline to transition and rapidly field mature commercial solutions from non-traditional performers to the warfighter.
The Department of War has mandated six Critical Technology Areas (CTAs) as the focus of its investment and transition efforts: Applied Artificial Intelligence, Biomanufacturing, Contested Logistics Technologies, Quantum and Battlefield Information Dominance, Scaled Directed Energy, and Scaled Hypersonics. Under the agreement, IQT will conduct technology scouting and technical due diligence across all six CTAs, as well as across enabling technology areas, while the Department identifies transition sponsors and pathways for validated technologies.
"In a contested global threat environment, technological superiority will not be determined by who invents a capability first, but by who delivers it to the warfighter fastest. The Department is fundamentally shifting its posture: we are moving from acting solely as a long-cycle technology developer to operating as an agile, credible, and rapid customer for America's most innovative non-traditional performers. Our partnership with In-Q-Tel eliminates bureaucratic friction across our six CTAs. Over the next 12 months, our benchmark for success is simple and unambiguous: moving validated commercial prototypes out of the lab and into active operational field evaluations with our combatant commands," said Hon. Michael Dodd, Assistant Secretary of War for Critical Technologies.
The integration leverages In-Q-Tel's proven venture capital methodology to vet early-stage commercial solutions that align directly with the Department's urgent mission requirements. By combining CT's strategic transition pathways with IQT's deep-tech scouting infrastructure, the partnership aims to significantly de-risk the integration of commercial hardware and software for national security applications, signaling to the commercial tech sector that the Department of War is open for business.
Joint pilot programs under this new partnership will begin in the coming weeks, targeting immediate battlefield bottlenecks. By aligning IQT's venture ecosystem with the Department's rapid transition pipelines, both organizations aim to establish a permanent bridge that converts commercial ingenuity into deployed military capability at the speed of relevance.
title: Department of War's Critical Technologies Office Partners With In-Q-Tel to Accelerate Technology From Non-Traditional Performers to the Warfighter

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Greg Casar (D-TX), Ranking Member of the Federal Law Enforcement Subcommittee, and Congresswoman Shontel Brown (OH-11) sent a letter demanding answers and transparency from the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director Kash Patel on the FBI’s planned increase of mass surveillance systems, such as Flock.

In May 2026, the FBI issued a Request for Proposals (RFP) to acquire automatic license plate readers (ALPR) systems, including Flock and Motorola Solutions, that offer the ability to search for license plate information “and other descriptive data such as vehicle description information, time/date criteria, and geo-location criteria.” Flock and Motorola Solutions, whose ALPR systems are used by local police departments, likely possess the capabilities to satisfy this RFP. While the FBI already runs a License Plate Reader (LPR) program through the National Crime Information Center (NCIC) to facilitate LPR information sharing with and between its law enforcement partners, the FBI’s plan to obtain direct access to an extensive network of cameras—such as those operated by Flock and Motorola—would dramatically expand the license plate data currently held by the FBI and institute “near real time” surveillance of civilians.

The Members of Congress write: “The American people are clearly concerned about law enforcement having access to Flock data and about government surveillance more broadly. Entering into a contract that would give the nation’s largest law enforcement agency access to Flock data across the country would subvert the clear preference of the American people.”

The Oversight and Government Reform Committee Democrats are requesting information by October 16, 2026.

Read the full letter here.

###

Congressman Greg Casar represents Texas’s 35th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives, which runs down I-35 from East Austin to Hays County to the West Side of San Antonio. A labor organizer and son of Mexican immigrants, Casar serves as the Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus for the 119th Congress. He also serves on the Committee on Education and Labor and the Committee on Oversight and Accountability.
title: Casar, Brown Demand Answers on FBI’s Plan to Buy Flock Cameras and Other Mass Surveillance Systems

Oakland, Calif. – The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) has delivered preliminary flood maps for Pima County and the Town of Marana, Arizona. The maps identify revised flood hazards within Brawley Wash, Black Wash, Altar Wash, and Brawley Wash Watershed including Puertocitos Wash / Arivaca Wash & Tributaries. The new maps will help building officials, contractors and homeowners make effective mitigation decisions, thereby contributing to safer and more disaster resilient communities.
Before the new Flood Insurance Rate Maps (FIRMs) become effective, there is a 90-day appeal period from October 08, 2026 to January 05, 2027. During that time, residents or businesses with supporting technical and scientific information, such as detailed hydraulic or hydrologic data, can appeal the flood risk information on the preliminary maps, which can be viewed at fema.gov/preliminaryfloodhazarddata.
Flood hazards are dynamic and change frequently for many reasons, including weather patterns, erosion and community development. Officials from FEMA and Pima County worked together to provide updated information that accurately reflects the flood risk. These changes may also affect future building standards or insurance requirements.
The local mapping project is part of a national effort led by FEMA to increase local knowledge of flood risks and support actions to address and reduce the effects of flooding on new and improved structures. FEMA encourages residents to review the preliminary flood maps to learn about local flood risks, potential future flood insurance requirements and identify any concerns or questions about the information provided.
Risk of flooding affects almost every corner of the nation. In total, 98% of counties have experienced a flood event, which makes floods the most common and widespread of all weather-related natural disasters.
For more information, contact the Pima County Flood Control District at (520) 724-4600 or https://pima-flood-control.app.transform.civicplus.com/forms/32953.

WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of the Treasury applauded the release of the 2026 update to the U.S. National Strategy for Financial Literacy from the Financial Literacy and Education Commission (FLEC), which is chaired by the Secretary of the Treasury and is composed of the heads of 23 federal agencies and the White House Domestic Policy Council.
“The newest United States National Strategy for Financial Literacy is a roadmap to help every American build the knowledge and skills needed to achieve financial security for themselves and their families,” said Secretary Scott Bessent. “The advent of Trump Accounts demonstrates what this approach looks like in practice. By giving young Americans and their families an opportunity to save and invest together, we can make financial education tangible, help a new generation establish sound financial habits from an early age, and build the knowledge and confidence to participate in our financial markets.”
2026 Update to the U.S. National Strategy for Financial Literacy
The Financial Literacy Strategy outlines the FLEC’s goals for advancing financial literacy and education across the United States and identifies priority areas and actions to help Americans build the knowledge and skills to make informed financial decisions, achieve their financial goals, and enhance their financial well-being.
The Financial Literacy Strategy establishes four priority areas for the FLEC:
- Youth Financial Capability: Build a foundation of basic financial skills starting in childhood and young adulthood to improve financial outcomes for the next generation of Americans.
- Saving and Investing: Increase Americans’ knowledge of saving and investing to build financial security and achieve their financial goals, including by promoting awareness of new savings and investment vehicles such as Trump Accounts for children.
- Digital Financial Literacy: Improve Americans’ knowledge and decision-making skills to enable the safe and confident use of digital financial products and services.
- Scams and Fraud Education: Equip consumers with the knowledge to recognize and avoid scams and fraud and the tools to mitigate the impact of potential losses.
The Financial Literacy Strategy also identifies best practices for delivering effective financial education, including providing actionable and timely education at key financial decision points, tailoring education to life stages and individual situations, reinforcing concepts over time, incorporating experiential and hands-on learning, supporting high-quality instruction, and evaluating program effectiveness.
The Financial Literacy Strategy was developed through consultation with FLEC-represented agencies, public input, and independent research on financial literacy and education.
Read Secretary Bessent’s letter as Chair of the Financial Literacy and Education Commission available here.
Read the full 2026 Update to the U.S. National Strategy for Financial Literacy available here.
The Financial Literacy and Education Commission
The Financial Literacy and Education Commission (FLEC) was established by the Financial Literacy and Education Improvement Act, Title V of the Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions Act of 2003 (P.L. 108-159). It provides a forum for its represented Federal entities to continue coordination and collaboration that advance financial literacy and education andincrease access to financial services for all Americans. FLEC-represented agencies develop consumer-friendly, trustworthy, and consistent educational materials and tools; conduct outreach to help consumers make informed and sound decisions that enhance their financial well-being; coordinate and implement research; and develop and implement policies to improve how financial education is delivered.
Learn more about FLEC and financial literacy resources at mymoney.gov.

title: The Financial Literacy and Education Commission Releases the 2026 Update to the U.S. National Strategy for Financial Literacy

DUBLIN, Georgia: A McRae, Georgia man and woman have been sentenced to prison after pleading guilty to child sexual abuse charges.

The sentence was imposed by U.S. District Court Judge Dudley H. Bowen and announced by Margaret E. “Meg” Heap, U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Georgia.

Noah Zackery Cason , 25, of McRae, Georgia, was sentenced to 240 months in prison and a $2,500 fine followed by 15 years of supervised release after pleading guilty to Transportation of a Minor. Cason was also ordered to pay an assessment in the amount of $100 to the Amy, Vicky, and Andy Child Pornography Assistance Fund. Cason must register as a sex offender upon completion of his prison sentence.

Cason’s co-defendant, Alexandra McLain , 26, of McRae, was sentenced to 120 months in prison and a $2,000 fine followed by 10 years of supervised release after pleading guilty to Possession of Child Pornography. McLain was also ordered to pay an assessment in the amount of $100 to the Amy, Vicky, and Andy Child Pornography Assistance Fund. McLain must register as a sex offender upon completion of her prison sentence.

There is no parole in the federal system.

As described in court documents and testimony, In November 2024, Cason traveled to Oklahoma to pick up and transport a minor child to his residence in McRae. The guardian of the minor child filed a missing person report and investigators determined that the defendants were the perpetrators through online activity on apps, including Snapchat and WhatsApp.

While travelling to Georgia, Cason engaged in sexual acts with the minor victim during a stop in Alabama. Upon returning to their residence, Cason engaged in sex acts with the minor victim and recorded the abuse, with McLain’s knowledge and encouragement. McLain was also present during several of the sexual assaults. Searches of the defendants’ electronic devices contained videos and images depicting Cason participating in sexual activity with the minor victim.

With the use of license plate readers, investigators confirmed the defendant’s vehicle had traveled along a route consistent with travel to and from Oklahoma and Georgia. Investigators tracked the defendants to their residence and initially contacted Cason who denied knowing the minor victim or of her whereabouts. After further questioning, Cason admitted to transporting the victim from Oklahoma to Georgia and to having sexual contact.

“These defendants preyed on a child’s vulnerabilities, and their monstrous actions have created irreparable harm,” said U.S. Attorney Heap. “This office has an unyielding commitment to protect children and serve justice for the victims and their families.”

If you are or have information about victims of child exploitation, contact the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children Cyber Tipline at report.cybertip.org or 1-800-THE-LOST (1-800-843-5678).

“There is no excuse for adults who exploit and sexually abuse children. The actions of these defendants caused profound harm to a child, and today’s sentences hold them accountable for that harm,” said Brad Snider, Senior Supervisory Resident Agent of FBI Atlanta’s Savannah office. “The FBI and our law enforcement partners will continue to aggressively pursue those who prey on children and use technology to facilitate their abuse.”

This case was investigated by the FBI, Human Trafficking Unit, Oklahoma Bureau of Narcotics, Amtrak (Okla.) Police Department, and Telfair County Sheriff’s Office.

This case was prosecuted for the United States by Southern District of Georgia Assistant U.S. Attorney Sherri A. Stephan.

WASHINGTON – A seven count Superseding Indictment was unsealed yesterday in U.S. District Court charging Maliktra Derenorcourt, 27, and Philippe Oliver Gadie, 34, both residents of the District of Columbia, with a multi-year scheme to allegedly enrich themselves by using fake or stolen identities to fraudulently obtain leaseholds on units at various apartment complexes without paying rent or bills, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

“This case alleges a calculated fraud operation that weaponized stolen identities, exploited the eviction system, and inflicted significant financial harm across the District,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “These defendants, one of whom is a foreign national unlawfully present in the United States, are charged with orchestrating a housing and Social Security fraud scheme that preyed on innocent victims and undermined the integrity of our housing system. We will not tolerate criminals who exploit our communities for profit and put the safety and security of law-abiding residents at risk.”

According to the Superseding Indictment, from at least November 2023 to the present, Derenorcourt, Gadie, and others allegedly conspired to obtain a large number of leases for residential units at numerous apartment complexes across Washington, D.C. and surrounding areas.

The conspirators allegedly used stolen or fabricated Social Security Numbers, so called “Credit Privacy Numbers”, and fabricated letters of employment in furtherance of their scheme. The conspirators then allegedly lived in the units themselves, or sold access to the units to third parties at a fraction of the value of the lease. Nearly all of the apartments that were fraudulently leased as a part of the scheme resulted in eviction proceedings for non-payment of rent causing significant losses for each of the apartment complexes involved. Currently, losses are estimated to be in the hundreds of thousands of dollars, however, the investigation into the extent and scope of the scheme is ongoing.

In Washington, D.C., the eviction process can span multiple months—even up to a year or longer. Derenorcourt, Gadie, and others allegedly utilized this lengthy process by submitting fraudulent lease applications in batches using the stolen or fabricated identities.

During the conspiracy, Derenorcourt, Gadie, and others also allegedly used BitCoin and Cash App accounts with stolen and fabricated identities to transfer money between themselves. Gadie used at least one victim’s name, social security number, and date of birth to open a Cash App account conducting hundreds of transactions in the victim’s name. The investigation into these accounts is ongoing.

Derenorcourt assisted with the scheme by posing as the pair’s female identity theft victims. Search warrants executed at Derenorcourt’s apartment recovered numerous luxury fashion items. Gadie, a citizen of Côte d’Ivoire in West Africa, is unlawfully present in the United States after overstaying his nonimmigrant visa.

This case is being investigated Homeland Security Investigations, with valuable assistance provided by the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation unit. The investigation was conducted by the Washington, D.C. Fraud Cell, which is a multi-agency task force established pursuant to the President’s Executive Order 14252 aimed at Making the District of Columbia Safe and Beautiful Again.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

Gadie was apprehended while living on a fraudulent lease at an upscale apartment in Southeast Washington, D.C.

Press Statement

Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, Spokesman Office of the Spokesman

October 2, 2026

Today’s designations by the U.S. Department of the Treasury target a Hamas military operative in Gaza and a France-based fundraising network that used sham charities and cryptocurrency to collect nearly $2 million for Hamas in recent years.

This action underscores the enduring U.S. commitment to dismantling Hamas’s global support networks and denying the group the resources it needs to plan and carry out terrorism that threatens the security of Americans, our partners, and the broader Middle East. It reflects close coordination between the Department of State, the Department of the Treasury, and the FBI to expose how Hamas exploits humanitarian and charitable structures abroad to disguise terrorist financing as legitimate aid work.

The United States will continue working with partner governments, including France, to identify and hold accountable individuals and organizations that provide Hamas cover to raise and transfer funds internationally. Disrupting these networks is central to broader U.S. efforts to isolate Hamas, protect the integrity of legitimate humanitarian assistance to Gazan civilians, and support conditions for lasting regional stability.

We are committed to ensuring that humanitarian aid can be delivered by reliable and safe organizations that advance legitimate Palestinian interests and lasting peace in the region.

Today’s designations were issued pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13224, as amended by E.O. 13886, the United States’ core counterterrorism sanctions authority. On October 31, 2001, the U.S. Department of State designated Hamas pursuant to E.O. 13224 for having committed, or posing a significant risk of committing, acts of terrorism that threaten the security of U.S. nationals, or the national security, foreign policy, or economy of the United States. Hamas is also designated as a Foreign Terrorist Organization pursuant to section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act. For more information on today’s action, please see the Department of the Treasury’s press release .

Transcript: Pressley Speaks Out on Cornell Case, Reaffirms Support for Survivors of Sexual Violence

Mornings with Zerlina Interview

October 1, 2026

ZERLINA MAXWELL: Welcome back to Mornings with Zerlina. Back with us, one of our favorite guests on the show—Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley, represents the seventh district in the great state of Massachusetts. Good morning, Congresswoman. Thank you so much for being back with us.

REP. PRESSLEY: Good morning, Zerlina. No matter the state of the world, it is always a joy to be with you. Thank you.

ZERLINA: I concur, and it’s one of those weeks where every single day, I’ve been waking up and sort of checking in with myself because when the news cycle is the way it is, and you are a survivor of sexual assault, you have to brace yourself for being triggered and for this whole national conversation to be happening in the wake of what happened at Cornell. So, my first question is really, how are you doing, and what are you, what are some of the things you’re thinking through as this story has become now a national story?

REP. PRESSLEY: Well, first, I hope you are doing okay, and I thank you for, you know, beginning with that prompt. I’m, you know, I would say I’m, I’m focused. I mean, certainly it’s heartbreaking and devastating.

But rape culture is real, and I think more of what I experience is that I am always surprised at the level of shock registered by people. It’s one thing to be, you know, shocked by the depravity of the action, the evil and the vileness of it all, which we should be. We should never become desensitized or numb to that.

But you know, until there is a complete, you know, cultural and systemic overhaul, both of our norms and our justice system, these things will persist.

ZERLINA: You use the term rape culture, which I think is really important to define for everybody, and also to unpack because we definitely do live in a culture where sexual assault, sexual harassment, is normalized, and there is plenty of evidence of that, including who is in the White House.

REP. PRESSLEY: Absolutely, who’s in the White House. You know, who I’m working, you know, daily to hold accountable from Ghislaine Maxwell and Jeffrey Epstein to what’s happening on our college campuses.

I should say, you know, as a survivor of a near decade of intra-family childhood sexual abuse and also campus sexual assault, I’ve been in Congress now since 2018, but prior to that, I served on the Boston City Council, and this is where my work in this space really began in terms of the work of survivors’ justice. Because it still accounted for the number one reason—rape on college campuses—why girls were dropping out. And, you know, there was this constant who’s responsible for the oversight and pursuing justice and accountability—is it campus police? Is it local jurisdictions?

You know, and so survivors and victim-survivors were, you know, this political pawn, this football, and their lives were hanging in limbo. And I know for myself, the work that I’m doing in fighting for restitution for survivors, particularly who have had their federal rights violated or experienced neglect in the way that the Epstein survivors have.

This is a life-altering experience. It is a life sentence. The harm is incalculable. That being said, while we have focused on the physical harm and the psychological and emotional toll, what often gets lost in that is the economic toll.

I remember while a student in college, on the heels of my sexual assault, many days I just could not function. I missed days at work, and I wasn’t working for enrichment or a resume. My household, my family needed that money. I missed days in class. I was not excelling academically at all because I was afraid to run into my perpetrator. And I was also triggered because, again, I was a survivor of a near decade of interfamily childhood sexual abuse. So it was compounding, you know, all of that trauma. It is nearly impossible to resume any kind of normalcy.

But the point is, the Center for Disease Control puts at a baseline that the average victim-survivor of sexual assault—you’re talking about $122,000 at a minimum. You know, mental behavior health services, impact on your total health, lost wages, losing jobs, losing housing.

So when I wake up every day, I just wake up that much more resolved to do the work of restitution for survivors, justice, and healing, and to do whatever I can to undo or to change who we have become culturally when it comes to rape, rape culture, and rape in every way. Rape as a tool of war. It is just systemic.

ZERLINA: One of the things that you said that I think is really really important is that the person who comes forward with their story about sexual assault—they have to survive the sexual assault, and then they have to survive the victim blaming and the reactions of everyone, and the failure of prosecutors or their university or their community to take their allegation seriously, and then you know follow the law. I mean, you’ve talked about survivors being harmed twice.

Talk a bit more about the ways in which we need to, as institutions and as communities, listen to the survivors and believe them. Because again, we’re not the judge and jury, right? Like I think that there’s this cultural shift that needs to happen even before we change the laws.

I mean, it’s important, the Survivors Restitution Act, absolutely. But we also need to have a deeper cultural conversation too about how we are responding as a community when somebody comes forward to this type of allegation.

REP. PRESSLEY: Absolutely, Zerlina. And to that end, I do just want to take a moment on the Cornell case specifically to just show this is an incredible example of the necessity and the power of the free press. I want to just acknowledge, you know, at a moment where we have an administration that is working actively to push lies and propaganda and to attack the free press, this is an example of why truth in journalism is so important.

Secondly, yes, it does, it is another violation that victim-survivors experience. You are not believed. You are blamed. I’ve told the story many times that despite the many third rail issues that people see me championing, the first time I ever received death threats was when I revealed my campus sexual assault. You know, as a sitting, you know, municipal elected, it was the first time I ever received death threats.

And then on top of that, so not you’re you know you’re not believed, you’re victim blamed, justice usually evades you, and then if there is a process for some sort of restitution or justice to pursue, you’re usually violated all over again because it is such an onerous process that you are navigating that is not being led by people that are usually trauma informed.

And so that’s why, you know, for my Survivors Restitution Act for this panel of adjudicators that would determine eligibility. That is one of our criteria: is that these are people that are trauma-informed.

I do want to just say this is so important, and thank you for the opportunity, Zerlina, for survivors and our loved ones. I just want to ensure that you have the immediate support you need and the resources that are available to you.

So, just you know, you can call RAINN’s National Sexual Assault Hotline, which is 1-800-656-4673. The National Domestic Violence Hotline, 1-800-799-7233. And if you’re in Massachusetts, you can reach out to the Boston Area Rape Crisis Center Hotline, as well as the Massachusetts Office for Victim Assistance and SafeLink. Just want to say that to any survivors listening.

ZERLINA: The other thing that you mentioned, and we’re talking about all of this in the context of who’s in the White House, but also the Epstein files and all of the Epstein files being released into the public domain, and no one in the United States losing their job or being the subject to an investigation—any of the people in power that were literally in these emails.

And when I think about the fact that it’s not just the alleged seven individuals that are part of this civil complaint, but the 57 individuals—including the seven that were in this group chat. And I think about how the group chat and the Epstein files and the Epstein emails and everybody, you know, having these conversations where everybody knows what they’re talking about allegedly—that speaks to the larger problem that we have to, I don’t know, get to the bottom of.

And that’s not something we can achieve through legislation, but by people who are in positions of power using their platforms to speak to the next generation of men and young men, and so how can we create this space to have that conversation? I mean, in the Obama era, they were running PSAs about consent, and I feel like that was such a long time ago.

REP. PRESSLEY: Yeah, no, I agree with you. I again, like on the issue of domestic violence, I would every year host something on White Ribbon Day, specifically just to enlist men, you know, in this work, and a lot of that work was happening on college campuses.

So I do think those are you know revenue neutral you know things that we can be doing. I mean, how do you shift culture? You shift behaviors? How do you shift behaviors? You know, it is fostering empathy. It is education. It is awareness. It’s tools. I think it’s you know it’s creating safe space, you know, for hard conversations.

But you know, if you are an adult proximate to any child, if you are a community mother, father, uncle, auntie, you know, in some sort of caregiving or parental role by blood or by bond—you are a child’s first teacher.

And so yes, there is a responsibility that we have in government and working with you know advocates and nonprofits and things like that to educate. But you need to be having those conversations, and there are tools available to help you navigate that. But you need to be having those conversations about consent with your children, you know any child that you have any connection to. That’s how we shift culture.

I would also say, Zerlina, that in the same way that I talk about my work to combat and root out and expose anti-Blackness, again the suffering, you know, of Black people around the globe—in many ways, is so normalized that it is almost unremarkable to people.

So you know, no one’s shocked if you say, you know, my husband was being surveyed, you know, and was targeted and experienced racial profiling at a traffic stop, you know—it’s like no one’s outraged by that because that has become a normalized, conflated part of our experience in America, right? Same reason why we talked previously in my work in Haiti that people could be very affected by the images coming out of Ukraine, but not feel similarly about Haiti, right?

So the same is true for girls and women. If I said I’m signing my daughter up for a self-defense class, no one would blink at that. When the larger question is, why do you have to do that? Why have we decided that that is an that that is a normalized part of what it is to be a girl, to be a woman.

That this is just a conflated part of our experience. That at some point you will experience sexual harassment. That at some point you may have to fend off someone. And the monsters, you know, are not usually someone lurking in a bush pouncing on you. It’s someone you know that you know, maybe someone even that you love.

So that is, those are the deeper things that we need to get at. You know why is that acceptable? Why is it okay that women in this country, you know, can’t access health care to save their life, you know, it’s like it’s just such a…So those are, those are the deeper issues that we have to get at, you know, because it’s unacceptable.

I don’t want—my daughter is an 18-year-old college freshman right now, you know, and the fact that the questions that we had to ask ourselves as parents, you know, even in determining what state she would go to school in. And what—and I want to say this about the schools, Zerlina—you know, they never want this stuff out because they don’t want someone to be less inclined to send their child, you know, to a school, and so they suppress, you know, a lot of not just the data, you know, you just you don’t know.

But so we’ve got some culture work we have to do. But in the meantime, I’m out here going hard in the paint for survivors’ restitution, justice, and healing, and pushing for accountability on the Oversight Committee every day.

ZERLINA: Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley, Democratic Representative for the Seventh District in Massachusetts, where my alma mater, Tufts University, is located I should mention. Thank you so much for being with us this morning. It’s always a pleasure to chat with you.
title: NEWS: Pressley Speaks Out on Cornell Case, Reaffirms Support for Survivors of Sexual Violence

WASHINGTON – Dayvon Darius Marson, 31, a previously convicted felon residing in the District, was sentenced today in U.S. District Court to 24 months in federal prison in connection with his possession of a loaded pistol -- an unbranded, non-descript P90 ghost gun -- and attempting to flee from a police traffic stop with it at a crowded gas station, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

“This conviction is part of our ongoing mission to crack down on gun violence and protect residents and visitors in the nation’s capital,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “Through Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful, which supports President Trump’s Executive Order, our continued efforts have removed more than 2,000 firearms from the hands of criminals.”

“This conviction is part of our ongoing mission to crack down on gun violence and protect residents and visitors in the nation’s capital,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “Through Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful, which supports President Trump’s Executive Order, our continued efforts have removed more than 2,000 firearms from the hands of criminals.”

Marson pleaded guilty on April 30, 2026, before Chief Judge James E. Boasberg to a charge of unlawful possession of a firearm by a felon. In addition to the 24-month prison term, Chief Judge Boasberg ordered Marson to serve 3 years of supervised release. Federal prosecutors had requested a 24-month prison sentence.

According to court documents, on Feb. 26, 2026, about 6:15 p.m., Metropolitan Police Department officers were patrolling the 3800 block of Minnesota Avenue NE, with members of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), and the FBI.

While patrolling, members noticed a Toyota Avalon sedan with heavily tinted windows at the Citgo gas station. Marson was in the driver’s seat and a young child in the rear-passenger seat. Officers questioned Marson, who could not provide a driver’s license. Speaking with Marson, an MPD officer spotted a half-empty bottle of tequila on the floor behind the driver’s seat.

The MPD officer ordered Marson to step out of the vehicle. Marson refused to do so. An ATF special agent opened the driver’s door and also ordered Marson to step out of the vehicle. Marson again refused to comply. Marson then put the transmission in “drive” and stepped on the accelerator, causing the vehicle to jolt forward as the ATF agent held onto the door. The vehicle dragged the ATF agent several feet before it collided with another parked vehicle.

After a brief struggle, members restrained Marson. As they did so, members spotted a brown P90 handgun with no serial number laying on the driver’s seat on which Marson had been sitting. The firearm was loaded with one round of .40 caliber ammunition in the chamber and 12 rounds in the magazine. During a search of Marson members recovered 11 multi-colored pills in a clear plastic bag from his socks. The pills were field-tested and yielded a positive indication for amphetamines.

This case was investigated by the Metropolitan Police Department, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), and the FBI Washington Field Office.

The matter was prosecuted under the Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful initiative by Assistant U.S. Attorney Mark Levy.

Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful supports President Trump's Executive Order that cracks down on gun violence, prioritizes federal firearms violations, pursues tougher penalties, and seeks detention for federal firearms violators.

Scott Statement on the Trump Administration’s National School Voucher Scheme
WASHINGTON – Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03), House Committee on Education and Workforce, released the following statement after the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s new proposed rule, entitled “Federal Scholarship Tax Credit.”
“America's public school system is founded on the promise that all students should have access to a high-quality public education. Today, the Treasury Department issued a proposed rule to implement the massive federal voucher scheme that was included in the Republicans’ ‘Big Ugly Bill.’ The program effectively diverts billions of taxpayer dollars away from public schools through the voucher program to subsidize private school education. Today’s proposal goes even further by prohibiting states from adding requirements to ensure the program meaningfully benefits public schools and the students who attend them. It also prohibits states from adding additional requirements to ensure students do not face discrimination when accessing educational services.
“Voucher schemes are inefficient, ineffective, and an expensive tool to privatize public education. If just 20 percent of eligible donors participate in the voucher scheme, the cost to the taxpayer would be roughly $37.6 billion — more than all federal spending on Title I and the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) combined. Meanwhile, data from existing state voucher programs shows that most students who benefit from those programs are already enrolled in private schools. Yet ninety percent of America’s children attend public schools. Despite this, public education has gone underfunded for decades. Without long term, sustained federal investment, schools and educators lack the resources they need to teach all students effectively.
“Moreover, when federal dollars go to public schools, schools are required to use that money to serve all students equally without discrimination. By funneling these dollars into private schools, taxpayers are unwittingly paying for schools that neglect underprivileged communities, are permitted to ignore civil rights laws, and can freely discriminate against students without accountability.
“Public dollars should be spent on public education. Just imagine what we could do if this money were used to improve all of America’s public schools instead. Democrats are committed to investing in public education for all communities — not just the privileged few.”

EPA Finalizes Interim Cleanup Plan to Address Mercury Contamination from Wappinger Creek Superfund Site in Dutchess County, New York
NEW YORK – U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has finalized its interim cleanup plan for removing mercury-contaminated sediment and soil from the upper portion of the Wappinger Creek Superfund site in Dutchess County, New York.
“The EPA is committed to protecting the health of Dutchess County residents and restoring the environment along Wappinger Creek,” said EPA Regional Administrator Michael Martucci. “This cleanup plan demonstrates our dedication to addressing historical contamination and ensuring a safer, healthier community for generations to come.”
The cleanup plan includes dredging and digging up contaminated sediment and soil from the creek bed and sides of the creek, transporting it to an EPA-approved off-site disposal facility, and then filling in the dug-up areas with clean material and restoring these areas. EPA’s interim cleanup plan will protect human health and address the greatest source of contamination resulting from historical industrial activities, while the agency continues its investigation at the site.
EPA will monitor conditions after the cleanup to confirm the effectiveness of the remedy and use the results to guide any future actions at the site. The agency held a public meeting on July 30, 2026, at the Grinnell Public Library to provide an overview of the cleanup proposal and answer community questions.
The EPA’s cleanup plan, including the EPA’s response to public comments, will be available at the Wappinger Creek Superfund site profile page.
Please see epa.gov/superfund for additional information.
