OAKLAND, Calif. – This week, FEMA awarded more than $50.6 million in grant funding to fire departments, first responder organizations, and other institutions focused on firefighter safety and fire prevention in California and Arizona. These awards will enable agencies to get the equipment, staff and support they need to carry out their critical, life-saving missions. This week’s fire grant funding brings the total amount awarded to Region 9 this year to nearly $70 million. Nationwide, FEMA awarded $648 million through its three fire grant programs.
“Firefighters and other first responders are everyday heroes, helping their neighbors and communities when they need it most,” said FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton. “Through this grant funding, FEMA is building the capability of these local organizations to respond to disasters and emergencies. By empowering fire departments to get the staff, training and equipment they need, FEMA is strengthening the resilience of American communities nationwide.”
The funding continues the Trump Administration’s support for firefighters and other first responders in California and Arizona. FEMA is administering these funds through its three fire grant programs: the Assistance to Firefighters Grants (AFG), the Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) grant program, and the Fire Prevention and Safety (FP&S) grant program. Examples of awards issued this week include:
- More than $13.2 million to County of Los Angeles in California to hire firefighters as part of the SAFER grant program.
- More than $4 million to City of San Buenaventura in California to hire firefighters as part of the SAFER grant program.
- More than $3.5 million to City of Sacramento in California to hire firefighters as part of the SAFER grant program.
- More than $3.3 million to City of Salinas in California to hire firefighters as part of the SAFER grant program.
- More than $1.8 million to Santa Rita Fire District in Green Valley, Arizona to improve operations and safety as part of the AFG grant program.
- More than $1.4 million to the Firefighter Cancer Support Network Inc. in El Monte, California through the FP&S grant program.
For information on all the awards issued this year, visit the fire grant program webpages on FEMA.gov: the Assistance to Firefighters Grants, the Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response grant program, and the Fire Prevention and Safety grant program.

FAYETTEVILLE – Two Northwest Arkansas men were sentenced to serve a total of 246 months combined in federal prison for drug trafficking and ammunition related crimes. Tony Bonds Jr. , age 25, was sentenced on September 28, 2026, to serve a total of 150 months in federal prison for using a communication device to facilitate the distribution of Fentanyl and for being a felon in possession of ammunition. Jared Haynie , age 30, his co-defendant, was sentenced on August 27, 2026, to serve 96 months in federal prison for using a communication device to facilitate conspiracy to distribute Adderall and conspiracy to distribute Fentanyl. Both men were linked to a Fentanyl overdose death that occurred in Farmington, Arkansas in 2022. The Honorable Chief Judge Timothy L. Brooks presided over the sentencing hearing in the United States District Court in Fayetteville.

According to court documents, officers with the Farmington Police Department responded to a Fentanyl overdose resulting in death in the morning hours of June 18, 2022. The ensuing investigation linked both Bonds and Haynie to the deceased. Phone records, interviews and other evidence revealed that both Bonds and Haynie used their cellular phones to commit drug trafficking crimes. Additionally, Bonds unlawfully possessed multiple rounds of .9mm ammunition while on felony state probation in multiple cases.

United States Attorney Kevin R. Holmes of the Western District of Arkansas made the announcement. The Fourth Judicial District Drug Task Force, Washington County Sheriff’s Office, State of Arkansas Probation and Parole, Drug Enforcement Administration, Washington County Coroner’s Office, and Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives investigated the case. Assistant United States Attorney Kimberly D. Harris prosecuted the case.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

Related court documents may be found on the Public Access to Electronic Records website at www.pacer.gov

US Labor Department finds railroad illegally terminated employee who refused to work during severe weather
LITTLE ROCK, AR – A U.S. Department of Labor Occupational Safety and Health Administration whistleblower investigation has concluded that Union Pacific Railroad Co. violated the Federal Railroad Safety Act when it removed from service and later terminated a North Little Rock yardman who notified management of nearby lightning and federal safety standards.
OSHA determined that the employee voiced concerns about nearby lightning, cited OSHA and NOAA lightening safety guidelines, initiated a safety stand-down, and refused to work until the storm passed. Within minutes of the stand-down, Union Pacific removed the employee from service and was later charged with insubordination. Union Pacific terminated his employment on May 30, 2024.
On June 10, 2026, OSHA ordered Union Pacific to remove from the employee’s employment records any reference of the incident, and pay back wages, lost benefits, compensatory and punitive damages totaling at least $304,869, and attorney’s fees. Union Pacific filed objections to OSHA’s order and has requested a hearing before a U.S. Department of Labor Administrative Law Judge.
OSHA’s Whistleblower Protection Program enforces 25 whistleblower statutes that protect employees from retaliation for reporting violations of workplace airline, anti-money laundering, commercial motor carrier, consumer product, criminal antitrust, environmental, financial reform, food safety, health insurance reform, maritime, motor vehicle safety, nuclear, pipeline, public transportation agency, railroad, safety and health, securities, and tax laws.
Editor’s note: The U.S. Department of Labor does not release the names of employees involved in whistleblower complaints.
title: US Labor Department finds railroad illegally terminated employee who refused to work during severe weather

text:
SEATTLE, W.A. — U.S. Representative Pramila Jayapal (WA-07) is introducing a new policy framework that reins in artificial intelligence (AI) by requiring every AI company to hold a federal charter to do business in the U.S. The AI charter is modeled after existing regulatory frameworks, combining the round-the-clock federal oversight, strict safety mandates, and structural separation built into national bank charters with the rigorous pre-release federal testing required for nuclear materials and dangerous weapons. The charter would ensure that the public’s interests come first and that the government has broad authority to hold AI companies accountable before they create harm rather than addressing abuses after the fact. AI companies that don’t agree, don’t comply, or put the public in danger get shut down.

“The crux of this bill is simple: if you want to be an AI company in this country, you have to obtain a public charter that has a broad set of terms and conditions to operate and ensure public benefit without the harms,” said Jayapal. “For too long, we’ve allowed a few Big Tech companies to dominate the market. They have used mass surveillance to steal private information, labor, and creative work, building trillion-dollar empires on our tracked personal lives. AI corporations and Big Tech are now following that same playbook. My National AI Charter Act framework gets at the root of the problem by disrupting the way the AI market is structured to give a very few companies all the power over our data and what happens with it and instead establishes clear rules of operation for these AI companies and prioritizes safety over profits.”

To date, traditional Big Tech policies have tried to patch up problems around the edges after harm is done, treating data privacy, children’s safety, worker rights, market concentration, and all the rest as separate issues. That approach hides the full scope, reach, and systemic impact of Big Tech’s surveillance monopolies. The fragmented response has allowed their lobbyists to divide the broad coalition of their victims, narrow fights to single-issue bills that they stall, make the case for self-regulation, and ignore the root profit drivers incentivizing their bad behavior.

The National AI Charter Act takes a fundamentally different approach by addressing the full scope of AI harms comprehensively upfront. The charter would be required to operate AI and its terms and conditions would be mandatory. At its core, the charter framework recognizes that AI risks are connected and driven by underlying market structures, surveillance business models, and profit motives. AI companies would be banned from building empires, releasing risky models, stealing through surveillance, exploiting workers, or causing harm. Gating market access to companies that comply with these requirements would break Big Tech’s grip on AI and protect the public from dangerous AI models.

The framework’s new legal authorities to hold AI companies accountable would build on those that already apply. They would not preempt or replace federal, state, and local laws, nor would they prevent or impede law enforcement agencies from enforcing those laws against AI companies or their executives. Instead, they would strengthen the hand of prosecutors and plaintiffs by proactively confirming the many ways these laws apply to AI, rather than leaving it to judges to interpret case by case. Most importantly, making this illegal conduct a charter violation would create a powerful additional enforcement tool with serious, mandatory consequences.

The National AI Charter Act framework’s comprehensive approach would bolster existing law enforcement by:

Taking power back from billionaires and putting the public and workers first: The handful of billionaires and tech giants that control AI’s future are locked in a dangerous race to the bottom. The framework separates AI companies from Big Tech monopolies and bans their predatory commercial surveillance so that AI isn’t baked into the core Internet platforms everyone uses or trained with data harvested by tracking everything people do online. It also claws back Big Tech’s ill-gotten gains from their monopoly data to fund direct payouts to all Americans.

Preventing harm up front instead of chasing it afterward: AI harms can spread too fast for after-the-fact enforcement to stop them, and fines don’t remedy the damage or truly deter it from happening again. The framework’s upfront charter requirements are not just rules to follow; they are a mandatory price of entry into the AI industry and the condition for remaining in it. Companies must continuously comply or get shut down.

Drawing bright lines on the full range of AI dangers: AI’s dangerous capabilities cannot be prevented with technical rules that quickly become obsolete; they have to be comprehensively banned outright. Under the framework, AI systems capable of going rogue, creating catastrophic hazards, replacing skilled work, exploiting children, or causing other serious public harms are outlawed and cannot be released.

Putting the government in charge of safety at every stage: AI companies have admitted the risks of their own systems while still insisting they should police themselves. The framework replaces the AI industry’s failed self-regulation with round-the-clock federal oversight, testing in government facilities and approval to release, adversarial stress tests, and a government-controlled kill switch.

Imposing strict liability on AI companies and executives: As long as the price of causing harm is likely to cost less than the potential profits, AI companies will keep taking reckless risks. The framework reverses these incentives by holding AI companies and their executives strictly liable for lawbreaking, with loss of charter and criminal penalties for the most serious violations.

“At the end of the day, the American people are feeling a loss of control, of their personal data, of their jobs, of their ability to even know what they see online is real,” Jayapal added. “This legislation would restore a level of control and ensure that every search made online isn’t tracked, every family photo posted isn’t training an AI model, and every piece of our lives isn’t monetized by corporations.”

A wide range of experts have weighed in on the need for a comprehensive approach:

“The public has paid an extraordinary price for big tech’s self-regulation. Representative Jayapal’s framework learns from those mistakes. For generations we have required banks, drug makers, and nuclear operators to meet public terms before they do business, and AI companies should be no different,” said Lina Khan, Director, Center for Law and the Economy, and former Chair of the Federal Trade Commission.

“This legislative framework meaningfully advances the ball to establish a comprehensive set of reforms to address the potential for societal harms from AI,” said Jonathan Kanter, former Assistant Attorney General of the Department of Justice’s Antitrust Division.

“We really need a framework like this to start getting to the big question of how Americans want to regulate AI,” said Tim Wu, Julius Silver Professor of Law, Science and Technology, Columbia Law School.

“Innovation and safety are not opposing concepts; they’re two sides of the same coin—which is why regulation is vitally important. AI is rapidly transforming our classrooms, workplaces, and economy, but Big Tech must be held accountable for their business models, just like every other industry in the country. If these companies want to win the trust of the American people, they must respect the rules of the road. Representative Jayapal’s framework does exactly that by establishing preemptive guardrails that compel AI firms to serve the public interest, not just the narrow interests of shareholders,” said Randi Weingarten, President, American Federation of Teachers.

“The comprehensive approach being pioneered by Representative Jayapal’s National AI Charter Act gets to the root of the extreme harms of unregulated and out-of-control AI. The mandatory requirement to be chartered and operate only under strict guardrails and associated liability will hold companies accountable and ensure that protecting the public is considered first as tech is created. Public Citizen applauds this move to fight concentration and to defend children, workers, and the general public from pervasive harm,” said Lisa Gilbert, Co-President, Public Citizen.

“I’m thrilled that Representative Jayapal is taking such a leading role in addressing the enormous societal risks posed by increasingly powerful and uncontrollable AI systems. Efforts like the National AI Charter Act to address the full scope of AI harms are more important today than ever before,” said Anthony Aguire, President and CEO, Future of Life Institute.

“Big Tech companies have continually pulled the rug out from under families, workers, and small businesses to build powerful and unaccountable Big Tech monopolies that dictate to us how we should live our own lives. Enough is enough. We are proud to support the National AI Charter Act because it will establish desperately-needed rules of the road, punish AI companies that release dangerous products, and create the clear public benefit that the American people are calling for,” said Sacha Haworth, Executive Director, Tech Oversight Project.

“The same billionaires who walked away with huge tax breaks last year are now racing to take over AI. For years they’ve lobbied every attempt at regulation to death. Representative Jayapal’s plan goes after the source of their power: their monopolies, their surveillance, and their stolen data. It’s the first plan big enough to match the problem, and it puts families back in charge,” said Kristen Crowell, Executive Director, Families Over Billionaires.

“This is not a time for half measures. We are facing serious challenges, if not crises, on every possible front in this country, and we need leaders who are putting forward proposals that meet the moment. This framework puts humans at the center of the debate about AI and regulation and puts power back in the hands of people over the technology that shapes their lives,” said Shaunna Thomas, Executive Director, Guardrails Action.

“We have a long history of governing banks, utilities, critical infrastructure. In all of these, we have leverage over market interests, and the ability to gate access to the market on the condition that the public interest is protected. We need commensurate leverage over large AI companies, and this is the right lineage to draw upon,” said Amba Kak, Co-Executive Director, AI Now.

“Rep. Jayapal is right: if you want to run an AI company in this country, you should have to accept the public’s terms. For too long, Big Tech has acted first and answered for the harm later, if ever. A national charter would change that. We also support her proposal to structurally separate the AI stack. And we urge Congress to consider building on the authorities existing agencies already have. There’s more work ahead to make sure this framework can stand up to Big Tech’s lawyers and lobbyists, and we look forward to doing it with her,” said Nidhi Hegde, Executive Director, American Economic Liberties Project.

“We are in the midst of a reckoning on AI as working families and communities across the country are rightfully standing up and sounding the alarm on the growing harms that this technology is posing on our day to day lives. For too long, Big Tech CEOs have been able to divide and distract policymakers while they use the public’s own data to raise prices, push millions of working people into debt, and rake in record profits. It is long past time for policymakers to break Big Tech’s grip on AI and we applaud Congresswoman Jayapal for unveiling the National AI Charter Act Framework which marks a critical first step in reining in Big Tech and protecting families,” said Mike Pierce, Executive Director, Protect Borrowers.

“It’s unacceptable that Big Tech continues to abuse our data, turbocharge scams, and act with impunity. This framework reflects the interconnectedness of the harms that AI companies are already causing and the necessity of strong, robust enforcement mechanisms that can provide meaningful protections for consumers,” said Susan Weinstock, CEO, Consumer Federation of America.

“We welcome Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal’s leadership to address AI’s real harms. We’re encouraged to see a comprehensive, structural approach with sharp guardrails and bright lines. For too long, a handful of tech giants have written the rules and remade society to suit themselves. It’s high time the public wrote the future instead,” said Stacy Mitchell, Co-Executive Director, Institute for Local Self-Reliance.

“For far too long, the tech oligarchs and those whom they directly or indirectly fund have sought to normalize how the modern technology sector prefers to operate. Congresswoman Jayapal rightly recognizes as illegitimate those practices that tech oligarchs have long celebrated as creative and adventurous even as they violate longstanding laws and norms. In a democracy, it is publicly elected figures who are responsible for leading the future, not the oligarchic class,” said Jeff Hauser, Executive Director, Revolving Door Project.

“AI poses very real risks to safety, privacy, workers, competition, and more. This range of harms requires a comprehensive, structural policy response. In many critical industries, we mandate charters to do business, impose bright-line bans on problematic conduct, subject firms to independent inspection, and use other common-sense tools to reduce risks. The U.S. needs to deploy these same tools to keep powerful firms accountable and to put the public’s interest first in AI,” said Asad Ramzanali, Director of AI & Technology Policy, Vanderbilt Policy Accelerator.

“This is a smart framework that recognizes how powerful AI companies are already putting the public at risk, exploiting data, and consolidating control over critical technologies and markets. Adopting the charter model offers a sweeping yet adaptable way to welcome innovation while imposing enforceable obligations for safety and fair competition, placing necessary checks on private power, and ensuring corporations develop AI in the public interest,” said Courtney Radsch, Director of the Center for Media and Digital Governance, Open Markets Institute

“AI companies and their executives are threatening working people’s health, safety, and pocketbooks in their reckless race for profits. Congresswoman Jayapal’s National AI Charter framework would take on these threats in a comprehensive way by putting the public interest first and making the existence of AI firms contingent on their compliance with strong safety and privacy requirements alongside worker, consumer, and investor protections,” said Maya Jenkins, Senior Policy Analyst, Americans for Financial Reform.

An outline of the framework can be found here.

The framework was developed, in part, following a hearing that Jayapal hosted on the dangers of surveillance AI conducted by Big Tech.
title: Jayapal Introduces Legislative Framework Establishing National Charter System to Rein in AI

Yesterday, Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16), joined by Representatives Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC), Mark Pocan (WI-2) and Dina Titus (NV-1), sent a letter to Department of the Navy Secretary Hung Cao requesting more information on the use of swine in hyperbaric diving experiments.

The full letter can be found here or below:

Secretary Cao:

We are writing to express our strong concern regarding the Department of the Navy funded research projects involving the use of swine in hyperbaric diving experiments, specifically the recent study conducted at Duke University utilizing animal models to test breathing gas switches involving carbon tetrafluoride.

While we recognize the vital importance of ensuring the safety, health, and operational readiness of our divers and submariners, we remain deeply troubled by the continued reliance on animal testing when novel scientific methods and advanced models exist and should be fully exhausted. Specifically, the research recently published titled "Isobaric counterdiffusion of carbon tetrafluoride breathing gas to prevent severe decompression sickness" subjected juvenile swine to extreme pressure profiles, rapid decompressions, and severe physiological distress to evaluate decompression sickness mitigation, leading to mortality for some of the swine.

As advocates for animal welfare standards, we question whether the Department has thoroughly exhausted non-animal methodologies. We request that the Department of the Navy provide responses to the following questions within 30 days:

Have there been insistences on where alternative methods are the preferred method to live, animal testing? If so, what were the reasonings behind those decisions and the effectiveness of the results?

What specific validation protocols are used to ensure that all non-animal testing alternatives are fully exhausted before any animal models are approved for use?

Does the Navy enforce protocols or data-sharing agreements to prevent redundant animal testing on the same research questions across different laboratories or research groups

How many total studies are planned under this overarching research initiative, and what is the projected timeline for concluding all associated animal testing?

What specific military or operational necessity required the use of live pigs rather than advanced computer or lab-based modeling for this research? What total amount of federal funding from the Department of Defense has been allocated to institutions for animal testing over the past five fiscal years?

What specific steps are being taken by the Navy to transition toward non-animal methods?

Our national security and the health of our service members are paramount, but we must achieve these goals ethically and responsibly. We look forward to your prompt response and to working together to ensure taxpayer funds support both naval innovation and high standards of animal welfare.
title: Congresswoman Escobar Sends Navy Letter Requesting More Information on the Use of Swine in Diving Experiments

California Man Arrested for Smuggling More Than $300 Million in Export-Controlled Computer Servers to China
The owner of a San Gabriel Valley-based technology company was arrested today on a three-count federal indictment charging him with smuggling more than $300 million worth of export-controlled high-end computer servers containing U.S.-manufactured graphics processing units (GPUs) commonly used for Super Intelligence (SI) applications to China.
“SI is the defining technology of the era,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “The National Security Division will protect the American advantage in the chips that power this technology, a product of our unparalleled innovation and hard work, from illegal diversion by our economic and military adversaries.”
“Protecting America’s national security means keeping our advanced Super Intelligence technology from being used to strengthen our adversaries’ military capabilities,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli for the Central District of California. “This defendant allegedly used false paperwork and shipments through third countries to smuggle more than $300 million in export-controlled computer servers to China. We will aggressively prosecute those who put our national security at risk for profit.”
“The FBI’s investigation revealed that Lui allegedly sold the Chinese government hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of American Super Intelligence technology, in clear violation of U.S. export control laws,” said Assistant Director Roman Rozhavsky of the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division. “Controlling the export of advanced SI technology is critical to safeguarding our national security and defending the homeland, and the FBI will keep fighting for America’s businesses and economic security. We’re grateful to our partners across the U.S. government and private sector for their assistance, and we’ll continue holding accountable anyone who violates U.S. export laws to enrich themselves and help our adversaries.”
“Preventing the illegal export of controlled technology is critical to protecting our national security,” said Special Agent in Charge John E. Helsing of the Department of Defense Office of Inspector General Defense Criminal Investigative Service (DCIS) Western Field Office. “These technologies provide core advantages to U.S. forces, and ensuring they remain safeguarded prevents adversaries from exploiting them. Today’s action underscores our commitment to protecting advanced defense capabilities and enforcing the laws that keep them out of the hands of those who may threaten the United States.”
“The Bureau of Industry and Security is committed to using all lawful means to protect national security and hold violators accountable,” said Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Export Enforcement David A. Peters of the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security Office of Export Enforcement.
Greg Lui, 38, also known as “Yiu Kong Lui,” of San Gabriel, California, is expected to make his initial appearance and be arraigned this afternoon.
Lui is charged with one count of conspiracy to violate the Export Control Reform Act and the Export Administration Regulations, one count of outbound smuggling, and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering.
According to the indictment returned on Sept. 29, Lui owns Earthmade Computer Inc., a City of Industry-based technology company and closely held corporation.
From 2023 to 2024, Lui and his co-conspirators used Earthmade to buy and send export-controlled items to China without the required licenses issued by the U.S. Department of Commerce. Instead, they shipped these items to countries such as Malaysia and Singapore, where no such license is required, then illegally re-exported them to China.
The items in question were high-end computer servers containing GPUs manufactured by companies that specialize in SI computing. Lui did so despite knowing that the true end users of the servers he purchased were in China. As part of the scheme, Lui and his co-conspirators provided false documentation to U.S.-based manufacturers that misrepresented that the items would be going to permissible end users and end destinations that did not require an export license. After placing these orders, Lui employed various freight forwarding companies to ship the export-controlled servers to countries such as Malaysia and Singapore. Once the servers arrived in these locations, Lui worked with his coconspirators to reship the items to China. From January 2024 to October 2024, Earthmade received more than $176 million from two Malaysia-based shipment companies as part of the scheme.
According to the indictment, Lui executed this scheme knowing that U.S. government regulations barred the export of such high-end technology to China to protect the national security and foreign policy interests of the United States. According to U.S. government regulations, such high-end GPUs could make significant contributions to the military potential of other nations.
In January 2024, Lui emailed a conspirator indicating that a Malaysian transshipment company wished to purchase 70 servers with export-restricted GPUs. In that email correspondence, Lui attached an export compliance form that indicated that the Malaysian company was aware of U.S. export laws that restricted the sale, transshipment, or export of these specific servers.
Later that month, Lui submitted a purchase order to a U.S. manufacturer for 27 of these servers for approximately $7,614,000. He and a co-conspirator then caused the servers to be shipped from Los Angeles to Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. The packing list for this shipment indicated that the shipment contained 27 servers with GPUs, which were export controlled and could not be sent to China without a license.
In March 2024, a co-conspirator emailed a Malaysian government official that 27 servers had, in fact, been transshipped to a China-based buyer.
If convicted of all charges, Lui could face a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison on the conspiracy count, a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison on the money laundering count, and a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison on the smuggling count.
The U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security Office of Export Enforcement, the Defense Criminal Investigative Service, and the FBI are investigating this matter.
Assistant U.S. Attorneys Colin S. Scott and Joseph S. Guzman for the Central District of California and Trial Attorney Eli Ross of the National Security Division’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section are prosecuting the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Alexander Su for the Central District of California is handling the civil and criminal forfeitures of the seized property.
An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: California Man Arrested for Smuggling More Than $300 Million in Export-Controlled Computer Servers to China

Ninth Circuit Leaves Resolution Copper Ruling in Place
On Tuesday, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit rejected all petitions for rehearing in cases challenging a land exchange that is necessary for the Resolution Copper project in Arizona. The order leaves in place the March 13 decision by the court’s panel, which allowed the federal government to proceed with a congressionally mandated land exchange crucial to advancing development of one of the largest known copper deposits in the world.
“Copper is crucial for our nation’s electrical grid, national defense, energy technologies, and advanced manufacturing,” said Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General Adam Gustafson of the Justice Department’s Energy and Natural Resource Division (ENRD). “This project will assist in developing a continuous domestic copper supply, which will support national security objectives and strengthen the U.S. economy. The exchange has resulted in federal ownership of more than 5,400 acres of ecologically and culturally significant land in Arizona.”
In rejecting the plaintiffs’ numerous claims, the Ninth Circuit has now declined to reconsider the decision of its panel. This ruling is another major step toward ensuring the United States can meet growing demand for critical minerals.
Deputy Assistant Attorney General Robert Stander of ENRD argued the appeal. ENRD’s Appellate Section handled the matter on appeal, and ENRD’s Natural Resources Section handled this matter in the District Court.
title: Ninth Circuit Leaves Resolution Copper Ruling in Place

Grand Central Atelier Launches The Bruce Cole Lectures
"Echoes of the Renaissance" will feature a panel conversation celebrating new NEH-supported humanities initiative, with opening remarks from NEH Chairman Michael McDonald
Grand Central Atelier, a fine arts academy devoted to the preservation, teaching, and reinvention of classical art traditions, next week launches The Bruce Cole Lectures, an ambitious speaker series designed to spark a contemporary renaissance in traditional arts and humanistic inquiry. The series begins on October 6, 2026 with "Echoes of the Renaissance,” a panel conversation held at the historic The Players in New York City. The series is part of the academy’s Bruce Cole Humanities Initiative, a multi-year public program supported by a major grant from the National Endowment for the Humanities.
The kickoff event opens with remarks by Chairman Michael McDonald of the National Endowment for the Humanities, followed by reflections from Dr. Wilfred McClay, Professor of History at Hillsdale College and former member of the National Council on the Humanities, and Dr. Michelle Erhardt, Professor of Art History and Associate Dean of the School of the Arts at Christopher Newport University. A panel conversation will follow, moderated by Grand Central Atelier Founder Jacob Collins, a leading figure in the contemporary revival of classical realism.
The series is named in honor of the late Bruce Cole (1938–2018), a distinguished art historian of the Italian Renaissance and the longest-serving Chairman of the National Endowment for the Humanities. A recipient of the Presidential Citizens Medal and the Knight of the Grand Cross of the Republic of Italy, Cole championed the humanities as essential tools for a self-governing citizenry. His signature initiatives, We the People and Picturing America, brought iconic American art to over 80,000 schools and libraries nationwide. A prolific scholar and Distinguished Professor of Fine Arts at Indiana University, Cole authored fifteen books, including seminal texts such as The Renaissance Artist at Work: From Pisano to Titian, Italian Art, 1250–1550, and Art of the Western World.
Following the October 6th event, The Bruce Cole Lectures series will continue on December 4th, 2026 with a feature talk by Jacob Collins, where he will deliver an apologia for the traditional arts as practiced by Grand Central Atelier for over two decades.
Supported by a $2 million NEH grant, the Grand Central Atelier Bruce Cole Humanities Initiative is a two-year public program dedicated to enriching the study of art, history, and culture within the Atelier and educating the public about the history of art and traditional artistic techniques. The Initiative brings together artists, scholars, and the public to consider the enduring role of the humanities in shaping both personal and civic life. The Initiative will feature twelve public lectures, a two-day capstone symposium, two prestigious postdoctoral fellowships, and a digital publication.
For more information on The Bruce Cole Humanities Initiative and Bruce Cole Lectures at the Grand Central Atelier visit: https://grandcentralatelier.org/bruce-cole-humanities-initiative/
title: Grand Central Atelier Launches The Bruce Cole Lectures

CARNEGIE, PA – Today, Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17) and Congresswoman Summer Lee (PA-12) announced $11,023,181 in federal funding to upgrade thousands of feet of lighting and pavement on Runway 10L/28R at the Pittsburgh International Airport (PIT), further modernizing Western Pennsylvanians’ go-to airport.

The U.S. Department of Transportation awards this money through the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). The multi-phase funding will help extend the service life of the runway, minimize Foreign Object Debris (FOD), improve aircrafts’ ride quality, and make the airfield safer at Pittsburgh International Airport.

“We in Western Pennsylvanians should be able to rely on the safety and reliability of our infrastructure,” said Congressman Deluzio. “That’s why I am excited to announce another round of federal funding that will help make the Pittsburgh Airport one of the safest and most modern airports in the world.”

“Pittsburgh International Airport is one of the gateways to Western Pennsylvania, and the infrastructure behind it has to be safe, reliable, and ready for the people and workers who depend on it every single day,” said Congresswoman Lee. “This more than $11 million federal investment is exactly what public dollars should be doing: coming back home, strengthening the things our communities rely on, supporting good jobs, and making sure a major piece of our regional economy is built to last. I’m glad to see this funding headed home to Pittsburgh International Airport, and I’ll keep fighting to bring federal investment back to Western Pennsylvania.”

“Airports across the country are part of national critical infrastructure and federal support is key in helping to keep the national airspace moving. Pittsburgh International Airport is an important economic driver for our region and this grant helps to fund airfield improvements at PIT including runway paving and upgrading lighting infrastructure. Thank you to Congressman Deluzio and our entire federal delegation for their continued support,” said Pittsburgh International Airport CEO Christina Cassotis.

###
title: Deluzio, Lee Announce $11 Million More in Federal Funding for Safety Upgrades at Pittsburgh Airport

WASHINGTON – Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-MN), Chair of the U.S.-Africa Policy Working Group, Rep. John Garamendi (D-CA), Co-Chair of the Ethiopian American Caucus and member of the U.S.-Africa Policy Working Group, and Rep. Jim McGovern (D-MA), member of the U.S.-Africa Policy Working Group, released the following statement on hostilities in Ethiopia:

“We are deeply alarmed by increasing violence in Ethiopia, including the Ethiopian military strike last week on an aid convoy delivering assistance in Tigray.

"The 2022 Pretoria Agreement that silenced the guns in Northern Ethiopia committed all parties to ceasing hostilities, protecting civilians, allowing humanitarian access to those affected, and undertaking comprehensive transitional justice to hold those responsible for human rights abuses and violations responsible. Unfortunately, this agreement has not been upheld, and these conditions have not been met.

"This increased conflict threatens the entire country and the region as a whole, which is already reeling from the previous war in Northern Ethiopia and the devastating conflict in Sudan. Ordinary civilians are bearing the brunt of this violence.

"We urge all parties in Ethiopia to immediately recommit to peace negotiations and uphold their responsibilities under the Pretoria Agreement. Ethiopia’s neighbors and the international community must work to defuse tensions and facilitate peace.

"We also urge the U.S. State Department to work with all parties to end the violence and hold those responsible accountable. The people of Ethiopia deserve peace and justice.”

###
title: Omar, Garamendi, McGovern Release Statement on Hostilities in Ethiopia

The Department of War releases updates to Hostile Fire Pay (HFP) and Imminent Danger Pay (IDP), marking the first major adjustment to these special duty pays in more than two decades. The increased rates are designed to appropriately compensate Service members for the varying levels of operational risk they face while serving the United States around the world.
The updated policy increases the monthly rate for HFP to $450 and the monthly rate for IDP to $275, effective October 1, 2026.
Since October 2002, both HFP and IDP pay have been set at a flat monthly rate of $225. The new tiered model better reflects the differences between serving in an area where danger is possible and facing hostile fire.
Application of the new rates:
HFP will be issued at the full monthly rate of $450 for any month in which a Service member is exposed to a hostile fire event.
IDP will be prorated at $9.16 per day, up to a maximum of $275 per month, based on the number of days a Service member is present in a designated imminent danger area.
If an IDP-designated area escalates into active combat, commanders can transition personnel from IDP to HFP immediately. This provides a clear and timely mechanism to acknowledge heightened risk levels.
Consistent with Department policy, Service members may not receive both HFP and IDP for the same period of service.
Service members and their families are encouraged to consult their command financial specialists or local finance offices for detailed information on how these changes will appear on the Leave and Earnings Statements (LES). Finance personnel will also be available to answer questions regarding individual entitlements and eligibility.
The Department, under 37 U.S. Code § 351, is granted statutory authority to increase HFP to a maximum amount of $450 per month and IDP to a maximum amount of $275 per month, as authorized by Congress and outlined in federal law and the National Defense Authorization Act. The Secretary of War is authorized to establish any amount up to the statutory ceiling.
title: Statement by Chief Pentagon Spokesman, Sean Parnell, on the Department of War's Historic Increase to Hostile Fire and Imminent Danger Pay

Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25), the Military Construction, Veterans Affairs and Related Agencies Appropriations Subcommittee Ranking Member, released the following in response to recent comments by U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth regarding a possible new military base:

Brad Schimel, First Assistant United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Wisconsin, announced that on September 30, 2026, Sara Luma, age 30, was charged with Unlawfully Voting as a Non-Citizen, contrary to Title 18, United States Code, Section 611.

The criminal complaint alleges that Luma was born in North Macedonia and is a citizen of that country. She is not a United States citizen. On November 5, 2024, Luma voted in the federal general election in the city of Sheboygan, Wisconsin. Luma was not allowed to vote in federal elections in Wisconsin because she was not a United States citizen.

The criminal complaint further alleges Luma registered to vote on the same day as the election and signed the Wisconsin Voter Registration Application form falsely certifying that she was a citizen of the United States. Luma was interviewed by a federal law enforcement agent and admitted to registering and voting in Sheboygan on November 5, 2024.

Immigration court records indicate that Luma was taken into custody when seeking to re-enter the United States on August 13, 2026. In September 2026, as part of removal proceedings, she was allowed to self-deport to North Macedonia. If Luma attempts to reenter the United States, she will be subject to arrest on a warrant issued in the case.

“Protecting the integrity of our elections is critically important,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Schimel. “It is illegal for non-citizens to vote and the consequences of doing so are quite serious. I hope this case and others that may follow will educate people on the law and serve to deter any non-citizen from voting illegally.”

A criminal complaint is only a charge and is not evidence of guilt. The defendant is presumed innocent and is entitled to a fair trial at which the government must prove her guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.

October 1, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced its annual funding opportunity of up to $400 million to advance the frontiers of scientific knowledge and lay the foundation for future technologies and innovation. The funding delivers on President Trump’s Executive Order Restoring Gold Standard Science by supporting rigorous, transparent, and mission-driven research across DOE’s Office of Science to strengthen America’s scientific and technological leadership.
“Foundational research is where the breakthroughs that shape America’s future begin,” said DOE Under Secretary for Science Darío Gil. “Through this investment, we are empowering our nation’s researchers to pursue bold ideas, push the boundaries of discovery, and build the scientific foundations for tomorrow’s technologies—strengthening America’s global leadership in science and innovation.”
The funding will support research across DOE’s Office of Science and its major programs to tackle some of the nation’s greatest scientific challenges and accelerate discoveries in areas critical to America’s future. Research will span Advanced Scientific Computing Research, Basic Energy Sciences, Biological and Environmental Research, Fusion Energy Sciences, High Energy Physics, Nuclear Physics, and Isotope R&D and Production.
The Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO), informally known as the “Open Call,” is issued annually at the beginning of each Fiscal Year (FY). It provides a vehicle for DOE’s Office of Science to solicit applications from institutions for research support in areas not covered by more specific, topical NOFOs issued by the office in FY 2027.
More details about this Notice of Funding Opportunity can be found here.
DOE’s Office of Science is the nation’s largest supporter of basic research in the physical sciences, funds research at hundreds of universities nationwide, and stewards 10 of DOE’s National Laboratories.

WICHITA, KAN. – A Kansas businessman pleaded guilty to firearms and racketeering offenses.

According to court documents, Justin Lane, 37, of Maize pleaded guilty to one count of prohibited person in possession of a firearm and one count of interstate use of facilities in interstate commerce to aid in a racketeering enterprise.

Lane is the owner of High Hopes ICT which includes multiple storefronts. On November 13, 2025, law enforcement executed warrants at six business locations and Lane’s home. Officers found a significant quantity of high potency THC or marijuana products as well as paraphernalia.

As part of his plea agreement, Lane admits using his businesses to sell gummies, vapes, and other items he knew contained THC or marijuana. Lane ordered products from outside of Kansas and used commercial companies for deliveries to his Kansas business locations which constituted the use of interstate commerce to promote an unlawful business (selling marijuana and THC products) which is prohibited by state and federal law.

Because of a previous felony conviction in U.S. District Court for the District of Kansas for the possession of an unregistered firearm, Lane cannot legally possess firearms, silencers, or ammunition. Law enforcement found firearms at two of Lane’s businesses and an additional 28 firearms, six silencers and ammunition at Lane’s home.

Law enforcement submitted for forensic testing the marijuana seized during controlled purchases from Lane’s businesses as well as searches at High Hopes ICT. The test results were positive for THC in excess of the amount allowed by state and federal law. As for gummies, undercover officers purchased at some of the stores, staff advised them to only use a portion of the gummies at one time due to the strength of the THC contained in a single gummy. This was indicative to law enforcement that the gummies also contained THC in excess of the amount allowed by state and federal law.

Lane is scheduled to be sentenced on January 5, 2027. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

The Sedgwick County Sheriff’s Office and Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives (ATF) are investigating the case.

###
title: Maize man pleads guilty to firearms and racketeering crimes

Representative Ocasio-Cortez and Senator Schumer Introduce Bicameral Legislation to Restore Health Coverage for 450,000 New Yorkers
Press Release
Because of Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act, over 450,000 New Yorkers lost Essential Plan coverage.
WASHINGTON, D.C. - Today, Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14) and Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) led the entire New York Democratic delegation in the introduction of the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act. The Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act would restore health coverage to the nearly 450,000 New Yorkers who were kicked off of the Essential Plan under the Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
“Congressional Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act represents the largest loss of healthcare in American history. Apart from cutting nearly $1 trillion from Medicaid, this bill specifically targeted New York by gutting the Essential Plan and stripping almost half a million New Yorkers of their health insurance. We must take immediate steps to repeal the harmful impacts of H.R. 1 on New York” said Representative Ocasio-Cortez. “Today, I am introducing the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act alongside Senator Schumer and the entire New York Democratic Delegation to reinstate federal funding for the New York Essential Plan and ensure that New Yorkers can once again access this critical health program.”
“Make no mistake, the ‘Big, Ugly Bill’ has been a disaster that has left American families sicker, poorer, and less safe,” said Leader Schumer. “Republicans promised lower health care costs, but they delivered soaring premiums, sky-high deductibles, and coverage ripped away from millions – all to give billionaires and big corporations a tax cut. In an act of political retribution, Republicans specifically targeted New Yorkers, kicking nearly half a million people off their coverage. Leaving working families with no affordable alternatives isn’t policy; it’s punishment. And it undermines public health and the health of our vital hospitals and community health centers. We must work to pass this legislation, reverse this cruel policy, and restore health insurance to all New Yorkers.”
“H.R. 1 decimated New York’s Essential Plan, ripping health insurance coverage from hundreds of thousands of New Yorkers and weakening the finances of every hospital in the State. That’s why the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act is so critically important. It would repeal this terrible HR 1 policy and establish a permanent option for expanded basic health plan coverage. New York’s hospital community is deeply grateful to Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, and the New York delegation Democrats for championing this effort to expand health insurance and strengthen New York’s health care safety net,” said Kenneth E. Raske, President, Greater New York Hospital Association.
“Losing coverage can force patients to delay care, skip medications, or make impossible choices between their health and other basic needs. Community health centers care for everyone who walks through their doors, whether they have insurance or not, and as more New Yorkers lose coverage, the strain on CHCs and their patients grows,” said Rose Duhan, president and CEO of the Community Health Care Association of New York State. “Ensuring New Yorkers have coverage helps patients get the care they need, when they need it, from providers they know and trust. CHCANYS is proud to support the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act.”
“HANYS strongly supports the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act, which would reverse H.R. 1’s harmful limitations on New Yorkers’ eligibility for this affordable health insurance option and provide states the flexibility to extend this coverage to individuals with incomes up to 250% of the federal poverty line,” said Thomas J. Quatroche Jr., PhD, president and CEO, Healthcare Association of New York State. “Affordable health coverage is becoming out of reach for many New Yorkers, and H.R. 1 threatens to leave even more people uninsured. HANYS applauds Senate Minority Leader Schumer and Rep. Ocasio-Cortez for introducing this important bill and for their ongoing dedication to protecting and improving all New Yorkers’ access to healthcare coverage and care.”
“This legislation would reverse some of the worst harms of H.R. 1 and allow more New Yorkers to access affordable health insurance coverage,” said Mitchell Katz, MD President and CEO of NYC Health + Hospitals. “Our health care system is grateful to Senator Schumer and Representative Ocasio-Cortez for their leadership and commitment to keeping New Yorkers connected to care.”
The legislation would repeal the One Big Beautiful Bill Act’s premium tax credit eligibility restrictions, fully restoring funding for the Essential Plan. In addition to restoring the program, the legislation would provide all states with the option to expand health coverage through the Affordable Care Act’s Basic Health Plan.
This legislation is cosponsored by the entire New York Democratic delegation including: Senator Gillibrand (D-NY), Leader Jeffries (NY-08), and Representatives Clarke (NY-09), Espaillat (NY-13), Gillen (NY-04), Goldman (NY-10), Kennedy (NY-26), Latimer (NY-16), Mannion (NY-22), Meeks (NY-5), Meng (NY-6), Morelle (NY-25), Nadler (NY-12), Riley (NY-19), Ryan (NY-18), Suozzi (NY-3), Tonko (NY-20), Torres (NY-15), and Velázquez (NY-07).
The full bill text is available here.

SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico – On September 23, 2026, a federal grand jury returned an indictment charging Faustino David Reyes-Rodríguez, 25, of Ponce, PR residing in Caguas, with possession, receipt and distribution of child sexual abuse material, announced Héctor Ramírez-Carbó, Acting U.S. Attorney for the District of Puerto Rico. The arrest follows an investigation by Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) with the assistance of the Puerto Rico Police Bureau (PRPB) and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Puerto Rico.

According to the indictment, from in or about December 2025 to May 2026, Reyes-Rodríguez knowingly received and distributed child exploitation material. Moreover, from July 2024 to May 2026, the defendant possessed images of child pornography including images of toddlers, and prepubescent minors in his cellular phone and tablet.

“The U.S. Attorney’s Office will continue to work with its law enforcement partners to aggressively investigate and prosecute persons who use technology to victimize children who are victims of child exploitation crimes,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Ramírez-Carbó. “The U.S. Attorney’s Office and HSI encourage potential victims to come forward if you have knowledge that this defendant or any other adult has engaged in this type of criminal behavior. Tipsters may remain anonymous.”

“As we begin Fiscal Year 2027, this arrest stands as a stark warning to those who exploit children: HSI is relentless. Predators often use the anonymity of gaming platforms and messaging apps to pose as children, weaving webs of deception to prey on the innocent, ”said HSI San Juan Acting Special Agent in Charge Yariel Ramos. “Regardless of the technology they hide behind, our commitment to finding these offenders and protecting our most vulnerable remains unwavering. We will find you, and you will be held accountable.”

Rivera-Santos had his initial appearance before U.S. Magistrate Judge Marcos E. López and was ordered to remain temporarily detained at the Guaynabo Metropolitan Detention Center pending further proceedings. If convicted for the charges the defendant faces the following penalties: (1) receipt of child exploitation material - a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment of five years and a maximum term of imprisonment of 20 years; and (2) possession of child exploitation material - a maximum term of imprisonment of 10 years. All charges of conviction are to be followed by a term of supervised release after imprisonment of no less than 5 years up to life. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Daynelle Álvarez-Lora of the Crimes Against Children, Human Trafficking and Immigration Unit, prosecuted the case. The Puerto Rico Crimes Against Children Task Force led by HSI was in charge of the investigation, with the collaboration of the Puerto Rico Police Department. To report suspicious activities, call 787-729-6969.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc .

According to court documents, beginning in April 2026, agents from the DEA and HCSO detectives began an investigation into Bowden’s drug distribution activities. Between April and September 2026, DEA and HCSO employed various techniques in furtherance of the investigation. Bowden was observed by law enforcement meeting with various individuals in his vehicle and at his mother’s residence to conduct narcotics transactions. Upwards of ten narcotics transactions occurred each day between Bowden and his customers.

This case was investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration and the Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office. It will be prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Erik Daab.

This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. HHS Office of Refugee Resettlement Identifies Six Types of Fraud in the Biden Administration’s Unaccompanied Alien Children Program
WASHINGTON, D.C. — October 1, 2026 — The Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) today released a memorandum detailing six documented forms of fraud perpetrated by various parties against the Unaccompanied Alien Children (UAC) Program during the Biden Administration.
During the assessment, HHS' Office of the General Counsel and ORR identified fraud by actual and potential sponsors, individuals in ORR custody, and individuals in a country of origin. In some cases, sponsors' fraudulent documents or false information contributed to unaccompanied minors being released into unsafe situations, resulting in abuse — and, in rare instances, death.
"The Biden Administration failed in its most basic responsibility: protecting vulnerable children in federal care," said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. "It weakened safeguards and prioritized speed over scrutiny, leaving children exposed to fraud, exploitation, and abuse. Under President Trump, HHS is restoring rigorous oversight, verifying who takes custody of these children, and putting their safety first. We will hold this system accountable and never sacrifice a child's safety for bureaucratic convenience."
When an unaccompanied minor arrives at the U.S. southern or northern border, the Department of Homeland Security refers that child to ORR's care. In most cases, ORR is responsible for vetting potential sponsors before releasing a UAC to that individual. From 2021 to 2024 approximately 479,000 UAC were referred to ORR.
With a sharp increase in UAC referrals during the Biden Administration starting in 2021, ORR relaxed certain sponsor vetting policies and expedited the releases of UAC. In Fiscal Year 2024, ORR denied less than 1% of sponsorship applications.
In 2025, at the direction of HHS leadership, OGC conducted a review of ORR Child-Level Event cases that occurred under the previous Administration. ORR's data showed that the average rate of intentional documentation fraud, regardless of the number of children assisted, remained at approximately 77% of reported Child Level Events (CLEs). ORR received 1,669 CLE reports of fraud between October 1, 2023 and October 31, 2024. OGC reviewed a subset of these 1,669 reported instances of fraud and, of those reviewed, identified that approximately 85% involved intentional document fraud.
Types of fraud identified were:
- False or fraudulent documentation of identity
- Manipulated photographs
- Misrepresented or unverifiable addresses
- Fingerprint-related fraud
- Failure to disclose household members
- Misrepresentation of age by UAC
The report concludes that intentional documentation fraud perpetrated by some sponsors created conditions that put UAC at risk and, in some instances, released them into dangerous or harmful situations.
In one instance, in August 2023, ORR released a 15-year-old girl to a sponsor who purported to be the UAC's biological brother. ORR did not request fingerprints or DNA to verify the relationship. In October 2023, authorities determined that the sponsor was not related to the UAC and had allegedly raped and impregnated her. The sponsor has been charged by the state, and the case is under investigation.
In another case from July 2024, ORR released a 17-year-old boy to a sponsor who claimed to be the stepsister of the UAC. The purported sponsor presented Venezuelan documents that HHS could not authenticate. In October 2024, the UAC was found dead in the back seat of a car, with his genitalia exposed, along with an unconscious 30-year-old male.
OGC's review concludes that strengthened vetting requirements — such as enhanced identity checks – might have prevented some of these fraudulent practices and reduced risk to children.
More information and the complete HHS ORR memorandum can be found here.
Like HHS on Facebook, follow HHS on X @HHSgov, @SecKennedy, and sign up for HHS Email Updates.

CISA Launches Cybersecurity Awareness Month: Securing the Next 250
WASHINGTON – The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) kicks off Cybersecurity Awareness Month today. CISA updated our Cybersecurity Awareness Month page with additional information, tips, and resources, including for business and government organizations—if you haven’t done so yet, be sure to check out this year’s toolkit.
This year’s theme is Securing the Next 250, highlighting the need for everyone to play their part in strengthening the country's infrastructure against cyber threats. At a time when nation-state backed cyber threats continue to increase and super intelligence is transforming both threats and security, it is more important than ever that those that own and operate the nation’s critical infrastructure take steps to protect it.
“Whenever critical infrastructure is disrupted, so are the businesses and communities that depend on vital services,” said Acting CISA Director Nick Andersen. “That’s why CISA is prioritizing the security and resilience of critical infrastructure, and state, local, tribal, and territorial government (SLTT), whose systems and services sustain us every day. This includes things like clean water, secure transportation, quality healthcare, secure financial transactions, rapid communications, and more. However great or small—every organization that touches critical infrastructure is vital to ensuring uninterrupted services to America’s communities.”
Business and government organizations that own, operate, or support critical infrastructure should take core actions to help secure the systems and services that make America a great place to live and do business.
The following four practices are foundational and should be as automatic as buckling a seatbelt:
- Teach employees to avoid phishing scams. Recognizing and reporting suspicious emails and links may prevent cyber intrusions.
- Require strong passwords. Long, random, unique passwords make accounts harder to breach.
- Require multifactor authentication. Adds an extra layer of protection if a password is compromised.
- Update software. Keeps systems protected against known vulnerabilities.
Take the Next Steps to Level Up Your Defenses
- Use logging on your systems: Log activity so your team can monitor signs that threat actors may be trying to access your systems. Learn how to monitor key information to protect your business.
- Back up data: Incidents happen, but when you back up critical information, recovery is faster and less stressful. Put a backup plan in place that aligns with your organization’s recovery point objective to protect your systems and keep things running smoothly.
- Encrypt data: Encrypting your data and devices strengthens your defense against attacks. Even if criminals gain access to your files, information stays locked and unreadable. Make encryption part of your security strategy
- Get a .gov domain: Government entities, including SLTT governments, can get a .gov domain for additional security – check out get.gov for more information.
- Report cyber incidents to CISA at cisa.gov/report
- Have an incident response plan and use it: Organizations should develop, maintain, update, and regularly exercise IR plans for common threat scenarios such as ransomware attacks. Ensure drills are realistic and include all relevant stakeholders, such as organizational leadership and legal counsel, in addition to technical personnel. IR plans should be reviewed and drilled on an annual basis at a minimum.
- Be prepared for system disruptions: Organizations should develop and execute plans to recover and restore service to critical assets or systems that might be impacted by a cybersecurity incident. Consider including the ability to execute mission essential functions without access to critical assets or even internet access (e.g., shift to paper-based operations, radio communications, etc.)
And for those who own or operate critical infrastructure, we invite you to join us in practicing the 3Rs of Cybersecurity: Reduce, Replace, Recover:
As Cybersecurity Awareness Month 2026 begins, let’s remember that safeguarding our nation’s critical infrastructure is a shared responsibility. Whether you’re a business leader, government official, or an employee on the front lines, your actions matter. By embracing foundational cybersecurity practices and preparing for the unexpected, we can build a more resilient America—one where essential services remain secure and communities thrive. Together, let’s secure the next 250 and beyond.
###
About CISA
As the nation’s cyber defense agency and national coordinator for critical infrastructure security, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency leads the national effort to manage, uncover, and reduce risk to our digital and physical infrastructure Americans rely on every hour of every day.
Visit CISA.gov for more information and follow us on X, Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram.
title: CISA Launches Cybersecurity Awareness Month: Securing the Next 250

EPA Announces the Completion of Eight Five-Year Reviews for Cleanups in the Heartland and the Start of Seven More
LENEXA, KAN. (OCT. 1, 2026) – The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has completed eight Five-Year Reviews for Superfund sites in the nation’s Heartland. These reviews provide EPA with the opportunity to evaluate the implementation and performance of a site’s cleanup remedy to determine whether it remains protective of human health and the environment.
Recently completed Five-Year Reviews that have been filed in their respective Administrative Records and uploaded to their site profile pages are listed in the chart below.
What’s Next? Sites with Non-Protective Remedies
The remedies at Minker/Stout/Romaine Creek in Imperial, Missouri, and Chemical Commodities, Inc. in Olathe, Kansas, were deemed not protective of human health and the environment.
In Imperial, the remedial project manager for the site has scheduled meetings with community members to discuss these findings and is planning a removal action to address the potential exposures to dioxin at the site. A removal action is a quick response taken to address immediate threats hazardous substances can pose to the public. A fact sheet that summarizes the Five-Year Review is available online.
In Olathe, the EPA Region 7 site team continues to work with the potentially responsible parties to delineate the extent of contaminated groundwater plume migration. EPA continues to conduct vapor intrusion testing; inspect vapor intrusion mitigation systems (VIMS); and install VIMS where needed. EPA will hold a public meeting to discuss the findings of the Five-Year Review and discuss the path forward at the site.
What’s Next? Sites Where Protectiveness Statements Were Deferred
At the Hastings Groundwater site, OU14, managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, a determination on the protectiveness of the remedy was deferred until additional information can be gathered from structures overlaying the contaminated groundwater plume.
In Ogallala, EPA Region 7 has deferred a protectiveness statement while gathering more information from the contaminated groundwater plume and the evaluation of nearby residential and commercial buildings overlaying the contaminated groundwater plume.
In Winfield, EPA Region 7 deferred making a protectiveness statement until additional sampling is completed and more information is gathered. The groundwater extraction treatment system is preventing contaminated groundwater from reaching water supply wells.
Five-Year Review Starts
EPA Region 7 has also begun the Five-Year Review process of the following sites:
- Conservation Chemical Company in Kansas City, Missouri
- Former Nebraska Ordnance Plant in Meade, Nebraska
- Fort Riley in Junction City, Kansas
- John’s Sludge Pond in Wichita, Kansas
- Oronogo-Duenweg Mining Belt in Jasper County, Missouri

These reviews are taking place in conjunction with Five-Year Reviews that started earlier in 2026.

EPA performs Five-Year Reviews at sites where hazardous substances remain on the site above levels that would allow sites to be returned for unlimited use and unrestricted exposure in accordance with the statutory authorities granted to the agency by the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) and the National Contingency Plan (NCP).

COLUMBUS, Ohio – Federal agents arrested a Reynoldsburg man today on charges alleging he committed new child sex crimes while already registered as a sex offender.

Justin James Jackson, 23, is charged with producing child pornography, a federal crime punishable by 15 to 30 years in prison. Registered sex offenders face a penalty enhancement of a mandatory 10 years in prison consecutive to any other sentence imposed.

Jackson appeared in federal court at 1:30pm today.

According to charging documents, in August, the FBI’s Columbus Child Exploitation and Human Trafficking task force received information regarding a 12-year-old victim in Kansas. The minor allegedly sent nude photographs and videos of herself on Discord and TikTok at Jackson’s request.

Jackson later allegedly threatened to send the explicit images and videos to the victim’s family and friends if she did not continue to meet his requests.

The defendant’s criminal history includes two convictions of attempted illegal use of a minor in nudity oriented material and of illegal use of a minor in nudity oriented material for extorting an 11-year-old victim for nude photos of themselves in July 2022. This case was investigated by the Pickerington Police Department.

Dominick S. Gerace II, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Ohio; and Jason Cromartie, Special Agent in Charge, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Cincinnati Division; announced the charges. Assistant United States Attorney Tyler J. Aagard is representing the United States in this case.

This case is part of Project Safe Childhood , a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by U.S. Attorney’s Offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims.

A criminal complaint merely contains allegations, and defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law.

Under Secretary of the Air Force Matt Lohmeier visited with U.S. Air Forces Europe-Air Forces Africa and U.S. Space Forces in Europe and Space Forces Africa leadership, Airmen and Guardians during an immersion visit at Ramstein Air Base, Sept. 24.
The visit, which included stops at the USAFE-AFAFRICA headquarters, SPACEFOREUR-AF headquarters, 86th Airlift Wing, 603rd Air Operations Center, and 435th Air Ground Operations Wing, provided an opportunity for Lohmeier to meet with command leaders and subject matter experts, who offered insights on current and future missions, challenges and opportunities.
“It’s a true privilege to visit Ramstein and see firsthand all the critical missions they execute in support of our warfighters,” Lohmeier said. “The motivation, service and expertise they display give me confidence our warfighters are ready to fight and win. We, as senior leaders, need to ensure they receive the most technologically advanced capabilities to execute their mission.”
He started the day off with a workout session with SPACEFOREUR-AF Guardians and leadership, reinforcing that maintaining physical standards helps ensure military members are resilient and ready for anything the service demands of them.
“Fitness is part of readiness, and leaders have to set that example,” Lohmeier said. “Whether you are at home station, deployed or on the road, taking care of yourself physically helps ensure you are prepared to lead and accomplish the mission.”
Then Lohmeier received briefings on command missions and current operations. He spoke with U.S. Air Force Lt. Gen. Jason T. Hinds, USAFE-AFAFRICA commander, to discuss how the command defends the strategic approaches to the United States and generates airpower across two continents in support of U.S. European Command and U.S. Africa Command.
“It was extremely valuable to meet with General Hinds to discuss how USAFE-AFAFAFRICA protects the U.S. homeland with our allies and partners,” Lohmeier said. “It is clear that our forces project combat-ready airpower in Europe, Africa and beyond, deter aggression, and are prepared to win decisively should deterrence fail.”
He also joined Airman and Guardians for a working lunch at the installation dining facility where he heard directly about their mission challenges and successes, offering ongoing leadership support as they work to maintain readiness and a focus on warrior culture.
The visit continued with a tour of the Air Defense Operations Center, a first-of-its-kind facility in the Air Force to become operational. The ADOC is designed to detect and counter emerging aerial threats to help subject matter experts build an approach that is catered to those threats and host nation considerations throughout Europe.
Lohmeier finished the visit by meeting with U.S. Space Force Brig. Gen. Christopher Fernengel, SPACEFOREUR-AF commander, to discuss joint warfighting initiatives and integration with other combatant command components. As a rapidly changing warfighting environment unfolds, a shared understanding and collaboration of how space capabilities are planned and employed is critical to the success of the joint force.
Lohmeier’s visit is a part of a larger European area of responsibility immersion to engage with Airmen and Guardians throughout the theater. He also recognized multiple members with coining ceremonies for their exemplary service.
“Readiness starts with our people,” Lohmeier said. “The professionalism and commitment to readiness from the Airmen and Guardians I met at Ramstein today are exactly what our Air Force needs as we prepare to defeat the threats in theater.”
title: USecAF sees Ramstein AB Airmen, Guardian readiness firsthand

BUFFALO, N.Y. - U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Dilbar Gul Dilbar a/k/a Dilbar Gul Taj Ali Khan, a citizen of Afghanistan, pleaded guilty before U.S. District Judge Frank P. Geraci, Jr. to Visa fraud. He was then sentenced to serve six months in prison.

Dilbar is a citizen and national of Afghanistan. In November 2017, he paid someone to compile and submit an Afghan Special Immigrant Visa Application to the United States on his behalf. Dilbar was aware that the person he had paid submitted a false and fraudulent approval letter from the Chief of Mission in the US Embassy Kabul, but he swore and affirmed that the evidence submitted was true and correct.

In October 2021, Dilbar paid another individual to compile and submit a second Special Immigrant Visa Application to the United States. Once again, Dilbar swore and affirmed that the evidence submitted was true and correct when, in fact, he was aware of a high probability that the evidence submitted contained at least one false representation. As a result of the false representations, in April 2024, Dilbar was granted a Special Immigrant Visa, admitted to the United States, issued lawful permanent residency status, and permitted to reside in the Western District of New York.

The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Meghan K. McGuire. The plea and sentencing are the result of an investigation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Allen D. Davis, II.
