United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the New York Field Office of Homeland Security Investigations (“HSI”), Pete Gizas, and Commissioner of the New York City Police Department (“NYPD”), Jessica S. Tisch, announced today the arrests and unsealing of an Indictment charging DWIGHT FLOWERS, TERRENCE PORTER, and TALEAK HARRIS with trafficking nearly 100 firearms, including a “Glock switch,” ammunition, and approximately 700 grams of cocaine in Manhattan and the Bronx. FLOWERS and PORTER were arrested yesterday in Nassau County and FLOWERS was presented this afternoon before U.S. Magistrate Judge Valerie Figueredo and detained; PORTER is expected to be presented tomorrow. HARRIS was arrested yesterday in Virginia. The case has been assigned to the Honorable Lewis J. Liman.

“The illegal flow of firearms puts New Yorkers’ lives at risk, and we will not stand by and allow it,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “As alleged, Dwight Flowers, Terrence Porter, and Taleak Harris illegally trafficked dangerous drugs and almost 100 firearms—including long-arm rifles, pistols, and a machinegun—into the Southern District of New York. To anyone trafficking illegal guns in New York City: you are on notice. We are watching, we are working with our law enforcement partners to track these weapons and those who move them, and we will hold you accountable.”

“The illegal flow of firearms puts New Yorkers’ lives at risk, and we will not stand by and allow it,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “As alleged, Dwight Flowers, Terrence Porter, and Taleak Harris illegally trafficked dangerous drugs and almost 100 firearms—including long-arm rifles, pistols, and a machinegun—into the Southern District of New York. To anyone trafficking illegal guns in New York City: you are on notice. We are watching, we are working with our law enforcement partners to track these weapons and those who move them, and we will hold you accountable.”

“As alleged, the defendants built a steady pipeline of illegal guns into New York City, selling nearly 100 weapons across five transactions in Manhattan and the Bronx and creating a grave threat to those who live, work and go to school in these communities,” said HSI New York Acting Special Agent in Charge Pete Gizas. “The determined efforts of HSI New York, as a co-leader of the Homeland Security Task Force, together with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York, the NYPD, and DEA resulted in the seizure of this cache, including a firearm equipped with a machinegun conversion device, and the dismantlement of this alleged iron pipeline. Every New Yorker deserves to move through their neighborhood without the danger created by illegal weapons trafficking, and HSI stands committed to making that expectation a reality.”

“This trio of criminals thought they could traffic nearly 100 firearms and a substantial amount of cocaine in our city without consequence, but they were wrong,” said NYPD Commissioner Jessica S. Tisch. “Because of the brave undercover work of our NYPD investigator, these guns and drugs will never make it onto our streets. I thank our fearless officer and law enforcement partners for their thorough work to shut down this operation, and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York for their continued commitment to holding gun traffickers accountable.”

According to the allegations contained in the Indictment and other public filings:(1)

From on or about June 2026 through September 2026, FLOWERS, PORTER, and HARRIS sold approximately 93 firearms to an undercover law enforcement officer with the New York City Police Department across five transactions, which took place in a commercial parking lot in the Bronx and on the street in Manhattan. HARRIS supplied PORTER and FLOWERS with the firearms that they sold to the undercover law enforcement officer. In addition, PORTER and HARRIS sold the same undercover law enforcement officer hundreds of grams of cocaine during these same five transactions.

Moreover, in September 2026, FLOWERS sold the undercover law enforcement officer a firearm with a machinegun conversion device installed. That device is a part capable of converting a semiautomatic firearm into a firearm capable of fully automatic fire. A photograph of the machinegun conversion device affixed to one of the firearms FLOWERS sold to the undercover law enforcement officer is below:

Photographs of the firearms and narcotics sold by FLOWERS, PORTER, and HARRIS across the five transactions are depicted below:

* * *

FLOWERS, 58, of Queens, New York, PORTER, 50, of Queens, New York, and HARRIS, 49, of Chester, Virgina, are each charged with one count of conspiring to commit firearms trafficking, which carries a maximum sentence of 15 years in prison.

In addition, FLOWERS and PORTER are together charged with one count of conspiring to distribute and possession with intent to distribute cocaine, which carries a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison; one count of distribution and possession with intent to distribute cocaine, which carries a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison; and one count of firearms use, carrying, and possession in connection with a drug trafficking offense, which carries a maximum sentence of life in prison and a minimum sentence of five years in prison. FLOWERS is also charged with four additional counts of distribution and possession with intent to distribute cocaine and three additional counts of firearms use, carrying, and possession in connection with a drug offense, as well as a count of possession of a machinegun, which carries a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison.

The statutory maximum and minimum sentences in this case are prescribed by Congress and provided here for informational purposes only, as any sentencing of the defendants will be determined by the judge.

Mr. McDonald praised the outstanding investigative work of HSI New York's JFK Homeland Security Task Force, the United States Marshals Service, and the NYPD.

The case is being prosecuted by the Office’s Violent and Organized Crime Unit. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kathryn Wheelock and Rebecca Delfiner are in charge of the prosecution.

This prosecution is also part of the Homeland Security Task Force (“HSTF”) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of U.S. law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States.

The charges contained in the Indictment are merely accusations, and the defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty.

Rep. Frankel: FAA Refuses Community Requests for More Time to Weigh In on Mar-a-Lago Flight Restrictions
WEST PALM BEACH, FL – Today, Rep. Lois Frankel (FL-22) released the following statement after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) rejected requests from local leaders to extend the public comment period on its proposal to make the current airspace restrictions around Mar-a-Lago permanent:
“The FAA has turned down requests from local leaders and residents to extend the public comment period beyond the October 2 deadline before deciding whether to make the Mar-a-Lago airspace restrictions permanent. The FAA’s refusal to give our community more time to be heard is a disappointing disservice to the thousands of residents who will be directly affected by this proposal.
“A decision with permanent consequences for our community deserves transparency, careful consideration, and genuine public engagement—not a rushed process. The fight is not over.”
As a result of the U.S. Secret Service request to the FAA to protect airspace over Mar-a-Lago nearly one year ago, residents have experienced significant changes in aircraft traffic causing noise and pollution. Previous flight paths affected approximately 2,200 homes and 5,000 residents, while the new routes affect more than 11,000 homes and 21,000 residents, businesses and schools. 
Residents have until October 2 to submit comments to the FAA.
###
title: Rep. Frankel: FAA Refuses Community Requests for More Time to Weigh In on Mar-a-Lago Flight Restrictions

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) and Congresswoman Ashely Hinson (IA-02) led a bipartisan congressional letter to Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Mehmet C. Oz, MD and Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation (CMMI) Director Abe Sutton to address maternal health.

The representatives urged CMS to develop and test a demonstration model through CMMI that uses telehealth and remote monitoring technologies to improve maternal health outcomes. The letter calls for the CMS to leverage technology to make pregnancy and postpartum care safer, more accessible, and more effective, while generating evidence to support broader adoption of innovative maternal healthcare solutions.

Healthy Moms Healthy Babies America stands in support of Congresswoman Williams and Congresswoman Hinson’s bipartisan effort to improve maternal health outcomes.

The Members wrote:

“As sponsors of the Tech to Save Moms Act (H.R. 8317), we write to encourage the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), through the Center for Medicare & Medicaid Innovation (CMMI), to pursue a demonstration model that advances the goals outlined in our legislation and leverages technology to improve maternal health outcomes nationwide.”

“The United States continues to face an unacceptable maternal health crisis, with disproportionately poor outcomes in rural, underserved, and high-risk communities. As CMS has previously recognized, innovative telehealth payment and service delivery models for maternal health represent an important opportunity to improve access to high quality care, particularly for patients facing provider shortages, transportation barriers, and other challenges that impede access to maternity care.”

The Members requested that the CMII evaluate, develop and test a demonstration model that:

Expands access to maternal telehealth services and remote monitoring technologies for Medicaid beneficiaries during pregnancy and the postpartum period;

Supports the screening, monitoring, and management of common pregnancy-related and postpartum health complications;

Improves access to care in rural and urban underserved, low income, and high-risk communities;

Evaluates the impact of technology enabled interventions on clinical outcomes, patient engagement, and program costs with an eye toward closing health gaps socioeconomic, geographic, and racial and ethnic divides; and

Identifies best practices for broader adoption within Medicaid and other CMS programs.

The Members said:

“As we have stated publicly, innovative technology can play an important role in addressing our nation’s maternal health crisis, and we should be using every available tool to make pregnancy and postpartum care safer, more accessible, and more effective for families across the country. We appreciate CMS’s continued commitment to addressing the maternal health crisis and we look forward to working with you directly.”
title: Congresswomen Nikema Williams & Ashley Hinson Call for Technology Improvements to be Utilized to Advance Maternal Health

Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Invests $426 Million to Eliminate Bottlenecks and Congested Highways Across U.S.
The grants will fund highway upgrades and expansions to improve U.S. supply chains
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy today announced a $426 million investment into critical infrastructure projects in 12 states through the Department’s Nationally Significant Multimodal Freight & Highway Projects (INFRA) program.
The Department is making investments to address the top congestion bottlenecks in the country, expand capacity for critical bypasses that serve thousands of freight trucks daily, and add multiple lanes to some of America’s busiest highways.
The investments will go towards building great, big, beautiful infrastructure projects, including:
- $85 million for Florida DOT to construct a general use lane in each direction along approximately 20 miles of I-4 between State Road 434 and State Road 472 in Seminole and Volusia Counties. The project will expand freight capacity and relieve bottleneck congestion, saving time and money for American families and freight carriers.
- $25 million for the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority to deliver direct safety benefits by converting a congested four-lane expressway into an eight-lane standard freeway with median barriers and auxiliary lanes, implementing a safety strategy that targets a corridor collision rate 30 percent above the statewide average. The project also eliminates a critical freight bottleneck on the National Highway System.

Ranking Member Raskin, Rep. Whitesides Demand Watchdog Probes into Taxpayer-Funded Trump Campaign Ads
Lawmakers Ask Federal Watchdogs to Investigate Administration Officials for Violating Federal Law by Using Public Funds for Propaganda Ads
Washington, D.C. (October 1, 2026)— Rep. Jamie Raskin, Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Committee, and Rep. George Whitesides called on the Government Accountability Office (GAO) and the U.S. Office of Special Counsel (OSC) to formally investigate the Trump Administration’s use of taxpayer dollars to produce and air ads promoting President Trump in the weeks before the midterm elections. The lawmakers are seeking a full accounting of what the ads cost, who paid for them and whether officials broke federal law.
“The Trump Administration knows what they are doing is unlawful, as evidenced by their halfhearted attempts to defend their actions. An anonymous White House spokesperson called the ads ‘educational,’ and suggested that they are ‘clearly not political’ because the ‘president is not on the ballot.’ Yet just a few short weeks ago, at his poorly-rated Republican National Convention, President Trump pleaded for his rapidly dwindling ranks of supporters to vote, begging them to ‘pretend, please, that I’m on the ballot.’ The White House can’t have it both ways,” wrote the lawmakers.
On September 23, the White House began airing a 30-second ad labeled “Paid for by the U.S. Government.” Dozens of images of Trump flash across the screen while a singer implores viewers to “love me” and UFC President Dana White calls Trump the “toughest and most resilient person” he has ever met. Days later, the Administration aired another government-funded ad featuring Trump walking down a hallway as audio from a political rally attacks the “Deep State” and promises to “expel the warmongers” from government.
The White House has labeled the ads “public service announcements,” a patently false characterization of taxpayer-funded praise for the President. One credits Trump with reviving American manufacturing, even as the United States has lost tens of thousands of manufacturing jobs during his second term. Another boasts that he is defending law and order while federal immigration agents have shot at least 21 people since he returned to office. And Trump uses an ad paid for by the public to rail against “warmongers” while his war with Iran has taken the lives of 22 American servicemembers and cost more than $43 billion.
The lawmakers are asking federal watchdogs to investigate potential violations of multiple laws, including:
- Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2026: Section 718 prohibits the use of appropriated funds for unauthorized domestic “publicity or propaganda.” GAO has explained that the prohibition reaches government self-promotion, including “self-aggrandizement” and “puffery.”
- Hatch Act of 1939: Federal employees may not use their official authority to interfere with an election. Although the President is exempt from the Hatch Act, Administration employees who helped create, approve or distribute the ads are not.
- Anti-Deficiency Act: Federal officials cannot authorize expenditures beyond what an appropriation permits. If Congress prohibited spending public money on propaganda, officials cannot lawfully charge taxpayers for these ads.
- Federal criminal statutes: Federal law prohibits the theft or knowing misuse of public money.
Ranking Member Raskin and Rep. Whitesides demanded that GAO identify the source, accounts and total amount of taxpayer funds used to produce and distribute the ads across major television markets and official White House social media channels. They also requested a legal determination on whether the ads violate federal law. The lawmakers asked OSC to investigate potential Hatch Act violations and determine who should be held accountable.
“President Trump is obviously desperate for the American people to ‘love’ him, a problem that goes beyond your jurisdiction. But stealing taxpayer dollars to pay for Mr. Trump’s narcissistic ego trips is plainly illegal. Your agencies have an important responsibility to hold accountable members of his Administration who violate the laws and policies under your purview,” concluded the lawmakers.
Click here to read the letter
title: Ranking Member Raskin, Rep. Whitesides Demand Watchdog Probes into Taxpayer-Funded Trump Campaign Ads

RAPID CITY - United States Attorney Ron Parsons announced today that U.S. District Camela C. Theeler has sentenced a Rapid City, South Dakota, man convicted of Possession of Child Pornography. The sentencing took place on September 28, 2026.

Kevin Davison, 49, was sentenced to five years in federal prison, followed by five years of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund and $570 in restitution for the examination of his digital devices.

Davison was indicted for four counts of Receipt of Child Pornography and one count of Possession of Child Pornography by a federal grand jury in September 2025. He pleaded guilty to the Possession of Child Pornography on April 21, 2026.

Between May 2022 and September 2023, Davison used an internet-based application, his laptop, and two cellular phones to upload photographs of clothed minors who were known to him. The application used artificial intelligence technology to “remove” the clothes of the minors in the photographs and replace the clothes with AI-generated nude bodies. Each of the images were then modified to appear that they were engaging in sexually explicit conduct. In addition to these images, he had several other images constituting child sexual abuse material.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse, launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the DOJ’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children, as well as identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc .

This case was investigated by the South Dakota Internet Crimes Against Children (ICAC) Task Force, the South Dakota Division of Criminal Investigation, and the Box Elder Police Department. Former Assistant U.S. Attorney Heather Knox and Assistant U.S. Attorney Kathryn N. Rich prosecuted the case.

Davison was immediately remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service.
title: Rapid City Man Convicted of Child Pornography Charge Sentenced to 5 Years in Federal Prison

Record recruiting allows Coast Guard to restore full operations at six stations
WASHINGTON – Record recruiting results are allowing the Coast Guard to fully staff six stations and restore full operations in 2027. The stations operated at reduced capacity because of workforce shortages. Additional stations will return to full operations in the future.
The Coast Guard prioritized six stations to return to full operations in 2027 based on operational risk and mission demand:
- Station Castle Hill, Rhode Island
- Station Milford Haven, Virginia
- Station Saginaw River, Michigan
- Station Vallejo, California
- Station Golden Gate, California
- Station Rio Vista, California
“Record recruiting is giving us the people we need to strengthen frontline operations,” said Adm. Kevin E. Lunday, commandant of the Coast Guard. “Returning these stations to full operations means more Coast Guard men and women serving in our communities and greater capacity to respond when the American people need us. This is an important step, and more stations will follow.”
The Coast Guard reduced operations at several units in 2023 and 2024 through its Force Alignment Initiative in response to workforce shortages. The initiative shifted personnel to higher priority units and missions while maintaining the Coast Guard’s ability to meet operational demands.
Record recruiting reversed that trend. The Coast Guard now has the personnel to fully staff these six stations and restore capabilities that were reduced.
Returning these stations to full operations will increase capacity for search and rescue, maritime security and law enforcement. It will also increase Coast Guard presence in the communities these stations serve and strengthen the Coast Guard’s ability to respond to crises or contingencies on the water.
Reconstitution of these stations, to include staffing and restoration of full operations, is contingent upon Fiscal Year 2027 appropriations. The Coast Guard will continue to prioritize the return of stations to full operations based on operational risk, mission demand, and availability of funding. Additional stations will be announced in the future.
###
About the U.S. Coast Guard
With more than 95,000 miles of shoreline, 25,000 miles of navigable rivers and 4.5 million square miles of U.S. exclusive economic zone, the U.S. Coast Guard defends the Nation, protects the marine transportation system, regulates and safeguards ports and waterways, leads the Nation in maritime drug interdiction and secures the maritime border. As a member of the joint force, a law enforcement organization, a regulatory agency and a member of the U.S. intelligence community, the Coast Guard employs a unique mix of authorities to ensure the safety and integrity of the maritime domain to protect the economic and national security of the nation. More than 76,000 members of the Coast Guard operate a multi-mission, interoperable fleet of more than 220 cutters, 185 fixed and rotary-wing aircraft, 1,300 boats and its own dedicated cyber command to protect critical maritime infrastructure.
More information about the U.S. Coast Guard can be found at www.uscg.mil Follow @USCG on X and Instagram, like us on Facebook, subscribe on YouTube and follow LinkedIn—connect with us.
Make a difference on land, at sea or in the air with the Coast Guard. Visit GoCoastGuard.com to find out how to be part of our team.
-USCG-
title: Record recruiting allows Coast Guard to restore full operations at six stations

The “Get Active” initiative will bring events promoting physical fitness and student success to schools across the country
AUSTIN, TX – Today, U.S. Secretary of Education (ED) Linda McMahon joined U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., the President’s Council on Sports, Fitness, and Nutrition (the Council) appointed Chair Bryson DeChambeau and Vice Chair Paul “Triple H” Levesque, and WWE superstars at an Austin-area high school to announce the U.S. Department of Education’s partnership in the Get Kids Active campaign, a nationwide effort to get America’s kids moving and build a healthier, stronger generation.
Over the coming months, officials from ED, HHS, members of the Council, and other Administration officials will visit schools across the country to promote the revived Presidential Fitness Test and inspire excitement for physical fitness. The new campaign will also emphasize the important role physical activity plays in supporting students’ health, focus, and success in the classroom.
“Strong minds and strong bodies go hand in hand. When students are active, they are more focused, more engaged, and better prepared to learn,” said U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon. “The Department of Education is proud to partner with the Department of Health and Human Services and the President’s Fitness Council to take this initiative directly into our schools and encourage students across the country to get up, get moving, and stay active.”
“President Trump restored the Presidential Fitness Test, and now we are taking that challenge directly to students across America,” said Secretary Kennedy. “We are getting kids moving, challenging them to set goals, build strength, and discover what they can achieve. I thank Secretary McMahon and President’s Council on Sports, Fitness & Nutrition Chair Bryson DeChambeau and Vice Chair Paul Levesque for helping us make physical fitness a priority in schools and build a stronger, healthier generation.”
“In WWE and throughout my life, I’ve learned that physical discipline builds far more than strength - it builds character, confidence and resilience,” said Paul “Triple H” Levesque, appointed Vice Chair of the President’s Council on Sports, Fitness, and Nutrition. “As Vice Chair of the President’s Council, I’m proud to partner with Secretary Kennedy and Secretary McMahon to bring the ‘Get Active’ campaign to schools nationwide and empower students to reach their full potential.”
Following the announcement, WWE superstars joined students for a workout and fitness activities, putting the campaign’s message into action and encouraging students to make movement part of their everyday lives.
According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), students with higher grades are more likely to engage in physical activity for at least 60 minutes per day on all 7 days and play on at least one sports team. Similarly, a 2025 study conducted by a professor at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro found that just nine minutes of exercise can help improve a student’s academic performance.
title: U.S. Department of Education Joins “Get Active” Campaign to Get America’s Students Moving

text:
Winter weather comes in many forms, but freezing rain can often be the most impactful. Unlike snow or sleet, freezing rain falls as a liquid, and then freezes on contact with cold surfaces, creating a hazardous layer of ice. 
The National Weather Service forecasts and measures what’s known as radial ice, the thickness of ice accumulation on a cylindrical object, like tree branches or power lines.
Why? Because it’s the direct link to real-world damage. Just a quarter-inch of radial ice is enough to snap branches and bring down power lines, even less if it's windy!
Want to measure it yourself? 
	- Locate an ice-covered object that is out in the open, such as a small tree branch.
- Position yourself to see both the thickest and thinnest ice portions around the object.
- Using a ruler, measure the thickest part of the ice, from the edge of the object to the edge of the ice.
- Measure the thinnest part of the ice using the same method.
- Average the two measurements to calculate the total ice accumulation.
Measurements as small as 0.01” are recorded and archived for use in the historical record, in post-storm analyses, and for verification.
The next time you get freezing rain, if it’s safe to do so, go measure how much radial ice you received and report it to your local Weather Forecast Office! Find your local office by visiting https://www.weather.gov/, then type in your location in the top left corner.
title: October 1, 2026 - Get Ready for Winter: Learn How to Measure Ice

As Grocery Prices Skyrocket, Brown Sounds Alarm on New Trump SNAP Cut Taking Effect Today
As cuts kick in 5 million have already lost SNAP after Trump cuts
Washington, D.C. - Today, Congresswoman Shontel Brown (OH-11), Vice Ranking Member on the House Agriculture Committee, warned that another SNAP cut from H.R. 1, the Republican Reconciliation Law, has gone into effect.
The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) is federally funded and administered by states. H.R. 1 cut the federal share of funding for SNAP administrative costs in half, meaning that states are now required to cover 75% of SNAP administrative costs. Nationwide, this represents billions in reduced funding for SNAP.
In Ohio, this has meant a loss of an estimated $38 million in SNAP funding effective today, and potential annual cuts of $67 million. Earlier this year, the Republican-controlled Ohio legislature allocated only $12.5 million to cover this gap, leaving Ohio’s largest counties (which administer SNAP locally) with a substantial funding deficit. Cuyahoga County received the same administrative funding patch as Ohio’s smallest counties and now faces a funding gap of $7 million. For state-by-state estimates of SNAP funding cuts effective today, click here.
The reduction of administrative funding leaves states and counties with fewer resources to process applications, determine eligibility, and ensure families receive the benefits they are eligible for. This massive funding cut also jeopardizes other state and local services as states struggle to replace this lost funding. A similar cost shift, cutting federal payments to states for SNAP benefits, will go into effect October 1, 2027.
“Trump and Republicans in Congress passed tax breaks for millionaires and billionaires on the backs of families who are already struggling to afford sky-high grocery costs. Over 5 million Americans have already lost SNAP food assistance because of Trump’s cuts, and today, another SNAP cut from the Big, Ugly Law kicks in. Trump and Republicans have handed states huge SNAP funding cuts, with more cuts coming next year. Worse still, these administrative cuts are coming as Republicans have also made SNAP more difficult to access. They’ve created new paperwork and new requirements, then cut the funding used to enroll people. It’s a devastating gut punch and it’s intentional: this is a plan to wreck state SNAP programs and push millions off of SNAP and into hunger. Congress must fix these cuts through the Farm Bill and protect families who rely on SNAP to keep food on the table,” said Congresswoman Shontel Brown.
According to USDA data, more than 5 million Americans, including about 2 million children, have already lost SNAP since H.R. 1 was enacted in July 2025. In Ohio, over 120,000 people have already lost SNAP.
H.R.1’s SNAP cuts were enacted alongside cuts to Medicaid and other programs to pay for tax cuts that overwhelmingly benefited large corporations and the wealthiest Americans. The Republican Farm Bill which passed the House and is currently under consideration in the Senate, locks in $187 billion in SNAP cuts. Republicans rejected all Democratic attempts to roll back SNAP cuts in the House Farm Bill.
Separately, a SNAP cost-of-living-adjustment, or COLA, took effect today. The COLA was authorized through the 2008 Farm Bill, and Republicans have repeatedly attempted to kill and weaken SNAP benefit increases. Last year, Brown introduced The Hunger Free Future Act, new legislation to block any changes to the Thrifty Food Plan, which uses economic data to determine benefit size, which would result in benefit cuts.
###
title: As Grocery Prices Skyrocket, Brown Sounds Alarm on New Trump SNAP Cut Taking Effect Today

WASHINGTON — Congressman Gil Cisneros (CA-31) and Congresswoman Judy Chu (CA-28) introduced the San Gabriel Basin Restoration Fund Reauthorization Act, which would remove the funding cap for the ongoing groundwater treatment by the San Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority, reauthorize funding at $250 million, and support the completion of the ongoing water restoration project. The San Gabriel Basin provides drinking water for over 1.5 million residents in the San Gabriel Valley and Los Angeles County, including the cities of Azusa, Baldwin Park, City of Industry, El Monte, Irwindale, La Puente, South El Monte, and West Covina. The San Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority signed on as a supporting organization.

“The San Gabriel Valley relies on the clean drinking water provided by the San Gabriel Basin,” said Rep. Gil Cisneros. “Since 2000, the San Gabriel Basin Restoration Fund has supported the Water Quality Authority’s work to clean and restore contaminated groundwater in our region. This legislation would remove funding hurdles and provide the support needed to bring this decades-long project across the finish line. Earlier this year, I worked with Congresswoman Chu to secure critical federal Community Project Funding for the restoration fund, and we’re committed to passing this legislation to further accelerate groundwater cleanup. Clean drinking water is a fundamental human right, and every family in the San Gabriel Valley deserves direct, affordable, protected access to it.”

“The San Gabriel Basin provides drinking water to more than 1.5 million people across our region, but it still carries contamination left behind by industries of the past,” said Rep. Judy Chu. “For decades, the San Gabriel Basin Restoration Fund has powered the Water Quality Authority’s work to clean up our groundwater, and this bill would provide the long-term federal support needed to finish the job. I’m proud to join Congressmember Cisneros in leading this effort, building on our work securing federal Community Project Funding for this project. Families across the San Gabriel Valley deserve a safe, reliable, and sustainable source of drinking water for generations to come.”

Full text of the bill can be found here.

Rep. Cisneros is a member of the House Committee on Small Business, the Ranking Member on the Subcommittee on Contracting and Infrastructure, and on the Subcommittee on Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations. He is a member of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and serves on its leadership team as the Freshman Representative.

title: Reps. Cisneros, Chu Introduce Bill to Fund Clean Drinking Water

Treasury and IRS Issue Proposed Regulations to Implement the Education Freedom Tax Credit
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service issued proposed regulations to implement the new Federal Scholarship Tax Credit under section 25F, commonly known as the Education Freedom Tax Credit, the first federal tax credit supporting private contributions for K-12 scholarships. Under the proposed regulations, eligible taxpayers may claim an annual credit of up to $1,700 for qualifying contributions, or up to $3,400 for married couples filing jointly. Treasury and the IRS also issued companion temporary regulations to establish key procedures for states and Scholarship Granting Organizations to prepare for the launch of the tax credit on January 1, 2027.
The proposed regulations advance the Administration’s priorities of expanding educational freedom, restoring parental rights, returning power to the states, and putting American students first.
“Under President Trump, this Administration continues to transform America’s education system to meet the needs of each student,” said U.S. Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “The Education Freedom Tax Credit marks a new chapter in educational freedom and opportunity by establishing America’s first nationwide school choice program and empowering states to give students and families more options. Thirty states have already opted in, and we encourage all 50 states to participate so every American student and family can benefit.”
“Education freedom is the key to unlocking opportunity and success for our next generation of students,” said U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon. “The Education Freedom Tax Credit, the largest expansion of school choice in history, will supercharge those opportunities for millions of children. I am profoundly grateful to President Trump and our partners at Treasury for ensuring that every child has access to the education they need, not one limited by ZIP code, family income, or government‑imposed barriers.”
“The IRS is committed to helping American families by implementing this important new law that gives them freedom of choice when deciding how to educate their children,” said IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano. “To further that goal, these rules provide states, scholarship-granting organizations, and taxpayers with the clarity they need to prepare for this new education tax credit.”
THE EDUCATION FREEDOM TAX CREDIT
Beginning in 2027, the Education Freedom Tax Credit will expand educational opportunity by encouraging private contributions to participating Scholarship Granting Organizations (SGOs). Individual taxpayers may claim a nonrefundable federal income tax credit of up to $1,700 for qualified cash contributions to eligible SGOs and married taxpayers filing jointly may claim a combined credit of up to $3,400, which will use those funds to provide scholarships to eligible elementary and secondary school students. Participating states may opt in to the program and identify eligible SGOs. Taxpayers may contribute to an eligible SGO regardless of their state of residence, allowing them to support qualifying scholarship organizations across participating states.
The credit is designed to support scholarships for K–12 education expenses, helping families access educational options that meet their children’s needs. Scholarships may support a broad range of qualified elementary and secondary education expenses, including private-school tuition, academic tutoring, special-needs services, books, supplies, computers and other equipment, and other qualifying expenses connected with a student’s enrollment or attendance.
By 2030, Treasury and the IRS estimate that the program could support 600 to 700 SGOs, with more than 11 million taxpayers making nearly $26 billion in qualified contributions annually and funding as many as 2.2 million scholarships each year.
PROPOSED REGULATIONS
The proposed regulations provide detailed rules intended to make the new credit accessible to families and administrable for taxpayers, states, and SGOs while protecting scholarship funds from fraud and abuse.
The regulatory package addresses:
- Increasing Access for Students: The proposed regulations provide rules for applying the statutory household-income limitation and would generally disregard non-cash items, such as imputed return on home equity. They also provide streamlined eligibility verification rules for certain families participating in needs-based programs, foster children, and certain students receiving tutoring or special-needs services in low-income areas. Treasury and IRS estimate that, under the proposed rules and safe harbors, approximately 96 percent of children in participating states would be eligible to receive section 25F scholarship funds.
- Expanding Educational Choice: The proposed regulations provide that participating states would not be permitted to impose SGO operating requirements that are more restrictive than those established by section 25F, including restrictions based on the type of school scholarship recipients may attend or the types of qualified education expenses scholarships may fund. The proposed regulations also would not permit a State to use discretionary certification standards to exclude otherwise qualifying SGOs.
- Expanding Opportunities for Scholarship Organizations and Families: The proposed rules provide a framework for multistate SGOs, including an operational requirement safe harbor for qualifying organizations whose activities are at least 85 percent scholarship-granting activities. Treasury and IRS estimate that this safe harbor could enable approximately 450 additional organizations to participate and increase qualified contributions by up to $3 billion annually.
- Ensuring Taxpayers Can Access the Maximum Credit Allowed by Law: The proposed regulations provide a taxpayer-favorable ordering rule for individuals who may qualify for both state tax credits and the new federal credit. They also provide rules for carrying unused section 25F credits forward for up to five years and generally permit taxpayers to rely on an organization’s inclusion on the IRS SGO list when making a contribution.
- Protecting Taxpayers and Scholarship Funds: The proposed and temporary regulations establish reporting, verification, and audit requirements designed to prevent duplication, improper payments, and other fraud or abuse. They provide for IRS portals for participating states and SGOs, unique donor numbers that avoid requiring SGOs to collect donors’ Social Security numbers, annual SGO reporting and audits, and procedures for removing organizations that fail to satisfy applicable requirements.
COMPANION TEMPORARY REGULATIONS
The companion temporary regulations provide states and SGOs with rules they need now to prepare for 2027, including procedures for state elections and certification of SGOs, electronic registration, donor acknowledgements, and reporting of qualified contributions. These procedures are intended to give taxpayers certainty that contributions are being made to qualifying organizations and to give states and SGOs sufficient time to establish the systems necessary for the incentive’s launch. Taxpayers, states, and SGOs may rely on the proposed regulations for qualified contributions beginning January 1, 2027.
Treasury and IRS previously sought public input on implementation of section 25F and previewed the forthcoming regulations in June. The proposed regulations reflect stakeholder feedback received during that process on issues including student eligibility, SGO operations, state administration, reporting, and program integrity.
Section 25F was enacted in 2025 and applies to taxable years ending after December 31, 2026. The credit is available for qualifying cash contributions to SGOs in states that voluntarily elect to participate. An SGO generally must be a section 501(c)(3) public charity, maintain qualified contributions separately, satisfy statutory scholarship and operational requirements, and be included on the applicable state’s SGO list.
A fact sheet on the Education Freedom Tax Credit is available here.
Learn more about the participating states here.

I look forward to seeing the many impacts of the University of Toledo’s research in our Northwest Ohio communities and beyond in the years to come.”

The awards include:

$401,618 for research on the relationship between gut bacteria and blood pressure regulation under Dr. Tao Yang

$249,000 for research on the Zika virus’s harm to blood-retinal barriers under Dr. Sneha Singh

$455,827 for research on opioid toxicity in the human body under Dr. Issac Schiefer

$768,796 for research on Lyme disease prevention under Dr. Mark Wooten

$1,675,569 for breast cancer research under Dr. Jianmin Zhang

$496,344 for research on developing pancreatic cancer therapies under Dr. Shi-He Liu

$448,793 for research on early cell development in the reproductive process under Dr. Tomer Avidor-Reiss

$502,610 for research on arthritis and spinal disc degeneration under Dr. Mohammad Yunus Ansari

As a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, Congresswoman Kaptur is dedicated to securing bipartisan support and funding for Northwest Ohio communities. PORTLAND, Ore.—A Fairview, Oregon, man was sentenced to federal prison today for possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine.

Matthew Moultrie, 41, was sentenced to 10 years in federal prison and 4 years’ supervised release.

“Removing drugs and guns from our streets is vital to protecting Oregon’s communities. When offenders repeatedly threaten public safety, we have a duty to hold them accountable,” said U.S. Attorney Scott E. Bradford for the District of Oregon. “This sentence reflects the serious harm Mr. Moultrie has caused—and the danger he would have continued to pose—to Oregonians.”

“Mr. Moultrie showed a complete disregard for the law by trafficking deadly drugs while armed, despite a prior drug conviction and repeated encounters with law enforcement,” said Robert A. Saccone, Special Agent in Charge, DEA Seattle Field Division. “This sentence holds him accountable and sends a clear message that DEA and our Homeland Security Task Force partners will work tirelessly to protect our communities. Through Fentanyl Free America, we are disrupting the fentanyl supply chain, reducing the availability of synthetic opioids, and saving American lives.”

According to court documents, the investigation began when Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) agents saw a courier from a Mexican drug trafficking organization (DTO) get in Moultrie’s car for an apparent drug transaction. The agents then stopped and searched Moultrie’s car and found about 220 grams of fentanyl, 65 grams of meth, and a gun.

Later, DEA agents and Multnomah County Sheriff’s Office (MCSO) deputies found Moultrie as he exited a motel room. Moultrie admitted to possessing a handgun and a half-pound of meth. Agents found 386 grams of meth, 5 grams of fentanyl, and two guns in his motel room.

Due to Moultrie’s criminal history, he is a career offender. His criminal history includes drug trafficking and firearms offenses.

On January 7, 2026, Moultrie pled guilty to possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine.

U.S. Attorney Scott E. Bradford for the District of Oregon made the announcement.

This case was investigated by the DEA, Multnomah County Sheriff’s Office, Oregon State Police and Clackamas County Sheriff’s Office. It was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Lewis S. Burkhart.

This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Portland comprises agents and officers from FBI, HSI, DEA, USMS, IRS-CI, ATF, USPIS, CBP, TSA, U.S. Coast Guard, Oregon Air, Army National Guard Counterdrug program, and Oregon-Idaho HIDTA with prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Oregon.

The Oregon-Idaho HIDTA program is an Office of National Drug Control Policy sponsored counterdrug grant program that coordinates with and provides funding resources to multi-agency drug enforcement initiatives.
title: Career Criminal Sentenced to 10 Years in Federal Prison for Possession with Intent to Distribute Meth

Krishnamoorthi Hails Restoration of 988 LGBTQ+ Crisis Line Following His Efforts
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), author of the bipartisan 988 LGBTQ+ Youth Access Act and a Vice Chair of the Congressional Equality Caucus, hailed the restoration of specialized LGBTQ+ crisis line services through the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline after the Trump Administration shut them down in July 2025. After Congressman Krishnamoorthi helped secure $33.1 million in federal funding earlier this year to restore the program, he partnered with allies in Congress and LGBTQ+ and mental health advocates to pressure the Trump Administration to use that funding and bring the “Press 3” option back online.
“I’m proud that we secured the funding to restore this lifesaving LGBTQ+ crisis line and successfully pressured the Trump Administration to bring the program back,” Congressman Krishnamoorthi said. “When an LGBTQ+ young person reaches out for help in a moment of crisis, they deserve to reach a counselor trained to understand and support them. This program should never have been taken away, and now we need to make sure it stays available for every young person who needs it. I’m grateful to The Trevor Project, NAMI Chicago, Equality Illinois, the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention, and all the advocates and young people who worked alongside us to bring these services back.”
Congressman Krishnamoorthi introduced the bipartisan 988 LGBTQ+ Youth Access Act in September 2025 after the Trump Administration shut down the specialized services. The legislation would require HHS to maintain dedicated crisis support for LGBTQ+ youth and reserve at least 9 percent of annual 988 funding for those services.
After Congress provided funding to restore the crisis line, Congressman Krishnamoorthi repeatedly pressed the Department of Health and Human Services to follow through. In May, he joined Representatives Sharice Davids and Seth Moulton in a letter to HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. demanding a timeline for restoration and answers on the Administration’s implementation of Congress’s funding. He also helped lead four public events in Chicago and Washington calling for the crisis line’s return, including a May press conference at NAMI Chicago, a June roundtable with LGBTQ+ young people and advocates, a July press conference in Washington, and a September roundtable and press conference with Illinois mental health and LGBTQ+ leaders.
title: Krishnamoorthi Hails Restoration of 988 LGBTQ+ Crisis Line Following His Efforts

BOSTON – A Providence man pleaded guilty on Sept. 24, 2026 in federal court in Boston to transporting child sexual abuse material.

Mark Huynh, 40, of Providence, R.I., pleaded guilty to one count of transporting child pornography. U.S. Senior District Court Judge F. Dennis Saylor IV scheduled sentencing for December 19, 2026. Huynh was arrested and charged in February 2026 .

In 2025, Huynh was arrested at Boston Logan Airport entering the country with an active arrest warrant in Rhode Island for second degree molestation of a child. Searches of Huynh’s electronic devices revealed a video of a second minor victim whom Huynh had also molested, in addition to multiple files depicting child sexual abuse material involving victims as young as toddlers. Huynh has also pleaded guilty to state charges arising from his abuse of the victims.

The charge of transporting child pornography provides for a sentence of no less than five years and up to 20 years in prison, at least five years and up to a lifetime of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Jeff Grimming, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the Homeland Security Investigations New England made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Boston Field Office. Assistant United States Attorney Eric L. Hawkins of the Major Crimes Unit is prosecuting the case.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse, launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the DOJ’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children, as well as identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc .

SAN ANTONIO – A Bexar County man was arrested and charged federally for possessing a firearm with an obliterated serial number after he allegedly made a threat to attack the Texas State Capitol, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas.

According to court documents, on Sept. 29, Benny Caldera Jr., 40, of Converse, allegedly told another individual that he was going to the Capitol and would “shoot it up,” specifically expressing his anger toward the American Israeli Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC). A criminal complaint alleges Caldera Jr. said of AIPAC, “These people have to be exterminated.” The complaint further alleges Caldera Jr. stated in a recorded conversation that he made up his mind and said goodbye to his parents.

The Texas Department of Public Safety (TX DPS) received a report of Caldera Jr.’s alleged threats on Tuesday and obtained a state arrest warrant and a search warrant for his residence. The FBI assisted by conducting surveillance. TX DPS agents arrested Caldera Jr. inside the residence on Wednesday.

During the search of Caldera Jr.’s residence, TX DPS Criminal Investigation Division (CID) agents allegedly located a .357 revolver loaded with six rounds and a 12-gauge shotgun in his master bedroom closet along with six 9mm rounds. The criminal complaint alleges that the serial number on the side of the revolver frame was obliterated and appeared to have been filed off.

Caldera Jr. is scheduled for his initial court appearance today before U.S. Magistrate Judge Elizabeth Chestney of the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas. If convicted, he faces up to five years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

“This defendant is in federal custody today thanks to a perceptive and concerned citizen seeing something and saying something,” said U.S. Attorney Simmons. “Had the alleged threats not been taken seriously and reported to law enforcement, we could have a very different and tragic story to tell today. I appreciate the diligent efforts of our partners at Texas DPS and at the FBI, and I again urge everyone to take threats like this seriously and report them appropriately. You never know the impact you may have and the number of lives you could save.”

OXFORD, Miss. – Last week, a criminal complaint was filed charging Yahya Mohamed Mosleh, 51, and Islam Yahya Mosleh, 18, a father and son, with possession with the intent to distribute controlled substances in connection with a death investigation of two University of Mississippi (Ole Miss) students. According to the complaint, on Sept. 21, an Ole Miss student, later declared dead, was found in his dorm room. The cause of death appeared to be consistent with a drug overdose. In the victim’s room, law enforcement found packages, some with missing tablets, of suspected kratom derivatives.

About an hour later, a second Ole Miss student was found deceased in a separate location. The cause of death appeared to be consistent with a drug overdose. Also found in his room were packages of suspected kratom derivatives.

Law enforcement identified a suspected link between the kratom derivative substance packages and a local vape, tobacco and beer store, and has executed several search warrants in connection with this investigation. Store clerk Yahya Mosleh and his son, Islam Mosleh, have been arrested and suspected kratom derivative controlled substances have been seized from the store.

Kratom is a plant-based product that has become increasingly popular in the United States for its stimulant and pain-relieving effects. Natural kratom is considered a stimulant in low doses and an opiate-like sedative in higher doses. Kratom derivatives, such as MGPI, MGM-15 and MGM-16, are now schedule I controlled substances and can be significantly more potent than natural kratom leaf products and morphine, with associated high risk of severe addiction, overdose, and death. Such kratom derivative controlled substances have been marketed and sold over the internet, and over the counter via head shops and convenience stores in the Northern District of Mississippi and throughout the country. Compounds like MGPI, MGM-15 and MGM-16 have been referred to as “gas station heroin.”

U.S. Attorney Scott F. Leary for the Northern District of Mississippi made the announcement.

The Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), Lafayette County Sheriff’s Office, Oxford Police Department, and the University of Mississippi Police Department are investigating the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Clyde McGee and John Herzog Jr. for the Northern District of Mississippi are prosecuting the case.

A criminal complaint merely contains allegations. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: Father and Son Arrested on Criminal Complaint in Suspected Connection with the Death of One of Two Students at the University of Mississippi

text:
From frequent moves and deployments to balancing education and family responsibilities, military life can create unique childcare challenges for Airmen, Guardians and their families.
The Air and Space Forces Aid Society, the services’ official relief organization, offers several programs to help families with childcare costs during different stages of military life.
“Childcare can quickly become an added source of stress for military families, particularly during a move, deployment or other major transition,” said retired Command Chief Master Sgt. Kris Spencer, AFAS chief operating officer, who oversees the organization’s programs and support services. “Our goal is to provide practical support that gives families greater flexibility and helps relieve some of that burden.”
Childcare assistance available through AFAS includes:
Giving Parents a Break
Provides families up to $120 per dependent child over a three-month period to give parents an opportunity to take a much-needed break during periods of stress. To qualify, families must be referred by a unit commander, first sergeant, medical provider, chaplain or Military and Family Readiness Center personnel.
Childcare for PCS
Provides $200 per dependent child up to age 12, with a maximum of $1,000 per family, to help cover childcare during a permanent change of station. Assistance is also available for retirement, palace chase, and separation moves. All Air Force and Space Force families qualify regardless of rank or finances.
Education Childcare Grant
Provides up to $750 in childcare assistance for eligible military spouses approved for the AFAS Bee Arnold Spouse Tuition Program, helping offset childcare costs while they pursue education or career goals.
For these programs, approved funds are sent directly to families through Zelle or ACH, providing the flexibility to choose the childcare option that best meets their needs.
“We want Airmen, Guardians, and their families to know these resources are available and easy to access,” Spencer said. “When childcare is a challenge, AFAS is here to help.”
To learn more or to apply, visit afas.org.
title: AFAS offers childcare assistance to Air Force, Space Force families

AKRON, OH – U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) recognizes October as Domestic Violence Awareness Month and is reintroducing the Skills Against Violence Act. This bill would establish a new Gender-Based Violence Survivor Workforce Program at the Department of Justice's Office on Violence Against Women. The office would award grants to domestic violence and sexual assault service providers and coalitions with a documented history of effective work in this field. The bill authorizes $40 million per year for fiscal years 2026 through 2030.

Grants could fund employment counseling, occupational training, job retention counseling, and counseling on re-entering the workforce. They could also fund outreach to survivors and to employers that support a safe workspace, along with support services such as child care, disability and elder care, transportation, professional clothing and equipment, legal services, and gender-based violence and mental health counseling. Grantees would report annually on how many survivors received workforce development, occupational training, and support services, how many entered employment, and how satisfied survivors were with the services. The Director would then report to Congress every two years, beginning two years after enactment.

Rep. Sykes previously introduced the Safer Homes and Families Package, a comprehensive legislative slate consisting of four bills to protect survivors and strengthen support systems nationwide: the Fair Social Security for Domestic Violence Survivors Act, the Better Care for Domestic Violence Survivors Act, the Break Free from Domestic Violence Act, and the Electronic Stalking Act.

“Every person deserves to live free from fear and violence,” said Rep. Sykes. “I’m committed to standing with survivors and delivering real solutions that help them rebuild their lives. During Domestic Violence Awareness Month, we honor the courage of survivors and highlight the urgent need for stronger protections. The bills I’ve led reflect our promise to create safer communities where every person can heal, thrive, and live with dignity."

"A paycheck can be the difference between staying and leaving. Economic abuse occurs in 99% of domestic violence cases and is one of the most powerful ways abusers keep survivors trapped,” said Maria York, Director of Policy and Communication, Ohio Domestic Violence Network. “Here in Ohio, intimate partner violence costs our state nearly $1.2 billion every year, including $227.7 million in lost work productivity. ODVN applauds the Skills Against Violence Act for investing in job training, career support, and wraparound services like childcare and transportation that survivors need to build lasting financial independence. We're grateful to Rep. Sykes for being a continuous champion for survivors, this Domestic Violence Awareness Month and every month."

“Each of these bills represents a critical step toward removing the barriers that keep survivors trapped in unsafe situations,” said Teresa Stafford Wright, CEO of Hope & Healing Survivor Resource Center. “The Fair Social Security for Domestic Violence Survivors Act, the Better Care for Domestic Violence Survivors Act, and the Break Free From Domestic Violence Act all recognize that safety, health, and financial stability are deeply interconnected. By expanding access to financial resources, trauma-informed care, and safe housing options, this legislation affirms that survivors deserve not only protection from violence but the opportunity to rebuild their lives with dignity and independence.”

“Survivors should not have to choose between healing and thriving, nor should they have to finish healing before they are given opportunities to thrive. When survivors have access to skills training, safe working spaces, and opportunities to build sustainable careers, healing and economic independence can happen alongside each other. That is what creates pathways toward long term self sufficiency,” said Dr. Antoria Gillon, Founder and CEO of From Ordinary to Extraordinary.

“The National Network to End Domestic Violence (NNEDV) is proud to support the Skills Against Violence Act. Economic security is a critical part of safety for survivors of domestic violence. Financial abuse, disrupted employment, damaged credit, and other economic barriers can make it harder for survivors to leave an abusive relationship and build a safe, stable future for themselves and their families,” said Tonia Moultry-Pace, NNEDV Interim President & CEO. “We are grateful to Congresswoman Sykes for introducing the Skills Against Violence Act, which will create meaningful workforce development opportunities for survivors and help them build the skills and economic stability needed to rebuild.”

The Fair Social Security for Domestic Violence Survivors Act would lower the current 10-year marriage requirement for spousal Social Security benefits to five years for individuals who divorce due to domestic abuse. This change would prevent survivors from being financially penalized for leaving unsafe relationships and help them achieve economic independence.

The Better Care for Domestic Violence Survivors Act invests $50 million over five years in a pilot program to train healthcare providers in evidence-based, trauma-informed care. Because survivors often seek medical attention during or after abuse, this initiative would help healthcare professionals identify and support victims more effectively, potentially saving lives through earlier intervention.

The Break Free From Domestic Violence Act ensures survivors of domestic violence, stalking or sexual assault can break a lease without penalty, giving them the freedom to leave dangerous living situations without facing financial or legal consequences.

The Stop Electronic Stalking Act would prohibit the use of personal tracking devices to track people without their consent. Rep. Sykes introduced similar legislation in the Ohio legislature which was later signed into law by Governor DeWine.

In Ohio, there were 157 domestic violence fatalities from July 1, 2024, through June 30, 2025, including 11 children. This marks a ten year high in fatalities due to domestic violence in Ohio. In 2025, 3,703 incidents of domestic violence were reported in Summit County, and 2,215 incidents in Stark County.

Rep. Sykes has long been a champion for survivors, earning bipartisan support and delivering tangible results. Last year, Rep. Sykes secured a $500,000 Transitional Housing Assistance grant for Domestic Violence Project Inc., providing critical resources to help survivors rebuild their lives. She has also co-sponsored the Healing Partnerships for Survivors Act, Safe Vehicle Access for Survivors Act, Crime Victims Fund Stabilization Act of 2025, Lori Jackson-Nicolette Elias Domestic Violence Survivor Protection Act, the National Domestic Violence Awareness Month Resolution, & the Trafficking Survivors Relief Act of 2025. Throughout the appropriations process, she has been a strong advocate for funding for domestic violence and family violence programs, signing onto bipartisan requests for robust funding in FY27.

As a member of the Ohio House of Representatives prior to her time in Congress, Rep. Sykes authored Ohio H.B. 1, which became law and extended protective orders to victims of dating violence for the first time in the state’s history.
title: Rep. Sykes Recognizes October as Domestic Violence Awareness Month, Leads Legislation to Protect Survivors of Domestic Violence

Washington, DC – The U.S. Senate passed Congresswoman Dina Titus (NV-01)’s End Tax Penalties on American Hostages Act. This legislation would prevent U.S. citizens who have been taken hostage or wrongfully detained abroad from incurring penalties for late tax payments while they were held. Representative Claudia Tenney (R-NY) joined Rep. Titus as cosponsor of the legislation which is now on its way to the President's desk.

“I am pleased to report that my End Tax Penalties on American Hostages Act passed the Senate and is on its way to the President's desk,” said Rep. Titus. “It goes without saying that no one who has endured wrongful detention or been taken hostage abroad should face the additional burden of onerous tax penalties incurred through no fault of their own. This bill would eliminate that unthinkable possibility by cutting red tape in our tax code and codifying a critical support mechanism for wrongful detainees, hostages, and their families here in the United States.”

This bill extends certain federal tax deadlines for U.S. nationals who are unlawfully or wrongfully detained abroad or held hostage abroad and their spouses. The bill also allows for an abatement and refund of additional taxes, interest, and penalties assessed to such individuals for failing to meet a federal tax deadline during a period of detention.

Specifically, under the bill, the period during which a U.S. national is unlawfully or wrongfully detained abroad or held hostage abroad is disregarded in determining certain federal tax deadlines, including deadlines for

filing a return for and paying federal income, estate, gift, employment, or excise taxes;

a tax credit or refund claim; and

the determination, assessment, and collection of additional taxes, interest, or penalties.

The bill requires the Department of State and the Department of Justice to annually provide the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) with lists to identify U.S. nationals who qualify for an extension.

The bill also requires the IRS to (1) abate and refund additional taxes, interest, and penalties assessed for any tax year ending during a period of detention for which an extension of a federal tax deadline is permitted; and (2) establish a program allowing U.S. nationals unlawfully or wrongfully detained abroad or taken hostage abroad (or their spouse or dependent) to claim a refund of additional taxes, interest, and penalties assessed for any tax year ending during a period of detention from 2021 to the bill’s enactment date.

The legislation’s full text can be found here.

title: Senate Passes Titus Legislation to Protect Hostages and Wrongful Detainees from Tax Penalties

SANTA ANA, California – Four illegal aliens were arrested today out of five total charged in separate federal criminal complaints charging them with using other people’s Social Security numbers to obtain credit, mostly from retailers, then running up tens of thousands of dollars in debt which they sought to erase by filing for bankruptcy.

The following defendants were arrested today and are expected to make their initial appearances this afternoon in United States District Court in Santa Ana and Los Angeles:

Abel Ávila Martínez, 48, of Buena Park, who previously was removed from the U.S. in 1999;

Walter Anastacio Castellanos-Pérez, 53, of Rancho Dominguez;

José Alfredo Chávez-Cabello, 54, of Long Beach; and

Verónica Espinosa-Cortés, 54, of Bell Gardens, whom an immigration judge ordered removed from the U.S. in 1996.

Law enforcement continues to search for the following defendant:

Moisés Ortuño-Claras, 47, of Anaheim.

Each defendant is charged with fraud in connection with access devices over $1,000. Ávila, Chávez, Espinosa, and Ortuño are Mexican nationals. Castellanos is a Guatemalan national.

“This sweep resulted in the arrest of five illegal aliens charged with stealing Americans’ Social Security numbers to obtain credit, run up debt, and then seek to erase over $140,000 through bankruptcy,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli. “These defendants allegedly exploited both our financial system and the bankruptcy process and face up to 15 years in federal prison if convicted.”

“As the watchdog of the bankruptcy system, the United States Trustee Program is committed to addressing fraudulent and abusive conduct,” said Peter Anderson, U.S. Trustee for Region 16, which covers the Central District of California. “We appreciate the commitment of the U.S. Attorney’s Office and our law enforcement partners to ensuring that bankruptcy is not a safe haven for fraudsters.”

“Today’s arrests highlight the very real harm caused when individuals misuse Social Security numbers to obtain credit. These schemes leave innocent people to deal with the fallout of fraud and financial damage,” said Christian Assaad, Acting Special Agent in Charge, Social Security Administration, Office of the Inspector General, San Francisco Field Division. “We will continue working with our federal partners to hold accountable those who exploit others and compromise the integrity of our financial system.”

“Identity theft inflicts severe and lasting damage on the financial well-being of hardworking Americans,” said Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Los Angeles acting Special Agent in Charge Erin Burke. “These arrests send the clear message that HSI and our partners are dedicated to rooting out financial fraud and protecting the public from those who lie and steal to illegally enrich themselves at the expense of innocent people.”

According to affidavits filed with the complaints, from February 2025 to May 2025, the defendants each filed for bankruptcy protection in U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Central District of California. Each bankruptcy filing included a signed, sworn declaration from each defendant stating under penalty of perjury that he or she used a Social Security number (SSN) not assigned to them to obtain credit.

In each case, the defendants used the credit to accumulate items of value and running up credit card debt, mostly from retailers, and the true SSN holders did not authorize the defendants to use their SSN for any purpose.

Espinosa reported incurring a total of $10,982 in debts including from furniture retailers and a jewelry store. Ortuño reported $63,974 in debts from retailers such as Old Navy, Macy’s, Lowe’s, The Home Depot, and Sam’s Club. Ávila reported incurring $15,964 in debt while Castellanos and Chávez reported debts of $32,961 and $19,153, respectively, mostly from credit cards obtained from retailers.

For example, in November 2021, Espinosa was approved for Daniel’s Jewelers credit lines with a total limit of $3,717, obtained through a misused SSN and in June 2024 made a $1,000 purchase at that jewelry store in Culver City.

From May 2022 to May 2023, Chávez used a MyPremier credit card with a credit limit of $1,000 to accrue purchase charges and cash withdrawals totaling $1,238, obtained through the misused SSN, with the transactions predominantly occurring in Long Beach.

In February 2023, Ortuño was approved for a Bass Pro Shop credit card with a credit limit of $6,000, obtained through the misused Social Security number (SSN) issued by Capital One Bank. He made the application online and in December 2024 used that credit card to make multiple purchases in Orange County for the total amount of $3,522.

In March 2023, Castellanos was approved for a Best Buy credit card with a $2,000 credit limit, obtained through the misused SSN issued by Citi Bank. In May 2023, he used that store credit card to purchase an appliance at a Best Buy store in Compton for approximately $1,206.

In November 2024, Ávila used the internet to apply for a PayPal credit card through the misused SSN and was approved for one with a $6,250 credit limit. In January 2025, he used that credit card to make a $1,185 purchase at a Guitar Center store.

A criminal complaint merely contains allegations. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

If convicted, each defendant would face a statutory maximum sentence of 15 years in federal prison.

Special Assistant United States Attorney Yi-Fan C. Everett is prosecuting these cases.

HOT SPRINGS – Three Hot Springs residents have been sentenced to more than 46 years combined in federal prison to be followed by terms of federal supervised release for methamphetamine distribution and firearm offenses. The Honorable District Judge John Thomas Shepherd presided over the sentencing hearings, which took place in the United States District Court in Hot Springs.

According to court records, in 2025, law enforcement agents conducted undercover controlled purchases of methamphetamine from Morris Zane Allen, age 60. Ultimately, law enforcements agents determined that Kimberly Medina, age 56, was delivering methamphetamine to Allenat the direction of the leader of the drug trafficking organization, KeAndria Haywood, age 37. Law enforcement agents conducted a search warrant at Allen’s residence and found Allen in possession of a large amount of methamphetamine and a firearm. Haywood was encountered on a motor vehicle traffic stop and found to be in possession of multiple controlled substances, to include methamphetamine and a firearm, along with United States currency utilized for some of the previous controlled purchases of methamphetamine with Allen.

On December 1, 2025, Morris Zane Allen pleaded guilty to Possession with the Intent to Distribute of More Than 50 Grams of Methamphetamine and Possession of a Firearm in Furtherance of a Drug Trafficking Offense. On December 2, 2025, Kimberly Medina pleaded guilty to Possession with the Intent to Distribute of More Than 50 Grams of Methamphetamine. KeAndria Haywood appeared before the Court on May 4, 2026, and pleaded guilty to Conspiracy to Distribute More Than 50 Grams of a Methamphetamine, Possession with the Intent to Distribute of More Than 5 Grams of Methamphetamine, and Possession of a Firearm in Furtherance of a Drug Trafficking Offense. On September 30, 2026, all three defendants appeared in separate proceedings before District Judge John Thomas Shepherd. Morris Zane Allen was sentenced to a term of 240 months imprisonment to be followed by 10 years of federal supervised release. Kimberly Medina was sentenced to a term of 53 months imprisonment also to be followed by 5 years of federal supervised release. KeAndria Haywood was sentenced to a term of 260 months imprisonment to be followed by 10 years of federal supervised release. In total, the members of the Drug Trafficking Organization led by Haywood were sentenced to 553 months, or more than 46 years combined, of imprisonment.

United States Attorney Kevin R. Holmes made the announcement. The Drug Enforcement Administration and the Hot Springs Police Department investigated the case. The Office of the Prosecuting Attorney for the 18th East Judicial District also assisted with the prosecution and investigation of this matter. Assistant United States Attorney Bryan A. Achorn prosecuted the case for the United States.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the U.S. Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.
