Congressional candidates collected $2.8 billion and disbursed $2 billion, political parties received $1.4 billion and spent $1 billion, and political action committees (PACs) raised $8.3 billion and spent $6.5 billion, according to campaign finance reports filed with the Federal Election Commission that cover activity from January 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026. Disbursements for independent expenditures reported in this period totaled $643.4 million. Communication costs reported to the Commission totaled $2.1 million and electioneering communications filings totaled $517,691 during this period.
Activity from Jan. 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026
(figures in millions)
This summary of campaign activity in the 2025-2026 election cycle provides a benchmark for comparison with the same reporting period in other cycles. Supporting data tables are linked at the end of each summary section below.
United States House and Senate candidates running in the 2026 election cycle reported raising a total of $2.8 billion and spending $2 billion between January 1, 2025 and June 30, 2026. Candidates for the two chambers reported combined total debts of $366.7 million and combined total cash-on-hand of $1.3 billion as of June 30, 2026.
The following table summarizes campaign finance activity of House and Senate candidates through June 30 of election years since the 2013-2014 election cycle.
18-Month Financial Activity of Congressional Candidates*
(dollar figures in millions)
The 315 candidates running for Senate in 2025 and 2026 reported total receipts of $864.3 million, disbursements of $614.2 million, debts of $40.6 million and cash-on-hand of $379.4 million.
The 2,427 candidates running for the House of Representatives reported combined total receipts of $1.9 billion, disbursements of $1.4 billion, debts of $326.1 million and cash-on-hand of $957.7 million in the 18-month period. In addition to the 2026 primary and general elections, these numbers encompass financial activity associated with the 2025 and 2026 special elections in Arizona’s 7th Congressional District, California’s 1st and 14th Congressional Districts, Florida’s 1st and 6th Congressional Districts, Georgia’s 13th and 14th Congressional Districts, New Jersey’s 11th Congressional District, Tennessee’s 7th Congressional District, Texas’ 18th Congressional District, and Virginia’s 11th Congressional District.
Data summary tables for reports submitted to the Commission through June 30, 2026 by 2025 and 2026 congressional candidate committees can be found here.
National, state, and local political party committees reported combined total receipts of $1.4 billion in federal funds, disbursements of $1 billion, debts of $21.7 million, and cash-on-hand of $488.5 million as of June 30, 2026. Of those totals, party committees other than the two major political parties reported receipts of $7.5 million, disbursements of $6.9 million, debts of $0.2 million and a combined cash-on-hand of $2.1 million as of June 30, 2026. (See the footnote in the following table for a list of these other party committees.)
The following table summarizes 2025-2026 campaign finance activity of the Democratic National Committee (DNC), Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee (DSCC), Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC), Republican National Committee (RNC), National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC) and National Republican Congressional Committee (NRCC), as well as each party’s state and local committees and other party committees.
Political Party Activity from Jan. 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026
(figures in millions)
Individuals, for whom contributions to national parties were limited to $44,300 per year during the 2025-2026 election cycle, were the largest source of federal funds for party committees’ traditional accounts. Democratic and Republican party committees reported receiving $413.6 million and $367.7 million, respectively, from individuals. PACs and other political committees contributed $61 million to Democratic party committees and $50.3 million to Republican party committees as of June 30, 2026.
Democratic and Republican House candidate committees transferred $34.7 million and $26.9 million, respectively, from their campaign accounts to their national congressional party committees. Democratic Senate candidate committees transferred $310,000 to the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee. Their Republican counterparts transferred $111,000 to the National Republican Senatorial Committee.
Provisions of the Consolidated and Further Continuing Appropriations Act, 2015 (Pub. L. 113-235), signed into law in December 2014, enable national party committees to establish accounts to defray certain expenses incurred with respect to Presidential nominating conventions, national party headquarters buildings, and election recounts and contests and other legal proceedings (collectively, “segregated party accounts”).
The segregated party accounts of national party committees reported receiving $256.3 million between January 1, 2025 and June 30, 2026. Of that total, the Democratic national party committee segregated party accounts received $87.9 million, while the corresponding Republican national party committee accounts received $168.4 million.
The recount and other legal proceedings accounts reported the highest receipt total across all the segregated party accounts: $126.8 million. Headquarters and convention accounts raised $111.4 million and $18.1 million, respectively, through June 30, 2026.
Data summary tables for reports submitted by political party committees to the Commission through June 30, 2026 can be found here.
Based on reports filed with the Commission from January 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026, 9,176 federal PACs reported total receipts of $8.3 billion, disbursements of $6.5 billion, debts of $39.4 million, and combined cash-on-hand of $3.3 billion.
The following table summarizes campaign finance activity of PACs based on PAC type in 2026. This table includes both separate segregated funds (SSFs), which have connected organizations such as corporations or labor organizations that establish, administer, or raise money on their behalf, and nonconnected committees.
PAC Activity from Jan. 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026
(dollar figures in millions)
Contributions by PACs to federal candidates seeking office in the 2025-2026 election cycle totaled approximately $350.2 million as of June 30, 2026. PAC contributions to Senate and House candidates totaled $56.6 million and $293.5 million, respectively. There were no reported contributions by PACs to 2028 presidential candidates as of June 30, 2026. Independent Expenditure-Only Political Committees are prohibited from making contributions to candidates.
Data summary tables for reports submitted by PACs to the Commission through June 30, 2026 can be found here.
Independent expenditures reported to the Commission through June 30, 2026 in connection with presidential and congressional elections in the 2025-2026 election cycle totaled $643.4 million.* Independent Expenditure-Only Political Committees accounted for $529.6 million of all independent expenditures disclosed to the Commission, Committees with Non-Contribution Accounts reported $97.3 million, and other PACs reported $11.5 million. Independent expenditures made by persons other than political committees totaled $4.8 million, and party committees reported independent expenditures totaling $233,461.
Data summary tables for independent expenditure filings submitted to the Commission through June 30, 2026 can be found here.
*A political committee must itemize its payments for independent expenditures once the calendar-year total paid to a vendor or other person exceeds $200 with respect to a particular election. Any other person (e.g., individual, partnership, or group of individuals) must file a report with the Commission at the end of the first reporting period in which independent expenditures with respect to a given election aggregate more than $250 in a calendar year and in any succeeding period during the same year in which additional independent expenditures of any amount are made.
Electioneering communication filings totaling $517,691 were reported to the Commission in connection with activity between January 1, 2025 and June 30, 2026. An electioneering communication is a broadcast, cable, or satellite communication that refers to a clearly identified federal candidate and is distributed within 30 days prior to a primary election or within 60 days prior to a general election. These communications do not expressly advocate the election or defeat of a federal candidate.
Data summary tables for electioneering communications filings submitted to the Commission through June 30, 2026 can be found here.
A provision of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971, as amended (the Act), allows corporations and labor organizations to communicate to a “restricted class” of individuals on any subject, including express advocacy of the election or defeat of any Federal candidate. The costs of such communications must be reported to the Commission when the cost exceeds $2,000 per election but are not considered independent expenditures. This provision of the Act predates the Supreme Court decision in Citizens United v. FEC, which struck down the ban on independent expenditures and electioneering communications financed by the general treasuries of corporations and labor unions.
The Commission received filings from 22 organizations during the reporting period, disclosing spending of $2.1 million in costs for communications to those organizations’ restricted classes between January 1, 2025 and June 30, 2026.
The data summary table for communication cost filings submitted to the Commission through June 30, 2026 can be found here.
The Federal Election Commission (FEC) is an independent regulatory agency that administers and enforces federal campaign finance laws. The FEC has jurisdiction over the financing of campaigns for the U.S. House of Representatives, the U.S. Senate, the Presidency and the Vice Presidency. Established in 1975, the FEC is composed of six Commissioners who are nominated by the President and confirmed by the U.S. Senate.

CONCORD – The United States Attorney’s Office for the District of New Hampshire launched the newest location for the Federal Government Pro Bono Program this week, bringing the 30-year institution to the Granite State during National Pro Bono Month. The New Hampshire Branch of the Federal Government Pro Bono Program will connect federal attorneys and paraprofessionals with legal service organizations in New Hamphsire to assist those in need across the Granite State. Today, those legal service organizations and interested federal employees met in the first ever New Hampshire Federal Pro Bono Program Fair.

“Public service for many at the U.S. Attorney’s Office means not only holding lawbreakers in New Hampshire accountable and recovering precious taxpayer resources illegitimately obtained through fraud or other schemes, but it also means doing what we can in our individual capacities to serve our fellow Granite Staters,” said Erin Creegan, U.S. Attorney for the District of New Hampshire. “With the launch of New Hampshire’s Federal Government Pro Bono Program, we hope to establish sustained partnerships with New Hampshire legal service organizations that can have a positive impact for our citizens faced with navigating the legal landscape and court systems on their own. We will continue to look for more opportunities for federal attorneys and paraprofessionals to volunteer for Granite Staters in need.”

Legal Service Organizations participating in today’s pro bono fair included: Administer Justice Saturday Legal Clinic, Court Appointed Special Advocates New Hampshire (CASA), 603 Legal Aid, New Hampshire Bar Association, New Hampshire Legal Assistance, and Veterans Legal Justice.

Speakers at the event included U.S. Department of Justice Pro Bono Program Manager and Chair of the Federal Government Pro Bono Program Lara Eilhardt, as well as New Hampshire Supreme Court Associate Justice Melissa B. Countway. Justice Countway spoke to interested federal practitioners about the value of pro bono, and the practice in New Hampshire state courts.

Federal government attorneys have engaged in pro bono work since the 1970s. In 1996, with the issuance of Executive Order 12988, the Department of Justice began to lead federal agencies in creating policies encouraging their staff to volunteer. The Order assigned the Attorney General to coordinate the government-wide endeavor. The U.S. Department of Justice administers today’s Federal Government Pro Bono Program. Other branches of the Program outside New Hampshire include Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, Colorado, the National Capital area, Los Angeles, Maryland, New York City, Dallas, and the San Francisco Bay area. For more information about the Federal Government Pro Bono Program, generally and in New Hampshire, see https://www.justice.gov/jmd/pro-bono-program , and the New Hampshire Federal Volunteer Guide .
title: U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Hampshire Launches Federal Government Pro Bono Program and Holds Fair to Highlight Volunteer Opportunities for Federal Employees

SALT LAKE CITY , Utah – A federal grand jury in Salt Lake City returned an indictment charging three Utah residents with robbing a credit union after one of the defendants approached a teller, handed over a threatening note demanding cash, and claimed to have an explosive device in his backpack.

Thomas Domingo Bustos, 31, of Layton, Utah; Brelyn Sanchez, 37, of Ogden, Utah; and Fidel Ybarra, 52, of Riverdale, Utah, were initially charged by complaint on September 15, 2026.

According to court documents, on September 4, 2026, officers with the South Salt Lake Police Department and members of the FBI’s Violent Crime Task Force responded to a robbery that occurred in South Salt Lake City, Utah. The credit union teller reported a male, later identified as Ybarra, entered the credit union carrying a backpack and passed a note to the teller that demanded cash and indicated he was holding an explosive device in his backpack. Ybarra then opened the backpack displaying what appeared to be an improvised explosive device. As a result, the teller handed Ybarra $1,234.00. Ybarra exited the credit union and fled in a red Dodge Durango. Sanchez was later identified as the driver. Through surveillance video, law enforcement identified a second vehicle, a red BMW, in connection with the robbery. Both vehicles were registered to Bustos. The investigation revealed that Bustos planned the robbery, created the hoax explosive device out of fireworks and duct tape, and drafted the demand note. Sanchez and Ybarra then met up at a residence and Bustos took the money.

Bustos, Ybarra, and Sanchez are charged with credit union robbery. Their initial appearance on the indictment is scheduled for October 2, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. in courtroom 8.4 at the Orrin G. Hatch United States Courthouse in downtown Salt Lake City.

United States Attorney Melissa Holyoak of the District of Utah made the announcement.

The case is being investigated jointly by the FBI Salt Lake City Field Office’s Violent Crime Task Force, and South Salt Lake City Police Department.

Assistant United States Attorney Carlos A. Esqueda is prosecuting the case.

This week, the U.S. Senate passed H.R. 1190, Congresswoman Janelle Bynum’s (OR-05) bipartisan Expanding Access to Capital for Rural Job Creators Act. The legislation would help rural small businesses overcome barriers to accessing capital.

The bill updates the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 by requiring the SEC’s Office of the Advocate for Small Business Capital Formation to report annually on the unique challenges rural businesses face when seeking investment. These reports will give Congress better information as it considers ways to improve access to capital for rural job creators.

"Rural small businesses shouldn’t have to work twice as hard just because of their ZIP code,” said Congresswoman Janelle Bynum. “The Senate passing this bill gets us one step closer to changing that. Rural entrepreneurs have the ideas and the hustle. They deserve a fair shot to grow them into something bigger."

“Rural small businesses are essential to communities across Montana, but too many still face unnecessary barriers when trying to access capital,” said Congressman Troy Downing (MT-02), the bill’s co-lead. “I’m proud of our legislation, which will help make sure rural businesses are no longer overlooked when Congress considers how to expand access to capital and support job creation.”

Senator John Kennedy (R-LA.) led the U.S. Senate companion bill to passage.

“Rural small businesses are the backbone of many communities across America, but too many face challenges accessing capital. I’m glad the Senate passed our bill to make sure Congress understands those challenges and help rural job creators grow their businesses, create jobs and serve their communities,” said Senator Kennedy.

Read the bill HERE.

Background:

The SEC’s Office of the Advocate for Small Business Capital Formation is required to identify problems that small businesses face when securing access to capital and submit an annual report to Congress.

Currently, the Office’s list of applicable entities are minority-owned, women-owned, and disaster-stricken small businesses.

This legislation would require the SEC’s Office of the Advocate for Small Business Capital Formation to add rural small businesses to its list of applicable entities.

title: Bynum’s Bipartisan Bill to Expand Capital Access for Rural Job Creators Heads to President’s Desk

USDA Highlights the Ways Cooperatives Support Trump Administration Priorities During National Cooperative Month
(Washington, D.C., October 1, 2026) — U.S. Department of Agriculture Secretary Brooke L. Rollins today issued a USDA proclamation (PDF, 575 KB) to recognize October 2026 as the Department’s 62nd anniversary of National Cooperative Month.
“Cooperatives are a powerful engine of economic growth for our nation and central to President Trump’s America First agenda to strengthen our economy and empower communities,” said Secretary Rollins. “Today we celebrate our partnerships with these cooperative organizations and reaffirm our commitment to advancing the vital work they do to create jobs, build local prosperity, support critical infrastructure, and expand opportunity for rural America.”
Since the start of the Trump Administration and under the leadership of Secretary Rollins, USDA has invested more than $18.1 billion in loans and grants to support 242 cooperatives to spur economic development, invest in critical electric and broadband infrastructure, and build prosperity through rural cooperatives supported by USDA Rural Development’s programs.
During Cooperative Month, USDA will highlight ways the Department is investing in cooperatives and creating stronger and more resilient communities. Supporting cooperatives strengthens farmer profitability, expands market access, encourages innovation, creates jobs in rural communities, and reinforces the America’s role of leadership in agriculture, food production, and farm security.
This year’s theme for the month-long celebration is “Built for this Moment,” as selected by the National Cooperative Business Association. This theme acknowledges the electric co-ops delivering essential infrastructure to rural America, the food co-ops that support local farmers and agricultural producers, the housing co-ops creating lasting affordability and the worker co-ops preserving local businesses.
USDA Rural Development offers a variety of financial assistance and services to assist rural businesses, including cooperatives and agricultural producers. For more information on cooperatives, visit USDA Rural Development Cooperative Services.
If you’d like to subscribe to USDA Rural Development updates, visit our GovDelivery subscriber page.

title: USDA Highlights the Ways Cooperatives Support Trump Administration Priorities During National Cooperative Month

Kamlager-Dove, Bacon Reintroduce Bipartisan Bills to Expand Medicaid Eligibility for Foster Youth
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Foster Youth Caucus Co-Chairs Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-CA) and Rep. Don Bacon (R-NE) reintroduced a legislative package to promote greater health equity by expanding Medicaid eligibility for foster youth.  
The Foster Youth Dental Act of 2026 would expand Medicaid eligibility for foster youth by providing more incentives for dental providers, increasing Medicaid enrollment opportunities, and preventing lapses in coverage.  
The Expanding Coverage for Former Foster Youth Act would broaden Medicaid-to-26 eligibility for former foster youth by removing enrollment restrictions, including those who exited to kinship guardianships or emancipated before 18, and requiring states to conduct coordinated outreach and enrollment efforts. 
“We must support the health care needs of the more than 23,000 young people who age out of our nation’s foster care system each year,” said Rep. Kamlager-Dove. “I’m proud to reintroduce these bipartisan, compassionate bills alongside Rep. Bacon to close persistent gaps in our health care system that too often force foster youth to go without the care they deserve. As Co-Chair of the Foster Youth Caucus, I remain committed to working across the aisle to ensure every foster youth has access to the resources they need, from health care to education, employment, and beyond.” 
“Having access to health care can make the transition to adulthood easier for former foster youth,” said Rep. Bacon. “Without a traditional support system, foster youth face an increased risk of chronic illness and need for mental health and dental care. Ensuring that former foster youth are eligible for Medicaid and have access to dental services helps prevent them from falling through the cracks. I’m pleased to co-lead this package with Rep. Kamlager-Dove to strengthen support for young people as they transition out of foster care.” 
The bipartisan Congressional Caucus on Foster Youth provides a forum for Members of Congress to discuss and develop policy recommendations to strengthen the child welfare system and improve the overall well-being of youth and families. The Foster Youth Caucus is committed to ensuring that our nation's vulnerable, yet resilient, youth are provided with the opportunities and support necessary to succeed. 
# # #
title: Kamlager-Dove, Bacon Reintroduce Bipartisan Bills to Expand Medicaid Eligibility for Foster Youth

MONROE – On September 21, 2026, United States Chief District Judge Terry A. Doughty sentenced Scott Perry Griffin , 50, of Dubach, to 204 months in federal prison for Conspiracy to Distribute and Possess with Intent to Distribute Methamphetamine followed by five years of supervised release. He pled guilty on June 6, 2026.

According to court documents, between May 16 and October 9, 2025, Griffin conspired with several others in a scheme to distribute methamphetamine. Investigators obtained a wiretap on a co-conspirator’s phone and intercepted communications between multiple narcotics distributors, including Griffin. Agents intercepted calls on July 2 on which Griffin ordered 1.25 pounds of methamphetamine from a major supplier. After Griffin was supplied, agents used a confidential source to purchase one ounce of methamphetamine directly from Griffin. Griffin was arrested later that night following a traffic stop by a Lincoln Parish deputy that revealed $729 in small denominations in Griffin’s pocket. The deputy also uncovered a bible case containing two digital scales, clear baggies, and 263 grams of methamphetamine.

U.S. Attorney Zachary A. Keller for the Western District of Louisiana made the announcement.

The Drug Enforcement Administration and Lincoln Parish Sheriff’s Office investigated this case. It was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney J. Aaron Crawford with assistance from Legal Assistant Amanda Morgan.

This case was prosecuted as part of Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN), the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities . Learn more at www.justice.gov/psn.

You may find a copy of this press release (and any updates) on the website of the United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Louisiana at www.justice.gov/usao-wdla .

Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Western District of Louisiana at www.lawd.uscourts.gov or at https://www.lawd.uscourts.gov/cmecf-pacer, under Case Number 3:25-cr-00299-04.

EPA Proposes Action to Unleash American Energy in Gulf of America
DALLAS, TEXAS (Oct. 1, 2026) – U. S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) proposed air permits to allow for construction on the Blue Marlin Offshore Port in the Gulf of America off the coast of Cameron Parish, Louisiana. If finalized as proposed, EPA’s actions will enable Blue Marlin to export around 80,000 barrels of crude oil per hour resulting in around 605 million barrels per year. The Trump EPA is committed to unleashing American energy and strengthening supply to lower costs for Americans across the nation.
“This project is not just about expanding infrastructure, it is about providing good-paying energy jobs and lowering prices at the pump by unleashing the full potential of American energy. If finalized as proposed, the Blue Marlin Deepwater Port will bring prosperity to not only the Gulf of America states but to Americans across the nation,” said EPARegional Administrator Scott Mason. “American families win when we encourage innovations in engineering technology that allow home-grown energy dominance to flourish while maintaining high environmental standards.”
“There has been no greater champion for the energy industry than President Trump and his Administration. The Blue Marlin Offshore Port project demonstrates that there has been no better home for energy dominance than Louisiana,” said Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry. “I’m grateful to President Trump and Administrator Zeldin for working with us to make this project a reality. This is a win for Louisiana and the nation!”
"Louisiana leads the world in advanced energy production, and Cameron Parish is certainly at the forefront of American energy dominance. When finalized, EPA’s proposal will build on that strength while creating excellent jobs for Louisiana families,” said Representative Clay Higgins (R-LA-03). “My office has fought for deepwater projects, and Blue Marlin reflects the Trump administration's aim to expand American energy policy worldwide. I look forward to seeing Blue Marlin at 100% production.”
After thorough review, EPA is proposing two draft permits: a Prevention of Significant Deterioration preconstruction permit and a title V federal operating permit. In order to maintain strong air quality protection throughout construction and operation, the project will use vapor-capture technology to prevent the release of volatile organic compounds as crude oil is transferred onto the carriers to protect air quality. A dedicated vapor collection system and vapor combustion units at the port will also ensure an expected 99 percent vapor-capture efficiency, preventing excess emissions from the transfer and loading process. This ensures that increasing crude oil exports can occur while maintaining air quality standards in the area.
EPA’s review and issuance of air permits is just one part of the overall permitting process for the Blue Marlin Deepwater Port. EPA will accept public comments for 30 days following publication of the proposal. For more information, please visit: https://www.epa.gov/caa-permitting/public-comment-and-hearing-opportunity-blue-marlin-offshore-port-llc-bmop-deepwater.

Bonamici, Moore Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Safely Dispose Opioids
WASHINGTON, DC [10/1/26] – Representatives Suzanne Bonamici (D-OR) and Riley M. Moore (R-WV) introduced bipartisan legislation to help people securely and safely dispose of unnecessary prescription medication.
The Safe Disposal of Opioids Act aims to stop prescription drug abuse by establishing a national grant program to install and maintain roughly 10,000 secure disposal receptacles across the country. These drop boxes will be conveniently located throughout healthcare facilities and community pharmacies where patients pick up their prescriptions, providing an easy way to dispose of excess medication.
"Providing a safe, easy way to get rid of unused medication is something we can do right now to protect families and neighbors across Oregon and the country," said Congresswoman Suzanne Bonamici. "When people have a convenient place in their community to drop off leftover opioids, it keeps medication out of the wrong hands, reduces the risk of abuse, and gives everyone peace of mind. This bipartisan legislation will make a real difference in keeping homes and neighborhoods safe."
“The dangerous scourge of opioids has devastated communities across West Virginia, more than anywhere else across the country,” said Congressman Riley M. Moore. “We must do everything we can to keep these deadly drugs off our streets and prevent unused opioids from being diverted for abuse. I’m proud to be the Republican leader on the Safe Disposal of Opioids Act, and I support commonsense solutions that help protect our families and communities.”
The grant program is funded through a fee imposed on pharmaceutical manufacturers that produce opioids. The legislation includes a rebate program to prevent the cost from being passed on to patients in hospice or with cancer who rely on opioid medication for pain management.
The Safe Disposal of Opioids Act legislative text can be viewed here.
Bonamici first introduced this bipartisan bill in 2018 based on feedback she got while hosting a series of community discussions about the opioid crisis in NW Oregon.
###
title: Bonamici, Moore Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Safely Dispose Opioids

BOTHELL, Wash. – This week, FEMA awarded more than $9 million in grant funding to fire departments, first responder organizations, and other institutions focused on firefighter safety and fire prevention in Idaho, Oregon and Washington. These awards will enable agencies to get the equipment, staff and support they need to carry out their critical, life-saving missions. By empowering fire departments to get the staff, training and equipment they need, FEMA is strengthening the resilience of American communities nationwide.”
FEMA is administering these funds through its Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response, which provides funding to hire more firefighters as well as for recruitment and retention efforts. Awards issued this week include:

Three Members of Violent Memphis Street Gang Sentenced for Attempted Murder in Aid of Racketeering and Firearm Charges
Three members of the Unknown Vice Lords (UVL), a violent street gang in Memphis, Tennessee, were sentenced to a total of over 42 years in prison for conspiring and attempting to commit a gang-related murder and firearms violations.
“These individuals showed a blatant disregard for public safety by engaging in a gang shooting in the middle of a residential neighborhood,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Gang violence terrorizes our communities, fosters fear, destabilizes neighborhoods, and endangers the lives of law-abiding residents. The Criminal Division is standing up for the rule of law. We will continue to dismantle these criminal organizations to zealously protect the safety and security of American citizens.”
“The days of criminal gangs controlling the streets of Memphis are over.” said U.S. Attorney D. Michael Dunavant for the Western District of Tennessee. “Gang culture, rivalries, and beefs beget more senseless gang violence that endangers innocent citizens. If you are a member of a criminal gang committed to a lifestyle of lawlessness, no matter your rank, role, or nickname - your days are numbered - there will be a reckoning.”
“ATF’s primary mission is to ensure public safety by combating violent crime,” said Special Agent in Charge James VanVliet of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) Nashville Field Division. “Individuals who deliberately engage in violent activities such as retaliatory gang shootings render our communities vulnerable to great harm, instill fear, and ultimately diminish the quality of life for all citizens. The ATF will continue to work with our local, state, and federal law enforcement partners to aggressively investigate offenders who render our communities unsafe.”
The following individuals were sentenced:
- Antwon Brown, also known as Yayo, 33, of Memphis, was sentenced to 300 months in prison for attempting to commit murder and discharging a firearm into an occupied residence.
- Cordera Douglas, also known as Chuckie Dee, 37, of Memphis, was sentenced to 87 months in prison for conspiring to commit murder.
- Willie Merriweather, also known as Willie, 42, of Antioch, Tennessee, was sentenced to 120 months in prison for conspiring to commit murder.
According to court documents, Brown, Douglas, and Merriweather were all ranked members of UVL, also known as The Ghost Mob, which is a criminal enterprise that controlled territory throughout Memphis, Arkansas, and Mississippi. Members of UVL committed murders, assaults, and drug trafficking on behalf of the enterprise.
Court documents allege that on Sept. 6, 2020, rival gang members opened fire on UVL members and their families, injuring four people. Merriweather, who was a high-ranking UVL leader, ordered a retaliatory attack. Douglas participated in a gang meeting planning retaliation. Shortly after midnight on Sept. 7, 2020, Brown traveled to the residence of the rival gang members armed with assault style rifles and wearing masks and gloves. Brown intentionally shot approximately 40-50 bullets into the residence with the rival gang members inside. Neighborhood security cameras captured the shooting. In the video, Brown is using, carrying, and firing multiple firearms into the residence.
Co-defendant Ricky Rogers, Jr., also known as Double R, RR, 32, of Memphis, is set to be sentenced on Nov. 5.
Co-defendant Tevin Richardson, also known as Santana, 34, of Memphis, is set for trial on April 4, 2027.
The ATF and Memphis Police Department investigated the case.
Trial Attorneys Lisa M. Thelwell and Dennis Robinson of the Criminal Division’s Violent Crime and Racketeering Section are prosecuting the case, with substantial assistance from the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Tennessee.
This case is part of the Criminal Division’s Violent Crime Initiative to prosecute violent crimes in Memphis, Tennessee, and surrounding areas. The Criminal Division and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Tennessee have partnered, along with local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies, to confront violent crimes committed by gang members and associates through the enforcement of federal laws and use of federal resources to prosecute the violent offenders and prevent further violence.

Brown Introduces Legislation to Address Nationwide Veterinarian Shortage, Encourage Next Generation to Work in Animal Medicine
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Shontel Brown (OH-11), Vice Ranking Member on the House Committee on Agriculture has introduced legislation to create a competitive federal grant program supporting work-based learning programs exposing high school-aged students to veterinarian medicine.
The VET CARE Act (Veterinary Expansion and Training for Comprehensive Animal Resources and Education Act) authorizes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) to provide federal grants to schools, 4-H or FFA organizations, veterinary clinics and hospitals, or veterinary and animal health offices to create, develop, or expand work-based learning programs focused on veterinary medicine.
In 2025, the USDA identified veterinarian shortages in 46 states. According to a 2025 report by the Ohio Department of Agriculture, The Ohio State University College of Veterinary Medicine, and the Farm Journal Foundation, Ohio faces a veterinarian shortage of 600 to 1,000 veterinarians by the next decade. That report surveyed Ohio stakeholders who rated the severity of the crisis at a “7.9 out of 10.”
Due to a lack of servicing and providers available, farmers and ranchers in all regions face a bottleneck of services due to overcrowding at shelters, private practices, and emergency care facilities.
“If we want more veterinarians serving our ranchers and rural communities, we need to start by showing young people that this is a career they can pursue. The Vet CARE Act would help schools and communities give students hands-on experience and a real look at what it means to work in veterinary medicine. By introducing students to these careers early, we can open doors for young people and build a stronger pipeline of veterinarians for the communities that need them most,” said Congresswoman Shontel Brown.
The VET CARE Act is supported by the American Association of Veterinary Medical Colleges and The Ohio State University.
“Through our mission of promoting excellence in academic veterinary medicine, the American Association of Veterinary Medical Colleges (AAVMC) knows that efforts to alleviate the veterinarian workforce shortage start long before students reach professional school classrooms. That is why we are encouraged by the VET CARE Act's work-based learning programs, which will give high school students real, hands-on exposure to veterinary medicine and a clearer pathway toward long-term employment in large-animal and food-animal veterinary practice, where our nation really needs help. We are proud to endorse a bill that aims to strengthen the veterinary pipeline from the ground up,” said Emma K. Read, Chief Executive Officer of the American Association of Veterinary Medical Colleges
“Addressing veterinary workforce shortages requires a long-term commitment to building and sustaining the pipeline of professionals who protect animal health, public health, and our food systems. Through our Protect One Health in Ohio (Protect OHIO) initiative, we are collaborating with the State of Ohio, agricultural partners, Ohio colleges and communities across the state to recruit and support future rural and large-animal veterinarians, reduce financial barriers to veterinary education and help graduates return to serve the communities that need them most,” said Dr. Rustin M. Moore, Rita Jean Wolfe Endowed Dean at the College of Veterinary Medicine at The Ohio State University. “The VET CARE Act would complement and amplify these efforts by creating additional opportunities for students to gain practical experience and pursue careers in the rural and agricultural communities in Ohio and across the nation where this highly specialized workforce is needed most. We are grateful to Congresswoman Brown for their leadership in advancing this important legislation and for recognizing the critical roles that veterinarians, veterinary technicians, animal scientists, diagnosticians, epidemiologists, food-safety specialists, animal-husbandry professionals and others across the agricultural workforce play in protecting our nation’s animal health, food supply, public health and rural communities.”
"Preparing the next generation of veterinarians and animal health professionals is essential to Ohio agriculture and the strength of our rural communities. The VET CARE Act would strengthen the pipeline of rural and large-animal veterinarians through expanded hands-on experience, rural community immersion, and partnerships with schools, 4-H, FFA, and communities across the state, while training our future workforce. We greatly appreciate Congresswoman Brown leadership in advancing this important legislation," said Dr. Cathann A. Kress, Vice President for Agricultural Administration and Dean of the College of Food, Agricultural, and Environmental Sciences at Ohio State University.
###
title: Brown Introduces Legislation to Address Nationwide Veterinarian Shortage, Encourage Next Generation to Work in Animal Medicine

CHICAGO — The former Chief Executive Officer of an Illinois railcar management company has been charged in federal court with embezzling more than $22 million from the company.

MICHAEL CALOMINO served as CEO of a company that provided railcar management services for clients who owned railcars throughout North America. The company contracted with the railcar owners to provide, among other things, maintenance and repair work on the railcars, often collecting funds from clients in advance of services to be arranged.

From 2016 to 2025, Calomino embezzled more than $22 million from the company by fraudulently converting funds held by the company on behalf of clients, according to a criminal information filed Wednesday in U.S. District Court in Chicago. Calomino transferred the money to personal bank accounts for his own use, including to pay gambling expenses, the information states.

The information charges Calomino, 69, of Frederick, Md., with one count of wire fraud. Arraignment in federal court has not yet been scheduled.

The information was announced by Andrew S. Boutros, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois; Ryan Whalen, Special Agent-in-Charge of the Chicago Field Office of the FBI; and Ben Wagner, Inspector General, Tennessee Valley Authority Office of the Inspector General. Valuable assistance was provided by the U.S. Trustee Program. The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorney Jeffrey Snell.

The public is reminded that an information is not evidence of guilt. The defendant is presumed innocent and entitled to a fair trial at which the government has the burden of proving guilt beyond a reasonable doubt. Wire fraud is punishable by up to 20 years in federal prison. If convicted, the Court must impose a reasonable sentence under federal statutes and the advisory U.S. Sentencing Guidelines.
title: Former CEO of Illinois Railcar Management Company Charged With Embezzling More Than $22 Million

Washington, DC -- Representative Gregory W. Meeks, Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressing concern over the reported conduct of U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle and the use of her role as a U.S. government official to advance personal and private commercial interests, including those of foreign companies.
In the letter, Ranking Member Meeks seeks answers regarding reports that Ambassador Guilfoyle threatened that the U.S. could use its influence to undermine Greece’s sovereign democratic government, reportedly invoking Romania as precedent; promoted the commercial interests of a Greek construction and energy company during official diplomatic engagements; and repeatedly allowed a registered lobbyist for that foreign company to participate in meetings with senior U.S. government officials and official foreign interlocutors.
Ranking Member Meeks called for the Ambassador’s removal if these allegations are accurate.
An excerpt of the letter is below. A copy is available here.
“According to a Wall Street Journal investigation published on September 25, 2026, Ambassador Guilfoyle told attendees at a March dinner with Greek and American officials, while discussing the impending collapse of then-Romanian Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan's government, that the United States could bring about similar political change in other countries, including Greece. This allegation has prompted public concern in both Greece and Romania about whether the United States government interferes in the democratic governments of its NATO allies. Greek opposition parties have publicly sought answers from their government regarding the reported remarks.
“The same reporting raises separate concerns regarding Ambassador Guilfoyle's relationship with Christos Marafatsos, a registered lobbyist for Greek construction and energy company Aktor Group. Federal lobbying records cited by the Wall Street Journal show that Aktor paid Mr. Marafatsos $160,000 through June 2026 to establish connections with, among others, the Department of State, Department of Energy, and Executive Office of the President. The Journal further reported that Mr. Marafatsos accompanied Ambassador Guilfoyle to numerous official U.S. government meetings, including meetings with foreign heads of government and other senior officials, and that some participants were not informed that he was a paid lobbyist for Aktor, with some foreign officials reportedly mistaking him for the Ambassador’s chief of staff.
“These concerns are heightened by reporting that Ambassador Guilfoyle has promoted Aktor or Aktor-affiliated energy projects, during official engagements throughout Southeast Europe.” 
###
title: Meeks Investigates Conduct of U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle

Washington, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Marilyn Strickland (WA-10) and Congressman David P. Joyce (OH-14) introduced a bipartisan Multigenerational HOMES (Housing Opportunities for Modifying Existing Structures) Act. The bill is one of a kind in that it will provide a tax credit for homeowners who renovate their homes to accommodate an elderly family member, a family member with a disability, or a family member who will be a live-in caregiver.

“This bill helps keep families under one roof at all stages of life if they choose to care for their aging family members,” said Strickland. “The tax credit provides families with additional in-home care options.”

“As a member of the Congressional Assisting Caregivers Today Caucus, I know how important it is to give families the flexibility to provide care without leaving the homes and communities they know,” said Congressman Joyce. “The Multigenerational HOMES Act would help families adapt their existing homes to meet their changing needs, making it easier for loved ones to live together while making better use of our existing housing stock. By giving families more options to share a home and care for one another, we can reduce the costs and pressures of finding additional housing while empowering families to make the decisions that work best for them.”

The tax credit can be used to make renovations such as adding handrails, stairlifts, wider doorways, and separate entrances. This makes it more affordable for families who choose the option of in-home caregiving for aging relatives.

“NAHB commends Rep. Strickland for introducing legislation to help families remain in their homes. The Multigenerational HOMES Act would provide a tax credit for homeowners to make renovations that accommodate family members with accessibility needs or disabilities. Caregivers face many challenges, and supporting their ability to keep loved ones together under one roof is both important and beneficial,” said Bill Owens, Chairman, National Association of Home Builders.

“Families live and care across generations, even when our homes and public systems are not designed that way. The Multigenerational HOMES Act would help families create safer, more accessible homes where older adults, people with disabilities, caregivers, and loved ones of every age can remain connected and supported. This is prevention through connection – and a practical investment in family stability, independence, and dignity,” said Kristen Kiefer, Executive Director, Generations United.

The legislation is endorsed by: AARP, Generations United, the National Association of Home Builders, and the National Association of the Remodeling Industry.

###
title: Strickland Introduces Bipartisan Intergenerational Housing Bill

House, Senate Introduce Bill to Lower Cost of Community College
WASHINGTON – Today, House Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (D-VA-03), Representative Adelita Grijalva (D-AZ-07), Representative Teresa Leger Fernández (D-NM-03), Representative Madeleine Dean (D-PA-04), and Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) introduced the America’s College Promise Act of 2026. The bill would make community college and two-year Tribal Colleges and Universities more accessible by waiving tuition fees for eligible students.
“Community colleges play a unique and vital role in providing students access to a quality postsecondary degree. Regrettably, the chronic underfunding of community colleges is jeopardizing their ability to support their students and communities,” said Ranking Member Scott (D-VA-03). “The America’s College Promise Act is a major investment in expanding opportunities for students and rebuilding a stronger economy.”
“Students in Southern Arizona and throughout the country should not have to take on tens of thousands of dollars of debt to get a college education,” said Representative Grijalva. “The America’s College Promise Act will provide two years of free in-state tuition and fees for students enrolled in community and technical college programs. Whether they’re just starting out or returning to the classroom later in life, every student deserves the opportunity to learn new skills and pursue higher education. By expanding access to education and workforce training, we’re strengthening the workforce that businesses and local economies depend on.”
“In New Mexico, we know free community college can unlock the doors to a brighter future. The America’s College Promise Act builds on New Mexico’s example by making sure students across the country can attend community college without the burden of tuition and fees,” said Representative Leger Fernández. “Our bill will provide funds for services students need to earn their degrees and reduce the financial burden for low-income students to attend TCUs, HBCUs, and MSIs. From recent high school graduates to experienced workers who want to go back to school — every student deserves the opportunity to keep learning without the fear of drowning in debt.”
“As a professor, it was a privilege to witness students claim their education and seize their futures — yet the real fear and burden of immense student loan debt often deters young adults and returning students from expanding their learning,” said Representative Dean. “The America’s College Promise Act provides tuition-free community college courses and expands funding for HBCUs and trade schools, making the path to higher education and career readiness available to more Americans and future generations.”
“Every Wisconsinite deserves the opportunity to get the education and skills they need to land a good-paying job and build a better life, no matter where they come from or how much money their family makes,” said Senator Baldwin. “But for too many working families, the rising cost of higher education leaves students saddled with debt for years to come, or it is simply out of reach. That’s why I am proud to work with my colleagues to remove barriers and lower the cost of community college, so more Wisconsinites have the opportunity to compete, succeed, and live a good middle-class life.”
The America’s College Promise Act of 2026 will make the skills and credentials necessary to succeed in the workforce more accessible to all students by creating a new federal-state partnership to provide two years of tuition-free community college.
Specifically, the America’s College Promise Act of 2026:
- Creates a partnership between the federal government and states to waive tuition and fees for two years of community and technical college programs for eligible students, while promoting key reforms to accelerate student success;
- Creates a sliding scale for federal share beginning at 100 percent for the first year and ending at 80 percent for the fifth and subsequent years;
- Ensures that programs offer academic credits that are transferable to four-year institutions in their state, or occupational training that leads to recognized credentials;
- Maintains and encourages state funding for higher education;
- Establishes a student success fund to improve enrollment, retention, transfer, or completion rates and labor market outcomes for underserved student populations, including students of color and low-income and first-generation college students, who attend community and technical colleges at disproportionate rates;
- Waives two years of tuition and fees for eligible students at tribal colleges and universities; and
- Establishes a new grant program to provide pathways to success at historically black colleges and universities and minority-serving institutions by covering a significant portion of tuition and fees for the first two years of attendance for low-income students.

MOLINE, Ill., - A Texas City, Texas, woman, Dorothy Barber, 54, was sentenced last week to 18 months of imprisonment, to be followed by three years of supervised release, for wire fraud. Barber also was ordered to pay $311,768.85 in restitution.

According to court documents and statements in court, Barber, along with others, recruited and assisted other individuals to fraudulently apply for Paycheck Protection Program (“PPP”) loans during the COVID-19 pandemic. PPP loans were supposed to be used for certain qualifying business expenses. Barber, who fraudulently obtained her own $20,000 PPP loan, also received kickbacks from other individuals whom she assisted in obtaining loans.

At the sentencing hearing on September 24, 2026, U.S. District Judge Sara Darrow said that Barber took advantage of a program meant to serve as a safety net for employers and to preserve peoples’ livelihoods during a vulnerable time in history. Judge Darrow stated that “these types of crimes come with real consequences.”

A federal grand jury returned an indictment against Barber in May 2025. Barber pleaded guilty in December 2025.

“Our office is committed to prosecuting individuals such as the defendant who took advantage of a program designed to help small business owners in the midst of the pandemic,” said United States Attorney for the Central District of Illinois Gregory M. Gilmore. “Stealing money from government programs is a fraud on the taxpayers and diverts these critical financial resources away from legitimate funding needs. We are grateful to our federal and local partners for their work in investigating these crimes.”

“Ms. Barber is one of many fraudsters who exploited a program created to helped legitimate small business owners crippled by the pandemic,” said IRS Criminal Investigation Special Agent in Charge William Steenson. “IRS-CI special agents are unwavering in their commitment to bringing justice on behalf of all taxpayers by exposing those who stole from CARES Act pandemic relief programs. Our work in conjunction with the U.S. Attorney’s Office and other federal law enforcement agencies should make pandemic era thieves nervous as we ramp up efforts to track them down.”

The statutory penalties for wire fraud are not more than 30 years’ imprisonment and up to a $250,000 fine.

The Small Business Administration and the Internal Revenue Service investigated the case with assistance from the Galesburg Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Jennifer L. Mathew represented the government at sentencing.
title: Texas Woman Sentenced to 18 Months in Prison for Wire Fraud

California Man Arrested for Smuggling More Than $300 Million in Export-Controlled Computer Servers to China
The owner of a San Gabriel Valley-based technology company was arrested today on a three-count federal indictment charging him with smuggling more than $300 million worth of export-controlled high-end computer servers containing U.S.-manufactured graphics processing units (GPUs) commonly used for Super Intelligence (SI) applications to China.
“SI is the defining technology of the era,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “The National Security Division will protect the American advantage in the chips that power this technology, a product of our unparalleled innovation and hard work, from illegal diversion by our economic and military adversaries.”
“Protecting America’s national security means keeping our advanced Super Intelligence technology from being used to strengthen our adversaries’ military capabilities,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli for the Central District of California. “This defendant allegedly used false paperwork and shipments through third countries to smuggle more than $300 million in export-controlled computer servers to China. We will aggressively prosecute those who put our national security at risk for profit.”
“The FBI’s investigation revealed that Lui allegedly sold the Chinese government hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of American Super Intelligence technology, in clear violation of U.S. export control laws,” said Assistant Director Roman Rozhavsky of the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division. “Controlling the export of advanced SI technology is critical to safeguarding our national security and defending the homeland, and the FBI will keep fighting for America’s businesses and economic security. We’re grateful to our partners across the U.S. government and private sector for their assistance, and we’ll continue holding accountable anyone who violates U.S. export laws to enrich themselves and help our adversaries.”
“Preventing the illegal export of controlled technology is critical to protecting our national security,” said Special Agent in Charge John E. Helsing of the Department of Defense Office of Inspector General Defense Criminal Investigative Service (DCIS) Western Field Office. “These technologies provide core advantages to U.S. forces, and ensuring they remain safeguarded prevents adversaries from exploiting them. Today’s action underscores our commitment to protecting advanced defense capabilities and enforcing the laws that keep them out of the hands of those who may threaten the United States.”
“The Bureau of Industry and Security is committed to using all lawful means to protect national security and hold violators accountable,” said Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Export Enforcement David A. Peters of the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security Office of Export Enforcement.
Greg Lui, 38, also known as “Yiu Kong Lui,” of San Gabriel, California, is expected to make his initial appearance and be arraigned this afternoon.
Lui is charged with one count of conspiracy to violate the Export Control Reform Act and the Export Administration Regulations, one count of outbound smuggling, and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering.
According to the indictment returned on Sept. 29, Lui owns Earthmade Computer Inc., a City of Industry-based technology company and closely held corporation.
From 2023 to 2024, Lui and his co-conspirators used Earthmade to buy and send export-controlled items to China without the required licenses issued by the U.S. Department of Commerce. Instead, they shipped these items to countries such as Malaysia and Singapore, where no such license is required, then illegally re-exported them to China.
The items in question were high-end computer servers containing GPUs manufactured by companies that specialize in SI computing. Lui did so despite knowing that the true end users of the servers he purchased were in China. As part of the scheme, Lui and his co-conspirators provided false documentation to U.S.-based manufacturers that misrepresented that the items would be going to permissible end users and end destinations that did not require an export license. After placing these orders, Lui employed various freight forwarding companies to ship the export-controlled servers to countries such as Malaysia and Singapore. Once the servers arrived in these locations, Lui worked with his coconspirators to reship the items to China. From January 2024 to October 2024, Earthmade received more than $176 million from two Malaysia-based shipment companies as part of the scheme.
According to the indictment, Lui executed this scheme knowing that U.S. government regulations barred the export of such high-end technology to China to protect the national security and foreign policy interests of the United States. According to U.S. government regulations, such high-end GPUs could make significant contributions to the military potential of other nations.
In January 2024, Lui emailed a conspirator indicating that a Malaysian transshipment company wished to purchase 70 servers with export-restricted GPUs. In that email correspondence, Lui attached an export compliance form that indicated that the Malaysian company was aware of U.S. export laws that restricted the sale, transshipment, or export of these specific servers.
Later that month, Lui submitted a purchase order to a U.S. manufacturer for 27 of these servers for approximately $7,614,000. He and a co-conspirator then caused the servers to be shipped from Los Angeles to Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. The packing list for this shipment indicated that the shipment contained 27 servers with GPUs, which were export controlled and could not be sent to China without a license.
In March 2024, a co-conspirator emailed a Malaysian government official that 27 servers had, in fact, been transshipped to a China-based buyer.
If convicted of all charges, Lui could face a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison on the conspiracy count, a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison on the money laundering count, and a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison on the smuggling count.
The U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security Office of Export Enforcement, the Defense Criminal Investigative Service, and the FBI are investigating this matter.
Assistant U.S. Attorneys Colin S. Scott and Joseph S. Guzman for the Central District of California and Trial Attorney Eli Ross of the National Security Division’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section are prosecuting the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Alexander Su for the Central District of California is handling the civil and criminal forfeitures of the seized property.
An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: California Man Arrested for Smuggling More Than $300 Million in Export-Controlled Computer Servers to China

ATF and CHP arrest Los Angeles man on federal fentanyl and machine gun charges
LOS ANGELES, Calif. – Agents with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and officers with the California Highway Patrol arrested Christian Laird, 34, of Los Angeles, on Sept. 30, 2026, on a federal indictment charging him with fentanyl trafficking and illegal firearms offenses.
The five-count indictment, returned in the Central District of California, alleges that on or about July 1, 2025, in Los Angeles County, Laird possessed with intent to distribute approximately 822.5 grams of a mixture containing fentanyl, as well as a separate quantity of approximately 15.1 grams of a mixture containing fentanyl.
"Fentanyl and machine gun conversion devices are a dangerous combination, and when they are in the hands of someone who is prohibited from having a firearm, the risk to our communities is severe. A Glock switch turns a pistol into a machine gun that can fire dozens of rounds in seconds. ATF's mission is to protect America's communities from violent crime driven by the illegal use of firearms, and our special agents and task force officers focus on dismantling those who are prohibited persons and fuel violence. We are grateful to our partners at the California Highway Patrol for their work on this case, and we will keep working side by side to take illegal weapons and deadly drugs off our streets," said ATF Los Angeles Field Division Special Agent in Charge Kenny Cooper.
The indictment also alleges that Laird, a prior felony conviction, illegally possessed a Glock Model 22, .40 caliber semi-automatic pistol equipped with a machine gun conversion device, commonly known as a "Glock switch" or "auto sear," in furtherance of those drug trafficking crimes. These devices allow a semi-automatic pistol to fire multiple rounds with a single pull of the trigger. Federal law prohibits possessing such a weapon.
Charges:
- Count 1: Possession with intent to distribute 400 grams or more of fentanyl (21 U.S.C. §§ 841(a)(1), (b)(1)(A)(vi))
- Count 2: Possession with intent to distribute fentanyl (21 U.S.C. §§ 841(a)(1), (b)(1)(C))
- Count 3: Possession of a machine gun in furtherance of drug trafficking crimes (18 U.S.C. §§ 924(c)(1)(A)(i), (c)(1)(B)(ii))
- Count 4: Unlawful possession of a machine gun (18 U.S.C. § 922(o))
- Count 5: Felon in possession of a firearm and ammunition (18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(1))
An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
This case is being investigated by ATF and CHP and is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of California.

Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representatives Norma Torres (CA-35) and Chuck Fleischmann (TN-03) introduce a bipartisan resolution recognizing October 2, 2026, the first Friday of October, as National Manufacturing Day.

The resolution celebrates the important role American manufacturing plays in strengthening the economy, driving innovation, supporting supply chains, and creating good-paying, family-sustaining jobs in communities across the country.

“Supporting the Manufacturing industry is key to growing the Inland Empire’s economy and creating pathways to good-paying careers in our region,” said Congresswoman Norma Torres. “Every year, I have the opportunity to visit manufacturers across my district and see firsthand the innovation, skill, and hard work that keep our economy moving. Manufacturing Day is an opportunity to recognize these workers and businesses while encouraging the next generation to explore careers in this growing industry. I am proud to once again partner with Congressman Fleischmann to celebrate American manufacturing and the people who make it possible.”

"Whether it’s the cars we drive, the homes we live in, or the products we use every day, manufacturing touches every part of our lives. It creates good jobs, helps our communities thrive, and gives workers the chance to build new skills and brighter futures. That’s why it’s so important to take a moment to celebrate the people behind America’s manufacturing industry. I’m proud to work with my colleagues on this bipartisan resolution. I will always stand up for American manufacturing in Congress,” said Congressman Fleischmann.

Manufacturers contribute approximately $2.9 trillion to the U.S. economy, accounting for roughly 11 percent of gross domestic product. Nearly 12.9 million Americans are directly employed in manufacturing, with millions more jobs supported throughout supply chains and related industries. American manufacturers are also major drivers of innovation, investing hundreds of billions of dollars in research and development.

Congresswoman Torres has made supporting manufacturers and developing a skilled workforce a priority in the Inland Empire. Through her annual “Made in the 35th” manufacturing tour, Torres visits local manufacturers to hear directly from employers and workers about their needs, highlight locally made products, and promote career opportunities in the industry.

Torres and Fleischmann have also worked together to strengthen American manufacturing and supply chains. Their bipartisan National MEP Supply Chain Database Act was included in the CHIPS and Science Act (Public Law No: 117-167) to help manufacturers better prepare for and respond to future supply chain disruptions.

The full resolution can be found HERE.

WASHINGTON – Langston Wedge, 20, of Upper Marlboro, MD, was sentenced today in the Superior Court for the District of Columbia, for charges related to a shooting at the Power Nightclub in Northeast that injured five people, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro.

Wedge pleaded guilty, on April 6, 2026, to two counts of aggravated assault while armed and one count of possession of a firearm during a crime of violence, in the D.C. Superior Court. On October 1, 2026, Judge Errol Arthur sentenced Wedge to 10 years in prison to be followed by five years of supervised release. The Court denied without prejudice the defense request for a sentence under the Youth Rehabilitation Act.

According to the government’s evidence, in the early morning of November 2, 2025, Wedge, who was with a group of friends, got into fight with others outside the Power Nightclub at 2335 Bladensburg Road Northeast. Power Nightclub was hosting a Halloween-themed costume event. The event was crowded and some celebrants spilled out into a line on the sidewalk in front of the club. At 1:47 a.m., Wedge started shooting wildly toward the crowd, and panicked attendees scattered and ran for cover. During the shooting, five people and a vehicle were struck with bullets. One victim was shot in the leg. A second victim was shot through the back and the upper arm and continues to experience pain and discomfort from his injury. Two victims were each shot through the thigh. And one victim was shot through the right side of his chest and lost an enormous amount of blood, spending three days in ICU with a punctured lung.

Prince George’s County Police arrested Wedge on November 17, 2025. At the time of arrest, the defendant was in possession of a Glock 26 .9mm handgun with a magazine capable of holding 30 rounds of ammunition. Ballistics evidence showed that this was the firearm used to shoot the five victims at the nightclub, two weeks earlier.

Picture of Glock 26 .9mm handgun recovered from defendant at time of arrest.

Wedge was arrested in D.C. on December 10, 2025, and has been in custody since.

Joining in the announcement was Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll of the Metropolitan Police Department.

In announcing the sentencing, U.S. Attorney Pirro and Interim Chief Carroll, commended the work of those who investigated the case from the Metropolitan Police Department and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF). They acknowledged the work of Assistant U.S. Attorney Nickolas Reck, who prosecuted the case.

NEW ORLEANS, LA – DIONTE DORSEY , (“DORSEY”) , age 45, of New Orleans, was sentenced to 48 months imprisonment, followed by five (5) years of supervised release, by the U.S. District Judge Carl J. Barbier on September 24, 2026, announced U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle. DORSEY had previously pled guilty to Counts 1, 4, and 8 of the indictment pending against him. DORSEY was also ordered to pay a $300 mandatory special assessment fee.

DORSEY was charged in Count 1 with conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute controlled substances, in violation of Title 21 U.S.C. §§ 841(a)(1), 841(b)(1)(A), and 841(b)(1)(C).

DORSEY was charged in Count 4 with possessing firearms in furtherance of drug trafficking crimes, in violation of Title 18 U.S.C. § 924(c)(1). DORSEY was charged in Count 8 with maintaining a drug-involved premises, in violation of Title 21 U.S.C. § 856(a) and Title 18 U.S.C. § 2.

According to the indictment, beginning at a time unknown but continuing until at least May 8, 2024, DORSEY and other individuals maintained three residences in the Algiers neighborhood of New Orleans for the purpose of packaging and distributing narcotics, including fentanyl, cocaine, and heroin. Numerous drug overdoses that occurred around one of these residences alerted law enforcement to this drug trafficking activity. After the execution of multiple search warrants at these residences, DORSEY and other individuals were arrested, and numerous firearms and large amounts of fentanyl were seized from these residences. DORSEY possessed these firearms to further this drug trafficking conspiracy.

U.S. Attorney Courcelle praised the work of the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Louisiana State Police, and the New Orleans Police Department. The prosecution is being handled by Assistant United States Attorney Stuart Theriot of the Violent Crimes Unit.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities .

MENLO PARK, CA – A controversial development at 80 Willow Road is facing a significant roadblock after the Menlo Park City Council refused to approve it.

Days before, the property’s owner, billionaire Vitaly Yusufov, drew scrutiny for his reported ties to Kremlin officials and individuals linked to organized crime when Congressman Sam Liccardo (CA-16) called on Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to launch an immediate federal review of the project’s ownership and financing. Liccardo urged the Office of Foreign Assets Control and the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States to investigate Yusufov and consider sanctions if the review uncovered sanctionable conduct.

“We need more housing, but our housing shortage cannot turn our communities into safe harbors to avoid sanctions or launder illicit funds,” said Liccardo. “This marks an important step toward keeping Kremlin-linked money out of our community and protecting our national security.”
title: Tower Development with Alleged Kremlin-Linked Owner Hits Roadblock

CHICAGO — Congressman Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04) led his colleagues Congresswoman Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Congressmen Mike Quigley (IL-05), and Jonathan Jackson (IL-01) in a letter to the U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee, condemning the violence by Israeli settlers, police and military in the village of al-Mughayyir in the occupied West Bank. The legislators, who represent several constituents with relatives living in the village, are calling attention to the alarming situation where recently five Palestinian residents under the age of 20 were killed, others including a nine-year old boy have been shot, and food, basic needs and even education have been restricted.

“They have destroyed homes, businesses, and farms, uprooted thousands of olive trees, stolen livestock, blocked food and other necessary supplies from entering the village, and devastated the entire local economy,” state the Members of Congress in the letter. “Those residents who are not murdered by Israeli forces are condemned to a horrific existence marked by poverty, deprivation, and terror.”

“This is not an isolated situation; it reflects an intentional policy of violence and terrorism inflicted by Israeli forces across the occupied West Bank to further the ethnic cleansing and genocide of the Palestinian people,” continues the letter. “Shamefully, the U.S. government has consistently backed this policy by continuing to provide military aid to Israel and failing to act to stop these rampant attacks. This is morally unconscionable and directly affects the U.S. citizens who live in al-Mughayyir or who (like several of our constituents) have relatives that live there.”

The Members urged Ambassador Huckabee to visit al-Mughayyir, hold a town hall with its residents, and specify concrete actions the U.S. government will take to intervene with the Israeli government. “At minimum, the Administration should follow the lead of our allies and impose sanctions and a trade ban on settlements, but much more is required to end our government’s longstanding support of the mass atrocities committed against the Palestinian people,” demand the Members of Congress in the letter.

A full copy of the letter can be found here.
