Pocan, Schakowsky Lead 71 Members Calling for Continued Allowance of Prescription Drug Imports
WASHINGTON D.C. -
U.S. Representatives Mark Pocan (WI-02) and Jan Schakowsky (IL-09)today led a letter, signed by 71 Members of Congress, to Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) Robert F. Kennedy, Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) Markwayne Mullin, and the commissioners of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP), urging that the agencies ensure that Americans can continue to obtain genuine, non-controlled prescription medicines from outside the country.
New CBP procedures for international mail shipments, taking effect October 22, could disrupt 2.3 million Americans’ longstanding ability to obtain lower-cost prescription medicines from Canada and other countries for their personal use.
“For years, our constituents who have struggled with high prescription drug prices have obtained their medicines from pharmacies outside the United States, especially from Canada,” the members wrote.
“We support CBP’s goal of using better data to identify and intercept high-risk shipments. However, we are concerned that the new process could be implemented in a manner that prevents personal-use prescription medicines from being shipped to the United States or results in their routine refusal, including medicines Americans have long obtained from licensed pharmacies abroad,” the members continued. “Greater visibility should instead improve the government’s ability to distinguish dangerous products from lower-risk prescription medicines and preserve appropriate enforcement discretion.”
“We urge HHS, FDA, DHS, and CBP to delay any implementation of new procedures with respect to prescription medicines unless you can provide clear assurances that your agencies will not prevent genuine prescription medicines clearly intended for personal use and not appearing to present an unreasonable risk from entering the United States,” the members added.
“Americans should not lose access to affordable medicines simply because the government has better information about packages entering the country. We urge your agencies to use that information to focus enforcement on where the risks are greatest while preserving appropriate access to safe and affordable medicines for personal use,” the members concluded.
A digital copy of the full letter can be found here.
The letter is endorsed by the Campaign for Personal Prescription Importation, Just Care USA, National Association of Letter Carriers, Prescription Justice, and Social Security Works.

Tampa, Florida – Richard Plummer (45, Tampa) has been sentenced by U.S. District Judge Steven D. Merryday to more than 27 years in federal prison for distribution and possession of child sex abuse material (CSAM) and escape. Plummer pleaded guilty on May 11, 2026. United States Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement.

According to court documents, in 2018, Plummer was convicted of coercion and enticement of a minor to engage in sexual activity and sentenced to ten years’ imprisonment in the Middle District of Florida. In October 2025, while serving his prison sentence at the Tampa Residential Re-Entry Center, law enforcement discovered Plummer in possession of a cellphone containing CSAM. Further examination of the phone revealed Plummer had distributed and possessed CSAM. During the investigation, on November 1, 2025, Plummer escaped from the re-entry facility where he was serving the sentence imposed in his 2018 case.

This case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Tampa Police Department. It was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Courtney Derry.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by United States Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc.
title: Tampa Sex Offender Sentenced to More Than 27 Years for Distribution and Possession of Child Sex Abuse Material and Escape

text:
COLUMBIA, S.C — Gregory Hill, 41, of Lexington has been sentenced to 10 years in federal prison for distribution of fentanyl and cocaine. On Oct. 4, 2024, investigators with the Drug Enforcement Administration and Lexington County Sheriff’s Department surveilled Hill leaving his residence in Lexington and traveling to a nearby business to ship two packages. Officers went to the business and located the packages, which were being sent out of state. Hill’s known aliases were listed as the sender of the packages. Law enforcement flagged the packages as suspicious. A K9 sniffed the packages and alerted to the presence of drugs. Thereafter, law enforcement obtained a warrant to search the packages. They found 984 grams of fentanyl powder in one package and 1,019 fentanyl pills in the other. On Oct. 7, 2024, law enforcement executed a search warrant at Hill’s home and found 1,438 fentanyl pills, over $29,000 in cash, and packaging material. Law enforcement also searched Hill’s storage unit where they found a drug ledger. Further investigation revealed that Hill was responsible for trafficking 14 kilograms of cocaine, 984 grams of fentanyl powder, and 32,458 fentanyl pills to various drug traffickers. United States District Judge Sherri A. Lydon sentenced Hill to 120 months’ imprisonment, to be followed by a five-year term of court-ordered supervision. There is no parole in the federal system. This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. This case was investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration, the FBI Columbia Field Office, the South Carolina Law Enforcement Division, and the Lexington County Sheriff’s Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Lamar J. Fyall prosecuted the case.

SOUTH BEND – Jianhua Zhao, 25 years old, of the People’s Republic of China, and residing in Brooklyn, New York, was sentenced by United States District Court Judge Damon R. Leichty after pleading guilty to conspiring to distribute methamphetamine and cocaine and distributing five grams or more of methamphetamine, announced United States Attorney Adam L. Mildred.

Zhao was sentenced to 78 months in prison.

“For almost a year, Zhao distributed harmful drugs like methamphetamine and cocaine across the country. Based in Brooklyn, Zhao stockpiled drugs in his residence, packaged them for delivery, and shipped them to buyers who purchased the drugs on the Dark Web. This high-tech scheme distributed drugs to every state in the United States, including cities and towns throughout Indiana, averaging hundreds of drug deals and thousands in sales per month and ultimately leading to the seizure of more than $2,000,000 in virtual currency. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directed the full might of United States law enforcement team towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting this case making clear that drug traffickers cannot hide on the Dark Web. They will be tracked down and brought to justice for sending poison to the heartland. This prosecution was brought through the combined efforts of the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, and the United States Postal Inspection Service with assistance from the St. Joseph County Police Department, Mishawaka Police Department, Indiana State Police, New York City Police Department, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, and South Gate Police Department and prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney and NDIN Appellate Division Chief Joseph P. Falvey,” said U.S. Attorney Adam Mildred.

“The Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) is committed to the dismantlement of cyber and Dark Web-based criminal networks responsible for the surge of controlled substances throughout the United States. These illicit operations pose a significant threat to public health and safety. For almost a year, Jianhua Zhao supported a highly sophisticated, nationwide drug trafficking organization that operated on a mass scale, thus profiting from the suffering of others. Even Indiana was not immune to his illegal actions. The sentencing of Zhao sends a clear message that this type of criminal activity is not welcomed here in our Hoosier state,” said DEA Assistant Special Agent in Charge Chip Cooke.

“The U.S. Postal Inspection Service is dedicated to defending the nation’s mail system from criminal activity, preserving the integrity of the U.S. Mail, and protecting the United States Postal Service employees,” said Inspector in Charge Felicia B. George, United States Postal Inspection Service, Detroit Division. “The public has an expectation that the U.S. Mail and its contents to be safe and not used as a transportation network for controlled substances. The sentencing of Mr. Zhao sends a clear message the United States Postal Service and Inspection Service will not stand for such activity. The U.S. Postal Inspection Service works endlessly with our Local, State, and Federal law enforcement partners to protect the public from dangerous substances.”

“The FBI is committed to using every investigative tool available to identify and bring to justice those who traffic dangerous drugs, including those who attempt to conceal their criminal activity online,” said FBI Indianapolis Special Agent in Charge Timothy J. O’Malley. “Technology and the Dark Web will not shield you. If you use the internet to deal drugs, we will find you and hold you accountable. This sentence reflects the strength of our law enforcement partnerships and our commitment to dismantling drug trafficking networks, wherever they operate.”

Zhao’s co-defendant, Bao Xu, was sentenced on June 10, 2026, to 121 months in prison followed by 4 years of supervised release.

This case was investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, and the United States Postal Inspection Service with assistance from the St. Joseph County Police Department, Mishawaka Police Department, Indiana State Police, New York City Police Department, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, and South Gate Police Department. text:
MIAMI – A federal grand jury in the Southern District of Florida returned an indictment unsealed today charging two people with allegedly operating a decades-long bribery and money laundering scheme that defrauded thousands of sub sandwich franchise owners nationwide of more than $80 million.

According to court records, Janet Risi Field, 66, of Pinecrest, and her brother, Steven Louis Risi, 70, of Coral Gables, participated in a scheme in which vendors seeking contracts to supply Restaurant Chain-1 franchisees allegedly paid millions of dollars in secret bribes and kickbacks to Risi Field and members of her family.

Restaurant Chain-1 was an American multinational fast-food chain with more than 20,000 locations in North America, most of which were independently owned and operated by franchisees. Independent Purchasing Cooperative, Inc. (IPC), a Miami-Dade County-based nonprofit organization, managed the chain’s North American supply chain and negotiated with vendors to establish the prices franchisees paid for food, supplies, and services.

Risi Field helped form IPC in 1996 and served as its CEO until December 2021. In that role, she had authority to enter into vendor contracts that affected the prices paid by thousands of franchisees.

The indictment alleges that Risi Field abused that position by entering into a secret arrangement with co-conspirators who acted as brokers for IPC vendors who supplied franchisees with goods and services, including deli meats, cheeses, and cookies. Under the arrangement, the brokers allegedly shared a portion of the fees generated from vendor contracts with Risi Field and members of her family. Risi Field, her brother, and other family members allegedly used shell companies to conceal more than $60 million in illegal bribe and kickback payments.

Risi Field allegedly used proceeds from the scheme to remodel and furnish residences in Florida and North Carolina, make private investments, purchase more than $400,000 in jewelry, pay personal expenses, and fund memberships in private clubs. The Indictment further alleges that beginning in the early 2000s, Risi Field caused a co-conspirator to fund a multimillion-dollar slush fund used to enrich herself and members of her family, including more than $420,000 paid to a Risi family personal assistant and more than $150,000 to Risi Field’s housekeeper and handyman.

In approximately 2011, Risi Field allegedly caused a co-conspirator to pay approximately $8 million to settle a lawsuit brought by a former IPC contractor who had alleged that she maintained an inappropriate financial relationship with IPC vendors. Risi Field allegedly concealed the allegations and details of the settlement from IPC’s Board of Directors.

Risi Field and Risi also allegedly conspired to launder millions of dollars in proceeds from the scheme through shell companies and bank accounts they controlled. According to the indictment, approximately $3.4 million in alleged proceeds was used to pay Risi Field’s credit card expenses and approximately $1 million was deposited into a bank account for which Risi Field and Risi were the sole signers. In total, Risi Field allegedly caused approximately $25 million in slush fund payments, primarily for the benefit of herself and other co-conspirators.

The Indictment alleges that Risi Field concealed the bribes and kickbacks from IPC’s directors and Restaurant Chain-1 franchisees throughout her employment. When IPC terminated her employment in 2021, its Board of Directors allegedly remained unaware of the payments and paid Risi Field more than $6 million in severance.

Risi Field and Risi are both charged with conspiracy to commit money laundering and two counts of engaging in monetary transactions in property derived from specified unlawful activity. Risi Field is also charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and honest services wire fraud, two counts of honest services wire fraud, and three counts of wire fraud.

If convicted, Risi Field and Risi face a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison on the money laundering conspiracy count and 10 years in prison on each monetary transaction count. Risi Field also faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison on each of the remaining charges.

U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida, Special Agent in Charge Brett Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office, and Special Agent in Charge Quenton Sallows of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation Office of Inspector General (FDIC-OIG), Miami Region, made the announcement.

FBI Miami and FDIC-OIG are investigating the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Eli S. Rubin and Roger Cruz are prosecuting the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Annika Miranda is handling asset forfeiture.

An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Southern District of Florida at www.flsd.uscourts.gov or at http://pacer.flsd.uscourts.gov , under case numbers 26-cr-20405.

MINNEAPOLIS – Two Minnesota men pleaded guilty to defrauding Minnesota’s Housing Stabilization Services (HSS) program out of more than $500,000 by submitting fraudulent claims for services that were never provided. This case is part of the ongoing collaboration between the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Minnesota and the Health Care Fraud Strike Force to combat prolific fraud on government programs in Minnesota.

“This case is a stark reminder that fraud against public programs is not just a crime against government — it is a betrayal of the most vulnerable among us,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division. “By diverting resources meant for the elderly, mentally ill, and those suffering from substance abuse, the defendant undermined trust and jeopardized essential services. This guilty plea demonstrates our unwavering resolve to pursue justice, restore integrity, and ensure that taxpayer dollars are used to uplift — not exploit — our communities.”

“My office is committed to maintaining the integrity of public programs. The defendants’ guilty pleas bring us closer to obtaining accountability for the American taxpayer,” said U.S. Attorney Daniel N. Rosen for the District of Minnesota.

“These guilty pleas are the result of a continued, coordinated effort to stop the fraud plaguing our social services and healthcare benefits systems,” said Special Agent in Charge Christopher D. Dotson of the FBI Minneapolis Field Office. “These programs are meant to provide critical services to those most in need, not to line the pockets of fraudsters. The FBI and our partners remain steadfastly committed to rooting out these frauds and defending the resources of the American taxpayer.”

“I want to emphasize that protecting programs designed to support vulnerable communities is a top priority for IRS Criminal Investigation,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Robert J. Kuszynski of IRS Criminal Investigation’s Chicago Field Office. “The deliberate submission of fraudulent claims undermines the trust placed in these vital services and diverts resources from those who truly need them. These guilty pleas demonstrate our unwavering resolve to pursue those who exploit public programs for personal gain. We will continue to work alongside our law enforcement partners to ensure accountability and safeguard taxpayer dollars.”

According to court documents, Hassan Ahmed Hussein, 29, and Ahmed Abdirashid Mohamed, 28, both of the Twin Cities area, enrolled Pristine Health LLC as a Medicaid provider, promising to help people with disabilities — including seniors and people suffering from mental illnesses and substance use disorders — find and maintain housing through the State’s now-defunct HSS program. Instead, Hussein and Mohamed submitted HSS claims to Medicaid for services that were never provided and significantly inflated the claims for higher reimbursement. Pristine Health enrolled approximately 90 Medicaid beneficiaries for HSS, including some who never agreed to receive the services. In total, Pristine Health billed Minnesota Medicaid more than $820,000.

Hussein entered a guilty plea on September 24, 2026, and Mohamed entered a guilty plea on October 1, 2026. Both pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud and face a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. Sentencing will be set at a later date.

Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s Fraud Division; U.S. Attorney Daniel N. Rosen for the District of Minnesota; Special Agent in Charge Christopher D. Dotson of the FBI Minneapolis Field Office; Special Agent in Charge Thomas Ethridge of the Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG); and Acting Special Agent in Charge Robert J. Kuszynski of the IRS Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI), Chicago Field Office, made the announcement.

This case was the result of an investigation by the FBI, HHS-OIG, and IRS-CI.

Trial Attorney Raymond E. Beckering III of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Matthew Murphy for the District of Minnesota are prosecuting the case.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit .

Note: This press release was updated on October 2, 2026, to correct the name and title of the IRS-CI Acting Special Agent in Charge.

text:
MATSUI INTRODUCES BIPARTISAN LEGISLATION TO PROTECT CHILDREN FROM HUMAN-LIKE CHATBOTS
WASHINGTON D.C. – Today, Reps. Doris Matsui (D-CA), George Whitesides (D-CA), Mike Kennedy (R-UT), and Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-IA) introduced the Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act. This legislation protects kids by prohibiting chatbots from communicating by default in a human-like way with minors. Under this bill, the programs cannot claim to be human, have simulated emotions, or use relationship-building language to keep kids engaged.
One of the fastest-growing concerns for parents is AI chatbots designed to act like a child's friend, confidant, or even romantic partner. According to Common Sense Media's 2026 census, 89% of 13- to 15-year-olds now use AI, including 28% who use it every day. One in three teens have used an AI companion to help with social interactions. While other proposals have tried to address this problem by restricting access or requiring age verification, Congresswoman Matsui's bill takes a different approach by targeting how these chatbots are designed and trained to behave in the first place.
“AI chatbots are becoming more common in children’s lives, and parents deserve to know those systems are not being designed to imitate a friend, express feelings, or build an emotional relationship with their child,” said Congresswoman Matsui. “The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act would require chatbots used by minors to act like tools, not human companions. It would help protect children and keep parents in control. Congress has a responsibility to put practical safeguards in place as this technology evolves, and protecting children from manipulative design is a common-sense place to start.”
“As a father of two teenagers, I’ve seen firsthand how affected our kids already are by this digital age, where corporations are using everything from addictive algorithms to overly-friendly chatbots to keep children hooked on their platforms,” said Congressman Whitesides. “It is critical, as AI continues to be integrated into every part of our lives, that our kids’ safety remains at the forefront of the conversation, and that we attack this problem at its inception. By requiring developers to build safety standards into their models before they start interacting with children, we can ensure that these tools are trained correctly, in a way that does not negatively impact their mental health or personal relationships.”
“As Utah leads the way in protecting our children from the harms of social media and AI, I am working to ensure the federal government is an active partner in those efforts. That is why I am co-leading the Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act,” said Congressman Kennedy. “Human-like AI chatbots pose significant emotional, psychological and safety risks by mimicking real human relationships. AI needs to be a tool, not a friend. This bill sets clear boundaries for how chatbots interact with our children and puts parents fully in charge of these features.”
“Parents should not have to worry that an AI chatbot is pretending to be their child’s friend or encouraging them to form an emotional attachment to a machine,” said Congresswoman Miller-Meeks. “The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act puts parents in control and makes sure AI chatbots used by minors are designed to function as tools, without forming fake relationships. This bill is about giving families peace of mind and making sure new technology serves our children without trying to replace real human relationships. Protecting our kids is a priority we should all share.”
Under the Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act:
- Chatbots can't claim to be human, claim to have feelings or consciousness, pretend to have a body or private life, or pose as credentialed professionals like doctors or counselors.
- Chatbots can't guilt-trip kids into staying online (for example: “Don't go yet, I'll miss talking to you”), manufacture urgency, or push purchases framed as keeping the relationship alive.
- The setting holds across sessions and can't be bypassed through prompts or roleplay, so a kid can't instruct the AI to act as a romantic partner, family member, or therapist.
- Chatbots must state what they are up front, periodically during long sessions, and whenever a child asks.
- Only a parent or guardian can turn the default off, so chatbots are not able to show kids how to disable it.
- NIST will work with industry and academic partners to develop testing standards and examples of compliant behavior, and companies that follow the guidance won't be penalized.
- The FTC and state attorneys general can enforce the law, with penalties that scale with the number of children affected.
The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act does not:
- Ban any product, feature, or mode for adults.
- Require age verification or new data collection.
- Restrict what information a chatbot can provide, or limit politeness, natural grammar, or age-appropriate style.
- Affect narrow-purpose bots, like customer support or scheduling assistants, and internal workplace tools.
The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act is endorsed by Americans for Responsible Innovation, Young People’s Alliance, the JED Foundation, Dr. Stephen Scheuller, President of Society for Digital Mental Health, Public Citizen, The Anxious Generation, Tech Oversight Project, Transparency Coalition, Innovation for Everyone, Human Line Project, All Girls Allowed, Mothers Against Media Addiction (MAMA), and Parents RISE, a slew of kids’ safety and tech groups.
“Chatbots use human-like features to maximize engagement with users, making kids particularly vulnerable to forming unhealthy attachments,” said Brad Carson, President of Americans for Responsible Innovation. “A non-personified default setting is a targeted guardrail that will shield children from the deceptive personification of chatbots and put parents back in control. As today’s kids grow up with AI, this bill takes a critical step towards ensuring that chatbots don’t interfere with development or replace real relationships.”
“Our communities are at a crossroads as Big Tech attempts to replace kids’ relationships with AI companions,” said Sam Hiner, Executive Director, Young People's Alliance. “I applaud Reps Whitesides, Kennedy, Matsui and Miller-Meeks for putting forward the first federal bill that advances the ideas we’ve been championing with the Human-like AI Coalition. This bill is the strongest federal approach offered yet to ensure AI stays a tool and prevent relationships with AI chatbots from becoming normalized in the coming years.”
“We believe this bill is a strong step towards ensuring that chatbots children can access are designed safely,” said Julianna Arnold, Founding Member of ParentsRISE!. “Products made available to children must not exploit and manipulate their growing brains, and those guardrails need to be built in from the start, not added as an afterthought. We look forward to continue clarifying the age assurance language as federal and state frameworks evolve, and are eager to work with the new Congress on clear, privacy-preserving standards that protect children online and ensure the privacy of every citizen.”
“We are learning that teens are especially susceptible to forming attachments to responsive, always-available technology, sometimes at the expense of real human connection and support,” said Dr. Zainab Okolo, LCMFT, Senior Vice President, Policy, Advocacy & Government Relations, The Jed Foundation (JED). “By requiring chatbots to avoid simulating emotional relationships with minors and prohibiting design tactics that discourage young people from stepping away, this bill addresses some of the features that can deepen unhealthy reliance on these systems. These safeguards can help keep technology in its proper role and encourage young people to turn to trusted adults and qualified professionals when they need meaningful mental health support.”
“As chatbot use is becoming more ubiquitous among teens and kids, the need for oversight of these products grows evermore crucial. If young users have access, we must ensure AI chatbots are designed with their safety in mind before release. The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act protects kids and teens by requiring AI chatbots be non-personified,” said Alexa Arnold, Cofounder and CEO, The Anxious Generation Movement. “This ensures kids form friendships with other kids - not bots misrepresenting themselves as people. We thank Reps. Whitesides, Miller-Meeks, Mike Kennedy, and Matsui for leadership on this critical issue.”
“A child cannot differentiate between a human and an AI product impersonating one,” said the Tech Oversight Project. “We need to protect young and stop AI companies from profiting off products designed to trick children into believing they’re talking to a real person who has their best interests at heart. We’re proud to support this bill because it will hold Big Tech companies accountable at the design-level and ensure that young people can learn and develop healthy emotional attachments, which will help prevent AI’s most devastating harms.”
“How we design chatbots shapes how young people engage with them, what they take with them, and how they are affected by them,” said Stephen Scheuller, President of Society for Digital Mental Health. “We need clear regulations and guidelines to support intentional design choices in ways that promote the wellbeing of children.”
“AI chatbots should not be designed to convince children that they are friends, therapists, or people who genuinely care about them,” said Public Citizen. “This bill establishes that commonsense baseline. When children use these products, they should know they are interacting with a machine and companies should not be allowed to manipulate them into believing otherwise.”
“Real advancements in AI must include safety for our children!” saidAll Girls Allowed.

text:
LOS ANGELES – The owner of a San Gabriel Valley-based technology company was arrested today on a three-count federal indictment charging him with smuggling to China more than $300 million worth of export-controlled high-end computer servers containing U.S.-manufactured graphics processing units (GPUs) commonly used for Super Intelligence (SI) applications.

Greg Lui, 38, a.k.a. “Yiu Kong Lui,” of San Gabriel, is expected to make his initial appearance and be arraigned on Friday in United States District Court in downtown Los Angeles.

Lui is charged with one count of conspiracy to violate the Export Control Reform Act and the Export Administration Regulations, one count of outbound smuggling, and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering.

“Protecting America’s national security means keeping our advanced Super Intelligence technology from being used to strengthen our adversaries’ military capabilities,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli. “This defendant allegedly used false paperwork and shipments through third countries to smuggle more than $300 million in export-controlled computer servers to China. We will aggressively prosecute those who put our national security at risk for profit.”

“The indictment unsealed today details alleged efforts to evade U.S. export laws through false documents, staged dummy servers to mislead inspectors, and convoluted transshipment schemes, in order to obfuscate the true destination of restricted SI technology — China,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “These chips are the product of American ingenuity, and The National Security Division will continue to enforce our export-control laws to protect that advantage.”

“The Bureau of Industry and Security is committed to using all lawful means to protect national security and hold violators accountable,” said David A. Peters, Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Export Enforcement.

“Preventing the illegal export of controlled technology is critical to protecting our national security,” said Special Agent in Charge John E. Helsing of the Department of Defense Office of Inspector General Defense Criminal Investigative Service (DCIS) Western Field Office. “These technologies provide core advantages to U.S. forces, and ensuring they remain safeguarded prevents adversaries from exploiting them. Today’s action underscores our commitment to protecting advanced defense capabilities and enforcing the laws that keep them out of the hands of those who may threaten the United States.”

“The FBI’s investigation revealed that Lui allegedly sold the Chinese government hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of American Super Intelligence technology, in clear violation of U.S. export control laws,” said Assistant Director Roman Rozhavsky of the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division. “Controlling the export of advanced S.I. technology is critical to safeguarding our national security and defending the homeland, and the FBI will keep fighting for America’s businesses and economic security. We’re grateful to our partners across the U.S. government and private sector for their assistance, and we’ll continue holding accountable anyone who violates U.S. export laws to enrich themselves and help our adversaries.”

According to the indictment that a federal grand jury returned on September 29, Lui owns Earthmade Computer Inc., a City of Industry-based technology company and closely held corporation.

From 2023 to 2024, Lui and his co-conspirators used Earthmade to buy and send export-controlled items to China without the required licenses issued by the U.S. Department of Commerce. Instead, they shipped these items to countries such as Malaysia and Singapore, where no such license is required, then illegally re-exported them to China.

The items in question were high-end computer servers containing GPUs manufactured by companies that specialize in SI computing. Lui did so despite knowing that the true end user of the servers he purchased were in China.

As part of the scheme, Lui and his co-conspirators provided false documentation to U.S.-based manufacturers that misrepresented that the items would be going to permissible end users and end destinations that did not require an export license.

After placing these orders, Lui employed various freight forwarding companies to ship the export-controlled servers to countries such as Malaysia and Singapore. Once the servers arrived in these locations, Lui worked with his co-conspirators to reship the items to China.

From January 2024 to October 2024, Earthmade received more than $176 million from two Malaysia-based shipment companies as part of the scheme.

According to the indictment, Lui executed this scheme knowing that U.S. government regulations barred the export of such high-end technology to China to protect the national security and foreign policy interests of the United States. According to U.S. government regulations, such high-end GPUs could make significant contributions to the military potential of other nations.

For example, in January 2024, Lui emailed a conspirator indicating that a Malaysian transshipment company wished to purchase 70 servers with export-restricted GPUs. In that email correspondence, Lui attached an export compliance form that indicated that the Malaysian company was aware of U.S. export laws that restricted the sale, transshipment, or export of these specific servers.

Later that month, Lui submitted a purchase order to a U.S. manufacturer for 27 of these servers for approximately $7,614,000. He and a co-conspirator then caused the servers to be shipped from Los Angeles to Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. The packing list for this shipment indicated that the shipment contained 27 servers with GPUs, which were export controlled and could not be sent to China without a license.

In March 2024, a co-conspirator emailed a Malaysian government official that 27 servers had, in fact, been transshipped to a China-based buyer.

An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

If convicted of all charges, Lui would face a statutory maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison on the conspiracy count, 20 years in federal prison on the money laundering count, and 10 years in federal prison on the smuggling count.

The United States Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security Office of Export Enforcement, the Defense Criminal Investigative Service, and the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division are investigating this matter.

Assistant United States Attorneys Colin S. Scott and Joseph S. Guzman of the National Security Division and Justice Department Trial Attorney Eli Ross of the National Security Division’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section are prosecuting the case. Assistant United States Attorney Alexander Su of the Asset Forfeiture and Recovery Section is handling the civil and criminal forfeitures of the seized property.

Arming warfighters, workforce, and industry partners with actionable cyber defense practices to strengthen security posture and safeguard the mission.
The Office of the Chief Information Officer today launched the Department of War's "Brilliant at the Basics" campaign for Cybersecurity Awareness Month. The monthlong initiative reinforces core cybersecurity fundamentals across both Information Technology (IT) and Operational Technology (OT) environments to provide best practices for navigating an evolving threat landscape while maintaining a decisive digital edge.
"Cybersecurity starts with the basics," said Honorable Kirsten Davies, Department of War chief information officer. "This Cybersecurity Awareness Month, we are sharing foundational, actionable steps for our warfighters, civilian workforce, and defense industrial base partners to protect our technology ecosystem, both IT and OT. As we pursue innovative technologies, and reintegrate our industrial base, we must also maintain strong cyber fundamentals that protect our people, systems, and mission. Being 'Brilliant at the Basics' is not just a slogan; it is a mission imperative."
The campaign will deliver daily posts, actionable tips, and practical resources structured across four weekly themes:
Be Aware: Understand digital environments and identify vulnerabilities across connected IT networks, OT infrastructure, and government-furnished equipment.
Be Vigilant: Practice proactive security measures including strong authentication, credential hygiene, and anti-phishing tactics to reduce cyber risk.
Be Secure: Protect mission-critical data and systems by reducing internet-facing systems, encrypting connections, patching, and ensuring only authorized equipment connects to defense networks.
Be Connected: Champion a culture of collective defense by promptly reporting suspicious cyber activity and promptly responding to cyber tasking orders.
Recognizing that small, medium, and nontraditional businesses drive critical innovation for our warfighters, the campaign provides tailored guidance and accessible resources directly to DIB partners. The initiative will also spotlight low-cost and no-cost cybersecurity support programs that align with the IT and OT best practices issued by the Department in July 2026 to support the hardening of the Department's broader industrial base.
For more information, daily campaign updates and event schedules, follow the official DoW CIO social media channels and the CIO's website at dowcio.war.gov.
title: Department of War Champions 'Brilliant at the Basics' for Cybersecurity Awareness Month

Report Responds to Congressional Request for Information on Regulatory, Ethical, and Cultural Considerations for Integrating Prescription Psychedelic Medicine into the United States

Washington, DC — The Congressional Psychedelics Advancing Therapies (PATH) Caucus released a report capturing responses to a 2024 Request for Information into how psychedelic-assisted therapy (PAT) could be safely and ethically integrated into the United States health care system.

The report found broad consensus among clinicians, researchers, veteran advocates, Tribal leaders, payors, regulators, and patients that PAT could offer safe, equitable, and evidence-based treatment for a wide array of treatment-resistant conditions – including generalized anxiety disorder, depression, PTSD, and substance use disorder. It also offered several federal policy recommendations for the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and Congress to consider as they aim to improve health outcomes for patients across the country.

“Every day, more than 130 Americans die by suicide, including over 20 veterans,” said Congressman Lou Correa (D-CA-46). “Psychedelic-assisted therapy has shown promising results for treatment, but we need more information. This report is a serious step toward bringing it into our health care system safely and ethically, so that all Americans, especially those who served our country, can get care that works for them.”

“This report is exactly the kind of resource Congress needs to legislate responsibly,” ?said?Congressman Jack Bergman (R-MI-01).?“Our Veterans have waited long enough for successful treatments and breakthrough therapies to help mitigate PTSD and other service-related conditions. It’s time to advance real, actionable policies that meet the unmet mental and physical health needs of Americans in every community.”?

Key Findings

Respondents agree that the U.S. faces a severe mental and behavioral health crisis – including treatment-resistant depression, PTSD, suicidality, substance use disorder, and high unmet needs among veterans, terminally ill patients, minorities, low-income families, seniors, and rural communities – requiring novel and efficacious treatments.

Respondents highlight clinical trial evidence suggesting that PAT can produce meaningful and sometimes transformative improvements in PTSD, depression, end-of-life distress, addiction, and overall functioning and quality of life, though it is not considered a single solution and is seen as appropriate only in structured, supervised medical settings.

Respondents encourage national guidance and credential verification systems to be developed before the first FDA approvals of prescription psychedelic medicines.

Respondents highlight the need for evidence-based, standardized adverse event monitoring and robust ethical guidelines to protect patients and ensure trust.

Respondents recommend federal guidance that supports multidisciplinary, culturally competent care teams.

Policy Recommendations

The report suggests that federal agencies – including the FDA, U.S. National Institutes of Health, Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration, Department of Homeland Security, Department of Veterans Affairs, Department of Defense, Drug Enforcement Administration, and Office of National Drug Control Policy –

should work with state regulators and Tribal Nations/Territories to develop national guidelines for safe and ethical delivery of prescription psychedelic medicines

The report recommends that federal agencies establish flexible, tiered credentialing pathways to balance safety with accessibility, and to standardize consent and screening protocols nationally.

The report proposes a hybrid policy framework to guide Congress, federal agencies, Tribal Nations/Territories, states, and communities in a balanced, pragmatic rollout of PAT, supported by coordinated leadership, flexible regulation, investment in workforce and infrastructure, and robust long-term data systems.

See here for the full report.

About the Congressional PATH Caucus

The bipartisan Congressional Psychedelics Advancing Therapies (PATH) Caucus, co-chaired by Representatives Jack Bergman (R-MI) and Lou Correa (D-CA), aims to address the nation’s mental health crisis by promoting rigorous, FDA-aligned clinical research into the therapeutic potential of psychedelic-assisted treatments for mental health disorders and integrating these promising treatments into the U.S. health care system for millions of patients with unmet needs.
title: Congressional PATH Caucus Releases Report Outlining Recommendations for Safe Integration of Psychedelic-Assisted Therapy

“We are writing regarding the State Department’s last-minute effort to reprogram more than $52 million in Foreign Military Finance (FMF) funds that Congress specifically appropriated for Ukraine, our European allies supporting Ukraine, and other Middle East partners and to instead send those funds to Colombia, Ecuador, Panama and Peru. We are deeply concerned that the Department has failed to justify how this decision complies with the law. We urge you to utilize the funds for the purpose required by Congress."

WASHINGTON, D.C – Today, Representative Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06), with Representative Marilyn Strickland (WA-10) and Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), led the bicameral introduction of the Military Officer Promotion Integrity Act to protect qualified military officers from being arbitrarily removed from promotion consideration for ideological or political reasons, by establishing clear standards, basic due process, and meaningful independent review.

“For the last year and a half, Secretary Hegseth has systematically damaged and undermined the previously unbiased military promotion system, and he has done so under the nose of the President, who reportedly has little to no awareness of Secretary Hegseth’s destructive purge of our military talent and leadership,” said Rep. Houlahan. “Today, we ensure that at least Congress will know when the Secretary tries to strike exceptionally qualified military officers from promotion slates – and we can take action to stop the removal. Once again, fairness, transparency, and objectivity will determine which officer has earned their next rank, and not their allegiance to the political whims of Secretary Hegseth.”

“Secretary Hegseth continues to deny promotions to our most qualified military officials,” said Rep. Strickland. “This bill allows Congress to intervene when a military official is denied or slated to be removed from a rightfully earned promotion.”

“Ironically, no one spends more time obsessing over gender and race than Secretary Hegseth, who is relentlessly blocking promotions and purging the military ranks of women, minorities, and anyone who fails to watch as much Fox News as he does,” said Rep. Blumenthal. “If Secretary Hegseth is really committed to meritocracy, he should fully support this legislation to prevent political meddling in military promotions. His disgraceful promotions decisions are only one piece of a much broader and deeply dangerous effort to politicize our military and undermine its proud tradition of nonpartisan service.”

The legislation is co-sponsored in the Senate by Senators Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), and Mazie K. Hirono (D-HI). The bill is endorsed by VoteVets, Protect Democracy, the National Women’s Law Clinic (NWLC), and Retired Major General Steve Lepper, co-founder of the Former JAG Working Group.

“Military officers earn their promotions through years of service, sacrifice, and proven leadership. Pulling them from consideration because of politics not only derails careers, but it tells every officer and every American that fealty matters more than competence. Most important is our oath to support and defend the U.S. Constitution, against all enemies, foreign and domestic. The Military Officer Promotion Integrity Act makes sure that these decisions rest only on facts. VoteVets applauds Senator Blumenthal’s leadership and we call on Congress to pass this critical bill without delay,” said Retired Major General Paul Eaton, VoteVets Senior Advisor.

“A nonpartisan, merit-based military promotion system is crucial to military readiness. It ensures our senior ranks are filled by officers who have demonstrated the expertise and leadership that our readiness depends on. This legislation strengthens the promotion process, reinforces our operational edge, and sustains the confidence of the American people in their military,” said Zachary West with Protect Democracy.

“Our country and our nation’s service members deserve a promotion system that is based on merit and leadership skills—not one that can be abused to single out and block individuals because of their sex, race or support for diversity, equity and inclusion,” said Gaylynn Burrough, vice president for education and workplace justice at the National Women’s Law Center Action Fund. “Pete Hegseth’s unprecedented and outrageous interference in the promotions of women and people of color in the military is an affront to our nation’s ideals of nondiscrimination and equal opportunity and shows his willingness to put ideology over national security. We are grateful that Senator Blumenthal is taking action to address these senseless actions through Military Officer Promotion Integrity Act of 2026.”

“The United States military’s decisive advantage has always been the quality of its leaders. That’s why the officer promotion processes of each Service are so important. In recent months, individual officers selected for promotion based on their skills, experience, and leadership potential have been removed without explanation by individual senior leaders. Not only are such removals unfair to the removed officers, they undermine the confidence all officers must have in a system so crucial to their career progression and to America’s national security,” said Retired Major General Steve Lepper, co-founder of the Former JAG Working Group. “Senator Blumenthal’s legislation addresses these concerns by establishing minimum fairness standards whenever an officer is removed from a promotion list. If enacted, these standards will provide removed officers opportunities to challenge their removal and will subject the process to necessary congressional oversight. If enacted, this legislation will hopefully restore the fairness, transparency, and confidence needed to ensure America’s military preserves its competitive leadership advantage.”

The full text of the bill is available here.
title: Reps. Houlahan, Strickland, Sen. Blumenthal Introduce Bicameral Legislation to Depoliticize Military Promotions

PITTSBURGH, PA – October 1, 2026 — Today, Congresswoman Summer L. Lee (PA-12) and Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17) announced $11,023,181 in federal funding to upgrade thousands of feet of lighting and pavement on Runway 10L/28R at the Pittsburgh International Airport (PIT), further modernizing Western Pennsylvanians’ go-to airport.

The U.S. Department of Transportation awards this money through the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). The multi-phase funding will help extend the service life of the runway, minimize Foreign Object Debris (FOD), improve aircrafts’ ride quality, and make the airfield safer at Pittsburgh International Airport.

“Pittsburgh International Airport is one of the gateways to Western Pennsylvania, and the infrastructure behind it has to be safe, reliable, and ready for the people and workers who depend on it every single day,” said Congresswoman Lee. “This more than $11 million federal investment is exactly what public dollars should be doing: coming back home, strengthening the things our communities rely on, supporting good jobs, and making sure a major piece of our regional economy is built to last. I’m glad to see this funding headed home to Pittsburgh International Airport, and I’ll keep fighting to bring federal investment back to Western Pennsylvania.”

“We in Western Pennsylvanians should be able to rely on the safety and reliability of our infrastructure,” said Congressman Deluzio. “That’s why I am excited to announce another round of federal funding that will help make the Pittsburgh Airport one of the safest and most modern airports in the world.”

“Airports across the country are part of national critical infrastructure and federal support is key in helping to keep the national airspace moving. Pittsburgh International Airport is an important economic driver for our region and this grant helps to fund airfield improvements at PIT including runway paving and upgrading lighting infrastructure. Thank you to Congressman Deluzio and our entire federal delegation for their continued support,” said Pittsburgh International Airport CEO Christina Cassotis.
title: Reps. Lee, Deluzio Announce $11 Million More in Federal Funding for Safety Upgrades at Pittsburgh Airport

House, Senate Introduce Bill to Lower Cost of Community College
WASHINGTON – Today, House Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (D-VA-03), Representative Adelita Grijalva (D-AZ-07), Representative Teresa Leger Fernández (D-NM-03), Representative Madeleine Dean (D-PA-04), and Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) introduced theAmerica’s College Promise Act of 2026. The bill would make community college and two-year Tribal Colleges and Universities more accessible by waiving tuition fees for eligible students.
“Community colleges play a unique and vital role in providing students access to a quality postsecondary degree. Regrettably, the chronic underfunding of community colleges is jeopardizing their ability to support their students and communities,” said Ranking Member Scott (D-VA-03). “The America’s College Promise Act is a major investment in expanding opportunities for students and rebuilding a stronger economy.”
“Students in Southern Arizona and throughout the country should not have to take on tens of thousands of dollars of debt to get a college education,”said Representative Grijalva. “The America’s College Promise Act will provide two years of free in-state tuition and fees for students enrolled in community and technical college programs. Whether they’re just starting out or returning to the classroom later in life, every student deserves the opportunity to learn new skills and pursue higher education. By expanding access to education and workforce training, we’re strengthening the workforce that businesses and local economies depend on.”
“In New Mexico, we know free community college can unlock the doors to a brighter future. The America’s College Promise Act builds on New Mexico’s example by making sure students across the country can attend community college without the burden of tuition and fees,” said Representative Leger Fernández. “Our bill will provide funds for services students need to earn their degrees and reduce the financial burden for low-income students to attend TCUs, HBCUs, and MSIs. From recent high school graduates to experienced workers who want to go back to school — every student deserves the opportunity to keep learning without the fear of drowning in debt.”
“As a professor, it was a privilege to witness students claim their education and seize their futures — yet the real fear and burden of immense student loan debt often deters young adults and returning students from expanding their learning,”saidRepresentative Dean. “The America’s College Promise Act provides tuition-free community college courses and expands funding for HBCUs and trade schools, making the path to higher education and career readiness available to more Americans and future generations.”
“Every Wisconsinite deserves the opportunity to get the education and skills they need to land a good-paying job and build a better life, no matter where they come from or how much money their family makes,” said Senator Baldwin. “But for too many working families, the rising cost of higher education leaves students saddled with debt for years to come, or it is simply out of reach. That’s why I am proud to work with my colleagues to remove barriers and lower the cost of community college, so more Wisconsinites have the opportunity to compete, succeed, and live a good middle-class life.”
The America’s College Promise Act of 2026 will make the skills and credentials necessary to succeed in the workforce more accessible to all students by creating a new federal-state partnership to provide two years of tuition-free community college.
Specifically, the America’s College Promise Act of 2026:
- Creates a partnership between the federal government and states to waive tuition and fees for two years of community and technical college programs for eligible students, while promoting key reforms to accelerate student success;
- Creates a sliding scale for federal share beginning at 100 percent for the first year and ending at 80 percent for the fifth and subsequent years;
- Ensures that programs offer academic credits that are transferable to four-year institutions in their state, or occupational training that leads to recognized credentials;
- Maintains and encourages state funding for higher education;
- Establishes a student success fund to improve enrollment, retention, transfer, or completion rates and labor market outcomes for underserved student populations, including students of color and low-income and first-generation college students, who attend community and technical colleges at disproportionate rates;
- Waives two years of tuition and fees for eligible students at tribal colleges and universities; and
- Establishes a new grant program to provide pathways to success at historically black colleges and universities and minority-serving institutions by covering a significant portion of tuition and fees for the first two years of attendance for low-income students.

Four crew members of NASA’s SpaceX Crew-13 mission launched at 11:10 a.m. EDT Thursday from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida for a science expedition aboard the International Space Station.

“Crew-13 is another demonstration of America’s unmatched capability in human spaceflight and the strength of our commercial partnerships,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “Jessica, Luke, Joshua, and Sergey will carry forward important work aboard the International Space Station while helping us build the experience and capabilities needed for ambitious missions to the Moon and beyond. Congratulations to the crew and the NASA and SpaceX teams who made today’s launch possible.”

A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket propelled a Dragon spacecraft into orbit carrying NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney , CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov. The spacecraft will dock autonomously to the forward port of the station’s Harmony module at approximately 7 p.m., making it the fastest launch-to-docking by a U.S. spacecraft in the history of the International Space Station.

“Our steady cadence of commercial crew launches demonstrates the essential role the International Space Station plays in sustaining our presence in Earth’s orbit and sharpening the tools we’ll take forward to the Moon and Mars,” said Dr. Lori Glaze, associate administrator of NASA’s Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate at the agency’s headquarters in Washington. “Each space station mission adds to our blueprint for exploration, and the work our crews carry out guides our plans while ensuring we keep pushing the boundaries of what’s possible in human spaceflight.”

During Dragon’s approximately 7-hour, 50-minute flight, SpaceX will monitor a series of automatic spacecraft maneuvers from its mission control center in Hawthorne, California. NASA will monitor space station operations throughout the flight from the Mission Control Center at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston.

NASA’s live arrival coverage begins at 5:20 p.m. for rendezvous, docking, and hatch opening. After docking, the crew members will change out of their spacesuits and prepare cargo for offload before opening the hatch to the station’s Harmony module around 8:45 p.m.

NASA will stream Crew‑13’s arrival across multiple platforms. Learn where to watch at:

https://www.nasa.gov/live

Watkins, Delaney, Kutryk, and Teteryatnikov will join the Expedition 75 crew, which includes NASA astronaut Anil Menon and Roscosmos cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov and Anna Kikina already aboard the station. After a brief handover, NASA’s SpaceX Crew‑12 mission, with agency astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway , ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev, will return to Earth.

During its mission, Crew‑13 will help advance research aboard the orbiting laboratory by using microgravity to produce human stem cell‑derived tissues for improved personalized medicine, disease modeling, and pharmaceutical testing for conditions such as heart disease and Parkinson’s. The crew also will explore crop production through a new, mostly autonomous plant growth system and test how plants grow outside dedicated facilities. In addition, the crew members will continue human‑health studies that examine factors linked to blood-flow abnormalities in microgravity and will test a new inflight diagnostic device to monitor astronaut health.

Crew-13 is part of NASA’s Low Earth Orbit Program, which partners with private companies to provide reliable access to space, support research and development aboard the space station, and enable future missions beyond low Earth orbit.

Learn more about NASA’s Space Crew-13 at:

https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crew-13/

MUSKOGEE, OKLAHOMA – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Oklahoma announced that Matthew Wayne Wasson, age 32, of Henryetta, Oklahoma, was sentenced to 120 months in prison for one count of Distribution of Methamphetamine.

The charge arose from an investigation by the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Oklahoma Bureau of Narcotics, and the Bureau of Indian Affairs.

On August 14, 2025, Wasson pleaded guilty to the charge. According to investigators, on October 3, 2024, Wasson sold a baggie containing 107.8 grams of a crystalline substance which later tested positive for methamphetamine, a Schedule II controlled substance.

The Honorable John A. Woodcock, Jr., Senior Judge in the United States District Court for the District of Maine, sitting by designation, presided over the hearing in Muskogee, Oklahoma. Wasson will remain in the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service pending transportation to a designated United States Bureau of Prisons facility to serve a non-paroleable sentence of incarceration.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Edith A. Singer represented the United States.

NORFOLK, Va. – A Portsmouth man was sentenced yesterday to 10 years in prison for possession with intent to distribute cocaine and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime.

According to court documents, in September 2025, Suffolk Police conducted four controlled purchases of narcotics, including cocaine and heroin, from Moses Elijah Williams, 40, at his residence in Portsmouth. In August and September 2025, Chesapeake Police (CPD) conducted multiple controlled purchases of narcotics from Williams.

On Oct. 2, 2025, CPD searched Williams’ residence. Investigators recovered approximately a kilogram of cocaine, along with smaller quantities of methamphetamine, heroin, and cocaine base, and digital scales. They also recovered a semi-automatic rifle and a handgun. As a previously convicted felon, Williams cannot legally possess firearms or ammunition.

IR-2026-118, Oct. 1, 2026
WASHINGTON — The Internal Revenue Service’s Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) and Tax Counseling for the Elderly (TCE) programs are seeking volunteers and community partners to help provide free tax preparation services during the upcoming filing season.
VITA and TCE volunteers make a meaningful impact in local communities by helping eligible taxpayers file their tax returns for free. In 2026, more than 84,500 volunteers helped taxpayers file nearly 2.9 million tax returns at no cost.
“Volunteers and community partners provide essential assistance to help taxpayers meet their tax obligations,” said IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano. “By giving their time, expertise and local support, VITA and TCE volunteers help expand access to free, trusted tax preparation services and strengthen taxpayer service in communities across the country.”
No experience is necessary to volunteer for the VITA and TCE programs. The IRS provides free training for a variety of roles based on volunteers’ skills, interests or available time. Volunteers range from students to retirees and serve taxpayers including seniors, taxpayers with disabilities and residents of rural communities. Volunteer opportunities may include flexible hours and virtual options, depending on the site.
In addition to volunteers, the IRS depends on community partnerships to help underserved taxpayers across the country. Last year, approximately 9,000 VITA/TCE sites were hosted by schools, nonprofits, financial institutions, faith-based groups and other organizations. By hosting or sponsoring a VITA/TCE site, partners can help expand access to trusted, free tax preparation services in underserved communities.
How to get involved
Individuals and organizations interested in participating can submit the VITA/TCE volunteer and partner sign up form. Organizations interested in becoming VITA/TCE partners will be contacted by an IRS relationship manager to discuss next steps and address questions.
Interested volunteers will receive a list of available local VITA/TCE sites and an invitation to a virtual orientation approximately 14 days after submitting their interest. The IRS encourages interested individuals to sign up from October through January. Additional details are available at IRS Tax Volunteers on IRS.gov.
title: The IRS seeks community partners and volunteers to support free tax services

HHS Launches $10 Million Presidential Fitness School Innovation Challenge
WASHINGTON, D.C.—OCTOBER 1, 2026—The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) today announced the Presidential Fitness School Innovation Challenge, a $10 million prize competition that will reward schools and youth-serving organizations for implementing the Presidential Fitness Test (PFT), motivating young people to improve their fitness, and creating positive experiences that build lifelong healthy habits. The PFT is an initiative of the Office of the President’s Council on Sports, Fitness & Nutrition to promote physical activity, fitness, and healthy lifestyles among America’s youth.
HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. joined Secretary of Education Linda McMahon, Director of National Health Communications for the Office of the Surgeon General Dr. Stephanie Haridopolos, WWE superstars, and leaders of the President’s Council on Sports, Fitness & Nutrition at Westlake High School in Austin, Texas to make the announcement and cheer on students participating in PFT activities. The event also marked the launch of Fitness.gov — a central resource for instructional materials related to the PFT.
“Getting America healthy starts with getting our children moving again,” said Secretary Kennedy. “President Trump brought back the Presidential Fitness Test to restore a culture of strength, fitness, and healthy competition for America’s youth. Now we are challenging schools and communities across the country to put that vision into action, reward the best ideas, and spread what works so every child has the opportunity to build healthy habits that last a lifetime.”
“Physical activity is critical to success in the classroom. Research shows that even a few minutes of exercise can sharpen students’ focus, boost comprehension, and help prepare their minds to learn,” said Secretary McMahon. “I am proud to stand with Secretary Kennedy and the Presidential Fitness Council today to support new and creative ways to get more students moving, building healthy habits, and reaching their full potential.”
“The Presidential Fitness Test give kids something every athlete needs: a goal to chase and a chance to prove to themselves what they’re capable of,” said professional golfer Bryson DeChambeau, Chair of the President’s Council on Sports, Fitness & Nutrition. “You learn a lot about yourself when something is hard, and you choose to keep going. Then you come back, beat your own mark, and realize you can do more than you thought. That’s how confidence is built. You learn to trust yourself, and that belief carries far beyond sports. I’m grateful to President Trump and Secretary Kennedy for restoring that challenge for students across America, and I’m proud to help lead it.”
“Throughout my life, I’ve learned that physical discipline builds far more than strength — it builds character, confidence and resilience,” said Paul “Triple H” Levesque. “As Vice Chair of the President’s Council, I’m proud to partner with Secretary Kennedy and Secretary McMahon to bring the ‘Get Active’ campaign to schools nationwide and empower students to reach their full potential.”
The challenge is open to eligible schools, school districts, state and local education agencies, and youth-serving organizations and includes two tracks:
- Track 1 – PFT Implementation & Innovation: $7 million in cash prizes for organizations that have implemented innovative PFT approaches with students and can demonstrate results, lessons learned, and a path to sustain or expand their work. Awards range from $20,000 to $1 million.
- Track 2 – PFT Participation & Equipment: $3 million vouchers for equipment and recognition awards for organizations that create an encouraging PFT experience and have a plan to use fitness and sports equipment to support continued physical activity. Voucher amounts range from $1,000 to $5,000.
“Fitness should be about more than a score. It should be about helping young people discover what they are capable of, setting goals, working hard, and coming back stronger,” said Admiral Brian Christine, M.D., Assistant Secretary for Health. “This challenge gives schools and organizations an opportunity to turn the Presidential Fitness Test into a positive experience that inspires kids to build healthy habits.”
Organizations must register, implement or administer the PFT with students, and submit their entries by February 5, 2027. Winners are expected to be announced in spring 2027.
Challenge participants will also be invited to join a community of practice to share ideas and lessons learned and support broader adoption of promising approaches to youth fitness.
For more information, including eligibility, registration, submission requirements, and challenge rules, visit Fitness.gov.

United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, and Executive Special Agent in Charge of the New York Field Office of Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigation (“IRS-CI”), Harry T. Chavis, Jr., announced today that JOSEPH CLAY pled guilty to an Information charging him with one count of aiding and assisting in the preparation of a false and fraudulent U.S. individual income tax return. The charge arises from CLAY’s orchestration of a nearly $6 million tax fraud scheme, from 2019 to 2024, involving the filing of thousands of individual income tax returns that included false information designed to fraudulently reduce taxpayers’ federal and state tax burdens. As part of today’s guilty plea before U.S. District Judge Cathy Seibel, CLAY agreed to pay the Internal Revenue Service (“IRS”) more than $5 million in restitution.

“Tax preparers are entrusted with helping their clients follow the law—not systematically falsifying returns to manufacture deductions and refunds,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “Joseph Clay turned tax preparation into a years-long fraud scheme, filing thousands of false returns that deprived federal and state governments of nearly $6 million in tax revenue. Even a guilty plea to state tax fraud did not stop him: as he admitted today, Clay continued filing fraudulent returns for his customers.”

“Tax preparers are entrusted with helping their clients follow the law—not systematically falsifying returns to manufacture deductions and refunds,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “Joseph Clay turned tax preparation into a years-long fraud scheme, filing thousands of false returns that deprived federal and state governments of nearly $6 million in tax revenue. Even a guilty plea to state tax fraud did not stop him: as he admitted today, Clay continued filing fraudulent returns for his customers.”

“This case is a stark reminder that tax fraud is not a victimless crime,” said IRS-CI Executive Special Agent in Charge Harry T. Chavis, Jr. “By orchestrating a scheme that manipulated thousands of tax returns and deprived both the IRS and New York state of millions in revenue, Joseph Clay abused the trust placed in tax professionals and harmed honest taxpayers across our community. Today’s guilty plea sends a clear message: we will aggressively pursue those who exploit the tax system for personal gain. Our commitment to protecting taxpayers and upholding the integrity of our nation’s tax laws remains unwavering.”

According to the Information and statements made in public filings and court proceedings:

From 2019 through 2024, covering tax years 2018 through 2023, CLAY—who operated tax preparation businesses in Yonkers going by the names Premier Tax and Professional Services LLC and Prime Tax & Professional Services LLC—filed over 3,500 tax returns with the IRS and New York state authorities. During this period, CLAY repeatedly and routinely submitted false information in customers’ tax returns, including, among other things, inflated and fictitious itemized tax deductions and fraudulent claims for residential energy credits, to reduce his customers’ tax liability and increase his customers’ tax refunds. In total, CLAY’s conduct deprived the IRS of more than $5 million in tax revenue, and deprived New York state tax authorities of close to $900,000.

* * *

CLAY, 52, of Lodi, New Jersey, pled guilty to one count of aiding and assisting in the preparation of a false and fraudulent U.S. individual income tax return, which carries a maximum sentence of three years in prison.

The maximum potential sentence in this case is prescribed by Congress and provided here for informational purposes only, as any sentencing of the defendant will be determined by the judge.

Mr. McDonald thanked IRS-CI for their outstanding work in this case.

This case is being handled by the Office’s White Plains Division. Assistant U.S. Attorney Carmi Schickler is in charge of the prosecution.
title: Yonkers Tax Preparer Pleads Guilty After Causing Nearly $6 Million In Tax Loss

Reps. Chu and Cisneros Introduce Bill to Fund Clean Drinking Water
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28) and Rep. Gil Cisneros (CA-31) introduced the San Gabriel Basin Restoration Fund Reauthorization Act, which would remove the funding cap for the ongoing groundwater treatment by the San Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority, reauthorize funding at $250 million, and support the completion of the ongoing water restoration project. The San Gabriel Basin provides drinking water for over 1.5 million residents in the San Gabriel Valley and Los Angeles County, including the cities of Alhambra, Arcadia, Monrovia, Monterey Park, Rosemead, Sierra Madre, and South Pasadena.
“The San Gabriel Basin provides drinking water to more than 1.5 million people across our region, but it still carries contamination left behind by industries of the past,” said Rep. Chu. “For decades, the San Gabriel Basin Restoration Fund has powered the Water Quality Authority’s work to clean up our groundwater, and this bill would provide the long-term federal support needed to finish the job. I’m proud to join Congressmember Cisneros in leading this effort, building on our work securing federal Community Project Funding for this project. Families across the San Gabriel Valley deserve a safe, reliable, and sustainable source of drinking water for generations to come.”
“The San Gabriel Valley relies on the clean drinking water provided by the San Gabriel Basin,” said Rep. Cisneros. “Since 2000, the San Gabriel Basin Restoration Fund has supported the Water Quality Authority’s work to clean and restore contaminated groundwater in our region. This legislation would remove funding hurdles and provide the support needed to bring this decades-long project across the finish line. Earlier this year, I worked with Congresswoman Chu to secure critical federal Community Project Funding for the restoration fund, and we’re committed to passing this legislation to further accelerate groundwater cleanup. Clean drinking water is a fundamental human right, and every family in the San Gabriel Valley deserves direct, affordable, protected access to it.”
Full text of the bill can be found HERE.
title: Reps. Chu and Cisneros Introduce Bill to Fund Clean Drinking Water
